"com of vong village", specialty of hanoi when autumn comes. there is legend about how com (young sticky rice) was born in vong village. in an autumn of thousands of years ago, local people there suffered a huge storm which destroyed all paddy fields where rice was about to be in flowering period. the locals had to collect and roast remaining young rice to eat. the dish as the last resort turned out to have distinctively delicious taste and later become a delicacy of the village. there is legend about how com (young sticky rice) was born in vong village. in an autumn of thousands of years ago, local people there suffered a huge storm which destroyed all paddy fields where rice was about to be in flowering period. the locals had to collect and roast remaining young rice to eat. the dish as the last resort turned out to have distinctively delicious taste and later become a delicacy of the village. the dish is said to be a signal of autumn with its plain but elegant taste, especially when it is enjoyed with ripe aromatic banana or persimmon. but it should be the process of making com that illustrates its grace better. first rice collected from field is threshed and sieved. then well rounded rice seeds are selected and roasted. it is necessary to stir steadily to keep the heat stable. after that roasted seeds are crushed about ten times and finished com is wrapped in lotus leaves to absorb their subtle scent. apart from traditional com, people nowadays make young sticky rice cake, sweetened young sticky rice paste. young sticky rice cake, together with yellow-colored wedding pastry, is symbol of steadfast and eternal love and becomes an indispensable item in engagement ceremony in vietnam./.

"dome of the chain" was named after the iron chain that sits in the middle of its dome and is located east of the dome of the rock mosque, about 3 meters away from its eastern gate. it is a small beautifully decorated and shaped structure with only pillars and no walls. it has 17 pillars in total. 11 of them are connected to an outer circle, and 6 of them are connected to an inner circle. they are all connected in a way that allows the spectator to see each and every pillar without any covering the other, while also containing a very special mihrab/niche. it was a place where the prophet david peace be upon him used to handle judicature cases and it was given the moniker "the court of david". the dome of the chain was constructed at the time of the umayyad dynasty when the caliph abd al-malik ibn marwan reigned.

"el puntudo" is a beautiful hike through a great jurassic park like landscape. if you are lucky as me and there are no clouds, you can overview almost the whole island from the top. take a bicycle to the start point (around 30min from bellavista or 1h from puerto ayora, download "organic maps" app and there you see the path). then it is a 3.5km hike and only 300m altitude change, can be done in around 1h. the way was very muddy in some parts, preferably you go with high hiking shoes... i saw nobody except a cute giant tortoise.

"exploring langtang national park: a himalayan gem of nature and culture" introduction: - langtang national park is nepals first himalayan national park established in 1976. - located in the central himalayan region it covers an area of 1710 km² across nuwakot rasuwa and sindhupalchok districts. - known for its stunning landscapes rich biodiversity and cultural heritage it is a prime destination for trekking and nature enthusiasts. geographical features: - the park ranges from 1500 m to 7234 m langtang lirung peak. - features diverse terrains including lush forests alpine meadows, glaciers and highaltitude lakes like gosainkunda. - the langtang valley is often called the valley of glaciers due to its dramatic glacial formations. biodiversity: - flora rhododendron oak pine and juniper forests alpine shrubs and medicinal herbs. - fauna home to endangered species like the red panda snow leopard himalayan black bear and langur monkeys. - over 250 bird species including the himalayan monal and blood pheasant. tourism and trekking: - popular for the langtang valley trek gosainkunda trek and tamang heritage trail. - offers a mix of adventure cultural experiences and scenic beauty. - less crowded than everest and annapurna regions providing a more serene trekking experience. - major stops include kyanjin gompa langtang village and sacred gosainkunda lake. socio-cultural and religious significance: - inhabited by the tamang and sherpa communities with rich tibetan buddhist influences. - kyanjin gompa and other monasteries hold spiritual importance. - the annual gosainkunda pilgrimage attracts thousands of hindu and buddhist devotees. climate change impact: - melting glaciers threaten water sources and biodiversity. - increased risk of landslides and flash floods due to erratic weather. - local communities face challenges in agriculture and livestock rearing. best time to visit: - spring, march-may: blooming rhododendrons, clear skies, moderate temperatures - autumn, september- november: stable weather, excellent visibility, ideal for trekking - monsoon, june-august: heavy rainfall risk of landslides, less recommended - winter, december- february: cold with snow at higher altitudes, suitable for experienced trekkers how to get there: - by road: 6-8 hours drive from kathmandu to syabrubesi, starting point for treks. - by flight no direct flights nearest airport is in kathmandu - permits required: tims card and langtang national park entry permit obtained in kathmandu or dhunche. final thoughts: - a perfect blend of natural beauty adventure and cultural richness. - less commercialized than other trekking regions offering an authentic himalayan experience. - climate change poses a threat making sustainable tourism crucial. - highly recommended for trekkers wildlife lovers and those seeking spiritual solace.

"the cable car museum in san francisco is a fascinating and unique destination that offers visitors an in-depth look at one of the city's most iconic modes of transportation. located in the historic cable car barn and powerhouse, the museum provides a blend of history, engineering, and culture that makes it a must-visit for locals and tourists alike. the exhibits are thoughtfully curated, showcasing the evolution of cable cars from their inception in the late 19th century to their continued operation today. you'll find beautifully preserved historic cable cars on display, including the first cable car ever built, which adds a personal and nostalgic touch to the experience. the museum also features detailed explanations of the mechanics behind the cable car system, including the underground cables and pulleys that power these vehicles. watching the machinery in action is a highlight, as it offers a rare glimpse into the inner workings of this ingenious transportation system. interactive displays and informative panels make the museum engaging for visitors of all ages. whether you're a history buff, an engineering enthusiast, or simply curious about san francisco's unique character, the cable car museum has something to offer. the staff are friendly and knowledgeable, always ready to answer questions and share interesting anecdotes about the cable cars and their role in the city's history. the museum's location in nob hill adds to its charm, as the surrounding area is steeped in history and offers stunning views of the city. admission is free, making it an accessible and budget-friendly option for anyone exploring san francisco. donations are welcome and help support the museum's efforts to preserve and share this important piece of the city's heritage.

"the kennedy falls trail is an excellent hike! the park is in great shape, and the views are absolutely stunning. the waterfall, as always, is beautiful and totally worth the effort. the hike from the start to the point where the chain is located is fairly easy, with only a gentle elevation gain, so it’s not too challenging at first. however, from that point onward, the trail becomes much more technical, requiring extra caution and preparation. there are several fallen trees across the trail, and with the recent freezing temperatures, some sections are icy. additionally, the ground is very muddy and slippery, so it’s important to be careful. make sure to wear sturdy hiking boots, bring trekking poles if possible, and consider wearing ice cleats to avoid slipping. also, keep in mind the timing—it’s approximately a 4-hour round trip, so plan accordingly. with the right gear and preparation, this trail is an amazing adventure, even in winter conditions. highly recommend it for anyone who loves nature and a bit of a challenge!"

"visited the historic imam hakim mosque in cairo, one of the prominent mosques built during the fatimid caliphate (909-1171 ce). the mosque is named after imam al-hakim bi-amr allah, the sixth fatimid caliph and imam of the ismaili branch of shia islam. construction began during the reign of imam al-moiz lideenillah and was completed in 1013 ce during imam al-hakim's reign. the mosque had fallen into a dilapidated state over the centuries but has undergone a remarkable restoration led by the dawoodi bohra community's spiritual leader, the late dr.syedna mohammed burhanuddin saheb. the restoration project involved removing approximately 3000 trucks of debris and garbage, revealing the mosque's original grandeur. a notable feature is the ancient well in the center, believed to date back to the original construction. the well adds historical significance and showcases the architectural ingenuity of the fatimid era. the restoration has brought back the mosque's former glory, making it a must-visit for history enthusiasts and those interested in islamic heritage.

(note: i write these reviews in part for my own nationwide business clients, for travel and activity inspiration. follow me for more! i’m a financial planner - cfp®️practitioner - with a focus on retirement wealth strategies, primarily serving businesswomen and lgbtq individuals. #virtualplanningcraftedwithcare®️) this may have been my favorite tourist attraction of all. i greatly enjoy anthropology, so this site did not disappoint. it's located right on the coast, on a high cliff. you experience a cool breeze from the water even though the temps can get scorching. the site is well organized and well maintained. they have lots of informational plaques that you can read. we opted to get a tour guide, which for us was terrific in helping us navigate the space but also because our guide shared a lot of knowledge with us as he pointed out the most historically significant sites within the whole ruins complex. tip #1: getting in. we opted to rent a car and drive from our resort about 30 mins away. highways were safe and well marked and our gps from our phones worked really well. finding the place was easy. however, when you first approach the ruins, you will be bombarded by unofficial "tour guides" who will be a middle man in getting you the tickets you need. they will offer to organize it all for you and navigate you to the entrance. given this was our very first experience with this, we "fell for it". we did it so you don't have to. all these guys do is offer to translate from english to spanish, which is unnecessary since everyone speaks english. then they will find a guide for you, tell you were to park and buy your ticket. for that, you end up paying a significant up charge for this “service”. i recommend that you drive right by them until you get to the parking area. there you can pay for parking, find an official tour guide with a federal mexican id guide badge, and purchase your tickets. if you take a tour bus, this won’t be an issue, but then you are stuck on someone else’s time schedule and you can’t move around the property as freely. tip#2: what to bring. you’ll be away from the major towns. while things will be available for purchase, it will be pricy as this is how locals make their money. i’m perfectly fine with that on occasion, but too much of this and you’ll overspend very easily. so, bring your water bottle! the ruins will not allow plastic to enter the site, so you’ll have to leave it behind or buy yourself a reusable bottle at one of the shops. next, it’s very hot any sunny. consider bringing or buying sunblock because there is limited shade. alternatively, the guides all carried umbrellas for shade. if you’re carrying a backpack, that’s an even better idea. they will check your bags, but you can bring them in. note: you can not bring in lighters or tobacco or any kind of drugs (including marijuana). finally, they do have several rest rooms, but they do not always have toilet paper available. bring some with you. they often are missing toilet seats, so if you need to be able to sit for mobility reasons, be prepared to bring some sort of seat cover or clorox wipes, etc., to clean the toilet bowl. though, we did find that the staff kept rest rooms very clean in most places. i found them cleaner than i find most public rest rooms in the us. overall, we found tulum to be good exercise. might not be appropriate if you have a wheelchair or other mobility needs. it was also very educational. the crowds got big, so go early and try for a weekday. appeared to be lgbtq-friendly and family-friendly if you are travelling with kids. the cost was also quite reasonable because of current exchange rates. nothing in mexico was what i’d consider expensive for the perspective of a new englander.

**co loa citadel: a historic landmark of vietnam’s ancient heritage** located about 20 kilometers to the north of hanoi, co loa citadel is one of vietnam’s most important historical and archaeological sites. believed to have been established in the 3rd century bc, it was the capital of the first vietnamese state, ruled by king an duong vuong. the citadel holds immense historical significance, offering visitors a glimpse into vietnam’s ancient history and the origins of its culture and civilization. the citadel is surrounded by impressive earth walls and moats that were originally designed for defense, with sections of the fortifications still visible today. visitors can explore its ancient gates, temples, and remnants of royal structures, all set amidst a tranquil landscape of rice fields and lush greenery. the most notable landmark within the citadel is the an duong vuong temple, dedicated to the legendary king who founded the citadel. the peaceful atmosphere of co loa citadel, combined with its historical richness, makes it a fascinating place for exploration. the site is particularly popular during festivals, when locals gather to honor their ancestors and celebrate vietnam’s ancient heritage. co loa citadel offers a unique blend of history, culture, and natural beauty, making it a must-visit destination for anyone interested in vietnam's past.

**fantastic horseback riding experience – highly recommended!** from the very first contact via whatsapp, everything went smoothly and clearly. responses were quick, and even last-minute, we were still able to book at the end of march—super convenient! upon arrival, we received a warm welcome, and everything was well-organized. in addition to a helmet, we could also borrow chaps—ideal for extra comfort and to protect our pants while riding. the guidance from enrique and niki was enthusiastic and knowledgeable. they shared a lot about the land and life as a gaucho, which made the ride even more special. the best part was that it wasn’t a standard tourist ride with a large group walking in a single-file line. instead, we could ride side by side, and for those who wanted, there were plenty of opportunities to trot or even gallop. of course, there was no pressure, so it was also a great experience for those who preferred a more relaxed pace. the route was stunning and diverse: we rode uphill, downhill, through forests, across open plains with breathtaking views, and even through small river crossings, which added to the adventure. in short, an amazing experience for both beginners and advanced riders. absolutely recommended!

**khuê văn các: a timeless symbol of hanoi’s academic heritage** situated within the historic văn miếu–quốc tử giám complex, khuê văn các is an exquisite pavilion that stands as a symbol of vietnam’s dedication to learning and culture. located in the heart of hanoi, this site was originally built in 1070 as a temple to honor confucius and became home to vietnam’s first national university, quốc tử giám. khuê văn các, constructed in 1805, remains one of the most iconic architectural highlights of this cultural treasure. the pavilion’s design is a harmonious blend of traditional vietnamese architecture and confucian principles. elevated on four sturdy stone pillars, its wooden structure features intricate carvings and latticed windows resembling the sun’s rays, signifying enlightenment and knowledge. the tiled roof and red-painted wood add to its timeless beauty. surrounded by lush gardens, serene courtyards, and ancient banyan trees, khuê văn các offers a tranquil atmosphere that inspires reflection. the site also houses stone steles inscribed with the names of successful scholars from imperial examinations, emphasizing the deep respect for education in vietnamese culture. as a unesco-recognized site, khuê văn các is not only a historical monument but also a vibrant reminder of vietnam’s intellectual legacy, making it a must-visit for anyone exploring hanoi.

on foot, navigating ridges and canyons while absorbing panoramic views. trails cater to various fitness levels and trekking experiences. * **stargazing:** free from excessive light pollution, moonland touch the extraordinary.**

**stumbled upon a hidden gem (that’s apparently not so hidden)** so there i was, enjoyed a bumpy ride with my dining crew to this “off-the-beaten-path” restaurant that turned out to be about as secret as a kardashian pregnancy. one peek at the menu and i realized i wasn’t the first food explorer to discover this place – judging by the identical photos from years past, this spot has been instagram-famous longer than avocado toast. fair warning: the portions here are what i like to call “european elegant” (translation: bring snacks). unless you’re planning to survive on good vibes and artistic plating, i would suggest a strategic pre-dinner appetizer at home. think of it as culinary foreplay. the service comes with complimentary photobombing – the server had an uncanny ability to appear in every single shot like some sort of dining paparazzi. note to management: maybe teach the staff the ancient art of “duck and cover” when phones or camera come out? despite feeling like i had been pranked by every food blogger before me, the experience was solid enough to earn a return visit. i’ll be back when they inevitably roll out their “new” seasonal menu (fingers crossed it doesn’t look suspiciously familiar too).

**sydney town hall – inner city icon and civic splendor (210 words)** sydney town hall, perched prominently on george street, is an enduring civic landmark steeped in history. built in two main stages between 1869 and 1889 on the former old sydney burial ground, it showcases a commanding second empire victorian design and was constructed with local sandstone. approaching from the grand façade and ascending its broad sandstone steps (a popular rendezvous point), visitors enter a high‑ceilinged vestibule adorned with ornate mosaics, columns, and chandeliers. inside, centennial hall is breathtaking: its grand organ—once the world’s largest—boasts nearly 9,000 pipes and the rare 64‑foot contra trombone stop. the richly decorated woodwork, stained‑glass windows, and historic plaques underscore the hall’s role as the place of democracy and cultural events across generations. while guided tours are not currently offered, the building’s grandeur speaks for itself. it remains operational as a government venue, concert hall, and event space, yet retains much of its original interiors after more than 130 years. looking ahead, the upcoming **town hall square** project promises to transform the public space fronting the building into a verdant, pedestrian-friendly plaza.🚧 with construction slated to begin in 2028, the square will redefine how locals and visitors engage with this heritage site. combining historic gravitas with evolving civic life, sydney town hall offers a richly layered and unforgettable experience—an architectural jewel and community centre wrapped in one.

06/11/2025 this was a super challenging yet amazing hike! my mom and i hiked this trail together as our last day activity in hawaii, and it was definitely a highlight! the trailhead is a little difficult to find, just look for the sign on the tree, and to park, you just have to find somewhere around the neighborhood. it rained pretty much the entire time we hiked, which made the trail a lot more difficult and muddy. it is unmaintained, which means that there will be a lot of bushwhacking through plants of all kinds, and you will most likely get extremely muddy. i would recommend to wear long pants, i wore some leggings that only covered half of my legs and i got really scratched up. at the third waterfall, there’s the option to either rope climb up the waterfall or go on a small, extremely unmaintained path next to it, which is the option that we chose. the trail that we chose is still extremely difficult, though! there was a lot of slipping and i almost fell down the trail at some point, but a log that was jutting out caught me in the small fall. the crater at the top is beautiful, and after seeing the crater, there is the option to either take the return trail back down the ridge, or go on the trail that will have you summit the peak and then hike the entire crater ridgeline. we personally chose to summit the peak and then hike the entire ridge, but i would only recommend that to extremely experienced hikers! please be safe, it’s a very fun, but also very dangerous hike that people have to get rescued off of every month!! bring lots of water and wear adequate shoes, even if it hasn’t rained, it will still be muddy! overall, we hiked around 7.5 miles and it took us around 9 hours, so plan for all day if you’re doing the full thing!

2024-06-14. beautiful views for midnight sun, but trail is not very safe by north american standards. steep, no railings or supports, and little signage except at forks and with occasional cairns. trekking poles were critical for me, especially on the descent. google maps is insufficient for this hike (and i assume many in the area), so do download one of the norwegian map apps in the app store and use that. norgeskart outdoors was the most useful for me. effectively there are two trails to the main saddle, then a scramble to the top of what we’d call the “haystack” in the us. the dalen trail is the primary trail, and there is another trail branching off the linken trail about 70% to the linken summit. the majority of the elevation gain is to reach the saddle. on the eastern side of the saddle (closer to svolvær and the sea) is a prominence, which seemed nice and did not require a scramble. the haystack is the summit and is at the western side of the saddle. consult the topo map and my screenshot. there are two approaches to the haystack: one is an unprotected scramble along the north edge (doable but very exposed), and the other has an ~8m chain. i went up the north scramble and down the chain. i’d recommend the chain for both, in retrospect. i took the main dalen route up and returned via the cutoff to linken. dalen is more consistent of a climb: it starts climbing and maintains the same grade. there are duckboards in the areas of heaviest mud, but even after 5 days without rain, it was damp on the north approaches. dalen intersects with linken at around 10% into the linken trail, and i actually liked that. i think the more you stay on the gravel road for linken, the safer the trail is. i would recommend the linken trail to the intersection to tjeldbergtind at 70%, but it is incredibly steep. the steepest section gains 100m elevation in ~150m distance. it is deceptive after the fork, because the first ~250m only gains about 40m in elevation, then sharply increases. this felt downright treacherous on the descent, and it was in ideal conditions. the view is lovely, and i’m very happy to have experienced it at midnight during the midnight summer season. i think it is worthwhile, but i think it is critical to understand how the trail conditions are unsafe for the inexperienced. the nearby djevelporten is a steeper elevation gain, but tjeldbergtind demonstrates why the 505 sherpa stairs were necessary. i hope that they make the same investment for sections of tjeldbergtind, too.

4.5/5 stars: old faithful, yellowstone i recently visited old faithful in yellowstone national park, and it was an unforgettable experience! this iconic geyser is a must-see attraction, and i was impressed by its majesty. *highlights:* - *impressive water show:* the eruption was truly breathtaking, with water shooting high into the air for around 2 minutes. the sound of the geyser erupting was exhilarating! - *predictable schedule:* i waited around 20 minutes for the eruption, which is relatively short compared to the maximum wait time of 90 minutes. the park's prediction system is quite accurate, making it easy to plan your visit. *tips:* - *check the schedule:* plan your visit according to the predicted eruption times to minimize wait times. - *bring a jacket:* it can get chilly while waiting for the eruption, especially in the mornings or evenings. - *respect the environment:* stay on designated boardwalks and follow park rules to preserve the natural wonder. *overall experience:* old faithful is an awe-inspiring natural wonder that exceeded my expectations. the wait was worth it, and the eruption was a thrilling experience. if you're visiting yellowstone, old faithful is a must-see attraction that will leave you in wonder.

5 stars royal mara safari lodge was a dream! the spacious, renovated tents offer complete privacy and comfort, all nestled along the serene maasai river. each day we enjoyed 4-course meals that rival fine dining—paired with stellar wine options and top-tier service. the raw, breathtaking exposure to nature was perfectly balanced with the reassuring presence of maasai warriors. every detail was handled with world-class hospitality. truly nothing left to be desired... except more time to stay.

5 stars – breathtaking views of venice visiting st. mark’s campanile was a highlight of our trip to venice. you take a convenient elevator ride to the top, and the moment the doors open, you’re greeted with absolutely spectacular views of the entire city. from the top, you get a panoramic look at st. mark’s square, the grand canal, and the rooftops of venice stretching all the way to the horizon. it’s peaceful, awe-inspiring, and gives you a whole new appreciation for the beauty and layout of this historic city. if you’re in venice, this is a must-visit spot. the views alone are worth it, and the elevator makes it accessible for everyone. don’t miss it!

5 stars — a dreamy yacht experience in dubai! our experience with dream boats dubai was nothing short of magical! from the moment we stepped aboard, we were welcomed with warm hospitality, a beautifully set-up lounge area, and the most serene views of the water. the boat was spotlessly clean, tastefully decorated, and felt more like a floating living room than a typical chartered yacht. as a mom of three, i’m always looking for family-friendly experiences — and this ticked all the boxes. the kids were thrilled with the variety of snacks and drinks, and we adults got to relax with arabic coffee and enjoy the calm, luxurious vibe. the setup was picture-perfect, with a lovely arrangement of refreshments, cold drinks, popcorn, and even fresh flowers adding to the charm. what really impressed me was the attention to detail: everything from the gold arabic coffee pot to the personalized trays, qr code menu, and plush pillows (with quotes!) made us feel pampered and at home. the crew was professional yet friendly, and they made sure we had everything we needed without being intrusive. whether you’re planning a family outing, birthday celebration, girls’ day out, or even a romantic cruise, this is one of the most relaxing and scenic ways to enjoy dubai from the water. it’s a hidden gem that offers a calm alternative to the typical party yachts. highly recommend dream boats for anyone looking for a luxurious, calm, and memorable experience in dubai — especially if you’re traveling with kids or just want a laid-back vibe with 5-star service. we’ll definitely be booking again soon!

5/14/2025 wild trail! mud and rocks were very slippery, it was a wet day (rained for about 10 minutes just before i started). kind of treacherous climbing the trail beside the 3rd waterfall all the way back and around the crater. the side trail for waterfall #3 is a slick muddy surface. at one point, i spent 10 minutes trying to get up a few steps because i kept sliding back down. plenty of class 2 scrambling, and probably occasionally some class 3. there were a few extra difficult spots for me to climb up from the top of the 3rd waterfall until the summit (short lady). that part is also just mud. the ridge return after the crater was more moderate until it joins back up with the main trail. my legs got all scraped up, i was quite muddy, and very wet. i still wouldn’t choose to wear pants though. countless stream crossings and ropes. really is a ‘hard’ level trail, requires some route finding, cautious footing, upper and lower body strength, mental fortitude. it’s got all the typical riskiness of a hawaiian hike and then a lot more. saw 7 other people. took me 8h 15 min. used 2.5l water and ran out about 5 minutes before the trailhead. saw 1 boar.. it ran away.

5/5 - fantastic experience! touring israel with assaf was the most eye-opening and genuine experience. traveling with a group of approximately 39 people, i felt organized, informed, and supported at all times. assaf went above and beyond to make certain that we were prepared for each site by explaining the cultural norms, attire, and any supplies we would need (ex. water bottle, sweater, sunglasses). prior to arriving at a site, he took time to explain multiple perspectives of what made the site significant, not only historically but present day. assaf is highly intelligent, thoughtful, and engaged; frequently checking in to see if we had any questions and contributing to the discussion. he is an excellent story teller. really, there was never a dull moment. i can confidently say that i walked away from the trip a more informed, compassionate, and enriched person. i speak for our group when i say, thank you so very much assaf! for keeping us safe, stretching our minds, and sharing the deep origins of israel. much respect for your professionalism, timeliness, and organization! for anyone needing a tour guide, boker tours is the way to travel!! i give them my highest recommendation without any hesitation.

6 grueling hours by boat from sorong, on a sea that can be choppy, at 25 knot /hour, that's a bumpy ride.....fortunately we split the trip in two, and spent a night mid way. that place is better than anything we can watch on insta. nature does not need any editing here. we can't edit something perfect. the colors are almost too real to be true, the environment is still pristine, although it's slowly becoming a popular destination...the distance from sorong will keep it preserved a few more years hopefully..... transparent water, white sandy bottom, you can scan through the sea from top to bottom just by looking from the boat deck. the karstic mounts look like popcorn on the emerald sea, popcorn covered with green vegetation. it's incredible and only aerial pictures can truly reveal the awesomeness of this place. if magic is a place, then here it is.

7 weeks i stayed at barefoot conservation as a volunteer. i can only say it was a one in a lifetime experience with the wildest encounters i’ve had. in the first week i swam with a omura whale with her calf and in my last week i swam with 8 manta rays who were feeding. barefoot conservation has taught me a lot about marine life and what it means to be a good diver. as a diver you should always try to contribute to the ocean and i think barefoot does that. with their great surveys and teaching divers to be considerate when they are diving. special thanks to the science team who taught me about the marine life and surveys. this gave me a whole new view on my dives. and also thanks to iris and matt for managing everything, even when it was not always easy. i want to comment that the negative reviews are from people who can’t adapt to the simple lifestyle that is at barefoot (that i loved) and that simon is not very good in the communication. but if you can adapt to that, you’re going to have great time at barefoot. at last i want to say that the dogs (kentang, ringo, sweat potato & foxy) and of course cat suki, made everyday joyful 💙 i really respect everyone who works at barefoot, keep up the good work. and i hope that someday i can come back 🤍

8/15-asahiyama zoo tonight i decided to go to asahiyama zoo for a night adventure. there were a lot of people going there for a pilgrimage during the night hours (only 8/10-8/16 a year are open for the animals to see visitors at night). i took the bus to the destination (get on the bus at platform 6 of asahikawa station) and arrived at the destination after about 40 minutes. i started to meet the animals. this park is really big, and there are shuttle buses to run specific animal exhibition areas. watching the animals at close range and laughing with children, the thing that touched me the most was... the hippo's sports parade. due to the venue, the hippo seemed to be doing the parade in a certain area, and the polar bear seemed to feel a little anxious because of the crowds of people, so he greeted people... of course, my favorite thing was the king penguins holding their heads up and posing for you to take as many photos as you want, showing their superstar side... time passed quickly, and it was time to go back to the hotel... this is a night of sports and walking, and also a night of returning to nature... 🙂

a baía dos golfinhos, oficialmente chamada baía dos golfinhos ou baía dos golfinhos rotadores, é um dos lugares mais mágicos e preservados de fernando de noronha. é famosa mundialmente por ser um dos maiores santuários naturais de golfinhos-rotadores (stenella longirostris), que ali entram em grupos todos os dias ao amanhecer — um espetáculo raro e comovente da natureza. acesso e preservação o acesso à baía é altamente restrito para preservar o ecossistema local e proteger os golfinhos. não é permitido descer até a praia. a observação só pode ser feita de cima, no mirante dos golfinhos, após uma trilha leve e bem sinalizada dentro do parque nacional marinho. por isso, é importante chegar cedo, entre 5h30 e 7h, quando os golfinhos costumam entrar na baía em grande número, saltando, nadando em sincronia e se exibindo naturalmente. experiência de observação a experiência no mirante é silenciosa, contemplativa e emocionante. ver dezenas, às vezes centenas, de golfinhos livres em seu habitat natural é um privilégio que poucas regiões do mundo oferecem com tamanha proximidade e regularidade. o local também oferece uma vista panorâmica espetacular da costa de noronha, com o mar em tons hipnotizantes de azul e verde. envolvimento com a pesquisa científica a baía também é um importante local de estudo e monitoramento dos golfinhos por parte do projeto golfinho rotador, uma referência em conservação marinha no brasil. há painéis informativos ao longo da trilha, o que enriquece a visita com conteúdo educativo e ambiental. dicas vá cedo para garantir a melhor chance de ver os golfinhos. leve binóculos, se possível, para uma observação mais detalhada. mantenha o silêncio no mirante para não estressar os animais. combine a visita com a trilha que leva à praia do sancho, já que os acessos ficam próximos. conclusão a baía dos golfinhos é um lugar de contemplação e respeito à natureza. mais do que uma atração turística, é um símbolo da importância da preservação ambiental em fernando de noronha. uma visita que sensibiliza, emociona e reforça a conexão com a vida marinha. indispensável para quem busca experiências autênticas e transformadoras em meio à natureza.

a beautiful experience even in the rain. we visited the national orchid garden on a rainy day, but that didn’t take away from the experience at all. in fact, the rain made everything feel even more lush and peaceful. the garden is absolutely stunning, with a breathtaking variety of orchids in every shape and color. it’s thoughtfully laid out, easy to explore, and full of quiet corners to pause and admire the plants. we came with our two young daughters, ages 5 and 6, and they were absolutely delighted. they loved wandering through the misty paths, spotting different flowers, and especially enjoyed the section with celebrity orchids named after famous visitors like princess diana. they were so curious and excited to learn about the flowers and who they were named after. the garden is very well maintained, with a nice balance of open and sheltered areas, so we were able to stay mostly dry. everything felt calm and clean, and the staff were friendly and helpful. the cool house was a favorite—it felt like stepping into a magical rainforest. to top it all off, the girls enjoyed some ice cream at the end, which made their day even sweeter. this place was a highlight of our trip and a wonderful spot to spend a couple of hours. whether you're a plant lover or just looking for a peaceful and beautiful place to visit, this garden is a must-see. five stars from all of us.

a beautiful hiking trail. our azores vacation started with this trail. it's a linear trail that starts at this point and ends at a village. it's written 5.9 km and 2 hrs, but it's definitely way more than that. we aren't super fit people. so we went at a normal pace. the entire length is 9.5 km (our watch confirmed it) and took us 4 hrs to complete. from the main trail head, one has to deviate to see salto do carrago, salto do prego, and an abandoned village sanguinho. we visited only salto do carrago. definitely wear good hiking shoes you trust and carry water and some food. even at this start point, there are no shops. the first 2 km from this trailhead was the adventurous part. muddy and at some places slippery. one has to be careful. you can take a dip at the waterfalls. the last 2-3 kms of the trail were steep and downhill. we parked our scooter at this trail head and took a taxi from the village at the end of the trail to return back to this point. we saw some people start at the village and go to salto do prego and/or sanguinho, maybe the entire trail. if you start at the village, the first few km are very steep, and most of the trail would be uphill.

a beautiful natural setting with four thermal pools of varying temperatures. the coolest one is at the top, just beneath a small waterfall — perfect for a refreshing contrast to the warmer lower pools. the facility is located about 200 meters from the entrance. everything is clean, well organized. the pools are surrounded by greenery, giving the whole place a very relaxing jungle vibe. changing cabins are simple wooden structures under a shelter and aren't very spacious. the ones at the top tend to be less crowded. lockers are available (for a fee) and just big enough for a small backpack. there are also several benches where you can leave your belongings, but be aware that there is no large shelter in case of rain. toilets and showers are available on site, though queues are common during busy hours. one ticket gives you 1.5 hours in the pools, but you can still enjoy the surrounding area outside of that time. i highly recommend booking your tickets online in advance. you can select a specific time slot for your visit and make sure there’s availability when you arrive. overall, it’s a fantastic experience that i 100% recommend.

a beautiful park for a relaxing walk, with lovely riverside restaurants. it’s usually quite crowded and popular with tourists. you can combine your visit with a river cruise and buffet, or simply enjoy a stroll, ride the ferris wheel, visit the haunted house, or explore small shops and dine at local restaurants with scenic views. the food options are diverse and delicious.

a beautiful park on the outskirts of tokyo, towards tokyo bay. a short walk from the old fish market, its a nice and peaceful way to walk off any food coma you suffer after the market. some nice places to sit and relax. location is the old shoguns hunting lodge & facilities to entertain dignitaries. all the original buildings were destroyed in ww2, but have been rebuilt using traditional techniques to the original design from records. a beautiful place to relax. visit if you can, you will enjoy your time. we stayed for a couple of hours.

a beautiful park when the cherry blossoms are in full bloom. so much land to explore and the zoo was an unexpected surprise, the animals there are so nice to see. even when it was raining on the day my friends and i attended, it still looked incredibly beautiful. i will definitely be coming again to see the cherry blossoms next year, and also this summer when the weather is perfect for an outside picnic.

a beautiful patch of greenery connecting two streets, between the two uws parks. it really provides some nice respite from the rest of the concrete-filled blocks.

a beautiful picturesque place full of beautiful flowers, neat and clean camps, food so delicious that you'll always eat more than your capacity, fun bonfire activity. and the highlight of the place is their service that warms your heart. tip: you can see stars and constellations with naked eyes post 11 pm 100% recommend this place.

a beautiful place with mesmerizing views. a spacious family friendly lodge. i owe it to myself to revisit the serengeti sopa lodge again. the staff is so kind and helpful (thank you)! the cafe time is a must do while staying at the lodge. the dining experience is superb, providing a great introduction to some classic cultural cuisine.

a beautiful place. a green, peaceful, and atmospheric garden on the island of the sun. the garden offers a magnificent view of lake titicaca and the snow-capped mountains in the distance. the garden houses a small museum, but with interesting exhibits, especially the interesting costumes and masks. the ascent requires some physical fitness due to the very high altitude – starting from approximately 3,800 meters. however, it's worth it, as it's a place where you can find peace.

a beautiful revival of old central market i loved the concept of turning the old central market into a vibrant, artsy space celebrating local creativity. it’s wonderful to see so many local artists and makers showcasing their souvenirs, arts, and crafts—each piece reflecting a unique hong kong influence and spirit. i especially appreciated the dedicated space that shares the rich history of the market. it was thoughtfully presented and made the visit feel even more meaningful and enriching. beyond the art and crafts, there are plenty of nice spots for food, groceries, restaurants, and coffee too—making it a lively and welcoming place to explore, relax, and support local businesses. a beautifully reimagined space that blends heritage, creativity, and community all in one!

a beautiful river canal right through the middle of the city. very relaxing and serene. while we were there, there was a pop-up library with little seats and lanterns following the riverwalk. a beautiful serene experience in the middle of the chaos of the city. definitely worth a visit!
a beautiful salar! many kinds of breeds of birds here and you'll probably get lucky to see flamingos as well. there's also a big lake area. enjoy the long walks around the salar here. a must visit!

a beautiful sea wall with lots of people. **scams are common** people telling you about salsa festivals or the last day to buy half price cigars. they are just basic scams. it happens 4 or 5 to us over the course of two days.

a beautiful short 15 minute walking track from manly surf club at the south end of manly beach to shelly beach in manly, new south wales, australia 🇦🇺. it’s the shelly beach eco structure walk around cabbage tree bay which hugs the coastline all the way to shelly beach. located in manly next to the manly surf pavilion. it offers fantastic views of both manly beach and shelly beach. keep an eye out for the little silver ornaments attached to the rock walls along the walkway. they are easy to miss but add to your experience. it’s a flat walk which is suitable for all ages and disabilities including wheelchairs. there’s a couple of shops and a cafe approximately halfway along and there’s also toilet and facilities. this is directly across from the historic fairy bower rockpool not far from the shops and cafe. you can get here by getting the ferry from circular quay to manly wharf and walking up to manly beach, turn right and follow to the manly surf pavilion. after finishing the walk at shelly beach, if you are so inclined, you can further walk up to the lookout on the headland for amazing views of the northern beaches. would highly recommend 😊

a beautiful site, according to orthodox tradition this is the location of our blessed mother's empty tomb. i believe that no assertion is made to the location of her passing (dormition). a lovely little eastern orthodox chapel. supposedly the place where the virgin mary was buried and later was resurrected - only her shroud was left behind. this is where the disciples entombed mary after her death. also the cave where jesus was betrayed by judas to the romans and pharisees for 30 pieces of silver. the tomb of the virgin mary is situated near the church of all nations and the garden of gethsemane. visiting the tomb is a memorable experience: visitors must go deep underground, down a staircase that was carved in the rock during the twelfth century. immediately surrounding is a sparkling array of iconography, hanging from the ceiling and decorating the cave walls. medieval art, including a painting of the madonna and child, adorn this sanctuary.

a beautiful temple located in the heart of bangkok, known as wat pathum wanaram (วัดปทุมวนาราม). i’ve visited this serene place many times to pray for good luck and enjoy its peaceful ambiance. the temple's stunning architecture and tranquil surroundings make it a perfect escape from the city's hustle and bustle. whether you’re seeking spiritual blessings or just looking to appreciate its beauty and calm atmosphere, this temple is worth a visit. a hidden gem in the busy city that offers both cultural and spiritual experiences!

a beautiful temple which is best visited during a service or during the rain for a nice change of aesthetic and if you have already visited many temples. as with most major attractions i recommend aiming for off peak. rainy days are great, early morning, of simply off-peak from things like golden week etc. for such a large temple, because it is active, there isn't much 'to-do' but do have a seat during a service or just sit quietly in the temple and have a moment to soak it all in.

a beautiful walkway that leads to the beach not far from taronga zoo entry point. the views of the harbour and the party boats vibes are magnificent, while under your feet there’s pristine nature, a lizard ( #australianwaterdragon) appeared right to the edge of the track while we were passing. i took some cool pics with iphone portrait mode (im a hobbyist photographer so was quick). the walking trail is an off-road track, meaning not suitable for mobility or child param, there are steps and tree roots. we had our 1.5 year old son with param, also had baby carrier with us, i carried him and wife was pushing the empty param lifting over the steps. i looked up the reviews before for this information about accessibility, it wasn’t mentioned as i could see, so now i decided to cover the accessibility question. the nearest beach access isn’t far though so you can push/lift the param if you are two and rather fit. it is definitely worth the try, this is an amazing place.

a beautiful, wondrous place to just be. lush and green. although other people around you still have a presence of peace. as a matter of fact, you can hear many birds, you might think you are at the zoo. it’s amazing.

a beautiful-looking arena — from the outside. but once inside, expect: – 🍔 long food queues for bland frankfurters and limited options (most sold out early, no signage) – 👀 poor sightlines due to low seat incline and railings blocking the view – 🚌 underwhelming transport capacity — toei buses leave crowds stranded – 🧭 excessive detours even in extreme heat or pouring rain — staff enforce long routes with no shelter i attended the volleyball match in april and the basketball game in july. in both cases, waited over 20 minutes for food, only to find most items sold out. walked nearly 1km in 35°c heat just to enter the venue. and from my seat, the railing cut off half the court. this is the worst-designed arena i’ve visited in the past five years. built to impress on paper, not to serve real fans. a regrettable use of taxpayer money.

a bit of a tardis, with lots of info and things to look at, but unfortunately very bizarrely curated. it felt like someone has dumped everything they had about the dolomites into one place, and it was very confusing trying to get a sense of the ‘story’ of the area. labelling was very absent, moving from ‘section’ to ‘section’. the little info screens were infuriatingly out of order going from page 2 to 4, to 1 etc. and auto-scrolling quickly so you have no time to digest it all. it was just a very confusing place, and i love learning about the history of places and getting a sense of how it all fits together. the ‘treasure hunting’ was good for 20 mins for the kids, otherwise the museum has little of appeal, given the poor organisation and presentation. a bit of a waste, but still worth a visit on a rainy day, like we had, i guess the huge, and very extensive collection of decorations and ornaments and cute items, as well as bistro and deli section make this place still worth visiting, in a cool building and good location very centrally in san candido.
a bit of adventure and a lot of breathtaking picturesque scenarios in one place. one of the easiest hikes in sri lanka. up and down time approximately 6hrs.

a blessed place. i really like it here. unfortunately now for a week i couldn't come due to disease condition, but all the monks are dear to me. looking forward to celebrate holy mass again. together. „whenever two or three gather in my name“...
a boat on the neil river had restaurants and cafe i loved especially cavo island the food and the place and special thanks for haidi from reception and ahmad almasri the waiter.

a botanical park and mini art museum. estimate an hour to visit all the art galleries scattered in the park. the confectionary shop rokkatei features six local flowers which are featured as the wrapping paper can be seen there (depends on the seasons) entrance fee applies for the park, not for the cafe. there was self-serviced free coffee and a cookie at one of the galleries (no.3)

a breathtaking experience we started the mount batur adventure @ 05h00, and it was absolutely worth the early wake-up. the ride up in the jeep was already interessant and impressive, driving through the rugged black lava fields in total darkness added a sense of excitement and mystery 😉 the hike itself is a bit steep and chilly, but the views at the top are truly breathtaking. watching the sunrise above the clouds, with lake batur and the surrounding mountains slowly appearing in the morning light, was unforgettable 🙏🏼 what struck us most was the massive area covered by the lava flow from the 1926 eruption, which engulfed an entire village. seeing how much was destroyed is really impressive and makes you feel small. it does get a bit crowded ( ~80 jeeps), but the guides were kind and made everyone feel safe and supported throughout the climb, after all found their parking spot it gets quite 🧘🏼 an unforgettable and unique experience. raw nature, stunning views, and a real sense of awe. highly recommended for early birds

a breathtaking natural wonder! it is truly a one-of-a-kind experience. the boat ride through the cave is peaceful and awe-inspiring, with massive limestone formations and clear explanations from the guide. the scenery around the site is just as beautiful—lush forest, wildlife, and calm blue waters. it's well-organized, but expect some waiting due to its popularity. definitely worth the visit!

a breathtaking perspective above the mars valley. a selenar landscape, full of unbeatable shapes, textures and colors. a collection of rocks, amazing gift from the mother's nature. geology at its best features here, a dance of the planet in the sunlight and mostly on sunset candle gold light.

a breathtaking slice of bangkok history and architecture. wat ratchanatdaram worawihan, known as the “temple of the royal niece,” was commissioned by king rama iii in 1846 to honor his granddaughter, princess sommanass waddhanawathy ￼. its centerpiece is the stunning loha prasat (“metal castle”), a rare multi-tiered temple adorned with 37 metal spires symbolizing the virtues toward enlightenment ￼. despite its central old town location—at ratchadamnoen klang and maha chai road—the temple offers a calm, almost serene atmosphere. the loha prasat stands 36 m tall with three tiers (24 spires at the base, 12 in the middle, and a single top spire) and houses a buddha relic at the summit ￼. the structure’s design is modeled after ancient temples in shravasti (india) and anuradhapura (sri lanka), both of which no longer exist—making this one of only three such metal-palace structures worldwide ￼. visiting at sunrise or late afternoon offers the best lighting and atmosphere. the outer garden plaza, opened after the adjacent cinema’s demolition, now showcases a pavilion and statue of king rama iii 📍 intersection of ratchadamnoen klang & maha chai rd, phra nakhon, bangkok 🕘 open daily, 9 am–5 pm (approx.) 💡 tip: best visited in the early morning or just before sunset for gorgeous light and fewer crowds. #thailand #bangkok #thebestintheworld#traval#วัดราชนัดดา

a breathtaking spot in hong kong, surrounded by beautiful greenery with amazing ocean and mountain views. it’s so peaceful and scenic that it almost doesn’t feel like you're in hong kong. however, i was disappointed by our experience at the buddhist art museum. the staff came across as quite self-important, and with so many security personnel and strict rules, it felt as if mr. li ka shing himself might have been visiting. this sense of arrogance really detracted from what is meant to be a peaceful and tranquil place. my friend and i wanted to try the zen calligraphy session, which you can find as you leave the museum exhibition. the system for lining up and signing up wasn’t very clear, and the staff seemed a little annoyed and distant when we asked questions. they suggested we come back for the afternoon session, but luckily we managed to get a spot in the morning one. overall, i’d say this place is definitely worth checking out at least once. just be sure to book your visit in advance, and if you can, try to plan your trip during the cooler months, since hong kong’s summer heat can make it pretty tough to fully enjoy the experience outdoors.

a breathtaking unesco world heritage experience – underground river, puerto princesa the underground river in puerto princesa, palawan, is nothing short of a natural wonder that leaves you in awe. as a unesco world heritage site, this remarkable river winds its way through stunning limestone caves, creating a surreal and peaceful environment. the boat tour is an unforgettable journey into the heart of nature, where you'll be surrounded by incredible rock formations, glowing stalactites, and crystal-clear waters. the experience is not just visually stunning but also humbling, as you witness the raw beauty and tranquility of this hidden gem. the guides are knowledgeable and friendly, sharing fascinating insights about the cave’s history, geology, and rich biodiversity. the river is home to unique species, and the surrounding forest is teeming with life, making it a perfect spot for nature lovers. the sense of serenity and the pristine beauty of the place make it feel like you're stepping into another world—one where time slows down, and the natural world thrives in its most unspoiled form. whether you're a fan of adventure, photography, or simply soaking in breathtaking views, the underground river is a must-visit destination that should be on every traveler’s bucket list. visiting the underground river is an experience that resonates long after you leave. it’s a testament to the power of nature and a reminder of the importance of preserving such extraordinary places for future generations. a true highlight of palawan!

a breezy respite from the heat and the crowds of san marco. i took the vaporetto over very early to take some pictures, but nothing was open yet. i got back on the #2 line and continued around the city. but i came back a couple hours later to take the tour of the monastery.

a brief story about how amazing the spa is. we turned into the alley where the spa is located and a man came up to my friend and i and purposefully worked to lead us away to a different spa. he told us we would get a better deal, but the other spa he showed us on google had far worse reviews. we assume that he was being paid to poach their visitors. that’s how good this place is. if this happens to you, do not go with them. contrary to some views expressed, we did not feel rushed by this place whatsoever. they took us without a reservation mid afternoon on a weekday. i ordered the 30 minute scrub and 45 minute massage for 550 dirham. it was perfect and still competitively priced with other spas in the area. everything felt sanitary/legit. highly highly recommended.
a bucket list experience if ever there was one. our pilot, bethany, made our wedding day flight a perfect experience. great info, fun flight, amazing views into one of the natural windy of the world!

a bucket list item - wow! it’s not cheap but for us it was worth every penny (part of the ticket price also goes towards the park conservation). a top tier luxury experience, from the car that collected us to the pre-flight ginger tea and coffee to the post-flight champagne and bush breakfast. we felt very safe the entire time (even my mum who is super scared of heights). our pilot, abeid soka, was amazing - they are real pros here! we were lucky to see hundreds of hippos and also elephants, hyenas and zebras. i wouldn’t hesitate to book this again.

a built walkway with hundreds of steps eventually reaching, continuously upwards, the plains of abraham. the views over the river are phenomenal, with a 180 degree plus panorama. if you're interested or just plain lucky, you may hear the navy at work. tough climb to the end if you have young children to attend to. free admission.

a bustling area but a great spot to visit and admire. the whole area is clean and well kept and there’s so many coffee shops and cafes nearby to sit and watch the world go by. this church takes you back in history to the days when jesus christ carried the cross down the road of pain to the location of his crucifixion. a very powerful spiritual journey. located in the historical part of jaffa old city. restaurants and shops nearby. close to the jaffa port and promenade. worth a visit day and night. a melting pot for all nations, here tourists mix with us locals. a major tourist attraction point in tel aviv. i love the food aroma, especially on a friday morning.

a bustling municipal market in the monastiraki district. here you'll find everyday ingredients from meats, fish, produce, herbs, cookware, and more. it is a great site to visit and see the ingredients that locals use to prepare their meals. we were a bit turned off by one of the herb stores that tried to gouge us as tourists on the price of products.

a calm and quiet environment. we were shown around by a friendly young monk. the villagers were lending their hands in the daily chores of the monastery. the sight of the river spreading in the valley, cattle grazing, the distant mountains and the clear skies made a beautiful sight from the monastery.

a calm clean beach with excellent views for sunset. i didn't care for waikiki beach; however this beach reminded me of those in chill west maui beach vibes. there were also bench area and picnic tables, as well as a restroom

a center or a social organization, a non-profit organization established since 1991 with the purpose of nurturing, treating, and rehabilitating children of war veterans and war veterans who suffered from the consequences of agent orange/dioxin exposure during the war in vietnam who are currently facing many difficulties in life. for the above-mentioned war veterans' children, when returning to the village, they will also receive special education, integration education, career guidance, vocational training, and create conditions for them to integrate into the community. the center is managed by the central committee of the vietnam war veterans association, with operating costs supported by the state. the center also receives financial and human support from social organizations, economic organizations, non-governmental organizations, charitable individuals, and war veterans from a number of countries.

a charming and fun destination for all ages. the whimsical design creates a magical atmosphere. it’s easy to access by train or bus and makes for a great half-day trip. inside, you can watch how the cookies are being made, explore chocolate-themed exhibits, and even join a hands-on cookie decorating workshop. the garden area is beautiful, especially in spring and winter. a perfect spot for families, couples, and anyone with a sweet tooth.

a charming little museum that's definitely worth a visit — if you can get in. tickets are very affordable, but the online reservation system gets booked out quickly each month, which makes planning ahead essential. that said, the limited entry means the museum never feels overcrowded, unlike many popular european museums where you can barely move. one of the highlights was a short, exclusive film screening — really well done and engaging. the museum is also child-friendly, even for younger kids, which makes it a good family outing. there’s a café and a restaurant on-site, which is a nice bonus. the only downside is that the layout can be confusing. the signage isn’t very clear, and it’s easy to get turned around. it might be intentional to create a sense of discovery, but it can be a bit frustrating at times. overall, a unique and enjoyable experience, especially if you’re looking for something quieter and more manageable than the big-name museums.
a charming place. re-live korea's ancient period as walk through this pavilion admiring the serenity the royal grounds.

a childhood dream at 10,000 feet! 🚁🌄 okay, yes — was it expensive? absolutely. my wallet cried a little. but was it worth every single cent? without a doubt, yes! from the moment we arrived at maverick helicopters in grand canyon village, everything was smooth, friendly, and incredibly well organized. the staff made us feel like vips, and our pilot was an absolute legend — calm, professional, and somehow both tour guide and top gun at the same time. we felt completely safe and completely thrilled all at once. and then — that moment — liftoff. suddenly, we were soaring over one of the most jaw-dropping places on earth. the grand canyon is not just a national park; it’s a living, breathing wonder of nature, and seeing it from above? utterly surreal. it’s like mother nature flexing on us all. but here’s the personal twist: as a kid, i used to spend hours playing that old pc game comanche by novalogic — pixelated helicopters flying through canyons and dreaming of the real thing. today, that dream came true in the most spectacular, high-definition way possible. check out our photos — no filter needed, nature did all the work. 😉 maverick helicopters, you made this big kid’s dream come true. expensive? sure. regret it? not for a second. thanks for an unforgettable experience!

a chill, wide open green space right in front of the reichstag, perfect for a quick break while exploring berlin. it’s got a cool vibe with people lounging, snapping pics, or just soaking in the view of that epic glass dome. you can really feel the history here, but it doesn’t feel heavy, more like a peaceful, reflective spot in the middle of the city buzz. great place to hang out for a bit, especially on a sunny day.
a chinese buddhist temple. phuket vegetarian festival takes place here every year. there are many vegetarian restaurants around this temple.

a classic cafe when in vienna, they say, you must pay a visit to this cafe. and that’s what i did. i went in around 8pm, so was fortunate there was no queue. the ambience is beautiful with people enjoying themselves with friends or family and having a coffee. the place is lit up beautifully and the decor lives up to its reputation. furnishings are classy as well. table was a bit small for the number of things we ordered though. we tried the famous pancake. it was not so sweet and nice. the apple pie was surprisingly good though. together with a nice drink, it was wonderful to soak in the ambience of this classic cafe. service was prompt and attentive. they did their best to make sure we got whatever we needed like an extra plate, fork etc. they wanted our experience to be a good one. and i gotta say we appreciated it. definitely a place to visit when in vienna.
a clean and comfortable place, with many beautiful and unique ornamental plants. suitable for bringing friends, girlfriends, and family.
a clothing store with a rare attention to detail and care that is exceptional in an overly commercialized world. an wonderful place to visit with very special clothes.
a collection of artworks (mostly italian) inside a well preserved sequence of reception rooms. the ceilings are opulent but i have seen better stately homes. i still enjoyed this though!
a collection of great vintage clothing, shoes, and accessories at every budget. the sales assistant was also helpful and friendly.

a competent, fast-paced guide who is very knowledgeable about his work. he makes us feel safe, even though it's an activity that can always involve risks. he takes us to lesser-known and less-crowded canyons so we can fully enjoy them. my wife and i have now done a total of 11 canyons with him, as well as many friends. thanks, gerard! we'll continue enjoying canyons with you.

a complete waste of time. we drove 1.5h from the east—we’re art and architecture enthusiasts and were looking forward to this museum. this place was the ultimate letdown. waste of my time and money. 1. exhibitions were mid, 5/10 at best. collection and curation very very very underwhelming. 2. not worth 30,000 won 3. staff was extremely rude, subtly roll her eyes, slammed things (lightly but wad??), showed and attitude and shouted at us 4. after multiple museum runs this trip, i can conclude jeju is scenic and has great architecture with bad service and not-so-worth-the-trip art

a couple of friends went to this garden for seeing the van gogh’s flower show. we took 2 & 1/2 hours to get there from nj, but it is worthy. the whole garden is filled with flowers and plants with specialties varieties . we also have lunch at hudson garden grill , the food is delicious and tasty. if you have aaa membership please go to aaa either online or in person to purchase the tickets will save you 15% for discount. but if you walk-in to purchase tickets at gate only get you $4 discount! please make sure book the tickets in advance to save your time, otherwise will have long wait in line. you will need to have big bottle of water because you are going to walk a lot specially in summer time. carrying your sunglasses and hat with sunblock and water are must have. if you are a walker then don’t need to take bus from subway stop to the garden only 11 minutes by walking.

a cozy bar with friendly staff and large projectors to watch live football(soccer) games. there is also a separated stage room to watch and listen to live music. not the best sound but definitely a great experience!

a crazy place! so flamboyant, so full of life and junk 😍 here you can buy whatever you wanted and even things you never knew existed. :d the the noise, the people and all the shiny and not so shiny items around you... like a live caleidoscope. we ended up with a cigarette lighter (no one smokes), an almost full set of small cups, some exotic coins and a lot of fun. to wrap it up - i love the place.

a cruise on the nile in cairo is an interesting addition to exploring the city, especially as an optional option in a trip to cairo and giza. the boat may not be the most luxurious, but it is safe, and the cruise allows you to look at the city from a completely different perspective. this is an opportunity to admire both modern and older architecture of cairo, as well as see with your own eyes the contrast between the old and new parts of the city. although the smog may slightly obscure the views, the atmosphere of the nile and its surroundings remains unforgettable. a cruise offers a break from the intense sightseeing, so it's worth considering if your tour schedule allows it.
a cute little area in a sleepy town with a few cafes and restaurants scattered throughout.

a day with khlafa in fez is the best way to immerse into the history of the medina and get a real taste of the culture. khlafa gave us insights and lessons about the food, architecture, gardens and language that i can’t imagine having learned with anyone else. he was able to navigate through the narrow streets and take us to the hidden gems along the way! i highly recommend khlafa’s warm welcome and rich knowledge to give you the best tour of such a wonderfully preserved city.

a decade of diving excellence with extra divers qantab! i've been diving with extra divers qantab in muscat since 2016, when i took my open water course with them, and it's been an absolutely incredible journey. from those first breaths underwater to countless dives since, their team has made every experience memorable. what truly sets them apart is their great diving team. they are not just instructors and guides; they are passionate, knowledgeable, and genuinely fun to be around. every dive feels like an adventure, filled with laughter and shared wonder at muscat's vibrant underwater world. it's a unique experience that keeps me coming back year after year. if you're looking for real professionals in the city, extra divers qantab is undoubtedly the place to go.

a decent spot, especially on a hot day, but crowded and chilly water. parking is available nearby up, and entry to the natural ocean pools costs €3. a locker facility where you can store belongings coast 5€. the water is cold, particularly in the pools closer to the ocean. there’s a shallow kids’ area and a deeper section for adults. worth a visit if you don’t mind cold water, great for a refreshing dip and scenic photos.

a definite must-go! highly recommended. mr sung welcomed us at the entrance of the garden with huge smile and a firm handshake, i could feel sincerity in our 1-2words conversation. my friend wore a purple hat, mine was pink cap, we each received an umbrella thats the color of our 'hat' :d this place is more than a garden, it inspires gratitude to mother nature. the bonsais/landscape are well curated, definitely a soulful learning experience for me. purchased a book called '草木人生' at the watchtower. the view is perfect, the space if well maintained. glad we made it there.

a definite must-see attraction since it is the tallest building in the world. you have to visit at least once if visiting dubai to experience the view. great experience despite the long wait to enter. views are simply amazing despite only going up to floor 124. i had purchased tickets a day ahead and was in line 30 mins ahead of reservation time, but i still only got in after more than an hour of waiting. a long wait to get back down as well. they should limit tickets better per timeslot.

a definite spot of interesting for people who are interested in the country history. i only learned about it before on tv when i was a teen boy. a very quick touch through history textbooks in classroom is nowhere compared to this fantastic museum. it tells how the war started and the suffering of innocent people between 1991-1995. the weapons used and items in the city collected from the war were displayed with detailed explanations. the entire structure of the fortress is also a good way to see the signs of war. not sure the walls in and out were actually damaged by any bullets or rockets but i think they were. on the top level you however will see the today peaceful warm sunset of magnificent dubrovnik. it makes us even more convinced that freedom and peace are not something comes automatically. we have to treasure them.

a definite visit if you’re traveling with kids, cuz they’ll love this place! but it’s equally entertaining for grown ups! lovely architecture and the musical show that happens in the evening is lovely to witness! and of course perfect place to buy lots of cookies and chocolates!
a delight on saturday nights in havana
a delightful discovery. large works of art set in a courtyard surrounded by artisan spaces.

a delightful oasis in the heart of sapporo, nakajima park in june is a lush haven of greenery and serenity. the trees are in full bloom, offering a cooling canopy for leisurely strolls. families, couples and children enjoy its expansive lawns and charming walking trails. the pond is particularly picturesque, with rowboats gliding across the calm waters and ducklings trailing their mother along the banks. despite the overcast skies during our visit, the park buzzed with a festive atmosphere thanks to the vibrant rows of food stalls selling everything from grilled meats to traditional sweets. a perfect blend of nature, culture, and community spirit — a must-visit if you’re in sapporo during early summer.

a delightful shop, with accessories to enhance your outfits with great taste, or rather, venetian style. in a less touristy area of venice, making it quiet and delightful. it's one of those places that hasn't yet become overcrowded. worth visiting, worth supporting.

a delightful small shrine that features wild boars statues and figurines, which are connected to shrine legend. directly across the street from the imperial palace grounds (gosho 御所), halfway between imadegawa subway station to the north and marutamachi subway station to the south. they also have various wild boar figurines for sale.

a desert safari in dubai is a famous tourist activity that typically includes a ride in a 4x4 vehicle through the desert, dune bashing, a traditional arabic bbq dinner, and entertainment such as belly dancing and fireshow. many visitors enjoy the thrill of the dune bashing and the opportunity to experience traditional arabian culture.

a different kind of experience with light dance & belly dance on the move. the cruise moved slowly allowing the guests to enjoy every bit, foods were delicious, the service was very good, extremely supportive staffs.
a different kind of museum that uses more lighting's for its exhibitions. very cool and i would highly suggest you to come and take a look.

a different part of hk typical concrete jungle, where one can find rows of shops and stalls selling fresh flowers and plants. the abundance of colourful and delightful flowers, orchids and plants is such a wonderful sight to behold and have a refreshing stroll through.

a dive center that takes care of every detail to make sure you have the best possible experience. what impressed us the most was the attitude of the instructors and captains—you can truly tell they love what they do.

a do-not-miss property! the game viewing and guides are spectacular, especially if you’re interested in big cats. the rooms are the most beautiful that we’ve ever stayed at, and the staff goes above and beyond to make sure you have an unforgettable experience. we had hippos, wildebeests, and monkeys all outside our room that we could watch while relaxing in our private pool. it’s extremely luxury without feeling stuffy. bravo to andbeyond for creating such an incredible piece of paradise in the serengeti! we can’t wait to be back.
a dozen copies of michelangelo's the dying slave sit atop this building. incredible!

a dream come true at wadi rum dream camp our stay at wadi rum dream camp was nothing short of incredible. everything about the experience was perfect – the accommodation, the location, and the hospitality. we stayed in the martian tent, which was both comfortable and unique, offering breathtaking views of the desert. the staff were exceptionally friendly and welcoming, making us feel at home from the moment we arrived. their attention to detail and genuine care for the guests were truly remarkable. the food was delicious, with plenty of options to enjoy after a day of exploring. speaking of which, the excursions were absolutely fantastic – from jeep tours to starry nights in the desert, every moment felt magical. a special thank you to fahad, abdullah, abood, and nael for making our stay so memorable. your kindness and dedication truly stood out. wadi rum dream camp truly lives up to its name. i highly recommend it to anyone looking for an unforgettable experience in the desert.

a dream come true to visit this place! had a wonderful time, the weather helped as it didn't rain and we could wander around and take our photos! also, luckily it wasn't massively overrun by tourists.

a experiência de visitar o parque nacional da tijuca é única e maravilhosa. um dos lugares com mais diversidade biológica do planeta. é super necessário e recomendável conhecer este parque. quando for, aprecie a paisagem, o som da natureza, a mata, a fauna. e por favor, não jogue lixo na mata.
