a fabulous huge castle to visit with a spectacular garden and great views over all below. there are many buildings inside to see with fabulous interiors furnished the way it was long ago. i took the walking tour of the inside of the castle, which is a good idea! this a popular site so it is always very busy. there is a coffee and gift shop. the parking lot is large, but fills up fast so get there early. it is quite the walk up the hill to get to the castle from the town below. if you have walking problems, they will allow you to park in a special area closer to the castle, if you ask. from the castle, you can see the wallace monument in the distance and the river where the famous battle of stirling bridge was. a separate company gives guided tours of the stirling bridge battle site. i took that tour, which was wonderful and the tour guide can show you where the original bridge was on a tablet, stephen of braveheart tours is a great tour guide!

a fabulous one day tour of the salt flats. brian was our young, fantastic guide - and spoke very good english. he is a careful driver and is extremely good at getting the perfect fun shots on the salt flats …. with all the necessary props. we stopped to have a very tasty lunch at the salt hotel, and had a perfect end of the day with a beautiful sunset (and i won’t give away the very nice surprise in store for you!) our group gelled very quickly and we got on very well throughout the day, exchanging photos and videos on our whatsapp group. all in all one of the best days so far on our six months in south america. can highly recommend andes salt expeditions (and see if you can request brian as your guide!)

a fabulous time! we stayed in tilney manor for 3 nights. everything was exceptional. such a beautiful experience seeing all the wildlife, jan was our safari guide, he has experience is knowledgeable and ever so humorous to be around! thank you to tilney staff for management of our rooms, the delicious meals and an all round a memory my husband and i will reflect on for a lifetime! definitely recommend to anyone looking for an ethical safari experience and still be close to cape town!

a fantastic and safe watersports experience for the whole family! we had a truly memorable time trying out watersports during our recent visit to perissa. the team was professional, welcoming, and clearly experienced, making the whole process smooth and enjoyable. what really stood out for me was how comfortable and safe my 6.5-year-old daughter felt throughout the activity. the staff took great care to explain everything patiently and made sure she was confident and happy before starting. it’s not always easy to find places that combine fun with such a strong sense of safety—especially for families with young children. the equipment was in excellent condition, the beach setting was beautiful, and the overall atmosphere was relaxed yet well-organized. highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy water activities in santorini with peace of mind. we’ll definitely be back!

a fantastic family escape! this park near rehab city gate 2 is a gem for anyone looking to spend quality time with loved ones. the expansive green areas were perfect for our picnic, offering a refreshing break from the city bustle. it was a joy to see my family relaxed and happy, enjoying the simple pleasure of being outdoors. highly recommended for a fun and rejuvenating family outing!

a fantastic gem of a place brimming with art. this is the antique former home of the famous pamphilj family. i am completely obsessed with this prominent roman family of the 16th and 17th centuries after having read many books about them. the house is so well preserved it really feels like you’ve stepped back through time. i actually felt quite moved to be in their home and really could imagine what it would have been like to live there all those years ago. there are a great deal of incredible paintings to look at. it took me a couple of hours to really take it all in. the audio guide is fantastic and well worth listening to to learn more about the house and the collection of art it contains. also, i may have simply been lucky but it felt much quieter here than at other similar attractions. this really added to the magical historical atmosphere! the gift shop is also worth a visit - i’m a big fan of pretty bookmarks and they had plenty, plus many other beautiful gifts.

a fantastic green oasis offering stunning views and rich history! 🇮🇹🌳 situated directly across from the colosseum, this expansive park provides breathtaking panoramic vistas of the amphitheatre and palatine hill – truly unbeatable photo opportunities! 📸🏛️ it’s also home to significant archaeological ruins, including large sections of the baths of trajan and an entrance to the domus aurea. despite its historical depth, it's a popular spot for locals to relax, stroll, or for kids to play. a perfect blend of nature, ancient wonders, and urban tranquility. 💖🌟 absolutely essential for any rome visit! ✨

a fantastic little corner of moroccan history. i learn about this place on atlas obscura and i thought it was just fascinating. there’s so many pictures, souvenirs and details that you can spend a good amount of time just looking at all the kings of this beautiful country.

a fantastic place to step back in time! fort york offers a rich historical experience with well-preserved structures, engaging exhibits, and knowledgeable staff who bring the past to life. it's perfect for families—kids and adults alike will enjoy exploring the grounds and learning about canada’s military history. the site is easy to navigate, with plenty of informative displays, and the atmosphere truly immerses you in the 19th century. whether you're a history buff or just looking for an educational outing, this is a must-visit spot in toronto! don't forget to check out the show of the day and its schedules.

a fantastic shopping & dining experience. i recently visited the mall and had a wonderful time exploring everything it had to offer. the shops were amazing, plenty of great brands, stylish boutiques, and something for every taste. i also tried the food court, which had a delicious variety of options, and i was impressed with the quality and flavors. the overall atmosphere was lively, clean, and well organized. whether you're looking for shopping, dining, or just a nice place to stroll around, i highly recommend checking out this mall. i’ll definitely be back.

a fantastic spot to start your wild life safari in kenya. the closed location to nairobi and it offers all possible sightings that the masai mara could offer. just go there with your dslr and capture the wilderness unwind ! the tent 🏕️ accommodation gives you that exotic feel. night skies are awesome here !

a fantastic way to discover paris! this boat cruise was truly the highlight of my time in paris! the captain philippe was not only skilled but also incredibly knowledgeable about the city’s history. he shared fascinating stories and facts in such an engaging and personal way that made the experience even more special. cruising along the seine while learning about paris gave me a unique and memorable introduction to the city.

a fantastic way to experience london from a fresh perspective! the river cruise offered stunning views of iconic landmarks like tower bridge, the london eye, and the houses of parliament — all without the city crowds. the live commentary was informative yet fun, and the pace was just right to soak in the sights. great for both first-time visitors and locals wanting a relaxing break on the thames.

a fascinating and beautiful natural spot in hokkaido. the walking trails are well-maintained and offer amazing views of steaming vents, bubbling hot springs and unique volcanic terrain. it’s a peaceful yet otherworldly experience. the paths are easy enough for most visitors. while there is a noticeable smell of sulfur in the air, it’s quite bearable and just part of the experience.

a fascinating and interesting museum in a lovely town. the museum tells you about the cultural and social history of the dolomites as well as the geology. the displays look stunning and are easy to understand. i particularly liked learning about early women climbers and botanists.

a fascinating and thorough set of exhibits that explore the taboo issue of "the big sleep". the history behind the exhibits was very interesting and there was so much info i couldn't read everything. if you have an interest in the macabre, you should certainly make a stop. plus the employees were cool and were ready for any questions i had. 10/10.

a fascinating deep dive into the mind of picasso! the museum showcases not just his famous paintings, but also sculptures, sketches, and personal collections. it's beautifully curated inside a historic mansion in the marais. perfect for anyone wanting to see the many sides of picasso’s genius.

a fascinating diversion from the dirty street chaos outside. seek out the objects with the gold ‘legends’ - it certainly makes the case for islamic superiority in culture and science in the middle ages when we were living in muddy squalor in mud huts

a fascinating experience with a rich history. there may not be a lot to it but a quick visit to the cave and hot water basin is worth your time. the park staff is exceptional, friendly, and helpful. be advised, do not purchase admission online from tripadvisor or any other vendor. all you get is a self guided audio tour around the area not admission to the park itself. this is deceitful advertising. to add insult to injury, our 'tour' was scheduled for october 16th, a day the park was closed.

a fascinating slice of bali’s spiritual and cultural history. goa gajah (elephant cave) is a compact but powerful temple site just outside ubud, known for its dramatic stone-carved entrance and serene jungle surroundings. the cave itself is small but rich in atmosphere, with ancient carvings and shrines that reflect both hindu and buddhist influences. outside, you’ll find peaceful bathing pools, moss-covered ruins, and a lush ravine that feels like a hidden sanctuary. 💡 tip: don’t be fooled by the vendors outside trying to sell sarongs—you’re given one as part of your entrance fee. even with long pants, i was still provided a sash to wear around my waist, so no need to buy anything extra.

a fascinating sprawling building, with excellent temporary exhibits of contemporary art and architecture. the various courtyards seem to be everywhere, we managed to see the model workshop and were shown photos of the final layouts of the vast and intricate miniatures.

a few days ago i went to il nuovo mercato at the mall of san juan and it was really a great culinary experience. it's truly like a farmers market but with a lot more variety. i ordered the seafood soup which was so incredibly delicious and i also had the pasta with lamb. the lamb meat was so tender and delicious. my daughter had the spaghetti with clams, also really good and my son had the pizza with pepperoni's. he also ordered fish & chips which were also extremely good. i recommend il nuovo mercato to anyone that loves variety, big portions and delicious cuisine. and the views are delectably beautiful.

a focal point of reference for moving around jerusalem. its majestic structure provides for one of the most spectacular accesses to the old town. recommended to go through this walking, as if you do it by car you may easily end up stuck. wherever you walk in jerusalem, at some point you will always come across zion gate.

a free planetarium which has a lot of potential. unfortunately, exhibits are mostly in korean which made it hard to enjoy for my 4 year old. it was also cloudy when we visited so the stargazing activity was closed.

a free to visit work of art. originally built during the 12th century, it was largely destroyed during the earthquake of 1667. it was rebuilt in roman baroque style. reconstruction began in 1673 and it was completed four decades later in 1713. some beautiful paintings in particular look out for the triptych of the "assumption of mary" by titian, above the main altar.

a free, must go spot in rio! there are 4 lookouts with different views. very clean, well maintained, and safe. the only negative is not enough toilet and there was no toilet paper. easily accessible via public transportation or free carpark if driving.

a friend told me about this new bar in wynwood and i wanted to like it since it is very close to home. i decided to go for happy hour. first mistake. happy hour is advertised on the website as 6pm-10pm on thursday night. beer is listed as $5. i ordered a beer and paid cash before opening a tab to make sure everything was legit. bartender charged $6 and i verified the happy hour lasted until 10pm and he said no it ends at 9pm now but they haven't gotten around to changing the website yet. i tipped him $3 anyway since i am a good tipper so my $5 beer really ended up costing me $9 which is a regular price for wynwood so no biggie. the biggest problem was the music. when i walked in junto al almanecer by j alvarez was playing (thanks to shazam lol i had no idea what he was saying it was in spanish and even with a basic understanding of spanish i couldn't understand any of it) and an old britney spears video was playing on the screen. i didn't understand the vibe. on a thursday night it was pretty empty to be expected and the 4 other people that were there when i arrived all left at 9pm when the happy hour ended. at 9pm they opened the back patio and a live hip hop dj started playing. i finished my beer and left. not sure i will go back.

a friendly shopkeeper. we had our main tent broken down by the wind, and i had to run there to buy a new tent. i arrived just when the shop closed, yet the shopkeeper was super nice and reopened the shop just for me to buy a new tent. many thanks. large selection of sport equipment and especially fishing equipment, but also tenta, clothes and gas canisters.

a fun and vibrant place to buy a souvenir or two. there are plenty of restaurants serving delicious greek food and thirst quenching drinks. some of the restaurants have toe tapping live music. a lovely place to while away a few hours with an awesome view of the acropolis, especially at night.

a fun experience for kids and family which i enjoyed very much, not much people which was great. bar close by for drinks and the wave pool was amazing! the only thing which you have to be careful of is that atcthe beginning of the wave pool, there is a sandpaper type floor which i assume is for grip, but could damage swimsuits or knees (from experience) so be careful for that! if you stay at the resort, make sure to stop by!
a fun place for a chopi right before sunset, after a long day wandering around the city center.

a fun way to spend a few hours! there are live animals to view, even guinea pigs to pet. they have an impressive train set with information on the transcontinental railroad. there is also a lot of art on display. there is plenty to view and do, including the incredible views of the city from the hill.

a fun way to spend an hour or two in the countryside of ubud, riding various single and couple swings with a magnificent view of the lush green fields. plenty of great staff available to ensure safety and also for taking photos and videos, and we had plenty of time to complete our visit as we preferred. we were not rushed and complete the various attractions as our time suited. be aware that there are a number of bali swings in this area, so if you’ve booked ahead, ensure you are at the correct location. we turned up at the wrong site first! :-).

a fun, immersive cocktail experience mixed with immersive theatre. the sets are beautiful, and the actors are fantastic, and it’s perfect for a date night or a night out with friends (although if you’re just looking for somewhere to drink and chat, definitely not the vibe). the cocktails aren’t amazing, although they are displayed and made in fun ways, but go for the overall experience and the novelty and you’ll have a really fun night.

a fun-filled day for the whole family! waterpark at fantasia was an absolute highlight of our trip! the park is clean, well-maintained, and offers something for everyone — from exciting slides and splash zones to relaxing pools and shaded lounge areas. the kids had a blast exploring all the themed areas, and we appreciated the attention to safety with lifeguards stationed throughout the park. everything felt very family-friendly, and the atmosphere was vibrant and welcoming. staff were friendly and helpful. whether you’re visiting with young children or teens, fantasia waterpark is a fantastic place to cool off and have fun. highly recommend!

a fun-filled family day at dubai mall we had such a great time at dubai mall as a family! it’s not just a place for shopping, it’s full of fun and exciting things to do, especially if you have kids. our child absolutely loved it and didn’t want to leave! one of the best parts was the dubai aquarium and underwater zoo. the huge tank with all the fish, sharks, and stingrays was amazing. our child was fascinated, especially when we walked through the glass tunnel and saw the sea animals swimming above us. it felt like we were underwater too! the penguins and other animals in the zoo area were also fun to watch. next, we went to kidzania, a play city where kids can dress up and try different jobs like firefighter, doctor, chef, and more. our child had a blast – it was fun and also educational. we could see he was really enjoying himself while learning new things at the same time. we also checked out the vr park a place full of virtual reality games. there were some great options for kids, and even we adults enjoyed trying a few games! in the evening, we stepped outside to watch the dubai fountain show, right next to the burj khalifa. the water dancing to the music was beautiful, and our child watched it with wide eyes – such a magical moment. we had dinner at one of the many restaurants in the mall – lots of options for families, with friendly staff and kid-friendly meals. it made the whole day easy and enjoyable. even though the mall is huge, it’s well-organized. there are clear signs, places to sit, baby changing rooms, and it’s stroller-friendly too. that made it very comfortable for us as parents. overall, dubai mall was a fantastic place for a family outing. there’s something for everyone, and it’s definitely a place we’d love to visit again. our child had so much fun and kept talking about the aquarium and kidzania for days. highly recommended if you’re in dubai with kids!
a gate with expansive view of cairo from the top of minarets. very narrow stairs. we were there alone for more than 30min, not very popular with tourists. 150egp per adult, 75 per child.

a grand stairway steeped in history and drama – jesuit stairs, dubrovnik tucked away in the heart of dubrovnik’s old town, the jesuit stairs are one of the city's most iconic and photogenic landmarks — and for good reason. climbing this elegant baroque staircase feels like stepping into a scene from a historical drama (or quite literally, game of thrones), thanks to their dramatic design and cinematic location. the stairs connect gundulić square with the jesuit church of st. ignatius at the top. designed in the 1730s by roman architect pietro passalacqua, they were clearly inspired by the famous spanish steps in rome, and they offer a similarly grand atmosphere — though on a much more intimate scale. from the base, the view upwards is absolutely stunning, especially early in the morning before the crowds roll in. as you climb, you’re surrounded by stone walls, baroque architecture, and the kind of old-world charm that dubrovnik is known for. at the top, you’re rewarded with a peaceful square and a chance to pop into the beautiful st. ignatius church, which is well worth a look inside. for game of thrones fans, this is also where the infamous “walk of shame” begins — though you won’t feel any shame taking a hundred photos here. it’s that picturesque. tips: visit early or late in the day for the best light and fewer people. if you’re into photography, bring a wide-angle lens — the architecture deserves it. it's a short climb, but wear good shoes; the steps can be slippery when worn down by centuries of footsteps. verdict: a must-see in dubrovnik, whether you're a history buff, a got fan, or just a lover of beautiful places. don’t miss it!

a great trail for your furry friends. you can do a short loop or go further down to the reservoir or repulse bay. if you’re feeling really energetic, do violet hill and the twins but be prepared for the 1000 steps!

a great trip with a great tour guide! we were deciding between renting a car and buying a trip and we couldn’t have made a better decision to book with azores group. the guide (diogo) was talkative, he explained everything to us, gave us some fun facts about the islands and answered all of our questions. the tour was definitely worth the price, we saw much more than we expected. the guide took us to places we would not even think about to go there ourselves. we enjoyed the trip so much that we immediately booked another, to see the other part of the island. highly recommend!!
a great vast area for different art exhibitions, worth visiting if you are a lover of fine arts

a great venue to visit especially if you are an avid manga or comic book reader. has a great homely vibe to it coupled with the general quietness maintained to give visitors a great reading experience. possessing a great collection of manga from various eras beginning in the early 1930s, has exhibits that go into depth regarding the historical trends, styles and stories of manga and their authors and even has a small video game section. what stuck out most however, were the casts of the hands of various authors and artists, and the exhibit on adapting manga into animation form. however, it may appear dull for certain visitors

a great venue, easy to find and a short walk from charring cross station. a beautiful theatre with friendly and helpful staff. we watched the amazing “just for one day” the live aid story. the performances by the entire cast were fantastic!! with an incredible live band on stage giving the music we all know new life for this musical. a funny, emotional, poignant and inspiring story the whole world has heard. you’ll laugh, you’ll cry, you’ll cheer, you’ll sing.
a great walk up from the medina with a beautiful outlook as the reward. fez sits below as you gaze out to the mountains beyond.

a great way to experience the old quebec city walls. take the stairs up to the ramparts, giving a vantage point view of artillery park. cannons lined up on the walls, but be careful not to lean over as it is quite a steep drop down to the street. city parking available nearby with affordable maximum daily limit.

a great way to experience the uros islands, away from big tourist groups, close to nature, getting an (arm) workout on top. very interesting to learn about how the islands are built and the livestyle on the islands. it was a very authentic experience and ronny was great at communicating before and during the trip.

a great way to explore the first district without horse torture and still in a carriage. the carriage is so eye-catching that many people take photos and videos or wave, just great. highly recommended!

a great way to see the sights from a different perspective and with some interesting commentary. my wife and i took a one way trip from greenwich to westminster as a relaxed alternative to the usual public transport options. the onboard bar is cash only but i didn’t see that mentioned anywhere during booking, nor was it mentioned when we were told about the bar on the pa - fortunately i was carrying some cash and the items are reasonably priced.

a great workout. we started at 6:00am and got great parking near the trailhead and were 2 of few people. on the way down there were herds of people, shoulder to shoulder on the trail. do yourself a favor and start as early as possible. it was a great climb and would do it again. took 2 hours to get to the top.

a greek-orthodox monastery, built as a fortress, located in the rehaviah valley (cross valley). according to tradition it is the site of the tree that was used to build the cross of the crucifixion. the monastery was initially built in the byzantine period, during the 5th c ad. it was repaired by caesar justinian in the mid 6th c. the monastery was destroyed during the persian invasion (614ad). in 796 the arabs butchered all the residing monks. it was rebuilt in the 11th c by a georgian monk, and enjoyed better times during the times of the crusaders. the site was a large center in the 13-14th c, and hosted a hundreds of georgian monks, scholars and poets. at the end of the 17th c the monastery changed control from the georgians to the greek-orthodox church. the number of residents has decreased over the years to a few. the monastery is open to the public and is kept by a few resident monks. it is a popular visiting site for the christian pilgrims who visit jerusalem.

a green space for a walk, with a lake that allows people to swim in (we saw people did swimming today there in this weather of 5°c!) dogs are allowed off leash here. some benches available. have a broad pointview over the river and city.

a group of 4 of us did this hike. we found it very easy for those who don't hike very often. there are lots of places to stop and rest. we even saw some families hiking with young kids and prams. we walked to kleiner scheidegg and took the train down. incredible views! it cost a fair bit to get up the cable car and down on the train but it was well worth it. we loved every minute.

a group of us attended a rum tasting session at this amazing chateau. the experience was very personable, and for an additional cost, we also got to try the full range of their more expensive rums which were far nicer. although we did not eat here, we will return to do this as the food looked good and it is in a lovely setting.

a guide walked us through the tanning process that has remained largely unchanged for centuries. it has a very strong odor and they are kind enough to hand you sprigs off mint to smell and mask the odor. as usual the trip comes with a large variety of products that they will try to sell you, but they will not be offended if you decide to buy nothing and walk away.
a hard walk to the top but amazing view once you get there. definitely worth the walk up.

a heartfelt alaskan experience with dog gone it dog gone it is more than just a dog sled tour — it’s a deep, authentic glimpse into the world of the iditarod and the incredible people (and dogs!) behind it. this husband and wife team, mike and caitlin, have built their sled dog team from the ground up with true passion and care. from the moment caitlin picked us up at our hotel, we felt warmly welcomed and immersed in the spirit of alaska. she was an exceptional guide — knowledgeable, friendly, and full of fascinating stories about life in the last frontier. the experience itself was unforgettable. you don’t just meet the dogs — you step into their world. you feel the love and dedication mike and caitlin pour into their team. most importantly, the health and happiness of the dogs are clearly their top priority, which made the experience even more meaningful. if you’re looking for something truly special that will leave your heart full and your curiosity satisfied, look no further. we can’t recommend dog gone it enough!

a hidden baroque oasis in prague! this peaceful garden, part of the wallenstein palace, features manicured lawns, elegant fountains, a serene koi pond, and free-roaming peacocks. perfect for a quiet escape from crowds.

a hidden gem among dubai's malls! we spontaneously decided to visit dubai hills mall for the first time — and we were genuinely surprised! the mall is bright, open, and beautifully designed with a very elegant and modern feel. it's easy to navigate thanks to the wide walkways and clear layout. there are also large touchscreens throughout the mall to help you find stores and orient yourself. one of the highlights for us was the indoor play areas for kids — truly fantastic! the mall is super modern, incredibly clean, and features a stylish parking garage with several well-placed entrances and exits. we had a great experience and will definitely come back!

a hidden gem for history lovers (and it's free!) i was surprised by the quality and depth of the displays. there's a lot of history packed into this collection, and it's presented in an engaging way. i spent a good amount of time exploring the various exhibits and definitely left with a better understanding of new orleans' past. if you're the kind of person who enjoys museums and historical sites, i would definitely suggest setting aside at least an hour to explore. it's a worthwhile and free activity that offers a great insight into the history and culture of new orleans.

a hidden gem for runners in rome i absolutely love running in parco della caffarella. it’s full of greenery and has lots of hidden spots to explore. from the higher paths, you can even catch glimpses of the city. it’s perfect for trail training, with a mix of flat and uneven terrain, plus plenty of hills and slopes to challenge your workout. a peaceful and versatile park that’s ideal for both serious runners and nature lovers.

a hidden gem in boracay! we followed google maps and were pleasantly surprised to find that punta bunga beach is a public beach. we parked at movenpick resort (crimson hotel is right beside it) and walked our way down. the beach is clean, peaceful, and less crowded—perfect for a quiet escape. the sand is comparable to station 2. the water is a beautiful gradient of turquoise and deep blue. you can even spot shangri-la’s jetty port from the shore. definitely one of the best beaches we visited on the island.

a hidden gem in cairo! the gayer-anderson museum offers a stunning collection of art and artifacts in a beautifully preserved historic house. each room is a unique journey through egyptian and islamic history, with gorgeous architecture, intricate woodwork, and a peaceful rooftop view. a must-visit for history and art lovers!

a hidden gem in sedona with many hiking trails of varying difficulty levels. i took one trail down to the river, which was beautiful; it took me 15 minutes to go down and 25 minutes to come back up. the river was lovely, and the water was refreshing. i visited around 4 p.m., and it wasn’t crowded—the weather was perfect. the whole area is stunning and great for photos. another trail i tried was along the edge, which was nice but a bit challenging if you have pets or children. overall, i highly recommend this place if you’re in sedona.

a hidden gem in the heart of athens, the numismatic museum offers a fascinating journey through history via coins. housed in a stunning neoclassical mansion, its rich collection and elegant atmosphere make it a must-visit for history and art lovers alike.

a hidden gem in the highlands! my visit to the falls of foyers was absolutely breathtaking. the cascading waterfall surrounded by lush greenery felt like stepping into a nature lover’s dream. the walk to the viewpoint was peaceful and well-marked though a bit steeper than expected, offering stunning views at every turn. a perfect escape from the bustle with a refreshing reward, revitalising, and 100% worth the trip! 🌊✨

a hidden gem in tokyo kyufurukawa garden offers a beautiful blend of western-style rose garden and traditional japanese landscape. the seasonal flowers, especially the roses in spring and autumn, are breathtaking. peaceful atmosphere, well-maintained paths, and a lovely place to take a stroll or relax with nature. a must-visit if you love gardens or photography.”

a hidden gem in vienna! i can’t believe this place is free! blumengärten hirschstetten is like walking through a living postcard. 🌸 from lavender fields to indian and mexican gardens, every section feels like a different country. the summer flowers were absolutely stunning—colors everywhere! the palmenhaus was my favorite—tropical plants, turtles, birds, and a little waterfall. super peaceful! and the mini-zoo is adorable, with goats, owls, and even rare turtles. perfect spot for families, couples, or anyone who loves nature. the playgrounds and fun sculptures make it great for kids, too. easy to reach by tram or bus, and it’s way less crowded than the big touristy spots. you can easily spend 2–3 hours here just wandering, relaxing, and taking photos. totally recommend for a chill afternoon surrounded by beauty.✨

a hidden gem just steps from the old town! beach šulić is a small, peaceful cove with crystal-clear water and a relaxed vibe. perfect for a refreshing dip after exploring the city. you can walk straight into the sea, jump off the rocks, or use the ladder—there’s something for everyone. there’s even a beach bar nearby and basic amenities like showers and toilets. it gets busy in the afternoon, so come early if you want a quieter experience. a must-visit for anyone looking to unwind by the water in dubrovnik

a hidden gem of roman grandeur at galleria colonna: if you’re looking for an unforgettable and slightly lesser-known cultural experience in rome, galleria colonna is a must. we visited on the first saturday of may, arriving around 9:30 a.m., and were pleasantly surprised to find that no advance tickets were necessary — we walked right in, purchased our tickets on site with no hassle at all. i was traveling with someone who has a disability, and the staff was incredibly responsive and accommodating. i had emailed them in advance to inquire about accessibility, and they replied quickly with clear and helpful information. once on-site, they were kind, attentive, and made sure our visit was comfortable. as for the gallery itself — it’s breathtaking. a palace still technically owned and partially lived in by the colonna family, whose history stretches back for centuries. the rooms are lavishly decorated, with stunning ceilings, classical sculptures, and monumental paintings that speak to both artistic and political legacy. walking through the main gallery feels like stepping into a scene from a baroque dream. the hall of mirrors, the antique marble statues, the masterful paintings — it’s immersive and beautifully preserved. what struck me the most was how intimate and personal the experience felt, far from the heavy crowds of more touristic sites. you get the sense that you’re truly in a living piece of history, one that is still lovingly maintained by the family whose name it bears. highly recommend this visit — especially if you’re interested in history, art, or architecture. it’s an elegant, peaceful, and enriching experience right in the heart of rome.

a hidden gem with breathtaking views mount norquay lookout is truly a must-visit if you’re anywhere near banff. the air is crisp and refreshing, and the panoramic views are absolutely breathtaking❤️🙏 a view to die for. it’s the kind of spot that makes you pause and just soak in the beauty around you. whether you’re there for a peaceful moment, stunning photos, or to simply take in nature at its finest, this lookout offers an unforgettable experience. highly recommend adding it to your alberta adventure list!

a hidden gem with epic views and timeless atmosphere. pre rup is a beautiful and often overlooked temple in the angkor complex. built from warm reddish stone, it glows at sunrise and sunset, giving it a dramatic, almost mystical feel. the steep staircases lead you to the top, where you’ll find one of the best panoramic views of the surrounding jungle and distant rice fields. it’s less crowded than angkor wat or bayon, which makes the experience more peaceful and personal. the temple’s layout — with its central tower and guardian lions — is classic khmer design, and the worn brick gives it a rugged charm. go early morning or late afternoon for cooler weather and perfect light for photos. a must-see for temple lovers and those who want something a bit quieter but equally majestic.

a honeymoon dream come true – fairmont mara safari club is simply the best our honeymoon at the fairmont mara safari club was nothing short of extraordinary. from the moment we arrived, we were embraced with warmth, care, and a level of hospitality that can only be described as world-class—and deeply human. wallace welcomed us at reception with a calm kindness that instantly made us feel at home. the entire experience was impeccably overseen by nancy, whose leadership and eye for detail ensured that every aspect of our stay was seamless and special. our game drives with david were spectacular—he’s a gifted guide who brought the mara to life with deep knowledge, storytelling, and respectful admiration for wildlife. every drive left us in awe. the luxurious tented stays, right on the banks of the mara river, were peaceful, romantic, and perfectly appointed. hippos grunted nearby as we drifted to sleep, and the surrounding landscapes were pure serenity. the location, near a white rhino conservatory, is secluded and rare—a true hidden gem ideal for couples or families. richard, our housekeeping superhero, kept everything pristine with such care and kindness. rueben guided us on a breathtaking bush walk—his wisdom and presence made it a highlight of the trip. and the food? divine. the drinks? endless. we were spoilt rotten—in the best way possible. simon , our server, was a delight—gracious, attentive, and always with a smile. the entire restaurant team pulled off a heartfelt surprise cake, song, and dance celebration that we’ll never forget. it was joyous, emotional, and so full of love. fairmont mara safari club isn’t just the best place to stay in the masai mara—it’s a sanctuary of warmth, wonder, and deep connection. every person we met left a mark on our hearts. we came for a honeymoon, but we left with memories that will last a lifetime. thank you, from the bottom of our hearts, to the whole team.

a journey to the stars — literally and emotionally. visiting the indian astronomical observatory in hanle was one of the most unforgettable experiences of my ladakh trip. situated at over 14,500 feet, it's not just one of the highest observatories in the world, but also one of the most peaceful places i’ve ever been to. the drive to hanle is long and remote, but breathtaking — endless plains, snow-dusted mountains, and no crowds. once you arrive, the silence is striking. the observatory stands quietly against the dramatic landscape, almost like it’s watching the universe for us. if you're lucky enough to visit on a clear night (and most nights are crystal clear here), the sky is unlike anything you’ve seen before. millions of stars are visible to the naked eye, and the milky way feels almost within reach. it’s easy to see why this place was chosen for deep-sky observation. the observatory itself is impressive — it houses powerful telescopes used by scientists across the globe. while visitors can’t always go inside the main domes, even seeing them from a distance is inspiring. knowing serious space research is happening quietly here, in the middle of nowhere, gives you a sense of pride and wonder.

a large, beautiful temple complex with a huge number of interesting, unique statues, ornaments and structures. next to the main vihara, there is another smaller one - also an interesting and important building - here, in addition to a large number of statues, there are three images of the supreme buddha made in the form of stone heads. a large chedi - stupa - a place where part of the fragment of buddha's ashes is usually kept - adds grandeur to this complex. this is a very large, mysterious and solemn complex that is definitely worth visiting while on vacation in phuket. there is a very calm, peaceful atmosphere here and there are not many tourists. here are: bell towers; bells; compositions from the life of the enlightenment of monks and many other interesting things that may not leave space on the memory card of gadgets and cameras, but will leave pleasant emotions and memories of this place for a long time! full information with video and easy navigation - in the app 👉 phuketon

a large, beautiful temple, located in a very picturesque place. khao rang samakkitham is one of the most beautiful temples in phuket. a large, multi-level temple, which can be explored from the left or right side, they are connected - a visitor can enter from one side, go through all the rooms and exit from the other. there are many beautiful statues here, one of them is a huge statue of buddha - perhaps the largest on the island - it is installed on the roof, on a white pedestal and looks mesmerizing, shimmering gold in the rays of the sun, watching the movement of the laity. nearby there is a high bell tower that is open to access. there, on the roof, is a very beautiful vihara. inside, it is completely decorated with amazing, heavenly-golden frescoes from the life and path of enlightenment of buddha. on one of the walls, among the frescoes, you can see the entire chakri dynasty, which has invariably ruled thailand. full information with video and easy navigation - in the app 👉 phuketon

a lovely and interesting place to visit, though it is more a neighborhood curiosity than an actual tourist attraction. the reason for my visit was because i walked past it daily during a month-long stay in tokyo. i enjoyed the rooftop garden, which sits at about six stories above ground level. this is high enough to afford a view (partially obstructed) of mt fuji, but then, in clear weather, this is true of any vantage point in tokyo that is both high enough and facing the right direction. although i rate it 5 stars, i would not rate it above numerous other attractions throughout tokyo. there are many more spectacular gardens and other interesting attractions throughout tokyo which should be higher on your list (shibuya sky, for example, is less than a mile away, 4x higher and offers 10x superior views, for a reasonable price). the meguro sky garden is free to visit, but it is not set up as a formal tourist destination. although it is easy to access, there is no information booth or visible staff personnel that i encountered on my visit. on the contrary, it felt very much like i had stumbled onto a neighborhood park, albeit six stories in the air, and requiring an elevator ride to get there. the garden is also smaller than one might imagine from the ground: most of the space is actually air, since the largest portion of the interior space is taken by a stadium sized athletic field at ground level. it was a worthwhile visit for someone who was living in the neighborhood. i could see the entire clean, lovely space in 30 minutes or so. i would not recommend it as a separate trip, however, unless you have a specific or special interest in this type of architecture.

a lovely mosque that i enjoy going back to every now and then. it reminds me of morocco and andalusia. it’s also clean and on the way to qurum .

a lovely outing overall, though i must admit i expected a bit more from the interior. that being said, what remains of the original structure has been beautifully restored and really showcases the historical charm of the building. the preserved architectural details are impressive and clearly maintained with care and respect for the building’s heritage. while the interior space may be somewhat limited in terms of exhibitions or furnishings, it still offers a unique glimpse into the past. it’s definitely worth a visit, especially for those interested in architecture or history. even though the experience inside was a bit more modest than i had anticipated, i still truly enjoyed the stop and would recommend it to others looking for a short but meaningful cultural visit.

a lovely parc floral to escape to when city life becomes too loud or too speed. beautiful flowers everywhere, peacocks...water ponds. protect that place because it is one of the most beautiful green spaces still existing in paris.
a lovely park next to the national gallery with winding paths, plenty of hidden nooks with benches, and a pond with lots of water fiwl.

a lovely park of serene south maroubra. sadly, the coastal walk is not always accessible like today 25th oct 2023. you can hear the guns going off on the shooting range situated in the parklands, the restricted area is fenced. not a good idea to ignore the signage.
a lovely park with many interesting sections. a porcelain factory where mozart and beethoven had performed, a lovely beer garden and a really fun playground.
a lovely park. plenty of seating around.
a lovely part of town just to hang out and chill, especially at night with the lights, reflecting off the water.

a lovely place for a run or a walk or just to soak in a nice coastal vista. there is a lot to see, so to speak, with nice walkways, bridges, jetties, a marina and architecturally beautiful buildings. and there is a nice sea breeze as you do all these things.
a lovely place for a walk with terrific views all around the peninsula. this was a great way to check out the harbor and queenstown.
a lovely place to find a few interesting kitchen items. a well curated and attractive shop.
a lovely place to shop for fresh fruits and vegetables and more...personal and professional treatment

a lovely place to spend a morning. a small collection that combines elements of the national gallery and the v&a. plenty of history in the house and the exhibits are well curated. the items on display on the ground floor provide an insight into a different era and well worth taking the time to view everything. the galleries on the first floor are interesting and have a broad range of art work. the cafe is a little pricey but food and drink was tasty. no need to buy tickets to enter but exhibitions on the lower ground floor are only accessible by tickets purchased in advance online. highly recommended.
a lovely place to spend a weekend with kids. beautiful gardens, perfect for a short walk or a relaxing picnic. parking is $4 cad per hour. peaceful, family-friendly, and full of great photo spots!

a lovely place to spend the afternoon/evening with friends or family. there is a nice selection of alcoholic as well as nonalcoholic drinks plus snacks. plenty of cozey space with many options for games and kids entertainment. it is run by lovely people and we look forward to our next visit. dogs are welcome and they even host birthday parties!

a lovely place, well maintained. the wildlife is well cared for, and there is a demonstration inside the hut where you can have butterflies placed on you. price is a bit steep as it very small but if it's being used to maintain the place, then it's fine. my daughter enjoyed learning about the butterflies.
a lovely place. top parking middle and lower parjing to the sataf itself, good path even for light walkers.

a lovely shaded trail that is great for training for overseas hikes. it doesn't matter if you're here in the middle of the afternoon – the trees provide ample shade that you need not worry about the sun (although the humidity would be a constant). the trail comes to life especially on a saturday morning, with people usually coming for a leisurely walk up and down. it's become a weekly staple for us, and hiking up and down makes for a good social activity to bring people together.

a lovely short walk (around 2hours from youth hostel to cairn and back) perfect for 9yr old. birch forest, heather, lochans and a windy cairn to reach at the top so has a wee bit of everything. bonus of aviemore right there for lunch. park at youth hostel, follow path under the road then up the hill (stay left). follow signs for exit on return trip for different route.

a lovely small museum that houses the modern history of athens. there are two internally connected buildings. the older one was built in 1833 and it was used as the home of king otto when he arrived at athens (1836 - 1843). the second building was built in 1859. you need a guided tour to fully understand and enjoy it. highly recommended for greeks.

a lovely spot if you enjoy nature and historical settings—great for a calm walk. the secret garden tour is worth it, but make sure to book in advance (slots open about 4–5 days ahead), and the tour lasts around an hour. some of the entrance staff weren’t very helpful and came off as a bit rude, which took away from the overall experience.

a lovely spot to enjoy a few relaxing hours outside. the rooftop green space is ideal for picnicking, flying kites, or simply taking in the fresh air and panoramic city views. it offers a calm, family-friendly atmosphere and a refreshing escape from the hustle and bustle of urban life. more than just its aesthetic appeal, the space also plays an important functional role managing flood risks, preventing seawater intrusion, and serving as a freshwater reservoir to help meet the city’s water demands. it’s truly remarkable how it blends eco-friendly infrastructure with a welcoming public area.
a lovely spot to enjoy views of the irrawaddy river and stunning sunsets! it's open until late, making it perfect for a relaxing evening visit.
a lovely spot to enjoy views of the irrawaddy river and stunning sunsets! it's open until late, making it perfect for a relaxing evening visit.

a lovely spot to visit if you're excited to see penguins 🐧 in their natural habitat! however, just a heads-up they do have a strong smell, so it might not be comfortable to stay for too long. interestingly, if your main goal is just to see the penguins, you can spot quite a few by simply walking along the public pathway, they were clearly visible during my visit. this way, you can enjoy the experience and even save on entrance fees. thanks!
a lovely square, it worths going
a lovely steel construction bridge, that is good to appreciate from the shoreline, coming from, kitsilano beach.
a lovely temple, one of the nicest ones i have seen whilst travelling around se asia. this costs 10,000 dong per person but it is well worth it!
a lovely viewpoint over sapporo. in august, the lavender was already cut, so no lilac blooms, but otherwise nice.
a lovely walk and opportunity to see finches, mockingbirds and woodpeckers.
a lovely walk and opportunity to see finches, mockingbirds and woodpeckers.

a lovely walk. i enjoyed here as i was able to walk all the way to the market as well as a few shopping areas. along the route you're able to stop and relax under the bridge or anywhere along the path. one particular evening they had set out chairs and tables along the route... a must visit.
a lovely, quiet walk at bukit batok nature park—lush greenery, cool shade, and that peaceful quarry view made it feel like a hidden retreat in the city.

a low key port preferably for those who need to spend some time in calm and far from hustle bustle of city area. dhow cruise ride a major attraction. takes you around 8!km one ways to see the fjords and remote villages. dhow stops for swimming in two spots for about 30 mins.

a lush green oasis in the mist of mexico city. walk, sit, chill, people watch, meditate and marvel at this incredible urban garden, special section to meditate or read. playground for kids. dogs everywhere! vendors on the perimeters.

a magic place, unique and full of geological history, unfortunately ruined by tons of people spending hours in taking selfie and tiktoks of themselves nobody in the world will take care or will consider. but they’re happy for this, continuing considering they are the protagonists, while here the protagonist is only the nature.

a magical experience from start to finish. on a rainy ramadan evening, the cloud forest was the perfect escape — cool, peaceful, and breathtaking with its indoor waterfall and sky bridges. later, the supertree observatory and the garden rhapsody music & light show were absolutely amazing — a must-see! it felt super safe and enjoyable, and i was happy to share it with my family. truly a once-in-a-lifetime experience in singapore. 🌧️🌙🌿✨ i recommended ☝️🤩🤷

a magical experience from start to finish. on a rainy ramadan evening, the cloud forest was the perfect escape — cool, peaceful, and breathtaking with its indoor waterfall and sky bridges. later, the supertree observatory and the garden rhapsody music & light show were absolutely amazing — a must-see! it felt super safe and enjoyable, and i was happy to share it with my family. truly a once-in-a-lifetime experience in singapore. 🌧️🌙🌿✨ i recommended ☝️🤩🤷

a magical experience in the dubai desert! the desert safari tour was filled with excitement and wonder at every turn. dune bashing was an absolute thrill, and watching the sun dip below the horizon was truly breathtaking. the traditional dance performances and sumptuous dinner made for a perfect ending to a perfect day in dubai.

a magical experience in the heart of wadi rum from the moment we arrived at wadi rum dream camp, we were overwhelmed by the warm hospitality. we received an incredibly kind welcome and were even upgraded from a simple room to one of the beautiful glamping tents — a fantastic surprise that set the tone for our entire stay. the staff is truly the heart of this camp. abdohlla, fahad, abood, and nael made our trip unforgettable. abood prepared the most amazing food, which we enjoyed under the starry sky. fahad and abdohlla kept us company around the campfire, shared stories, and showed us around the desert at night — a magical experience we will never forget. we also got a tip about taking a jeep tour in the desert, which the camp arranged for us. nael was our driver and guide, taking us to some of the most spectacular places in wadi rum. the tour ended with an unforgettable sunset over the mountains — a memory we will cherish forever. wadi rum dream camp is more than just a place to stay — it’s an experience that touches your soul. thank you to the entire team for making our stay the best we’ve ever had. we’re already longing to return!
a magical place with a very special atmosphere... if you're lucky, you might have it all to yourself like i did... so don't tell everyone!

a magical stay at pan pacific singapore – unforgettable service and stunning views from the moment we stepped through the front doors of pan pacific singapore, our experience was nothing short of magical. the check-in process was smooth and welcoming, setting the tone for what would be an unforgettable stay. our room offered a breathtaking view of marina bay sands — waking up to that skyline every morning was like something out of a dream. every detail of the room was thoughtful, elegant, and comfortable, making it a perfect retreat after a day of exploring the city. one of the absolute highlights of our stay was the pacific club lounge. the food was incredible, and the champagne breakfast was a luxurious treat we looked forward to each morning. but what truly made it special was agnes, our server. her warmth, professionalism, and attention to detail took our experience to the next level. agnes made us feel genuinely cared for and went above and beyond to ensure everything was perfect. she’s a true gem and a shining example of excellent hospitality. we can’t thank the pan pacific team enough for making our time in singapore so memorable. we’re already looking forward to our next visit!

a magical stay at pangong lake 🌌 staying at misty hills cabin by pangong lake was truly one of the most unforgettable experiences of my life. from the moment we arrived, we were warmly welcomed by the staff who made sure everything was comfortable and seamless. the location is absolutely unbeatable – waking up to the breathtaking view of the lake surrounded by the majestic himalayas felt like a dream. the rooms were clean, cozy, and thoughtfully designed to keep you warm in the chilly weather. even at such a remote location, the hospitality was top-notch. the food was delicious and freshly prepared – exactly what you need after a day of exploring. what i appreciated the most was how peaceful and serene everything felt. watching the stars at night, with the gentle sound of the wind over the lake, was something i’ll cherish forever. highly recommend this place to anyone looking to experience the raw beauty of ladakh without compromising on comfort. will definitely return someday!

a magical stay on the coastal jeju island jeju is a true paradise – breathtaking nature, turquoise waters, volcanic beaches, and a sense of tranquility like no other. every morning, i enjoyed peaceful walks along the coast, taking in the stunning ocean views and lush landscapes. the local cuisine is a delight, from fresh seafood and kimchi to jeju’s famous mandarins. i highly recommend visiting seongsan ilchulbong at sunrise for an unforgettable experience, as well as unwinding in the island’s natural lava pools. a perfect destination for relaxation, reconnecting with nature, and escaping the everyday hustle.

a magical stay with helpful staff and lovely facilities. rooms are nicely furnished with great landscape views. food was good, guides helpful and beds were comfortable. we did the atv riding which was fun, morning walk which was instructive, and evening drive on which we saw lots of oryx. we also arranged a hot air balloon trip which was truly a wonder (separate review). if you are coming from the north then there is probably not as much wildlife to see here, but being in the desert is another kind of amazing.

a magical treat for harry potter fans – must watch! if you're a harry potter fan, harry potter and the cursed child is an absolute must-watch. the two-part show brings the magic of the wizarding world to life in a way that’s both nostalgic and completely fresh. the stage effects are jaw-dropping, the storytelling is gripping, and the performances are spot-on. it's truly an unforgettable experience. that said, i’d highly recommend booking seats in the stalls or dress circle. the view from the balcony is quite high up, and depending on who’s sitting in front of you, your view could be significantly obstructed. for a show that relies so heavily on visual effects and detailed stagecraft, you’ll want the best vantage point possible. it’s worth the extra spend for a better experience. the two parts are long, so plan accordingly—maybe even see them on separate days if you prefer not to sit through a marathon session. but trust me, it’s worth every minute. the way they’ve used lighting, illusions, and movement is unlike anything i’ve seen on stage before. you’ll leave the theatre feeling like you’ve just stepped out of hogwarts. whether you grew up with the books or just enjoy the films, this show captures the magic and emotion of the original series while adding a whole new dimension to the story. don’t miss it—you’ll be spellbound!

a magical walk through an ancient, untouched forest. you can truly feel the power of life in every plant here. tiny saplings that haven’t even reached your knees have been standing strong for over 20 years. the number of oak acorns scattered on the ground even serves as an indicator of the forest’s overall health for the year. when you’re tired, gently rub the leaves of the fragrant cypress—its calming, earthy scent brings an instant sense of peace and relaxation. photos and videos barely capture a tenth of its true beauty. i highly recommend experiencing the delicate balance of this rich ecosystem in person. my only regret? i didn’t spot a brown bear 🐻😂

a magnificent city park. there is everything you need: places for relaxation, various sports grounds, running tracks, here everyone will find no matter what age you are, just walk and enjoy ancient chinese places secluded from view

a magnificent climb of approximately 500 meters of elevation gain (300 meters / 50 meters of elevation gain) with views of the lofoten islands throughout the route. it's about a 5-minute drive from camping rystad. parking is readily available on the paved shoulder near the cattle grid/ferist. climb requirements: => endurance: okay. (fresh mountain air and good views; a short break will give you courage and energy.) => technique: good. (some sections between 100 and 250 meters of elevation gain require scrambling on hands and knees and/or are muddy in rain. the path is quite narrow but fairly easy to follow.) => time to summit/downhill: 2 x 75 minutes.

a magnificent excursion on a private boat to flat island and gabriel islet, and the crystal-clear lagoon. the crew was very pleasant, attentive to our safety, and gave excellent advice on snorkeling areas. the meal was also very tasty, and the view from the table was breathtaking. turquoise as far as the eye can see! we loved these moments with them.

a magnificent historical city from the middle ages. the walls completely surround the city. if you want to tour along the city walls, there are three entrances. it deserves to be one of the cultural elements on the unesco world heritage list. if you want to walk along the walls, there is a fee of 40 euros. it is worth it. the walk can take about 1-1.5 hours. the view along the walls is beautiful. however, in order to enjoy the city, it is necessary to get lost in the back streets within the city. each street is more beautiful than the other. comfortable clothes and shoes are important since you will be going up and down the stairs constantly. there are very nice cafes and hotels in between. but it is usually a very crowded city. you can enjoy it better by visiting in the early hours.

a magnificent place indeed! the waiting line was quite long even during a weekday, but overall worth the time. the basilique itself is just like any other magnificent church (at least to me), the one thing i would 100% recommend is to pay the ticket and take the stairs up, the view is amazing and you can really explore some less travelled corners of this beautiful historical site. though it is quite tiring to climb all the way up so please do be prepared.
a magnificent plaza offers a breathtaking view of the church, historic buildings surrounding it, the university where einstein taught, and a prominent memorial in the center.

a magnificent retail destination: al ghurair centre during my stay at the swissôtel al ghurair, i had the pleasure of visiting al ghurair centre, a truly magnificent and expansive shopping mall. as the first modern shopping mall in the middle east, al ghurair centre holds a significant place in dubai's history. established in 1981 in dubai's deira district, it has grown to become a premier destination for both locals and tourists, seamlessly blending a rich heritage with contemporary offerings. in 2013, al ghurair centre underwent a significant expansion, enhancing the visitor experience with the addition of 150 new stores, a world-class entertainment center, popular dining concepts, 60,000 square feet of office space, a serviced apartment complex, and a 5-star hotel with direct access to the center. al ghurair centre boasts an impressive array of features, offering a comprehensive experience that extends beyond mere shopping. the mall is home to over 250 retail brands, providing an unparalleled shopping journey with a diverse selection of fashion, electronics, and home goods. dining is a delight with more than 50 restaurants, including a dedicated dining district and food court, catering to a wide range of culinary preferences, from international cuisine to middle eastern delights. for entertainment, al ghurair centre offers a state-of-the-art cinema with 18 screens, perfect for movie enthusiasts. families can also enjoy attractions like sparky's, which features an indoor skating rink, a roller coaster, and other exciting activities. additionally, the mall features a captivating water show with a triple burst jet, adding a touch of spectacle and visual appeal. al ghurair centre is truly a one-stop destination, and i highly recommend it to anyone visiting dubai.
a magnificent view of the region’s pristine nature.

a marked hiking path amongst the ruins of the arab village, with their crumbling stone houses, a water spring and a pool. very very steep walk on the renovated road, so suitable only for very strong people, especially if you're gonna climb it back...
a market have "everything" from haircut & tailor & new as 2 hands clothes & electric bikes & food, vegetables +++++ good local price‼

a massive waterfall with swimming holes at the top and down below. there's a bumpy, dirt road for several kms leading in. there's picnic area and camping spots. the view of the basin and the waterfall is definitely worth the extra bit of the drive. there's lots of steep steps and slippery, wet rocks on the path. consider the areas when bringing children for safety.

a masterpiece of joseon dynasty architecture, gyeonghoeru pavilion stands as one of the most iconic symbols of royal splendor within gyeongbokgung palace. originally constructed in 1412 and rebuilt in 1867, this elevated structure is gracefully perched above a lotus pond, supported by 48 stone pillars and surrounded by tranquil waters. once used to host foreign envoys and royal banquets, the pavilion offers a rare glimpse into the refined elegance and diplomatic significance of korea’s royal court. today, it remains a stunning reminder of korea’s cultural heritage and architectural finesse—a highlight for any visitor to the palace.
a medium size structure located close to the northern wall. not very well restored, you can mostly see walls and partial remains of two columns. not very impressive to be honest.

a melhor trilha de fernando de noronha, mais longa, difícil, mas vale muito, cada passo. as vistas são espetaculares, muito especial.

a memorable and amazing experience of the expedition of hiking to the topmost point of africa at 5895 m.. however a word of caution: a serious 3 to 4 months of training should be done before the trip to ensure that one can reach the summit without any major problems. 5 to 8 day routes are available.

a moderate trail. creeks along the walk. at the lower falls, there was a long line (we waited 30 min) to enter a cave for closeup view of the lower falls. the sound is majestic when getting so close to the waterfall. arrive early to get a parking spot. we got here around 9:30am and there was ample space in p2 but when we were out around 10:40am all space was taken.

a moderate-hard trail. overcrowded at the beginning (12 a.m.) and hard to go around the slow people since there is no space on the trail to get around them. otherwise a really nice environment and scenery.

a moderately challenging hike to an awesome natural bridge. i recommend using collapsible trekking poles that you can place in your backpack as you scramble up rocks and steps over the final 20 to 30 foot ascent near the bridge. the bridge itself can be intimidating as you view it from the side. but once you walk out on it, you realize it is actually 8 feet wide or so at its most narrow point. those with a fear of heights will likely still be uncomfortable. for those who make the jaunt, memorable photos at the bridge and along the hike await. morning hiking is recommended to avoid the heat of the day. and as always, when hiking, be certain to bring plenty of water and some nourishment, such as nuts, fruit, trail mix, or sandwiches for your hike. staying healthy is vital!

a modern marvel in paris i was truly impressed when i first saw the grande arche de la défense. even more so when i learned it was built in the 1980s — i honestly thought it was just 5 or 10 years old! its modern design feels so fresh and timeless. what makes it even more fascinating is the alignment: the grande arche sits perfectly on the “axe historique” — a straight line that connects some of paris’s most iconic landmarks, from the louvre and the arc de triomphe all the way out here to la défense. standing there, you feel like you’re part of a living timeline of parisian history, stretching from past to present. paris never ceases to amaze at every turn, and the grande arche is a must-visit if you want to see how the city blends history with modernity.

a modern, green, calm park at the edge of the old city. you can find many places to sit and relax as it gets really quiet and serene. free access, free toilets, clean and with only few people roaming around during ramadan, this is all you can ever need from a park in a busy city.

a modest and in its way beautiful church. the view from the clock tower is amazing but the way up is really narrow and steep. not recommended to big/tall people! the adjacent cafe is really nice as well and the exhibition in the cellars quite interesting. the waiters an the cafe are able to speak german.

a moment of awe in the heart of bangkok. 🇹🇭✨ this temple is absolutely breathtaking — a masterpiece of architecture with intricate details, golden accents, and vibrant mosaics that make you feel like you’ve stepped into living history. despite the crowds, the atmosphere remains peaceful and deeply respectful. the sheer scale of the main statue is mesmerizing, and every corner is bursting with rich symbolism and artistic beauty. whether you’re drawn by culture, history, or just want to admire the craftsmanship, this place is a must-see. 💡 travel tips: ⏰ go early to beat the crowds 🎨 take your time to soak in the details 👕 dress respectfully (no shorts or sleeveless tops) 🛍️ don’t miss the nearby souvenir shops for affordable treasures a true highlight of bangkok — one that leaves you calm, inspired, and in awe. 🌸✨
a monastery founded by the "crazy" lama of the gobi around 1820. come hear the fascinating stories of a mongolian - poet, painter, composer, educator, holy man.

a moomintous museum. if you like all things moomin this is a must visit. they have a nice cafe with moomin themed snacks and lots of moomin history. if you rented a lotte car there’s a discount on the entry tickets

a more high-end market, clearly designed for tourists and noticeably fancier than the typical street markets in bangkok, with higher prices to match. beautifully located right in front of the river, which adds a special charm to the atmosphere. i lived nearby during my stay, so i visited several times. the market has a large indoor food hall and an outdoor area filled with hundreds of food kiosks. i had tom yum at one of the restaurants , it was delicious and also tried fresh fruits from the market. overall, a very elegant and enjoyable place to explore.
a mosque, school and hospital at the same complex. the architecture is amazing. i never get bored from visiting it.

a most breathtaking exhilarating experience on the zipline. superb logistics even with overnight blizzard conditions creating fresh japow snow. heavenly views zipping down over the snow covered trees and the ski area. easy approach from our stay at park hyatt niseko. the chairlift to reach the top to start the zipline was super luxury with heated leather seats and a covered hood to protect from the elements while viewing the spectacular snow surroundings. we were a couple and they arranged for a side by side zipline experience - very unique. the adventure staff is polite, friendly and very competent. all in all, a standout topnotch experience in our whole ski trip to niseko. not to be missed.

a much better experience than actually hiking diamond head. weekday there was plenty of street parking. absolutely gorgeous views with sparkling diamond rocks. it was not busy from a tourist perspective, but there was a large homeless population living nearby. very little shade, but a nice paved pathway to walk from street level down to the beach.

a much easier path than the morne blanc. previously installed steps are missing in a few places. wonderful nature at your fingertips and a downright stunning view from the final spot under the roof. highly recommended to all!

a museum for everyone. they had three temporary exhibitions (don quixote, thom mayne, world press photo of the year) and one massive permanent exhibition of fine ceramics, silver, and furniture. i was constantly amazed by the things i saw in different sections and how comprehensive their themes were. there was also a beautiful garden that took my breath away. strongly recommend paying a visit!

a museum of egypt's past christian history. it houses the collection of preserve woodwork, archways and courtyards. inside you'll find the icon, textiles and manuscripts that tell the powerful stories of faith and christian art. i am glad i made time for it.

a museum on top of monte rite. it is an unique museum. to go there, we can take a shuttle bus that costs 9 euro per person or 13 euro for round trip. we can also take the hiking trail. the entrance ticket for an adult person is 8 euro. it's worth to visit. the view around it is stunning.
a museum showcasing a good collection of works by renoir and cézanne, plus some nice collectibles from the french collector paul guillaume. perfect spot for art lovers.
a must do hike in noronha! i highly recommend to get a tour guide, not only you will learn more about the place but also because it is a steep and rocky hike. definitely worth it!

a must do hike while in cape town! either in the morning or late afternoon for sunset. during the warmer months, it can get quite hot. the trail is fairly easy but towards the top there is some climbing needed. the trail does have a non climbing route, but the climbing one is very well curated to avoid any dangerous scenarios. highly recommended and a definite must do while in ct!

a must do if in ella, highly recommend for sunrise: best view and you can beat the heat. leave at 430a from nearby train station. use alltrails gps if you prefer over guide. trail is a bit rough in places, but a great challenge and exciting journey in the dark. fee is 950 lkr at the top. given the crowds i’ve seen so far in ella, this was serene and refreshing: there were only around 20 people.
a must do if you like to see reptiles and other small creatures. the knowledge they share is great. they share about the history and the geography of namibia and take you to up the dunes as well.

a must-see gem in toronto – beautiful in both summer and christmas seasons! casa loma is truly one of toronto’s most iconic and magical places. whether you visit in the summer when the gardens are in full bloom, or during the christmas season when the castle transforms into a winter wonderland, this historical site never fails to impress. i visited during christmas time and it was a unique experience. walking on hallways and in the garden with lots of decoration and festive vibe was so memorable. the architecture is absolutely stunning, and walking through the grand halls, secret passages, and beautifully preserved rooms feels like stepping back in time. each corner of the castle tells a piece of toronto’s rich history. in the summer, the outdoor terrace and gardens are breathtaking, offering perfect photo opportunities and a peaceful escape from the city. in the winter, casa loma is completely transformed with festive lights, decorations, and seasonal events that bring the magic of the holidays to life. whether you’re a history lover, architecture enthusiast, or just looking for a unique experience in toronto, casa loma is a must-visit all year round. don’t miss it!

a must-see jewel of dubrovnik: minčeta tower if you haven't seen minčeta tower, you haven't truly seen dubrovnik. rising proudly above the ancient city walls, minčeta is more than a fortress — it is the soul of dubrovnik's heritage. with its round crown and stone-clad strength, it stands as a symbol of the city's resilience, history, and unmatched beauty. walking up to minčeta, you are not just stepping onto a monument — you are stepping into centuries of human craftsmanship, determination, and architectural genius. the views from the top are nothing short of breathtaking: terracotta rooftops tumbling toward the sparkling adriatic sea, framed by mountains and sky. minčeta is not just a part of dubrovnik — it is a guardian of its spirit. missing it would be like reading a book and skipping the final chapter. it is a place where history whispers through stone, and every step echoes with stories from the past. a visit to dubrovnik without minčeta is an incomplete journey. with all its power and beauty, it deserves to be seen, remembered, and treasured — as one of the world’s greatest human-made wonders. zazapress
