a must-see piece of puerto rican history! visiting san cristóbal castle was one of the highlights of my trip to old san juan. the views alone are worth the visit—panoramic sights of the atlantic ocean and the colorful city below. you can really feel the history walking through the tunnels, dungeons, and massive stone walls. the fortress is incredibly well-preserved, and the info plaques throughout make it easy to understand how it was used to defend the island. i recommend going early in the day to beat the heat and crowds. wear comfortable shoes and bring water—it’s a lot of walking, but so worth it. whether you're into history, photography, or just taking in some of the best views on the island, san cristóbal is a must-visit in puerto rico.

a must-see – even after 30 years this was my third visit to the van gogh museum over the past 30 years, and it continues to impress. the layout and timeline of van gogh’s life and artistry are beautifully curated—thoughtful, emotional, and easy to follow. fortunately, i realized in time that advanced, timed-entry tickets are required and was able to book a slot 2.5 days out. definitely plan ahead! the audio tour truly elevated the experience. we started with just the highlights but ended up switching to the extended version because we enjoyed the storytelling and insights so much. highly recommend for all ages—whether it’s your first visit or your third.

a must-see, but plan ahead i thoroughly enjoyed my visit to the van gogh museum. the collection is, as expected, breathtaking, offering a powerful and intimate look into the artist's life and work. the curation is excellent, tracing his development from early pieces to his iconic masterpieces. the gift shop on ground floor is lovely. however, a major drawback is just how incredibly busy it is. the museum is a top destination, and the crowds can be overwhelming, making it difficult to fully appreciate some of the artworks. it's a testament to the museum's quality, but it definitely impacts the experience. a crucial piece of advice for anyone planning to go: this museum is always booked out. you absolutely must book your tickets online well in advance of your visit. spontaneous visits are almost impossible, and you will be turned away. if you prepare for the crowds and secure your ticket ahead of time, it's a truly unforgettable experience.

a must-visit cultural and scenic landmark in bali! tanah lot is absolutely breathtaking, with the ocean. the coastal views are stunning, and the spiritual atmosphere adds a unique charm. one of bali’s most iconic spots, this temple is stunning on clear days and at sunset. expect strong winds and waves that add to its dramatic charm. explore both sides of the temple for unique views. nearby, a lively market offers reasonably priced souvenirs from local vendors there are a couple of special experiences here — you can view the holy snake (for a fee) and receive spring water near the entrance in the ocean. the area is popular with tourists, so expect crowds, but it’s well-managed with lots of local shops and stalls along the way. a beautiful blend of nature, culture, and tradition — highly recommended!

a must-visit evening shopping in siem reap!** i recently visited the reverside night market and had an unforgettable experience! nestled near the river, this market comes alive at dusk with twinkling lights, creating a magical and relaxed atmosphere. it’s smaller than other markets in siem reap, but that adds to its charm—less crowded and easier to explore. **what i loved:** - **food variety:** the food stalls are a highlight! i tried authentic cambodian dishes like fish amok and bbq skewers, along with fresh coconut ice cream. vegetarian options were clearly labeled, which was a plus. - **unique souvenirs:** the handicraft stalls sell beautifully crafted items—silk scarves, wooden carvings, and eco-friendly products. bargaining is expected, and vendors were friendly and patient. - **ambiance:** live acoustic music near the river made the evening feel special. there’s also a cozy seating area to unwind with a drink. **tips:** - go early (around 6 pm) to avoid the small dinner rush. - bring cash (small bills) for easier transactions. - don’t miss the $1 foot massages—perfect after a day of temple-hopping!

a must-visit for art lovers in barcelona! the picasso museum offers a fascinating look into the artist's early life and development. i was especially impressed with the chronological display of his work, which really shows his incredible talent even as a young man. the museum is located in a beautiful historic building, adding to the experience. i highly recommend buying your tickets online in.

a must-visit for authentic cambodian culture!** the old market (phsar chas) in siem reap is a vibrant and bustling place that offers a true taste of local life. from fresh produce and exotic spices to handmade crafts and souvenirs, this market has it all. the atmosphere is lively, and the vendors are friendly—many are happy to chat and share stories if you take the time to engage. what i loved most was the food section, where you can try delicious cambodian street food at unbeatable prices. the **amok curry**, **grilled meats**, and **fresh tropical fruits** are must-tries! bargaining is expected, so don’t hesitate to negotiate politely for the best deals. the market is centrally located, making it easy to explore after visiting nearby attractions like pub street. it can get crowded, especially in the evenings, but that just adds to the authentic experience. **highly recommended** for travelers who want to immerse themselves in cambodian culture, support local vendors, and take home unique finds!

a must-visit in singapore! 🌸 the gardens are stunning, beautifully maintained, and full of unique plants and flowers. the cloud forest and flower dome are breathtaking, and the supertree light show at night is magical. perfect for families, couples, or anyone who loves nature!

a must-visit location whether you're buddhist or not, this is situated near the airport, a trek from the heart of hong kong (hiking optional and also worth it if you're into hiking). you can take the tram up, which gives great views of the island and surrounding areas and airport, or hike it up by taking the local bus from the local station (or walk like i did) to the trail entrance, and take in some gorgeous views. the afternoon that i went (go early!), there were thunderstorm delays, so factor in weather when you go. july may not be the best time, but certainly was worth it. also check out po lin monastery on the premises, which is an active temple and has monks out and about the area. pro tip: if you hike, you'll invariably see small paths that deviate from the trail; people live there, so take care with not doing too much exploring :)

a must-visit mosque during ramadan asma bint alawi mosque in qurum is a true gem in muscat, offering a deeply spiritual and serene atmosphere, especially during ramadan. the mosque's stunning architecture, with its intricate islamic designs and peaceful surroundings, creates the perfect environment for prayer and reflection. during ramadan, the mosque comes alive with beautiful taraweeh prayers, soulful recitations, and a strong sense of community. the well-maintained prayer halls, excellent acoustics, and spacious areas for both men and women make it a comfortable place for worshippers. whether you're looking for a place to strengthen your faith, experience a spiritually uplifting night, or simply admire the mosque's beauty, asma bint alawi mosque is a must-visit during the blessed month. #ramadan #spirituality #muscatmosques #taraweeh

a must-visit museum! great vibes, we can learn much from history, how economics evolving, how mathematics influences in every major of science, how plane changes from time to time, evolution theory, how dna passes and many more! so excited and wonderful experience!

a must-visit place while in cairo! the citadel of salah el-din is a massive historical complex with stunning architecture, incredible panoramic views of cairo, and deep cultural significance. the site includes the impressive mosque of muhammad ali, known for its grand ottoman-style design and iconic domes. you’ll also find smaller mosques, museums, and military exhibits within the citadel walls. it’s a great spot for history lovers and architecture enthusiasts alike. the area is quite large, so wear comfortable shoes, and since it can get very hot—especially during midday—bringing a hat or umbrella is highly recommended.

a must-visit spot for sunset lovers just find yourself a spot facing the serene expanse of water and the setting sun, and you’ll feel your worries melt away. there’s something profoundly soothing about watching the horizon blaze with color, surrounded by the gentle sound of waves. it’s the kind of place where you can feel gloriously alone in a crowd, lost in nature’s beauty. a word of practical advice: if you’re carrying food, stay alert! the local seagulls are seasoned thieves, ready to swoop in the moment you glance away. it’s all part of the waterfront charm—but don’t say you weren’t warned! overall, it’s a wonderful experience for everyone. if you’re single, come here to reflect and find yourself. if you’re married, it’s a place to rediscover the quiet voice of love. and if you have kids, you can soak in the views while they enjoy street food and free games along the promenade. it’s truly a must-visit destination. if you’re coming from farther away, i highly recommend using the go train—convenient, scenic, and stress-free.

a must-visit spot in jeju is the artificial forest with towering trees and various trails, perfect for short strolls or longer hikes. the atmosphere is cool and humid, ideal for nature lovers and families. kids will delight in spotting insects and spiders along the way. the paths, including a barrier-free option, accommodate wheelchairs and strollers. despite challenging parking, with most spots on the street, the experience is worthwhile. the trail loop starts and ends at a point with facilities including restrooms and food trucks offering refreshments and snacks. this forest is an essential part of the jeju experience.

a must-visit spot in london! portobello road market is such a fun and vibrant place to explore. there’s a great mix of food, local products, vintage finds, and unique little shops. one of the highlights for me was discovering an interesting vegan bakery – full of creative and delicious options that are hard to find elsewhere. the fresh fruit stands were also impressive – everything looked super fresh and was noticeably cheaper than in supermarkets. it’s a great spot to grab some snacks or ingredients for the week. i love the energy of the area, and there’s always something new to see. i’ll definitely be coming back again – it’s perfect for a relaxed weekend stroll, especially if you enjoy good food and local vibes.

a must-visit spot inside dubai mall! chinatown here is beautifully designed – vibrant lanterns, traditional-style architecture, and super instagrammable corners. the food options are great too – loved the dim sum and hotpot! it’s like stepping into a little slice of asia right in dubai. less crowded than other parts of the mall, so it’s perfect for a relaxing stroll or a cozy meal. definitely coming back to try more places!

a must-visit temple in bangkok, rich in historical significance and adorned with beautiful buddhist sculptures. the entrance fee is only 100 baht, yet the peaceful and inspiring experience is truly priceless. located in the heart of the city with easy access and surrounded by famous street food stalls, it’s a perfect stop for anyone exploring bangkok.

a must-visit water park for families! we had an absolutely fantastic time here! unlike other water parks we've visited across vietnam, this one truly had something for every member of our family, making it a standout experience. our daughters had a blast—especially our 5-year-old, who was thrilled to be able to go on most of the water rides, which isn’t always the case at other parks. meanwhile, our youngest loved splashing around in the wave pool and gently cruising along the lazy river. it was the perfect balance of fun and relaxation. entry was surprisingly affordable—we only paid 140,000 vnd each, even though the sign listed 190,000 vnd. not sure why, but it was a pleasant surprise and great value for money. highly recommend this spot if you’re looking for a fun-filled day out with the kids!

a national treasure!!! fantastic display of the history of the revolucion in mexico. requires a separate ticket from the monumento de la revolucion - in the same facility. historic photos, videos, documents, sculptures. inapam discounted entry tickets for senior citizen mexican residents. a tremendous exhibition. a must see in cdmx!

a naturally decorated garden... eye soothing in any time round the year... free of tickets... perfect place for capturing some awesome photos... this summary reflects the late autumn view of the garden...

a nature wonder which is a must to see. is huge, you feel little and senseless. the park is really well organized with shuttle bus which transport you everywhere (as you cannot go with your private car), easy to find stations and the right bus to take. is really crowded but in certain path you can have your time and space. remember it is around 2000 meters above sea level, so can be cold in certain months or time of the day, be prepared.

a neighborhood favorite, legion park farmers market. open every saturday. arrive early to secure a good parking spot and take advantage of the yoga sessions, fresh produce, bakery and many other vendors. great for the whole family.

a new-ish addition to the greek capital's extensive constellation of museums of all sorts, b&e houses one the world's largest, and most magnificent, private art collection. private in this case means eclectic, reflecting the personal, and excuisite, tastes of basil and elise goulandris. it is housed in a meticulously restored early 20th century neoclassical building, unobtrusively extended to several times its size, primarily underground, and also in the former yard and on the roof. this loving bequest to the people of greece was decades in planning, and delayed by years of litigation, involving relatives of the childless goulandris couple, and even government entities. excellent works from the 20th, and late 19th century, by art superstars, primarily paintings (all the great impressionists, also picasso and others); drawings and prints; bibelots; a very unique, signed theotokopoulos (el greco); sublime sculptures; and high-value home furnishings. to say that this feast for the eyes warrants multiple visits is an understatement

a nice 30 minute walk from town, i highly recommend this to anyone staying in the area. the lake is nearby and makes for great views afterwards. watch your footing when you start the stairs inside as the stone section is not even/equal heights and it is dark. easy way to say you visited a castle ruins while on vacation and it didn't cost a penny! the tree on top of the castle had me puzzled however good on it for clearly thriving for many years, and hopefully many more.

a nice area to visit on the way to ella rock. costs 500rs per person. you can walk down from the train tracks in about 5 mins and have a refreshing and cooling time standing in the spray of the waterfall! no opportunity to swim here though.

a nice area to visit while visiting dubai. it was nice to see this side of dubai, the streets, the traditional shops and i would recommend the boat ride to the souks for a full experience (only 2 aed)

a nice area to wander around in with lots of to and plenty of choice for eats. stay for dinner to get the best views. there is a park for the kids, but be careful - there are many areas with no rail at the water's edge.

a nice bit of jungle to walk through with good views of the city. the point itself is a 15 minute walk from the cable car station but a nice view from there and a small merlion statue. walk through the cafe and gift shop to get to the bells of happiness and then go down the stairs from there. recommend taking water and mosquito repellent.

a nice castle and grounds. lovely waterfalls, flowers and scenery. the castle itself was nice but i've been to better. all the staff were friendly and provided some extra information when asked. also saw a couple of seals not far from the castle walls. a short video at the end of the tour also gives some history to the castle, told by the current owner. not suitable for those using wheelchairs as a lot of the paths in the gardens were either quite narrow or very bumpy. inside the castle, it being from the middle ages, had a lot of stairs and no lift (pretty sure this would be mentioned on the official website). there is, of course, a gift shop, in fact two, one inside the castle and one outside along with a cafe. prices are as expected in these kinds of places.

a nice easy day out for those with kids. plenty for them to see and do. some lifts were not working when i visited. i hope this is sorted quickly! pre-booking is a must as the tickets sell out often. not a fan of the fact you can't purchase a ticket just for the day. instead they sell a year long ticket where you can go as many times as you like so long as you pre-book a time slot. in all likelihood you will go once and never again. once you've seen it you've seen it. the shop is full of london paraphernalia for all ages from plush toys to pins and badges. prices vary so prepare to spend more than you originally planned. plenty of choice but some items can be harsh on the pockets. though all excellent quality items - hence the price. all in all a pleasant half a day out but i probably won't be going again.

a nice easy hike from copacabana, took us less than 30min to get from town to the top. 10bs entrance free and beautiful view from the top. there is no information on the site so it’s worth reading up on it before visiting. it’s a great short excursion from copacabana and worth visiting just for the view!

a nice easy hike from copacabana, took us less than 30min to get from town to the top. 10bs entrance free and beautiful view from the top. there is no information on the site so it’s worth reading up on it before visiting. it’s a great short excursion from copacabana and worth visiting just for the view!
a nice experience, an evening trip around the lake, weekends with a large crowd, food performances and more, a family event
a nice gem in nyc. and free! this is a well-maintained collection of gardens (french, italian and english). take a nice stroll while taking in the view. it’s definitely worth the trip.

a nice hike with a rewarding 360 degree view which will astound you with any direction you look. but my reason for writing this review is to inform you of the shop near the summit. after a moderate hike in the sweltering july sun i was happy to find some shade, what i found was so much better - a welcoming family that didn’t pressure sales but offered true companionship. i sat and talked with them for hours and gained local insights into the region that would have otherwise gone unnoticed. the shops was also incredibly interesting to peruse, but the conversation was fascinating. from the shop, there is a backroad that winds down a valley gorge into regions of the park that largely ignored but incredibly interesting. my sincere thanks for the time, the insights, and guidance, your friend,

a nice historic house museum to check out. crazy to think that when that house was built there was nothing around. now it's totally surrounded. worth checking out. the staff member that was there was full of knowledge and shared a lot of interesting facts and details.
a nice hotel with excellent coffee. really attentive service and value for the money.

a nice kayak tour with a perfect pace and length for almost beginners. the two guides were both very nice and easy to approach. the other guide taking pictures of us for free was a really nice touch. the route and special adds were also nice as we got to see lots of “blue waters”

a nice little cruise on the 'sea shell' yacht with my family it's the first one for us and the crew on deck, captain robert and his first mates ganesh & mey were really hospitable and really friendly and made our experience much better on this trip. we would highly reccomend a cruise with them!
a nice little factory outlet right next to the fish factory. tuna in all its variations. the entrance to the factory grounds is on the seafront. just ask for entry.

a nice little green area in the heart of the old city. it is very close to the chateau frontenac. a tall and beautiful statue with water fountain ⛲️ in the middle of the park is mind blowing during a hot summer. it has a lot of historical and cultural significance in the history of québec city. visitors can see the québec city tourism information centre just in front of the park. if you get extra time from your tour you can spend hours and hours just watching the beauty of the park and the city as well.
a nice little piece of history to check out if you’re in the area.

a nice little secluded stretch along the side of the saint lawrence. there are some nice hiking stretches with a lot of up and down stairs. it will get your heart rate up. the beach is swimmable and not deep. the sand is not white but nor is it dirty. good views of the river, bridges, levi and obviously anything going on in the river. nothing nearby (drinks, food, shops) so bring everything that you want to have with you.

a nice little temple worthy of a walk in and around, quaint little bridge that crosses over to a beautiful little temple 🛕 suitable clothing is recommended although not everyone was adhering to this, photography inside the temple is prohibited and you'll be told!! 50vnd entrance fee is nothing, just a few quid, lake view is nice and considering it location it's very peaceful

a nice little zoo if you like that sort of thing, and the tour guide was knowledgeable. birds were well looked after, and good variety of plants. the guide said everything always inspected and suitable for the birds, but for me it was just a lot of birds in small cages. there is also a good cafe and gift shop.
a nice locals market in town

a nice monastery right on the opposite side of the big budha. there are multiple exhibition halls depicting the big budha details and construction journey and other key information of buddhism in hong kong. it has a stunning hall with so many buddhas all in gold plating. it is so magnificent and beautiful. the area is quite large and very well kept and managed by the authorities. you feel a very nice vibe and silence all around. do not miss this place!

a nice museum with a lot of sculptures and statues. we spent about 1.5 hours there and had a lot of fascinating marble works to see. ticket per person is €9. worth a visit. there is a locker area for coats and bags for free.

a nice oasis on union street right along the main bike route. lots of seating out front to sit, relax, and watch the world go by (or steady stream of bikers). serves up a limited offering of hot and cold drinks. everything is one size to keep it simple. they also have prepared sandwiches as well as small selection of pastries, including pastel de nata (portuguese egg tarts). also, unique for a small coffee shop, they have in house baked sourdough bread loaves and soft serve ice cream. there are an eclectic mix of dry goods (coffee beans, etc.) as well as imported tin sardines from portugal! got the americano and the matcha latte. both had great flavours. sour cherry muffin was tasty.

a nice park to relax in or go for a jog. most of the park is tree lined paths and bench areas though it has a few extra sections. there is a beautiful butterfly garden on the south side that i'd recommend. a herb / rose garden. a dog park. and a lake for viewing birds... though they were hiding during our visit.

a nice park to sit and relax after a nice walk on brooklyn bridge. it's very close to the bridge and many food, drink vendors outside. there are benches to sit on and a nice fountain. a quiet respite from the hustle bustle outside.

a nice park to walk around and hang out with beautiful statues and fountains. beautiful art museum- should visit but must get tickets in advance. tickets were sold out and lots of people still trying to get in.

a nice place in center of town with the tulum sign, a sports complex, a children's playground, usually some vendors and many other things. playground is nice and usually shaded. the nicest one we have found in tulum. evenings have different events that varies night by night. during our few months living here we saw everything from mayan historical dances to children's dance and luau performances to live music, etc. lots of shops and restaurants nearby too.

a nice place to see the greek traditional clothes, lots and lots of jewelry! very clean, straight forward sellers, you can take home souvenirs from here. you will have differentiated prices in jewelry stores from gold - silver and stainlesss steel! great greek designs for jewelry.
a nice place to share a romantic moment with your loved one. but when i arrived there, the building behind the garden was under construction, so i couldn't enjoy the vibe to the fullest.
a nice place to visit, but don't expect much. cars going over the bridge ruin otherwise unique and calm atmosphere.

a nice place to visit, charles dickens museum was the home of the author. see how he lived and hear a moderator tell you interesting facts about his life and his family members. there’s a lift, if you feel you can’t make it upstairs to any of the five floors. there’s also.a tea room, if you want a nice cup of tea, a coffee or a snack. you will also find cards, bookmarks and many souvenirs to buy including books and cloth bags, all dickens, among other items to buy. take home a keepsake, or give to a dear friend. i enjoyed my visit immensely!
a nice place with possibility to shower and get cold drinking water. the umbrella and stool is to be paid for.

a nice quaint winery. we shared the sigalas integral wine tasting with 8 wines as well as a cheese & cold cuts platter with local meats and cheeses. everything was amazing from the sommelier to the wines and platter…. oh and of course the sweet resident cat ♥️
a nice ride with medium excitement. love the story/experience around the mine and grizzly bears. i liked this the most among all rides in hk disneyland, my 10 and 12 years old kids loved it too.

a nice short little hike to stretch your legs in banff. i've never seen a hot springs marsh and just loved the moss growing under the frost. we were told we would see lots of birds, but we saw/heard none. you could see all the minnows swimming in the flowing warm waters though! very neat!
a nice square that is a bit quieter than the main medina, some nice shops and the spice market. eating is not such good value here.

a nice stop to slow down and take in the sights, with photo opportunities at every corner. there are a lot of vendors and cuban people close by, with a park directly across the street. there is a lot of history and its relatively cheap for what you get, so take your time and enjoy.

a nice temple made on the 2nd floor of a building. reach the spot as given on google maps, find the entrance to the building and take the lift to the 2nd floor. well maintained temple with nice murtis as well as guru granth sahib. wish they could also add mahavira's and gautama, the buddha's murti as well. do visit when in tsim sha tsui.

a nice traditional experience to see how silk is made and shop some unique pieces. worth a visit.

a nice tranquil public and free garden to visit, just outside of the medina. peaceful, lush and with plenty of shade, it is easy to forget about the chaotic streets of marrakech just outside the garden walls.
a nice uphill hike from the falls to some ruins called druin an aird. well marked, wide trails and worth the walk.

a nice workout with a view! paved with stairs... 2 miles of gorgeous views and native plants & animals.

a night owl market and felt super safe as a solo female traveller, despite wandering into dark alleys. full market open from around 11.30pm to 3am. some venders do start packing up at 2.45m. it's not a souvenir market for a tourist . it's for wholesalers. it's so great for b2b. the wholesale prices are amazing, with a single purchase price still pretty good imo. some vendors do honour the wholesale prices, provided you're not a rude jerk about it. crazy markdowns on monday and tuesdays. lots of food options, the 15baht ice cream lolly man is a life saver: it's hot as it's crowded.

a nightclub in the best location. the staff and djs were friendly, and i had an amazing time—what a great party! the dj’s music selection was top-notch! i’ll definitely come back again! the place was packed and full of energy!

a nile river cruise in cairo offers a truly unforgettable experience, combining the serene beauty of the river with the excitement of a lively evening. as the boat glides along the iconic waterway, guests are treated to breathtaking views of the city’s skyline, the illuminated landmarks, and the ancient pyramids in the distance. the evening includes a delicious dinner featuring traditional egyptian cuisine, with a variety of flavorful dishes to indulge in. as the meal winds down, the atmosphere shifts to a lively celebration with vibrant music and dance performances, including traditional belly dancing and folkloric shows. the combination of scenic beauty, exquisite food, and dynamic entertainment creates a magical ambiance that leaves guests with lasting memories of an unforgettable night on the nile.

a once in a lifetime experience! i received the sound journey with akal that was life transforming. he is definitely a magician and sound wizard!. i was transported into a different world the moment i stepped into the circular sound chamber. there are so many gongs, bowls, chimes, it was a feast to my senses to be surrounded by so many incredible instruments! i was laid down comfortably and guided on a most amazing and glorious adventure, like being on a magic carpet ride. i was transported into a timeless dimension of beauty and grace. i felt like i had been cradled by the loving universe for a very long time, returning feeling very relaxed, refreshed and knowing that " every little thing is going to be alright". thank you iala and akal for guiding me on such a healing and transformative journey.

a once-in-a-lifetime experience – what a beautiful vacation! we recently returned from a three-week adventure through south africa and zimbabwe, organized by safari explorer, and we couldn’t be more impressed. the entire trip was beautifully curated and ran like clockwork — not a single issue from start to finish. we began in the stunning wine regions of franschhoek and stellenbosch, which offered a relaxing and luxurious introduction to south africa. from there, we moved to grootbos private nature reserve — a hidden gem that gave us a deep connection with nature and a peaceful, unforgettable experience. our time in cape town was equally special. we explored table mountain, took city tours, and soaked up the vibrant coastal beauty. every moment was well thought out, giving us a true feel for the city’s energy and charm. from there, we flew to thornybush, a private game reserve just outside kruger national park, for a four-day safari experience at saseka tented camp. staying in a tented camp was a first for us — and we loved it! we were lucky enough to see all of the big five, and the guides were simply exceptional. the entire team made us feel safe, welcome, and fully immersed in the safari experience. our journey ended with a trip to victoria falls in zimbabwe — truly one of the natural wonders of the world. the falls were breathtaking and a fitting grand finale to a remarkable journey. a special thank you to lauren maker from safari explorer. lauren was outstanding — attentive, knowledgeable, responsive, and always one step ahead. she made sure everything went smoothly and was always available whenever we had a question. her attention to detail and care were evident throughout the entire trip. thank you, lauren, and thank you safari explorer, for giving us a trip we will remember forever. highly recommended! petra and ernst lieb
a panoramic viewing point of hong kong south. lamma island is easily seen on a clear day.

a paradise for watersports lovers, especially kitesurfing, windsurfing, and paddleboarding. thanks to the steady, reliable wind. the beach is huge, so even in peak season, it never feels crowded. powdery white sand, turquoise water, and a laid-back vibe make it a must-visit. perfect for both adrenaline and relaxation!

a paradise in kenya. famous for its huge african elephants other than numbers of animals. a huge variety of birds are also there. driving down the park with africas highest peak mount kilimanjaro is a lifetime experience.

a park located right across the istana and plaza singapura that most people may not know or visit even if they past by frequently. it is not big but well maintained and pleasant. the greenery provides a good respite from the malls and hotels along orchard road

a park of contentment holding reminiscences of past contestations, as revealed by various political and war commemorations. in a sliver of the park running parallel to the rue saint-louis stands a bold monument in imperial style commemorating the dead who fought in the boer war. this was a war not supported by the canadian public (as elsewhere in the empire, such as australia), and in the end only volunteers joined the empire's forces. eleven did not return alive, and their names are written on a bronze plaque attached to the plinth. atop the plinth is a bronze statue of a soldier holding a flowing flag. it was unveiled on 15 august 1905 in the presence of lord grey, governor-general of canada. distant in time, distant in purpose, a disaster in outcome. https://www.veterans.gc.ca/en/remembrance/memorials/national-inventory-canadian-memorials/details/3882

a park with natural spa. buy tickets online in advance! the price of the ticket was 10 eur for adults, the price for a locker was 2 eur. lockers are quite old, and do not have much space inside (i put my backpack and my shoes inside the locker). your ticket is valid for 1 hour and 30 minutes, i suggest buying ticket for the first time slot (from 9.00 am to 10.30 am), at that slot there aren't that many people inside yet, you have a lot of empty parking spaces, and you most likely get an overall better spa experience. spa has 4 natural pools. pool at the top is the most beautiful with a waterfall, and the coldest water (water temperature around 24 degreec celsius). three pools below are smaller and the water thete is much warmer (probably around 40 degrees celsius, different temperatures on each pool). close to the pools are two shower cabins, and two toilets (one for males and one for females). you get the keylock for the locker at the wodden cabin by the toilets. i think there can be max 100 visitors at the same time slot in the spa. i recommend visiting the spa, if you are visiting the island, it is really one of a kind experience.

a particular highlight of the seawall promenade around stanley park. the overlook itself is dramatic, with panoramic views of the bridge and the craggy mountains with their rainforests and cantons, as well as views of the city on the other side. if you can only look at one fragment of the sea walk, i highly recommend this one. still, the lighthouse itself is no less exceptional. it is rustic and quaint, the emblem of an older point in the city's history, but it has now been restored, and its vibrant colors contrast the rippling gray water.
a peaceful and calm place

a peaceful and unforgettable part of our jubilee pilgrimage ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ we visited rome for the holy year and chose june for its warm but bearable weather – the perfect time to enjoy the vatican gardens. the open bus tour was a highlight of our trip: peaceful, enriching, and visually stunning. the lush greenery, fountains, and sacred architecture created a deeply moving atmosphere. the audio guide provided insightful commentary without being overwhelming – it truly enhanced the experience. we loved every moment. after the gardens, we entered the sistine chapel directly, skipping the museum galleries as we had visited them before. the chapel was very crowded, but still worth it – a sacred space that never loses its impact. we booked the garden visit about 2–3 weeks in advance, and it included the museum ticket. absolutely recommended – especially during the jubilee year.

a peaceful escape just minutes from honolulu! round top forest reserve offers lush trails, cool breezes, and stunning panoramic views of the city, diamond head, and the ocean. it’s perfect for a short hike, a scenic drive, or just relaxing in nature. bring good shoes—some trails can get muddy—but the beauty is well worth it. great spot for sunrise, sunset, or a quiet picnic.

a peaceful green escape in the heart of the city audubon park is a beautiful oasis in new orleans — the perfect place to unwind and enjoy nature. i took the streetcar out and walked through the park on my way to the zoo, and it ended up being one of the highlights of the day. the wide paths are great for walking, running, or biking, and the canopy of trees offers plenty of shade — which was especially appreciated on a warm june afternoon. it’s peaceful, scenic, and full of charm, with locals and visitors alike out enjoying the space. whether you’re heading to the zoo or just looking for a relaxing stroll, audubon park is a lovely spot to slow down and soak in the natural beauty of the city.

a peaceful green space at the southern tip of manhattan, with stunning views of the statue of liberty and new york harbor. great place for a walk, ferry rides, or just relaxing by the water. beautiful gardens, historical monuments, and a calm break from the city buzz. perfect start or end to a visit to liberty and ellis island.
a peaceful haven with fantastic gardens and beautiful buildings. visited here many times this trip as it is so tranquil. also, there are lots of very friendly cats, which i loved.

a peaceful hidden gem in ella. kital ella waterfall is small but very charming, surrounded by lush greenery and the calming sound of flowing water. the walk along the railway track to get there is beautiful and adds to the adventure. it’s a perfect spot to relax and enjoy nature. i highly recommend it!

a peaceful hidden gem in the hills of sha tin visiting the ten thousand buddhas monastery was one of the most memorable experiences of my trip to hong kong. the peaceful hillside location, paired with the hundreds of golden buddha statues lining the path, created an atmosphere that felt both spiritual and surreal. each statue has a unique expression and pose, which made the uphill walk surprisingly fun and thought-provoking. the monastery itself is beautiful and serene, with intricate architecture and stunning views over sha tin. it’s not a functioning monastery (no resident monks), but it holds deep cultural and historical charm. just be prepared for the stairs—it's quite a climb, so wear comfy shoes and bring water. if you're looking for something off the typical tourist path that connects you with both nature and culture, this place is a must-see
a peaceful little oasis in marrakech. clean and safe, near the koutoubia mosque.

a peaceful little paradise amidst the concrete jungle. elaborate and artistic decorations throughout. many buildings sprawled around the lush gardens that are worth exploring. the hunting lodge gives an interesting picture of taxidermy as well as local customs and habitat. well maintained garden. there is also a riverside path/garden for an extra 5 l.e. for an extra little peaceful retreat.

a peaceful oasis in the heart of trastevere. the orto botanico di roma is a beautiful escape from the busy streets, with a wide variety of plants, including bamboo groves, orchids, palms, and a charming japanese garden. it’s a lovely place for a calm stroll, especially in spring when everything is in bloom. some areas feel a bit overgrown and could use more upkeep, and mosquitoes can be an issue in warmer months, so bring repellent. overall, a relaxing and affordable way to enjoy nature in the city.

a peaceful shrine devoted to boars after a legend of thousands of boars saving an ancient ruler and healing his legs. thus many people come here to pray for healthy legs and for leap of fortune for their business. no info in english, but very fascinating.

a peak easy to climb either from braemar hill or mount parker. the view from this peak is great. here you have the east half of victoria harbour and lye mun of east kowloon as well. from the east foot of the this hill you can explore further to wong nei chung or tai tam.

a pedra da proa está localizada no parque nacional da tijuca, possui esse nome pois seu formato lembra a proa de um navio. me acompanhe nas redes sociais: @ponturista 🪨 o acesso pode ser feito próxima a bifurcação da estrada do redentor, a estrada do sumaré e na mesa do imperador, por onde eu subi. 🪨 a trilha é bem sinalizada, possui cerca de 1km e leva em torno de 35 minutos para ser concluída (da mesa do imperador até lá). antes de chegar ao atrativo você terá que escalar um pequeno trecho de pedra, marcada com ferros fincados.

a perfect blend of nature and fun – a park for everyone! this park truly offers the best of both worlds. on one side, you’ll find a peaceful and charming green area with a pond full of ducks, perfect for a relaxing walk, biking, or even a picnic under the trees. it's an ideal spot to unwind, enjoy nature, or just let the kids run free while you sit back and take in the serene atmosphere. on the other side of the park is a huge amusement area that’s packed with games and attractions for all ages. from thrilling rides to fun games for kids, there's something here for everyone. we tried the giant ferris wheel, which gave us amazing views — definitely a highlight! the ride cost €6 per person, and it was well worth it. keep in mind that while entry to the general park is free, each amusement game or ride has its own separate fee. there’s also a fantastic section within the park filled with restaurants! you can visit day or night. it’s a great area to relax after a walk or a fun ride, and it's equally enjoyable for both adults and kids. all in all, this park is a must-visit. whether you're looking for a calm afternoon in nature or an exciting day of fun, it has it all in one place!

a perfect blend of scenic beauty, architecture, and relaxation alamo square park is one of the most memorable spots in san francisco and easily earns a perfect 5/5 in my book. it offers one of the most iconic views in the city — the famous "painted ladies" with the san francisco skyline rising behind them. seeing this view in person feels like stepping into a real-life postcard, especially around sunset when the golden light hits the victorian facades just right. the park itself is clean, well-maintained, and spacious, with rolling green lawns ideal for a picnic, reading a book, or simply relaxing while enjoying the view. it’s elevated enough to offer breezes and sweeping views, and there are several benches strategically placed for you to take it all in. i noticed a good mix of both locals and tourists, and the atmosphere was friendly and peaceful. there’s a dedicated off-leash dog area, which adds a lively charm to the park without being disruptive. for those who enjoy walking, the surrounding neighborhood is a treasure trove of beautifully preserved victorian architecture. every corner reveals a house more picturesque than the last. despite its popularity, the park doesn’t feel overcrowded. it’s a refreshing green space in the middle of the city with cultural, architectural, and visual appeal. whether you're a photographer, a casual visitor, or just someone looking to unwind, alamo square park delivers a memorable san francisco experience. a must-visit, especially for first-timers to the city.

a perfect example of how social economy is implemented into an urbanised and historical athenian neighbourhood. social services, marketplaces, educational courses, community events all rolled in one. children and family friendly atmosphere, municipal market is here to stay and thrive.

a perfect family outing last weekend, my partner, our little one, and i set out for a leisurely stroll along the cronulla beach walk—and it couldn’t have been lovelier. here’s why it’s our new favourite family adventure. from the moment we began at north cronulla, the wide, smooth promenade made pushing our pram effortless. there are gentle inclines, clear distance markers, and plenty of room to chat side-by-side without worrying about uneven ground. halfway along, we paused at a patrolled section of sand where lifeguards keep watch in peak season. we dipped our toes while our baby splashed happily in the shallow water—perfect for peace of mind and sandy giggles. with a babe in tow, it helps to have options: we found shaded benches overlooking the surf, public showers to rinse off, and clean restrooms just steps from the sand. it made nappy changes and snack breaks a breeze. my partner and i treated ourselves to takeaway flat whites and açai bowls at a beachfront café. they wrapped everything up neatly so we could sip and stroll—our little one even snuck a bite of banana puree between sips! further along the walk is a lovely playground nestled among norfolk pines. we parked the pram, let our baby explore the swings, and enjoyed a picnic on the nearby grass—complete with barbecues and dappled shade. watching the foamy waves roll in, hearing our baby’s delighted coos, and feeling the salt breeze together—it was the perfect way to reconnect as a family outside the usual routine. whether you’re with little ones, toddlers, or grown-ups only, the cronulla beach walk delivers: it’s safe, beautiful, and packed with conveniences for families. if you’re after a stress-free, picturesque outing with your partner and baby, this is the spot to make those sunny weekend memories! ps there was a sausage stall with chiken sausage! i am still finding there page . but cant find them they have theeee maizing fooood ! it was oktoberfest something bit too good !!

a perfect hiking trail, that is not very difficult to climb, somewhere between easy to moderate however there are some parts that require a lot of climbing, and usage of ladders and chains to climb which might be challenging for others. the trail offers a breathtaking view of the city, the ocean, table mountain as well as the robben island (though it’s quite far). safety is not much of a concern, especially when coming in the morning as there’s a lot of people and groups doing the hike. parking is available at the starting point, though it is limited. i do not recommend doing the trail when it is raining or wet, as the rocks become very slippery. but in overall: a 10/10 hiking trail.

a perfect oasis: garden pod exceeds expectations! i am absolutely thrilled with the garden pod, and it truly deserves a glowing five-star review! from the moment we arrived, i was impressed by its outstanding container design. it's not just a structure; it's a beautifully crafted piece that seamlessly blends into gardens by the bay and marina bay sands. the design philosophy is clearly minimalistic, and it's executed flawlessly. every element feels intentional and serves a purpose, contributing to a clean, uncluttered aesthetic that is both calming and modern. it's proof that less truly can be more. inside, the pod continues to impress. the great kitchen island feature is an absolute game-changer. it provides ample workspace, a perfect spot for a morning coffee, or a convenient area for entertaining. it's robust, well-integrated, and incredibly versatile. what truly sets this garden pod apart is how complete it is with stuff. it felt like a truly turn-key solution. every essential was thought of, from clever storage solutions to integrated lighting. there was no need for me to scramble for additional items; everything i needed was already there, testament to thoughtful planning by the designers. and finally, the convertible sofa beds are pure genius! it's incredibly comfortable as a sofa during the day, perfect for lounging with a book or enjoying the garden view. then, with minimal effort, it transforms into a cozy bed, making the pod an ideal guest room or a peaceful retreat for an afternoon nap. overall, this garden pod is a triumph of design and functionality. it's a serene, stylish, and incredibly practical addition to my home, and i wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone seeking a high-quality, versatile outdoor living space.

a princípio, tivemos uma pequena chateação no erro da pousada. nos direcionaram para uma pousada mal localizada, com muitos pernilongos e distante do centro. tivemos esse desgaste logo na chegada em noronha, mas depois do mal entendido, pagaram nosso táxi para a pousada correta e ficamos muito próximo do centro. eu fazia tudo a pé. os passeios foram sensacionais. até o ilha tour que poderia ser totalmente frustrante por conta da chuva, o guia bruno foi sensacional, numa resenha boa do início ao fim. outro guia sensacional foi o davi. extremamente paciente, educado, gente boa... em resumo, se não fosse a chateação de início, eu daria 5 estrelas, mas de resto, foi tudo perfeito. obs: bruno e davi fizeram umas fotos sensacionais. salvaram os registros hehe. cada captura... quem disse que guia apenas leva para o lugar? sem contar que os caras possuem um conhecimento gigante de cada parte da cidade no que concerne a história. repertório cultural gigantesco.

a professional dive center. sandi and maria manage the dive center owned by the local people who run the same homestay. they only allow experienced divemaster who knows the area really well to guide the dive. so you're safe diving with them. however, remember to stay within your limit. the dive sites include mioskon, blue magic, chicken reefs, cape kri, and the surrounding areas. for the morning dives, the boat departs to the dive site at 8 morning. they can also pick you up at your homestay. after the first dive, we take a break in nearby island, having tea/coffee and some fruits. then you can either opt out or join the 2nd dive and return at noon. for afternoon dive, the boat departs at 2.30 pm. they also run one-day trips and diving in farther area, e.g. piaynemo. the price is for one boat, divided by up to 5 people.

a profound journey through vietnam’s history visiting hoa lo prison was a deeply moving experience. the museum offers a stark and powerful glimpse into vietnam’s turbulent past, from its days under french colonial rule to the vietnam war. walking through the preserved cells and exhibits, i was struck by the resilience and courage of those who endured unimaginable hardships within these walls. the displays are informative and thought-provoking, providing insight into the struggles for independence and the complexities of war. it’s a sobering reminder of the cost of freedom and the strength of the human spirit. a must-visit for anyone seeking to understand vietnam’s rich and challenging history.
a properly controlled hiking trail, spectacular views and easy walking

a property still in private ownership, free for members of the historic houses association. the castle is beautiful, from the outside and inside. the grounds are a masterpiece, all maintained by a team of four full-time gardeners. what a joy this place is. staff were lovely. cafe, shop, clean toilets, large carpark within easy walk. all perfect.

a public park in the middle of the red city, you can take some time to breathe the fresh air and get away from the noise .. the place is very quiet, a piece of tranquility .. suitable for children to discover the sounds of birds that shape them ..

a quaint store front, easy to miss but worth a visit. i went in to buy a wallet, card holder, and passport holder. the options are great, and they have so many colors. the leather felt soft, and the workmanship was there to see. the designs are more on the conservative side but that is exactly what i wanted. have a look, as this is a gem next to all the mass produced options nearby

a quick disclaimer, i have not really watched or read moomin. the place is surprisingly large, the museum is based in a lighthouse i assume moomins house. in addition within that there is another lighthouse you can go in that has multiple floors. the place is full of moomin comic snippets, life size characters along with other art and history about the author. the cafe is huge! the staff are really friendly and the drinks are really quirky. this was a nice laid back day to the holiday. it didn't take us all day to get around but i'm sure you could spend a whole day here.

a quiet and peaceful museum showcasing works from egyptian artists of the past 100–200 years. while exploring the exhibits, you can escape the chaos and intensity of cairo for a while. definitely worth a visit. the entrance fee for foreigners is only around 20 egp, which is quite reasonable.

a quiet gem in the heart of the old town – dubrovnik cathedral the cathedral of the assumption of the virgin mary, often simply referred to as the dubrovnik cathedral, is a beautiful slice of serenity tucked within the city’s bustling old town. while it might not shout for attention the way some european cathedrals do, it rewards those who take the time to step inside with elegance, history, and a cool moment of calm away from the summer crowds. from the outside, the cathedral is graceful and restrained, with baroque curves and a stately dome that peeks above the city’s rooftops. step through the doors, though, and you’re met with a bright, airy interior filled with soft light, marble columns, and gilded details that speak of centuries of devotion and careful craftsmanship. one of the highlights is the cathedral’s treasury, which holds an impressive collection of relics — including (according to tradition) a fragment of the true cross and relics of st. blaise, dubrovnik’s beloved patron saint. even if you're not religious, the artistry and historical significance here are captivating. the altar painting by titian, depicting the assumption of the virgin, adds another layer of artistic prestige to the space. it's a reminder of dubrovnik’s cultural connections and its long-standing importance as a crossroads of east and west. things to know: entry is free, but a small donation is encouraged if you visit the treasury. photography is allowed (no flash), but it’s a place of worship, so be respectful. great spot to cool off and reflect while exploring the old town.

a real fun and yet pretty easy hike. the views along the trail of the surrounding red rocks were simply amazing. the highlight, of course, was the caves themselves. the trail itself had graduate changes in elevation, until the last 10 minute where some steep steps were required to reach the caves. we took the wrong fork where soldier pass trail and soldier pass cave trail separated (see my last photo for clarification). it was a blast to check out the caves even for a senior citizen. by the way, the trail passes through the 7 sacred pools, but they were on the dry side. there were several jeeps that came on to the trail, but only up to 7 sacred pools. after that, only hikers, no jeeps nor mountain bikers. parking can be difficult and shuttles didn’t operate when we visited. though if you wait around, a space will become available as hikers were constantly arriving and leaving.

a really stunning building in the downtown area. definitely one of the best place to view the city from above. tickets booking opens 2 weeks prior to my date. smooth booking process, and you verify the booking at the receptionist's by showing them the email. we came 30 mins after the booking hour (due to heavy rain in the morning) but still gained our access. it's completely free to enjoy 2 different gardens. one in the upper level (the 51st floor) with outdoor garden planting many familiar family trees. and this is the best view you can have. the other is on the level 18-20 with more trees. on the day we arrived, level 19-20 were under maintenance, so we can only visit level 18 and 51. highly recommend everybody to go to this place if you're on a budget.

a really unique little machine i came across near the shrine. for just 100 yen, you can watch a tiny mechanical shrine scene with lanterns, a torii gate, and even movement. it feels nostalgic and charming, like a mix of tradition and old-school entertainment. worth trying if you want a fun and unusual cultural experience while walking around

a relaxing lagoon that we visited duting our tour. it has a picturesque view that visitors will definitely enjoy and relax. while visiting this place, a boat will be provided which can carry up to two people. the natural view is amazing which is not common in other places. the waters are calm and the weather is not too hot because of the large rocks surrounding the lagoon. tour guides are also helpful when visiting the place as they can take photos or even help with moving the boat to the other lagoon.

a relaxing, beautiful way to explore cairo! the nile cruise was smooth and peaceful, with amazing views all around. i was surprised at how quiet and relaxing it felt. the guide was friendly and made history come alive. meals were fresh and full of flavor, served with care. i loved seeing the birds flying over the water—it added magic to the journey. it’s the kind of experience that makes you slow down and really enjoy the moment. great for couples or

a scenic hiking trail leaves from the picnic area and provides great views into yellowstone river canyon. the trail begins with a steep ascent from the picnic area, but after about 200 feet of elevation gain the trail levels off and follows the river upstream (southeast). you cannot access the river from the trail (if you want to access the river, hike down to the bridge near the picnic area, or take the trail from canyon falls). watch your step along the trail because it is a very steep drop into the canyon below, and i would not bring small children on the trail for safety reasons. it's an out-and-back hike, about 1.5 miles one way (3 miles round trip). along the way, you can see people on the other side of the river at some of the scenic turnouts near canyon falls. there's not much shade, so on a sunny day, consider using sunscreen. enjoy!

a scenic tour along siene river of paris. prepare your cameras and make sure your batteries are fully charged. capturing the memories and mesmerising building structures are the shots you would remember and make you say ... i've been there. as you enter the cruising ship. go up and turn right to get into the front side for a perfect view. tickets are required.

a sculpture that pays homage to the citrus orchards of jaffa, home to the famous "jaffa oranges". an interesting piece of art, incorporating a real tree suspended between the adjustment buildings. definitely a stop for a photoshoot during a day trip to jaffa.

a serene and spiritual escape in the heart of the city. 🏮stunning architecture with rich colors and intricate details.known for its “what you request is what you get” belief. loved watching locals perform traditional fortune telling. peaceful gardens and quiet corners to pause and reflect. a cultural and spiritual must-visit in hong kong!

a serene and welcoming experience this place is an absolute must-visit—even if you're not religious, the sense of peace you feel upon entering is truly remarkable. it’s spacious and never feels overcrowded, which adds to the tranquil atmosphere. the entire facility is exceptionally clean, and i was impressed by how well it accommodates wheelchair users. the staff were incredibly friendly and polite, making the experience all the more pleasant. i highly recommend booking your visit online in advance to ensure smooth and easy entry. 🚫 _note:_ shorts and short sleeves are not permitted, so be sure to dress appropriately out of respect for the guidelines

a serene and well-maintained park. the beauty of the place is evident from the moment you enter. it's filled with pavilions displaying a variety of plants, allowing you to appreciate nature and its beauty. the park offers opportunities for relaxation and other moments of serenity and peace.

a serene escape just minutes from downtown banff, vermilion lakes viewpoint offers breathtaking reflections of mount rundle and the surrounding peaks. this picturesque spot is perfect for wildlife viewing, photography, and enjoying stunning sunsets over the tranquil waters. easily accessible by car, bike, or a short walk, it’s a must-visit for those looking to experience the natural beauty of banff in a peaceful setting.
a serene, beautiful forest area. there are squirrels around but i didn't see any other small animals. there's a convenient boardwalk trail so you won't get your shoes muddy.

a shaded park for an escape from the heat. it is the last remaining element of the gothic church saint-jacques-de-la-boucherie. the church was the patron of the butchers, that were in the area. after all, the market les halles is just around the corner. but even though the original church was built in the 12th century, tour saint-jacques as we know it today was built only between 1509 and 1523. the 52 meters high tower served as a bell tower for the church, and stood as a significant stop for pilgrims on the camino de santiago (way of st. james). the church itself was demolished during the french revolution, leaving just the tower behind. over the centuries, the tower has taken on new roles. for example, functioning as a weather observatory in the 19th century before being classified as a unesco world heritage site in 1998

a shopaholic’s dream in bangkok! visited pratunam morning market early in the day—one of bangkok’s busiest and most vibrant wholesale hubs. i arrived around 6 am, and the energy was amazing: freshest clothes, unbeatable prices, and a bustling local atmosphere ￼. ✅ great bargains – many stalls require buying 3+ items for wholesale rates (50–250 thb each) ￼. ✅ variety – wide range of clothing, accessories, and souvenirs in a mix of outdoor alleys and nearby air‑con retail areas ￼. ✅ fun vibe – locals and tourists bartering, the aroma of thai street food in the air, plus foot‑massage stalls to relax after browsing ￼. only caution: watch your belongings in the crowds—some reviewers have had bags pick‑pocketed . bottom line: if you love fashion and don’t mind the early start (and hustle), this place is a must-visit.
a shopping passage, (hands-on)-art gallery, the upside down museum and much much more can be found here. great place to spend some unplanned time. indoor and outdoor.
a shopping passage, (hands-on)-art gallery, the upside down museum and much much more can be found here. great place to spend some unplanned time. indoor and outdoor.

a short 30 minute hike up for some beautiful views of the island and mount halla. the hike itself is more steep at the beginning and about 10 minutes in they have built walkways to make it easier to climb up. the hike does start to get a bit flatter and easier. once at the top there are some incredible views and also an opportunity to go into the japanese tunnel where the soldiers used to be placed. it is very dark in there so be mindful of your step. on the way down is the same 30 minutes but do have to watch where you are walking especially once you get off the walkway. it can be slippery if it has rained. would recommend trainers at least. absolutely work the hike!
a short and beautiful walk up the hill for a 360 view of the island

a short drive from cape town, the park is an absolute must to visit not because of its fame but because of its beauty. you can see wild animals, both marine and land, roaming free, and the famous light houses are built in a castle like setting the offers good exercise with the reward of stunning views.

a short gondola ride from wengen (14.50 chf with a 50% mountain pass) there’s a short but steep walk to the top, but the panoramic view is absolutely stunning. one of the best views i have seen. there are also playgrounds and restaurants nearby, making it a great spot for families and anyone who wants to enjoy the scenery.

a short gradual uphill hike on trail from roadside to a series of falls. had a great time getting into the water under falls in two different places. on a very rainy day the trail was slippery in spots and river water was not clear. highly recommend nonslip water shoes to walk on trail and river rocks.

a short intermediate hike with amazing view of the other side of bow falls. i said intermediate because its easy at first due to steep decent but you got to climb it all back up and kids had a bit of hard time. about 150m elevation gained on way back up but its totally worth it for the view. there is a tiny beach at the very bottom but beaware of rocks and watch your step. parking can be very limited on a busy day there is another lot on east side but its a bit of walk. no washroom though so be prepared. over all highly recommended. follow for more.
a short, free hike with lots of wind. the trail begins on a small road, then you arrive at an area with benches where you can enjoy the view.

a shrine dedicated to the god of sake. a few minutes walk from the train station, this is a small complex of buildings, including a sake museum just before the entrance. everything is beautifully maintained. it strikes me as a very active and community minded shrine, celebrating and commemorating many local occasions. it doesn't officially open until 9:00am, but i was able to just walk in at 8:00, when it was cool and although busy with workers, there were no other visitors. i particularly enjoyed the garden, with a stream running through it. it was a peaceful place, despite being so close to the station and a busy intersection.
a simple and beautiful antique market to stroll through.

a simply stunning location in the highlands. if you go in the autumn prepare for all weather. we had rain one minute, bright sun the next! you'll get wet crossing streams so wear wellies or waterproof walking boots. from the loch affric circuit car park, walk anti-clockwise around the loch to do the full loop. the first section is along a private road, however, walkers can use it as it then leads onto the unpaved walking path. expect to walk for a good 5 to 6 hours to complete the circuit, depending on how many pictures you stop to take of the first class scenery.
a simply wonderful place 🤩🤩🤩 inherited over time by the incas 😁, where you can see on the horizon the majesty of lake titicaca, inca thunuhuiri ✌
a site with a wide variety of activities for all ages, with very high quality and excellent service.

a slice of paris, in the heart of cairo.❤️🇪🇬 i was surprised with its old architecture buildings, wide streets and classic elegance. there's a timeless feel to it, like you stepped into a different era, and it's giving an old paris vibes! i'm really glad the hostel i rented was nearby! i enjoyed walking around! definitely one of my favorite spots in the city!
a slightly challenging climb for those who aren’t fit but the views are worth the effort and the gorgeous little beach is the perfect spot for a refreshing cool down.

a slow-moving river of grass, the everglades teem with wildlife—alligators, manatees, and birds. explore by airboat, kayak, or walking trails like anhinga trail (0.8 mi). bike the shark valley loop (15 mi) for panoramic views from the observation tower. a highly recommended way to see the park is the airboat tour, which gets you deep into the wetlands for incredible wildlife sightings. winter is ideal—dry, cool, and mosquito-free. the landscape is subtle but captivating, shaped by water, time, and countless creatures.

a small and peaceful ancient temple that’s located next to a school and orphanage. it’s very old and doesn’t require an angkor wat ticket to enter. there is a newer monastery nearby where monks stay. it’s very nice if you would like to pray quietly. sometimes there’s motorcycle traffic around the area. we were also approached by one of the english teachers at the school and donated some money to the orphanage. not a must-visit destination if you are here for sightseeing. but if you would like to pray and make some offerings it’s very good.
a small and peaceful park. it's good for short jog or walk. experience climbing up and down its steps tp get good exercise. i went during a weekday and came across only few people.
a small but authentic german square or platz. the biggest impression is left by the charming old building with the wonderful clock.
a small but beautiful japanese garden in vienna (19th district). peaceful atmosphere, lovely design, and perfect for a quiet walk or a moment to relax. definitely worth a visit!
a small but beautifully kept shrine dedicated to one of the most important onmyōji - abe no seimei. we took the bus here from nijo castle. this shrine is also close to the kyoto imperial palace.

a small but cozy place for a enjoyable coffee break! i had a cappuccino which was very soft and well steamed. the home-made chocolate cake was very delicious too with a deep chocolate flavour and tasted fudgy and moist. the ambience is very relaxing and the owner super friendly :) highly recommend!

a small but great dive shop with sweet and engaged staff, high level of security and a lot of nice dive spots. i’ve been to mauritius twice and done 26 dives with this shop and i’ve felt more than welcome every time. i’d recommend them to anyone! miss you guys ❤️

a small but interesting temple that houses both taoist and buddhist deities under one roof. it’s a unique blend of traditions and worth a visit if you're in the area. do remember to remove your shoes before entering the main temple as a sign of respect. photography is allowed, but be mindful and respectful when taking pictures. overall, a peaceful place with cultural significance, great for those interested in spiritual sites.

a small but nice green space that connects to the bigger arbraska chauveau area where they do zip lining. too bad these little parks along this road don’t have a better view of the little creek/river. it would make for some very cool vantage points. 😎
a small but sweet park in rome. the walk up is t worth the sweat. we went in spring so the smell of orange flowers was in the air.
a small but very interesting theatre with ocassionally modern plays or performance shows. good surround sound and lighting system

a small dome on the mount of olives, we had to wait in line for some minutes while other groups went inside. once inside, it took just a minute or two to see and pray there, so it was a fast visit. it was a little cramped inside, we were a group of 50. definitely a must-do on a holy land tour!

a small food hall with delicious home cooked thai food. many different options of food. we tried the chinese noodles as well as rice plate with curry, fried fish, fried chicken, and vegetables. all were fresh and excellent. there is even a drink stand where you can buy thai tea, chrysanthemum tea, and thai coffee. extremely affordable as well. 50-100 baht per dish. there are fans so there are minimal bugs however there is no ac so can be a little hot and humid inside. still worth the visit.

a small garden behind the library with a decent variety of flowers and fountain/buildings to see. occasionally there will be photoshoots in the background, so may need to squeeze by while there is only one main loop, there are many subtle paths stemming out- usually to a bench.
a small garden with outdoor modern sculptures along the seine and near the zoo with lots of seating and a small playground for toddlers. nice break from the hectic and busy city.

a small gem of a museum that is not as well known as others. the architecture of the place is remarkable, but we also enjoyed the exhibits. some rooms are dedicated to special exhibits. when we visited, in 2023, they had an amazing one on the night life in "old" cdmx (la noche nos pertenece) which was absolutely fascinating. one of those places that is worth visiting and revisiting once in a while to see what is new. highly recommended.

a small little museum with lots to get you thinking. i really enjoyed reading about the works of art, my faves were the yoko one chess set and the fish aquarium on the 4th floor. doesn’t take long to go through, but you can take as long as you want as they have little camp stools you can use to sit and take in the art. lovely little museum shop with gorgeous cards and postcards.

a small, ennobled temple, is located in the old city, near the school building - mongkol nimit. despite the fact that the territory is not the largest, there are enough interesting and beautiful buildings here. one of them is a chedi (stupa) - you don't often see this structure because it contains a piece of buddha's ashes or a famous monk is buried there - one of them is located here! this is a very beautiful and majestic building - you can take unusual photos against its background. closer to the school building there is a small wooden building with beautiful statues of buddha, opposite which there is a building where a practicing monk receives people, to whom they come to fulfill their wishes and other worldly requests. full information with video and easy navigation - in the 👉 phuketon application

a small-scale museum in the wealthy area in tokyo (omotesando）. architectural style of the main building is modern japanese. the breath of exhibition is small which there are only dozens of exhibits in each room. the outdoor garden is beautiful and i consider it more exciting than the indoor exhibition.

a smaller museum but very well done. loads of information, well laid out, and had an interesting exhibit on ginger meggs!! great little museum about some of sydney's history. it's very professional looking and obviously well-maintained. there's a cool scale model display of the first fleet ships that brought the first european settlers to australia.
