a special and unique museum. it may be small but it packs in a range of exhibits, love tokens, photographs, personal stories from film stars, writers and people like me. you can't help but feel the warmth that the museum creators intended. at the end of our visit my partner sang some classic love songs to the museum owner. it was a wonderful moment in our holiday. love really does make the world go round!

a special mother-daughter escape in tomamu hokkaido i recently spent six days at club med in tomamu hokkaido with my 14-year-old daughter, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable trips we’ve ever taken together. the resort is beautifully located — surrounded by peaceful snow-covered forests and gentle slopes. from the moment we arrived, there was a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. everything was well-organized, which made it easy to just settle in and enjoy our time without stress. my daughter loved the ski school. the instructors were kind, patient, and really good at building confidence. as a parent, seeing her enjoy that freedom (in such a safe environment) was incredibly rewarding. the food deserves a mention too — fresh, varied, and surprisingly excellent for an all-inclusive setting. we tried everything from japanese to international comfort foods, and dinner always felt like an event. we also enjoyed the little tea breaks with hot chocolate after skiing — small moments, but so special. what i appreciated most was how easy it was to spend quality time together. we joined a few activities, watched the evening shows, and even just enjoyed quiet chats in the lounge after a long day outdoors. no schedules, no pressure — just connection. for any parent traveling with a teenager, this place strikes a really nice balance: they can be independent, have fun, and explore — while you still get to enjoy time together in a truly beautiful setting. we left feeling refreshed and a bit closer to each other — and that, to me, is the sign of a great trip.

a special occasion let down by disappointing extras my partner and i spent months saving for the shark dive xtreme at sea life sydney. this wasn’t a casual outing—it was a carefully planned anniversary experience. we spent close to $1000, including $200 for the photography/videography package, to make it truly memorable. while the core dive was fantastic, the media package and lack of personal touches left us disappointed—especially given how much this experience meant to us. ✅ the positives: the pre-dive briefing was friendly and informative, covering safety, diving basics, and facts about the marine life. during the dive, the instructors were professional, ensuring safety and pointing out different shark species. being underwater with these creatures was unforgettable. ❌ where it fell short: 1) the media package ($200) this was the biggest letdown—especially for a special occasion. there was no effort to capture us together until my partner had to firmly request a couple photo as we were being asked to exit. without that, we’d have no decent shot marking our anniversary. the footage felt rushed, repetitive, and poorly framed—despite only 3 participants (2 experienced divers). no guidance on posing, no communication about filming, and no attention to details like removing hoods for better photos. the final content looked nothing like sea life’s polished promotional images. for $200, it felt like a tick-the-box task, not a service designed to capture meaningful memories. for context, i’ve attached a short video example—just as i looked up and engaged with the shark, the videographer held the shot for barely two seconds before panning away to film a nearby wobbegong shark. instead of capturing what could’ve been a great moment, the focus quickly shifted away. it’s a small example, but it reflects how little attention was placed on the guests in a package meant to capture our experience. with personal cameras prohibited, we expected better care. sadly, the poor media quality overshadowed what should have been a highlight. 2) a missed opportunity for a thoughtful gesture before the dive, instructors showed us shark teeth they’d found that morning. as we were part of the first session (with up to three daily), it was clear this wasn’t uncommon. my partner was excited by the idea of finding one, and when we asked if guests could keep any, they said yes. we weren’t expecting a keepsake and were content without one—until we saw how disappointing the media package was. only then did we reflect that offering one of the three teeth found that morning could’ve softened the experience and made it feel more personal. for staff, these moments are routine. for us, this was a once-in-a-lifetime experience we’d saved for. small gestures like that can make a huge difference when other areas fall short. it’s not about expecting extras—it’s about recognising simple ways to turn a transactional experience into a memorable one. final thoughts & suggestion: • the dive itself was fantastic—safe, exciting, and well-run. • the media package lacked care and didn’t match the premium price. • the experience felt procedural, missing opportunities to make guests feel valued—especially when celebrating something special. suggestion for sea life sydney: you deliver a great core experience, but focusing more on guest care—whether through consistent, thoughtful photography or small gestures—would elevate this significantly. when guests mention a special occasion, a little extra attention leaves a lasting impression. for future guests: the dive is worth it for the thrill, but be cautious about paying extra for photos/videos—unless improvements are made.

a special treat for a special person, my wife. the waiters were friendly everyone enjoyed a fantastic cruise taking in paris on the water. this has to be a must for us next time we visit. we had a fantastic voyage and wondered at all the senary en route. a massive thank you to all the friendly staff. merci

a spectacular delight for nature lovers. any number of days are not enough. spring time is the best season. do your research and make your bookings long in advance to avoid last minute disappointment. you will carry home memories to last a lifetime.

a spectacular journey: mount batur sunrise trekking review i recently embarked on the mount batur sunrise trekking adventure, and it was an experience that exceeded all expectations. from the moment we began our ascent to the breathtaking summit our guide was very professional and took us through the route in an impressive manner . our guide was not only knowledgeable but also incredibly personable. he provided insightful commentary along the way, sharing fascinating tidbits about the local flora and fauna, as well as the history and significance of mount batur itself. his expertise ensured a safe and enjoyable journey for all participants. as we reached the summit just in time for sunrise, the panoramic view that greeted us was nothing short of awe-inspiring. the vibrant hues of the sky painted a mesmerizing backdrop against the silhouette of neighboring peaks, while the tranquil lake batur shimmered below. thanks to google maps, we were able to identify key landmarks and points of interest, enhancing our appreciation of the surrounding beauty. overall, the combination of reliable navigation and the expertise of our guide made for an unforgettable adventure on mount batur. i highly recommend this experience to anyone seeking an exhilarating outdoor excursion.

a splendid experience in my lifetime. we got there at around 9 a.m. the monks were chanting their morning prayer but still they waved their head and allow us to enter. it is a very monastery with an eye catching view with a very soothing and peaceful atmosphere. we enjoyed a very special herbal tea in their world's oldest kitchen.

a spooky and theatrical dive into london’s dark past. the actors are incredible, and the sets are well-designed. it’s a mix of history and horror with a bit of humor thrown in. not for the faint of heart—but definitely entertaining!

a sprawling complex carved into the slope of the capitoline hill, once teeming with senatorial offices, state archives, and maybe even shops — an ancient combo of commerce and bureaucracy. built under emperor trajan around 100 ad, it’s now a museum offering interactive exhibits, multi-level views of the forum, and basement chambers filled with thousands of amphorae. 😄 contrary to the name, it was probably more government hub than market, but “mercati” stuck. entry costs a modest fee and the terrace views of the imperial fora are postcard-level stunning. if you're tired of the colosseum crowd, this place offers breathing space and fewer selfie sticks.

a spread out vast area with vista of the city, numerous water features and artworks. unfortunately the sustainability museum was closed, as part of the gardens by the bay setup. an easy walk around without the massive crowd.

a square filled with history — and a quiet echo of eternity. piazza san marco is one of the most breathtaking places in venice. surrounded by majestic buildings, the famous basilica, and the sound of bells and footsteps, it’s a space where time seems to pause. every stone speaks of beauty, culture, and reverence. and yet beyond the art, the arches, and the golden mosaics of st. mark’s basilica, there is something deeper: a longing for the eternal. a longing that no monument, however grand, can fully satisfy — because our hearts were made for more. “lord, you have been our dwelling place throughout all generations.” (psalm 90:1) the square may belong to history, but our lives belong to him — the one who reigns above time, above kings, above cathedrals. in the quiet of this square, we are reminded: god is not far — he is near. in the stillness. in the grandeur. in the soul that looks up. may every square become a place of praise. and may the glory of god shine brighter than gold, even in the heart of venice.

a step back in time at havana theatre visiting the havana theatre in cuba is like stepping into a time machine that whisks you back to the golden age of cinema and performance. the theatre itself, an architectural masterpiece, exudes old-world charm with its ornate façade and grand interiors, a testament to cuba’s rich artistic heritage. but the magic isn’t just inside—the scene outside is equally mesmerizing. a parade of vintage, candy-colored classic cars lines the streets, their gleaming exteriors reflecting the vibrant energy of havana. these rolling relics from the 1950s make you feel as if you’ve slipped into a bygone era, where glamour and nostalgia coexist in perfect harmony. the fusion of historic elegance and living history creates an atmosphere unlike anywhere else in the world. whether you come for a show, a glimpse of havana’s cultural soul, or simply to soak in the mesmerizing spectacle of time standing still, the havana theatre is an experience that lingers long after you leave.

a stunning 15 century hammam turned museum… unfortunately not operational but for $2 it’s worth the quick walkthrough to take photos of this marvelous place.

a stunning ancient amphitheatre located just beneath the acropolis, which makes it truly one of a kind. i’ve been twice and both times were great experiences. the atmosphere is magical, especially as night falls and the stage lights up. however, the stone seating is extremely uncomfortable—after two hours or more it becomes quite hard to enjoy the show fully. still, i’d definitely recommend the experience; it’s absolutely worth it.
a stunning architectural masterpiece in muscat, offering a peaceful escape from the chaos of city life. its serene atmosphere and intricate design make it a truly calming✨

a stunning architecture calls you to explore this gift from carlos slim to cdmx. free admission and even open on mondays contrary to the norm with the city museums. it is a corner full of excitement, traffic, people and multiple things to do. i explored its five levels at leisure and ended at the gift store for some memorabilia. it's a visual pleasure that honors mr. slim's late wife. regardless of your personal preferences i do consider it to be a must stop while in this fascinating city that never stops giving us pleasures. if you stop by the restroom...it's a work of art on its own!

a stunning cathedral. rio de janeiro’s saint sebastian cathedral is an impressive modern building in downtown rio. it is dedicated to the saint sebastian, who has some statues on the inside. the whole structure is an awesome testament by edgar de oliveira da fonseca to ancient mayan pyramids. the coloured windows are fantastic. the massive building’s clear structure inspires humility and introspection.

a stunning collection of modern artistic ceramic. many moving and inspiring pieces. quiet setting in lovely peaceful house in 18th century style. like many smaller museums and galleries in havana a helpful guided tour is provided for tip. a memorable and worthwhile experience for anyone who appreciates modern art.

a stunning experience – must visit in dubai! dubai frame is truly a breathtaking attraction that offers one of the best panoramic views of the city. i highly recommend planning your visit around sunset, so you can enjoy both daylight and nighttime views — it adds a magical golden touch to everything and makes the experience even more memorable. the entry and exit points are on different sides, so don’t rush to take the elevator up right away. take your time to explore the exhibition and historical gallery on the ground floor, which beautifully showcases dubai’s past, present, and future through interactive displays. once you reach the top, the skywalk glass floor is just wow! walking on it while looking down is thrilling, and the 360-degree view of the dubai skyline is absolutely stunning — especially at night when the city lights up. you can also pick up some nice souvenirs from the top, which is a thoughtful touch for visitors. the ticket price is aed 52, but i booked through platinumlist for aed 46, which was easy and convenient. the correct entrance is through zabeel park gate 4, and it's accessible from both adcb and max metro stations — very convenient for public transport users. overall, an unforgettable experience and highly recommended for both tourists and residents. a perfect blend of architecture, culture, and amazing views!

a stunning garden outside of the hustle and bustle of marrakech centre. the garden is beautiful. it's full of amazing plants, vistas and colours. i really recommend you see this if you're in marrakech. it's around an hour walk from the centre. pre-book your tickets and be prepared to wait in line outside!

a stunning garden outside of the hustle and bustle of marrakech centre. the garden is beautiful. it's full of amazing plants, vistas and colours. i really recommend you see this if you're in marrakech. it's around an hour walk from the centre. pre-book your tickets and be prepared to wait in line outside!

a stunning house typical of the american colonial style and with a lot of family history. there's almost no reference to the life of the slaves upon whose backs the money was made.....maybe that reflects the fact that the family still live and work here. either way it's a sad omission in an otherwise impressive place

a stunning location with incredible historical depth. the museum is beautifully maintained, and walking through the ruins at night adds a special atmosphere. the lighting outside highlights the ancient structure perfectly, making it feel almost surreal. it’s a peaceful place to explore, even more so after dark. highly recommended for anyone interested in roman history or architecture.

a stunning monastery located in the castle district of prague. the cost to enter is about $11 usd per person, but it is worth it. amazing beauty. the courtyard is stunning with beautiful painted ceilings all the hallways that lead around the courtyard. the church in the monastery is beyond words. amazing decoration, paintings, and statues. the loreta monastery is a must see when visiting prague. we loved our visit.

a stunning monastery located in the castle district of prague. the cost to enter is about $11 usd per person, but it is worth it. amazing beauty. the courtyard is stunning with beautiful painted ceilings all the hallways that lead around the courtyard. the church in the monastery is beyond words. amazing decoration, paintings, and statues. the loreta monastery is a must see when visiting prague. we loved our visit.

a stunning mosque with great architecture in the capital city of oman is here. humbling people to the greatest god (allah) can be found in this mosque. it's not only a must place for muslim but other believers are also welcome.

a stunning mosque with sunni imams. the mosque is clean and beautiful and large. taraweeh here was a really beautiful experience. although after everything two rakats somebody at the front was reciting something. they did it without a microphone and i'm not sure who it was or what they were doing or if this is an innovation or not but perhaps mentioning it someone will be familiar with the practice more than i.

a stunning museum that fully reveals the world of van gogh. i recommend wearing headphones to completely immerse yourself in his world… the only drawback is that at some point, i noticed that there were really too many visitors... perhaps the management should limit the number of visitors...

a stunning natural formation located on the wonderful and mysterious volcanic island of jeju. after descending from the central volcano, we taxied through the soft and idyllic jeju countryside to this unesco park. the tickets were incredibly cheap and we were fortunate enough to claim the last ones of the day. the underground tube plunges quick into the earth. the stairs you start out on soon end, and the decline levels off into a flat, wet, and cold surface of black basalt. within the earth is an amazing place to be. the artificial lights are spectral, shining in pools of water gathered in the wrinkles of the hardened lava floor. there's very little to complain about here and the sights are unforgettable. a trip to jeju is not complete without a descent through this prehistoric tube into the earth. 5/5. would descend again.

a stunning park full of history. we visited the park of the aqueducts as we wanted to see not only the aqueducts but also the filming locations for the grande bellezza and ripley. i am also a huge roman history buff so wanted to see these incredible structures up close! the park is not only full of history but also very peaceful and pretty. it is popular with runners and dog walkers. we visited on a cold but bright february day. i can imagine in the summer it is a great place for a picnic. it’s on the outskirts of central rome but well worth the visit.

a stunning park that i feel fortunate to have come across in central marrakech. it's an oasis, the trees are beautifully clipped and shaped, the shade is delightful and it has a calm peaceful atmosphere. the red pathways also make a pretty colour contrast to all the lush greenery. a must visit.

a stunning place to visit. just a few minutes walk from the train station, and you are in breath-taking scenery. there are lots of different walking trails. dotted around the loch, there are children's play areas. there is also a castle and walled garden that you can explore. the nearest toilets are at the castle. there were picnic tables. there are hard surface paths around the loch. these are wheelchair accessible. dog walking off lead is allowed.

a stunning place to visit. just a few minutes walk from the train station, and you are in breath-taking scenery. there are lots of different walking trails. dotted around the loch, there are children's play areas. there is also a castle and walled garden that you can explore. the nearest toilets are at the castle. there were picnic tables. there are hard surface paths around the loch. these are wheelchair accessible. dog walking off lead is allowed.

a stunning place with a beautiful view and an area reminiscent of rome. there are rocks around a fountain and a unique design that i have not seen anywhere else. there is a nice building up on the hill and in the middle a lovely cafe/bar with drinks and pizza, located in a small vineyard. a recommended park for families, couples' trips and on beautiful days to enjoy the views of prague
a stunning place with beautiful views looking over the pride lands from the stupa. the photos don't do justice the colour of the rocks.

a stunning place. it's just hard to wrap your head around the fact that the city was built more than three and a half thousand years ago. thanks to spyridon marinatos, who began excavations in akrotiri in 1967, for his intuition and knowledge and, of course, to the site staff for the excellent organization of viewing
a stunning river! the river is serene and wildlife is everywhere. i was fortunate enough to see an egret hunting!

a stunning roadside viewpoint offering mesmerizing views of mount batur and the surrounding landscape. perfect for a quick stop to soak in the beauty especially during clear weather. be mindful though, clouds can quickly roll in and cover the mountain. the view is absolutely worth it, but be cautious of local item sellers nearbythey can be quite persistent. it's mostly just a viewpoint, not a hike or full stop, but a memorable spot for photos and a quick bit of shopping if you're interested. definitely a great memory if you're passing through!
a stunning ruin in a beautiful atmospheric landscape. do bring a midge net in the warmer months though or you'll be eaten alive!
a stunning viewpoint between the fjords. the climb is not difficult and the duration of the climb is from 45 minutes to 1.5 hours. a magnificent view of the fjord and the city of klaksvik opens up.

a stupa on a small hill looking over the majestic irrawaddy river. at its feet is a small bustling collection of food stalls selling tea, pea rice topped with a luscious fried egg, steaming milk, grilled shrimp, corn on cob, and fried baby shrimp fritters. a great stop for breakfast and prayers while temple running around old bagan.

a substandard place that overs water sports and other sea trips. we visited there on june 2019 and by far this is the worst experience that we had in bali. the total thing is a big scam where they ask prices as most premium but most of their equipments are rundown and risky for tourist. in addition, extra caution must be taken as the hygiene is below standards. once you arrive, they will push to convince you to take a package of various activities, yet when i evaluated the prices and safety, i refused their expensive offer. eventually, we rented a glass boat to the nearby turtles farm, and it turned that taking the glass boat is worthless and paying extra money for nothing. if you want to ruin your precious vacation time and money, then this is the perfect place.
a super cheerful and pretty street! it's tiny but spectacular for a few photos.
a super chill and scenic walk from interlaken west station. the sights at the finish are absolutely stunning. it's a simple half an hour trek and even kids can handle it.
a super fun way to enjoy the nile and see cairo from a different perspective.

a super solid trail. 10 miles round trip if you’re just going for the bottom. down for 80% of the way to the river, so be prepared for a push to get back up. first couple of miles is down with nicely made trails compliments of old miners. some of the best steep switch back trails i’ve ever seen. 3rd mile is quite technical with gives the trail a lot of flair imo, made the trail exciting and challenging. last part was fairly flat before descending the mesa. i also visited the last chance mine at the trail t before the mesa and i would highly recommend doing that if you have the time. it’s a glorious decent that will test you if you’ve never raw dogged a mesa wall decent before. the mines are also super cool, and while you can’t go into them, it’s still super cool to see. if you only had time for either the mines or the mesa decent to the valley i would go for the mines. as the decent to the river is long and fairly boring. don’t miss this hike, 100% worth your time. only 5 hikers on the trail in november, mild snow the first half mile.
a superb afternoon with quad marrakech horizon. everything was perfect. thank you all. i highly recommend their services. brand new equipment.
a superb buggy and quad driving experience with my family at la palmeraie. the team is very friendly and the route is worth the detour. we had a great time 👍

a superb concert in a marvellous venue - the engineers museum. with classics like "the blue danube", a soprano, a baritone,and even a little ballet. a very enjoyable 65 minutes (although was advertised as 80 minutes) with lovely music and even some humour. would certainly recommend and would go again

a superb experience and a fantastic way to explore the rainforest in this region. we opted for the diamond view, though i wouldn’t say it was truly worth the extra cost — the only differences being a glass-bottom cable car and the ability to skip the queue. there were amazing stops along the route, and the waterfall was absolutely beautiful. you might even catch sight of some wildlife. the ride itself is thoughtfully designed — safe, with stable platforms, and very smooth from start to finish. the staff were excellent throughout. i’d wholeheartedly recommend it!

a superb location, at the end of the world. a warm welcome from our hosts and an exceptional view of the lake with an unforgettable sunset. very comfortable and excellent food. a truly timeless experience. an excellent memory.

a superb place for a short walk. short but challenging as the initial climb up can be very steep. after the steep uphill slope climb, next challenge will be steps climb. the steps climb is also extremely challenging. good thing the weather was good with slight drizzle. ample parking place so no worries to parking your car there. can easier complete the hill walk within 1 hour or so.

a superb way to see this part of london. mike supplied every single bit of info required before the trip and was quick to respond to any questions we had. the day itself was superb, and we were lucky with the weather. would 100% recommend this as a great way to spend a day / afternoon in summer in london.

a sweeping panorama of majestic alpine mountains under brilliant blue skies, with a lone paraglider soaring gracefully in the distance. hear the whisper of the wind mingling with soft background chatter. feel the awe of nature’s grandeur and the freedom of the open sky.

a symbolic spot marking the crossing of the arctic circle, located right in the main square. you can wave to the live webcam, see yourself in real-time, or send a greeting to friends in other countries. in santa’s village, you can also buy a certificate confirming your arctic circle crossing—for €10, of course, because like most attractions here, almost everything comes with a price tag.
a temple dedicated to the cremation of local people. lots of small buildings and cool statues of elephants located around the corners as a sign of goodluck and prosperity.

a temple which is really peaceful. the cafes inside are very good. the toilets are free and very, very clean. better than usa and western europe. unlike what some caucasian reviewers say, it does have toilet paper and water both. why do europeans expect asians to keep tp in public toilets when your own public toilets don't have water? isn't this western entitlement and bit of racism?
a temple with an impressive big buddha statue. the temple is large in size and well-equipped with restrooms, coffee shops.

a temple with an intriguing past concerning a deity, a returned sword, and a kingdom struggling for independence. worth a visit in the cool hanoi evening, either to take in the juxtaposed history and modernity, or to simply people watch. also comes with not just one, but two (very dead) turtles on display. apparently they used to inhabit this tiny, serene lake. in all, 5/5 experience.

a thorough and well curated look at the counterculture in american history. while the focus is certainly on the hippies that made this neighborhood famous, this is a broad and thoughtful look at all the aspects of counterculture. wonderful!

a thrilling adventure at bearhill husky in finland! what a fantastic experience! the dogs were full of energy and chomping at the bit to get going. at first, they seemed a bit aggressive, but we were reassured it was just pure excitement. once we took off, you could really feel their power and enthusiasm forging ahead. the sleds move fast with the huskies leading the way, and cruising across the frozen lake was a moment in time i will never forget! i'm so glad i dressed warmly in layers with reliable snow boots. it was cold out there but i was prepared! they also had a room filled with everything you could possibly need to stay warm, puffy suits to put over your clothes, socks, boots, gloves, blankets, and more! the tour leader was incredibly passionate, sharing her knowledge about every aspect of dog sledding from grooming and training to the dogs' careers on the team and their well-earned retirements. it’s clear these dogs are well loved and very well cared for by the staff. it was an amazing experience i’d highly recommend!

a thrilling adventure at ugong rock, palawan if you’re looking for an adventure that gets your heart racing and your arms burning (in the best way possible), ugong rock adventures in palawan is the place to be! i went in thinking it was just a casual climb—but wow, was i in for a surprise. the journey started with spelunking through tight limestone formations, squeezing through narrow gaps, and using ropes to pull myself up steep rock faces. there were moments when i questioned my life choices (and my upper body strength), but the amazing guides kept things fun and encouraging. the climb was intense but so rewarding. at the top, the panoramic view of the surrounding forest was absolutely breathtaking! but the real highlight? the superman-style zipline descent! instead of taking the seated option, i went full superhero mode, soaring face-first over the lush greenery below. the rush of wind, the insane speed, and the feeling of flying made all the effort worth it. ugong rock adventures is a must-visit if you love adrenaline, nature, and a good challenge. just be prepared to work those muscles—and don’t skip leg day before coming! (jan-2023)

a thrilling dune bashing with our polite and safe driver riaz. it was a beautiful scenery at sunset when light casts warm hues across the sand. food and entertainment were good. overall an amazing experience with my family inclusive of my elderly mum.

a timeless landmark since 1321 leadenhall market is one of london’s oldest and most beautiful marketplaces, originally established in 1321. located in the heart of the city of london, it blends centuries of history with modern elegance. the victorian roof, colorful facades, and cobblestone paths make it feel like a movie set—and indeed, it has famously appeared in films like harry potter. this covered market offers a delightful mix of boutique shops, restaurants, and traditional pubs. it's a great place to enjoy lunch, browse unique stores, or simply admire the stunning architecture. even if you’re not shopping, the atmosphere alone is worth the visit. whether you're a history lover, architecture enthusiast, or curious traveler, leadenhall market is a must-see destination that captures the soul of historic london.

a timeless marvel — must-see in rome! visiting the colosseum was an unforgettable experience! the sheer scale and history of this ancient amphitheater are absolutely awe-inspiring. you can almost hear the echoes of gladiators and roaring crowds as you walk through its storied arches. it is very crowded, especially during peak hours, but that’s a testament to how iconic it is. i highly recommend buying tickets in advance — it saves a ton of time and hassle. tickets average around €20 per person, which is a fantastic value for such a world-renowned landmark. whether you're a history buff or just soaking in the beauty of rome, the colosseum is a must-visit. bring your camera, wear comfy shoes, and prepare to be amazed!

a timeless masterpiece, but better in autumn🗼 the eiffel tower is truly a breathtaking historical landmark. i’m still amazed that such a grand project was built back in 1889 and has been preserved so well to this day. as a historical monument, it’s nothing less than a masterpiece. that said, i’d strongly recommend visiting in autumn or spring. we went in the summer, and the crowds were overwhelming – it makes the whole experience less enjoyable. we didn’t go up the tower itself, as all our friends who had visited before advised us against it. they said it wasn’t worth the long queues and the ticket price. honestly, we enjoyed the tower much more from the outside and from other viewpoints in the city. another downside is the aggressive street vendors around the tower. every few steps you hear “buy this, buy that” — keychains, water bottles, t-shirts, photos. honestly, it takes away from the magic of the place. but despite this, the eiffel tower is one of those places you have to see at least once in your lifetime. standing beneath it and realizing its history is truly unforgettable.

a timeless symbol of freedom🍁 visiting the statue of liberty is a powerful and humbling experience. standing tall on liberty island, she’s more than just a monument—she’s a symbol of hope, resilience, and the promise of new beginnings. as you approach by ferry, the view of lady liberty rising against the manhattan skyline is breathtaking, especially on a clear day. the journey begins at battery park, and the ferry ride offers stunning views of new york harbor. once on the island, you can stroll through the museum that traces the statue’s history and significance. learning about how she was gifted by france and assembled piece by piece adds a deeper layer of meaning to the visit. for those who climb to the pedestal or crown (with advance reservations), the views are incredible. you see the sprawling city, the quiet water, and feel like a tiny part of a much larger story. the audio tour provides great context, bringing the statue’s meaning to life beyond just its towering figure. what’s striking is how she continues to inspire people from all over the world. whether you're a first-time visitor or a returning one, there's a sense of awe and reflection that never fades. this isn’t just a tourist stop—it’s a reminder of the ideals america was built on. a must-visit, rich in history, emotion, and iconic beauty
a tiny park.

a tiny, narrow, colorful street where local artists exhibit their works - some of which can be purchased. a place exceptionally detached from the rest of fez, bombarding with a multitude of colors and shapes. the impression of dystopia is even stronger in the evening. it is worth walking along this street while visiting the medina.

a ton of cars and different types. entry at 12€. spent about 90' taking my time reading and taking photos but could stay longer. three floors of showing. close to the metro was a bonus. perfect for kids (who listen and don't touch the cars) and all car enthusiasts.

a ton of fun and only 20-25 minutes from the city! our family of 4 had an excellent experience and we appreciated how easy it was especially since our teenage kids had never ridden quads before. our guide went at a good pace dictated by how comfortable the kids were and sped up as they figured it out. stopped for some pics and had tea/snacks half way through the ride. there are more advanced features as well for experienced riders. it’s easy to drive to if you have a car if not, they can arrange transportation. we liked that you did not have to combine the ride with other things you can just do the quads for 1 or 2 hours.

a tough but absolutely stunning hike up table mountain — 100% worth the effort! the views are breathtaking all the way up, and the sense of achievement at the top is unbeatable. definitely bring at least 1l of water per person, and a snack or two for energy. you’ll want it! the trail follows yellow footprints painted on the rocks, which is super helpful — though they can be hard to spot in places where the paint has chipped off, so keep your eyes peeled. a challenging hike, but an unforgettable experience for anyone who loves the outdoors. 🥾⛰️☀️

a tough hike, but highly recommended for those who appreciate a challenge and awesome sunrise views! i was kindly accommodated on short notice by the dekwar team who provided professional and top-tier service throughout - from the punctual pick up and drop off by the team’s driver, kadek, to my guide lulut’s patience and encouraging spirit during the whole journey. definitely the tour service to choose for this epic mountain ⛰️✨

a tourist friendly shooting range in interlaken. we found this place during our road trip in switzerland from taiwan. we don’t even have a shooting license and experience in pistol shooting but luckily they provided professional instruction that can make you from zero to hero. we had a great time experiencing shooting here and learned some useful techniques. we will return again someday and would like to recommend this place to others who are looking for a good shooting experience.

a tourist trap. but! you still have to visit the eiffel tower! it’s expensive to take the elevator to the top, but wow, what a view you get! there was a bit of chaos at the top when a line formed to go down. it was almost panic-inducing because the space was very tight and people started pushing. almost everyone seemed anxious and wanted to leave quickly. but being up there and seeing the whole city was still worth it. you could take great pictures. when it started getting dark, it was really beautiful as the eiffel tower lit up nicely! if you’re in paris, you have to visit. there’s a nice lawn outside where you can have a picnic. many local sellers try to sell souvenirs at high prices, so try to haggle if you really want a blinking plastic eiffel tower. expect it to take about 2 hours from standing in line at the bottom to getting back down when you’re done.
a touristy area, but a good place to stop while touring the island to get lunch, peanut ice cream, or hit the water on a boat tour.
a tranquil treasure with astounding accomodations and stunning seascapes. the associates are so kind and accomodating!

a travel company enters itself as a location of the white city. however, the location is outside the unesco boundaries. a photo of the histadrut building on arlozorov street was built by bauhaus architect dov karmi, but not as a bauhaus. misleading advertising.

a tribus adventure é uma assessoria esportiva que não só tem como objetivo te tornar um atleta amador ou profissional melhor, mas, sobretudo, de agregar e unir pessoas de diferentes idades e vivências num mesmo propósito; propagar energia e a experiência de treinar em meio à natureza que o rio de janeiro proporciona; fomentar a busca pelo melhor que você pode se tornar como ser humano e como atleta, seja na atividade em que escolher, seja ela natação, bike, corrida de asfalto ou trail run, ou todos eles juntos! sou uma pessoa mais feliz com a tribus.🧡🖤

a trilha começa na vila do trinta onde tem a portaria do icmbio que faz o controle dos visitantes que agendaram a trilha (pode agendar pela internet) e que poderão fazer a trilha. tem uma lojinha com chapéu, blusa uv, água, biscoito...além de banheiro público gratuito. é uma trilha praticamente toda plana, bem tranquila até para crianças.

a trilha da pontinha-caieira é lindíssima, vale muito a pena. o jailson foi um excelente guia e explicou bastante sobre a flora e fauna, tirou belas fotos nossas e foi muito atencioso e cuidadoso durante todo o trajeto. aproveitamos e fizemos a canoa havaiana no dia seguinte. ver o nascer do sol foi uma experiência única. valeu jailson!

a trilha do piquinho é uma das experiências mais recompensadoras de noronha para quem curte caminhadas curtas com visual incrível. com cerca de 1,2 km (ida e volta), ela leva ao segundo ponto mais alto da ilha, com vista privilegiada do morro do pico e da costa. o percurso é feito em cerca de 30 a 40 minutos (dependendo do ritmo), com subida íngreme e terreno de pedras, exigindo um pouco de preparo físico e tênis com boa aderência. não é necessário guia, e o melhor horário para subir é no início da manhã ou fim da tarde, só tomem cuidado pq a trilha é fechada e a noite fica mais complicado a volta!

a trilha do piquinho, em fernando de noronha, é uma das mais curtas e recompensadoras do arquipélago. com cerca de 800 metros (ida e volta), ela começa em um caminho sombreado por vegetação nativa e segue por um terreno rochoso que exige atenção e preparo físico moderado. apesar de breve, a trilha é desafiadora na segunda metade, com trechos de subida íngreme, pedras soltas e apoio por cordas, o que a torna emocionante para quem busca aventura com segurança. o grande atrativo da trilha está no topo do piquinho, uma formação rochosa com vista privilegiada de 180°, de onde se pode avistar o morro do pico, o porto, a cacimba do padre, o mar de fora e até os famosos dois irmãos. o pôr do sol visto deste ponto é um espetáculo à parte e costuma ser o momento mais fotografado pelos visitantes. por essa razão, o fim da tarde é o horário mais recomendado para realizar o percurso, embora o terreno deva ser evitado em dias de chuva devido ao risco de escorregões. é possível fazer a trilha sem guia, mas o acompanhamento de um profissional credenciado é indicado, especialmente para quem não tem experiência em trilhas ou se sente inseguro em ambientes de altura. o uso de tênis apropriado, roupas leves e protetor solar é essencial, assim como levar água e uma lanterna caso o retorno aconteça após o pôr do sol. a trilha do piquinho é uma experiência única para quem visita noronha, combinando natureza, desafio e paisagens inesquecíveis em um percurso breve, porém impactante.
a trilha foi muito legal, mas a maré não estava tão adequada para as flutuações...vale a pena colocar na lista de passeios...

a trilha para o pedra da proa tem início na rua estrada do redentor. logo após a curva, você se deparará com uma escada de madeira, a qual você deverá seguir. no decorrer da trilha você passa pelo mirante da cumeeira, freira e morro do queimado. a paisagem é espetacular, proporcionando uma vista deslumbrante do cristo, lagoa, pão de açúcar e pedra da gávea entre outros. a trilha é muito tranquila sem muita dificuldade. optamos pelo retorno sair na mesa do imperador.

a trilha pontinha-caieiras tem cenários lindos que margeiam a costa do mar de fora. são cerca de 3h de passeio com duas paradas para snorkel em piscinas naturais. a variedade de vida marinha no dia em que fomos estava fantástica! a caminhada nas pedras vulcânicas também foi sensacional. essa caminhada exige um pouco de preparo e não recomendo caso você tenha algum problema nos tornozelos e joelhos. se suas articulações estão boas, vá em frente e aproveite esse passeio lindo!

a trilha é fácil em geral. uma parte exige descer e depois subir um morro segurando/apoiando em uma corda. o percurso é curto, mas fizemos 2 paradas para banho. o percurso oferece 2 piscinas de mergulho, mas é necessário coletes salva vidas e uma máscara de snorkel. algumas pessoas não estavam preparada (sem coletes) e não puderam entrar em uma piscina. também é proibido o uso de protetor solar, usamos camisas com proteção uv e é recomendado.
a trilha é tranquila, mas possui um trecho de decida que é necessário cautela para não se machucar. no fim, a trilha é 10/10! as piscinas naturais são incríveis.

a true cultural treasure! the coptic museum, founded in 1908 by marcus simaika pasha, is located in the heart of old cairo and houses the world’s largest collection of coptic christian artifacts. it beautifully traces the history of coptic egypt from the 3rd to the 19th century, showcasing the deep roots of christianity in egypt. the museum itself is an architectural masterpiece, with detailed wooden ceilings and serene courtyards that reflect traditional coptic design. the collection includes ancient manuscripts, stone carvings, textiles, icons, and more—each piece telling a unique story of egypt’s christian heritage. informative bilingual labels (arabic & english), a calm atmosphere, and a location near important sites like the hanging church make this a must-visit for anyone interested in egypt’s diverse and rich history.

a true experience. the pictures you find online might make you think they've been photoshopped. but no, the water actually has these fantastic colors and is crystal clear. the waterfalls are magnificent. the hiking trails are easy to walk. the inclines are moderate but not suitable for people with limited mobility. dogs are allowed on leashes. what we missed were trash cans. our dog had a major bowel movement right at the beginning of our trip, which we, of course, disposed of in the appropriate bag. unfortunately, we then had to lug this full bag around with us for hours, as there are no trash cans anywhere along the trail. so, a tip for all dog owners... let your dog take a poop first... concerning overcrowding: yes, it's very, very crowded. in some corners, the queues are incredibly long, and you have to wait. that can be quite annoying.

a true gem – nature, conservation, and wildlife! ebony forest was one of the most impressive and meaningful places we visited in mauritius. the small museum at the entrance gives great insight into the island’s early, colonial & environmental history – and it’s shocking to learn that only about 2% of the original native forest remains due to 400 years of deforestation and exploitation. this makes the reserve’s conservation efforts even more valuable. the forest trails are absolutely beautiful and peaceful. you can spot endemic species like the mauritius flycatcher, geckos, fruit bats, and – if you're lucky – the rare echo parakeet, especially in the late afternoon just before closing when they fly home to their nesting sites. according to our tracking, the walk from the museum to sublime point (truly sublime views indeed!) is roughly 2.5km with a minor incline. you have two options: a small forest trail and a broader concrete path and both paths lead you to a little boardwalk through an area where lots of flycatchers fly around you. one of our personal highlights: the free-roaming giant tortoises! 🐢 we spotted two just next to the trail, which was such a lovely surprise. unlike chamarel, where the tortoises are kept in a small fenced area, here they really wander freely – and it feels so much more natural and respectful. also highly recommend the charming gift shop, full of local, eco-friendly crafts and souvenirs. a must-visit for anyone who loves nature and wants to support important conservation work on the island.

a true hidden gem, trok mor market is tucked away in an alley just around the corner from the famous giant swing, in front of wat suthat thepwararam. at first glance, the alleyway seems unremarkable, especially in the early hours, but step inside, and it suddenly bursts into one of the liveliest markets in bangkok. the market offers everything—from fresh seasonal fruits to seafood like fish (even flounder!), shellfish, and so much more. a wide variety of ready-to-eat foods, snacks, and drinks make it a haven for food lovers. every vendor is a local, selling homemade specialties perfected over years, resulting in truly delicious food. so far, i’ve tried a scrumptious red pork and duck vendor, a stall selling homemade bao buns, and another offering incredibly tasty chinese donuts. overall, trok mor market is an amazing place to eat while exploring!
a truely authentic and charming farmers market - what a blessing 🥰🌿💚

a truly amazing hike, but preparation is key. * authorization is required to climb the volcano, so book your spot well in advance. * the path has checkpoints, so a very early start is essential to make it to the top. * this is a tough, challenging hike to 2000m, so be ready for a good workout. * don't count on a clear view from the summit. it's often foggy due to the climate, but the experience is still worth it!

a truly beautiful and awe inspiring little hike with fantastic views. the star of this half of the track is the stopping point at the arrayanes path bit. a short, but gorgeous loop around a set of arrayanes trees in all their beauty. there's a wooden walkway guiding that loop for a reason, to preserve the trees' wellbeing. don't get off to get pictures and trample their roots! all in all, beautiful experience, and this track connects to several others that can help you get a wonderful sense of this gorgeous natural park. i highly recommend continuing after the arrayanes path into moreno lake (lago moreno), then after you exit, take a short right walking alongside the roadway to enter the roman bridge (puente romano) track to your left all the way down hidden lake (lago escondido) and logs' bay (bahía de troncos)! then you can either retrace your steps, or continue north once you're back at the roman bridge to go to villa tacul and the trek up llao llao hill (cerro llao llao) that ends up near where the first arrayanes track started.

a truly beautiful and peaceful place to explore! the views over the bay are stunning, and the coastal walk is easy and enjoyable for all fitness levels. the historic captain cook’s landing site adds a meaningful touch, making it both a scenic and culturally significant stop. however, a couple of things to keep in mind: there are limited bathroom facilities and not many parking spots close to the main attractions. i’d recommend arriving early, especially on weekends, to avoid a long walk from your car.

a truly beautiful experience! the best of all - the animals truly look happy and taken care of. you can never know for sure, but it really seems like everyone is really passionate about their jobs and doing their best to give all the animals the best care and love. their enclosures are spacious, beautiful, and clean. if you’re going a day tour, definitely do both the safari and the marine park. aim to come as soon as the park opens, there’s really a lot to see and do. you don’t want to miss any of the shows and feedings. plenty of chances to interact with animals safely and respectfully. all the shows are entertaining, and educational.

a truly beautiful museum, showcasing exquisite artworks from the past within an equally stunning modern architectural setting. the new building is a masterpiece of taste and design, and the garden complements it perfectly, both are simply breathtaking.

a truly enchanting stay at dar tahri riad my recent stay at dar tahri riad was nothing short of magical. this isn't just a hotel; it's a beautifully restored 14th-century home that transports you back in time while offering every modern comfort. the restoration has been done with incredible taste, preserving the traditional style and unique character of the building. the intricate tilework, stunning carved wood, and the peaceful courtyard are all maintained in immaculate condition, a testament to the care put into this place. the location is perfect. tucked away on a quiet street in the heart of the medina, it's a peaceful escape from the bustling souks but still within easy walking distance of all the main attractions. what truly makes this riad stand out is the people. the cleanliness is impeccable; every corner of the riad is spotless. but most importantly, the hospitality from fayssal and aziz is exceptional. their kindness and genuine warmth made me feel like a valued guest, not just a customer. they were always available to offer a helpful recommendation, a cup of mint tea, or simply a friendly chat. i can't recommend dar tahri riad highly enough. if you want an authentic, beautiful, and peaceful experience in fez, this is the place to stay. you'll leave with wonderful memories and a deep appreciation for the beauty and hospitality of morocco.

a truly ethical elephant experience this sanctuary is a safe haven for rescued elephants. they live freely, without chains or riding, and are clearly well cared for. the staff shows real love and respect, focusing on the animals’ wellbeing. it’s a beautiful place that truly puts the elephants first. highly recommended for anyone who values ethical animal tourism.

a truly fantastic way to spend my birthday morning up here in the cairngorms. my girlfriend treated me to a surprise birthday safari trip with highland wildlife and birdwatching safaris which involved a 5:30am get-up to begin the safari but boy was it worth it! nothing was too much trouble for steve and his enthusiastic greeting at 6am was the perfect start to the day and set the scene for things to come. we journeyed through the diverse habitats of the aviemore area (all within 15mile radius!) from upland glen to caledonian woodland we covered it all and saw a fantastic array of wildlife. some of the highlights included being greeted by a reindeer at the entrance to the cairngorm ski centre, seeing ospreys deliver fish to their young through the amazingly powerful telescope and witnessing the very rare (we were told 80-120 breeding pairs in the uk) black throated diver surface in the lock meters away from the land-rover. speaking of the land rover, the “bird-mobile” as i heard steve mention it was immaculately clean and comfortable. equipped with all the latest mod cons such as heated seats and even screens in the seats to view some of the previous tour photographs. steve even accommodated my golden retriever which was really good of him as we had no one to look after him whilst the tour was on. all in all steve’s attention to detail to ensure we were comfortable throughout the trip was clear to see. 5* care and hospitality! to sum it up we loved everything about the trip and really thought we got our moneys worth. would recommend it to anyone without hesitation as an activity and a great way to get introduced to our native wildlife and appreciate the diversity just outside our doors, which is now more important than ever given recent events. birthday well and truly made, thanks to safari steve! we would love to come back in winter as the wildlife is forever changing and shifting with the seasons! many thanks, rufus and esme

a truly great trail, well used and well maintained with some of the best views on the island. there are a lot of steps but these are generally well placed and in good condition as of january 2025. there are a few benches to rest on in places with great views and toilets only at the start of the trail and then again where it turns towards the beach.

a truly iconic and one of the great scottish castles you can see in scotland with a host of things to see and do and packed full of interesting history. the range of things to see and do include the queen anne garden, the castle exhibition, palace & royal apartments, stirling heads, chapel royal, museum of the argyll and sutherland highlanders museum, tapestry exhibition, great hall and great kitchens and all of these things are a magnificent sight and true masterpiece to see. the queen anne garden offers a stunning array of colour from the flower borders adding a different and interesting dynamic to the castle and brings some vibrancy to it. the castle exhibition provides a riveting and informative synopsis of the history of the castle and the people that lived there along with the changes that have taken place to it. the chapel royal is a wonderful airy space and you can some wonderful murals, which are stunning on the eye. the palace offers some great reconstructed apartment rooms such as the bedrooms where you can see some great tapestries and four poster beds and there are guides in each of the apartment rooms who are very helpful and detail some useful facts about life for people living in the apartment rooms during the medieval period. in the great hall which is one of the iconic bits of the place and you can see the wonderful whalebone roof and you can admire the vastness of it. in the stirling heads exhibition you can learn about how the heads were made and you some of the stirling heads which are extremely exquisite and amazing up close and one of the best wood carvings ever made and certainly the best for their period. the tapestry exhibition details the story of the stirling tapestries and how they were made and woven in the studio on site and the great kitchens you can see how a reconstructed medieval kitchen was set up and worked and see how busy and chaotic it was and also see some of the food eaten and there is some interesting information about how the food was cooked and eaten and the diets people had. as you walk around the castle you can enjoy beautiful picturesque views of the surrounding areas and get a clear idea of what a stronghold this place has been for centuries and there are guided tours to enjoy at intervals where you can more interesting facts about the castle from the guides who deliver them in an enthusiastic and passionate fashion and there are audio guides to enjoy which you can obtain from the entrance for a small fee and these detail further interesting facts about the castle. the argyll and sutherland highlanders museum details an informative history of the regiment and is contributions to british army over the years and the battles they have fought in and there are some interesting artefacts to see such as uniforms and medals to see.there is a cafe on site selling a delightful range of food and drink at reasonable prices and also there are shops selling souvenirs at reasonable prices. overall this is a fantastically iconic and a truly first class place to visit and makes for a wonderful and amazing historical day out. definitely well worth to a scottish national treasure and well worth a visit whilst in stirling.

a truly iconic new york experience! the views from the top are absolutely breathtaking, offering panoramic vistas of the entire city. it's a must-do for any visitor, and the historical exhibits leading up to the observatory are really well done and informative. be prepared for crowds, especially during peak season, but the efficiency of the staff keeps things moving along. highly recommend!

a truly impressive view! while the focus at surprise corner is more on the fairmont banff springs hotel, this viewpoint gives you an even better view of the mountains and the valley of the bow river. at the trailhead you can also see the unique rock formations on the river bank, which are known as “hoodoos” in canada. with a bit of luck you will also see a few animals here. there are a few benches along the trail that are suitable for a short break. the trail from surprise corner to the hoodoos viewpoint is about 4.5km long and can be completed in about an hour.

a truly lovely place to visit! this flower park is a beautiful escape into nature, where the peaceful surroundings can truly relax anyone. the vibrant colors and calming atmosphere make it a wonderful spot for a walk or simply to unwind. it’s also an ideal destination for families, offering plenty of space and sights for everyone to enjoy. definitely worth the visit!

a truly relaxing and memorable experience with blue safari’s southern catamaran cruise blue safari’s southern catamaran cruise was the perfect blend of leisure, scenic beauty, and top-notch hospitality. from start to finish, everything was exceptionally well-organized. the online booking process was smooth and hassle-free, and the booking team patiently answered all my queries over whatsapp—something i truly appreciated. on the day of the cruise, we were warmly welcomed by the blue safari team at pointe des régates in mahébourg. a quick speedboat transfer brought us to the beautiful catamaran, where our journey began at 9:30 am. we were greeted with a cheerful welcome and a helpful tour briefing by our lovely host, rose. the cruise was led by captain jack and his wonderful four-member crew, who ensured we were comfortable and well taken care of throughout. we were a small, friendly group—two families and a few couples—which made the experience feel even more personal. our first stop was a snorkelling session, and i was thrilled to see my daughter try it for the first time. the crew was incredibly encouraging and made the moment extra special. as we sailed through the stunning blue-green waters, drinks flowed freely, and we found ourselves completely immersed in the tranquillity of the sea. rose shared interesting facts about the nearby lighthouse and surroundings, adding a thoughtful touch to the journey. next, we hopped on a speedboat to visit the breathtaking grse waterfall—a highlight of the trip. back on the catamaran, we were treated to a delicious barbecue lunch. relaxing on the deck with the sea breeze and panoramic views was simply mesmerising. by 2 pm, we reached the picturesque île aux cerfs, where we enjoyed a refreshing swim in the shallow turquoise waters. the island was well-equipped with facilities like showers, changing rooms, beach chairs, and cozy shack restaurants. after an hour of island time, we returned to the catamaran for a delightful tea and coffee session accompanied by freshly baked cake and soft background music. as rain clouds began to roll in, the team ensured we got back to the starting point safely by 4 pm. every aspect of the cruise was thoughtfully planned and executed. a special thanks to rose, whose warmth and hospitality made us feel completely at home. this was truly an experience of a lifetime—spending quality time with family, disconnected from the digital world, surrounded by serene waters and breathtaking views. highly recommend this day cruise if you’re visiting mauritius! be sure to check their website for more cruise options based on your location—there’s something for everyone.

a truly unforgettable five-star safari experience – eagle island lodge from the moment we arrived at eagle island lodge, we knew we were in for something extraordinary — but what we experienced far exceeded our expectations. nestled in the heart of the magical okavango delta, this five-star lodge offers the perfect balance between luxury, adventure, and untouched natural beauty. our stay was nothing short of spectacular. the lodge itself is elegantly designed, effortlessly blending into its environment while still delivering every comfort and indulgence imaginable. from the warm welcome to the impeccable service, every detail was thoughtfully taken care of. what made our trip truly memorable were the exciting activities and immersive experiences. from mokoro (canoe) rides along the glistening delta channels to thrilling game drives, each moment brought us closer to africa’s heartbeat. we were fortunate to witness elephants bathing, hippos grunting in the waterways, and even a pride of lions relaxing in the golden afternoon light — experiences that will stay with us forever. every day felt like a new chapter in a grand adventure, yet also a chance to completely unwind. sundowners overlooking the water, nights under the stars, and meals that could rival any fine dining establishment — all combined to create an all-round unforgettable escape. what makes eagle island lodge stand out is not just the activities or setting, but the way it captures your soul. the sheer beauty of the environment, the serenity of the delta, and the genuine warmth of the people made this one of the most meaningful travel experiences we’ve ever had. we leave with hearts full of gratitude, minds filled with awe, and already dreaming about when we can return. if you’re looking for a place that redefines luxury in the wild and gives you memories to last a lifetime, eagle island lodge is it. five stars, all the way. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

a truly unique and captivating museum experience in rome! 🇮🇹🏛️ housed within a magnificently preserved former thermoelectric power plant, this museum creates a stunning juxtaposition of ancient roman sculptures and colossal industrial machinery. 🤯 the exquisite classical statues, from the capitoline museums, appear breathtakingly alive amidst the towering engines and turbines. it's a visually striking and thought-provoking blend of antiquity and industrial heritage, offering a fresh perspective on both. a hidden gem in the ostiense district! 💖🌟 absolutely unforgettable! ✨

a truly unique and fascinating museum! the icelandic phallological museum offers an unusual yet educational experience. there is an entry fee, and to access the museum, café, and souvenir shop, you’ll need to walk down a flight of stairs. the collection is extensive and well-displayed, and the overall visit is both quirky and informative. definitely a memorable stop if you're curious and open-minded!

a truly wonderful experience, aboard a very nice traditional boat, with the most welcoming and experienced crew, with delicious food and a ton of discoveries, above and under water!!! special thanks to our guide an, and his excellent french! to the cruise master, leo, best free diver! to the super chef and our housekeeper jonny! and to the most patient dingy captain, pablo!! unforgettable. everything and everyone.

a truly wonderful place for a peaceful walk, where you can fully take in the surroundings without distractions. i highly recommend visiting on friday mornings when the streets are empty.. no cars, no crowds just a serene, open space where you can breathe, unwind, and enjoy the quiet beauty of downtown cairo. it’s the perfect time to experience it at its best.
a truly wonderful place to snorkel. families of sea lions, turtles, iguanas and so many fish.

a unique and cultural experience in the heart of the old quarter. the water puppet show at lotus theater was charming and beautifully done, with live traditional music adding to the atmosphere. the stories were fun to watch, even if you don’t understand vietnamese. it’s a bit touristy and the seating can be tight, but still a memorable and entertaining glimpse into vietnamese tradition. worth checking out while in hanoi!

a unique and picturesque complex located in the southern part of sedona. featuring beautiful spanish architecture. the space is home to art galleries, gift shops, clothing boutiques, painting studios, and inviting restaurants. the setting is wonderfully relaxing, with each shop thoughtfully designed to blend with the surrounding natural environment. the backdrop of red rock formations enhances the connection to nature, while the soothing sound of the nearby creek adds to the overall charm. a delightful place to explore and experience the spirit of sedona.

a unique building by gaudí with a fascinating design. the wavy stone facade and the rooftop are simply stunning. the guided tour was informative and gave me great insights. super easy to get tickets on the spot, didn't have to wait.

a unique building by gaudí with a fascinating design. the wavy stone facade and the rooftop are simply stunning. the guided tour was informative and gave me great insights. super easy to get tickets on the spot, didn't have to wait.
a unique cistern, a bit challenging to get to, can be combined as part of the steph trip

a unique cocktail experience: was it worth it? yes, but i wouldn’t make it the one and only item you book on a night out. the staff were fantastic, the storyline engaging, and the theme and characters - great! we were hooked even despite the noise of those grouped with us and we enjoyed interacting with them! what let it down for us were the cocktails & the jumpsuits. the cocktails were not very unique, mostly overly sweet, and were more style than substance. the jumpsuits were also handed out quickly, not to size and not very well thought out for the heat. the day we went was 28c and some of our group got quite hot! all in all, a fun experience and made fun by the commitment and energy of the storytellers!
a unique experience

a unique experience at tijuca national park with our guide erik from get your guide. he was incredibly friendly, informative, and encouraged us to fully enjoy the caves and trails. the hike through the jungle was absolutely worth it—beautiful views, rich nature, and even some wildlife sightings.

a unique experience at tijuca national park with our guide erik from get your guide. he was incredibly friendly, informative, and encouraged us to fully enjoy the caves and trails. the hike through the jungle was absolutely worth it—beautiful views, rich nature, and even some wildlife sightings.

a unique experience in a heavenly place! we loved this outing with sea serenity! we were the first to arrive on these paradise islands, no one on the horizon, just us! the calm and gentle sound of the waves on the sand! it's magical! the whole team is adorable, and takes great care of us! a hearty, varied and delicious meal! this remains one of our best memories on the island! thanks again to you!!

a unique experience in the swiss alps. we hiked with 2 feet adventures in interlaken, and it was much more than a tour: it was a true connection with nature. our guide led us on off-the-beaten-track trails with spectacular scenery. everything was very well organized, authentic, and with a personal touch that made all the difference. ideal if you're looking for something more intimate, natural, and memorable in the alps!

a unique experience you can have in the wadi rum desert. from start to finish, mohammed and his friends' warm and friendly conversations, as well as their help in every aspect, made this experience amazing. we left with beautiful memories and great friendships, far beyond our expectations. the day after our stay, we went on a jeep tour in the desert with our friends, and the tour was fantastic, thanks to ibrahim’s wonderful guidance. i will definitely come back here to see them again.
a unique experience, excellent service, warmth, and kindness. emilia was the best. the excursions were 10 points. we'll be back!

a unique museum that proves and reinforces the historical facts regarding the belonging of the land of israel in general and jerusalem in particular to the jewish nation and people. contains factual details accompanied by archaeological findings and documents along the historical timeline from the dawn of history to the present day. there are also panoramic views of jerusalem both the old and the new city. a must-see!

a unique museum that proves and reinforces the historical facts regarding the belonging of the land of israel in general and jerusalem in particular to the jewish nation and people. contains factual details accompanied by archaeological findings and documents along the historical timeline from the dawn of history to the present day. there are also panoramic views of jerusalem both the old and the new city. a must-see!
a unique rock on the way to los tuneles

a unique, fun, and vibrant experience. bring cash and spend a lazy couple of hours here. boats will float up to yours and offer drinks or snacks, or an entire mariachi band might jump aboard and start serenading you! wish we stayed longer! will definitely do this again next time.

a uniquely vietnamese experience! we attended the water puppet show at lotus theatre near hoàn kiếm lake and had a lovely time. the show started punctually, and the seating was comfortable with a clear view of the stage. the stories were engaging and easy to follow, thanks to display screens showing the storyline in english, french, and vietnamese. it’s a must-do cultural activity when in vietnam. it's affordable, entertaining, and a great way to spend an evening in hanoi.
a vast beach with water as blue as the indian ocean, featuring an impressive tide is worth seeing. fewer maasai than in other locations. highly recommended!

a vast square with huge impressive and expensive governmental buildings. but i got so so sad, when i realized from the way of living there, that every revolution dies, upon becoming the establishment...

a very affordable yet 5 star quality service, a very nice tour driver mr. rasheed and smooth and hassle free entering border of oman. im alone in this travel but i dont feel alone with the whole group i enjoyed the water activities and the food and the best part is i enjoyed my relaxing moment in the boat having a nap after the lunch plus the very accomodating host they will help u in everything u need.

a very beautiful and amazing space with wonderful architecture. in the crypt were the tombs of great french writers and celebrities. i was able to visit the tomb of my favorite writer, victor hugo. it was an unforgettable experience. thank you

a very beautiful and diverse national park, perfect for trekking if you are not an experienced trekker, but also for reaching high peaks. the nature is breathtaking and diverse: from jungle forest, beautiful rivers and waterfalls, to grassland above the treeline. from syabru besi to kyangjin gompa you can basically not get lost, because there is only one path. good infrastructure and teahouses available. the village langtang and kyangjin gompa are breathtaking, the views of the mountains amazing. definitely would go there again!
