absolutely incredible dive shop with an outstanding crew! every single dive is handled with professionalism, and that extra effort that makes the whole experience unforgettable. they truly go above and beyond—whether it’s helping you spot rare marine life or creating a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. i also did my advanced certification there and it was great, we had some of the best dives while learning! the marine biodiversity in the south is spectacular, from gray reef sharks, to graceful rays and turtles and lots of swarms and great visibility in april. one absolute highlight? their magical sunset dives—gliding through the water as the sky turns gold and pink is something you’ll never forget. couldn’t recommend them more! a must-do if you’re in the area.

absolutely incredible dive shop — run by people with heart. we had an amazing experience with let’s dive. the owners are truly some of the kindest, most generous, and down-to-earth people we’ve ever met while traveling. they went above and beyond to make our time with them unforgettable. despite some boat issues, they rearranged everything so that my partner could complete his advanced course without missing a beat. they did everything they could to make it work — always with a smile and genuine care. the dives themselves were fantastic: well-organized, safe, and beautiful. the instructor was highly skilled and professional. the attention to detail was remarkable. after every dive, they cleaned our gear for us, gave us free pdf documents, and even gave us lifts back to our hotel several times. one day, we accidentally left some of our gear at the shop — and without us even asking or realizing it, they came back the next morning and delivered it to our hotel. that level of thoughtfulness is rare. they took the time to explain things patiently and never tried to upsell us. at one point, we considered buying the nitrox course, but they were honest and told us that in our case, it wasn’t safe or useful — “i won’t sell it just to sell it,” they said. same with a fish id book we looked at — they told us it wasn’t worth the money because it was missing too many species. that kind of integrity is priceless. and beyond diving, they have rescue dogs, help the local community, and just radiate kindness. they are incredibly accommodating, compassionate, and truly human. we really fell in love with them and recommend let’s dive to absolutely everyone. it wasn’t just a dive shop — it was a heartwarming experience.

absolutely incredible experience with kilimanjaro heroes from start to finish. customer service and communication was exceptional. tailored a 5 day safari to suit our budget which was very price competitive and assigned us the best ever guide jamal who was amazing with his knowledge of local birds (my husband is a mad birdwatcher and photographer) as well as making sure we found all the regular safari animals. exceptional english, so easy going and kind. highly recommend this locally owned and operated business. please support local 🙏🙏.

absolutely incredible experience with mexico kan tours! the entire team was outstanding—friendly, knowledgeable, and clearly passionate about what they do. from start to finish, the guides made sure we felt looked after and informed, providing detailed insights that really enhanced the trip. two standout tours for me were the cenote adventure with the amazing jessica—so fun and full of energy—and the sian ka’an expedition with miguel and macarena, who were simply fantastic. i’m not a confident swimmer, but miguel went out of his way to make me feel safe and comfortable in the water, even encouraging me to snorkel. i’m so glad i did—it was unforgettable! we got to see manatees, dolphins, and even crocodiles in their natural habitat. the whole experience was magical. i couldn’t recommend mexico kan tours more highly—professional, passionate, and simply the best. you’re in great hands with them!

absolutely incredible experience! charlotte and the team were so accommodating and able to squeeze me in on the half day trip at the last minute. charlotte and marie were fantastic at explaining how everything worked and gave really clear instructions so even as a beginner i could feel confident. the views were amazing and i can’t recommend the horse riding enough! if you have any doubts even if you’re a beginner just go for it

absolutely incredible experience! our santorini catamaran trip for the hen party was beyond amazing. from the breathtaking views to the attentive crew, every moment was magical. the catamaran was spacious and luxurious, perfect for our group. swimming in the crystal-clear waters and savoring delicious food and drinks while sailing along the stunning coastline made it an unforgettable day.

absolutely incredible experience! the jet skis were top-notch, well-maintained, and super fun to ride. the staff was friendly, helpful, and made sure we were safe and comfortable throughout the entire rental process. the location was stunning, and the views from the sea were breathtaking. definitely the highlight of our vacation and we’ll be back for more!

absolutely incredible experience. what can i say but a perfect day out. hosts were knowledgeable, friendly and would go out of their way to do anything for you. lovely catamaran, very clean and luxurious. no rush tour and amazing scenery. did a lot of research in choosing these guys and couldn't be happier. thanks for an incredible experience

absolutely incredible from start to finish! the entire boat trip was seamless, with such friendly and professional staff who went out of their way to make the experience unforgettable for us on a company trip. the food was delicious, the music was great, and the atmosphere was pure joy the whole way through. genuinely one of the best experiences i have ever had on a holiday, it made our trip! could not recommend this enough.

absolutely loved my visit to the national maritime museum in london! the exhibits are incredibly well-curated and offer a fascinating insight into britain’s naval history. there’s so much to learn, from famous sea battles to the lives of everyday sailors, and everything is presented in a really engaging way. the museum itself is spacious, beautifully maintained, and free to enter, which makes it even more impressive. i particularly enjoyed the section on polar exploration and the models of historic ships — they’re stunning! the interactive displays are great for both adults and kids, making it a perfect place for families as well. if you’re even slightly interested in history or the sea, this place is an absolute must-visit. it’s not just educational, but also inspiring. definitely one of the best museums in greenwich, and i’d recommend it to anyone visiting london.

absolutely loved our entire experience! fantastic deal: $70 usd/person for catamaran ride to and from isla mujeres, all you can drink on the boat, snorkeling in the reef, buffet all you can eat (and drink) lunch on the island, back to the boat to ride up to the city area for shopping at exploring. it’s an all day affair! we did the noon departure and were busy non-stop until we sailed back at 6pm. caught the gorgeous sunset on the way back. the crew was friendly, accommodating, and hilarious! they kept us entertained with music, conversation, and continuous info updates. lunch buffet was good; we all know how buffets are! compared to my catamaran experience in playa del carmen, this was amazing (i only received some petty snacks on that other boat). some shopping you can do here but i’d save it for the main isla mujeres area. tons of shopping here. definitely do the golf cart adventure! $15 usd/person and you can get around quickly. we only had a little over an hour to explore (shopping, beach, and punta sur). if you can make it to punta sur, grab a gold cart and do it!! absolutely gorgeous cliff area with ruins and various statues. the ride there was fun too; lots of cool restaurants, architecture, and you get to see the locals in their true element. our experience here felt like we were on the amazing race! we had a blast and would definitely recommend this to anyone.

absolutely magical experience! my first time at the palace theatre and it couldn’t have been better. i went with my daughter to see harry potter and the cursed child, a breathtaking, epic production! the play is brilliantly staged, the actors are phenomenal, and the special effects left us completely blown away. if you're a harry potter fan, this is an absolute must-see. the play is in two parts (each around 3 hours with a 20-min intermission), and there’s a 2-hour break between part 1 and part 2. you can store your coats and bags for £1. drinks and snacks (including cocktails and non-alcoholic options) are available at the bar and can be brought into the theatre. the palace theatre itself is beautiful and historic, opened in 1891, it was originally intended to be the home of english grand opera. today it’s one of london’s most iconic west end venues, located right by leicester square station, in the heart of the theatre district. the atmosphere of the area is buzzing, especially in the evening, making it a perfect setting for a magical night out. highly recommend!

absolutely wonderful green escape of denpasar. you can meet here a lot of locals and als compete in a round of chess. they are really welcoming and nice. it’s one of the hidden gems in balis most overcrowded space.

activity 2: paddlewheeler creole queen – mississippi river cruise 🚢 📍1 poydras st, new orleans, la it was a 2-hour mississippi river cruise with creole queen, included in our go city pass (worth $47). you’ll need to reserve ahead, then exchange your pass for a paper ticket at the booth before boarding. bags get checked, and hang on to your ticket. (it’s needed again after the stop.) we boarded at 2pm (without the meal plan) and cruised past landmarks like the crescent city connection bridge, st. louis cathedral, domino sugar factory, and more. the highlight? a 50-minute stop at chalmette battlefield, site of the 1815 battle of new orleans, where general andrew jackson led u.s. forces to victory. even though the visitor center was closed, a park ranger was on site to give us a quick history rundown. we didn’t have time to walk to the national cemetery, which holds over 15,000 graves from various u.s. wars. it had just been beautifully decorated with flags for memorial day that something our guide said took 200 volunteers four hours to complete! 💡 a ship photographer offers printed photos at the end (he took the photos before on board.) — kinda pricey at $25 for two, but we couldn’t resist grabbing one as a keepsake. bonus: right next to the dock is riverwalk outlets where is perfect for a little shopping before or after the cruise! this river tour was a great mix of views and history. if you’re into both, definitely add it to your new orleans itinerary! our next stop: just a 3-minute walk to vue new orleans. activity 3 coming up!

after 10 years of living in japan, i finally visited the ghibli museum with my friends. we went towards the end of the day, and honestly, i wasn’t sure what to expect given all the hype and praise it receives. as someone who enjoys ghibli films but isn’t a die-hard fan, i found the experience pleasant but not mind-blowing. the museum is fascinating, especially for those interested in the mechanics of animation; it’s a wonderful place for kids to explore and learn. however, the overall space is smaller than i anticipated. the exclusive short films they screen monthly are fun and creative, but keep in mind there’s no english subtitles, which might be challenging if you don’t understand japanese. one thing to note, even though photos and videos are strictly prohibited inside the museum, some visitors still break the rules, which can be quite annoying and distracting from the experience. on a positive note, i have to say their bathrooms are surprisingly exquisite and impressive, definitely worth a mention! overall, it’s a good visit, especially if you’re a fan of miyazaki’s work or curious about the animation process. just keep your expectations in check. for a 1,000 yen ticket, it’s definitely worth seeing at least once.

after a long and unsuccessful ordeal, i decided to try andrea kölliker's methods, about which i had already heard and read many good things. although i had some doubts at first, i realized after the first session that this wasn't just "hocus-pocus." here, the root of the problem is truly removed, rather than—as is common in many therapies—talking about the same things over and over for hours, thereby wasting even more energy and creating negative emotions. i was able to examine and resolve many different issues and problems with andrea. i felt increasingly more powerful and fully alive again. all the energy and powerlessness are gone! you can come to andrea with all kinds of issues. using the emotion code, body code, and belief code, she successfully resolves the root causes in just a few sessions. simple, efficient, professional, and sustainable. she also has an interesting network of other therapists and specialists—all absolute professionals in their field.

after a scenic 20-minute cable car ride from grindelwald terminal, you arrive at männlichen, the starting point of the royal walk. we went early in the day to catch a good weather window, and it was absolutely worth it—the views were spectacular. tip: be sure to check the local swiss weather apps before you go. if it’s cloudy or raining, you’ll miss what makes this walk so special. timing it right makes all the difference. while some reviews (especially on ai or instagram) describe the walk as easy, it’s actually a steep gravel path—short but quite an incline. we saw several tourists, particularly from larger groups, struggling a bit on the way up. that said, it’s still accessible to most people with a bit of fitness. having hiked a number of peaks in the area, this was a welcome, easier option—a chance to enjoy incredible views without a full mountain trek. from the top, you can create a circular route by taking the next cable car down to wengen, continuing on to lauterbrunnen, and returning to grindelwald terminal by train via zweilütschinen. we actually chose to hike the full way down to lauterbrunnen, which offered even more amazing scenery.

after a wonderful two nights stay in january of 2014, came back for another stay in 2016. spacious rooms with luxurious beds. food was good mostly with the exception of a tough, gamey, dry steaks one night on my second stay. the staff were curteous and professional. wonderful views of the savanah from every room. about 20~30 minutes drive out from the hotel after breakfast, we came across a pride of lions napping on the low branches of a large tree. a truly unforgettable experience.

after an exhausting 18-hour journey from dar, we finally arrived at the lodge late in the evening. we drove straight up the ramp to the entrance, where the manager, sunith, warmly greeted us. the staff promptly took our luggage to our rooms, and sunith provided us with all the necessary details about breakfast, dinner, and the importance of walking with security due to the occasional presence of animals. we were escorted to our cottage and despite our fatigue, we couldn't help but admire it. it was clean, tidy, and equipped with modern amenities such as a western-style toilet, hot water shower, and bottled drinking water. security personnel escorted us between the main building and cottages in case of any run-ins with animals that may decide to pay a visit. we even spotted elephants in the distance, hyenas near the cottage and building, and a little tortoise navigating across the path. sunith and the entire staff went above and beyond to accommodate our vegetarian diet over the next couple of days - providing us with delicious breakfast, lunch and dinner. the food was good (don't expect 5-star dining in the middle of the jungle, but do expect a unique and a thousandfold more enjoyable experience to go with it). we also had the pleasure of enjoying the swimming pool with its tremendous view when we returned early from our game drive. i'd like to thank sunith and the staff - the chefs, attendants, security, and those working behind the scenes to ensure everything ran smoothly (plumbing, maintenance, etc.). managing such an operation in the middle of the jungle is no small feat, and they did an excellent job. i'm glad that happy moments tours arranged this lodge for us. i'd love to visit the lodge again, and wish them loads of success.

after attending a club unique timeshare presentation, i was given tickets for the sea angel cruise tour to phi phi island. i bought an extra ticket for 1200 bhat so my sister could attend too. the single ticket price was good compared to other tours. while the boat was beautiful, comfortable, and the crew friendly, the constant upselling of additional items became tiresome. since i paid 90-mins of my time only, i paid 1000 bhat to sit in "executive class" on the boat. this included seats on upper deck, light snacks, bigger lounge chairs that laid back with massagers, and access to the top deck of the boat. it was nice and extremely comfortable for the 4-hour rt. the stops at the various island locations were brief but nice. we couldn't get close to maya island and the pirate's cave because of the size of the boat. snorkeling was 45 mins at the national park area (another 400 bhat entrance fee) with equipment provided. it was beautiful. lunch was included, which was adequate but not exceptional and mostly indian food. overall, the tour felt geared towards maximizing profits but did provide a truly enriching experience. this was nice for comfort and planned activities. i would recommend taking a speed boat taxi to phi phi don (1 hr) and hiring a long boat to take you up close to the sites. this will give you a more relaxed and immersive phi phi island adventure.

after checking out a ton of places, we finally decided on royal mara safari lodge in mara north conservancy. i’d seen some pics online, and honestly, the rooms looked a bit old-school compared to some of the fancier resorts. i was a bit nervous about what we’d find. but as soon as we got there, everything was great! they welcomed us with some delicious apple juice, and the staff was super chill and friendly. they showed us to our room, and wow! it looked nothing like the photos i saw. they’ve totally revamped the place—it’s modern and stylish, just like the other resorts. plus, we had an amazing view of the mara river with crocs and hippos right outside! the room was perfect—bright, airy, and super private. the balcony was huge, and we even had a jacuzzi! there was this awesome guy assigned to us who showed us around and helped us get to the common areas. he even volunteered to take us out to see the hippos and crocs and gave us a full tour of the property. once we settled into our room, i was amazed by how much cabinet and storage space the room had. since we were a couple traveling, having two wash basins was so amazing ! the storage for our suitcases, toiletries, and clothes was really well thought out, so we didn’t have to live out of our bags. they had solar heaters outside each room for hot water, which was great. we did have a small issue with the hot water, but they changed our rooms right away! plus, there were no mosquitoes, though we were careful not to open the canvas too much. the place was clean, and they tidied up every day while we were out on safari. they provided a safe locker for our valuables and a 5-liter water can for drinking. the food was really good overall, but the only downside was that they served the same soup every day. a bit repetitive ! after locating the start point (turning right up a steep concrete drive near the water works) and then looking for some steps on a path to the right, the trail fairly steep, but generally easy to follow. at the top of the steps, it openes up to some shacks and a huge giant tortoise, where you follow straight on. you re-enter the woodland and there are a couple of possible routes. follow yellow dot markings on the trees and rocks. there are plenty of scramble sections and fallen trees to negotiate. again, follow the dots at any vague points. there is a tee junction near the top, turn left (yellow dot) then look for the arrow pointing straight up the steep, grippy rock. the view from the top is worth the climb as it opens up to a vast rock plateau and views over the airport to cerf island. 3.4 miles, 1650ft ascent, and 2 hrs to go up and down today. could be slippery in the wet. not well travelled but fairly easy to follow.

after seeing well over 30 shows at history, i can confidently say this is one of the best concert venues in the city. the sound is consistently great across the room - whether you’re close to the stage or near the back, the acoustics hold up. it’s also one of the more accessible venues i’ve been to - they offer designated accessible seating and staff are always helpful and accommodating. the setup feels genuinely inclusive. parking is plentiful in the surrounding area on event nights - usually in the $30-$40 range, which is steep but expected for toronto. that said, the convenience is worth it if you’re driving. one of my favourite features is the smoking area - you just need a stamp to re-enter, and they allow you to leave your drink on a table (with lids available for safety/reassurance). there’s also a table set up with cups right near the smoking section and a water refill station, so you can stay hydrated without missing the action. guest services is solid - they offer free earplugs (basic but decent) and recently introduced a “plugz” booth where you can purchase higher-end ones for around $14-$16. great to see ear safety taken seriously. food-wise, there’s pizza and candy available - overpriced, like most venues, but it hits the spot if you came straight from work or didn’t have time to eat before the show. lineups are minimal toward the end of most shows, which makes for a smooth exit compared to other downtown spots. all in all, history is well-run, thoughtfully designed, and consistently delivers a top-tier concert experience. it’s become my go-to venue in the city, and i’m always happy to return.

ah, fort denison—known to us convicts as "pinchgut." let me tell you about my unforgettable week there. it all started when i "borrowed" the sergeant's rum ration. as punishment, they ferried me to that rocky island in the middle of sydney harbour. the place was officially called rock island, but we all knew it as pinchgut—a name that fit all too well. the island was barely more than a sandstone lump, rising about 15 meters above the water. they'd maroon us there with nothing but bread and water, leaving our stomachs grumbling louder than the waves. some said "pinchgut" was a nautical term for a narrow passage, but we knew it described our pinched bellies perfectly. on my first night, i discovered i wasn't alone. a skeleton hung from a gibbet—a grim reminder of francis morgan, a fellow convict executed years before. they'd left his bones there to deter any thoughts of escape. with nothing to do but count seagulls, i decided to make friends with them. i named the boldest one "governor" and trained him to steal extra bread from the guards' supply boat. for a moment, i fancied myself the king of pinchgut, ruling over my feathered subjects. but all reigns end. after a week, they fetched me back to the mainland, thinner but wiser. i never "borrowed" rum again, but i did gain a lifelong respect for seagulls and a story that could make even the hardest lag laugh.

al azhar park in cairo, egypt, is a stunning blend of history, elegance, and natural beauty. perched on a hill in the heart of historic cairo, it offers sweeping views of the city’s skyline, including the minarets of ancient mosques and the citadel of saladin. once a centuries-old landfill, the site was transformed into a lush 74-acre green haven through a major restoration project initiated by the aga khan trust for culture and completed in 2005. the park features manicured gardens, fountains, walking paths, and traditional islamic architecture inspired by historic design. intricate stonework, shaded pavilions, and serene water features add to its charm. more than just a park, al azhar is a symbol of renewal—breathing life into an old urban area while preserving its rich cultural heritage. it’s not only a place to relax but also a bridge between cairo’s past and present.

al mouj marina is a stunning waterfront destination located in muscat, oman. it offers breathtaking views of the sea and the surrounding landscape. the atmosphere is vibrant yet relaxing, making it an excellent place to unwind. whether you're looking to take a leisurely stroll along the marina or simply enjoy the scenic views, you'll find a calm and inviting environment. **facilities and activities:** the marina is well-equipped with various facilities, including clean restrooms, comfortable seating areas, and beautifully designed walking paths. you can often see luxurious boats and yachts, which add to the charm of the location. there are also opportunities for water activities like boating and fishing, making it an ideal spot for adventure enthusiasts. families can enjoy picnics, walks, or playtime along the waterfront. **dining and shopping:** al mouj marina boasts a variety of dining options, from casual cafes to upscale restaurants. you can savor fresh seafood and local dishes while taking in the picturesque views. additionally, there are shops and boutiques where you can find souvenirs, local crafts, and unique items, making it a great place to pick up something special. **overall experience:** visitors to al mouj marina often leave feeling rejuvenated and happy. it’s a wonderful spot for nature lovers, water sports enthusiasts, or anyone looking to relax in a beautiful setting. whether you’re visiting alone, with friends, or with family, you’re likely to have a memorable experience at al mouj marina. in summary, al mouj marina is a lovely destination offering stunning views, enjoyable activities, and a peaceful atmosphere. if you’re in the muscat area, it’s definitely worth a visit!

al-hakim mosque is a peaceful and historically significant place, offering a serene atmosphere amidst the bustle of cairo. the architecture is beautiful and the sense of calm inside the mosque is truly special. however, it would be more welcoming if those at the entrance didn’t directly ask visitors for money simply for entering what is, after all, a house of god. donations should always be voluntary, and many people are happy to give when they feel respected and not pressured.

al-hakim mosque, located near the historic bab al-futuh gate in cairo, is a stunning example of fatimid architecture and one of the city's hidden gems. unlike some of the more frequently visited mosques, this one offers a more peaceful and contemplative atmosphere, making it an ideal place to explore islamic history without the crowds. the mosque’s scale is immediately impressive—its massive stone minarets, which date back to the 11th century, are among the oldest in cairo. the open courtyard, surrounded by elegant arcades, creates a sense of space and tranquility. recent renovations have been thoughtfully done, preserving the mosque's historical elements while making it clean and welcoming for visitors. inside, the simplicity of the prayer hall contrasts beautifully with the grandeur of its exterior. the columns and high ceilings give it an airy, spiritual feeling. it’s easy to imagine how this space has served worshippers for centuries, yet it remains functional and alive with quiet activity even today. visitors will appreciate how accessible and visitor-friendly the mosque is. entry is free, and staff or volunteers are often present to share information or answer questions. just like at other religious sites, it's important to dress modestly and be mindful of prayer times. the surrounding area also offers a glimpse into old cairo’s vibrant street life, adding depth to the experience. overall, al-hakim mosque is a must-see for those interested in cairo’s islamic heritage. it may not be as famous as al-azhar or the sultan hassan mosque, but it offers a serene, authentic encounter with fatimid architecture and spiritual history. a truly enriching stop for travelers looking to go beyond the typical tourist path.

aliʻiolani hale since 1874, ali‘iōlani hale has been the home of the hawai‘i supreme court. the building was commissioned by king kamehameha v and built between 1871 and 1874. the name means “house of heavenly kings.” the name ali‘iōlani was one of the given names of kamehameha v. he laid the cornerstone in 1872, but died before the building was completed. it was dedicated in 1874 by king david kalākaua. originally designed as a palace, king kamehameha v instead decided to use it as a government office building for the growing kingdom. it held the executive offices, legislature and judiciary. after the overthrow of the sovereign in 1893, the legislature and administrative functions were relocated to iolani palace, leaving ali‘iōlani hale for the courts. the hawai‘i judiciary remains the primary occupant. the king kamehameha v judiciary history center is also located in the building and provides public exhibits and programs related to hawaii's legal history. the address is 417 south king street, honolulu.

alright, i'll start by saying that the family who runs this place is incredibly kind...but after reading all the positive reviews i feel compelled to write a warning for other travelers since all the other reviewers seem to overlook certain things! first, you need to take a taxi out to what is basically a trash dump where they pick you up, you'll need a way to coordinate with them in spanish via cell phone prior. don't mind the dog fights at the pickup location. second, the rooms are very basic with only one light and no other electricity. there are plenty of blankets, but forget hanging out outside of your bed without your winter jacket on. third, there is no plumbing. you literally have an outhouse in your room!!! and since the outhouse door isn't designed to close all the way, you smell it! your outhouse has no running water. you get 2 bottles of water in your outhouse when you arrive that is also your drinking water. fourth, i arrived at 7 pm starving, so i got the dinner there. there is no menu, you just get whatever they're making and you have no way of getting any other food. they served a huge plate of meat and veggies with a sauce on it, but since i'm vegetarian they just gave me a child sized portion of steamed veggies and a few pieces of potato with no seasoning, oil, spices, butter, nothing!! went to bed hungry and disgusted and left early the next morning, cancelling my second night. saw a bunch of white tourists on the other island weaving grass with a bunch of other white tourists on my boat ride out of there and had to roll my eyes. sorry folks, but they're spending their days entertaining you for money. this isn't some special authentic experience, they want your money! if you're the kind of traveler who gets a high from being uncomfortable, and thinks tourist traps are authentic experiences with locals you'll love this place.

amazing and romantic experience on the bridge, if you get to find on left hand side the old men doing caricatures that is completing the experience. the charles bridge in prague is truly one of the most magical places in the city. whether you're visiting during the early morning mist or catching the golden hues of sunset, the atmosphere is nothing short of enchanting. walking across the historic stones, surrounded by baroque statues and the gentle flow of the vltava river below, you feel like you’ve stepped into a fairytale. what makes the experience even more romantic and memorable is the vibrant life along the bridge. musicians fill the air with soulful tunes, street performers entertain with their unique talents, and artists bring the bridge to life with their creativity. if you're lucky, you’ll stumble upon the old men doing caricatures on the left-hand side — a charming and nostalgic touch that completes the experience. watching them sketch brings a sense of timeless artistry, and getting your own portrait done is a fun, personal souvenir to take home. as day turns into night, the view of prague castle illuminated in the distance is breathtaking. the bridge becomes a living postcard, buzzing with emotion, history, and charm. whether you’re a solo traveler, a couple in love, or a family exploring the city, the charles bridge offers a romantic and unforgettable slice of prague.

amazing experience kiting under the golden gate bridge, and downwind ride back to treasure island! john is very cool, fun and professional, he’ll do everything to make the most of your time. 3.30: meeting john at treasure island. he’s ready to go, we jump on the boat for a nice 20mins boat ride to the bridge, passing by alcatraz for some nice shots 3.50: getting ready, pumping the kite, enjoying the view. nice surprise, a whale passes near the boat! 4pm: waterstart from the boat with a 15m kite. john has all sizes and will change if needed, as the wind may change during the session. in my session, the wind was light and stable at the start, much stronger at the end, but i sticked with the 15m. 4-4.40: riding beyond the bridge, under, back and forth. the water is very different depending where you go. you’ll have some flat water, some choppy areas, and some big waves where the current is strong. it’s a wide area where you can really enjoy your ride. 4.40-6.10: slowly getting downwind and riding with the view of the bridge, the city, alcatraz. i saw a couple of dolphins who passed by, very emotional moments! 6.30: back at treasure island. john airdrops me some very cool pics and videos, and he’s even created a very professional movie, which is now on my insta (and his). hope you liked my story and will want to do it. for me, it’s a must do, and the fun/cost ratio is definitely worth it!!! enjoy!

amazing experience. on the expensive side, but amazing nevertheless. the 4 day trip started with the low altitude flight over the scenic coast in cessna caravan. the pilot made announcements as we passed points of interests. we landed on lizard island which looked amazing too! the boat was clean and nice. the crew was amazing - i pretty much would have to give a shout-out to everyone, but i specifically want to call out rens - he was very proactive, professional and helpful (helped me burn out my mask because it was fogging, took videos when jumping into water, and was great overall). also calling out anton. but honestly, everyone. the chef (murray) also cooked amazing dishes. leo was a great trip director. diving was great. we were lucky enough to hit the trifecta (osprey, bougainville and holmes reefs). in terms of value for money, i would say that for the same amount of money we had a trip in bali with driver & accomodations for 12 days + 3 days of sight seeing. and arguably the diving in bali was the same or more fun. but this doesn't take away from this trip. 5/5 experience! also a huge shout out to sops for entering the water. the procedures for checking air for every diver while strictly not necessary, greatly increased the safety of diving. i also appreciated evening presentations and trivia night. the engine room tour was great too! overall it was a lot of fun.

amazing hike. park along the street in the neighborhood, being mindful of driveways and fire hydrants. the cul-de-sac is a no parking zone. there is restoration work going on right now, and you may be able to help carry water. the trail is very well marked (the valley and ridge hike start at the same place). there are a series of switchbacks, followed by some steep stairs (my knee was definitely sore the next day- some of the stairs were mid-thigh in height). the summit is fairly large and open, with breathtaking views. no rock scrambles, and no danger of falling from steep drop-offs. i imagine this could get pretty muddy and slick, but it was dry when i went. at the last stretch, the path is enclosed on both sides by a spikey plant, so you may want to wear pants (but i saw plenty of people in shorts). bring 2l of water or more, and plan for 3-4 hours to get to the summit and back. i went on a friday morning and it was fairly popular, i had to park pretty far away and i passed at least 50 people during the hike.

amazing muffulleta - best by far in new orleans! i ate multiple muffuletta's while here in nola and none come even close to the taste, flavor, and seasoning as the original home of the mufalleta (go figure). for me, the difference is the bread, the quality of meat, the volume and quality of the toppings, and the seasoning/oil. everywhere else i ate the muffuletta, the bread was thinner and didn't have the same flavor and fresh bread taste as what you'd find in a bakery. central grocery's bread tasted like something you'd get fresh from a high-quality bakery, which any sandwich maker knows the bread is one of the most important aspects of the sandwich. the second difference is the quality of the meat. anyone who goes to a traditional deli, especially like in new york knows the difference between high quality meat and low quality meat which can be tasted immediately. the same thing is true with the cheese. at central grocery, it's clear they have one of the highest quality meat selections in new orleans which generally makes the sandwich a completely different and higher quality taste. also, they sell the highest quality ingredients including fresh high-quality pickles, olives, and a bunch of other condiments separately, like what a bakery or specialized grocery store would have. the quality of the olives alone along with the other condiments, take the flavor and taste of the sandwich above the others i ate. lastly is the seasoning and oil used on the bread and meat. every other muffulleta i ate in new orleans literally tasted dry, even though the cheese was melted. it was because they all lacked the oil and seasoning that is used at central grocery, where even without the cheese being melted, the sandwich is moist and delicious. i thought i'd have to eat it heated which i did try as well. but in all honesty, i can eat it completely cold as it is provided and it tasted just as good due to the volume of oil and seasoning used on the bread and meat. when purchased you can get the muffuletta in either a half or a full and each comes with heating instructions. if you do decide to heat it, it's worth trying & makes it equally delicious. i prefer crunchier bread versus softer bread where the top and bottom is crunchy but the middle is soft and fluffy so that's the way i made it when heating it, but it comes with instructions to keep the bread soft if preferred. i normally eat a foot long hoagie sub when eating a sandwich and i could only finish half of the sandwich since it is huge! (see the attached photo and note that the plate used in the photo is a large dinner plate). overall, i didn't find another muffuletta place that made could even compare to the original at central grocery, but i'll keep looking. either way, if you are visiting new orleans and you like a quality sandwich with fresh baked bread, high quality deli and ingredients, and amazing seasoning, you need to make a stop at central grocery!

amazing places to visit. take water and sun cream because it is 15 mimutes walk in one way. and better come here in the morning. this is one of the most iconic places in namibia. it's a beautiful area where you'll find sun-scorched tree stumps rising from a cracked salt flat, surrounded by towering red dunes. deadvlei means "dead marsh." vlei is the afrikaans word for lake or swamp, and dead because everything around it seems otherworldly. deadvlei is a white clay pan located in sossusvlei, a valley between dunes in namib-naukluft park in namibia. it is the oldest desert in the world, dating back over 80 million years. the trees are estimated to be around 800 years old and died because there was no longer enough water to survive. the remaining tree skeletons are now black and scorched by the intense heat. from parking, you can pay 10$ for a jeep 4x4 to take you here if you can not go with your car.

amsterdam has no shortage of canal cruises, but we chose this company for the personal touch – and the fact they use electric boats. it was a last-minute booking on a scorching hot day, and we were so glad we did! our skipper was well-travelled and knowledgeable, sharing just the right mix of local history and stories about the people. with only around 12 guests onboard, there was plenty of space to relax, and drinks were available even if you hadn’t pre-booked a package. seeing amsterdam from the water gave us a whole new perspective, and it was such a calm, enjoyable way to round off our holiday. highly recommend this company and their cruise!

amsterdamse bos is a serene escape just outside the city buzz. lush woodlands, wide meadows, and calm waterways welcome all. perfect for cycling, rowing, or just lazing under the trees. kids adore the goat farm, adults find peace in nature’s hug. it’s amsterdam’s green lung—wild yet wonderfully tamed.

an absolute gem and a must-visit for anyone interested in vietnamese history and culture. we were immediately struck by the lively and beautifully maintained gardens. they offer a serene escape from the city's hustle and bustle, perfect for a leisurely stroll and some quiet reflection. the architecture is truly stunning, showcasing traditional vietnamese design with intricate details and a sense of timeless grandeur. each courtyard and gate tells a story, and you can truly feel the historical significance of the place. briefly, the temple of literature was established in 1070 as vietnam's first national university. it was dedicated to confucius, scholars, and sages, and for centuries, it served as a center of learning and intellectual pursuit for the country's elite. walking through its hallowed halls, you can almost imagine the students and scholars who once studied there, striving for knowledge and wisdom. overall, it's a wonderfully preserved site that offers a fascinating glimpse into vietnam's past. highly recommend!

an absolute gem of a shrine ⛩️ go-ō features the wild boar and is a shinto shrine dedicated to leg and hip health. you can also make other health-related offerings here. has numerous boar statues and also a collection of boars from around the country. so lovely! open early in the morning. ❗please be respectful when visiting places of worship.

an absolute hidden gem in golden gate park. while not too far away from the de young, this garden was empty when i visited. if you’re in the area, definitely stop by to take in the trees, the prose, and the peace.

an absolute hidden gem next to some of dubrovnik’s bigger beaches but this was by far, the best! it’s quite steep to get to with a 5 minute walk down various stairs from the top of old town but well worth it. lovely azure water, sunbeds that you can rent for €25 each (all come with umbrellas), a bar and restaurant and good music beach played throughout. it looks crowded but plenty of space for everyone. was so glad that tiktok helped us come across this!

an absolute must on the island. the walk is relatively easy. not too steep at any point. it took us around 4 hrs in total, including the break at the waterfall. the views and sceneries are breathtaking. you hike all along the levada until you reach the waterfalls. there are a few tunnels so a headlamp or a phone with flashlights is needed. and when busy (which i guess it’s always) the passing along the route can be a bit tricky. and the parking is very challenging. we arrive at 9.00 which was perfect. if you arrive much later, i’d suspect you struggle to park.

an absolute must see geological attraction when visiting yellowstone. all of the geysers and and other geological sites are definitely worth seeing, but the glory hole is just gorgeous. it's mesmerising. quick note, the morning glory is a one mile walk from the old faithful entrance. it's mostly flat terrain and is paved, but on a hot day it's a trek.

an absolute must see when in rome. now the sight of christian worship. this 1900 hundred year old structure was a place of pagan worship before. now filled with the life history of chirst. the reverence the crowd has here is inspiring. the architecture is like nothing else on earth. this place is massive! the story of the unique concrete, the giant open space at top and the marbled columns are magnificent. you must visit.

an absolute must-see when visiting paris. even though parts of notre-dame are still under restoration, the cathedral remains one of the most stunning examples of gothic architecture in the world. the level of detail in the stonework, the flying buttresses, and the iconic twin towers are breathtaking. you can walk around the outside and admire the building from multiple angles, including from the seine riverbanks — which offer some of the best photo opportunities. the atmosphere is peaceful and deeply historical. as of now, interior access is limited due to ongoing renovations (following the 2019 fire), but the progress is impressive, and you can still appreciate the grandeur of the structure. there are also information panels around the site explaining the history and reconstruction process. 👉 tip: visit early in the morning or around sunset for the best light and fewer crowds. 👉 nearby: don’t miss square jean xxiii behind the cathedral — a quiet little garden with a beautiful view.

an absolute no-go to book with this company. we had the worst galapagos tour experience with whale shark dive center. it all started with the organization: no welcome, no explanation, no communication. we gathered at 6:00 am, returned at 5:00 pm, and only snorkeled for about 1.5 hours. by noon, we had only been in the water for 30 minutes. the boat was terrible — a speedboat that constantly splashed us with water, so we ended up sitting on the floor most of the time. there was no information shared about the itinerary or where we were. several planned locations were skipped without any explanation. during the snorkeling, it was just free swimming — no guidance, no “tour” element at all. they promised photos and videos, but none were taken. the gopro footage (which we shot ourselves using their equipment) was of such poor quality that none of it turned out usable. the tour is called the “cormorant tour,” but when we finally saw one, we left after just two minutes. the staff was literally sleeping on the boat. worst of all: they hit two manta rays with the boat — and laughed about it. for a company that claims to be nature-oriented, this is nothing short of irresponsible and disgusting. even the price was questionable — people on board paid between $160 and $250 for exactly the same tour. when we tried to discuss our concerns with roy and daniel, a normal conversation was impossible. they turned off the lights and left their own office while our entire group was still inside. eventually, the neighboring restaurant had to threaten to call the police if we didn’t leave. whale shark dive center is unprofessional, uninterested, disrespectful, and absolutely not recommended — just like their tour. they treat the galapagos as a money-making product instead of showing genuine care for the animals. save yourself the money and the disappointment.

an absolute proper 5 star tented camp in serengeti with more than we could ask for. great, wide and spacious tents with amazing and modern amenities. excellent food, great staff, spectacular views. just what you need after a long safari drive in the vast plains of serengeti.

an absolute south florida treasure! i’ve been coming to monkey jungle for over 35 years, and it never gets old. in fact, the experience just gets better and better every time i visit. it’s such a unique place where humans are caged and monkeys run wild—you won’t find anything else like it! the staff is always friendly, knowledgeable, and clearly care about the animals. feeding the monkeys is such a fun and unforgettable experience, and it’s perfect for all ages. the grounds are well maintained, and the educational aspects make it not just entertaining, but meaningful too. monkey jungle has been a part of my life for decades, and i always recommend it to friends, family, and visitors. if you’re in south florida , this is a must-visit spot. i can’t wait to go back—again and again!

an absolute thrill from start to finish! set in a beautiful location, this waterfall canyoning experience combines adrenaline with breathtaking scenery. our top-quality, highly experienced guide had a great sense of humour and made us feel safe and confident the whole way. his fantastic local knowledge added depth to the journey, sharing stories about the area’s nature and culture. the day ended perfectly with an authentic traditional experience tasting toddy—a unique and delicious local touch.

an absolutely breathtaking place and a must-visit in croatia. the lakes, waterfalls, and forest paths look like something from a fairytale. everything is well-organized, with different routes to choose from depending on how much you want to walk. parking is inside the park and costs €2 per hour. there’s even a small market right next to the parking lot for snacks and drinks. from the parking, it’s about a 5-minute walk to the park entrance. we chose route e, which took around 1.5–2 hours with plenty of breaks for photos and videos — the views are stunning all along the way. the route ends at the top of the park, where you take one of the panoramic buses back to the entrance. the ticket price is €40 per person, and it already includes the bus and boat rides inside the park, which makes the visit even more enjoyable. it can get crowded, but the natural beauty makes it all worth it.

an absolutely incredible experience with horizon helicopters in maun, botswana! the reception staff were exceptionally friendly and went out of their way to accommodate our same-day flight request in the late afternoon. they even walked us outside to recommend a nearby coffee shop to wait in. our pilot, rob, was fantastic—engaging, professional, and ensured we had ample opportunities to take breathtaking photos during our scenic flight over the okavango delta. landing in the wild for a champagne toast was the perfect touch to an unforgettable adventure. horizon helicopters offers a range of services, including doors-off scenic flights, photography flights, private lodge transfers, and unique experiences like cultural village visits and tsodilo hills tours, all operated with highly experienced pilots using safe, reliable helicopters like the bell jet ranger and robinson series. their commitment to personalized, high-quality service makes them a must for anyone exploring botswana’s wilderness. highly recommend!

an absolutely magical evening! the seine cruise at night was breathtaking the sparkling city lights, the illuminated eiffel tower, and the romantic atmosphere made it unforgettable. the champagne was the perfect touch, adding elegance to the experience. everything was perfectly organized, the staff was welcoming, and the views were simply stunning. one of the best experiences in paris highly recommended!

an absolutely remarkable cultural landmark. the central prang is intricately decorated and beautifully reflects the sunlight, creating a striking impression from both near and far. standing by the river, it is not only a masterpiece of thai craftsmanship but also a place where the city slows down and breathes. watching the dawn from wat arun is an experience that stays with you long after you leave. there are rental shops around wat arun and also near the ferry piers, so you can easily dress up just for your visit and photos.

an absolutely stunning ancient woodland, i would recommend everyone visit! i was a bit worried at first not being able to find the tallest tree in northern europe, but the woodland is very clearly signposted. well worth taking the time to enjoy this epic place.
an absolutely stunning and sacred experience. i almost skipped it and wow would i have been a sucker. the building is stunning in its grandeur, and the chambers were quite moving to visit.

an absolutely stunning temple. i found beauty in every corner of this place. it is not located in the city center which creates an atmosphere of serenity, yet still accessible by grab / bolt. it's also free entry!

an absolutely unforgettable experience! i highly recommend it to anyone looking for quality and professionalism. the staff went above and beyond they were incredibly friendly, attentive, and made me feel welcome from the very beginning. every detail was handled with care, and their level of professionalism truly stood out. i couldn’t have asked for a better experience. i loved every moment!

an absolutely wonderful experience. my wife and i opted for the hamman and serenity massage. both were fantastic. we arrived an hour before our first treatment to enjoy the pools, one warm, one (outside) cool. staff were on hand to guide us through the process, and around the complex (which was labyrinthian), with plenty of mint tea and bottles of water to keep us hydrated. we opted to take our treatments together in our private rooms. the ladies providing the treatments were very professional and skilled. the serenity massage was unforgettable and left us both unbelievably relaxed! a must of you have the time in marrakech.
an absolutely wonderful, and well priced experience. would recommend 10/10 times! all three experiences (parasailing, under the sea walk and the tub ride) are all worth it, and well priced!

an adventure to remember! we were lucky to see all the animals possible: lions, rhinos, elephants, weldebeests, cheetahs, springboks, lot af different antelopes and birds, jackals. thanks to our guides max and rosh.

an affordable traditional market suitable for the whole family to eat and shopping. not only can understand the living habits and daily routines of the people, also it is such a good place to buy different snacks for tasting.

an airboat tour really completes your experience of the everglades. the little crocodile show was fun and she did a great job with the crowd and the animals. we saw a few gators and birds and it was nice and relaxing ride. i guess i was just expecting a bit more of a national park-like experience and education but it's definitely more of a tourist experience which is fine, just manage your expectations. facilities were great and the restaurant was okay. they add a charge if you use card in the gift shop and they add an automatic 18% gratuity in the restaurant even to a party of one.

an all day adventure awaits for anyone at capilano suspension bridge. it's got amazing sights and sounds. if you are feeling adventurous, you can go one step further & do the tree top adventure after a nature walking tour. there's a few places to sit and relax once you cross the bridge and have some snacks / ice creams / cookies. after that peruse around the gift shop and call it a day!

an alternative to reach waisai (which is the main island of geopark raja ampat) and considerably affordable. you could buy the boat ticket on the ticket booth with various range of price (start from idr 125.000 for the economic class). however, if you do not want to spend a money to pay for the luggage-carrier, please hold your belongings close to you and hold it by yourself until you reach the boat. because, the luggage carrier will take your belongings quickly after you depart from your car and you have to pay for their 'help'. also, look at the boat schedule and plan your flight to sorong carefully so you will not miss the boat.

an amazing ancient city carved in the rocks. the site is huge with multiple transport options available such as mules and horses. we decided to hike all the way to the last building called the safe. on the way there are multiple amazing buildings and sculptures to admire. it is truly an amazing place to visit and spend a full day there. they even do events at night with candles and lights. tickets are expensive but it is definitely worth it.

an amazing and amusing experience. and especial thank to the wonderful crew who guided the visit : selim, michael and the beautiful blonde driver whom made it possible!!! the service since the beggining to the end was pretty charm and intereseting, bc they told you about the history of the channels and some fun-facts about them most of the time, basically you enjoy but learn at the same time. i trully recommend this company, it really worth your time and your money.
an amazing building. i watched swan lake. the seat, lights and vibe was very good. i will try to come back again.😎👌
an amazing club to get you out on the waters of false creek and beyond. choose a kayak, stand-up, outrigger and more.

an amazing diving experience with karen as our instructor! karen is an expert in the marine world, and her knowledge truly enriched our adventure. despite doing a shallow dive, we were amazed by the variety of marine species we got to observe thanks to her expert guidance. it was thrilling to see species we had never encountered before, and it was incredible to witness how the fish seemed to follow karen, almost as if they were drawn to her. unfortunately, the current was quite strong that day, which prevented us from crossing the barrier to explore another location. however, even with this limitation, we had over an hour of bottom time, allowing us to fully enjoy the experience and immerse ourselves in the beauty of the ocean. in summary, despite the natural challenges, our diving experience with karen was exceptional. i would highly recommend this adventure to anyone looking to explore the wonders of the underwater world with an expert and passionate guide like karen. thank you for an unforgettable experience!

an amazing escape from the busy streets of prague. we started by the one end next to the science museum and enjoyed some beers at the beer gardens there. then, following the park will lead you to a new man-made pond which is definitely worth visiting.

an amazing evening on the nile cruise! if you want 100% enjoyment and unforgettable emotions — choose nile maxim. everything was top-notch: the service, the atmosphere, the food, and the entertainment program. the restaurant was a pleasant surprise — the food was truly delicious and varied. i had grilled shrimp, and they were absolutely delightful: juicy, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. and the chocolate cake for dessert was the highlight of the evening — rich, smooth, and simply amazing! the live music added a special charm, creating a cozy and festive mood. and the tanoura and belly dance show — it was true artistry! so colorful, energetic, and mesmerizing. and of course, the views… the night-time nile, the city lights reflecting on the water — it was breathtakingly beautiful and romantic. nile maxim isn’t just a dinner cruise — it’s a whole experience that’s truly worth having. highly recommended!

an amazing experience in the heart of cartagena’s old town. this lively and colorful square is always buzzing with life—street performers, local artists, and vendors fill the space with energy and culture. colonial-era buildings surround the plaza, many of them housing charming restaurants, bars, and cafés with plenty of outdoor seating. it’s a wonderful place to sit back, enjoy a drink or a meal, and take in the vibrant atmosphere. the iconic santo domingo church anchors the plaza with its beautiful colonial architecture and storied history. a well-known legend claims the devil once tried to leap from its roof. just steps away lies the bronze sculpture gertrudis by fernando botero—touching her is said to bring luck in love, making it a favorite photo spot for visitors. whether you come for the food, the music, the architecture, or the people-watching, this historic square is one of the most memorable places in the city. there’s so much to see, taste, and explore—you won’t want to miss it. that said, one word of caution: i did encounter a minor issue with a fruit vendor near the plaza. he initially quoted 4,000 pesos for a cup of watermelon slices, which seemed reasonable based on past experience. however, when i paid with a 50,000-peso bill, he returned only 35,000 pesos in change and insisted the price was 15,000. it served as a valuable reminder to avoid using large bills with street vendors whenever possible.

an amazing experience to be in person. this was the house of caiaphas. beneath the house there's a small dark pit where our lord jesus was detained overnight before he was crucified the following day. a must visit place in one's life time.

an enjoyable sunset tour with transport included - we were picked up at 3pm and brought to the pier. after boarding the boat and having a safety briefing, the crew busied themselves with serving drinks to everyone and preparing a bbq dinner - bbq chicken breast, prawns, tomato pasta, greek salad, bread and dips. there were 3 swim stops - first one in the sulphurous waters with patches of warm water from the volcanic hot springs - do note that the iron oxide can possibly stain your swimsuit and jewellery - so wear a dark coloured swimsuit if possible. next one was just off the red sand beach and last one was after the dinner in crystal clear waters with some small fishes. floats and snorkel equipment are provided. it was pretty choppy while we were watching the sunset due to the winds. the crew especially joe and nadia were very attentive and helpful and ensured that everyone was well taken care of. highly recommend this tour as although i was seasick, the views are spectacular and really a great add on to the land tours in santorini.

an excellent escape rooms series. we had so much fun with charlie who hosted us warmly and enthusiastically. this has been an excellent experience and very happy to find this in london. thanks to great staff!
an excellent experience for all the family and friends here in the patagonia region. i recommend it to everyone!

an excellent experience, very unique and wonderful, great choice for a sunday morning! all employees were very kind and willing to inform you and guide you in order to have a unique experience. a great idea, and the gifts from the store worth checking them out too, because they are indeed very unique!
an excellent farmers market -- fresh fruit and veg, cakes, wines from the region, excellent selection, too
an excellent ger camp in beautiful scenery: comfortable gers, modern and spotlessly clean bathroom blocks, great meals and top breakfast buffet in the restaurant.

an excellent morning hike if you are staying in san pedro. we went on a weekday and while we saw some other people, they were pretty sparse. it's a flat easy hike with a climb at the end. nothing too difficult going up, a little more challenging the other way, but nothing a novice that's in reasonable condition can't manage. it's beautiful as well. enjoy.

an exceptional experience in the heart of rome, with a stunning collection of masterpieces—wide ranging, eclectic, beautifully displayed and with gorgeous, impeccably maintained gardens with stunning views across the eternal city. the unusual tintoretto narcissus and the three salviati works alone are worth the trip, but masterpieces by van dyck, titian, passarotti, bronzino, allori, rosa, and dozens of others leave a lasting impression, as well as the palazzo itself, rich, magnificent and in impeccable condition. only drawback is the fact that you can only take self-guided tours on saturday, between 09:00 and 13:00. clear some space in your schedule to hit it!

an exceptional hike that will challenge you mentally and physically. depending on your level of physical activity it is not a trail i would recommend for someone just starting out. a wide trailhead at the beginning leads you into a well shaded forest and a small lake. the trail was wet and had some very soft areas with deeper areas of mud. the trail narrows in other parts where feet are in close proximity to one another. this is one of the best trails i have hiked thus far. be sure to make the extra 2.2 km walk to lagos do patas and up pico gaspar.

an exceptional journey. we told the expiration for my 40th birthday and the ride into the grand canyon was amazing. amazing staff and such a cool way to see the grand canyon from a different perspective. we flew out the approximate 45 minutes with the two of us in the front with the pilot and three other passengers in the back seat. once you land the provide you with a little snack and champagne toast. i highly recommend this as a part of your next trip to las vegas.

an exceptional place. the building itself is an outstanding example of italian architecture and it dates back to the 1920s. it houses some of the finest collections of paintings, sculptures and other objects. its collection of romanesque church paintings is noteworthy. it also contains some wonderful displays of local catalan art.be advised that there are lots stairs to get to the building even using escalators and great views from outside whit spectacular views of barcelona. the museum has a nice restaurant with wonderful views so you can take a lunch break and spend the day. there is also a casual cafe outside the museum with quick meals and refreshments.

an exceptional, haunting place far from the maddening crowds - essential deserted, just you and the dead. extraordinary mausoleums, if many under-maintained. at 200 pesos, the entrance fee is ludicrously low for the experience. consider tipping the under-paid reception staff as compensation!

an experience that i'll do it again and again. it is the best museum i have been to. i'll explain: first you could buy tickets on line or at gates ... no difference. tickets for egyptian (guided tour) are 350 for adults and 175 for kids or students. it's free for many categories like old veterans, martyrs families, public colleges of architecture and antique etc. it's cheaper for non-guided tour but i don't recommend it. there are golf cars at the entrance to get you to the museum for free. once you in you will be taken by the majesty of ramsis ii statue in front of you. you can take good photos here. also there's another photos spot on the statue's left hand (you can find my tut ankh amon photo). you can check the 10 statues of zoser also. when your time for the guided tour comes (every hour there's one) you will go with one of the professional tour guides (mine was robert rauf ... excellent one). he will go through the grand stairs then the 12 exhibition halls .... where the magic starts. the way they arranged the halls is perfect and the tour guide is cleverly go through the story of the oldest civilization on earth. the tour will take 90 min. and be aware... it will start exactly on time after you finish you can complete browsing the gallery or go for an authentic egyptian food at zouba restaurant or grab a cup of coffee at starbucks or buy some pharoah like jewelry or just get a memory gift from the official gift shop before you leave.

an experience to be repeated! you can't say you've seen venice without having taken a tour of the canals! our tour with livio was magical, thanks to him we were able to see venice through the eyes of a venetian.

an extremely spacious park with lots of fresh air and beautiful scenery to look at almost every turn. there's a bunch of cafés around the area if interested to sit and chill after a run or cycle. roads and pavements there are reasonably wide for cyclists to ride on and occasionally you get to see a range of animals there (otters, monitor lizards). it's a nice place to go to if you're thinking of a nice evening walk.

an historical place with rich history and a beautiful place of worship. it’s popular with visitors and locals alike and have great atmosphere. the place is a must visit once when you’re in kowloon, hong kong.

an icon of hawaiian history and heritage. the guided audio tour was very well organized without being overwhelming. the information presented in the audio narration was concise without missing important details - there were many excerpts included from letters and diaries of the hawaiian royals and their associates which added great atmosphere to the overall experience. the palace itself is beautiful and very well maintained. there are many spots on the palace lawns to sit and relax and take in the surroundings. there's also a massive banyan tree behind the palace, not sure how old, but nonetheless magnificent to behold. highly recommend visiting the iolani palace if you can.

an icon of luxury and elegance! ✨ from the moment you arrive, you’re treated like royalty. the architecture is breathtaking – truly a 7-star experience. 🏨 inside, every detail oozes opulence, from the gold accents to the world-class service. ✨ the dining options are exquisite, and the sea views are unforgettable. 🌊 whether you're staying or just visiting, it's a must-see landmark that defines dubai’s luxury lifestyle. 🇦🇪

an icon of the emirati landscape...so much more than just a tall building. we visited for birthday celebrations in the atmosphere restaurant for afternoon tea. the views, the ride up in the lift, are all an occasion. from entry via the armani hotel to ones chosen activity. then there's also the impressive photo opportunity of the exterior views. definitely make this end part if your itinerary, if looking to see some off resort sights.

an iconic and majestic monument in the heart of rome! the vittorio emanuele ii monument is not only historically significant, but also visually stunning – with its grand architecture, towering columns, and impressive statues. don’t miss the panoramic terrace at the top; the view over rome is simply breathtaking. it’s a must-visit for anyone exploring the city. take your time to walk around, soak in the history, and enjoy the atmosphere.

an iconic gateway into history walking through pile gate felt like stepping into a living medieval storybook. the grand stone entrance, perfectly preserved, leads right into the heart of dubrovnik's old town. it's not just a gate—it's a passage into centuries of history, with fortified walls, watchtowers, and a palpable sense of the past. as a world traveler and local guide, i was immediately captivated by the combination of architectural beauty and historical significance. whether you’re entering at sunset or catching the morning light, the stone glows with an old-world charm that’s impossible to ignore. perfect for photographers, history lovers, and those who just want to soak in the magic of one of europe’s most iconic walled cities. a must-see stop on your dubrovnik adventure.

an iconic modern landmark in prague. the dancing house’s unique, flowing design stands out beautifully against the city’s historic architecture. a must-see for architecture lovers and a great spot for photos by the river.

an iconic place to visit when in puerto rico. on the weekends this place becomes an outdoor club. tons of people visit to hear music, dance, eat and drink. they have various restaurants and bars to keep you happy. it is an awesome vibe. plenty of lights, neon, and music. parking is tough but they have various parking lots in the area. drinks are cheap and the food is good.
an iconic statue of the first king of the united hawaiian islands. you shouldn't miss a visit when staying in honolulu.

an ideal place to overlook the bay and watch the activity below. easy walking trail with lovely views of the coastline and little rock pools where you can take a quick dip on a hot summer's day. with little benches along the way, it makes for a scenic and ideal picnic spot.

an ideal space to share with the little ones at home, the museum is a journey through the history of cuban puppets and allows us to take a look at this art in the rest of the world. the experience is complete by witnessing a puppet show on site, every day of the weekend.

an important and significant landmark in cairo and as a matter of fact in egypt. a memorial place for the 2011 uprising. you are not allowed on to the monument itself but can enjoy it from a distance. no pedestrian crossings so best to observe from afar or take extra caution when crossing the road. it is very close to the old egyptian museum.
an important taoist temple in the region. must visit if you are here. inside, there is also a small shrine for the goddess of mercy. make a donation to support if you can.

an impressive and beautiful hall, very easy to get to, has excellent visibility of the stage (we were at the concert). the downside is the small number of buffets, which creates abnormal queues to buy drinks and something to eat. we gave up and it's a loss only for them. there are enough toilets. it's a shame there's no metro nearby. you have to walk at least fifteen minutes to get to the metro.
an impressive and beautifully restored building in the heart of havana. the architecture is stunning, and the interior is rich with history. a must-see landmark for anyone visiting the city.

an impressive and majestic spot. i didn't climb it, but the rock is seen from many different spots of the area. it looks climbable in some places but i believe that it might require special equipment. my camp was just below this landmark. if you are professional climber i am sure you can find spots for yourself there.

an impressive building with an equally impressive collection of cuban art from the 50s onward. entry is a ludicrous 65 pesos. some sections were closed for reasons unknown but the accessible parts were sufficient for an hour or two of quality viewing. all descriptive text in spanish only and they lack the profit-generating museum store one might expect. still, very much recommended.

an impressive cathedral, inside and out, in the city center, with exposed coral stone columns and arches. our walking tour has now reached the cathedral of cartagena. the brightly painted bell tower is easily seen from many vantage points in the city. the cathedral was constructed between the years of 1577 and 1612, and designed after other cathedrals in spain and the canary islands. the ornate, brightly painted and highly decorated 10-foot-tall doors are always open during day so pilgrims can enter without charge. the pulpit is constructed of rare and valuable italian carrara marble. the golden colored palanquin with four carrying poles, displayed inside is used to carry a large statue of a saint while in procession.
an impressive church! really liked the allegory and representations in the windows.

an impressive site to visit when in the gobi region. after driving for miles in the flat lands, tsagaan suvarga offers a pleasant surprise. photo opportunities. hiking. picnic? bring water and proper hiking shoes. sunscreen and bug repellent.

an impressively lovely gardens right along the inner city of vienna. everything is precise, orderly and beautiful. there’s a section where rose bushes are donated by people and it makes for a colorful pop along the walking path. we came on a rainy day but this would be a lovely spot to sit and spend more time when the weather is better. i loved how precise everything was set up here, the grounds are very well attended to and cared for.

an incredible 2-day adventure through one of jordan's most magical landscapes! i booked a one night and two day tour. habis was very quick and efficient with handling my reservation and answering questions (such as how to reach the village by bus). the tour itself was amazing! nayef, king of the desert, and best guide was incredible! he made the jeep tour fun, explaining the history and features of every stop. he's also a great cook and fun to chat with when we were at camp. i can't recommend them enough! if you want a magical and unforgettable experience, you should definitely do so with habis and his crew! i'll definitely come back in the future!

an incredible day with joey! the entire organization was beyond perfect. joey made sure to find spots where few other groups went, which made the experience very enjoyable! he personally searched for tortoiseshell turtles and starfish despite the difficulty of seeing them, to ensure the whole group could see and enjoy them. we were also lucky enough to be filmed and photographed by joey with his drone and gopro, which will leave us with wonderful memories of this experience. i highly recommend this agency for island hopping in port barton!

an incredible day! kurt and harry (our guide and driver) we're extremely knowledgeable, and they navigated us smoothly around the island to some of the most popular photo locations. snorkeling with the turtles was amazing, and equipment was provided. we experienced exceptional service and the company is extremely conscientious about the well being of the turtles and their natural environment. we felt safe and satisfied that we could leave the beautiful island the way we found it for future travelers. and, the most satisfying aspect of kurt and harry's performance, the tour felt very much like a group that grew closer from the wit and wisdom of the guide. we highly recommend this once in a lifetime experience!

an incredible experience ! the staff was friendly and agreable, and the food and drinks are unlimited. i will remember this tour my whole life, far from the touristic places you enjoy more barcelona and the sea ;)

an interesting little temple that you can visit in causeway bay is the lin fa kung temple on lin fa kung street west, only a 5-6 minute walk from the more famous tin hau (causeway bay) temple found near the tin hau mtr station. the temple is open daily from 7.30am to 5.00pm and is free to visit. the lin fa kung temple is a uniquely designed, small round shaped temple built in 1863 that is dedicated to kwun yum also known as the goddess of mercy. there is only one main chamber room with a ground floor level room, filled with interesting items of worship and altar area as well as a small upstairs level where more statues of intrigue await, including hundreds of small lotus lamps lit under the statue of kwun yum. a large rock makes up part of the back wall and is prominently exposed from the upstairs section of the temple. this is interesting to locate and have a look at. don't forget to look up because there is a very nice dragon fresco on the ceiling of the temple that is well worth taking a picture. you can visit the lin fa kung temple in as little as 10-15 minutes and it makes a great addition to a visit to the nearby tin hau temple, combined they can give you a sense of the religious affiliations many local people have with the deities of worship. this temple is particularly busy during kwun yum festival as well as the mid-autumn festival periods.
