an unforgettable journey my first visit to the leonardo da vinci museum in milan was absolutely **mind-blowing** from the moment i stepped inside, i felt like i was walking through the imagination of history’s greatest renaissance master. the museum brings da vinci’s inventions to life with stunning interactive models of his flying machines, war devices, and hydraulic systems. seeing his sketches transform into 3d working models left me speechless—you can touch, crank, and experiment with them! it’s not just a museum it’s a hands-on playground for curious minds. i was especially awed by the gallery of paintings section, where high-tech reproductions of works like *the last supper* and *mona lisa* reveal hidden details and restoration secrets. the anatomical studies room, showcasing his precise sketches of the human body, proved how far ahead of his time da vinci truly was.

an unforgettable journey with komodo luxury: a trip of a lifetime i recently embarked on a shared 3-day, 2-night adventure with komodo luxury aboard the lamborajo 3, and it was nothing short of extraordinary. from the moment we set sail, the experience exceeded all my expectations. our guide was exceptionally professional, providing insightful information about each destination while ensuring our safety and enjoyment throughout the journey. the boat crew handled everything with remarkable skill and warmth, making us feel right at home on the sea. every meal was a delight—the food was not just great, it was exquisite, offering a delicious variety that catered to all tastes. the service was impeccable, with every detail attended to perfectly. we visited numerous breathtaking destinations, each more stunning than the last. the highlight was undoubtedly our visit to komodo national park, where we had the unbelievable fortune of spotting six komodo dragons in their natural habitat—a rare and thrilling sight that few get to experience. as if that weren't enough, our adventure led us to manta point, where we swam alongside majestic manta rays. witnessing these magnificent creatures up close was an exhilarating experience that made our lucky day even more special. this trip was filled with unforgettable moments that i will cherish forever. komodo luxury provided an amazing journey with top-notch service, professional guides, and experiences that went above and beyond anything i could have imagined. if you're considering a trip to this beautiful part of the world, i wholeheartedly recommend choosing komodo luxury—you won't be disappointed.

an unforgettable liveaboard experience in raja ampat with scuba republic. six days of diving paradise, we saw manta rays, sharks, turtles, and stunning reefs. the crew was professional, the vibes with the group were amazing, and everything ran smoothly. i truly loved it. 100% recommended!

an unforgettable motorcycle experience through salar de uyuni with robin! while pricier than standard 4x4 tours, the value is exceptional. robin, initially reserved but deeply passionate, customizes bikes and routes to match your skill level. his extensive knowledge and genuine respect for the region shine through engaging conversations. his authenticity and expertise transform a simple tour into a rich cultural experience. the small group format (only tow!) enables meaningful interactions and a truly immersive adventure. absolutely worth the investment for motorcycle enthusiasts seeking a unique perspective of uyuni. thank you, robin, for an outstanding day of riding and discovery!

an unforgettable night at his majesty’s – hauntingly beautiful and utterly spellbinding seeing the phantom of the opera at his majesty’s theatre is nothing short of magical. from the very first note of the overture, the entire theatre seems to vibrate with anticipation – and what follows is an experience that’s breathtaking, emotionally rich, and visually spectacular. the theatre itself sets the perfect tone: opulent, intimate, and steeped in history. it feels like the kind of place where stories live in the walls, and phantom takes full advantage of that atmosphere. the set design is astonishing – every transition seamless, from the candlelit underground lair to the grand opera house stage within a stage. and yes, the chandelier moment is just as iconic as you imagine – it genuinely makes your heart skip a beat. the cast was phenomenal. the phantom was a perfect balance of menace, vulnerability, and tragic charm – his voice powerful and haunting. christine was luminous, both in her voice and presence, and raoul brought heart and strength to every scene. their chemistry made the story all the more gripping, and the emotion in the final scenes left many in the audience quietly wiping away tears. the music, of course, is unforgettable. there’s nothing like hearing “the music of the night” or “wishing you were somehow here again” live, surrounded by a full orchestra and wrapped in velvet sound. every song hits harder in person – richer, deeper, and filled with nuance that recordings just can’t capture. what makes phantom so enduring is that it’s more than just spectacle (though the spectacle is incredible). it’s a deeply human story about love, obsession, loneliness, and beauty – and at his majesty’s theatre, it’s told with elegance, passion, and care. whether you’re seeing it for the first time or the fiftieth, the phantom of the opera is a theatrical experience that stays with you long after the curtain falls. a true masterpiece.

an unforgettable nyc landmark! rockefeller center is a must-visit when you're in new york. the architecture is stunning, and there's so much to explore. we went up to the top of the rock and the views were absolutely incredible—especially at sunset. walking around the plaza, you’re surrounded by iconic sights like the prometheus statue and channel gardens. in the winter, the whole place transforms with the ice rink and that famous christmas tree—truly magical. there are tons of shops, restaurants, and even nbc studios, where you can take a behind-the-scenes tour. tip: if you have the new york pass, top of the rock is included—great value if you're visiting other landmarks too! whether you’re into history, architecture, or just want to experience the nyc vibe, this place has it all. highly recommended!

an unforgettable paragliding experience with patrick! i had the incredible opportunity to go paragliding with patrick, and it was truly unforgettable🥰 i’m usually someone who’s too scared to even get on a roller coaster, but patrick’s professionalism and expertise made me feel completely safe and at ease from start to finish!! we soared high on the wind, capturing the breathtaking swiss landscapes in all their beauty. patrick not only gave fascinating explanations about the views but also took plenty of amazing photos✨ he reminded me to look ahead and enjoy the moment, and even the spin maneuver turned out to be pure fun!!! this experience was so wonderful that i would gladly do it again. patrick is kind, humorous, and a true paragliding expert. i’m so glad i booked on such a perfect weather day🧚‍♀️ it made the experience even more special!! thank you, patrick, for making this such a safe and exciting adventure☁️✨ p.s. i forgot to take my altitude sickness medicine..! if i had, it might have been even more fun! but it was still absolutely amazing💪💪

an unforgettable ski experience at an’nupuri, niseko – march 2025 an’nupuri niseko is an absolute gem, and my recent ski trip there in march was nothing short of spectacular. despite the season edging toward spring, the snow cover was still excellent, offering pristine conditions across the mountain. i was lucky enough to score a perfect bluebird day—clear skies, not a breath of wind, and best of all, relatively uncrowded slopes that made for an incredibly enjoyable experience. what sets an’nupuri apart is its well-balanced variety of runs. from gentle slopes for beginners to more challenging terrain, there’s something for every skill level. the real highlight, though, is gate 2, where you can hike up to access the untouched backcountry behind the summit. skiing through virginia powder and weaving through the trees was an absolute dream—an exhilarating and deeply rewarding experience that any powder enthusiast would appreciate. compared to hirafu, an’nupuri feels underrated, which works in its favor. the lift system is efficient, keeping queues minimal, and everything runs smoothly.

an unforgettable snorkeling experience at the dimaniyat islands! the crystal-clear waters are teeming with marine life—colorful fish, vibrant corals, and even sea turtles. captain hassaan helped me a lot to spot turtles, fish, and other amazing sea creatures. it's a true paradise for sea lovers, with stunning natural beauty and a peaceful atmosphere. highly recommended!

an unforgettable sound healing experience we had the absolute pleasure of working with kymberley and her son risland during our corporate retreat in sedona, and the experience was nothing short of incredible. kymberley is a truly wonderful soul—her calming presence and soothing voice set the tone for a deeply healing and restorative session. kymberley went above and beyond to create a beautiful and impactful sound healing experience for our large group. her flexibility, professionalism, and intuitive understanding of the group’s energy made all the difference. risland added a lovely dynamic to the session as well—together, they make a powerful and harmonious team. everyone walked away feeling more grounded, balanced, and connected. it was a highlight of our retreat, and we’re so grateful to have had them with us. highly recommend!

an unforgettable stay amidst nubra’s beauty! we had a truly amazing experience at dream ville cottage in nubra valley. the location is breathtaking — surrounded by mountains and offering a serene, peaceful atmosphere. the cottages are clean, cozy, and well-maintained with all the essential amenities. the staff is incredibly warm and hospitable — always ready to help with a smile. special thanks to the owner/manager who made sure we were comfortable and even guided us about nearby places to visit like hunder dunes and diskit monastery. the food was simple, homely, and delicious — perfect after a long day of travel. at night, the sky was full of stars, making the whole place feel magical. highly recommended for anyone looking to experience the raw beauty of ladakh with a touch of comfort and genuine hospitality. would definitely come back again!

an unforgettable stay at jw marriott masai mara! from the warm welcome to the breathtaking views, everything was perfect. the staff went above and beyond, the food was world-class, and the game drives were magical. a true luxury safari experience that feels both personal and memorable. highly recommend for anyone visiting the mara!

an unforgettable stay in the heart of the desert! our experience at hasan zawaideh camp was nothing short of magical. from the moment we arrived, we were welcomed with such warmth and genuine hospitality—it felt like coming home. the manager and every single member of the staff went above and beyond to make our stay absolutely perfect, always adding thoughtful touches and ensuring every detail was taken care of. the local food was incredible—fresh, flavorful, and served with pride. every meal felt like a celebration of jordanian culture. whether it was the traditional dishes or the sweet tea under the stars, the dining experience was a highlight in itself. the camp was beautifully set up, clean, and comfortable, perfectly blending desert authenticity with modern comfort. but what truly set this place apart was the heart and soul behind it—the people. their kindness, stories, and attentiveness made our visit one of the most memorable experiences we’ve ever had. thank you, hasan zawaideh camp, for sharing the spirit of wadi rum with us. we left with full hearts, full bellies, and memories we’ll cherish forever.

an unforgettable stay on uros, the floating islands of lake titicaca. the room was cozy with breathtaking lake views, and the peaceful setting made it feel like a dream. my host was incredibly kind, he took me on a boat ride around the lake and shared stories about the rich history and traditions of the uros people. a truly unique and meaningful experience. highly recommended!

an unforgettable sunrise hike – devil’s bridge trailhead waking up early for this hike was so worth it. if you’re thinking about visiting devil’s bridge trailhead, do yourself a favor and go for the sunrise. we started in the dark, guided only by our flashlights (bring a bright one—you’ll need it!), and made our way up the trail with the stars still overhead. the climb isn’t too difficult, but it does get your heart pumping, especially as you get closer to the top. but once we reached the bridge and sat there, waiting for the first light—it was pure magic. watching the night fade into day, and seeing the sun’s golden rays slowly spill over the red cliffs and trees below, was one of the most peaceful, beautiful experiences i’ve ever had. you feel totally connected to nature, like you’re witnessing something ancient and sacred. the views from the top are breathtaking. sitting on the bridge with that backdrop feels surreal—it’s the kind of moment that makes you pause and just be. whether you’re into hiking or just want a powerful experience in nature, this one’s a must. highly recommend this hike to anyone visiting sedona. just go early, take your time, and soak it all in.

an unforgettable visit with highland titles – thank you, stewart! we absolutely loved our time with highland titles! from start to finish, it was an unforgettable experience — made even more special by our incredible guide, stewart. he was not only welcoming and knowledgeable but also a true advocate for conservation and the natural beauty of scotland. his passion for the mission of highland titles was evident in every part of the tour. we were incredibly lucky to snag a last-minute tour spot due to a cancellation, and we’re so grateful we did. ever since becoming a “laird and lady” of scotland and adopting the twin highland coos, we had hoped for the chance to visit the reserve. the personal tour exceeded our expectations — every part of the land, every story shared, every conservation effort explained was inspiring. one highlight was seeing the bee hives painted by local primary school children — a touching sign of the community connection highland titles fosters. another highlight (and possibly the biggest for my wife!) was meeting the highland cows — especially the twins and donald. being able to step into the pasture, feed them, brush them, and interact up close made for such a joyful and meaningful experience. it was clear these animals are cared for deeply and respectfully. thank you, stewart, for your energy, knowledge, and your genuine love for the land. and thank you to highland titles for doing the vital work of restoring and protecting one of the most beautiful places on earth. your efforts make a lasting impact — and our visit will be a memory we cherish forever.

andy and advantage grand canyon were terrific! they were able to find me a trip that worked perfectly within my narrow date window and their communications were impeccable -- both clear and detailed. they sent excellent overview materials and were very responsive to my every question. the trip itself, provided by wilderness river adventures, was amazing -- a truly once in a lifetime experience that i recommend to anyone interested in seeing the unique scenery of the grand canyon from the valley floor. roller coasting on the rapids by day, side hikes to beautiful waterfalls and camping out under the stars every night with great people and delicious meals was a trip of dreams i will never forget.

angel cruises really are the best in the area. do not hesitate to book! we had a totally magical day with nathaniel & hans. their boat was spotless and modern with so many lovely seating areas - really spacious. nathaniel & hans were delightful from the word go - funny, charming, really excellent skippers (my husband has his power boat license and said their driving was superb). the day was a ten out of ten from start to finish. we were told some really interesting facts about the history of mauritius, taken to some amazing spots. they make a mean cocktail and bent over backwards to make sure we had a great time. it was the highlight of our holiday. we had done another boat trip in the north of the island the day before and i have to say this trip was superior. plus….one more thing….they are just really cool, lovely, friendly guys who you absolutely want to be on a boat with all day. look no further, angel cruises absolutely rocks!

angkor wat is a unesco world heritage site that should be at the top of your list when visiting cambodia. this ancient temple complex will leave you mesmerized and deeply reflective, as it offers far more than just a glimpse into history—it’s a spiritual and architectural marvel that continues to inspire awe. the sheer scale, intricate carvings, and the way nature has gracefully intertwined with the ruins create a powerful atmosphere that’s hard to put into words. to truly appreciate its beauty, especially during the golden hours of sunrise or sunset, it’s important to plan your visit carefully. having experienced both, i found that sunrise generally draws fewer crowds, making it ideal for photography and for soaking in the serenity of the moment. watching the first light of day slowly illuminate the temple’s silhouette is a magical experience that stays with you. what’s truly remarkable is how the temple has withstood the test of time, maintaining its grandeur while blending harmoniously with the surrounding jungle. its enduring presence is a testament to the ingenuity and devotion of the khmer empire. just imagine how magnificent it must have been in its heyday—bustling with life, rituals, and royal ceremonies. travel tip: if you're planning to catch the sunrise, arrive at the temple gates by 4:30 am to secure a good viewing spot near the reflecting pool. bring a flashlight or use your phone light, as it’s still very dark at that hour. also, pack a light breakfast or snack—there are small vendors nearby, but having something on hand lets you enjoy the view without rushing off.

angkor wat is not just a temple, it’s an experience. the moment you step inside, you’re transported into a world of ancient architecture, spiritual energy, and stunning craftsmanship. the carvings, towers, and symmetry of the temple are simply awe inspiring. i visited during sunrise, and it was magical the golden light reflecting off the ancient stones creates a view you’ll never forget. the site is huge, so wear comfortable shoes, carry water, and take your time exploring. a must visit destination in cambodia for history lovers, photographers, and anyone seeking to connect with something timeless and grand.

anhalter bahnhof is a fascinating historical site in berlin with a deeply significant past, particularly tied to the holocaust and world war ii. once one of the city's grandest train stations, it was constructed in 1841 and became a bustling hub for travelers, handling tens of thousands of passengers daily. however, its history took a dark turn during the nazi era when it was used as one of three stations in berlin to deport around 55,000 jews, including 9,600 elderly individuals, to theresienstadt and other concentration camps. the station suffered extensive damage during allied bombings in world war ii and was eventually closed in 1952. most of the structure was demolished in 1960, leaving only a fragment of its grand façade standing today. this remaining portion serves as both a memorial and a reminder of berlin's turbulent history.

another interesting place we visited was the monumento nacional aos mortos da segunda guerra mundial, dedicated to the brazilian soldiers who fought and died during world war ii. the entire area was fenced off, but we tried to enter, and it turned out to be possible. given the strong military presence, with numerous soldiers guarding the site, it likely falls under the ministry of defense. the monument itself is an impressive architectural work, featuring a striking modernist design. in the underground section, we met a soldier who shared insights about the history of brazilian troops who fought in italy during world war ii. many people may not realize that brazil sent around 25,000 troops—known as the brazilian expeditionary force (feb)—to fight alongside the allies, particularly in the italian campaign. the memorial also houses the tombs of fallen soldiers, serving as a solemn and powerful tribute to their sacrifice. for those interested in history, this is an important site to visit in rio, offering a deeper understanding of brazil’s role in world war ii.

another magical experience and, by far, the most memorable stay of our 8-day trip. the camp’s strategic location within the greater maasai mara makes every game drive even more rewarding, and its position right by the river offers front-row views of the wildebeest crossing during the migration—an unforgettable sight to witness from the comfort of the camp and common area. a huge part of what made our stay so special was samson, our wonderful local guide, and joshua, our sharp-eyed spotter. their warmth, kindness, and deep knowledge of the bush made every drive fascinating and engaging, especially for our two children. edgar, the camp manager, and the entire staff went above and beyond to ensure we were comfortable and well taken care of throughout our stay. this is one of those rare places we truly hope to return to—a perfect blend of exceptional wildlife encounters, breathtaking scenery, and heartfelt hospitality.

anse georgette is one of the most beautiful, untouched beaches on praslin. the water here is a vivid turquoise, the sand soft and white, and the surroundings lush and serene,absolutely picture‑poster perfect. to visit, you must enter via constance lemuria resort and advance booking is required since access is limited. from the entrance, you’ll walk about 15 minutes through the hotel grounds and along a scenic path. the stroll may feel a bit long, especially in the midday sun, but the reward is a private-feeling paradise that’s more than worth the effort. there’s a tiny sunset bar near the beach that serves refreshing drink,think chilled juices and simple cocktails(their famous takama rum punch). don’t expect full dining or upscale cocktails, but the sunset views from there are stunning. it’s a charming spot to wind down in the evening. i’ve rated it 4 stars instead of 5 because the access is restricted and there are minimal facilities once you arrive, restrooms or shade. still for natural beauty, peace, and some memorable sunset moments, anse georgette is a must‑see in seychelles.

as a longtime fan of both the beatles and thoughtful curation, i was blown away by the paul mccartney photographs 1963–64: eyes of the storm exhibit at the de young. as an annual pass holder, i visit often—but this show is easily one of the most intimate and moving exhibitions i’ve experienced in years. these photographs, taken by paul himself, chronicle the band’s meteoric rise from late 1963 through their first tour of the u.s. in early 1964. what makes it so special isn’t just the historical weight—it’s how raw and personal the images feel. from candid shots backstage and in hotel rooms to moments of quiet reflection between john, george, and ringo, mccartney captures a whirlwind from the inside, at the eye of the storm. it’s rare to see beatlemania through the beatles’ own lens. and what’s astonishing is how sharp paul’s composition is—his use of light, motion, and framing rivals many professional photographers. the show is organized chronologically by city—liverpool, paris, new york, d.c., miami—and supported with engaging context that brings the era to life. major props to the de young for their presentation: the layout flows well, the lighting is respectful of these aged prints, and the optional audio guide adds depth without distraction. i’d recommend weekday visits to avoid the crowds. if you’re remotely interested in pop culture, photography, or 1960s history, don’t miss this one. even if you’ve seen all the beatles documentaries, this feels like a missing piece of the story—more human, more vulnerable. a beautiful exhibit by a surprising photographer.

as a professional tour guide in dubai, one of the most frequently admired stops on our journey is za’abeel palace. though the palace is not open for public entry, its grandeur, elegance, and cultural significance make it a favorite among my foreign guests. nestled in the heart of the za’abeel district, this official residence of his highness sheikh mohammed bin rashid al maktoum serves as a symbol of leadership, tradition, and vision. built in the 1960s under the late sheikh rashid bin saeed al maktoum, za’abeel palace originally stood on the outskirts of a then-developing dubai. over the decades, the city grew around it, yet the palace retained its regal charm. its name, “za’abeel,” meaning “thanks” or “gratitude” in arabic, reflects the nation’s values of respect, loyalty, and unity. the palace’s location—surrounded by palm trees, fountains, and manicured gardens—feels like an oasis amid dubai’s bustling modernity. the drive up to the outer gates is breathtaking. guests are often struck by the beautifully landscaped roads, the symmetry of the gardens, and the sight of guards in traditional uniforms. though access is limited to the main gate, the view alone makes it a perfect photo stop. the structure combines traditional islamic design elements with modern architectural touches, reflecting the balance between heritage and progress that defines the uae. each time i bring groups here—whether from europe, asia, or the americas—they’re always fascinated by the symbolism behind the palace. it becomes a moment of storytelling: i explain the royal family’s role, sheikh mohammed’s leadership, and his vision for dubai. for many, za’abeel palace is more than just a landmark; it's a window into the soul of the uae. guests are often intrigued by the palace’s connection to equestrian traditions. while the royal stables are private, i share stories of sheikh mohammed’s global achievements in horse racing. for those passionate about horses, this connection adds a meaningful layer to the visit. during special times like ramadan or uae national day, the area around the palace is beautifully decorated with lights and flags, enhancing the experience. visitors often comment on the patriotism and unity they sense, even from outside the gates. while our time at za’abeel is brief, it consistently leaves a lasting impression. the harmony between nature, architecture, and history evokes respect and admiration. for many tourists, this serene yet powerful location is a highlight of their dubai visit, sparking conversations about culture, leadership, and identity. za’abeel palace represents the essence of emirati pride—silent, dignified, and enduring. as a guide, i always look forward to this stop, not just for the beauty it offers, but for the deeper understanding it inspires in those who see it.

as an annual pass holder at the legion of honor, i’ve found the membership to be incredibly rewarding, offering access to a diverse array of exhibitions. one of the most captivating showcases was the 2024 exhibition, japanese prints in transition: from the floating world to the modern world. ￼ a journey through japan’s artistic evolution this exhibition traced the transformation of japanese woodblock prints from the edo period’s delicate ukiyo-e to the vibrant, western-influenced works of the meiji era. featuring nearly 150 pieces from the achenbach foundation for graphic arts, it highlighted the shift in subject matter and style as japan opened up to global influences in the late 19th century. ￼ ￼ highlights and notable works • katsushika hokusai’s “the great wave”: displayed for the first time in over a decade due to its sensitivity to light, this iconic piece was a centerpiece of the exhibition. • tsukioka yoshitoshi’s prints: his works bridged traditional and modern styles, reflecting the cultural shifts of the meiji era. ￼ • masami teraoka’s contemporary pieces: infusing traditional techniques with modern themes, his prints offered a satirical take on western influence in japan. ￼ exhibition experience the exhibition was thoughtfully organized, with clear explanations of the historical context and artistic techniques. docent-led tours provided deeper insights, and the museum’s serene setting enhanced the overall experience. ￼ final thoughts the japanese prints in transition exhibition was a testament to the legion of honor’s commitment to presenting culturally significant and visually stunning art. for art enthusiasts and history buffs alike, the annual membership offers unparalleled access to such enriching experiences. ￼

as an architect with a deep appreciation for **architecture, history, and cultural landmarks**, visiting the **cairo citadel** was an unforgettable experience. this towering fortress, overlooking the sprawling city of **cairo**, is an extraordinary blend of **military ingenuity and artistic brilliance**, standing as a testament to egypt’s long and complex history. #### **a walk through centuries of power** stepping through the **massive stone gates**, i was immediately struck by the **scale and strategic placement** of the citadel atop the **mokattam hills**. the vantage point offers breathtaking views, stretching all the way to the **pyramids of giza** on a clear day—an inspiring reminder of egypt’s layered past. built by **salah ad-din in the 12th century**, this fortress was once the seat of egyptian rulers for nearly **700 years**, guarding cairo from invasions and serving as a center of governance. walking through its corridors, i could almost feel the echoes of **mamluk, ottoman, and modern egyptian history** unfolding in every stone. #### **architectural marvels and hidden gems** the citadel is home to several incredible structures, but **muhammad ali’s mosque** is its crown jewel. the **ottoman-inspired domes, towering minarets, and alabaster walls** make it a visual masterpiece. inside, the blend of **lavish chandeliers, soaring ceilings, and intricate carvings** creates an ambiance of serenity and grandeur. beyond the mosque, the **mosque of sultan al-nasir muhammad**, with its distinctive **green domes**, offers a contrasting mamluk aesthetic that showcases cairo’s varied architectural timeline. i also enjoyed exploring the **national military museum**, which presents an insightful look into egypt’s **military history**, housing ancient weapons, armor, and historical artifacts. #### **a perspective beyond the stones** for someone like me, deeply engaged in the **construction industry**, the citadel serves as a **timeless case study** in **urban planning, defense strategy, and architectural evolution**. the mastery of **fortifications, water supply systems, and administrative layouts** speaks volumes about the ingenuity of its builders. moreover, the contrast between **military strength and artistic devotion** is striking—where else can you find **mosques, palaces, and museums housed within a fortress meant for war?** it’s a site that truly encapsulates egypt’s ability to weave history, faith, and functionality into a single place.

as i stepped through its gates, i was immediately immersed in a serene and sacred atmosphere. the monastery’s architecture, adorned with intricate details and vibrant colors, was a visual delight.

as massage enthusiasts, after an intense workout day with my partner, we were keen for a deep tissue massage. choosing this place was, without a doubt, the best decision.👌 from the very beginning, the experience was outstanding. the staff took the time to ask about our needs, preferences, and any health conditions. the massage was simply phenomenal: each technique was precise, applying the exact pressure to the areas that needed it. the therapists were extremely attentive, warm, and responsive, making us feel cared for and comfortable throughout the session.🤲 the place is cozy, spotless, and the atmosphere transports you to a state of complete relaxation. we’ll be back heaps. cheers to the team - you’re legends!💯

as massive war of the worlds fans we weren't sure what to expect when we did this experience for my birthday but we're not disapointed. from walking in to leaving the staff and the actors were fantastic. friendly chatty and helpful. we went for two vip tickets and that came with a meal two drinks a photo and a discount at the shop. it also came with a souvenir program but they had ran out so they took our address and will post them to us later. the experience itself was fantastic. genuinely scary in some bits so i dont recommend if you don't like a good scare or are of a weak constitution! i have mobility problems but still managed to do the interactive elements but someone in our group couldn't and there were alternative routes if needed, and it was all done in theme! we were bumped up a group as we got there early so we had a rather large group of survivors. i feel like if we had been in a smaller group the experience would have been diffrent, but it was still heaps of fun and the actors managed to make it feel more intimate even if we had a group of 14 i will say the vr headsets need fixing. all three of the headsets i used had some sort of fault. the first one kept showing the lens distance whenever you tried to turn your head and the other two kept white screening if you moved your head to much. it didnt distract from the experience but it did take you out of it a little especially when your a massive wuss like me and will jump and yell at any sort of jump scare. we had the red weed cocktail in the interval room and it was perfectly made. well done to the barman, he was very good at his job, and managed to serve everyone with time to spare because 20 mins wasn't a long time to make that many cocktails. we had food after in the spirit of man as it was part of our vip package. we also got two more cocktails blue new world and mist of mars. they were both really nice, the chocolate one was fantastic. i had the vegan burger and it was one of the best vegan burgers ive ever had. the fries were better than some of high end places weve eaten while in london. the pizza was massive. i 'won' a sunday as it was my birthday. what i could eat of it was nice my other half enjoyed it ( im allergic to ice cream lol the travesty) it was the thought that counts and they didn't have to do anything but a birthday treat is always appreciated. the prices in the gift shop were all nice and clear. but here comes my only major downside to the whole thing. the place is cashless. i had over 100 in birthday money i couldn't spend because i only had cash. then the payment systems went down. thankfully we had already paid for the things we wanted in the gift shop and were waiting for food when it happened. also the gift shop had few clothing items bigger than a small. again we would have spent a fortune if more things were in bigger size. i managed to get the hoodie i wanted but it was the last medium in the shop! all in all an amazing day vip worked out as really good value for money as we added up food drink programs lockers and the such and it came to more than what we paid for the tickets.

as my family and i were walking around the french quarter, we found our way to the frenchmen art bazaar. artists are set up with tables showcasing their artwork. to me it is like a small evening arts and crafts show. ok to to swing by to see, but not something i would make a point to visit. we enjoyed seeing the work from the artists around st louis cathedral.

as others have said, many many stairs, so be prepared. plan to go early as well. there is a cost for this attraction that is separate from the city walls entrance. nice views of the area, but really you can see the same view from the city walls. no history information is posted anywhere, which was disappointing. please note the opening times is not always correct for this attraction. in fact, today it closed early and there is conflicting information on the official website versus what is on the dubrovnik pass website. check the dubrovnik pass website first to see if there is changes to the hours! we arrived early and it closed at 2 pm but we didn’t understand why, turns out they’re setting up for a wedding in this place….great for those people but not for all the visitors. it really dampened the experience for us having to walk around all the crap they set up plus deal with the huge tour groups on game of thrones tours. i didn’t really take many photos just because of the crowds, and it was 9 am. in fact, so the math on if the dubrovnik pass actually makes sense for you and your situation because some places kids can get in free depending on age, but you pay for them with the pass if they’re under 7.

as part of the southern ridges, hortpark is a beautifully maintained gardening hub, perfect for nature lovers, walkers, and anyone seeking a peaceful escape. as part of the southern ridges. it features well-landscaped gardens and a tranquil atmosphere that many visitors appreciate. one of the highlights for me is the silver garden, where striking white and silver plants create a uniquely serene and picturesque setting. love taking peaceful walks from kent ridge park to hortpark and back—a refreshing route that’s perfect for light exercise. the well-paved trails, lush greenery, and quiet surroundings make it an ideal place to unwind, especially in the morning or evening. highly recommended for nature walks, garden enthusiasts, and anyone exploring the southern ridges!

as promised and advertised, the grand palace is grand in all the ways possible, so visitors need to plan in advance. if you wanna see everything, prepare to arrive there at most at noon, preferably even earlier, because it's open till only 3:30 pm. prepare for the crowds. they have a strict dress code (modest clothing) and it's respectful to stick to it. there's a map near the entrance, but i also downloaded one from the official website, to keep track of where i've been and where i wanna go next. don't be afraid to ask others to take pictures of you (especially if you're traveling solo) and be ready to do the same for others. to one of the halls you have to enter barefoot, so either have a bag to put your shoes in, or leave them on a rack (but take pictures of the number of the row, where you left your shoes, to be able to find them later). remember to have a hat, re-apply sunscreen and have wet wipes to clean your feet/hands. i was honestly in awe of everything, as it was my first time in thailand and bangkok. the architecture of the temples was stunning and impressive. while i was there, some of the paintings were being restored, so it was interesting to witness that process. the grand palace is a must see place, to get a glimpse of traditional thai temples, and culture as a whole.

as someone who isn’t very into sports, i thought that this was a very cool experience! you definitely learn a lot about the history and there are lots of good opportunities for photos. when we went we bought tickets online and there was no line to get in and also there were not that many other people there. i would recommend taking a trip here!

as the brochure mentioned, this would be the longest day hike you could undertake. my hubby (40) and i (35) were exhausted afterward! however, you get to experience different views from the rim and "feel" all the layers of millions of years of geological strata. i wouldn't say this point offers the best view of the colorado river since we could see more of it from the desert view. the hike took us 5.5 hours, with about 30 minutes stopped at cedar ridge and another 40 minutes at skeleton point for a snack break. considering all the stops, the actual walking time would have been 4 hours, but breaks are necessary to catch your breath, eat, hydrate, and take lots of pictures while enjoying the view. so, 1) plan the hike for 6 hours; 2) i personally think hiking poles are a must for this 6-mile hike; 3) bring plenty of water and snacks; 4) and enjoy! * we started at 7am, but definitely would start earlier if possible. the mornign shade was super helpful! coming back was hard with the full sun exposure!!

as the highest point in africa, i really feel privileged to have reached this point. the journey from the base camp was not very easy, and at some point, i felt like giving up, but i pushed myself until the end. takes about 7-8 hours on average to get here from barafu camp, and on your way, you pass the very magnificent glaciers. if you have some energy left, it's always recommended to go down to the glaciers as it adds to the summit experience.

as their motto goes, "set sail for a lifetime experience." we've been in santorini for nearly a week, and thanks to our host catherine, we were recommended to take a tour with my blue cruises. honestly, it turned out to be the highlight of our trip. i initially expected just a regular boat ride to visit some beautiful spots, but miltos made this journey absolutely magnificent! his english is impeccable, and his knowledge of geography and history is even more impressive. this made our tour not just breathtaking, but also educational and enjoyable. on top of that, he's such a humble person. i highly recommend anyone spending time in santorini, whether it's a short or long stay, to book a tour with them. a five-hour trip with my blue cruises is truly a lifetime experience! i'm beyond grateful that my fiancé and i had the chance to enjoy this extraordinary day! amazing views, perfect dinner! additionally, it's such a lovely family-run company. miltos' wife, who is just as kind and humble as he is, picked us up and also brought us back to the apartment. they are truly fantastic, wonderful people, the best guides you can get in santorini!

as this was both our first trip to south africa and our first experience with explorer safari, we were initially a bit sceptical. however, lauren’s meticulous planning immediately put us at ease, with every detail thoughtfully arranged from start to finish. the expertly curated itinerary allowed us to thoroughly enjoy our safari across two private game reserves. communication was prompt and attentive throughout, with lauren always ensuring we were well cared for. without a doubt, this was one of the best trips of my life, thanks to lauren and the entire team at explorer safari!

as this was our first liveaboard experience we were lucky enough to hit the jackpot by selecting the klm teman for our 4d/3n cruise in komodo. the boat was clean, spacious with lots of undercover areas to relax when not diving or snorkelling, the food was incredible and seemingly endless and the crew outstanding at making everyone comfortable and always, ‘safety first’. from the cheering of the crew on returning from the snorkel to the warm ginger tea as you get on the boat, to the briefing in the morning of the day’s plan, you can not fault the service. the diving and snorkelling spots were amazing with lots to see in the crystal clear water and extensive reefs. thanks to moses and the crew for a fabulous time.

as with everything else in europe it seems all attractions are becoming prohibitively expensive. at 40 euros, this is no exception, but it is a site that cannot be missed. we purchased our tickets in advance which is recommended ...skip the lines. we also got there early (9:30) and were off at noon. crowds were relatively light and we beat the heat! the crowds were much larger as we were exiting. the visit was excellent with tremendous pictures. walking the perimeter of the old city atop the walls is hard to beat. while there are lots of steps up and down, there were lots of opportunities to take a break. it is a lot easier to navigate this attraction at your own pace without crowds and heat. it is not hard to imagine the congestion in some places along the route with bigger crowds. take lots of water and remember, not a lot of shade. even at 40 euros, we recommend visiting this historical site.

as your local guide, i also recommend a visit to the siem reap river night market. located along the picturesque siem reap river, this market offers a slightly more relaxed atmosphere compared to pub street. it's an excellent place to browse for unique handicrafts, local artwork, and souvenirs, often at more leisurely pace. you'll find a good selection of food stalls offering delicious cambodian street food and refreshing drinks. it's a perfect spot for an evening stroll, enjoying the riverside breeze, and soaking in the local culture without the intense bustle of other areas.

as your local guide, i always recommend a visit to psar chas, or the old market, in siem reap. it's more than just a market; it's a vibrant slice of local life. here, you'll find everything from fresh produce and spices to souvenirs, clothing, and handcrafted goods. the atmosphere is bustling, filled with the sounds of daily commerce and the aroma of street food. it's a fantastic place to experience authentic cambodian culture, practice your bargaining skills, and pick up unique gifts. don't miss the chance to grab a refreshing fruit shake or some delicious local snacks while you explore!

as your local guide, i highly recommend a visit to wat preah prom rath, a beautiful and serene buddhist temple located right in the heart of siem reap. it offers a wonderful contrast to the bustling markets and streets. this pagoda is renowned for its vibrant murals, intricate carvings, and a stunning reclining buddha statue. the grounds are meticulously maintained, providing a peaceful oasis perfect for quiet contemplation and appreciating traditional khmer architecture and religious art. it's a truly spiritual and visually rich experience that offers a deeper insight into cambodian culture and faith.

ascending kilimanjaro over 7 challenging days and descending on the 8th was an incredible journey that pushed us to our limits. despite the deceptive images of easy terrain, the high altitude tested our endurance and spirits. day after day, my friends and i persevered, inching our way to the summit. with one friend reaching stella point, the two of us forged ahead to the peak, where, despite mild conditions, every breath was an effort. as we reached the summit and saw the "congratulations" sign, a flood of relief and exhilaration overwhelmed us. "i made it...!" echoed in my mind. a heartfelt gratitude goes to our exceptional guides, daudi and habibu, and the outstanding team. the ascent and descent would not have been possible without our familia moja!

at syntagma square, right in front of the parliament building, the hourly changing of the guard ceremony is a mesmerizing spectacle. the guards wear traditional uniforms featuring distinctive red shoes and perform slow, precise movements that showcase a rich heritage of discipline and honor. visitors love witnessing this unique ritual, which combines history, culture, and pageantry. the ceremony on sundays at 11 am is especially elaborate, with a full troop parade that adds to the grandeur. a visit here offers a glimpse into a proud tradition that has been maintained for generations and is a must-see for anyone exploring the city.

at the agricultural museum in dokki, cairo, was a vibrant celebration of egypt's rich horticultural heritage. as the oldest and largest flower exhibition in the middle east, first established in 1934, this annual event continues to captivate visitors with its diverse floral displays and cultural offerings. floral diversity and exhibitors this year's exhibition featured over 200 exhibitors showcasing a wide array of ornamental plants, rare species, and landscaping innovations. visitors were treated to displays of cut flowers, shade plants, succulents, and exotic cacti, reflecting both local cultivation and international horticultural trends. the inclusion of rare plant species cultivated in egypt highlighted the nation's botanical diversity and expertise. cultural and environmental initiatives beyond the floral displays, the exhibition emphasized environmental awareness and cultural heritage. workshops and seminars focused on the importance of ornamental plants in enhancing environmental quality and combating climate change. the event also featured traditional egyptian handicrafts, promoting local artisans and their contributions to cultural preservation. international collaboration and future outlook the 92nd edition marked a significant step towards internationalization, with participation from the food and agriculture organization (fao) and attendance by various foreign ambassadors. this collaboration aims to elevate the exhibition to a global platform, fostering international partnerships and trade opportunities in the horticultural sector. visitor experience the exhibition provided a delightful experience for visitors of all ages. affordable plant prices, starting from just 5 egyptian pounds, made it accessible to a broad audience. the event's layout facilitated leisurely strolls among the vibrant displays, creating an inviting atmosphere for families, gardening enthusiasts, and tourists alike.

at the end of october 2011, i went parasailing and had a truly unforgettable and wonderful experience! i was wondering whether to ask, but on the morning of the day, the weather was clear and the wind was calm, so i thought that if there was a vacancy, i would contact the number listed on the website via whatsapp. i received a reply within a few minutes, and was guided smoothly and carefully. by chance, there was a vacancy, and they came to pick me up at the hotel right away! the manager, mr. yoshida, who guided me, was very friendly and kind, and he taught me a lot of things (even about parasailing), which was very helpful. we boarded the boat and headed to the boat dedicated to parasailing. the boat rocked a little while waiting for the person in front to finish flying, so if you are sensitive to rocking, it is a good idea to take some motion sickness medicine. (the parasailing itself is stable, so i don't think you need to worry about motion sickness!) the actual flight time was about 10 minutes, but the wind was pleasant, and the beauty of the sea in the direction of isla mujeres was something you couldn't experience in the hotel zone! i was told that the water was so clear that you could see the sea turtles from above, but i didn't realize that i could! i was so impressed. it seems that you can't fly in the rain or when the wind is strong, so it's an experience that you can only have if you're lucky with the timing, but it's really wonderful and i recommend it. and above all, i was moved by yoshida-san's guidance and thoughtfulness, so if i have the opportunity to visit again, i would definitely like to consult with him about other activities! (thank you so much!) *i was told that there is a bus stop right in front of the marina in the hotel zone, so it would be cheaper to go back by bus! at the london palladium, there’s a new version of evita. it’s not the big, glittery show people might remember. instead, it feels more like a rock concert — simple stage, strong lights, and full of energy. director jamie lloyd tells eva perón’s story in a raw, stripped-down way. rachel zegler plays eva, and people say she’s amazing. she’s joined by diego andres rodriguez as che and james olivas as juan perón. the show runs from 14 june to 6 september 2025, for 12 weeks only. it lasts about 2 hours and 40 minutes, with songs like don’t cry for me argentina and you must love me. in one special moment, zegler sings from the theatre’s real balcony to the street below, while the audience inside watches on camera. tickets start at £29.50 for the cheapest seats, but the best ones can cost up to £245. there are discounts for seniors, groups, and weekday shows. zegler won’t perform on 14 & 28 july and 11 & 25 august — bella brown will take her place. the show is for ages 12+, with loud sounds, flashing lights, and some mature themes. the london palladium is near oxford circus and offers accessible performances with sign language, captions, and audio description. this version of evita is a bold new take — less glamour, more grit — and it’s only on for a short time.

augarten park is one of vienna’s most beautiful and historically rich green spaces. nestled in the heart of the city’s second district, this meticulously maintained park offers a perfect blend of tranquility, culture, and history. the first thing you notice upon entering augarten is how well taken care of it is. the gardens are immaculately groomed, with tree-lined alleys, colorful flowerbeds, and expansive lawns that invite visitors to relax, walk, or picnic. the park is family-friendly, with playgrounds for children and open areas that cater to joggers, dog walkers, and those simply looking to unwind. despite being a popular destination, it never feels overcrowded due to its generous size and thoughtful layout. what truly sets augarten apart, however, is its historical depth. dating back to the 17th century, the park was originally laid out as a baroque garden and has retained its classical charm. it’s home to the stunning palais augarten, a baroque palace that today houses the world-famous vienna boys’ choir. the palace and its surroundings provide a unique backdrop that adds a sense of grandeur to the entire park. a striking and sobering reminder of more recent history are the two massive world war ii flak towers that still stand within the park. these concrete giants, once used for air defense, serve as historical landmarks and symbols of vienna’s complex past. their presence offers a powerful contrast to the peaceful surroundings and invites reflection on the city’s wartime experience. whether you're a history enthusiast, a nature lover, or just someone in search of a peaceful place to spend an afternoon, augarten park is a must-visit. it’s a place where vienna’s layered history and natural beauty come together, making it both a serene escape and a living monument.

bab boujloud (also spelled bab boujeloud or bab boujloud) is a historic and iconic city gate in fez (fès), morocco, serving as the main entrance to fes el-bali, the city’s ancient medina and a unesco world heritage site. here’s a detailed overview: 1. historical background construction: built in 1913 during the french colonial administration, it replaced a simpler 12th-century gate. the original gate, designed with defensive angles to hinder invaders, remains visible but closed today. name origi: the name "boujloud" is derived from a corruption of abu al-junud ("father of the troops"), referencing a nearby military 2. architectural features design: a triple-arched gate in moorish-mauresque style, featuring intricate zellij tilework(geometric mosaics). - exteriorm: blue tiles, symbolizing fez’s famed cobalt-blue pottery. - interior: green tiles, representing islam. - arches: three horseshoe arches, a hallmark of islamic architecture, with the central arch accommodating pedestrians and vehicles. 3. cultural and practical significance - gateway to the medina: marks the transition into fes el-bali’s labyrinthine streets, souks, and historic landmarks like the bou inania madrasa and al quaraouiyine mosque. - daily life hub: surrounding cafes and restaurants (e.g., rooftop terraces) offer views of bustling activity—donkeys, vendors, and tourists mingling in the car-free zone. 4. unique details - locking mechanism: the french-designed gate locks from the outside, a reversal of traditional defensive gates, reflecting colonial control over medina access at night. - minaret views: from outside the gate, the arches frame minarets of the sidi lazzaz mosque (topped by stork nests) and the **bou inania madrasa. 5. visitor tips - best time to visit: early morning or late afternoon for photography and avoiding crowds. - nearby attractions: explore the souk el attarine (spice market) and dar batha museum for traditional crafts. bab boujloud is not just a monument but a living symbol of fez’s blend of history, artistry, and daily vitality. its dual-colored tiles and strategic role make it a must-see for travelers entering morocco’s medieval heart.

bab in arabic means 'gate' or 'door'; and 'jdid' means 'new' or 'modern'. the city of marrakesh, like all other cities in the middle eastern countries, had a protective (defense) wall around it and and to enter or exit the city, many gates were made. those gates were named. it is a common practice in the middle east. bab jdid was the new gate (or the latest addition) to the existing gates. it is a beautiful entrance, right in front of the famous hotel memounia and the historical koutoubia. years ago, it was just a crossing but now it has been much improved with a beautiful big water fountain, lighting and walkways leading to koutoubia. on the opposite, the same avenue leads to the famous menara garden, passing in front of the newly built menara mall. a beautiful area to walk in the evening.

bab jdid in fez is a modern gate that beautifully symbolizes the city’s blend of tradition and progress. its contemporary design seamlessly connects the old medina with the newer parts of the city, offering a fresh perspective on fez’s evolving character 🏙️. unlike the more historic gates, bab jdid has a peaceful atmosphere, providing visitors with a quieter experience as they enter the heart of the city. the surrounding area is vibrant and bustling, yet still exudes a sense of calm 🏛️, making it an ideal starting point for exploring both the modern and traditional sides of fez. whether you’re admiring the gate’s sleek lines or simply passing through, bab jdid is a testament to fez’s ability to honor its rich history while embracing the future ✨

bab mahrouk is one of fez’s hidden gems, offering a quieter, more intimate experience compared to the bustling gates of the medina. as i stood before the gate, the intricate details of its architecture—the stonework, engraved patterns, and arched passageways—captured the essence of the city’s rich history and craftsmanship 🏛️✨. unlike some of the more famous gates, bab mahrouk feels more personal and connected to the daily life of the people who pass through it. the surrounding neighborhood is a blend of old and new, with narrow streets and vibrant local life 🌿. it’s a perfect spot for those who want to explore fez beyond the usual tourist spots and experience the quieter, more authentic side of the city 🏙️. visiting bab mahrouk is a reminder that every corner of fez holds a story waiting to be discovered, and this gate is no exception—a gateway not only to the city but also to its timeless charm ✨

banteay kdei temple is a lesser-known gem within the angkor complex, offering a quieter and more serene experience compared to some of the more popular sites. the temple, like many others in the area, is partially in ruins, with much of it appearing to be destroyed and not fully maintained. this adds to its rustic charm, giving it a more authentic and ancient feel as if you're stepping back in time to an era long gone. the temple is surrounded by large trees, their roots intertwining with the stone structures in a way that’s both beautiful and a little eerie. the overgrown trees make the temple feel like it’s been reclaimed by nature, adding to its mysterious atmosphere. despite its state of disrepair, banteay kdei has a unique beauty that comes from its raw, unpolished condition. one of the highlights of banteay kdei is the large lake in front of the temple, which adds to the peaceful ambiance of the site. the reflection of the temple and the surrounding trees in the calm waters of the lake creates a stunning visual that’s perfect for photography and moments of quiet reflection. while exploring banteay kdei, it’s easy to get lost in its labyrinth of corridors and courtyards. the lack of crowds allows for a more personal and intimate experience, where you can take your time to appreciate the intricate carvings and the temple's unique layout. the temple's serene setting makes it a great spot to relax and absorb the history and natural beauty that surround you. in conclusion, banteay kdei may not be as grand or well-preserved as some of the other temples in the angkor complex, but it offers a peaceful retreat from the busier sites. the combination of its natural surroundings, the state of partial ruin, and the tranquil lake nearby make it a place worth visiting for those who appreciate the quieter, more reflective side of angkor.

banteay kdie is a stunning, lesser-known temple near the more famous ta prohm and preah khan. built in the late 12th century under king jayavarman vii, it combines the architectural styles of bayon and angkor wat, with intricate carvings and a serene, tree-covered atmosphere. unlike the crowded main temples, banteay kdie offers a peaceful experience where you can explore at your own pace. the mix of crumbling sandstone structures, towering roots, and quiet corridors makes it feel like a true adventure. it’s perfect for photography and history lovers!

banteay samre temple is a beautiful and often-overlooked hindu temple in the angkor region of cambodia, built in the 12th century in the distinctive angkor wat style. it's known for its intricate carvings, excellent state of preservation due to extensive restoration, and its peaceful, less crowded atmosphere compared to the more famous temples. visitors often find it a serene and rewarding experience, offering a glimpse into ancient khmer architecture and artistry away from the throngs of tourists. its detailed bas-reliefs and the overall resemblance to a "miniature angkor wat" make it a worthwhile visit for those seeking a quieter exploration of the area's rich history.

baphuon temple is an incredible architectural wonder within angkor thom. the raised sandstone walkway leading to the temple offers a majestic first impression, and the temple itself, once called the ‘world’s largest jigsaw puzzle’ due to its complex restoration, is both grand and peaceful. climbing to the top rewards you with beautiful panoramic views and a chance to admire the reclining buddha hidden at the back. it’s less crowded than angkor wat, making it a perfect place to enjoy the history and serenity of ancient cambodia.

barefoot conservation is a remarkable place. the staff and volunteers are a self selecting group of people interested in marine science and scuba diving, and with an adventurous spirit. if you've got to the stage of reading reviews then i believe this is one of the most memorable and rewarding adventures. i went with my daughter and we stayed for 5 weeks bar 2 nights in sorong half way to renew visas. thanks to: iris (operations manager), works very hard to ensure the smooth running of the site and deal with unexpected events. matt (diving instructor), very professional and good at explaining things with a great sense of humour. the marine science team, niko, tilly, septy and illman taught us a lot and were always willing to share their enthusiasm for their work and to pass on their knowledge to volunteers. local staff cooking our food, 3 meals a day 6 days a week, along with filling air tanks and driving the boats. excellent dive master trainees (dmts), thomas, seraina, bas, adela, we did a beach clean 2 evenings a week for about half an hour. going to 1 of 4 beaches and then sorting what we bought back to camp into hard plastic, soft plastic, glass etc, so it could be monitored / recorded. sometime the local children joined in collecting the rubbish and putting it in the collection bags which they enjoyed. there was a football match once a week with the locals on the local football field. generally a relaxed game and fun. the schools were closed for holiday while we were their but iris arranged for the children to visit barefoot camp and we setup 4 stands to explain about reef conservation and the marine science work carried out. their were prizes at the end for the children and they put colourful painted handprints on the wall next to a sign saying 'we are the ocean guardians'. the children loved it and were very excited. my daughter did her advanced and recovery diver while we were there and i brushed up on diving skills having not dived for some years. its a great place to do a diving course and matts an excellent instructor. also importantly if your there for a few weeks your diving twice a day so getting the repetition which i believe is crucial to making your diving skills second nature. the marine life is remarkable. second day diving at manta sandy there were about 8 reef mantas going round the cleaning station. seeing large reef mantas was quite common, sometimes passing a few meters away. there were large mantas and dolphins just of the barefoot jetty sometimes. one of the dmts had 2 dolphins swimming around her after her swim test. saw black tip and white tip sharks further away some days as well as so many other types of fish. we also started to notice smaller sea creatures like the 'nudis' nudibranchs, sea moths and pygmy seahorse, with encouragement and pointers from the marine science team. i wrote a list of objectives before going to barefoot with my daughter. 1. improve my bahasa indonesian. - tick, not a massive improvement but certainly progress. 2. improve marine science / reef conservation skills. - big tick, we learned so much. 3. improve scuba diving. - big tick, lots of great dives. 4. teach english in the local school. - did not happen due to school holidays, but don't feel i missed out as there was so much else going on. 5. memorable and fun adventures with alex. - absolutely, massive tick. what a great adventure. suggestions / observations: if you do any of the locals boat trips on a sunday, take the life jackets from barefoot. - try not to get minor foot injuries, boots rubbing / mosquito bites, as they take longer to heal in the climate. - bring plenty of waterproof plasters. - i bought my own bcd and octopus rig which was nice. also bought dive computers for us both to save renting and deposit. (suunto zoop novo 'lemon yellow') - bring a sleeping bag you can open up to sleep on and put on top of the mattress.

barron falls – absolutely majestic! arriving at the barron falls lookout after the scenic train journey was a truly awe-inspiring experience. the anticipation built during the winding ascent through the rainforest, and then, suddenly, you're presented with this powerful and breathtaking natural wonder. even from the viewing platforms, the sheer scale and force of the water cascading down the barron gorge is immense. the mist rising from the base creates a dramatic atmosphere, and the roar of the falls is something you can feel as much as hear. it’s a fantastic reward after the scenic railway trip. the different viewing areas offer varied perspectives, allowing you to appreciate the falls from multiple angles. the signage provides helpful information about the geology and ecology of the area, adding another layer of appreciation to the experience. the brief stop here as part of the kuranda scenic railway journey is perfectly timed to allow for some fantastic photo opportunities and a chance to truly soak in the natural beauty. it’s a stark reminder of the raw power of nature and a definite highlight of the entire kuranda experience. whether you visit during the wet season when the falls are at their peak flow or during a drier period when you can see more of the rock formations, barron falls is a must-see. the accessibility provided by the kuranda scenic railway makes it an easy and unforgettable addition to any cairns itinerary. don't forget your camera – you'll want to capture this incredible sight!

bazaruto archipelago, mozambique the six islands of the bazaruto archipelago—bazaruto, benguerra, magaruque, santa carolina, bangue, and shell—are a protected conservation area and national park off the eastern coast of africa. nicknamed the “pearl of the indian ocean,” the islands have only seen the arrival of big-name resorts within the past decade, like the impeccable andbeyond benguerra island in 2015. pro tip: this is one of the few habitats of the endangered manatee-like dugong, which sailors sometimes mistook for mermaids. getting there: fly to vilanculos on the coast of mozambique; from there, take a seaplane to your final destination.

be ready for crowds when you visit notre-dame, it was super crowded when i went. the good thing is, you don’t need a ticket or reservation. just join the line and wait your turn. it can take a while, but it’s definitely worth it. construction started way back in 1163 and took nearly 200 years to finish. walking inside feels like stepping back in time. one noteworthy thing is that the roof was built with wooden beams instead of stone, like many later cathedrals. that’s actually why the roof burned so fast during the big fire in 2019, it was mostly ancient wood, which caught fire quickly. if you look up at the roof, you’ll see those little stone creatures called gargoyles. they’re not just creepy decorations. some of them work as water spouts to direct rain away from the walls, and others were thought to scare off evil spirits. either way, they’re super cool and make great photos. overall, i think notre-dame is a must-visit if you’re in paris. it’s full of history, beauty, and a special spiritual feeling. even after the fire, it’s still an amazing place to see. i’m definitely planning to go back once the restoration is fully finished so i can see it in all its glory again.
