beautiful 12km round trip intermediate hike. took us just under 5 hours with a break at the falls. in one section, there is a chain to help climb down and up as it's pretty steep. dog friendly hike. the parking lot was full, and we had to wait for a spot. didn't take very long however. definitely recommend. i can see this to be a challenging hike for some as it can be technical in areas.

beautiful accommodations! excellent food! professional staff! daniel was our safari guide. his knowledge of the animals and their surroundings; his sense of humor; and his genuine concern for each of us made the experience memorable. i highly recommend this overnight safari!

beautiful all year round -but winter time can be a bit too cold. visited in late spring and surprisingly there are still snow at the peak. pretty view from the top, worth all of the trip going here. there is only one restaurant here, so prepare your food before you’re visiting.
beautiful amazing coastal walking made me relaxing weekend recommend little bit difficult and long than bondi coastal walk
beautiful ambience and food on the cruise. the team and artists were amazing, really enjoyed the experience. would highly recommend.
beautiful and a huge masjid. awesome architecture. was not rushy at all when we visited. big parking, ablution area and a prayer hall.
beautiful and a must see once in a lifetime at least! the stations of the cross are all throughout the quarter. we had an amazing day!
beautiful and accessible temple, some dogs are living there but they are not aggressive
beautiful and breathtaking view. to go down takes 25-30 mins from the parking. you are surrounded by pure nature. after 7pm you can go by car - before 7 pm only by bus.
beautiful and breathtaking view. to go down takes 25-30 mins from the parking. you are surrounded by pure nature. after 7pm you can go by car - before 7 pm only by bus.
beautiful and calm public garden with a nice view on the koutoubia mosque!
beautiful and calming place with a lot of black iguanas :)

beautiful and clean beach. well maintained. the place is so cooling and soothing. one can relax in the beach and watch the waves flow. this beach is very good in so many ways, its a best place for morning excercise and there are so many people come for work out, beach sports, surfing etc
beautiful and easy accessible viewpoint with a parking lot close by. you can also see waterfalls.

beautiful and easy hike that you can also adjust by turning to pr6, 6.1 and 6.3 on the way. the hiking routes are connected so you can make a circle and don’t have to go the whole way back to the starting point. i recommend to do pr6.2 and then 6.3 if you don’t like to go up, and the other way around if you like a bit of a challenge (e.g. hundreds of steps up) and then have a relaxing time at the lake and easy way back.
beautiful and easy trail, three best photo spot! bring some snacks and drinks with blanket, enjoy picnic at third spot.

beautiful and easy walk. i did this first thing in the morning to watch the sunrise and it was stunning. well maintained trails and some big gorgeous trees. there’s a lot of activities, like bowling, tennis, skating and frisbee golf. i didn’t partake in any but it’s awesome that it’s there. it’s a quick walk and the gardens, landscape, and views are worth it!

beautiful and exciting experience. we've had an amazing english speaking guide who told us all about the volcano, the processes of lava and magma, and nature. he is very knowledgeable. at the beginning of the hike, we saw a vermilion flycather, which is on the brink of extinction, according to our guide. but this is the best area to spot this beautiful little bird. the hike is beautiful with a different landscape every half our. the hike is doable from a moderate physical condition and up. the guides take good care of you and make sure you rest enough. we've booked with the tour operator rosedelco, which i would recommend to everyone

beautiful and fairly easy hike in good weather. paid parking at the bottom (around 40 norake kroner) and without doubt the most magnificent and most “lofooten-insta-friendly” peak picture 😊 islands and azure-blue water as far as you can see. the track itself is dirt and some gravel. few more steep parts but all you need is sturdy shoes. start the hike from the parking and make your way up the paved road going up towards the mountain. turn left after about 100m and follow the trotted down trail towards the snakebends and follow to the top. at a point you can chose to go left or right. if you go right, you walk around the mountain. you you go left you go to the peak. a big recommendation to do the peak 😊👍

beautiful and fun water parks for babies up to even my 11 years old. the water is clean and not cold. perfect height for my 2 years old. the bigger slide were fun for my 11 year old. the life guards are quick to come help an even give inflatable life jacket. i do worry about the cement steps to climb up the water park. and if you're hungry? no worries right next to to the water park they have hot dogs, nachos and plenty of juice to refill and go back. nonetheless you'll kids will love it! so will you as it will tire them out for mommy and daddy to relax after.

beautiful and giant gate. we lucked out and caught the changing of the guard. the custom and uniforms were beautiful and the ceremony extremely elegant! a large number of guests were wearing their own period costumes, which is typical since admission the palace grounds is free- made the visit amazing!

beautiful and hidden part of west scottish coast. we visited the ruins on the way to ardnamurchan campsite and were sooo surprised. apart from the majestic castle ruins, there is a beautiful 360 degrees view around the loch and the sea, hills and nature around. parking next to the beach. beautiful shells. almost no people.
beautiful and large park. the beach’s are amazing and the food shacks make some tasty treats on a hot summer day!

beautiful and less touristy temple. you must not officially pay an entrance fee but there is someone at the street that tells you to pay 50.000 per person for a ticket. we fell for it and i think the price is too high for what you get.

beautiful and lovely afternoon! don't spend the $40+ per person the surrounding hotels will happily charge you. this is completely free, something quite rare in costa rica. if you arrive by car an "official" in hi vis will ask for $10 for parking, you don't have to pay this but if you would rather avoid the awkwardness of saying no, then it's a small charge comparable. follow a trail by the side of the road, walk through the dodgy looking cut out wire fence and you've arrived. water is beautiful and warm. arrived at lunch time and was quite quiet, picked up as we left around 1pm. seen a rather large iguana but they didn't get in the water. lovely spot!

beautiful and majestic with great views. large open field up top where many fly kites. not much more than that but i may have missed some historical context. walked around the outside of the sea wall, from the docks, past the gate all the way around to the fort. will be hot but nice breeze once you're at the fort. and there are carts selling drinks at the fort!!

beautiful and most historically original of the palaces in seoul even if it wasnt the main palace. the secret garden is absolutely worth it. i booked the tickets for the secret garden online and it turned out to be a great decision since all tickets were sold out by the time we arrived in the afternoon.
beautiful and peaceful garden with plenty of spaces for resting and picnic. perfect for a chill weekend day!
beautiful and peaceful japanese garden space with running water instructures surrounded by vegetation.
beautiful and peaceful japanese garden with lots of sakura flowers and other plants! great for a stroll as it is super convenient. 3 mins from the hamamatsucho jr station!
beautiful and peaceful place for sight seeing. within town the local snacks are nice too.
beautiful and peaceful place. the mosque nearby has a very loud preaching in the late night and too early morning

beautiful and peaceful short walk to the waterfall. love the feeling of tranquility as you walk toward the waterfall. would love to come back during the fall. 2000 entrance fee worth every penny. no parking fee.

beautiful and peaceful. it wasn’t crowded at all. you can take the #250 bus in the direction of horseshoe bay from vancouver and get off at beacon lane for a short walk to the park and then there are a bunch of hikes through the forest and with views on the water, with the highlight being the light house (best seen from the west beach view). highly recommend. the trails are very up and down and have stones/roots on the ground, so definitely watch your steps.

beautiful and picturesque, loves the squirrels, birds and the many varieties of flowers just beautifying the garden and park. loved the playground for kids (and some for adults). this was overall a nice walk in the park

beautiful and popular beach. during low tide, many went to do beach combing - can find shrimps, hermit crabs and crabs there. public toilet is easily accessible and facilities outside the toilets for beach goers to wash their feet as well.

beautiful and quick hike to the cave!!! very tranquil at the sunset. i started off at the long canyon trailhead. the fork to the birthing cave is not marked. instead, there is a log in front of it. look at the picture below, right where there is a sign for trail you need to take a left turn behind the log towards the cave. that’s a quick and easy way!
beautiful and quiet place that's filled with peacocks. make sure you bring good footwear though.
beautiful and quiet spot! my go to place for relaxing and reading a book
beautiful and quiet. follow the trail and then walk the beach to the other side to see marine iguanas and birds. follow the path to the bay where you can swim and rent kayaks. beautiful walk.
beautiful and quiet. follow the trail and then walk the beach to the other side to see marine iguanas and birds. follow the path to the bay where you can swim and rent kayaks. beautiful walk.

beautiful and serene. the trails around the park are easy to negotiate and connect to more challenging trails. there is a portapotty and no running water. i enjoyed a 30 minute meditation while my husband snapped some pics that included some javelina that joined my meditation.
beautiful and serene. well maintained. there are restrooms and water fountains.
beautiful and spectacular place with great acoustics. artists are great and music is fabulous. i will be there every time i visit vienna!
beautiful and spiritually uplifting temple. it was a good visit and nice end of the repulse bay beach walk.
beautiful and stunning hike. the hike starts off steep but then it’s a breeze to get by! the views are certainly rewarding!

beautiful and stunning mosque. the whole area is full of history and imagery. the golden dome shines brightly, then you see the craftsmanship and intricate detail of the tiles. inside of course is the rock, surrounding by the mosque area. the dome again is decorated as is all the internal space. fantastic opportunity to visit and one not to be forgotten easily.

beautiful and thrilling experience great for the entire family. our family ranging in age from 11 to 65 all enjoyed this experience together. it was a peaceful walk through the woods that opened up to beautiful views of the lake. we had a wonderful tour guide and well trained horses that all had such personality. 100% recommend.

beautiful and unique experience - even though we had a cloudy sky. waking up to a magnificent sunrise, fresh air and 2 majestic oryx standing 5m away from us is something that not everyone has the privilege to experience - great full! big shout out to tony - our guide who added a bubbly and positive atmosphere to our short stay there - thank you! also, for couples that want some privacy and for the best sunrise view, room 9 is the one to choose, it’s a bit of a walk, but totally worth it! unfortunately we weren’t able to shower in the morning, as the water pressure was almost none existent and my steak for dinner was a bit tough, minor details that are easily changed ;)

beautiful architectural interior with a beautiful selection of cakes all fitting for the location. we booked online so when we arrived we were able to walk past the very long queue outside and go straight inside and we were seated immediately. the place is every bit as beautiful as all the photos and there was someone playing the piano which added to the elegant ambience. tea was beautifully served and the cakes were some of the best we’d had during our week in austria. there’s a vast selection on offer so it’s tough to choose something! and the ones we tried tasted as good as they looked. the cakes and the beverages were all very reasonably priced too. they also have a full food menu too which is also very reasonably priced. although this is known as a touristy place, i would definitely come back and try a meal here. maybe in the evening so we can enjoy the evening ambience. all in all a lovely experience.
beautiful architecture and a larger- than- expected museum on a lovely university campus.
beautiful architecture and lots of shops, and restaurants. easy to walk around

beautiful architecture with striking gold features, set against the backdrop of a serene pond—truly picturesque. the tour felt somewhat commercial, with a strong focus on directing tourists through nearby shops, which detracted slightly from the cultural experience, but was still acceptable overall. it would have been wonderful to see the interior of the building as well.
beautiful architecture. just think of this gorgeous building and what year it was built(1912). amazing

beautiful area in its own right which you come to after following the path from the mausoleum. good to see how living was back then for a man of this stature and how his environment was adapted with age. again walk around given path, no real waiting but you can take photos.

beautiful area of the archeological site. this space got very hot early in the day. minimal shade available.

beautiful area with lots of trails. really steep, but worth it to get to the top and (hopefully) see views of the city. visited in mid august and enjoyed the wildflowers blooming. parking exists from the bottom to the top of the park, so you can choose your own strenuous adventure. we parked closer to the top, then trailed down to haight street and enjoyed that area while walking to the golden gate park. after our visit there, we took a driverless waymo back to our car for a fabulous tour of sf.

beautiful area with lots to see about this historical building. visitor guide via qr code will provide audio explanation for lots of the room and special features. many levels to explore especially unique with some world war era exhibits. petty cool! on site pay parking available. good to spend a few hours to walk around and learn more about this casa lima. some higher levels will require walking up/down some staircase especially the top level .. recommended

beautiful area, but aren't they all!! they are still under a bit of construction. but great spot for a picnic.

beautiful area. we parked up top. they told us when we got tickets that the parking was included so that was good. i thought i had seen somewhere that it was also $12. we enjoyed the grounds, the bridge, doing a hike in the area and the stairs. parking was pretty busy as there wasn’t a lot of space up top. the trail on the other side of the bridge that leads you up river was awesome - peaceful and quite enjoyable. can stay on the trail or take the shelf alongside the river. ran into a long time resident who had given us that tip to go down to the river. also found myself thinking that you could save admission by parking on the other side of the river across the other side of the bridge that goes upstream. the stairs are a good workout!

beautiful area. we visited in winter and took a tour to see the stella’s sea eagles. the tour was great and was extremely informative. got to see quite a few eagles too. be sure to wear appropriate clothing as the weather gets very cold particularly if it’s windy.
beautiful around of the center of town to sit and chill. lots of rich covered grass seating and a small river that passes through the small park.
beautiful artisan gift shop with lots of beautiful variety. the owner was also so welcoming and kind.
beautiful as ever. some stretches seem to have lost their live oaks. (katrina?) need to replant some live oaks - we need the shade.

beautiful austro-hungarian fortress made for defensive purposes, giving vision to all surrounding area, great observatory point and it's almost invisible from sea level, so also from this strategic point, usefull. it was built after kicking of benedict monks from the lokrum island by french army of napoleon and later transformed it into military area for austro-hungarian dominance period. as four other islands of croatia that benedict monks were taking care of for around 700 years surrounding area is relatively untouched by human inference and left as national reserve area.

beautiful autumn garden full of pumpkins and plants. it’s done by local community . it’s one of the prettiest street decoration i have ever seen. it gives halloween vibes. it is a popular place to take pictures.

beautiful beach and great amenities. relaxing atmosphere. the restaurant is great with an amazing service.
beautiful beach and it was possible to swim here, comparing to other beaches at la digue. picturesque stones from the left and you can go snorkeling here as well. there are benches to sit and relax.

beautiful beach area not far out of the city with many areas to sit and enjoy the sun and swim. about a 15 minute walk from the pile gate, along the water to a fantastic swimming and sunning area. many flat places to sit or lay on a towel along with rocky areas that provide places to sit or jump off the rocks into the water. the views are amazing, quite a different area than the crowded downtown center. if you are in town for a few days and need a break, take the walk to dance beach, it's worth the walk

beautiful beach at the heart of city centre. we were in the month of june and it was not so crowded but july and aug is extremely crowded as what i have heard. don’t expect this as a sandy beach, do bring your slippers or water boots to enhance your experience in the water. there is a café too, but what i have heard as it is overpriced, but really a good spot to have a swim after the long day in the city centre.

beautiful beach at the north of the island. it is a small beach, very peaceful and nice. the sand is white and smooth, surrounded by palm trees and mangroves. the access is easy, but you need to downstairs from the top of the hill. important, the beach is inside the hotel, only guests can access by foot.
beautiful beach but maybe not worth the hike. we walked the shore and then up though a small path into the hotel area.
beautiful beach for the doggies. they love swimming in the water. there’s a hose to wash them down afterwards. perfect therapy for all dog lovers 🐶 🐩 🐕
beautiful beach not just for summer. try some diy firework from the street vendors or from daiso or nearby shops. sealife aquarium is within walking distance.

beautiful beach with a peaceful atmosphere. there was a warning sign for jellyfish, but it didn’t take away from the experience. it’s a relatively small beach for walking along the coast, but the size and location felt just right. i’d love to go back and reconnect with nature anytime. i already miss it!
beautiful beach with a shallow tidal pool. beautiful white sand with no shells and very few bamboo. you can park right by the beach and then walk down about 150m to where the beach starts.

beautiful beach with calm waters and beautiful „jungle“ in the back. a great spot for amazing sunsets. there is a beach restaurant, we didn’t visit though. there is a parking area and i would recommend leaving your car there as the last couple of hundred meters are quite steep. if you rented a small car it would most likely be a struggle :)
beautiful beach with lots of kelp and jellyfish 🪼 washed up ashore. it was a beautiful day on a beautiful white natural beach. we weren’t impressed that the signs say it is unsafe.
beautiful beach with soft pink tinged sand. enjoyed a fresh coconut for 40k.

beautiful beach with white sand and blue water. great place to take photos. nice black volcanic rock. very family friendly. there are bathrooms and an open air changing area for men and another one for women. amazing place to watch the sunset. there are a few cafés around if you are hungry and want to buy something to eat.
beautiful beach! gorgeous water and lovely white sand! the water was cool and crisp! lots of parking spots, though it’s paid parking (not too expensive though, 2000krw).

beautiful beach! the views are absolutely amazing at all times of the day. the early morning is pretty calm but it gets fairly busy in the late morning and early afternoons. the sand is amazing however try stay closer to the hilton pier as the further southwest you get, the rockier the ground gets underwater. beautiful place to swim and lay out.

beautiful beach, although watch out with the massive waves and undertows, especially if you have children with you. there are no life guards and lots of exposed rocks on both sides of the beach so keep yourself in the middle of the beach if you are swimming
beautiful beach, good parking next to beach. supermarkets, restaurants, coffee next to the beach.
beautiful beach, way more touristy than jumbiani beach. lovely and quiet night wandering on the beach.
beautiful beach. blue water and black volcono rocks. so beautiful to watch and in spring it ll be double beautiful because of yellow flowers (canola flowers)

beautiful beach. visited a couple of times. a little quieter than waikiki beach and kuhio beach. waves can be high. one of the days we were lucky to see a seal, which swam right up close to the shore.
beautiful beach. white sands. i imagine it would be nicer in the warmer months when you can enjoy the water. otherwise, there's not much to do here. photo ops are plentiful, though.

beautiful beyond words..pl book ticket for guided tours online, they fill up fast.. though they sell offline tickets 30 mins before the tour from the opera house( but these are unsold tickets so not sure if you would one, but you may try your luck). arrive at the venue 15 mins before the time..it is a must visit place in vienna.. highly recommend this one
beautiful big garden. it takes around 15 minutes walking from the upper palace to the lower palace. wear a hat or take an umbrella if you visit in summer here in case the sun is too harsh.

beautiful blend of history, spirituality, and scenic views. crossing the vibrant red thê húc bridge to reach the temple feels like stepping into another world. it’s a peaceful spot to pause, appreciate local culture, and enjoy a unique perspective of the lake. definitely worth a visit while in hanoi!

beautiful blend of trendy americana and cool, vintage italian (with some new pieces thrown in), all at high but reasonable prices (€15-185). a curated collection of men’s and women’s jackets (leather and 80s printed), shirts, pants, skirts, belts, plus limited shoes & dresses. many options, mostly small sizes. gender neutral changing rooms. one small ledge to enter, plenty of space inside for ♿️. if you’re into vintage and looking for a unique souvenir or new outfit for the next part of your european tour, it’s worth your time. while it’s not my favorite vintage shop in venice, it’s perfect for what it is (trendy, curated, clean classic pieces at a price you can afford). my best finds: d&g leather belt with cheeky mod belt buckle (€15), vintage maroon silk bomber (kids xl €35), leather vest (€45), and burberry trench coat (€350). fantastic decor, but the best, rare pieces are all not for sale, so best to refrain from looking up at the shelves, lest you be tempted by what you cannot have. very friendly owner. she will help if you ask. and locals shop here too, which says a lot 😉

beautiful botanical garden maintained by volunteers. i’ve been lucky to find it open on mid-day thursday outside of officially stuffed hours. variety of plants, trees and flowers. quaint brick paths to explore garden’s corners. so much more than typical community garden.

beautiful botanical indoor garden. you can easily loose concept of time and you are admiring all the plants. beautifully created space to see the plantes from 3 levels. would highly recommended if you enjoy plants and nature
beautiful both in the morning
beautiful breezy place. you can take a nap inside the empty canon holes on the wall. the walled city is very walkable, feels safe, people are friendly, and plenty of cool things to experience.

beautiful buddhist monastery at an altitude of 4,031 m (13,225 ft) in suru valley of kargil district (leh ladakh union territory of bharat) on padum-sankoo-kargil road. situated on a ridge and provides fabulous view of surrounding landscape. people are very nice, polite and kind hearted. they offer tea with puri and chana for us during the morning prayers. worth visiting.
beautiful building
beautiful building and statue. only saw exterior.
beautiful building with a lovely garden. note: you can walk around the garden without needing to pay for the museum which is $5. so i highly recommend it!!

beautiful building with some really spectacular pieces worth seeing. building is clean with professional & helpful staff however, it is in need of some basic upkeep/repair - especially the second floor. definitely worth the visit!
beautiful building, and nice cocktails with booths to drink them in.
beautiful buildings and art collections. but the site is not well maintained: filthy and the garden is very neglected. overall pricey for what it is, but a nice site

beautiful but busy place. well kept gardens with a large sinkhole at its centre. lots of tourists at peak times as all the local tour companies come here. it’s worth a visit if you’re passing by or visiting other local attractions like wadi shab. parking is free and there is access to very basic toilets.

beautiful but busy — get there early! the bamboo forest was absolutely beautiful, but as many have mentioned, it does get very crowded. what surprised us, though, is that the bamboo grove is actually just a small part of a much larger, stunning park. if you’re an early riser, it’s definitely worth heading there first thing in the morning to enjoy the peaceful surroundings before the crowds arrive. the town itself is super charming, but most shops don’t open until around 10 a.m. one highlight for us was visiting the former home of an old japanese actor — admission was only 1,000 yen and totally worth it. the gardens were gorgeous, and there were plenty of great photo spots.

beautiful but demanding hike. the trail starts with a steep section up to about 350 meters above sea level, on a rocky forest trail with lots of roots and some slippery sections. the views on the sea immediately appear. above the tree line, you can take a side trail to see the view on grunnfør fjord and its beautiful colors. the trail further to matmora now follows a ridge. first gently, but you have to cross a few steeper sections, where you will have to be careful. people with vertigo will not have fun here. the last section still follows the ridge, but here it is a scree field. from the top, you can see the vesterålen alps, the mainland, most of lofoten and more. stunning. i highly recommend hiking it in the evening (only during midnight sun season). i used 1h40m up, but jogged for quite some time and did not take any breaks. more reasonable hiking time up would be 2.5-3 hours, a bit shorter down. one of the better hikes i have done. be careful and enjoy! 😊
beautiful but full of trash and broken bottles. good for photos but be very careful of the bottles.
beautiful but very crowded. you can rest here and enjoy the atmosphere.
beautiful cacti garden with a large amount of different cacti from around the world. some of them are several meters high. here you can sit down and enjoy nature.

beautiful castle and gardens to explore, dog friendly in the woodland areas and outside castle. tearoom with outside seating area. beautiful gardens round castle. you can purchase a ticket for castle and gardens or just separate if you dont want to visit both. excellent parking great for dog walks staff really friendly and helpful

beautiful castle and gardens. the castle is a family home so it is closed friday/ saturday - best to phone beforehand before visiting. the castle is really well maintained and loved. it has a really good feel to it. the cafe is excellent - a good range of food and gluten free options. the staff are really grand very helpful. the gardens are a joy to walk around.

beautiful drive with loads of adventure! from horses, cows, and sheep temporarily blocking the highway to long winding roads between snowcapped mountains, green valleys, and mirror lakes ... this route had it all. we drove it at the end of winter, but i think it's probably amazing year round. san martin de los andes and villa angostura are two essential stops along the route. you can expect it to take all day but there's really no need to leave early unless you really want to savor every view point. you can get to san martin for a late lunch or early dinner, then head back to bariloche, assuming that's where you started. staying the night in any of the three towns is probably easy. i saw a lot of signs showing availability. driving through the andes is an incredible experience, and i think this route might be one of the best. of note, one route was under construction and didn't feel safe to drive. it was route 65 to villa traful. every other road felt very safe and comfortable.

beautiful hike! the hike is free (unlike many around the faroe islands), with a lovely view of the lake right next to the open ocean. you can park in town or drive further right up to the beginning of the trail, however note that there is only space for maybe 4-5 cars here. the trail itself is marked with orange posts most of the way - it is advertised as moderate in difficulty and suitable for children, however it was harder than i expected. the beginning is fairly straightforward, however the descent down to the lake is somewhat steep, uneven, muddy, and slippery. you can return via the same path, or by hiking up through frostgjógv gorge - this is fairly steep and the terrain consists of grass and then rocks (see attached pictures). best to allow 2-2.5 hours round trip depending on fitness and pace.

beautiful hike. confusing in where it starts/ends. we parked just outside of porto da cruz where its just a dead end at someone's backyard. beware the "no parking" signs - i heard that some people get their car tires slashed by parking there. people just park along the side of this road and then walk up the dead end area, for about 20 minutes its just dirt road. then you have the start of the trail. its forest with some small waterfalls, exposed area, then forest again, then you reach boca do risa. we considered going to machico from here and continuing on the canical hike as others have done but we did about 30 minutes of it and it is a tough hike up and through the mountains. we were not prepared and it looked like rain. turned around and headed back to the car. it was about 10km, 28k steps, and took about 3 hours in total if we had turned around at the boca do riso viewpoint. note that that some people are talking about a longer hike, and some are talking about the in and out hike from varada larano to boca do riso. no bathrooms, bring plastic bag, tissue, hand santizer. don't leave garbage on the ground. hiking poles helpful if you have a mild fear of heights

beautiful hike. don't trust google maps for the location of janela do inferno. park at the parking lot in front of the small park with the hamburger stand. the trail starts to the right of the park if you're facing it. it looks like a dirt road. after a few kilometers on the dirt road, you'll see a small wooden sign for janela do inferno. follow that trail, then look for the yellow and red markers on small wooden posts for the trail. the yellow and red equal sign means go straight. if there's one with an angle it means turn in the direction it's pointing. if there's a red and yellow x, it means don't go that way. bring a flashlight for the tunnel. and prepare yourself to feel like indian jones.

beautiful restored byzantine monestary/chapel! this is where jesus was asked how do we talk to god. he replied with a good example. the lord's prayer. ask forgiveness first, so god can hear the rest of your prayer. beautiful place

beautiful royal temple. very popular for wedding pic taken and blessing ceremony. official residence for the 20th supreme patriarch of thailand. it’s advisable to wear white attire when visiting this temple and cover shoulders and knee for being respectful. secondly if you are here for photo taking, white is encourage for a beautiful pic against the colourful tiles. inner circle of the temple are not open to public unless you are invited.

beautiful scenery and snorkeling! i wish we could have watched the monkeys a little longer though. jennifer was the best tour guide and definitely in her element. she did such an amazing job!!! i really appreciated her and the rest of the crew! fantastic job!

beautiful scenic walk. it’s a bit hard to find the starting point but once you do the trail is easy to follow. beware that there are limited bathroom facilities for the first few miles. once you reach the end you’ll need to find a way back to your car and the bus near the port is infrequent. the trail itself is mostly easy and flat.
beautiful selection of unique pieces of pottery with excellent customer service.

beautiful serene space for holistic learning and experiences. owner sonya has a goal of yourh outreach and assimilation through education in life skills and emotional character development. we had our wedding there and the ambiance and care could not have been better.

beautiful setting for this luxurious tented lodge. from fully furnished lodge, individual pools, comfortable lounge all is available for a relaxing stay. plenty of activities (safaris, boat, pagoda, ...) delicious food and wonderful service complete the offer.

beautiful shopping and dining with modern style leading into old world allys that have small family run shops with many items that reflect the culture and history of the region.

beautiful shrine located not far from nijo castle, only 20 minute walk or few minutes by bus. i came to this shrine mainly for its association with japanese olympic champion figure skater yuzuru hanyu’s seimei program, there were several prayer tablets dedicated to him ❤️ but i could also really feel that this is a very special and divine place, and i was able to pray peacefully 🙏 very quiet with occasional worshippers coming and going, not completely empty but no where near busy or crowded. highly recommend a stop by if you walk past

beautiful site and amenities. i discovered balnea spa because i received a gift card for my birthday so my husband and i decided to make a day out of it with our 2 teenagers. the overall experience was very good. the balnea message is amazing the best we ever had. the amenities were clean and well maintained. after the message we took advantage of the amenities. a few observations: people do not respect the rules. a lot of people had their phones, even if it was written everywhere that it's not allowed. people were reserving all the chairs that had shades even when 100 signs was saying not to do it. unfortunately the management did not say anything. they have a beautiful setting on the lake with those floating matresses on the water. unfortunately the same people were using them the whole day and we did not have a chance to try them.either add more or have a reservation schedule. a few people waited for them with no success. $$$ the package i was gifted included 2 balnea messages. 4 wine tasting and access to the site worth $490 plus tx. we purchased 2 additional tickets for our teens to access the site for $200 plus tx.we had lunch at the restaurant: one green been salad (20 green beens) with 5 small pieces of smoked salmon, 2 soupes one small cheese plates (10 bites) 2 baskets of bread. 2 small glacess of wine and 2 rise: $170. outside of these observation the experience was very good. if you can afford it, i do recommend this place.

beautiful site. unfortunately, it is commonplace for the orthodox priests to be rude and unspiritual to visitors. not all of them are rude, but several are. i have experienced this myself multiple times, having lived in jerusalem for 1.5 years. sad misrepresentation of jesus, but being able to be at the site is still great.

beautiful small park with a unique fountain of dogs. the hands were really cool to see. plenty of benches to sit on and relax. the only downside was the drunk homeless loafing around on the wall by the fountain and it was very crowded and busy there towards late afternoon. otherwise, clean and something worth seeing.

beautiful small park, relaxing feel - great for families and couples. entrance is through the kin ha restaurant. pay 450 pesos per person for a beach chair and access to water activities (kayak, snorkel, life vests, outdoor pools). get 300 pesos back in food/drink. it’s a great deal for beautiful water & views.

beautiful small theater, where 90% of the seats are great. i was on the first row in the first balcony, excellent view. bought tickets online, and it was very easy to access my seats with the digital tickets. in february, the heating was very high, good for light clothing. seats are comfortable with very little leg-room. sound is good given the size of the venue; a 20-minute intermission will give you time to visit the bar or just admire the architecture.

beautiful small trail near the city centre. accessible almost year round. during spring floods the trail and the duckboards may be underwater. good place to watch birds, especially during migration time of the year. there's a small bird watching tower at end of the trail. dogs must be kept on leash. only minus side is the traffic noise from the highway.
beautiful snorkling, so many colorful fish and saw a reef shark, feels like coral is beginning to grow back here, little more color around! definatly worth a visit
beautiful spa outside the medina, staff super friendly, everything very clean, hammam treatment and massage were wonderful. you feel like a newborn afterwards. highest recommendations

beautiful spot for photos and relaxation. best swimming spot when it’s a hot day as it’s usually not too busy with heaps of space to chillax on the lakefront too. public toilets are also located here with a couple picnic benches to sit and enjoy the view. i would recommend insect repellent as there are some sand flies.
beautiful spot for views of 1wtc and the hudson river

beautiful spot just next to kings landing harbour of game of thrones film location.

beautiful spot off a gravel/ unsealed road. easily accessible but a very dry area. beautiful short hike to a stunning waterfall. bring swimmers and a packed lunch. there’s easy access into the pool at the bottom of the falls and a rope swing for all to try. if you’re ballsy some guys were jumping off the rocks next to the falls. deep enough at the bottom. stunning waterfalls unlike most other in the area and much less known. i got a tick on the trail so be cautious

beautiful spot to have a swim with a beautiful view of dubrovnik walls. there are steps into the sea making it really accessible, especially if you don't have water shoes. you can also swim around to the cave.

beautiful spot to visit if you are in qurum park, the waterfalls look so real, and the sound of water is giving a good vide to the whole place. there are stairs to go up and enjoy a splendid view of all the park; it is a perfect spot to take memorable pictures as well.
beautiful spot to walk around amsterdam. very friendly to pets and families.

beautiful spot with a lovely view of the falls. we visited in the dry season, so there wasn’t as much water as we’ve seen during the wet season, but it’s still worth stopping by. unfortunately, queensland rail was doing track maintenance on the day of our visit, so we couldn’t walk down to the lower platform for a closer look. be aware that the toilets are long drops and quite smelly – in the qld summer heat they’ll likely be worse! 🤢🤭😂 still, a lovely site to take in the scenery when in the area.

beautiful spot! the wheel was amazing and we got to go around three times. what a fantastic view of the hotel zone and beyond. the whole area had so much to do from shopping with lots of stores from high end boutiques to our usual go-tos, to an aquarium, restaurants, ripley's - definitely worth spending some time here!

beautiful spot, and i found my favorite lighter here. bob marley "get up, stand up", and barely used. i sat for an hour and took in the air. the area is lively yet not too overstimulating and the sun shines brightly on you as you watch the city.

beautiful spot, but a bit crowded at the bridge in early august. sky car is recommended to get to top. some of steps are worn and could be challenging for those with balance issues. also, the bridge over the falls moves and sways slightly, so be aware of that if it is a problem for you.

beautiful spot. friends of the gardens run tours at 10am mon to fri and there's a bird tour tuesdays at 7.30am! look out for the friends of the garden visitors centre as well as the council run visitors centre - lots of awesome souvenirs in both, with friends of the garden very decently priced.

beautiful square in paris, large corinthian brass column of july dominates the square. the column is topped by a beautiful gold statue of the spirit of liberty. the national opera house is located across the street. wonderful new opera house to see opera and ballet productions!

beautiful square with a mix of palaces, old buildings and a park. one really interesting detail is that the tiles on the road near the palace are made out of wood. according to our guide, a mayor of the city at the time, ordered that they put wooden tiles so that the horse carriages don't make too much noise while he is having a siesta.

beautiful staircase! leeds to a church. it was definitely a popular picture spot long before its game of thrones fame. gets super crowded by lunch time so if you want to get a proper photo you need to ho super early in the morning.
beautiful stairs to let you look at the amazing view. beautiful stone staircase allowing access to the heights of the island and admiring the view.

beautiful stay with amazing service and facilities. the camp is surrounded by beautiful mountains all around and the place has bonfires too. rooms were spacious and clean. the owner and workers were so helpful and generous. we booked the tent camps however, they upgraded our room without even asking and for no cost. the food was incredible and they provided everything we asked for. on our visit, we were feeling sick due to high altitude and the owner was so kind that they took us to hospital on their own. you can book this accommodation for very low prices and all the places in the area are easily accessible from here.

beautiful stay, a lovely isolated place if you want peace and quiet, away from hustles tourist, this is the place 💎💎💎. we stayed at the lake house, all what we needed were there, from kitchen utensils, washing machines, etc. the communication and instructions from the management was clear, so please read your email and the notes inside the house. please remember this is self service accomodation, don't expect to see the concierge, receptionist or the staff. but the staff was the phone call away and always nice, helpful and ready to assist you. if you order for breakfast, the staff will deliver your breakie the night before. they also update the guest house about the info of the weather, temperature and possibility the sight of the northern lights. the helpful staff even accommodate my son with the fishing rod in march as fishing was only in summer time. he caught pink salmon, rainbow trout from the ponds, what a great experience. the bed were comfy, the whole house always warm, the best thing was there's no cold draft we can feel get inside the house at all considering it was freezing outside and super windy. we've been travel to best resorts in 15 different countries, hvammsvik nature resort and spa is in our top 5 lists. we definitely will come back again!!
beautiful store and very helpful staff. i got my beautiful venetian cape here in spring 2022 made with wool from the lamb in the dolomites and previously used by the italian army. love it.

beautiful store located in the heart of the shopping district. this store was fabulous. all the latest and greatest not available in the usa. bring your wallet because you cant stop at 1 item. margherita was our sales associate and she know s her product.
beautiful store, very helpful and friendly staff. i received attentive assistance and a generous amount of samples. the selection of perfumes is small, but the scents are wonderful.

beautiful tao temple. accessible easily via metro as the metro stop is right in front. it has a big garden area and walkways. also in front of the main temple structure you can see devotees with incense sticks and sticks beating themselves as part of forgiveness of sins. a very different aura and vibes felt here. as you enter the temple there are many sculptures seen. a must visit place and you can easily spend couple of hours here. the ponds have so many fishes and turtles in them.

beautiful tea plantations. you can sample free tea as often as you like, and you can see the entire tea processing facility. it's truly amazing. the gorreana tea plantation in the azores is europe's largest and oldest operating tea plantation.

beautiful temple (wat), builded above an artificial lake. also, there is a little museum and the buildings where the monks and the buda believers can stay for a retirement period. it is quiet and clean place

beautiful temple and worth visiting, but the scams and gimmicks are getting tiresome. when you pay the entrance fee, they take you over to a wall and try to get you to purchase a sarong. when you decline, they then try to rent you one. a free one is already included with the ticket. we had to get borderline unfriendly for them to get the point that we were not buying or renting one. then they force you to go with a guide. that was okay as she was helpful and made navigating the area easier. we offered a small tip at the end. however, along the way, we had a few people approaching us to buy things.

beautiful temple by the lake. it’s in the hoan kiem district. we went in the noon on a weekday. it was humid. no wait time. there were a few tourists though. no entry ticket. beautiful architecture & serene temple. there are preserved bodies of two turtles inside. mini skirts, shorts etc are not allowed inside the temple.

beautiful temple dedicated to the chinese folk god of literature and martial. one shall be attracted to its green tile roof and red spiral incense coil hanging from the roof. not one but many. a tourist can also make an offering with candles or incense sticks as they have an electronic machine in the temple itself. select what you want and pay, you will get a receipt and show it at the counter. a local guide may help you do the rituals in the correct way. 🙏
beautiful temple site, built during the reign of khmer king rajendravarman ii, east mebon is a 10th-century hindu temple dedicated to lord shiva

beautiful temple situated in middle of chaos. situated between siam center and center world mall. very calm place and situated near shopping area so can visit anytime. free entry for tourist also. best place for meditate.

beautiful temple which befits its nickname of metal castle. the spires are exquisitely designed and the whole structure stands majestically as a symbol of thai creativity and craftsmanship. definitely worth visiting for tourists who appreciate such good architecture. a small payment is required if you are interested to learn the making and history of loha prasat in bangkok.
beautiful temple — before entering one has to wear a kamen (sarong) which are available at the entrance for a small fee. ancient temple, built on a previous cultures temple on a sacred hill ..

beautiful temple! a must while visiting jerusalem. no entrance fee. however, check the entrance time, winter 7:30 am to 11:30 am and 1:30 pm to 2:30 pm; summer 7:30 am to 10:30 am and 1:30 pm to 2:30 pm. closed on fridays. the place can be accessed through a walkway from the dung gate. be respectful dress appropriately. highly recommend.

beautiful temple, but the weather poured – could have been even better a stunning and historic site with amazing views and truly unique nature all around. the temple itself and the elephant cave are fascinating to explore, and the surrounding rice fields, cliffs, and small waterfalls make the visit worthwhile. there’s a special atmosphere here that you feel as soon as you enter. unfortunately, it started pouring rain shortly after we arrived, which made it hard to fully enjoy the area and limited the experience a bit. with sunshine or dry weather, this could easily have been one of the best temple visits in ubud. still absolutely worth seeing – especially if the weather’s on your side!
beautiful temple, quiet and peaceful. i stopped there on the way to north bali. can be very busy when there is a ceremony. there is a fee on the entrance.
beautiful temple, very well conserved. one of the temples that you can't miss if you visit bagan

beautiful temple, very well-kept territory and stunning sunsets! you need to be careful with monkeys, because there is a risk of being left without glasses and phone. but the overall impressions are wonderful!

beautiful temple, you’ll need to walk a little bit to explore it. there is an entry fee that includes the entry, sarong, 1 way transport up to the temple and guide. the guides may not be very knowledgeable though. vendors may force you to buy offerings for the temple, but its not mandatory and can ignore them.

beautiful tented camp in the middle of the serengeti. we did not expect to stay in such a comfortable abs luxurious place on safari. the staff were very polite and accommodating - even filling up our shower with hot water when called upon. the food was delicious. during the night a giraffe came right up to our tent. amazing and unique experience to be sleeping in tents in the serengeti.
beautiful tented rooms. great turn down service. it does get a bit cold in the rooms. portable heaters would be a nice touch. beautiful grounds. did was excellent.
beautiful theater located next door to famed casa de la música. opened in 1941. it is encased within the edificio rodriguez vazquez, an 11 story building, that combines businesses, 64 apartments.

beautiful theatre in the heart of soho. came to see meow meow (cannot recommend highly enough) and the weather girl. the bar area is quite small so can get busy especially prior to a performance but drinks are reasonably priced. the theatre itself is up two sets of stairs but there is a lift available. seating areas are in side or stalls block and all offer great views of the stage. standing places are available at the back too. staff all very friendly and merchandise is available in the small shop/box office before you leave.

beautiful theatre to watch lion king! loved the intricate details on the walls and ceiling it added to the event. i wished there was more light in the audience before the show so i could see the details a bit more clearly. my tickets were high up in the grand balcony and when i mean high it was high close to nose bleed. i don’t know if there were elevators - it wasn’t offered to me and i was dead climbing up the stairs so note to people with mobility issues it will be difficult to go to the upper level. i wasn’t sure if my seats were too high to enjoy and no it was still perfect. very clear view and sound was amazing. seats are not the most comfortable and everything is a bit squished. if people come late you are constantly getting up to let people by which was frustrating. you can rent binoculars to see stage better. it wasn’t needed but rented anyway for the experience which was fun. theatre offers drinks and some snacks wish it was a better selection. overall thoroughly enjoyed the experience!

beautiful theatre with lots of interesting shows. the staff however isnt very friendley, they were reluctant to let me in to take some photos, they did eventually but not for free - typical cuban behaviour.

beautiful traditional korean houses. can only look at the exterior.

beautiful traditional theatre , we were in the crows nest on benches ! well friday ticket grab £10 opening night. the play was best of the year! that doesn't mean it is what ever people say. we left 1/2 time it wasn't good 😊 and the seats were so un-comfortable and i suffer with poor seating, my fault , cheap seats are cheap 😁 . anyway if there's a good play on and oh you like a lot of stairs then pay a visit. keep an eye open for deals etc for a cheap night out or have some luxury in the expensive seats. summery. stairs, traditional, deals.

beautiful trail but very, very challenging terrain especially after rain - the trail is very steep, rocky and or muddy at certain areas. for one of the descends (leading to a crossing across the river) i'd even reccomend bringing a rope just in case. it drops down about 5 meters almost vertically with only minimal steps carved into the mud. nonetheless - the view is spectacular

beautiful trail that runs along the south boundary of yellowstone. if you're looking for wilderness and peacefulness, definitely go east from here. there's mountains, rivers, creeks, thermals, hot springs, and beautiful wildlife to be seen.
beautiful trail through amazing landscape. took us 2.5 hours easy hike.

beautiful trail to an amazing view. the path is very clearly marked and well maintained. it has some runnable splits in case you are into that. i started at opening hours (8:00 am) and came across some people trail running the descent when i was about to complete it. if you do it non-stop, it will take you about an hour to reach christ the redeemer. it is not an easy trail, keep in mind that it is about 4 km (about 5 km until christ) with more than 600m total elevation gain. if you take breaks and take your time to enjoy the trail, try to spot animals, etc., it should take about two hours. an amazing experience if you are into this, much more rewarding than hopping on a van, plus less crowded. bring water (aim for 2 litres per person) and some snacks too, especially if you do the descent as well.

beautiful trail with a variety of route options. whether you're up for a quick 20-minute stroll or a longer 1–2 hour hike, there's something for everyone. the scenery is stunning, with lush forestry and peaceful surroundings.
beautiful trail, very clean, most amazing views. gets very busy around 9am so i'd advise an early start and a nice big group of people. it is dog friendly too
beautiful trail, with fun stops along the route and easy incline. can be walked easily even by novice hiking or just casual strolling. the scenery is lovely and area has some interesting sites :)

beautiful trail. bring plenty of water! turn off to subway cave is ~2miles in. see my review for the subway cave for detailed instructions. come early, y’all. parking fills up quickly. it’s $5 (as of 2025) to park for the day. trail is easy to moderate. views are fabulous. bring 2-4l of water!

beautiful waterfall! go on a day where it has rained earlier in the day or late the day before. we wore water shoes with grip which we found to be great for this trek but if you have sensitive feet hiking boots are recommended. it can be a little steep at times but the waterfall is worth it. bug spray is a must!!! you will get tons of pictures of the mountain landscape on the hike and on the ride up. stop at places on the ride up or go in a convertible to get the best shots. bring water. at least a bottle per person. be prepared to carry small children part of the way. recommend hiking booties for dogs with sensitive paws. also recommended not to go in the water of the stream as it can contain pathogens from local pigs that live in the mountains. can be especially harmful for dogs if you let them drink from the stream.

beautiful waterfall, just be careful if you hike it shortly after rain. when we went the trail was slippery with puddles everywhere. half of our party didn’t make it to the falls due to the trail conditions.

benizelos mansion is a charming and historically rich attraction located in the heart of athens’ plaka district. as one of the oldest surviving urban mansions, it offers a unique glimpse into athenian life during the ottoman period. the mansion is beautifully preserved, showcasing traditional architecture with intricate woodwork, stone walls, and antique furnishings that transport visitors back in time. the best part? entry is free, making it an accessible stop for travelers interested in history and culture. while there is no mandatory fee, a small donation is kindly encouraged to help maintain this historic gem. visitors often appreciate the intimate guided tours or detailed information available on-site, which add depth to the experience. walking through the rooms, you can admire the elegant design and get a sense of the lifestyle of a wealthy family in the 18th and 19th centuries. the mansion’s peaceful courtyard is a lovely spot to rest and reflect amid your busy athens sightseeing. benizelos mansion is an excellent complement to the nearby acropolis and the vibrant streets of plaka, offering a quieter, more personal experience. for history buffs and casual visitors alike, it’s a hidden treasure well worth a visit.

best part of the stay this is an absolutely underrated gem. the resort is situated on the island of sebayur (45 minutes by boat) from labuan bajo (flores airport) and in addition to being the gateway to a unesco heritage site, has an incredible house reef teeming with life. getting there- we stayed at bali overnight and took a morning flight to labuan bajo (flores island) via batik aithe resort arranges for an airport pickup. if you arrive early, you can stay at the resort office in labuan bajo near the port. the staff there were very friendly and attentive. a private speed boat to sebayur departs around midday and the staff will get you to the boat on time. the island- the highlight of the island is the reef and as i mentioned above, it is amazing. not so much schools as clouds of fish in every direction. there can be quite a bit of tourist traffic through this area and i had tamped down my expectations as a result but it was probably the best house reef i have seen. the resort also offers a guided night snorkel expedition and i would highly recommend it as well although it may not be everyone's cup of tea. in 7 days of snorkeling, i saw turtles, several species of damselfish and angelfish, titan triggerfish, moorish idols, grouper (night snorkel), blue clawed lobster (night snorkel), batfish, wrasse, coral trout, parrotfish, surgeonfish and sweet lips to name just a few. it's also nice to canoe in the lsland waters. we took our 3 year old out for a paddle while she listened to her favourite moana songs. apart from the reef, it's also worth climbing to the top of the island to take in the sunrise over the bay. accommodation- the accommodation consists of individual raised moana-style cabins. right opposite each cabin and adjacent to the beach are a pair of pool lounger chairs under an umbrella, looking out over the water. each cabin has a verandah with chairs, a small table, a drying rack and beanbag. the cabin itself has a king bed, a wooden cupboard with a safe and decent air conditioning. wifi is decent at the dining area and near the jetty but is patchy at the cabin itself. food- for dining options, you have a large covered eating area, right on the beach opposite the jetty. the kitchen is open for breakfast (6 to 9), lunch (12 to 2) and dinner (6 to 9). mostly the food was fresh and delicious with the exception of things such as ice cream. the lunch menu was a bit limited but the dinner menu is great. my highlights for the food were the beef rendang, pisang goreng, pizza, seafood basket, the dessert fruit platter and for my daughter, the pasta. there was also a small crate of old toys which provided my daughter with enough entertainment most nights and allowed us to eat our dinner in peace. there is a bar up near the waterfront and some comfy loungers to relax in. staff- the staff were just fantastic, always ready to lend a hand or get you what you need. alex, the resort manager, was always available for a chat for any concerns or questions, as were rifa and claudia. the rest of the staff were great as well, so much so that my normally reserved 3 year old knew all of them on a first name basis and by the third day, would confidently walk up to any of them to take her to the jetty or to investigate a crab or some strange insect she had just found. the resort can also arrange for informal babysitting at 150000 rp an hour and it was absolutely worth it, as it allowed both of us to go snorkeling together. i also wanted to thank the owners joe and julian who arrived on the third day of our stay and took the time to come and meet us and ask us if anything could be done to improve our stay. we are deeply indebted to joe as she always made the time to accompany us on many snorkeling excursions on the house reef and always tried to find interesting things for us. she also accompanied my wife when they visited manta point on a custom trip with the dive boat and it was a far better experience than the full day excursion, both in the lack of crowds and in the number of mantas they saw peacefully feeding.

beyond the tourist trail: unveiling the hidden layers of cheonjeyeon waterfalls. cheonjeyeon waterfalls, often described as a three-tiered cascade, holds more secrets and stories than its straightforward name suggests. my recent visit revealed not just stunning natural beauty, but also poignant history and breathtaking panoramic views. the journey begins just a stone's throw from the ticketing office, leading you to what's marked as the first waterfall. however, don't be surprised if you're greeted by a serene pond, the cheonjeyeon pond. it's a beautiful sight in its own right, but the 1st waterfall only truly comes alive after a good rain, a reminder of nature's dynamic artistry. a gentle 3-5 minute stroll along a mostly flat path brings you to the undisputed star of the show: the 2nd waterfall. with a dedicated viewing platform, you can truly appreciate the power and beauty of the water as it plunges into the pool below. it's truly a refreshing yet serene experience. as you continue your exploration, drawn perhaps by the elegant arch of the seonim bridge, take a moment to notice the significant memorial sculpture nearby. the this poignant tribute commemorates the victims of the jeju 4.3 incident, a tragic chapter in the island's history. it's a powerful reminder that even amidst natural beauty, there are important stories to remember and learn from. crossing the seonim bridge (선임교) feels like stepping into a korean legend. this graceful arch is more than just a connection, it's a part of jeju's rich cultural landscape. on the other side, a short ascent leads to the cheonjeru pavilion (천제루 天帝楼). be sure to climb to the upper floor for a truly panoramic vista of the surrounding lush greenery. and remember to seek out the small, hidden viewing deck beside the pavilion, offering a distant, almost aerial view of the magnificent 2nd waterfall. the final tier, the 3rd waterfall, presents a more adventurous trek. a 10-minute walk along wooden stairs leads you to this shorter cascade. while the view from the side might feel a little less dramatic compared to the second waterfall, the journey through the shaded woodland offers its own charm. it's a good reminder that sometimes the path itself is part of the experience. tips: 1. the only toilet facilities are located before the ticketing office, by the parking area. make sure to take advantage of them before you begin your exploration of cheonjeyeon's wonders. 2. in case you are confused, the geo location is actually the 3rd waterfall.

beyond words! my cousin and i were visiting denali for the first time and had just "landed" in town after taking the bus from talkeetna. it was a blue sky day and we decided to walk and explore as we were not able to check in to our hotel for another couple hours. we decided to walk the strip with gift shops and look for restaurants and just stretch our legs after the ride. we locked eyes with matt with denali adventures as we were ascending the steps and he immediately greeted us with a friendly smile and told us we should "take a plane tour today!" my cousin and i were a little skeptical at first, but we were encouraged by matt's enthusiasm and emphasis on the fact that this was the best day, with the best conditions for flying all season! he emphatically showed us video of the flight and photos of how beautiful the park is from above. given that the park was closed we were strongly considering taking the offer to fly. my cousin and i talked it over during our lunch at a restaurant (black bear) recommended by matt that was fantastic as well! we decided to take the tour! we didn't know when we would be able to return, and we were reminiscing about how our parents had not been to the park in over 25 years. our flight was incredible! our pilot was captian kurt! he was well informed and when we were not listening to the audio guide was excitedly telling us about how this was one of the best days he had seen all year! we had a very smooth ride with nobody getting an upset stomach. which we were very happy about. we were able to see all of denali and this is more rare than we expected. i would highly recommend this tour to anyone who is visiting the area. our experience from booking to touching back down was a spectacular. this was not a planned adventure for us but it will be the part of our trip we will be talking about the most for many years to come! see the photos below for how incredible the day was! thank you denali adventures!

birthplace of hazrat maryam (عليها السلام) . the church of saint anne also known as the madrasa al-salahiyya (مدرسة الصلاحيه), is a roman catholic church, located at the start of the via dolorosa, near the lions' gate and churches of the flagellation and condemnation, in the muslim quarter of the old city of jerusalem. . her father’s name was imran ibn mathan. her mother’s full name was hannah bint faqudh. they were both very religious and held a high status in the eyes of allah (ﷻ). hannah was deprived of a child until she reached old age. it so happened that once she was seated under the shade of a tree when she saw a bird feeding her little baby. she was moved by this sight, and wept supplicating to allah (ﷻ) for a child of her own. she vowed that if she were to be gifted with one, she would offer the child for the services of the sanctuary, bayt al-maqdis. . she fell pregnant. her husband, imran, died before her delivery, therefore maryam (عليها السلام) was born as a yatim (an orphan). hannah took good care of her until she grew up, and to fulfill her oath, she offered her to the sanctuary. . the normal custom was that only males were offered in the service of the bayt al-maqdis. however, maryam (عليها السلام) was accepted. all the worshippers wanted to look after her but prophet zakariyya (عليه السلام) was chosen to be her guardian because he was her uncle.

book this trip, you will not be disappointed. i recently returned (having only just visited in december 2024) from the most unforgettable riding trail holiday in morocco, and i can’t stop smiling every time i think about it. from start to finish, the experience was nothing short of brilliant. the culture, the horses, the people- everything was brilliant. the landscapes we rode through were breathtaking — you cannot explain how brilliant the moroccan desert and sand dunes are until you experience it yourself. each day brought a new view that felt like something out of a movie (which i guess is true!). the horses were incredibly well cared for, sure-footed even in a fast canter/ gallop and responsive, making every ride a joy, whether we were cantering across open terrain or navigating more technical paths. i couldn’t fault my horse and secretly wanted to take him home with me. what truly made this trip stand out was our guide, abdel- his knowledge of the land, culture, and horses was remarkable, and his calm, confident presence made everyone feel completely at ease. he struck the perfect balance between professionalism and warmth, sharing stories, offering insight into local traditions, and ensuring each rider felt supported and safe. i do not envy his job and my only advise to others is be totally honest with yourself about your riding capabilities - these are fast rides, on forward horses- they have horses to suit those less experienced but they need to know this in advance. the lunches in the middle of the desert were incredible and i’ve made friends for life. it wasn’t just a holiday — it was an immersive, soul-enriching journey through one of the most beautiful corners of the world. i came away feeling inspired, connected, and already dreaming about my next visit to the coast instead. the fact i have been twice now with this company, once in december 2024 and again in april 2025 speaks volumes. i did the horses, dunes and nomads trail ride both times and loved it. if you’re considering a horseback adventure, i can’t recommend this experience highly enough. morocco on horseback is something everyone should do at least once!

breathtaking hike to the top of madeira ⛰️🌺 the pr1.2 vereda do pico ruivo trail is absolutely stunning. it’s one of the most rewarding hikes in madeira — leading you to the island’s highest peak with jaw-dropping views along the way. the path is well-maintained and winds through dramatic ridges, volcanic rock formations, and clouds floating beneath your feet. the air is fresh, the silence powerful, and the landscape feels otherworldly. whether you start from achada do teixeira or connect from pico do arieiro, this trail is pure magic. on clear days, the 360° views from the summit are unforgettable — you feel like you’re standing on top of the world. it’s not the easiest hike, but it’s 100% worth the effort. bring good shoes, layers, and your camera — you’ll remember this adventure forever.

bukchon hanok village is one of the most charming and culturally rich areas in seoul. nestled between gyeongbokgung palace and changdeokgung palace, this historic neighborhood is home to hundreds of traditional korean houses, known as hanok, many of which date back to the joseon dynasty. walking through its narrow winding streets is like traveling back in time — the wooden beams, curved roofs, and stone walls create a picturesque atmosphere that’s perfect for photography. the area is not just a tourist attraction; many hanoks are still private homes, so visitors are encouraged to keep noise to a minimum. along the way, you’ll find small art galleries, traditional tea houses, craft workshops, and cozy cafes that offer a taste of korean culture. there are also several designated viewpoints where you can enjoy stunning panoramas of the village, the city skyline, and the surrounding mountains. visiting in the morning or on weekdays is recommended to avoid crowds. wear comfortable shoes, as some streets are steep. overall, bukchon hanok village offers a perfect mix of history, architecture, and local life — a must-visit for anyone exploring seoul.

bulabog beach, located on the eastern side of boracay, is a paradise for adventure seekers and those looking for a quieter alternative to white beach. known as the island’s watersports hub, it’s the best spot for kiteboarding and windsurfing, especially during the amihan (northeast monsoon) season. what i loved: ✔ watersports heaven – if you love kiteboarding, windsurfing, or parasailing, this is the best place in boracay to do it. ✔ less crowded – compared to white beach, bulabog is much more peaceful, making it great for relaxation away from the tourist crowds. ✔ beautiful sunrise views – since it's on the east coast, you can catch a stunning sunrise over the water. ✔ laid-back vibe – the beachfront has a mix of boutique resorts, hostels, and cafés, giving it a chill and relaxed atmosphere. things to consider: ⚠ not ideal for swimming – the beach has seaweed and strong winds most of the year, so it’s not the best for casual swimming. ⚠ stronger winds (seasonal) – from november to april, the wind and waves are strong, making it perfect for water sports but not for sunbathing. ⚠ less developed than white beach – fewer restaurants and bars compared to station 2, but still has a good selection of places to eat and stay. final thoughts: if you’re a kitesurfing or windsurfing enthusiast, bulabog beach is a must-visit in boracay. even if you’re not into watersports, it’s a peaceful spot to enjoy the sunrise, take a walk, or escape the busier white beach crowds. recommended for adventure lovers and those looking for a different side of boracay!

buy tickets online so save time and money ! get three buckets of food because you can go through the safari many times and you will run out of one order of food is $18 that includes two buckets of grain and two filled with lettuce. buying the willow for $6 for 6 twigs is not worth it. we loved the safari especially the bison, elk, zebras and giraffes. use your front camera to ensure you don’t hit the deer that surround your car! we had a blast here. the african safari in ontario is great too and that one has monkeys we arrived around noon and it got pretty busy around 3pm. great for the entire family the walk through safari is really nice too.

buza gate, one of the lesser-known entrances to dubrovnik's old town, offers a unique and charming entry point for those looking to explore this historic city. known for its understated beauty, buza gate provides a quiet escape from the more crowded entrances, allowing visitors to appreciate the city's medieval charm at a leisurely pace. as you pass through buza gate, you'll find yourself immersed in the old town's labyrinth of narrow streets, each lined with ancient stone buildings that echo stories of centuries past. the old town itself is a treasure trove of historical and cultural attractions, including the magnificent city walls, the rector's palace, and the dubrovnik cathedral. while specific entrance costs can vary, here are some general prices for key attractions in dubrovnik's old town: 1. **city walls**: approximately €30 for adults. these iconic walls offer breathtaking views of the city and the adriatic sea. 2. **rector's palace**: around €15. this beautiful palace now houses a museum showcasing the city's rich history. 3. **dubrovnik cathedral**: entry is often free, but donations are appreciated. the cathedral is a stunning example of baroque architecture. buza gate itself is free to access, making it an ideal starting point for budget-conscious travelers wishing to explore dubrovnik's rich history and stunning architecture.
by far the best beach in tel aviv

by far the best hot spring experience i’ve had. i visited 3 times during my stay in são miguel – and each visit felt just as special as the first. the staff are incredibly kind, patient, and welcoming – their service truly stands out. the surrounding vegetation is lush and absolutely beautiful, creating a serene and almost magical atmosphere. everything is clean, well-maintained, and thoughtfully designed. i can’t recommend it enough!

by far the best mosque in cairo! the design is very nice and relaxing with the walls made out of pure white marble while also preserving ornaments from over a thousand years ago. this mosque is very nice for prayer (i imagine) but also a pleasant place to get away from the chaos of the surrounding streets. definitely recommended!

by far the best side trip my wife and i ever booked in our 30 years of traveling. yes, getting to hold the tiny puppies was amazing, but i enjoyed their presentation even more! to get a real look into the life of a real family raising and racing iditarod athletes was fascinating. mike and caitlin have a passion that you can’t help feeling yourself by the time your visit is over. the whole team there was friendly and super engaging. if you love dogs or sports or freedom or following a dream or just meeting great people, take this tour!

by far the best surf class i have ever been to. everyone is super nice, friendly, and professional. all the instructors are amazing, including jeff, alan, stephen, and others whose names i did not catch but had great conversations with. i had tried surfing classes before in santa cruz in capitola beach, and half moon bay, but none of them were as good. this was the only class where i was able to stand up on my very first session, learn the techniques, and most importantly have so much fun. i also bought my used board and wetsuit from alan, and both he and jeff helped me choose the right sizes. they made me fall in love with surfing. if there is one place to learn how to surf, this is absolutely it. i cannot wait to take more lessons. they also even gave me the confidence to practice on my own. truly an amazing experience. ♥️♥️

by far the cheapest place to buy your souvenirs, 14k for 2 baseball caps to name but one. i saw camouflage bottoms elsewhere, but got exactly the same here at less than 1/2 the price ( with a little haggling as i bought 2 pairs 😆) even was directed to some toilets, that unknowingly was in a flower market so for a change they smelt amazing. it’s a maze of alleyways so be prepared to do a lot of walking in very busy paths.
