by far the most beautiful place i saw in tokyo. an art deco house so well preserved it was enchanting. would recommend it to anyone. the glasswork is exquisite and even the cafe is very nice. if you like beautiful architecture and object take a couple hours at least to see all of this. we saw it at the end of the day and the lighting was enchanting.

by far the most beautiful sunset we have ever seen. the beach has crystal clear waters with white sand and the coconut trees make it the most tropical scenery. is for sure one of the best tropical beaches in the world.
by far, the best vessels, best crew and the best service. our trip to the islands of bazaruto archipelago was unforgettable. nothing is too much for them.

byron is an absolute gem! he is extremely professional but what i appreciated about him immediately is his ability to offer kindness naturally. i came to him as a stranger inquiring about the jetskis and left with an unforgettable santorini experience. to honor a guest in a foreign country is something i’m personally going to always remember. gregory was also very patient and taught me how to safely operate the jetski. 10/10 recommend this company.

cabalgata with paredes family. this was the real surprise of my third visit to puerto natales from australia. it is very scenic, breath taking and contemplative ascend with the climax at the summit. the contact with the gentle noble horses is very therapeutic. lots of beautiful native flora. i felt very small in this vast land and something within me just made me feel grateful. the horses and equipment were highly supervised by the owners and i felt safe. hot coffee and tea with scones inside the house after the ride was most wellcome. there is a lot more to puerto natales than the torres. i highly recommend this excursion and i rate it 10/10.

café schwarzenberg is a beautiful and historic café with a classic viennese atmosphere. the coffee and pastries were excellent, and the staff were polite and professional despite being quite busy. during my visit, i did notice a couple of disgruntled customers who had a complaint and were ultimately given their meal for free. as i was leaving, one of them even joked loudly that she’d “try complaining every time” to get free meals, which was a bit surprising. that said, my own experience was very pleasant. the service was attentive, and the quality of food and drink was wonderful. i’d still recommend it to anyone looking to enjoy an authentic viennese experience.

cairns botanic gardens is a pleasant place to visit with a cozy little café and clean restrooms. it’s a peaceful spot with some nice walking paths and tropical plants. however, compared to botanic gardens in larger australian cities, it’s relatively small and doesn’t feel as well-maintained. worth a quick visit if you’re nearby, but not particularly impressive overall.

cairo festival city is an excellent choice for kids and parents, the kids can go play in magic planet all day, then have lunch/dinner in the food court or any other restaurant, the shops there have variety of local and international brands with prices that suits everyone. we love cfc ❤️

cajun encounters showed me an awesome day! derek, our bus driver, was super knowledgeable and entertaining on our ride to the swamp. he pointed out lots of interesting things and was filled with so much knowledge. once we got to the swamp, captain jacob took great care of us on our boat ride. he was so informative and hilarious. captain jacob pointed out so much wildlife and allowed us to get great photos. awesome guided and i will absolutely take this tour again next time i come to nola.

calauit island national park is probably one of the best parks or zoos i’ve ever visited. the guides were very informative and incredibly friendly, making the whole experience more enjoyable. one of the highlights was feeding the giraffes — you can even touch them, but only within the designated feeding area, as it’s not safe to approach them elsewhere (they might kick!). you also get to interact closely with both giraffes, zebras and deer, which is something you don’t often get to do in regular zoos. there’s a truck ride that takes you to the farthest side of the reserve where you can see additional animals in a more natural setting. during our visit, they were still building new enclosures for more animals that will be added soon, which is exciting for future visitors. for a small fee, you get a unique and memorable wildlife experience that goes beyond what typical zoos offer.

caldera yachting santorini was an absolute highlight of my trip. their ship, the mesousa, is truly excellent—well-maintained and comfortable, providing a perfect platform for enjoying the aegean sea. ​the experience was elevated by the exceptional attention to detail. the service was very good, with a dedicated crew who were genuinely nice staffs and went out of their way to ensure everyone had a memorable time. from the moment we boarded until the last glimpse of the breathtaking sunset, every aspect was handled with professionalism and warmth. highly recommended for an unforgettable santorini sunset.

camden market is a paradise for foodies 🤭 you can find all sorts of tasty food and fun desserts there. we wanted to try a bit of everything, but after tasting a few of the yummy ones, we were already full and couldn’t eat more. one of them was their famous chips – we queued for about an hour in the blazing heat 😓☀️, but honestly, i have to say it wasn’t worth it! overall though, it’s a lovely place and a fun experience – just be ready for big crowds!

camden market is undoubtedly one of london’s most iconic and bustling retail destinations, with a rich history that dates back to the 70s. known for its eclectic mix of shops, stalls, and food vendors, this vibrant market is the epitome of london’s diverse culture. visitors can immerse themselves in a lively atmosphere filled with a wide range of unique goods and eye-catching architecture. while it can get crowded depending on the time of day, experiencing camden market is entirely worth it. a visit here is an absolute must; you wouldn’t want to miss out on the unforgettable charm and energy that this incredible place has to offer.

came for 2 main reasons: ocular visit for a potential business opportunity, and celebrate the founding anniversary of el nido. from the moment my feet touched the ground, i started to feel treated the palaweña way. everything was well taken care of. from the hotel transportation, lodging, food and restaurant choices, to the specialty of the house, their signature private tours. it was my second time to visit el nido, and i honestly had more fun this time. through palaweña, i got to live like a local for 11 days, learning about their culture and way of life by the beach, while reconnecting with nature, appreciating every opportunity we oftentimes take for granted. ever grateful to the owner, ms. wineth, for always being a message/call away. from food recommendations, chill quiet spots to hangout on, last minute requests, literally any thing under the sun! one of the main highlights of my trip was the private tour i requested at sunset. i got to enjoy snorkeling in peace, as the sun slowly bids good bye for the day. it may seem normal for others, but that specific setting was what i have been needing for the longest time. so thank you, palaweña, for making it happen. one for the books and definitely not gonna be the last!

came on a saturday morning, place was bustling with people, shops mostly open, and the atmosphere loud but full of energy. it was crowded, but that’s part of the charm. the market felt alive, with locals and tourists mingling together. there’s a huge variety of food stalls, from fresh seafood and sushi to grilled snacks, along with plenty of dry goods, spices, and souvenirs. it’s also a popular spot for locals to buy quality ingredients. a fun, vibrant place to experience tokyo’s food culture, but be prepared to squeeze through the crowds!

came on a sunday afternoon to do a little work and hang out. a great neighborhood gem that’s cash only. friendly bartenders, tasty beers and delicious food for an amazing price!! the patio in the back is a great spot to chill and catch up with friends. would highly recommend! burger with tater tots was only $13 total! a solid burger with tasty tots (although a little over fried) but def worth it

came on july 28 2025. attended the segway tour which consists of 45 minutes of training and a 1-2 hour tour across the park on the segway(highly recommended.). good scenery and there is an area for children to have fun with water parks, slides, inflatable castles and even a hill where they can play sisyphus with a large red ball. good for family trips.

came thanks to showfilmfirst and had a great experience. the actors were all very good, and my sister and i enjoyed following the stories of different trails. if you go for the first time, you'll probably only have time for two trails because a lot of it is trying to figure out where to go (also some characters roam, so hard to find them at times). i will agree with some reviews saying that it gets a bit repetitive, but because i really enjoy all things immersive, i didn't mind so much. nor when i had to wait between 5-10 minutes because there were queues to speak with certain characters. however i understand others might find this a bit more tedious. we paid for the £20 cocktail experience, and with that i have to admit it felt like a bit of a letdown. it promised unique character interactions, which were essentially just following another trail (and one of the actors didn't exactly seem sure about the storyline). as you can buy any other cocktail for half the price, it didn't really feel worth the 30 minutes that could have been spent doing one of the main trails. however as it's optional, i'm not letting it affect my rating. it is definitely more for extroverted people (or at least people who can fake being extroverted), as there's a lot of talking to characters, and it feels like a better experience when you can have a good back and forth with them. in terms of accessibility, i will say some of the walkways are narrow, can get very congested, and there are really only options for seating in the main town hall area, so keep that in mind if booking with wheelchair or mobility aid users. there is a lot of walking involved. i appreciated the website having a hint option, as in certain places you can essentially get the answer outright and not have to wait around for simple word answers (and sometimes the answers aren't too clear, if you can't hear the characters very well). but i'd highly recommend actually trying to go to each point where you have to talk to a character, because it's worth it! in terms of food, i found you get a decent portion for the price, and the drinks are a decent strength as well, though i did finish mind quite quickly as any time you spend eating will be during the time you could be following trails, and with the drinks, some of the cocktails come in shallow glasses so you can't really rush around with them. will definitely be going back in the future, as i said, you only really have time for two or three trails, so coming back for repeat performances can be good to explore the other ones.

came to buy presents for family and was not disappointed! gorgeous shop with a friendly owner who was great to chat to and spoke great english :) great for tea cups and tea sets, chopstick rests, plates, bowls, with some particularly beautiful sake sets!
came to buy some ski outfits for my daughter. huge store, modern and clean, friendly customer service, good price. they have anything you need for outdoor activities.

came to check this out as my son is a big fan. considering the facilities are mostly under construction, i wasn't impressed that they were still charging full pop for admission as the only good experience was the museum portion. overall to go through and see some trophies and some video highlight reels. it was an expensive expedition and along the way to get you for some photo ops which they get you for another 60 euros on the way out. for two people at almost 200 euros, this was the more expensive option versus going to other stadiums in the country. i would wait till they're done building the new stadium and then it would be worth it.

came to check this out since it looked fun. 1st of all you can’t pre book tickets. once you buy, you go straight into the line up. then you’re herded into the sled (no pleasantries were exchanged of or acknowledgments occurred) not cuz i’m not friendly…plus we were bumper to bumper with the sled in front of us so we didn’t reach full potential i’m sure. they also walked part of it for like 5 mins. the cherry on top??? they finally looked at us when we thanked them and demanded tips!! we were so startled by this i had no idea what was going on. my partner had some change and gave it to one gentleman (i had nothing) and the man, i kid you not looked at us with disgust and disdain. we were so shocked by it all, i just wanted to get out of there, then was intercepted by another rollercoaster ride pic person that was taken near the end… and i said no thank you and they kept at it. this whole experience ruined it for me, but there are parallel universes right? i could’ve had a great time then..

came to fiorino for dinner, and it exceeded our expectations! really enjoyed getting to order food family style, since there was so much we wanted to try. we got the butternut squash arancini, sformato (cauliflower souffle), vegetarian gnocchetti, panzanella salad (not pictured here) and for dessert the olive oil orange cake - everything was delicious - we really loved the gnocchi and cauliflower souffle! the ambience was really cute, i can imagine it would be super cozy in the winter, but also perfect for summer nights too with some great food! our server bianca was really great and attentive, and gave us her suggestions too! i would definitely go back, seeing as they add in new items for seasonal flavours. excited to check out the londsdale location soon!

capilano river park is one of the most stunning natural spots in vancouver, offering a perfect blend of pristine wilderness and recreational opportunities. the park is famous for its scenic river and the iconic capilano dam, which stands as one of its main highlights. the dam provides breathtaking views of calm waters surrounded by lush greenery and towering trees. the sound of flowing water, paired with the backdrop of mountains and forests, creates a serene and energizing atmosphere. the park’s natural beauty is truly captivating. every corner of capilano river park offers something unique, from rushing rivers and rocky cliffs to ancient trees. in the fall, the changing colors of the leaves create a picturesque setting, while spring brings fresh air and vibrant greenery. even in winter, the park’s peaceful ambiance offers a magical escape. the untouched nature makes it an ideal place to disconnect from the hustle of city life. one of the standout features of this park is its long and unspoiled hiking trails, perfect for outdoor enthusiasts. these trails wind through dense forests and alongside the river, providing incredible views of wild nature. along the way, you’ll find wooden bridges and various lookout points that make the hiking experience even more memorable. the trails cater to different levels of hikers, making it accessible for everyone. if you’re looking for a tranquil and beautiful place to enjoy nature, capilano river park is an excellent choice. whether it’s capturing the breathtaking scenery, walking along the scenic trails, or simply enjoying the peaceful environment, this park offers an unforgettable experience. make sure to visit the dam and explore the amazing trails during your trip!

capilla del santo cristo de la salud. chapel of holy christ of health. this information below was used from a google search i did for this chapel. as the story goes, during the san juan bautista celebrations of 1753 a rider, baltazar montanez, lost control of his horse and plunged to the cliffs below. the spanish secretary of government don mateo pratts was watching the drama unfold from a nearby balcony, and allegedly cried out, “christ of good health, save him!” though the horse didn’t survive the fall, the young rider did. tucked away in the corner of the old walled city of san juan is a tiny chapel, one of the most beautiful and secluded monuments in the old capital. it was built on top of the ancient stone walls that protected puerto rico's capital in 1753 to celebrate a miracle. since then, tens of thousands of faithful visitors have come to this humble chapel to pray for cures. that same year, montanez built the small chapel on the exact spot where he fell over the cliff. the altar was built in shining silver and gold leaf, surrounded by beautiful oil paintings by the famous puerto rican artist jose campeche. much of the modestly sized but immaculately appointed chapel hasn’t changed since then. but over the decades it has been slowly added to by believers who come to the chapel seeking their own miracles. tiny silver ornaments decorate the chapel, each one representing some ailing part of the body. these small milagros, or miracles, represent a cause of pain for the pilgrims, and take the form of miniature silver legs, arms, hearts, and lungs. today the church is reverentially cared for by a group of local women, volunteers called “la hermandad del santo cristo de la salud” (the sisterhood of the holy christ of health). it is only open on tuesdays and religious days. this location is right next to the park of el parque las palomas. they are side by side, can't miss this spot. you also have la casa estrecha which is located right on the opposite side of the park.

casa del noreste: tulum’s ancient enigma and the legends it inspires amidst the striking ruins of tulum, mexico, the casa del noreste (house of the northeast) stands as a quiet yet significant relic influence still echoes through the yucatán peninsula. the casa del noreste is part of the residential area of tulum, reflecting the architectural style and social organization of the ancient maya. constructed from limestone, the casa del noreste features thick walls and a flat roof, typical of the buildings in tulum. the structure is believed to have served as a residence for high-ranking officials or priests, given its proximity to the city's central ceremonial areas. the house's design, with its small, narrow rooms and limited ventilation, suggests it was built to withstand the harsh coastal environment, protecting its inhabitants from the intense sun and tropical storms. the casa del noreste also played a crucial role in the social and religious fabric of tulum. as part of the city’s residential quarters, it would have been a place where important decisions were made, rituals were performed, and the sacred knowledge of the maya was passed down through generations. while the casa del noreste is rooted in history, it is also shrouded in legend, with stories passed down through the centuries adding a layer of mystery to this ancient structure. one such legend tells of a maya priest who lived in the house and was believed to possess the ability to communicate with the gods. according to the tale, the priest was said to have foretold the arrival of strange visitors from across the sea—an eerie prediction that some believe hinted at the eventual arrival of the spanish conquistadors. another legend speaks of a hidden treasure buried beneath the casa del noreste. it is said that during a time of great turmoil, the inhabitants of tulum hid their most valuable possessions within the walls of this house, entrusting them to the gods for safekeeping. despite numerous searches and excavations, the treasure has never been found, fueling speculation and curiosity among both locals and visitors. these legends, while unproven, add an air of mystery to the casa del noreste, drawing those who are intrigued by the intersection of history and myth. walking through the ruins of the casa del noreste, it’s easy to imagine the lives of those who once called this place home. the walls, though weathered by time, still stand as silent witnesses to the daily rituals, conversations, and secrets of the ancient maya. the house’s strategic location within the city, along with its legends, suggests it was more than just a residence—it was a space where the spiritual and the mundane coexisted, where history was both made and remembered. the casa del noreste in tulum offers a unique and intimate glimpse into the life of the ancient maya, blending historical significance with the rich tapestry of local legends. as part of the broader story of tulum, this house stands as a reminder of the city's past—its people, their beliefs, and the mysteries that still surround them. for those who visit tulum, the casa del noreste is a must-see, inviting exploration not only of its physical space but also of the stories and myths that continue to captivate and inspire.

catedral de san cristobal, or havana cathedral, is one of eleven catholic cathedrals in cuba. this stunning edifice is nestled in the plaza de la catedral on calle empedrado, between san ignacio mercaderes, habana vieja, and serves as the seat of the roman catholic archdiocese of san cristobal de la habana. the thirty by forty-nine meter rectangular church previously housed christopher columbus' remains from 1796 to 1898, prior to their transfer to seville cathedral. the gravestone was inscribed with the words "oh remains and image of great columbus, be preserved one thousand years in the funerary urn." the remains were later returned to spain in 1898 after the cuban war of independence. havana cathedral is a magnificent roman catholic cathedral of which natural coral stone were used to build. it has been recognized by unesco as a world heritage site. the cathedral's baroque façade is instantly recognizable, with two large, asymmetrical bell towers framing the grandiose stone exterior, considered one of the most beautiful in the americas. this 18th-century baroque cathedral is dedicated to the virgin mary and is one of the oldest cathedrals in america. the adjacent plaza de la cathedral is usually the most crowded tourist spot in old havana, providing an impressive and historical setting. its façade a true marvel, especially in the afternoon when bathed in sunlight. when accessible, the interior offers a fascinating glimpse, striking a balance between sobriety and intrigue. with no admission fee and no guided tours available, visitors are free to explore at their leisure. as a historic cathedral, it proudly showcases a blend of colonial and modern art, welcoming visitors with complimentary admission and providing leg wraps for women as required, all within the picturesque setting of a colonial plaza. our visit to the cathedral took place at noon. it was exceptionally hot, to the point where we felt like we were melting. unfortunately, the church was closed, denying us the opportunity to admire its beautiful interior. this site is a top tourist recommendation. visiting in the morning or evening is advised. we heard that the cathedral's nighttime view is breathtaking. if possible, visit the cathedral in the morning and at night.

chamarel waterfall is one of the most impressive natural sights in mauritius. surrounded by lush greenery, the waterfall drops from a height of about 100 meters, creating a stunning view. it’s a peaceful and scenic spot, perfect for nature lovers and photographers.

chamarel waterfalls in mauritius is often cited as the island's highest single-drop waterfall, plunging approximately 100 meters (around 300 feet). its sheer drop is comparable to the height of the statue of liberty, making it a truly awe-inspiring sight. the waterfall is set amidst lush, green tropical forests and dramatic rocky canyons, creating a picturesque backdrop. it originates from the river saint-denis, fed by three distinct streams. there are easily accessible viewing platforms offering fantastic perspectives of the cascading water and the surrounding landscape. some prefer the higher viewpoint for a full panorama. the falls are often most impressive during the wetter months (may to december) when the flow is at its peak. in drier periods, the water might split into multiple streams. the waterfall is located within the chamarel seven coloured earth geopark, so a visit often combines seeing both natural wonders. an entry fee covers access to both. crowds:as a popular attraction, it can get crowded, especially during peak tourist season. mosquitoes: it's advisable to bring mosquito repellent due to the lush surroundings. in short, chamarel waterfalls is a must-see in mauritius, offering breathtaking views of a powerful and tall waterfall in a beautiful natural setting, often combined with a visit to the unique seven coloured earth. there is an entry fee of 800 mur per person. there is ample car parking available

charles bridge – a must-see with real charm we started our morning with breakfast and then set out for a walk to charles bridge, one of prague’s most iconic spots. as we got closer, it was clear why this place is so popular — the atmosphere is lively, full of history, and has that unmistakable charm that draws people in. yes, there were a lot of people, but it didn’t feel overwhelming. in fact, the crowd added to the vibe. the views from the bridge are lovely, even though the water on both sides didn’t look particularly clean or inviting. still, the architecture, statues, and overall setting more than made up for it. along the way, especially coming from praha 1, we passed through some clean and well-kept streets, lined with small local shops and artists. there were quite a few people drawing portraits for money — it’s all part of the charm and makes the walk feel lively and local. if you ever find yourself in prague and ask around for what to see first, chances are most people will point you straight to charles bridge. that was exactly our experience — it came up again and again as a top recommendation, and after visiting, i can see why. definitely worth a visit. it’s a perfect place for a relaxed walk, soaking in some history, grabbing a few photos, and enjoying one of the most iconic spots the city has to offer.

che pau teng is a natural landmark known as the rhino rock located near the hilltop found on the stanley peninsula. it can be visited by way of a couple of trail routes found at and near the end of wong ma kok road south of the stanley village. the simplest route starts at the bus stop at the end of the road right next to the stanley fort. this is a paved walk up to the transmission station before turning into a natural trail through shrubs and winding over, around and even through boulder piles until you reach the iconic landmark. unfortunately, when i passed by recently, i found this trailhead closed to the public and unavailable for access. the second route starts around 500 metres back on wong ma kok road, north of the regalia bay residences. you'll find two small buildings and a trail that begins just next to the lower building. you'll climb southward at first beside a pipeline for around 40 metres before beginning a fairly sharp ascend up the hillside to the southeast. the trail requires some minor navigation skills and good footwear. i recommend gloves as well as you have to do some scrambling at times. you'll go through some thick wooded stretches, low hanging bamboo and boulder outcrops before reaching the same transmission station where the two routes meet. there are great viewpoints throughout on the second route, particularly looking back to the north at stanley. even if it is more challenging, it is worth taking for the views alone. you'll be rewarded with more fine views of the sea from the boulder piles near and at the rhino rock. inherently, the che pau teng landmark does clearly resemble the face of a rhinoceros. note: neither trail route up to the rhino rock is well documented nor do they show up properly on google maps. however, if you upload hiking trail hk, you can see both routes fairly well on their more detailed maps of the stanley peninsula. note: the hike isn't particularly long but it is steep and route two is fairly requiring. bring sufficient water and a hat for the areas that are exposed to the elements. note: to reach the trailheads, you can walk down wong ma kok road around 20-25 minutes south of the village. during stretches of the road, there are no pavement sidewalks so you have to walk directly on the street. if this makes you uncomfortable, just take bus routes 6x or light green minibus 14 from the village to the end of the road where you find the trailheads.

chouara tannery is one of the three tanneries in the city of fez, morocco. built in the 11th century, it is the largest tannery in the city. it is located in the fes el bali, the oldest medina quarter of the city, near the saffarin madrasa along the river. since the inception of the city, the tanning industry has been continually operating in the same fashion as it did in the early centuries. today, the tanning industry in the city is considered one of the main tourist attractions. the tanneries are packed with the round stone vessels filled with dye or white liquids for softening the hides. the leather goods produced in the tanneries are exported around the world. the most notable feature of chouara and the other local tanneries is the numerous stone vessels filled with different colored dyes and white liquids. hides of cows, sheep, goats, and camels are processed by first soaking in a series of the white liquids – made from various mixtures of cow urine, pigeon feces, quicklime, salt, and water – in order to clean and soften the tough skins.

christ the redeemer is one of the new seven wonders of the world. it's a statue of jesus christ, located on the top of corcovado mountain in rio de janeiro, brazil. the statue is 30 meters in height and it stands on a 8-meter pedestal. construction started in 1922 and completed in 1931, taking a total 9 years to construct it. it's a major tourist attraction in rio. reaching the place involves a scenic train ride from the city to the mountain top, then elevator and some steps. a visit to the statue is something magical. the view of the city and mountains are also breathtaking. there is a little chapel at the back of the statue. we also saw some cute monkeys, which are relatively small in size being a major tourist attraction, it's usually very crowded. its visible from several points, including the sugar loaf mountain. if possible take a helicopter tour to view the statue from the top, it's magical.

church of st peter in gallicantu for a number of reasons the church of st peter in gallicantu is one of the most beautiful churches in jerusalem, it commemorates the apostle peter’s triple denial of his master, his immediate repentance and his reconciliation with christ after his resurrection. from here you have a stunning view of the mount of olives and the temple mount a very interesting place to visit. a modern chapel built on ancient foundations. the top two levels have very pretty byzantine style chapels. the downstairs has a dungeon where jesus may have been imprisoned before his interrogation by ciafas. it is also reportedly the place where peter denied knowing jesus three times. an amazing experience to be in person. this was the house of caiaphas. beneath the house there's a small dark pit where our lord jesus was detained overnight before he was crucified the following day. the view from the lower terrace gives perspective of jesus' journey and the archaeological significance of the site.

coliseum – love in the land of legends the coliseum, once an arena of blood and bravery, now stands silent — but not empty. its ancient stones breathe stories, and if you listen closely, you can almost hear the heartbeat of a thousand years. but when you stand there with your girlfriend, the place transforms. you don't just see the history. you feel it — in her eyes, in her smile, in the way she brushes her hair as the roman wind dances through it. you walk through arches that have seen emperors... but in that moment, the only queen is her. you sit on a worn-out step, where once roman crowds cheered — and now it’s just the two of you, laughing over an inside joke, sharing a gelato, or taking a silly selfie that somehow feels... eternal. 🏛 what makes it special with her: she reads the plaques, you pretend to be a gladiator 😄 you take her picture, but she’s too busy taking in the view you both pause, look around… and realize: > "we’re not just in rome — we’re writing our own chapter in its history." 💬 roman whisper: "tempora mutantur, sed amor manet." > times change, but love remains. and in the coliseum, surrounded by the ghosts of glory and greatness, your love feels just as powerful. 🧭 final words: the coliseum is a place built for warriors — but when you're there with the one you love, it feels like it was built just for that moment. just you. just her. and a story that even time won’t forget.

come pay your deep respects to the socially conscious kings and queens of hawaii in recognition of their inspirational, lasting contributions. high up in nuuanu valley is sacred land. here the kings and queens along other members of the royal hawaiian family and predominate associates are at their final resting place. most of the royals were deeply committed christian's, with a ferverent desire to loving serve their hawaiian people. the curator of these hallowed grounds asks that all who come respectfully honor the mana (the spirit) of this sacred space. these benevolent forward-looking royals left remarable legacies, which their peoples enjoy today. they built churches, fostered learning and education by establishng prominent schools. they attended to the health care needs of those under their charge by erecting leading hospitals. they left parks and gardens for all to enjoy. for more details about the direct contributions of the respective monarchs, please visit my various posts. these include: the queen's medical center pob 1 (queen emma), the physicians building pob 2 (queen emma), along with the cathedral of saint andrew (all established by queen emma). kapi'olani regional park (queen kapi'olani) and queen kapi'olani garden are other entries. kapi'olani community college (queen kapi'olani) and k.c.c. farmer's market are still other contributions. please also visit my "king kamehameha state" and "king kamehameha celebration" entries. i believe, they will introduce you to some of the very popular local traditions.

coming from vancouver, canada, where we’re used to the lush greenery of stanley park, i was so impressed by the royal botanic garden in sydney. it’s similar in the way it brings nature into the heart of the city, but with its own unique charm. the garden is a peaceful oasis right by the harbour, and it offers incredible views of the opera house, especially when you’re winding through its winding paths — it’s like playing a game of hide-and-seek with iconic sydney landmarks! what really stood out to me was how beautifully the birds and nature seem to live in harmony with the visitors. there’s a sense of calm here that makes you feel completely at ease, as if the space was designed for relaxation and connection with the environment. from the palm grove with its towering palms to the vibrant seasonal displays at the calyx, each section of the garden offers something special. i also loved the rose garden during spring — it was simply breathtaking. the bennelong precinct, with its gorgeous views of the harbour, is another highlight. this place is a perfect spot for a peaceful stroll, a picnic, or just a moment of reflection. it reminds me a bit of central park in new york, where the city’s energy mixes beautifully with the surrounding nature. what’s even better is that it’s free to enter, making it accessible to everyone. if you're in sydney, don’t miss the royal botanic garden — it’s an unforgettable experience that perfectly blends nature, history, and some of the best views in the city.

coming to st. mark's square is a unique experience. magnificent. in addition to the beautiful st. mark's basilica and the magnificent doge's palace, we immediately notice the beautiful buildings. the procuratie are three connected buildings (procuratie vecchie, procuratie nuove and procuratie ala napoleonica) in the shape of a horseshoe, in st. mark's square. these are historic buildings with offices where the procurators of st. mark, esteemed officials of the city and the venetian republic worked. the history of the origin of these buildings is extremely interesting. doge sebastiano ziani (1172 to 1178), after buying land from the nuns of sr. zaccaria, had a building erected in the square with loggias like galleries, which later served as the apartments of the procurator of san marco. later in the 16th century when the old buildings burned down in a fire the procuratie vecchie was built. the procuratie vecchie, is a renaissance building, 152 m long on the north side of the square, which continues to the torre dell'orologio. were designed by the architects bartolomeo bon and guglielmo dei grigi, and later by jacopo sansovino in the first half of the sixteenth century completed it, in 1538. the old procurators have two floors, on the ground floor there is a loggia with arcades (50 arches that are harmoniously connected with 100 windows in the upper two floors). they were completed in 1640 by longena. during the kingdom of italy the building was adapted for the royal residence (palazzo reale). today, the upper floors of the new procuratorate are the museo correr, the museo del risorgimento, the archaeological museum, the venice public administration and part of the marciana library. in the arcades of the procuratie vecchie and the procuratie nuove are the most famous, oldest and most expensive venetian cafes: gran caffè quadri, caffè florian (casanova, ghoete ... favorite place) which opened its doors on december 29, 1720, and caffe lavena (richard wagner favorite place). the procuratios took the form of a horseshoe (or inverted u) after napoleon bonaparte decided to demolish the church of san geminiano, thus gaining space for new procuratorates, called the ala napoleonica, the napoleonic wing. what to say, there is always a wonderful atmosphere here. people like to visit shops, coffee bars, museums ... in this area because there is a rich history here.

conman alert sauzier waterfall is a breathtaking destination and a must-visit spot for nature lovers. the best part is its accessibility—you can drive right up to the parking area, and after just a 2-minute walk, you're at the stunning waterfall. it’s an ideal spot for a swim and to enjoy the serene surroundings. however, visitors should be cautious of certain deceptive practices at the site: ticketing booth issues: some individuals at the ticketing booth may take payment but hesitate to issue tickets. this is a concerning practice that needs the immediate attention of the owners and management. parking scam: as you approach the last stretch of road before the parking area, there might be a con artist claiming that the waterfall is booked for a private function. they may then try to redirect you to park elsewhere and take a longer route called the "broadway mangrove." be cautious and avoid falling for this trick. despite these challenges, sauzier waterfall itself is an incredible experience and well worth the visit. a little vigilance can ensure your trip is memorable for all the right reasons.

construction of the bridge started in 1905 and finished in 1908. the bridge has a length of 169 m (554 ft) (one of the shortest in prague) and a width of 16 m (52 ft).[1] the bridge connects the prague districts holešovice and the old town (staré město). the bridge is constructed of stone (pillars) and iron (arches). up to 1961 the roadway was made of wood – a hard species named jarrah from australia. the road got slippery in the rain, so it was paved for safety reasons. [1][2] the bridge's architects were jan koula and jiří soukup. art nouveau style sculptures (including four put on 17.5-m-high pylons) were created by sculptors klusáček, wurzel, popp and amort.[3] the bridge was named after czech writer svatopluk čech who died around the time of the bridge's completion (1846–1908); its opening became a feat of the czech nation.[4] during the occupation of czechoslovakia by nazis, the name of the bridge was changed (1940–1945) to mendel bridge (mendelův most), after gregor mendel (of german ethnicity).[1] in 1971–1975, svatopluk čech bridge went through major reconstruction, in 1953–1956 and 2000–2001 through smaller reconstructions. in 1984–1987 the sculptures were repaired. as the only art nouveau style bridge in the czech republic, it is protected by the state as a cultural monument. it is used by tramways, cars and pedestrians.

customs house is the kind of place that surprises you even if you have walked past it a hundred times on the way to circular quay. the sandstone façade looks suitably grand from outside, but step through the doors and the foyer opens into a bright atrium with a glass floor that reveals a detailed scale model of sydney. you can spend ten minutes just tracing familiar streets with your eyes while ferries slide past outside the big windows. it feels like a small snapshot of the city within the city, and it instantly sets a curious mood for the rest of the visit. the building is beautifully kept, with contemporary touches layered over its 19th century bones. the city of sydney library lives here, which means quiet corners, free wi fi, newspapers, and art books you can leaf through between strolls. temporary exhibitions and installations pop up around the ground level, so there is often something new to see without paying a cent. if you want to make an occasion of it, the rooftop restaurant serves up harbour views that are hard to beat for a celebratory lunch or a slow drink at sunset. even a quick coffee at one of the street level spots feels elevated simply because of the setting and the constant theatre of the quay outside. practicalities are easy. entrances face both the quay and macquarie place, lifts run to all floors, and staff at the information desk are relaxed and helpful. the atrium is a cool refuge on hot days and a dry shortcut when the weather turns. i like to pair a visit with a walk along the foreshore to the opera house, then circle back through the rocks. customs house works as a destination and as a moment of calm in the middle of sydney’s busiest postcard.

cyber park arset moulay abdeslam is a serene public garden located in the heart of marrakech, morocco. this beautiful green space, also known as cyber park, covers an area of approximately 10 hectares and is a blend of traditional moroccan garden design and modern technological innovation. the park features a variety of plants, including palm trees, fountains, and lush flowerbeds, creating a peaceful environment perfect for relaxing or strolling. one of its unique aspects is the integration of technology — the park offers free wi-fi and several interactive screens providing information about the park’s history, flora, and the city of marrakech itself. the park’s design is inspired by traditional moroccan gardens, with elements such as arched walkways, water features, and a collection of mosaic tile work. it also has a special focus on sustainability, with eco-friendly features like solar-powered lights. cyber park arset moulay abdeslam is an ideal spot for both locals and tourists looking to unwind while enjoying the fusion of nature and technology in the heart of marrakech

breakfast includes pancakes, donuts, and similar items. drinking water is available on-site, but keep an eye on the cleanliness of the water dispenser. we found larvae or worms in the drinking water, which is completely unacceptable. the toilet and shower facilities are simple but relatively clean. the transfer from the airport to kri went relatively smoothly. the diving in the area was fantastic, and we rented equipment from a dive center in waisai, which was impeccable. the air in the tanks smelled bad, and we suspect this caused headaches after several dives. there are no safety procedures for diving, no oxygen, first-aid equipment, or anything else. therefore, you need to be mindful of your own deco time, as the divemaster has a lax attitude towards safety and does not take it particularly seriously. it didn't feel like a homestay; there was a lack of hospitality, and we didn't feel welcomed upon arrival, feeling a bit out of place. however, it must be said that the owners are generally problem-solvers and do everything they can to ensure you have a good diving and snorkeling experience. compared to other homestays on kri, this place pales in comparison. the place generally needs a lot of tender loving care and maintenance in all areas. we had paid for the transfer in sorong in advance, but no driver ever showed up, so we took a taxi. we had a good 6-night stay, but there are some significant considerations we would make if we were to stay here again: * diving safety. * cleanliness of drinking water. * type of accommodation.

definitely a place that will blow your mind with their illusions concept especially the chairs and table miniatures concept. worth a detour although would have prefer more activities and a restaurant to have food and beverages.

definitely a place to visit. wonderful architecture, stunning murals and religious furniture. not forgetting the 228 steps to the top of the dome and panoramic views of berlin there's also a lovely cafe to end your visit €10 entry fee or €7 with a city pass.
definitely a place worth a visit! the design of this large park is beautiful and practical (water element, shade, earth leveling).
definitely a tough climb but there was a wide range of folks on the trail, kids all the way to seniors, so you can do it! the panoramic view at the top is so worth it.
definitely a treat!

definitely an unforgettable experience. dirt bike trail was challenging but with scott leading the tour, you will have the confidence and skills you need to make it through. scott also gave some insight about the history of the area, but you should book a tour and find out yourself! an amazing half-day tour overall, and will be doing this again! thank you!

definitely breathtaking place with gorgeous view of the tower. very crowded. to be noted: there is no access for strollers/wheelchairs from the gardens. there was a ramp only from the street for 3 steps, the rest are blocked or not possible to use. paris is very unwelcoming for strollers/wheelchairs from my point of view.

definitely corniche is much better than before. it’s clean and safe to walk with young kids. they have a good variety of shops around coffee shops, restaurants and souvenir places. only thing is that prices are quite high there. they also provide boat trips with affordable prices. they charged only 50 ep per person when we went. the boat trip was nice. we loved it indeed.

definitely get tickets in advance and consider an audio guide so you can move at your own pace. the collection is varied, comprised of many portraits, frescos, a brueghel, maps, globes, china, weapons, and music. we went solely to see beethoven's eroica. it is on display as well as a haydn manuscript dedicated to mozart, schubert, strauss, etc. a few pages of sheet music are digitized for browsing: more of that would be appreciated! we had a package with a mini-concert: that was very well done. the view of prague from the balcony is breathtaking. in sum, there's a little something for everyone, but getting here can be a challenge unless you are young and fit: it's a long walk over very uneven cobblestones. p.s. if you get a bathroom code, don't forget the # or * after the numbers!

definitely go to the chocolate making class. we had so much fun decorating our bars. the place itself is really cute and desserts looks absolutely amazing. we got hot chocolate with added baileys- delicious. everybody working there is super nice.

definitely go walk along el malecon. watch people just chilling and fishing. kids playing. people swimming. people watching other people people-watching. that's weird! great scenes of the city. go at evening. watch the sunset. you'll never be able to convince yourself it was real.
definitely going to .ake another trip next time they are having a concert.

definitely going with dragon dive komodo again in my next trip! did a 8d7n dive-and-stay package (18 scuba dives) with them. having been diving for years in many different countries across asia, i can confidently say that i have one of the best experiences with dragon dive komodo. safety: highly prioritised for all the divers and their team. boat intro done daily and dive briefing done before every dive ensuring that everyone is well aware of the the safety measures. they never fail to emphasise on important information (e.g. missing diver procedure, low on air procedure, etc.) and welcome clarifications. i rented some gear (bdc, reg, dive comp) with them and all were in good serviceable conditions. they also were careful in handling my own dive equipment. i recall an instance when my dive group was consuming air much quicker than i did, they had another dm to surface with them so that i and some others could carry on our dives safely. really 5-star in the way they conduct their diving business. accommodation: good location, short walk to the harbour and to the main street where most of the shops, restaurants, cafes are located. stayed in a private room, which was well equipped good flushing, strong shower pressure and good ac. sheets were fresh and tidied daily. a security guard is on duty every night to guard the compound. service: the accommodation staff, dive guide and boat crew carry good command of english, amongst other languages, and were articulate in communication. expectations and relevant costs were clearly communicated. they were meticulous in providing service, even in the little things (e.g. giving recommendations on activities/food, helping to arrange airport transfers, checking in on how the dives felt, etc.). everyone was generally friendly, approachable and genuinely helpful. a shoutout to some of the staff and dive guides/dmts who made my stay really enjoyable, and made it harder for me to end my trip: james, karin, sarah, leo, marsel, rudiy, moggy, tian, stefan, geri, felix, william ... so many more people but their names escape me. big thank you! areas for improvement: - some parts of the accommodation is under renovation so it might get a little dusty and messy around. i'm sure that things will definitely be better after the works are completed. the restaurant is also not in operation so breakfast is only provided on the boat. as for the fitness space provided, it's really barely equipped and maintained, but to be fair, that's not their main business. - some of the misc. costs (e.g. rental fees, marine park fees, etc.) had to be paid strictly in cash, even though i could pay the balance for my dive-and-stay package using credit card. - in order to have things done efficiently, the boat and dive crew would be super focused on clearing out the boat at the end of the day. but it is a little awkward for the whole group to just disperse at the pier without a closing dressing after disembarkation. didn't really give us divers (and i say this for some other divers whom i've met on my trip) an opportunity to full appreciate the team at the end of the day.

definitely not as easy as i expected based on all the reviews, but still doable even for a beginner. the start is easy, yes, but unless you stop at the very first platform, the trail becomes more challenging. at times it felt more like climbing than hiking. we didn't go all the way to the summit, but the view was already amazing where we stopped! the hike took us around 2 hours with a small break at the top.

definitely one of the better areas to walk around here. we got to experience lots of wildlife and got some great pictures. it’s gets very windy when you are close to the coast but overall, definitely worth a visit.

definitely one of the most picturesque beaches we went to in the seychelles. it is located in the l'union state which requires an entrance fee of 150 scr per adult. there isn't 1 beach here, just keep going around the boulders (or the walkway on land) to get to different stretches of beach. a few beach shacks are around if you fancy a drink. water is very shallow and calm. fish come right up to you once you take a couple of steps in. the beaches are popular with tourists so not the best swimming experience but the setting of soft sand, giant boulders and jungle is wonderful nevertheless. definitely worth a visit.

definitely one of those “you have to do it at least once” dubai experiences — at the top, burj khalifa is surreal 🌆✨ the ride up is so fast and smooth, and when the elevator doors open, you're suddenly above the skyline. the view from the 124th and 125th floors is unreal — the city looks like a model, and sheikh zayed road stretches out like a silver ribbon all the way to the horizon. sunset is stunning (if you don’t mind the crowd) — the golden light hits the buildings just right, and when the city lights start coming on, it feels like a movie. you can see the fountains dancing from above, and even spot the desert fading into the distance. it’s not cheap, but for the experience and those views? worth it. just book in advance, and try to time it well — golden hour or night views are both magical. and yes, the instagram photos are even better in real life.
definitely our favorite beach in mahé, quiet, there are restaurants close by, marking spots, plenty of shade and the water is quiet.
definitely our favorite sunrise spot. temples feel within reach and the balloons fly across the sky right near by. worth the early morning drive.

definitely reccomend booking your mount batur trek here!! our local guide parno was amazing, very informative, caring and helpful in taking us up & down the mountain and providing a delicious breakfast too! communication through whatsapp was great and they were super understanding of our concerns about the weather & pick up/drop off was seamless! thank you!!

definitely recommend checking out this interesting shopping street with nice retro feel, 3 different shrines and lots of traditional snacks and household goods. start off your tour by taking the cute tokyo sakura tram and get off at koshinzuka station. much to explore from old style coffee shops, restaurants, piping hot taiyaki snack, traditional sweets, macha store, maruji store selling all sorts of red underwear and household goods. bought tenugui towels and sobakawa buckwheat pillow for bargain price of jpy158 and jpy1100 respectively. look out for shop in middle of this 800m street selling the cheapest beauty/health care i've seen in tokyo (cash only). one can easily spend half/full day to re-discover olde worlde charm that many may have forgotten.

definitely recommend this place! it’s a tourist spot, but it wasn’t overcrowded and is huge, so you definitely have enough space to be secluded. the mask bar is unique and fun, and the walk-up bar is cool. there are also blue slushies that go perfect. i recommend bringing flip-flops. you’ll get a wristband for your locker, so you don’t need to worry about remembering your locker number. there are spots on the wall that you can scan your wrist, and it will tell you which locker was yours. if you want to bring your phone out into the lagoon, you’ll want to bring a protective bag. there are steam baths and a sauna. my husband was reserved about going, but after saying it was amazing and definitely worth going, i agree. also, remember to put conditioner in your hair if you have long hair from the showers to help protect it.

definitely recommend to come here if you like relaxed browsing without being constantly disturbed and pressured by vendors (the way it usually works at the more touristy markets in siem reap). the market is quite small but has a decent selection of jewelry, handmade bags, honey, spices, knickknacks etc. beware that this market is fixed-price and that vendors will not allow bargaining— trust me, we tried, the most we got off was 1$ off a 40$ purchase because i convinced my friend to get the same 20$ bag that i purchased. prices are definitely higher but since most things are handmade i think it’s worth it.

definitely recommend, although it gets tough near the top. like others have said, the trail start turns off before the maps say, around 190m left to go on google maps when the trail begins on your left. there's two distinct sections, first is incredibly walkable with 5 rest stop shelters - the second is very steep and jungly. took me 1hr to go up the first section, and 1hr 45 for the second section. coming down, the top half took 1hr and the bottom half 40 mins. got very muddy - be especially careful if it rains, and it gets darker than you'd expect as well. did it on my own but slipped a few times coming down because of the wet - met two other groups, both 2 people with 2 local guides. one very nervy clifftop path near the top!

definitely the best choice i made regarding petra ! 1. you need to have valid tickets for petra before going here. 2. go to little petra (free shuttle but with lot of waiting time, or taxi 10jd). 3. you can begin your journey from here - directly hiking (2h to the monastery) - or by taking the truck (5jd / person) - be careful sometime its overcrowded so you will have to wait at least 45 min for the next ride and sometimes there is nobody so you’ll have to wait to have more people … i definitely recommend to take the truck - the most beautiful part of the hike is from the drop point (1h to the monastery). and you will walk all the way long … 4. you will arrive in the front of the monastery and you will enjoy descending the stairs instead of climbing them ;) 5. you’re welcome !

denali air (5 stars) this was almost a last-minute decision. initially, i hadn’t planned on taking the flightseeing tour because it seemed too expensive when i was organizing the trip. however, on the way from the train station, our driver had to pick someone up from the “glitter gulch” area who had just taken the tour. they highly recommended it, so it got me thinking. after checking in at our hotel, i noticed the denali air van parked outside the office. it felt like a sign, so i called them as soon as we got to our room. they had availability the next day at noon. when i gave my phone number to the young lady on the phone, she asked, “where in utah are you from?” it turns out her family lives just a few blocks from where we lived for almost 20 years! i also asked if they offered a military discount, which saved me $80. they picked us up right on time from our resort, and we headed to the airstrip, which was conveniently close. i asked the driver if he knew where we could find contact lens solution, as my wife had forgotten hers. he suggested trying sled dog liquor and grocery in “glitter gulch” or three bears groceries in healy, though that one was a bit farther away. check-in was smooth, and we were divided into two groups. our pilot, bob, was fantastic—funny, informative, and an excellent pilot. our group had seven people, and the other group had six. we flew in a twin-engine beechcraft, which i was relieved about since i avoid flying in single-engine planes. bob took us on an incredible journey around mt. mckinley, now known as denali, making sure everyone had the chance to see and take pictures of the breathtaking views. the weather was perfect with clear blue skies, and they even provided sunglasses if you forgot yours (though we didn’t need them). the flight lasted about 90 minutes, covering 100 miles there and 100 miles back, plus time circling the mountain. there were some bumps along the way, as you’d expect in a small plane flying over mountains and valleys, but bob (with one “o”) did an excellent job minimizing them with his skilled piloting. my recommendation: this is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. if you don’t do it on your first trip, you’ll find yourself coming back just to experience it later.

denali park bus tour. i didn’t find much if any value from this glorified school bus ride. our driver/guide lisa was very knowledgeable but unfortunately on some kind of power trip. treated me and other adults like school children. i had a $20 bill ready for her tip but after her abrasive scolding when my leg cramped in the tight seats and i had to stand momentarily - she lost all my respect and the tip. didn’t see much - some dall sheep off in the distance, ‘couple moose and roadside birds. denali wasn’t obstructed by clouds but so far off in the distance you had to squint or zoom lens to see it. it was part of our tour so i dunno published cost. whatever the cost i wouldn’t do it again with that driver even if it were free. i really don’t like to give poor reviews but gotta call it as i see it. disappointing, painful and rude is what i remember.

deoksugung palace: where humble beginnings lead to royal grandeur tldr: deoksugung palace offers a captivating blend of korean history and diverse architecture, from its unassuming entrance to its grand halls and western influences. it's a unique and worthwhile exploration of seoul's royal heritage. standing before daehanmun (大漢門), the main gate to deoksugung palace, it's easy to imagine the city's pulse shifting around this once less prominent gate. there's a sense of quiet resilience in its facade, hinting at the stories within. royal palace pass: snagging the royal palace pass for just krw 6,000 felt like unlocking a secret treasure map to seoul's royal heritage. five incredible sites for less than the price of two individual tickets? yes, please! royal guard changing ceremony: the rhythmic beat of the drums and the vibrant colors of the joseon dynasty uniforms bring history to life right before your eyes at the royal guard changing ceremony. it's a captivating 20-30 minute spectacle that truly transports you back in time. junghwajeon (中和殿): walking into the courtyard of junghwajeon, the undisputed heart of deoksugung palace, you can't help but be amazed by its majestic presence. the intricate details of the roof seem to whisper tales of royal ceremonies and the weight of history held within its walls. imagine the dignitaries who once stood on those very rank stones this building truly stands out as the palace's most beautiful structure. seokjojeon stands in stark yet harmonious contrast to the traditional architecture, a stately neo-renaissance building that speaks of a fascinating period of cultural exchange. the western-style garden and fountain offer a moment of unexpected european elegance. seokjojeon: then, a delightful surprise! seokjojeon stands in stark yet harmonious contrast to the traditional architecture, a stately neo-renaissance building that speaks of a fascinating period of cultural exchange. the western-style garden and fountain offer a moment of unexpected european elegance. jeonggwanheon (靜觀軒). this pavilion elegantly blends eastern and western design elements and once served as the esteemed home for royal portraits of the joseon dynasty. its unique character is a testament to the palace's diverse history. deokhongjeon (德弘殿) : for a truly serene and visually stunning experience, seek out deokhongjeon (德弘殿). built relatively recently in 1911, this hall exudes a harmonious and majestic aura from every angle. its refined architecture and artistic details make it arguably the most photogenic spot within deoksugung palace. perhaps the best part? you might just find yourself enjoying its beauty in relative tranquility, away from the crowds. gwangmyeongmun gate: this wasn't just any entrance, it was the main gate leading directly to hamnyeongjeon, the sleeping quarters of king gojong, the last king of joseon and the first emperor of the korean empire. don't just breeze through deoksugung - take your time, wander through its diverse structures, and let the stories of its past unfold before you. it's a unique perspective on seoul's royal heritage that's well worth savoring

desde 8 anos comecei a fazer "cooper" com meu pai em brasília. e a nadar para melhorar uma bronquite crônica que tinha na infância. e passei adolescência e vida adulta sempre correndo (e nadando menos) de forma irregular, períodos regulares seguidos de longos períodos sedentários. mas sempre gostei de fazer trilha e andar até mirantes e cachoeiras. quando voltei a correr aos 48 anos e larguei o cigarro perguntei a um amigo triatleta que atividade eu podia fazer. a pedida foi a melhor possível, o irmão rodrigo tostes indicou a tribus adventure e destacou o trabalho social realizado, apontando para a prática de trail run nas florestas e praias e trilhas da cidade e estado do rio de janeiro e de tantos lugares para onde essa turma de corredores e atletas que deslizam com suor e sorriso no rosto. tenho minhas dificuldades de agenda porque viajo muito a trabalho, mas mão arredo o pé. a tribus pra mim é família de força, saúde, técnica e respiração, ceia partilhada, viagens lindas para dentro de si e ao mundo, uma forma de conexão tão leve e tão pura com tantas pessoas tão legais, educadas, cheias de histamina, humor e vida. não são os vinte quilos que perdi nem as milhas de terra, pedra, mato, areia e chão da vida que ganhei. é a cuca legal e a cabeça de um modo positivo operante perguntando: "cadê aquela galera? saudoso do próximo treino, da próxima prova, da próxima trip! a tribus abala geral!!! venturoso adventure. aluizio napoleão

desert explorers adventure centre, located in swakopmund at the edge of the namib desert, offers an exciting mix of adrenaline-pumping and serene experiences. nestled between sweeping dunes and the atlantic, this center is best known for its thrilling quad-biking tours—guests can choose rides from 30 minutes up to two hours, winding through golden dunes and rocky terrain with expert guides ensuring both safety and scenic insights . for those seeking non-motorized experiences, sandboarding (both stand-up and lie-down), tranquil camel treks, and guided nature walks introduce you to the desert’s unique plant life and “little five” creatures . with a strong commitment to environmental stewardship, every activity is conducted responsibly, combining thrilling adventure with ecological awareness . the centre also hosts creative combo packages—like pairing dune rides with desert breakfasts or sundowners—making it easy to customize your visit . it is open daily (typically 8 am–6 pm) and includes convenient add-ons such as gear rental, refreshments, and even camel rides and skydiving options . positioned about 1–2 km from swakopmund town center, it’s easily accessible by car, taxi, bike, or on foot . desert explorers adventure centre is a dynamic destination where the shimmer of the sea meets the endless dunes, offering both sky-high thrills and quiet desert moments. whether it's quad biking adrenaline or peaceful camel strolls, it delivers unforgettable memories in namibia's stunning coastal desert.

desert safari and dune bashing is a wonderful experience in dubai. you would be picked in land cruiser 4×4 from hotel or at a designated place and will be driven around 25 km from city of dubai to desert area. the experienced car driver will take you to dune bashing and desert safari ride for approx 20 min. the roller coster ride in desert will be a life time experience. the excitement and adventure is beyond explanation. if you want to ride quad bike, you have to spend heavily (approx 250 aed) for 20 min. overall the experience was wonderful

desert safari in dubai – unforgettable experience! our desert safari in dubai was absolutely amazing! from the thrilling dune bashing in a 4x4 to the peaceful camel ride across the golden sand – every moment was unforgettable. we captured so many beautiful photos and videos in the desert. such a perfect mix of adventure and breathtaking views. highly recommended!

desert safaris dubai offers one of the best desert safari experiences you can find. we paid 125 aed per person, which was excellent value for everything included. our journey began with azmat, our driver, who contacted us the same day and picked us up from our hotel in a nearly new 4x4 vehicle. he was incredibly polite and accommodating, even providing hotspot wi-fi during the 40-minute ride to the desert. we first stopped at a quad biking camp where we rented bikes for just 50 aed—an absolute thrill! azmat then took us on an exhilarating 30-minute dune bashing ride, showcasing his expert driving skills. we paused for sunset photos and sand skiing, and azmat kindly offered to take our pictures. a short drive later, we arrived at the desert camp, where we enjoyed snacks followed by a delicious bbq dinner with unlimited soft and hot drinks. the evening was filled with entertainment, including three dance performances and a fire show. around 9:30 pm, azmat drove us back, wrapping up a truly memorable day. his professionalism and experience made all the difference. highly recommended for anyone visiting dubai!

desert season camp is a magical experience! i stayed with my husband in a bubble, and it was beyond amazing. the camp is extremely clean, and the staff were very helpful. i requested the bubble glass to be cleaned upon arrival for a better view, and within 5 minutes it was done ♥️! the camp is located deep in the desert, offering breathtaking views and peaceful surroundings. if i had more vacation time, i would’ve extended my stay for sure. i’ll definitely come back again for a longer visit♥️ mr. ahmed, the owner, and all the staff were incredibly polite and welcoming. the room was air-conditioned and the camp well-lit at night. the bathroom was super clean and fully equipped, which is a top priority for me, and i honestly give it a 100/10. the food was absolutely delicious! there was a nice evening event after dinner that added a great vibe to the stay. unfortunately, we didn’t have enough time to try the desert activities, but that’s another reason i’ll come back! the photos online truly reflect the real experience. the price is more than reasonable for the quality and service provided. highly recommend this camp especially for couples or solo travelers looking for a peaceful getaway.

deserted, remote island reached by rubberduck. beautiful stretches of white sand with wonderful snorkelling opportunities around the island. we identified at least 15 different tropical fish, while paddling in the warm water. no facilities on the island and all food and water to be brought along- and take all refuse back with you.

designed by architects renzo piano and richard rogers the centre pompidou has a very unique architectural design that turns the building’s insides out. all the structures pipes, beams and tubes our exposed and on the on the structure’s outside. also, centre pompidou is large cultural center with an enormous library, music and acoustics research center. the museum has one of the largest collections of modern and contemporary art in the world. legendary modern and contemporary artists such as: warhol, picasso, duchamp, miro, pollock, rothko, matisse and braque are just a few of legendary modern and contemporary whose works are on display

despite it being rather touristy - we loved it here. could spend all day here. we visited may 15, starting at 8am, and spent approx. 2.5 hrs on site. parking is free and i advise purchasing the tickets in advanced - although it’s less busy first thing, as we were leaving it got really busy - too busy for my liking…so go early. or go late in the day to avoid that. everything is laid out nicely, explained well and there’s always someone around if you have a question. the wrist band given is unique, allowing you to get into your locker and make extra purchases on your account without needing actual money (you just pay when leaving). you can get into the hot spring inside the building or out front of the building & you’re welcome to wear water shoes - there’s definitely some weird stuff you step on in the pools fyi. and it’s very easy to run into rocks under the water. there’s a small snack bar inside, seating seems to fill up fast but there’s extra seating upstairs if it’s full. it was so windy here my waterproof phone case got incredibly steamy inside, creating water inside the pouch. after a bit i just took my phone out, took my pics and put it in my locker. many people seem to do this.

despite many people saying to avoid due to tourist trapping, it’s really going to be up to you make the decision if certain stalls are worth it. most spots that require longer waits generally prove to be better but feel free to look around to see what people may have missed. super packed so expect to march like herding sheep but the food experience was nice to have tried being in there.

despite my little experience in motorcycling, i really grew up with the training done with instincts rider. a very good pedagogy with above all practice covering all aspects: stability, speed control, acceleration, braking, obstacles and the list is long ! the terrain of the training is excellent. thanks to our coach hamza who gave us confidence in ourselves. i highly recommend instincts rider (for my part it was a gs 1250 adv :))
despite rainy weather, spirits remained positive and i had an awesome time! super sweet guides. and very helpful!! definitely using the same company next time i come back to zanzibar!

despite the fact that most of paths were closed and we were unable to visit the entire park (april 25), and the entry price was not reduced, it is still worth going. setting and feeding the giant tortoises is as unforgettable experience. there are other animals too: crocodiles, lemurs, monkeys, iguana, insectarium, etc. as well as beautiful tropical plants and restaurant with tasty food. my husband tried crocodile meat for lunch!

despite the rude older waiter snapping at us as we accidentally entered through a side door, this cafe visit was a lovely experience. we were accommodated down the back of the restaurant, and a lovely waitress looked after us efficiently and was very politely and friendly . i had lots of gluten free options to choose from also. food was tasty and very well presented. esp the cakes!

despite what people on here say, i was there on a friday two days ago and it was open! nice goodies, you can mostly negotiate the price, there are second hand clothes and a lot of soviet paraphernelia, watches, badges, but also vintage israeli everyday objects.

detour africa curated an amazing 6-day namibian highlights tour for me. special mention goes to james. the package was perfect for my budget and the trip met my expectations in terms of organisation. the best part - all the accommodation spaces were excellent in terms of the quality of the rooms, food, and staff friendliness. furthermore, we had a friendly and knowledgeable tour guide - i learned a lot about namibia from the whole experience. i highly recommend detour africa.

devdan show bali - great entertainment! we had previously seen the ramayana ballet and the kecak dance, and the devdan show was a fantastic addition to our bali experience. the performance was impressive and well-produced, offering a modern twist on traditional indonesian culture. our driver was excellent-very friendly and informative. he even asked if we wanted to stop by a supermarket and shared lots of interesting insights along the way. highly recommended!

devin in the fish/meat department is the best. he listens and then meets your requests with perfection. he packs your items with care, never has extraneous ice on the scale, and is always friendly. excellent customer service and always a job well done. bravo devin!

dhammayangyi temple is the largest temple in bagan, known for its massive brick structure and mysterious history. though unfinished, its impressive size and well-preserved exterior make it a fascinating site to explore. inside, the corridors are narrow and dimly lit, adding to its unique atmosphere. despite some damage, the temple remains one of the most striking landmarks in bagan and is definitely worth a visit.
