dhathuruveringe market is a popular maldivian farmers market in maldives’ capital city, malé - situated directly on the sea front by malé north harbour. the market specialises in local fruit and vegetables such as dragon fruit, papaya, taro, screw pine, rambutan, purple mangosteen, custard apple, mango, coconut and more. you can also find maldivian delicacies such as addu bendi (a sweet treat, made from grated coconut and golden syrup)

dhow cruise for sunset @ 04:30 - 06:30. this cover the coastline gulf of oman & onboard provides all refreshments. dhow has upper duck, front area, air condition space and toilets. this suits for private parties, dinner cruise charter, coastal cruise etc

diamond head crater trailhead is a challenging but rewarding hike. climbing up a volcano isn’t easy, so pace yourself if it gets tough—you’ll reach the top at your own speed. the effort pays off with breathtaking panoramic views that are truly unforgettable. it’s a must-do for active visitors wanting a mix of exercise and incredible scenery. wear good shoes, bring water, and prepare for some steep sections. overall, this hike is definitely worth the sweat and time.

did 3 dives, saw many turtles, manta ray, beautiful coral reefs. the boat is comfortable, the crew is great and the food is great as well. always something on the table, pancakes, waffles, bread, ham, fruits, rice, veggie option,… nothing but great things to say ! would definitely recommend! the hotel’s nice. couldn’t try the restaurant as it’s being renovated. the personal is nice and helpful. rooms are clean and the bed is comfortable. thank you for everything !

did a 2 day safari with a big group where we were divided into 3 jeeps. had the pleasure of getting becki as our guide who was the best guide we could've asked for! he was so kind and told us so many facts about the park and animals. had a great experience and would 10/10 recommend it to anyone!!

did a day trip here for my birthday and it was fantastic. the property and all the springs are immaculate. great customer service and decent food. drinks were good but expensive. was a perfect way to spend a saturday! it's worth the hike to get to the springs behind the falls on the river. beautiful hike!

did a fantastic 400km over 5 days, fully supported mtb ride out of cape town with daytrippers. great organisation with good food and drink stops, amazing accommodation and friendly and helpful staff. no request was too hard. daytrippers catered the multi-day ride for both experienced riders and beginners, with a sag wagon for those who felt they were unable to continue. it was a wonderful experience and i would do another tour with them again in a heartbeat. highly recommended.

did a great circular walk in perfect weather—no midges, but quite some flies, so bring insect repellent. we went clockwise, starting on the coire loch trail (yellow), then joined the dog falls trail (red), and added the final viewpoint spur (white). took about 2 hours. the lake and forest were nice, but the dog falls themselves were hard to see in their full splendour. the final viewpoint was the highlight—amazing views over loch beinn a’ mheadhoin and the mountains, with two small benches perfect for our picnic. trails are marked as strenuous but very manageable. paid parking (£3, coins/card), free toilets at the start.

did a solo trip to ladakh and used their services for staying and also for travelling across ladakh, it was a ten day trip. i was very well taken care of all throughout the journey. very good guidance on showing me places of importance and also showing me places that are hidden natural treasures. very good hospitality, great food, warm culture. got to explore their culture. i never felt alone. they also curated the whole trip for me according to my likes and dislikes. thoroughly enjoyed and overall a great experience
did a tow foil session with dmitry at manawa. super knowledgeable about the spot, great equipment, and really looked after me really well. highly recommend. thank you guys.
did an avalanche course with neal. was very informative. had a great day, would definitely recommend

did circular route and went to woodstock cave and out by devils peak start. everything looked so fresh after rains, lots of little waterfalls. beautiful views of cape town harbor. meridian hiking club.
did full day pass. lots of pools, sauna, chairs. the restaurant was yummy. the lake was open and very fun to swim in. great relaxation and experience.

did my open water course at dragon dive komodo with james who is an amazing instructor! super chill and patient, explains things really well, and makes sure you feel safe the whole time. had so much fun, and saw a manta on my first ever dive, pretty hard to beat!! ended up staying on for some fun dives after my course and had a great time. the whole team in the dive shop and on the boat is friendly. safety is prioritized for all diver on the boat. just some small improvements:the wetsuits could be in better condition, the food on the boat is pretty basic, and one of the boats felt a bit crowded during the first few days of diving (though another one was in repair while i was there). in general, awesome shop, great vibe, and unforgettable diving, i would definitely recommend!

did my research but did not imagine to find a malaga experience in the middle of mountains area in sri lanka. very busy and tailored to tourists only. we probably assumed it will be more for hiking tailored rather then clubbing scene and bar scene. in overall it is a good experience because there is a lot of things to see around ella in the reach of an hour drive,however itself town it is just not great and fabricated to tourists only, so would re-consider my stay in the town next time, because it can be very misleading.

did not enter as we had been to too many museums in rome. this is a popular one to check out if you are into arts and heritage. from here, you can walk to the nearby piazza navona and then the pantheon. nearby you can easily get food and drinks. so have a great time walking and admiring cultures and history in rome!
did not enter the cemetery. also, there were some yellow tape, minor construction going on at the location. couldn't really take pictures. reason for 4 stars.

did not enter, just took pics (my daughter in the pic) 2nd narrowest building in the northeast. if you are in old san juan, it is around the corner from the bird park. beautiful place. have not done the tour but reviews say it can be scheduled.

did not have a good experience unlike the rest. for the price paid (50euros) it’s really not worth the money. felt masseur was not well trained in technique and also hard to communicate as they don’t speak english. the towels also smelt musky. you could shower there after the massage and toiletries are provided. however the experience before the massage was good, they provided snacks and tea by a nice old man who brewed it on the spot. nice place to take photos also around the courtyard.

did not really like this place. maybe it was because we went on a saturday. bought an umbrella for $15, and it was so filmsy that i tossed it an hour later. the sign also mentioned that it was $10, but i'm not sure why they charged $15. as for the stuff here... you can probably get it cheaper online. go here once for just the experience.

did not really rate the actual museum as very few exhibits and very little information in english so we had no real idea as to what we were looking at. however, the building itself is beautiful and definitely worth seeing. also has a lovely coffee shop/terrace area and an exhibition of artwork.

did our cooking class this evening and it was incredible!! it was just me and my partner so nice and personal, food was really good and whole experience was brilliant. our chef channy was super helpful and patient :)

did the "3 islands in 4 days" tour and it was stunning. spending 4 days in the galápagos was nothing short of magical, and this trip exceeded all expectations from start to finish. the team at guiding galápagos went above and beyond to organise a seamless itinerary. i was mostly out exploring, which is exactly how i wanted it. every day was full of discovery, yet somehow still felt relaxed and unrushed. we visited a wide variety of landscapes — from lava fields to pristine bays — and had plenty of opportunities to swim, hike, and spot wildlife. i was constantly amazed by how close we got to animals i’d only ever seen in documentaries. picture snorkeling with sea turtles, watching pelicans dive for fish, and seeing marine iguanas laze in the sun just a few feet away. what really made the trip special was the insight and passion of our local guides. they shared stories, history, and ecological facts that made each stop feel meaningful. it wasn’t just sightseeing — it felt like learning from people who genuinely love and protect these islands. if you’re looking for a well-organized, enriching experience that fits a lot into a few days without feeling hectic, i can’t recommend „guiding galápagos“ enough. this trip will stay with me forever.

did the 30th anny trip with my wife, daughter and her bf...blown away by yellowstone and much gratitude to yellowstone hiking guides as spencer made our van trip amazing where we hit the grizzly/moose/wolves trifecta on may 22nd! then two days of amazing hikes with emily jo (geysers near old faithful and lamar valley our final day). emily jo is an amazing talent, a wealth of knowledge, knew how to keep us and the animals safe and laughed at my dad jokes both days! 😁 i give emily jo and yellowstone hiking guides my highest recommendation to experience yellowstone.

did the 3d2n expedition from coron to el nido! an experience i will never forget, one of the best trips i've ever done! very well organised, the spots throughout the day were amazing with no other boats around for most of it! the food was outstanding and the team was great! highly recommend!

did the cape peninsula tour with curiocity. even though it was raining, togeda (our tour guide) made sure to make the experience worth our while by providing information and facts about cape town i never knew about. the highlights of the tour were definitely the penguins and lunch at bertha’s. will definitely do it again
did the crocodile spotting tour, would definitely recommend!! seen 3 crocodiles and eventually learned how to ride a jet ski

did the evening class, was an authentic experience and a good way to get a feel for the village life, our tour guide phearom was very knowledgeable and excellent english, he gave us a new appreciation of a cambodian lifestyle. the chef mai was very friendly and easy going, teaching us their village style cooking with delicious and fresh ingredients.

did the golden gate / alcatraz kiteboarding afternoon session and it was a great time! john did a really good job taking videos and photos of the experience which was great to document the memories. everything was run really smoothly and very easy in terms of the set up/pick up/drop off. would definitely recommend to others.

did the grand canyon flight with western ranch experience! was absolutely amazing! our pilot dillon was great , very informative , accommodating and funny thank you dillon and the 5 star team for giving us the best experience!
did the hip hop cruise we had a ball!! will definitely do again

did the monkey experience as advertised at my hotel with my family of 5. the monkeys were cool, and the tour guide noel very good. but they don’t allow pictures to be taken. rather they have a photographer following the group taking pictures that you can purchase at the end of the excursion. everything was an upsell with this trip. $95/person ($475 for 5) cost for the excursion, but you have to pay for food, drinks (even the water that was advertised to be included was a water cooler with paper cups that gives you two sips at a time). between food, drinks, pics for purchase, etc this trip could have easily cost $700-$800 if you bought all the extras (we did not). and the swimming at the lagoon to end the excursion was not advertised, so since we didn’t wear or bring bathing suits we couldn’t participate. also, what was advertised as a 4 hour excursion took 6 hours. it really wasted our day. i do not recommend.

did the mount batur trek with parno and had a great experience! he picked us up on time, ensured we reached the sunrise viewpoint early, and made multiple stops as requested. he provided breakfast, water, and even clicked amazing photos for us. highly recommended!

did the nile cruise from luxor to aswan with ahmed as our guide. it was an amazing trip. ahmed is a very knowledgeable guide, professional and friendly. boat was very comfortable with great meals. ahmed made the excursions very easy and gave a lot of history surrounding the temples.
did the one hour tour and had a great time with family! the guides were awesome and gave us a quick class and then we were racing through the sea. will definitely do it again!

did the one stop in the canyon sunset flight. from pick up at hotel to drop off at hotel, everything was top class. friendly, professional awesome staff. our pilot - myles - was terrific. his last canyon flight apparently as he's moving onto pastures new. cannot recommend this experience or company enough. thank you.

did the overnight boat trip with a group of friends and we had an amazing time. highly recommend it! the car ride from dubai was seamless and comfortable. the boat itself was brilliant and the crew ensured we had the best time. staying overnight on the boat was a very special experience. we saw so many dolphins swim alongside our boat both during the day and the morning after. the area of musandam is an incredible place. 5 stars!

did the partially open part of pr1, along with pr3. this section was the highlight, i recommend you go before sunrise, set up at the viewpoint next to weather station and then start the hike after seeing the sunrise.

did the platteklip gorge walk in jan 2025. took 2 hour to hike up and another 2 hours to go down. beautiful views all around. bring lot of water and suncream. cold and windy at the top. warm jacket or wind breaker a must.

did the self-tour (90mins video+walking) and just loved it. whether you are an architect expert or not (i'm not) this is a secret jewel in your visit to tel aviv, as you will see with different eyes from then on. the city historic background and it's beautiful buildings are not a coincidence. very nice people in the center too. definitely 10/10!

did the side by side and zip lines. atv course is smaller with not many obstacles. repeating same trails multiple runs. lagoon is cool but small. zip line was ok. last one gets you soaked. be prepared. dominican lunch was good. no cameras allowed, photographers take photos but want $80. everything is a little over priced

did the snorkeling with seals snorkeling. one of the first trips of their season. saw and swam with a seal and snorkeled over some beautiful sea anemones. dry suit equipment all provided and you go out on a rib which is always fun. wear leggings and a couple of warm top layers for under dry suit. lovely skipper and guide.

did the sunrise hike up to the viewpoint and it was so worth it!! we started at 4:00am from ella and we got there just in time for the sunrise at 5:50. there is an entrance fee so make sure to bring some cash but it was not much (i think 930rs or something like that). there are two viewpoints and the first one is usually more crowded (both very beautiful). breathtaking views - definitely worth the hike!!

did the tour from flores to lombok in march 2025. the first day was packed with sunrise hike on padar island, then komodo dragons and pink beach and snorkeling with mantas. the other days were less packed and we spent most of the day cruising on the ship, since you have to cover quite some distances. the snorkeling with the whale sharks was incredible! nanda was a super host and guide and impressed us with his singing skills and live for oldies music. we danced through the storm on deck. the boat is in good condition and super spacious (we were 13 people). could be a bit cramped during high season. the food was great too. a perfect way to get from flores to lombok!
did the whole loop and opal peak. definitely the steepest hike in jasper national park!

did this 14 km (to and fro) hike in the first week of february, and it was absolutely stunning! the trail was covered in snow, and flurries were falling throughout the hike, adding to the magical winter atmosphere. it’s mostly flat with a gentle incline, except for the last quarter, which has a slightly steeper section—but nothing too challenging. be prepared for a long hike, especially in snowy conditions. waterproof footwear is a must, and i highly recommend microspikes or crampons for better traction. the parking situation was a bit tight—the first lot was paid, but the other three seemed free (though nearly full). the highlight was an 85-90% frozen waterfall at the end—totally worth the trek! highly recommend this hike for a serene and scenic winter adventure.

did this in late august 2024 with fine weather. parked in the paved area. further up the unpaved road (and trail) were a few parked cars. at the end of the unpaved road were 2 parked cars. i was fine with parking in the paved area designated on google map as the trailhead. past the unpaved road/trail it was grassy and often wet and muddy with rather severe muddy sections best avoided, especially in the steep sections. fabulous views in decent weather.

did this on a cruise excursion. it was great! adonis and luis made for a fun trip. would highly recommend. scenic views, nice equipment, a small picnic lunch and swimming. and their base camp is a cool little spot built into the rock. definitely the highlight of our short time on the island.

did this walk during a weekday and it was really quiet can imagine this place at the weekend being quite busy. there is good area for parking for cars and camper vans. the route is pretty self explanatory just walk straight and don’t turn off at any of the crossroads which did make us ponder for a bit. it’s a challenging walk but not overly hard (if unfit or with kids this will take longer some big inclines). would recommend taking water. there were a lot of annoying flys on the way up and not many areas for stopping and resting. some great views at the top.

did tour a with discover el nido — big boat (way roomier than others), relaxed vibe, and good crew. james and jason were very nice. the hammock nets on the sides were a nice touch, perfect for relaxing between stops. would book with them again.

did tour to misali. it's not really a tour. they get you in a boat and you go to the island for food and snorkeling. not much guiding or explanation. don't pay the rangers if they ask you for a conservation fee. it's a lie. your 80 usd pays that and other costs.

didi was great and very patient with us as it was our first time rock climbing. we had so much fun and his english was amazing. he had great conversations and learned alot about brazil. the tour itself was hard but well worth all the effort but it was definatly difficult not much trail more climbing the mountain on rocks although we felt very safe with didi by our side! it was rewarding exciting and beautiful views. much better than taking the cable cars. i highly recommend!

didn't expect it to so as good. i thought that you need to go somewhere far to see such views, but it is here in the city. it is very calm here and there are almost no people. there are meadows, hills, ponds and streams - fantastic place. recommend visiting.
didn't expect this much. this is the best tour in rio. thanks!!!
didn't go too far up my kids are afraid of heights. however, it is beautiful and peaceful up there. i would love to go all the way next time.

didn't match our expectations, but was a worthwhile stop. we'd read about and hoped for a relatively private, natural and hot pool. it was none of those things. upon arrival 12 people were already there, but the owner proudly asserted that she could accommodate 25 in the three small pools. the cost for entry is ~3000 icelandic kroner per person (see photo) for 1.5 hours. the pool itself was warm, not the hot that we'd hoped for but adequate for a relaxing stop. the algae in the pool was extremely slippery - be very careful getting in and out. overall, we enjoyed the stop after resetting our expectations.

didn't need to queue for long with my go city prebooked tix. a small museum, approx 1 hr to get around. some great wax works but definitely not to size. some interactive areas which is entertaining. would recommend

dominus flevit church - mount of olives - jerusalem : stands in mount of olives, opposite to the walls of the old city of jerusalem - dominus flevit in latin means the lord wept – when jesus first entered into jerusalem on the first palm sunday, looking down on the city, he prophesied its destruction and wept over it - in ad 70, jesus’ prophesy proved true when roman legions besieged jerusalem and burnt the temple and levelled the city - the church is designed in the shape of a tear-drop to symbolize the tears of christ - constructed between 1953 and 1955 - designed by the italian architect antonio barluzzi – looking from here, tourists get a panoramic view of the old city of jerusalem located opposite on the temple mount (mount zion) – a spot which offers the history of jews, christians and muslims.

dominus flevit is one of the attractions at the mount of olives, situated a fair distance up the slope past the church of saint mary magdalena. opening hours are 8-11.45am and 2.30-5pm daily. there is a small church on the grounds that is famously shaped like a tear drop, to commemorate the belief that christ wept for jerusalem upon this site. you can enter the small church, sit for a brief rest from climbing the steep street up to the church grounds. within the church, you will see a beautiful view of the old city when peering out the window behind the alter. there is a cross in the window screen. it marks the spot in the old city where the church of the holy sepulchre is found. from outside the church, there are additional resting places with outstanding views of the old city from this vantage point upon the mount of olives. overall, dominus flevit is a nice inclusion to the mount of olive attractions but quite a climb which could be challenging and tiring for some.

don’t forget to record an outdoor walk on your fitness device for record! so surreal. i’ve seen the brooklyn bridge in paintings, movies, tv shows—even on the black-and-white shower curtain hanging in my own bathroom. but to stand on it, to see it stretch across the east river in person… there’s something almost sacred about that moment. the bridge has watched over so much history since it opened in 1883—connecting manhattan and brooklyn, spanning generations, revolutions in architecture, and waves of change in new york itself. it was the first steel-wire suspension bridge ever built, and at the time, the longest in the world. now, it’s an icon etched into the heart of the city and the people who walk it. surprisingly, the best view isn’t at the manhattan entrance. the most breathtaking moment is when you’re looking back from the brooklyn side—skyline in the distance, the cables framing it all like a work of art. getting there is part of the experience. once you reach the district and federal courthouses, just follow the signs—or follow the crowd. they’ll lead you to one of the most unforgettable walks you can take in new york.

don’t let ongoing renovations stop you from visiting. these free public gardens are beautiful to wonder through and enjoy a peaceful moment to yourself. i enjoyed seeing the turtles sunbathing by the waterwheel. at one point i spotted a plump squirrel in one of the greenhouses, little guy must be living good in there. the dedication and time put into these overflowing garden is incredible, and well worth the 15 minutes it takes to walk through the greenhouses.

don’t miss out on this beautiful pristine botanical gardens! super cheap 10k per person and you can rent bikes, scooters inside if you’d like. we walked around the entire gardens all to ourselves, super peaceful and away from the crowds. the cactus garden was a highlight.

don’t miss this. lots of planes and relics from the war. we saw pieces of the usaf u2spy plane that was shot down, and lots of russian guns, etc. if you are a military buff this is interesting and free! if you don’t like looking at military stuff, pass on this spot.

don’t park near the calheta way if you are looking for an easy hike. it’s the longer way to the falls. and your shoes may get all wet if you use the tunnel for a short cut. quite a bit of claim to the cafe too. use the other car park that has a mini bus service to the cafe if you prefer less trouble. at the cafe you are looking at around €6 per sandwich. the cafe has great service. the sandwich tasted nice. the route from cafe to risco waterfall is largely flat and easy. the seemingly easier way to 25 fontes was closed at the time i visited so you will need to take the steep route. it gets slippery even on a sunny day so take the right shoes and equipment for safety. i think the view at risco was nicer than 25 fontes. so if you only have time/energy for one thing or just want a leisurely walk, then i’d say go for risco.

doota mall, situated directly opposite ddp, is a duty-free shopping center in dongdemun. it offers a diverse range of brand outlets catering to both children and adults. the top floor provides a stunning panoramic view of dongdemun plaza, while the basement houses korean cuisine restaurants. while doota mall is a haven for brand enthusiasts, it is essential to note that it does not offer significant discounts throughout the year like some other venues. the operating hours are from 11 am to 10 pm.

dormition abbey was such a beautiful and somber place to visit. the place where jesus christ 🙏 had his last supper. the holy ground where he walked. my thoughts inside this abbey were surreal and peaceful. a must see location for all.

dove car wash and casa cenote with koox this week. juan carlos and sofia were both great. everything was explained well, and i felt safe the entire time. juan carlos explained everything in detail and had everything ready when i arrived. all of the equipment seemed to be of nice quality and the entire trip went smoothly. i would dive again with them again next time i’m in tulum. check them out if you are looking for a dive shop in centro area.

dove with karen, what an incredible and amazing adventure! karen is kind and patient and definitely knows her way around the site. i loved diving with her and seeing her marine family! her posse of fish friends followed us from beginning to end swimming among us like old friends. we saw so many types of life, i am still in awe! was an amazing experience i won’t ever forget, and would recommend a hundred times over for divers of any level! thank you so much karen, you are a gem in san juan!

dr. tarantino was the perfect guide for this tour. anytime a phd. can be equally informative and humorous is worth the price of admission. the views are spectacular, and the service on board makes this a must do on any trip to nola.
dragon mountain lives up to its name. this is a good a place as any to see the galapagos land iguana.

dragon’s back hike – scenic but too crowded 😅 we started the hike around 11 am on a friday in may from shau kei wan (exit a2) and took a bus to the junction of hk trail section 7 & 8. e-wallets like octopus were accepted. while the views were stunning, the trail was surprisingly crowded even on a weekday. it was hard to take photos without people, and the heat added to the discomfort. we ended up turning back halfway due to the crowd. for a quieter experience, go early or avoid peak seasons.
dramatic viewpoint of falls. to see the force of the river, and how the rocks make it rapidly change course and churn over the brink is breathtaking and refreshing.

drawing on a centuries-old tradition, mývatn nature baths offer bathers a completely natural experience that begins with a relaxing dip amidst clouds of steam rising up from a fissure deep in the earth's surface, and ends with a luxurious swim in a pool of geothermal water drawn from depths of up to 2.500 meters.

drawn in by the glowing gold rooftop of wat traimit. at night, it shines even brighter against the dark sky — absolutely stunning ✨ i’ve passed through chinatown bangkok so many times and somehow never noticed this beautiful buddhist temple. but this time, something about it just pulled me in. sadly, i couldn’t go inside… was wearing shorts😭 tip: there’s a dress code for entering the temple — next time, i’ll come wrapped and ready!

dreamy setting for a ski touring base. beautiful cabins with a sauna and fjord to jump in. only 15 mins drive from svolvaer airport. meals are hearty and healthy, with a terrific selection to make a packed lunch from. extensive wine list too. the views from the cabins are magnificent from the moment you wake up until you go to bed. cabins were spacious, cosy and luxe, even though the site describes them as being quite basic. the beds, pillows and duvets were divine. i'm sure long days outdoors contributed, however this week was some of the best sleep i have ever had. loads of space for drying clothes and leaving kit out, and the cabins were always warm and welcoming. drinks are very reasonable for norway and there is an aquavit bar on the top floor. wonderful. i hope i get to return here one day.

dropped by the national art center today. the exhibitions on display were more on the beginner side—felt a bit like student works—but the building itself more than made up for it. the architecture is stunning, with a spacious, immersive atmosphere that’s worth experiencing on its own. i’m planning to come back to try their french restaurant next time—it sits at a high vantage point with views that pair perfectly with a good meal.

dropped in late morning with the kids in tow, which was a bit of a gamble but actually worked out better than expected. the current exhibition was bold and visually engaging, even if a few pieces flew over the kid’s head. the gallery space is light and surprisingly forgiving for families with wide walkways and no crowding. the kids absolutely loved the flower exhibition! that said, it's definitely more of a grown-up experience. no café inside, but plenty of options nearby. staff not particularly friendly and kept to themselves.

drunken elephant mara exceeded all our expectations! the service was outstanding—every staff member went above and beyond to ensure our comfort and make our stay truly special. the biggest advantage is its proximity to the safari gate, making early morning game drives incredibly convenient. the food was fantastic, the tents were cozy, and the overall experience was seamless. thank you jazeera and team

dubai creek harbour is definitely the most magical location in dubai.famous for its best restaurants and hotels, lavish properties and shopping malls;reminiscent of the lost arabian world. both sides of the dubai creek are surrounded with old-style markets, heritage buildings and museums.

dubai creek is a must-visit destination that beautifully showcases the city’s blend of history and modernity. the waterway has played a vital role in dubai's trading history and continues to be a vibrant part of the city. one of the highlights is taking a traditional abra ride across the creek for just 1 aed – a simple yet charming experience that gives you a feel of old dubai. on either side, you’ll find bustling souks like the gold souk and spice souk, filled with energy, colors, and the aroma of spices. the creekside promenade is pleasant for a stroll, especially in the evening when the area is lit up and the temperature is cooler. you can also find heritage sites, museums, and cafes that offer great views of the water. whether you're interested in culture, shopping, or photography, dubai creek has something to offer. it’s a refreshing contrast to the city's skyscrapers and luxury malls.

dubai desert safari experience was absolutely unforgettable! from the thrilling dune bashing to the serene camel rides, every moment was packed with excitement. the stunning desert landscape was a sight to behold, especially during sunset when the sand glowed in beautiful hues. i also enjoyed the cultural performances and delicious traditional dinner under the stars. it was a perfect blend of adventure and relaxation, making it a must-do when visiting dubai! 🐪🌅

dubai desert safari is a breathtaking and mind-blowing experience, offering a perfect taste and adventure that dubai has to offer. our host and driver, farooq, made the trip truly unforgettable. his warm personality and exceptional desert driving skills were simply the best, made us enjoy and exhilarate the entire time.

dubai festival city mall is a great spot to sit and relax, especially outside by the waterfront. the outdoor area is peaceful with plenty of seating, making it a nice place to unwind and enjoy the view. inside, the mall offers a wide variety of shops and dining options, catering to all kinds of needs. a major plus is the ikea located within the mall — super convenient for home shopping. make sure to catch the fountain and light show in the evening — it's definitely a must-watch and adds a special touch to the visit. ideal for a laid-back weekend outing with shopping, food, and scenic views.

dubai festival city mall offered a spectacular celebration during eid al etihad, making it a prime spot to witness the uae’s 53rd national day festivities. the highlight of the evening was the breathtaking fireworks display over festival bay at 9:40 pm on december 2. complemented by live music and vibrant roaming entertainment, the event radiated festive joy. the mall itself was transformed into a visual delight, adorned with intricate decorations reflecting the uae’s vibrant spirit. visitors enjoyed a variety of activities, including live performances, and cultural showcases, creating a festive atmosphere for families and friends alike. the imagine water and laser show added a mesmerizing touch, blending technology and storytelling with captivating visuals and music. this celebration beautifully honored the uae’s unity and cultural pride, offering a memorable experience for all who attended

dubai hills mall is lovely – spacious, bright, and easy to navigate. great mix of shops from high street to premium brands, plus a handy geant for groceries. loved the dining terrace and the indoor attractions (roller rink, storm coaster, reel cinemas) – perfect for families. parking is plentiful, though it can be a bit busy on weekends. overall, a modern, well‑curated destination worth visiting!

dubai mall avenue is an upscale extension of the dubai mall, located in the heart of downtown dubai. connected directly to the mall and the burj khalifa/dubai mall metro station via a climate-controlled bridge, the avenue offers a luxurious and convenient shopping and lifestyle experience. this stylish promenade is lined with high-end boutiques, elegant cafés, and fine-dining restaurants, attracting both tourists and residents. it features a sophisticated architectural design, with natural lighting, sleek interiors, and a calm ambiance that contrasts with the bustling energy of the main mall. popular brands along the avenue include chanel, rolex, cartier, and other global fashion and jewelry icons, making it a go-to spot for premium shopping. dubai mall avenue also provides direct access to several key attractions, including the burj khalifa, dubai fountain, and the address hotels. its wide, clean walkways and elegant atmosphere make it ideal for leisurely strolls, business meetings, or luxury retail therapy. whether you're shopping for designer goods, grabbing a coffee in a peaceful setting, or simply enjoying the upscale environment, dubai mall avenue delivers a refined urban experience that complements the grandeur of downtown dubai. it's a must-visit for those seeking luxury, convenience, and elegance in one place.

dubai mall is huge and has everything! you can shop for anything, from designer clothes to electronics. there's also an ice rink, aquarium, and tons of restaurants. it can get super crowded, especially on weekends, so be prepared for that. overall, it's a great place to spend the day!

dubai mall is without doubt an impressive place. it’s huge, well-maintained, and has almost everything under one roof — from shops and restaurants to entertainment and attractions. the space inside is well spread out, so even with the heavy crowds it doesn’t feel suffocating. walking around is enjoyable, and you really get the sense of being in one of the world’s top malls. that said, there are a few things that could make the experience smoother. first, it would be very useful if the mall offered a free service for keeping small bags or shopping parcels. many people spend half a day there, and carrying things around the whole time can get uncomfortable. a simple bag-drop counter would make visits more relaxed and practical. second, the mall could improve child-friendly facilities. while there are plenty of attractions for kids, parents would benefit from more accessible services like clearly marked stroller paths, extra family washrooms, or small rest areas for children. these small touches would go a long way in making the mall more comfortable for families. parking is another area that could use improvement. the mall has one of the largest parking facilities in the city, but it can be confusing. clearer, more visible signs would save visitors a lot of time when finding their way in or out, especially after a long day of shopping.

dubai mall zabeel is an extension of the main dubai mall, offering additional retail and dining options. visitors can access it directly from the mall or take a seven-minute walk from the dubai mall metro entrance towards the zabeel side. one of the convenient features of this extension is the free buggy cart service, which transports visitors between dubai mall and zabeel, making the journey more comfortable. transportation options are well-managed, with taxis readily available both at the entrance and downstairs, ensuring ease of commute for visitors. on the right side of zabeel, you will find key outlets such as lulu hypermarket, mcdonald’s, and ibn sina pharmacy, along with a few other retail stores and elevator access. the left side features additional shopping outlets, offering a mix of fashion, lifestyle, and convenience stores. the extension provides a more relaxed shopping experience compared to the main mall, with less crowding and easier accessibility to essential stores. whether you’re looking for groceries, fast food, or pharmacy needs, this area is a convenient stop. the overall layout is well-organized, and the availability of taxis makes it a hassle-free extension of dubai mall for quick shopping or dining.

dubai mall’s chinatown is a vibrant and beautifully designed space with traditional lanterns, neon signs, and chinese-themed decor. it’s a great spot for photos and offers a variety of authentic chinese restaurants, bubble tea shops, and unique stores. located near the dubai ice rink, it’s a fun cultural escape right inside the mall.

dubai marina mall is a well-balanced spot for a relaxed shopping and dining experience, with added family entertainment and scenic marina views. it’s smaller and less overwhelming than mega-malls, with a good mix of mainstream retail and casual fun. watch out for parking challenges and crowd spikes, but with smart timing and preparation, it makes for a pleasant stop in the marina area.

dubai marina mall is one of those hidden gems that blends charm with convenience. it may not be the biggest mall in dubai, but that’s actually part of what makes it so enjoyable — it has a cozy, open layout with beautiful indoor spaces and waterfront views just outside. what really sets marina mall apart is the variety and uniqueness of its shops. unlike the larger malls that tend to repeat the same big-name brands, this one mixes well-known labels with smaller boutique-style stores, giving you a more interesting shopping experience. whether you’re looking for fashion, gifts, or even just a relaxing coffee spot, you’ll find something different here. it’s never overwhelmingly busy, and that calm vibe adds a lot to the experience. great place for a peaceful walk, quality shopping, or a relaxed meal by the marina. definitely worth visiting if you’re in the area or looking for something a little more refined and easygoing than the massive retail hubs.

dubai, the city of wonders, never ceases to amaze its visitors with its stunning architectural marvels and luxurious experiences. one such unforgettable experience awaits you at the dubai marina cruise dinner. from the moment i stepped aboard the cruise ship, i was captivated by the glitz and glamour surrounding me. the elegant ambiance, coupled with the breathtaking views of the dubai marina skyline, immediately set the stage for an unforgettable evening. the highlight of the cruise dinner was undoubtedly the spectacular buffet spread. the selection of international and local cuisines was a treat for the taste buds. as we indulged in the delectable fare, the cruise ship glided through the iconic dubai marina, offering us panoramic views of the magnificent skyline. to complement the delightful culinary journey, a live entertainment program was provided.

dumbo is such a cool spot to visit! we loved the cobblestone streets, trendy shops, and amazing food options. the views of the manhattan skyline and brooklyn bridge are stunning — perfect for photos, especially at the famous washington street view. a great place to walk around, grab a bite, and soak in the city vibe. a must visit!!

dune 45 viewpoint in namibia offers a surreal experience in the heart of the namib desert. the dune, standing at around 80 meters tall, is located 45 kilometers from the sesriem gate, which is how it gets its name. the climb to the top is steep but relatively short, often taking about 20 minutes. as each foot sinks into the fine, reddish-orange sand, there’s a sense of walking through one of nature’s most ancient landscapes—the sand here is said to be over five million years old. the view from the summit is absolutely spectacular. at sunrise or sunset, the dunes come alive with glowing hues of gold, crimson, and deep orange, creating sharp contrasts of shadow and light along the ridgelines. the surrounding sea of sand stretches endlessly, interrupted only by the occasional acacia tree or dry riverbed. it’s a paradise for photography, with changing angles of light offering endless frames of beauty. the area is also peaceful and untouched, making it a meditative place to pause and soak in the vastness of the desert. the soft, iron-rich sand shifts subtly with the wind, often erasing footprints within minutes, adding to the mystical atmosphere. dune 45 is a truly unforgettable spot in namibia’s sossusvlei region, blending natural wonder with a quiet sense of timelessness.

dune 7 is a must-visit if you are in the swakopmund-walvis bay area as it is an iconic and beautiful natural wonder to behold. the climb itself isn't too strenuous if you take it slow and start at the longer side from the left of the dune. it is definitely worth it when you reach the top and are able to take in the amazing views of the surrounding area. it is good to note that there is an entrance fee now for all visitors, even if they don't plan on climbing the dune. when i visited, the fee was n$ 100 per person for those from sadc countries, but i have to say it has contributed to the overall safety of the area. if you aren't planning on climbing the dune you can still take in it's beauty from the parking area outside the gate. i was however disappointed with the overall cleanliness of the area. the area at ground level of the dune was dirty with lots of small litter spread around, and the bathrooms were dirty as well. the staff were also very lacklustre. they weren't very helpful or friendly and gave the impression that they didn't really want to be there. given that an entrance fee is now being charged, i think the staff could do a better job of keeping the area clean. overall, i would have given dune 7 a 3 out of 5, however i always enjoy visiting and climbing it and definitely think it is still a must visit.

dunrobin castle is probably the best castle we have visited in quite some time. we were blessed with the weather so we decided to visit the castle grounds first. the gardens are very well tended. fortunately the gardens are laid out before you as you wander around the side of the castle. there are lots of steps so just be aware. on the same level as the gardens is the museum. the museum is a display of its time. the cafe offers quite an array of food on its menu. the castle is well set out and leads you into the different eras of the occupants of the castle. the exhibits are excellent and the room recreations give an idea of what it must have been like to live in the castle. there is a gift shop, it is however not very large. the items for sale are as a result limited.

durar tours made our musandam khasab trip unforgettable! from a comfortable dhow cruise to thrilling dolphin watching and snorkeling, it was an adventure of a lifetime. special discounts for all group sizes and a dedicated team made the experience seamless. highly recommend durar tours for a fantastic khasab tour!

during a walk of the area, consisting of the arc de triumph and the the famous champs élysées, this is the perfect place for us to stop for lunch, there is the bestest vegetation, tunnel, to shelter from the rain with seating, tourists seem to miss it.

during my first (solo) visit to sivilay thai massage, i experienced an amazing deep tissue massage from paola. her technique is great and the atmosphere she and her team create from start to finish is so welcoming, relaxing and comfortable. the studio is beautiful and extremely clean and tidy. soothing scents, heated massage tables, gentle music all add to customers' wellbeing. and of course, preferences and health issues are carefully considered. when i mentioned to paola that i am traveling with my family, she immediately came up with a custom family massage package - so a few days later, we all went back together! this experience was another highlight. my five-year-old received their first ever gentle kids massage while my husband and i could enjoy our own massages. all in one room, with so much love and consideration for our little one. we all had an amazing time! thank you so much for this special event! ❤️ to summarize: at sivilay, you get a luxury experience for a more than reasonable price!

during my last visit to swakopmund, i explored the desert with tommy's living desert tours, which was an amazing experience! it is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to learn about and experience the unique desert ecosystem firsthand. the tour starts with an exciting 4x4 ride into the desert, where you get to stop intermittently to explore the remarkable fauna and flora of the region. we saw snakes, chameleons, geckos, and various different insects and plants. our hosts, duan and andrew, were incredibly knowledgeable about the desert and were able to answer all of our questions. the drives through the dunes were exhilarating, and we were even able to climb up one of the dunes during the trip. the desert offers endless photo opportunities, and you'll walk away with some spectacular photos and memories to cherish. we also had a rest stop where we were provided with snacks and drinks. it's worth mentioning that at the rest stop there were also toilets available. this tour has given me a new found respect and awe for the desert. it is truly a remarkable place, and i am so grateful for the opportunity to have experienced it with tommy's living desert tours. if you are looking for a unique and unforgettable experience in namibia, this is a tour you don't want to miss and something you will never forget!

during my stay in são miguel (azores), i visited a ceramic factory-store in lagoa, where i purchased several pieces that i found truly beautiful and representative of the region. however, the service i received—particularly from the woman who assisted me—was disappointing. when i asked her to ring up the items and wrap them properly, i explained that they were gifts and would be traveling back to my country with me. she assured me she would wrap them well. yet, after charging me, she began wrapping the pieces using just a sheet of newspaper and attempted to bundle several fragile items together. when i asked her to please wrap them individually, her attitude became noticeably reluctant and unprofessional. to make matters worse, she didn’t even offer a bag to carry them. had i not already paid, i would likely have left everything behind. the service was cold, careless, and unpleasant—hardly what one would expect from a business catering to visitors hoping to take home a special souvenir. sadly, when i look at these pieces back home, what i’ll remember won’t be the beauty of the azores, but the poor customer service i received. it’s unfortunate that such lovely items are overshadowed by such a negative experience.

during my time at high park for the cherry blossom season, i was completely blown away by the beauty! the park was transformed into a breathtaking sea of pink/ white blossoms, creating an incredible atmosphere. there were so many walking paths, making it easy to spend hours exploring the area. i was pleasantly surprised to see few horse rides happening inside the park, which added a unique touch to the experience. it was pretty crowded because of the cherry blossoms, so if you’re hoping to take photos at the prime spots, be ready to wait a bit. but honestly, the lively energy made it all worthwhile! one of the highlights was how dog-friendly the park is—lots of people were out enjoying the day with their furry companions. the nearby lake was also a lovely addition, with people fishing and relaxing by the water. i’m already looking forward to next year’s cherry blossom season! high park is an amazing place to soak up nature, enjoy a leisurely walk, and appreciate the stunning beauty of the blossoms. it’s a must-see in toronto!

during my trip to dubai, i had the chance to visit the dubai old village, and it was a truly special experience. i think the dubai old village is a great place for anyone who wants to explore the real roots of the city. it’s perfect for tourists who love culture, history, and photography. i would definitely recommend this place to anyone visiting dubai. it was one of the best parts of my trip because it helped me understand the history and culture of the uae in a beautiful and peaceful setting.

during my visit to fes, i was eager to try a traditional moroccan hammam. however, it wasn’t easy to find a highly-rated spa, as many providers make it unnecessarily difficult for customers to get detailed information about their offerings and prices, and the service often leaves much to be desired. at laaroussa spa, everything was perfect: a fairytale-like atmosphere straight out of 1001 nights, excellent, friendly, helpful, and unobtrusive service, an easy booking process via their website, an extraordinarily warm welcome, and a beautiful hammam followed by a wonderful massage.🥰 while the prices are slightly higher than some other providers, the quality and service are unbeatable. after the hammam, i was invited for tea on the rooftop terrace of the riad, which was a truly beautiful way to end my visit there. the view is breathtaking, and the atmosphere is so peaceful. while i can't afford to stay overnight in this amazing riad😅🙈, i will definitely treat myself to another hammam and massage on my next visit to fes.😊

during my visit, i had the pleasure of witnessing a traditional dance performance in a public space. the energy, rhythm, and artistry of the dancers were absolutely captivating. the way they moved in harmony, expressing their culture and heritage through each step, made it an unforgettable spectacle. it was a privilege to watch such a vibrant and authentic display—truly a highlight of my visit.

during our recent visit to quebec, my partner and i treated ourselves to a day at balnea spa in bromont — and what an unforgettable experience it was. although cameras and mobile phones are strictly prohibited on the property (a rule we grew to appreciate), i must say it’s a shame i can’t share the majestic views we enjoyed from the infinity pool. breathtaking doesn’t begin to describe it — the serenity of the landscape, combined with the gentle sounds of nature, felt like something out of a dream. we explored everything the spa had to offer: the turkish saunas, multiple hot tubs, and panoramic lounges, all thoughtfully positioned overlooking a pristine lake. the air was fresh, the ambience silent and calming — it was, in every sense, a sanctuary. midway through our spa circuit, we stopped at lumami, their on-site restaurant. as someone who’s lactose intolerant, i’m often cautious when dining in quebec, where cheese and cream are heavily featured. but lumami was an absolute revelation. the staff were wonderfully accommodating, and the menu was designed with such care and creativity, i felt completely at ease. we started with their artisan bread and a stunning snow crab salad with fiddleheads, candied leeks, basil, and a delicate buttermilk vinaigrette. for our main, we shared a plate of black cod with salsa, wilted swiss chard, and carrot beurre blanc — each bite was a celebration of flavour and texture. everything was light, fresh, and beautifully balanced. from beginning to end, our time at balnea was restorative, peaceful, and so deeply appreciated. if you're ever in the region and in need of true relaxation, i cannot recommend this oasis enough.

during our recent visit to rome, we had the incredible opportunity to explore the museo dell’ara pacis, home to the iconic ara pacis augustae (altar of augustan peace). this ancient monument, commissioned in 13 bc by the roman senate to celebrate emperor augustus’s return from his victories in gaul and spain, is a stunning representation of roman art, peace, and prosperity. the intricate reliefs on the altar not only depict mythological stories but also provide a unique glimpse into the historical events of the time, offering visitors a rare look at roman culture and power. the museum itself, designed by renowned architect richard meier, is a striking blend of modern and ancient elements. its glass walls allow natural light to pour in, casting beautiful reflections on the altar, creating an almost ethereal atmosphere that enhances the monument’s intricate details. we were particularly impressed by how the museum’s design preserves the altar while allowing visitors to engage with it in such an immersive way. for those interested in history, art, or architecture, we found that about an hour is sufficient to tour the museum and appreciate the displays. the informative plaques and video guides in multiple languages were helpful in enriching our understanding of the altar’s significance. the museum also offers a great educational experience with its exhibits that provide context about the augustan era and the peace ushered in by augustus’s reign. the museo dell’ara pacis is open daily from 9:30 am to 7:30 pm, with the last admission at 6:30 pm. admission is €14 for adults and €8.50 for concessions. if you’re planning to visit multiple museums in rome, the mic card provides free entry for 12 months for just €5, which we thought was a great deal. we were truly impressed by our visit and would highly recommend this museum to anyone visiting rome. it’s a must-see for history buffs and anyone interested in the legacy of ancient rome!

during our road trip in alaska, we were en route from anchorage to fairbanks, and denali state park was a must-visit spot along the way. denali, also known as mount mckinley, holds the distinction of being the highest mountain peak in north america. as we journeyed, the sight of this majestic mountain towering into the clouds from distant viewpoints along the road was truly stunning and breathtaking. the road was flanked by immense mountains and expansive forests stretching as far as the eye could see, creating one of the most beautiful views we have ever seen. it became evident why people are drawn to traveling in alaska, especially denali state park; its vastness and tranquility offer an unparalleled opportunity to immerse oneself in nature. with nothing to disturb us, we found peace in the serene environment of denali state park, surrounded only by mountains, roads, and occasionally encountering wildlife such as moose and bears.

during our vacation in santorini, the memory i will surely take with me as the most beautiful is our visit to the santorganics estate. strolling among the aromatic plants at sunset was a magical sight. dimitris and maria, the wonderful owners of this family business, gave us a lovely tour and explained the cultivation methods as well as the process of making their organic products. at the end of our walk, we also tasted sant organics products. the organic herb-infused olive oil stole our hearts. a bottle traveled back with us so we could share its unique flavor with our friends and family. dimitris and maria, thank you so much for this fantastic experience you offered us.

during our visit to banff last summer, we also took the opportunity to explore the fascinating cosmic ray station on the summit of sulphur mountain. this historic site, which dates back to the 1950s, is not only a unique piece of canadian history but also an interesting stop for anyone curious about science and the history of space exploration. the cosmic ray station, now part of the sulphur mountain summit experience, originally served as a research facility to study cosmic rays, high-energy particles that come from space. the station’s weathered building still stands as a testament to the groundbreaking research that took place there. it’s located right at the top of the mountain, offering stunning views of the surrounding area. the building itself is small but fascinating, and there are several informational signs that explain its purpose and the science behind the research that took place there. walking around the area, you can really appreciate the historical significance of the station while also soaking in the spectacular views that stretch for miles. the juxtaposition of the scientific history with the natural beauty of the surroundings creates a surreal experience. visiting the cosmic ray station was a highlight of our trip—it was a cool, educational detour while enjoying the great outdoors. if you find yourself on sulphur mountain, it’s definitely worth the short walk to this historic site. it's a perfect blend of history, science, and nature, all in one incredible location.

easily one of my favourite places to eat in vancouver and a one-restaurant-as-a-whole-ass-argumemt why eastvan is just better than westend/downtown. first of all, this place is simple and unassuming, even rustic. great staff here, glad they were able to squeeze us in on the patio this evening (usually dont have any trouble getting a table here but larger parties can be a bit challenging without a reservation here. the food was stupendous --- panzella was great as always (i miss the o.g. vs that had preserved watermelon and pumpkin seeds, but this evenings' was just as good and beautifully presented 🥗). the polpo/porkbelly appy is incredible -- thank you, asya (from keefer bar), for the reccomendation. we also did the carpaccio (incredible!), chicken daviola (consistantly amazing... the balance of heat and sweatness is sensational with the fingerling potatoes and roasted broccolini. my friend really enjoyed the gnocetti as well -- that was his and our servers favourite. i really enjoyed the arincini and the frito misto as well... the latter was beautifully battered with a great dipping sauce [we could have used a liiiitle biiiit moooore]. finally, their tiramisu is the best in the city. full stop. had to try the semifreddo and liked it as well... like an indulgent offspring of a ferrero roche and an ice cream snickers bar. great stuff ✨️✨️💯 also: notice how many 6/5 scores there are here... this could be my highest-rated-by-plate restaurant 🔥🔥🔥 ps: 2y ago you guys had a veal on polenta that was to die for... i would love to see that make a return to the fall menu 🤗🫡😋🥰

el castillo: the majestic guardian of tulum’s sacred coastline rising dramatically above the turquoise waters of the caribbean sea, el castillo is the most iconic and revered structure in the ancient maya city of tulum, mexico. this formidable temple, perched on the edge of a limestone cliff, has stood for centuries as a sentinel overlooking the coast, guarding the city and its inhabitants with its imposing presence. both a beacon for ancient mariners and a sacred site of worship, el castillo is steeped in history and legend, offering a profound connection to the spiritual and cultural world of the maya civilization. el castillo, which translates to "the castle," is not just the largest structure in tulum but also the most significant in terms of its religious, political, and navigational roles. built during the postclassic period of maya history, between the 13th and 15th centuries ad, el castillo served as both a temple dedicated to the gods and a lighthouse of sorts for the bustling port city of tulum. the temple's strategic location atop a 40-foot cliff provided a commanding view of the surrounding sea and land, making it an ideal spot for overseeing trade routes and detecting potential threats. the maya, who were skilled sailors and traders, used el castillo as a landmark to guide their canoes safely through the treacherous coral reefs that lie just offshore. at night, fires were lit at the temple, creating a beacon visible to ships approaching the coast—an ancient navigational aid that underscores the maya’s sophisticated understanding of maritime travel. architecturally, el castillo reflects the classic maya style, with a steep staircase leading to a small temple at the summit. the temple’s façade is adorned with carvings and niches that likely once held statues of deities, including the descending god—a mysterious figure often associated with the evening star (venus) or the setting sun. the orientation of el castillo also aligns with key astronomical events, such as the solstices, reinforcing the temple’s role as a sacred site for the observance of celestial phenomena and their influence on the agricultural and religious calendar. as with many ancient structures, el castillo is surrounded by a rich tapestry of legends that add to its mystique. one of the most enduring tales speaks of the guardian of the east wind, a powerful deity believed to inhabit the temple and protect tulum from hurricanes and other coastal storms. according to legend, the guardian would emerge from the temple during times of great peril, using his divine powers to calm the winds and seas, ensuring the safety of the city and its people. local lore also tells of a hidden treasure buried within the cliffs beneath el castillo. it is said that during the final days of tulum, as the spanish conquistadors advanced through the yucatán peninsula, the city’s rulers gathered their most precious treasures—gold, jade, and sacred artifacts—and concealed them in a secret chamber deep within the rock. the entrance to this chamber was sealed with a curse, intended to protect the treasure from being discovered by the invaders. over the centuries, many have searched for this legendary cache, but the treasure—and the curse—remain undiscovered. another legend associated with el castillo is that of the white lady of tulum, a ghostly figure who is said to appear at the temple on moonlit nights. according to the story, the white lady was a priestess who served at el castillo during its heyday. she was known for her beauty and devotion to the gods, but she tragically fell in love with a warrior from a rival city. forbidden from being with him, she took her own life, and her spirit has since haunted the temple, eternally mourning her lost love. visitors to tulum occasionally report sightings of a pale figure near el castillo, adding an eerie yet romantic aura to the site.

el-tahrir square, a pivotal location in egypt's history, stands as a testament to the resilience of its people. this vibrant public space is surrounded by remarkable landmarks such as the towering ramses ii obelisk and the historical carlton hotel. the square has been a symbol of revolution, representing the dreams and aspirations for change among egyptians. as traffic flows through this bustling area, it serves as a crossroads between past and present, where ancient history meets modern life. el-tahrir continues to be a gathering point for both locals and tourists eager to explore its rich heritage and significance in shaping egyptian identity. whether viewing the stunning architecture or reflecting on its role in pivotal moments, el-tahrir square remains an emblem of hope and unity in egyptian society.

electric bus to kuranda • return kuranda scenic train. a very enjoyable trip up to kuranda, our driver/guide, jeff, was very informative and entertaining. had a great time at the rainforestation but found kuranda itself to be a bit of a tourist trap. the scenic railway on the way back was made even more enjoyable due to the refreshments (alcoholic) included in the gold upgrade.

elegant & refined old school grand cafe. we booked here for lunch after our historical walking tour and it was the perfect spot to relax & absorb all the amazing history we’d just learnt. firstly the indoor seating area is just beautiful and so elegant and stylish. secondly the service was excellent- super friendly and welcoming. thirdly, the food was superb- they have a wonderful all-day menu. very traditional austrian food. the sausage plate was utterly delicious, as was the potato salad. the grand finale was the cakes - wow, the glass cake cabinet is lined with one beautiful cake after another. and perfectly paired on a hot summers day with an ice coffee. perfection. make sure you book in advance. highly recommended.

elephant care nai dee offers a truly ethical and heartwarming elephant experience, focused on rescue and rehabilitation without rides or cruelty. the staff are funny. friendly and knowledgeable, and the elephants are clearly well cared for and respected. from feeding to bathing them in the river, every activity felt natural and meaningful. a must-visit for anyone who wants to support responsible tourism and see elephants treated with the love they deserve.

elephant haven is a wonderful organization to rescue baby elephants and reintroduce them into the wild. by supporting them financially, you can stay there and interact with the baby elephants up and personally. the staff is fantastic and the chef cooks wonderful meals! the elephants are so friendly and loving. i learned so much about elephants!! definitely worth the investment; if you’re an animal lover!!!

elias is a legit komodo, manta, turtle, and shark whisperer! no other explanation. please give him a raise! we saw 3 komodos, giant turtle, shark, and mantas too many too count!! we even saw mantas swimming at the surface from the top of padar island. he also takes great pictures and gives you tips on the best photo spots! there were few hiccups like we did not leave on time but i understand herding cats is not easy and they are at the mercy of clients' punctuality. also you really have to be a solid swimmer at the manta point. the crew did their best with a leader in the front and another guide at the back but with current and hundreds other swimmers from other boats it can get confusing quick. yes, the boat will move ! take your time to orient yourself to where it's at so you don't swim away too far. the bigger the visitors the harder it gets. there were only 28 of us and about half stayed on the boat thankfully. i was very fortunate to stay close to elias who navigated us to an out of this world experience of being "ambushed" by giant majestic mantas. that alone is worth the ticket fee. we had good lunch at komodo a delicious servings of biscuits and nescafe after the last snorkeling point. a concern i have is the lack of signage on proper etiquette. the crew explained it in english in the begiingbut i still saw east asia tourists taking pieces of corals for souvenirs, stepping on them, touching the wild life etc etc. also i don't know what's the impact of being disturbed by hundreds of snorkelers daily, but perhaps some focus on sustainment can be put in place. the return trip to drop us back in hotels got a bit hectic too. but honestly, i was in such dopamine high i was absolutely happy and grateful for the experience. i'd say it easily beats my diving trips in the maldives! 10/10, i will be back with friends and colleagues
elite experience with lovely vibes.. everything is just perfect.. but with royalty comes a high price..

ella is truly one of the most beautiful and peaceful destinations in sri lanka! surrounded by lush green mountains, tea plantations, and breathtaking waterfalls, this little town feels like a paradise. the atmosphere is so relaxing, with cool weather. there are plenty of things to explore – from the iconic nine arch bridge and little adam’s peak to the scenic train rides that give unforgettable views. the cafes and restaurants in ella are cozy and full of charm, offering both local and international flavors. whether you’re looking for adventure, nature, or just a peaceful escape, ella is the perfect place. highly recommended for anyone visiting sri lanka! 💚

ella rock is one of my go-to adventures whenever i'm in the area. what i love about it is the peacefulness — far fewer tourists than at more popular spots. the hike itself is a real challenge, tougher and longer than the climb to little adam’s peak, but so worth it. there's a small entrance fee of 1000 rupees. along the way, i missed the cheerful old lady who used to sell that unforgettable salty lemonade. be prepared: prices at the few stalls are a bit higher, but if you forget to bring water, you'll be thankful they're there. and the view from the top? absolutely breathtaking — endless hills rolling into the mist, pure freedom. it’s the kind of view that makes every drop of sweat worth it.

ellen was my pilot on this experience and it was great! this was something i will certainly never forget! she was so friendly and walked me through everything i was scared about. the views were absolutely stunning and cannot be beat. i highly recommend this experience if you’re in the area!

ellinjaa falls is part of what’s known as the waterfall circuit and next to milla milla falls is one of the most scenic falls. also a great place to have a swim and enjoy what the tablelands are all about in this beautiful part of the tropics, the water is quite cold but great on a hot day. the short walk thru the rainforest is well maintained with some steps and a bitumen path. not recommended for wheelchairs in my opinion.

elsie's peak. an easy walk up for young and old. first time for me, but what breathtaking views once you're at the top! it can be used for trail running as well as it's quite a quick walk as well. always hike in groups, never alone for safety purposes.

emilie at galápagos bike & surf helped us in every way during our stay in isabela. we contacted her the night before our arrival and she quickly arranged tours to tintoreras and los tuneles. both were great prices. los tuneles was on the best boat with a great guide. all during our stay any questions we had she was quick to respond and advise. when we arrived at the airport emilie just happened to be there and gave us a ride to our airbnb. when we left isabela she arranged our speed boat ferry to santa cruz. thank you emilie for making our trip to isabela so easy, so enjoyable and so memorable!

emilie is amazing! she is very situationally aware she notices and sees everything! i was struggling with my mask as i was adjusting it she had turned to check on me in that same moment and assisted me it’s like she had a sixth sense. she is very informative about her plans for whatever you have booked. i booked a private dive tour and it was fantastic seen sooooo much! she definitely knows her stuff about the ocean. if you’re looking for a peaceful guide she is the one! she pointed out everything she saw to make sure i seen it to! seen my first shark i was so excited! definitely book with emilie!

emilio and axel were fantastic! they were incredibly helpful, especially for those who don’t know how to swim — patient, supportive, and very informative. the ceviche was delicious, and we loved being able to play our own music. overall, i highly recommend taking the tour with them!

emmanuel was fantastic. he taught me how the kite power transfers through the opposite hip and shoulder (to the riding direction) allowing me to make some big improvements in both getting up and then getting the power to ride upwind. stoked to come back.

emnoronha made our trip so memorable! this was my first time going to fernando de noronha and had no idea what to expect or what to do. the team did an amazing job at giving us recommendations on what to do, as well as booking excursions for us. all of the tour guides were wonderful and this was the best trip i’ve taken, due in part to emnoronha! if you’re thinking of booking with them i highly recommend it! can’t wait to go back!

emst athens is a cultural breath of fresh air, sleek, modern, and thoughtfully curated. the exhibitions balance bold contemporary voices with global perspectives, creating an inspiring space that sparks thought and conversation. a must-visit for art lovers and curious minds alike. athens isn’t just ancient history anymore! i love the acropolis views from the cafe on the 4th level and the fact that the ticket is reusable for a second visit within a month!

enchanting place! wonderful lava tunnel complete with a knowledgeable guide. the tunnel has separate entrance and exit points with built in lighting and safety railings. the walk back to the ranch is filled with great views of nearby islands and giant tortoises roaming free. they served a delicious lunch and even have a very unique ‘boat house’ for overnight guests. this place is a true hidden gem.

encounting the king of the animals world was truly a highlight of the botswana safari. incredible beautiful seeing them still freely roaming around. we stayed at tawana, natural selection, an unique unforgettable experience. we want to be back for more.

end of season fishing was below average but i had an amazing experience. julian was fantastic - and i mean fantastic - as a teacher for two first time fly fishermen. he was infinitely patient with two complete beginners. after getting the hang of casting, my friend and i landed seven trout on the small side, which makes sense given the spooky nature of the trophy sized ones. it was lovely watching the kingfishers out fish us. also, the lunch was amazing and very filling. wear sunblock, a gaiter, and bring a hat. definitely book at least 2 days in case one day is slow. i’d love to be back in the future, hopefully with more experience under my belt and better casting distance!

ended up here by chance looking for a beach and went back 3 more times. the food is a simple but delightful menu with loads of flavor. the drinks are done well with lots of thought and pizazz, the cappuccino tastes like the beans were roasted this morning. and the staff, feels like family. they truly go out of their way to make you feel at home. special shout out to my new bff iva! she was truly a delight but honestly the whole bar staff are amazing and friendly!!
ended up here following the royal gardens. nice layout, more on the forest type of appeal. preferred the royal gardens which are right next to this.

endless blue was our boat and has the most amazing crew! from the beginning of the tour, they were very attentive and caring for everyone on board. the food was delicious, and we had plenty of time to swim at the scheduled stops. i highly recommend the tour to anyone looking for a unique experience in santorini! it was by far the best experience on this beautiful island! thank you very much, guys!!!

english speakers, don't let the few number of reviews on google detract you from gliding with asa rio brasil hang glider. absolutely recommended 🙌once you get to the launch pad and see how professional they are with safety checks and super friendly staff, you will be glad you booked with them! the flight was epic! stunning views and worth every real! do it!

enjoy a deep drive into the history of the west india docks, located in an actual warehouse. very interesting details from the 1500s onwards, from slave ships to the sugar trade; from wwii to the present face of canary wharf. equally informative for kids & adults. and it's free!

enjoy a leisurely evening stroll before sunset and witness the breathtaking spectacle of stars falling over the horizon. visit in august to be captivated by the thousands of kites dancing in the sky. afterward, explore the area beneath the wall, where you'll find a delightful array of restaurants, souvenir shops, and pubs to enjoy a drink. ;)
