enjoy florida’s river of grass. wildlife ranges from anhingas, to turtles, and plenty of gators. great for birdwatching. make sure to have protective clothing or long sleeves if you are sensitive to the sun or mosquitoes. plenty of informational posts for self guided tours.

enjoy kili gifted us with such a wonderful and seamless experience! at no point on the trip did we ever have to be concerned with where we were headed or how we were going to reach our destination. david covered all of that for us and worked with pounds east africa (another awesome safari contact in kenya) to make sure we were always taken care of. david even got us enjoy kili shirts, which came in really handy since we might have under-packed for our trip to tanzania. the accommodations were splendid - we stayed in a lovely little hotel before and after the safari, and the team (thanks david!) even bumped up our room tier during the safari stay from the tent we chose to an amazingly comfortable room! we are so, so grateful for this. it was actually such a blessing because we visited during the 'long rain' season and while it never rained in the day, the nights were incredibly stormy. this meant we had really comfortable sleep and were ready for the safaris each morning. additionally, the lodge we were at even had a fantastic performance on the first night with dancing and exciting acrobatic presentations. it was like the movie bring it on but even better. the food at our lodge was simply amazing. they provided lunch (our guide would be given big containers of a mix of local dishes, which we scooped from to individual plates that would be washed by the lodge staff later - really helps with saving the earth, i loved it!), as well as dinner and it was honestly all divine food. our guide stanley was the best! he's a responsible, knowledgeable, reliable and kind guy who's so open to learning about different cultures and teaching us more about his. it was great fun listening to him tell us about all the animals and flora and fauna we spotted. who knew warthogs prefer to reverse into their burrows over going in head-first? i didn't! but i do know now thanks to stanley haha. we could ask him about literally anything and he was happy to share more. the safari itinerary we were given was also great - we got to see such diverse, beautiful environments and consequently saw so many different animals. overall, enjoy kili was great. definitely recommend their service, and everyone we came into contact with was wonderful. thank you david and stanley!

enjoyed visiting this museum and was captivated by its well-curated and modern exhibits. there was a strong incorporation of local industries, presented through easy-to-understand and interactive activities. the setup felt cozy and was easy to navigate. the science lab, where visitors could don lab coats and conduct experiments, was a particularly engaging feature. i visited on a public holiday, and the crowd control was well managed. be sure to drop by the gift shop for some interesting toys or kits to bring home.

entertaining visit for anyone interested in animation but it’s especially focused on children. adults will appreciate it as well. the building itself is playful and contributes to the overall feel of the visit. the artwork is simply stunning. it was also impressive to see the resources they used to design the movies. they had books about the anatomy of animals to architecture. it all helps to give the films character and life. be warned, it’s not easy to get tickets. they have a screwy sign-up system where you have to be online at a certain time on the 10th of the month preceding your hoped for visit. i was in a queue for 45 minutes and was able to get something on one of the days i was scheduled to be in tokyo. i didn’t get the time i wanted so i scheduled everything around the time i got. the 10 am slots went very quickly and we got 4 pm entry. we were told to bring our passports for id but all we needed was the qr code on our ticket. they don’t allow photos inside, only outside. absolutely worth seeing if you care at all about the subject.

entrance fees 800yens on 3rd floor for the day (if not going out) - table tennis on 8th floor - shower room etc .., badminton on the next room (separated). crowded from pm7:30~pm9:00, usually there is a lottery to get 1 table ... that means even you pay entrance fee 800y, you are not sure at all to play ! lottery is renewed every 1h. so you might just wait 1h the next lottery, and maybe never play if you loose every time to get a table. when there are more people than tables, a lottery determine who can play for 1 hour. but this lottery is quite not appropriate : for example, unfair players come at 3 (5) people, they get 2(3) tables at lottery (because 5 players participate to lottery) but eventually 1 table is occupied by only 1 person, rather than 2 players (as impair umber of player). so if you are coming with a partner (2 person), and send 1 person to lottery and he/she fails in lottery, you can just watch 1 table occupied by a lucky lottery player, who is just not playing because he is just alone ! so be aware that this place is crowded in the evening, and rules are not so fair sometimes. if you come in day time, i think there are more tables than players, so there is no lottery. be careful in the evening time. better consider another place with eventually some possible reservations.

entrance is free, and it leads straight into the old town and city center of dubrovnik. this is also one of the main gates where you can start walking the city walls. although it’s very touristic with lots of souvenir shops, stepping through feels like entering a medieval city that still holds its historic charm.

entrance to the trail is through jose do canto gardens (4€ per person). should take 1h to go and come back but the gardens are huge so spent a couple of hours in there. you might be lucky and find the church open too. the end of the trail by the waterfall looks dangerous and unsafe with lot of fallen trees and rocks

entry comes with the dubrovnik pass, and there is a lot on display. this is not the most plush palace we have seen, but the content is very well presented and informative. also, it can take a bit of time to go around if you read everything. the most interesting section i found was near the end, photographs of dubrovnik during the war. they are displayed in a tunnel (like a bomb shelter) and capture the level of destruction that was inflicted. also, these pictures bring added realism, considering that war is still evident in the world today. the palace is worth a visit.

entry is affordable, and the area is well-maintained considering how popular it is. i appreciated the local touches, from the traditional balinese architecture to the offerings placed near the pathways. there are plenty of shops along the entrance path, selling everything from souvenirs to local snacks. it can feel a bit touristy, but it’s easy to see past that once you reach the coastline. we tried some local food near the temple, and i was pleasantly surprised. the satay was fresh and nicely grilled—very flavorful. however, i didn’t enjoy the peanut sauce as much; i personally prefer the richer, slightly sweeter malaysian-style version. the banana fritters were okay—crispy on the outside, soft inside, but nothing particularly special. what really makes tanah lot worth visiting is the overall experience: the scenery, the cultural significance, and the peaceful energy of the place. it’s popular, yes, and can get crowded, especially during sunset—but with a little patience and the right timing, you’ll find moments of serenity and awe. highly recommend it for anyone visiting bali. just be sure to bring your camera, wear comfortable shoes, and maybe arrive a bit earlier than sunset to beat the crowds and soak in the full beauty of the place.

entry process was quick and easy, locker room and showers were clean and the pools were amazing. did the 3 mud masks and an in water massage which was so amazing i highly recommend it. it was busy but it was big enough we never felt crowded and if you want total peace just go to the phone free zone and no one will be there ha!

entry ticket :yes restaurant: inside yes night stay : yes heaven on earth : yes :) parking : yes don’t miss this spot if you are in bali and on the way to ulun danu beratan temple. it’s a tropical garden plus a flower nursery. this place is an instagrammable place and a hidden gem on the hills on the way to the bedung area. visited as a couple and i never seen such place and won’t compare it with australia botanic gardens but it’s gives me fantastic vibes while drizzling from the top. plenty things to do here and i might stay here a night but didn’t plan in advance. will visit next time with kids. ⛱️

established in 1988, san francisco maritime national historical park celebrates america’s maritime heritage on the pacific coast. the 50-acre park has grown around aquatic park cove, a protected area in the san francisco bay. the park showcases the city’s seafaring past. the park includes a fleet of historic vessels, a visitor center, a maritime museum, and a library/research facility. formerly referred to as the san francisco maritime museum, the collections were acquired by the national park service in 1978. the historic fleet of the san francisco maritime national historical park is moored at the park's hyde street pier. the fleet consists of the following major vessels: balclutha, an 1886 built square rigged sailing ship. c.a. thayer, an 1895 built schooner. eureka, an 1890 built steam ferryboat. alma, an 1891 built scow schooner. hercules, a 1907 built steam tug. eppleton hall, a 1914 built paddlewheel tug. the visitor center is housed in the park's 1909 waterfront warehouse, located at the corner of hyde and jefferson streets. the city of san francisco declared the four-story brick structure a historic landmark in 1974.

este monumento ao general osório, herói da guerra da tríplice aliança (guerra do paraguai), o primeiro monumento da república, foi construído em 12 nov 1894 pelo renomado escultor rodolfo bernardelli, sendo usado o bronze de um canhão tomado na guerra do paraguai. em suas laterias possui dois médios relevos representado dois episódios desta guerra: a batalha do tuiuti e passos da pátria. este monumento serviu também como mausoléu por 100 anos até o seu corpo ser transferido para a cidade de osório (rs). outro fato interessante é que osório era tão querido que esta estátua foi construída com dinheiro de doações da população carioca. quem passava pela praça xv a uns 5 anos atrás ainda podia ver cinco bolas originais da guerra em cada coluna e um gradil de ferro ornamentado cercando todo o monumento. no ano de 2014 todas as bolas de canhão foram roubadas de madrugada e também todas as grandes ornamentais que cercavam o monumento e assim mais uma vez nossa história vai se apagando...

etosha national park in namibia is one of the best places to experience wildlife up close. the park is huge and has open grasslands, salt pans, and waterholes where animals gather, especially during the dry season. the highlight is the etosha pan, a vast white salt flat that shines under the sun and turns into a shallow lake after rains, attracting flamingos and other birds. the park is home to elephants, lions, rhinos, giraffes, and many types of antelopes. watching animals at the waterholes is easy and exciting since many come to drink water throughout the day. the roads are good for self-drive safaris, and there are well-maintained camps with basic to comfortable facilities like lodges, shops, and restaurants. the sunsets in etosha are beautiful, with golden light spreading over the savannah. the peacefulness of the wild and the sound of animals make it a memorable place.

exceptional resort/staff/experience and all very accessible .... difficult to know where to start writing this review as i can honestly say i have never felt more spoilt and more welcome in a location as a result can sometimes find it difficult to fully relax.. moreover, although i attained my open water diving qualification 20 years ago and absolutely loved diving, i have always shied away from the sport due to me thinking i wouldn't be able to fully participate post accident ... sorido bay and all the staff there very quickly corrected that assumption... everything in the resort was completely accessible and even if it wasn't, they were always on hand to assist, be that helping get on and off boats, putting together the kit, or even simple things like ensuring we had a table near the coffee station and bar... on to the actual resort: complete paradise!!!... the pictures you will see online are incredibly accurate ... the villas are very spacious, very clean and you walk out from your "balcony" area on to the beach and the water.... you will go home with all your clothes clean as they provide daily laundry service as part of the package.. can't begin to explain how magical the diving is and if you are a complete beginner, the dive instructors can guide you through your experience or even your open water qualification should you wish (have to mention how incredible our instructor oscar was with my kids and managed to get them both qualified within 4 days which is a feat beyond any expectation).... the boat crews were all fantastic and what is really incredible is the "family" feel every evening where you all share stories of the day and they even put on a live music session for the last night... for those who need to catch up on emails while away, the wifi is very reliable... lastly, although i loved the diving... one of my lasting experiences was the final day of snorkelling around the resort where we swam with black fin sharks, leopard sharks, and a very friendly turtle.... i can 100% guarantee, if you visit sorido bay, you will not want to leave.

fairy falls stands as one of yellowstone’s hidden treasures, tucked away at the end of a challenging forest trail that tests visitors’ determination. the waterfall’s striking beauty stems from a fascinating geological story written in volcanic rock and shaped by countless years of water’s patient work. the falls cascade over a sheer cliff carved from ancient rhyolite lava flows - dense, silica-heavy rock that hardened during volcanic eruptions long ago. these tough volcanic layers formed protective caps over weaker rock beneath. when fairy creek began cutting its path through the plateau, it carved through these different rock types at varying speeds. the softer underlying layers wore away much faster than the resistant rhyolite above, creating the undercut cliff face that allows water to plunge straight down. generations of flowing water have continued sculpting the landscape, hollowing out the pool at the waterfall’s base and making the cliff even steeper. the massive 1988 fires actually played a role too, burning away vegetation on the slopes above and speeding up erosion that feeds into the dramatic contrast between the narrow ribbon of water and its rocky amphitheater. the 1.6-mile hiking trail winds through recovering lodgepole pine forests toward the falls, which drop roughly 200 feet into their carved basin. the entire canyon reflects the broader story of how post-ice age flooding and steady stream erosion have sliced through the yellowstone plateau’s volcanic layers, revealing the different hardness of rock strata beneath. fairy falls perfectly demonstrates this ongoing geological dance - where fractured volcanic bedrock stands firm against erosion while the weathered, softer layers underneath gradually wash away, leaving behind this elegant waterfall that tells the tale of both yellowstone’s fiery volcanic past and water’s relentless sculptural power.

fantastic experience! my partner and i did the ‘sea experience’ which comprises swimming with dolphins, packed lunch and whale watching . it was €210 each. we parked in the underground parking just opposite the office and it was €10 for the day. the check in was easy and smooth, we went out on a speed boat for both activities and the drivers were great doing some big spins after the animal watching was over. the guides were very knowledgeable and respectful of the animals. they were friendly and answered all our questions. we saw two species of dolphin (bottle nose and grey spotted atlantic). we also saw a huge sperm whale and sei whale. we got very lucky and it was amazing to see these animals. the vegetarian lunch was an egg omelette baguette with salad, crisps, a pear, juice carton and water. my partner has food allergies and this was catered for. for the swimming with dolphins we swam three times and saw dolphins 2/3 times. the first time we saw at least 100 dolphins swimming below us. amazing experience, not quite what i’d expected but still incredible. you slide off the side of the boat into the centre of the dolphin pod but as soon as you dunk in they dove down into the depths and out of view so it is a fleeting but still amazing experience. i would highly recommend this company.

fantastic experience! such a warm and welcoming crew that made the experience fun and relaxed. we knew it was going to be a great time when we saw a whale in the distance and captain sundance immediately turned the boat for us to see it! our whole family enjoyed the experience—they had every kind of floatation device available for everyone’s comfort level, even had a floating raft to hang on to in case you didn’t want to swim openly in the water. we saw so many fish and turtles! the crew was very attentive, keeping us all together and making sure we didn’t get too far from the boat or too close to the turtles. they were great about pointing out where the turtles were so we wouldn’t miss them! also, holly and emily’s knowledge of sea life was great and we learned a lot and gained even more respect for the wildlife. mahalo, honolulu snorkel company! we’ll be back again!
fantastic experience! was able to fly for a long time. everybody was professional and very nice! sunset experience was extra special!

fantastic experience! we contacted andy who after understanding what we were looking for in a rafting trip gave us excellent guidance for two sixty-year-olds and three twenty somethings. the outfitter we chose was beyond expectations: food was really good and freshly made (no scout freezed dried meals here), guides were skilled at their craft guiding us down the river, taking us on side hikes and explaining how we could swim the rapids. they shared insights into the canyon geology and entertained us with stories from grand canyon lore. our guide, jake, sat up one night, pointed out the various constellations and share a plethora of information about the skies with us. shout out to jake, jeff and joe from tour west! we were all trepedatious about the food, endurance, weather and (*cough, cough*) restroom facilities. absolutely no need to worry. they know what they are doing so don't let that stop you!

fantastic experience, once in a life time! swimming with the dolphins, snorkelling in the coral gardens, great boat ride. we did this trip with with our children (4 and 8) and my parents (70+ yrs) and this was thoroughly enjoyed by all. very comfortable, clean boat and comes with all the kit you need (masks/snorkels/flippers). a major highlight on our mauritian family holiday. special mention on our captain (sorry not sure of the spelling), felt safe and happy the entire trip. also thank you to aleyna, for getting this trip sorted out and lined up for us, appreciate the personal manor in which you engaged with us as if you were sorting this for your own family. thank you.
fantastic experience, our guide subhani was superb catering to our every need. the quad biking, camel riding and sand boarding was exceptional. would highly recommend!

fantastic experience, would highly recommend 👌 my 10 year old son absolutely loved it and so did we. extremely well thought out and unique activity. the ninja guide made it fun and highly entertaining throughout, he really made a big effort to make sure we all enjoyed ourselves. highlights were definitely the ninja star throwing and samurai sword use! nice photos opportunities, well done guys. great way to spend around 45mins - 1 hour of ninja fun.

fantastic experience. i highly recommend coming out to give it a try if you are visiting zanzibar. they had great transport service for getting us to and from our hotel. they offered phone protectors to allow you to take photos under the water which were great!

fantastic experience. ivan was a brilliant host who was very accommodating. the perfect place to rest after doing the salkantay trek and machu picchu. if you are staying one night only and want to go to one of the bigger islands (eg taquile) you will need to get there early on the first day and arrange in advance. make sure to ask about all the activity options available to you when you arrive. due to bus times we weren't able to do that. we nevertheless were able to explore the floating islands around us with ivan (including seeing a tortora reed museum) and do some kayaking. the food was delicious and the beds were the most comfortable in peru by far. highly recommended!

fantastic experience. wonderfully informative, amazing surroundings, friendly and very knowledgeable team. a privilege to stand in the rainforest, learn the gibbons' history, listening to the them sing and watching them swing and climb around their enclosures. this experience is about education and rehabilitation so don't go expecting to get close or to handle the gibbons. you will help prepare their food and if you're lucky you'll feed them using a basket attached to a rope and pully. there's a carpark, cafe and toilets very close by. i suggest taking the early tour as the waterfalls were empty of people when we arrived but by the time we left every pool and path was busy with families bathing and picnicking.

fantastic first kayak with manly kayak centre! my first kayaking experience with manly kayak centre was fantastic! the instructor was incredibly helpful and patient, making me feel comfortable and confident from the start. the centre was well-equipped, and the briefing was thorough. paddling along the beautiful beaches around manly was a truly special experience, offering stunning views. thanks to the excellent guidance, i thoroughly enjoyed exploring the coastline from a new perspective. highly recommend manly kayak adventures for beginners and anyone wanting to enjoy manly's beautiful waters!

fantastic hike for a breathtaking view of rio de janeiro. aim to arrive early, at 8am, to get a quick parking space in the lot next to the entrance. the trail is beautiful and full of vegetation and animals. tip: there's no shadow in the top! bring water and sun protection.

fantastic hike with waterfalls! we hiked about 5 miles and were rewarded with beautiful views of the madeira countryside. there are some really narrow points with no guard rails or ropes as you walk along the trail. not for those who suffer from vertigo.

fantastic hike, advice to wear appropriate hiking shoes and gear. we saw so many struggling with flip flops and not even a water bottle. we were lucky with parking, get there early or there won’t be parking.

fantastic hike, long (parking to top) and steep. possible in one day if you are in good shape. under 7,5h is possible (almost jogging). don't forget 50 nok in cash to pay the parking, or use vipps if you are norsk.

fantastic hotel! beautiful property with a very detail oriented and caring staff. the food was great and the setting is gorgeous. if they would just heat the hot-tub up a little this place would be perfect, but even without the hot tub, you can’t really ask for more than the tierra provides.

fantastic intro to cairns — highly recommend! this tour is a great way to get your bearings if you’ve just arrived in cairns. chris, our main guide, was incredibly knowledgeable and kept the stories and history coming the whole time — we learned so much and really enjoyed his energy. he even pulled over at one point so we could see wallabies up close, which was such a nice touch. james, our guide at the museum, was also excellent. i’m still impressed by how much he was able to share in just 30 minutes — it was super engaging and packed with fascinating info. the only part i’d tweak is the 20-minute drive through the area affected by the floods — that time could’ve been better spent with james at the museum or enjoying more time at palm cove beach. and don’t even get me started on the scones — absolutely incredible! definitely try the ginger beer too if you haven’t already. all in all, a really enjoyable and well-run tour.

fantastic little gem of a camp right next to the talek gate. the camp and rooms were a lot nicer than we were expecting. i think they are constantly improving and upgrading. tents: we stayed in the most basic tent type and it was great. we booked two tents and each had a double and single bed. the beds were comfy and had lovely clean, cosy bedding. the bathroom was basic but did the job, lovely products provided. drinking water in the rooms and for brushing teeth, it was replenished every day. strong wifi in rooms. food: we had the packed breakfast both days and it was perfect. our driver dennis found great spots to set up the breakfast buffet. we had lunch packed one day and back in camp another. again lovely, and we appreciated the break midday. the dinner was limited but everything was very tasty. there was always a nice soup followed by curry, rice, and veg, and then a cake for dessert. there was always tea and coffee available. safari: we used dennis, booked via the camp. he was amazing. he could spot things miles away and we saw everything except a rhino. he was also great company and very fun. i think we paid $260 per day for the whole day. we started at 6am and on the first day we were shattered and came back to camp around 4.30, the second day we decided to have a break back at camp for lunch and then had an afternoon/sunset drive. that worked well. getting there: we booked a driver, francis, via the camp. we were collected from navaisha and returned to nairobi. it cost around $450 for 4 of us, so a lot cheaper than flying and didn’t take that much more time overall. the camp is small and there isn’t much to do other than safari so with two teens in tow we were worried about getting bored. but as we were out on safari most of the time it was fine. we had early-ish evenings so didn’t really have any time to fill. everyone seemed to return to their tents straight after eating so we felt a bit in the way staying in the bar, like we were keeping the staff up. special mention to dalmaz who is a joy. he brightened every meal time and was always popping up with his big smile. all the staff were so friendly and kind, we felt very safe there. on our last evening we were lucky enough to see all the staff do a traditional masai performance. they pulled my son up to join in and he was thrilled, said it was the best time of his life! we stayed in july and the weather was perfect. cool night and low/mid 20s during the day. we were a bit cold on the first morning so asked to borrow blankets on the second morning which really helped. would be a nice touch if these were provided to use in the safari trucks. perhaps they are during colder weather. bring cosy clothes for the mornings and change into shorts for the afternoon.

fantastic location, the view of the mara is breathtaking. the journey to and from the car park is a bit of an experience in itself, but worth the journey. the staff are super friendly. the "tent"s are just amazing with each one set amongst the trees. can get a bit noisy with all the monkeys around, but the tents are secure, and there's plenty of staff around to scare them away.
fantastic market and so cheap. really enjoyed roaming around and shopping here. lots of s.x toy shops too for those into that kind of items. atmosphere is fun.

fantastically vibrant night market with an unbelievable amount of stalls selling anything you can think of. the food options are delicious and cheap, and the whole area is clean and tidy. great place to visit for a real taste of the bangkok craziness.

fantástico we did 2tours the sulfur mines & tintoreras… both stupendous!!! pablo & gonzalo were wonderful, in the sulfur mines tours, it was fascinating & got to also see the cave of sucre, with an amazing delicious lunch. where they showed us different tropical fruits in their own backyard. absolutely amazing! also saw horses & cows on the road, along with flamingos too!! the same in the tintoreras tour, tito & his crew were so great as well! they were so informative, patient, extremely knowledgeable! we were able to see starfish, sea horses, blue boobies, white tip sharks, turtles, etc…. so much in this tour! highly recommend both tours with this agency so reliable & affordable! so very happy thank you!!!

favorite hike in sedona! but beware: it is not an easy one. it is long and much more of a climb than a hike. wear the right shoes -- don't necessarily need hiking-specific ones -- that have enough traction. some scrambling and steep steps along the way. bring enough water and a snack. there are points along the way where you can sit and relax. be sure to follow the white diamond marks to ensure you're on the path! for those who are in good shape, this is probably a moderate hike. for those who aren't in the best shape or are new to hiking, it's hard. it's the length that can make it challenging more than the climb, but if you have any doubt, doe mountain just across the road may be the better option. if you're up for the 4-5 hour round-trip trek, the top is so rewarding!!

filipino review 🇵🇭⛩️ batuan temple – a beautiful balinese heritage site batuan temple is a well-preserved, traditional balinese temple that showcases stunning architecture and intricate stone carvings 🏛️✨. it’s less crowded than other famous temples, making it a peaceful spot to explore and appreciate bali’s culture. visitors are required to wear a sarong, which is provided at the entrance. the temple is well-maintained, and the details on the gates and shrines are impressive. unlike some other touristy temples, there’s no pushy selling, making the experience more relaxed. a small donation is required upon entry 💰, but it’s affordable. there’s not much walking involved, making it an easy visit for all ages. overall, batuan temple is a great place to experience bali’s spiritual and artistic heritage without the heavy crowds. a quick but worthwhile stop!

floating down xochimilco's canals on a trajinera was an absolute dream! the vibrant colors of the boats, the lively mariachi music drifting across the water, and the scent of fresh flowers in the air created an intoxicating atmosphere. i loved watching the vendors paddle by, offering everything from tacos to textiles, and even bought a beautiful woven blanket as a souvenir. the calm rhythm of the water was incredibly relaxing, and i spent most of the ride just soaking it all in, chatting with friends, and enjoying the unique cultural experience. it felt like stepping back in time, a delightful escape from the hustle and bustle of mexico city. the lush greenery along the banks and the occasional glimpse of a small island garden added to the picturesque charm. every moment was a pure joy, a truly unforgettable mexican adventure!

floating markets in thailand are a vibrant and immersive glimpse into the country’s traditional way of life. these markets, where vendors sell goods directly from boats on rivers and canals, are not only a means of trade but also a cultural attraction that draws both locals and tourists. among the most famous is the damnoen saduak floating market in ratchaburi, known for its colorful boats piled high with tropical fruits, vegetables, and local snacks. while it offers the quintessential floating market experience perfect for photography and first-time visitors, it can feel overly commercialized and crowded, especially later in the day. another popular destination is amphawa floating market in samut songkhram, which stands out for its late afternoon and evening operations. it’s especially well known for freshly grilled seafood and relaxed boat rides that offer a chance to see fireflies after sunset. amphawa tends to attract more locals, making the experience feel more authentic, particularly on weekdays. for those who prefer to stay within bangkok, the taling chan floating market offers a more intimate and less touristy experience. though smaller in scale, it features delicious food, including seafood and traditional desserts, and often hosts live thai music to enhance the local ambiance. overall, thailand’s floating markets are a delightful blend of culture, cuisine, and community. they are best visited early in the day or during off-peak hours for a more relaxed atmosphere. each market has its unique appeal, and visiting one (or more) offers a memorable insight into thai life along the waterways.

for fresh, organic food in miami, the coconut grove farmers market is the place to be. i hadn’t been in a few years, but stepping back into this vibrant marketplace felt like coming home. the energy is still incredible, filled with friendly vendors, fresh local produce, and a community-focused atmosphere that makes it one of the best outdoor markets in miami. one of my favorite finds? the lasagna lady, serving up mouthwatering vegan and vegetarian lasagnas packed with flavor. whether you’re plant-based or just love good food, this is a must-try! i also stopped by modern ancient perfumes, where i discovered beautifully crafted natural perfume oils—perfect for those who appreciate non-toxic, holistic fragrances. and of course, the fresh fruit stand was overflowing with tropical delights like ripe mangoes, papayas, and coconuts, making it a true taste of south florida. beyond the food and shopping, this market is a haven for those looking for all-natural beauty products, organic produce in miami, and handmade goods from local artisans. while parking has changed due to the new apartment building next door, it’s still absolutely worth the visit. if you’re looking for a miami farmers market with vegan food, holistic products, and great vibes, this is it. i’ll definitely be back!

fortín del escambrón, nestled along the coast of san juan, puerto rico, is a quiet and scenic spot that offers a peaceful alternative to the city’s more frequented landmarks. though smaller in scale, the fort carries a strong presence with its weathered stone walls and commanding view of the atlantic ocean. what makes this place truly special is its stillness. unlike busier sites, fortín del escambrón feels almost hidden — a space where you can hear the waves crash against the rocks, feel the breeze off the ocean, and simply take in the moment without interruption. there are no crowds, no distractions — just a quiet harmony between the historic structure and its natural surroundings. the view is stunning. the water below glows in rich shades of blue, shifting with the sun and clouds. it’s the kind of spot that invites you to slow down, take a breath, and absorb the landscape. the fort itself feels grounded and timeless, perfectly placed where land meets sea. whether you’re exploring san juan’s coast or looking for a tranquil escape, fortín del escambrón offers a beautiful and contemplative space. it’s a place to pause, reflect, and connect with both history and nature.

from everything i researched i think it's the most "ethical" place we've seen. so i decided to visit it. most of the things made sense. our guide was very knowledgeable and told us a lot of useful information. i love that they have space to walk around however they walk with assistance. i understand about traumas etc. they also walk between the trees for exercise. there is a strict no touch policy which i loved. i love how the elephant waste was used for a garden and also to manufacture paper. they were two things i was unsure of. we had a long talk about how riding elephants and bathing elephants are wrong. from the historic plaque outside: with its rich edwardian baroque details, classical composition, steel frame and fireproofed surfaces, the birkbeck building represents a transitional period of urban commercial design which combined historical style with modern technology. built in 1908 for the canadian birkbeck investment and savings company, this four-storey office building is typical of many small financial institutions prevalent in central business districts of canadian cities before world war i. designed by george w. gouinlock, the birkbeck building was restored by the ontario heritage trust in 1987.

fuente raíces is located at the end of "paseo de la princessa". the central figure is a goddess soaring into the sky, representing freedom. surrounding elements include a horse emerging from the sea, symbolizing puerto rico as an island; two adults with a child, representing the puerto rican family; dolphins and a nymph, symbolizing hospitality; a jibaro and a black woman, representing african culture; and the central goddess, symbolizing freedom. the fountain is situated at the end of the paseo de la princesa, a scenic promenade in old san juan, offering picturesque views of san juan bay and the historic city walls. it is a popular spot for both locals and tourists, often serving as a backdrop for photographs and a gathering place for cultural events and performances.

fyrish monument offers a fantastic hike with breathtaking coastal views over the firth of clyde. the trail is relatively easy, making it perfect for all ages and fitness levels, whether you’re a seasoned hiker or just out for a relaxing stroll. as you walk, you’ll enjoy lush greenery, fresh sea air, and chances to spot local wildlife. the monument itself adds a historical touch, making the journey even more special. sunsets here are absolutely stunning, with golden hues reflecting over the water. this hike is perfect for any day, any occasion—whether you’re looking for a peaceful solo walk, a family outing, or a romantic evening stroll. with well-maintained paths and a gentle incline, it’s accessible for everyone, offering a rewarding experience without being too challenging. whether rain or shine, dunure monument’s beauty never fades, making it a must-visit spot for nature lovers, photographers, or anyone looking to unwind in scotland’s stunning coastal landscape.

g swing bali is a must-visit attraction in bali! the giant swing experience was exhilarating and breathtaking - the views of the surrounding landscape were stunning! the staff were super friendly, safety-conscious, and helped us feel at ease throughout the experience. the facilities were also well-maintained and clean. i loved every moment of it - the thrill, the scenery, the excitement! can't wait to come back and do it all again! highly recommend g swing bali to all thrill-seekers and adventure-lovers out there!

galapagos dive and surf made my dream come true in the enchanted islands! i felt so comfortable that i’ve returned for over 50 dives with them. i completed my open water and advanced certifications, and i’m thrilled to continue taking more courses with them. their brand-new cressi equipment, modern tanks, and sophisticated digital technology are exceptional. the young, cheerful, and professional team always goes the extra mile on every dive. plus, the snacks, free dive computer for each diver, and even dan world insurance are fantastic bonuses. 100% recommended, dive and surf is everything that’s right in life!

galapagos travelers is an excellent dive agency located in santa cruz island. the guides are always ready to provide the best service and make sure you have the most fun and safe experience you could have underwater. the crew is incredibly well prepared, the boat is very comfortable and everyone is very friendly. i highly recommend you dive with galapgos travelers when you visit the galapagos islands.

galovački buk is a beautiful national park. it's crystal clear turquoise waters are sandwhiched by it's picturesque rocky hillsides and waterfalls. the park offers many routes of travel depending on the time constraints of those that go to visit. we chose to do the 4-6 hour hike, i jogged through a good portion of it and was able to complete it in under 4 hours. if you stop and smell the flowers, it could take some time. i loved it. it was absolutely beautiful. the paths are wooden planks for the majority of the way. some travelers were in sandals, even a lady wearing heels, so the path is easily walkable. it is a little pricy at 40€ each adult. but you do pay for the upkeep of the park along with shuttles that include boat rides and trams.

gardens by the bay east offers a stunning panoramic view of singapore’s skyline, featuring landmarks like marina bay sands and the singapore flyer. unlike the more touristy main gardens, this quieter section provides a peaceful retreat with lush greenery, open spaces, and a scenic waterfront promenade. it is a favorite spot for joggers, cyclists, and photographers seeking breathtaking sunset views. the serene environment makes it ideal for picnics and leisurely strolls. with fewer crowds, visitors can fully appreciate the beauty of the city’s skyline reflected in the waters of marina reservoir. gardens by the bay east is a hidden gem in singapore’s urban landscape.

garrafón in isla mujeres – luxury, privacy & unforgettable experiences located on the southern tip of isla mujeres, garrafón natural reef park isn’t just a scenic marvel overlooking the caribbean—it’s also become one of the most exclusive venues for private events in the mexican caribbean. i had the privilege of attending a private event at this breathtaking location, and it genuinely exceeded every expectation. from the moment we arrived, the service was flawless—discreet, attentive, and remarkably personalized. the setting is magical: dramatic cliffs above turquoise waters, manicured gardens, and golden-hour lighting that transforms any gathering into a dreamlike experience. private events like no other garrafón offers a truly exceptional venue for intimate weddings, high-end corporate events, or upscale private celebrations. for our event, the entire park was reserved, granting us exclusive access to premium experiences like snorkeling in protected coral reefs, kayaking, temazcal rituals, and ziplining over the sea. the culinary aspect was equally outstanding. a tailored gourmet menu blended authentic mexican flavors with global cuisine, prepared by private chefs. each dish was expertly paired with wines and signature cocktails, elevating the entire dining experience. highest recommendation if you're looking to create unforgettable memories in a private, luxurious setting, garrafón in isla mujeres is without a doubt one of the top destinations in the mexican caribbean. its unique combination of natural beauty, top-tier service, and exclusivity makes it the perfect backdrop for any upscale private event. rating: 10/10. highly recommended for those who value excellence, privacy, and extraordinary.

gates of heaven at lempuyang temple – a mixed experience we scootered 2 hours from canggu as first time bali visitors to visit the famous gates of heaven at lempuyang temple. the ride itself was scenic and enjoyable, especially as we got closer to the mountains. the temple is undeniably beautiful—rich in history and culture, with sweeping views that make the journey worthwhile on their own. what most people don’t tell you, though, is the reality of the photo situation. after paying for entry at the bottom, you’re assigned a number for the iconic “floating reflection” photo. what followed was a surprising 1–2 hour wait just to have your number called. many visitors spend this time either relaxing or exploring the surroundings, but it’s definitely something to plan for if you're on a schedule. once you're near the top, you'll likely be offered the chance to dress in traditional balinese attire for an additional fee. the original price quoted to us was 750,000 idr, but we negotiated it down to 500,000 idr—though pricing may vary depending on your negotiating skills or timing. in the end, we decided not to wait for our photo turn and instead took in the atmosphere, architecture, and stunning views. even without the instagram-famous shot, it was still a memorable experience. if you're going primarily for the photo, just be prepared for the wait and some extra costs.

gavalas we heard in advance of our santorini trip is one of the oldest wineries in the town and is one of the must try wines. so we knew we had to go! we booked the explore santorini tasting experience a couple of months in advance of our trip. i recommend booking plenty in advance if you can as the winery is very small. we were greeted by one of their employees and were seated at one of the outdoor tables a few minutes later. they provide some light eats as well to accompany the wines. they then have a guide to provide a history of the winery and a tasting guide to each of the wines. it was very educational and all wines were really good! we bought 3 bottles of wine to take home with us to enjoy later to remember our trip. there were a few items that i thought were strange and would consider some negatives: -they don’t accept american express in their location to purchase wines. it was strange because you could pay for the tour in advance with amex, so that had me a little puzzled. -we asked for water between wine selections and then were charged a euro or two for the water. it’s not so much about the charge, but it’s more so that wineries typically provide water during tastings (and it was done at another santorini winery during this trip). and we purchased around 120 euros in wine, so the water charge was nominal for the winery. would we come back? absolutely. and we love the wine and look forward to purchasing gavalas wine when we get back home as well!

gem of history in the rocks! enter from either the gloucester walk or from playfair st. from playfair street, you'll need to go down a little laneway in the arcade, which is a little wow experience! 8 terrace homes used to be here, but they were demolished in the 1930's. the area used to be a slum, and much was demolished during various plagues and redevelopment projects. for more, check out susanna's place and the big dig behind it! the fake furniture they put in these foundations is oddly oversized, but you can imagine living in these cramped spots on a steep hill with toilet and bathing facilities in the outside communal area. a great stopping point between george street and the bridge steps, to either go over the harbour bridge or through to observatory hill.

geunjeongjeon (근정전), the majestic throne hall of gyeongbokgung palace, is the crown jewel of seoul’s joseon-era heritage. as the centerpiece of korea’s most iconic palace, this grand hall—with its double-tiered roof, intricate dancheong (colorful paintwork), and elevated stone platform—epitomizes royal authority and architectural brilliance. built in 1395, it hosted coronations, state affairs, and diplomatic receptions. today, visitors can marvel at the ornate throne under a ceiling adorned with golden dragons, while imagining the grandeur of past ceremonies. the surrounding courtyard, flanked by rows of rank stones (banyaekseok), adds to the imposing atmosphere. time your visit for the 10 am or 2 pm palace tours (or weekdays for fewer crowds) to fully appreciate its historical weight. at night, the illuminated hall becomes even more magical during special seasonal openings.

geunjeongjeon, the throne hall of gyeongbokgung palace, stands as a powerful emblem of royal authority and joseon-era statecraft. designated as korea’s national treasure no. 223, this grand structure was where coronations, royal audiences, and major ceremonies took place. with its double-roofed architecture, intricate dancheong painting, and stone courtyard arranged by official rank, the hall reflects both confucian order and majestic artistry. today, geunjeongjeon captivates visitors not only for its historical significance but also for its breathtaking architectural symmetry, offering a vivid glimpse into korea’s regal past

go early! it’s an oven below the rim and once the sun passes over the cliffs (mid morning/early afternoon) you won’t be able to escape the blazing heat. it can easily feel above 100 below the rim. stay hydrated (preferably a few days or maybe even a week prior to the hike) but include electrolytes - this is important! this is not your average hike. do your research on common mistakes and don’t forget downhill feels a lot different than coming back uphill, which you most certainly have to do. no dogs allowed. take a backpack with plenty of hydration and a snack. sitting in the shade at cedar ridge point enjoying an apple and mixed nuts while taking in the view was one of the best experiences. we felt accomplished and prepared ourselves for the hike back, gaining over 1000 feet in elevation. there are no water sources on the trail itself, so you’ll need to bring your own. parking is limited and not allowed at the trailhead, use the shuttle (it’s free). it’s 1.5 miles each way. it’s not easy, but it’s doable. i do not recommend it for people with ankle, knee, or back issues. i would also be hesitant to recommend this trail for anybody with high blood pressure or heart issues, especially in the heat of the day. i give 5 stars for the scenic views. but keep in mind this is not a paved trail, it’s marked, but rocky and can be uneven.

go on this 4x4 tour packed dune rides and sledding, desert tour, seashore dash if u like laugh aloud edge-of-seat thrills. all you need is a madmax leather jacket or harkonnen battle suit to feel like you’re in a movie surrounded by majestic dunes. the guides gerhard n charles are so much fun and really know how to drive dunes which is crucial- and experts on the desert. pickup was 7.30ish and we headed to walvis bay which is their main gathering point. we took off in 2 jeeps:- headed first to a salt mine with its huge enclosed (stay in jeep if u can’t stand terrible ammonia laden fumes!) salt pans with feeding flocks of greater and lesser flamingos (these ones are pinker). we were so unlucky to have heavy dark skies as the pans supposedly are a vivid pink color but looked grayed out. it was a bit of a long drive thru this area, the only suggestion i have is to cut this part 15-20 min shorter as could’ve spent more at the desert, dunes and shore. then we headed to the adjoining namib naukluft park desert, and charles loaded us with fascinating facts - from how beetles stand in their heads to roll dew droplets down to their mouths, the variety of animals that can survive here and to how much hidden water there is under the arid landscape. gerhard suddenly dashed off and dug up an iridescent skink (legless lizard) to show us- can’t figure out how he knew where to look. we then raced full speed on a narrow strip of beach, between towering dunes slowly marching to sea and wildly crashing waves of the atlantic. trigger warning- jackals scavenging on dead or dying seals (kept my eyes closed but i’m still grieving). they gave us 15 min to clamber up a huge steep cliffy dune for photos. then we drove farther into the desert on crazed rides up and down dunes for fun (theirs as much as ours! these guys get a kick out of our reaction). they are excellent drivers- it takes an expert to not rollover sliding down and revving up steep inclines and sliding sands. we hit several vantage points to catch iconic photos of sandwich bay, and two others areas. if you visit skeleton coast you must do this or similar tour even if you’re not a selfie fan…on a clear day the crystal blue of the bay against the reds or golds of the dunes is simply breath taking. oh let’s not forget the hilarious sledding. i’m old but will jump on anything that won’t kill me. finally- leaving the dunes meant an exhilarating mad dash against the tide on the narrowing stretch of sand. i’ve been all over the world adventure travels, zip lining, culture, history and culture tours, wildlife safaris, high altitude hikes …and this tour is top 3 in terms of fun. mainly cos the guides openly enjoy being with their clients in an environment they love. big plus- the price was good compared to other tours. thank you charles and gerhard! keep on rocking…. note - the 6 seater jeep’s far back seat windows don’t open so u wanna avoid sitting here if possible. my small group shared the jeep with an italian couple (bloggers) who didn’t budge from the good seats so we rotated in the back. also don’t miss tasting the amazing samosas they provide in the short drinks and snack break.

google maps leads you directly to the trailhead. there are probably 6 parking spots available. i only saw 4 other people on the trail on a saturday, so parking wasn’t an issue. while this trail is not “maintained” i would like to thank the good stewards who have placed and provided upkeep on the ropes throughout the trail. you are the real heroes and make this hike more possible. overall, this is your standard island hike with mud, ropes, and ridges. if you don’t hike or exercise strenuously at home, and come on vacation here thinking you can do this hike, i would advise against it. the first mile is slow as you are going through the rainforest, and having to be precise with your footing. after you get to the first waterfall, things start to pick up and the thrill of this hike begins. shortly after is the second waterfall, then third. the third waterfall has many tiers you will have to climb. once you get to the top of it, you are released onto the ridge and views of the crater. you continue to climb, and eventually peak before starting your journey around the crater and down. the way back is much faster as the trail appears to be more groomed as it is out of the rainforest. it took me a bit over 2.5 hours (moving time) to summit, but only 1.5 (moving time) to return to my vehicle. with breaks, close to 5 hours total. why this is not on alltrails i don’t know, but i’ve included a screenshot of a hike someone posted on there with a map of it in the past. you won’t need it. the trail is clearly marked and at no point did i ever feel lost. it says it was 5.7 miles, but my garmin tracked it at 4.5. additionally, at no point were things too sketch to where i had a thought of turning around. there is a moderate level of thrill the entire time, but not sketch. i would recommend 72oz of water via a camelbak or backpack. you need all 4 of your limbs consistently for this hike, so don’t bother sacrificing one to carry a water bottle. there are also many opportunities on the way up for water filtration. i would not encourage bringing a small dog because the winds at the top of the ridge can scream, and potentially blow your dog down the mountain (again, not sketch, but precaution). have fun!

gorges viewpoint, nestled within the verdant expanse of the black river gorges national park in mauritius, is a must-visit for nature enthusiasts and anyone seeking breathtaking panoramic vistas. imagine standing at an elevation, with an unobstructed sweep of undulating green hills and deep gorges stretching out before you. the viewpoint is strategically located to offer the **most dramatic perspective** of the island's largest national park. you'll be able to trace the rugged contours of the black river gorges, carved over millennia by natural forces, revealing a tapestry of dense forests and cascading waterfalls in the distance. on a clear day the view extends beyond the immediate greenery, offering glimpses of the western coastline of mauritius, with the shimmering indian ocean meeting the land. the air is often fresh and crisp, carrying the sounds of nature from the forests below. accessibility is a key advantage of gorges viewpoint. it's conveniently reachable by well-maintained roads within the national park, making it a relatively easy stop for most visitors. you'll often find designated parking areas nearby. being situated within the black river gorges national park, gorges viewpoint serves as a fantastic starting point or midpoint for exploring other natural wonders in the vicinity. the popular alexandra falls, known for its picturesque cascade, is often a short drive away. similarly, the unique geological formations and vibrant hues of chamarel (seven coloured earth and chamarel waterfall) are also within reasonable driving distance. for those who enjoy capturing memories, gorges viewpoint is an absolute paradise for photography. the ever-changing light and the vastness of the landscape provide endless opportunities for stunning shots. it's also a perfect spot to simply pause, breathe in the natural beauty, and appreciate the tranquility of the mauritian highlands. while the viewpoint itself doesn't offer extensive amenities, its primary draw is the sheer magnificence of the natural scenery. it's a place to connect with the island's interior beauty and gain a deeper appreciation for its diverse ecosystems. the recommended time to visit gorges viewpoint is generally during the drier and cooler months, from may to december, when the weather is most pleasant for outdoor activities and the views are often clearer. however, the scenery holds its charm throughout the year, with the lushness varying with the seasons.

gorreana tea plantation is a must-visit for anyone interested in history, sustainability, and scenic beauty, offering a rare glimpse into europe’s oldest, family-run tea factory where you can watch traditional production methods in action. with free tours, organic teas, and breathtaking atlantic views, it’s a unique and memorable experience for both tea lovers and curious travelers. i had the pleasure of visiting the gorreana tea factory on may 19th, and it was truly a highlight of my trip to são miguel. it's the only tea plantation in europe, which is fascinating in itself, but the experience goes beyond just that. you can walk freely through the beautiful, lush tea fields, taking in the stunning green landscapes. then, head inside to see the historic machinery still in operation, which is incredibly cool. best of all, they offer free tea tastings! you get to sample their delicious black and green teas, learning about the process from leaf to cup. the gorreana tea factory offers a unique and relaxing experience, perfect for all ages. whether you're a tea connoisseur or just looking for something different to do, i highly recommend adding it to your são miguel itinerary. don't miss out on this piece of history and delicious local flavor!

great dive shop! excellent divers and outstanding boat crew!! what more could you ask for? saw tons of hammer heads and white tip sharks. we found a huge school of black striped salema. we were able to sit in it as they swam all around us. it was a once in a lifetime experience. the master diver took plenty of photos/videos of us and the fish. they handed them over at no extra cost at the end of the dive. something to note for any new divers looking to dive in this area from any of the dive shops. it is a long day for two dives. 7am to 3pm because you are taxied ~35 min to the pier, you have to wait for the boats to process and load (~1 hour), then you can get on once your boat is loaded, and you’re off to the dive site. it is a similar process when you get back but much quicker. putting us back at the dive shop at about 2:30pm. the divers are guiding you through this process. we never felt lost or forgotten. they did a great job taking care of us. there is a little shop at the pier selling food and drinks. places to sit and rest while you wait. the bathrooms are clean but it cost $0.50 to use them and you have to ask for toilet paper. this shouldn’t reflect on the dive shop. much of it is out of their hands. they were great and i would definitely dive with them again.

great gobi a strictly protected area is a nature reserve in gobi desert, situated in the south-western part of mongolia at the border with china. a similar reserve in the gobi exists further to the west - the great gobi b strictly protected area. both reserves form one unit, the great gobi strictly protected area (spa), which encompasses a total of 53,000 km2. great gobi a is one of the last refuges for critically endangered animals, like wild bactrian camels and gobi bears. the reserve is an important refuge for some endangered large mammal species, such as the wild bactrian camel (camelus ferus), which was identified as a separate species in 2008 by the veterinary university of vienna, the gobi bear (ursus arctos gobiensis), the snow leopard (uncia uncia), the argali wild sheep (ovis ammon) and the mongolian wild ass (equus hemionus hemionus). especially for the wild camel the reserve is important, since it is one of three last locations, where the rare animal can be found. due to the remoteness and large size of the reserve, it is hard to estimate population numbers or population trends. estimates for the population of wild camels in the reserve range from about 350 to 1950 individuals. wolves (canis lupus), which are also found in the reserve, might be a threat for the calves of wild camels. however, the effects of these predators on the camel population are unclear. twenty km from the reserve is the wild camel breeding centre at zakhyn us, which was established in 2004 with 12 wild camels which had been caught by mongolian herdsmen. there were 22 wild camels at the breeding centre in 2014 and in 2013 two bull wild camels were released into the reserve with satellite collars. one of them has formed his own herd with five female wild camels. the breeding centre which is financed by the wild camel protection foundation and administered by the director of gobi "a" covers 40 hectares. in 2008 the veterinary university of vienna confirmed after extensive dna testing that the wild camel is a new and separate species which separated from any other known camel species over 750,000 years ago.

great place! fantastic activity. staff is very nice and knowledgeable. you can learn a lot about the dogs and the raices. it was great experience to be able to ride with the sledge dogs cart.

great spot to get a view or the lower manhattan skyline. hopefully you don’t have the lights shining obstructing your pictures like they were for me.

great spot to view the wetlands from, epic views!

great spot with a wide variety of trampolines. part of the area is shaded, which is nice. it's a fun place for kids to visit with their friends, and teenagers could enjoy it as well, especially in a group. there are also activities for toddlers. plus, there's a lovely cafe overlooking the rice fields.

great spot with lots to see; a large interesting sinkhole/cavein to overlook, pretty views of the mountains and strange rock formations. kinda tricky to get to however. since the trail begins in a neighborhood, you must park outside of the neighborhood by the playground and take a shuttle bus to the trailhead. check the times on the sedona website. definitely worth the trip despite this.

great spot, off the beaten path. we biked up here from ayora, there is a protected bike lane until the turnoff, then traffic is light, although some of the climbs are steep. if you’re fit it’s a great ride and the downhill is a blast! you can self tour here to see a collapsed crater, circle the property to see tortoises and birds, then ascend to the peak for an amazing view of the east side of the island. we only had an hour because we arrived at 4:30, but i would plan for 3 hours or so if i went back (not including the bike ride t from town).

great spot. beautiful waterfall just a stone’s throw away from a major road and a few high rise. none of this can be seen or heard whilst there! the 10 min trek through the sugar cane fields great with friendly farmer folk waving on by. the only negative is the scrouts of the population who leave their litter there. take a towel take a swim take a photo take your rubbish.

great spot. cute rooms. convenient location. friendly staff. fantastic breakfast. *do not have them get you a taxi! 30 euros for less than 10min ride is wild. especially in a junky van with no seatbelts. the driver seemed like he could hardly see, made us both ride up front with him, and pulled some wild maneuvers to let us out on the road. bizarre and unsafe experience.
great stadium - intimate, good facilities, clean - good coffee!! access is a little difficult - leave yourself extra time if you’re using the free stadium carpark!! (capacity - 6,000 people)

great staff with great service. namely, yuni manager on floor scuba diver instructor tomi was great for supporting us with extreme water phobia and cover come it to experience such great seawalk along with his on boat staff vanus.. thank you all.

great stargazing tour. best experience. jorge is really a good guide and explained so many things in a great way. then they organized this great “breakfast” and he took some incredible pictures. he is interested in giving the best experience to his clients. he showed us so many stars, star clusters, planets… it was incredible. don’t think about the price just book the experience. it is more than worth it. we enjoyed every minute nevertheless the low temperature. don’t wanna miss this experience. the pictures below are made by myself. but he even gave me some advice since i am a beginner in astro photography. thanks jorge and of course your assistant.

great starting point to walk to the colosseum. the tower is still in tact and the area is full of history.

great state park, just a heads up it is $10 per person not per car so the can definitely get pricey. every day at 10am they have a ranger guided nature walk that takes about an hour. we chose to go on it and enjoyed it. this is a park you do have to walk, it's not one you can drive around and see things. make sure you drive down to the creek, it's beautiful.

great stay at earthsong. cabins are very nice (no tvs and not wifi inside the cabins, though some wifi on property) and the area is super quiet with beautiful views. it's a 25 minute drive to denali park with plenty of opportunities to encounter moose along the way (more so than inside the park). totally worth staying here if you're looking to disconnect in a beautiful place. ty and the staff are wonderful which adds to the experience.

great stay here. did the touristy boat where you see the floating islands, then was picked up and taken here. staying with the family at uros qhantany lodge gave amazing insight into how a real family lives on the reed islands and had a much more authentic feel then the tourist show i had seen on the other islands. high recommended if you're looking for an amazing adventure and to experience living (for a night) on one of these floating islands.
great stay in the valley of nubra. cold desert in walkable distance best time: august stayed during full moon night and the view was memorable. food : homely & common area for eating. service : 8/10

great stay with a few minor setbacks we recently stayed at this hotel and overall had a wonderful experience. the location is a bit secluded, which offers peace and quiet, but it also made accessing some amenities slightly inconvenient—especially for us, as we were traveling with an elderly family member and a newborn. the hotel itself was fantastic and definitely worth the price. our room was clean, well-maintained, and the bathroom amenities were great. the staff truly stood out—they were incredibly friendly, attentive, and made us feel very welcome throughout our stay. one downside was the halal breakfast option, which required a bit of a walk. this was quite troublesome given our family’s situation. it would have been thoughtful if the hotel provided a tram or shuttle service to make it easier for guests in similar situations. the swimming pool looked inviting but was unfortunately too crowded during our visit, with limited seating available. on a brighter note, i want to thank the hotel for going the extra mile to fulfill my special request for a birthday celebration. the complimentary cake was absolutely delicious and added a personal touch to our stay. despite the few inconveniences, we had a lovely time and would definitely return. thank you for the memorable experience!
great stop. lots of bus tourists and can busy. goto the far end for a great view. but the better view backward up the valley can be found 300 metres away along the road tucked in a wooded dip.
great store, high quality, and friendly staff. handmade masks, you can find a beautiful product at any price

great store. love the selection of chocolates, good fruit and vegetables, nice bakery section. also good selection of kombucha and the best selection of tinned fish i've seen in new orleans. the store is beautiful inside and staff are friendly.

great street food. passed by this place several times and finally had the chance to try it. the meatballs are a must, a little pricey but definitely worth it. how to describe the taste... "the ingredients basically wage war on your tongue." the pasta was cooked to perfection and the sauce was incredibly rich. the staff was super friendly and chill. next time i will try the pizza.

great street vendor food. all kinds of food to choose from. it's cheaper here than nearby myeongdong. usually crowded with shoppers. the atmosphere is lively. you can get really full for several bucks and eat all kinds of food
great stretch of beach. a nice walk from my stay in copa, and well worth the time and effort. you can check out the fort on the way, through ipanema beach.

great sunrise experience at mount batur! the mount batur sunrise trip was so much fun! we took a jeep to the top, which made the whole experience even more exciting and unique. the view during sunrise was absolutely stunning — truly one of the best i’ve ever seen. the jeep ride was smooth and added a sense of adventure to the trip. we paid 500k idr per person, and it was definitely worth it for the amazing view and overall experience. highly recommend for anyone visiting bali!
great super market for your traveling and day to day needs. they also sell liquor too. great general grocery store. the hot food they serve at lunch was also good and affordable

great supermarket with excellent prices and a wide variety of products. the fresh pastry section is especially delicious, and the staff are always friendly and helpful. a perfect spot for both everyday shopping and little treats!
great swimming spot. there was a fair amount of people there, but still felt like you can be on your own. the rocks in the shore were quite sharp, swimming shoes recommended.

great theatre, we watched back to the future, what a fantastic show. it surprised me with wonderful acting and singing. the guys did a fabulous job and the theatrics were excellent. the foyer is quite small.

great time out on the bay and in mccovey cove. sebastian was very helpful getting us prepared for our trip. we saw a couple of seals and enjoyed the giants game.

great to see the artwork and the history behind the roman empire. you have to buy the multi-tickets for the forum and the colosseum. also to be noted when you purchase your tickets they usually have a time to go in so don't start the line until your time to go in.

great tour operator! we did both the kilimanjaro and safari tour with the kilimanjaro brothers and it was all more than excellent. very friendly and service-focused crew, authentic (local), attention to detail (great lodges with some special arrangements for our honeymoon), and we had a lot of fun! they have positive and flexible/can-do mindset. i think price-quality wise also the best out there.

great tour with an awesome guide. very informative and entertaining at the same time. it was a cruise from westminister to tower bridge including a return ticket from butler's wharf. we even had time to explore tower bridge, the surrounding and visit a local pub before we went back to westminister pier. i really recommend it. it was a great way to see a lot of london sites in an hour.

great tour with the 2d1n trip in komodo ! nice team, nice crew, really good chef the food was delicious ! all the spots were worth it, the organization was perfect. time to chill a bit and to discover. only sad points : we could not see mantas… it’s not the high season so we were unlucky…

great tour! jimmy and juan and pako were so friendly! they gave us a great time and explained everything. the tequila was delicious and same with the local beer. juan even let me try and drive the boat. nice guys and fun tour!

great tour! leaving earlier than other boats allowed us to enjoy the amazing spots without the crowds. the staff was really friendly, and the food and drinks were excellent. definitely an experience i would recommend!

great tour! nick was our guide and was extremely knowledgeable of the wildlife in the area; birds, fish, and of course gators 🐊 personally, i recommend the covered boat tour which provided shade, allowed you to move/walk around, and was pretty quiet (so it didn’t scare off the wildlife).

great tour! unfortunately it rained…hard…and we were soaked & cold but the tour itself was worth it. guide was knowledgeable. coffee making was fun & learned a lot of new things about the process. lunch was tasty. wear boots or sturdy shoes. bring toilet paper for using the toilets.

great tour, amazing tour guide! what i really liked was how careful the driving was and how much jp knows about the culture, history and landscape particularities. it was very informative i felt safe all the way through. great experience, great guide. thank you!

great trail for beginner/intermediates. we took about 3.5 hours to get up and we stopped to enjoy the view and had several snack breaks. we hiked up and took the tram down. it was challenging but very very rewarding. suggest going to the bathroom before starting and packing some snacks as well. the restaurant at the peak is not vegetarian friendly, so we decided to have a small picnic near the peak and we had a blast. it’s another 35-40 min to the summit of the mountain. many folks we met at the peak did not hike up and they took the tram up and did the summit hike then tram back down. if you are able i strongly recommend you do the hike it is so rewarding!
great trail in rio, great view of the city and the beautiful beaches, it worth the effort, cellphone for uber is difficult
great trail just under 16km. not too difficult but quite alot of stairs if you have bad knees. beautiful views all the way !

great trail, but comes with some challenges. lots of exposed roots, especially after you pass the lake (in the middle of the trail). the view on vancouver, burnaby, richmond is spectacular, assuming you have good weather at the top. i saw some folks in flip-flops, not recommended for sure. please be prepared and wear proper footwear for this trail.

great trail, get there before noon or else it'll be a rather hot hike back. it's a 3.5 mile (each way) up and back trail with several river crossings and great views. at the end , make sure you keep going to get to a really spectacular waterway. wade your way through. id also bring some flip flops or water shoes to navigate the water at the end, it's doable barefoot but the pebbles aren't pleasant underfoot.
great trail. all dirt so be ready for mud. lots of tree roots and rocks so watch your step. beautiful views.

great trail. it was a pretty easy hike up to the summit. we started early so our wasn't busy up top. epic views. i would say the best views for the effort. extremely busy on the way down. passed sooooo many groups. ended with a cold plunge at the hot springs.

great trek, tough after rains. be ready to dirty your shoes, back and pants. don't carry too heavy a load. really fun time with a partner or family, don't go alone! the trek took about 4 hours (le pouce classic - green color) give me a like if this helped.

great trekking experience! our guide made was absolutely great- very friendly, funny, helpful and knowledgeable! in addition to great walk in the village & swimming by the waterfalls surrounded by beautiful nature we had chance to try local fruits and see how they are grown. also we saw monkeys in the natural wild environment!
great trip and great driver, i felt very safe and well looked after! chefchaouen is also a very beautiful place must-see in your morocco travel !! thank you fez city tour for this great day!

great trip to the dive spot that also offers snorkeling, stop to the sandbar, swimming with the sharks and stingrays, photo opportunity with a sea lion, and party on the boat. the staff was entertaining and friendly. it was a lot of fun!

great trip, great travel agency! we planned the trip via email. responses were quick, and we received a good itinerary that perfectly matched our wishes. from airport pickup, throughout the trip, and even drop-off, everything was taken care of. the drivers were experienced and excellent. the guide was helpful, took care of everything, and nothing was too much trouble. all we had to do was enjoy beautiful ladakh. and that's exactly what we did! i can wholeheartedly recommend timeout ladakh.
great trip, nice to do this trip with smaller numbers.

great true icelandic experience for a tourist spent over an hour just jumping between the tubs and pools and steam rooms. very clean and convenient as well. showers are equipped with soap and lockers are plentiful so you can store all your belongings. there is also a bathing suit dryer so you don’t have to worry about having it stink up your bag

great urban park. this is in the heart of the city. you can still hear the hustle and bustle of cars but it's beautiful regardless since you're surrounded by trees. very serene! did not see a restroom. no tickets required.

great value for money! i opted out of the transfer and took an uber instead, which worked well (i booked via getyourguide). just note that you’ll need to stop by the reservation office first to exchange your online booking for a paper ticket—so be sure to factor that into your timing. the food and entertainment were excellent, and the top deck offered stunning sunset views.

great value for money. my husband and i enjoyed the show -- fun, energetic and participatory. we bought our tickets from klook, and it was about 10k won cheaper per person. the trade off was that we could only choose our section, not the actual seat. but it was fine. the theatre wasn't packed, and it looked like everyone would have a good view regardless of the seat. it's a 5-man show without real lines, so it's perfect for foreign tourists. the only draw back is that it's a bit secluded from the city centre, so we couldn't get a taxi and had to wait 30 mins for the bus.
great value! had a brilliant time with a group of 6 traveling together.
