great vibe with a wading pool and plenty of space for picnics! the walk along the esplanade is lovely too.

great vibe, a bit touristy but otherwise good. we found useful souvenirs (not just the normal stuff with a flag on it), good food and drink, and we also got some good recommendations on where to go next by the wonderful persons in one of the shops. highly recommended. we went here on our first day and it was a blast. there were also street performances in front of the market!
great vibes and excellent support for every guest’s need, definitely recommended!

great vibes at the rooftop bar! we didn’t have food, but the drinks were solid and the atmosphere made it all worth it. special mention to the garfield waiter who moved us to the best table when it was possible. perfect spot for a relaxed evening with a view!

great viennese cafe with long history and magnificent architectural design. originally opened in 1903, it was redesigned in 50th by famous architect oswald haerdtl. most of his work has been preserved and restored recently. you can still sit on his original chairs and sofas and, please, do not miss all the light fixtures. it's truly one of a kind and brings the whole aesthetic of the place together. it's quite busy cafe, so i would suggest making a reservation. you might need to wait a little for a waiter, as they all are busy attending many other hungry customers. the food was good, as expected. we opted for a schnitzel, and it didn't disappoint. don't forget to check out on the latest news at the newspaper rack - old viennese tradition. those newspaper holders with hooks are beyond cute.

great view at the ocean and city at the seaside. the road here is hard for beginners or with manual gearbox car. when you will gry there it's really worth it. one of those incredible, breathtaking views on madeira. the city at the bottom of the mountain offers many attractions - also a great place to rest for a while. local restaurants serves really tasty local dishes.

gyeonghoeru pavilion – a floating gem inside gyeongbokgung palace hidden within the walls of gyeongbokgung palace lies one of seoul’s most stunning architectural treasures: gyeonghoeru pavilion. built in 1412 during the reign of king taejong, this elegant pavilion was designed as a venue for royal banquets and celebrations. surrounded by an artificial pond and supported by 48 sturdy stone pillars, it appears to float gracefully above the water—a vision of harmony and balance. what makes gyeonghoeru so captivating is not just its size or historical importance, but its perfect blend with nature. in spring, the pavilion is framed by cherry blossoms; in summer, it reflects in the green water, creating a dreamy scene. autumn brings warm, golden tones, and in winter, a serene blanket of snow gives it a quiet, almost poetic charm. architecturally, gyeonghoeru is a masterpiece. the open design allows cool breezes to flow through during warmer months, making it both functional and beautiful. its tiled roof and painted eaves showcase the refined elegance of joseon-era craftsmanship. standing by the pond, you can almost imagine the royal gatherings that once filled the air with music and laughter. today, visitors from around the world come to admire this pavilion’s timeless beauty, capturing photos and reflecting on its rich history. gyeonghoeru pavilion is more than just a part of gyeongbokgung palace—it’s a living symbol of korean heritage and an enduring testament to the artistry of the past. for anyone visiting seoul, it’s a stop that should not be missed.

had a wonderful stay at explora and thoroughly enjoyed the experience overall. the food was excellent, with gourmet dinners and fantastic breakfast spreads, and the views of the paine massif and the horns were absolutely stunning. the excursions offered were well-curated and a highlight of the trip. however, there were a couple of areas where my experience could have been better. room ventilation: the central heating system in the rooms made them quite warm at night. while opening the windows helped, it also let in daylight, which can be disruptive if you prefer to sleep early, like i do. mount británico hike: this was the most disappointing part of my stay. the guides maintained a very fast pace, which felt rushed and didn’t allow me to enjoy the stunning scenery or take photos at the many beautiful viewpoints along the trail. as an avid hiker, i usually maintain a good pace, but i prefer to hike at a speed that allows me to truly appreciate the journey, not just the destination. the guides seemed intent on returning by 5 pm to catch explora’s private catamaran, which created unnecessary pressure. ironically, we ended up returning at 7 pm because i couldn’t keep up with the pace. if the guides had planned for a later return, i could have completed the hike to mount británico and enjoyed it without feeling rushed. for a trip to patagonia, which is often a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, this was a significant disappointment. i hope explora can revisit the scheduling and pacing of their excursions to better accommodate guests with different hiking styles and ensure a more enjoyable experience for everyone. overall, explora is a fantastic place to stay, and i hope my feedback helps improve future visits for other guests.

had an amazing time on the sunrise kayak tour. chris and his team were absolutely amazing, friendly and professional. the views of sydney harbour were spectacular and watching the sunrise was just phenomenal. highly recommend for tourists and locals alike!

had an amazing time wakesurfing with honu. the crew is very friendly and helpful.

had an amazing time with our guides tater tot and dirt mouth! both are very knowledgeable about the area and made the tour that much more interesting. they were very safety conscious as well as adventurous. there is briefing before heading to make sure that everyone is comfortable riding an atv. would recommend 10/10 if you’re visiting denali. although we didn’t get to see any wild life, we did see some amazing g views of mount healy and the town.

had an amazing time with pink jeep tours in sedona! the views were stunning and the ride was a perfect mix of fun and adventure. our guide, steve, was awesome super knowledgeable, friendly, and great behind the camera. he got us some incredible family photos we’ll treasure. highly recommend!

had an amazing time with this team! from the moment we got on board, everything was smooth and well taken care of. the yacht was in great, the crew was friendly and helpful, and the whole vibe was just super chill. it ended up being one of the highlights of our trip. would definitely do it again!

had an amazing trip aboard coral sea dreaming! our crew members quentin and ivan were incredible! quentin was very kind and knowledgeable; ivan took me for my first ever dive and was so calm and caring when i was nervous. the view of the stars and moon during the night on the reef was beautiful! since i was on the boat for 2 days, i got to really connect and make friendships with the other passengers. i suggest bringing a card game to share and play!

had an amazing trip with reef experience! the entire crew was professional, knowledgeable, and very accommodating! you can tell they do this nearly every day. i especially appreciated our dive guide macha! she was very patient with a relatively new diver and was able to locate and point out numerous reef species during our dive! the food prepared onboard was superb and plentiful and my hotel pickup was right on time. if you are coming to cairns, this is the company you need to book your gbr dive trip with! you won’t regret it!

had an amazing trip with the wife who has never gone white water rafting before. the athabasca 2.5 hr package was perfect and the guide eddie was amazing. he showed us all of the mountains, creeks and explained the history of the area while we were going down the river. the best part was he made sure that everyone got to experience the rapids in a way they were comfortable. my wife was a bit terrified to start and came out smiling and asking when we could come back and do the harder one. way to go eddie!! yahoo

had an awesome experience with red rock balloons yesterday. was with a group of 12. none of us had ever been up before. they were so patient with us. mark was so nice. it was a beautiful day. so mesmerizing. truly something everyone should do.

had an awesome hike! what great views, hikes, talks and more. saw sloths with babies, monkeys, snakes, bugs, ants, lizards, birds, raccoons and more. so many cool plants along the way - which was just unbelievable 🤩 our tour guide jose was really awesome and even took some great photos he sent us afterwards which was super nice. we did the combo with the bridges, volcano and waterfall with lunch and we were very impressed - this was probably our favorite part!

had an awesome time doing the full day jeep tour and overnight stay. was apart of a group of three so it was a very relaxing and quiet experience. our guide did a good job of giving us brief explanations and sending us off into the right direction at each location, didn’t rush us and made an effort to navigate around other groups so that we could experience some of the sites more peacefully. lunch and dinner were great, the staff made great company and were very friendly. my highlight of the night was walking out into the desert with one of our guides to make a fire, look at the stars and draw pictures in the sand. absolutely amazing experience!!!

had an incredible day with the helibike team! super professional and patient. trails were the perfect mix for multiple skill levels. can't wait to go again!

had an incredible diving experience with this team! from start to finish, everything was smooth, safe, and a lot of fun. dive master steven (with a v!) was professional, calm, and clearly passionate about what he does-he made the entire dive feel easy and enjoyable. special shoutout to captain happy flower, who lived up to his name with great energy and a steady hand at the helm. highly recommend diving with this crew-whether you're a beginner or experienced, you're in excellent hands. looking forward to the next one!

had an incredible paragliding experience with omar as my pilot. i’m a below-knee amputee and was honestly a bit nervous, but omar made me feel completely at ease from the start. super professional, calm, and just a legend of a guy. the flight itself was smooth, fun, and unforgettable. absolutely recommend getting the media package, the photos and videos are insane! thanks omar

had an unforgettable hiking experience at 7 cascades with ya nature! the scenery was absolutely breathtaking, and the hike was both adventurous and refreshing. a big thank you to our amazing guides mathieu and thomas—they were knowledgeable, friendly, and made the whole journey feel safe and fun. highly recommend ya nature for anyone looking to explore the natural beauty of mauritius!

hanoi flag tower (cột cờ hà nội) is one of the city’s most iconic historical landmarks. built in the early 19th century, it stands tall within the vietnam military history museum. the tower’s well-preserved architecture, with its red brick structure and intricate details, reflects vietnam’s rich history. climbing to the top offers a panoramic view of hanoi, making it a great spot for history lovers and photographers. the national flag proudly waving at the top adds to its significance. the surrounding museum provides deeper insights into vietnam’s military past. overall, hanoi flag tower is a must-visit for those interested in history and culture. it’s a simple yet powerful symbol of vietnam’s resilience and pride.

hanoi old quarter is the heart and soul of vietnam’s capital, offering a perfect mix of history, culture, and energy. walking through its narrow streets feels like stepping into a different world—one filled with charming colonial buildings, ancient temples, and the constant buzz of motorbikes. each street is unique, often named after the traditional craft once sold there, like silk street or silver street. the food here is incredible! from famous pho (vietnamese noodle soup) to delicious banh mi (vietnamese sandwich), the street food vendors serve some of the best meals you’ll ever eat. don’t forget to try the famous egg coffee at one of the many cozy cafés. shopping in the old quarter is also an adventure. markets and small shops sell everything from souvenirs to handmade crafts at bargain prices. be ready to practice your bargaining skills! despite the hustle and bustle, hanoi old quarter has a unique charm. whether you’re watching a traditional water puppet show, enjoying a beer at ta hien street, or simply wandering around hoan kiem lake, there’s always something exciting to see. it’s a must-visit for anyone traveling to vietnam!

hark! let it be known that upon the eve preceding our voyage, we didst wander into the keeper’s hall, where boats are granted to noble folk and commoners alike. without hindrance or delay, we inquired as to the renting of a vessel for the morrow. verily, the master of the boats gave us cheerful assent, and thus was our request fulfilled without protest or toil. come the morrow, at half past the third hour past midday, we did claim our sea-chariot—a fine vessel of decent girth, fit for a company, and fueled to the brim—for but 300 gold coins of the realm. with sails not, but motor true, we set forth unto a fair and crimson shore, known in those lands as red beach. there we cast anchor and did take respite upon the gentle waves, leaping into the briny deep. though the waters were chilled for but the span of five heartbeats, warmth did soon embrace us as though the sea itself did welcome our company. thereafter, we made course to the heart of the great fire-mountain—the volcano, whose fury lies slumbering. yet alas! the west winds did blow with much ire, stirring the waters into tempestuous chaos. we were forced to abandon our quest and steer our craft away from that churning passage. yet fortune favored us still, for we happened upon a sheltered bay, where we dropped anchor once more. the waters there were warmer still, likely by the grace of hidden hot springs that bubble from the earth's breath beneath. as the day waned, we did chart our return by the green path, though the sea remained unruly. yet our spirits were high, and soon we returned once more near red beach. there, with anchor set and hearts content, we beheld the setting of the sun—an awe-striking visage, golden and crimson upon the sea’s edge. truly, a glorious venture it was. to all travelers of these lands i proclaim: partake of this noble boat-renting service, for it shall bring thee joy and wonder beneath the sun and stars.

have to say that this was the most risky hike i've done in oahu, it stars muddy and wet the first feet, but great views of the forest and the stream. the first half mile is muddy and with lots of slippery roots, you have to cross the stream many times too. after that, you'll get to a split in the trail where you can choose which way you are going on the loop ( i'd recommend following the stream because the other trail is easier to get down when tired). the next mile from here will take you to the first waterfall, is muddy and slippery as usual, so really be careful with your step, it's very easy to get injured. from the first waterfall things get even more sketchy but also more "fun", because for the next 200 ft you have to walk on the side of the waterfalls, ( there are some ropes in the very sketchy parts). after all that adventure, you'll get to the kaau crater with a nice view to the caldera, and the trail keeps going up on a very narrow ridge until the top of pu'u palikea mountain where you can see to the east side of the island ( when sunny, but clouds really like to stay on top of these mountain range). finally after that, you can return using the trail around the ridge and the crater, and the way back is definitely safer on this side of the loop. this is definitely not a beginner trail, the mountain range here keeps their own weather and being rainy, wet and slippery is an almost everyday fact. using a trail maps app is very useful too, i use mapy and showed all the trail with waterfalls included. consider at least 6 hr for the whole trail.

having recently embarked on a norwegian joy alaska cruise in may 2025, i offer this balanced and objective review to provide insights for prospective cruisers. the journey through the stunning alaskan landscape provided many memorable moments, and the ship itself offers a comfortable and engaging environment for exploration. service and staff: a resounding success one of the most consistently positive aspects of our experience on the norwegian joy was the exceptional service provided by the crew. from dining staff to cleaning personnel, the team demonstrated a remarkable commitment to guest satisfaction. the attentiveness and friendly demeanor of the service crew in all areas of the ship truly enhanced our cruise. a special mention must be made of the cleaning service team. our stateroom was maintained to an impeccable standard daily, demonstrating their efficiency and dedication. furthermore, the "washy washy" team at the garden cafe entrance, with their cheerful reminders about hygiene, added a delightful and effective touch to onboard health protocols. their efforts were genuinely appreciated and contributed to a clean and comfortable environment for all. dining experience: highs and opportunities for enhancement the food options on the norwegian joy generally ranged from good to excellent, with particular highlights being the overall quality and variety of flavors available. the dedication to catering to diverse dietary needs was evident, and we found the indian food option to be particularly impressive and a great choice for vegetarians, offering flavorful and satisfying meals. this commitment to specific dietary preferences is a definite strong point. however, a key area for potential improvement lies in the variety of menus within the complimentary restaurants. while the quality of the food was commendable, we observed that the menus in the main complimentary dining venues remained largely the same each day. this can lead to a sense of repetition over the course of a longer cruise. introducing rotating daily menus, or offering themed nights, would significantly enhance the dining experience and provide more culinary exploration without requiring guests to venture into specialty dining options. shore excursions: ample time for exploration for those eager to immerse themselves in the alaskan ports of call, the norwegian joy proved to be well-organized in providing sufficient time for shore excursions. the pacing of port visits allowed for thorough exploration, whether participating in organized tours or venturing out independently. this ample time at each destination meant we never felt rushed, allowing us to fully appreciate the unique beauty and activities each alaskan town had to offer. overall impression: the norwegian joy provides a solid platform for an alaskan adventure. its attentive service, dedicated cleaning crew, and thoughtful consideration for dietary needs (especially the excellent indian vegetarian options) are definite strengths. while the consistency of complimentary dining menus presents an opportunity for future enhancement, the overall experience is positive, ensuring that guests can focus on the breathtaking scenery and unique experiences that an alaskan cruise offers. for those seeking a comfortable and well-serviced journey through this stunning region, the norwegian joy is a commendable choice.

having very recently returned from an eight-day motorized rafting and hiking trip through the grand canyon with colorado river and trail expeditions (crate), i can recommend them for your grand canyon adventure without hesitation or qualification. the boatsmen, walker and abel, and their capable assistants pheobe and matt, guided us with consummate expertise through the many thrilling rapids and on daily hikes of varying lengths, and their knowledge of the local history, geology, archaeology, flora, and fauna, freely shared with us all, was admirable. the food was delicious and plentiful – even for this hardcore vegetarian – and crate seamlessly provided for all the logistics, including the rafting and hiking, our helicopter transport from the depths of the canyon, and the flight back toward las vegas on smaller prop planes. all in all, crate provided an extraordinary experience through a truly extraordinary landscape. a few caveats: this trip does require some physical exertion, as one was expected to help pack and unpack the rafts, as well as set up one’s camps (which, in fact, was a great part of the fun and group-experience). having said that, one of our trip members suffered some unexpected moderate physical limitations throughout the trip, and the crew capably and compassionately assisted him and guided him, without detracting their attentions from the rest of the group. also, some of the hikes were more rigorous and offered more exposure than necessarily advertised by the crew; however, it was easy enough to avoid any hikes, or portions of hikes, that one felt was beyond one’s capacity. all in all, one of the most memorable, awe-inspiring, and eye- and mind-opening trips i’ve done in my seven decades!

hawaiian mission houses historic site and archives located in 553 s. king street honolulu, hawaiian mission houses historic site and archives (hmh), is an active site for hawaii’s history since 1820. it is also a national historic landmark (listed in 1965). this one-acre site in the historic capital district in downtown honolulu, hmh preserves hawai‘i’s oldest western-style house, the 1821 mission house, as well as the 1831 chamberlain house, the 1841 bedroom annex, a cemetery, a collections storage vault, a gift shop, and multi-purpose space. the library, which holds both english and hawaiian archival material, over 80,000 digital pieces and is home to one of the largest collections of hawaiian language books in the world. reserve tickets at least 24 hours in advance. general admission is $20.

hemis national park, located in the east part of ladakh in the states of jammu and kashmir, is a renowned national park of the region. established in 1981, it covers an area of about 4,400 square kilometres and is named after the famous hemis monastery located within its boundaries. in the park, you can explore diverse wildlife, including rare and endangered species like the tibetan wolf, snow leopard, eurasian brown bear, and bharal (blue sheep). the history of hemis national park is closely tied to the efforts of conservationists and wildlife enthusiasts to protect the unique biodiversity of the region. the park was established with the aim of conserving the fragile himalayan ecosystem and providing a sanctuary for the region's wildlife. over the years, it has become a significant centre for wildlife research and conservation efforts, attracting you in all its glory. hemis national park is not only important for its biodiversity but also holds cultural significance due to its association with the hemis monastery, one of the wealthiest and most prominent monasteries in ladakh. the monastery, which dates back to the 17th century, plays a crucial role in the spiritual and cultural life of the region, where you can witness vibrant festivals and religious ceremonies throughout the year.

here is one of the several entrances to tjiuca park, where the horto waterfalls complex is located. there are several - (1) quebra, (2) chuveiro, (3) jequitiba, etc. they are located on the solar da imperatriz-parque lage section of the transcarioca trail. the first waterfall (quebra) here is right at the entrance. a rather difficult trail leads to the next 2: chuveiro ('shower waterfall) and jequitiba, only for physically fit people and in proper non-slip footwear. not suitable for small children. the path is steep, rocky, requires a bit of climbing in several places and sticking to the chain. after 3 waterfalls, the trail joins the transcarioca trail and becomes a bit easier.

hidden among the lush jungle and overlooking the turquoise waters of the caribbean, sagrada tulum is a place where the spiritual and the historical converge in the heart of the ancient city of tulum, mexico. often referred to as the "sacred tulum," this site is a focal point of reverence, mystery, and legend. unlike the more prominent temples and ruins, sagrada tulum is a serene and lesser-known gem that offers a profound connection to the spiritual legacy of the maya civilization. sagrada tulum is believed to have been a central spiritual site within the larger tulum complex, serving as a sacred space where rituals, prayers, and offerings were made to the gods. the maya, known for their deep reverence for nature and the cosmos, saw places like sagrada tulum as bridges between the earthly realm and the divine. here, they would seek guidance, protection, and blessings from their pantheon of deities. the site’s architecture, though modest in comparison to the grand temples like el castillo, is marked by its simplicity and harmony with the natural surroundings. constructed from the region’s ubiquitous limestone, the structures at sagrada tulum blend seamlessly with the landscape, symbolizing the maya’s belief in the interconnectedness of all things. the use of natural elements in the construction and the orientation of the buildings suggests a deliberate alignment with celestial events, reflecting the maya’s sophisticated knowledge of astronomy. one of the most intriguing aspects of sagrada tulum is its role as a place of healing. historical records and archaeological findings indicate that the site was a sanctuary for those seeking physical and spiritual healing. the maya believed that certain locations possessed natural energies that could be harnessed for curing ailments and restoring balance. sagrada tulum was one such place, where priests and healers would perform rituals to invoke the healing powers of the earth and the gods. as with many sacred sites in the maya world, sagrada tulum is steeped in legends that have been passed down through generations. one of the most enduring tales is that of the heart of the earth, a powerful crystal said to be hidden within the sacred grounds of sagrada tulum. according to legend, this crystal was a gift from the gods, imbued with the power to heal the sick and protect the city from harm. it was said to glow with an inner light, pulsating with the heartbeat of the earth itself. the legend tells of a maya priestess, known as ixchel, who was the guardian of the heart of the earth. she was revered for her healing abilities and her deep connection to the gods. it is said that during a time of great drought and sickness, ixchel used the crystal to restore life to the land and heal the people of tulum. the gods, impressed by her devotion, granted her eternal life so that she could continue to protect the crystal and the sacred site. even after her death, it is believed that ixchel’s spirit remains at sagrada tulum, watching over the crystal and those who come to seek its power. visitors to the site have reported feeling a deep sense of peace and well-being, as if the energy of the heart of the earth still radiates through the stones and the surrounding jungle. another legend speaks of the song of the wind, a haunting melody that is said to be heard on certain nights when the wind blows through the ruins. the maya believed that this song was the voice of the gods, a reminder of their presence and a call to the faithful to remember their teachings. some say that the song is a guide for lost souls, leading them back to the sacred site where they can find peace and redemption.

hiking diamond head was one of the highlights of our trip to oahu. the trail is well-maintained and manageable for most fitness levels, though there are a few steep sections and stairs toward the top that definitely get your heart pumping. be sure to bring water and wear proper shoes—it can get hot, especially midday. the views from the summit are absolutely breathtaking. overlooking waikīkī and the vast pacific ocean, it’s the kind of panoramic view that makes the effort totally worth it. there are plenty of spots at the top to take photos and just soak it all in. the path can get crowded, so going early in the morning is a great way to beat both the heat and the crowds. parking is limited, but there are also walking paths and bus stops nearby if you’re coming without a car. whether you’re into hiking or just want a memorable vantage point, diamond head is a must-do on oahu. it’s a great mix of history, nature, and stunning scenery.

history and adventure all in one for my bucket list. parts of the underground canals and rivers date back to 1652. they used to supply the passing ships with fresh water. later these rivers flowing through the city became pleasant walkways shaded by oaks with bridges going over them. as the years passed and the city expanded they were eventually covered up and forgotten. cape town was once known as the little amsterdam in a foreign country.

history says that the cave is used by king ravana to hide the princess sita. located about 2 km from the ella town. the cave lies on the foundation of a cliff, and is one of the great tourist attractions in sri lanka with a historical value. excavations within this historical cave revealed evidence of human habitation dating back to 20,000 bc. the cave lies 1, 370 meters (4, 490 ft) above sea level, and measures 50 ft wide, 150 ft long and 60ft high. the cave is also believed to be connected to the cave in dowa rock temple in badulla. the network of caves and tunnels are all man made, connected to all the important cities and served as swift secret passage ways through the mountains.

hoanib made our skeleton coast dreams come true!!! my husband and i have wanted to come check out this extreme landscape for a decade and were finally able to make the trip. our stay with hoanib was just perfect. the camp is extremely tasteful and comfortable, the food was delicious and very well-portioned, and we loved that everything is run on solar and the decor blends in so well with the landscape. the staff was simply spectacular, especially our guide, charles! he knew everything about everything, was an excellent driver and very easy going. we also spent a lot of time with thereza over gin and tonics - i felt like i could be friends with her if we lived in the same city! the day trip to the skeleton coast was a highlight, as was the fascinating brown hyena talk that an on-site biologist gives (do not miss it!). another highlight was getting to do some hikes around camp with charles, thereza and brighton! finally, we loved our pilot, andre!! great, smooth flight and such a charming guy. all in all, we had such a great time and strongly recommend hoanib to anyone looking for something different from the traditional safari experience.

holy cow, such a big and beautiful city park with so much to do and see in it. plenty of meadows and picnic areas to enjoy, a lot of trails to walk with so many plants and flowers that you'd think the park was the botanical garden but actually that's just a part of the park that's also very much worth visiting.

holy moly this was the funniest tour i’ve ever been on. we’ve seen a lot of magnificent places and our driver nick drove excellent and even took us on an adventurous ride through one of the scenes. he also searched for gold with us which was successful for everyone. the tour was not just about lord of the rings, we also got some extra history knowledge about the places we drove past. it’s safe to say that we had a great time with our guide and i am looking forward to seeing him again. *part 2 here we go again, second time. if i could give 5 and a half star i would. this trip just had that special ick for a lord of the rings fan. this time around we actually were at the scenes, which was a bit rare at the first half (not anyone’s fault of course). we got to see a lot more places which also were a bit more iconic at times. when we made a break, nick took out some prop swords and capes and we posed a little in front of minas tirith. from a fan perspective this part of the trip was definitely the best. a tourist might find the first one better because of some unrelated activities like gold searching or the rocky and bumpy drive through the river. no matter which one was better, nick was always on point. he’s very talkative and always finds something to talk about, whether that’s history facts or some neat little detail about lotr. i would recommend this trip to anyone and pray for you to get nick as your driver.

holy. first time hiker here and that was challenging. the trek up the mountain will make you stop every few steps to rethink your decisions and maybe turn back but don't!! persevere! the yongsil track is the most beautiful and scenic hiking trail i hallasan mountain and it is worth it once you get to the witsil oreum. bring a wind breaker because it gets so windy at the top and good walking shoes with some grip on em. there are a lot of rocks and steps!!! those with some fear of heights may want to rethink climbing it because of how there are some parts of the trail that really just overlook the bottom. it truly makes you realise how amazing, beautiful and gigantic hallasan is and how small you are in retrospect.

hom spa cartagena is a great place to come when you are in cartagena. my massage therapist was jade and she is by far the best there is. she creates a calming and welcoming atmosphere that puts you at ease. what sets jade apart is her attention to detail and genuine care. after each session, i walk away feeling not just relaxed but truly restored.

honestly, i didn’t expect to enjoy the dubai frame this much — but it totally surprised me! the views from the top are absolutely insane… one side you see the old dubai, and the other side is all the shiny skyscrapers. it really makes you appreciate how far the city has come. the glass floor was such a cool (and slightly nerve-wracking 😅) experience — definitely a fun moment if you’re with friends or family. the little museum at the beginning was also really well done and gives some nice context before you head up. my 1.5 year old loved walking on the glass walk!!! it’s super organized, clean, and surprisingly quick to get in and out, even with tourists around. i’d definitely recommend going around golden hour for the best views. worth a visit whether you live here or you’re just passing through!

honestly, it just has such a vibe. i'd heard about it forever, but we just never made it until now. we went with the whole family, and it was seriously amazing.i went in thinking we'd spend, like, an hour in there, maybe two tops, just snag a few silly photos and head out. but dude, we totally lost track of time! we ended up staying for well over two hours, just cracking up and snapping pictures. seriously, it's mind-blowing how those illusions work. we were all just posing, laughing, and totally became kids again, just fully immersed in all the crazy scenes. and get this, it wasn't just the little ones—the kids and us adults had an equally fantastic time. it's genuinely something everyone can enjoy together. it's such a unique and memorable experience. highly, highly recommend it for a fun family day out.

honestly, it was a really great musuem. a lot of interesting info about the modern (and ancient) olympics, cool visuals as well as a beautifully designed museum. it mostly catere to adults but kids can have fun as well! we were the only tourists present at our arrival (and maybe saw 8 other tourists during the visit), i can't imagine why not more people are visiting this! it was really nice and for sure one of the highlights to our trip. if you are doubting to visit due to the distance from the city center, don't, its worthwhile! i even recommend taking the metro, as the metrostop is across the olympic village, and you can take a cool walk through the olympic village to get to the museum. all in all, strongly recommended!

honestly, there’s nothing particularly special about these gardens—i guess i was expecting more. that said, it’s still a nice place for a walk before or after visiting the palace, since you’re already there. the plants, flowers, and greenery really depend on the season, so the overall impression might vary depending on when you go.

honestly, this mall has all the stores that you could ever need… except that you’ll never find them because the architect must have been tripping balls when he designed this outline lol. almost all of the stores have curved edges and there’s lots of floors, but no maps. you can’t even see around the corner before it’s too late. i wish i could say i’d never go here again, but this mall has all of the easy shopping stores and franchises from around the world. it’s a nightmare, but i’m sure i’ll go again 😂 are the photos nice? yes. will i be trapped forever? also yes 👏

honestly, visiting the empire state building was such a cool experience. you always see it in movies and pictures, but standing there in person feels completely different. the building is massive, and the lobby inside is beautiful. everything is set up really well for tourists, so it doesn’t feel too confusing even though there are a lot of people. the museum on the way up was actually pretty fun. i didn’t think i’d care much about it, but it shows how the building was made and all the history behind it, which makes the visit feel more special. then the elevator ride to the top is super quick—it’s kind of exciting how fast it goes. the view from the top is unreal. you can see the whole city, from central park to the statue of liberty, and even out into new jersey. i went in the afternoon and stayed until it got dark, and that was the best choice because you get both the daytime city view and then the night skyline all lit up, which is amazing. it’s a little pricey, but honestly worth it for the experience and the views. definitely something you should do at least once if you’re in new york.

hong kong disneyland castle hub: a magical entrance ★★★★★ the hong kong disneyland castle hub is the heart of the park and a truly magical sight. the castle itself is a stunning architectural masterpiece, towering over the surrounding lands. the castle hub is a bustling hub of activity, with visitors from all over the world gathering to take photos, enjoy performances, and simply soak up the disney atmosphere. the surrounding areas are well-maintained, with beautiful landscaping and themed decorations. a highlight of the castle hub is the nightly light show, which transforms the castle into a dazzling spectacle of light and sound. it's a truly unforgettable experience. overall, the hong kong disneyland castle hub is a must-visit for any disney fan. it's a magical place that captures the essence of disney and creates lasting memories.

hong kong disneyland shines as a compact, culturally rich disney park with standout attractions like world of frozen, mystic manor, iron man, and the elegant castle of magical dreams. a perfect blend of classic charm and modern innovation, especially for families and disney lovers. to make the most of your visit: consider arriving early, using fast passes, pacing yourself across one day, and setting expectations around dining and peak crowds.

hong kong ocean park is one of the highlights of our trip and i personally didn't regret visiting the place rather than disneyland. my friends and i were so lucky to see the sloth, panda, and the arctic fox up close. we also tried a couple of their rides which we really enjoyed. the place is perfect especially for people who have motion sickness as the place has a variety of activities to enjoy. i would love to go back here with my family next time.

honor a ponce de leon! eternal glory to our distinguished adventurer! visiting the tomb of the illustrious juan ponce de león in the cathedral of san juan bautista is to relive the greatness of the spanish empire at its maximum splendor. the majesty of the sepulcher is worthy of puerto rico's first governor. here lies the man who sought the fountain of youth but found something more valuable: immortality in the history of the magnificent spanish empire. this cathedral, witness to hispanic civilization in the caribbean, guards the remains of one who represented the eternal values of hispanidad. every stone of this temple speaks of that glorious time when the sun never set on our territories, when puerto rico was a fundamental part of spain.

honorio helped us with booking a trip to isle mujeres and it was an unforgettable experience. all we can drink on the way there and we got to snorkel on our way to the island. the island is so beautiful and the water is really clear. we spent 3 hours at the beach and get back on the boat. highly recommended and it’s worth the $130 a ticket.

hoodoos trail offers a stunning hike with plenty to see along the way. there are at least three different scenic points worth visiting, and i highly recommend making time to explore them all. each viewpoint provides a unique perspective, whether it's a closer look at the towering hoodoos or a breathtaking bird's-eye view of the lake in the valley below. the natural beauty of the surroundings makes this trail an unforgettable experience. that said, the trail can be a bit challenging, especially if youare hiking with children. the path has several inclines, and it’s not well suited for strollers, so be prepared if you're bringing young kids. there are a few benches and chairs scattered along the trail where you can stop to rest, which is a welcome relief during the steeper sections. we did not hike all the way to the base of the lake, but based on what we saw and the pace of the trail, it would likely take an hour or more to reach it. even without going all the way down, the views from the upper points are more than worth the effort. overall, this trail is a rewarding experience for nature lovers and hiking enthusiasts alike.

hop on hop off bus tour offers a lot of attractions on the way where you can explore in one's own time and join another bus when you are done. great opportunity to sit back and listen to the history of cape town, watch beautiful scenery.

how do you really rate something as unique as the thăng long water puppet theater? to be honest, i was initially disappointed that the 8:00 pm show we wanted to see was sold out two days in advance. we barely managed to grab seats for the next night’s 8:00 pm show—and when we arrived, it was packed wall to wall, sold out again. and for good reason. the show was simply amazing. my first experience was 20 years ago, and sitting there again brought me right back—i felt like a kid. this time, i had the joy of watching my son experience it for the first time, and he was moved beyond words. it’s not just a show—it’s a blend of culture, history, music, and magic on water. one minor (but notable) issue: the seating is a bit low, so depending on where you're seated, the head of the person in front of you might block part of the view. but honestly, even that couldn’t take away from the performance. it’s easy to see why it’s sold out so often. absolutely recommended. i could watch it again and again.

hulhumale rashu market, located in phase 1 of hulhumale, is a convenient and lively place for daily shopping. it offers a mix of essential services and local charm. one of the key features of this market is the presence of a maldives islamic bank (mib) atm, making banking and cash withdrawals easy for shoppers. the market also includes a few cozy cafés serving short eats, perfect for a quick snack or tea break. local vendors sell a variety of fresh vegetables, fruits, and all types of coconuts—ideal for cooking, drinking, or making coconut-based products. whether you're a resident or a visitor, the hulhumale local market is a great spot to experience the local lifestyle and shop for fresh produce and daily essentials.

hunder sand dunes are an absolutely unique and amazing place located in the nubra valley of ladakh. these sand dunes, located at an altitude of around 4,000 meters, are a striking feature of this cold desert region, contrasting with the rugged snow capped mountains and the shyok river. this area is known for its white, silver sand, bactrian camels (double-humped camels) and the surreal experience of an arid desert amidst snow-capped mountains. it is a very popular tourist destination where you can also enjoy riding on a bactarian double humped camel and watch some traditional ladaki folk dances and performances as well. a must visit place when visiting the beautiful nubra valley in ladakh.

hung hom kwun yum temple is a historically significant and culturally revered temple in hong kong, dedicated to kwun yum (guan yin), the goddess of mercy. she is widely worshipped by those seeking blessings for prosperity, success, and protection from misfortune. inside the temple, the statue of kwun yum is enshrined as the primary deity, drawing devotees who come to pay their respects and offer prayers. additionally, the temple houses other revered chinese deities, such as cai shen (the god of wealth) and yu huang (the jade emperor), making it a spiritually significant site for a variety of blessings. however, one notable aspect of the temple is the heavy presence of incense smoke, which can make breathing uncomfortable and cause eye irritation. the temple is frequently filled with worshippers lighting incense sticks as offerings, resulting in a thick haze throughout the premises. visitors who are sensitive to smoke or have respiratory concerns may find it beneficial to bring a mask or a cloth to cover their nose and mouth. overall, hung hom kwun yum temple is a deeply spiritual and sacred place, offering a profound cultural and religious experience. while the overwhelming incense smoke may be a challenge for some, those who can tolerate it will find the temple a meaningful destination for worship and reflection in hong kong.

hyangwonjeong pavilion is a beautiful two-story hexagonal pavilion located within the grounds of gyeongbokgung palace in seoul, south korea. it was built in 1873 by king gojong and is situated on a small island in the middle of hyangwonji pond, connected to the main palace grounds by a wooden bridge known as chwihyanggyo. the name "hyangwonjeong" translates to "pavilion of far-reaching fragrance," reflecting the serene and tranquil setting. the pavilion is a prime example of traditional korean architecture, blending harmoniously with the surrounding nature, and is particularly stunning during the spring and autumn seasons when the pond is surrounded by blooming flowers or colorful fall foliage. visitors can admire the pavilion from the surrounding area, but direct access to the pavilion and bridge is typically restricted to preserve its historical integrity. the pavilion is a popular spot for photography due to its picturesque reflection on the water and the overall peaceful atmosphere it creates. hyangwonjeong pavilion is located towards the northern section of gyeongbokgung palace, so visitors should allow time to walk through the palace grounds to reach it. it’s a quieter part of the palace compared to the main halls, offering a tranquil space for reflection. while visiting gyeongbokgung palace, exploring the hyangwonjeong pavilion area is highly recommended, especially for those looking to capture the scenic beauty of traditional korean architecture set against a natural backdrop.

i absolutely love mackenzie house! off the beaten tourist track, this wonderful spot in toronto celebrates william lyon mackenzie, one of canada’s greatest (and under appreciated) reformers. if you cherish history and are devoted to democracy, this is a must-visit. the house is beautifully preserved and offers a fascinating look into the 1860s. while younger kids may squirm with boredom through the house, adults will find the stories engaging. a standout feature is the historic printing press demonstration, showcasing the era's journalism. it's also worth noting that mackenzie fought for the abolition of slavery and worked with mary ann shadd a pioneer in her own right, being the first woman and first black printmaker in north america. despite some recent damage from a leak, the city has done well to keep the house open. if you cherish history, mackenzie house is a true treasure! and yes, that’s my caricature of the one and only william lyon mackenzie.

i absolutely love the saladin citadel. it’s one of my favorite historical sites in egypt. the architecture is breathtaking, and the sense of history is truly powerful—you can feel the weight of centuries in every stone. walking through its courtyards and looking out over the city is an unforgettable experience. that said, my visit was tainted by a strange encounter with security at the entrance. i was stopped for my id, which is fine, but then i was asked a series of weird and intrusive questions—like “why are you here?” and “are you meeting anyone?” they even asked if i live in egypt. to make things worse, they held onto my id and told me i wasn’t allowed to enter alone. eventually, they did let me in, but i had to retrieve my id on the way out. it was honestly unsettling. i came to enjoy a historic site, not be interrogated like i did something wrong. the citadel deserves better visitor management—especially for solo guests. still, the site itself is worth visiting. just be prepared for some unexpected questioning if you’re going alone.

i absolutely love the singer, but the museum doesn't really have much to offer. there were few pictures, dresses umm wore, and a few medals achieved throughout her incredible life. it takes 10mins to visit the whole thing so a bit disappointing. was sitting outside for a while as the views of the river nile from the outside park are truly beautiful but then the staff from nilometer told me i need to buy another ticket for nilometer to sit in the park which sounded ridiculous since it's part of the actual umms museum. so not sure if they tried to make me pay additional money or you actually had to pay to sit outside! so i left the place annoyed. i think you will learn about umm more from the internet than the museum, especially since they don't even play her music inside.

i am a local and these 3 stars represent a long-term frustration on how wenceslas looks like. a beautifully restored museum & a statue of saint wenceslas overlooking an avenue that functions more as a parking place. i'm definitely most excited to finally see work is being done transforming it into a public space for people similarly to what you see in the lower part of the square. if you're visiting prague, please be advised that the upper portion of the square (from the top down until midway to můstek) is undergoing a complete renovation but mind you all businesses, shops, subway stations on both sides are open. if you're driving then many parking places are now unavailable as you see in the photos. the works will reintroduce trams with car traffic drastically restricted. this 1st phase of the project started in may2024 with about 3+ years to complete. have a safe trip and next time we'll be posting pics of a much nicer place...

i am posting this review late because even months later i am thinking about what an incredible experience i had with phernando at larimar concept. from the moment we met at the boat, phernando, was incredibly friendly, warm hearted, full of interesting information and positive energy. my girlfriend and i had one of the best days on the boat touring the island and seeing incredible wildlife. phernando cooked us an unbelievable lunch. the captain was excellent. the day was perfect. i can’t wait to spend more time in fernando de noronha with phernando. now a friend of ours. come visit me in chicago phernando! let me show you the same hospitality you showed us.

i am rarely writing recensions but during this cooking class we have got so much personal attention by the team of the reveal angkor hotel so that this is a heartfelt wish to write this one. we have been with four people in siem reap for just few days and by some circumstances that are hardly to describe we tried to find a cooking class very spontaneously. the first contact in the afternoon to the hotel by email was answered very quickly and because of the flexibility of the hotel we could unsophisticatedly find an arrangement for the same evening. when arriving at the hotel we were cordially received, got a detailed explanation about the evening and then could start. typically the cooking class includes a shopping tour on the local market to buy all the food and other ingredients needed for the meal. since our cooking class was late and the market was already closed we skipped this but everything that we needed was there and placed well-arranged on the table. the menu that we prepared had 4 dishes. the explanation and the support of the master chef was great and also the management was involved to not have just a cooking class but to get a sustainable cooking experience. of course we have had our own cooking result as a dinner which was a very delicious one. we could enjoy the meal (same as its preparation) in a relaxed atmosphere and we all were glad about this evening. thank you very much to teng and your team! marcus

i am rating this trail between moderate and hard, trending towards hard because although the terrain is flat, the complete lack of cover from the sun made it quite challenging, heat-wise. when there was cloud cover the heat was fine. there are some portions of the trail that are covered in beach sand which adds to the challenge. despite the heat, my family (including my 10 year old) loved the trail and we spent over 5 hours in total there as we took our time on the way back, stopping to swim in tide pools and at the sandy/coral beach. highly recommend taking dips to cool off along the way. we would do this in both directions next time if we returned on a similarly sunny day. we saw 3 seals and several albatross.
i am reviewing the food stall 25. a freaking amazing seafood quesadilla and jambalaya. so flavorful and delicious!

i am so astounded by how insanely affordable the prices were for a) the quality (as in taste) of the food, and b) how filling the portions were—especially the cheesesteak, which was quite hefty and loaded. i had the grilled chicken saj, and my favourite part was definitely the garlic sauce on the side. the flavour wasn’t overpowering but worked well with the potatoes and pita. the grilled pita was also a highlight for me, but i do wish that the chicken was a bit more flavourful. they did not skimp out on the fillings however, which i appreciate. the cheesesteak was also great, i loved how warmmm and comforting it was and how soft the bun was.

i am so confused and suspect this is a scam. there is a cash box, a basket with sarongs and a guest book at the entry. it was my understanding that you make a donation to rent the sarong for your visit. when we walked up to the entry 2 locals who were sitting further up the road with a group of men called out at us. they then started to approach us and in very broken english tried to tell us there was a minimum donation of 20k per person. as there is no information or signage at the box, i was a bit suspicious of their motivation and they became very aggressive when i started to ask questions. my wife had already picked up a sarong as we were about to make our donation when they approached. he snatched it from her and started to yell at her. after a really nice day exploring the area, this experience was really confronting and my family felt very threatened by their behavior. they had no identification and their aggressive behavior makes this feel very much like a scam. i would not recommend a visit to this temple, it’s not worth the hassle.
i am so excited that i was able to visit before the tours ended for the year. thank you, cabarfeidh, for opening a small portion of your life to us.

i am so glad that we chose west end on the thames to celebrate our anniversary with family and friends. from our initial enquiry through to the day itself the service has been professional, helpful and thoughtful. throughout the planning eliza and the team really took time to listen and understand what we were hoping for and we were certainly not disappointed! on the day itself we couldn't have been better looked after by eliza and her team. we have had so many lovely messages from our guests who, like us, had a fantastic time. thank you to all at west end on the thames, i can't recommend you highly enough!

i am so grateful that i chose divers den to learn how to scuba dive on the great barrier reef (name a better classroom than that!). through the 6 day 3 night padi open water & advanced course offered here, i spent 2 days learning in their pool facility and classroom. the remaining 4 days and the next 3 nights were spent on the great barrier reef on their liveaboard vessel. this was truly an experience of a lifetime, and i am so thankful for my instructors audrey and jonathon for their knowledge, persistence, and passion. the entire crew on the liveaboard vessel was extremely hardworking and ensured everyone's safety and comfort. i am now a confident advanced scuba diver because of divers den and their amazing team!

i am so happy i skipped the gym this day. now this is what we call a five-star experience! we originally planned to spend just a couple of hours at aeroxspace adventure, but we’re so glad we chose the full-day pass—we ended up staying for nearly five hours and loved every minute. the activities were genuinely challenging and fun, offering a great mix of physical and mental games that kept both kids and adults engaged. we tried just about everything, and each zone offered something unique and exciting. the staff were fantastic—friendly, patient, and always ready to help. a special shoutout to the team who helped us recover my wife's apple watch after it fell into one of the foam pits. they took the time to carefully search and eventually found it—truly above-and-beyond service. the food was surprisingly great for an activity center, and the overall vibe was energetic and upbeat, just what you’d hope for in a place like this. ☁️ if you’re looking for a break from bali’s sun and surf, or if the weather turns rainy, this is a perfect alternative. 💰 money well spent and memories well made. highly recommended!

i am so happy to find a local / farmer market in berlin. they open from 09:00 - 15:30. the market is big and sells various things: veggies, fruits, herbs, plants, cheese, fresh fish, fresh meat, clothes, handmade jewelry, and many more. surprisingly found a food truck selling kibbeling 🐟🫶🏻 cant wait next week to explore more!

i am solo traveller and i booked a full day tour to wadi bani khalid and wahiba asand desert. khalil was my guide, he was veru accommodating and kind and make sure i am comfortable during my trip. i was amazed with the beauty of the desert it was very relaxing and peaceful. thanks to my kind guide khalil. highly appreciated.

i am thrilled to express my heartfelt gratitude for the extraordinary journey curated by local safaris africa. this south african gem not only unveils the marvels of africa but also crafts a global odyssey, making every moment a tapestry of awe and wonder. exceptional service, unparalleled adventures – they redefine the art of travel. highly recommended for those seeking an extraordinary exploration of our world.

i am truly amazed with the service given by go dubai desert safari. we have booked at 8.30 but somehow there's trouble that we couldn't get there on time and finally we made it at 9.30. however, the drivers were very understanding about the situation that we had, always smiling whenever we talked. the only question that the driver asked was "are you all happy?". the hospitality is at top level, they have served us with kindness and friendliness. they took a lot of our pictures proactively. i could say that this is the best decision ever to go with go desert safari. best service, best price, best trip, best experience!

i am usually not a beach person, however from the moment i set foot on the shore of hongjodangoe haebin beach on udo, jeju, i was captivated! the sand was incredibly white, made of crushed coral, and sparkled beautifully against the turquoise sea. walking on it felt like stepping on powdered jewels, unlike any other beach i've ever been to. what elevates hongjodangoe haebin beach to a truly celestial level is the surrounding landscape. the dramatic volcanic cliffs that frame the beach provide a stunning backdrop. beyond the visual splendor, there's a palpable sense of peace and serenity that permeates the air. it's a place where time seems to slow down, allowing you to fully absorb the beauty and tranquility. whether you choose to simply relax on the shore (something i surprisingly found myself doing) take a refreshing dip, or explore the fascinating rock formations, hongjodangoe haebin beach offers an unparalleled escape from the everyday. in summary, my experience at hongjodangoe haebin beach was nothing short of divine. as someone who typically avoids beaches, i can wholeheartedly say that i fell in love with this beautiful place. it's a place of breathtaking beauty, profound tranquility, and an undeniable connection to the raw power and artistry of nature. if you ever find yourself on udo, jeju, a visit to this extraordinary beach is not just recommended – it's an absolute necessity for the soul. five out of five stars – a true gem of the korean peninsula that even converted me, a non-beach-lover!

i am very glad that we took this tour of the whole island minus the west side. justin our tour guide was such a delight and very insightful. i learned a lot about the island and highly recommend you do this tour especially if it’s your first time in hawaii. you get to see hanauma bay which is breathtaking and snorkeling with the turtles.

i am very grateful that i found my way to andrea. right from the start i felt understood and in good hands. her empathetic nature and professional approach helped me make positive changes in my life. i can warmly recommend andrea to anyone who is looking for trustworthy and competent support.

i am very happy with the services we got at this place and i highly recommend it to anyone visiting marrakech. the hammam was performed by fatima and aicha and the massage was performed by rajoe and kawtan. clean place, they greet you with tea and provide cold water for you at all times, this place deserves a 10. all perfect and highly recommended .

i am very happy with this place. this was my first time in the mara national park and it was beautiful. the camp is beautifully decorated and very clean. i felt completely safe and i enjoyed every day. the food was very fresh, there was always a buffet on offer and we could choose what to eat. the food was mostly based on vegetables and fruit. there was meat with every meal but we all preferred to choose their fresh fruits. the avocado was the most delicious avocado i have ever tasted. the people who work at the camp are very friendly and are always on the move to help you with anything you need. i recommend leaving a tip because these people really deserve it. all the employees are from the maasai tribe and are very fun and cheerful. in the evening when it gets dark, someone always follows you to the owl because the tents are arranged so that everyone has their own privacy and are 15 meters apart from each other. the camp is very nicely decorated and provides a space for work where you can also have a coffee or some other drink on the way. the atmosphere is always great and the view of the greenery makes you constantly happy. i will definitely come back again and choose this camp again. all praise for the owners and employees! a clear 5!

i attended all 3 workshops in april/may 2019 with the lovely wikitoria oman, it was the most amazing spiritual experience of my life, not only to learn ancient gifts passed down, but also to have breakthrough releases of trauma/kehua/and makutu during my own healing session. wikitoria is so humble in her mahi, and very masterful and intuitive in her skills. she was able to release blockages for me that no other healers have been able to and found things others were not aware of. i found her loving caring wairua spirit made it easier to trust not only in her but in myself to release a lot of blockages and trust in my own capabilities as a light worker. i feel like a completely different person, and have even noticed physical changes in myself and thought patterns. it is an cultural/spiritual experience i think all who try can only benefit from. nga mihi.

i booked a tour last minute and they were very accommodating and very helpful! i highly recommend! the tour was lovely, it was their xc tour. i like that these guys adjust the tour according to the level of the riders. in my group there was myself, a german lady, and a man and woman from netherlands. everyone was wonderful. it was a beautiful day, i was grateful we had fantastic weather. i think the beginning of the tour was a bit much of pointless pedaling lol. but that was fine since the scenery and environment was really new and amazing to me. i'm very glad i booked a tour, this place seems really different than other places i've ridden. madeira island doesn't seem like an area with a vast trail network in one location where i can just park a car and go ride around all day, like other places i've traveled to. it seems more like a series of shorter connected tracks via fire roads or regular roads. that are ridden one after another. at least that's my experience on this tour and what i was guessing based on looking at trail forks. so, if i was to ride alone it seems like a shuttle situation is needed, or a really long ride uphill back to the car lol. i think it's always beneficial to ride with people who know this area. and all the trails we ride on tour are legal trails so that is good! i got picked up in funchal in the morning and we picked up the other people too and then went to the top of the mountain to start the ride. the guide ride with us and the driver stayed with the van and trailer followed us down the whole time so we can leave our bags and items in the van, and people always can go and drink some water if they left their bottle in the van. another great thing about this tour is, they took pictures and videos of us! that was so cool and unexpected! i almost always ride alone so i never have pics of me riding. haha! that was a treat! overall this was a great day and a great tour and i recommend booking a tour with this company!
i booked a tour to santa fe. really nice experience can definitely recommend!

i booked an 8 am tour on sunday the night before for a group of four. we were paired in a total group size of eight with our tour guide named julio. he was extremely knowledgeable, funny, and enthusiastic in answering our questions. because of him we were able to see many different animals and wildlife that we wouldn’t have been able to spot otherwise. you can tell he truly enjoys his job as his energy is just so rich and positive. while we were a group of adults, i personally felt like a kid again. the trail was beautifully maintained, yet it preserved the beautiful nature for the wildlife to prosper. i’m so grateful for the experience and to the owners of this park for conserving the land. the hanging bridges were also extremely safe and sturdy. definitely book this to learn more about the wildlife in costa rica! you won’t regret it.

i booked an hour massage appointment for me and my lady before our vacation ended. wish i booked sooner so that i could of experience it twice. a very nice location with a lovely spa decor, colors, & natural lighting that is located in a safe area. the staff was very professional, & the massage felt soooo gooood🙌🏾. thank you to isabel, maddy, & the staff for an experience. * highly recommend *

i booked it through booking.com, and the one-hour tour was totally worth it! the guide shared a lot about the architecture and history, and we passed by so many great photo spots. the cheese platter was really big and super tasty, and the rosé made the whole experience feel really relaxing. the only downside was that the boat we were on didn’t have windows that opened, so it felt a bit stuffy. but overall, it was a great experience. next time, i definitely want to try the evening cruise to see the canal lights at night! the staff were very thoughtful, and the explanations were super clear and informative. highly recommend it!

i booked the 3 day enduro tour offered by uyuni motorcycle tours. robin the owner & guide of the company has a lifetime of enduro experience. he knows the area as the back of his hand, guiding us through the best tracks and points of interest in the mountains. robin is helpful and will set up the tour based on the preferences and experience of the riders. along the way robin tells stories about the local culture, nature, history, and his dakar experience, which gives the tour a depth on top of the amazing off-road riding through the andes. we ride approx 250 km + every day, most of which off-road. the day starts at 9 am. by 6 pm we are back from a long day drive, to relax in a good accomodation. i can totally recommended uyuni motorcycle tours, if you wish to discover the salt plain & mountains surrounding uyuni and have a great enduro experience.

i booked the caribbean ritual and it was the best decision i ever made. the massage was so relaxing. the staff was so nice! i arrived early and was quite sweaty from my walk. they gave me water and allowed me to cool down and accommodated my early arrival! this was truly one of the best massage experiences i’ve had and would recommend everyone try it. plus, it’s so affordable!

i booked the city canal cruise through getyourguide during my visit to amsterdam in june of 2024. if you're looking for a really laid back tour of the canals i definitely recommend doing this tour. the staff were all really friendly and very helpful when answering questions. they provide audio devices and headphones that will play the pre-recorded tour in many different languages. i really enjoyed learning about the city, the canals, and the history!

i booked the exclusive group booking for my friends hens party. the staff wer3 so wonderful both during the booking process and on the day of our treatments. they made all of us, especially the bride feel so pampered. included in our booking was tea, coffee, and juice with a platter of snacks. there was 6 of and we each got to choose a spa treatment as well as use the complimentary spa pool and sauna. i myself booked a massage with jot and she was so talented. i felt like a whole new person after. the other staff including our host, nikola and other employees soti and orlin were fabulous as well. will definitely be back!

i booked the fez tour based on the reviews and we couldn’t be happier! mohamed was very knowledgeable and helpful, his english was great! and he speaks many languages. we had lots of great conversations while we learned. we highly recommend this tour and mohamed in particular! many thanks, fez city tour

i booked the five island trip for 72eur and it was well organized, but for this price i expected also to enter island aux aigrettes if you are so close at it! they should book entrance and a tour on it for everyone in my opinion and include it in the trip.

i booked the half day tour to fitzroy island and really enjoyed it! the team on the boat were super friendly and pointed out manta rays in the sea. we got really lucky and saw 3 manta rays just from the boat! i had a fantastic time snorkelling the great barrier reef, the water wasy so clear and the reef is so colourful so much sea life. this is a great day out and i’d highly recommend

i booked the top deck experience for me and my partner katharine (couple in our 30s from sf). i read a lot of reviews and wasn’t sure about the feedback on the age of the boat and the food etc. for us, those complaints were off base - the whole thing exceeded our expectations. all of the staff are like genuine friends and it makes the atmosphere fun and supportive. the communication was clear, the structure of the day gets you lots of chances to snorkel or dive, every staff member will help you with any issue. the food was plentiful and solid considering we’re out on the ocean. the room was clean and light. we slept great on the bed. the highlight of the whole thing was being paired with juan as our top deck host and personal dive instructor. we really had the most amazing time and felt so taken care of. i would recommend the upgrade to anyone nervous about diving. he’s charismatic, knowledgeable, patient (also handsome). he spent extra time with us getting us comfortable with the dive. he led katharine by the hand when she was less confident. he encouraged us to do more and found a a ton of great coral and fish to look at. he even explained everything we saw under water after the dive. it’s just a really great experience. you have to understand that it’s a boat from 1986 and not a 5* hotel in new york. if you have reasonable expectations they will be comfortably exceeded. so much fun!

i booked the traditional hammam and 45 minute massage. it is on the pricier side and i compared to a lot of other hammams offering a private experience. i did opt for this spa based on the positive reviews and the longer massage component as hammam is not necessarily meant to be relaxing. my booking did go over by 30 minutes (so 1 hour for hammam and 1 hour for massage including a small break in the middle for snacks and rehydration) not that i am complaining! the experience was really good and i can’t recommend it enough. the riad garden for after treatment tea is also stunning with some very friendly tortoises!

i booked this camp for my trip, due to certain reasons i couldn't go for this trip! i requested them for a refund.. they promised me they'll refund within a week, and it's been 12 days today of no response and no refund. tbh, i didn't even expected them to refund my amount, just took a chance at it and they promised me, but after our 1st conversation when they promised me, the manager lady became rude and then since then i've called and messaged her so many times, yet no reply and no refund.

i booked this flight online with little research and went into it with a little hesitation. it was amazing! from the shuttle picking us up from the hotel, to the staff in the waiting area, and our amazing captain. everything felt so safe and it made the experience very enjoyable. our captain was awesome the whole experience was amazing. when i was booking this experience, someone commented “don’t think, just do it” and that is exactly what i was thinking the whole time. i would go back again in a heartbeat. just do it!!
