i did the clear kayak. it was a fantastic experience. also they were so nice! it was fun to do and even if you’re not photogenic, they will help you with the poses and everything. i’ve got beautiful photo’s and a video. next time i will definitely do it again!

i did the day skipper for a week with kevin and he was the perfect instructor you hope to have. not only was he super patient and able to explain things calmly in different ways, but also pushed you to learn more details and improve as soon as you were getting in your comfort zone. great problem solving and people skills to make sure all runs smoothly and people get together as a crew! see you hopefully soon

i did the discovery dive with abyss this may and highly recommend it! maro and my diving instructor srdan explained everything very clearly and in detail, i felt completely safe at all times and i had a lot of fun hearing their stories. since this was my second time scuba diving they also let me try adjusting my bouyancy myself, and srdan gave me a great explanation for how to do it and gave me lots of help throughout the dive. if you're curious about diving in general or what it's like to dive in croatia, go with abyss! the water where you dive is so clear and you'll see lots of different animals, it's a fantastic experience!

i did the fenland trail in the evening on my way back to banff town from vermilion lakes, and it was the perfect little detour to end the day. it’s an easy, flat loop through beautiful old spruce forest, and you really feel tucked away in nature even though you’re so close to town. i loved how quiet it was in the evening — just the sound of the creek and birds. i took my time crossing the wooden bridges and stopping to watch the light fade through the trees. it’s only about 2 km so it doesn’t take long, maybe 30–40 minutes at a relaxed pace. some tips from my walk: • if you’re at vermilion lakes, it’s really convenient — you can walk or drive a couple of minutes to the fenland trail parking lot. • it’s a gravel/dirt path, really easy to follow and suitable for all ages. • bring bug spray if it’s warm — mosquitoes come out near the water, especially at dusk! • there are benches along the trail if you want to just sit and listen to the creek. • i’d recommend doing it before it’s fully dark — there are no lights on the trail, so plan for daylight or bring a headlamp if you’re late. this was a nice, gentle way to wind down after visiting vermilion lakes — peaceful, easy, and you end up right near town. if you want a quiet forest walk without needing to drive far, fenland is a great choice. i’ll definitely do it again next time i’m in banff!

i did the fly roundtrip with sunlover and it was absolutely unreal. the views from the helicopter over the great barrier reef were stunning. once we arrived on the pontoon, we had enough time for a quick snorkel, a glass bottom boat tour, and even grabbed an ice cream before heading back to cairns. such a great way to experience the reef 😍

i did the guided big paine trek with chile nativo in november 2024, it was the best hiking experience i ever had! the agency is really helpful and assists you with any inquiry or advices you might need. they offer different circuits which are all well detailed on their websites. they gently recommended other agencies and shops in other parts of patagonia for the rest of my trip as well, i really appreciated this! torres del paine was an amazing discovery for me, i initially came to visit the famous towers but ended up discovering so much more along the way. at times i could look in any directions and be stunned by the majesty of all the nature around me. our guide, catalina, was exceptional, she shared her knowledge and passion for patagonia, the park and nature with a contagious joy and energy. she showed us along the way many animals, plants, mountains and much more and taught us about them and their relationship to the park and the region. she went out of her way each day and each night at each camp to accommodate to our group and make our experience amazing! chile nativo also handled the reservation at each camp, we had the tents ready with sleeping bags and mats when we arrived, food was included at every refuge as well and was quite good! we also took the porter option, the team was very nice and efficient, our dry bags we’d always ready for us at the camp and the porters always prepared some surprise for us when we arrived. thank you to all the team for that amazing experience! i hope i’ll have an other occasion to visit patagonia with you!

i did the interlaken canyoning with the best guides! i felt so safe but most importantly had so much fun! rappelling, cliff jumps, rock slides. truly was the #bestdayever! buzz tour guide approved! 💛💙

i did the large circuit excursion, they take you to see villa la angostura, villa traful and two of the 7 lakes. it lasts almost all day, they picked us up at the hotel at 8:30 a.m. and we returned around 5:30 p.m. beautiful route and views. the excursion costs $57,600 per person if you pay by transfer/cash and $72,000 if you pay by card and they have 6 interest-free installments. celina attended to us! in my case i had paloma as a guide who is a genius, she gave us historical context during the trip of the architecture and forms of the landscape. he also gave us a lot of information about the flora and fauna of the place. she was always kind, attentive and receptive to our questions. as a transporter we had cristian who is a genius at driving on very narrow gravel roads!

i did the market tour, fruit tasting, and cooking class with romario. it was great to see the market and learn about all of the native fruits and vegetables. the fruit i tasted was incredibly fresh and delicious. i thoroughly enjoyed the cooking class. we made 4 courses, all of which were flavourful and different to anything i’ve cooked before. i will definitely be making the dishes when i go back home. this is a must do activity if you are in cartagena. thank you romario and team for a wonderful experience!

i did the open water dive course here and i couldn’t recommend it enough. you’re made very welcome by the whole centre, everyone is so kind and it’s a great environment. as for the course itself, our instructor charlene was just amazing and made the learning feel comfortable, safe and fun. thank you charlene and the whole centre!

i did the parasail. it was fun and the beautiful view of the beach with the turquoise water and hotels. loved it. i had a awesome time with my son ,and my fiancé. i really recommend to do this if coming to visit family and friends or for vacation.

i did the parasail. it was fun and the beautiful view of the beach with the turquoise water and hotels. loved it. i had a awesome time with my son ,and my fiancé. i really recommend to do this if coming to visit family and friends or for vacation.

i did the sian ka’an float tour with omar. it was amazing, it was a nice smaller group, food was excellent. omar was friendly and knowledgeable, he had lots of insider info and was really accommodating. the following day i did the chichén itz’a tour with christian, again, excellent. smaller group, he was friendly funny and knowledgeable. food was excellent, the cenote was amazing and not as crowded as it looks. definitely worth the money. they seem to have a different exchange rate than what is current so be sure to bring a few extra pesos. the stop on the chichen itza tour is a fun place to shop, so again bring some extra pesos.

i did the sunrise tour during my three week visit to sydney and it was the best thing i did. chris, the tour guide and his team, were informative, funny and charismatic. all were super upbeat throughout and took time to ensure everyone had a unique experience. we were on the water for approx 2hours in total, there were regular stops with picture perfect views and chris shared his knowledge of the area. i’d love to return to do the sunset tour but would not hesitate to do the sunrise again as that scenery would not get old!! also the best way to start any day! thank you so much for an experience i’ll never forget.

i did the tour in july and was septic because of the comments but gave it a try. he told us we do minimum 2 stops but more if we find wildlife on the way but that's never guaranteed but likely. positive: the guide was really nice, there was nearly always 1 person on top of the boat for lookout! we made 4 stops on the way there for a whale, dolphins, jumping tunas and mantas. we even tried to snorkel with the dolphins but they were too few and fast. but we snorkeled with the mantas which was amazing!! he snorkeled with us and took videos as well. we also felt that the boat is always slowing down when there are animals near! we did the 2 snorkel stops on a bay which were amazing! they showed us birds as well and explained a little ! on the way back we did another snorkel stop after 1 hour so in total there were really 5 stops and we came back at 17:00! the boat was nice and basic. you get wet in the corners but otherwise it's really fine. we all got wetsuits anyway! sometimes when they drove slowly we were allowed on the top of the boat - which was really cool as well!! negative: yes it was a bit poor communication in the beginning.. it would be nice to hear from someone where we are going - what's the plan - what's the itinerary or anything. you needed to ask a lot. the breakfast was at 10:00 which is a bit late and not so plentyfull so bring some snacks! all in all it was a great trip! they never promised too much. yes we didn't see an orca but that's rare.. otherwise they did everything to make it special! it's not cheap but it was way better than a basic snorkel trip!!

i did the tour to paranella park and the waterfalls and it was absolutely beautiful. i personally wish i had more time at paranella myself but the tour guide knew just the right amount of time to spend at each location and accommodate all the guests on the tour. it was spectacularly beautiful.

i did two dives with wreck bay diving centre at kicker rock. even thought i made an inquiry about the dive the day before, they were able to get me a spot. they got me to try on the wetsuit and gear the day before and we were to depart san cristobal early the next morning. pros: sitting at the front of the speed boat and the initial stop over at the beach was really nice; they gave us snacks on the boat too in between activities. we got to see hammerhead and black tip sharks which is what i wanted to see. the instructor also had go pro videos that he gave us. cons: i realised that there was some miscommunication as i was told by the dive centre that i was the only diver for kicker rock, but it turns out there were actually two of us. then, before i tried my wetsuit on for the dive, the diving instructor said it was too big for me and that it should be tighter (the staff the day beforehand didn’t check this for me) - luckily the instructor had a spare short-sleeved wetsuit on the boat that i could wear underneath to avoid getting too cold underwater. furthermore, once we got into the water for the dive, i had trouble equalising and every time i signaled to the instructor that there was something wrong, he’d signal back “ok” and turned around, which made me feel like he wasn’t paying attention to my safety, even though he had emphasised that that’s what was most important in our brief. also on the second dive, he just kept descending before i could equalise properly and now i have ended up with barotrauma (internal bleeding in my middle ear). luckily the hospital on san cristobal is free for emergencies, but i am really disappointed that my safety wasn’t prioritised - now i cannot dive for the next 6-8 months. on both dives, i surfaced with blood noses and the instructor said it was normal and it happens to divers but he didn’t seem to think it was a big deal; and in retrospect, it was a big deal given my barotrauma. additionally, i noticed he didn’t ensure that the other diver and i got all the details for us to log the dives - other dive centres in my experience would’ve sat down with us to ensure we have correct details to log but this instructor didn’t; i even sent a whatsapp message to the dive centre asking for this information but they never responded to me. i would suggest booking diving with a different centre if you can.

i did two tours with one day africa both as a solo traveller. the first, a street art walking tour of the maboneng district was great. in a group of 4 with 3 other females (one other solo traveller and 2 who were travelling together) i felt safe being accompanied by our guide in a busy area and he gave good advice on keeping valuables hidden and how locals will engage with us. the tour was informative and interesting and the street art was amazing. you definitely can’t walk around this district on your own and get any value from it without knowing the background. good value for money and would recommend. however, i then did a walking tour of soweto having been recommended it by others. i was again a solo traveller and was the only person on the tour. it was an ok experience over all but i feel it necessary to point out/feedback some negatives. 1) the tour did not include admission fee to nelson mandela’s house and i felt obliged to pay the fee with no warning as the tour guide includes this as a 30min stop within the walking tour. of course i could have declined but felt rude doing so. it is an additional cost that is not mentioned as an optional upon booking and i felt a bit taken a back by this. 2) the tour guide had a trainee with him who was learning - i had no problem with this but they did regularly converse together in local dialect which i felt a bit rude as i didn’t know what they were saying to each other and it made me feel uncomfortable 3) a stop at the poorest slum area of the township was part of the tour and the guide handed me over to a local resident to take me round this area. i didn’t realise that the guide was not accompanying me and i was left alone with this person whilst the tour guide waited outside. i did not feel safe nor comfortable and i did not feel it was responsible to leave a lone female traveller and that the tour guide should have accompanied me. i only realised that the tour guide was not coming with us too late and didn’t feel comfortable asking for them to accompany me. the person showing me around then asked for money at the end of the visit as he said no one pays him to show tourists around. (i didn’t have any cash on me anyway as it happens). we then walked rather than advertised ride a minibus taxi to the last stop at the orlando towers. mixed experiences overall but i thank the guides for their knowledge and effort.

i did two very nice hikes in summer, lasting just around 3-4 hours each. one to the top of luosto, and another to 'pyhänkasteenputous ja -lampi' and the swamp area nearby. both were very beautiful, and the paths were really good.

i didn't even know this garden existed until my friend took me here. i don't know about the ticket price though as she has an annual subscription. it is a huge garden and we took about 2 hr to explore the whole garden. trees are meticulously trimmed and planted and it is so beautiful. i visited the rose garden and it would be more beautiful when you visit during the cherry blossom time. i also like the japanese garden area. if i live in nyc or had much more time, i want to spend the whole day in here reading a book. it is a calming and peaceful place. highly recommend to visit here.

i didn't get the opportunity to see this little geyser in action, but the gerserite cap is spectacular. it looks almost like dead coral or perhaps a smaller version of the "anemone geysers" of upper geyser. definitely a unique area, as vixen is surrounded by translucent, opal pools that make the scenery feel otherworldly.

i didn't have a car to park so wasn't paying attention to see if its free and the time limit. there are quite a few parking spaces here. the entrance is towards park street. one side of the parking lot is the skate park while the botanical gardens is on the other. further down the drive leads to the ice skating arena and the tennis courts.

i didn't really enjoy my experience here. the person operating the ticket booth demanded a bribe from me after giving me the student discount that they should be giving me anyway. the museum has no ac. most of the artifacts have no blurbs, or none in english, leaving me confused as to what a lot of things were and where and when they were from, as well as their significance. the staff in the king tut exhibition were extremely adamant on not letting anyone take any pictures, demanding that people delete them if they see that they did. however, paid tourist groups literally got their picture taken by a photographer in front of the mask, so they clearly are just greedy and want money. i still got some pictures of course.

i didn’t know much about this park until i decided to go discover that part of quebec city, it’s a big trail go through a couple of beaches linked to parc cap rouge, very nice views and walk, pet friendly, be aware there is many steps up and down through the trail, it’s very recommended, it’s part of the 50km sentier pedestre littoral

i disagree a bit with the previous posts. while the views from the top are indeed very beautiful, the hike is a bit tiring. passing through the dwarf birch, the passages there are narrow and steep. walking along the upper section beyond the tree line, we encountered hot and windless weather, which significantly hindered our ascent.

i discovered impressive traditional art! we visited for christmas. it was festive, warm and the staff was really friendly. it's an extraordinary experience especially for families. the chidren's playground has a treasure finding play rarely found at any other place and childrean really love it! i recommend visiting the museum. it's worth it!

i discovered mary royet spa through a simple google search. while many spas appeared, hers immediately stood out thanks to the glowing reviews and perfect 5.0-star rating. i booked the super deep and complete facial cleansing with hydrafacial - hydrodermabrasion and a 60-minute relaxing deep tissue massage. from the moment i walked in, mary greeted me warmly and made me feel completely at ease. as someone who had never had a facial before, i appreciated her guidance in helping me choose the right treatment for my skin type. although i follow a daily skincare routine, i didn’t realize how transformative a professional facial could be. after the session, my skin looked noticeably brighter, smoother, and had a healthy, radiant glow—no more dullness or dryness. the massage that followed was equally impressive. i shared my problem areas with mary, and she tailored the massage to focus on those specific points. her attention to detail was outstanding—she intuitively found where i carried the most tension, and i felt genuinely rejuvenated afterward. overall, the experience was relaxing, professional, and incredibly effective. the pricing is also very reasonable for the quality of service provided. if you’re in cartagena, do yourself a favor and book a visit to mary royet spa—you won’t regret it!

i discovered the high vibe collective when i was looking for just the right healing experience for my first retreat. at midlife, i desperately needed a soft-landing place to heal, rest, and receive support for some major loss and life changes i had been going through and holding onto for so long. as soon as i pulled up to the gate, i knew i had landed somewhere really special. aaron and stephanie welcomed me with such kindness and care that i immediately felt comfortable and safe. the property and accommodations were so beautifully kept and in harmony with the most stunning red rock desert landscape all around. peace and nature abound there. every single part of my retreat experience was thoughtful and individualized just for me. all of my senses and smallest needs were cared for. i arrived feeling exhausted, heartbroken, and unsure of my path forward. i just knew i could trust the magic of this place to do its thing with me... and it most definitely did. i couldn't fathom this retreat was going to heal me from root to sky. their exceptional warmth and kindness, amazing healing treatments, ongoing intentionality and care, delicious food, plus the scenery, space, music, conversations, feedback, and meditations shared helped me to heal in such a deeply meaningful and transformative way. i can't give enough stars!! when i left, i cried because i was so moved by how much love i received there, and how much better i felt!! i was able to let go of so much pain, heartache, and old conditioning while there. i left with my head held high and my spirit lighter. i felt so loved and seen. being around such lightness reminded me who i am and who i'm meant to be in this life. what a remarkable gift! thank you. i am continuing to integrate what i learned and am feeling more aligned and at peace than i have in decades. my deepest and most heartful thanks to stephanie, aaron, and the whole high vibe collective for a truly authenticating reset.

i dived in central raja ampat with olin dive for 2 days, and i had a blast. as i was traveling solo, i joined other people who dived on those days. the divemaster (cikis) was great, and the owner (olga) was quite helpful. the dive sites were great. the first day on the closer dive sites was a bit dark underwater as it was cloudy and raining, but the second day on dive sites toward piaynemo had much better visibility as it was sunny with clear sky. on the third day, unfortunately, the 2 dives did not happen to to scheduling issue, and so the dive center helped arranging a trip to kali biru, which was a very nice place.

i dived with mobula divers 3 days in a row in april 2025 and would absolutely recommend it! if the busy and touristy el nido is too much for you - grab a ride and go to sibaltan, it’s a secret gem not even an hour away. mobular divers are super professional, provide very good equipment, as well as well organised dives. the team (boat crew, shop crew and diving crew) know their job and are always fun to be around. they mostly do 2 morning and 2 afternoon dives. it’s maximum 5 divers per dive guide. their bangka boat is in very good condition and you always dive from the boat. the owner jhong has a special place in my heart - always honestly smiling, very knowledgeable and professional, he would make anyone feel save and in good hands. the price is absolutely fair - it includes gear and diving, as well as a burger between the dives. the coral reefs are in amazing condition, the marine life is thriving and in case anyone needs to read it - there is no guarantee for manta encounters, it’s wild life guys! thank you to the whole crew, i hope i can be back soon! 🐠💙🩵

i do not recommend this activity at all. the facility is poorly maintained and lacks basic cleanliness. the showers are open, uncovered, and emit a strong, unpleasant odor, which significantly detracted from the experience. additionally, the boats frequently stop working during the activity, causing delays and frustration. while the staff are friendly, their kindness doesn’t make up for the overall poor conditions.

i do not recommend this store for renting trekking equipment. my husband and i had a terrible experience. we rented two pairs of trekking poles from this store and the equipment they gave us was in poor condition. the poles presented problems at the beginning of the trail because no one could open them. they were completely stuck. after many attempts and use of force, we managed to open them. when we arrived at the shelter, we saw that the rosettes on my husband's poles had come off and were lost along the way (which was terrible because we would be facing snow on the next day). on the second day of the trail, while we were descending a secondary peak of the mountain, on snowy terrain and crevasses, one of my husband's poles simply broke in half, causing him to fall. he was not hurt, but the equipment broke in a situation that should not have happened. confirming our suspicions and the mountain guide’s suspicion that the equipment was in poor condition. as if all this were not enough, when we returned it to the store and explained what had happened and how it all happened, we were accused of having damaged the equipment. according to the attendant, the rosettes came loose and the trekking pole got stuck and (later) broke, all due to misuse on our part. they charged us a high fine and did not acknowledge any fault for the problem. we were 100% dissatisfied with the equipment we rented and even more so with the hostile way we were treated at the store. luckily no one got hurt as a result of the bad equipment they gave us to climb the mountain. i believe there must be other better places in the city for this type of rental.
i don't do much shopping but lots of individual shops here. there also are many restraunts. my friend did find some jewelry to buy for his wife. small store fronts for the most part.

i don't know where to start with how i feel about my stay at life is good. i've traveled to many countries, and i've never felt so at home as i did here. this isn’t a party hostel—it’s the kind of place where you go to recharge, rest, and connect. the best part is, there's a ton of nightlife and a plaza right around the corner (less than a 5-minute walk). it was the perfect balance: i could go out for drinks and dancing, then return to a safe (secured by a locked gate), peaceful place to sleep. the location is ideal, with everything you’d want to see in the city within a 15-minute walk. breakfast is included, made to order, and absolutely delicious—with free water, coffee, and tea available all day. the hostel has its own restaurant, which is also great (i recommend the shrimp/crab pasta), and a 2-for-1 happy hour for drinks. there are lots of nearby restaurants, plus an ice cream place right next door. it's close to several other hostels too, which makes meeting other travelers easy. the rooms are very clean (tended to every morning), with nice ensuite bathrooms and air conditioning. there’s even a rooftop hot tub—they were just finishing renovations on it during my last day. what really makes this place special is the staff. i’ve never felt more welcome anywhere i’ve stayed. from señora maria (la jefa/general manager) to the amazing housekeeping team, every single person was kind, helpful, and genuinely caring. they rotate roles so you get to interact with everyone, and i didn’t even know who the general manager was at first—she was waiting tables! i mentioned i wanted to practice spanish, and the entire team—including the manager—jumped in to help and encourage me. the staff is available 24/7 and responds quickly to any concerns. be sure to check out the cooking class and paint/brunch class—both were so much fun! i didn’t want to leave at the end of my stay. i came as a solo traveler and left feeling like i had a colombian family. gracias por todo. ¡hasta la próxima!

i don't typically write reviews, but kilimanjaro heroes played such a pivotal role in my tanzania experience that i felt compelled to share. for the month leading up to my arrival, they maintained daily and timely contact via whatsapp, answering every question i had with detailed justifications and references. they took all my desires, concerns, and time constraints into account and built a seamless itinerary that included airport pickup, hotel lodging, an 8-day kilimanjaro trek on the lemosho route, a 4-day safari, a coffee farm tour, and transportation to dar es salaam (continuing on to zanzibar). the trek was incredible. the team met us at the hotel in the morning, where onesmo carefully checked our gear to ensure we had everything necessary for the hike. we stopped by the office to pick up a few missing items, and the keys hotel kindly stored the extra luggage we didn’t need on the mountain. our two tour guides, onesmo and theophil, were outstanding. their knowledge of the terrain, weather patterns, and timing was spot on, allowing them to make accurate predictions that helped us navigate the route efficiently. onesmo frequently stopped along the way to provide insight into the unique plants, animals, and geological formations that make kilimanjaro such a breathtaking landscape. more than anything, onesmo and theophil fostered an incredibly positive atmosphere, filling the trek with great conversations and continuous jokes. on the first day of our hike, it happened to be my friend’s birthday, and after dinner, the team surprised us with a cake and a small celebration. this was above and beyond our expectations and made for an unforgettable moment. the food the chef (shedrack boka) was amazing! i still don’t know how he managed to prepare such high-quality meals on the mountain, but every dish exceeded my expectations. fresh fruits, crisp vegetables, handmade bread and crepes, delicious soups, stews, and curries—it felt like restaurant-quality dining in the middle of the wilderness/mountain top. along with the chef, twalibu self doubled as both a porter and a waiter, ensuring we had everything we needed, from hot water for washing to tea, coffee, snacks, and toiletries. his attentiveness made the experience even more comfortable. the porters now, let’s talk about the porters (ally suley, vicent mishana, richard batholomeo, thomas lonyoki, jonathan hosea, and abas idd). their strength and endurance were nothing short of inspiring. yes, they carried our gear and often raced ahead to set up camp before we arrived, but they also provided unwavering encouragement throughout the trek. their singing, cheering, and motivation made us feel like part of a true team, pushing us forward as we conquered kilimanjaro. final thoughts i couldn’t have asked for a better experience. the professionalism, expertise, and warmth of the entire kilimanjaro heroes team made this journey unforgettable. based on my experience, i feel more than comfortable recommending them to anyone looking for a top-tier guide company to take them up the mountain.

i don’t even know how to p it this into words, but i’m so glad i came here, i’m genuinely going to come to his majesty’s theatre just to watch the phantom of the opera. colleen rose as christine daaé was portrayed with impossible grace. her final scenes caught in my throat, the way her compassion was so beautifully depicted and her voice made me speechless. the phantom’s voice was unreal, so deep and emotionally charged. every time dean chisnall as the phantom made the entire theatre fall into complete silence every time he sang. his music was so painfully beautiful it almost brought tears to my eyes. adam rhys charles as raoul was beyond ethereal, you can truly feel his sincerity in every promise and every soft high note. the rest of the cast was flawless, the ensemble sharp and energetic, and the vocals during the masquerade gave me utter chills. the theatre itself is stunning and elegant, perfect to ensure you feel like you’re in a gran opera house in paris, the chandelier furthermore making you feel the special atmosphere. the acoustics were perfect; every voice, every note, and every instrument was carried with such clarity and richness. the staff were lovely, the bar was efficient and responsive to every inquiry. after the show we were able to get the booklets signed by the cast members and it ultimately wrapped up this amazing theatrical show. if you’ve never seen the phantom of the opera go here, even if you’ve already seen it, go again. the casts currently and the performance are something truly extraordinary. i left the theatre floating and i still currently am.

i dropped in on the randall museum on a saturday to reminisce about the the times when my young son, now 26, and i used to frequent the museum. it was so enjoyable and chock full of wonderful, lively and well-maintained exhibits - and all info is indigenous to the area. each exhibit was wonderfully geared to each species and looked so authentic and well thought out! the staff was incredibly approachable and truly added to my ever-so-pleasant experience. donna at the front desk was welcoming and nick was in the midst of creating a soon-to-be "safe haven" for one of their racoons who has some particular challenges. it is well on its way to becoming a life-size, indoor habitat in the shape of a tree! it's hollowed, well-reinforced tree limbs will provide a dark, quieter refuge for the raccoon when large, perhaps louder, groups of school children visit. the thoughtfulness and care going into this product seems to be just one example of how they truly care about the quality of life for those in their exhibits. the whole museum underwent a remodel since i was last there, and it's truly fantastic! it's for old and young alike, and many of the exhibits are at the height of children! where so many venues tell children not to touch, that's not the case here. buttons to push, info cards to open and read, toy trains to push on the train table and much to learn about climate change, keeping the ocean clean and how the city was formed and what's underneath it. you could even experience an earthquake at a build-your-own lego table! and for the young electric train enthusiasts in your life there is a huge layout complete with shops, mountains and tunnels and many varied train lines! and on certain saturdays you can run your own trains on their tracks! for an added bonus, you can take a hike around the mountain and catch some of the best views of the city! also, they offer classes to take, such as pottery, and have a wood shop as well. they are also open to suggestions for any new class or workshop you might want to teach! let me just say if you haven't taken your children to the randall museum you've got to do so. this place is truly a local treasure! - and it's still evolving! you can't beat the price which is free! (donations welcome!)

i enjoyed it. it is a huge long trail that connects all the way to mirador lago moreno (the exit is where it says "information turística". from there you can go right or left on the main road cto chico to puerto lopez or villa tacul. i recommend to right because the bus terminal is at villa llao llao. it is bus 20 and it stops 10min walk from this park. however, if you take right and visit the other attractions (which are connected by other trails cto chico) then head back left and go to puerto lopez (10h20pm is last bus). 12am is last for bus 20. cost per ride 100 pesos. you can rent a bike (approx 4k), rent a car or take bus (but it does half the loop of cto chico). no bus between terminal bus 20 and puerto lopez (bus 10 goes the other way around). i spent 1 day using bus 10 and the other bus 20). it is really beautiful trails.

i enjoyed my visit here very much. good range of works, clearly presented. the tree of life (basement) could have a short (18"-high) mirror put behind it so we can see the back of it. the third floor has a curious, neutral-to-positive take on a megalomaniac. it doesn't suitably confront the issues of kidnapping (saying someone was just 'seized'?) and other injustices that were, at best, glossed over, and at worst glorified. even if they weren't explicitly condoned it seems they were laid vulnerable to misinterpretation by young audiences. i get that it's a fine line not to be too presentist. but there could be a more balanced representation of augustus: e.g. detailing further the political turmoil. perhaps put more emphasis on how his pursuits destabilised poland (a historical fact), how his legacy is marked as much by overreach as artistic brilliance, how he saw leadership less as a duty than a spectacle. and so on. if this seems out of place in a ceramics museum, fine, but then much of the existing text in veiled reverence of augustus should also be omitted. highly recommend this engaging and diverse museum.

i enjoyed my visit to aoao sapporo. i was very happy that the signs and write-ups for each animal were both in japanese and english. my primary purpose of going here was to see the penguins but there were also other fascinating animals here. it was also nice that they had a cafe and sitting area near the penguins. the collaboration with spongebob was also cute - with the figures from the cartoon adoring several tanks and locations. it was easy to buy and use tickets from klook.
i enjoyed my visit! the food amazing and customer service fabulous and generous! i recommend to others

i enjoyed our visit here. the museum was nicely laid out, with good explanations and with interesting exhibits. i learned a lot. before the 1970´s they dived in thin cotton outfits, which is just nuts to see. it’s amazing how these women lived. please come and support this museum. there is a refillable water purifying station too- just lovely! ☺️
i enjoyed shopping here, the quality of the clothing is great for the price. so many stores and also some food stands. i suggest paying cash, some stores don't accept cards. i can't wait to go back!

i enjoyed the experience quite a bit, i saw and heard many animals up close and met a lot of very nice local people. the porini mara camp was very comfortable, with lots of wildlife in and around the camp. i actually had an elephant feeding about 5m away while i was stargazing outside my tent. got to watch 3 lionesses and 10 cubs eat a zebra, including hearing the bones crunched. otoh, the food was mediocre and the game drives felt a little like being in a zoo. the animals are so used to the land rovers that we'd pull up to lions and elephants only a couple of meters away. i felt like the guides were good, not great. we did most of our sightings from behind the animals - not the best angle for photography. and the guides talked to each other in swahili more than they did to us in english. i went in april, which is the slowest month of the year - expect big crowds on game sightings if you go in a busy season. i saw everything i hoped for in the offseason and still some sightings were still crowded with cars. i haven't been on any other safaris, so i have nothing to compare this trip with. however, i really enjoyed it and i'm very glad i did it. it felt like an 'entry level' safari, so if i do it again i think i'll look for something more adventurous.

i enjoyed the service at the spa. everyone was nice. the place was clean and didn't feel too crowded as it's big. the view is incredible. the food at the restaurant was great. the spa was clean and relaxing. however when evening time arrived the clients were not respecting to stay quiet. people were talking loudly and it was hard to relax which wasn't the case in the afternoon.

i enjoyed the snorkel tour. they have good equipments, every one gets a new snorkel and we get to keep it. the tour only lasted about 2.5h not 3-3.5h as advertised. snacks served on board were delicious and they have bottled water/margarita. one thing that falls short is that a few of us got cut by the ladder on our knee when going back into the boat. i think this is a safety concern, hope it will be addressed.
i enjoyed the time here and hope to see more exhibitions. each work of art was inspiring. admission fee is 2000 won.
i enjoyed this amazing tour, very lovely guide! prefect for your honeymoon! we started with a walk to the gondola pick-up point and heard about the history of venice :)

i enjoyed this visit so much! the museum is taking feminist approach and both of the main exhibits were about woman. don't be fooled by the catalog stand in front of dressing rooms, there's a big gift shop with more stuff down the stairs. about the tickets, it's okay if you don't arrive exactly on your time, the time almost doesn't matter.

i enjoyed visiting the market, reminded me of being no. latin america. that was until the bill came. the “restaurant” an open air stand, charged me $25 for a a plate of ceviche and a soda and fries for my kid. it was delicious. maybe i was charged gringa prices, they didn’t have prices in the menu. 😂 those were miami beach prices guys, not cool.

i enjoyed walking along the streets, very interesting to see and to smell everything. but they are a bit crowded and you need to be watchful of the motorbikes. i felt safe walking alone but i think later in the evening there are some streets which are very empty of people and i think you need to be a bit more cautious. the people are very friendly. they are not too pushy, of course they want to sell products and make some money but they are not over pushy and they are very polite. always negotiate the price. most shops are authentic but there are some selling “genuine fakes”. i recommend you visit if in marrakesh

i entered on myself. once or twice, i was asked either i am jewish, and then, after i sad no, i was wished a good day and i was left in peace to do whatever i was willing to. of cause i was respecting all the rules described at the entrance.

i expected more. everyone we spoke to said it was world class. i disagree. the entire deep sea area is mostly video screens and not a lot of actual displays. the kids stuff was good. kept em busy while i struggled to find a seat to sit. obviously. it cost us $230 to get us in. that is way too much. maybe $30 a person at most. no discounts. pay to park. food is expensive. kids were ready to leave at hour three. kc zoo aquarium is better in my opinion. there were some cool things and marine life but the price is too much. plane and simple.

i expected too much... for the price, there was no sense of hospitality. in both good and bad ways, it felt like i was being attended to by a local friend, and they didn't explain anything to me unless i asked them, and the places i added as options were over before i could even ask where i wanted to go, as i just got out of the car and walked past them. it was a very frustrating trip. i had requested drinks that were unique to the area, but i was disappointed when they brushed it off and said, "there weren't any." i had seen other people on instagram say that they had prepared them, and i had asked about them about a week before and hadn't heard that they couldn't prepare them, so i thought they had prepared them, but i'm telling myself that they must have been busy (but i'm sad). i was really looking forward to it after seeing the instagram post, but there wasn't much support and the guide was often fiddling with his phone, which made me sad. i thought they would be flexible in responding to my requests, but there was no point in having a private tour with a japanese guide, and it was a poor value for money. i wonder if i should have said what i wanted to do and what i didn't like at the time... at the time of booking, additional fees that i wasn't told about at first were added later, so i couldn't say that i didn't like it if i had made a request and it resulted in an additional fee or a dispute. next time i go to cancun, i think i'll join the best value for money english cheap tour. that way, i can accept any kind of treatment because it's cheap. i've written a lot, but it's just that the cost performance is bad, and i was able to make my own plan and go to many places, so i'm satisfied with that. i recommend it for those who can't go to the places they want to go on a group tour. however, if you expect too much, you may end up sad like me, so i recommend not expecting too much and joining.

i experience infinima few times and staff is always professional, very skilled and execute the swedish technique with all specifics it deserves. and you get some fresh fruits and time to relax before and after the session, this is very appreciated not to be rushed out. i highly recommend

i experienced my first “white water rafting” here! the staff are excellent. very friendly and knowledgeable. i did the wilderness explorer and it was a nice laid back ride. we had a guide oaring so i was able to take pictures and enjoy the scenery. there are more challenging rivers but this option is awesome to just float down the river and experience a few little waves for fun. our specific guide was jeremy. he made us all feel safe and is very knowledgeable with all things rivers and rafting. he is very experienced and we really enjoyed our time. they do have waterproof floating phone holders available for purchase (i bought one and love it!). before you go just know they only have portopotties so if you’re not into those go to another restroom before you go. they give you everything you need to be safe, and are able to lock up valuables while you are rafting. if you are on the fence about rafting my advice is definitely go for it!! it’s worth it!

i feel incredibly lucky to have added such an experience to my life. seeing the mona lisa with my own eyes is certainly a unique experience, but i don't think you should overlook all these magnificent works just for the mona lisa. every room, every work, holds a unique story. it might be a lengthy trip, but i'd love to come back and see each work in its own different details.

i feel like it was a blessing that things didn't work out with walks n talks. paula did not communicate well with us, even though we had made contact 5 months prior to our hiking adventure. she gave the indication that she was available for our time space, but she actually had paid for tours booked already! as it got closer to our hiking dates (the week of our hike start date), she informed us that she was booked for the days we had wanted her, but we could join some of those hiking groups if we wanted. all in all, things worked out as we found that most of the hikes we wanted to do, we could without a guide. yay!
i feel like the description is a bit misleading. it's more like a historic clock box that happens to also have historic traffic lights on it. still cool to see on your way to berlin mall though.

i feel like we lucked into having the best experience of all the people we saw in hanauma bay that day. nyle was the difference maker - i felt sorry for everyone else who only got to see what was in close. she showed us so much more and we had a great time. nyle was everything you'd want in a guide and she even sent us great photos and videos afterward. if you aren't going to snorkel with nyle, i would recommend doing something else.

i felt like i was in a candy store. soooo much to see and eat. those beignets me was the best towards the end.
i felt like i was walking in a fairy forest. peaceful and beautiful forest. a great place to relax to the sounds of the waterfalls. moderate hike. free parking lot. highly recommend.

i found pure kitesurf after i tried with other school in cartagena and it was not much of a school. jesse and other instructors were amazing, worth the cost i quickly learned control and was deep in el mar , body dragging, and more. beautiful shop to relax in hammock and soak up the ambiance. i’m ready to dj house music during busy season.

i found ripley’s believe it or not really interesting — there’s definitely a lot to see and some truly bizarre and fascinating exhibits. it’s a fun mix of oddities, history, and curiosities that kept me engaged the whole way through. that said, i’m not sure i’d do it again today. it feels more like a one-time experience. still, if you’re in the area and have a bit of time, why not? it’s quirky, entertaining, and definitely different from your usual museum visit.

i found the rio serrano in the torres del paine area was perfect. the view, the room's size, and the price were reasonable given the area. the staff was reasonably helpful, and the hotel offered the option to pre-order food to take on trails and trips, or order before a certain time the morning before. it felt as if the hotel could have done more to bring other guests together by offering a nightly campfire or some other activity that is not just a movie. i also wish the hotel would offer the outdoor grilled lamb as an option in a regular cadence. the food was reasonably good, i wish there was more variety in a rotating menu, given the length of stay - i bled through all the food options, and it felt repetitive and boring. however, given this is chile and i've travelled for years to santiago, i am happy at my stay and the hotel and would come back.

i found this experience/attraction completely underwhelming. it's a small ground. the cafe was closed and had no signs indicating this. so there was numerous tourists walking to the cafe to find it closed with no other alternatives available for even refreshments on a hot day. the tortoises was by far the best thing in the botanical garden.

i found this mall very crowded and honestly quite hyped. except for the fact that you get almost every other brand here, which is great. still, it’s an amazing place overall, especially with attractions like ski dubai and so many dining options. worth a visit if you’re in dubai, but be ready for the rush.

i found this operator online and the communication was essy and very pleasant and accomodating. they went above and beyond to make my experience wonderful. from the pick up to the game drive. everthing was taken care of. i got to see all the animals, the beautiful national parks.the opportunity to witness the great migration in the serenheti was truly aweinspiring and our guides expertise ensured we didn‘t miss a single moment of this natural wonder. can‘t wait to return for more! 👌❤️

i found this place very peaceful.i came here with my friends and everything was very good,here is a good facility of kitchen,toilet and there is also a place for bonfire also.with these the sunset view from here is amazing.i will suggest all of you that if you got a chance to visit thiksey,leh.must visit here.....
i gave the experience to my parents, they loved it and came back fascinated. thank you very much for everything!!!

i gave this museum a 3 star.but only because it is way overpriced. it is basically about the size of two rooms. i paid $58 for 1 child and 1 senior. which was more expensive than a hockey hall of fame. prices matter on everything these days because families are struggling.so i do believe that this exhibit is quite overpriced. was it interesting... yes. was it interactive... yes. the staff were very friendly and helpful offering to take pictures for you. the museum was clean. and it was not overcrowded. it was easy to get to on front street. honestly the only thing that i can say wrong is that the exhibit was very small and that they were absolutely overpriced. if the cost had been thirty dollars instead of fifty eight i would have given a five star. but the cost of getting into this exhibit was what i paid for both of us to ride the go train and our tickets to the hockey hall of fame.

i gave this ride to my girlfriend for her birthday and it really did not disappoint. sergio's attention was a luxury, the ride was beautiful, i really recommend it, it's worth what you pay. sailing along the nahuel huapi is a beautiful experience, when we arrived at a port we ate croissants and so on.

i get so happy when a city takes care of it's public parks and beaches. this beach and park was so clean and very big, but can get crowded sometimes. beautiful views and the sand/sea was much nicer than any other beach and park i went. it was just an half hour from muscat located in matrah area.

i give 5 stars to colors of zanzibar for the amazing culinary tour. aziza was our guide and she amazed us with her passion for her culture and all of her knowledge. i asked her so many questions and no matter what, aziza knew the answer. she made us feel comfortable and welcomed in zanzibar. we have told all of our canadian friends about the culinary tour and recommend booking one with aziza. the most memorable experience of our trip, thank you colors of zanzibar 🇹🇿

i give it 5 stars for something sentimental. my grandfather lived his entire life inside the factory. he was the financial accountant and his brother was a master beer taster. my father was born there. son of an italian woman and my grandfather from bilbao spain and all my uncles until the factory intervened. thanks for the photos.
i got a 30 minute massage. it was excellent. relaxing music and good lotions. highly recommend.

i got a classic ticket this morning on the red bus to see table mountain route and the hout bay route and got pensioners rate from a nice friendly lady nandipha diphoko who explained everything to me. i recently moved from durban to cape town 2 years ago and went on this red bus 30 years ago. it was so nice to be going on it again. i decided just to go for the ride and see all the places. the city sightseeing red bus is amazing. the driver and staff were fantastic. a great way for people to get around and see all the top attractions on this hop on hop off red bus. i thoroughly enjoyed it.

i got a headspa + face and neck massage done here with a blow dry afterwards. it was so relaxing and the team really took their time to give the best quality service. all the team were welcoming and very nice. will definitely be back whenever i come to fes.

i got a last minute ticket, there was only one left. i enjoyed the show, it was quite amusing. the history of water puppet was also quite fascinating which can be found easily on the walls of the theatre. the artists were also quite professional even with some technical issues they still performed like nothing happened. the story of each act is quite meaningful as well. however, the lady in the counter needs some help with attitude.

i got a two day pass with ski rentals. the total came out to about $200, so $100 per day. you can’t even ski without rentals for that price in most places in the u.s. i also used their bus service to get there from sapporo and back. accommodations at the resort were expensive, so it was an easy way to save money. the bus service is prompt and efficient. the snow was a dream, and all the lifts were open during my two days there. as you can see from the photos, there were no crowds, which made the skiing even better. on the first day, the visibility was great, and you could see the sea of japan from the summit. absolutely stunning. all the workers were kind and friendly. the food was okay, but i wasn’t there for the food anyways.

i got invited by a friend here to enjoy the beach view and have great lunch. the service was so great and food was very delicate. i had salad with tahini. i just love jewish people their energy is amazing! the food is so fresh there! and sitting by the beach enjoying the great view. what’s more to ask? it’s one of my best memories there.

i got my aida level 2 certification with freediving seychelles, it was an absolutely amazing experience, highly recommend! sophie is a professional and super friendly instructor, and dedicates all her attention to her students to make freediving a fun and challenging experience for each of us. thank you so much sophie for this experience and for following up with my equalization challenges, i can’t wait to freedive with you again! :)

i got off at wrong station and had to walk for more than twenty minutes :) i expected street food stalls lined up along the way, but i was very surprised to see that inside, there was only a few🙄 at the entrance, you can buy your drinks and enjoy with your food 💥 overall, portions in thailand are small, but the dish i had (though i can't remember its name) was very delicious. 😋 if you're in the area, you can stop by, but if you're like me and plan ahead, it might be a bit disappointing. 🌺

i got the chance to visit the limited time exposition of the chilean tv program '31 minutos' personally, this tv program means a lot to me, and of course to us the mexicans. marking a special moment in our childhoods and stills making them to new generations. on the exposition, we could see a closer look at the making of the program. the real puppets that the staff used for the show, we got access to some of the original scripts of the show, a special gallery based on the show and more. ohhh also, there's a special dynamic where you can make drawings of the characters of 31 minutos. the dynamic is limited to a couple times per day. the exposition will be until january 12th. and i highly recommend buying tickets in advance, if you want to buy them on the same day you want to visit, is so probably to find no available tickets at the box office.

i got the four-hand massage here and it was excellent. patricia and johanny were great. they made sure i was comfortable and followed my instructions. i like my massages strong and both women did an awesome job. i left feeling sooo loose and relaxed. would definitely recommend!

i got the philly cheese steak which is supposed to be one of the best in town. the food is okay, above average but nothing stands out. the portion could be a bit more generous. i would consider it again for a quick bite, but wouldn't go out of my way to get it.

i got the rice bowl and the fried chicken. it was great value for the large portion and good amount of veggies. i was able to split it with my mother and still have leftovers for the next day. i'd get it again if i was in the area.

i got the smoky bulgogi fries and it tasted amazing. everything was great, and the sauce was addicting. only downside with this is the price. at $18, you get about 10-12 waffle fries, some meat sprinkled with a bit of shredded cheese, and a scoop of sour cream. although pricey for what you get, i'll likely have it again.

i got to know about wanderer tours and travel through a google search. i was quite impressed with the way che presented the itinerary. we were lucky enough to get faizel as our guide for the first 2 days and for 2 more days during our 9 days trip. garth and darlington were also very nice and professional. rashid was nice as well. we felt very comfortable with faizel; never felt bored with him. we had a great time in cape town and will surely consider wanderer tours and travel next time we visit cape town. the only reason why i am giving 4 stars instead of 5 is because we paid for a specific service but same was not provided when requested. when i queried the admin staff on the matter, she kind of ignored/discarded my query.

i gotta admit this place was recommended to me by my dad so i was skeptical at first given we have different taste pallets but i was pleasantly surprised by this place. service is very nice, they understand english if needed and their food is more than fair for the price. the tom yum wasn’t as sour as i prefer but their tom kha gai was perfect. definitely recommend it if you’re looking for a quick bite from something local!
i grew up here, it was old and awesome. i lived here from around 2001-2005. i don’t think you can live here anymore, but it was such a cool place to live and explore.

i grew up surfing but hadn’t had any luck getting my daughter out on a surfboard until today, because she was scared of having the big board when the sets would roll through. she and my younger son went out with ryan and sam and had the best time. ryan and sam were fabulous….super nice, funny, and superbly skilled at keeping the kids out of the impact zone while towing them all around the point and into so many waves. i am thoroughly impressed by their skill and my kids had a blast. we’ll be back shortly for more lessons.
i guess one of the must-see attractions in rio. the view is even more enjoyable when you hike up via the trail. that being said, that hike is not a walk in the park.

i had 2 trips with aqua world- isla mujeres and jungle tour, both trips were absolutely amazing. the jungle tour snorkelling is the best snorkelling i’ve ever done we saw a turtle! staff are so friendly, informative and helpful, they even let me reschedule the tour for a different day due to an illness on the day. thank you so much i would highly recommend!

i had a ball! it was my first time and they were very patient! they also allowed us to go out next to each other so my friends and i wouldn’t feel alone! also provided cool beverages to refresh us after the fun over the sea! 10/10 i really enjoyed myself and they’re very affordable for travelers!

i had a beautiful time here at sopa. the food was nice every meal, the service i think is what really stands out! everyone working there was so police and always with a smile. the rooms are beautiful, the whole resort is. only complaint which i think may be common, the wifi does not extend to rooms, only communal area, and phone connection not present in rooms either. if the work could be extended to rooms would be 1000% better.

i had a blast kite surfing for the first time at freestyle academy kitesurfing in boracay! my instructor, toto, was an amazing teacher - very patient, professional and a good laugh!! really loved the atmosphere of the surf shop, amazing coffee and lots of smiley faces. great place for all abilities. i did the full beginner course and felt like i progressed loads in only 3 days. 10/10 recommend.

i had a blast on the kayak tour on lake gutierrez! i booked very last minute and they were totally accommodating with transfers to and from my hotel included. the guides were very kind and personable. i felt safe and comfortable the entire time. they had all the necessary equipment and shared tea and croissants with the group during a halfway stop on the tour to admire the views. i would book with them again for other tours!

i had a great experience at the spa. i payed the hammam and massage (720 dhs) and it was perfect and so relaxing. loubna took good care of me and she explained every part of the process because it was the first time i went to a moroccan hammam. first, you have to undress entirely and they give you a small underwear to cover. they keep your personal belongings and clothes in a room with key. then, you go to the hamman and stay there few minutes while you wait for the masseuse. the hammam is a so beautiful inside with the stones and structure. after, the masseuse comes and puts organic soap in all the body and she starts scrubbing with an exfoliant glove. then she bathes you and you’ll feel like a baby again! after that, she puts a cream in your body and face and you have to keep it a few minutes while you stay at the hamman. then, she bathes you again with hot water buckets. the hamman process is about 45 minutes. after that you have to take a shower and they provide shampoo and douche soap. you have some minutes to relax and they give you some snacks (nuts, raisins and dry peaches) and water. after a while, you go to the massage room and she will make you choose among two kind of aromatic oils. the massage is full body and so relaxing, although i was expecting more focus on my back. in the meantime, they use some relaxing music and you can even feel asleep because it is so relaxing! the total time of the massage is about 40-45 minutes. before and after the experience, they offer you some complimentary mint tea at the terrace. the bistro also has some alcoholic options to drink and can even enjoy dinner after the hamman and massage experience. the place is super clean and i felt safe all the time as a solo woman traveler. thank you again for the great experience! 😋🌎🍽️✈️ sabor kairos

i had heard great things about tokyo disneysea, but i honestly wasn’t prepared for how different and enjoyable it would be compared to the disneyland park next door. from the moment we entered, we noticed a much more unique and mature theme running throughout the entire park. it’s clear this park was designed to appeal to older kids and adults while still maintaining the disney magic. the day started with light rain, which might have helped keep the crowds smaller. this worked in our favor, as we were able to explore without feeling rushed or stuck in long lines. the water-themed rides and attractions added a refreshing twist, and the overall design of the park felt like a mix between adventure, fantasy, and exploration. some of our highlights included the indiana jones ride, tower of terror, and the detailed harbor areas that made us feel like we were somewhere far from tokyo. the toy story mania section was fun and immersive, with incredible attention to detail. the nighttime illuminations and ambient lighting created a wonderful atmosphere. the cast members were friendly and made every interaction enjoyable. if you’ve already been to a disneyland park elsewhere and only have a single day, i would highly recommend prioritizing tokyo disneysea. it’s a different kind of magic that still delivers unforgettable moments. i’ll definitely be coming back on my next visit to tokyo.

i had high expectations for the tour, but the experience was far from great. the guides pushed forward despite thundering weather, which was both reckless and unprofessional. their focus seemed to be on completing the tour regardless of the dangerous conditions. we were picked up from ubud at 2:30 am in pouring rain. i asked the driver if it was safe to trek in such weather, and he said the guide would make the final call at the starting point. we arrived around 3:30 am, and it was still pouring with thunder rumbling. after waiting an hour, the guide initially canceled the trek, but when the rain briefly stopped, he decided to proceed. unfortunately, the rain soon resumed, and the trail was far more challenging than the agent had described. it wasn’t a moderate path—it was rocky, requiring climbing in parts and extremely slippery in the rain. the thunder felt dangerously close, and i was terrified. in such weather, visibility was nonexistent; we spent three hours climbing up and down, seeing nothing but mist. i wish they had canceled the trip from the start instead of forcing us to continue in those conditions. the rain is too strong that we even lost one of our phone.🥲

i had one of the best experiences today ever. we met charlie who offered their services with different options, from a short 20 minutes tour to a private hour and twenty minutes with a guide and a captain. we decided on a private tour. the tour takes you first near the ruins where you can see them from the sea, the guide eric explained each building with a lot of details and passion in both languages english and spanish, his knowledge of mayan history is amazing. then we went to an area where multiple boats stopped for a dive. our captain jackson carefully anchored and they provided us with all the proper equipment and instructions for the snorkeling experience. we were able to see multiple turtles swimming and eating the sea grass, sting rays, fishes of all sorts and sizes. then our guide brought us towards the coral reef where we snorkeled for a while, seeing all different colors and shapes of corals. overall the experience was fantastic, personalized and far from those who said in other reviews "they ran over other swimmers". thank you charlie and the crew for a fantastic afternoon, we enjoyed every second of it and i highly recommend the experience. be respectful with the environment, do not touch the animals, stay close to your guide and enjoy the experience.

i had planned to go there for sometimes and finally after a long day running around with my wife and attending few social events needed a tasty delicious food and not thinking about calories. this place will be our future to go place if we're in need of good heavenly food. my wife avoids pasta most of the time (concern about calories) but since actually she was the one more in need of hearty food, she ordered orechietti pasta with prawns. she had it a week ago and still raving about it, i can't believe that she finished the whole plate (i can honestly that never remember seeing her to go through the whole plate). i ordered bomba chili prawns to share. if i have an opportunity to choose my last plate before i go, will have as many of it that i can handle with their freshly toasted garlic bread. and the prawns for both dishes were so tenders that they almost melted before you know it. i also ordered mezze rigatoni with meat ball. i always fall for meatball and they didn't disappoint, they were awesome, i might go for different pasta next time. it was well past 10pm and was too late, otherwise i would have gone for some desert (i'm sure with the quality of our dishes, desert is also good).

unfortunate event. my first trip was a very emotional trip to kenya and i felt so magical being at this property. it really allowed me a space and time to be with myself. and unfortunately this second stay really tainted my full experience in kenya and i am super disappointed both with the fraud of the tour company, but also how this hotel ended up handling it. it was not super straightforward and elliptical). there are so many more modern properties in the masai mara now and going forward if we ever went back to kenya (which we probably won’t after this) we’d probably recommend staying at somewhere a little bit more updated. we ended up having to cut our trip short as our second hotel also had the same issue with our tour company and could not accommodate us and we had no other options little less uncomfortable for us, especially given we had been there before, reviewed them so positively and decided to come back as a repeat customer.

i had the absolute joy of seeing girl from the north country at the old vic on saturday evening, and i can’t stop thinking about it. from the very first note, the musicians and singers wrapped the entire theatre in an atmosphere so rich and heartfelt that it felt like being transported to another time and place. the voices — oh, the voices! — soared with such emotional honesty that you could feel every word deep in your chest. each song, beautifully interwoven with bob dylan’s music, was delivered with such soul that it left me breathless more than once. the musicians were extraordinary too, effortlessly shifting from delicate, intimate accompaniment to full-bodied, heart-shaking crescendos. the story itself is deeply moving — tender, raw, and profoundly human. it’s a tapestry of intertwined lives, hardship, and hope, told with such compassion that by the final moments, i found myself with tears in my eyes, and i wasn’t alone. this is theatre at its most powerful: music and storytelling working hand-in-hand to touch something universal in all of us. if you have the chance to see it, don’t hesitate. it’s a night that will stay with you long after the lights come up. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

i had the pleasure of joining a custom photo tour with juca, and it was truly an exceptional experience. from the very start, juca was a warm and welcoming presence, making our private group of 3 feel at ease right away. his extensive knowledge of terceira island’s hidden gems and local spots was impressive, and it was clear that he was genuinely passionate about sharing the best that the island has to offer. what stood out the most was juca's dedication and patience. he took the time to ensure that we had ample opportunities to capture the perfect shots, never once rushing us or making us feel pressured. his insights and tips were incredibly valuable, helping us to see the island in a new light and capture stunning photographs. we also enjoyed the local lunch spot that added a wonderful cultural touch to our day. make sure to bring cash for this. if you’re looking for a photo tour guide who is not only extremely informative but also warm and accommodating, i highly recommend any of the tours he offers. it was a fantastic experience, and his enthusiasm and expertise made the tour memorable and enriching.

i had the pleasure of joining capt. gisela for a tour of the amsterdam canals on the afternoon of 23 july. this was a highlight of my visit to amsterdam. instructions sent by email for the meeting location were easy to follow and gisela graciously allowed me and another two guests early. our tour was just over 90 minutes, as she took us down a slightly more scenic return route, and i was impressed by her knowledge of the city as a local. she spoke at length about the city's history, architecture, and historical figures, including anecdotes about the kidnapping of mr. heineken. she carefully balanced humor and professionalism while she navigated us through the busy waterways, seamlessly switching between english and dutch. after the tour, i received an automated email from capt. dave with a list of wonderful recommendations for the city, a testament to the company's attention to detail and thoughtfulness. it seems that most of the canal cruises are offered by the same five or six companies. i would highly recommend future visitors book a tour with capt. dave, whose small, locally-owned business and smaller-sized boats offers a respite from the larger crowd on land and in the water. dankjewel, gisela, for a wonderful tour! i will certainly recommend my friends and family members book a tour with capt. dave when they have the opportunity to visit amsterdam in the future.

i had the pleasure of visiting the bar, and it truly lives up to its reputation. the ambiance is posh and elegant, with a timeless, classy interior that immediately sets the tone for a refined evening. the cocktail presentation was exceptional - visually stunning and expertly crafted. i also ordered wagyu sliders, which was delicious and satisfying, a perfect pairing with the drinks. as expected from a five-star hotel outlet, the menu is on the pricier side, but the quality and experience justify the cost. the highlight for me was the live jazz music, which added an extra layer of charm and sophistication to the atmosphere. it's a fantastic spot whether you're looking to impress guests or simply enjoy a luxurious night out. highly recommended for those who appreciate fine cocktails, gourmet bites, and live music in a luxury setting.

i had the pleasure to be with get a ride madeira for a private xc tour on january 2025. the entire day was memorable, from the pickup in funchal, to the coffee in poiso and of course to the 4 hours ride from pico do ariero to machico beach, riding through the amazing landscapes of madeira island. tiago, the guide, was extremely skilled and prepared and was able to adjust the tour based on my riding skills. helvio assisted us with the van during all the day and took some beautiful drone videos! definetly an experience to recommend to whoever wants to enjoy a mtb day in madeira!
i had the pork leg rice by a lady within a street . it was amazing , and affordable too. 5 stars for the pork leg rice

i had the privilege of experiencing the burj al arab six years ago, starting with an unforgettable breakfast. the hotel management graciously offered a guided tour, allowing me to explore every category of room and all the luxurious amenities the hotel has to offer. the interiors were stunning, and the attention to detail was truly exceptional. as for the breakfast, it was beyond impressive – an exquisite spread with top-tier options that perfectly matched the hotel’s reputation for luxury. i recently visited the hotel again, this time from the outside, and it remains as iconic as ever. the architectural grandeur, especially the sail-shaped structure, continues to leave a lasting impression. if you're ever in dubai, a visit to burj al arab is an absolute must. it's the epitome of elegance, service, and unmatched luxury. highly recommended!

i had the privilege of joining an amazing komodo tour with komodo luxury aboard the phinisi named lady grace with my mother, father, and two brothers last june on a private trip. from the moment we stepped on board, we were warmly welcomed by the friendly and responsive crew, who ensured our comfort throughout the journey. sailing on lady grace was an unforgettable experience, blending luxury and heritage for an authentic exploration of the region. the rooms were incredibly comfortable, providing a perfect retreat after a day of adventure. the journey through the stunning landscapes of komodo national park was remarkable, where every moment was filled with awe and wonder. we visited the mesmerizing pink beach, with its pink sands and crystal-clear waters creating a perfect backdrop for relaxation and unforgettable photos. this unique beach is a must-visit and truly enhances the allure of the trip. meeting the komodo dragons on komodo island was a highlight i’ll never forget, offering a thrilling encounter with these majestic creatures in their natural habitat. komodo luxury tours offers a premium travel experience that seamlessly combines luxury, adventure, and natural beauty. from gourmet dining onboard to guided excursions to hidden gems like pink beach and komodo island, every aspect of the journey was meticulously planned for a truly memorable adventure. the food onboard was delicious, with every meal offering a new culinary delight, enhancing the overall experience of the trip. this was a unique and extraordinary experience for my family. thank you, komodo luxury! if you’re looking for a unique and luxurious way to explore komodo national park, i highly recommend komodo luxury. their exceptional service, attention to detail, and commitment to creating unforgettable memories make them the perfect choice for a luxury adventure in komodo national park. 🥰🏝️

i had the privilege of taking a trip to turkey with wilderness travel. it was an incredibly special experience and the most memorable trip i've ever been on. the wilderness travel team puts so much thought into their itineraries and the guides are so knowledgeable and kind. you really feel taken care of! wilderness travel balances adventure and luxury so well. the food was incredible at every meal. we had the opportunity to hike, kayak, and snorkel. we learned about turkish culture and history. it was all around an incredible trip that i will never forget!

i had the privilege of visiting the jama'a al-imam nur al-din al-sa'alimi mosque recently, and it was a truly enriching experience. the mosque is not only a place of worship but also a stunning piece of architecture that reflects the rich cultural heritage of the area. the interior is beautifully maintained, with intricate designs and an atmosphere of tranquility that makes it perfect for prayer and reflection. the mosque staff are welcoming and always ready to assist visitors with any questions they might have about the mosque or its history. one of the highlights of my visit was the peaceful ambiance both inside and outside the mosque. the courtyard is a serene space where one can sit and enjoy a moment of peace. additionally, the mosque's cleanliness and the organization are commendable, making it a comfortable place for both regular worshippers and first-time visitors. overall, the jama'a al-imam nur al-din al-sa'alimi mosque is a must-visit for anyone in the area, whether you're looking to deepen your faith or simply appreciate a beautiful and historic site.
