i have to say for a lodge in the middle of nowhere, it is amazing. the public areas are clean and tastefully decorated with couches and chairs. there is also a pool which was a lifesaver during the afternoons when the temperatures were in the mid 30's ( and it is now winter whilst we were here.) the staff were friendly and helpful and nothing was too much trouble. we got to see my favourite wishlist which was the desert lion and elephants- truly amazing!! also the animal life one might take for granted.....giraffe, snakes, birds and buck, especially springbok. we were fortunate enough to witness a lion trying to take down a baby giraffe but unfortunately for him, the giraffe got away. still, it was nature at its rawest. the lodge also has a section solely dedicated to hyena research. which was very interesting. the only downside to the lodge is: 1. there is no ac in the rooms. at 35° during the day it is really uncomfortable at night. 2. the pool area could be a little bigger, with 8 rooms, it is a tiny area. we tried to go swim but there is just not enough space. outside of that, it is an amazing experience.

i have to warn you of three important things we had no clue of when doing this hike: 1) the neighborhood where trailhead is located is extremely sketchy 2) transport: the only way to go to trailhead is to walk 30 min uphill towards trailhead in the heat or hire a motorbike. 3) the trail itself is also completely uphill for 1h15 min in hot, humid air, to the top. i consider it a short, yet difficult hike. we took uber to trailhead, but uber refused to go up saying cars aren't allowed. from the main street, there is 30 minutes uphill walk to trailhead and the entire path is through favelas (slum neighborhood of rio). i do not recommend to solo female or even 2 female travellers to go alone. dont even risk it! you can take a motorbike which presumably charges 20 real per each way, 7 real if you speak portugués. then entrance fee is 10 real cash. the hike is 1h15 min completely uphill and about 50 minutes down back to the trailhead. then add another 25 minutes to walk back to the main street to uber back. honestly what we did which was outright stupid, was to follow google maps for walking path and to walk within the favelas to come back. we got lost. we saw people with guns, and i am thankful we made it back safe! the view at the top os outright breathtaking! i highly recommend getting motorbikes and go as a group of 2 or 3.

i have truly nothing but compliments for our time at zenguelemo. we stayed for four nights in a bungalow as part of our honeymoon, and it was the best part of the entire trip. the lodge helped us arrange an external helicopter in as well as scuba diving, which were both seamless. but the true joy of the experience came from the lodge itself. it’s in the most gorgeous possible location with an incredible snorkeling reef and sea turtle habitat literally steps away, and its position facing into the bay means you get gorgeous sunsets over the water. everything was impeccably clean and thoughtfully furnished, with plenty of cute touches like folded swans and flower petals for our first night. their community-owned and sustainability-focused model is a true leader in the field. the community staff were extremely friendly and knowledgeable (especially patty and tómas, who attended to us all weekend), and a delight to chat with, while jj and kate were also attentive and answered all our questions about the project. everything was extremely personalized and tailored to our tastes and interests, and the small boutique size of the lodge really enabled us to feel cared for and truly relaxed. usually you expect resort food to be just decent, but we were absolutely blown away by how incredible the meals were. multiple dinners were more delicious than many michelin starred dinners i’ve had. the staff even put together a dinner on the beach with champagne on our our last night, which was magical. we are beyond happy with our choice of zenguelemo, not only is it less expensive than comparable accommodation on the archipelago, it is leagues ahead of them in every possible aspect. do not hesitate and book now!

i highly recommend taking arizona route 89a, starting from the exit (exit 337) off i-17 s. head south through the stunning griffin springs area, passing harding spring trail and continuing through the breathtaking west fork of oak creek. you'll eventually reach slide rock state park, a popular yet still somewhat hidden gem known for its natural rock water slides and beautiful swimming areas. along the way, you’ll find several campgrounds nestled in the forest, perfect for an overnight stop or a peaceful break. the views throughout this stretch are absolutely phenomenal—towering red rock cliffs, winding canyons, and scenic forest drives. if you continue past slide rock, the route takes you into sedona, where you’ll encounter even more incredible vistas. from sedona, you can extend your trip by heading toward jerome, a historic mining town perched on the side of a mountain. important note: do not attempt this route with a vehicle over 40 feet long or while towing anything larger than 40 feet. there are restrictions, especially over mingus mountain, and the road is narrow and winding. despite being a long and often slow drive, this journey is absolutely worth it for the scenery and the unique experience it offers.

i hiked this trail today march 22 with a friend, the weather was perfect for hiking. we got there around 8:30am, but there were a lot of cars parked near the trail entrance. we started walking on the trail around 8:45am, and one way it took just over 90 minutes. the last 10 minutes were more difficult, otherwise this is a flat and easy trail most of the time. along the way you can see the sun moving on the mountains, the landscape can be quite stunning. there isn’t much amenity to speak of, only one toilet at parking so that’s an issue, especially today given it’s a saturday and the middle of spring break. we started going back around 10:40am, and many people arrived for a late start of hiking. in terms of difficulty, for me with a slender body i would rank it as easy to moderate. there are many viewpoints to visit in the area, but we just focused on the trail. worth returning for repeat visits.

i hiked upper falls on friday august 4th. upper falls is 7 miles round trip according to the sign however online sources say it’s anywhere from 6-8 miles round trip. i left at 6 am and completed the hike at 12 pm, so 6 hours total, i’m not a very fast hiker so that includes my rest time and time spent at the top of the falls. this is a very steep hike with 3000 feet of elevation gain so bring lots of water!! this hike has gorgous views of the valley i suggest leaving at early as possible so that you can hike in the shade, i was able to avoid the sun hiking up but not on the way down. leaving early is the best way to avoid crowds as well!! i only saw about 10 people total on my way up it was perfect. on the way down the rocks can be a little slick as most of them are covered in sand or dirt, if you have hiking poles i would bring them with you! i wish i’d brought some to prevent sliding on my way down!! i hiked to the upper falls lookout, there is an option to hike closer to the waterfall if you go down the stairs with a railing but i chose not to do that. so if you just go to the lookout you won’t see the waterfall.

i hired an enfield for two days and enjoyed my experience. i wish i’d have known how busy it would be with the sri lankan new year holidays, but i managed to find some beautiful quiet back roads around ragala. the bike was in reasonably good order. overall, recommended!

i hired sandwich harbour 4x4 for an excursion to the dunes. sandwich harbour is absolutely stunning. sand dunes hundreds of feet high, bumping up against the untamed sea. i was hypnotized by the golden sand juxtaposed by white foam waves and blue hues of the ocean waters. the 4x4 was perfect for a spectacular ride up and down the steep and magnificent mountains of gold. the wind blowing the scent of the ocean across the dunes is mesmerizing. this natural wonder is a must see on anyone’s visit to namibia. my only suggestion for the company is to enable the ability to book as a solo guest. the website requires a minimum of three in order to book, so i overpaid for two “children” that were never there. 😆

i hired the london rose for my sister's hen party and it was absolutely brilliant. i couldn't believe that it was such a reasonable price for such a large vessel - especially in central london on a saturday night! craig was really accommodating with access for me to measure up beforehand and decorate on the day. he also answered any questions i had really promptly over email. we had the bbq food on the night which was brilliant - it was high quality food and there was loads of it. the staff on the night were just amazing - a big thank you to jack and the rest of the crew - caterers, bar staff and dj included - thank you all for making it such a brilliant night. i would definitely recommend these guys for any celebration.

i initially booked beyond boracay adventure, but it got canceled since they didn’t meet the required number of participants. they offered me a refund or to join the next scheduled trip — so i decided to hop on the island tour instead. at first, it was a bit awkward (i’m a shy person, and i tend to struggle keeping up with conversations, especially with foreigners — in this case, 1 from australia, grant; 3 from london, fiona, josh, bradley; 3 from spain, aina, joan, nico; 1 from taiwan, ken; 1 from the us, sarath and 2 of us from ph, grecca bradley’s partner). but as the day went on, i didn’t regret booking this activity at all. even though it was a small group, it turned out to be so much fun. i eventually connected with everyone — especially fiona and ken — and even got a little too competitive during the games (to the point where i was “arguing” with nico 😅). if you’re a solo traveler like me, whether it’s your first time in boracay or not, i’d definitely recommend this activity. special shoutout to jae and gregg, and the rest of the crew, for keeping us safe and making sure we had a great time. ✨ haqqy life boracay – where strangers become friends, and every sunset feels like home. ✨

i initially contacted andean ways enquiring about a private transfer from copacabana and to puno. with the efficient response i received i enquired about a few other tours and trips we were hoping to do. i ended up arranging our entire bolívar peru adventure through andean ways, including uyuni salt flats and star gazing, copacabana and isla del sol, puno and the floating islands, cusco sacred valley tours and an amazing hike to huchuy qosqo, they even organised sighting andean condors! the customer service and communication with fredy has been excellent, we had to make several last minute changes to arrangements, nothing was too much trouble. every trip they had arranged perfectly, excellent knowledgable guides, drivers etc. the trips were, where possible, off the beaten track and less touristy. even the lunches were great. i wouldn't hesitate to recommend andean ways, just a pity they only cover peru and bolivia.

i joined abdel and slimani on the epic 4-week long trail through morocco. we did 900 km and it was absolutely amazing, what an adventure. our guides were fantastic, they took very good care of us and of the horses. the horses were absolutely incredible, some did the entire 24 riding days, a few got replaced along the way and everyone had a horse that suited his or her abilities. the food was fresh and tasty; pancakes, cereal and many other things for breakfast, fresh salad and a warm dish for lunch and soup and another warm dish for dinner. the camping spots were really nice. the 3 hotels along the way were "ok", i think we were all happy with a bed and a shower so nobody complained 😂 this was definitely a challenging ride and most likely it's not for everyone. you can't be a whiner or a complainer, you can't be too "sensitive" about horses and you have to let go of your european mindset. what i mean by that is, the horses are very well taken care of, they get plenty of food and they are in excellent condition but this is a 4-week ride with many many kilometers per day (most days around 35 km, several days of well over 40 km, and even one day of 51 km) so some horses will clearly be tired on some days and walk a bit slower, some will start the day a bit stiff with sore muscles, some will be sensitive walking over the rocks in endless river beds, on the day of the sandstorm they didn't have lunch because the buckets would fly away, and so on... but at the end of the ride we had absolutely nothing but respect for their endurance, their toughness and their spirit. what made the ride even better was the spirit, the mindset, the character and the sense of humor of all the riders and of the guides. we were a very diverse group of 9 women and one man, many different nationalities, different riding levels, ages between early 20's till late 60's but we blended into one great group so fast and so easily. everyone was kind, caring, funny, genuine, tough, considerate, open minded, helpful and 100% ready for this incredible adventure. spending a month with 9 "strangers" can be a fun experience or it can be a bit of a nightmare, in this case it was so much fun, it is by far the loveliest group of people i've ever ridden with. this was the adventure of a lifetime and i definitely recommend it !

i joined atoll in august 2024 to complete my divemaster training, and i can honestly say i had the best 3 months of my life. arthur, shrimp, seb and jeff are the best team i could have ever asked for. on my very first day they instantly made me feel so welcome and i immediately felt as though i was part of the team. the course itself was taught fabulously - arthur and seb were extremely thorough and made the course so enjoyable. i definitely wasn’t the most confident diver prior to starting my divemaster training, but thanks to them i now feel completely comfortable and confident in my ability. the dive sites themselves were absolutely incredible, with so much to see everywhere you go - whale sharks, manta rays, octopus, guitar fish, turtles, sting rays, grey reef sharks and so much more! the boat is super spacious and comfortable. and as i’ve mentioned, the team are the best seychelles has to offer! i cannot recommend atoll divers enough… you should absolutely book in to dive with them! i can’t thank you all enough for such a fantastic experience - i miss you already will definitely be back soon!

i just returned from an incredible oars trip down the colorado river and up the bright angel trail. this experience was absolutely life-changing — even more impactful than i imagined. the natural beauty of the canyon, the stars, the petroglyphs, the wildlife — all breathtaking. but what truly made the trip extraordinary was the oars staff. every guide was professional, kind, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about the river and its history. our trip leader was phenomenal — empowering her team while creating space for us as guests to get the most out of the experience. every member of the crew brought their own unique strengths, from deep geological expertise to engaging storytelling, strong logistics, advocacy for the land and native peoples, and just sheer joy in what they do. they struck the perfect balance between taking care of us and letting us feel the adventure. i came home not just with amazing memories but with a deeper appreciation of the canyon and the people who work so hard to share it responsibly. can’t recommend this trip highly enough.

i just returned home from my trip to mt. kilimanjaro national park with my team from kilimanjaro brothers climbing adventure. i completed the 8 day climb on the lemosho route. i booked my trip as a solo hiker. i utilized the "5 star climb" option that they offer. this option included a large tent, a mattress to sleep on, a great food menu including many local foods, and a personal porter. it was definitely worth the small upgrade fee. when i first decided to book this trip, i didn't know what company i was going to book with. i starting reading reviews on tripadvisor. i narrowed it down to kilimanjaro brothers climbing adventure because of their stellar reputation and the great reviews. it was very important to me to find a local company, as well as a company that treats their porters fairly. the group i was with included 11 people and myself. you can tell that these guys love their job. they seemed like a very tight knit group, like a family. after selecting my company, i selected the lemosho route. this route is supposed to offer great acclimatization. we had instances where we would hike to our next camp, do an acclimatization hike, and then return to camp. i think this really helped with my acclimatization. "hike high, sleep low." this route is also supposed to offer better scenic views, which i agree with. i had many questions along the way. george mtaki was very fast in answering emails. during my climb, i was constantly being asked how things were going. they truly cared about my well being and my experience. they were quick to assist with pictures and offer history about the mountain and culture. on summit night, my guide priscus and my summit porter charles offered nothing but great and much needed encouragement. they really helped me summit and i will forever be in their debt. i had the best experience possible in tanzania and i believe it was all due to kilimanjaro brothers and their excellent staff. i highly recommend you use them for your climb also. you definitely won't regret it. visited october 2016

i just stumbled across this place recently looking for cuban food. now i'm determined to eat at every single restaurant here. the cuban food was really solid. the service was excellent. the place is very relaxed and laid back but the food is upscale in a way. everything is very unique and delicious. tonight, i went to olives, crackers and cheese for the best grilled cheese sandwich i've ever had. seriously, i've been to places that have specialty grilled cheese and this place blew it out of the water. there are so many elements that can go wrong in making one. the bread... the bacon... the balance of caramelized onions... the way the cheese interacts with the entire thing. i can confidently say that this place absolutely knocked it out of the park. the bread had just the right amount of crispiness. the bacon was tender but not even remotely mushy. the onions were spot on. i got a great sandwich and a real salad for 20 bucks. not just some lettuce with a package of salad dressing. tomatoes, cucumbers, croutons and cheese. a great place for some healthy food i will definitely have to try the charcuterie. the burmese tea is fantastic as well as the guava lemonade at the caribbean restaurant. not only will i be back this week for the caribbean food, but i plan on being a regular at most of these restaurants. if you want good food without breaking the bank and a casual environment, this is the place to go.

i just visited the ankor market supermarket in siem reap, and i'm still reeling from the shock of how clean it was! i mean, i've seen cleaner gas station bathrooms, but this place takes the cake. it's so spotless that i'm starting to think they have a secret army of cleaning ninjas working overnight. but seriously, ankor market is a great place to stock up on all your cambodian essentials, whether you're a local or a tourist. i picked up some amazing cambodian chocolate, coffee, and sweets that i'm pretty sure will last me until the next khmer new year (just kidding, i'll probably devour them all by tomorrow). the prices aren't exactly rock-bottom, but hey, i was on a tight schedule and didn't have time to go bargain-hunting. besides, i was too busy marveling at the aisles of pristine shelves and wondering if they had a 'no dust allowed' policy. the staff, on the other hand, were a bit of a mixed bag. they weren't exactly rude, but they seemed to be competing in some sort of 'who can be the most indifferent' contest. i had to go on a treasure hunt to find someone to help me, but when i finally tracked them down, they were friendly and efficient. all in all, i'd give ankor market 4 out of 5 stars. it's a great place to shop, even if the staff could use a bit of a caffeine boost (maybe they should start selling cambodian coffee in the break room?). definitely worth a visit, especially if you're looking for some authentic cambodian goodies!

i left the museum more confused than anything else. the beautiful old building is completely empty, unused, despite its great potential. the main building, the modern part, is very, very large... and it feels empty. the entrance fee is cheap, but at the same time, i wouldn't have paid more for only two or three rooms with so little content. i learned a few things, thanks to google translate since everything is in japanese. what was shown was fine, but where are the artefacts? i wouldn't call a museum a place that shows more projections of artwork than actual art pieces in "flesh-and-blood". they did have a temporary exhibition on top of the permanent one but it was about the new season of an anime that just came out, and i was looking to learn about japanese/kyoto's history. i left almost convinced that i had missed a good part of the museum, but i asked two staff members and apparently not. the ground floor is also very confusing, with scattered shops and empty spaces... it's a real shame, there is a lot of potential for such a museum in a country and a city with such a rich history. the texts should also be translated, or at least have some audios in english that summarize them. museums should be accessible to everyone as long as people are respectful of the place. i'm still giving it 3 stars because the staff was very welcoming, a lady from the staff took the time to explain certain parts to me in english, thank you very much to her.

i lived near this market for close to a year. i enjoyed starting my mornings off with an easy stroll to this market to get some donuts and some hot cambodia breakfast. i routinely bought my household goods, groceries, clothing, and killed time at this market place. i made new friends and saved a lot of money by shopping here in the long run. there’s a really cool car park on the top of the market, with stalls that provide seamstress and tailoring services, salon and barber shops as well as cold drinks, and sometimes food. i also found the entire area around the market and the vendors to be a friendly and hospitable place. there was always something new to discover, and i really miss living next to this market. to meet new people who traveled from deep in the countryside to come closer to the city to sell their goods and food was a very unique cultural experience and it definitely helped me with my language skills while living here. you need to support your local markets! this is not a big money superstore like the air-conditioned glossy supermarkets that are popping up everywhere now, this is the riel cambodia!

i loved my visit to the park. the aqueducts were beautiful and there were a lot of walking paths that were well maintained. a great break from the usual sites in rome. i’d recommend you take the day, rent a bike and ride the via appia antica as well.

i loved our visit with the kiddies. i was nice to see all the little independent businesses. lots of coffee shops, bakery stalls. fruits, honey and cheese stalls. of course it was very busy and hard to go round with pram due to some cobble areas and cars going round but overall we managed. everyone had card machines which made life easy. wish there was more areas to sit. some decent halal options. and yes yes the viral £8.50 strawberries are worth the hype.. que up for this it goes very fast. i wouldn't personally go again as it was so crazy packed out but loved my visit x

i loved riding this boat! it was a unique experience that you don't get to have often, i did find it weird that our dinner schedules were moved around last minute but they made up for that with the live jazz music and the view on the boat. the food was great but i wished it were better, i can't wait to ride this again when i travel here again!
i loved that we were able to find a health food grocery store during our stay in puerto rico, they had everything we needed to stay eating healthy while traveling.

i loved the aga khan museum—it presents islam in a sophisticated and authentic way, just as it truly is. the exhibits feature ancient islamic details that are rich, meaningful, and deeply inspiring. most of the staff are elderly, and their kindness and warmth made me feel like i was being welcomed by grandparents. visiting this museum feels like stepping into another world—calm, spiritual, and beautifully serene. the architecture of the building is truly distinctive, both inside and out. everything is spotlessly clean, and the choice of colors and the attention to detail are simply exceptional. this is by far the most beautiful museum i have ever visited. i truly appreciate the efforts of every employee working there.
i loved the book store, and the aesthetic in general, ideal for any tourist to visit

i loved the experience there! you can see, taste and smell the local life! all the local fruits, vegetables, spices, nuts, dried and smoked fish. and yes, we bought a bunch of local delicacies as souvenirs(coconut candies, sea almonds, local honey, dried mango, breadfruit chips and more). i recommend to visit this place while you are in male.
i loved the experience!!! highly recommended, marcela was the best.

i loved the historical part of old dubai. the landscape, tastes, flavors and color are amazing. you can come in about 4 or 5 pm and the temperature will be good, go from marina until the burjuman metro station (about 5 aed), and there walk or take a small ferry (it cost only 2 aed). the ferry option is good if you want to take a small trip and see the landscape of dubai creek that's beautiful. i definitely recommend this place
i loved the place and will soon go there again. it's just breathtakingly beautiful and the environment is enchanting. with their tasty coffee ☕ and serene environment its just the right destination.

i loved the way the animals were well treated.thumbs up for everyone who works there,as i recommend to everyone looking to find themselves a furry friend for life.godbless you all.

i loved this beach. it really felt like paradise. there are changing rooms and lockers which are around 2,000 but the restrooms are free. the umbrellas were free and the water wonderful! very shallow and good for kids but rocks on the side which could be sharp. absolutely stunning location. very near the bus stop and had a car park as well. loved it!
i loved this market israeli vintage antiques and collectors items

i loved this museum! i am particularly interested in the settlement era of iceland's history, so this was really interesting for me. there were lots interesting exhibits to read and explore. i spent a couple of hours there! i am disabled. the museum is wheelchair accessible with accessible bathrooms, although the museum floor itself is undulating. be a little cautious. the museum is free for disabled people, but you have to ask. they don't seem to suggest this discount, no matter how disabled you look!

i loved this nature scene in the city, i think it's quite small, but it is definitely worth a visit, especially in the late springtime. the koi fishes were beautiful and the whole garden just had a really good feeling about it.

i loved this park very quiet and i just felt like laying on the grass. we did pass by some people doing drugs but we wouldn’t have noticed if this guy didn’t come over to tell us we were in a part of the park where they do drugs. very nice of him. other than that i liked it a lot. it’s not so busy. and we even passed by people making music and danced a bit. i would go again to have a picnic.

i loved this spa! i’m definitely planning to go back and highly recommend it! it was surprisingly busy for a thursday, but thankfully it’s so big that it didn’t feel too crowded. there were plenty of sauna options and the view was beautiful. the waterfalls in the cold bath were stunning. overall, such a great experience — and i loved that they offer unlimited robes and towels!

i loved this spot, because this is where i saw an elk for firts time. i feel like they just neglected the sixth bridge. by the time you come from maligne canyon view point to 6th bridge the water is flowing in river and not any more falls. it's still pretty with picnic tables and all , and easy to dip your feet in water though.
i loved this walk. it’s is not just one view. you get lots of great views. good idea to do clockwise to avoid steep rocky descent.
i loved touring cuba! this place was beautiful!

i loved visiting ceramics verdi—it was fascinating to watch the pottery being made and hand-painted right there in the studio. the attention to detail is impressive. i picked up a small espresso cup as a souvenir, and it’s a beautiful reminder of the experience. highly recommended for anyone who appreciates handmade art!

i loved visiting the palace. the old and new wing were beautiful and it was nice to read all the information about the different rooms. to travel there was very easy by bus. i do recommend buying your tickets before you visit, because it can be crowded and you can basically immediately enter if you have your tickets ready.

i loved visiting this botanical garden - just one of four amazing gardens in prague. it was fascinating. it had many plants from other continents and everything was clearly labelled and put together with other plants sensitively and beautifully.

i loved visiting this gallery, the photography of jeju-do is beautiful and offers an interesting perspective into the different emotions of the island through the changing of the seasons. the artist also has an inspiring story that increases the beauty and sadness of the moody and emotion enhancing photography. the garden is also a delight, scattered with small clay figure sculptures throughout. worth the trip off the beaten path to experience a little bit more of the island.

i loved visiting this place. it's a great place to go and have fun with friends or your partner. i went for a birthday party and loved it. the tour was good, with stops for the restroom. along the way, they sell you almost everything: corn on the cob, potatoes, blankets, beer, pulque... rental a mariachi band. it's a little pricey ($300 pesos/$15 per song), but it's worth the fun, haha. go and have fun! bring cash; few accept transfers or card payments. cash only in the water.

i loved visiting — it felt like a calm retreat hidden away from the busy medina. the detailed artwork, especially the tiles and carved wood, was incredible. wandering through the quiet courtyards gave me a real sense of peace. it’s a beautiful, reflective space that really stayed with me.
i loved watching the sunset on this beach. super quiet and a beautiful view!

i lucked out by calling denali adventure tours because our previous days plan was cancelled by inclement weather. other tour companies i found were booked out for a week or longer. i spoke with whit who asked what i was looking for. i simply replied "something epic, for 3 adults preferably today". he chuckled, "i have just the thing. small aircraft flight around the summit of denali." oh hell yes! with a credit card over the phone, we went to the local airport 3 hours later. the flight was on a piper navajo, a 6 person (plus pilot) twin engine aircraft. one hour flight, with recorded narration and stories by the pilot. the flight was smooth and omg worth it! we saw the glaciers below, and circled the denali summit as promised.the experience was absolutely breathtaking. thank you whit for the most memorable experience

i made a mistake when scheduling the routes. i used part of the jeep road as a shortcut. actually, you should not. these are busy roads for pink jeep carrying tourists having fun on bumpy rocky roads. kinda not safe for both if you use the jeep route. the target for this trail is the chicken point and submarine rock. it is an easy trail. standing on top of submarine rock was fun, especially when we hiked in the rain. by the way, i think it is the hardest one among dry creek road (to devils bridge, 1 mile/one way) and schnebly hill road (to mary go round rock, 3 mile/one way) if you want to drive yourself.

i made a reservation with his tour. it was a tour of 11 people. the bus arrived on time and there were no japanese except us. there was a japanese instructor named tomomi, and after the other instructor explained it in english, she explained everything in japanese, so it was okay if i couldn't speak english. other instructors, including tomomi, are also very friendly. after receiving an explanation, i enter the sea. i'll see a turtle in about 45 minutes. the weather was nice and there were a lot of turtles, so it was a lot of fun. the water temperature was a little cold, so it would be cold after it went up, but there was no problem if i put on a jacket. if you're wet, it's cold and you won't be able to enjoy watching the diamond head or the hula dance show, so i think you need a towel and a jacket. the ship shakes a lot, so if you are prone to getting sick, i think you should be prepared. but i'm glad i joined this tour because i can see beautiful scenery and cute turtles. if i have the opportunity, i would like to participate in other tours with tomomi. they also take a lot of photos, so i think it's great to make memories in hawaii. thank you very much.

i made some google and found sering. he had great support us before the trip and on the trip. some recommend places were good and beautiful. i will contact him if i have a chance to visit leh in the future.

i mainly came here to buy big packs of bottled water but it’s a supermarket well stocked with lots of different products and brands at reasonable prices. the first couple times i came here i was still unfamiliar with the currency and the checkout girls were very patient and honest (i gave them way too much and they helped pick out the correct lesser notes)

i make a point to have lunch here whenever i'm in berlin on a friday. check out the turkish food vendor with the steaming hot pots of vegetable and meat specialties... or fresh turkish bread rolled up and filled with meat or vegetables as a fast and very popular take away snack. around the corner is an excellent thai food truck, too. i like to request one of their vegetarian noodle bowls and combine it with their fresh homemade chicken coconut curry (€6 in 2023 for this special order). lots of other markets set up for business. fruit market vendor, for example, offers samples of his ripe fruits to sample.

i mean i dont even know how to describe the perfect flow of this trip. there is so many people included in the organization and all is communicated and flows perfectly and you can relax at all times knowing they are taking care of you and your safety. there was a stop at rissani with a guided tour, stop for lunch, stop to feed the monkeys, anything that was asked it was arranged. dris was an amazing guide. i organized the trip to morocco so i do know how much effort organisation takes but this is a well oiled machine, works perfectly. well done guys!!!

i mean, it’s a beach in hawaii so it’s hard to give it less than that, but it was the rockiest of all the beaches i went to during my week on oahu. it’s a real locals spot and not the place to go surfing, but if you want a chill day in some calm waters with some stunning views, maunalua bay has it.

i must agree with the reviews saying that you cannot find this place if you can’t read japanese. there was only one sign next to the elevator saying “take the elevator to the 5th floor for sky garden” i can understand if they want to keep it for the locals since it was so peaceful without the crowd. there are vending machines to get cold drinks and a small sitting area inside in case you feel exhausted under the sun. i loved how they designed the garden 😍 of course the entrance is free and you can access via both elevator and by road.

i never review places but this was above and beyond exceptional. the owner took my mother and i out on a personal tour and it was second to none. great views, quality service, and great conversation. i strongly recommend this tour.

i originally came to the galápagos hoping to see sea turtles on a cruise boat. while everything on the cruise was beautiful and i could see many things, i was a little disappointed that i didn’t get to see any sea turtles (it had always been my dream to swim with them.) that’s why i decided to book with guiding galápagos. i wanted the chance to snorkel with sea turtles and visit the famous black beach. i had the absolute best time on the tour with them!! the guide (yazmany) was incredibly experienced and knowledgeable, and knew exactly where to go for the best underwater sights. it was very special to me to see all the amazing marine life, from sea turtles, huge marine iguanas, stingrays and many colourful fish. the people on board were extremely nice, we had delicious snacks, even saw dolphins on the way and the black beach is nothing short of amazing! all in all, this whole day was something i’ll never forget. if you’re looking for a unique adventure and a perfect day out on the water in the galápagos learning from local experts, i can 100% recommend this company to you!!

i rarely write reviews because it's not really my thing, but this time i feel compelled to share my experience. i went out on john’s boat yesterday. it was just me, john, and another person who was taking a kitesurfing lesson from him. i'm an experienced kiter, and i only needed to rent gear and get a lift from the boat. from the moment i arrived, i sensed something was off. john seemed stressed and irritated, as if my presence was a burden and would interfere with the lesson he was giving. despite that, the agreement was that i would stay as close as possible to the boat while he taught the other student. i did exactly that for a couple of hours—until the wind dropped. at that point, john picked up the student (who was only about 100 meters from me) and took him to a spot with better wind, leaving me stranded in the middle of the water with no wind. they went so far i could barely see the other guy's kite. i waited for over an hour, freezing and starting to experience cramps. still, john never returned for me. luckily, the wind eventually picked up again, and i was able to cross the bay and land in berkeley. i borrowed a phone from someone on the street and called john, who eventually came to pick me up. when he arrived, he just laughed and said, "i told you i couldn’t pay attention to you because of the lesson." i'm still alive because i’m experienced—and because i was lucky that the weather and currents were on my side. but yesterday, things could have ended very differently. john's complete disregard for my safety put my life at serious risk. he saw me out there for over an hour and made no effort to help. in my opinion, this was not only irresponsible—it borders on criminal negligence. i genuinely question whether he even has a license, and if he does, i don’t believe he deserves to keep it. if you value your life, do not go out to sea with this person.

i read several reviews before choosing which trails to hike and decided to start with rocha do chambre, as people described it as easy to moderate compared to misterios negros, which was rated moderate to hard. i am not a regular hiker, but i’m not out of shape either. surprisingly, i found rocha do chambre much harder than misterios negros, but also more entertaining and scenic. the terrain was incredibly varied. i’d say hiking shoes are essential, as there’s a section with volcanic stones and many areas covered with tree roots. the part where you have to climb using ropes can be quite challenging if, like me, you don’t have much upper body strength. i was very glad i followed the advice to hike the trail clockwise (there was no rain and there was not much mud). some people mentioned that it gets harder at the 3 km mark, but they were probably hiking counterclockwise, since after 3 km the trail became much easier for us. i would definitely recommend this trail and would do it again. when we were leaving around 14:00, there were so many cars parked, so i’d recommend arriving before noon.

i really enjoyed it here. the historical buildings were really interesting. not too many tourists although a school trip of kids showed up while i was coming back. at first i was worried that the dry river bed meant there would be nowhere to swim but if you just keep following it, you will get to some natural pools. there is one which is lower down that everyone seems to stop and think about jumping into, if you want to swim in there you just need to go around and climb down the hill. its not easy but thats the only way. mildly bothersome having random people come up and just stand there watching you swim, i know theyre wondering how to get down themselves but it feels a bit weird. water is also quite chilly. also the steps have lots of places where you can fall and in general the soil was very dry and loose. you may fall on your back or trip unless youre careful. the historical buildings themselves are cool and the swimming ties it all together and makes it generally a place i would recommend visiting. the stairs will get tiring though

i really enjoyed my visit to ilhéu da aves. the garden is beautiful and very well maintained, with a wide variety of colorful and exotic birds. what impressed me the most was the open space where you can walk among the birds and observe them up close. in the zoos in my country, birds are usually behind glass, which makes it hard to see them properly — so this was a very unique and pleasant experience for me. the only downside is that i found the entrance fee a bit high. however, overall, it was definitely worth it, and i would recommend it to anyone visiting madeira.

i really enjoyed my visit to the natural history museum in london. the building itself is absolutely stunning! the architecture alone is worth the trip. it’s easy to reach via the underground, and entry is free (although i do recommend booking a time slot online in advance). inside, the museum is clean, well-maintained, and full of fascinating exhibits. there’s a wide variety on display - from fossils and gemstones to volcanoes - and everything is presented in a way that’s both informative and engaging. i also visited a temporary exhibition on space and the question “could life exist beyond earth?”, which was really interesting. (note: this exhibition required a paid ticket, but it was well worth it in my opinion.) the main downside was how crowded it got, especially in popular sections like the dinosaur gallery. also, the café prices were quite high, which is something to keep in mind if you're planning to eat there. overall, a great experience that combines science, history, and stunning architecture. i’d definitely recommend it!

i really enjoyed visiting dormition abbey, it’s marked as the spot where mary, mother of jesus, died. the building itself is so beautiful and big, i wanted to enter and see it’s interior but it was closed and i was told that it’ll open in 2 months. it is also located next to last supper room according to christianity. it’s totally recommended while you’re in jerusalem.

i really enjoyed visiting the musée national picasso-paris (part of paris museum pass). it’s a beautiful museum in a historic building (starting from the antique statue at the corner of the entrance), and it has one of the best collections of pablo picasso’s art. you can see his paintings, drawings, and sculptures. the museum is well organized, and you can follow picasso’s journey through different stages of his life and work. one thing to know before you go: you must leave your bag in the cloakroom, which is downstairs. it’s free and safe, but it’s better to travel light if you can. there’s also a small garden behind the museum. it’s a nice quiet place to sit and relax. the entrance to the garden is inside the museum too. it’s worth finding though. picasso was a master of traditional art, but he chose to be creative and free, "like a child". you can really see that in the artworks on display. the museum is not too big, so you can enjoy it in one visit. the staff are helpful, and the signs are in english and french. i highly recommend it to anyone visiting paris.

i really hesitated before writing this review because the staff and crew were genuinely kind, warm, and attentive — they truly did their best and i feel bad sharing a negative experience. but i believe others deserve to know what to expect before booking. sadly, the experience did not live up to the name komodo luxury. apart from the lovely staff, there was very little that felt luxurious. the boat was not well maintained, not particularly clean, and we did notice some cockroaches, which was very disappointing given the high price. the comfort level was far below what we were expecting. the itinerary is identical to dozens of other boats doing the same route in komodo — there was nothing exclusive or special about the experience, except for the much higher cost. most of the people onboard felt the same way, and recent reviews reflect that too. by the end of the trip, we were honestly just counting down the hours until we could get off the boat. it was such a letdown, especially given how excited we were beforehand. if you’re seeking a more comfortable and upscale experience, i would honestly recommend staying at a resort in or around labuan bajo and doing day trips to the islands by speedboat. it’s not far and allows for more comfort and flexibility. again, i feel terrible writing this because the crew was truly wonderful, and none of this is their fault. but i personally would have appreciated seeing a review like this before booking — it would have saved me a lot of money and helped me enjoy komodo in a more comfortable way.

i recently did a reef cruise that took us out to moore reef and then over to fitzroy island for lunch — and honestly, it was one of the best trips! everything was really well-organised, boarding was smooth, and the crew was super friendly and welcoming. the boat itself was clean, spacious, and comfortable, which made the ride out really relaxing. once we got to moore reef, we anchored at a large pontoon where the real fun began. snorkeling was amazing — the water was clear, the reef was full of fish, friendly turtle, and beautiful corals. i also did a dive and it was very well guided, thanks to vance master diver. they also had an underwater viewing area and a slide into the ocean, which added a fun. after all the water activities, we headed to fitzroy island where lunch was waiting. it was a great spot to chill out and the food was surprisingly good — fresh, tasty, and plenty of options. the island itself is beautiful, so it was nice to just relax on the beach for a bit before heading back. i highly recommend for anyone wanting a fun, and easy way to experience the great barrier reef!

i recently did the bow falls trail in banff, and it was such a refreshing and scenic experience—perfect for anyone looking for a short, easy walk with rewarding views. the trail is very accessible, starting right near downtown banff, close to the banff springs hotel, so it’s easy to fit into your day even if you’re short on time. it’s mostly flat and well-maintained, making it great for families, casual hikers, or anyone who wants a gentle nature break without a strenuous climb. the highlight, of course, is bow falls itself—a powerful, wide waterfall on the bow river that’s beautiful to see up close. there are several viewpoints along the trail where you can watch the water rushing over the rocks and feel the mist on your face. the sound of the falls is really soothing and adds to the whole nature vibe. along the way, you’ll pass through some lovely forested areas with plenty of shade, and if you’re lucky, you might spot local wildlife like birds or squirrels. there are also benches and picnic spots if you want to take a break and enjoy the surroundings. a few tips from my visit: • the trail is fairly short (about 1.5 to 2 km round trip), so it’s doable even if you only have an hour or two. • wear comfortable walking shoes — the path is mostly dirt and gravel but well-maintained. • bring a camera or phone for photos; the falls and river views are fantastic, especially on sunny days when the water sparkles. • if you want to extend your walk, you can connect to other nearby trails like the bow river trail or stroll over to the banff springs hotel for some history and maybe a coffee. • early morning or late afternoon are great times to avoid crowds and enjoy softer light for pictures. overall, bow falls trail is a beautiful, easy escape right in banff that lets you enjoy nature’s power without much effort. whether you’re traveling solo, with family, or friends, it’s a peaceful spot that i’d recommend adding to your banff itinerary!

i regret visiting this zoo as i ended up actually sharing the sadness and depression that a lot of the animals there are enduring whilst being trapped in old, tiny and dirty enclosures. they say going to prison and being confined to a cell changes a man physically and psychologically, the same can be said with the animals here. being locked up in small (by global standard) enclosures with very little space to move around and the lack of stimulation will naturally affect them mentally. it was heartbreaking to see the polar bear, tiger and the lion (to name only a few) look so downtrodden and depressed. whilst i understand that the zoo is relatively old and is rundown in many areas with quite a few empty exhibits and enclosures, it seems there has recently been some work towards renovating and rejuvenating the place, however the money looks like it's being spent in the wrong areas. why splash all the cash on flashy new toilet facilities or an information centre when it should be invested in upgrading and improving the living facilities of the animals there? whilst it's 75% zoo and 25% amusement park, it's probably best to scrap the amusement park aspect, reduce the number of species on display and improve the facilities for the main attractions - quality over quantity, if you will. if the animals are happy, lively and running around, the public will come see them and make repeat visits but those that come at the moment will leave with a feeling of sadness for the animals as the facilities are so poor and the animals don't look well. this is 2024, so the ethical treatment of animals should not be dictated by the facilities and doctrine set in place from last century. being a city owned zoo, i get that tax payer dollars fund it, but at the same time, if you can't afford to maintain and operate it properly, then perhaps it's better to just shut it down completely? why allow the poor wildlife to suffer unnecessarily? 👎

i spent an entire month here, diving six days a week, obtaining both my advanced open water diver as well as my emergency first responder & rescue diver certification. the communication with cassie from the office had been flawless since the beginning, and made organizing my trip from home very easy. all my questions were answered briefly, and all the paperwork (questionnaires, bills for safety deposits) were detailed and delivered promptly. my daily pickup from friwen island was reliable, and gave me the opportunity to pick a homestay a bit further away from the dive centre. the abundance of dive sites meant that even after having done over 50 dives with them, i barely went anywhere twice. i really loved the fact that they keep on rotating dive sites in a way that ensures that even if you stay for an extended period of time, you will unlikely end up at the same dive twice. since there are two boats for the two morning dives, whenever there was a boat going to a dive site that i had already been to, i found my name assigned to the boat that was going to the other location—no need for asking. they also have a wish list where divers can submit dive site request, and all of the requests were granted within the next two days. they always ensure that there are enough guides on each boat, which means that there will never be more than four people assigned to one guide. on average, though, my group would consist of 2-3 divers per guide. they do a really good job at evaluating every new diver‘s abilities, certifications, as well as air consumption. i found that really amazing, because it means that you will be paired with divers who match your own profile, and you will be able to get the most out of your dives. i joined all of the day trips tarzan has to offer (except for wayag), and every single one of them was nothing but fantastic. if you are wondering whether you should spend the extra money, the answer is a hard-resounding yes! the dive centre itself has a very warm and welcoming family-like atmosphere. within a short time, i felt like i was part of the team, and after a month, it was hard to say goodbye. with the owner being german, and the dive guides being local, you truly get the best of both worlds. everything is up to western standards when it comes to organization, cleanliness, equipment maintenance as well as safety procedures. at the same time, the guides welcome you with their indonesian warmth and jolly attitude without exception, while being able to show you the reefs like only a local could. their knowledge of the waters of raja ampat is truly impressive, and i felt safe and very well taken care of, no matter which dive we went on. as for my certifications, the instructors (ute & mario) were nothing but professional, patient, and eager to answer all of my questions. the groups are kept small, and i never saw more than two students per instructor for any of the courses that were given while i was there. i had one other student with me on my navigation dive for the advanced open water diver, but apart from that, i had the luxury of receiving a one-on-one treatment for both my aowd as well as my rescue diver course. i felt well-prepared, and can confidently say that i got the most out of those courses. if you have the time and spare change, tarzan really is the right place to bring your skills to the next level. all in all, tarzan diving truly is a wonderful dive centre, and i can assure you that you will have a fantastic time here, no matter how long you stay. every person i met during my month there was sad to leave, and i feel that speaks for itself. i am holding all the memories close to my chest, and hope i will be able to return one day!

i spent months researching travel in israel and creating an itinerary for my family to visit this extraordinary and historical part of the world for more than two weeks. i soon realized that because the entire country is so steeped in political, biblical, religious, and world history, it would be impossible to see and understand it in a meaningful way without input from an expert local guide—and i set out to search the internet, travel guides, and travel magazines for the best private tour guide in israel. after many hours of research, i decided to contact arik from arik private tours in israel. hiring arik to drive us all over the country—from north to south and east to west—and show and tell us about the extraordinary geography and history of israel—turned out to be a great decision. arik picked us up every morning and was in a good mood as we set out to explore another part of israel. arik is exceptionally knowledgeable about religious history and the history of israel and the middle east. but what makes arik a great tour guide is that he is also very personable, fun, authentic, and witty—and he embodies the local israeli culture. through our interactions with arik over the course of almost two weeks—and watching arik interact with local jewish and muslim people—we gained real insight into the local culture and gained a special understanding of life in israel. now, long after our time with arik in israel, we still fondly remember him and quote some of his one-liners. if you are looking for a private tour guide in israel who will do more than drive you from site to site and recite some of the historical significance of each location, you should stop looking and contact arik. you'll be glad you did and the memories you make with arik will last a lifetime.

i spent the day exploring camden for the first time and it completely lived up to its reputation—vibrant, lively, and packed with character. we started by wandering through the markets, which are an experience in themselves. it’s a proper feast for the senses—street food aromas drifting through the air, music playing, and stalls selling everything from vintage fashion to handmade jewellery and odd little curiosities. it’s easy to get happily lost for a while. after eating (there’s so much choice, it’s almost overwhelming—in a good way!), we rounded off the day with a canal boat trip. it was a lovely, peaceful contrast to the energy of the markets, gliding through the quieter side of camden and beyond. i’d recommend pre-booking as it was busy, but totally worth it. overall, camden has a raw, creative charm that’s hard to find anywhere else. i’d definitely go back—maybe next time for the live music or a night out.

i spent the last leg of my honeymoon after cape town and kruger here, and it was a great way to unwind and relax the must-do activities to do among those included are the castaway picnic, sunset dhow cruise, and snorkeling (2-mile reef is spectacular). the helicopter ride over is also ultra scenic. the swimming with horses is also fun. the village tour gives you a better understanding of how the local villagers live. one thing to note is that the rooms can let bugs or even geckos in due to not being fully sealed off from the outside. so do not be surprised by this. the meals are high quality and the service offered by your butler is top notch. the staff does a great job of making you feel at home and catered to. it was a relaxing to just sit out on the beach (which your room is just a few steps in front of) or at the pool or at the swinging bed and read. going in the july / august may be better and less muggy, but ultimately late february / early march was best for our timeline. at that time of year there was mugginess during the day. tip: at night if you go in the water, you can see some bioluminescence.

i spent the morning riding with dbt nz and it was the highlight of my time in new zealand. scott and the team are all legends, their passion for riding and the outdoors is evident from the moment you arrive at their hub in queenstown. these guys are legit, scott competed on the mx gp world tour in his youth and still tears up the track daily. tours are catered to your experience level and not only did we have an epic day riding through the infamous skippers canyon- an epic playground of endless tracks that the team know intimately, my riding improved immensely due to scott’s experience and advice. truly enjoyed my time with this crew, they’re super welcoming and great company on the trial, taking photos and giving a casual tour as you ride. my only regret is not having more time to explore skippers canyon with these guys for a few more days. many thanks lads!

i spent three days working with andrei in april 2025. andrei took the time to educate me on the learning process before signing up. he outlined everything clearly and helped me map out a schedule that worked for me and my family. as we got into the lesson plans, everything was exactly as he described. andrei is a knowledgeable and patient professional, getting up to speed with how to manage the gear, each step, and doing it safely takes time. i felt safe and confident throughout the process. andrei did a fantastic job.

i spent three unforgettable nights at this wonderful place. the view was absolutely beautiful, the rooms were clean and comfortable, and the food was incredibly delicious. the reception staff and all the team were extremely respectful and kind, which made my stay even more enjoyable. there were a few small insects, which is expected given the location in the middle of the jungle, but overall it was an absolutely fantastic stay. highly recommended, and i would definitely love to come back.

i spent time at f-one wingfoil center this past weekend taking some beginner introductory classes. i would recommend to reach out and book in advance as they easily get full for lessons! i have some experience in kiting, but this is an amazing sport to learn! the instructors are very knowledgeable and great at demonstrating but also being able to verbally communicate each step of the sport. very cool atmosphere around the shop itself and all the staff are so helpful for anything with booking in advance to planning the next lesson and fitting you correctly with the gear for the conditions on the day and your skill level. when you get to a level of being in the water on the foil the school uses radios for communication which is an amazing way to learn when starting out and getting tips in areas that you want to improve. 100% recommended this place for wing foiling in boracay, and even the philippines!
i started from 3 am. and reached around 5 am. the path was slippery after the rain. the view was beautiful and peaceful. not crowded at all. good for exercising.

i started to have pain in my knee while running and training for my first marathon. i went to sport performance and they were immediately able to tell me what the issue was and begin to help me recover. everyone there was friendly, professional and extremely knowledgable. with their help i was able to complete my first marathon and continue to fix the issue i was having with my knee. i would highly recommend them to anyone looking for physical therapy!

i stayed at 4 accommodation spots across raja ampat and the eco lodge was the best. as a scientist who monitors the health of marine ecosystems in western australia, it was incredibly heartening for me to see the amount of effort that jack (the owner) goes to in order to maintain a healthy reef with such limited resources. jack can be seen doing coral restoration diving on the house reef daily or working in the permaculture garden. the latter meant that the food was phenomenal, great mix of local dishes and western comforts like woodfired pizza with home-grown ingredients.the staff were exceptional, the service polite & friendly. if you're into marine conservation & want your tourism money to be used for good, then i highly recommend this place 🙌🏻

i stayed at barefoot conservation for 9 weeks and got my advanced open water whilst there. matt was an amazing instruction and i can say i feel so confident diving due to matt’s teaching! the living conditions are basic but managed well with the limited resources. the cleanliness of the camp is down to the volunteers to keep clean which is amazing as those who want to keep the space clean put in the effort, i had no problems with the cleanliness of the camp in my 9 weeks. iris works so hard on a daily basis, with no days off and still makes the camp environment so welcoming and warm. she does soo much to ensure an amazing experience for the volunteers. there will obviously be bumps in the road but she handles them with speed and efficiency that there is no need to worry for the volunteers! the science team, niko, tilly, septy and illman, are the most desecrated team i could have wished for. it is so clear just how much they care for the raja ampat area and want to pass on their knowledge to all volunteers who are there. the many projects on the go at one point in time are managed so well and i never once felt like i was not making a contribution. they made sure all of us we trained to a high standard to contribute to the data collection. the local staff deserve so much recognition for the work they put in daily, the skippers waking up to pump tanks and drive the boats and the chef for cooking 3 meals a day for 6 days a week is commendable. on sundays the volunteers cook for themselves, the equipment and food available is limited due to the remoteness of the island so it can be a bit tricky. the rooms are so beautiful, i could not of imagined a better accommodation before i arrived. the animals in the camp are so sweet with a couple fights here and there but they made the time so much more enjoyable. ringo is the sweetest dog and loves pets, sweet potato and kentang are so cute and it’s amazing to have animals that are always around. they even walk with you to the shops and around the village. suki and foxy are also very sweet. the diving in raja ampat is breathtaking and the staff do all they can to ensure you see as much beauty as possible in you time there! the community projects are less than advertised but still an amazing experience to be able to take part in. the english lessons once a week are so rewarding and interesting learning for us and for the kids. the football match on tuesday is an amazing way to get the kids involved with the volunteers. overall i loved my time there and am planning to go back and get my dm certification because i loved it so much. a massive thanks to iris, matt, niko, tilly, and septy for making the experience even more enjoyable!!

i stayed at camp with my wife and 10 year old son in july of 2024. the experience was the best in our two weeks in alaska. there is a magic in this place that traces back to the founder's commitment to experiential learning and environmental stewardship. my son was the only child in the group and the staff made an extra effort to learn about his interests and engage with him. i dream of going back daily. and this isn't advertised: camp denali has special concessioner status that the other lodges in kantishna don't have. this allows them to drive along the denali park road and guide hikes within the original park boundaries (wonder lake area and along park road). the other lodges cannot guide within the original park boundaries. additionally, there no views of denali from the other lodges which are situated in much lower lying areas.

i stayed at jasmine. it's easily the best in terms of view and a general feeling of 'openness', if that's what you want. all other pods look out into an enclosed yard, which means a lot more privacy. from jasmine, you can sort of see the public walkway (through the trees), and part of the jasmine living room doors are visible from the main thoroughfare. however, the part of gbtb that the pods are located are very quiet; i was there over a weekend and i maybe saw 5-10 people walk past each day. i believe the outdoor areas of some of the pods are 'linked', in that you could walk from one to the other. but it's all cleverly designed and landscaped so you don't realise it, and it does feel private. i was there for a birthday celebration, and had considered booking the entire compound so i could bring more guests. in case you're thinking of booking all 4 pods for a big party, be prepared that each pod is designed to feel quite self-contained, so effectively rather than one central party you'll likely end up with 4 satellite parties. there are (understandably) no direct sight-lines to/from each pod. i reckon if you're at gbtb you want to 'get away' from the bustle of city life, and for this, the garden pods absolutely nail it. i think the price tag is reasonable.

i stayed at serengeti safari lodge in december 2024 for one night. this is a wonderful lodge in the serengeti and i’m so glad i was able to stay here. when i arrived i was greeted by a large dinner spread containing lots of options of different food and dessert which was very much needed after a long safari day. the room was clean and large and given the remote location i was very impressed by how nice it was. the staff were also great and allowed me to come for breakfast early (before the official start time) as i had a really early start the following day. they also packed me a tasty and large packed lunch to keep me going during the next day of my safari!

i stayed at serengeti safari lodge in december 2024 for one night. this is a wonderful lodge in the serengeti and i’m so glad i was able to stay here. when i arrived i was greeted by a large dinner spread containing lots of options of different food and dessert which was very much needed after a long safari day. the room was clean and large and given the remote location i was very impressed by how nice it was. the staff were also great and allowed me to come for breakfast early (before the official start time) as i had a really early start the following day. they also packed me a tasty and large packed lunch to keep me going during the next day of my safari!

i stayed at the andbeyond grumeti river lodge in july for four nights with my wife and couldn't be happier with the experience we had. we knew it was one of the most luxurious properties in the serengeti, but we didn't expect the level of service to be so outstanding. the staff is exceptionally attentive to the point of picking up your preferences very quickly. the room is beautifully decorated with incredible amenities such as a plunge pool (cold and ideal for hot days), a comfortable bed, and a spacious shower. the food was phenomenal, with all the alcoholic beverages you desire. i didn't like to see the lack of appreciation from some guests towards the staff. even though this property is pricey, it doesn't give you the right to act rudely. remember that the safari guides driving the vehicle are responsible for providing you with an excellent experience. in other words, they know where all the animals tend to be and communicate with other guides to learn where the animals are at any moment. therefore, remember to be kind and treat them with respect and dignity. they aren't your private chauffeur, even though that's what it appears to be. lastly, remember to tip them at the end of each day. that's the recommendation from our travel agent, and we saw most people not doing it. i highly recommend this property to anyone wanting the best safari experience in luxury. thanks, joseph (manager), frank (buttler), willie (safari guide), and everyone else for an incredible experience.

i stayed at this hotel for a week on vacation and really enjoyed it. the location is excellent, and although there's some construction nearby, it was quiet inside the room. the breakfast was one of the highlights - plenty of options and very good. the staff were also very friendly. i highly recommend it for anyone looking for a well-located hotel with breakfast included. since i was out exploring singapore during the day, i mainly used the hotel to sleep and have breakfast.

i stayed for an hour in this park, enjoying the beautiful weather and relaxing in nature. it was so refreshing to see groups of people gathered together, talking and spending quality time away from social media — just enjoying life. it’s a really nice and peaceful place, perfect for unwinding and reconnecting with the moment.
i stayed for the honeymoon and it was amazing. one life time experience. the migration was right by us so we could watch it from our tend. the food was good too. highly recommended

i stayed here for 8 days on a business trip and had a very pleasant experience. the rooms were clean, quiet, and comfortable; perfect for unwinding after work. breakfast each morning was fresh and satisfying, with a good selection. a special mention goes to ms. may in the cafeteria, who was always friendly and helpful. overall, this is a great option for a cost-effective and comfortable stay. i highly recommend it for both business and leisure travelers.

i stayed here for a week. i would say this island has a good internet than other islands in raja ampat. it was covid when i got here so the island wasn’t that busy, that’s how i enjoy it! there are 4 warungs around for you to get a snacks, drinks, soap, etc. the local people are nice and there are a manta researchers who stay there as well. the have a clean public toilet, got a free warm shower at the day and cold shower at night😂 the island is pretty small, just need 30 minutes to see all of the island. there are so many beautiful shells around the beach. it’s a maldive in indonesia! firstly time saw a nemo here, there are many beautiful clams, the fishes and corals are beautiful. i enjoyed my stay here and would love to come back here as soon as possible!

i stayed here in june of 2023, and let me just say that this is hands-down amongst the top-3 of all lodges i've had the pleasure of staying in ! we stayed in the 'family' room, and honestly, i think my entire apartment can fit in it with ease ! you get a fully-stocked mini bar (no alcohol), a super-comfy bed, numerous charging stations accommodating eu & uk plugs, a gorgeous rain shower (as you look at the hippos), plus a bathtub for you to unwind in after your safari. don't get me started on the delectable food... i highly recommend this lodge. you won't be disappointed. oh, there's a gym too...:-)

i stayed here on the final night of my gobi desert tour, and it was the perfect way to end the journey. the food was delicious, everything was spotlessly clean, and the wi-fi was fast and stable — which is rare to find in remote areas of mongolia. even after visiting many places across the desert, this guesthouse stood out as exceptionally good. the quality and care put into every detail made it feel like a true oasis. the owner was incredibly friendly and clearly experienced. i was amazed to learn that he had studied in santa monica, usa, and even worked as a sushi chef — no wonder his english is absolutely perfect. if you’re traveling through the gobi and want a comfortable, reliable, and welcoming place to stay, i can’t recommend this guesthouse enough.

i stayed in david's place for two days in july 2024, but it has been enough to feel at home... i loved the genuine kindness of david, the loving attention and the fantastic food of his wife, and the competent company of their daughter, who took us around to the sacred places. it was unbelievable making a bracelet with their tecniques... i really liked that this family loves their island, with its memorable history and culture. and you will end up loving it, too. wish i had more days, also to contemplate the view of the lake from our bedroom window ... thanks to all. giusy

i stayed on arborek at barefoot conservation for a month. it was my first time travelling by myself and i used it as a starting point for my trip. it was a great place to start. the staff were all super friendly and very easy to talk to. the group was so homely and all the volunteers get along well. the science was incredible, i came an unqualified scuba diver and became an advanced certified diver during my stay. i learnt so much about all the species that inhabit raja ampat and took part in numerous reef checks and surveys which were so much fun! i highly recommend going here if you are into marine biology and even if not, what a great place to learn:)

i stayed one night with my family in two double bed rooms and one triple bed room. recommended!! everything was fantastic. room was clean and nice. staffs were well mannered. best thing is their swimming pool. it is amazing and beautiful. we also enjoyed free pass by monorail due to the booking in this resort. it may be same in case of sentosa's other resorts bookings also. though i'm not sure. only negative thing if i say that they close their kitchen at 10pm. so after that you can not order and eat anything. we didn't know. but good thing is that there is a 7-eleven beside their kitchen. so we survived the night somehow.

i stayed there in may as a first time visit (in the country of mongolia). i really enjoyed the experience, the huts were very spacious and clean, we also had booked one with an integrated bathroom, so we didn’t have to go to the outside toilet at night. i liked the traditional elements of the inside interior. the owners are exceptionally friendly and always happy to help. as we arrived late on our first evening, they stayed up to ensure we arrive safely. they also had great suggestions regarding sightseeing in the area. the meals are cooked fresh every day and offer an insight in mongolian cuisine. i absolutely recommend staying there!

i stayed with gilber and mariela for two nights and i had an experience like i have never had before or ever will. they were incredibly helpful ahead of arriving and arranged for a taxi and boat to collect us, same for the return journey when they provided blankets and hot water bottles at 4am. the food they served was delicious and the activities they provided were very interesting (fishing, history of the uros, tour of the community) i suffered from altitude sickness and they went above and beyond to help me. they came to the main land, took me to the doctor and arranged for my prescription and ticket to be collected while i recovered. i cannot recommend titikaka iquina lodge, gilber and mariela enough. you have to stay here if you go to lake titicaca!

i stopped by trajan’s forum in the evening, and it was pretty cool! it’s not as hyped as the colosseum, but it’s got its own vibe. the ruins, the columns—all so old it kinda blows your mind. there weren’t too many people in the morning, not too few either—just enough to enjoy it without a crowd. i stood there, looking at the stones, imagining how lively it must’ve been back in the day. neat place, definitely worth a look in rome!

i strongly recommend isabel k spa. first, my facial was very good. the aesthetician was very thorough at every step. also, the place is very clean and welcoming. overall a very professional spa location. i have to note that the owner went above and beyond to help me with a difficult situation. i left a necklace in the facial room and realized i had left it that night/the day before i was going back to the states (sunday when they are closed). i wrote to them late saturday night, they responded first thing in the morning on sunday and the owner agreed to go on her day off/sunday to return the necklace. i was extremely impressed and grateful for it! this was certainly a gesture of honesty and professionalism worth noting.
