i stumbled upon this tour while searching for a kayak adventure that can take my 4-year-old in cancun, and it turned out to be an absolute gem. david, the owner, went above and beyond by tailoring the experience to our needs, showcasing genuine care for his customers. a minor injury threw a curveball the night before our scheduled tour, but david’s flexibility and concern for safety impressed us. we rescheduled for another day at 7 am, and what initially worried me about the morning chill turned into a delightful “sunrise cruise.” the vibrant sky, crystal-clear waters, and fabian, our guide, made the early start worthwhile. fabian was a star—capturing stunning photos, introducing us to wildlife like stingrays and sea stars, and guiding us through a thrillingly narrow mangrove channel. the whole tour felt both adventurous and safe, a testament to the expertise of the guides. i highly recommend this experience to anyone seeking a unique nature encounter in cancun. the combination of a family-friendly approach, breathtaking scenery, and knowledgeable guides made it an unforgettable journey.

i think the sfmoma is better. a strong start for a 4-star review, but i mean it. i may have a bias towards modern art, but i prefer art that makes me think. while the deyoung has small sections on recent and contemporary works, most halls are lined with classical portraits, old furniture, and ancient artifacts. therefore, the deyoung museum feels like a history museum rather than an art one, with many sections categorized by eras and time periods instead of artist or genre. while both the deyoung and the sfmoma have beautiful buildings, the sfmoma is less dated, better maintained, and offers a lot more art. with that out of the way, the deyoung is still an exquisite museum. the african exhibit was my favorite. the items displayed here feel so otherworldly, with exaggerated features and unconventional forms. and yet, they are undeniably human, preserved and presented so nicely in this quiet, dimly-lit room. honorable mentions are a particular kind of heaven by edward ruscha and petunias by georgia o’keeffe. i have a few positive comments to add. one thing i find admirable is the deyoung’s ability to keep their artworks in their ‘natural’ states, framing and setting them up in certain ways, or even going as far as to keep them open to the air. that’s a little dangerous in my opinion, but also something i respect. additionally, the employees are extremely sweet and helpful, and youth admission is 100% free! now for a few genuine criticisms. first, organization. besides the temporary and special exhibitions, the theme is lost in a lot of these galleries. some collections of art may be from the same time period, but have little if any correlation between one another, which takes the visitor out of the viewing experience. second, minimal information. a lot of works and selections need explanations or further analyses. there was even one artwork that seemed to be missing a plaque. third, a lack of interactive activities. they have art carts for sketching on saturdays, but that’s about it. i know it’s an art museum, not a playground, but the deyoung could benefit from something more interactive, even if it’s as simple as a permanent corner where guests can get creative. sfmoma has a number of those. overall, not my favorite art museum in the city, but still a must-visit! 4/5.

i think the view from morro dois irmãos is the most beautiful in rio de janeiro. the trail to the top is of medium difficulty: short, but quite steep, and it can get slippery if it has rained. i wouldn’t recommend it for those who don’t enjoy hiking. however, to enjoy a view of this magnitude, i’d say it’s the easiest trail in rio. to get there, you’ll need to take a “mototaxi” (r$7–10 per person) from the entrance of vidigal favela, or you can walk up — which takes about 30 to 60 minutes, depending on your pace. once the mototaxi drops you off, you’ll pass a soccer court and soon see signs for the beginning of the trail. there’s a “voluntary/mandatory” contribution of r$10.00 collected by local residents (make sure to contribute), and from that point on, the trail is up to you. the path is fairly open and well-trodden due to the high number of visitors, but poorly marked. halfway through, there’s a small stop where you can buy beer, water, soft drinks, and some snacks, and sit on small chairs with a view that’s already stunning. from there on, the trail gets steeper and more slippery. i did the hike in 40 minutes, but if you’re not used to hiking, it may take you between 1 and 2 hours. bring something to eat, but always respect nature and take your trash back with you.

i think their entrance fee is almost same with aqua planet in pampaga, which makes it too pricey considering this is a mini version - a lot smaller than ap. however, we still enjoyed our short stay in the afternoon. this is sulit if you're a guest of astoria and you get a free pass here, just like what we did.

i think this is one of the best things to do in sydney. it is absolutely incredible paddling out into middle harbour. there are so many great things to do; a nice chilled out paddle with friends over to clontarf beach and over to balmoral beach for a coffee stop, or exploring the hidden bays up middle harbour. in summer if i'm lucky there's even a little boat that chugs around selling ice creams & coffees on the water - my overseas friends go nuts about this! (this business isn't related to sydney harbour kayaks). i've always found their equipment to be really well maintained and they have some really nice high end kayaks and surf skis for hire. the staff are friendly and right into paddling. in summer it can get busy so i've found it pays to call ahead and make a booking, plus put on lots of sunscreen. if you're a frequent paddler like me, you can also buy an annual pass which works out to be really good value. this has to be the best "gym" in the world!

i think this is the best store in boracay🙆 the owner here was very accommodating to my urgent request. the owner also introduced me to some good hotels in boracay. i recommend this store & reasonable.
i think this is the most underrated viewpoint in athens, not much people mention it but definitely worth to hike up here and enjoy the sunset city view

i think this is the one and only experience in greece that is close to a palace. king othon and queen amalia spend a couple of years in this building. very nice decoration plus some digital installations that are not high-tech but manage to deliver the atmosphere and experience of the 19th century. the museum consists of 2 buildings, the ticket cost 5 euro and you'll probably spend around an hour in it. behind it there is a very nice bar that you can try and have a drink 🍸. definitely recommended!

i think this place is quite overrated, at least the things we saw there. outside the stores ist mostly 'made in china' and they charge you a fortune. then you see some stores, i guess they get kind of famous on tiktok or so, but nothing special or "made in china" too. i think this was an excellent tour for the adventurous person. jorge was very kind and supportive, provided a ride from and to my hotel, and took photos for everyone. the equipment was necessary and of high quality. please know this is not a rappel, exactly. you will climb up and down hanging ladders but the equipment is necessary for safety and it is still very fun to descend into the cave and explore it.

i think visiting this temple with a knowledgeable guide enhances your experience. my initial reservation about visiting quickly dissipated as my guide discussed the temple's rich history and present-day use. you can feel the thousand years (+) of history; only if the stones and carved images could speak! sarongs are provided for free, along with assistance to put on and remove.

i thoroughly enjoyed this museum! lots and lots of exhibits with great explanations. i was particularly interested in the settlement era. there was a lot of great stuff about that, as well as the switch to christianity from paganism. i am disabled. the museum was accessible with accessible bathrooms. it is also free for disabled people, but you have to ask. they don't seem to offer the free pass, no matter how disabled you look!

i thoroughly enjoyed this museum! true hawaiian culture to enjoy here. the house is beautiful and the guided tour information was extremely informative. any additional questions no matter how trivial we're beautifully explained by the intelligent history expert who has big goals and a great hawaiian history to share. only took about an hour to walk through, although you can go much faster if you don't read the tour guide.

i thought i will find this place as the soul of muscat, unfortunately it wasn’t. you see omanis only as shoppers but not as salespeople or serving customers. in the other side i found some souvenirs that i can add to my collection from the world. one hour is more than enough for the visit. night time would be better as the market is not conditioned.

i thought it was a real shame that almost the entire neighborhood was under renovation, and you couldn't really see it all. many paths and areas were closed off. i would have loved to explore otherwise. but what i was able to see was beautiful. i found it historically and culturally rich. very different from modern dubai. here you can see how the "native arabs" really lived in the past. it was still very interesting.

i thought shiretoko might be the most beautiful national park in hokkaido, but after visiting akan-mashu... well, maybe it was the weather that we were blessed with! a must-visit in hokkaido! i had already visited in winter, but it was completely transformed in summer.

i thought that no one cared about tuong art anymore, but i was surprised when i went to see the comedy "miracle medicine" and saw that most of the young people came to see it, not the elderly or the old. i suddenly realized that it was not that this art was forgotten, but that we were too indifferent. it was wonderful to see that the younger generation not only continued but also promoted traditional cultural values, with great enthusiasm. the young people have really done a great job in bringing tuong art closer to the young. they not only inherited but also created and renewed traditional cultural values, making tuong more lively and accessible. the limited edition playing card set is designed in a sophisticated, luxurious, and meticulous way, making tuong both elegant and attractive... the 2nd floor of the theater is designed as an exhibition space, introducing the bold imprints of tuong art through the ages, including: costume from outstanding plays. musical instruments and items related to the art of tuong. the vietnam tuong theatre, established in 1959, is a professional art unit under the ministry of culture, sports and tourism, with the mission of preserving and promoting the traditional art of tuong of the nation.

i took a walk around city hall park during my lunch break, and it was the perfect mid-day reset. the park is nicely maintained with plenty of greenery and a peaceful vibe, even in the heart of the city. although the fountain isn’t working, the space still feels relaxing and worth the visit. there are benches if you want to sit and people watch, and the surrounding architecture gives the park a classic new york charm. if you’re nearby and need a quick break from the office, it’s a great spot to clear your head.

i took my bike in to have the wheel trued, and two weeks later, the hub seal broke. they washed their hands of the problem by saying they don't remove the hub when changing spokes and truing the wheel, but in my case, the cassette had burrs they didn't remove, and the entire sprocket assembly came out. they didn't check the position of the dust cover when reattaching it. finally, they gave me a hard time with the damaged hub. as "service," they sold me a hub and didn't charge me for assembly... even though i had a healthy hub and they mistreated the repairer during the work, claiming they had "too much work," i consider it a joke. i sincerely do not recommend this shop's service; they damage parts and take no responsibility.

i took my down’s syndrome and deaf brother on a trip through road scholar, organized by the denali education center. not only was it a great experience and facility but they went way above and beyond my expectations to make my brother feel at home. they supplied not one but two als interpreters to make sure he understood all the lectures and discussions that were part of our trip. food (healthy gourmet buffet) and accommodations were excellent as was the energetic and friendly staff. field trips offered a variety of options for different activity levels and budgets. the dec also organized our trip to ankorage and seward and provided great field trips, accommodations and food options in these places as well. the train ride in the window enclosed gold star car with full meals included was my favorite along with the visit to a sled dog kennel where we got to play with puppies. i can’t say enough great things about these people and the experiences they provided for myself and my brother ❤️.

i took my partner on his birthday as he loves cars. i found it interesting too. it is a wonderful collection with a nice range. well kept. the place was comfortable with seating too. i would recommend!

i took the 12:30pm khmer cooking class on a thursday in siem reap, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable parts of my trip! from the moment a tuk tuk picked me up and whisked me away to the peaceful countryside, i knew i was in for something special. to my surprise, i was the only guest in the class, which meant i had not one, but three amazing chefs all to myself! sky, one of the instructors, was incredibly helpful and friendly. he gave me a tour of their beautiful garden and introduced me to the herbs, vegetables, and ingredients that would be featured in the dishes. it was such a lovely and grounding start. i chose to make mango salad with dried shrimp, fish amok, pineapple fried rice, and banana with coconut milk, and every single dish turned out absolutely delicious. the chefs were not only patient and engaging but also thorough in their explanations. they even offered suggestions for substitute ingredients i could use back home and promised to send me the full recipes afterward (a total lifesaver!). even when a heavy rainstorm rolled in during my meal, sky and sorya continued checking on me to make sure i was comfortable and enjoying myself. their hospitality was truly next level. highly recommend this experience to anyone visiting siem reap, even if you’re solo! you’ll walk away with a full belly, new skills, and the warmest memories.

i took the afternoon safari, the initial welcome was good and the buffet, while rushed, was okay as well. time for the main event. zero communication about boarding the busses. you're just told "this one is not yours". you just have to wait and check for each bus in turn. when we finally boarded, right from the start the guy drove like he wanted to drop everyone out of the bus. a lady literally fell to the ground, and parents were complaining to the driver about their kids being flung across the seats. he clearly didn't care. whenever we encountered any animal, he stopped and talked about 30 seconds. after which he just turned his back and within 10 seconds, with zero warning he would just start driving again. phones fell, people gasped, water bottles were flung across the floor... all in all, a very very bumpy ride, super uncomfortable, you don't really get to see any animals up close. the hippopotamus will always be under water according to the guide's own explanation. so, you only see something like floating rocks from afar and you're suppose to assume they're hippos. very little pause for any pictures. you can expect to see (from afar): 1 lion and 3 lioness, 4 elephants, a few zebras, 3 giraffes (from veeery far), some gnou and 2 rhinos. (and hippos that look like floating sticks in the distance).

i took the gravest risk in february 2023 kilimanjaro climb at the age of 68 (i told close ones that i might not come back from that trip before departing sri lanka). it went well up to the last camp (kibo hut). it was below freezing and snowing. my oxygen level at a dangerous low of 65 but i wasn't feeling. appetite lost and couldn't eat enough food but agreed to continue starting 11pm. safely reached gilman's point 5685m (first of 3 points at the summit) at dawn where i expected to have breakfast. we were 2 hikers, and each one had a guide and 2 porters. other hiker was a fast climber (viet 70km marathon runner) who didn't like my slow pace and went ahead earlier with her team. my breakfast had gone with her guide. then continued to next stella point 5756m. after that i reached the ultimate goal uhuru peak 5895m and sat on a boulder. i had passed out and when i regain half consciousness, i was flat on ground with oxygen feed. took the iconic photo and the guides decided i had to be brought down asap. came climbing down with 2 aides to kibo hut (last camp). then i was transferred on a single wheel manual stretcher to next camp horombo hut from where i was taken to a hotel in the nearest city by 4wd suv. full recovery took several weeks. kilimanjaro hike is open to non-climbers but i took the shortest (cheapest at $1500) 5 day option. 6 day hike includes an acclimatization hike before the last leg. as a lesson learned i recommend choosing 6 or more days.

i took the half day rainforest tour. communication was excellent regarding the reservation. the van picked me up on time at my hotel. diana was very fun and informative. we didn't get to swim in the river due to a flash flood warning so, she took us to a beach instead. i had a great time and would book with this company again.

i took the historic tour with creole queen. i had an excellent time. dr. tarantino gave a knowledgeable yet entertaining intro to the history of louisiana. we stopped at the grounds of the last battle for lousiana between america and the uk. the national park guides gave an excellent recount of the events. then, i had a nice meal, great lousiana cuisine taste (nonstop buffet while the ride lasts). lovely bartender chappi put together the right mix of drinks to make everything more enjoyable. th weather was excellent to enjoy amazing cruise views. highly recommend without hesitation.

i took the sierra chincua tour in january and it was a perfect day trip from mexico city. there was a nice car for the longish drive, about 4 hrs each way. the butterfly sanctuary was stunning. the butterflies were flying all around and the views were fabulous. the hike was about 2.5 miles and not terribly hard or technical. there was enough effort to feel the payoff when getting to see the butterflies. afterwards, lunch and a guided stroll in angangueo was a treat. we had diego as the guide and he was attentive, knowledgeable, and helpful. i highly recommend this tour.

i took the tour to española island with scuba kicker rock and it was an unforgettable experience. everything was very well organized, the guide was excellent, and the tour allowed us to see blue-footed boobies, albatrosses, and sea lions in their natural habitat. the island is simply spectacular. i recommend this agency 100%!

i took the two (2) hour denali-air circumference flight. it was incredible. to experience denali the from the air is “ah” inspiring, and overwhelming. the approach to denali is almost poetic…starting in low-elevation plains and river valleys of taiga forest, which transition into high alpine tundra, and gradually elevates to jagged granite snowy mountains. climaxing with the grandeur and magnitude of denali’s snowy glaciated cliffs and peaks. chris was our pilot. he did a great job. chris is a steady handed pilot, who had great knowledge of the area, and a fun attitude. go/book with confidence!

i used this service on my first trip to cancun. i had originally booked a different tour, but there was a problem with the tour company and the tour was canceled a week before, so i used this service. it was a last-minute reservation, but they responded quickly and courteously, and customized it according to the places i wanted to go. (cancun → chichen itza → cenote ikil → cenote suitun → valladolid) they set the order of the places i wanted to go to, taking into consideration the crowding, so i was able to enjoy the tour without experiencing any crowds, and they also prepared drinks, towels, and other equipment, so i was able to visit the tourist spots empty-handed. it takes about two and a half hours from cancun to head to the chichen itza ruins, but manager yoshida told me interesting stories about mexico and prior knowledge of the ruins, so we got there in no time. there were also photo spots and detailed explanations inside the ruins, so it was a very interesting experience. after that, they took a lot of photos at the cenote, so i was able to record a lot of memories. for lunch, we were taken to a restaurant serving yucatan cuisine, which is hard to find in japan, and it was a very satisfying lunch that left us full. throughout the tour, we were given video and photo guidance and posing instructions for each photo, which made it a very memorable and valuable experience. after this tour and our trip to cancun, both my wife and i have become completely captivated by the charms of mexico. we would definitely like to go to mexico again, so we hope to see you again next time we travel.

i used to visit kew gardens way back in the late 80s and early 90s when i was young when we'd come to the beaches to visit family. i played in the plunge pool, on the playground structures, and ran around the large open spaces. it's lovely to see that it's still very much the same 30 years on and that this generation can enjoy it as i did back in the day. now, i can further enjoy the large mature trees and the small grove of dawn redwoods in the southeast corner. well worth wandering through the gardens if one finds themself in the beaches.

i usually don’t write reviews for the malls , but i feel this issue needs to be taken more seriously as it affects both customers and the staff. every time i come to circle mall, i am approached in the parking lot by multiple workers running towards my car, offering to wash it. if i say no, i end up feeling uncomfortable, and honestly, it puts both me and them in an awkward situation. i can see these workers are only trying to earn a small income, often standing for hours in extreme heat — 50+ degrees outside, and even hotter in the parking. they have no proper shaded seating or ventilation, and it’s clear they are pushed to compete with each other in this way. this is not only unpleasant for customers, but also unfair to the staff. i stop them almost every day, asking them kindly not to run, because i feel bad for them. but i shouldn’t have to feel guilty each time i park my car in a mall i visit daily. a very simple solution can solve this problem: • place a visible phone number or whatsapp contact where customers can request car washing service directly by sending their parking slot number (for example: “car at 186, please wash”). • this way, customers who want the service can request it, and workers no longer need to run around or pressure people. i am not against these workers; in fact, i respect their hard work. but this system is uncomfortable, unprofessional, and has been mentioned in many other reviews already — yet it seems not to have been taken seriously. i sincerely hope circle mall management will finally address this issue in a proper way.

i usually go to museum when the weather isn’t good but seeing this museum bathed in sunlight was beautiful. i love this type of architecture so i highly recommend it. it was really peaceful. there’s various exhibition and most of them are free for students ! also famous reference to the animated movie 「your name」.

i usually make a point of using my swimsuit at least once on holiday, and after researching the various lidos, i chose this one because it seemed to be the quietest—and we’d actually walked past it the day before. i didn’t fancy one with a crab as a lodger or rough waters that wouldn’t suit my mum. this one isn’t the closest to town amenities, but that’s probably why it stays so peaceful. we had a bit of a laugh getting in. there’s a little kiosk outside with turnstiles, and as we were fiddling with some doorknobs trying to figure out where to go, a head suddenly popped out the other side to greet us—scared the life out of both of us! we paid for two sunbeds and access, and i also bought a padlock. ironically, i’d taken one out of my bag while packing, thinking i wouldn’t need it—so definitely bring your own to save a couple of euros. inside the complex, it was lovely and quiet—though bear in mind this was a weekday in may with temperatures around 20°c. still warm enough to enjoy without the crowds. we spotted some lockers, and since i had my swimsuit on underneath my clothes, i just got changed right there. mum went off looking for the ladies' changing rooms. there was some work going on around the pool and it was a bit overcast, so most people were just sunbathing—but me and mum had a proper go in the pool. it’s one of those that’s shallow around the edges and deeper in the middle—great if you’re not a super confident swimmer. it overlooks the sea too, and you can walk further down to a section that lets you into the ocean itself, though it was a bit choppy that day. upstairs seemed to have a spot for kids or teens, and there looked to be a café, though i couldn’t tell if it was open. at the end of the day, we went back to get our stuff from the lockers and got whistled at a bit awkwardly—turns out we’d been using lockers next to the gents. but there weren’t any clear signs saying they were for men only, so we just shrugged it off and headed over to the proper ladies' changing area. overall, it was a chilled and peaceful experience—definitely one of the quieter lidos. i don’t think i’d cope with it in peak season, but for a calm, low-key day, it was perfect.

i visited the big buddha on lantau island. it was amazing! the buddha is huge and beautiful. the area around it is peaceful and quiet. i went in the afternoon, and it wasn't too crowded. i liked that i could take my time and enjoy the view. how to get there: you can take the *ngong ping 360 cable car* from tung chung town centre. the cable car ride is about 25 minutes and offers stunning views of the surrounding landscape. i recommend a crystal cabin for the clearer view. alternatively, you can take *bus 23* from tung chung town centre. the bus ride is about 45 minutes. for more information and tickets, you can visit the ngong ping 360 website. overall, the big buddha is a must-see attraction in hong kong. it's easy to get to, and the views are amazing!

i visited the burj khalifa and went up to levels 124 and 125, and the views were absolutely worth it. the elevator ride up was incredibly fast and smooth, but surprisingly, it didn’t have a view—just a digital display showing the floor numbers as you ascend. still, it builds anticipation well. once at the top, the 360-degree views of dubai are breathtaking. from the city’s skyline and highways to the desert and coastline, it’s a surreal perspective you don’t get anywhere else. level 125 was slightly less crowded and had a beautiful interior with traditional arabic patterns, which added a nice touch.

i visited the palawan wildlife rescue and conservation center during my recent trip to puerto princesa, and i’d say it was one of the more eye-opening parts of my itinerary. the place is often referred to as the “crocodile farm,” but there’s actually more to it than just crocodiles. as soon as i got there, i was greeted by the sound of birds and the smell of fresh foliage—yes, it has that “wild” vibe right off the bat. the tour started with a short orientation inside a small museum-like area, where i saw an actual preserved skeleton of a massive crocodile that used to live there. it’s jaw-dropping in size—literally. from there, we were guided toward the hatchery area, where baby crocs are kept in separate enclosures. i was both fascinated and slightly unnerved seeing dozens of baby crocodiles squirming around. they looked harmless but knowing what they’d grow into gave me chills. then came the highlight: the adult crocodile enclosures. there’s a sturdy metal walkway above their pens, and i could see at least a dozen large crocs lounging in the mud or half-submerged in water. one of them let out a deep rumble-like hiss, which made everyone on the platform stop in their tracks. it reminded me these animals are powerful predators, not just zoo attractions. what i appreciated most was that this center isn’t just a tourist spot—it has a strong conservation and rescue mission. they also care for other wildlife, like hornbills, eagles, and other rescued animals. some are in rehabilitation, while others are permanent residents due to injuries or being raised in captivity. the facility isn’t flashy or commercialized, but it serves its purpose. it’s educational, humbling, and worth visiting if you want a closer look at palawan’s natural biodiversity—and a better understanding of why conservation matters. pros: • up-close view of crocodiles at all stages of life • educational and conservation-focused • chance to see rescued birds and mammals cons: • some areas need maintenance • not ideal for people who don’t like the sight (or smell) of wild animals would i recommend it? yes—especially if you want to experience something raw and real in palawan beyond beaches and islands.

i visited the royal air force museum london today and had a fantastic experience. the collection of aircraft is impressive and well presented — from iconic wwii planes to modern jets. the exhibitions are informative, interactive, and suitable for all ages. the museum does a great job of combining history with personal stories, making it engaging rather than just technical. it’s free to enter (donations welcome), and the staff are very friendly and knowledgeable. the layout is spacious, with plenty of room to explore at your own pace. there are also cafés and a gift shop on-site. highly recommend this museum for anyone interested in aviation, history, or just looking for a great day out in london.

i visited this hotel on a solo vacation, i have been to la fortuna previously, so was looking for a quiet, peaceful place with hot springs, not in the city center. and this hotel has met my expectations. it is stunningly located with a direct, close-up view of the volcano, with a beautiful, well-kept garden full of frogs, lizards, and birds. you can also hear howler monkeys every day. there are several hot springs, each of them well-maintained and with a slightly different temperature. the establishment is clean, non-intrusive, offers a lot of rest space with hammocks and beach chairs that provide intimacy and peace. and the staff is very accommodating. i was staying in a bungalow, which is very basic, but comfortable, has hot shower water, very comfy bed and a small terrace. same with the food, there are a few options to choose from, more than enough for a stay of 2-3 days, and all the food is fresh, tasty, and plentiful. if you're a solo traveller or a couple, and look for peace and rest, this is a great place to stay.

i visited this place first when i came to germany and it all felt so unreal. loved the vibe over here and it was an amazing experience. i visited the mall and it was good. there were few food trucks and seating for having some relax time while just enjoying the view and surrounding. i visited on a weekend in summer and there were many people around having fun. overall a happy place.

i visited this place in october 2023. it’s located near phra ram 9 station, surrounded by tall buildings. the area is quite spacious and very clean. there are lots of food and drink vendors here, offering everything from traditional thai food, seafood, indonesian food, and even halal options! everything i tried tasted really good, especially the mango juice—it was super refreshing. payment you can pay with cash or qris (but make sure to check first, not all qris options work—only banks partnered with indonesian banks seem to be accepted). i paid with qris twice without issues, but sometimes it didn’t work. prices the prices are relatively affordable, especially the seafood, which is much cheaper than in indonesia where it’s usually pretty pricey. personally, i’d recommend this place over chatuchak market.

i visited this place in the morning and low tide, better for exploring the shore. get under the rocks, see the amazing marine life. i recommend aqua shoes to explore. also have in mind that is not the best time for swimming. if you prefer that visit the place at high tide.

i visited this shopping mall eight years ago, and honestly, it has declined quite a bit in terms of brand variety and available discounts. still, with a little patience and wandering around, you can find some good deals. on the ground floor, right by the main entrance, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants that make the shopping experience more enjoyable. the lulu store is also on the ground floor, where you can pick up your daily essentials.

i visited this unique looking pagoda at the same time as its more illustrious neighbor, thatbyinnyu. at the time, i was pretty much the only person there, probably because the place is fenced off. visitors can no longer climb the steps to the top, which must have been the main attraction of the place a few years ago. i can understand why this thirteenth century pagoda was fenced off. the wonderful brickwork is delicate and would easily be destroyed by climbers. the unique architecture with gradually receding terraces and the setting make it an essential place to visit.

i visited this view point by car as my one day grand canyon trip in beginning of november. wow this is one of the most beautiful views of grand canyon. i could spend hours just sitting and watching but cold weather in november is limiting it. decent amount of parking spots but no bathrooms available at this viewpoint.

i visited through the indigenous walking tour, and if you’re planning a trip to the bata shoe museum, i highly recommend choosing this option. it was truly the highlight of my weekend. the tour offered a beautiful cultural exchange and was incredibly engaging. it deepened my appreciation for mother earth and the indigenous communities who are working tirelessly to preserve their traditions while generously sharing their stories with us. i won’t spoil too much, but it was deeply informative and meaningful. as for the museum itself, the exhibits were thoughtfully curated and offered fresh perspectives. while the space may be on the smaller side, it’s filled with fascinating and beautifully presented pieces. the staff were also fantastic, knowledgeable, friendly, and eager to help. kudos to the whole team! i wholeheartedly recommend visiting.

i visited tokyo night & light at the tokyo metropolitan government building in shinjuku during a recent trip to tokyo, and it was a highlight of my stay! this free observation deck on the 45th floor (202 meters up) offers stunning 360-degree views of tokyo’s skyline, especially magical at night when the city lights up. i found tokyo night & light to be a must-visit for anyone wanting a budget-friendly way to experience tokyo’s iconic skyline. it’s perfect for families, couples, or solo travelers. i’d definitely return on my next trip to catch another sunset over the city!

i visited train night market srinagarindra last weekend and really enjoyed the unique atmosphere. the market has a few muslim-friendly food stalls and even a prayer room, which makes it convenient for muslim visitors. the overall vibe is vintage, with retro décor, old-school shops, and a lively crowd. one of the highlights is the large airplane placed in the market, it’s become an iconic spot for taking photos. a great place to shop, eat, and soak in a nostalgic yet vibrant night market experience.

i walked from manly city to the north shore of the sydney harbour nationalpark and had such a wonderful time! the walk is truly beautiful. stunning nature, great lookouts and what a beautiful view over the ocean. you can even see the skyline of sydney if you walk to the city lookout. i also walked the fairfax loop which i would definitely recommend doing! there is so much to enjoy: nature, cliffs, the skyline of sydney and birds. the return walk to manly took me a little more than two hours. if you stop more often and walk a slower pace it‘s probably around 2,5 to 3 hours. there also is a cafe on the north shore which looked really nice!

i walked from rua josé linhares to this spot. the road was blocked off just for runners and bikers. it was sweet. if there is good weather people are out and about. lots of vendors and plenty of spots nearby to eat. i was able to negotiate a good price for surf board rentals as well right next to pedra. would highly recommend visiting if you want to tan, take pictures, surf, eat, play volleyball. they have it all. somewhat crowded but everyone was respectful.

i walked the 13th course station olle trail and it was a little difficult because there were stairs going up, but after the stairs, the flat trail was cute and nice. it may be a bit boring and uninteresting, but it's fun to chat and enjoy small things to see, and to look at pretty flowers that have forgotten the season in the spring-like weather even though it's winter. lunch at the korean buffet restaurant in nakcheon village is also great! if you have time, stop by july & august and try a corn latte~~ it’s a cute photo spot.

i walked the easiest trail (eoseungsaengak) with a tour group. -> tour: jeju island southern unesco mt.halla one day bus tour -> booked via booking.com thoughts about the trail: it takes 30-40 minutes to reach the mini peak, and easy to walk as the path is mainly made up of dirt paths and boardwalks. one does not need to be very fit to do this route. if you do some simple walking cardio in your daily life, this route is easy. the mini peak is very windy, enjoy the view and make sure there are no loose belongings. :) thoughts about the tour: i recommend going with a tour, as it could bring tourists to different locations without worrying about transport. my tour consisted of 5 different locations including hallasan, and we had a decent to good amount of time for each location. the tour recommended the easiest trail as most people would be able to complete it. if u would like to walk the more difficult trails (>3h per direction), an alternative arrangement would have to be made. a shoutout to peter who was my tour guide. [guy in the middle of the group photo is peter] he was very humorous, and shared a lot of interesting information about jeju island. if u need any assistance (e.g. photo taking, lunch ordering), he will not hesitate to help. thanks to him, i enjoyed the tour a lot. :d

i want this review to be extraordinary just like grand canyon whitewater company. after reserving a spot i received an email from grand canyon whitewater whereby i was given a link to their website with all the information i would be needing to know. there were videos on youtube about how to pack, what to pack and what to expect. fellow rafters were invited to leave a bio explaining a little bit about themselves. i was going on this adventure with 25 people that i didn't know for a total of 10 days. once we were off the bus and loaded onto the rafts, we were at the mercy of our guides. no turning back, no cellphone service and best of all no contact with anybody other than my new river family. our crew was incredible. every meal was perfection. with precision they quickly could set up the kitchen cook the meals and serve it up to us hungry rafters. every day on the river brought a new adventure. matt was very informative about the geology and all the stories from past explorers. office guy dean who came along on this trip surprised everyone when he brought out his guitar on the seventh day and serenaded us. he was good. blake and anna were the boatsmen on the other raft. they always had smiles on their faces and were willing to help out with anything. our crew definitely made our trip outstanding. taking a trip like this is life changing. i'm so thankful to everyone that helped me enjoy an experience i wouldn't have been able to do without you all. crystal

i want to give an honest, realistic review of spa eastman. my impressions line up much more with the 3ish-star reviews than the glowing 5-star ones that contain so many superlatives (many of which frankly feel written by non humans). this review is from a real local visitor who spent a day there. pros beautiful day when i visited, and the outdoor hot tubs are lovely. some of the original décor, even as it ages, still has a creative and beautiful charm. some genuinely down-to-earth, hardworking, and friendly staff. treatments were punctual, done with kindness and professionalism (though i’d rate them average overall). restaurant service was attentive and the food is good if you enjoy creative, health-focused cuisine. cons many areas are in visible disrepair (see photos). for a local day trip it was fine, but if i had traveled far or given this as a gift, i would have been very disappointed. locker room is in the worst shape: peeling paint, rust on mirrors, badly damaged lockers, old blow dryers, and no comfortable seating to finish getting ready after a shower. i am unclear why they would not replace 4 hair-dryers that are in such bad aesthetic condition. odd clutter and storage items are left in guest areas, like the front vestibule and around the pools — not what you want to stare at while relaxing. disorganized atmosphere: scattered pool chairs, non-cohesive design styles. inconsistent, untimely, and even some rude communication from the “hospitality” staff. towels! (and other small details): despite having a full day of treatments and lunch paid for, i was told conflicting things about whether i was even entitled to a towel! it took me quite some time to obtain a towel and a robe. guests should never be made to feel awkward over something so basic. unfortunately, the way i was then later handled at check-out (due to their confusion, not mine) left a bad taste and ended the day on a sour note. bottom line my day was “okay,” thanks to the hardworking treatment staff and servers. but overall, spa eastman feels a bit tired, moderately disorganized, and not gift-worthy in its current state. i would not bring someone here expecting a polished, 5-star experience, nor would i give it as a gift i’d feel proud of. with some investment in upkeep, organization, and true hospitality training, it could live up to its reputation again. until then, expect more of a 3-star reality than a 5-star escape.

i want to sing the praises for our guides, emily and bert, on the may 15-22 raft b expedition. emily’s awareness of every bend and rock in the river and bert’s knowledge of the canyon’s geology and fantastic cooking skills made this an unforgettable experience. in addition, they both offered words of encouragement and a helping hand on some of the trickier parts of the trails we hiked. i wanted to share some feedback regarding the 11-day diving package we received as compensation for the canceled trip due to the unfortunate boat accident. overall, it appeared that both the rooms and various facilities had seen better days, with maintenance seemingly lacking, particularly in the wet areas. cleanliness was also not up to standard. the kitchen could benefit from some improvements, as the meals were monotonous, often overcooked, and lacked variety in flavor. unfortunately, i also experienced a significant gastrointestinal infection during the trip. additionally, the beer was priced at $10 per 0.32 liters. on a positive note, the dive guides were helpful and professionally competent. however, the dive sites we visited presented a mixed picture; many corals were dead, and water clarity varied. photographers should be prepared for frequent currents, which can make photography challenging. nonetheless, there were positives, such as the presence of numerous large and diverse fish species. all things considered, i would not choose to return to this location.

i was actually a bit disappointed. whilst i was lucky enough to enjoy this experience with a very dark moon, you are only actually on the water for about 45 minutes. out of this, you paddle away from the boat ramp (not much glowing), through the brightly glowing bit for about 5-10 minutes and out the other side, into another not very luminescent area. then the guide (we had david, who was excellent as a tour guide) spends about 15 minutes talking about the glowing creatures, which was quite interesting, and about 15 minutes about star constellations. this all happens whilst you're drifting back to where you started. so, i felt like i only actually experienced the brightly glowing area for about 10 minutes (most of which you're paddling or looking at the sky) which was quite disappointing. although star constellation talks are interesting, it's not what i had paid to see. if the talks could happen whilst you are floating in the highly glowing area, i think that would be much better, as you would have more time to actually see the luminescence.

i was extremely disappointed with the lala area for the kygo concert on march 1st. first, the ticket process was a complete letdown. we purchased gold (floor) tickets under the impression that it would be general admission for a dj concert. instead, it was seated, and assigned at random—i assume based on purchase time—which resulted in our friend group being separated. (note: it was impossible to even find a floor seating chart online, so i am posting a copy here for future reference). in fact, many in the gold section ended up with worse seats than those in the stands due to the layout. moreover, the floor seats were so tightly packed that there was barely any room to move, jump, or dance, which completely ruined the experience. to make matters worse, the venue was severely under-equipped with food and beverage options. with only four stands serving food, there were lines of 500 to 1,000 people during the 30-minute break between the opener and kygo. even after the show began, a queue of around 50 people could cause you to miss 30 to 45 minutes of the performance. and even if you waited in that line, there were technical issues with the beer and chuhai machines causing service delays. on top of that, all of the vending machines had run out of water, so you couldn't even get quick hydration if you wanted. net-net: drink before you come and/or sneak in beverages because if you rely on lala area to serve, you will be disappointed. lastly, the exit process was chaotic. around 10,000 people were funneled through a single narrow exit point, creating a frustrating bottleneck. while the courteous behavior of the japanese crowd helped ease tensions, it was still disappointing that the venue lacked multiple, efficient egress points. in short, i would never consider attending another concert at this venue.

i was looking for a one-of-a-kind experience, and jet skiing next to a volcano was exactly what i was hoping for. the instructors were incredibly kind, knowledgeable, and went out of their way to make sure we felt comfortable and prepared. the views? absolutely breathtaking. we had the entire lake to ourselves, which made the experience feel even more special and unforgettable. one of the things i loved most was the freedom—they don’t ride alongside you. instead, they give you a walkie-talkie for safety, which allows you to fully enjoy the adventure at your own pace. to top it all off, at the end of our jet ski tour, i asked if there was anything else to do in the area. they immediately recommended an atv tour, reached out to the company for us via text, and made sure we were booked for the last ride of the day at 2:30 pm. the whole experience—from start to finish—was seamless, exciting, and truly unforgettable. highly recommend!

i was lucky enough to join an aussie drifterz tubing tour in november 2024 as part of my university trip to cairns. while i didn’t go through the full booking and payment process myself, i did get to enjoy the tubing experience from start to finish, and it was a fantastic time. we were booked on the morning session at the little mulgrave river, which meant meeting the team outside our hotel around 8 am for a half day adventure. our guide ben met us on the bus and was great at getting us prepped for the day. he explained our itinerary, including a stop at a petrol station for last minute supplies and a toilet break, and made sure we were all ready to go. super helpful and made everything run smoothly! once we arrived at the river, it was easy to grab a tube from the trailer, which had been delivered by kai. we also geared up with life vests and helmets, both essential for safety regardless of swimming ability. before hitting the water, we had a quick safety briefing covering river conditions, signals, and what to do if anything went wrong. getting on the river with a full busload of people was a bit of a process, but once we were in the water, it was easy to spread out. you could float peacefully on your own or link up with mates for a group ride. kai and ben followed along in kayaks, guiding us through the rapids and taking awesome action shots along the way. the rapids were small but fun just enough to keep things interesting. although we got stuck a couple of times, the river was high enough to carry us along without too much trouble. near the end of the journey, we reached a deeper section where we could hop out for a swim. we also had a go at standing on our tubes, which quickly turned into diving into the water when we lost balance! it was a fun way to wrap up, with lots of laughter and good vibes as people slowly made their way out of the river. there weren’t any toilet facilities at the river itself, so we dried off and changed what we needed to for the trip home. they even looked after us at the end with juice boxes and muesli bars before we boarded the bus. by 1 pm, we were back at the hotel after a smooth drop off. i absolutely loved this experience. floating under the trees, watching the leaves drift past, and soaking up the calm of the river was such a peaceful and refreshing way to spend a morning. the river was alive with sights and sounds, and the whole experience was made even better by kai and ben, who were incredibly friendly, supportive, and attentive, especially to some of our group who were feeling a bit nervous. i’d definitely recommend giving river tubing a go if you’re up north, and aussie drifterz are the team to do it with. they did a wonderful job supporting our group, and i truly enjoyed every moment!

i was lucky enough to join mario and the surfski warehouse/ learn to paddle crew from the very beginning, jan 2021. my 14yo son and i paddled right through winter and are still going strong paddling 5 days a week with the team. we thoroughly enjoy the community, coaching, location, variety and results. we are achieving things on the water that we could never imagine, from 24km spit to bondi round trips, downwinders from long reef to spit, pb 12km timetrials on narrabeen, double and single races on a friday. ever time on the water we are pushed and getting fitter and better. thank-you mario and the ltp crew!

i was shocked by what i experienced on a whale watching tour in mauritius. initially, i had considered booking with vitaminsea, but luckily, i changed my mind. their website promotes respect for the animals and nature — but out at sea, there was no sign of that. numerous boats cut across the whales’ path, driving so close they could almost touch them. it felt more like a hunt than an observation. we encountered a mother and her calf — and the reality is, a calf needs to surface for air more often than its mother, leaving them both vulnerable to such relentless pursuit. to me, this was the opposite of showing respect for wildlife and nature. companies should live up to the promises in their advertising. i hope there will be more regulations and enforcement in the future to give the animals more space.

i will admit i know nothing of abe no seimei except for the most basic info available on the shrine's website and wikipedia. i can, however, offer my impressions and observations of the shrine when i visited it recently. i am usually one who avoids and pretty much loathes commercialism but i'll make a small exception for this place mainly because i found it quite fun. when i decided to drop by one late sunday morning, i was surprised to find quite a few japanese visitors and tourists. i took the city bus and it dropped me off almost at the doorstep of the shrine. the outer torii gate has a traditional signboard that bears the shrine's emblem or kamon of a 5 pointed star. this is quite rare because most signboards typically bear the name of the place. if i had to hazard a guess i think the star acts as a talisman against evil and helps to reinforce and magnify the protective powers of the gate. the outermost gate actually sits right on the kerb side of the main road so you will find the shrine hard to miss. please do bow before you enter and keep to the side when walking in. this is basic shrine etiquette that applies to all shrines. upon entering the outer gate, you'll see a stone effigy of the yokai that does seimei's bidding, guarding a little bridge on the left. you may want to read up on the significance of crossing the bridge before you do it, or you can simply throw caution to the wind for that instagram shot. just behind the bridge is a tiny hut run by a lovely little silver haired granny. tons of souvenirs to fill your pockets here but bear in mind that while all the gifts are approved for sale by the clergy, they have not been blessed by the priests and so are not considered amulets. tip: the amulet counter closer to the heart of the shrine has a range of amulets and keepsakes that have already been blessed if that's what you want. you can, of course, buy stuff from the little old lady and try your luck looking for a priest to bless your purchases but i wouldn't count on it if i were you, and i wouldn't hold my breath. they aren't always around when you want them and note that fees may apply. check the official website if you are thinking of visiting. it should prove both interesting and useful. once you're done with the outer perimeter, walk straight to the second torii gate and yes, a little bow and keeping to the side will be nice. on the right, is a small fountain resembling a traditional grain mortar with spring water flowing from small spouts. this was obviously a clever replacement for the traditional scoop and trough found in most temples and shrines. thanks to the very creative and progressive clergy and personnel of the shrine, this is obviously their solution for the extra care and hygiene required by covid. thanks to their idea, you can safely purify your hands and mouth at this shrine before going any further to pray and converse with the deities. i quite like the shrine because it has a fun and spritely vibe to it despite the straightforward commercialism spelt out on the website. in case you're wondering, you won't need much time for a visit. half an hour should do the trick unless you're really into japanese culture and spirituality. bring 5 yen coins to toss into alms boxes - they are considered lucky and perfect for this purpose at all temples and shrines in japan. for those like me, who went looking for sen no rikyu's old abode, all you'll find is the stone post planted just outside of the inner gate on the left.

i would definitely recommend taking the sky tram (despite the cons). it made climbing a mountain doable for a family with kids. the views were incredible (even from the tram boardwalk) and it was so cool to be at the summit. we also ate at the restaurant, which was good and overpriced as everything is. i appreciated the tram guide’s information -such as, it can take 50 years for a plant to bloom in this climate with less oxygen and a 60-day-a-year growing season. if you have kids, book the deal for a morning tram ride that gives you a kid free with each adult purchase! that said, we were definitely disappointed to have paid so much for the ride to then be packed in so tightly on the ride up that we couldn’t even turn to see things. you literally couldn’t move. the tram was running behind because of wind (understandable) but some people who had a later ticket time were allowed on our already crowded tram. you definitely can’t relax and enjoy the ride as they advertise. the ride down had less people and so we were actually able to see things.

i would give 4 stars if less entry fees. the temple is nice, but except for the holy spring, average to other big temples. it was not too crowded when we visited on a thursday late morning. normally lots of esoteric/ spiritual western people there to take a bath in the holy water. for them it may be a 5 star location. currently several constructions ongoing. up the hill is some location, from where you can get a nice view on the temple.

i would give 6 stars. the crab w creamy omelette on rice was so delicious and the spicy salmon salad had thick cut pieces of fresh fish which was so satisfying. even the crispy flatbread and salsa was so good, i ate it all even though i was full. love the vintage vibes, the decor is also beautiful

i would give them 6 stars if i could. my wife, alexandra, and i are celebrating our honeymoon. &beyond grumeti was the first leg of our trip. the entire staff is so friendly and genuine that even though we were only there for 3 nights, we truly feel like we'll miss them. from roja, joseph, and sophie, to mike, ally, jackson, and our amazing guide willie, the only thing we experienced the entire time we were there was world-class hospitality. the rides with willie, watching all kinds of wildlife, and the encyclopedic knowledge he has about everything related to nature, were the highlights of each day. the food was great, the rooms and common areas were beautiful. if you can book a stay with them (they're frequently fully booked, for good reason) do it right away.

i would give this company 10 stars if i could! they were excellent at communicating and helping with the zillion questions our group had. they helped get our bags delivered to the house in niseko and dropped off our lift tickets so we were ready to go the morning after we arrived. the accommodation options were top notch and we loved the house we stayed in. planning a trip to japan is overwhelming but these guys truly made it so easy and seamless. we will 100% use them again when we return!

i would have rated the rooms five stars if they were fully air conditioned. just the bed is air conditioned under the gauze mosquito netting at night. the website or travel agent doesn't reveal this detail. the bathroom is completely open to the outside, so you sweat as soon as you get out of the shower. and it is very hot there in late november. the reef is spectacular, so if you don't mind being hot and sweaty most of the time, go for it. be prepared for the 16 hours of travel to get there from jakarta.

i would highly recommend this day trip to michaelmas cay. the coral was spectacular and there were so many fish and turtles. kid friendly, my 7 year old had a great time. massive thanks to the guy in the little boat that found a turtle for us while we were snorkelling which we were able to swim over to. big bonus was the amount of people, with number restrictions it meant you weren’t on a boat with 200 people. also being able to relax on the cay and see thousands of migrating birds was pretty cool too. staff were so friendly and helpful. food was delicious and there was heaps of it. if you can afford the extra $100, hire the gopro so you can capture all the moments in the water

i would highly recommend this place to anyone who loves the ocean and its creatures. port khasab musandam offers a unique opportunity to explore the arabian gulf's diverse marine life. with crystal-clear waters, we observed an array of marine creatures, including fish, jellyfish, and dolphins. if you're interested in snorkeling or scuba diving, there are plenty of opportunities to do so in port khasab musandam. you can explore the colorful coral reefs and see firsthand the vibrant underwater ecosystem. for those who prefer to stay above the water, boat tours are available, offering a chance to spot dolphins and other marine mammals. i highly recommend this place to anyone in and around the middle east or if you are visiting from anywhere and you happen to be in the uae, visit port khasab musandam. visas are easy to obtain at the border post for most countries.

i would highly recommend you go zip-lining with panorama zip-line while you visit dubrovnik. it doesn’t take up all of your day, so if you are only there for a day or two, you still have time to go elsewhere. our guides were philip and “big g”. they both spoke really great english, and for big g, you can hardly even tell that he’s croatian. he studied abroad in america for his college. they were both really chatty, telling us about history and answering any and all questions we had about the area. in particular, philip gave us some food recommendations and gave us some history that i didn’t know. and i gotta say the recommendations he gave were amazing. he recommended sebastian, which is family owned and operated. it was the best fish (mussels and tuna steak) i’ve ever had. you get a total of 4 zip lines, divided up between 2 zip lines. you stop in the middle of one of them and can get a very nice view of the city. they also take photos of you and your family overlooking the city. the drivers, coming from an american driver, are very skilled, as the road to get up there is very narrow. we had mario and nikola. i would definitely recommend when visiting dubrovnik.

i'm giving this 5 stars because it is a beautiful place with an unmatched collection of ceramic pharmacy vessels...and surprisingly, it is an active pharmacy as they had a little box that they were selling basics like ibuprofen out of (love the quirkiness of cuba!). however, if you are expecting a real museum with lots of information, this is not it...it could be, but sadly it is just a well-preserved store. perhaps one day when more investment floods into cuba, they will do more with this place, but then, that would not be the real cuba, would it? do stop, but don't expect to be informed or entertained (if ever in new orleans, definitely go to their pharmacy museum as it is amazing).

i'm happy to give this place a 5 star now as long as they didnt change their entrance fee rule again. i paid 100k per person and with thet i get a voucher with the same amount to spend in restaurants and shops. if you come here just to have coffee then you'll lose money but if you come here to a full meal and sightseeing then it's so worth it! the place itself is very peaceful. i love eating while looking at the rice field and mountains.
