i'm maori born and raised on the east coast. my wife and our two girls are canadian born and raised. we flew home from canada to visit whanau over the christmas/new year period. wife and kids wanted to experience rotorua's cultural and scenic wonderland. wife booked te pō (hāngī dinner buffet + haka) package online. you get to see, hear and taste māori culture with a hāngī buffet dinner and cultural performance. a delicious hāngī buffet at the pātaka kai restaurant & bar, which overlooks a geothermal wonderland. we enjoyed freshly sourced produce, traditionally cooked meats and vegetables, kai moana (seafood), and a selection of sweet desserts. my wife and girls were captivated by the cultural performance in the beautifully carved meeting house, te aronui a rua. the performance includes a pōhiri (traditional māori welcome), waiata (song), mōteatea (chant), poi, and haka. we didn't attend the evening stroll down to pōhutu geyser and sip on hot chocolate as my oldest girl felt tired. the staff said we could come back the next night free of charge to visit the geyser and sip on hot chocolate. empowering night and cultural experience for the family. mauri ora ❤️🤍🖤🌿

i'm not a church fanatic, but you have to see this one. the stained glass windows in the upper floor are world-class! it's really unbelievably beautiful when the sun reflects in the glass. there are smaller shops downstairs, and a very nice tour up the small stairs upstairs, which is very cool. i recommend a visit, also visit in the afternoon, because you have to wait outside to enter, in the afternoon you will wait in the shade, also buy tickets in advance.

i'm not the biggest fan of artworks, however i was fascinated but the additional 'deep dive' cards dotted about, explaining more detail about an artists style or methods. it made the experience much more enjoyable and i maybe even have a better appreciation of the artists... the cafe is worth a visit too. the timeslot you booked send to be fairly flexible - we arrived an hour early and it was not a problem to enter.

i'm not usually one to write reviews but this experience was truly amazing and review worthy.(we did the el yunque rainforest hike) our tour guide julian was very informative and made the experience fun while also making sure i felt safe! it's not the easiest trail but both of our guides were so helpful and the best part is they were taking awesome pics of my son and i the whole time which are memories i will cherish forever! i cannot recommend booking with this company enough, i would not go anywhere else when i come back to puerto rico! truly thankful for this amazing time - waterfall slide, rock climbing, jumps, beautiful scenery and good vibes!
i'm pretty sure the place already had stopped operating a long time ago, didn't know about the reviews and they seem to be not updated.
i'm pretty sure there is a vortex around here. my drone got pulled towards the rocks and lost camera footage. luckily i pulled it off by return to home button. nice and mysterious place thou.

i'm so glad i found this peaceful spot. it's truly amazing how much calmer i feel surrounded by nature 🌳. this is the perfect place to just breathe and let go of all the stress. i really needed this mental break to clear my head and focus on what's important. sometimes, all you need is a quiet moment like this 🧘‍♂️. #peace #calm #nature

i'm so in love with the variety of produce they offer. i'm forever a customer. with every purchase there's always something to learn from the owners they are full of knowledge and always friendly. i would recommend this farmers market to all!

i'm so pained to write this but it must be known what an awful tour we had with this agency for a very high price. we were promised a more private and intimate tour of the cenotes based on the promises on their website when they just took us to the buuts' ha' cenote club which was painfully overcrowded. cesar the man responsible for this experience claimed it was high season and all the cenotes would be busy. we found this to be deeply untrue when we went to cenotes on our own just by using google maps and online guides. those cenotes were so much more private and intimate. please do not book tours with them. save yourself the money. that being said our tour guide nelson and surrial our driver was very nice there was just a lot of dispute over the itinerary for the private tour that i wanted with my partner. i was hoping for a more romantic experience but honestly it was one of the worst parts about my trip to tulum.

i'm still giving this 5 stars, but this hike was fairly challenging due to the rain and snow at the top. recommend leaving extremely early if you want a good view of the towers, because the day we went, it was extremely cloudy and snowy. it was freezing at the top and we were already soaked from the rain, and the last mile or so is particularly tumultuous. still would recommend as the hike is beautiful, but i wish we would have gotten a better view of the torres.
i'm surprised, the park is really really nice. bright green grass, clean, very cared for. the only thing is that there isn't much shade, but i guess we just have to wait for the small trees to grow

i'm using paris museum pass, just join the line via entrance c. this is one of the coolest art museums in paris, it’s a must-visit if you’re van gogh's fan or simply into art. what makes it really special is that the building itself used to be a huge train station, it was the gare d’orsay, built around the early 1900s. instead of tearing it down, they turned it into a museum, which means you get this amazing mix of old industrial architecture and art all in one place. inside, the museum is packed with incredible artworks, mostly from the late 19th and early 20th centuries. you’ll find tons of famous impressionist and post-impressionist paintings here, artists like monet, degas, renoir, van gogh, and cézanne. if you love those bright, colorful paintings or want to get a feel for the art that changed the world, this is the spot. besides paintings, the museum also has sculptures, decorative arts, and photography. it’s pretty manageable in size, so you don’t get overwhelmed like in some bigger museums. the museum sits right on the left bank of the seine, close to the louvre and the charming saint-germain area. so, it’s easy to fit it into a day of exploring paris. it's recommended to visit here. :)
i've always liked mom's grilled cheese but i don't find myself near their food trucks often enough. came across them at the shipyards xmas market in december and had their christmas hammy with bacon.

i've always wanted to go to north safari sapporo. it was a little after the obon holidays, but it was still summer vacation, so there were quite a few people there. there were more animals and rare animals than i expected, and it was the first time i'd been so close to the animals!! some kids just saw the sign at the entrance to the dangerous forest and went back, saying, "no, i'm scared, i don't want to go in!", so even if you go inside, as long as you don't enter the danger zone, there are lots of cute owls (it was the first time i'd seen so many owls!) there are also foxes, raccoons, and bears, so i think kids will enjoy it too (*^^*) there were some creatures in the danger zone that made me scream! lol i didn't think there was a more exciting facility than this♪ it's a place that both adults and children can enjoy. this time, i took a bus from makomanai station to jozankei onsen. (the same destination can be reached from sapporo station.) if you get off at toyotaki kaikan, a shuttle bus will come to pick you up at the location, so it's very convenient to get there! it was also great that you could buy tickets online for 100 yen off. i'd like to go again in the winter season♪

i've always wanted to visit here, and finally we went this last weekend. spaced out over three floors there was so much to see. the museum was busy but it didn't feel packed and there was plenty of space to walk around and take in all the beautiful displays. unfortunately it was unbearably hot (due to the heatwave) and we didn't have much time. therefore we didn't get to see everything, but what we did see was great. this place is full of history and interesting items and you could spend all day here. the garden was lovely but shade was limited, and it was lovely to be allowed to cool my feet off in the water. we also brought some gorgeous one off earrings in the gift shop. the staff were all super helpful and friendly and the museum was spotlessly clean. i would definitely recommend, but make sure you have a whole day.

i've been around a long time and bought plenty of gear from different places, but 4wd supacentre has really impressed me. prices are fair, the range is huge, and the gear holds up well in the real world. the staff were friendly and didn’t rush me — even took the time to explain a few things i wasn’t sure about. reminds me of how customer service used to be. i’ll be back for more.

i've been coming here for twenty years. it's really cool to see all the different stuff they have. it's always changing they're always adapting. and if you're into crafts, they have a lot of unique things

i've been diving for over 20 years and can honestly say i just had the best week of diving in my life. raja ampat is an incredible place to dive and olin made sure we had the best possible experience. the dive masters are fantastic, my partner did her advanced course and her instructor afri was also really great. all the dive and boat crew we met were friendly, fun, professional and great at their jobs. the boats were good, the big boat for longer trips and the small boat for the closer sites. they always have fresh water, fruits, coffee and teas between dives. we travelled light and rented equipment from the shop, all of which was perfect. we started at the shop, checked and fitted all of the equipment and agreed where we wanted to dive - manta ridge and blue magic were a must. day to day organisation is by whatsapp and you need to be a little flexible because the schedule can change depending on conditions and other divers, but over 5 days they made sure we got to all the locations we wanted to see. we stayed at the dive shops own accommodation which was a great deal, very convenient and comfortable. breakfast was brought to us every morning, we ate packed lunch on different islands between dives every day and you can get easily into waisai town for a meal in the evening. people say that raja ampat is the best place in the world to dive, so we had high expectations, but it's even better than we imagined. we saw lots of mantas, including oceanics, 4 different types of sharks, turtles, peacock mantis, bumpheads, napoleons, and so much more. the guides made sure we also saw the small stuff that you might easily miss like glass shrimps and pygmy seahorses. from the boat we saw omura's whales, pilot whales and dolphin. we leave tomorrow and are already talking about coming back next year or the year after, we would definitely choose olin again.

i've been going to rio for over 15 years now and have always had the desire to jump off the ramp at pedra da gavea. in fact my inlaws drove me up there 2x and i would watch as both paragliders and hang gliders would jump off the ramp, high above the thick forest of são conrado. so i finally bit the bullet and ordered my wide through rio natural. the reservation process was quick and easy and daniel was available on whatsapp to answer my questions (great customer service points there) i was dropped off at the bustling landing spot at the end of são conrado, where i met with my "instructor" guto...very friendly yet professional and made me feel 100% at ease with the experience. i took an suv up to the launch pad, up the winding steep road that snakes up to the top of the mountain. once at the ramp, our glider was ready to go and so was guto, there was very little wait time. he calmly briefed me prior to takeoff, as well as the landing and we did a couple of simulated runs until he was confident i was ready. the flight itself - there's just no describing it. there's hundreds of videos capturing the experience on youtube but until you hop off that ramp and feel the brief free-fall as the wind catches your wings, you simply haven't lived. guto steered our glider to a small hill to the left to get some updraft. the view as you cross over the hill and see rocinha on the other side is simply divine. guto also allowed me to fly the ship and make some turns, just to get a better taste of the experience. all in all our flight lasted about 12m (not much in updrafts that day i guess) once on ground we sat at a cluster of monitors where i could review pics and videos of my flight - there are 2 gopros setup and you can choose which one you want to download (i ordered both angles!) while sitting at the "multimedia" station, i had a chance to meet the legendary "mosquito", a long-time hang glider veteran from way back. i hope to do this again - the day was perfect for flying, and rio natural made the experience even more unforgettable!

i've been here many times and have enjoyed it, until today. paid the entry fee, changed in the changing room, and headed to the pools only to find that the water was tepid, cool, not hot. every pool was not warm, and the water was not flowing through the pools like it normally is. was in the park for 15 minutes. i asked for a refund and was told i had used the park for 15 minutes and they would not refund my money for me and my 3 family members.

i've been in wadi rum for the first time in may 2022 and it’s one of the best memory i have from a trip. the place is first breathtaking, and i had the chance to be on tour with rachid and his family. i've stayed for 3 days and 3 nights, the experience was really immersive ; i didn't feel like a customers because we were a small group with the guide and they really included us and share about the place and the history. during the days the guide took us in the desert to hike in incredible places and we get to see the sunset at good spots everyday. after, at night, we got some food with them in front of a fireplace and slept in the caves, we could see the stars at night it was magical. i’ve asked to stay one more night because i wanted to experience it some more time !

i've been learning to kite surf for about 2,5 years, i've been unlucky with the wind quite some many times and almost gave up hope. i'm so happy that i can finally kite well now with just 2 days on the water with an instructor! the best thing is that there is a walkie-talkie taped to your helmet, so you are in constant contact with your instructor, which means you get tips and tricks while riding. this speeded up my development massively! on my first day of practicing i was able to ride and on my second day i was able to go upwind. dennis was a great and patient instructor and i never felt too much or as if i wasn't picking things up fast enough. before i came to the philippines i was in contact with jen for 2 weeks to keep tabs on the wind. the contact was great throughout this period and jen turns out to be even lovelier in person. everyone in the kite school is very friendly and happy to help and go the extra mile. also great thanks to steph for helping me out with the little things like putting spf on and keeping my valuables safe. i've taken lessons with more than 4 kite schools in the last 2,5 years and isla kitesurfing is the best by far. if you are going to the philippines and want to learn to kitesurf, i highly recommend isla kitesurfing!

i've been looking forward to seeing it more than any other place but it was so crowded that i couldn't go up. i visited during the weekend and a day before the national day so many photo spots around the tower were closed. i took pictures outside instead. the best thing about it, is how it's visible from any street in the surrounding area. i'll go again next time to go up and see the view.

i've been lucky enough to attend a few shows in london theatre but in my humble opinion this particular theatre was really lovely. may not look like much from the outside but inside very stylish and really pleasant. seating was nice too. highly recommended venue. we watch the mj musical which was excellent!

i've been on maverick twice, and my dad has taken it ten times. this is our favorite thing to do when we take a trip to vegas, and it never fails to disappoint. the first time i came, buck was our pilot. he was super funny and narrated the entire ride. he obviously has a passion for flying and the wildlife and ecosystems of the las vegas area. he discussed the declining water levels of lake mead and how the government created the lake and designated areas for local tribes. buck played classic rock the whole ride, which was fantastic. the ride was easy, and we never felt unsafe. this trip, i want to say andrew was our pilot (we were group three for the 5:30 pm fourth of july sunset canyon flight), and we had a great ride out into the canyon. the air was rough, but he handled it like a champ. andrew told us he was flying until around 1 am for the fourth, but he never would have let any sleepiness or fatigue show. he talked extensively about the geology of the landscape and had a good conversation with my brother about the helicopter once he found out that my brother wanted to be a pilot. every pilot that i've had has also made a breaking bad joke while flying to the fuel station, which is another point in my book. the employees working inside are very friendly and super helpful. we have never had any cleanliness complaints or any issues with facilities whatsoever. the bus that we rode last night was a bit hot since i'm not sure that there was airconditioning, so you may want to take an uber, but it did not take away from the experience since the driver was very kind! 11/10 would recommend for anyone, even people who may be a bit wary of flying!

i've been to athens a few times. i'm my humble opinion, this is the best viewpoint in the entire city. this is where they take the postcard photos for the acropolis. the position here is just perfect. i hiked up here extremely early to catch the sunrise at the acropolis. it's really a magical place.

i've been to many ski resorts, but niseko is heaven for skiers or snowboarders. not only does it combine four major ski resorts, but each has its own variety of slopes, and you can ski from the top of the mountain to the other resorts without having to take a shuttle bus. all facilities are well maintained, the staffs here are very friendly and helpful, if you have any questions they will able to help you in different leagues. the only downside to niseko is the high prices, as it is located in the mountains away from the city, so if you want to ski in and out be prepared for accommodation and restaurants, to be more expensive than most other places in japan. but i will still give it 5 🌟

i've been to new orleans seven times and this is my first time trying the muffuletta! and i wanted it from the place that created it, central grocery and deli! the muffuletta was great! we all loved it! even my grandson and he's a picky eater. the muffuletta was huge, could easily feed four people.

i've been to paddle barn a few times since it first opened and i've always felt welcomed by both pj and leo. my first lesson was great, i was very nervous but pj made sure that i had the basics down and took his time to make me feel at ease. i was impressed that i was able to stand by the end of the lesson. i've also joined in with the paddle fit class which was also a fun experience. i didn't think i'd ever be able to do 10 squats while balancing on a paddle board but i did. during the summer i took advantage of the great membership offer and was able to take a board out whenever i felt like. i've participated in classes, gone out a few times with my 11 year old son and had friends join me and i've always had a friendly welcome and enjoyable time. its been great watching how the shop has developed and all the hard work put in by the owners. if you're looking for a good friendly place to try sup paddle barn is your place.
i've been training with manu for a while now, and i'm thrilled with the time and dedication he puts into all the events he organizes. i know all the participants are delighted! i recommend him!

i've been waiting for a little while now to post this review, in the hopes that i would properly edit the pictures i took on my tour mike. you see, mike is fantastic. not only as a photography instructor and guide, but just a genuinely cool human. what's not cool, is my lack of willingness to edit my photos. so please enjoy my unedited photos, that i took on the most fabulous venture out with mike. hire this guy, he knows his stuff.

i've been wanting to try this place for quite some time now. am i ever glad i did. from the moment we walked in, the servers were extremely friendly and helpful to recommend beat sellers. being a noodle shop, you don't get the smell of soup and noodles on your clothes, which is a good thing. we ordered the recommended curry chicken with shanghai wide noodles and the boat noodle with vermicelli. if you like noodles a bit chewy, i'd recommend the shanghai noodles. the chicken was cooked very nicely. fall off the bone. the curry was rich and flavorful. i just wished they had given a little bit more broth. the boat noodle had beef shin, meat balls , and liquid pork blood mixed into the soup. it was very tasty, but a tad on the salty side. all in all, excellent with extremely good service.

i've been whale watching in many different areas, and this was one of the best experiences. some of what's special: - the spotters working on land guarantee that if you go out on the boat, you will see whales - having a marine biologist on board providing tons of info - zodiac boats which means everyone will get to see - crew behavior, making sure not to disturb the animals - resident sperm whales! sperm whales are great for whale watching anyway, because they spend quite a while at the surface between long, deep dives. this gives you plenty of time to watch them while they breathe and recover. the resident females here often have calves with them! - lots of resident dolphins are a bonus. definitely go whale watching with naturalist if you are in azores! we definitely plan to return earlier in the year to see migratory whales as well. pics were taken with my iphone (!).

i've dived all over the world, but the trips with octopus oman are always special. their sites around the daymaniyat islands are full of life—this time i saw eagle rays and a cuttlefish! the team is knowledgeable, safety-focused, and friendly. definitely the top choice for scuba diving in oman.

i've done 11 canyons with gerard! he's become our go-to canyon guide. he's super fast and inspires a lot of confidence. he controls the canyons like the back of his hand and takes us to some lesser-known and super cool ones. we'll definitely continue canyoning with him. thanks, gerard!

i've had my trip with love boats uae recently in speed boat with my family the trip was a to make a tour around the palm to see some icons there such as both of the atlantis hotels and we went also to see burj al arab hotel and dubai eye which took 90 mins for all and it was such a great experience the toir were brilliant the atmosphere were also great the guys on the boat were friendly and they helped us also in taking photos highly recommended if you're visiting dubai soon! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

i've lived across the road from this "forest" for almost 30 years, it is utterly lacking any management. mongoose and rats scurry about, and by nightfall gunfire is heard almost daily. overgrown shrubs and tree branches partially block a road full of potholes, and there is no sidewalk. hiking is a joke. the hill is barren and vegetation is long gone. at least it is not urbanized, but this natural pocket could be so much better.

i've lived in arizona since i was 15. can't believe i finally went to the grand canyon at 46. i was completely impressed with the view, the colors of the canyon, and the wildlife. it was freezing, but i didn't care, well worth it.

i've made the discovery to enter in that timeless place. got a red bracelet, made a prey for family and walked around to contemplate and just take the time. for those lucky who live nearby wat damnak, going through it seems like to give your soul a chance to start the day on the most positive way possible.

i've now done the phi phi sunrise tour twice and loved the experience equally both times. the trip is relaxed and easy-going from pick up to drop off. the guides are warm, helpful and passionate about making your experience awesome. seeing the sun rise over the islands on the way out to phi phi was a highlight both times. maya bay is a popular tourist spot for a reason, it is absolutely stunning, and with this trip you can beat the crowds and the heat and experience it at it's most calm and quiet. as an ecologist i am also very impressed to learn about the conservation efforts in this area, and we were lucky enough to see baby sharks in the bay - no swimming is allowed here in order to conserve the shark nursery area. after maya bay there are a bunch of snorkelling, wildlife watching and swim spots, followed a relaxed hour at a beach with loungers and a bar on the way back to phuket. we so much wildlife including monkeys, sea eagles, seahorses, angel fish, parrot fish and clownfish. food is plentiful with meals or snacks and water offered between every stop, with a final delicious buffet lunch at the marina. the ride to phi phi was just over 1 hour, and the water was a little rough when i went in the low season (july), so if you are uncomfortable on a bumpy boat i recommend doing this in the high or shoulder seasons.

i've rented dozens of kayaks in dozens of countries and can honestly say the deep cove is one of the best. every staff member was safe, patient, kind, and explained everything in detail. the safety measures were top notch and helped my senior parents feel comfortable. the quality of kayaks and rentals equipment was top notch as well. definitely arrive early and book your rental ahead of time especially on busy weekends. as north vancouver locals we will keep coming back and bringing our friends and family.

i've run all of pallas-yllätunturi national park, and it is without a doubt an amazing breath taking place to go to and experience. i often dream of returning to such a unique place to visit these old and eroded fells

i've run into this food truck at various locations, but it truly shines when parked at brewers row in port moody. after indulging in a few pints, there's nothing quite like their chicken and fries to cap off the experience. the breading—mysteriously crunchy, possibly thanks to something similar to rice krispies—keeps the chicken perfectly crispy on the outside while retaining its juiciness inside. don't let the simple appearance of their bibimbap fool you, as the flavors are deep and satisfying. this truck has earned a solid spot in my go-to list for dependable and delicious street food.

i've seen this place on tiktok and have been curious since. so when my guide in fez took me here, it caught me by surprise as i didn't expect i would visit this place while in fez. i have a sensitive nose so the stench was absolutely horrid. i stuffed my nose with mint leaves which were handed to me at the entrance. i forgot the name of the staff who gave me the explanation but he was very kind, i asked him all kinds of questions and he answered all of them. i never cared about anything leather before. after visiting this place and learning how labour intensive leather making was, my appreciation grew. i'm amazed they kept the same process after thousands of years (mind you this tannery was founded in the 9th century). they have 3 floors for the leather products from bags, shoes, wallets, jackets, coats. i made my first leather jacket purchase here and i couldn't be happier. it is indeed very expensive, but i consider it worth it since all processes are natural. they can make a modification upon request and will deliver it on the same day to your hotel. the jacket i wanted was too big so they had it altered and also added 2 extra pockets on the side. beautiful.

ibn battuta mall is one of the most unique malls i’ve visited! each section is themed after a different country—like china, india, egypt, and persia—and the interiors are absolutely stunning. you feel like you’re traveling the world as you walk through. the designs, architecture, and decorations in each area are so detailed and beautiful—it’s not just a shopping trip, it’s an experience. the mall has a great mix of shops, cafes, and restaurants, plus a huge cinema and fun activities for kids. what i loved most is how easy it is to get there. it's directly connected to the ibn battuta metro station and also served by buses, so it’s very convenient if you're using public transport. whether you're shopping, sightseeing, or just looking for a cool indoor place to explore in dubai, ibn battuta mall is definitely worth a visit. it’s relaxing, exciting, and full of surprises around every corner!

ibn battuta mall stands out as one of the most amazing malls in dubai, offering an experience that goes beyond just shopping. the architectural design is stunning, with each section dedicated to a different country, creating a unique and immersive atmosphere. walking through the mall feels like taking a trip around the world, with each area perfectly capturing the essence and vibe of its respective country. our visit was made even more memorable by the great time we had at switch bowling. it’s a fantastic spot for some fun and friendly competition. the overall experience at ibn battuta mall was truly "wow," and i highly recommend it to anyone looking for a memorable day out in dubai. whether you're there for the shopping, the entertainment, or simply to soak in the incredible ambiance, ibn battuta mall is a must-visit destination.

iconic amphitheater makes for a stunning venue. if you’re in athens as a tourist book tickets to whatever is on here during your stay and go, you won’t regret it. be wary of the steep steps to get to the seats, take your time and be careful. sitting here amongst the crowd is a wonderful experience.

iconic and awe-inspiring landmark with remarkable architecture and deep historical significance. walking through its ancient walls offers a vivid glimpse into the grandeur of the roman empire. highly recommend joining a guided tour to fully appreciate its history, hidden details, and fascinating stories you might otherwise miss.

iconic beach in oahu. sit a watch surfers and sunrises. make sure to check out the duke’s statue. walk the beach. surf rolling in is a beautiful sight. there is places to swim in protected man made coves. surfboards are available for rental. plenty to see and experience.

iconic beach that is small and narrow which allows it to fill up quickly. try to arrive before 10am because by 11am the whole beach will be packed. the water is shallow and you can walk out what seems like miles without it reaching your chest. there are a few rocky areas so i would recommend aqua shoes. the waves are usually always tame and great for beginner surfers.
iconic clock tower of uyuni, located on the intersection with avenida arce, a pedestrian only mall with lots of restaurants and cafes on each side. a pleasant place for a stroll

iconic fort in havana beautiful surroundings with great view but unfortunately the place looks depleted and poorly maintained for a main tourist attraction the standard of maintenance is disappointing this city has a lot of beauty but the condition needs a lot of improvement
iconic gate at the entrance of the historical old city of fez. beyond this gate is the world's largest pedestrian city (according to locals' claims)
iconic landmark at the end of chinatown that you can see for great a distance. traffic is a bit high speed around here.
iconic monument in a huge square. popular tourist social share spot.

iconic nyc photo stop – absolutely loved it! this spot in dumbo is an absolute must-visit for anyone in new york. the view of the manhattan bridge perfectly framed between the red-brick buildings is stunning — it’s the classic instagram moment! i loved how vibrant the area felt, with cobblestone streets, street performers, and people capturing that perfect shot. it gets a bit crowded, but it’s totally worth the wait. whether you’re here for the views, the photos, or just soaking in the nyc vibe, this place delivers. don’t miss the nearby jane’s carousel and the riverfront walk for even more beauty!

iconic place in tokyo, if you come at certain times like 1pm sharp godzilla will roar and music will play. he will also blow smoke from his mouth and flashing lights will shine simultaneously. if you are in tokyo you gotta check it out, surrounded by tons of shops, restaurants and everything else!

iconic place what better place to watch the sunset? this of course, close to the city but not so close, is a place surrounded by the water of the pacific ocean and the green lung that delivers one of the best spots in sydney in my opinion. we have nearby toilets, water fountains, a wide coastal street for those who love to walk, run or just lie on the grass.

iconic, vibrant, unforgettable – sydney opera house during vivid i had the chance to visit the sydney opera house during the vivid light festival in 2017, and it was nothing short of magical. seeing this architectural icon illuminated with ever-shifting colours and stunning projections added an entirely new dimension to its already impressive presence. the atmosphere was electric, yet somehow intimate – the blend of light, music, and harbour views made for a truly unique experience. whether you're into architecture, art, or simply want to feel the pulse of the city, this is the place to be. highly recommended – especially during vivid. it’s sydney at its most inspired.

if i could give wat trai mit two hundred and fifty million stars, i absolutely would—and not just because that’s roughly how much the jaw-dropping 24-carat solid gold buddha statue is worth (yes, $250 million in pure gold!). this place isn’t just a monastery—it’s a breathtaking blend of spiritual serenity, jaw-dropping history, and golden magnificence. from the moment i stepped into the temple grounds, i felt like i’d walked into something truly sacred. the architecture is gorgeous, the atmosphere is calm and reverent, and then—bam—you see it. the golden buddha. weighing over 5 tons and glistening like it was handcrafted by the gods themselves. pictures don’t do it justice. it’s not just gold, it’s legendary. but it’s not just about the gold. the story behind it—how it was hidden under plaster for centuries to protect it from invaders, and only rediscovered by accident in the 1950s—is like something out of a movie. history lovers, art lovers, spiritual seekers—this place has something for everyone. the museum downstairs gives great context, and the monks and staff are respectful, kind, and happy to help if you have questions. you’ll leave feeling humbled, inspired, and probably googling “can i build a temple in my backyard?” if bangkok is a crown, wat trai mit is the solid gold jewel. do not miss it.

if i have to describe the berlin wall in one word it would be 'fulfilling'. having studied and heard a lot about its history, i was very keen on visiting this historical site. when i arrived there the first impression was that the berlin wall created, was an unwanted barrier between the west and east germany. west germany represented progress but the people in the east could not enjoy the fruits of economic growth and freedom. but in 1989, it all got changed and the berlin wall was broken. eventually, both east and the west germany got united. now, this berlin wall has 3 columns of the wall with sticky gums used as a stone by visitors on front and back. in the gap we can read the history of how this wall was built and during that division how the people in east germany suffered. also, how this wall was eventually broken. so, it was a great feeling for me to have visited this historical site in berlin. it is a must visit place for those travelling to germany.

if you are looking for sheet sets, clothing materials, buttons, clothing repairs etc then this market is perfect. if you cannot find what you are looking for then your clothing is extremely unique. very dirty in the walking areas however i am sure its organised
if you are looking for the beach with fine sand, this can be the perfect place. kids can enjoy sand play as much as they want. it became our favorite beach in jeju island.

if you are looking for the perfect dives in noronha, look no further. amazing team, kind and professional. i did my first ever 6 dives with them after passing my open water, each very special and without a lot of other divers. sharks, turtles, dolfins, sting rays, fish fish fish fish thank you to the entire team!

if you are looking to book a private tour, i highly suggest using mike with montana yellowstone tours! the communication was top-notch and the tour itself is going to be something that my family and i will never forget. mike truly cares about providing the best experience possible and that truly shows in the small details (providing coffee, pastries, lunch, and drinks). we booked the tour as a high school graduation gift for our son and one of his top requests was to see wolves and mike did his absolute best to make that happen. we saw bison, coyotes, wolves, falcons, ospreys, herons, and hawks. we will definitely book with mike the next time we come back!

if you are looking to enjoy a meal that you cook with your own hands in a location that is straight out of a fairy tale, look no further. arun cooking class was amazing! the location was scenic and the food was delicious. the teacher was really attentive and made sure that we all knew what we were doing. one of the best parts of the class was getting away from the city and enjoying wide open spaces and enveloping yourself in nature. it was definitely a highlight of our trip to siem reap!

if you are looking to visit a unique market that still is quite local, not too touristic and still has thai authencity, this is your market to visit! the market majorily focuses on food, but there are also some souvenir or gift shops. there are many different food options, really delicious and very affordable food. highly recommended!

if you are lucky enough to get the chance, try to come here for the amazing sunset view of the bagan temples. from the flat roof of this pagoda you have a 360 degree panorama of hundreds of temples in the surrounding countryside. this is one of the most amazing sights you will see anywhere!

if you are reading this, then you must be curious about what it's like to watch the america's cup ac75 boats out on the waters of the mediterranean sea...simply put, it's an absolutely amazing experience! nowhere else can you get this close to the boats, teams and action of the america's cup. if you are new to sailing as a sport, don't worry! the staff of rib spectator barcelona, christian, carla, and iam make you feel comfortable, and share their knowledge of the boats, teams and the history of the oldest trophy in sports. if you are in barcelona, or are coming to visit during the america's cup, and you do nothing else, you need to visit rib spectator barcelona for a day on the water you will never forget and memories you will cherish for a lifetime!!

if you are staying at the four seasons hotel, this palace is just around the corner. if you have seen all the other palaces in seoul, this one is not a must-stop as it is smaller and less impressive than the others. still, it has the same beautiful artistic decorations and layout.

if you are still looking for a snorkeling tour in oman, i would 100% recommend you book one at daymaniat shells. from the start, communication has been smooth, efficient and friendly. when we arrived today, we were greeted with a very warm welcome and clear information by the captain and nasser. we were gifted very nice water bottles and left the marina feeling relaxed and excited. when we came close to the islands, the captain spotted dolphins some kilometers away - and so we followed them. there were i swear more than 50 dolphins, among them even babies. afterwards we went snorkeling and saw sharks, plenty of fish, beautiful corals and of course many turtles. the snacks were tasty as well. it’s amazing to experience natures beauty with people who care for our magnificent planet and its animals. thank you team for the wonderful day - if we ever come back to oman we’ll be sure to book with you again. all the best 🙏🏼 sofie & aaron

if you are traveling to the yucatán península you need to book at least one tour with viajes conciencia. we did the manatee excursion and it was a dream. not only did we learn about mayan history we got to experience nature in it's purest form. limbert our guide was so professional and kind. communication was great and they made us feel safe. we had so much fun. if traveling to tulum i recommend to download the communication app whatsapp.

if you are up for something different and loads of fun, this is it. it is indeed quite physically demanding and you will need some training to get the hang of it. once you get it, it's so much fun! and also erwan the manager is friendly, very funny and great at what he does (he is also very patient with you). if you are in queenstown, definitely give this a shot! highly recommend.

if you come to phuket, you have to come here. the centre is not a zoo, it’s a rehabilitation centre for rescued gibbons from the tourist injury and elsewhere. they are doing an amazing job here and currently have 40 gibbons being rehabilitated. kas our guide was amazing and very knowledgeable. she told us all about how the gibbons are rehabilitated and then finally released. we went for the 1hr session which was 900 baht each which is very reasonable given that it is sound very important work. it’s also 400 baht to gain entry into the park which is to help support the rangers which protect the area from poaching. thoroughly recommend coming here.

if you come to puerto rico 🇵🇷 you must book with "seeing puerto rico tours and transportation." our tour guide lismar was simply amazing. she was nice, welcoming and just a loving soul. i have been to puerto rico times before but this time it was unforgettable thanks to her. we got to see a lot of places and now have alot of memories. you want to see puerto rico?? then i would strongly recommend this company!!!

if you find yourself in the vicinity of the dolomites, this picturesque spot with the dramatic backdrop of the marmolada glacier is worth the detour. the path around the lake is ideal for a leisurely walk. it’s relatively flat, well-marked, and suitable for all fitness levels. the trail winds gently around the lake, allowing for a relaxing stroll while taking in the breathtaking scenery.

if you find yourself wandering around covent garden, the jubilee market is worth a quick pop-in. i've stopped by numerous times over the years, and it's always a nice little detour. this compact market is a mix of artsy finds and touristy trinkets. it's the kind of place where you might stumble upon a unique handmade item or pick up that obligatory london souvenir for folks back home. there are also a few food stalls if you're feeling peckish. is it going to blow your mind? probably not. but it's a pleasant way to spend 15-20 minutes while you're exploring the area. the atmosphere is typically buzzing, especially on weekends, which adds to the quintessential london market experience.

if you have heard the grand canyon is just a large hole in the ground. you would be very incorrect. i was. it was one of the most beautiful, fascinating things i have ever seen. the wildlife, ancient ruins, and colors of the canyon were magnificent. i could not get enough of the views. it was like a surprise at every turn out. just when you thought it couldn't be more beautiful, it shined even brighter. don't hesitate or overthink. this place is truly a sight to behold and everyone should go at least once, if not twice lol. the only advice i would give is be ready for the crowds. be patient and willing to loop back around. it is worth it.

if you like flea markets, you'll have to check this place out. loads of stalls with old tat and interesting art pieces. there's lots of space and it wasn't too crowded when i went on sunday afternoon. you'll probably want to get there earlier though as some stalls were already packing up around 4pm.

if you like monkeys … you should go an visit the place… you will see them super close, however depending on location of your hotel it could take up to from 1 hour to 2 hours if you’re in the north.. i tell you this because once in the forest and once you find the family of monkeys you will see them for 5 min to 10 tops … i guess not to stress them, which is ok … the rest of the visit it to talk about the vegetation and look around so short visit for monkeys… they said they accept card but not.. just cash.

if you like pottery making or just buying various clay pots, bowls, teapots and vases then this is a must visit. i walked from the old town in hanoi which is not a trip for the faint hearted as was a good 4 hour walk there and 4 hours back. taxi will get you there in 30 mins so it is easily accessible. once in the village which is much more remote rural vietnam you have pretty much every building dedicated to manufacturing clay pottery items and you are surrounded by rural veg growing patches and banana plantations. i bought 3 different sized rice and pho bowls all which came to less than 300,000 dong so very cheap. locals are extremely friendly with all the kids saying hello and practicing their english but be aware not everyone here speaks english as this is very much outside of the usual tourist area but don't let that stop you as everyone willing to help as best they can.

if you like sand and dunes and trekking to the top of challenging dunes then go for it! windy day and not too hot so per the person at the gate i climbed barefoot! any shoes would fill quickly with very fine sand. getting to the top was somewhat challenging and required several rest breaks as soft sand is not so easy to climb on. best part was walking / sliding off the side! took about two minutes to descend! the ascent a lot longer! enjoy!

if you like to be away from the crowds like some of us do, if you don't mind dry and dusty environments and if you are not looking to climb on top of a pagoda, bulethi temple is just the place for you. i found this place by chance while driving around aimlessly on some of the back roads of bagan. my burmese driver and i were the only ones around. there are several small brick structures and two larger pagodas. the dusty setting brings them all together in one beautiful panorama.

if you like to chill on the cliff and jump in the water this is the place for you. a small bar were you can bye soft drinks, beers and more.

if you like to stay in a serene place nestled within nature, then this must be the homestay for you. with all amenities and a mini library our stay with family members were filled with joy. the owners were very friendly and provided all necessary services quite promptly despite power problems during those days. we did enjoy authentic ladakhi cuisine and had a great time.

if you like visiting historical cemeteries, this is the place to check out. make sure to be at the front of the vaporetto to get off quickly at the dock. like nyc subways, they didn't wait for us to get off the first time around with a big crowd by the exit, and we had to make a second trip to get back. bring a mosquito repellent. for some reason i got bitten more there than everywhere else in venice. once there, it's a treasure hunt - stravinsky and his wife, diaghilev, ezra pound and his partner, doppler, sections for the military, the clergy, babies, osorium, etc. if you like to visit the chapel, check the hours before you go. it's open only at certain times.

if you love adventure and "beautiful ruins" it's your place to come. access is quite complicated by car, but you can come by any bus to the city entrance and then walk down. you will find a spring and ruined and half ruined buildings of the arab village which was here once. the place i quite secluded, not inside the city, i would advise not to go there alone and probably not to visit there at night.

if you love animals and want to bring some joy in your life, see the sea lions! they are a joy to look upon! the noises they make will bring a laugh to your belly and smile on your face! best time 10/10 would recommend! went at night and it was still a blast! also it is completely free to look upon these gorgeous creatures!!

if you love coastal viewing and scene photo taking. you can spend around 1.5 hrs here. the route is short. easy to reach and walk even with your kids. but i'm highly recommend you wear a suitable shoe. and beware of slippery stone surfaces. you will have much fun over there. actually, i take more 100 shots along that short trip. 😅

if you love diving in beautiful turquoise waters, you can't go wrong with zanzibar as your destination and zanzibar dive as your service provider. they take care of all the details so that you can just focus on enjoying your diving experience. they will pick you up from your hotel, arrange your equipment, everything! definitely a once in a lifetime kind of experience.
if you love elephants this is surely the place to be, plus animals galore at your finger tip

if you love flowers and nature, this is the best place to visit. visit during weekdays for a enjoyable peaceful experience. even during the end of summer, we can still see roses. this place is great during the blooming seasons.
if you love fresh seafood, this is the place for you!!! there are a ton of options and are all reasonably priced. plus, the 3rd floor roof, has outdoor tables set up to enjoy your food.

if you love historical place and stuff, you gonna love this place. so much to see and so much stuff that will amaze you. worth to visit .they have mini pond with koi fish and 2 garden that perfect for family photos etc. note: entrance ticket fee -1000 yen, you can only enter within the time frame on your ticket. no early check in. taking photos inside the museum is allowed but not video taking. there is souvenir stuff available for sale on their shop located at their annex but pricey.
if you love orchids, it is worth going. there are always blooms and unique plants to see. our guide was the main grower and she was very informative and fun to chat with.

if you love orchids, this place is a must. they have a truly large number of plants, all sizes and varieties from all over the world. the cold area included orchids that are truly amazing, from areas difficult to reach. they were also exhibiting the winners of their annual competition. a wonderful walk to be impressed.
if you love the outdoors, this is the place to be. there are nice hiking trails, and awesome views. the air is clean and the trails are not that difficult to complete, even i could do it.

if you made it this far you get to enjoy the incredible views. but this hike is only halfway done. the way down is technical and with jello legs can be difficult. don’t be fooled by anyone saying this is anything less than difficult. one of the harder hikes i’ve ever done. enjoy the accomplishment and the views from the top!
if you need something for your pet, you've come to the right place. large selection for dogs, cats, birds, fish and reptiles. if you can't find what you're looking for, ask :)

if you only have time for one museum while you're in mexico city, make it this one. it does an amazing job of capturing the history, culture, and spirit of mexico all in one place. from ancient artifacts to modern design, every section has something striking to see. the building itself is beautiful and worth exploring on its own. there’s so much to take in, so give yourself plenty of time if you can. easily one of the highlights of our trip. we had to stand in line to buy tickets at the entrance, which took a little while. it might be a good idea to buy them online ahead of time if you want to save time and get in faster.

if you plan ahead (buy the tickets online, wear your swimsuit under your clothes, and bring a simple bag to carry your stuff in), it is actually a very pleasant experience to enjoy the hot springs. there were no huge line ups for the showers as well. we placed our bag on a bench close to the spot we were staying in the pool to avoid the hassle of using the lockers, and it was quite safe. overall a beautiful place to visit!

if you plan to eat the patagonian lamb barbecue, this is hands down the absolute best. this lamb was so good, i shed a few tears of happiness. i did the full day estancia la peninsula tour, and it was a highlight of my trip to patagonia. it was a perfectly relaxing day trip after spending 7 days in the torres del paine national park. i was super lucky to have beautiful weather and see some magellanic penguins from the boat. from the beginning to the end of this trip, it was absolutely magical. alejandro, our guide, was a fantastic and engaging storyteller who brought the history of this place back to life. donald was our estancia gaucho, boat driver, horseback ride guide, lamb barbecue carver, sheep shearer, and well i don't know if there is anything this guy doesn't do. he made all of the guests feel incredibly welcome.

if you visit after viewing videos on instagram, you might miss the true beauty in person. still, there are sights that are worth experiencing at least once. it's a natural marvel. the crystal-clear water provides a refreshing atmosphere. if you can swim, you can enjoy the water there. however, the bathroom facilities are not well-kept.

if you visit athens and you came not only for shopping this museum is very interesting place. it’s the old parliament and the first floor is dedicated to the history of greek. the most interesting part is the second floor where there is a new exhibition until summer 2025: refugees.the exhibition focuses on the demographic growth of greece - amazing!!!

if you visit cabo you have to book a trip on cabo blue! we had the best time. the drinks were flowing and the views were amazing. the crew made it so much and they were so friendly. we saw whales out of season and the captian made a detour so we could get a close up. the boat tour was a highlight of our trip and we can’t wait to come back. thank you amanda, uziel, kike, ricardo & lola!!!

if you visit hong kong, the giant buddha statue on top of the mountain is a must visit. the best way to get here is to take the cable car. you have to climb at least 2 to 3 hundreds stairs to get to the statue. the statue is hollow inside. you can walk in to visit the shops or museum. you can climb up for an even better view.

if you want a family adventure that will have everyone talking (and maybe screaming), try the 900-meter ziplining in dubrovnik! my kids and i had a blast—they’d have gone again if our schedule allowed. i’m not great with heights (i usually leave tree climbing to the squirrels), but the instructors were fantastic and made me feel completely safe. once i took off, the breathtaking adriatic views took my mind off my wobbly knees, and suddenly i felt like a superhero. the kids haven’t stopped raving about it. we got free drinks at the end—water for the kids, a little something stronger for the grown-ups—and you can pay extra for helmet cam videos, which are totally worth it for reliving the adventure (and proving that yes, i actually went through with it). easily a holiday highlight, and i’d recommend it to anyone—especially fellow reluctant adventurers!

if you want a medium hike with great scenery! this is the place. we have visited several times in our visits to oahu, in different months and every time it's pleasantly enjoyable. bring good hiking shoes, water, mosquito repellent (some months), umbrella (some months) and a good camera. the waterfall is not as thick sometimes but it's the trek that will leave you with good memories.

if you want a peaceful hike on your own, this is not it. it is quite busy and comercialized. there are shops on the way to the top and people trying to sell you bracelets when you’re waiting for the sun to rise up the top. all the bad stuff aside it is definitely worth it. it took us about an hour and a half to hike up the mountain from our hotel. we waited for about 45 minutes for the sun to rise and it was very spectacular. if you’re in bali i say you should do this. if you’re decently fit you can most definitely hike it in under three hour, if you’re not decently fit, you should work on that, but you can also take a motorbike up to the top. these make a lot of noise so if you’re hiking it can be quite annoying but the view up the top is worth every bit of agony.

if you want a place that’s back in and away from people and civilization this the place!! very relaxed atmosphere with very hospitable and hard-working owner and staff! they’ll make you feel at home and also very educational just sitting back with a cup of coffee and listening to stories of how it came to be back in the ‘80s. you’ll love every minute i can promise and it will be worth it i can guarantee!! at least if you enjoy the mountains and being back in.

if you want a semi challenging hike this is perfect for you! your heart rate would definitely go up when you’re climbing uphill. the mountain top view was rewarding - and you also get a good view of the rundle mountain. bonus: we saw some elks ago the way!

if you want an engaging presentation, this is the place to come! all the speakers were extremely knowledgeable and passionate about their work and exceptional presenters. make sure you arrange for transportation to the homestead to arrive in time to pet the puppies before the tour.

if you want to cook traditional khmer food and learn from an expert, mr savuth is a talented chef and brilliant teacher. not only does he speak fluent english, he is extremely kind and knowledgeable about shopping for, preparing, cooking and serving delicious cambodian food. the three course lunch we enjoyed cooking and eating was excellent. he is passionate about his subject and his cookery school on the outskirts of siem reap is delightful. he collected us from our hotel, showed us what to look for in the market then patiently demonstrated how to cook it. highly recommended!

if you want to experience the great barrier reef and only have a day to spare, there’s no better choice than booking with reef magic. the process is seamless: book online, head to the cairns pier, and hop aboard their spacious cruise, staffed with a team of professionals eager to assist. a special thanks to the entire reef magic team for their outstanding hospitality. we traveled with an 8-month-old baby and a pram, and the staff ensured we were comfortable and well-attended throughout the trip, making the experience stress-free and enjoyable. onboard, you can book additional activities such as scuba diving or snorkeling—even if you’re a complete beginner. guided snorkeling is open to everyone, including those who have never swum before. the expert team will literally handhold you, ensuring you feel safe and confident while exploring the stunning underwater world of the reef. the day starts at 8 am and concludes by 5 pm, giving you ample time to immerse yourself in this unesco world heritage site—the only reef visible from space. be sure to visit the underwater observatory on the reef magic pontoon and take a glass-bottom boat tour for a unique perspective of the vibrant reef ecosystem. this has truly been one of the most remarkable experiences of my life, leaving me with unforgettable memories and a deep appreciation for this natural wonder.

if you want to experience the soul of vienna, this is the place. elegant, historic, and full of charm — café landtmann is everything a traditional viennese café should be. the coffee is rich and carefully prepared, a true reflection of viennese coffee culture. the pastries are beautifully made, with just the right balance of sweetness and tradition — from the warm apfelstrudel to the iconic sachertorte. service is attentive, the atmosphere timeless, and the summer terrace one of the most peaceful spots in the city. whether it’s your first visit to vienna or your hundredth — landtmann always feels like home.

if you're a fan of music, or even just beautiful buildings, the tour of the vienna state opera is a must-do. i wasn't sure what to expect, but it was really fascinating. ​it's a guided tour, so you go with a group and a guide tells you all the stories. they take you through the grand staircases and these incredibly ornate rooms like the tea salon and the marble hall. everything is so elegant and detailed, and it's wild to think that parts of the building had to be rebuilt after being bombed in world war ii. you see the original parts and the restored parts side by side, and it's a cool mix of history. ​the highlight for me was seeing the auditorium and the stage from different angles. you get to stand in the royal box and look out, and it makes you feel like you're royalty for a second. ​the tour is about 40 minutes long, and you get so many interesting facts and stories. they tell you about the famous composers and conductors who worked there. it's a really great way to appreciate the opera house even if you don't have time to see a full performance. it's a good idea to check the schedule online and book your tour in advance because they're really popular

if you're a history buff or just appreciate unique and thought-provoking public art, the paseo de los presidentes in san juan, puerto rico is a must-visit attraction. this outdoor park features larger-than-life bronze statues of the nine u.s. presidents who visited the island during their terms in office, each accompanied by a plaque with information about their visit. the walkway of the presidents provides a fascinating glimpse into the complex relationship between puerto rico and the united states, and the impact that each president had on the island's history. the statues are beautifully crafted and well-maintained, and the park itself is a peaceful and inviting space for reflection and contemplation. located in the heart of san juan, the paseo de los presidentes is easily accessible and free to the public. it's a wonderful opportunity to learn about puerto rico's political history while enjoying a pleasant stroll through a lovely park. whether you're a tourist or a local, this unique attraction is definitely worth checking out!
if you're around venice, a visit to burano is definitely worth the time and cost. it's ok if you miss visiting parts of venice main island and go here instead.

if you're ever in the middle east, let alone jordan, you must add petra to your itinerary. it is one of the most beautiful places you could ever visit in the world and in your lifetime. the majestic views are courtesy of nature, that made that rock display take that form and red colour, as well as the ancient civilization of nabataeans, who carved that magnificent monument called "the treasury". petra is considered one of the 7 wonders of the world and it's a unesco world heritage site, so visiting this site isn't just a touristic activity, but rather a walk through a space that is both unique and breath-taking. while there, you should enjoy a camel ride, and put on the traditional headscarf to immerse yourself in the experience. i visited petra in december, and i was lucky that it didn't rain that day. it is recommended that you visit in the spring or autumn when the weather is mild and beautiful. either way, it's a lot of walking in open space, so don't plan your visit when it's very hot.

if you're going to visit puerto rico, you need to include el yunque! and the visitors center is the place to start. the architecture is functional and inviting, and intriguing. you should take in the informative movie as a starter. take time to look at the displays. have lunch in the great cafe. and certainly walk the paths through amazing forest surroundings. a day on el yunque and its amazing views on the ocean and landscapes below is a must.

if you're in cairo, this museum is well worth a visit. i know that it gets left off many tourist package itineraries which focus on ancient history. in my experience, this is a mistake. this museum provides you with a context of egypt over the centuries and the events that have shaped it into the country it is today. spare a couple of hours of your 'free time' and visit. who needs free time, anyway. you can rest at home.

if you're in oahu and looking for something unforgettable, book the tiki sunset cruise with the adventure boat! it’s seriously one of the most unique and fun experiences i’ve ever had on the island. we cruised out in the late afternoon with capt. chris, who was not only an expert captain but also hilarious, charismatic, and super knowledgeable about the area. he instantly made everyone feel relaxed and excited for the ride ahead. the boat is fast, smooth, and private — no crowds, just your group and the ocean. the highlight? we pulled up to this old-school hidden gem of a tiki bar — la mariana — that feels like stepping back in time. the tropical drinks are strong and delicious, the vibe is pure vintage hawaii, and the sunset views from the boat ride back? absolutely breathtaking. golden skies, ocean breeze, music playing — pure magic. this isn’t your average touristy tour. it’s personal, adventurous, and a total blast. highly recommend it for couples, small groups, or anyone looking to do something special and off the beaten path. book it. trust me. you’ll be talking about it long after the sun goes down. 🌺🌅🍹🚤 thanks capt chris!

if you're like me you'll probably want to know as much as possible beforehand to be best prepared for the experience. so i'll try to give you a few details, which hopefully help a bit. first of all the entrance area offers plenty of parking space. we arrived there mid of august 2025 at around 8:30 and were the 2nd car at the parking lot plus one guided tour entering the trail ahead of us, which we overtook pretty quickly. the good thing about the round-trip trails is that you don't have to make a decision in advance. all three trails (red, yellow and green) start at the same point and then divide some time later. so you can make the decision at each bifurcation depending on how you feel at that point of your hike. the green trail is more like a stroll and avoiding any of the lore difficult lava area. which also means you're missing the vista platform, which the red and the yellow trail offer. we originally planned to do the red trail, but after going up and down through a lot of lava, my 19 y/o daughter and i decided at the fork between the red and yellow trail to take the yellow trail instead. the best parts were already behind us (going through the lava and the jungle) and we also had had our share of steep steps and loose rocks. we weren't sure if the yellow trail was really the easier way (surely it's the shorter way with only 3 km vs. 5 km for the red trail), because right at the fork the yellow trail continues to go down steeply. but that fortunately ended pretty quickly and the rest of the yellow trail was quite pleasant. i can't say what you're getting to see extra taking the red way, but it looked to us like more of the same and definitely some additional up and down. since we had covered a lot of jungle already during our days in monteverde, i don't think we missed something that we hadn't seen before. i will add a map of the park for your convenience and also a few photos of the trail itself showing the worst parts you'll encounter so that you can make a good decision. we covered the yellow trail in roughly 1 hour. we were slowed down by the many steps up and especially the steps down, since you have to watch your step to not end up putting your foot on loose rocks and pumice stone. we also took plenty of photos. all in all it's a great walk, but even in the morning with only 25 degrees celsius you'll be sweating profoundly due to the height differences you need to cover. i'll give the yellow trail a medium difficulty rating. it's not an easy stroll and you have to watch your steps, but it is doable if this is not your first 5 km walk. bring solid footwear and don't even think of bringing a stroller. you will definitely regret it unless you choose the green trail. even without a guide, we got to see a single (male) coati right at the beginning of the trail, plenty of different birds, a big frog, a few butterflies, a small dragon fly, plenty of ants and lots of lava rocks and jungle. we've had enough guided tours in monteverde, so we didn't want to spend too much time listening to detailed explanations here again. but if this is your first tour in the jungle, you might want to consider taking a guide to get to see more of the animal life, which you'll otherwise most likely miss.

if you're looking for a beautiful and peaceful hike, i highly recommend the kranji nature trail. the trail includes a stunning coastal walk along the johor strait, which separates singapore from malaysia. it’s a fantastic way to enjoy scenic views and immerse yourself in nature. definitely worth a visit!

if you're looking for a chill break in mexico city, you've got to wander over to parque españa. it's not one of those huge, famous parks, but that's part of its charm. it's tucked away in condesa, and it's just this really lovely, leafy green space. it feels super relaxed and residential. you'll see locals out walking their dogs (lots of cute ones!), people jogging, or just sitting on benches reading a book. there are some nice pathways, a few statues, and just generally a really pleasant atmosphere. it's one of those places that feels like a real neighborhood park – calm, inviting, and a perfect spot to just be. if you've been doing a lot of sightseeing and need a quiet moment, or just want to soak up the local vibe, parque españa is a fantastic little oasis. it's especially nice if you're staying in condesa or roma norte and want to just go for a leisurely stroll.

if you're looking for a unique, thrilling, and fun experience in lapland, driving snow-adapted karting is an absolute must! the snowy track offers a rare combination of breathtaking views, adrenaline-pumping excitement, and pure joy. it was an incredible opportunity to break free from routine and try something that you probably won't find anywhere else. highly recommended for anyone who loves action and thrills with a special winter twist. don't miss out!

if you're looking for an awesome noodle dish while at psar samaki market, this is the one! there's a lot going on in this bowl. handmade noodles, broth, various meat parts, and my personal favorite, blood cakes. add in the fresh herbs and veg and you've got a hearty meal for just $1.25.

if you're looking for an unforgettable adventure, i highly recommend the kilimanjaro day trip and 4-day safari with serengeti wildlife safaris. from start to finish, the experience was flawless. the kilimanjaro day trip offers a perfect taste of the mountain's majesty, with stunning views and an excellent guide. the 4-day safari through tarangire, ngorongoro crater, and the serengeti is a wildlife lover's dream, with breathtaking landscapes and incredible .wildlife sightings, including elephants, lions, and the famous serengeti migration. the team at serengeti wildlife safaris stands out for their professionalism, expert guides, and exceptional service. whether you're a seasoned traveler or a first-timer, this experience is a must. highly recommended for anyone wanting to explore the best of tanzania!
