if you're looking for beautiful art by sedona artists, sedona artist market is the place to go. their 8,000 square foot art gallery has art selections from over 100 artists 🎨 in a wide variety of art categories to choose from. this includes paintings, photography, textiles, metal art, pottery, jewelry, wood art, and more. i was very impressed with the quality and beauty of the art offered there. i highly recommend this as a must-see destination when you visit sedona.

if you're looking for common souvenirs with a limited budget and good quality items, bo bae market is the place to be. for the same item or even better the price here is much cheaper than chatuchak weekend market. especially if you buy in wholesaler, you will get free item. prepare a big bad if you intend to shop here. they collection of dresses and other items also unique and cute. i feel want to buying everything.

if you're looking for out-of-this-world vegetarian options in siem reap, this is definitely the place. i went for the plant forward six courses menu, and it was absolutely amazing. from appetizer to main course and desert, everything was a delight and super tasty. i would say the amok what is the highlight of the night, and the jackfruit curry dip crisp rice cracker is the runner-up. i suggest you to take the wine pairing, because it did enhance the flavor of the dishes and they are all a very well balanced selection of wines. ms. laut explained me the content of every dish, making the whole experience even better. super recommend!

if you're looking for the absolute best dive center and tourist agency on isabela island, look no further! i wholeheartedly recommend booking your excursions with them. the cormorant tour is an absolute must for adventure and nature enthusiasts. we had the incredible and almost unbelievable experience of seeing orcas up close, and even more amazingly, snorkeling alongside penguins, cormorants, turtles, and playful sea lions! not only do they offer the most competitive prices we found, but their customer service is truly outstanding. make sure to speak with dani or roy – they are both fantastic, genuinely care about their customers, and go above and beyond to ensure you have the best possible experience.

if you're looking for the ultimate vip experience in bangkok, the pimp is the place to be. from the moment we arrived, we were treated like royalty. the club itself is stunning—modern decor, a high-energy vibe, and some of the most beautiful hostesses i’ve ever seen. we booked a private room, and it was worth every baht. the sound system was top-notch, and the atmosphere was perfect for a wild night with friends. one of the highlights was the live entertainment. the models were not only gorgeous but also knew how to keep the party going. we had bottle service with premium drinks, and the service was impeccable—never had to wait for a refill. i’ve been to many clubs around the world, but the pimp offers a level of luxury and fun that’s hard to match. if you’re in bangkok and want an exclusive party experience, this is the spot.

if you're looking to buy fruits and vegetables in bulk, this is the right place for you even if not in bulk you'll see a 25%-40% of cut in prices comparing to other shops and markets in oman. shopkeepers are a spot of stubborn when it comes to bargaining but anyhow do some haggling and you'll find the odds in your favour.

if you're passing through hanoi and want to discover vietnamese culture through art, i urge you to go to this theater: nhà hát cải lương hà nội. the original price for the 5 p.m. show currently going on is 490k, but right now, it's 30% off. the show is simply splendid: 45 minutes of fascination. it mixes dance, song, drama, and there's even a mini orchestra. the costumes are spectacular, as are the makeup, sets, props, and acting. there must be about twenty or thirty performers, while the audience is almost empty. although the drama is in vietnamese, you can guess the story, and there are sometimes short explanatory sentences in english. i was truly captivated by the magic of the performance. perfect! everything is just perfect !

if you're planning a trip to são miguel, pedro ferreira tours is an absolute must! our experience with pedro was the highlight of our vacation. from the moment we were picked up, pedro's warmth and enthusiasm set the tone for an unforgettable day. pedro's deep knowledge of são miguel’s history, culture, and natural wonders was evident throughout the tour. he expertly crafted a personalized itinerary that allowed us to explore the island’s stunning landscapes, including the breathtaking sete cidades and the lush furnas valley. his insights and stories brought each location to life in a way that no guidebook could. what truly stood out was pedro's commitment to ensuring we had a fantastic experience. he was incredibly accommodating, tailoring the tour to our interests and even suggesting local dining spots that turned out to be some of the best meals of our trip. his passion for the island is contagious, and his genuine care for his guests made the day not just informative but also genuinely enjoyable. whether you're looking to explore the natural beauty of são miguel or delve into its rich culture, pedro ferreira tours offers an exceptional experience that you won't want to miss. if you’re seeking an enriching, personalized tour experience in são miguel, pedro ferreira tours should be at the top of your list tell him mikey chourico sent you.

if you're planning to come here, try coming in the morning. the museum is huge and there's so many wonderful things to see! from ancient to modern, you will see art, statues, even early cinema films. this is perfect for family and friends!

if you're planning to visit el nido, look no further than **palaweña** for the most incredible island hopping experience! from start to finish, everything about our tour was nothing short of perfection. the team at palaweña went above and beyond to make sure every moment was magical. first and foremost, the **staff** deserves a special mention. they were not only incredibly knowledgeable about the islands but also some of the friendliest, most hospitable people i've ever met. they truly made us feel like part of the family, sharing stories, history, and personal insights about the stunning spots we visited. their genuine passion for the beauty of el nido added so much to the experience. the tour itself was perfectly organized, with a well-thought-out itinerary that allowed us to enjoy the **crystal-clear waters**, **hidden lagoons**, and **pristine beaches** without ever feeling rushed. the crew was super attentive, ensuring we had everything we needed. speaking of meals, the **food prepared by their chef** was beyond incredible! it was not only fresh and delicious, but also carefully presented, as if we were dining at a five-star restaurant in the middle of paradise. from perfectly grilled seafood to refreshing tropical fruits, every dish was bursting with flavor and truly captured the essence of the local cuisine. the meals alone were worth the trip! one of the highlights for me was the **personalized attention**. they made sure we explored some of the quieter, lesser-known islands, away from the typical tourist crowds. this made the experience feel truly exclusive and intimate. overall, i can't recommend **palaweña** enough. they don't just offer a tour, they provide an **unforgettable adventure** filled with breathtaking scenery, heartfelt hospitality, and delicious food. if you're visiting el nido, this is the agency you absolutely must choose! thank you, palaweña, for memories (and meals) that will last a lifetime! 🌊🌴

if you're planning to visit north playa (playa del carmen) in june, just a heads up — it's peak seaweed season. the beach was covered in thick seaweed, making it nearly impossible to swim or enjoy the shoreline. it’s not ideal for beachgoers this time of year. thankfully, we took a quick 20-minute ferry ride to isla mujeres, and it was a total game changer. crystal-clear water, swimmable beaches, plenty of great restaurants, and beach chairs everywhere. it turned our trip around and made for an amazing beach day. highly recommend heading to isla mujeres if you're in the area during the summer!

if you're someone who’s already been to the vatican museums, the capitoline, and the borghese gallery, and you're wondering what’s left in rome that feels less touristy but equally breathtaking… put the doria pamphilj gallery on your list. actually, scratch that—put it near the top. walking in, you don’t feel like you’re entering a regular museum. there’s something deeply intimate about it—like you’ve accidentally stumbled into someone’s ancestral home and they just forgot to kick you out. the palace is still privately owned by the pamphilj family, and you can sense that in every creaky floorboard and heavily gilded frame. it’s like the dust is part of the atmosphere… and i mean that in the best way.

if you're staying in the tourist district, and want to see ruins without driving hours out of the way, take a quick ride over to these ruins. you get the experience of the ruins in about 2 hours. it's inexpensive to get in, and they have artifacts from the mayan area on display as well. one thing to be cautious about, the elevators don't work to get to the museum, and it's a spiral ramp that takes you up about 5 stories that you have to walk. there is no air where the artifacts are, and it gets hot quick, especially after walking up the ramp. the ruins are on the ground level, and have walking paths to each ruin with signs on english and spanish. the signs with the artifacts are not in english. they have so many iguanas, or as my wife calls them baby alligators... smh, i kept telling her they are harmless as long as you don't mess with them, just watch where you step because they blend in well with the environment.

if you're thinking about a hot air balloon ride in sedona, don't hesitate - do it. yesterday, we flew with red rock balloons and had an unforgettable experience. mark and his crew were professional, kind, and full of knowledge. from the moment we arrived in the quiet morning light, we were made to feel completely at ease. watching the balloon inflate as the sun began to rise was breathtaking, and once in the air, the beauty was beyond words. the flight was smooth and peaceful, drifting above canyons and red rock formations as the golden light of sunrise spread across the landscape. mark’s guidance throughout made the journey even more special. after landing, we were treated to a champagne toast with mimosas, sharing laughs with the crew and fellow passengers. i had put this off for years, blaming the cost, but now i know i’ll do it again. it’s more than just a ride - it’s a memory that will stay with you forever. bucket list worthy in every way. we posted a short video with this review, but if you’d like to see more photos and stories from the road, follow us at "stray compass life" on facebook. we live full time in our rv and share daily blogs filled with nature, travel, and photography. tell red rock balloons we sent you. you won’t regret it. #redrockballoonssedona #redrockballoons #straycompasslife #fulltimervlife #bucketlistexperience #sedonaarizona #hotairballoonride #sunriseflight #rvadventure #travelphotography

if you're visiting san cristobal, you must do this tour! nicholas was our guide and he was so awesome and knowledgeable. the boat and its crew were amazing, the food was good, the people in the office were so helpful and accommodating. we asked a lot of questions and they had all the answers! the wetsuits, snorkels, etc, were great. highly recommend. don't come here without taking this tour! you're missing out on san cristobal if you don't do this!

if you've not been able to hike at all during your time in scandinavia, this will make up for it a bit. its a great experience especially in winters. the showstopper is obviously the polar bear 🐻‍❄️ but don't worry you'll most probably get a real good look, venus is highly active and enjoys walking in it's enclosure. the swan lake is mesmerizing in winter and makes you wonder how it looks in the moonlight. overall, a magical arctic experience.

if your a thrill seeker....this is a must add to your bucket list. staff were very professional and they were always making sure safety was number 1. something that i will never forget. you have to get there via a 40 minute trip in a big 4wd bus from queenstown. cars are not allowed.

if your looking for something different, yet amazing, this is it! who would have thought that a tent could be so luxurious at the same time as being in the centre of the serengeti! the camp really is five star (we were sceptical before visiting) and as good as any hotel! it is difficult to find anything that could be bettered. the tents were luxury palaces in their own right, with an en-suite. the food was excellent and there were welcoming drinks in the communal lounge. the whole site was set up perfectly and there was always someone on hand to escort you from your accommodation to the restaurant or to and from your vehicles. our tent opened up to a view over the serengeti plains and was perfect for drinking g&t and watching the sun go down! i can't recommend this highly enough. thank you very much for an excellent stay dan & anne

if your navigation says to take henry hannam drive, you'll be going on dirt and gravel road for kilometers. several small bridges but we were able to cross on our rental mitsubishi outlander so there isnt much problem. but the falls were worth it!
if you’re a fan of the games or just curious this place will answer all your questions not just about the 2020 tokyo olympics but the long history of the olympic games

if you’re a first timer in ski or snowboarding, this place is a perfect place to learn. they have a wide track for beginners, an some of easy track up the hill. so you wont get stuck on the bottom of the hill every time. they have international instructor as well, who has so many experiences. they all profesional and friendly as well. to be said, this is the best experience ever!

if you’re a tourist this is a great place to get introduce with mexican culture. they have different street foods, tacos store and the locals spends family time here. as a filipino the plaza reminds me of my home country. i felt safe wandering around.

if you’re after serene views, gentle breezes, and a slow afternoon away from crowds, mitra’s ranch delivers. it’s not about luxury or high-energy thrills—it’s about calm moments and open-air space. just be prepared that some facilities might appear a bit worn and less polished than expected. you can try a few light adventures: a giant slide, skywalk with zipline, giant swing, and horseback riding. however, activities felt a bit overpriced for what they offered, implying maintenance and quality issues

if you’re coming to cape town, this is an absolute must‑do! we did the 2‑hour sidecar tour and it was truly one of the highlights of our trip. cruising past the stunning camps bay in a vintage sidecar felt like stepping into a movie — the views were breathtaking and the experience was unforgettable. our driver, bev, made it even more special. she was incredibly sweet, warm, and knowledgeable, making us feel safe and completely at ease the whole time. bev’s passion for what she does shines through, and her kind energy turned a beautiful ride into an unforgettable memory. trust me, anyone coming to cape town has to do this activity — you won’t regret it!

if you’re considering spending your day enjoying a xochimilco boat tour, this is the best one! we had a group of 8 and there were some specific things we wanted to do and see. our boat captain knew exactly how to make it all happen. we had the best day…unforgettable!

if you’re craving authentic, flavorful shawarma, abdul at mr. shawarma food truck is the one to find! the food is consistently fresh, perfectly seasoned, and served with genuine care. abdul’s hospitality makes the experience even better—he’s friendly, professional, and always ensures you leave satisfied. the portions are generous, the service is quick, and the quality is unmatched. easily one of the best food trucks in the city. highly recommended!
if you’re debating this option or the national park, this is a superb option to view the volcano and see a beautiful lake. the intermediate trail is pretty tough… you have been warned.

if you’re eager to get under the water, i can recommend my experience with this dive center. generally the staff is professional, kind, and fun – and sam is an excellent instructor for anyone needing lessons of any level.

if you’re ever in sydney, whether it being your first time in australia, do check this place out! the zoo is pretty big so you’ll probably spend a good amount of time here. the place is well maintained by the keepers and the animals are very well taken care of. better yet, all the proceeds and money you’ll spend at the zoo whether it being the store or cafe, it all goes to the animals to help them even further. there’s giraffes, koalas, monkeys, foxes, seals and many more! oh and one more thing to add, i recommend buying tickets online as it is $10 cheaper than buying it physically

if you’re ever trying to lay low from a few overzealous federal agents (who clearly have the wrong guy), norris geyser basin is the place to be. feels like you’re not even on earth—more like mars, if mars had boiling acid pools, steam vents that hiss like angry snakes, and a sulfur scent strong enough to wipe your fingerprints clean. i wandered the boardwalks like a ghost with a backpack, soaking in the alien beauty and scanning the horizon for black suvs. the ground literally bubbles and hisses beneath you—makes it hard to tell if it’s geothermal activity or a tracking drone malfunctioning nearby. either way, it’s stunning. pro tip: the steam makes for great cover, and the constant gurgling sounds are perfect for masking heavy breathing after a sprint through the parking lot. come for the geysers. stay because your fake id says you’re “brent wafflehouse.” five stars. will return if not extradited.

if you’re heading to el nido and wondering which boat tour to book, stop looking — mad good is the one. hands down, this was the highlight of my entire trip. from start to finish, everything about the experience was, well… mad good. the crew was super friendly and made everyone feel like old friends from the moment we stepped on board. they knew all the hidden spots — not just the typical tourist stops, but secret lagoons, private beaches, and snorkeling spots where we had the reef almost entirely to ourselves. every place we visited looked like a postcard come to life. mark was specially friendly and kyle is the most welcoming dude! lunch was unreal — fresh grilled seafood, chicken, spring rolls, fruits, and island-style dishes that beat most restaurants in town. they even had options for vegetarians and made sure everyone was happy. and the vibe on the boat? pure magic. good music, chill atmosphere, plenty of time to swim, relax, and take in the insane beauty of bacuit bay. you can tell these guys love what they do — it’s not some rushed, cookie-cutter tour. they give you the time and space to actually enjoy el nido the way it should be enjoyed: at your own pace, surrounded by nature, with good people and great energy. 10/10 would recommend. if you want an unforgettable day in el nido, mad good lives up to its name.

if you’re heading to quebec city, do yourself a favour and take a walk down (or up!) the escalier casse-cou, also known as the breakneck stairs. i visited recently and honestly, it was one of those little gems that stick with you. the stairs might sound a bit scary by name, but they’re actually a fun and easy climb if you take your time. what really makes this spot special is the atmosphere all around. as you walk the steps, you’ll be surrounded by beautiful old buildings, cute little shops, and cozy cafes where you might want to stop for a coffee or some local treats. i’d recommend going in the late afternoon — the golden light on the stone streets and buildings is just magical, and it’s such a nice spot to snap a few photos. if you’re into history and like feeling connected to a place, you’ll love knowing that people have been using these stairs for centuries. and from the top (or bottom), you’ll get a lovely view of the charming petit-champlain area and even a glimpse of the st. lawrence river. plus, don’t miss the stunning view of the old palace nearby — its classic architecture beautifully complements the historic charm of the area. so, take a few minutes, slow down, enjoy the vibe — it’s not just a staircase, it’s a little piece of quebec’s heart. definitely worth the visit!

if you’re in barcelona and want to truly immerse yourself in the local culture, casa vicens is a must-visit. this was gaudí’s first major work, and the architecture is absolutely stunning, vibrant, detailed, and unlike anything else. i went on a public holiday and, surprisingly, the place was nearly empty, which made the experience even more special. it gave me the perfect chance to explore at my own pace and take amazing photos without the crowds. the audio guide is available via your phone and really enhances the visit, offering great insight into the history and design of the house. highly recommend adding this gem to your barcelona itinerary!
if you’re in canada or traveling, make sure to stop by this great place to relax with nature and release your stress.

if you’re in new orleans and want a break from bourbon street, i highly recommend hopping on a swamp tour. we wasn’t sure what to expect, but it ended up being one of the coolest things we did on the trip. the boat ride was super chill, and the guide was funny and full of stories about the area and the wildlife. we saw a bunch of alligators (some really close), birds, turtles, and even a raccoon wandering around the edge of the water. the swamp itself was beautiful—kind of eerie in the best way, with those mossy trees and calm water. definitely worth the time, especially if you like nature or just want to see something different. bring your camera!

if you’re in paris, you can’t miss this place. notre-dame cathedral is over 850 years old and one of the most iconic examples of french gothic architecture. construction started in 1163 and took nearly 200 years to complete. it has witnessed many key events in french history, including the coronation of napoleon and victor hugo’s famous novel the hunchback of notre-dame that helped save the cathedral. when i visited in the morning, i was honestly surprised by how crowded it already was. but despite the people, the stunning architecture completely mesmerized me. the details of the facade, the giant rose windows, and the impressive scale are unforgettable. highly recommended for anyone interested in history, architecture, or photography!

if you’re in phuket with kids, this place is a must-visit! it’s beautifully organized, clean, and offers a fantastic experience. upon entry, you’re given wristbands that you can top up with money and use for all purchases inside the park — no need to carry cash or cards. at the end of your visit, any unused balance is refunded, making the whole process smooth and hassle-free. there are also convenient facilities like locker rentals, towel rentals, and a shop where you can buy anything you might need for swimming. everything is thoughtfully arranged to ensure a comfortable and enjoyable day for the whole family

if you’re in san juan and looking for an unforgettable adventure on the water, look no further than vip jet ski adventures! as a first-time jet ski operator, i was a bit nervous at first, but that all changed the moment richie and benji stepped in. these two were absolutely phenomenal—professional, patient, and incredibly knowledgeable. richie made sure i felt comfortable and confident before we even hit the water. he explained everything clearly and made safety the top priority without taking away from the fun. benji, with his laid-back charisma and encouraging attitude, kept the energy high and made the whole experience feel like an epic adventure with friends. the views from the water were stunning—the historic coastline of old san juan, the shimmering caribbean sea, and even a few surprise spots that only locals seem to know about. it wasn’t just a ride, it was a guided tour with heart. what really sets vip jet ski adventures apart is the personal touch. richie and benji genuinely care about your experience, and it shows in every moment. for anyone visiting puerto rico—whether you’re a thrill-seeker or a first-timer like me—this is a must-do activity. you’ll leave with a huge smile, great memories, and probably some awesome photos too. thank you, richie and benji, for an incredible day. i’ll definitely be back!

if you’re in sedona and want the best off-road adventure possible, go straight to red rock rubicon jeep rentals and ask for kris. he’s the real deal, incredibly knowledgeable, down-to-earth, and passionate about making sure you have the best experience. his advice on routes and local spots was spot-on, and the equipment was in top-notch condition. kris doesn’t just hand you the keys; he sets you up for an unforgettable day with tips, insights, and genuine care for your safety and enjoyment. this is hands down the best way to explore sedona’s stunning red rock country.

if you’re in the island of sao miguel and thinking about a whale-watching tour, stop thinking—just book with beatriz and the team at terra do pico. this was, hands down, one of the most memorable days of our trip. from the very first briefing, we felt in expert hands. the team’s respect for the animals and their deep knowledge of the azorean ecosystem were obvious. we didn’t just see wildlife—we understood it. dolphins playing around the boat, majestic whales surfacing nearby… it felt like we were guests in their world. what made the experience truly special was how much we learned—not just about the animals, but also about the dramatic geological history that shaped these islands. the guides are natural storytellers and scientists at heart. if you want more than a simple boat ride—if you want to leave with wide eyes and a head full of wonder—this is the tour for you.

if you’re into history or just love being by the water, the san francisco maritime national historical park is a spot you shouldn’t miss. it’s right in the fisherman’s wharf area, so super easy to get to. first off, the historic ships are super cool. you can actually board them and see what life was like back in the day. the balclutha, this big old sailing ship, was a favorite of mine. then there’s the eureka, an old-school steam ferryboat, which has such a unique vibe. the visitor center is packed with interesting info and a great place to start your visit. just across the way is the maritime museum, in this awesome art deco building. it has all sorts of exhibits about shipbuilding, navigation, and life at sea – plenty to keep you entertained and informed. all in all, it’s a fantastic mix of history and scenic views. definitely worth a visit next time you’re in san francisco!

if you’re looking for a a decent kaftan that can be altered / tailored we’ve used “elegances de kaftan” hamza is super helpful and accommodating. go through the gates and walk around ten mins past the bank on your left and some food places further along on your right. great place to pick up local gifts at non tourist overinflated prices.

if you’re looking for a boat tour in santorini, stop scrolling and book this one. captain george and his assistant alias gave us the most unforgettable day of our honeymoon—an experience we’ll be talking about for years. george isn’t just another tour operator. he’s a one-boat, one-captain kind of host who’s been sailing the waters of santorini for over 10 years. while the big companies pack dozens of tourists onto crowded catamarans, george offers something far more special: privacy, authenticity, and heart. there were only three other guests on board with us, so the entire day felt like a private, luxury experience. george took us to hidden coves and quiet swimming spots away from the typical tourist routes—places we never would’ve found on our own. we swam with fish in the crystal-clear sea, then came back to a homemade meal of fresh greek food, amazing local wine from george’s homeland, and the best olive oil we’ve ever tasted. what really set this experience apart was george’s and alias’s deep knowledge of the area. they shared so much about the island’s geology, volcanic history, and culture in a way that was fascinating and easy to connect with. it made us feel so much more connected to santorini. the sailing itself was incredibly smooth—george is a true professional—and the sunset was absolutely stunning, with no other boats in sight. alias was also warm, funny, and incredibly knowledgeable. their passion for what they do was felt in every moment. george runs this business himself, and it shows. he pours his heart into every trip and treats his guests like friends, not customers. if you’re considering a sailing tour in santorini, don’t settle for a crowded group tour. book with george—you’ll get a deeply personal, top-tier experience that leaves you with lifelong memories and a new love for the island.

if you’re looking for a colorful, interactive place that showcases new orleans in the most creative way, i highly recommend jamnola! be sure to grab the 3d glasses—they make the artwork pop and bring the experience to life. my girlfriends and i had an amazing time exploring, laughing, and soaking in the vibrant energy.

if you’re looking for a hidden gem in cairo that blends history, art, and stunning architecture, the manial palace is an absolute must-visit. nestled on rhoda island along the nile, this palace was built by prince mohamed ali tewfik in the early 20th century, and it’s one of the most unique palaces in egypt. what makes it truly special is its fusion of different architectural styles – ottoman, persian, moorish, and even european rococo. every room you walk into feels like a different world, with exquisite woodwork, intricate tile designs, and stained glass windows that light up the interiors with a warm, magical glow. the lush gardens surrounding the palace add to the serenity of the place, and the layout itself feels very personal – more like a home than a royal residence. it’s not as crowded as other tourist sites, which gives you the space to really take in the beauty and details at your own pace. whether you’re a lover of architecture, history, or just looking for a peaceful escape in the heart of cairo, the manial palace is a fantastic spot to explore. don’t miss the throne hall and the private mosque – both are breathtaking.

if you’re looking for a truly hidden gem, hidden strawberry garden is the perfect spot. true to its name, this place is tucked away down a small lane, and you’ll need to go a bit further in to find it. what makes this strawberry farm stand out is the beautiful garden setting, which feels more natural and inviting compared to other places in the area. the owner is extremely friendly and polite, making the experience even more enjoyable. i contacted gandhi (his son) before visiting to check if it was strawberry season and if there were enough berries to pick—he was very responsive and helpful. • entrance fee: idr 10k per person • strawberry price: idr 70k per kg (pay for what you pick) • rules: no eating before paying if you’re in the area and want a fresh, peaceful strawberry-picking experience, i highly recommend checking out hidden strawberry garden!

if you’re looking for a truly unique and beautiful handmade piece, this is the spot! every item here is crafted with care and artistry…no two are exactly alike. 🪨💫 just a heads-up: prices aren’t exactly cheap… but totally worth it for the quality and detail. and yes, you can (and should!) negotiate. a little charm goes a long way 😉🛍️ perfect place to find that special piece that tells a story.

if you’re looking for a unique and unforgettable experience, this tour is a must! we booked a tour that included two cenotes and snorkeling with turtles — and it was absolutely amazing. we also paid extra for the atv, which was large and comfortable for two people. we noticed that other companies had smaller and less convenient ones. everything was well-organized, and we had such a great time. a special shoutout to our guide, deni — he was fantastic! he explained everything, showed us the best spots, and made the whole experience even more enjoyable. highly recommended!

if you’re looking for a vibrant, authentic bangkok experience, head to pak khlong talad at night! this 24-hour flower market offers fresh flowers at amazing prices and a chance to see the rhythm of real local life. the colors, scents, and atmosphere are unforgettable — plus it’s a fantastic spot for late-night photography! pro tip: bring cash, wear comfy shoes, and don’t be shy to chat with the friendly vendors! definitely one of the best hidden gems in bangkok.

if you’re looking for an epic experience on the colorado river through the grand canyon, don’t hesitate to book a trip with california river and trails expeditions! we just returned from an 8 day motorized trip, which was 100% awesome - hearty and plentiful food, good equipment (we slept comfortably!) and most importantly, highly skilled, caring, knowledgeable guides who helped us understand and appreciate the historical, natural, and geological aspects of this unique place on the planet. thank you, crate team, for a magical trip.

if you’re looking for an epic night out in bangkok, dj station is the spot to hit! this legendary club is all about good vibes. lots of choices ; mainstream gay pop hits, k-pop dance floors, dazzling drag shows, and even a karaoke corner where the queens own the mic . the crowd is a fun mix of locals, expats, and travelers, all there to let loose and dance until 2-3am. trust me, the energy here is next level. don’t miss it! my tip: when you enter, you’ll get 2 drink vouchers. head to the bartender and swap them for a pitcher drink. last photo. it’s usually a mix of local thai alcohol and a mixer. fair warning: it’s strong, so take it easy. enjoy responsibly, and get ready for an unforgettable night! 🎉

if you’re looking for an unforgettable adventure in the azores, i highly recommend the canyoning with azorean active blueberry. this was a truly unique and exhilarating experience – full of adrenaline, stunning scenery, and a deep connection with nature. the azorean active blueberry team is absolutely professional we felt safe and well-guided from the very beginning. the equipment was top-notch, and the instructors were not only technically skilled but also incredibly friendly and passionate about sharing their experience.

if you’re new to hiking, quarry rock is a perfect intro. it’s not too long (just under 4 km round trip), and while there are some stairs and roots, it’s totally doable with a moderate fitness level. the forested trail is peaceful, and the view at the top is a serious “wow” moment—it’ll make you want to do more hikes. just wear good shoes, bring water, and try to go on a weekday if you can—weekends get busy (specially the parking)

if you’re not inclined to do the whole 10-kilometre walk from the spit bridge to manly, a good option is to take advantage of the free parking on the lower streets of fairlight, where you can walk down and join the path for a nice 2 to 2.5km walk into manly. this way you can enjoy a lovely stroll and a day out in manly, but avoid the cost of parking in manly itself. the gently winding path hugs the shoreline and has a few ups and downs along the way, but is fully paved and easily walkable for all fitness levels. needless to say, the views are unbeatable. one of the best walks we’ve done in sydney. and plenty of dogs along the path for added smiles! 😁

if you’re planning a trip to east africa, i highly recommend wildlife safari kenya ltd. we recently returned from a 21-day adventure, and from the moment we landed in nairobi until we departed, they took care of us every step of the way, attending to every detail without compromise. our driver/guide, juma, was at our service from morning until night throughout our journey, which included stops at lake elementaita, masai mara, ol pejeta sweetwaters, and airport transfers during our trips to tanzania, zanzibar, and mombasa. thank you, juma—you made our trip unforgettable and added something extra special to every experience. in serengeti, komba kept us entertained with his great humour, and in mombasa, mazera made it even more meaningful by taking me and my uncle to visit my birthplace. a special thank you to stephen, who met us at the airport every time we transited via nairobi with juma, ensuring we were always on track and safely reaching our destinations. lastly, a big thanks to joseph and minesh for planning the entire trip and adding those personal touches that made our anniversary extra special. if you’re thinking of visiting kenya, i strongly recommend reaching out to joseph and minesh at wildlife safari kenya ltd. and if you can, ask for juma to be your guide—he was fantastic! thank you (asante sana) to everyone for making our trip to kenya, tanzania, and zanzibar truly unforgettable. we will definitely be back! prakash and sunita

if you’re trying to see the sunset at the mesa, i’d recommend arriving early. the lower parking fills up and is very small. the hike from the here is easy and there are handrails to help you reach the top. the upper parking is much larger and is $3. there is a gravel area across from this parking where you can see the sunset, too. i’d recommend this view for anyone that is not able to walk too far. if you park at the gravel lot, you can walk a moderate trail to the mesa, which can be found at the front right side of the lot, if you are facing out towards the city. be aware that both of these viewing spots get crowded. i was expecting it to be quieter as i had heard about people going out there to meditate/ experience the vortexes. very few people are doing that. it is mostly people talking loudly, children screaming, people on speakerphone calls, etc. we went both at the sunset and at sunrise to try to have a serene experience, but it was just not possible. if you are there to just see the views it is great, but you will not have a quiet time in nature. i would’ve enjoyed this more if i had known beforehand.

if you’re visiting baker’s hill, i highly recommend making a quick stop at mitra’s ranch since it’s just a short drive away. the main highlight of this place is the breathtaking panoramic view of puerto princesa, making it a great spot for sunset watching and taking photos. 🌅 the ranch itself has an interesting history. while it’s primarily known as a horse ranch, i got the impression that it may have also been a farm for cockfighting chickens in the past. the landscape is quite hilly, and i noticed that the horses looked exhausted, possibly due to the steep terrain. unfortunately, the overall maintenance of the area, including the parking lot, could be improved. a bit of renovation and better upkeep would definitely make the place more tourist-friendly, especially for those who want to sit, relax, and enjoy the view. when we visited, it was really hot, so i was glad to see a coffee shop near the entrance where visitors can grab a drink and cool off. if you’re up for an adventure, there’s also a zipline located below, but be aware that it requires going down steep steps, which may not be ideal for seniors or those with knee problems. overall, mitra’s ranch is a great stop if you’re looking for a quick photo op, a peaceful view of the city, and a breezy spot to watch the sunset. just don’t expect too many amenities, and be prepared for some uphill walking! 🚶‍♂️ ✅ pros: amazing city views, great for sunset watching, windy and relaxing atmosphere ❌ cons: needs better maintenance, steep steps not ideal for seniors, can get very hot during midday would i recommend it? yes, if you’re already in the area! just bring water, wear comfy shoes, and don’t expect too much beyond the view. 😊

if you’re visiting bali this is a must see. this was top 5 places to visit. once you arrive you are greeted by amazing views of well manicured gardens. there are so many photo opportunities throughout, if you love social media this is a must for you. during our visit there weren’t many people so we had the opportunity to take lots of pictures with no one in the background and didn’t have to rush. the entrance fee is very reasonable for what you get. if you’re alone or a couple bring a tripod to capture amazing portraits.

if you’re visiting manly, you definitely don’t want to miss sydney harbour national park — especially the north head area. we were travelling without a car and found it super easy and budget-friendly to get there. getting there without a car from the city to manly: catch a ferry from circular quay to manly wharf. it's a scenic ride that offers great views of the harbour. from manly wharf to north head: once at manly, take the 161 bus operated by keolis downer northern beaches. this loop service departs from manly wharf, east esplanade, stand c and heads towards north head. the journey takes approximately 4 minutes and costs between $1 to $4. buses run every 30 minutes daily from around 6:42 am to 7:42 pm. 🚶‍♀️ exploring north head north head offers stunning clifftop views, walking tracks, and historical sites. the fairfax walk is a popular short trail leading to several lookouts with panoramic views of the ocean and sydney skyline. it's a must-visit spot for nature lovers and photographers. 🚗 parking information (for reference) if you're considering visiting other parts of sydney harbour national park in the future, here are some parking details: bradleys head: $8 per vehicle per day. north head: $5 per vehicle per day. chowder bay: monday–friday: $3 per hour, up to $16/day. weekends & public holidays: $4 per hour, up to $20/day. payment can be made via card or phone at pay machines. coin payments are available at fairfax carpark machines only. holders of an npws all parks or multi parks pass can park free for up to four hours per day; additional time can be purchased. honestly, this is one of those places where nature just speaks for itself. peaceful, scenic, and full of history. we didn’t expect to love it this much, but it ended up being one of the highlights of our sydney trip.

if you’re visiting new york city for the first time, dumbo is a must-see. i recommend starting your walk in the williamsburg neighbourhood of brooklyn. from there, head towards the iconic intersection of washington st. and water st., where you’ll get a stunning view of the manhattan bridge framed perfectly between the buildings — ideal for taking amazing photos! then, continue walking across the bridge into manhattan. it’s a unique experience that blends architecture, history, and panoramic views. my tip: do this walk early in the morning to avoid crowds and enjoy a peaceful atmosphere, or at sunset when the skyline glows in golden tones and the city feels more alive. both options are truly magical.

if you’re visiting paris, joining anne and philippe down the siene river is a must !!! my maid of honor found them and it was the best part of my bachelorette! they are both amazing hosts and anne was so fun to talk to! she provided such an amazing tour and history lesson during our time on the boat. the champagne was also amazing, very crisp and refreshing. it was an elegant way to take in paris and all of its beauty! anne also served a couple of light eats and everything was heavenly. especially the preserve that her mother makes paired with the yogurt! they really know how to make you feel like the star on their boat!

if you’re visiting san francisco and don’t stop by pier 39 to see the sea lions, did you even really go? these chunky, blubbery legends have fully claimed this real estate rent-free since 1989, and honestly, they run the show. expect a full sensory experience: • the aroma (you’ll know when you’re close) • the soundtrack (think a mix of barking, snorting and occasional sea lion sass battles) • and the vibes (big lazy sunbaking energy with a side of “don’t you dare push me off this dock, carl”). they’re like a reality tv show playing live 24/7 — there’s drama, there’s romance, there’s the occasional passive-aggressive shove into the water. perfect spot for people-watching too — both human and sea lion variety. plus, it’s free entertainment (which in san fran is a real bargain). 💡 tourist tip: • go early for less crowds and peak sea lion drama. • bring a jacket — karl the fog loves to make surprise appearances. • don’t drop your phone in while taking 46 identical selfies.

if you’re visiting the grand canyon, do not miss sunset at hopi point. it’s hands-down one of the most breathtaking spots on the south rim to watch the sun dip behind the canyon walls. the panoramic views seem to stretch endlessly, and the colors—deep oranges, purples, and pinks—dance across the layered rock formations like a painting coming to life. i arrived about 30 minutes before sunset to grab a good spot, and the atmosphere was peaceful, almost reverent. there’s plenty of space to spread out, and the railings offer unobstructed views, perfect for photography or just soaking it all in. as the sun sank lower, the canyon lit up in warm hues and cast dramatic shadows that changed by the second. i highly recommend taking the park shuttle—it’s convenient, stress-free, and drops you right at the viewpoint without any hassle. truly a magical moment and a memory i’ll never forget. if you see only one sunset at the grand canyon, make it from hopi point.

im here in september currently. there are things you need to know. -this is not a hike, it is a climb do not come if: -if it has been raining -if you are old or unfit -if you dont have mountaineering boots or at least grippy shoes -if you do not have water shoes / aren't willing to walk barefoot on bumpy rocks -if you are alone, -if it is after 2pm. you will need an hour or so to climb each way. you dont want to do this in the dark. at the top of the canyon where you park your car, there are lovely views of a small dam and a river. you can definitely go and paddle in the stream or check out the abandoned houses before turning back if you realise the climb isnt for you. one of the houses is harder to get to because you need to cross the river and the path to it is disgusting stinky slop but its quite cool inside. there is a little water spout and a pool, a ledge to sit on and lots of frogs around. the climb down the canyon will take an hour or so. there are a couple of seriously sketchy bits for example a single wobbly wooden plank which goes over a 20 foot drop. there are decently long sections of the canyoning trail where there was no cellphone signal or data, so if you get stuck or hurt youre gonna be sat there until someone finds you. with that out of the way, the canyoning trail isnt too dangerous, but its definitely geared towards people who are physically fit and arent too afraid of heights. however, if you do make it to the bottom of the canyon, it is really wonderful. there are warm, shallow thermal ponds, and larger, cold pools to swim in. theres lots of space here for many people to go swim. when i came here there was only one group of other people. you cant see the base of the waterfall sadly, without putting yourself in serious risk, climbing the slippery boulders that surround it. i attempted to get as close as i could, and i couldnt safely get all the way up to the highest pool, despite being physically fit and determined. i barely got down again safely. but regardless, the waterfall area is stunning, fascinating, picturesque, and really fun to go swim around in and explore. well worth the climb down if you are able. as for the climb back up, it will not take you as long but i must warn you, i am only 5'7 and there were some footholds which i could only just barely reach, so if youre short you will need some help getting pulled up in a couple places, or will need to get creative. if youre an older person and are determined to do this trail then i would recommend perhaps bringing a friend and even maybe some rope. it hadnt rained when i went here yesterday, but the ground was still slippery. (september). it did rain right at the end as i was about to finish my climb back up, and i did lose my footing and begin to slide down the mountain towards a large drop. i caught myself on a tree, but i was left with some cuts and bruises so please be very cautious if it begins to rain. luckily it is a forest so you should be able to catch yourself on plants and trees if you fall like i did. lastly the road here is very narrow and you may have to reverse backwards up the road if an oncoming driver meets you, so if you are a bad driver then dont come. most people i saw come to this place on google maps took one look at the climb downwards and simply left the area. i hope that this review leaves you fully informed and gives you an opportunity to prepare. i just want to make sure nobody gets hurt or wastes their time driving all the way up those narrow roads just to turn around and drive back down again. however i cannot rate this lower than 4 stars, i have been here twice now and if you can make it down there it really is a great place. last piece of advice, dont forget to buy yourself food and drinks for when you get down there. youll be hungry

in andean belief, titicaca is the birthplace of the sun. with a surface elevation of 3,812 metres (12,507 ft), south america’s largest lake is also known as the highest navigable body of water in the world. enthralling and in many ways singular, the shimmering deep blue lake titicaca is the longtime home of highland cultures steeped in the old ways. copacabana is the heart and largest town on the shore, but the experience doesn’t end at the shore. there are trips to the many islands that speckle the shoreline (such as isla del sol, the sacred inca island), hikes to lost coves and floating islands, and chance encounters with locals.

in general, there are 2 popular routes to reservoir islands viewpoint. 1. take k66 from yuen long and get off at tai tong road 2. at tun mun station to take 43 mini bus to so kwun wat. if during the red leave season, the first route is preferable, however, will take an hour more in the hiking. for the route #2, it takes about 2 hours from the place you dropped off from the mini bus. you may gather with your friends at the exit f2 of tun mun station and walk along the road to ho pong road (河旁路). you may see paris london new york cinema. across the road, walk towards sun hui street market(新墟街市), you will see no.43 mini bus terminus. after 20 minute driving time, the bus will arrive at so kwun wat terminus. before starting the hiking, you may go to the opposite toilet. the road leading to the viewpoint is well constructed and easy to walk even under raining weather. conversely it is recommeded to have adequate sun screen preparation during hot seasons. after a half hour walk, you will reach a junction. the right fork of the road is to the viewpoint and left to wong nai tun (黃泥墩) reservoir. that is also the exit to take mini bus at tai tong road to yuen long after coming back from the viewpoint. about another half hour walk, you may arrive at the viewpoint. you may see quite a gorgeous and wide view of tai lam. unfortunately, it was cloudy when i came there.

in terms of history and architecture, this is one of the most remarkable cemeteries in the world. necropolis de colon is a reflection of the political, social and economic turmoil that has plagued the cuba capital for the past 60 years. the main entrance gate is an ornate, romanesque triple arch symbolizing the holy trinity. the symmetrical plan by spanish architect calixto de loira is laid out along two axes suggesting a crucifix, with the most impressive monuments and mausoleums built along the main road. what makes this havana cemetery on of the most important in latin america is its funerary monuments, sculptures and mausoleums that create a sort of open air museum. the varied architectural style of the graves - are a feast for the eyes, and the history of havana as told through its buried citizens is absolutely fascinating.

in the 17th century, the embankment was built by the villagers of yen phu and quan thanh on both sides. they are said to have divided the west lake into two sides and created an isolated lake (for fishing). thanh nien street existed from 1957 to 1958, when it was formed by a narrow embankment. during the lifetime of president ho chi minh, the youth and students of hanoi made it into the wide street it is today, according to his suggestion.

incredible experience at sunwapta falls – a must-visit stop! sunwapta falls is a breathtaking natural wonder nestled along the scenic icefields parkway. as soon as we arrived, the thunderous sound of the cascading water welcomed us with pure energy. the main viewpoint is easily accessible, making it a perfect stop for travelers of all ages. the powerful rush of water over the rocks, surrounded by rugged cliffs and lush forest, creates a truly mesmerizing scene. there’s also a short hike to the lower falls, which offers quieter moments and fewer crowds – definitely worth it if you have extra time. that said, if i had to compare it to athabasca falls, i’d say athabasca slightly edges out as the best. while both falls are stunning, athabasca offers a more dramatic experience with its wider, more forceful flow and deeper canyon. the infrastructure at athabasca falls also makes it easier to explore from multiple angles with better viewpoints and photo opportunities. still, sunwapta falls stands strong as a serene and scenic gem. it’s less crowded, and the short trail adds a touch of adventure. if you’re driving the icefields parkway, don’t skip it – but if you have to pick just one, athabasca falls is the winner for raw power and scale!

incredible place: well taken care of, well maintained, and wonderful for the real esthetics. every single season we go there with the whole family and look at beautiful exhibits. in spring - lots of daffodils and snowdrops, hyacinths and tulips. during summer- beautiful roses and all sorts and kinds of flowers. during fall and winter - it's great just to walk around and see the beauty of lake ontario. landscape is beautiful, lots of spots to sit down. parking is little small and a little crowded, but overall, ok. recommend to anyone who loves nature and flowers. good for wedding photography as well. it's gem that no so many people know about. dogs are not allowed. there's no playground. this place is not for picnics.

incredible ride from manali to leh with zanskar kanishka expeditions 🏍️❄️🏔️ i had the most unforgettable experience riding from manali to leh ladakh with zanskar kanishka expeditions. our guide, sonam, was absolutely amazing — kind, professional, and made sure we felt safe and well taken care of the entire way. the landscapes were breathtaking, but what made the trip truly special was how sonam guided us through every twist and turn with patience and confidence. from scenic stops to bike checks, he was always one step ahead. this wasn’t just a tour — it was an adventure i’ll never forget. if you’re considering this journey, go for it. with sonam and zanskar kanishka expeditions, you’re in the best hands.

incredible snorkeling trip – worth every penny! what an unforgettable experience! the snorkeling trip to daymaniat island was absolutely amazing. the staff were friendly, professional, and made us feel completely safe and welcome from the start. the boat was clean and comfortable, and the snacks and drinks provided were a nice touch. the snorkeling gear was top quality, and the guides made sure everyone was set up properly. the water was crystal clear, and the marine life was stunning—beautiful corals, colorful fish, and a truly magical underwater world. everything was well-organized and relaxed. you can tell the team genuinely cares about delivering a great experience. 100% recommend—this trip is worth every single penny!

incredible spot with the eiffel tower views. jardins du trocadéro is one of the most beautiful places in paris if you want that perfect shot of the eiffel tower. the view from here is great, many photographers hang out here, professional ones, instagrammers, couples taking engagement pics, tourists with selfie stick and more, it’s a whole scene. but it doesn’t feel overly crowded because the space is big and open. there are these gorgeous fountains and statues all around, and when the water is on, it adds such a cool vibe to the view. at sunset, the lighting is unreal, and once the eiffel tower lights up, it’s straight-up magical. the whole area feels very relaxed, even with a lot of people around. it’s also a great place to just sit and chill. you can bring a snack, hang out on the steps, or just people-watch (which is always fun in paris). street performers sometimes show up, and there’s a nice energy to the place without being overwhelming. only thing to note: watch your stuff. but overall, it’s safe and totally worth your time. if you're in paris and want the classic eiffel tower view with a great vibe and plenty of photo ops, this is the spot. you’ll probably end up taking way more pictures than you planned. 😄

incredible stay! this property is beautiful! we stayed only one night here but would have loved at least one more. the thermal springs are beyond words. and if you stay at the resort you get access to more of the springs and you can get in 2 hours before the public in the morning. this was the most relaxing part of our trip in costa rica and i highly recommend it. the hotel rooms were very nice too and the free breakfast was also very good. we’re ready to go back!

incredible time with captain jason, cristen, ken, and yayu. we had a pretty small group that moved fast and ran into our first dolphins within a few minutes. we saw two species and dove 4 times with the dolphins before lunch and then snorkelling the reef. definitely plan for the bigger boat if you are not a strong smimmer and comfortable in the water. the crew was very knowledgeable and friendly and they created a really fun atmosphere and did a great job of keeping everyone pushing to see more. the experience is intense enough that not using a gopro and focusing on swiming and looking around was a must. buying the photo package at the end instead was the thing i'm most glad i did. my only regret was not bringing a dry bag with a few more snacks. the bus ride made getting to the harbor very easy, but driving and parking offers the chance to continue on to the north shore for sights and beaches afterwards. 10/10 will bring the rest of the family back next time.

incredible tour! tj & lewis were very well informed, shared fun facts and were amazing hosts. excellent instruction and in setting everyone up in their kayaks! i’ve been on a lot of tours all around and haven’t had such great service. very much an intro to kayaking tour - anyone can go out without any experience. the coffee and views were phenomenal and i would highly recommend the tour - specifically tj & lewis as they made it personable & special. 10/10

incredible value, world-class museum but bring a translation tool! the museo nacional de antropología is easily one of the best museums i’ve ever visited and the entry fee is shockingly cheap for what you get (~$5) the scale, the depth of information, and the sheer richness of the exhibits make this a must-visit in mexico city. from the stone of the sun to massive olmec heads and full-scale temple replicas, every hall is packed with artifacts that bring ancient civilizations to life. the building itself is a masterpiece, especially the central courtyard and its iconic waterfall pillar. important tips: - purchase tickets online or be there early in the morning. it gets really crowded during the day. - all exhibit information is in spanish, with almost no english signage. if you're not fluent, make sure to bring a guide or use an ai image translator app it makes a huge difference in understanding the context and significance of what you're seeing. a must-see for history lovers, especially those interested in mesoamerican culture.

incredible vr zombie experience – a must-try! we visited sandbox vr for a stag do in the afternoon after a heavy night out, and it was the perfect activity. none of us had tried vr before, so we weren’t sure what to expect but it blew us away! from start to finish, it was one of the best vr experiences we’ve ever had. i don’t want to spoil anything, but there was tons of movement, awesome sound effects, and some hidden surprises that kept us on our toes. not sure how long the session lasts, but for the price, it’s absolutely worth every penny. you even get three videos of your gameplay to watch afterward in the reception area. we did **deadwood phobia**, and it was epic, five stars all the way! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ highly recommended, and we’ll definitely be back—next time, i’m bringing the missus!

incredible! me and my family went there to have a nice jet ski experience. we were completely blown away by the level of compassion that the workers had for us and the sheer fun of the jet skis. we had booked 1 jet ski for 30 mins which costed €100, we think that this was quite a reasonable price. if you are not too happy with the price to experience will make up for it and 10 times more. the jet skis allowed you to go extremely fast, my son went a whopping 56 kilometres an hour. the instructors gave us the freedom to do what we like on the water once we had reached a certain point, while also setting a few boundaries in case anything turns south. there was also someone taking pictures of us. the pictures were phenomenal, for just €20 they had given us access to just over 300 fantastic photos. me and my family were more than happy with the whole experience and we highly recommend to anyone else.

incredible! this property is situated in an absolutely amazing place, filled with amazing people- in short, embodies the spirit of masai mara!! the sekenani gate of the reserve is just a 10 minute drive away. the views are so good, one can't get enough of it. the suites are tastefully curated, and they have made sure everything is in congruity with the surroundings. the colors chosen and the materials used are a testament to this. as the property is unfenced, many animals roam around freely. the rooms are oriented in such a way that every suite gets a view of the waterhole, where animals come to drink water white often. they offer many activities, enough to keep one engaged even if not going on a game drive. now the best part of the property- the people who run the show. led by the dynamic suzan, each and every single one of them makes sure we have a comfortable stay. you are always attended to, and they walk the extra mile to meet any additional demands/ requests. mr. mccarthy, the owner, makes sure he has a word with every guest assuring them of a good time. the food is good, with the chef more than willing to customise things as requested. we chose this property over tens of others after many days of deliberation and that was probably the best decision of the trip! this place heals, go for it without hesitation!!

incredible! we came for our honeymoon and we’re blown away by the beautiful and comfortable rooms, the service, the staff and of course the safari!! on our last night they surprised us with a private candlelit dinner (so many candles!!). godfrey and gomms lead our safari and we saw more than we could have dreamed of. their knowledge was unbelievable! every question had a detailed answer. such comfortable and impressive vehicles. exceptional tracking and because the safari is so exclusive, you are able to get right up close to the animals. even the cats were close enough for iphone photos. no need for big lenses. we saw leopard, cheetah twice, countless lions including tiny cubs, aardwolf and a pack of 22 wild dogs!! just to name a few. all of which were prolonged and intimate experiences. the pools available for a cool off in the middle of the day were pristine and perfect. the views from the camp beautiful. outdoor and indoor showers. privacy. comfortable and enormous beds. the food was great and plentiful. jackson in particular looked after us well, but all of the staff were delightful and friendly. we loved the river boat cruise, that was very special. also the fishing was a fun activity. the camp’s attention to detail, blankets for cold mornings, swept walkways, warm towel to wipe the dust off your face every time you arrive back at camp and always a beautiful clean car to climb into. splash clearly takes great pride in their hospitality and in their care for the environment. we were so impressed and could not recommend them more highly.

interesting building to visit, free entrance if you visit the palace, constructed in european style as the emperor at the time wanted to impress the west. it features free tours at fixed hours and you need to register for them at the reception before the start of the tour, as ling as there are places available. the museum is closed on mondays and you can get your entry included in the palace pass as well. take note! you are not allowed to visit the museum on your own, only through booking a tour. tours are also available in english and, in order to visit, you are required to take off your shoes and get some slippers from the entrance. that was a bit unpleasant, as the slippers are not single-use or washed between visitors, so the slippers were very smelly and because of them my socks smelled like feet sweat (which, then, i had to put in my sports shoes to leave - giving my shoes the smell as well) - so, ultimately, i had to wash my shoes when i got home because they stank due to the slippers at the museum. not sure if you cab bring your own slippers, but i would have tried if i knew of this before.

interesting buildings, changing of the guards was neat to see, there's a canon fired off at noon, and some neat exhibits, you do need a guide and can't explore by yourself as it's still an active base. our guide was very good but the tour itself is a bit short as there's several going on at the same time, more time to explore would have been nice.

interesting buildings, changing of the guards was neat to see, there's a canon fired off at noon, and some neat exhibits, you do need a guide and can't explore by yourself as it's still an active base. our guide was very good but the tour itself is a bit short as there's several going on at the same time, more time to explore would have been nice.

interesting bustling market that isn’t a tourist trap. the locals love this place too. tons of variety here, you can buy fresh fruit and veggies, fresh seafood, italian food, german food, french food, etc. we also saw cafes, butcher shops, grocery shops, spice shops, ice cream shops, bakeries, jewelry stands, flower shops and this cool shop that only sold pickles and pickle socks! very reasonable prices too, we bought a pepperoni stick from one stall and it was only $1.25! perfect snack to munch on while walking around the market. they have a central food court that’s filled with unique places to eat (didn’t see a lot of chain restaurants) and lots of seating to sit down and enjoy your meal. some notable places included a stall that sold soup/broth, another that sold montreal smoked meat + fresh bagels, and one that sold pot pies (this one was super popular)! worth a visit!

interesting but ultimately a chalet / glamping / airbnb style stay, best for groups having an event. it is not a hotel or luxury accommodation (despite what google and certain online review articles would have you think). excellent location, nice environment and patio. surprisingly spacious apartment but clear signs of wear and tear / age. a cupboard was falling off its hinges when we checked in and handyman came to fix it during our stay. floor on first level strangely sticky and had stains. kettle was dirty on check in, although staff rectified this when it was pointed out. staff kindly gave us apartment tour and took time to guide us on use of stuff like hob and automatic curtains. can probably cook, but mini-fridge had strange smell. for some reason, free coffee / tea was stored under the sink (where the pipes were). main bed was excellent, floor to ceiling windows and swaying bamboo outside - pleasant views . bathroom serviceable, shower pressure good but plumbing not great - toilet occasionally had sewage smell. amenities basic and not the "luxurious selection of room supplies" on the official gardens by the bay website. had to manually request room slippers, toothbrushes etc - apparently there was supposed to be an email to sent to guests to request these things beforehand but we never received the email (to give benefit of doubt, this may or may not be because we booked through agoda). also note that (although this is fairly understandable given the garden location) there will be some insects. worthwhile for a gathering or function but if a hotel experience is what you want this is absolutely not it.

interesting historical building housing the story, and in fact the location, of the inquisition in cartegena as well as of the original indigenous inhabitants. exhibits are spread over two floors and it was easy to while away a couple of hours there. one improvement might be to add some explanations in english as most everything is only in spanish so if you don't speak spanish the historical explanations won't be helpful. guides may be available, but i didn't see any when i visited. entry was 25k cop with a 4k discount for seniors.

interesting little exhibition telling the story of early iceland through an audio visual experience. audio guides provided in english. . about 20 story boarded scenarios take you from the first discovery of iceland through to the reformation. there is also a chance to dress up at the end.

iolani palace is a beautiful and special place to visit in honolulu. it’s full of history and has a peaceful atmosphere. i didn’t know much about hawaiian royalty before, but the tour taught me a lot. it’s the only royal palace in the united states, which makes it quite unique. the building is stunning, both outside and inside. the rooms are well kept, and you can see where the kings and queens of hawaii once lived. everything is very elegant. from the wooden staircase to the royal dining room. you can really feel the history when you walk through the palace. i took the audio tour, which was very helpful and easy to follow. it made the experience more meaningful and helped me understand hawaiian culture better. the staff were also friendly and helpful. they gave clear directions and made sure everything ran smoothly.

isla blanca is truly a hidden gem among the beaches near cancun. tucked away from the hustle and bustle, it offers a serene escape for those in the know. what sets isla blanca apart is its untouched beauty. located far from the main tourist spots, it retains a sense of pristine tranquility. even when it does get crowded, especially on certain days, an early morning visit guarantees a secluded paradise. picture-perfect sunrises, tranquil waters, and empty shores make for an unforgettable experience. whether you're seeking solitude or simply want to enjoy a leisurely stroll with your furry friend, isla blanca delivers. it's a destination where every moment feels like a privilege, and one you won't soon forget. in conclusion, if you have the opportunity to visit isla blanca, seize it without hesitation. it's a beach that epitomizes the essence of unspoiled beauty, leaving visitors with memories to cherish forever.

it's an hours drive into sian kaan, was a little bumpy, but nothing compared to some of the cenote we had visited brain rattling roads to some! lunch is included on punta alan (beautiful fishing island). the boat held six plus captain and guide. they provided water and snacks as most tour's do and lunch was decent and you do work up an appetite but things did run out after we had seconds so fill up first time round and only hibiscus water is included so bring a little cash for tips and beers it was a brilliant experience i would recommend for all the family. a few things it's hot, and you're not always shaded. i sat in front, and my wife sat behind me for better shade. you are over water it gets really windy and loud. the boat ride can get a little bumpy when at full speed to travel across the vast waters, its safe and fairly smooth depending on the wind and chop. no cushions so my butt bones and more got a little sore. i had to sit on a life jacket to dampen it, but if your sat at thr back be fine. over the tour, we had seen many animals and birds it is not always guaranteed, but wow, were we lucky. two big crocodiles, dolphins with a baby now that was magical as we slowlycruisd along watching them hunt the baby was a highlight, pelicans, ducks, herons, frigate birds, birds of prey.. birds i can't tell. we did see a large loggerhead turtle, but only for the brief moments when it was close to the waters surface and taking breaths, not a great view! towards the end we stopped to snorkel in deeper water on the world's "second largest coral reef", that was ok most the people enjoyed it but i worked in egypt on a dive boat so most peoppe enjoyed it but for me was a little bland not so many colourful fish etc may have been the visibility was choppy as well at that time i was mostly helping my wife enjoy it. we also stopped in shoulder deep water for a swim, and that was just fantastic as the water here was crystal clear and super clam real instagram pic moment. then we stopped for a late lunch at the beautiful island. great for photos. then headed straight back to the beginning, which is a long and bumpy ride! i also used a spare life jacked to put my bag on so not to get wet instead of holding it or leaving it on the damp floor. on the way back we stopped by a big hammerhead shark i was told it was a real rarity and even the captains were taking selfies. if you have a gropro on a extendable stick your in for a real treat apply a strong sunscreen before you get on the boat and after you arrive for lunch from swimming. there are toilets and showers if they have enough water. only towels and change of shorts we took you will dry off fast. a powerbank, gopro, well fitted hat, and sunglasses as it gets windy, a rash guard top is ideal, but my wife had a light scarf over her shoulders when on the boat i also had my professional camera. the tour guide let me sit up front on the boat actually allowed me a few liberties, but i am experienced and they may be stricter on your tour for safety! it's a bit hard to find information about this place in english, so here's what to expect: 1) the entrance to this trail is located near -3.84874 -32.42087. when coming from the airport side, it is located on the left side shortly behind a restaurant. 2) the total time of this trail is about 15 to 30 minutes each way, depending on where and how fast you go. 3) in every case you will follow a jungle trail. as we were here in a dry period, most parts were really easy. 4) in every case the trail up to piquinho includes some rock scrambling, up to the top even climbing with a rope. climbing gear is not necessary, but should give a nice experience as well, as seen in one of the photos uploaded to this place. 5) there are two different places with a nice view. the first one is much more easy to reach. just follow the path until you reach a rock "tunnel" to the left. after the tunnel there are two rocks offering a nice view. i would still rate this part as moderate. not because it's so exhausting, but you don't want to fall down at the rock part. if you want to enjoy the best view, follow the rocks further uphill. this is real rock scrambling now, with some difficult parts at the beginning. you can see it on the picture. when almost at the top there are nice views to "two sisters" and the airport area. you won't see this from the first point. for the last part there is a rope which you will need to get up and down. i stopped here, but saw several guys going up the last 20 meters. 360° view from the top must be nice, but you can still obtain a nice view when not doing it. 6) make sure to get down before it gets dark. you don't want to be up on the rocks without seeing where to step. overall a really nice trail for about 2 hours total time. you don't even need a national park access card and we've seen 3 other groups doing the trail. sunset appears to be the preferred time, but - as said - make sure to get down in time. also make sure to wear long pants for the path through the jungle - the plants are stinging on your skin.

it's best to come to the observatory at night! things you should know: i. parking ordering a grab to get here is relatively easy. i recommend that as your form of arrival and departure so you don't need to worry about parking. parking has ample spaces available, but i would consider the fee expensive. ii. service you can buy your tickets online in advance. as for food? i know of a mcdonalds on the grounds ~ aside from that... if you want healthy food. i would eat beforehand. iii. recommendations everything about the gardens is beautiful and well maintained . if i had to recommend what you viewed ~ i would tell you to get tickets for the cloud forest and the supertree grove observatory. ideally, you'll want to start at the cloud forest, during daylight hours (17:00-17:30) and then make your way to the supertree observatory at night. the skyline is most beautifully seen when the sun is down! iii. capacity avoid holidays here! it gets quite crowded. however, if unavailable, it's still worth seeing.

ivan was an awesome skipper! we had a great day on the water with him. he drives, docks, and anchors the boat with expertise. he took us to some great locations, including beaches, places to eat, caves, and beaches. i highly recommend rewind croatia and especially ivan!

ivan was the best time a family could ask for! he took us to the most amazing spots of dubrovnik and knew exactly what he was doing. we stopped for a local wine tasting at green captain and it blew my family and i out of the water. ivan also recommended an amazing spot for us to eat lunch which was also a 10/10. everything was perfect thanks to ivan.
