i’d call this a modern centre of life for prague locals. i love the summer evenings here when the sun heats up the stones and those then radiate long into the night keeping the nights here even warmer. the place is lively with all kinds of bars on the boats. aside from the boats, no places to sit in the past few years, but this might change this season with the newly fitted spaces in the embankment wall.

i’d describe it as a unique experience. i give it mixed reviews and let me explain below: the good: you’re boarding a historic steamboat. the narration given by the captain is quite informative and generous. the boat has different seating areas so you can enjoy the views, or immerse into the “guts” of the ship by stopping by the engine room. it is fascinating. inside we got live music from a trio which was delightful and put heart and soul playing dixie music and other hits. our waitress was so polite and on top of making sure we were fed. the ice tea was great. i want to make sure i share that! the bad: the hosts and check in staff could learn to be nicer. they act disengaged and that draws down from the whole experience. although i know the ship is old, it does not feel well maintained. you step in and instead of a charming dining room, you get this 1970’s feel, with basic tables and not so comfy chairs. the ac feels inadequate, with spots cooling nicely while other spots are muggy. the store is simply “sad” and dead. it’s needs to be revitalized. the food is not very good, i’m sorry. the fish was dry and the only thing i enjoyed was the jambalaya and potato salad. i could tell the rest of the people were not impressed by the food by the look on their faces. you know… overall we enjoyed it because the experience is so different and unique, not both staff and interior design could be rejuvenated.

i’d highly recommend this place for a peacecul stay in mountains of nubra valley. this is also a safer place for your vacations. this place is must try. food is also decent. you’d feel good in the camp, it was a pleasant experience.

i’d like to appreciate not only the marvelous architecture—but let’s not forget the lighting engineers as well! 🤯 i was lucky enough to see her in all her glory during the day, but under the stars… oh, does she sing and shine so bright! truly a spectacular display and an absolute must-see.

i’d like to share our recent experience in west yellowstone, particularly regarding e-bike access on this trail. unfortunately, what started as an exciting opportunity to explore your beautiful area turned into a disappointing and even hostile experience. despite being told by some locals that the signs restricting e-bikes could be ignored, we were met with open hostility while riding the trail—including being yelled at by residents and warned by forest rangers. the message was clear: e-bike riders are not welcome here. it was an incredibly uninviting experience, especially considering that the community has invested around $300,000 in new infrastructure and educational signage along the trail. this exclusionary attitude doesn’t just hurt feelings it undermines the spirit of tourism and accessibility that many communities strive for. we ride e-bikes not for convenience, but because of age-related limitations. others use them due to disabilities or physical challenges. since our visit, we've spoken with several other travelers who reported similar encounters. it's clear this isn't an isolated incident. we understand there are concerns about the environmental impact of e-bikes. but if the trail runs alongside an off-road vehicle route with noisy, dusty, gas-powered traffic traveling at 35 mph it’s difficult to believe that e-bikes present a more serious disruption to wildlife. additionally, the argument that e-bikes are "too fast" doesn’t hold up: we were regularly passed by traditional cyclists, especially downhill, while our own average speed was a modest 8 mph. speed and impact are more about rider behavior than the type of bike. it’s important to recognize what’s being lost here. e-bike riders are being denied access to a trail rich in educational and recreational value—something that should be enjoyed by all visitors, not just a select group. consider the following facts from boltbikes.com: u.s. e-bike sales rose 240% from 2019 to 2021. e-bike sales are projected to hit 6.4 million units per year by 2025. 96.4% of riders say they enjoy e-bikes more than traditional bikes. 75% say they prefer e-biking over driving. e-bikes are not a passing trend—they are part of the future of accessible, sustainable travel. yellowstone national park has no such bike restrictions. west yellowstone risks developing a reputation as unfriendly or even hostile to visitors who choose (or need) to ride e-bikes. this policy does not reflect the inclusive, welcoming spirit that we believe this community wants to project. a few exclusionary voices are now shaping an image of the town that discourages return visits and word-of-mouth promotion. we urge you to reconsider this regulation. with thoughtful, inclusive planning, west yellowstone could become a leader in accessible outdoor recreation not a cautionary tale of division and lost opportunity.

i’d say 3.5 stars. great variety of items, especially mondepice spices & teas. nice selection of food vendors too. watch out for the prices.. a lot of vendors do not show or list their prices so when you go to pay for your $25 arepas (we got two so it was $50) you’re slapped with an overpriced side of couscous and a side of tabbouleh for $16 each. some of the tents have prices listed on signs but are crossed out. some transparency would be nice.

i’d say it’s in between moderate and difficult. better keep your hands free since it requires climbing for some part of the trail. the view is amazing and less crowded than deep cove. highly recommended for everyone. make sure you are following the orange mark to reach the top.

i’d wanted to visit this place ever since watching memoirs of a geisha, and it did not disappoint. it’s a beautifully peaceful spot—though the crowds of tourists can make it feel less so. walking along the winding paths is enchanting, but it can get a little frustrating when people constantly stop to take photos. still, the experience is well worth it. for a more serene visit, aim to arrive around 6:30 am, when the atmosphere is truly tranquil.

i’ll start by saying that our tour guide miguel (mike) was amazing, always friendly and respectful towards us! at the entrance the they tried to sell us a hold package and made us a deal for the gold vip package (don’t let yourself get into the trap) as well as many other thing such as mask and glasses for the atv drive. (it is not ethical to sell it as a “safety issue”, if you won’t provide them for free). nevertheless the experience let me a bit down. when i booked it (via get your guide) i thought the whole experience was based on the atv driving which i was really looking forward to and at the end a dip in the cenote with zip line. all i got from the atv was a circuit of 400/500m ish repeated 3 times for a total of 20-25 min. it was surly fun the first time but then it got a bit repetitive. the zip lines weren’t too bad but not as adrenalinic as they sold it and was composed by three very shorts rides (not very high either). the cenote tho was really worth the guide, beautiful water two spots to jump from, the first spot was 8.2m high and the second was 10m high included a zip line where you could hang and jump. last but not least the tequila tasting was outstanding. the lady explaining was really fun and acknowledged. to conclude the experience i got two free tacos and made me wait 40-50 min for our bus back insisting to sell the photo they took and the expensive drink the restaurant offer

i’ll use the pile gate — the main entrance to dubrovnik’s old town — as the starting point to share my two-day experience here. first tip: consider going to lokrum island, its private and you will definetely love it, second -> definitely get the full-day pass, it’s totally worth it. it covers bus rides, entry to the city walls (best visited early morning after 8, or in the evening for a magical sunset), the impressive lovrijenac fort with its panoramic views of the old and new town, lokrum island, and the surrounding bays, plus access to all the museums and galleries inside the walls. spending a full day exploring the old town gives you a fascinating glimpse into dubrovnik’s history, from its role in trade and sailing to its influence on the old economy and intelligence networks. a rich and rewarding experience not to miss.

i’m a big fan of open air museums and most nordic countries have one. i took public transportation 45 minutes to get to the museum and it was totally worth it! i learned so much about iceland and the people dressed in character are absolutely wonderful! there’s something for everyone here and i saw lots of families.

i’m a christian and a priest-in-training, and this just wasn’t for me in terms of finding a connection with jesus or feeling close to god. i can appreciate the craftsmanship of the building, and the significance of the site, but for so many reasons i felt sad and anguished in this place. worth a visit, but leaves you with much to reflect on. there were many other places on pilgrimage that left me breathless. the holy sepulchre was unfortunately not one of them.

i’m a cmas beginner diver and did 4 dives (2days) with them. the experience was amazing to say the least. the staff is kind, welcoming and always helps you with everything. i always felt safe and taken care of. on top of that it was also cheaper than other options i saw around. i would totally come back when i’ll visit seychelles again

i’m a pretty “beginner” hiker and had no problems with the trail. super great to start early am to have cooler air. the trail is mostly shaded. one thing to note is that some of the trail is not marked the best, but follow the foot tracks in the sand and also google maps is still accessible on the hike and is super accurate to where the trail is, just to make sure you’re on the right path. the “hardest” part is the last 10ish minutes of the hike if you’re just heading to the cave and back. it gets steep but its staircase style rocks. from the shuttle dropping us off, to see the seven pools & the cave, and back, took 2 hours. coming back is much much quicker than heading out there. there’s also a great step by step guide of the trail with photos on the earthtrekkers website. parking is free and so is the shuttle!

i’m a school bus driver and i made an unplanned visit here while i was waiting for a charter group to finish their trip. i’ve passed this house before but have never had a chance to stop and look around the grounds or go inside. the grounds are great, especially being at university and queen! they have pieces in the garden that were found underground, with information about the pieces and the home posted on signs along the inside of the fence. i was able to sit on a stone bench in the garden for a while before heading inside for a tour. there was a $10 admission fee, and by the end of my tour i felt like i severely underpaid! i was on my own, and nobody else was there for a tour while i was there. i was greeted by diane who took my admission fee and immediately started to tell me about the house. diane is an absolute gem! extremely knowledgeable (and captivating!) about the house, the campbell family, the businesses that occupied the house in the years following the deaths of sir/lady campbell, the background of william and hannah, their children and descendants, how the house was saved, how it was furnished—even educated me on the pieces furnishing the house! my only disappointment is that i had to get back to my shift and couldn’t spent the entire afternoon with diane at the house. the experience was one i won’t forget, and i’ve been telling everyone i talk to about it all evening. i’ll likely be researching more of the family/house’s history for months, i feel like i learned so much yet there is still so much to discover. if you love history and/or old homes (this one is 200+ years old!) you’ll love this place. and while i’m sure everyone there is knowledgeable, i hope you meet diane and soak up everything she has to say! i’d love to return on a day when i don’t have time restrictions. note: i only snapped a couple of photos outside, didn’t take any inside because i was enjoying the tour!

i’m always grateful to the owner of the saatchi gallery for offering free exhibitions. there are times when you do need to buy tickets for certain sections, though. since i live nearby, i often stop by and the artworks always lift my mood. if you’re visiting chelsea as part of your trip, i highly recommend popping in – and do have a look around the shop for souvenirs. most galleries have items you can only find there. there’s also a large bench under a big tree by the entrance – a perfect spot to sit and rest for a bit. oh, and don’t expect much in terms of service from the staff at the entrance or in the shop. they’re not particularly friendly, and unless you’re actually buying something, they tend to ignore guests and just chat amongst themselves.

i’m amazed with the amount of history that was collected and preserved throughout the years. you can see a lot of dedication, time and detail spent on the pottery, artwork and crafts. if you are history enthusiast i’d recommend a half a day, to truly enjoy and learn. perfect for an indoor activity.

i’m currently on a road trip from cape tribulation to melbourne and had the chance to enjoy three unforgettable snorkeling experiences: here with ocean safari, in the whitsundays with ocean rafting, and at lady musgrave with lady musgrave experience. all three were exceptional… but the one with ocean safari will forever remain the most beautiful day of my life. it was my very first snorkeling trip of this journey, and if i had known it would be the most magical experience of them all, i would have stayed right here in this little paradise and never left. a huge thank you to the team for their warm welcome, energy, and professionalism. and thank you to this magical place for giving me a memory i’ll cherish forever. 🌊🐠💙

i’m delighted and feel lucky enough to visit grand canyon. i had a great view of canyon, ridges and other wonderful places. it was a clear day with less crowded during my visit which made it more enjoyable. i enjoyed every single moment of my stay and cherished with once in a lifetime experience which i got from this visit.

i’m delighted to share my great experience last week at wat chalong temple,phuket. it was one of the stops in our city tour of phuket. wat chalong is a beautiful and peaceful place.it’s a magnificent historical artifact of 19th century. inside the walls and ceilings are decorated with beautiful paintings illustrating the life of buddha,as well as many donated golden statues.the temple’s calm and peaceful ambience is a perfect place to relax and learn about thai culture. i loved the people and culture here. phuket’s masses are friendly and welcoming! if you are in phuket, don’t forget to add wat chalong to your list!🙏🙏

i’m extremely disappointed, frustrated and angry regarding the turn of events today. we booked for the private catamaran, paid the mandatory 50% deposit to secure the booking and confirmed the booking only to find that we had been double booked and were told “sorry, we can’t help you.” had we known upfront that christelle and zile cruise was fully booked, it would have given us time to make another plan but unfortunately it’s our last day in mauritius. when trying to express our frustration over this, she proceeded to say “i don’t speak english” as if that should explain away the lack of organization and customer service. there was no accountability taken for her actions, instead blaming it on a mystery assistant when it was clear that she was the one spoken to. i would not recommend her services to anyone and do not plan on booking with her in the future.

i’m genuinely disappointed with the parking situation at this mall. i misplaced my parking ticket, it had simply slipped under my car seat and was difficult to find. despite the fact that i was well under the 2-hour free parking limit, i was told i’d have to pay a charge for loosing the paper. i tried to call the security number displayed in the parking area six times, not a single call was answered. in a city like dubai, and in 2025, i find it ridiculous that the system still relies on paper parking tickets. it’s an outdated and frustrating process, especially when losing something so insignificant results in such a steep charge. what made it worse was the attitude of the head of security. instead of being helpful or understanding, he spoke to me in a condescending tone, which only added to my frustration. i hope the mall management seriously reconsiders both their systems and their customer service approach.

i’m not a foodie, but i decided to visit mangwon market anyway—and i’m glad i did! the market was insanely crowded, yet remarkably clean. there were tons of food options and snacks, all at affordable prices, with everything looking absolutely delicious. my family had a fantastic time exploring the market, queuing for popular stalls, and trying out different local specialties. beyond the food, the market also had fresh and reasonably priced fruits, making it a great spot for both snacks and groceries. overall, an awesome experience—definitely worth a visit!

i’m not much of a museum goer or art aficionado; however, this museum and bukovac’s life and works really moved me. the size/location of the museum, all the painted walls, paintings, furniture etc. allowed one to leisurely enjoy the nice temperature in the home, every cozy/handmade detail and almost feel his spirit living on. surprisingly good. worth taking a look.

i’m so excited that the market has finally opened! it is much needed in the community. they have fresh produce, great lemonade & a variety of other products. the family that runs this market are some amazing, hardworking people who really loves what they do by providing resources to the community. please go out and support & spread the word!

i’m so glad i found this tour operator in el nido! their larger boat makes a huge difference, it offers plenty of space to move around, relax, and even sunbathe, making the experience much more comfortable than traditional boats. sometimes, they even play music on board, which adds to the great atmosphere. i did tour c with them, and it was absolutely amazing! the crew was incredibly friendly, full of energy, and always attentive to our needs. despite the big waves and strong currents, they went above and beyond to ensure we reached secret beach safely. a big shoutout to the guys for their effort and dedication, it truly made a difference. many thanks once again! the captain was outstanding—his skills in maneuvering the boat through challenging conditions were truly impressive. thanks to him, we always felt safe and relaxed, even in rough waters. they are very good photographers as well, they took us very nice photos. i also did tour a with this company, and it was another great experience. everything was well-organized, and the service was excellent. i highly recommend this company to anyone looking for an unforgettable island-hopping experience in el nido!

i’m so glad my wife and i ran into gayan when we got lost on the way up ella rock. besides taking care of us and helping us fight off leeches he was an absolute joy to hang out with. i have to thank him for the wonderful photos he captured and all of the botanical knowledge he shared. my only regret was that we didn’t have enough time after the hike to join him for rice and curry. i hope to make it back to ella to visit my new friend!

i’m so glad we found this place. what a great way to start our saturday. every part of the experience was perfect. booking, ambiance, staff, all top notch! my wife and i enjoyed a couples massage and we highly recommend it to anyone needing a relaxing but therapeutic massage.

i’m so sad i don’t live near by to be serviced by the lovely ladies at oasi! i came in after a long flight with my nails in the worst state, but i left beautiful nails and a relaxing vibe. i received a dry mani and pedi with builder gel. it’s very clean inside of this spa.

i’m super glad we accidentally stumbled across this free museum and decided to check it out! our tour guide was very knowledgeable and friendly and it was great being able to learn a bit more history about the city and what life was like in the 1800s. i highly recommend dropping by if you’re already at high park.

i’ve always had my doubts wether or not i’ll be comfortable being under water and get into the amazing world of diving. on my trip to galapagos, i was recommended to meet jesse and his team from apnea galapagos and see if i could be convinced into give it a shot. the moment i sat down with jesse and his crew, i sensed the professionalism and how knowledgeable he is which calmed my nerves a lot. he took his time to outline the course and all steps necessary to become a padi certified open water diver. i think it is very important to have a good instructor to build a good foundation early on, someone that’s calm and can have that effect on you underwater incase you panic or can’t remember what you should do next in a situation. jesse and his team did an outstanding job in all aspects, they met with me at my hotel a few times to go over the theory i had completed and also debriefing our dives that day and briefing our final dives and what to expect. i’m very happy that i made the decision to choose apnea galapagos for this amazing experience and obtaining my certificate. if you’re looking for a professional dive shop who has the knowledge and the experience, and not taking dangerous shortcuts, then i highly recommend jesse and his team. thank you for all you did and i’m looking forward to come back for my advance diver course soon.

i’ve always seen this food truck before and after transiting burrard station. i got the chicken saj which was tasty, garlicky, and not too heavy! definitely going to try the beef next time. highly recommend if you’re looking for something quick!

i’ve always wanted my first madame tussauds experience to be the one in london and i’m glad that finally came true. this was a great experience. seeing how life like the wax figures were, getting the red carpet experience and going through all these different world/portals. i didn’t know what to expect and i’m glad it went beyond any expectations i could’ve had. first, it’s best to book your ticket online, come early/ get the fast track ticket so you don’t have to be in line because there is always a huge rush. second, i enjoyed the fact that i got more than the value of my buck. this experience lasted about 2hours for me and that’s me not going through everything i wanted to since i was limited with time because i had to get to the airport. i like that it’s very interactive, from the scents, to the special effects. i highly recommend using public transportation as well to get here. london’s public transportation was very easy to maneuver and reliable

i’ve always wanted to have this experience but i wanted to find an ethical sanctuary and i don’t regret it at all to have picked this place. we got the morning feeding and bathing and i really saw how the elephants are happy, well treated and respected there. we feed them with bananas and we also prepared a bowl of rice and fruits to give to them. only 3 elephants wanted to bath and i really appreciated the fact that they are not forced to do anything that they don’t wanna do. all the staff were very friendly, the guide told us a lot about the elephants and we also got a photographer taking photos of everyone to be sent by our email. i highly recommend this sanctuary and i would go back many times :)

i’ve always wanted to know what this was because when i was in marrakech in february i was confused, but now i know. it’s one of the most beautiful things in marrakech for being the pink city, i love the history and authentic structure of moroccan buildings. these not too much to see but i think that i saw plenty without realizing it. these things you can see for free.

i’ve been coming to farm tomita in every season—spring, summer, autumn, and winter—and it never disappoints! the scenery is always beautiful, with lovely trees and flowers that change throughout the year. it’s a perfect place to bring friends, enjoy the atmosphere, and try some tasty food. each season also has its own fresh, seasonal vegetables, which are always a treat. definitely worth a visit anytime of the year!

i’ve been diving for years, and always diving is hands down one of the best dive shops i’ve ever worked with. they offer great prices and first-class customer service from start to finish. alvaro was incredibly responsive during the booking process and helped me set up an amazing dive package with both cenotes, ocean dive and whale shark snorkel. every part of the experience was top-notch. the captain was great, and diving with alvaro was a true pleasure. after comparing several shops in the area, i’m so glad i went with this one. do yourself a favor and book with always diving!

i’ve been here a few times and i think it’s a great place for children of all ages and adults. my favorite part of the museum is the aquarium. it’s so relaxing just watching the fish, sharks and string rays swim by. the other animals such as the birds, jellyfishes and seahorses were also amazing to see. i do think that some of the things should be improved, such as the wet lab and the planetarium shows. they’re not really entertaining for children. the interactive activity where you see the shark’s point of view was also broken during my visit. this time around, the smurf’s characters were present promoting their new movie. at first, i did not see the correlation between the smurf and physics lesson provided but the children enjoyed the dance party afterwards. although, i must say that the staff providing the physics lesson was very knowledgeable and entertaining. they also provided smurfs coloring pages, puzzles, crayons and temporary tattoos for the children to enjoy. as for the food, it is a bit overpriced but it was quite decent. i would definitely eat there again. i will also continue to come back to this museum as it’s fun and they keep changing some of the exhibits so there is always something new to see.

i’ve been living in thailand for five years, and chowpathi is one of the indian restaurants i always recommend. i make it a point to visit whenever i get the chance. the service is consistently excellent, and the staff are very knowledgeable about the food — they’re always ready to help with recommendations or adjustments. the menu offers a wide variety of both south and north indian dishes, as well as thai options. since indian food tends to be spicy, you can ask the staff to adjust the spice level to suit your taste. as someone from south india, i especially enjoy their dosa and idli. they also offer other favorites like pani puri, biryani, and thali meals. the menu is well-balanced, making it a great choice whether you’re craving street-style snacks or a hearty traditional meal. overall, chowpathi truly brings the taste of india to thailand, and i highly recommend it.

i’ve been on 3 tours with cameron in the last 2 weeks and have thoroughly enjoyed each one. if you’re looking to learn more about cape town and its surrounding areas, cameron’s tours give you a vision of how it used to be. his unique way of adding real quotes from old and well used books are a delight. he makes you see the area from a different perspective and his knowledge is astonishing! we’ve done his castle of good hope, woodstock and “obs” so far and are hoping to pick up another one before we return to england. i highly recommend them - a big thumbs up 👍

i’ve been on many different tours on the galapagos islands and have met quite a few guides, but there is one thing i am sure of: yazmany is by far the best guide to accompany you on your galapagos adventure! he is the owner of guiding galapagos expeditions. i absolutely loved all the snorkling trips and hikes we did together. i saw so many incredible animals: flamingo’s, sharks, turtles, marine iguanas, and so many different species of birds and other animals. yazmany is genuinely enthusiastic about everything the galapagos has to offer. he’s extremely knowledgeable about the islands and he is very passionate to share that with his guests. you can ask him anything, whether it is about the islands, evolution or wildlife. it is also clear that he is very respectful towards nature and all the animals we encounter. another highlight for me is that he takes the best pictures of all the guests throughout the trip, which is for me a great memory from my holiday. in terms or organization: yazmany always explained the plan for the day before we head on our trip, which made the trip smooth and structured for everyone. at the same time, he is always flexible and open to changes in the itinerary if this means a better experience for the guests. even after our tour ended, he helped me plan my further travels and gave great recommendations on where to go and what to do on the other islands, super helpful! he will truly make sure you have an unforgettable galápagos experience. the galapagos islands are a must visit for all nature lovers, and there is no better person to explore them with than yazmany. thank you again for this awesome adventure! when i return to the galapagos, i’ll definitely be booking all my tours with him and his company. highly recommended!

i’ve been on many many cruises. last week i was on an 8 day cruise aboard the norwegian epic. i can honestly say that it was the worst cruise i had ever taken. way too many people for the small common areas on the boat. the staff and customer service was absolutely horrid. the state of the ship was awful. soft spots in the floors, missing carpet, ran down chairs and even the cabin was ran down. i feel as if i paid full price for a half assed cruise. noodle bar was a total let down. followed suite with the rest of the cruise.

i’ve been on this cruise 4 times. i always take the group i’m with on the dinner cruise. the food was delicious!! unfortunately, they must have been shorthanded. the service was very slow. we had to ask for our drinks 3 times. it was also very hot. i don’t think that was totally in their control. it was unusually warm in paris for that time of year c i would go again. i have a good track record with them. however, this was not the best experience.
i’ve been there in dec 2016 was totally surprised to see such a nature and fascinating landscape

i’ve been to a few spice farms in zanzibar and have to say this is one of my favorites! extremely knowledgeable and kind staff that took the time to make this such an amazing experience! taking home some amazing spices now and already have made delicious tea with the fresh cardamom i picked up

i’ve been to brobike a few times now and every single time i’ve been helped in the kindest and most professional way. the staff take their time to explain everything clearly and with a lot of knowledge, they’re always incredibly friendly and helpful. you really feel well taken care of here. the value for money is excellent! i’m always happy to come back :)

i’ve been to prince edward theatre twice — once for the great gatsby and again for the michael jackson musical, and both experiences were absolutely amazing! from the very first show, i knew i had to come back — and i’m so glad i did. the atmosphere is welcoming and elegant, and the staff were all wonderful and helpful. i sat in the dress circle, which has a great view, and there’s a bar where you can relax before the show. there’s even a balcony above the bar, which adds to the charm of the place. everything was well-organized, but make sure to arrive early so you can be seated on time. the shows themselves were incredible, and the whole experience was unforgettable. i’m already looking forward to my next visit!

i’ve been wanting to visit this museum for years now and i finally got to see it. i bought 4 tickets for my family and i and it was 20 egp, i gave the guy 100 egp and i waited for my change and he said “are you going to take pictures” i said “yes” he said then that would cost another 20 egp which i don’t mind but i didn’t know or read any where that it cost money to take pictures, however i paid him and walked away. there was a museum tour guy he took us and told us where to go and gave us a few history notes of the things we were looking at, we thought he was really good at his job, after we left he followed my mother and asked for tip as he was expecting us to pay him for what he did which we had no idea about because where we come from tour guys come with the museum as that’s their position and job. my sweet mother apologized and tipped him and we left.

i’ve been working with them for a while now, and they’ve been amazing with my aquarium. my fish and corals have never looked better. it’s clear they’re passionate about what they do—everything is done with care and attention to detail. they’ve helped me build a balanced tank. i trust them completely with the health of my reef and wouldn’t go anywhere else!

i’ve chartered multiple boats/tours through botegena now and would not look elsewhere. the captains and guides are always very accommodating - my group typically leaves it up to them to show us their favorite spots rather than doing the touristy stuff and it’s a blast every time! 10 out of 5 stars!

i’ve crossed the burrard street bridge into downtown by foot a few times, and i love the walk across, especially on a sunny day. the pedestrian paths are more than wide enough to accommodate foot traffic to comfortably go both directions, and the views are stunning even when viewed through the grated —i always pause along the way to enjoy the surrounding cityscapes, false creek, and english bay as a reminder to not take any of it for granted. i’m so happy they city installed protected the bicycle paths in 2009, and have remained in place; i’d love to ride across one day.

i’ve done this 3 times in one month. its such a relaxing 6-7 hours of hiking. amazing cliff views, tranquil scenery and just as fun to do this alone or with friends. just don’t miss the last ferry or you will be stuck.. ubers keep cancelling when they choose drivers from cronulla.. there are several km of no phone reception and difficult track, so carry a plb if you need to.

i’ve had an amazing experience! roso is the best tour guide! he explained everything clearly, and made sure me my friend had an amazing experience. i will be returning for sure! please don’t hesitate to book with them!

i’ve had the best filter coffee ever here, from süssmund (borbonera if i recall correctly). hands down the fruitiest coffee i’ve ever had. special v60 menu (truly specialty coffee place), bean bags on sale, beautiful coffee accessories. must visit if you’re around the neighbourhood.

i’ve had the chance to visit the okavango houseboat ngwezi a couple of times, both before and after its renovation – and each stay was absolutely phenomenal. captain philip is not only a fantastic captain but also an incredible chef. he and the entire team go above and beyond to make your stay truly unforgettable. the cabins are very comfortable and come with private bathrooms and showers, adding to the overall luxury of the experience. during our time on board, we spotted elephants, hippos, lechwe, and even the rare pel’s fishing owl – all thanks to our guide kt, who made it happen after we asked about it.

i’ve had the incredible opportunity to volunteer at galapagos dive and surf, and i can confidently say it’s one of the best dive agencies in the islands. the team is not only highly professional and knowledgeable, but also welcoming and passionate about what they do. their commitment to safety, ocean conservation, and top-quality service is clear in every aspect of their work. the atmosphere at the agency is amazing—beautifully decorated with beach, surf, and diving themes that make you feel inspired and connected to the sea. the facilities are clean and well-organized, and the dive trips are run with precision and care. as a volunteer, i’ve seen firsthand how much effort goes into creating unforgettable and safe experiences for each guest. whether you’re a beginner or an experienced diver, galapagos dive and surf is the perfect place to explore the underwater world and become part of a passionate, ocean-loving community. highly recommended!

i’ve had the pleasure to do 8 tours now with cameron, and i’ve enjoyed them all and learned so much about my hometown. cameron makes history fascinating drawing on ‘living’ artefacts of the city to sew a story that connects modern cape town to its epic and stranger than fiction roots. paradoxes abound in this land of contradictions. cameron sheds light on the hidden layers of our city that still govern our ways of life!

i’ve had thousands of massages over the course of 30 years, and let me tell you thian is a godsend!!!! i was visiting a girlfriend, who also works here, but it was her day off. thian stayed late to take my session, and boy was i in luck!!! thank goodness because i was coming off of two days of sitting in planes and 10 days of sleeping in the car (freedom camping), bunking at hostels, etc. you get cramp spaces where i was not able to relax! her knowledge in clinical massage therapy alleviated a lot of frozen should issues and shoulder pain i have been experiencing. for the first time in a couple of years, i was able to move my shoulders and felt them open up. she got into places only i usually get into; i am also a massage therapist. so grateful!!! my piriformis, auxillary, serratus, tfl, itb, and every single area that was hurting felt relief!!! thank you thian!

i’ve heard so many great stories about this museum, and finally had the chance to visit yesterday. all i can say is wow!!! fabulously laid out and wonderfully descriptive of the history of storyville. from the early days of the louisiana territory to the founding of new orleans all the way through the early 20th century. it’s well worth a visit for both visitors and locals alike.

i’ve hiked quite a bit and this is probably the most beautiful thing i’ve seen in my life. the hike is very steep, an unrelenting climb for a little over a mile or two. but the reward is absolutely worth it. personally, i found the view on the backside of the mountain to be even better (see the second two photos). finding the rock outcropping of the third photo was a bit difficult but if you have alltrails it will show you how to get there. it’s definitely more exposed on the back side and not something i would’ve attempted with snow still on the ground. all in all, if you have clear skies you will not want to miss this hike!

i’ve never seen a place quite like this!!! the entire complex was so cool and we were able to get in right away on a friday night. take lots of pictures around in your best clubbing outfit if you’d like 🤭 the cover of the place gets you two drinks- okay, i’m a lightweight, but the two cocktails we got were strong 😂😂😂 definitely enough to get me through the night. the drag show that started at 11 was amazing!!! no one was really dancing beforehand but the vibe is generally very fun :)

i’ve only been riding an mtb for 3 years, and stick to the easier trails, but this was still one of the best things i’ve done in 4 trips to queenstown now. the tracks are well marked out, and pretty easy to follow, and the green and blue trails should be well within the abilities of most beginner and intermediate riders. even on a peak sunday it was still not too busy, and i rarely had to make way for the kids blasting down the trails. the one bottleneck is the gondola. they prioritise the day trippers, meaning the mtb queue was rarely under 20 minutes once you hit the bottom. that last bit down through a construction site is also tricky, and at the top you have to push through walkways and barriers to get to the trails. but this should all be fixed when the new higher capacity gondola is completed this year. i managed 7 rides on my half day 4 hour gondola pass, but you can easily stretch this by making sure your final gondola ride happens just before the expiry, and once you are up you can stay for as long as you want. i took a package deal from vertigo with the bike, gear and gondola pass and they did a superb job.

i’ve passed by this museum more than ten times, but this was my first time going inside—and i really enjoyed my visit. it has a souvenir shop, a café, and, surprisingly, plenty of restrooms. i recommend this place to anyone visiting the nearby palace—it's definitely worth a stop. it’s also free.

i’ve purchased multiple products from amma therapie and am always impressed with the quality. i stumbled across their website while searching online for quality, organic face masks. i didn’t only purchase masks, but many therapeutic compresses - lavender eye mask, shoulder heating pad, long wrap compress, and heart comfort cushion for babies. i really like the handmade products in addition to the hemp and organic cotton material. the order is always fulfilled and shipped quickly and with care.

i’ve ridden thru the park a few times and recently had a chance to walk it. there are so many smaller lovely spots to see and enjoy. weekdays are best due to crowds unless you want to see doggies, in which case the weekend is great for that.

i’ve stayed here in both the summer and winter and both times were phenomenal. paige and cody are excellent hosts and attentive to every detail of our stay. we love it so much there we’ve already booked our trip for 2025!

i’ve used simbaa tours for more than 10 trips to zanzibar and always refer friends/family to this company. they have a wide arrange of service they offer on the islands and beyond. mohammed and his team are always on time, the ride was safe/comfortable, service is always friendly and the price is very competitive for znz. while living in tanzania, simbaa tours is the only company my family used. i would recommend for solo travelers and large families alike, and for anyone looking for a ferry/airport ride to excusions, hotel reservations and more! can’t say enough good things about this company.

i’ve visited bangkok a few times, but i had never actually stopped at wat kanlayanamit woramahawihan despite passing it many times during boat rides on the chao phraya river. this time, we decided to set aside the time and explore it properly and i’m really glad we did. the temple has a peaceful but active feel, and there’s quite a lot to take in across the grounds. it was fairly crowded when we visited in the late afternoon, but it didn’t take away from the experience. one of the standout features is the towering seated buddha inside the main hall it’s incredibly impressive up close. near the entrance, you’re also greeted by striking and colorful yaksha (guardian warrior) statues, which give the temple a strong visual identity and make for great photos. wat kanlayanamit is a royal temple dating back to the 1800s and holds a special place in thai culture. it is known for blending chinese and thai architectural elements, and it’s home to one of the largest bronze buddha images in bangkok. if you’re exploring along the river, this is definitely worth adding to your list. it may not be as famous as wat arun or wat pho, but it has its own charm and character that really leaves an impression.

i’ve visited hemis monastery many times, and it continues to be one of the most peaceful and spiritually rich places in this region. located about 41 km from leh, the monastery is nestled in a quiet valley surrounded by mountains, giving it a naturally serene atmosphere. near the monastery, poplar trees and other greenery grow naturally along the river, and this dense vegetation creates an humid and cool environment — it often feels as if a fine mist or light fog has been sprayed into the air, giving the place a soft, cloud-like feeling, which is rare in ladakh. there is also a pilgrim track that leads from the monastery up to a meditation cave, used by monks and spiritual seekers. as you walk along this path, you’ll notice wild rose bushes appearing sparsely along the way. inside the monastery, you’ll find tibetan architecture, ancient statues, detailed wall paintings, and a large buddha statue. a small museum displays rare scriptures and sacred relics. if you visit during the hemis tsechu festival, the cham dance performed by monks in colourful masks is truly unforgettable. as someone who visits regularly, i can say that hemis is not just a place — it’s an experience of peace, depth, and spiritual connection. highly recommended.

i’ve visited here duan a few times before heading back, and it’s definitely a place worth recommending. the food is consistently delicious, and the portions are generous – perfect for sharing or if you’re just really hungry! one of the standout dishes is their crab creamy eggs with rice – the egg is rich and creamy, and they’re generous with the big chunks of crab meat. it’s comforting and flavorful, something i’d come back for again. another dish i really enjoyed was the deep fried pork neck with noodles – the noodles are springy, and the pork neck is well-seasoned and tender. a must-try if you like bold flavors with a nice texture. we also tried the thai curry fish cakes – they were alright, flavorful but not the highlight for me. same goes for the prawn with stir-fried vermicelli – it was okay, but i personally preferred their version with instant noodles because of the texture. their tom yum is worth mentioning – spicy, fragrant, and hits the spot if you’re craving a kick. the omelette was simple but well-executed and tasty. overall, here duan serves up solid thai dishes with great portions, reasonable prices, and a comforting taste that keeps you coming back.

i’ve visited several markets in bangkok, and so far, pratunam market is pretty nice—definitely one of the best options i can recommend. it’s not too small or too big, and there are plenty of clothing options. i initially went there to check the quality of the products being sold, since many people mentioned how easy it is to shop impulsively in bangkok due to the low prices. however, i’m not a fan of low-quality clothes that don’t feel comfortable, aren’t flattering, and won’t last for years. unexpectedly, one of the stores i visited had clothes that actually met my standards—comfortable, flattering, and good quality. the store called new's image, i bought pants hehe :)) usually, sellers offer special prices if you buy at least three pieces. that said, not all the clothes are the same quality. in general, bottoms tend to have better quality, while with tops you need to be more selective. there are also plenty of food stalls around, and it’s not hard to find halal food for muslims. the sellers are mostly friendly. when i visited, it wasn’t too crowded but not too quiet either. i usually go in the morning for breakfast. most of the clothing stores are inside the market under a roof, so you don’t have to worry much about the weather.
i’ve visited this beautiful island for part of my venice trip. spectacular glassware and glassworks, tremendous talent and craftsmanship. you should come and see it in person.

i’ve visited this museum twice over the past few months and even the second time i discovered new things that i missed the first time - there really is so much to explore!! i’d say if you want to properly see and appreciate everything that this wonderful museum has to offer, you’ll need about 2.5 hours (maybe even more). it’s so beautifully well laid out and as well as predominantly discussing the lives of mountain people around the world, there is also a section about the original use of the castle - the building has been really well-preserved. at the top of the tower, there are beautiful views to be seen of bruneck and beyond!!

i’ve visited wat bowonniwet vihara many times before, but somehow this most recent visit opened my eyes to corners of the temple i’d never truly noticed. it felt like rediscovering a place i thought i already knew. the quiet, serene atmosphere on that day invited me to slow down and truly observe the beauty around me — from the richly adorned ordination hall to the intricately carved details along the cloister walls. the sunlight filtering through the colored glass ceiling panels made everything glow with an almost sacred warmth, and for the first time, i felt i was experiencing the temple not just as a visitor, but as part of its living presence. one of the highlights of this trip was finally making my way up to pay respects to phra phiraphinas, the revered buddha image enshrined in the upper section of the chedi. i’d heard about it for years, but had never taken the steps up until now. the moment i entered that quiet, golden chamber, something shifted — the space was peaceful, timeless, and filled with a sense of stillness that stayed with me long after i left. people came and went in silence, offering prayers and simply sitting, as if they, too, felt something special up there. afterward, i took my time strolling around the temple grounds and capturing some lesser-seen corners with my camera. from chinese-style archways to small white stupas tucked away behind the cloisters, and even shadows dancing off incense pots on the marble floor — every detail felt beautifully intentional. if you enjoy art, architecture, or photography, wat bowon offers more than just spiritual enrichment. it’s like an open-air museum that surprises you at every turn. getting there is fairly easy. if you’re lucky, you might find a parking spot inside the temple grounds, but if not, roadside parking is available — though you’ll need a bit of patience and local intuition! the surrounding area is a charming old neighborhood full of hidden gems and local food stalls, from hearty thai dishes to trendy little cafés. it’s a great place to explore on foot, especially if you want to combine culture with culinary adventures. even after so many visits, this temple continues to reveal something new each time. whether you’re seeking a peaceful retreat in the heart of bangkok or simply a beautiful spot to wander and reflect, wat bowonniwet has a quiet magic that lingers. i know i’ll keep coming back — sometimes to make merit, sometimes to take photos, but always to reconnect with that stillness that’s becoming harder to find in the city. and if you haven’t been yet (or haven’t been in a while), maybe it’s time to let yourself see it with fresh eyes — you might just discover a hidden part of bangkok that feels timeless, sacred, and deeply personal.

j. opens at dubai oasis mall: a new attraction on sheikh zayed road dubai's oasis mall has welcomed a vibrant addition to its retail lineup with the opening of j., a renowned pakistani clothing brand. known for its diverse range of traditional and modern apparel, j. offers a wide selection of menswear, womenswear, and kids' clothing. about j. established as one of pakistan's leading fashion brands, j. is celebrated for its fusion of tradition and contemporary style. the brand caters to diverse customer needs, from intricately designed ethnic wear to stylish ready-to-wear collections for all ages. its product line includes high-quality fabrics, accessories, and fragrances, reflecting the cultural richness of south asia while appealing to a global audience. positioned in the heart of dubai on sheikh zayed road, oasis mall serves as a bustling hub for shoppers. the introduction of j. not only adds variety to the mall's retail portfolio but also draws in south asian expats seeking culturally resonant fashion. the arrival of j. is expected to enhance the mall’s appeal by attracting more visitors, particularly from dubai's pakistani and south asian communities, who hold a strong affinity for the brand. this move aligns with oasis mall's strategy to diversify its offerings and solidify its position as a go-to destination for fashion, lifestyle, and culture in dubai. as j. establishes its presence in dubai’s competitive retail market, its unique blend of tradition and modernity is set to resonate with shoppers, further cementing the oasis mall as a thriving retail and cultural landmark.

jasper is one of those “once in a lifetime” places that you must visit (at least once). the scenery is astounding. you really cannot fathom it from pictures or videos, this is one place you have to see and experience for yourself. if you are in your own car you have to drive the icefields parkway from banff to jasper and stop at all the viewpoints. if you are visiting the icefields parkway visitor centre is one place you have to stop. even if its just for a quick look on the way along the icefield parkway. however i would highly recommend doing the glacier walk. this is one of the only places in the world where you can actually walk on a glacier and the ice rovers are great fun. the visitor center itself is really good, from clean toilets to a very good gift shop and starbucks coffee shop. there is a museum and other exhibits, but the tours are obviously the main attraction. the viewpoints offer some amazing views of the glaciers and mountains, with varied and diverse scenery even though its all mountainous. there are some lovely short walks and hikes along the parkway, which requires a bit of pre-planning, but its worth it. the one you have to do is the toe of the athabasca glacier, which is free and pretty easy this area is amazing, not only for the views, but for the fact this area is the only place in the world where the continental divide splits 3 ways, with water going to the atlantic, pacific and arctic oceans. the way the snow sits on the edge of the mountains is really impressive and the whole area is full of astounding scenery. put jasper on your bucket list of it isn’t already.

jerusalem herod’s gate herod’s gate, modest and less frequented than its counterparts, is a quiet but meaningful entrance into the old city’s muslim quarter. located on the northern wall, near bustling east jerusalem, the gate derives its name from its association with a nearby structure once linked, perhaps inaccurately, to king herod. in arabic, it’s called “bab az-zahra,” which connects it to a local neighborhood and reveals layers of linguistic and cultural history. unlike the grand facades of damascus or jaffa gates, herod’s gate exudes simplicity and function, making it a fascinating lens into the everyday life of the city. the gate’s current form dates to the ottoman period, and it was originally sealed and later opened in the 19th century to ease access between neighborhoods. passing through, visitors enter a more residential, authentic part of the old city where tradition is lived, not displayed. local shops, schools, and quiet homes fill the narrow streets just inside, giving a rare view into the rhythm of jerusalem beyond its most famous landmarks. herod’s gate may not boast ornate towers or tourist crowds, but its understated character offers something just as valuable: a genuine window into the lives that shape the city today.

jerusalem jaffa gate jaffa gate stands as one of the main entrances to jerusalem’s old city, offering a grand welcome into its ancient walls and vibrant quarters. located on the western side, this iconic gate connects the modern city with its historic heart and serves as a popular starting point for exploring the wonders within. built in the 16th century during the ottoman era, jaffa gate has witnessed centuries of change, from imperial processions to contemporary tourism. its name comes from the road that once led from here to the port city of jaffa, the ancient gateway to the mediterranean. today, it opens directly into the christian and armenian quarters and is just a short walk from the jewish quarter. the gate is flanked by the tower of david and the citadel museum, where ancient fortifications and immersive exhibits tell the story of jerusalem’s past. street musicians, bustling vendors, and the chatter of visitors from all over the world create a lively and welcoming atmosphere. whether arriving for the first time or returning again, passing through jaffa gate feels like stepping into a living story—one where sacred traditions, layered history, and diverse cultures all converge beneath jerusalem’s golden light.

jerusalem lions’ gate lions’ gate, also known as st. stephen’s gate, is a remarkable and symbolic entrance on the eastern side of jerusalem’s old city, steeped in religious tradition and historical weight. carved with stone lions—symbols of strength and guardianship—it leads directly into the muslim quarter and serves as the starting point for the via dolorosa, the path believed to be walked by jesus on his way to the crucifixion. the gate holds significance for multiple faiths, making it a powerful intersection of belief, memory, and devotion. its current structure dates to the 16th century, constructed under the rule of suleiman the magnificent, though the site itself has roots reaching far deeper into jerusalem’s layered past. as you step through, the road rises toward sacred ground, with mosques, churches, and bustling alleyways offering a profound sensory journey. lions’ gate was also a key entry point during the six-day war, marking a modern chapter in jerusalem’s complex story. whether you’re walking in the footsteps of pilgrims or tracing the steps of history, this gate opens more than stone walls—it opens the mind and spirit to jerusalem’s enduring mystery, passion, and spiritual resonance.

jerusalem new gate the new gate is the youngest of the old city’s entrances, yet it serves a unique and vital role in connecting the ancient world with modern jerusalem. opened in 1889 by the ottomans, it was created to give direct access to the christian quarter, particularly the french institutions and christian pilgrims who had been settling in growing numbers outside the walls. situated near the convergence of east and west jerusalem, the new gate symbolizes openness and dialogue between communities. its design is simpler than the city’s older gates, but it exudes a special charm—especially in the evenings when local cafes, boutique shops, and cultural centers buzz with youthful energy. this gate leads into quieter, cobbled streets lined with monasteries, churches, and schools, many of which date back centuries. it’s also a meeting point for contemporary jerusalem, where locals gather for music events, art shows, and street fairs that spill from the modern city into the old. more than just an entryway, the new gate reflects jerusalem’s evolving character—a place where tradition meets transformation, and history walks hand-in-hand with renewal. for those seeking both the sacred and the current, the new gate offers a graceful and welcoming threshold.

jnan sbil park, nestled between fes el-bali’s ancient medina and the mellah (jewish quarter), is a serene escape from the city’s relentless energy. established in the 19th century by sultan moulay hassan i and later opened to the public in 1917, this 7.5-hectare garden is a rare green lung in fez’s labyrinthine old city . its 2006–2010 restoration revived its historic charm, blending lush botanical diversity with moorish design think geometric fountains, shaded pathways, and over 3,000 plant species, including towering bamboos, fragrant orange groves, and a mexican cactus garden . the park’s tranquility is its standout feature. locals flock here at dusk to stroll beneath century old palms or relax by the central pond, where waterbirds flutter around a palm-covered island . the historic norias (water wheels) and oued fes river channels add a whisper of the past, though summer droughts occasionally leave streams parched . while the andalusian garden’s symmetry evokes spain’s alcázar, the vibe is distinctly moroccan families picnic on benches, students unwind between classes, and the occasional peacock struts near bird coops . practical but imperfect: entry is free, and crowds are thin compared to fez’s tourist hotspots. however, weekday closures (mondays) and early 6 pm shutdowns limit flexibility . the lack of signage in english or arabic may frustrate some, and while the on-site café noria serves decent moroccan bites, options are basic . for a post-medina breather, jnan sbil delivers. it’s not flashy, but its quiet beauty especially at golden hour captures fez’s soul better than any crowded souk. just time your visit wisely .

july 19, 2025 – day 16 in india we visited spituk monastery just outside leh, guided by angmo, whose gentle wisdom and mastery in buddhist philosophy made every moment truly special. she cared patiently for our 5‑ and 7‑year‑old daughters, answering their myriad questions with warmth and clarity. watching her kneel in respectful salutations to the buddha, and our girls copying her so tenderly, was the sweetest shared memory. spituk was originally founded in the 11th century by od‑de, the elder brother of lha lama changchub od. a famous translator, rinchen zangpo, foretold it would become an exemplary spiritual community—and so the name “spituk,” meaning “exemplary,” was born. over centuries it shifted from the kadampa lineage to the gelug (yellow hat) school in the 15th century. the monastery houses about one hundred monks and treasures a giant statue of the goddess kali that is unveiled only during the annual gustor festival. you’ll also find the striking skudung lhakhang with chinese‑style gilt roof corners, a statue of tsongkhapa in his yellow hat, and an unusual tsepame figure said to have come from his nosebleed. perched high on a hill at over 3,300 m elevation, visitors climb many stairs to reach the monastery. this ascent reflects both physical effort and spiritual symbolism: in himalayan buddhist tradition, building monasteries above ground encourages detachment from worldly ties and inspires rising toward higher ideals. the climb is itself a small pilgrimage. inside, photography is gently restricted, so we sat in silence and prayed. as we meditated, angmo softly hummed a sacred hymn meant to clear obstacles from our path. that moment—so unassuming and full of devotion—left me deeply moved. my daughters were enchanted by spinning the many prayer wheels. each spin is a blessing: turning the wheels is believed to release prayers into the universe, cultivating compassion and positive energy with each revolution. from the monastery’s terraces we gazed down at the indus river, its water tinged a soft orange in the afternoon sun. the views of the valley and surrounding mountain ranges created an overwhelming sense of serenity and awe. all in all, this place filled me with peace. i’m in awe. loved it here truly.

just arrived from a trip of a lifetime with kruger wildlife safaris. it has been a dream of mine to do a safari since my grandfather introduced me to the world of travel when i was young. from the moment your picked up in the private transfer van & taken to the camp that's located in southern kruger national park i knew this was going to be a great experience. the atmosphere of this place is absolutely awesome. our group was mostly young people & also solo travellers so its super easy to meet people we all got along very well on the outings & evening dinners. the drives i took the four day camping safari. this included four drives in total. one in the afternoon you arrive, two the second day morning & evening, one in the morning before you leave back to joburg. everyone i spoke with mentioned it was such amazing value for money considering what’s included. the vehicles they use are super new & amazing comfy this is so important as your out for three hours each drive, the seating positions are really high this gives you the best chance to spot animals in the brush. everyday we to a different routes to make sure we covered as much ground as possible. the great thing about using a company like this is that the drivers talk to each other concerning sighting so you have a much higher chance of seeing animals than a self drive. so what did we see? just got back from our 9 day safari, sleeping almost every night at a different hotel and mbalageti is the one i cannot recommend. rats, ants, spiders and scorpions, all in one night.... it is just too much. the location was good, it was a beautiful drive crossing a river with monkeys, and looking out from the porch area of the restaurant was beautiful. the pool was full of insects, the bar people were not super nice (could be the only not nice people all trip). the food was very good, beautiful display, tasty indian food and nice staff. the room they gave us at first, 18, was huge but it was clearly not well-maintained with missing railing, literal piles of bat poop around the entire house, rat poop also in little piles along the walls inside, and ants eating crickets on the floor inside. the views were a good distraction from the broken board on the floor and the rotten wooden deck. when i walked in the bathroom two rats ran across and sneaked out through the seam between the rocks and the tent material. i prayed they were gone for the day and didnt say anything to my family. my son discovered ants around the bidet in the other bathroom, and when i sprayed them with mosquito repellents all hell broke lose..... millions, i mean millions of ants came out of the volcanic rock that made the wall, they were pulling out the colony's eggs and were moving in like balls that would fall on the floor.... i have never seen anything like that. along with the ants a spider as big as my open hand also came out of the rock and jumped out almost to my shirt. house of horrors. we moved to room 1 and everything was spotless, clearly recently cleaned and tidied. next morning we were informed that our driver was bit by a scorpion that got in his pants as he showered before our drive. they gave him ibuprofen and said he was good to go. they didnt have any antidote or any means to treat anything serious in such a remote location. for these very unpleasant reasons, i cannot recommend this lodge to anyone. i liked the time limit with the electricity, i liked the walkie talkie situation, i enjoyed seeing the baboons stealing our food.... but having been to many tented lodges, this was the worst experience by far.

just incredible! the beauty of nature is simply unspeakable. everywhere you look. some useful tips: 1. it is about a 1h walk one way so with a short break you need to book 2,5h-3h. 2. you might be willing to arrive before 9 a.m. as later on parking might be a bit more difficult task - not impossible though. you will just need to park along the street and walk a bit longer. 3. the entry is 3€ for adult. 4. the are some food & beverages points at the start and at the end of the route. 5. just remember to bring some backpack with you as there are no dust bins on the way and you need to take back with you what you brought. 6.the route is not very demanding just take some appropriate shoes as it might be slippery in some parts. 7. its about 360m up there and back. 8. accessing the top at the end of peninsula is forbidden althought there is queue of people there anyway 9. basically there is a lot of people everywhere - another reason to arrive early (before 9 a.m.) or late after (5p.m. in summer time) 10. just enjoy it. it is one of the most beautiful places on earth!

just to note, the rector's palace and cultural-historical museum are one and the same place. the museum is inside the palace. a great & varied collection of things here. starting with a collection of religious art you move on to portrait paintings of celebrated citizens of dubrovnik. then a collection of stoneworks and old wood/iron chests for storage if valuables. don't miss the display on the ground floor of b&w photos from the war years of 1991/92. follow the stairs upto rooms on the first floor for a fine collection of furnishings and paintings. includes the well known oil painting "the rape of the sabine women" by pietro da cortona.

kappabashi kitchen street – a hidden treasure for culinary enthusiasts if you love to cook or appreciate good craftsmanship, kappabashi kitchen street in tokyo is an absolute must-visit. this stretch between asakusa and ueno is home to over 170 specialty shops, all dedicated to kitchenware. whether you’re after professional-grade japanese knives, beautifully glazed ceramics, or quirky plastic food models, you’ll find everything here in one long, fascinating walk. prices are far more reasonable than what you’d pay at retail stores back home. many items are sold directly by the manufacturers, so you’re cutting out the middleman and getting authentic, high-quality goods straight from the source. it’s a practical stop for anyone stocking up on essentials, as well as a fun place to browse if you’re just curious. we spent over an hour wandering from shop to shop and still felt like we barely scratched the surface. you’ll see knife shops offering custom engraving, stores selling restaurant signage, lacquerware, baking tools, and more. it’s a great blend of tradition and utility. kappabashi has been tokyo’s “kitchen town” since the 1920s, and its legacy continues strong. whether you’re a chef, home cook, or just a foodie, this place is a dream come true. bring a bit of extra luggage space—you’ll need it.

kbal spean is one of the most unique and spiritually significant sites in cambodia’s angkor region. often called “the river of a thousand lingas,” it’s a sacred site where nature and ancient khmer spirituality merge.

kbal spean: a local guide's hidden gem!!! as a local guide, i'm always thrilled to introduce visitors to the lesser-known wonders beyond angkor wat, and kbal spean is undoubtedly one of my top recommendations. often referred to as the "river of a thousand lingas," this ancient site offers a unique blend of natural beauty, historical significance, and a refreshingescape from the bustling temples. nestled deep in the jungle, the journey to kbal spean itself is part of the adventure. a pleasant trek through lush forest leads you to the riverbed, where the true magic unfolds. here, beneath the clear waters, you'll discover thousands of intricately carved lingas (phallic symbols representing shiva) and other hindu deities etched into the sandstone. it's a truly remarkable sight, showcasing the devotion and artistry of the khmer people centuries ago. beyond the carvings, the site boasts a beautiful waterfall, especially impressive during the wet season, where you can cool off and enjoy the serene atmosphere. the air is fresh, the sounds of nature are abundant, and the spiritual energy is palpable. kbal spean is perfect for those seeking a tranquil and culturally rich experience away from the crowds. it's a place where history, art, and nature converge, offering a deeper understanding of cambodia's ancient heritage. don't forget comfortable shoes, as the walk can be a bit uneven, but trust me, the reward is well worth the effort! it's a definite must-visit for anyone looking to explore the hidden depths of siem reap's historical landscape.

kew gardens is my favourite public park in toronto. it's a rustic, vast and beautiful enclave of greenery, picnic chalets, little forest paths, tennis courts and hockey arenas, a big baseball court, and many more. there is also a large playground and a mini water park with water toys where children can play and enjoy themselves. one may find themselves shifting from a sunny flower garden to a wooden bridge path surrounded on both sides by imposing trees providing a pleasant shade. there is much to see here and time feels as if at a standstill. the sheer size of the trees and the century-old library right next to this park often makes me reflect on the history of this place, where children played and laughed a hundred years ago in this park that likely changed very little in that time. a perfect place for a picnic or an adventure of exploration, kew gardens will be an instant favourite once you spend enough time here!

khufu pyramid — the oldest and largest of the giza pyramid complex — was built around 2560 b.c. as the tomb of khufu, the second pharaoh of the fourth dynasty. originally, the pyramid was clad in white limestone, with its tip covered in gold. the limestone, also called “royal stone,” came from the tura quarries some 800 km away, and how it was transported to giza remains a mystery to this day. the khufu pyramid is truly massive — it took us more than 10 minutes just to walk from the west side to the entrance on the east side. as we walked, i kept wondering how tens of thousands of huge stone blocks were stacked so precisely 4,500 years ago. and they say aliens weren’t involved? i’m not convinced. the route inside is long, hot, and stuffy. in some places, you have to bend or crouch to pass, and with the crowds, i was drenched in sweat within 30 seconds of entering. the burial chamber is small, containing only a single empty stone sarcophagus. small holes in the walls likely have astronomical significance, symbolizing the pharaoh’s soul ascending to join the gods. it also smelled terrible in there — we snapped a quick photo and got out fast. -1/1/25

kiwengwa beach being the much more popular, pongwe's beach is a quiet gem and personally much more appreciated. suited for swimming at high tides - the water can get comfortably warm on nice days - and suited for walking at all times. the restaurant of santa maria is a beautiful spot between the sea and a park with bush babies and pretty birds like lilac-breasted rollers.

kiwi park was a fantastic and unique experience. i am a big bird lover and i had so much fun watching the kiwis running around in their beautiful and well maintained habitats. the conservation talk was informative and i loved that the speaker walked around so everyone could have a closer look at the animals. overall i really enjoyed my tine there and i would highly recommend visiting and supporting these beautiful birds and reptiles of new zealand!
