koishikawa botanical garden in tokyo is an amazing place to visit, especially if you’re looking to experience japan’s natural beauty in a peaceful setting. it’s a bit away from central areas like shinjuku, shibuya, or tokyo station, so i highly recommend taking the train instead of walking. once you’re off the train, there’s still a short walk to get to the garden, but it’s manageable. if you’re coming from gokokuji temple, it’s actually close enough to walk, and doing so is a great way to explore the local area. we entered through a side entrance, near the greenhouse, not the main entrance, and i noticed right away that they have bathrooms available—which is always helpful. just a heads-up: there are no public trash cans in most places in japan, including here. so if you’re carrying snacks or drinks, make sure to bring a small bag to keep your trash with you. if you plan to visit, i strongly suggest going during peak seasons like cherry blossom season or summer. when we visited, it had rained the days before, so some of the paths were wet and muddy—not everywhere, but enough to make it slightly difficult to walk in some areas. even so, the experience was unforgettable. this garden had some of the most beautiful and massive trees i’ve ever seen in my life. truly breathtaking. it’s a place where you can just slow down and take it all in. i was so amazed that i didn’t even take many photos—i just wanted to be present and enjoy the surroundings. admission is only 7 dollars, which makes it a very affordable experience. if the weather is nice, you can even do a picnic—there are lots of lovely spots to sit and relax. in short, this is a place where you’ll find peace, beauty, and a deep connection to nature. just make sure to go during a good season and avoid the rainy days if you can. i highly, highly recommend it.

koishikawa botanical garden was truly a forest, with trees that looked to be 30 meters tall everywhere. i was happy and slightly shocked to find such a vast forest just 3 kilometers from the imperial palace. it's azalea season now, and i didn't know for the first time that tall azalea trees as tall as a person existed. i must visit koishikawa botanical garden again.

koko crater summit is a must-hike gem. challenging climb with epic views of oahu’s coast. stunning sunrise payoff. well-maintained trail, perfect for adventurers. bring water, grit, and enjoy the rewarding panoramic vistas at the top. 😎

koko head district park is a fantastic destination for both locals and visitors looking to enjoy outdoor activities. the park offers stunning panoramic views, especially from the top of the koko head crater, which you can reach via the challenging but rewarding koko crater stairs hike. the trail is steep and demands good physical fitness, but the breathtaking scenery at the summit makes it all worthwhile. besides the popular hike, the park features open fields, sports facilities, and shaded picnic areas, perfect for family gatherings or a relaxing afternoon. the park is well-maintained, with clean restrooms and ample parking. however, it's advisable to bring plenty of water, sun protection, and sturdy shoes, especially for the hike.

komodo dragons obviously sedated komodo area is absolutely stunning & the boat trip is beautiful. however the komodo island was simply depressing to see. we went in august which is the komodo dragon mating season. this means the chances of seeing one actually in the wild are very low. yet when we arrived the guides were all very excited that “there is a dragon”. after walking for 5 minutes on a well established path indeed there was a male dragon … so drugged he basically looked dead, surrounded by 50 people or so queueing to take a picture with him. it was a circus-like scene, one that makes you question where is humanity going. i don’t know how a place which harms these creatures in such a way can be called a national park … you’d be better off seeing them in a zoo. there were two more sedated adult dragons within 100m from each other which we went to see (they looked slightly better, at least they looked alive) and that was it, the “trek” was done because there were no more dragons (how could the “rangers” be so sure exactly where & how many dragons there are, i’m asking?). the “rangers” tried to explain that the dragons are not moving because they’re now resting … as much as i would love to believe this, it’s at least suspicious, that in a season where no dragons should be seen there are three adult males that happen to be resting right next to a tourist path … after asking lots of questions to the guides my theory is that every day there are a few “lucky” ones sedated and kept there for the show, i’m not sure if it’s always the same ones. i felt incredibly guilty to be part of this. looking at these beautiful, amazing creatures downgraded to this photo show for tourists was simply horrible. fortunately looking at the tourists around there were many people that obviously looked very uncomfortable. i think the news are starting to spread that the dragons are treated like this! we did actually see one young dragon which wasn’t sedated which was wonderful to see - the guide’s surprise to see it was hilarious on its own, nearly like he couldn’t believe there’s a dragon they haven’t caught & drugged. as a side note, on rinca island the guides made it clear that we would have to be very lucky to see one & indeed we didn’t see one which fills me with hope that at least on that island they are hopefully left undisturbed. or maybe i’m being naive? to top it all up, the komodo “national park”absolutely rips off tourists for money, with a 250k price per day per tourist for entry. glad to know the money i paid is probably going to be spend on sedating drugs instead of cleaning the sea from all the trash floating around!

kranji marshes offers a unique escape into nature, but it's a mixed bag in terms of maintenance and experience. located in singapore, the marshes are a good option for those looking to immerse themselves in a quieter, more natural environment away from the hustle and bustle of the city. the walking trail is decent, making for a pleasant trek, and i found that a 30-minute walk provided an opportunity to appreciate the surrounding flora and fauna. however, the lack of upkeep was evident. some paths were overgrown, and the area felt somewhat neglected, which detracted from the overall experience. one significant downside was the mosquito situation. i ended up with 18 bites during my visit, so i recommend bringing insect repellent or wear long sleeves and pants if you decide to go. the marshes can feel quite deserted, which might appeal to some seeking solitude, but it could also be a bit unsettling for others. overall, kranji marshes has potential for a refreshing nature walk, but be prepared for a few inconveniences along the way. if you are willing to overlook the maintenance issues and the pesky mosquitoes, it can be a worthwhile retreat into singapore's natural landscape.

kranji nature trail is a coastal trail stretch along the coastline of kranji overlooking johor straits. the hike brings you to bird hides, view decks, shelter huts and mid canopy walk that were strategically located along this scenic coastal trail. the trail is easy. and consist of hard tracks and boardwalks that sometimes extend over the waters. the entire coastal trail from sungei buloh wetland reserve kranji way ending at sungei buloh wetland reserve vistor's centre takes roughly an hour to complete. opening hrs is 7am to 7pm. toilet are available at both ends of the trail.

kranji nature trail is an absolute gem—quiet, leafy, and delightfully undisturbed. lovely place. walking there feels like stepping into a tranquil forest world, with elevated boardwalks, mangroves, woodland birds, and subtle layers of greenery all around. it's one of those peaceful corners of singapore that wipes the noise from your mind, especially perfect for when you just want some calm and green.

kyanjin is a village located in the langtang valley of nepal at an altitude of approximately 3,870 meters (12,697 feet). if you're thinking about a "lower" or less elevated area nearby, you might be referring to locations further down the langtang valley. a popular spot lower than kyanjin gompa is langtang village, at around 3,430 meters (11,253 feet). as you descend even further, you reach lama hotel at about 2,470 meters (8,104 feet). each village along this trekking route offers a unique perspective on the valley, with slightly warmer temperatures and varied vegetation as you go lower. let me know if you need more specific details about these locations or the trek!

kyoto international manga museum – a paradise for manga lovers! an absolute gem in the heart of kyoto! the museum houses an impressive and diverse collection of manga, including rare series dating all the way back to the 1960s. it’s not just about reading — it's also a fascinating journey through the history and evolution of manga, with insightful exhibits on how manga are created, from concept to final art. a unique and engaging experience for fans and curious visitors alike. one small note: the live manga drawing workshops are a great idea, but with only two instructors available, it feels a bit limited. with such interest, having more manga teachers would definitely elevate the experience even further. still, a must-visit for anyone interested in japanese culture, art, or storytelling.

kyoto national museum opened in 1895. the harmony between the gate, building, and rodin's sculptures that decorate the garden is beautiful. the museum displays traditional japanese buddhist statues, paintings, crafts, and more. the museum is large and has many exhibits, so you'll need at least 90 minutes to see everything.

lai chi kok park is a delightful oasis in the bustling city of hong kong. located conveniently near the mei foo mtr station, this park offers a perfect blend of traditional and modern elements, making it a must-visit for both locals and tourists. one of the standout features of the park is the lingnan garden. this beautifully designed area, with its traditional lingnan-style buildings, pavilions, and landscaped gardens, provides a serene and picturesque setting. the garden’s tranquil atmosphere is perfect for a leisurely stroll or a moment of reflection. the park is also well-equipped with various amenities, including a public swimming pool, sports grounds, children’s playground, jogging trails, and even a 200-seat amphitheatre. the sculptures and well-maintained landscaping throughout the park add to its charm and appeal. whether you’re looking to relax, exercise, or simply enjoy the outdoors, lai chi kok park has something for everyone. it’s a wonderful place to unwind and escape the city’s hustle and bustle.

lake titicaca is truly a marvel of nature, renowned not only for being the highest navigable lake in the world but also for its immense size, which makes it the largest lake in south america. our half-day tour, skillfully led by vicky from lima tours, allowed us to soak in the panoramic views and understand the unique ways in which the local communities live around this vast body of water. the cultural insights provided by the guide, coupled with the serene and expansive natural backdrop, made for an unforgettable experience. this tour of lake titicaca is highly recommended as a fundamental part of any visit to peru and puno. taking a guided tour enriches the experience, providing structured insights and safe navigation through the expansive waters, enhancing your appreciation of this significant natural and cultural landmark.

lamai is an outstanding safari camp! the lamai lodge is situated perfectly on the northern serengeti. the wildlife viewing and the guides are world class! food and hospitality are also excellent. i stayed for five days this past august and recommend it highly for either first time or experience safari goers. the lodge itself is imbedded into the natural environment so thoroughly that it is barely visible in the landscape. and the wildlife hardly recognize it being there either as buffalo and others wonder through during the night! you'll be safe though as staff are posted throughout the camp during the night. i highly recommend lamai lodge!

lamayuru (yuru gompa) – a “moonland” of serenity and culture a must-visit on the srinagar–leh highway—lamayuru is a timeless blend of stark lunar landscapes and spiritual calm. ancient monastery perched on cliffs: one of ladakh’s oldest and largest gompas, with origins in the 10th–11th century thanks to sage naropa and rinchen zangpo . surreal moonscape terrain: the area around the monastery offers dramatic barren formations that truly feel otherworldly—perfect for photographers and quiet contemplation . spiritual richness & festivals: home to ~150 monks and renowned for masked-dance festivals like yuru kabgyat and hemis tse chu . visitor-friendly with good access: located ~125 km from leh, it has a teahouse, basic amenities, and no permit requirements—ideal for a peaceful stopover .

lamayuru - the moonscape for tourist. it is known as the moonland of ladakh and situated at a distance of 115 km(s) from leh, one can easily cover lamayuru in a day return trip from leh. with its moonlike landscape, sometimes called the moonscape, lamayuru is captivating and divine. the presence of the ancient lamayuru monastery, nestled amidst this "moonland" landscape, adds to the area's unique charm and appeal.

lamayuru monastery is a historic and culturally significant monastery in ladakh, india. located 125 km from leh on the srinagar-leh highway, lamayuru monastery is one of the oldest and largest existing gompas in ladakh. founded by naropa, an indian scholar, in the 10th century, it was originally a bon monastery before being affiliated with the drikung kagyu school of tibetan buddhism. the monastery features stunning murals, including depictions of buddhist deities and mythological scenes. you'll find ancient paintings of cardinal kings and other significant artworks. the monastery complex houses beautifully decorated chortens and stupas. a small cave where naropa is believed to have meditated, featuring statues of naropa and marpa. a two-day festival celebrated in the second month of the tibetan lunar calendar, featuring ritualistic dance performances and sacred ceremonies. an annual masked dance festival is held in the monastery, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of the region. may to september, with pleasant weather and clear skies. the monastery is accessible by road from leh and srinagar. you can take a taxi or bus from leh or srinagar. there are various stay options in lamayuru, including hotels and guesthouses. try local tibetan cuisine at restaurants like niranjana lamayuru restaurant. no photography inside the prayer hall, and be mindful of other rules. entry fee rs.50/- per head.

langtang lirung, standing at an impressive 7,234 meters (23,734 feet), is the highest peak of the langtang himal, a subrange of the nepalese himalayas. ranking 99th in the world in terms of height, this majestic mountain is a significant attraction for trekkers and climbers who wish to experience the grandeur of the himalayas. with a prominence of 1,534 meters (5,033 feet), langtang lirung offers dramatic landscapes and challenging terrains. the first successful ascent was recorded on october 24, 1978, by seishi wada and pemba tsering, marking it as a notable destination for mountaineers. the langtang region is easily accessible from kathmandu, and one can complete the langtang valley trek to kyanjin gompa in about 5/6 days, making it an excellent option for trekkers who want a relatively short but rewarding experience. the trek begins at syafrubesi, a village in the rasuwa district, and takes you through dense forests, traditional tamang villages, and alpine meadows. the trek's climax is reaching kyanjin gompa, a small monastery that offers a spectacular view of langtang lirung, standing majestically against the vast himalayan sky. my journey to langtang was unforgettable, with every step revealing stunning scenery and a profound sense of peace. the combination of natural beauty, cultural immersion, and the warmth of the local people made it an exceptional experience. the trek provides breathtaking vistas of snow-capped peaks, glaciers, and serene valleys, offering a perfect balance of adventure and tranquility. i had the privilege of exploring this remarkable place just before the devastating nepal earthquake of 2015, which changed the region dramatically. despite the tragic event, the langtang region has remained resilient and continues to captivate visitors with its raw beauty and spirit. langtang lirung and its surroundings are truly a gem in the himalayas, offering an experience that lingers in one's memory long after the journey ends.

last summer, i stayed at the grand hyatt singapore for the first time, shortly after the hotel completed its renovations. i booked the terrace suite for the extra space. breakfast at strait kitchen was excellent, and the happy hour at 10 scotts (serving as the grand club) was equally impressive. this summer, i returned as a globalist member and again booked the terrace suite, which includes grand club access regardless of status. based on both my prior stay and experiences at other grand hyatt properties in asia such as grand hyatt taipei i expected globalists to have the choice of enjoying breakfast either at the grand club or at cafe (strait kitchen in grand hyatt singapore). upon check-in at the grand club (level 1m), i was told that breakfast was available only at the grand club and not at strait kitchen. this was disappointing for two reasons: 1. the grand club opens for breakfast at 7:00 a.m., while strait kitchen opens at 6:30 a.m. an important difference for early risers like myself. 2. other grand hyatt locations offer globalists and suite guests the flexibility to choose their breakfast venue, a courtesy i believe should be standard for a flagship property like singapore. restricting breakfast to the grand club for a globalist staying in a suite that already includes club access feels unnecessarily rigid. this has resulted my rating from 5 stars to 4 for this review.

last week, i went on a liveaboard in the seychelles with explorer 1. the liveaboard crew (christophe, julian and halil) were very profesional and clearly have been working together for a long time to make this the best experience possible. the explorer 1 is a made-for-purpose catamaran that is perfectly suited for diving. they only take a small number of divers, which means more attention to detail and less crowded dive sites. the itinerary made by christophe made sure we got to all the best dive sites and we got to see all we wanted. we must have been very lucky, because all week we had calm seas, good weather and plenty of sea life. whoever said that sharks are a rare sighting, clearly has not been diving in the seychelles, as we saw sharks on virtually every dive (sometimes dozens of them on the same dive). the crew took us from mahe to praslin, then all the way to the north atol bird island and then back to la dique, hitting many dive sites on the way. apart from sharks, we encountered a total of six (!) whale sharks. one of them kept swimming around our group for about ten minutes, which was truly a wonderful experience. furthermore, we spotted a manta ray, many other rays, sea turtles, octopusses and much, much more. in between dives we were well taken care of, with delicious meals containing freshly caught fish, nice cabins and enough space to relax (in and out of the sun). most of the dives were deep dives and sometimes they were a bit challenging, so i would recommend some diving experience and definately an advance open water certification (or higher) and the use of nitrox (available on board). in conclusion, explorer 1 really delivered on the perfect liveaboard experience. the seychelles have beautiful diving options and this seems the best way to enjoy them!

lempuyang temple, one of bali's oldest and most revered temples, is a must-visit for anyone seeking a blend of stunning natural beauty and profound spiritual significance. located on the slopes of mount lempuyang in east bali, it's famous for its iconic "gates of heaven," which perfectly frame the majestic mount agung volcano in the distance. the journey to lempuyang is an experience in itself, taking you through the island's lush, green landscapes. upon arrival, you'll find a temple complex that is more than just a single photo-op. it's a series of seven temples spread across the mountainside, offering a spiritual ascent for those who choose to make the challenging climb. the most popular spot, and the reason many people visit, is the main temple with its famous split gate. the breathtaking view and the "water reflection" photo that has become so popular on social media are the main draw. it's worth noting that the reflection is a clever trick created by a local photographer using a mirror under the camera lens—but don't let that deter you! the result is truly magical and the view of mount agung is spectacular on a clear day. tips for your visit: go early! to avoid the crowds and the infamous long queues for the photo opportunity, i highly recommend arriving as early as possible. aim for 5-6 am to catch the sunrise and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere before the buses of tourists arrive. the early morning light also creates the most beautiful and atmospheric pictures. token system for photos: be aware that there is a token system in place for taking pictures at the famous gate. you will receive a token with your entrance ticket, and you'll wait for your number to be called for your photo session. this system helps manage the crowds and ensures everyone gets a turn. dress appropriately: as a sacred site, you are required to dress modestly. sarongs are provided or available for rent at the entrance. while the "gates of heaven" photo is a fantastic souvenir, the real magic of lempuyang temple lies in its serene beauty and spiritual ambiance. take the time to appreciate the intricate balinese architecture, the stunning views, and the sacred energy of this incredible place. it's an unforgettable experience that goes beyond a single photograph.

lions head is an absolutely gorgeous hike and easily one of the best spots to get fantastic 360° views of cape town, the ocean, and the surrounding table mountain national park. the trail is beginner-friendly and easy to follow, but definitely steep and a little challenging as well. you hike up and come back down the same way, and can turn around safely at almost any point if needed. the hike starts with a dirt path at a good incline, and most beginners hiking at a casual pace can complete the round trip in about 2 hours. make sure to factor in extra time for breaks, as needed, and to enjoy the incredible views from the top. challenge: higher up, you'll come across ladders and chains at two points and will need to climb over some rocks. however, no climbing experience is needed, but this portion of the trail may also be tough if you're uncomfortable with heights. safety: it’s usually quite busy, especially in the summer. this is probably one of the safest hikes in cape town due to the amount of foot traffic, but it’s always important to stay aware of your surroundings and don’t carry unnecessary valuables. some people bring cameras, just bring a bag or backpack to keep it in. what to wear: i recommend wearing sports shoes with good grip or comfortable trainers, and bringing at least a bottle (250ml) of water (more if it’s hot). even if the weather looks fine, pack a light jacket or a light long sleeve shirt, it can change quickly on the mountain. if you’re planning a sunrise or sunset hike, definitely bring a headlamp. wear comfortable clothes and consider a cap/hat on hot or high uv days. there are great spots at the top to chill, eat a snack, and take some memorable photos. just remember to leave no trace and take your litter with you as there are no trash bins on the route itself. sometimes there’s a small coffee/snack truck at the bottom of the trail. parking can be tricky during peak times or weekends, so plan ahead. no toilets or water points on the trail. dog walking is allowed in the table mountain national park, but i wouldn’t recommend it on this trail due to the light climbing up ladders. highly recommend this hike for visitors and locals alike!

lipton seat is absolutely beautiful and offers an amazing view! i visited from haputale town for the first time, and the road to get there is one of the most scenic routes i’ve ever traveled. the road has steep climbs, sharp 180-degree bends, and is quite narrow in many places. there are a few small spots where vehicles can pass each other, so you need to be a skilled and patient driver. some three-wheeler drivers will tell you that the road gets too narrow about 7–8 km from the top and try to convince you to take a tuk-tuk—but if you trust your driving, you can go all the way yourself. i drove a 2017 panda cross and had no issues. even smaller cars like the wagon r can make it to the top. only the last 1–1.5 km is a bit rough with some bumpy, stone-covered patches, but it’s still manageable with care. the road winds through beautiful tea gardens and has a calm, peaceful vibe. some people choose to walk, which is also a great option if you have time. there’s a real sense of serenity here—please help protect the environment while you enjoy it. definitely worth a visit if you’re traveling to haputale

little adam's peak viewpoint, ella - a must-visit for stunning panoramic views little adam's peak in ella is one of the most popular and rewarding hikes in the area, offering breathtaking panoramic views that are well worth the effort. named after the sacred adam's peak due to its similar shape, little adam's peak is much easier to climb, making it accessible to most visitors. the hike to the viewpoint is relatively short and straightforward, taking about 30-45 minutes from the base. the trail is well-marked and winds through tea plantations, adding to the scenic beauty of the journey. as you ascend, the views gradually open up, revealing the lush green valleys, rolling hills, and distant mountain ranges. once you reach the top, the 360-degree view is truly spectacular. you can see ella rock, the ella gap, and on a clear day, even the distant southern coast of sri lanka. the sunrise and sunset from this point are particularly magical, with the sky painting the landscape in hues of orange, pink, and gold. little adam's peak is an ideal spot for nature lovers, photographers, and anyone looking to experience the natural beauty of ella. whether you're an avid hiker or just looking for a leisurely walk with a rewarding view, this viewpoint is a must-visit during your stay in ella.

little petra is one of the hidden gems when exploring the ancient city of petra. it is located in the bayda village around 9 kms north of the petra visitor’s center. it is considered one of three official entrances into the ancient rose city. it is said that this place was the “industrial” part of the nabatean civilization where white wine and currency were made. the place consists of a small siq and a small treasury. the walking path is straight, and is 1 km long. the place consists mainly of chambers on the ground floor and a lower floor, as well as stairs to go up. most of the stairs on the right/left side are wiped, and it is recommended not to climb most of them. you pass through many chambers, pass through a souvenir tent, then climb stairs up to another tent. this second tent; another souvenir store, is the end of this walking trail. if you are into hiking, little petra has a hiking trail that leads to the monastery. the trail starts by riding a 4x4 (for a fee) to go to the start of this trail. then, you walk for around 4 kms before you arrive at the monastery. the trail involves stairs and muddy terrain, and walking close to cliff edges; thus caution is recommended (mainly if you are hiking with kids). once you arrive at the monastery, you either return back to the drop-off point, or you continue to qasr albint in the petra ancient city (another 3-3.5 km). if you decide to return back to the drop-off point, ask about the timings of the 4x4 car so that it takes you back to little petra. the hiking trail is quite clear either through stairs, or through a drawn path (using rocks). thus, having a guide isn’t necessary. the walking trail is served with small kiosks that sell drinks and snacks. some folks sell souvenirs, and you may bump into folks who offer donkey rides for a fee. make sure you have cash on you to pay as most don’t accept credit cards. entering little petra is free, but riding the 4x4 car to the start of the hiking trail comes with a fee. you can also buy tickets for the petra ancient city here, and they accept cash or card payment.

little western wall, also known as hakotel hakatanand the small kotel, is a jewish religious site located in the muslim quarter of the old city of jerusalem near the iron gate to the temple mount. the wall itself dates from the second temple period, (516 bce – 70 ce). it is the continuation of the larger part of the western wall and almost exactly faces the holy of holies. hakotel hakatan is not as well-known and not as crowded as the larger part of the western wall. this section of the wall is of deep spiritual significance because of its close proximity to the holy of holies. however, it is not the closest location to the holy of holies, as there is a location in the western wall tunnel which directly faces the holy of holies.

located about 45 km from the center of hanoi, duong lam ancient village is a destination for tourists who want to find old memories, admire the peaceful and rustic life. this place preserves well the characteristics of the old northern countryside with banyan trees, water wharves, communal houses, etc., ancient houses with unique architecture built with laterite and ironwood pillars. duong lam ancient village is the hometown of ngo quyen and phung hung, so it is called "the land of two kings". in 2006, duong lam was honored to become the first ancient village in our country and was awarded the national historical and cultural relic certificate by the state. in duong lam, there are many ancient pagodas with a long history and sophisticated architecture such as mia pagoda, on pagoda, etc. it is a pity that the ancient village is not preserved systematically and comprehensively. if it continues to develop in this direction, it may gradually lose its ancient character. a large enterprise is needed to plan, restore and preserve this relic.

located at 55 music concourse dr, san francisco, this museum is a standout destination that combines science, sustainability, and immersive design. inside, you’ll find a world-class aquarium, a planetarium with rotating shows, a four-story rainforest dome, and natural history exhibits—all under a living roof covered in native plants. the layout is intuitive, and interactive displays make it engaging for all ages. it’s a place where education meets wonder, and every corner offers something new to explore. beyond the public exhibits, the academy is also a working research institute, with scientists conducting studies in biodiversity, climate, and ocean health. the museum’s commitment to conservation is reflected in its programs and partnerships. whether you're watching penguins feed, walking through a butterfly-filled rainforest, or learning about tectonic plates, the experience is both inspiring and informative.

located at parkring 1, 1010 vienna, austria 🇦🇹 this is an amazingly huge park in vienna that extends from the ringstraße in the innere stadt first district up to the heumarkt (hay market) in the landstraße third district. the park is divided in two sections by the wienfluss (vienna river), and has a total surface area of 65,000 square metres (28 acres). scattered throughout the park are statues of famous viennese artists, writers, and composers. the opulent kursalon building on johannesgasse, with its broad terrace that reaches into the park, is the site of popular waltz concerts. there’s some beautiful sights to see throughout the park besides the statues for example the johann strauss monument and many others not to mention the fantastic flora which is planted, according to it’s species, to bloom at all times of the year. the park first opened in 1862. it’s also family friendly as there is a picnic area and basketball hoops and ramps for skateboarders. it’s all wheelchair accessible and a perfect spot to chill out on a hot day. we spent approximately four 4️⃣ hours just slowly exploring the ponds and generally enjoying everything the park had to offer. it was a great visit and would definitely recommend it to anyone. thumbs up!!! 👍👍👍

located at punta sur, the park celebrating mayan heritage boast the eastern most tip of mexico and the first to welcome the sun each morning. the sunrise did not disappoint nor did the spectacular cliffside views of the caribbean sea. we were also graced by the large sea turtles along the shoreline. hiking is easy going and the spray of the sea makes the experience all the more enjoyable. be sure to bring some cash to donate at the park entrance.

located at schonbrunn palace park, 1130 vienna, austria 🇦🇹. i highly recommend purchasing tickets online before going to avoid the long waiting times. admission is fixed admission times. we paid for the grand tour which included an audio guide. i liked this as i could go at my own pace. we explored the entire piano nobile of the palace: in addition to the private apartments of franz joseph and elisabeth, the south-facing reception rooms and the state apartments. we also got to see the rooms occupied by maria theresa. it was fantastic. this cost €32.00 which i think was quite reasonable. children are €23.00. there’s also the imperial tour which cost €27.00 for adults and €19.00 for children. this also includes audio guide. there’s other tours available on the website. one hundred and thirteen metres long, the palm house consists of a 28-metre high central pavilion and two lateral pavilions which are three metres lower. linked by tunnel-like passages, the pavilions contain different climatic zones: a ‘cold’ house to the north, a temperate zone in the central pavilion and a tropical zone in the south pavilion. the building itself is work of art, simply beautiful and inside is magnificent, so lovely to just explore and take in the beauty of all the stunning greenery. after exploring everything including the gardens, the palace etc we were there for practically the whole day. we took our time exploring. we had lunch at one of the cafes that is there, the food was delicious. there’s a large selection of places to choose from. we did a lot of walking and i definitely recommend wearing comfortable shoes. overall, the palm house was amazing, i truly loved it. would definitely recommend. thumbs up!!! 👍👍👍

located at the center of plaza de la revolución square in the vedado area of havana, the josé martí memorial stands as an iconic landmark. this impressive monument measures 142 meters in height and 78.50 meters in diameter, making it the tallest structure in havana. it consists of a star shaped tower, a statue of marti surrounded by six columns, and gardens. its grandeur serves as a testament to the profound admiration cubans hold for their national hero. upon arriving at the square at noon, we encountered sweltering heat, limiting our stay for long period. regrettably this constrained us from visiting the museum and observatory tower. next time then. for future reference, it is advisable to plan visits during the morning or evening when temperatures are more tolerable. guided tours in english are available without charge, with the expectation of a tip.

located close to wat ratchabophit, trok mo market (open from 5am to 10am) is one of my favorite morning destinations. if you want a slice old bangkok, and feel the warmth and charm of a well established thai-chinese community, trok mo is the place to go. besides a great array of food - basically every thai dish going and baked goodies - the market also has clothing, home gadgets, and sneaker stalls. being close to the temple, many monks also walk though the market receiving alms from locals. like most great places and experiences, it’s the people that make the place and i’m always charmed by the vendors in this market. “come again, you are welcome like this is your home” was one memorable line expressed to us during our last visit. the human touch can’t be replicated by ai and it’s a great reason to visit this gem of a market - they keep it real at trok mo, you gotta love it and long may they run!

located in a cozy complex that is modern and chic, aga khan provides a glimpse into the islamic culture and traditional art that is both astonishingly stunning and intellectually inspiring. we spent the afternoon in the museum and learnt a lot of about the culture. the permanent exhibition brings artefacts from around the world into the building, with many approaching a thousand years of age and still preserved in very good condition. we were slightly disappointed from the fact that the collection is quite limited, and i wasn’t sure if there is a particular story telling in how the museum collection is planned. it was by region and i feel like i did not learn a lot about how islam was developed in each region and the contrast and the similarity. the special exhibition we saw was from the calligraphy and we did learn more about the specifics of it, but some of the information was overlapped with the permanent exhibition. overall it was a joyful 1-2 hour visit but it wasn’t a whole afternoon activity.

located in the building of tokyo mid town, the museum has about 2 floors of exhibition. mostly, they are those prestigious artifects involving people's everyday's life, including trunk, ceramics, glass and room separator, aligning with the fundamental concept of "art in life." i like the western kings on horseback as this masterpiece is an early example of western-style painting in japan. the painting refers to an image on the margin of a world map published in amsterdam, magnified, colored, and finished in this large format. the kings are said to be, from the right, the king of persia, the king of ethiopia, and henry iv of france. the identify of the figure on the far left is disputed, with the king of england. this piece also represents how japan connected to the outside world and how miraculous it survive through the tokyo bomb in ww ii.

located in the city’s east, this is a beloved neighborhood park known for its strong sense of community and cultural integration. originally designed in the late 19th century by l.a. springer, only the southern section—with its lawns, tree clusters, and small pond—was completed, while the northern area remained undeveloped for decades. between 2010 and 2018, the park underwent a major redesign led by buro sant en co, aiming to improve connectivity, accessibility, and integration with the surrounding urban fabric.

located in the heart of vienna, austria, the botanic garden, originally known as the hortus botanicus vindobonensis, is a verdant oasis brimming with natural wonders. steeped in history dating back to its establishment in 1754, this enchanting garden offers a captivating journey through time and biodiversity. as i strolled through its winding pathways, i was immersed in a tapestry of vibrant colors and fragrant aromas. from exotic orchids to towering palm trees, the garden boasts a diverse collection of plant species from around the globe, each with its own fascinating story to tell. one cannot help but marvel at the garden's rich heritage, which has witnessed the advancements of botanical science over the centuries. it has served as a haven for scholars and nature enthusiasts alike, fostering a deeper understanding of the natural world. whether you're a seasoned botanist or simply seeking solace amidst lush greenery, the botanic garden in vienna offers an unforgettable experience for all. i thoroughly enjoyed my visit and left with a newfound appreciation for the beauty and complexity of plant life. truly, it's a must-see attraction for anyone exploring the cultural treasures of vienna.

located in the hemis national park, ladakh, india, hemis monastery is a significant cultural and spiritual center. hemis monastery was founded in the 11th century by lama tsongkhapa, the founder of the gelugpa tradition. the monastery belongs to the gelugpa tradition of tibetan buddhism. hemis monastery is an important cultural heritage site, showcasing the region's rich history and traditions. the monastery features a mix of ladakhi and tibetan architectural styles. the monastery is adorned with beautiful mural paintings depicting buddhist deities and mythological scenes. the monastery houses several important statues and artifacts, including a large statue of the buddha. the monastery celebrates the hemis festival, a two-day festival featuring masked dances and sacred rituals. celebrated in june or july, the festival showcases the rich cultural heritage of the region. the festival features masked dances, depicting various buddhist deities and mythological characters. hemis monastery is located 45 km from leh, in the hemis national park. the best time to visit hemis monastery is during the summer months (june to september). the monastery is accessible by road from leh.

located just behind the fort york historic site, the fort york visitor centre is a must-visit destination for history enthusiasts and curious minds alike! what sets it apart is that it offers more than just history; it covers a range of engaging topics such as fashion, covid-19, and the arts. the visitor centre at fort york houses an impressive exhibit space, including a 2,900 square foot exhibit gallery. one of the highlights is the 'immersive experience' exhibit that takes visitors through the events leading up to the battle of york and the explosion of the fort's grand magazine. i highly recommend visiting the visitor centre, especially if you've already explored the nearby heritage site. it provides a fantastic opportunity to delve deeper into various subjects in a comfortable indoor setting. during our visit, we did encounter a minor setback as some of the audio and video devices were not functioning properly, which limited our participation in the exhibition. however, despite this small hiccup, the overall experience was still remarkable. if you're looking for an amazing indoor experience that goes beyond traditional historical exhibitions, the fort york visitor centre is the place to be. don't miss the opportunity to explore the fascinating displays and learn something new!

located next to bukit timah nature reserve, hindhede nature park offers an easy, family-friendly escape into nature. originally a granite quarry, the park has been transformed into a scenic retreat with gentle walking trails, lush greenery, and the picturesque hindhede quarry as its highlight. the quarry lookout provides a peaceful view of the reflective waters, making it a great spot for photography or quiet relaxation. the park features a well-maintained playground, including a nature-inspired climbing structure, slides, and swings, which makes it a fun stop for families with children. the trails are mostly flat and shaded, ideal for a leisurely stroll or a short nature walk without the need for strenuous hiking. along the way, you can also catch glimpses of monkeys in the trees, adding to the natural experience. with its serene ambiance and accessible paths, hindhede nature park is a lovely destination for those looking to connect with nature without venturing too far from the city.

located on ford island, non-dod id cardholders will need to take the free shuttle bus from pearl harbor visitor center. if your a dod id cardholder, you can drive your pov across the bridge. they do have security personnel there to check ids before you cross. once at the museum, there is a dignified memorial to the crew of the uss oklahoma who were lost on dec 7, 1941 just outside of the entrance to the uss missouri. the dock area is wheelchair accessible but not on the ship. the dock area has a souvenir shop, small eatery, outdoor tables, and the ticket booth. once on the ship, you can take the group guided tour or go on your own. if you fo the latter, you won't get lost because there are plenty of directional signs on the bulkheads and others waking around you. the length of the tour depends on how much you want to see. few notes: - military and retirees get discount on tickets - there are a lot of ladders, a few tripping hazards when you walk through bulkhead hatches, and a lot of walking. - free parking if you drive your own vehicle across. - like many tourist locations, they have you take a group photo where you can buy an assortment of selections at the end of your tour.

located on the way up to the monastery, the façade of the lion triclinium is decorated with a doric frieze with the head of medusa at each end. above the doorway there is a circular window now eroded so that door and window join forming a keyhole, and over the pediment there is an urn. in the interior, there are three benches (hence the name triclinium). the lion triclinium dates back to the first century ad, and its name is due to the two lions carved at the base of the façade. the lions are symbols of the vegetation goddess atargatis. a baetyl in a niche is carved to the left of the doorway possibly representing the main nabatean male deity dushara (see review image). if you are hiking up to the monastery, a small detour to this triclinium is well worth it. you will suddenly be away from the marching crowds and quite possibly find yourself all alone marveling at this secluded marvel within petra.

loch fleet and littleferry. absolutely stunning places to stop for a picnic, to admire the views to break up a long journey to inverness or the highlands or part of a day out in the area. loch fleet is near dornoch/embo. it is a huge sea loch with a beautiful mountain back drop. great place to see seals and a variety of wild birds. seals can be seen swimming in the waters or basking on the sand banks when the tide is out/incoming. lots of wading birds, oyster catchers, ducks, geese, curlew, gulls etc. just over the dornoch bridge is a turning to littleferry. this is the other side of the loch where an old water mill is situated and a small dock where ferries used to run from. the drive will take you through a long stretch of wooded area until you reach the end. no vehicle access to the mill but i think you can walk it on foot (private road). littleferry has a small white beach and gorgeous blue waters. very tropical looking. it is nestled into a small area of houses hidden away. no facilities here either. we did try fishing here but were robbed of our bait, fishing rod and reel by a passing seal. that was an expensive trip out that day. along loch fleet there are several parking areas (please don't park in the passing places as it's a single track road) and an area with a couple of benches and bins (please put your rubbish in them or take with you). it is kept clean and tidy and a lovely place to stop. does get very busy with motorhomes and camper vans though. the road is very busy so be careful if you have small children. no facilities here (no toilets or shops), nearest are in embo. no fishing, wild swimming, kayaking or collecting ragworm etc here as it's a protected area rspb. there are also the castle ruins of skelbo. (skelbo castle is a ruined 14th century keep, located near dornoch, sutherland, scotland. the remaining wall is best preserved at the northern side of the castle. the remains are protected as a scheduled monument). well worth a stop off. there have not been many occasions whereby i have not seen a seal. 🙂🦭

loch lomond is another heavenly beauties of scotland. it has towering mountains, glittering lochs, dense woodlands and several islands. here, you can see the mountains are kissing the water and the sky at the same time. you will see unreal beauty, if you visit on a bright sunny day. very close to balloch railway station. the river cruise is a must, where you will enjoy the water, stunning mountain views and several islands in the journey. perfect weekend trip for your family. the kids will enjoy the fullest. we took the silver dolphin cruise which was amazing. a must visit place, if you are in edinburgh or glasgow.

lofoten islands completely exceeded our expectations—five days felt far too short to take in everything this magical place has to offer. we explored a variety of locations, each with its own unique charm and beauty. starting in svolvær, we hiked up to djevelporten, where the views over the town and fjords were absolutely stunning. the sherpa steps made the climb manageable, though a bit steep, but totally worth it for the scenery. we also visited henningsvær and its famous football field, which sits right by the ocean with a backdrop of small islands and dramatic mountain peaks. the town itself was cozy and full of character. eggum offered a peaceful coastal walk with wide views of the sea and sky, while haukland and uttakleiv beaches gave us some of the most beautiful sunsets we’ve ever seen—plus, we even spotted whales in the distance! we hiked to kvalvika beach, a hidden gem surrounded by cliffs and soft sand. though we didn’t camp, it’s on our list for next time. we also did the hanen hike, along with several shorter trails in the area. every place was a mix of adventure and serenity. lofoten is unforgettable—absolutely worth the trip. 😍🇳🇴

london city cruises is a fantastic way to see the city from a whole new perspective. the experience was smooth, fun, and full of great sights along the thames. the crew were absolutely amazing – friendly, funny, and full of interesting facts about the landmarks as you sail by. they really added to the atmosphere and made the trip memorable. it’s also great value for money, especially if you buy a day family ticket, which lets you hop on and off the boat throughout the day. it’s perfect for sightseeing at your own pace and ideal for families or groups who want to explore different parts of london without the stress of the tube or buses. the boats are comfortable and offer both open-air seating and indoor areas, so you can enjoy the trip in any weather. if you're visiting london, this is a must-do activity – fun, relaxing, and a brilliant way to experience the city's iconic river!

london eye river cruise offers unique thames perspective with informative commentary about historic landmarks. our guide was very knowledgeable and engaging. the 40-minute journey passes westminster, tower bridge, and shakespeare's globe while providing excellent photo opportunities. weather can affect enjoyment, so dress appropriately. great combination with london eye visit for comprehensive sightseeing experience.

london eye river cruise – a wonderful experience! the london eye river cruise was a very nice and informative experience. it offers a great opportunity to see all the major landmarks along the river thames. the highlight of the trip was the live commentary by hannah, who seemed to have in-depth knowledge and made the journey even more engaging. the cruise lasted about an hour, and it was definitely worth it. it was not only educational but also a relaxing way to enjoy the sights of london. i’m glad we got the opportunity to experience it and spend some quality time with family.

london museum docklands is a fantastic place to visit! the museum is child-friendly, with plenty of interactive exhibits and events—we visited on a saturday, and there was a special event happening. entry is free, and it was great to see so many families and kids enjoying themselves. the museum is well-organised across multiple levels, with clear directions and maps to guide you. the galleries are fascinating, offering a deep dive into the rich history of the docklands and london in general. there’s also a nice café on the ground floor for a break. highly recommend for history lovers and families alike!

long overdue review for mantastic scuba yves! wehad the most incredible experience with mantastic scuba at raja ampat! the professionalism of yves, the owner, truly set the tone for an unforgettable adventure. from the moment we arrived, it was clear that safety and customer satisfaction were their top priorities. the equipment was brand new and top-notch, and their boat was not only spacious and comfortable but also equipped with music speakers, adding a fun vibe to the journey. one of the most memorable aspects was that my girlfriend, who has always been afraid of the ocean, completed her open water certification with them. the patience, encouragement, and expertise of the team helped her overcome her fears and achieve something she never thought possible. it was an emotional and rewarding moment for both of us. the diving itself was spectacular. raja ampat’s untouched marine ecosystem is a diver’s dream, with vibrant soft corals and an abundance of marine life. exploring these pristine waters alongside such a friendly and welcoming group of people made the experience even more special. we can’t thank yves and the mantastic scuba team enough for creating such a wonderful experience. we’ll always treasure the memories we made here, and i know we’ll be back someday for more adventures. highly recommended for anyone seeking world-class diving and exceptional service!

long story short - this was the most memorable experience i have ever had at any marriott, or hotel in general (as a frequent traveler, marriott ambassador with 150+ nights last year). every single staff member here is absolutely fantastic and ensures you have a memorable, personalized experience. before we arrived, they helped ensure our travels would be seamless, and were very willing to accommodate any specific requests (it was our honeymoon, and we were given a lovely honeymoon suite that included a personal pool). thank you to wilson and the rest of the front desk team for that. the main experience - the safari, is flexible in how you enjoy it - your driver will work with you to schedule game drives based on what you want (later morning, longer drives, eating breakfast in the bush, etc.). the land cruiser's the jw uses are absolutely state of the art, and the best you'll see going through the masai mara. the reserve is one of the few places in the world you can see all big 5 / big 9 / etc. in one day, and your guides will know where to go on any given day to help you find the action. shout out to eric for being extremely personable and giving us the perfect game drive every day, and teaching us many things about the animals we saw and general life in kenya. additionally - the food is great, you will have a server who is with you for the entirety of our trip (we were lucky to have killian, who made every meal a fun time), and you can always ask for custom items with enough notice. the drinks are very high quality as well (victor, the doctor is your bartender - request the signature masai mara). the room is always immaculate, and they do a great job of maintaining it when you are on your drives / eating (thank you james). the canon studio is an amazing perk, with the camera/lens you are given allowing for excellent quality photos, and they will even help you with editing afterwards (felix also gave some great coaching to help improve our photography skills). overall - if you are looking for a memorable once in a lifetime experience, do not think twice and book the stay at the jw masai mara, you absolutely won't regret it.

lots of fun with sea vancouver and captain connor! we did the city & nature tour and the whole experience was great from the very beginning, starting with the booking process, with the team from sea vancouver answering all our questions and advising us on the best tour for our group. the day of our tour the weather was beautiful, with clear blue skies and warm temperatures, but the conditions on the sea were a bit rough due to strong winds. we were informed of this prior to the tour and still chose to go ahead with it. we couldn’t be happier we did so. our captain, connor, was super skilled and made us feel safe at all times. because of the windy conditions, the ride was bumpy, but very fun. like a rollercoaster on water. we got to see lots of things, to name a few: the ships in english bay, the beautiful houses along west vancouver, a couple of small rocky islands with seals chilling on them, spanish banks and kitsilano, and the vancouver skyline with mount baker in the background as we headed back. we did this tour with a group of friends visiting from abroad, and from a trip packed with lots of cool activities, this probably was the one we enjoyed the most. we recommend it 100% and would repeat it any time! a couple of final notes: - we were lucky seeing mount baker. this is possible only on days with clear skies, so don’t take that view for granted. - if it’s windy, like the day we did the tour, be ready to get wet, even if you are wearing those fancy floatation suits (very cool-looking, lifesaving, but not waterproof).

loved the saturday street market. lots of local vendors with many crafts. up close at the docks and boats. dramatic views of the surrounding mountains. of course many places to eat. enjoy this wonderful park and surroundings in any season. this evening we will take a cruise on the historic t. s. s. earnslaw.
loved the sculptures, the room upstairs had very interesting acoustic as well as natural imagery formed along the wall.

loved the steps! beautiful and such artistic mosaic creations, i cannot wait to go back and climb them all over again! in addition, the place was quiet, nearly deserted, and offers a fantastic birds eye view of the setting with the urban skyline in the background and the ocean on the west side

loved the theatre! went here to watch hadestown and had an amazing time!!! we had seats on the balcony which was unfortunately a climb up stairs that were kind of steep but was still fine! this was the view from our seats, could definitely still see the stage perfectly clear which was 🤩
loved the thrill. definitely something i would love to do again. i also loved that they used degradable plates and utensils to serve their meals
loved the viatour thames river tour with live commentary. local flavor. very entertaining.

loved the vibe at minibar. the music, the drinks and more importantly the service was on point. shout out to trent and willy who took very good care of us at the bar. the mango margarita was delicious!

loved the vibrant art scene, handmade jewelry shops, and breathtaking views of the surrounding red rocks. the village is home to over 40 art galleries and studios, showcasing an impressive array of local and international artists. from paintings and sculptures to pottery and glasswork, the diversity of art on display is staggering. a beautiful courtyard, which features a stunning fountain and plenty of seating areas, adds to the charm. def must visit!
loved the view from balcony area it's 10 dinar to climb up. go in morning for the best light.
loved the view from balcony area it's 10 dinar to climb up. go in morning for the best light.

loved the viewpoint of pedra bonita, it’s an amazing place to see all of rio and catch the sunset. be aware that if you go at sunset it’s dark to get back down, and it’s not easy to get an uber back, you have to walk the road a long bit back.

loved the walk i had last evening. pleasant. 10mins short walk from mapletree business city mbc. get in touch w nature after a stressful day at work, breathe fresh air and clock some steps b4 day ends. park is well maintained, clean, some mosquitoes but not that much that it’s unbearable. there are a few nurseries too.

loved these baths, low key vibe. the views were breath taking with the infinity pool effect. easy to grab drinks. several pools with different temperatures with the hottest one by the bar. electronic wristband lockers to keep all your stuff safe. a must visit if you are husavik!

loved this area. it's a very popular "kiez" in berlin (kiez is a berliner term for specific neighborhood within a neighborhood). felt very local, non-touristy, with lots of families, restaurants, parks, and on thursdays (when i was there) and saturdays, it hosts a very popular outdoor organic market. also, it's the neighborhood where artist kathe kollwitz lived and worked. note: the very same kathe kollwitz who will be the subject of a major show at moma next year.
loved this beach except there isn’t any shade so you have to bring your own. most people with tents were respectful and set up at the back. there’s a trail on the east side to walk along.

loved this bluegate boat tour! logistics were perfect and the crew was informative and friendly. we went straight from arriving at the airport, had lunch at a cute cafe nearby and got right to exploring the faroe islands. we saw puffins! highly recommend!
loved this community space. vancouver needs more like it. super friendly staff and a fantastic mango kombucha

loved this experience! the pools were all natural and set into the rocks and beach. the mountains around it were stunning and so picturesque! the tubs weren’t too hot - a good mix of warm and hot. definitely recommend doing a cold plunge in the ocean and warming up again in the baths. few people carried around their towel (it was summer) and there was nowhere to really hang them up at each bath. suggest leaving it in the change room so it is really dry when you are all done. bring flip flops for sure. we didn’t use the swim up drinks window but the service and drinks looked great. we did have lunch there afterwards and wow - the food was so so good! both of our dishes - the vegan soup and the avocado toast - were surprisingly high quality with really yum flavour profiles. delicious! highly recommend! hidden gem. worth the drive!

loved this experience! we took the cable car to the top and hiked to bachalpsee — the lake was still partially frozen. there are several options to go back down, but unfortunately, they were all sold out except for the cable car, which we ended up taking again. if you really want to try one of the other activities for the way down, i recommend buying tickets in advance. or, you can always choose to hike!

loved this experience.. 20-30mins or so (by car) from sabang. great value for the experience, nice forest walk and then some caving walking and a few easy ladders to eventually end up at zip line. i’ve been on a few zip lines and this one was pretty cool…
loved this free small museum. great japanese contemporary art and not crowded early march.

loved this hotel and the grounds. our room was the perfect size and had an amazing view of the volcano! the food was good at the restaurant and we enjoyed the night tour and natural history walk. we saw a lot of animals on-site and our kids became skilled at spotting them. all the staff was fried and very helpful. a few tips: there is no ac but a small battery operated fan was great to help dry things (without everything stays a bit damp - they have laundry service). bring binoculars and a flashlight for spotting animals. there is a lot to do in the area but leave at least a day to explore the grounds at aol - the waterfall is beautiful. slow down when visiting.

loved this local park. we were staying about 2 blocks away. it was a great find. we even packed a picnic and spent the afternoon like the locals. there was a lovely playground where our son played for hours. plenty of shaded spots under trees, there is a lovely carousel and canteen too
loved this market and this neighborhood. it was filled with adorable bookshops, shops, and on saturdays they have a farmers market and i got roadside oysters!! so lovely. reminds me of park slope.

loved this museum! the cycladic figurines are super unique and the whole place is really well curated. it’s not too big, so it’s easy to take your time and really enjoy the art. the building is gorgeous too, especially the neoclassical part. definitely worth a stop if you're into ancient art or just want something a bit different in athens.

loved this place for caring about elephants and offering those fun tours where we fed and washed elephants. we were given instructions on what to do and what not, and had a great time interacting with these wonderful animals. washing them with brushes was a special experience for sure, they enjoyed it! be sure to wear a swim suit for this activity - you will be all wet!
loved this place to hike. the views both from on the way and the top were amazing (in clear weather). and yes, it can be done only within 2-3 hours.

loved this place. i went with my son's and their friends for a birthday party. i joined in on the game. definitely 5 stars as it's a unique experience. everyone enjoyed themselves and raved about it. i would have been better for those watching if they served more non alcoholic drinks like coffee etc. but, as a gaming experience it was top tier. i would recommend it, and go again.

loved this place. so much less commercial than bear world. they don't even compare. we went in the late afternoon which i would not suggest as it was hot and a lot of the animals were hiding in the shade but we still saw everything. the foxes are amazing. really all of the animals were awesome. the staff is super friendly and very knowledgeable. well worth the drive and time to go see.

loved this place. we went with a guide so we had only 20 minutes to get inside the lagoon, so if you want to enjoy it more i definitely recommend going solo, without a guide. it’s not far from the city at all. the water is cold but i personally didn’t find it freezing like people told me it was. it’s so nice to just be floating there. bring your towels with your if you’re planning to get in, they have a place where you can shower (no soap or anything, just water) you have a limit time in the shower as well, but it’s time enough to get the salt out of your skin. i recommend to slick your hair back or else it will be like a stone lol.
loved this spot! the pink iguana is such a relaxed beach bar with awesome music, super friendly staff, and the drinks are good. great vibes all around, perfect place to hang out and unwind.

loved this tour! we did a group adventure with andrés and the sights were unbeatable. secluded with breathtaking views of waterfall and native foliage. cliff jumping may be challenging for some but the best part of the tour! andres is super chill and encouraging, and you can sit things out if needed. super cool, authentic experience

loved this trail! much less crowded than most areas of the park. skip the section that goes along the road, it’s weird and unnecessary. i went clockwise and recommend that direction. there is a lot to see: different sections of the river, the hoodoos, the forest, the lookouts, the landscape, so many cool things!
loved this! the staff were friendly and the boat was clean with a well stocked bar which also serves snacks. the band were really good and added to the great experience.

loved this. such great fun, well organised, easy pick up arrangements etc. highly recommend. only thing i would say, is you could lose the tea stop. the journey back to base after this is a short one, so it didn't feel necessary

loved this. will definitely do again. i’d say it’s not accessible so if you can’t do stairs or you have a stroller it’s not ideal. but if you can’t the sights are amazing. you’ll see whales and seals and beautiful rock formations. the path is pretty easy to moderate. a lovely time. and finish it with a dip in the sea and a beer.

loved visiting here and showing my kids the wonders of this earth! the geyser erupts about every hour and 20 minutes. so if you miss it... don't worry! just stick around for a while (visit the visitors' center and watch the movie, etc.). i was worried about getting a good viewing location for watching old faithful but there is plenty of room for everyone, and we were there in july.

loved visiting this gem in the middle of the city! a beautiful garden to explore around the property. the tour was free and the best part. the tour guide did a fantastic job explaining the history of the house with some humour. highly recommend.

loved visiting this gem in the middle of the city! a beautiful garden to explore around the property. the tour was free and the best part. the tour guide did a fantastic job explaining the history of the house with some humour. highly recommend.

loved visiting this ruin unsupervised but we'll maintained. definitely worth the hike (6km in total) from interlaken. right on the river's edge in the forest, metal steps allow to reach the top for a lovely view.

loved visiting this site! so much to see. i particularly enjoyed the links with paul and his time in athens- something i hadn't considered at all. fascinating seeing the changes over time, the additions and reductions, as well as the sites that represented so much that is central to greek religious and democratic history- seeing actual ostrska in the museum and the balloting 'machine' for jury duty will both stick in my memory. amazing to see the temple of hephaestus in such good condition too. more could have been made of the opportunities presented by all of this though: the museum shop was a shocker. even the ladies behind the desk- constituting almost the entirety of it- looked surprised when i walked in.
