lovely 3h private yacht cruise to dubai‘s most interesting places like marina, jbr, palm, atlantis, burj al arab, madinat jumeirah hotels and a romantic sunset. captain aravind and team took care about our wellbeing, children and parents were happy. we had some beverages and food as well and could play some music playlists on a gigantic jbl speaker. surely a recommendation and a bucket list item.

lovely and beautiful... the "fake greek temple" is at least 200 years old, so it doesn't feel fake or modern. watch out for mosquitoes if you come in the evening. there is a small parking lot around the south side, parking is 30 pesos and the guys are extremely friendly and helpful - they will watch your car or motorcycle and give you directions if you need it
lovely and clean beach, lots of food options when you walk down the beach. lost count of volleyball courts and enthusiasts #fun

lovely and cozy museum + beer hall. the former site of the yebisu brewery in tokyo. the museum exhibits are free to view for yourself, or you can book a paid guided tour online in advance. very nice for anyone interested in japanese beer and history. the beer hall feels spacious but cozy. the beers on tap are a bit more expensive than the might be elsewhere, but they are some premium and or limited release brews, delicious and perfectly poured and all have a nice description on the menu.

lovely and nice but not my favorite. the plants around the fountain could use more upkeep but in the grand scheme of things, places like this in paris are beautiful. i had a lovely walk and sought refuge in the shade of trees as it got uncomfortably hot.

lovely and spacious mall right across yeongdeungpo station. within the mall there are many food options catering to different tastes. importantly there is a large supermarket making it convenient for shoppers wishing to buy home wares.
lovely area, busy every night with family entertainment. really nice. just watch the main road next you it.. its very dangerous

lovely area, great for a coffee in the day and it's beautiful at night with all the lights from the surrounding buildings. handy spot for the hop on hop off buses too. it's a shame so many shops have closed, the area doesn't feel as exciting anymore especially since westfield mall is gone. still worth a visit and to see the tram start.

lovely artistic work of art depicting honolulu’s king kamehameha. gold and black standing proudly is the king across the street from the great palace and hawaii’s united states customs and courthouse. located in the heart of the business downtown district. it’s a must stop to see the statue and surrounding landscape of native hawaiian trees and palms.

lovely arts museum with a great selection of new comers and established artists. especially the robbie williams arts collection was a welcome and lovely surprise. i liked the audio guide for free a lot! sometimes a bit more information would have been appreciated. oh and securities that ask people to step away from art. art was touched several times for the purpose of selfies..

lovely atmosphere with good views just outside the walls of old city. was with a group and we did 3 wine tastings. the ongoing story encompasses both the history of israel and the history of israeli wine. i like sweeter wine so really enjoyed the tastings (with a cheese platter).

lovely authentic murano glass shop and the sweetest little shop owner, he makes all items himself. he doesn't speak english, but we made do with google translate. i bought a bunch of glass candies and was shocked by the low price. i actually hope he increases pricing because his pieces are beautiful, and he deserves to charge much more than all the tourist traps with glass from china around.
lovely beach with calm waters. could see many turtles and some sharks while free diving.
lovely beach with calm waters. could see many turtles and some sharks while free diving.
lovely beach with white sands torques sea with no algi and nice place to catch the sun setting. easy access on hop on hop off bus service which is very regular

lovely beach, went for several swims, but has mainly pebbles not much sand , i did not see any lifeguards , not sure if they were there . has a restaurant and bar and you can hire umbrellas and loungers.

lovely big area to sit and they now have a lake filled to the top! very relaxing on a sunny day, the baths were good. we spent roughly an hour here. lots of chairs about. i would recommend going on the first sunday of the month as it’s free.

lovely boat and experience cruising the seine and seeing all of the paris sites. the captain and skipper were amazing and very knowledgeable-- their love of paris and the river were obvious. highly recommend!

lovely boat tour. secured, enjoyed. i was giving 2 bottle of wine after the tour. the best sea tour i have been. we went to all the attraction site. alexandro is so nice and friendly. he explained all the attraction site to me. bulano, mulano and so on. gulia always respond to message quickly and she's lovely. she also give me discount . thanks gulia and alexandro
lovely calm area to kayak and friendly staff

lovely castle worth visit. i recommend to buy audio guide too. overcrowded however it's well organized at the entrance. it's good to buy a ticket online with a time slot in advance and then just go straight to the entrance skipping all that huge queue in front of ticket office. as for gardens from april you need to pay additional €10, (€9 for kids) to see it. the gardens plus parc are huge so if you are tired of walking you can just rent a golf car or wait for a little train that goes to all interesting sites. there are few takeaways and restaurants there too. the gardens and parc are well kept however it wasn't breathtaking for me. at least not in april.

lovely club. great atmosphere. i saw the amazing coloseum there. the size of the place makes the show very intimate. there are sitting tickets and standing tickets, which are simply- stand wherever you want as long as you don't block the view to anyone. if you are not standing or seating next to the bar, it will be almost impossible to get a drink once the show had started. i've had a lovely evening there.

lovely coffee house, a unique mix of old school furniture and flair combined with light filled rooms with high ceilings, lovely vibe. ample outside seating as well, inside you can also find the numerous newspapers to browse. super nice topfenstrudel, very topfen forward. coffee is available in decaf as well, and waiters are quite quick and friendly, some more than others but i felt well cared for. i also liked the cups and plates in prückel design.

lovely concept for nyc. i arrived at 16:05 on the third friday in april. i’d missed wednesday as i was at the library and there was an author talk. a few people were already set up reading and on computers. a few couples and friends groups were taking photos and having snacks. i took a late lunch and read. unfortunately there were two people on the tree house disturbing the grounds. talking and arguing loudly about a missed double date. they stayed there until 6pm when i left. very inconsiderate to other guests and tourists. i’ll email the organisers and suggest 30/45 minute increments so everyone gets a turn. the flowers were labelled. i was surprised cohosh comes on blue and not just black. lovely little plaque for spam cat on my second photo. i will go back another day to enjoy a more peaceful atmosphere - hopefully. i took the m9 & the m14sbs are local. this will be beautiful when on full bloom. a few more benches or lawn chairs would be nice as there are a few sparsely patches of mud. run solely on donations - there’s a box for cash and a qr code. i hope to update if they take outdoor furniture donations

lovely day trip. we started at boulders beach to see the penguins, headed to cap of good hope and ended at the two oceans light house. we took the furnicular ride as well. tickets here readily available and reasonably priced. the views were breathtaking. we hiked up the mountain at cap of good hope which was rewarded with extraordinary views. highly recommended.
lovely environment. there was a queue taking the vaporetto so i'll advise you get there atleast 1hour ahead of time. visited a glass making factory for free and dropped a token to support their work
lovely establishment with several different food options from thai, jamaican, cuban, sushi, oysters. a great inexpensive place where you can sample from a variety!

lovely evening experience with city cruises last weekend. we got to see the wonderful sunset whilst taking in the beautiful evening views of london. the cruise was long enough for us to also get night views with all the bridges brightly lit up. very relaxing and fun with great commentary from staff. make sure to book in advance as tickets do sell out fast.

lovely exhibits and a wonderful collection of items in each. the dinosaur section has a scale model of a t-rex and a skeletal model of another big dinosaur. the birds section is also very well showcased. the 100 treasures are also very detailed and well curated.
lovely experience for the family! amazing strawberries & ice cream🍓. great learning on how everything grows, we had the place to ourselves.
lovely experience. the beach’s are nice, and there are stairs along the coast to easily access.

lovely experience. was almost private going in the middle of the week. the museum and wine tasting were amazing. loved the design of the place it’s the second best wine museum in the world! worth trying! don’t be discouraged when arriving, the museum is underground and wine testing and shop on a beautiful and modern hidden place

lovely falls so pretty. easy to get to shame no real walking track just a very short loop along the creek. nice spot for a swim if warm enough. we went to the falls tea house but it was closed with nothing on google or fb to say it's closed

lovely farmer's market selling fresh produce - mostly vegetables and some other products like pepper, honey, strawberries etc. bought really sweet and fresh strawberries from one of the stalls and they were absolutely divine. highly recommended for a short walk around just to take a look :)

lovely flea market with lots of variety of things to buy. the perfect place to find souvenirs. the prices were reasonably good but you can find cheaper things on the more off peak roads but it’s not a huge difference in price. definitely worth visiting!

lovely food hall set within a former church, with multiple food options and seating over two floors. it can be quite busy, with music occasionally loud, but nice place for a drink or bite when in the area. outside seating is also available upstairs, accessible from near the texmex. prices can vary from quite affordable for london to remembering you’re in mayfair. a few places don’t have substantive vegetarian options, but many do. lift and stairs help connect the floors. toilets available in the basement. they look nice on the surface, but some didn’t flush or have seats, and only one hand dryer in the women’s so a bit limited functionality.

lovely gardens by the water. you can tell it’s being taken care of and the admission fee is definitely worth paying (300¥ per person). there are many benches you can sit on, paths you can walk on, lovely bridges across ponds and some traditional tea houses offering matcha and sweets🍵 it feels so calm and is the perfect place to escape rushed tokyo, in tokyo🧚
lovely gardens surround koutoubia mosque. it gives some shade, a few people selling things.

lovely gardens, interesting range of plants. best bit definitely the tortoise enclosure (although i feel they should have more space and enrichment). only negative is the ticket office only accept card payments, no cash.

lovely gardens, we had a lovely stroll around the water and the gardens. there are shops where you can buy drinks and souvenirs if you want. this place is really beautiful and right next to the airport so you often see plans flying right over the pavilion.

lovely greenery a few days after the rain. eeveral different paths to be walked at leisure.
lovely handmade items. worth the stop! the natives here want to share their experiences & crafts. cash or card.

lovely hidden beach with lounge rentals and umbrellas (65 euro for 2 w umbrella) bar, cafe, and restroom available. less crowded than by dubrovnik wall but many steps down and pebble beach, bring water shoes. lovely day!🏖️

lovely hidden food garden that allows you to join in and seed the garden. you can find rhubarb and squash and it has some great flowering plants. it can be very busy during sunny weekends due to a bar/restaurant just next to it.
lovely horse riding experience provided by anna. the horse is very gentle and anna explains a lot about the faroe culture. definitely worth it!

lovely hotel with lovely staff. my wife and i stayed for 2 nights and you felt they couldn’t do more for you. the room was comfortable and spacious. the hotel has same day laundry service available which is very convenient. the rooftop bar is a nice spot at night and if you go for breakfast opening at 06:30 you can watch sunrise and the famous balloons of bagan drift from west to east.

lovely lake side walk in a tranquil nature reserve that has many wooden bridges and even a wild sandy beach. can you spot the rubber ducks that are part of the interlaken adventure duck hunt that passes through this amazing nature reserve?
lovely levada walk. unsurprisingly mostly flat, but has two short tunnels and one very (v...e...r...y...) long tunnel. a couple of waterfalls to walk through/under.
lovely little bench area right along the canal

lovely little circular walk going up the side of the quarry and then through the woods back down to the town. good views out over the loch at the start. you can park beside the tourist centre and the co-op.

lovely little green garden tucked away on a unassuming street. the place is really well kept and maintained with lots of interesting little touches scattered throughout. there is plenty of shade and seating around the garden providing a peaceful escape from the hustle and bustle of the city. there are lots of interesting statues to look at and pieces of architecture scattered around. lots of people sitting around having lunch, on their laptops and just getting some rest. a really gem in the city to get some peace and quiet!

lovely little place in nature. there are rivers, lots of beautiful and medicinal trees. there are benches abd tables for a picnic. quiet and peaceful. easy to visit just follow the track. a little museum also with some old tools.

lovely little ride up the river. we had tickets for the zoo as well which worked out slightly more expensive than booking the two separately. it was chilly being january but blankets on each seat were a very cosy added touch. staff were friendly although not chatty. the boat schedule didn't follow the zoo closing times either which we had hoped to get the boat on to camden but the zoo closed 30 minutes before the boat was due (not sure if it closed early due to the dark drawing in early) so we walked instead. would like to do it again in summer.

lovely little spot. 4-5 short hikes on well signposted map. lovely for quiet stroll. just a small carpark with a very friendly, informative man in a small cabin, information hut. there is a board outside where hikers can pencil down what they have seen on their hikes. the only place during our 5 day trip where we bumped into highland cows.

lovely little walking route with views of the lake. benches for the perfect lunch stop. for a tranquil lake video with gentle wave sounds, filmed at this location, head to our youtube channel - peaceful viewpoints.
lovely local legends. shopping refreshments and wonderful local tunes.
lovely location along the nenano river. cabins are very nice. food, programs, and hikes are excellent.

lovely location, food was great, staff were friendly, epic shower with loads of hot water, food was good. bubble tent was great fun, we could see stars from our bed. it’s a pressurised tent so there is a fan but not too noisy. no shade if you wanted to chill in camp unless you went into one of the main buildings so no view. as it’s half board i think water should be provided with food. the tours are not arranged through the camp they are arranged with the bedouin that transfer you from the village so the reception has limited info on prices and itineraries and found it confusing with pick up times.
lovely location. enjoyed the museum tour and the information

lovely market with a selection of produce, meats and cheeses, a few bakery stalls and a couple food stalls. there’s also small gift spots for handmade items like soaps, clothes or jewelry. it won’t take long to discover but it’s a great saturday visit!
lovely market with lots of amazing designs.

lovely multi themed garden and park. wonderful flowers and walking paths. lots of animals to see too.

lovely museum with a great exhibition when we were there. the house itself is beautiful and then the art was incorporated in the environment of the rooms. the garden is also lovely to walk around in. not too crowded.
lovely natural park with historical building from colonial era

lovely nature walk. if you are wanting to take your family or we'll behaved dog for a walk this trail is for you. in the morning a coffee truck is available, support the vendor selling dog bed accessories.
lovely open space. very relaxing in the middle of the hustle of toyoko. free. places for the kids to run around. the history is also amazing.
lovely outdoor space at the top floor of vivocity
lovely outdoor space at vivo city. children are playing at the playground happily. amazing view from here to sentosa. a must go!

lovely park extremely well maintained with lots of information about the komodo dragons we were even luckily to see several of them basking in the sun
lovely park for a walk. it’s bigger than i thought and home to many birds. there are benches to sit and enjoy the surroundings. public toilets are available for €0.10.

lovely park in the middle of downtown, surrounded by the best stores of the city. with a boulder that is over a billion years and diferent sections, it's a little oasis, great to take the kids or enjoy a quiet time in your day relaxing with a cup of tea or coffee. beautiful christmas lights and decorations turn it into a winter wonderland on this holiday season.

lovely setting, but some concerns we visited during our stay in madeira and took a taxi to get there. you have to buy your ticket inside the gift shop, which felt a bit backwards, usually that’s something you do at the end, not the beginning. the staff were a group of women chatting amongst themselves, and it took a moment to get their attention. there’s a nice variety of birds to see, most of which appeared to be in good physical condition. however, many of the cages felt quite small, and i couldn’t help but wonder whether the animals get enough space or exercise. one moment that really stuck with us was near the end, in the conservatory section. a lone swan was blocking the exit path, having slipped through a chain barrier. he clearly wanted to escape and didn’t seem to have much space to move around. we couldn’t leave until the gift shop attendant came and chased him back in. when i asked how often that happens, she just said, “yeah, quite often,” which didn’t sit right with me, it felt like he just wanted more freedom. on a positive note, the café was pleasant. we had a drink and a coffee, both nicely made and reasonably priced, with good service. the whole place can be done in about 30 minutes to an hour if you include time at the café. overall, it is a charming idea in a beautiful setting, but the enclosure sizes and that swan encounter left me feeling a bit sad.

lugard road lookout: unforgettable panoramas of hong kong 5 stars breathtaking views, easy access, and a touch of history make lugard road lookout an absolute must-visit for anyone exploring the peak. here's why it deserves its top rating: 1) spectacular vistas: perched at 1,300 feet above sea level, the lookout offers panoramic vistas of hong kong island and kowloon. the city skyline sprawls out before you, with towering skyscrapers, bustling harbors, and verdant hills creating a mesmerizing tapestry. it's truly a sight to behold, especially at sunrise or sunset. 2) effortless accessibility: a short, scenic walk from the peak tram terminus leads you to the lookout point. the path is well-maintained and offers stunning views along the way. even for those not accustomed to hiking, the climb is manageable and rewarding. 3) historical significance: the lookout was named after sir francis edward lugard, a former governor of hong kong. it served as a strategic vantage point during the colonial era and now offers a fascinating glimpse into the city's past and present. 4) tranquil atmosphere: despite its popularity, lugard road lookout retains a peaceful ambiance. you can often find a quiet spot to soak in the views and admire the city's beauty without the crowds. don't miss it! if you're looking for a breathtaking panoramic experience in hong kong, lugard road lookout is an absolute must-visit. its stunning views, easy accessibility, and historical significance make it an unforgettable attraction.

luli island is a unique stop in the honda bay island-hopping tour, known for its sandbar that “sinks and rises” with the tide — hence the name lulubog, lilitaw. it’s a cool natural feature and a fun photo spot, especially during low tide when the sandbar is fully visible. the island is generally good for swimming, lounging, and quick stops, with shallow, calm waters and a few shaded areas to rest. there’s also a small diving platform for those who want to jump into deeper water. however, the place clearly needs better maintenance. during our visit, there was noticeable floating marine debris along the shore, which took away from the otherwise beautiful scenery. while this might depend on tides or weather, more regular cleanup would definitely improve the experience. with increasing tourist traffic, upkeep is important to preserve the island’s appeal. snorkeling isn’t ideal here, as there’s not much marine life, and the island can feel crowded when multiple tour groups arrive at the same time. facilities are basic, and there’s not much to do beyond swimming and taking pictures. pros: • unique sandbar that appears/disappears with the tide • good for swimming and photos • quick, convenient stop during honda bay tour cons: • floating marine debris; area needs better upkeep • crowded during peak hours • limited activities and marine life overall: luli island is an interesting and photogenic spot, but it would benefit greatly from more consistent maintenance and environmental care. a worthwhile part of the honda bay tour — just don’t expect to spend too long here.

luxury glamping experience + excellent hospitality we had an amazing experience at tutc's chamba camp thiksey, staying for a total of 4 nights in july 2025 which included full board and tour guide/driver. accommodation: we stayed in the presidential suite tent, which was spacious, clean, and very comfortable. it had all the modern amenities you need - air conditioning, heating, power sockets, even wifi. our view looked directly at the thiksey monastery, nestled between the ladakh range and the zanskar range. this is the most luxurious glamping experience we've had, and we've tried several across india, sri lanka and africa. food: menu changes daily and comprises a mix of european/western cuisine and indian cuisine. we went mostly with the indian selection and the food was delicious. arnap from the restaurant ensured we were kept delighted at every course. service: this was where chamba camp thiksey truly shines and sets itself apart. the camp manager, piyush, and vikash, made sure we were well taken care of, checking in daily and helping us with our experiences/itinerary. our dedicated 24/7 butler saurabh, tended to us throughout our stay, had great initiative, was attentive to our needs and ensured we were comfortable. experiences: for my wife's birthday celebration, the camp went above and beyond by setting up a private breakfast for us with a picturesque view, and even a freshly baked birthday cake! at night, we went stargazing with pooja, who was very knowledgeable and adept at showing us constellations with their powerful in-house telescope - this is a highly recommended experience. guide and driver: our guide, tundup, and driver, rigzin, were with us from the start picking us from the airport upon our arrival, and dropping us off on departure. tundup is an excellent, knowledgeable guide who led our excursions and activities, with great recommendations for views and photo spots. rigzin is a skilled driver who navigated the roads/passes safely and with ease. we always felt we were in good hands. special mention: altitude sickness needs to be carefully prepared for when coming to ladakh. as i didn't acclimatize well, i requested to be brought to the hospital. piyush, saurabh and tundup/rigzin all worked in tandem to make my hospital stay as comfortable as possible. when i was brought back to camp in the evening, they were prepared with an oxygen tank in the room. our itinerary had to be changed and all involved were flexible and accommodating. everything was seamlessly taken care of. i'm grateful for their assistance and care throughout this episode. throughout our stay both my wife and i felt safe and taken care of. overall, we had one of our best stays and experiences, and we would highly recommend chamba camp thiksey and tutc overall.

lydia took us on a great walking tour through oia and beyond. she helped us see the town through a local’s eyes, peeking inside ancient structures and winding through back streets to arrive at those famous, breathtaking santorini views. the tour ended at the lovely sigalas winery, where we enjoyed five different wines and a platter of delicious greek snacks. knowledgeable, considerate and upbeat, lydia turned what could have been an overwhelming experience into one of our favorite days in the islands! when we returned to oia another day, we knew exactly where we wanted to shop, sightsee and have lunch, thanks to lydia. we were connected to santorini walking tours through bespoke greece, the agency which coordinated our entire trip. i highly recommend both companies to get the most from a greek vacation!

lydia was an amazing guide. full of information with a great spirit, enthusiasm and friendliness. we were able to see the less traveled and uncrowded places on the island and learn a lot about its history and customs. would totally recommend it!!!!
lydia was the best guide we have ever had! she did a great job of educating us on the history and culture of the island - and cheering us on during the hike. highly recommend!

lynn canyon suspension bridge is a beautiful spot for a short walk and easy trail with great views and forest vibes. the bridge itself is cool, and leads to a pool at the end of the path. went on a weekday and wasn't super busy. can get busy but is typically less crowded than capilano. great alternative for visitors.

ma on shan country park (the section closest to yiu on estate of ma on shan) a nice getaway from the city. easily accessible either by hiking or cycling up the paved road, or driving or hailing a cab to get to the country park bbq area. from there, you can just enjoy being surrounded by lots of trees with patches of blue and white right above you on a good day. a 20-minute hiking trail for families and beginners right outside the bbq area will allow you to have some mild workout without breaking much sweat. for people who love adventures or more extreme form of hiking (but still without the need for eqiupment), there is a difficult trail which begins at one of the lookout points of the family trail and takes you all the way to the peak of ma on shan, if you can bear the steep climb.

ma on shan country park is a park located in the central neck of the sai kung peninsula in the eastern new territories of hong kong. the park covers an area of 28.8 square kilometres and links sai kung country park and lion rock country park to form an extensive recreation area on the ma on shan massif. wikipedia
ma on shan hike great views to sai kung country park the highest peak is 700 m. for experienced hikers. highly recommended - incredible sea and mountain views

ma on shan peak. with a height of 702 metres (2,303 ft), it stands among the ten highest mountains in hong kong. the mountain borders sha tin and tai po districts. this is one of the best hikes i’ve done in hong kong and it is really worth you doing it. it is best to start the hike at ma on shan bbq site. there the trail leads up on the ‘family trail’ this will lead tp what looks like a dead end, ignore this and hop the fence. the real hike will begin . it starts off easy enough, with muddy but well defined path through the trees and vegetation. the trees disappear and make way for lush green vegetation and mountainous vista ahead of you. don’t stop, just keep going forward. the trail was excellent, the wind blowing and the fresh air around you. invigorating keep going up the path, youll come to a dead end and a barrier. igonore this, hop over it and continue going up. it gets steeper and more challenging as you go up but it;ll be worth it. the views also get better and better as you go. the trail leads to what is known as pyramid peak, im unsure why i guess it kind of looks like a pyramid (maybe). what do you think? the views from the top are simply awesome, and well worth the challengin climb. you’ll be glad you did it to end the hike follow the signs and go back to a village and get the bus to sai kung. from there you can get a bus back into the city.

maasai mara national reserve is an incredible safari destination with an abundance of wildlife that truly impresses every visitor. the variety and number of animals seen are remarkable, offering unforgettable game viewing experiences including lions, leopards, elephants, zebras, and more. the ticketing staff at the reserve are notably friendly and helpful, making the entry process smooth and welcoming.

machico - teleferico da faja do larano - machico; ~23km round trip, 6 hours. we started hiking from machico. the trail starts just before the tunnel to canical, you can search for levada de canical on google maps to see the location. there are no signs or information about the trail, but apparently it starts by the front door of the last house before the tunnel. first 30 minutes you follow the levada through what feels like backyards of local people, then you reach the road - cross it and look for continuation of levada. there was, when we walked it, a written direction for "bocca do risco" on the white concrete. after another 30 minutes or so you should start paying attention to the right side of the trail and look for a path leading up the mountain. there is also a sign about bocca do risco, so it should not be hard to notice. from there it's pretty much straight forward - you'll reach the path along the ocean, turn left and pretty soon there will be plenty of opportunities for beautiful landscape viewing. once we reached teleferico, we did not go down to porto de cruz, because we didn't fancy the hike back up.

macritchie reservoir in singapore is a nature lover's paradise. the lush greenery and serene waters create a perfect escape from the city's hustle and bustle. the treetop walk offers breathtaking views and an exhilarating experience. the well-maintained trails are ideal for hiking and jogging, providing a great workout in a beautiful setting. wildlife sightings, including monkeys and birds, add to the charm. whether you're looking for a peaceful stroll or an adventurous trek, macritchie reservoir is a must-visit. it's a wonderful place to relax, enjoy nature, and recharge. highly recommended for everyone visiting singapore.

made an 8 km trek of the macritchie treetop walk. from the venus parking area to the sight it was roughly 3km plus an additional kilometer of walking in the treetop vicinity itself. we took a couple of hours of leisurely walk admiring nature both flora and fauna. there were several monkeys, lizards, birds, alligators and turtles we found along the way. we certainly took the time to appreciate the dense forest vegetation and breathe in clean air. after the walk, we were drenched and exhilarated with the experience. we look forward to a longer walk next time.

made it up to dragon’s back this morning led by some of my favorite hosts, manpreet singh and robert wilde. dragon’s back refers to the ridge's undulating, spinal shape that resembles a dragon's back when viewed from above. the trail, officially part of section 8 of the hong kong trail, is a popular hiking route known for its scenic views and relatively easy difficulty. when in hong kong, come and experience the trails. happy hiking!

madri gras museum of costumes and culture is a really fun and friendly place to visit while in new orleans. staff is very helpful. lots of very fancy costumes. you can put on some of these and take pictures.we took our grandchildren and they enjoyed themselves.

magic experience with kerry, alphonso and the other members of the crew. we spent 3 days and 2 nights with sailaway, navigating to a new island everyday and sleeping in the camp on the mainland. the experience is amazing : snorkelling in wonderful turquoise waters, special mention to two mile reef, virgin white beaches and dunes, dolphins, turtle and dugong watch, barbecue on the boat, sailing with the dhow… but all the crew’s and kerry’s kindness and attention should be highlighted: free accommodation upgrade, dedicated meals cooked according to what we like, attempt to gently approach each new animal seen from the boat, popcorn cooked on the boat… we had dinners with kerry who cooks and welcome us at his own home table. he’s worked his whole life in tourism and his willing to share good times with people is felt every minute. thanks a lot to sailaway!

magic garden truly lives up to its name—lush greenery, peaceful atmosphere, and thoughtful touches everywhere. it’s the perfect spot to unwinds and reconnect with nature. the staff were warm and welcoming, and the setting felt like a secret sanctuary. highly recommended for anyone looking for serenity away from the crowds.

magic island is a fantastic spot, but if you're not into cliff jumping, it might not be the best destination for you, as this is the primary activity available. the island offers a variety of jump heights, ranging from 3 meters (10 feet) to 10 meters (32 feet). the highest jump i attempted was 7 meters (22 feet), and it was already quite terrifying—good luck to anyone brave enough to try the 10-meter jump! there is an entrance fee of 250 pesos (approximately 4.27 usd as of july 24, 2024) to get in, which is something to consider when planning your visit. overall, magic island provides an exhilarating experience for thrill-seekers and cliff jumping enthusiasts. if you're up for the challenge, it's definitely worth the visit.

magical and serene.⛩️🍃 tucked deep in the kyoto mountains, kifune shrine feels like a portal to another world. the iconic lantern-lined staircase is even more breathtaking in person, especially on a misty day. the forest air is crisp, the sounds are peaceful, and there’s a calm energy that’s hard to describe — you just have to feel it. perfect spot to pause and reconnect with yourself.

magical evening atmosphere! palais de chaillot is truly stunning at night. the architecture, the view of the eiffel tower, and the overall ambiance create a magical setting. it’s the perfect spot for an evening stroll, photos, or just taking in the beauty of paris under the lights. highly recommended for a peaceful yet awe-inspiring nighttime experience.

magical, one of havana's most striking places. an exponent of early 20th-century art nouveau, it was the recreation ground for the brewery founded by blanco herrera. you can still breathe in the luxury of the encanto lounge, now enveloped by the lush nature surrounding the almendares. there's so much to discover there. if you have the chance to go, don't miss it.

magnetic hill in leh is a truly unique and fascinating stop! while the "magnetic" pull is widely believed to be an optical illusion, it's still incredibly fun to experience. you park your vehicle in neutral on a designated spot, and it appears to roll uphill, seemingly defying gravity. beyond the illusion, the surrounding landscape is breathtaking. it's a great spot for photos and a quick, quirky break on your leh itinerary, often combined with visits to sangam point and gurudwara pathar sahib. a definite conversation starter and a memorable part of the ladakh experience!

magnetic hill is a fascinating spot near leh where the landscape creates an optical illusion, making vehicles appear to roll uphill against gravity. surrounded by stunning mountains, it’s a quick yet intriguing stop on the leh–kargil road. a fun and must-see experience for travelers in ladakh.

maha bodhi phaya - the buddhist temple - was built in the xiii century by the king hitlominlo. it's modeled after the mahabodhi temple in bihar (india), where buddha first achieved enlightenment.

maha bodhi phaya is a unique temple in bagan, inspired by the famous mahabodhi temple in india. its distinct pyramidal design sets it apart from the typical bagan pagodas. the detailed carvings on the exterior make it an interesting site to explore. it’s worth a visit if you want to see something different from the usual temple architecture in the area.

mahali mzuri is an extraordinary resort. super comfort, a fabulous team of people to take care of you, led by their ever smiling & caring managed marianna. add to that their stunning location. just on the ridge of the valley.. so you get to see the wildlife just below the deck & balcony of your tent. finally, their guides who take you on the drives into the mara are all very knowledgeable, proficient and very friendly & helpful. would definitely recommend mm to anyone who wants a luxurious stay in the mara. 👍 🙂

mahali mzuri was the second and final leg of our masai mara holiday. we didn't think anything could top our previous experience, but mahali mzuri is a different world. it is secluded, and quiet but you still see animals right from your tent and the minute you get out for your game drive. the staff: bob, newtown were the best we've ever met and made our whole stay the most memorable holiday!

mahmoud mokhtar museum, one of the unique museums in cairo fir art lovers, although it is small but has a the most wonderful sculpture work of the great mahmoud mokhtar. the lighting focused on the pieces need to be stronger, and a brochure needed for the life of this great artist, it surely needs more attention. the grave of mahmoud mokhtar lays inside the museum.

mahmoud mukhtar is of course one of the big names in egyptian art, that's why this place is not only important for his legacy, it's also important for hosting many artistic events, festivals and galleries (here are some photos from cairo comix 8) i also love the location of this museum facing the opera house.

mahshico bibimbap is my favorite food. i love that i can choose from more than seven kinds of vegetables and beef, pork, and chicken. if you are looking for a healthy meal, you should definitely try bibimbap. i highly recommend it.

mahébourg hasn’t seen large-scale tourist development, so it retains lots of authentic charm. it’s a great place to get a taste of real mauritian life, see fishermen heading out on their wooden boats, and shop at lively local markets alongside an interesting museum, local eateries, and street food stalls, where you can chat with vendors while sipping on fresh coconuts and snacking on gato merveille (fried crispy dough served with tomato chutney).

mahébourg waterfront is a peaceful and scenic spot in mauritius with stunning sea views, a lovely walking path, and historical significance. it’s great for a relaxing stroll, especially in the morning or evening. you can explore nearby markets and local food stalls too. some parts may need better maintenance, but overall it’s a calm, charming place to visit.

majestic and pristine. you need to see it to believe it. soak in the history while the sun scorches your skin - don't worry just being an umbrella, you will need it if you are visiting this place in summer. to live it more, visit the acropolis museum.

majestic and unforgettable – a true masterpiece of ancient architecture the odeon of herodes atticus is an absolute highlight when visiting athens. standing in this beautifully preserved ancient amphitheater is a truly humbling experience. the architectural details, the semi-circular seating, and the grand backdrop of the stone façade are simply breathtaking. it’s incredible to imagine the performances that once took place here – and even more amazing that the venue still hosts concerts and cultural events today. the views from the upper levels are spectacular, offering a panoramic glance over the city and surrounding hills. whether you’re passionate about history, architecture, or just looking for an inspiring place to visit, this is a must-see. the combination of cultural richness and scenic beauty is unbeatable. highly recommended – you’ll leave with goosebumps and a deep appreciation for ancient greek civilization. (photos included speak for themselves – this place is extraordinary!)

make reservations before attending! also keep in mind there's only a small lot before entering. so expect to pay for parking inside the park if you're heading there in a vehicle. we walked there instead and the trail was well paved the entire way albeit mimicking a rock formation which helped with grip. there was a small incline along the entire trail. the trail is not smooth enough for strollers (happened to see one of the trail and they have to removed their child from it). expect it to be hot, so take some water and don't underestimate it. we also received very light rain which was welcome. you'll experience several bunkers on your way up. near the top you'll be given the option, loop around or go up a set of yellow stairs. you'll get greater fulfillment from going up the stairs first and then looping back around on the way down (but again you know your body better so listen to it). once up the yellow stairs you'll get welcomed by a spiral stair case to take you to the top of the large bunker with beautiful views.

malabar headland national park contains a really wonderful coastal walk with spectacular views. some parts of the walk are on an elevated footpath. this helps the area to be accessible and suitable to a wide range of users. it is a popular spot for runners/ joggers as well as families with young children. i found the vegetation and rock formations along the walk really interesting. the park was peaceful and calming. i would recommend visiting here!

maligne lookout, even after the wildfire, holds a haunting kind of beauty that speaks volumes. the charred trees stand like silent storytellers, whispering tales of resilience, wild winds, and the animals that still roam freely through the recovering landscape. there’s something powerful about standing there, feeling the breeze weave through the skeletal forest, and realizing that nature, even in its scars, is breathtaking. it’s a place that reminds you of the strength of the wild and the quiet hope of regrowth.

malik & his team were great! he was even able to find us dolphins during our drive! we followed the current so it worked out great. they showed an absolute love for diving & sea life. at one point our guide left us to pick up and move an anchor that was destroying the reef. just a good person. would highly recommend booking a dive with zanzibar dive.

mall of the emirates is a premier shopping destination featuring a huge variety of international and local brands, from luxury labels to high street favorites. beyond shopping, it offers excellent dining options, entertainment like ski dubai, and family friendly activities. the mall is spacious, clean, and well-organized, making it perfect for a full day of shopping, dining, and fun.

mall of the emirates is one of my favorite places in dubai—it has everything under one roof. from luxury shopping and amazing restaurants to entertainment for all ages, it never disappoints. but what truly makes it special is ski dubai. the idea of skiing indoors in the middle of the desert is unbelievable until you experience it yourself! whether you’re skiing, playing in the snow park, or just meeting the penguins, it’s unforgettable. the whole mall is clean, organized, and super easy to access thanks to the metro station right inside. highly recommended for both tourists and locals!

mall of the emirates is one of the best malls i've visited. great mix of luxury and popular brands, lots of dining options, and the indoor ski slope is amazing. it's clean, well-designed, and easy to access. definitely worth spending a few hours here when in dubai.

mall of the emirates – a shopping marvel with a metro advantage mall of the emirates is truly one of the most impressive shopping destinations i have ever visited. the first thing that catches your eye is its breathtaking interior design — a blend of elegance, modern architecture, and spacious walkways that make the entire shopping experience feel grand and comfortable. every corner is thoughtfully designed, from the decorative ceilings to the bright, well-lit interiors, creating an atmosphere that makes you want to explore for hours. one of the most convenient aspects of this mall is its well-organized parking. whether you’re arriving by car or being dropped off, the signage is clear, spaces are plenty, and the entry/exit flow is smooth. on top of that, its direct connection to the mall of the emirates metro station is a big plus — you can literally step off the train and straight into the mall, making it hassle-free for both tourists and residents. during my visit, i also stopped by the apple store inside the mall with the intention of buying an apple watch for my sister. the store had many staff members present, but surprisingly, no one approached me for quite some time. i waited for several minutes, looking around and expecting assistance. finally, a staff member came over and helped me through the purchasing process. while i did manage to get what i needed, i must say the service at this apple store did not meet my expectations. with such a reputed brand, i expected a more proactive and welcoming approach to customers. overall, mall of the emirates remains a must-visit for its stunning interiors, excellent facilities, easy metro access, and wide range of shopping options. however, if you’re visiting specific stores like the apple store, your experience may vary depending on the staff service at that particular outlet.

maltby street market is a great little street with various mobile food vendors. more relaxed than borough market and still great food. pro tip: pick up an amazing cheese toastie and chill in the wine bar. then hit the vegan dessert stand. amazing desserts that you would never guess are vegan!

mama mia is in english. you should know the story well or speak english very well, as the actors spoke quickly. it was a great evening. if you'd like a drink or to leave your coat, you can only do so with a ticket.
mamilla avenue is one of my favorite spots in jerusalem, i like it so much there. you can spend your afternoon there shopping, eating… recommended!

mamilla was a tiny neighborhood located on the seam that connects old and new jerusalem. its incredible story of destruction, division, unification and renewal begins at jaffa gate where, in the early 1900’s, dozens of shops, consulates, banks and guesthouses completely covered the area from just outside the gate to today’s idf square. a beautiful promenade with a wide selection of excellent brand stores that will satisfy the most exigent shoppers. the complex includes several fine restaurants and cafes which would make a perfect compliment to your shopping. the mall is located in a strategically important location between the old city and jaffa street.

man mo temple @ central – a peaceful stop for blessings & good vibes 🧧🙏🇭🇰 when in hong kong, it feels right to visit the temple and receive some positive energy. we came to man mo temple on a friday in may, with a bit of a “symbolic mindset,” just to pay respects and wish for good luck. the intense incense, hanging coils, and historic interior make the place feel sacred and timeless. whether you believe or just want to experience local culture, it’s worth stepping in to “catch some good fortune.”

man mo temple in hong kong is one of the city’s most atmospheric and historically rich landmarks, offering visitors a serene retreat from the urban bustle. built in the mid-19th century, it is dedicated to man cheong, the god of literature, and mo tai, the god of war—two deities revered by scholars and those seeking success in examinations and justice. the moment you step inside, you’re greeted by a dim, almost mystical light filtered through coils of burning incense hanging from the ceiling. the scent of incense fills the air, creating a meditative and timeless ambiance. the temple’s interior is adorned with intricate wood carvings, antique plaques, and traditional chinese architectural details that speak to its heritage. shafts of sunlight cut through the haze, making it a dream for photographers who love capturing moody, atmospheric scenes. while it’s located in the heart of bustling sheung wan, the temple feels like stepping back into another era—calm, contemplative, and deeply spiritual. for those interested in cultural photography, the contrast between the smoky light, red decorations, and golden altars offers an array of compositions. visitors are welcome to explore respectfully, and the temple remains not only a tourist attraction but also an active place of worship, where locals come to make offerings and seek blessings. it’s an unmissable spot for anyone wanting to experience hong kong’s traditions up close.

marina barrage is a shining example of singapore’s innovative urban planning, transforming a functional dam into a vibrant recreational hub. this is not just a flood control reservoir, it is hidden oasis in the heart of the urban jungle. why i like it: * spectacular panoramic views and photo perfecture: the expansive green roof is a serene, open space perfect for a picnic, relax and photography. from here, you'll be treated to breathtaking vistas of the iconic marina bay sands, the singapore flyer, and the entire city skyline. * perfect for cyclists: marina barrage serves as a popular path for cyclists, with a direct connection to the bay east garden at marina east. it’s a great way to enjoy a scenic ride along the waterfront. * family friendly : there's a water playground for the kids to have some splash too! * accessibility for everyone: the facility is free access, fully wheelchair-accessible, and clean public toilets are readily available. getting here * take the thomson-east coast line (tel) to gardens by the bay mrt station (te22). * take exit 1 and walk straight for about 5 minutes to reach the barrage. pro-tips for your visit: * sun protection: if you're visiting during the day, remember to wear a hat and apply sunscreen. the open rooftop offers little shade, so stay hydrated! * visit the sustainable singapore gallery: plan your visit between 9 am and 6 pm to explore the sustainable singapore gallery, which offers fascinating insights into singapore's journey toward environmental sustainability.

martin runs a first class operation right from the get go. on planning the trip, he was extremely responsive and usually responded within the hour if not day on questions we had and what we wanted out of our trip. from the way he communicated, i knew he was running a tight operation. we booked 2 separate overnight trips with his company, one on the collon cora and one on the limay. two totally different rivers and glad we had the chance to experience both. the arrangements were just as advertised. prompt pick up, professional guides, all the details thought of. the overnight trips were awesome. rods and flies were included as well as expert guides and rowers for our boats. when we arrived at lunch, a table and chairs were quickly set up with delicious food and a bottle of malbec with each lunch. when we arrived at camp each night, our tents with cots and sleeping bags were already set up, which allowed us time to relax. food was incredible. we had french fries for dinner one night to accompany our steak!. we fished in march and mainly using streamers. the collon cora was beautiful and had plenty of aggressive trout to catch. over the three days, we must have covered almost 30 miles of river. the limay river was absolutely gorgeous. we floated through the amphitheater section and with the changing leaves, the scenery was breathtaking with gin clear water. the fishing was slower, but we caught several fish of a lifetime for our family. we don't usually return to a location just because there are so many other places to see, but we are seriously considering returning to bariloche to fish with martin and his crew again a following year. i wouldn't hesitate to book with him again. well done to you and your crew, martin.

me and my wife did enjoy the excursion overall. the stop at the park was absolutely beautiful, and the cave swim with a live dj was without a doubt the highlight – proper good fun and a real vibe. the whole park you stop at is stunning, great showcases of the local food, coffee and chocolate. but when it came to the actual buggy ride… let’s just say it could do with some fine tuning – excuse the pun. from the get-go, things were a bit chaotic. we’d specifically asked (and paid) for one of the big can-am-style buggies but were initially lumped into a small two-seater. it was low on fuel, so they eventually moved us into the proper one we’d booked – result, or so i thought… there must have been at least 100 people in our group, split into convoys, but even early on it was clear there were issues. as we made our way out to the trails, loads of locals were running alongside the buggies trying to high-five you, sell fruit, or ask for tips. with the sheer size of the group, we were crawling along, and i genuinely felt a bit on edge as kids darted in front of vehicles. once we hit the trails, the pace didn’t improve – 10–15mph max, and often slower. i’m comparing this to a previous buggy tour i did in cape verde where we could let rip in a proper 1000cc monster. this was very different. every time i tried to pick up a bit of speed, i was told to slow down again. the huge convoy meant it was stop-start the entire way, which quickly became a bit tedious. after what felt like a short loop – maybe a few miles plus the stop – we had a chaotic 50+ buggy u-turn on a narrow trail, then headed back. not exactly adrenaline-fuelled. as for the buggies themselves – the smaller two-seaters looked like they’d seen better days. when we were finally upgraded, i realised the brake pedal barely worked and the doors wouldn’t stay shut. one bloke had his bonnet fly off mid-drive and managed to catch it! we saw at least 5–6 breakdowns along the way, and even an exhaust fall off one. that said, credit where it’s due – the staff were really friendly and tried their best despite the language barrier. when we got back, they had showers ready, a tidy little shop, and some genuinely warm hospitality. we even bought a nice pair of zol sunglasses. so all in all, yeah, we had a laugh and made the most of it. but compared to my previous experience, this one felt a bit underwhelming, slightly mad, and in need of a serious rethink. my advice for all it’s worth? probably take out less people, fix up the buggies a bit more and let people go a little faster if they like. that’s where the adrenaline is. oh and maybe charge less for photos? you might sell more. $100+ seems crazy

miradouro da santinha is a lesser-known but stunning viewpoint in porto moniz, madeira. it offers breathtaking views over the porto moniz natural swimming pools, the coastline, and the vast atlantic ocean. how to get there • located just a few minutes uphill from porto moniz. • easily accessible by car via local roads. • a short walk from the main town center if you prefer to explore on foot. what to expect • panoramic views – a perfect bird’s-eye view of the natural pools and surrounding cliffs. • great for photography – especially at sunrise or sunset. • peaceful spot – less crowded than other viewpoints, making it a great place to relax. nearby attractions • porto moniz natural swimming pools – just below the viewpoint. • fort of são joão baptista – a small historic fort nearby. • seixal beach – a short drive away, featuring madeira’s best black sand beach.

mirante dona marta in rio de janeiro is a must-visit for breathtaking views of the city, especially at sunrise and sunset. perched at 362 meters above sea level, this viewpoint offers panoramic scenes of iconic landmarks like sugarloaf mountain, christ the redeemer, and the sprawling beaches of copacabana and ipanema. at sunrise, typically around 5:30 am, the sky is painted in soft hues of pink and gold, casting a gentle glow over the city as it wakes up. the tranquil atmosphere is perfect for capturing the serene beauty of rio in its quietest moments. as the day ends, the sunset at mirante dona marta, usually around 5:45 pm, is nothing short of spectacular. the vibrant colors—ranging from deep oranges to fiery reds—create a dramatic contrast against the darkening silhouette of the city. watching the sun dip behind the mountains and seeing the lights of rio begin to twinkle is a magical experience that encapsulates the city's unique charm. whether you’re a photographer or just a lover of natural beauty, mirante dona marta is an unforgettable spot to witness the wonders of rio’s skyline.

mma dinare tented camp is located in sankoyo concession, 272 kilometres from maun, south-eastern side of the delta, adjacent to moremi game reserve. this camp is one of under one botswana sky safaris. the camp is built on a deck overlooking the gomoti river and wonders how it looks like during raining season. i visited this camp for the first time in april 2021, lodged for 4 full nights, and loved every aspect of my stay down here. mmadinare is breathtaking, beauty at its best and its worth every cent one has. the hospitality is top class as well as the staff. the evening borne fire and stories makes the place remarkable. the area has great sightings in terms of wildlife and birdlife. my game drives were graced with sightings of lions, elephants, giraffe, kudus, tsessebe, zebras, impalas, buffalos, and a wide variety of birdlife. the activities done in this camp covers traditional mokoro (my favourite), game drive (morning, afternoon and evening), and bush walk when the grass is not too long. the camp has 10 tented rooms that overlooks the gomoti river. the tents are set on timber decks, have hardwood floors and wooden door frames for a sturdy feel, and canvas walls with large mesh windows i stayed in room 4 and it has a great view of the river and the reception area, which makes it remarkable. my highlights for this trip was traditional mokoro, variety of game and story telling around borne fire. definitely mmadinare deserves a second visit, this time around in summer.

moderate trail with incredibly rewarding views. a must for any tourist staying in tamarin and interested in hiking. the start of the trail is a bit hard to find so i will describe how to access it, pictures attached. make sure to start very early in the morning to avoid the scorching heat. bring plenty of water. from the location on google maps (at the base of a staircase), follow the road to the left and the sign "jogging track". this will take you down a steep rubble road, from which a small path departs and crosses a dry river bed. follow the trail and you will be at a bifurcation, choose "sentier z" (easier ascent), then just continue. there will be a second sign for "sentier z" about 300m later, be sure not to miss it. after that, the trail gets very easy to find all the way to the top. it took us about 1 hour for the ascent and the same amount of time for the descent. if you're not an experienced hiker, consider about 3 hours in total (with some time on the top). there are some red berries in the bushes at the top, they are edible and the locals gather them. give them a try! the trail is not technically difficult (all steep sections are secured with ropes) but is physically challenging, as it's a direct and rather steep ascent, with virtually no flat sections. enjoy it!

mongkhon nimit temple, also known as wat mongkhon nimit, is a historic buddhist temple located in old phuket town. it is known for its beautiful architecture and cultural significance. what makes mongkhon nimit temple special is its distinctive chinese-influenced architecture, which features intricate carvings, colorful artwork, and ornate decorations. the temple is dedicated to the chinese goddess guanyin, also known as the goddess of mercy, and is a popular place of worship for locals and tourists alike. while mongkhon nimit temple does not serve food or offer specific attractions, it is worth visiting for its cultural and historical significance. visitors can explore the temple grounds, admire the architecture, and learn about the local buddhist culture. in terms of warnings, visitors should dress modestly and respectfully when visiting mongkhon nimit temple, covering their shoulders and knees. additionally, visitors should be respectful of the surroundings and avoid causing any disruptions. there are no specific restrictions to enter mongkhon nimit temple, but visitors are expected to behave respectfully and follow the rules of the temple. to get to mongkhon nimit temple from phuket town, you can take a taxi or tuk-tuk. the temple is located on dibuk road, which is one of the main roads in old phuket town. if you're driving or riding a scooter, there is parking available in the area, but it can be limited, especially during peak hours. it's a good idea to arrive early or park in a nearby parking lot and walk to the temple.

monkey jungle is miami’s longest-running wildlife park opening back in the early 1930’s!! it is a historic icon and i have fond memories of going there when i was a young child. the park was much different back then, i am referring to circa 1975 to the 1980's with my parents. one of the monkeys reached out to me took my eye glasses off my face. my parents tell the story fondly. fast forward like 30 years and here i am taking my own kids to this same park, however the layout is much different. my kids and myself absolutely love feeding the monkeys by putting peanuts in basket and the monkeys are on top and pull up the basket and then put it back down for more peanuts. it is just the coolest and no more monkeys reaching out taking off your glasses. feeding the monkeys was never like this before and that is because of hurricane andrew in 1992. we are so lucky that this wildlife park is still here today. the path of hurricane andrew went directly thru monkey jungle causing catastrophic damage that you can not imagine. if they were not already dead, apes, monkeys and gorillas roaming the streets. god bless the staff and caretakers of monkey jungle, they stayed on site helping the animals that were hurt, helping the animals find their way home. courageous amazing people!!! the wings of aviary is one of the additions that was added to the park after hurricane. monkey jungle is such a fun family park, we are so lucky to have this in miami.

morning markets are one of the hidden gems of thailand, perfect for those not looking solely for its nightlife draws. bring your kids here for a child-safe but educational experience on thai food culture. this is where real thais go. upon entry, expect to be greeted by a 750m stretch of shops and pushcarts lined on each side of the alley. they fall into several categories. you have fried foods ranging from chewy sweet potato balls to savoury yam balls filled with pork, grilled foods like the moo ping (pork skewers) or the delicious chinese red sausage, soups and noodle dishes like the innard stew (sounds bad, is delicious). there's even a coffee pushcart selling cafe quality ice lattes. let your taste buds and not your eyes, judge, as they don't look all tame. for drinks, there's your classic thai iced milk teas (both green and orange versions, no difference if you ask me), coffees, soy milk, juices, etc. an interesting thing to note is that many of the vendors are thai but of chinese ethnicity, mostly of the teochew sect/dialect. many of them are second or third generation thai-chinese and they've brought over tau sar piahs (mung bean pastries), char siu (red roast pork), siu yuk (roast pork) and other foods from their cultural roots to thailand, some with a thai twist to it. i hope you find this short street as rewarding and fascinating as i did. there's a lot to notice when you open your eyes and give things a chance.

mount batur, locally known as gunung batur, is an active volcano situated in the kintamani region of bali, indonesia. standing at 1,717 meters (5,633 feet) above sea level, it is one of bali's most iconic natural landmarks. the mountain is part of the larger batur caldera, which was formed by volcanic activity thousands of years ago. this caldera encompasses a lake, also named lake batur, which adds to the area's scenic beauty. ​ mount batur holds significant cultural importance for the balinese people. it is considered a sacred site, with numerous temples located in its vicinity. the mountain is believed to be the home of many gods, and it plays a central role in various religious ceremonies and festivals. ​ for adventure enthusiasts, mount batur offers a popular trekking experience. the most common trek is a sunrise hike, which begins in the early hours of the morning to reach the summit before dawn. the hike is moderately challenging, taking approximately 1.5 to 2 hours to ascend. along the way, trekkers are treated to panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. upon reaching the top, the sight of the sun rising over the island is a rewarding experience. ​ the area surrounding mount batur is also known for its natural hot springs, providing a relaxing way to unwind after the hike. additionally, the caldera houses several villages, including kedisan, songan, trunyan, and toya bungkah, where locals engage in agriculture and fishing. these communities offer insights into traditional balinese life. ​ in 2012, unesco recognized the cultural and geological significance of the mount batur caldera by including it in the global geoparks network. this designation highlights the area's unique geological features and the importance of preserving its natural and cultural heritage. ​ visiting mount batur provides a blend of adventure, cultural enrichment, and natural beauty, making it a must-visit destination for travelers to bali

musée guimet is a treasure chest of civilizational memory and as i come from the very soil where those deities were once sculpted, worshipped, and philosophized over, it felt more than just awe. i've seen vishnu not as a concept but as carved permanence. i stood before bodhisattvas whose eyes seem to have watched over centuries of seekers. what i experienced isn’t just art, it’s an ancestral pulse. terracotta figures from the indus valley, the tantric grace of cham sculptures, gilded tibetan mandalas, chola bronzes radiating devotion. it's the cosmos of my land, mirrored and preserved across oceans and empires.

mutrah souq is one of the oldest markets in the sultanate of oman, located in the mutrah area. it is not visible from the outside, as it extends deep into the city with narrow, winding alleys covered by wooden ceilings—one of the market’s most charming features. the air is always filled with the scents of frankincense, incense, and traditional arabian perfumes. the market is known for its wide variety of goods, including handcrafted silverware, traditional daggers (khanjars), fabrics, copper and pottery items, clothing, footwear, gold, a rich assortment of spices, and much more. the market is well maintained and very clean. quick tips: bargaining is expected: most vendors anticipate negotiation, so start with a lower price. best time to visit: in the evening after sunset — the atmosphere is better and the weather is cooler. parking: can get crowded, especially on weekends.

my 45-minute helicopter flight over the grand canyon with maverick helicopters from tusayan, arizona, was nothing short of spectacular—an experience i’ll treasure forever! from the moment we arrived, everything was top-notch. the flight terminal was bright, modern, and welcoming, with a well-appointed gift shop offering reasonably priced souvenirs that made for perfect keepsakes. our pilot was fantastic, introducing himself warmly and personally escorting us to the helicopter. the safety briefing was clear and professional, setting us at ease before boarding. the smooth lift-off and brief hover were thrilling, and from there, the adventure only got better. our flight path took us over the stunning kaibab national forest, with the grand canyon looming tantalizingly ahead. the moment we soared over the canyon’s rim was absolutely unforgettable—land dropped away beneath us, and suddenly we were flying within the grand canyon itself! the sight of the rock formations and the vast, awe-inspiring expanse of this natural wonder left us speechless. throughout the flight, our pilot provided fascinating commentary about the canyon’s geology and landmarks, enriching the experience with every detail. maverick helicopters delivered an impeccable experience, seamlessly blending professionalism, comfort, and thrill. the views from the sky offered a perspective of the grand canyon that’s simply unmatched, making every moment worth the investment. i wholeheartedly recommend this tour and maverick helicopters for an extraordinary adventure you’ll never forget!

my 66 year old mom and i just went on an 8 day trek with kilimanjaro brothers and it was one of the best things we've ever done in our lives. there are a few things you really want when looking at kilimanjaro treks, and kili brothers really met all of them and exceeded our expectations! the first thing is equipment. having all the things you need on the mountain is extremely important and we were pretty worried about the fact that we didn't want to buy everything and lug it around with us. they offered a rental option for very reasonable prices, and we were shocked when they took us to their storage place! they have literally everything, and plenty of different choices. we were happy to load up on extra gear we needed. the equipment itself was pretty good, though had some issues with zippers on my sleeping bag and my trekking poles. our guides were amazing at helping though, so it wasn't too much of an issue. the second thing is having knowledgable guides. we were so impressed with the kili brothers guides. we had commander joseph and the assistant guide was justin. they were both incredibly helpful, funny, and knowledgeable. justin knew practically everyone on the mountain, and has been up and down kili and meru hundreds of times. too many to count he said. this has been his career! commander was also unbelievable as he has been doing this ten years, and was an absolute pleasure to trek with. he was constantly joking and distracting us from the difficulty of the trek, and it seemed like him and justin knew every inch of the lomosho route. the third thing is food and the porter team. the team that came up with us was absolutely incredible. they were all so friendly and helpful, even with things that they didn't need to be. they would always cheer with us as they passed us on the trail, and they did some singing for us two or three times at the camp. this was one of the reasons we picked kili brothers, because they reportedly treat their team well. i can definitely say that our team was happy and many have them have worked for them for many many years. it was great to have such a strong and bonded team, and we were so so so grateful for them for what they do. their job is insanely hard, but they do it with no complaints and at every step all they want to do is help you. now, the food.... as a foodie, i was really wondering what the food would be like and i was blown away. i ate better on the mountain than i did for the whole week prior traveling through south tanzania. seriously. mr food was the chef (robert), and he was extremely creative and talented and making delicious soups, breakfasts, to go lunches, everything. it was like having a personal caterer who ran up ahead and made sure when you arrived you had everything you need to be full and fueled. i can't believe some of the stuff we ate, sitting at many thousand meters above sea level. however, while all of these things are wonderful and we were super happy with them, what made kili brothers so amazing was how much their team really cared. detas was the cameraman, and yet he was with you every step and willing to help. he literally held my hand and arm as i walked the last 100 meters or so to the summit, and i cried i was so grateful. commander and justin were also the strongest, most helpful people i may have ever met. my mom needed help after the third day and justin and commander took turns holding her bag for the rest of the trip! for me, i would have turned down on summit night if it wasn't for justin and commander taking my bag and encouraging me to keep going. at the end of the day i think this is what makes kilimanjaro brothers so worth it. i told the team the day after summit, and i've never said more true words: "i didn't know if i could make it up to the summit, but i know for a fact that i wouldn't have made it without you." without commander, justin, detas, mr. food, and all the incredible porter team...i just never would have made it. they are the support system that allowed me to persevere, and i will forever be grateful for them.

my dad and i had an awesome time on the water with ozpaddle, sophie absolutely made the experience. her passion and knowledge for kayaking and nature really shone through. it started with a mini masterclass in proper technique and how to paddle effectively using the lightweight carbon fibre paddles. we can definitely use the skills learnt for future adventures. she was so welcoming, full of energy, and kept us laughing the whole way. we did the 8am tour, and it was perfect - a calm harbour and beautiful morning sun. sophie recommended this time, and she was spot on! the photos she took were fantastic. she also shared some great facts about sydney harbour, pointed out all the historic sites, and told brilliant stories. both about the harbour and her own kayaking journey. it was a special and unique experience, i couldn’t recommend it enough!

my dad and i really enjoyed this easy hike a while ago. you can see the beautiful scenery without much effort here. it only takes about 2 hours to walk the whole park, and most of the roads are flat, which is very suitable for novice hikers. if you are lucky enough to come here in june-july, you can even see whales migrating. it is also a good place to watch the sunrise and sunset. oh, one more thing, there is a shooting range in the park. make sure to check the official website before you come to see if the shooting range is open. if the shooting range is open, the most beautiful route by the sea will be closed.😮‍💨

my daughter absolutely loved it and it definitely got her more confortable and excited about surfing. i personally, thought it was going to be more a "learn to surf" camp. saying it out loud now, i realize that was my assumption and not necessarily the surf camps fault for my misunderstanding. i assumed, i would drop her off monday and by friday she would be popping up or even paddling into waves. that was not the case for my daughter or most the kids i saw out there. the kids looked like they had lots of fun and were given a lot of room to just play in the surf, on boogie boards, and could grab an instructor to push and hold the surf boards while they stood on the surf boards in the white water. i am not saying it was a negative experience just a heads up to future parents that the camp is much more of a free form surf camp.
