overall a good experience at a reasonable price, as long as you know what to expect (and don’t fall for scams)! you are picked up and dropped off at your hotel or wherever, i was picked up near dubai frame and dropped off in deira. first we went to a quad rental place which i read about, where you visit a shop to spend 120 aed on a scarf to cover your face and an overpriced 30 minute ride. i didn’t pay for either, but the ladies with me begrudgingly paid 500 aed for a bike for two + vat. if you don’t pay you wait in the air-conditioned waiting room for however long it takes, this was the only waste of time for me. next, you go to the sand dune bashing which was sooo fun!! our driver drove especially crazy so you get thrown around but i loved it!! lasts about 7-10 minutes they say, it was enough for me. you then have about 15 minutes or so to take pictures, again my favorite part, however there’s soooooo many other cars it’s hard to get a shot without them. the guide can help you. next, we went to the camp where they have free camel rides but the camels are abused! all of them have their mouths covered and one that was being ridden kept groaning. the handler kept yanking on the rope so hard to force them up and back down… worst part of the tour by far, i wish it wasn’t included. the main show is fine, but again they try to upsell you 50 aed for the vip section to eat food faster but i think it’s not needed. here’s the schedule: - unlimited tea for about 30 min waiting - veg starter (pakora) and soft drink - first dance 💃 - dinner served around 30 min later - last two dances start right after dinner (belly dance, then fire dance) - drive home i was worried about the food due to other reviews but there was a lot to choose from, however 98% of it was vegetables. if you are someone who only likes kebab, you will be disappointed! they give two pieces of chicken and one of mutton for the meat. the food was delicious! and plentiful. everywhere we went had soap, and the show camp had unlimited water, which i appreciated. you do have to get used to telling people no thank you when they try to sell you something, but for the affordable price tag i think it was worth the travel to the desert! my guide was ali and he wasn’t rude but definitely not the friendliest person, and he was not happy to have to drop me off deep in deira near al marhaba bus station.
overall a good experience. pros: service is great. rooms were clean. gym was awesome. buffet is amazing. cons: too many kids (were noisy). bidet is missing in toilets.

overall a good hike. need to take a motorbike up to the trailhead. bring mosquito spray as they were pretty bad. the view is definitely worth the hike, and there was a vendor selling water, gatorade, and beer. the photographer was great with helping move the wait time as there was a ton of tourist wanting to take that ig photo. make arrangements with motorcycle guys to pick you back up and an uber or car service if you are heading back to rio.

overall a great trail, entry fee is 50 dkk. views from the trail are nice. according to a hiking app, the trail there should go further up the hill, but we could not find the path and returned when we saw warning signs.

overall a nice garden, worth having a walk there. the front area looking at the emperor’s house is a bit empty but offers a nice contrast between the numerous pines and skyscrapers. the inside of the garden itself is beautifully maintained, with pretty trees, flowers and even some toads!

overall a pleasant experience. reception staff gave a brief overview of the museum when i pick up the ticket. budget around 2-3hr for this small museum would be ideal, especially if you would like to enjoy a drink at the cute indoor cafe. free wifi available for you to download the museum app on the spot. bring your own headphones. they offer videos with sign language explanations for a large number of exhibits, which made the experience inclusive for the hard of hearing community as well.

overall a very nice experience. you need up to 2 hours to finish all the lines, depending on how your group is big. the very last zip line is supposed to be the biggest fun and is not, since most of the time it stops way before the end over the river. i would recommend fixing it.

overall a wonderful place to visit and see beautiful exhibits, with some of them being interactive. definitely the main drawback here is the amount of people, not so much that it’s hard to move around, but definitely difficult to get nice pictures or videos of the exhibits. went on a monday, and was still surprised to see a good amount of people there, can’t imagine how nightmarish this place could be on a weekend or holiday when it’s packed. also the initial overview of how to explore the museum is extremely disorienting, taking you into a room of pitch darkness and then playing a video was unnerving. definitely worth checking out! just be careful of the crowds! also i didn’t share the same issue of not being able to find this place, there’s pretty clear signage around that direct you to the basement where the exhibit is. also be sure to buy tickets in advance!
overall experience was amazing, equipment was excellent, the owner was super helpful and gave us lot of tips, highly recommend that place, don’t look further!

overall experience was very nice and interactive. they were really trying to involve everyone possible and their acting was also pretty decent. what i didn’t like was that the guy at the front waiting for us to buy our tickets was kinda aggressive and was trying to speed our process up. we were just deciding what our second attraction would be , he took over the screen like we didn’t know what we were doing. aside from that it’s a nice experience especially for the kids. but it isn’t worth the price. just a one-time activity to do with your kids.
overall great views of the hotel and the gardens by the bay. nice shortcut to reach both locations. to find the entry point from the hotel slightly more complicated than i expected.

overall i was very unhappy with my stay at balmers hostel. i even tried to find somewhere to switch to but couldn’t with such short notice. if you come in the summer be warned, it is so hot in the rooms. when i arrived there was already a floor fan on and it was about 20° hotter in the room than it was outside. truly unbearable. on my second night i asked for additional fan which is the only way i was able to sleep but by the next night it was gone and i had to get it again. additionally, the room is so small, if everyone is trying to access their things at once it’s impossible. the bathroom and showers were also unfortunate. there was no counter space at the sinks and no place in the shower to place your belongings to keep it dry. it does have a kitchen that people loved but every time i used it there were staff cleaning it so i was constantly being moved around to accommodate them. keep in mind, these were prime meal time hours, outside of the time they close the kitchen to clean it. i genuinely don’t understand how this place has such great reviews unless it’s from people who truly are only there to party and don’t care much for their actual accommodations.

overall it was a lovely evening in a lovely venue. a little bit of everything to keep everyone interested 😂. the orchestra was great and the female opera singer was powerful & delightful. the mandatory cloakroom fee of 2 euro is annoying and unnecessary.

overall its quite fun for the ice museum it would be quite cold, so be sure to wear sufficient winter wear. a blanket is provided to enter they have a ice slide too. it's quite exciting and thrilling with the smooth speed . 3d museum should be the same as other 3d museum, but still quite fun to explore.

overall no real safari and money not worth it. it’s a big zoo, animals are fed by the resort. the breakfast and lunch is really bad. it’s nice to see the animals and having close photos. but it didn’t felt good. we were happy that we’ve got the last truck, which wasn’t that crowded. at all no recommendation.

overall peak experience and definitely a highlight of my new zealand trip. for the geothermal part the geysers are fascinating and you really get to experience it close. i like how they conserve the māori culture very well and the presentation is awesome. the night hāngī buffet is great with a wide variety of choices to choose from. they additionally have a session after the māori performance where they’ll take you on a ride for geysers with hot chocolate served. i didn’t participate that one but you can surely go try that out.

overall really cool concept and place to shop especially the unisex casual floor. the salesperson at the vintage store was really friendly and helpful and also the salesperson who helped us at olive young spoke multiple languages and even did our tax refund on the spot. food atelier located on b2 with lots of places to choose from. we ordered seafood kimchi hot pot for 9,000 krw and a grilled pork plate for 15,000 krw from magomi. both dishes were fresh and big servings. we enjoyed the meals so much we came back to eat from them again another day. the drinks from auntie anne's were really nice and refreshing. we ordered the peach tea ade and apple mango ade both under 5,000 krw each. would recommend going to doota even if only to look around as very different from westfield in australia where you go in and out of each shop, here you just walk around the open plan floors. some shops definitely have better quality products than others. great location among the hustle and bustle plus very easy to get to from our hotel in dongdaemun. fun shopping experience for our first time in seoul and the first mall we went to.

overall super delightful village esque shopping center with great art, ambience, and luscious courtyards. overall i could use more of a grab and go for a quick drink or snack versus a sit down restaurant experience which here will cost you. i did try the cake place and coffee place which had some options but for something light grab and go or even some water would have been great.

overall the park is nice landscape and layout. but certainly not enough animals. we walked around the entire zoo within 1.5 hour include zip line fun. it’s clean park, staff were friendly. animals look great and health, just wish there were more types of animals.

overall the stay was lovely, the room was comfortable and the shared bathrooms were very nice. one thing that was frustrating is that for a place designed for relaxation, my room faced a parking area where i heard trucks backing up several times overnight, waking me. it was very hard to feel rested and relaxed when i had such poor sleep. other than that, everything was great and the breakfast was delicious. this place is a very particular kind of experience, not your standard hotel! all of the food is incredible. so fresh and healthy!!

overall, great experience on the island and with this company. friendly bi-lingual staff was extremely accommodating, and the tours of the island were exceptional. the staff was quite knowledgeable of the islands history and how to give direction-they allowed you to explore on your own, but provide guidance when necessary/wanted. i would recommend this company to anyone touring the island.

overall, i have to say that i am a little disappointed with the cormorant tour. on the one hand, a large part is the boat trip on a relatively small ship for 11 people. secondly, several snorkelling spots had been promised, in the end there were two. we returned 2 1/2 hours earlier than planned and when looking for orcas or manta rays we didn't really get the feeling that people were looking. the park ranger was looking at his mobile phone 90% of the time (see photo). our guide richi really did his best and was super ambitious and hard-working. which made the whole experience a lot better. nevertheless, for well over 200$ you expect (despite the unpredictable nature) that at least the promised time will be kept.

overall, it was a good experience, although a bit overpriced. the food quality was good, and the entertainment during the cruise was average. the highlight of the evening was the staff – they were exceptionally friendly and cheerful, the min cost per person is 2k

overall, it’s a nice nightclub with a great atmosphere and good music. however, i found the security presence around the restrooms a bit excessive—it felt strange having to pass two guards just to use the bathroom.

overall, my experience at camp fire in wadi rum was really nice. the welcoming was warm, the people were kind, and the food was delicious. the camp itself was well set up and the desert setting was magical. however, i did have an uncomfortable experience during the night. around 2 a.m., a bedouin man knocked on my tent and asked me to open the window. when i raised my voice to tell him i was in bed and wanted to sleep, he told me to be quiet because everyone else was sleeping. then, realizing i wasn’t going to open the tent, he made up an excuse to justify why he was there in the first place. eventually, he left after i clearly said i wanted to sleep. while nothing happened beyond that, i felt scared and uncomfortable. i didn’t feel safe enough to leave my tent afterward — not even to use the bathroom or ask a friend if i could sleep in their tent. that moment really affected how i felt about the night overall. i still appreciate the kindness of the rest of the staff and the beauty of the experience, but i think it’s important for the camp to make sure all guests feel completely safe, especially at night.

overall, this is a very beautiful resort. we've stayed there before. i gave her a two rating because the beautiful resort was overrun with tourist that had day passes, and those that spent a good deal of money to enjoy the hot springs were unable to do so the place was overrunwith detours for morning tonight was very hard to even find a decent place to sit or enjoy the spring i don't believe i will be going back there for quite a while.

overall, we were really impressed by kalahari breeze safaris. we booked early so were able to fully tailor the trip, and found maria really helpful in putting together an itinerary which we loved, providing lots of info and advice based on what we said we wanted to see. we joined together a 3-night camping trip in the okavango delta with a further 4 nights camping in moremi and savute, ending the trip in chobe and victoria fall. we loved the wild camping and found it a highlight to sleep in remote locations amongst the wildlife. although maria stressed it was not a luxury safari, it was certainly not a budget experience, with nice large tents, comfy camp beds, ‘en suite’ toilets and good, filling food 3 times a day cooked on the campsite fire, or in an adapted oven buried in the ground. the food was really good – and they had no issues with providing gluten-free alternatives for my wife throughout the trip. we had two guides during the trip – master in okavango and clifford in moremi/savute. we found both to be excellent and really friendly – we loved listening to their stories around the campfire at the end of the day. both guides were local to the area we visited with them and their knowledge of the area and the behaviour of the animals really added to the trip. we couldn’t complain about the animal sightings, including a couple of close encounters with leopards, a pride of lions fighting over a recent buffalo kill, and a rare sighting of a brown hyena. we found the lodges in between the camping trips to be of good quality and very comfortable. the final part of the trip in zimbabwe was handed over to a local tour company and they provided equally good service. in particular, we found our guide who took us around victoria falls park to be really friendly, and knowledgeable which helped make that part of the trip really memorable. the lodge in zimbabwe was the best of the trip. we booked from the uk but picked a local safari firm as we believe it is better to contribute to the local economy, rather than go through a third party. we are really glad we did as they were helpful throughout – answering my many questions before we left, providing a lot of guidance throughout the booking process and when we arrived in botswana. botswana itself is a lovely country with very friendly people, loads of wildlife and stunning scenery. we will definitely we going back, and will not hesitate in using kalahari breeze again.
overcrowded. you can only visiti on specific hours because it is a residential area. lots of small shops around. very beautiful old buildings and a nice view of seoul from the top.
overgrown and needs to be maintained. no public restrooms.
overhyped hike. i recommand to merge it with the tunnel and pr6.7 (full of ajonc 😐) to make a loop
overlooking the mesmerising kowloon peninsula. one of the best viewing points in the city!
overpriced

overpriced and overrated island, locals do not speak any english even though they thrive on tourism, no supermarkets to be found. make sure to check the sea condition before you arrive because if the sea is uneasy, you cant do any water activity and water activities are the core of this island. we spent a week there during the swell and there wasn't much to do. on the positive note, its a beautiful place, most likely the most beautiful place i've ever seen in my life. the locals are nice and friendly if you manage to break the language barrier. once you land and get the park entry ticket, go ahead and book to several hikes. we took our time and only got to do one of them. book ahead because everyone wants to do it and you might miss out. dont worry if you regret, no penalty if you dont show up. after that you will need to contact victor the guide because on most of the hikes you are required to go with a guide and he is the only one that speaks english. taxis are expensive, if you plan to stay there for several days it might be a better idea to rent a vehicle (bike/buggy). i wish someone would have told me all that before i arrived there, would have saved me so much precious time. the pic is of sancho beach, they say its the best beach in the world. i dont know, it sure is pretty but you cant really enjoy it because of the hoards of tourists.

overpriced and overrated. expired milk & yogurt sit on shelves. in-house dinner kits go bad before expiration date. bakery goods are bland. chicken salads have half a bite of chicken total. the check out staff is slow and cold. i have had to throw out over $60 worth of products that expired day of purchasing or went bad days before their expiration date.

overpriced and underwhelming. not worth it! i was really disappointed by the van gogh exhibition in london. the ticket price is shockingly high for what you actually get. the experience felt more like a shallow digital show than a meaningful exhibition of van gogh’s work. there’s very little depth, no real artworks, and overall it felt more like a marketing product than a tribute to the artist. definitely not worth the money – i left feeling let down and honestly a bit ripped off. save your money for a real museum or exhibition.

overpriced for what it offers – r$100 per person adds up quickly if you're a family. we paid r$100 per person, which may not sound like much individually, but if you're traveling with a spouse and two kids, it adds up fast – and honestly, it didn’t feel worth the cost. there are better experiences on the island that offer more value for the price. consider your options before booking.

overpriced nice walk with a view in the end. car par and tickets for two people are 225 scr total. at first you walk on an earthy road that is flat and broad like for a truck. only at the end you finally get a slightly more challenging route that leads to an observation tower (it’s small and not impressive). the views are nice, like any view from the top would be. i felt lucky to observe the seychelles black parrots

overview - easily accessible trail for hiking - about 2 to 3 hour walk - take no. 6 or 66 at exch sq - beautiful scenery and good for family walk with pets. it is quite easy to go to violet hill, just by taking bus from exchange square bus terminal at central and drop off wong nai chung reservoir park. walk toward parkview, you may find the entrance of violet hill. the hiking will start with a lot of steps but not dangerous and easy to manage. you just walk in your own pace with systemic breathing, you will not feel tired. you can walk along, or with your friends, or your family with kids and pets. it will take about 2 hour walk to repulse bay. around chinese new year, a lot of people will go to see chinese bell flowers. in fact, you can see the beautiful sea view as well as the green bushes covered by red chinese bell flowers. as there are so many steps, be cautious when you go downhill to tse kong bridge (紫崗橋) where is the junction to repulse bay (right hand side), tai tam (left hand side) and the twins ( front ).

owner myo zaw is an amazing man! he can book tours, bus tickets, private taxis, and boat tours. the e-bikes are in great condition and function perfectly. well priced and the best way to see bagan. he works very hard to help in any way he can. best service in bagan by far! they also have a facebook page with information on services and prices.

owner was super friendly and passionate, museum is super awesome! every inch is punk and it clearly took a lot of time to create. i especially enjoyed listening to the songs and finding some new favorites. totally worth it for tourists and locals alike
owner was very helpful in finding a wetsuit despite me being nearly 7ft tall. didn’t upsell me either for my needs. will be going back
owner was very kind, let us sample the products and threw in a freebie. really great array of products and trinkets

pablo at seven lakes was amazing, he helped us arrange a car for a few days at very competitive rates compared to the big companies, and also some outings in bariloche that were amazing. they also offer custom packages for people looking for something more bespoke, in both seasons. we visited during summer and did lots of hiking, the car was indispensable for getting around easily. would easily go back!

padar island is absolutely breathtaking! the hike to the top is a bit challenging, especially in the heat, but every step is worth it once you reach the summit. the panoramic view of the three bays with their contrasting colors is truly unforgettable. go early in the morning to catch the sunrise, it’s magical. don’t forget water, good shoes, and your camera. a must-visit spot when you're in komodo.

padar island is the first stop on the day trip package with most touring operators. you get to climb the top of the hill here and see some breathtaking views of the nature, the hike is worth the effort. the steps are easy to climb on except at the last section where it gets a little difficult for people who are mostly sedentary otherwise.

paddle boarding on lake brienz was amazing. beautiful, picturesque and fun. nicole was great, you can message her on whatsapp, she helped us figure out the bus and how to get there. i would highly recommend!!
pagoda visited during ceremony toilets near by foe free

paid $65 a ticket. that covers general membership to wait in the regular line. you need to have your ticket purchased before you are allowed to wait in the regular line. very busy when they first open. i see why they recommend coming in the 2nd half of the day or so. aquarium was pretty cool! jellyfish variety and sea otters were my favorite part. love that it is right on the water. also loved seeing the otters in the wild behind the aquarium on their provided telescopes

paid 15k shilling pp. we recently visited this beautiful local indigenous garden and had a wonderful time! i appreciated the opportunity to hold the camaleons - it was a unique experience. however, i did feel that the tour could be improved by providing more specific information about the local wildlife, particularly the different butterfly species. one important note: please be extremely careful when entering the camaleon enclosure, as it's easy to accidentally step on them. overall, i would still recommend this garden to nature lovers and those looking for an authentic local experience.
paid 250 to get in the door and after less than 10 minutes of massaging got hassled by the girl for 1000 more. settled on much less but was only there for about 40 minutes total. wouldn’t recommend

paid 9000 yen for two to silent world - its essentially puzzle / board games played in silence. the game design had pretty silly parts to it but the worst part was the anticlimatic ending that ruined the whole experience. if it wasn't so overpriced, i'd consider their other "escape rooms" but i really should have listened to the 1 star reviews. so here's another to add to the pile.

paid the ticket to get a quick glimpse of different spanish regions without flying. but things artificial here and the plaza was replaced with plastic cover for seatings. can’t see well but none the less we had a good time walking and see the view over looking the city. the shops are cute too.
paige was amazing and the tour was definitely worth it. recommend to anybody visiting cairns and loves hiking/waterfalls.

paintings might be massed produced. everything looks very similar, so it could be a print where they add custom oil painting textures on top of the canvas. workers may or may not have unofficially unionised, the bags wont go under $10, and the shirts and dresses $8. check alibaba prices before purchase. outside of that, fun experience haggling with the vendors cus they'll try to charge you a lot more for their products. 😂

paisagem muito bonita e a história da raquel macabra. para apreciar a paisagem não pode descer até a caverna. tem corais preservados no local, certo tem que preservar. achei muito bonita a paisagem de quem chega vira à direita.

paje beach is absolutely stunning! the white sand, clear turquoise water, and laid-back vibe make it one of the best beaches in zanzibar. it’s perfect for relaxing, swimming, or trying out kitesurfing—especially during windy season. there are great beach bars and restaurants nearby, with fresh seafood and chilled drinks. whether you’re looking for adventure or just a peaceful escape, paje beach has it all. highly recommended.

pak tai temple is a traditional chinese temple dedicated to the taoist deity pak tai (also known as the supreme emperor of the dark heaven) and is located in the wan chai district of hong kong island. although it is located in a relatively urban area, there are nearby parks where you can find a place to rest and enjoy the surroundings. here's some information about pak tai temple and the nearby park: pak tai temple: pak tai temple in wan chai is one of the oldest temples in hong kong, dating back to the early 19th century. it is known for its architectural style, intricate decoration and religious significance. the temple offers a tranquil and spiritual atmosphere in the midst of the bustling city. nearby park: victoria park is a large public park located in causeway bay, which borders wan chai. it is one of hong kong's most popular parks and offers various amenities and places to relax. here you will find lush greenery, walking paths, benches and open spaces for leisure activities. victoria park is an ideal place to rest and relax after visiting pak tai temple. in addition, wan chai is surrounded by the natural beauty of victoria harbour, and the waterfront promenade provides a pleasant setting for a leisurely stroll and relaxation. while there are other parks and resting areas near pak tai temple in wan chai, victoria park is the most notable and accessible option nearby.

palace downtown & burj khalifa view we had an unforgettable experience staying at the palace downtown. the hotel is pure elegance — from the traditional arabian architecture to the exceptional service. our room had a stunning view of the burj khalifa and the dubai fountain — it honestly felt like a dream. waking up to the world’s tallest building right outside the window was incredible. the location is perfect, just steps away from dubai mall and the fountain show. highly recommended for a luxurious and memorable stay in the heart of dubai!

palace with western architecture design ans built during the time of emperor gojong as the royal library. there are exhibits about the important turn in korean history. it was a witness to the infamous eulsa treaty (japan-korea protectorate treaty), an illegal treaty forced by japan, was signed in 1905.

paradise, found if your dream is to experience a tropical paradise that's still largely untouched by people, your next travelling destination should be wayag island seen here. it's part of the raja ampat district in the province of west papua, indonesia. most of the roughly 50,000 inhabitants of this district live on or around its four main islands, batanta, misool, salawati, and waigeo. the remainder of raja ampat is made up of roughly 1,500 smaller islands, cays, and shoals – astonishingly, hundreds of these tiny islands have yet to be explored by humans. divers and snorkelers, especially, treasure raja ampat and its vast and diverse reef system, which is considered one of the most biodiverse places in the world. located roughly seven miles above the equator, raja ampat covers nearly 10 million acres of land and sea, and is home to 540 types of corals, more than 1,000 types of coral reef fish, 700 types of mollusks, and a variety of warm-blooded marine animals like the dugong. the ecosystem, which is part of a larger tropical ocean area called the coral triangle, is so diverse it's sometimes referred to as the 'the amazon of the seas.' © amazing aerial agency/offset by shutterstoc

pariser platz is a historic square located at the eastern end of berlin’s iconic unter den linden boulevard, just in front of the brandenburg gate. named after the french capital following prussia’s victory over napoleon in 1814, it has long been a symbol of berlin’s rich history. once a vibrant center of aristocratic life, the square was heavily damaged during world war ii and remained desolate during the cold war due to its proximity to the berlin wall. since german reunification, pariser platz has been beautifully restored and is now surrounded by notable buildings, including the hotel adlon and embassies, making it a cultural and architectural hub in modern berlin.

part therapy, part chaos, all-out fun. for $17 a head, you get 45 minutes inside a controlled demolition fantasy. up to ten or maybe fifteen people per room—can’t remember exactly, but enough to feel like a small riot. each person gets ten items to destroy: plates, bottled, printers, whatever’s been begging to meet a sledgehammer. if you’re feeling ambitious, you can pitch in with friends and buy larger targets—appliances, tvs, things that once mattered to someone. it’s weirdly satisfying to obliterate something functional just for the hell of it. then there’s the paint room: a full-on war zone where you’re handed a loaded paint gun and told to go wild. no rules, no canvas, just your friends and a room waiting to get jackson pollocked with your chaos. you’ll walk out dripping in color, a human art experiment gone wrong in all the right ways. if you want to take it a step further, you can rent the entire place out—three hours for somewhere between $1200 and $1500. i don’t remember the exact number, but if you’re celebrating something—or need to exorcise a particularly bad breakup—it’s worth every penny. locals (kama‘āina), military, and weekday warriors get discounts, and honestly, there’s nothing else like it in hawaii. it’s the only one of its kind, and it delivers. the staff are cool, helpful, and somehow not fazed by watching strangers destroy things for fun. it’s weird, it’s cathartic, and it’s an absolute blast.

penataran agung lempuyang temple is a stunning and culturally rich site, and it truly breaks my heart to give only 3 stars. the staff are incredibly friendly and helpful, and the grounds offer countless photo opportunities, including the world‑famous “heaven’s gate” view with the mountains perfectly framed behind you. the experience is very well organized with a fair system for guests, calling numbers for photo turns and providing a photographer who uses your phone and a mirror to create that iconic reflection effect. the reason for the lower rating is the wait. unless you arrive by around 5 a.m., you can expect to wait anywhere from 2 to 6 hours for your turn at the main photo spot. for many visitors this makes the visit exhausting and limits the time you have to enjoy the temple itself. it is still worth seeing for the beauty and cultural experience, but the long wait keeps it from being the magical stop it could be.

perched at over 14,000 feet above sea level in hanle, ladakh, the indian astronomical observatory (iao) ranks among the highest observatories in the world. its remote himalayan setting offers pristine skies, minimal light pollution, and ideal conditions for stargazing and astronomical research. visitors can marvel at advanced scientific work while soaking in the serene beauty of the surrounding landscape. a vital hub for space exploration, the iao is also an emerging hotspot for astro-tourism, blending cutting-edge science with the awe-inspiring backdrop of the mountains.

perched atop singapore’s iconic marina bay sands, the skypark observation deck is nothing short of breathtaking. from sunrise to the city’s glittering skyline at night, the 360° views are cinematic. gardens by the bay, the flyer, and the entire marina bay stretch laid out like a living postcard. the experience feels effortlessly luxurious yet accessible, with smooth entry, helpful staff, and vantage points perfect for photos or quiet contemplation. a must-visit for anyone wanting to see singapore from its most elevated perspective.

perched on a hill overlooking port louis, citadelle (fort adelaide) is a 19th-century fortress built by the british. named after the wife of king william iv, queen adelaide, it offers panoramic views of the city, harbor, and surrounding mountains. constructed from black basalt rocks in a moorish style, the fort was intended to protect the port and quell potential local unrest but was never used for military purposes. today, it stands as a historical landmark offering insights into the colonial era. visitors can explore the well-preserved grounds, view old cannons, and enjoy the 360-degree vistas. the former barracks have been transformed into **boutique shops**. the fort is also becoming a cultural hub, hosting events and performances. a visit to citadelle provides a blend of history and stunning scenery, making it a worthwhile stop in port louis. it's recommended to visit in the late afternoon to enjoy cooler temperatures and potentially a beautiful sunset over the city.

petra, jordan – a breathtaking wonder of the world visiting petra, jordan, was an unforgettable experience, truly deserving of its status as one of the new seven wonders of the world. from the moment i walked through the siq—a narrow, winding canyon flanked by towering sandstone walls—i was in awe of the sheer beauty and mystery of this ancient city. reaching the iconic treasury (al-khazneh) was a surreal moment. the sight of its intricate carvings emerging from the rock face was nothing short of magical. as i explored further, i was amazed by the vastness of petra. the royal tombs, the street of facades, and the massive monastery (ad-deir) were all remarkable, each telling a story of the nabataean civilization that once thrived here. the hike to the monastery was challenging but absolutely worth it. the panoramic views from the top were breathtaking, offering a moment of peace and reflection amidst the rugged beauty of the desert landscape. along the way, local bedouins selling handmade crafts added to the authenticity of the experience. petra is more than just a tourist site—it’s a journey through history, culture, and stunning natural beauty. whether visiting by day or witnessing petra by night, when the treasury is illuminated by candlelight, the experience is nothing short of magical. i highly recommend this trip to anyone who loves adventure, history, and the wonder of the ancient world.

phenomenal. one of the best geysers in yellowstone, better than old faithful but nowhere near as crowded. you will need more patience to see it tho, it only erupts once or twice a day and then within a four hour window. i think that time can be whittled down tho depending on how much observation it’s been given. if you drive past and see a lot of people waiting don’t be afraid to ask someone where it’s at. it’s worth waiting for. doesn’t always reach as high as old faithful, but eruptions last much longer. it is also perfectly named, erupting in majestic bursts out of a large terraced platform. watching the water cascade down these terraces is almost as fun as the eruption itself. the eruptions are rather variable in size and consist of many series of bursts. usually the first series is the largest, but even a “weak” eruption is worth the wait. if you’re waiting and the eruption is not imminent a fun geyser can be found across the road. walk back the the pullout for surprise spring and watch out over the flat area to the east. about a hundred yards away is boytroidal geyser, which is comparatively small but erupts with an explosive start every 5-8 minutes. if you watch carefully you may see the entire pool of water lift in a large “blue bubble”

phimeanakas temple, nestled within the grand expanse of angkor thom in siem reap, offers a glimpse into the spiritual heart of the khmer empire. visiting this temple with my family was a remarkable experience that left us in awe of its historical significance and serene beauty. unlike the more famous temples like angkor wat or bayon, phimeanakas is often quieter, allowing visitors to fully immerse themselves in its peaceful ambiance. climbing its steep, ancient steps, we found ourselves transported back in time, imagining what life must have been like during the reign of the khmer kings who once walked these grounds. the view from the top, while modest in comparison to some of the larger temples, provided a serene overlook of the surrounding jungle, with towering trees embracing the structure in a timeless embrace. what struck me the most about phimeanakas was the palpable sense of history. the temple, once part of the royal palace complex, is said to have been a site of great ritual importance. as we explored the stone corridors and admired the intricate carvings, my family and i felt as though we were retracing the steps of cambodia’s ancient royalty. for those who appreciate quieter, less crowded spots within the angkor complex, phimeanakas is a must-visit. it’s a temple that exudes mystery and tranquility, offering a unique and intimate perspective on the grandeur of angkor thom. whether you’re a history enthusiast, a culture lover, or simply looking for a peaceful place to reflect, phimeanakas temple will not disappoint.

phnom kulen: a sacred escape into nature as a local guide, phnom kulen national park is a destination i highly recommend for those looking to combine natural beauty with spiritual significance. often considered the birthplace of the ancient khmer empire, this sacred mountain offers a refreshing escape from the temple crowds and a chance to connect with cambodia's rich history and stunning landscapes. the highlight for many visitors is the impressive waterfall, which provides a perfect spot for swimming and relaxation, especially on a warm day. beyond the cascades, you'll discover the river of a thousand lingas, an extraordinary site where thousands of phallic symbols are carved into the sandstone riverbed, a testament to ancient hindu beliefs. another significant stop is the preah ang thom pagoda, home to a massive reclining buddha carved into a natural sandstone boulder. the panoramic views from the top are truly breathtaking and offer a sense of peace and tranquility. phnom kulen is not just about historical sites; it's also a place of lush jungle, diverse wildlife, and a cooler climate, making it ideal for a day trip. i always encourage visitors to appreciate the serene atmosphere and the deep cultural importance this mountain holds for the cambodian people. a perfect blend of history, spirituality, and natural beauty, offering a unique perspective on the angkor region!

phsa kroum market (also spelled psah krom) is a bustling local market in siem reap, offering a true taste of everyday cambodian life. unlike the more touristy markets in the city, this spot is where locals shop for fresh produce, meats, spices, and street food at affordable prices. highlights: ✔️ authentic local experience – this is not a tourist market; you’ll see cambodians buying groceries, grabbing breakfast, or enjoying a quick snack. ✔️ delicious street food – try khmer noodles, grilled meats, fresh fruits, and traditional sweets. the fried bananas (chek chien) and num pang (cambodian sandwiches) are must-tries! ✔️ affordable prices – much cheaper than markets like psar chaa (old market), making it great for budget travelers. ✔️ fresh produce & seafood – vibrant selection of tropical fruits, vegetables, and live fish. things to note: ⚠️ not a tourist market – few vendors speak english, and signage is mostly in khmer, so be ready for gestures and simple exchanges. ⚠️ cash only – bring small riel or usd notes. ⚠️ early hours – best visited in the morning (6–9 am) when the food is freshest. final thoughts: if you want an off-the-beaten-path market experience away from souvenir stalls, phsa kroum is worth a visit. it’s messy, lively, and full of local charm—just come with an open mind and an empty stomach!

phyang monastery, also known as gangon tashi chodzong, is a captivating spiritual and cultural gem located just 15 kilometers west of leh, ladakh. nestled amidst the stark beauty of the himalayas, this 16th-century monastery offers an unforgettable blend of ancient buddhist tradition, architectural elegance, and breathtaking natural scenery. as one of the few drikung kagyu monasteries in ladakh, phyang holds significant religious importance. the monastery complex is beautifully preserved, with elaborately painted prayer halls, age-old thangkas, and a remarkable four-meter statue of buddha that inspires awe and reverence. the sense of peace within its walls is truly profound—whether you're a spiritual seeker, a history enthusiast, or a casual traveler, you'll feel a deep sense of calm and wonder here. the monastery also houses a fascinating museum that showcases over 900 years of history, including rare buddhist artifacts, scriptures, and even ancient chinese and mongolian weaponry. it offers an insightful glimpse into ladakh’s spiritual lineage and cultural exchanges across centuries. if you're lucky enough to visit during the annual phyang tsedup festival (usually in july or august), you'll witness vibrant mask dances and age-old rituals that bring the monastery's spiritual heritage vividly to life. reaching phyang is easy—a scenic 30-minute drive from leh through a picturesque landscape of high desert and rugged mountains. the monastery is less crowded than others like hemis or thiksey, which allows for a more personal and reflective experience. the monks are welcoming, and guided tours can occasionally be arranged for deeper understanding. highly recommended for those looking to explore ladakh’s spiritual heart beyond the usual tourist trail. phyang monastery is more than just a place to visit—it's a place to experience. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

phyang monastery, located about 15 km from leh, is a hidden treasure of ladakh that beautifully blends history, spirituality, and breathtaking scenery. perched on a hill overlooking the vast indus valley, this monastery belongs to the drikung kagyu sect of tibetan buddhism and holds immense historical and cultural significance. while it may not be as famous as some of the larger monasteries in ladakh, its peaceful atmosphere and stunning surroundings make it a must-visit for travelers looking for an authentic experience. history and significance founded in the 16th century by king tashi namgyal, phyang monastery has been a center of buddhist learning and meditation for centuries. the monastery is home to numerous monks who dedicate their lives to prayer, study, and maintaining the sacred traditions of their sect. it houses a remarkable collection of ancient murals, thangkas (tibetan buddhist paintings), and religious artifacts that showcase the rich artistic and spiritual heritage of the region. one of the most fascinating aspects of phyang monastery is its strong connection to tibetan buddhism’s drikung kagyu lineage. this sect is known for its deep-rooted meditation practices and teachings, and visitors can often witness monks engaged in prayers and rituals that have been passed down through generations. the monastery also houses a school where young monks receive both spiritual and modern education, preserving ladakh’s monastic traditions while adapting to the contemporary world. architecture and art the monastery’s architecture is a classic example of traditional tibetan buddhist design, with whitewashed walls, golden rooftops, and intricately decorated interiors. the main prayer hall is adorned with vibrant murals depicting buddhist deities, historical events, and teachings from sacred scriptures. these paintings are not only visually captivating but also serve as an important means of preserving buddhist philosophy and culture.

piazza san marco, or st. mark's square, is the principal square in venice, italy, and one of the most famous public spaces in the world. it has been the heart of venice for centuries, serving as a center of political, religious, and social life since the middle ages. surrounded by iconic landmarks such as saint mark's basilica (basilica di san marco), the doge's palace (palazzo ducale), the campanile (bell tower), and the procuratie vecchie and nuove (historic buildings), piazza san marco is known for its architectural grandeur and historical significance. the square is paved with intricate patterns of marble and features elegant cafes, shops, and restaurants that attract visitors and locals alike. one of the highlights of piazza san marco is its role as a gathering place for festivals, processions, and cultural events throughout the year. the square's open space, surrounded by arcades and historic buildings, offers stunning views of the basilica's domes and the bustling waterfront of the venetian lagoon. piazza san marco continues to be a vibrant hub of activity, drawing millions of tourists who come to admire its architectural treasures, soak in its atmosphere, and experience the timeless allure of venice's cultural and historical legacy.

pier 39 is absolutely iconic and the sea lions are the real stars of the show! these adorable marine mammals have been calling k-dock home since the 1989 earthquake, and watching them is endlessly entertaining - they're constantly sunbathing, barking at each other, and diving into the water. peak season is january when you can see over 2,000 sea lions, though summer numbers are lower but they're still there year-round. the sea lion center offers free educational exhibits about these amazing creatures, plus there's a 24/7 webcam if you want to check them out online first. but honestly, seeing them in person is so much better - their antics will have you laughing for hours! beyond the sea lions, there's tons to do here. the two-story venetian carousel is beautiful, aquarium of the bay has 20,000 local marine animals, and street performers provide free entertainment throughout the day. shopping and dining options are endless with 110 stores and restaurants - definitely try the dungeness crab sandwich! located right at beach street & embarcadero in the heart of fisherman's wharf, it's super accessible by public transit. there's 24-hour parking across the street. the pier itself is free to explore, though individual attractions charge admission. pro tip: bring a jacket as it gets windy, and plan 2-3 hours to really enjoy everything. winter is best for maximum sea lion action, but any time of year is great for this quintessential sf experience!

planning a trip to costa rica isn't easy, since you have so many choices. rather than stay on the coast, where many friends recommended, we chose to immerse ourselves in the rain forest (despite being the rainy season) - which is truly unique to this beautiful country. friends also recommended trying different hotels, but we chose to spend the entire week at the springs at arenal, just outside of la fortuna. boy, did we make the perfect choices! we had a the most glorious week, taking excursions each day to zip-line, hike two different volcanos and numerous breath-taking waterfalls, tube down the azure-colored rio celeste, and white water raft down the balsa river. the best, however, was starting and finishing our days at the springs. each morning, we opened our drapes to the most majestic view of the arenal volcano and had a delicious breakfast with breath-taking views. then, after a full-day of activities, we got home in time to enjoy natural spring baths that soothed our aching muscles. the hot springs at the hotel's club rio were particularly special. what really sets the springs apart is the staff. everyone is always smiling and quick to greet you. if ever the phrase "pura vida" applies, it's here at the springs. enjoy!

planting fields arboretum is such a beautiful and peaceful escape from the city! the grounds are incredibly well-kept, with something lovely to see in every direction — from vibrant gardens to quiet wooded paths. the greenhouse is a must-see, filled with exotic plants and a tropical feel that’s great year-round. it’s the perfect place for a long walk, a picnic, or just some time to relax in nature. the historic coe hall adds a charming touch, and there’s plenty of space to explore without feeling crowded. definitely one of my favorite spots on long island — a hidden gem worth visiting in every season.

playa ruinas at tulum is a breathtaking fusion of natural beauty and historical intrigue. nestled below the iconic cliffside mayan ruins, this beach offers turquoise waters and soft white sand, creating a serene escape. visitors can marvel at el castillo towering above while enjoying a swim or sunbathe. perfect for photography, history lovers, and beach enthusiasts, it combines a cultural journey with coastal tranquility. early visits ensure quieter moments in this stunning paradise.

plaza de la proclamación is a beautiful, historic square in the heart of cartagena’s old town, right across from bolívar park and next to the cathedral. anchored by the stunningly restored palacio de la proclamación, now a cultural center. a statue of pope john paul ii stands at the entrance to the plaza, and the entire space feels alive with history, architecture, and local life. during my visit to the plaza, i came across an elderly man sitting quietly with a few bags of corn. as i approached, he stood and as if on cue, birds flew to him, perching on his hands, shoulders, even his head. he fed them in a way i had never seen before: holding kernels between his teeth, letting the pigeons gently take them from his mouth. the trust between them was astonishing, clearly nurtured over many quiet, patient encounters. he welcomed me to take photos without asking for anything in return. his kindness and the silent bond he shared with the birds left a deep impression on me. i offered him 20,000 pesos as a small thank you. in the heart of a bustling city, this quiet, beautiful moment reminded me that connection and gentleness still thrive, often in the most unexpected places.

plaza de la trinidad, the beating heart of getsemaní (pronounced 'heth-se-mah-nee'), is a captivating crossroads of cultures and experiences. to simply say it's a 'town square' feels like an understatement; it's a vibrant, living stage where the world comes to play. i found myself drawn back time and again, spending hours just observing the fascinating tapestry of humanity unfolding before me. travelers from every corner of the globe mingle with locals, creating a truly electric atmosphere. the sensory delights don't stop there. the air is thick with the tantalizing aromas of street food, a culinary adventure in itself. from arepas sizzling on grills to the sweet scent of tropical fruits, there's something to tempt every palate. the surrounding bars, each with its own unique character, offer a dizzying array of beverages, ensuring you'll find the perfect drink to complement the evening's mood. what truly sets plaza de la trinidad apart is its laid-back, effortlessly cool ambiance. it's a place where time seems to slow down, allowing you to fully immerse yourself in the moment. my airbnb's proximity, a mere ten feet away, was a stroke of luck, granting me front-row seats to this nightly spectacle. even at 2 am, the plaza felt remarkably safe and welcoming, a testament to the neighborhood's vibrant yet peaceful spirit. the magic truly begins to unfold between 9 pm and midnight. as the sun dips below the horizon, the plaza transforms into a lively hub of activity, illuminated by the warm glow of streetlights and the chatter of excited voices. for a truly unique experience, visit on a sunday. the church, with its doors wide open, provides a serene counterpoint to the lively atmosphere, offering a moment of spiritual reflection and a profound sense of peace. the juxtaposition of the lively square and the tranquil church creates a divine and unforgettable experience. plaza de la trinidad is not just a place to visit; it's a place to experience, to savor, and to remember.

plaza las américas in san juan is absolutely stunning and such a unique shopping experience. the mall is huge, bright, and beautifully designed — from the tall ceilings with skylights to the palm trees that give it a tropical yet modern feel. everything is spotless, well-maintained, and welcoming. what makes it even better is the variety you can find here. there are so many stores, from international brands to local puerto rican shops, plus a wide selection of restaurants and cafés where you can relax in between shopping. you can easily spend hours walking around without ever feeling cramped, since the spaces are open and airy. the atmosphere feels both elegant and family-friendly. it’s more than just a mall — it’s really a destination where you can shop, dine, and enjoy a comfortable environment. every time i visit puerto rico, plaza las américas is a stop i never want to miss. it’s not just about shopping, it’s about enjoying the beauty and energy of one of the largest malls in the caribbean.

ploče gate is a beautiful entry into dubrovnik’s old town, featuring amazing clover-shaped (quatrefoil) wall openings with great views. these gothic-style details are a unique part of the city’s heritage and architectural beauty, well worth stopping to admire.

ploče gate serves as a magnificent entryway to the eastern side of dubrovnik's old town, offering a charming and slightly quieter alternative to the bustling pile gate. as you approach ploče gate, you'll be greeted by its impressive stone arches and historic architecture, which seamlessly blend into the iconic city walls. passing through ploče gate, you're immediately transported into the enchanting world of dubrovnik's old town. the cobblestone streets are lined with beautifully preserved medieval buildings, each telling its own story of the city's rich past. the old town is a unesco world heritage site, and it's easy to see why, with its stunning gothic, renaissance, and baroque churches, palaces, and fountains. one of the highlights of entering through ploče gate is the breathtaking view of the bustling harbor and the shimmering adriatic sea. this vantage point offers a picturesque scene, perfect for photography enthusiasts and those who appreciate scenic beauty. exploring the old town from ploče gate allows you to wander through quieter, less crowded streets, discovering charming squares and hidden gems along the way. whether you're indulging in local cuisine at a quaint café, shopping for unique souvenirs, or simply soaking in the historical ambiance, ploče gate and the old town provide an unforgettable experience for anyone visiting croatia.

pr39 smi – quatro fábricas da luz this easy trail winds through forest and open areas, passing the ruins of four old hydroelectric power stations — quiet, mossy, and full of history. locals often swim in the river pools, and there’s a rope swing near the start for jumping in on warm days. along the way, you’ll see waterfalls, basalt walls, pipes, and old canals reclaimed by nature. the round trip takes about an hour, depending on photo stops and whether you take a refreshing dip. a large parking lot is on estrada regional 1-1, so no need to drive down to lugar da praia / trinta réis. cross the road and head downhill between the houses to start the hike — you won’t miss any highlights.

pr9 - about 12.6 kms round trip to caldeirão verde and back. a long, lush, green and relatively flat trail with a few dark tunnels and pretty waterfalls. took us about 4.5 hours starting at 13:00. outbound we met a lot of traffic on the trail, it was more quiet heading back. make sure to bring a torch or a headlight. the trail is rather standard and monotone for the first hour, before you hit the first tunnel. the last bit with the tunnels and the waterfall is nice. due to the trail being flat, it's relatively easy. only a few stairs during the trail around the first waterfall. if you suffer from vertigo or fear of heights, there will be challenging bits. however the trail is nicely fenced at the most narrow bits. parking became a lot easier post lunch time, when most of the morning teams returned. it's a nice hike, but honestly. if you have the fitness level and only a few hiking days during your trip to madeira, i'd highly recommend pr6 (25 waterfalls one) instead of pr9. it's virtually better in every aspect. more options, more changing scenery, more waterfalls, a more pretty levada and beautiful mountain ranges. however no tunnels as the only downside.

prague's old town hall is one of the city's most beautiful historical landmarks. it is a famous astronomical clock built in 1410 ad, the third of its kind, attracting crowds of tourists every hour. it offers a stunning panoramic view of prague's red rooftops, old town square, and the vltava river. the building's historic atmosphere and well-preserved interior make the experience even more special. if you visit prague, don't miss a visit to this iconic landmark! the clock is located on the south wall of the old town hall in old town square. the clock mechanism consists of three main components: the astronomical disc, which represents the position of the sun and moon in the sky and displays various astronomical details; statues of various catholic saints standing on either side of the clock; the "march of the apostles," an hourly display of animated apostles and other sculptures, notably a skeleton representing death, striking the time; and a calendar disc with medallions representing the months. according to local legend, the city will suffer if the clock is neglected and its good work is jeopardized. a ghost attached to the clock is said to nod its head in confirmation. legend also states that the only hope lies in a boy born on new year's eve.

pre rup temple is one of the most impressive and underrated temples in the angkor archaeological park. built in the 10th century by king rajendravarman ii, this stunning hindu temple is a masterpiece of khmer architecture and offers a quieter, more peaceful experience compared to the crowded angkor wat. what i loved: - breathtaking sunset views – climb to the top tier for an unforgettable panoramic view, especially during sunset. the reddish bricks glow magically in the golden light. - rich history & architecture – the temple’s unique pyramid-style structure and intricate carvings showcase the brilliance of ancient khmer craftsmanship. - less crowded – unlike the more famous temples, pre rup offers a serene atmosphere, perfect for photography and quiet exploration. - great photo opportunities – the combination of towering prasats (towers), ancient stonework, and surrounding jungle makes it a photographer’s dream.

probably one of the most beautiful beaches in the world! white sand, impressive granite boulders, and turquoise waters in a stunning setting. the walk through l’union estate to get there is beautiful in itself. i visited in august, and the sea was pleasantly warm — around 26–28°c, which is normal for the seychelles that time of year. even so, this is a place you should experience at least once in your life.

probably one of the most beautiful places to shop or have afternoon tea. quite well maintained considering how old it is. we had afternoon tea at the tea palace where the teapots and teacups were divine. all of life’s indulgences can be found her - fine chocolate, beautiful clothes, shoes and souvenirs, art, jewellery, tea, spices and much more. easy to get to via light rail, bus or car - parking entrance in york st.
probably one of the nicer geysers if you're lucky to catch the eruption. it's on the boardwalk near old faithful.

probably the best 'promenade' in the world. easy parking nearby, access subway takes you under the railway onto the walkway start. turn right and head south. you'll end up at the well photographed coloured beach huts and can go a little further almost to kalk bay
probably the best architect and interior designer in israel for hotels, residential and commercial properties
probably the best coffee i had in vienna. very tasty and well prepared. friendly staff and a relaxed atmosphere.

probably the best coffee in vienna, definitely top 3. the flavour of the 8.6 flat white was really good and the milk work was the best i’d had in the city. setting is, of course, brilliant and it’s a good place to come and chill.

probably the best excursion i have ever done on a trip. you board, the crew explains the rules, there’s unlimited wine s d soft drinks on coses, beer for purchase, and they feed you dinner. i had a pork souvlaki, that was amazing. it came with fresh greek salad, stuffed grape leaves and tzatziki. the crew was super fun, and the swimming and snorkeling was amazing. 10/10 would book again.

probably the best hostel i've stayed at, the staff was incredibly friendly, and the rooms and facilities were clean. there is a bar open from ~17:00-22:00, and unfortunately after 22:00 you can't hang out in the outside area (due to noise regulations as i understood it). i saw some reviews about pillows being bad, but didn't have any issues, i guess that depends per person. there's a lot to do in interlaken and surrounding area, the hostel is only a ~15min walk from the train station interlaken west&ost, and there's a supermarket close by too. as a solo traveller, the common areas and bar are were great, and there were daily activities planned as well (bingo, dancing classes, kayaking). had a great time here, shoutout to the aussie bartender.
probably the best place to see lavender in sapporo during july season without the need going to furano. less international tourists coming to this garden.👍

probably the best water park in thailand if not in asia. the park is huge with many water slides and other fun attractions for kids at all ages. we went in the low season so the weather was a bit rainy but not too bad at all, so there weren't too many people and almost no queues. we even took a cabana for 70$ for the entire day, which was awesome beacse the kids had a relatively easy time remembering exactly where we are and come back between slides to eat and drink.

probably the biggest food market in the country, and maybe the oldest one. it is way over fruits, vegetables, and food. people can enjoy great pubs here, restaurants with global and local food, an amazing atmosphere, and tourists from many countries.

probably the most beautiful monastery around leh. most of the people take the main road and cross the bridge. i'd recommend going to hemis first and then taking the back road to stakna. the views are incredible this with almost no crowds or vehicles and you get to see stakna from a vantage point like no other, with an amazing backdrop of the mountains.

probably the most beautiful monastery of ladakh with the mix of paintings and big buddha statues. unique place. cannot take pictures which allows for a nice environment. closed for one hour for lunch.

probably the most expensive activity to do in bali, but totally worth it. not the tourist trap i thought it would be. all so well arranged, clean. staff is so available and friendly. slides are perfect. really you do not need a place to sit at any gazebo, there is so much to do and there are plenty of options to relax.

probably the most famous flower fields in furano given how all the tour buses were stopping here. very crowded with tourists. the flower fields were nice and well maintained but i cant help to feel that other less crowded ones nearby were more lush and more enjoyable. still, worth a visit. especially enjoyed the gentle fragrance of lavender wafting in the air

probably the most professional dive shop. the staff are incredibly friendly and so helpful with setting up your gear - from the tanks to helping you put on your fins. i got sea sick before our second dive and they were so helpful in making me feel better and getting into the water first. dive sites are incredible - visibility of over 15 meters, gorgeous coral and incredible sea life including sharks, rays, turtles and massive fish. we did 4 days and wish we’d done more!

probably the most underrated temple in kyoto by far! i mean there’s a reason it’s a unesco world heritage site. it is not as popular as most other temples in the area which is great! no queues or crowds. you will get your money’s worth. be sure to go inside all the temples if you can. photography is prohibited inside the temples but it is definitely something to behold! we were lucky enough to be able to visit the temple during one of their special night viewings. there’s something special about seeing the statues inside the temples light up while still being surrounded by the darkness of night. the temple garden was also quite beautiful to walk around, especially at night.

probably the nicest, cleanest, and most luxurious hot springs experience we’ve ever had!! we went off season so it was super empty and all of the amenities were amazing. super clean and well maintained. the way they designed the experience to also be symbolic of the local tribes journey to the area was incredible. we did the 2 hour restorative journey, which i highly recommend unless you also plan to get a massage!

probably the second most famous formation in yellowstone after grand prismatic. this is a site you have to visit, either as the last one on the geyser trails from old faithful, or better still as part of doing the biscuit basin trail, which a lot less people get to experience. due to the way the platforms are arranged, if you want to get a complete shot you need a selfie stick giving you at least 3m/10ft height. you can then get some amazing shots. i would definitely recommend spending some time doing this and the rest of the trail.

procuratie vecchie is a remarkable historical building located in venice, offering a glimpse into the city's rich architectural heritage. the structure is beautifully preserved, showcasing intricate designs and craftsmanship. it's a must-visit for anyone interested in exploring venice's history and architecture. the atmosphere around the building is serene, making it a perfect spot for a leisurely stroll and appreciation of the city's past. highly recommended for history buffs and architecture enthusiasts looking to immerse themselves in venice's cultural legacy!

profitis ilias is highest point of santorini and 360 view is magnificent with holy vibe. you can visit church, enjoy sunrise and sunset beside view. air is super fresh and sometimes it is foggy. if you want to experience inside foggy feeling then this is the point. just go and enjoy, fully recommended.

pros: • peaceful oasis in the heart of the city • beautiful landscaping and serene atmosphere • great spot to relax between attractions • easy to access during a short walk cons: • not a large garden, more of a quick stop former yasuda garden was such a lovely surprise during our day in tokyo. tucked away in a busy area, it offered a peaceful and relaxing break from the city bustle. we stopped here on a short walk between attractions and were so glad we did. the landscaping is beautiful and the atmosphere is calm—exactly what you need to recharge. highly recommend this spot as a quiet respite during a busy day of sightseeing.

provides a delightful overlook of old town and the rest of dubrovnik. the stones and mortar, the layout, and the strategic views ooze of the history of the fortress. it harkens to a time when people cared about form and function in combination, not one over the other. be cautious of the slick surfaces and wear good walking shoes, sandals will not help you. the steps are deep and steep, with handrails that don’t always give confidence. just know, even if it feels “unsafe” compared to other things you could do, just know that you will regret not walking this section of the old town fortress wall.

psa: visit the garden. that 600 yen fee was one of my best purchases. out of all places i visited in japan, heian jingu garden is where i took the most photos. as for the main shrine itself, it was under renovation when i visited so i couldn't yap much about it. it was a weekday afternoon in late spring and i had the honor to experience the garden with no other soul in sight. it's either tourists are sleeping on this place, kyoto overtourism is a hoax, or i slipped into a glitch on the matrix. anyway, just look at the pictures and you'll understand why this place is dangerous. one minute longer and i might delude myself that i'm the main lead in an imperial drama, instead of the npc.

psar chaa (old market) is an all day market located between the famous pub street and the siem reap river. this is a place for both locals and tourists alike depending on what you are looking for. you will find a high number of stalls selling food stock, vegetables, fruits, meats, fish pastes, rice, spices, candies and other sundries. you will also find shops selling souvenirs, t-shirts, silks, artworks and other typical items for tourists. some of the old market exterior is of french colonial architecture. otherwise, i'm not certain how far back the market history dates back. in the area of the old market, visitors will also find many bars, cheap eat restaurants, fruit shake stands. many more are found a short walk north to pub street. for more souvenir and related shopping, you can cross the siem reap river and spend more time at the art centre night market which kicks off around 4pm every afternoon.

psar krom 89 is a local market and a new market open in 2020. you can buy any products products include: fresh fruits, fresh flowers, apparel, consumer goods, general consumables, gloves, electronic equipment, music accessories, fresh vegetables, fish, meat you can find local breakfast, lunch, dinner, khmer cake and khmer dissert
public rooftop park with elevator access and views of both the manhattan bridge and brooklyn bridge. bench seating.
