puentes colgantes arenal – mistico park the park itself is beautiful and the walk through the hanging bridges is amazing, with stunning scenery and well-maintained trails. however, our guided tour was a bit disappointing compared to what we observed with other groups. our guide didn’t seem very interested in stopping to look for wildlife, while other guides nearby were actively scanning for their groups. the tour also wrapped up in just under two hours, when it was advertised as two and a half, so it felt a bit rushed. overall, the park is absolutely worth visiting for the scenery alone, but i would recommend ensuring you get a guide who’s enthusiastic about spotting wildlife if that’s an important part of your experience.

puerto pañuelo is the perfect starting point for a scenic catamaran ride to isla victoria. the embarkation was smooth, and the journey across the lake was stunning, offering magnificent views of the surrounding landscapes. it’s a fantastic way to explore the beauty of the region and reach isla victoria effortlessly.

puerto princesa baywalk is honestly one of the best public spots in the city if you’re looking for a relaxing place to hang out. i love going there late in the afternoon, especially just before sunset. the sea breeze, the view of the water, and the warm colors of the sky make it a peaceful and beautiful spot to just slow down and breathe. the walkway is wide and great for casual strolls or biking, and there are usually families, couples, and tourists around—everyone enjoying the same calm vibe. there are food stalls along the area too, selling grilled seafood, street food like fish balls, and cool drinks, which makes the experience even better. what i appreciate is that the area feels safe and generally clean. but i do hope the city government continues to maintain it well—not just the pathway and landscaping, but also the facilities. one thing i noticed is the lack of clean, accessible restrooms. that would make a big difference for both locals and tourists. it would also be great if they could add more shaded areas or resting spots, especially for older visitors and families with kids. it gets really hot during the day, and a few more covered benches would go a long way. still, even with those improvements needed, the baywalk is a gem in the city. it’s not commercialized or overly crowded, and that’s part of its charm. it gives you a real sense of the local life in puerto princesa—calm, simple, and close to nature.

pulled into their parking lot that they share with moon dog pizza. this irate guy named dennis comes out saying i can’t park in that parking lot with my trailer because they need to drive jeeps in during the day. dude scares my kids and wife. we never touched their property line. pretty sad you have to get that upset over a vehicle and trailer turning around.

punta bunga beach in boracay is a hidden gem that offers a tranquil and private escape in station zero, away from the hustle and bustle of stations 1 - 3. the beach is surrounded by lush greenery, and its pristine sands and crystal-clear waters create a picturesque setting. while punta bunga is a public beach, it's not always easy to access. some hotels fronting the beach may give the impression that it's private, but it's open to everyone. this is definitely worth a visit.

punta sur is definitely worth a stop when exploring isla mujeres by golf cart. the views over the cliffs and turquoise water are stunning, and the area is home to plenty of iguanas basking on the rocks. it’s a peaceful spot for a short break, take in the scenery, and snap some great photos before carrying on around the island.

punto panorámico on the circuito chico offers a dreamlike view, especially on a sunny day. the expansive vista of lakes and mountains is absolutely breathtaking. it's the perfect spot to take in the beauty of bariloche and capture stunning photos. a must-stop on the circuito chico!
puppet show is mist visit.

pura kehen was the main temple for the bangli kingdom. built in the 13th century, this temple is quite unique compared to other temples in bali. on the walls you can see chinese porcelain plates, which shows that the chinese already traded with the balinese. there is also a banyan tree growing out of the temple, which is very interesting.

pura kehen 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 pura kehen is a breathtaking and culturally significant temple that truly captures the essence of bali’s spiritual heritage. 🛕✨ this sacred site is not only a stunning architectural masterpiece but also holds deep importance for the balinese people. the temple's intricate carvings and grand entrance are awe-inspiring, showcasing the incredible craftsmanship and attention to detail. 🪷 the lush surroundings and peaceful ambiance make it a perfect place for reflection and appreciation of bali's rich culture. walking through the temple grounds, you can feel the spiritual energy and the strong connection the locals have with this sacred space. 🙏 it’s an amazing opportunity to learn about the traditions and religious practices of bali. 📍location: located in bangli, it’s easy to reach and well worth the trip. 💵 entry fee: affordable, and it goes towards maintaining this beautiful site. pro tip: wear modest clothing and bring a sarong to show respect for the local customs. visiting during a ceremony adds an extra layer of cultural experience. pura kehen is a must-visit for anyone exploring bali's spiritual and historical landmarks. highly recommended for its beauty and significance! 🌴✨
pura keren is a temple by the side of the road. there very few tourists when we visited thus it was not crowded. we got to stay and explore the place quietly and peacefully.

pura samuan tiga is a hidden gem nestled in the village of bedulu, near ubud. despite its grandeur, this temple remains undiscovered by most tourists. you can freely enter, but be sure to wear a sarong—a traditional garment required for temple visits. we had the entire place to ourselves, allowing us to explore at our own pace. it’s undoubtedly one of the best temples we’ve visited. we even had the privilege of meeting a local priest who shared fascinating stories about this sacred site.

pura samuan tiga is where balinese and others get their prayers for various life situations. please treat this as an important temple for bali hindus and respect their sanctity. please wear appropriate balinese traditional clothes and enter, not as a tourist, but as someone praying for harmony. this is not for your instagram or tiktok, but a sacred place.

pura taman ayun was an unforgettable experience! ⛩✨ i highly recommend visiting with a guide – they know the best times to go when there are fewer tourists, and you might even get to witness a traditional ceremony up close 🙏🎶. it’s such a special feeling to be there, hearing the sounds, seeing the colors, and feeling the atmosphere in real life 💛. truly magical and a must-visit in bali! 🌺🌿

pura tanah lot is simply breathtaking! 🌊🏯 the temple’s location right on the rocks by the ocean makes it one of the most iconic sights in bali. visiting during sunset is pure magic 🌅✨ – the colors, the sound of the waves, and the silhouette of the temple create an unforgettable atmosphere. even with other visitors around, the place feels peaceful and special. a must-see for every bali trip! 🙌🌺

pura ulun danu beratan is one of those places that truly takes your breath away. set right on the edge of lake beratan in the cool highlands of bedugul, this temple feels like it’s floating on water. it’s not just a spiritual site, but also a balinese icon—with its unique architecture and peaceful surroundings. the mountain backdrop, calm lake, and fresh air make it a perfect spot to pause, take photos, and just enjoy the beauty of bali. definitely worth a visit. however, there are areas where the site management could improve the overall visitor experience. at peak hours, the temple grounds often become congested, with large tour groups crowding walkways and disrupting the peaceful atmosphere. in some cases, chaotic tourist behavior—such as loud conversations, disregard for sacred zones, or climbing on restricted areas—detracts from the temple’s spiritual significance. these issues highlight the need for more professional crowd management, clearer signage, and on-site staff presence to guide and educate visitors. given the sacred nature of the site, more attention should be placed on preserving its calm and respectful atmosphere. simple steps like timed entry, designated quiet zones, and reinforced cultural etiquette could make a big difference.

pure magic from start to finish! santa claus village in rovaniemi is an absolute dream come true—for kids and adults! there's something special here for everyone, and the entire place feels like stepping straight into a winter fairytale. i visited this place on 31st march 2025. i had the most amazing day, starting with the unforgettable moment of meeting santa claus himself—he's every bit as warm and wonderful as you'd imagine! the magic didn’t stop there. i got to enjoy a thrilling husky ride through the snow and even met real reindeer—it was like living in a christmas postcard. every detail is beautifully done, and the whole village is buzzing with festive spirit. whether you’re sending postcards from the official santa’s post office or just soaking in the snowy vibes, you can’t help but feel the joy. highly, highly recommended for families, couples, solo travelers—everyone. you don’t just visit santa claus village… you feel it in your heart. ❤️🎅❄️

putting my mother to rest at better place forests allowed a large part of my grief to rest as well. today i went for a visit in lieu of my first birthday without her. ashley was amazingly patient with me, provided a friendly greeting and send off, and encouraged me to explore. i spent more time than i anticipated having a walk and finding nature’s ways to decorate our tree. better place continues to prove our final decision was a great one. what a blessed feeling.

pyathetgyi pagoda, a large brick temple in bagan, myanmar, is known for its impressive size and unique double-cave design. built in the first half of the 13th century by king kyaswa, it's a significant cultural landmark and a place of worship, offering stunning views of the surrounding landscape, especially at sunrise and sunset.

pötzleinsdorfer schlosspark is definitely one of the more unusual parks in vienna — and that’s exactly what makes it special. unlike the perfectly manicured gardens you usually find in the city, this park feels much more natural, almost like stepping into the countryside. it’s really big too — you could easily spend hours walking around. especially in spring, it’s absolutely worth a visit. the park is filled with wild garlic (aglio orsino) in bloom, and if you go at the right time, you’ll see entire fields covered in tiny white flowers — it honestly looks like a sea of blossoms, or like it snowed in spring. it’s just beautiful. there’s also a small greek-style building with statues that were rescued from an old theater that burned down years ago — a really charming touch. the park is perfect for long walks, peaceful runs, and even exploring further into the wienerwald (vienna woods) if you feel like adventuring a bit more. near the entrance, there’s also a nice playground area for kids and even some goats and sheep playing in a fenced area. if you’re looking for a quieter, less touristy park where you can enjoy nature at its best, this is the place to go.

queen emma point at hickam air base in hawaii is a hidden gem that deserves recognition for its breathtaking beauty and serene atmosphere. nestled within a military base, this spot offers a unique blend of natural splendor and historical significance, making it a must-visit location for those who have access. the panoramic views from queen emma point are simply stunning. overlooking the pacific ocean, the vantage point provides visitors with an expansive view of the water, complemented by the backdrop of lush hawaiian landscapes. the tranquility of the area is perfect for moments of reflection or a peaceful escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. what makes queen emma point particularly special is its historical context. named after queen emma of hawaii, who played a significant role in the islands' history, the area offers a glimpse into the rich cultural heritage of hawaii. this historical significance adds an enriching layer to the visit, connecting visitors with the past in a meaningful way. accessibility to queen emma point might be limited due to its location within hickam air base, so visitors should ensure they have the necessary permissions or are accompanied by someone with access. however, those who do get the chance to visit will find it well worth the effort. in summary, queen emma point is a beautiful and peaceful spot that offers stunning views, a serene atmosphere, and a touch of hawaiian history. it's a perfect place for reflection, relaxation, and appreciation of the natural and historical beauty of hawaii. mtc

queen emma summer palace is a hidden gem tucked away in the lush nuʻuanu valley of honolulu — and well worth the visit if you’re interested in hawaiian history and royalty. because it’s not as well known as other tourist sites, it’s refreshingly quiet and uncrowded, giving you space to truly enjoy the atmosphere at your own pace. the palace, also known as hānaiakamalama, was the summer retreat for queen emma, king kamehameha iv, and their son prince albert. the building itself is beautifully preserved, and walking through the rooms is like stepping back into the 19th century. inside, you’ll find a rich collection of original furnishings, clothing, artifacts, and royal portraits — almost like a mini museum that offers a personal and intimate look into the life of hawaiian royalty. what really made our visit special were the incredibly friendly and knowledgeable staff, who were more than happy to share insights and answer questions. their passion for the history and cultural heritage of hawaii made the experience all the more meaningful. whether you’re a history buff, a culture lover, or just looking for something peaceful and off the beaten path, queen emma summer palace is a quiet treasure in honolulu. a short drive from downtown, it’s easy to fit into your itinerary — and you’ll be glad you did.

québec city’s largest urban park—and the site of the famous battle of the plains of abraham—is just across the street. outside the city walls, to the west of the citadel, stretches the green expanse known as the plains of abraham [also known as battlefields park (parc des champs-de-bataille)], where in 1759 the british, led by general wolfe, fought the french under montcalm and won. the battle of québec (the pivotal moment of the french and indian war when the french were forced to cede new france to great britain) took place here. the park is also home to the remains of two martello towers, later additions to québec's fortifications. begun in the late 1930s, the joan of arc garden designed by louis perron has a fabulous display of flowers from spring until fall. it is the perfect place to enjoy some fresh air. while you're sure to see a few historical elements (like the occasional ornamental cannon and defensive towers known as martello tower), make sure to pay specific attention to the manicured gardens – don't miss the stunning joan of arc garden – and the riverfront vistas. it’s lovely to see this field on cloudy days. benches are there near martello towers, have a seat and admire the beauty of st lawerence river battlefields park is an outdoor recreational site, right in the heart of the city! in the winter, you can go cross-country skiing or snowshoeing along the groomed trails or go skating on the ice ring. in the summer, the park becomes a popular picnic area.

raja ampat, or the four kings, is an archipelago located off of the northwest tip of bird's head peninsula (on the island of new guinea), southwest papua province, indonesia. it comprises over 1,500 small islands, cays, and shoals around the four main islands of misool, salawati, batanta, and waigeo, and the smaller island of kofiau. the raja ampat archipelago straddles the equator and forms part of the coral triangle, an area of southeast asian seas containing the richest marine biodiversity on earth. the coral triangle itself is an approximate area west-southwest of the philippines, east-northeast and southeast of the island of borneo, and north, east and west of the island of new guinea, including the seas in between. thousands of species of marine organisms, from the tiniest cleaner shrimp and camouflaged pygmy seahorses to the majestic cetaceans and whale sharks, thrive in these waters. administratively, the archipelago is part of the province of southwest papua. most of the islands constitute the raja ampat regency, which was separated from sorong regency in 2004. the regency encompasses around 70,000 square kilometres (27,000 sq mi) of land and sea, of which 8,034.44 km2 constitutes the land area and has a population of 64,141 at the 2020 census;[2] the official estimate as at mid 2022 was 66,839.[3] this excludes the southern half of salawati island, which is not part of this regency but instead constitutes the salawati selatan and salawati tengah districts of the name of raja ampat (raja means king, and empat means four) comes from local mythology that told of a woman who found seven eggs, in one version this woman was boki tabai, daughter of al-mansur of tidore and wife to gurabesi. three of the seven hatched and became kings who occupied raja ampat islands, the fourth hatched and settled in waigama but later migrated to kalimuri (seram). in another version, the fifth egg hatched into a woman (pin take) who later washed away to biak, married manar makeri, and later gave birth to gurabesi. the sixth egg hatched into a spirit, while the seventh egg did not hatch and turned to stone and worshipped as a king in kali raja (wawiyai, waigeo). historically the 'four' kingdoms were waigeo, salawati, sailolof, misool, and waigama. locally waigama is not considered one of the raja ampat, while sailolof is not considered one of the raja ampat by tidore.the first recorded sighting and landing by europeans of the raja ampat islands was by the portuguese navigator jorge de menezes and his crew in 1526, en route from biak, the bird's head peninsula, and waigeo, to halmahera (ternate). islam first arrived in the raja ampat islands in the 15th century due to political and economic contacts with the bacan sultanate.[5] during the 16th and 17th centuries, the maluku-based sultante of tidore had close economic and political ties with the islands, especially with gurabesi.[5][6] during this period, islam became firmly established, and local chiefs began adopting islam.[6] as a consequence of these ties, raja ampat was considered a part of the sultanate of tidore. after the dutch invaded maluku, it was claimed by the netherlands. the english explorer william dampier gave his name to dampier strait, which separates batanta island from waigeo island. to the east, there is a strait that separates batanta from salawati. in 1759 captain william wilson sailing in the east indiaman pitt navigated these waters and named a strait the 'pitt strait', after his vessel; this was probably the channel between batanta ratchapradit sathitmahasimaram temple was built in 1864 his intention is that this temple shall be one of the three main monasteries of the city according to the tradition since sukhothai period, namely wat mahathat, wat raja burana and wat ratchapradit sathan. his majesty king mongkut originally named the temple as "rajapradit sathitdhammayuttikaram temple”, (the temple of the dhammayut order) specifically dedicated the land especially to dhammayut monks. his will manifested in the royal edict, the marble slab behind the buddha’s hall, and the poems engraved on the monastery-zone marker pillars. after that the name was changed to "wat ratchapradit sathitmahasimaram”, (the temple with the great monastery zone markers). since there was no chapel in this temple, they used the zone marker pillars around the temple, both the buddha’s and the sangha’s zones, to indicate the boundary that the ceremony can be performed. in 1665, his majesty king mongkut invited phra sāsanasobhaṇa (sa pussadeva), the to-be 9th supreme patriarch of thailand to be the first abbot. he was king rama iv student and one of the ten first monks in the dhammayut order. his majesty king mongkut paid great attention in decorating the temple with fine arts. he demanded that the carving on the door and windows emulated that of wat suthat, the inside window carved in the japanese style of wat nang chee, on top of every door and window having an emblem of the crown, the king’s sigil, and the stars on the ceiling inspired by that of wat rajapraditsathan and wat suwan dararam of ayutthaya. furthermore, there are paintings of deity groups roaming freely over the sky, the mural of royal ceremonies in 12 months which were painted in the reign of king rama v with the background of the previous reign in order to reflect the prosperity under the rule of king rama iv. inside the temple is the famous buddha image, phra sihanga patimakorn, under which is where the royal ashes of king mongkut were placed. there are a large number of his majesty king mongkut’s relevant edifices and antiquities in wat ratchapradit such as the royal temple which illustrates the great crown of victory on the gable, the crown-topped pulpit as rama iv’s sigil. pāsāna cetiya (the marble pagoda) is a sri lankan style pagoda, inspired by the detail in the commentary of mahāparinibbāna sutta that the emperor ashoka had built the rock-pagoda prasat phra boromarup and prasat phra trai pidok are the khmer-styled buildings, inside of which are the statue of king rama iv and 150 years-old palm-leaf manuscripts of the pali canon in the book-shaped wooden boxes respectively. originally, these buildings were constructed in the reign of king rama v with marbles with the four-faced god, brahman, on the top, then they were rebuilt in the reign of king rama vi.

really awesome side of the road stop on the ice fields parkway. it has restrooms, enough parking, and an absolutely wonderful view of the beautiful natural landscape. it also has a viewing scope and benches. this is definitely a great place along the road to stop, stretch, and enjoy the incredible scenery.
really beautiful and scenic place. horses roam freely in the area and in winter it’s just so pretty to see them graze. the path can be quite steep for elderly with bad knees though so do take note.

really beautiful and well-curated museum that’s much bigger than the outside suggests. very affordable at 12 euro fee (except for special exhibit, which is extra). could easily spend many hours here. loved the mix of culture, history, and art; the rooftop cafe is also so beautiful and has good drink and food options.

really beautiful bridge, definitely worth parking there and walking out. would not recommend walking there, it is a long hike. really beautiful bridge, river and forest. the bridge itself looks and feels very authentic. i absolutely recommend stopping by here for quick sightseeing.

really beautiful castle that sits just off the tiber in rome. you can only wonder what its splendor was like when first built. originally built as a mausoleum for hadrian (yes the guy who built the wall in england). over time it was used as a fort, prison and pope's residence. take the many stairs inside to the top and walk around the rooms which contain many paintings and other artifacts. well worth the visit. unlike some other museums disabled people have to pay to enter.

really beautiful hike but the weather turned on us about a third of the way through, making the rest of the hike quite challenging . it was still fun (lots of waterfalls, caves, fruendly birds) but we didn't get to see any of the amazing views. learn from our mistake and make sure you check the weather forecast before you go. final thing: it's super cheap and easy to get to by public transport: bus 56 from funchal at 8:10 and 10am takes 45 mns for less than 3 euros pp. return from portela on bus 53 (bus stop down some stairs and opposite a restaurant) took 1h30mns.

really beautiful hike surrounded by lush forest, with a constant soundtrack of birds chirping. just don’t expect stunning views of the lagoon; it’s more about feeling immersed in the valley, where you can pass the giant tortoises and spot deer if you’re lucky. we did the yellow route and then switched over to the red to finish earlier—something their official map doesn’t indicate is possible but is clearly marked (and shown on alltrails), which made the whole thing 3 hours, a perfect length for us to do between breakfast and lunch.

really beautiful in the royal tomb area!

really beautiful place to visit! not a far hike at all, could take a small child in a carrier. a stroller would b much more difficult. so cool to see the falls from different views at the top and bottom. go check it out!
really beautiful spot to lookout on thunersee! the pathway to get there is well kept and a very enjoyable walk along the rivers. highly recommend a visit.
really beautiful trail! the best experience. it took us 2/3h in total. the weather was amazing so the views breathtaking🇫🇴

really beautiful, choose to walk the backside of the viktoria peak to enjoy the jungle side. well worth the hard workout. was walking on a saturday morning and was almost totally alone all the way up to the peak.

really best way how to go through every interesting place in paris. it's nice traveling by boat with simple stations and basic water and food in boat "coca cola machine" and goes through interesting places by default - it's 2 hours of time only on boat! it's a lot of stops, but you can choose only some of them of course and just left the boat on next one or even it is possible to (almost on every stop) go across the river by bridge and thanks to it you can make the journey significantly shorter (can go from the second stop to stop before last)

really big beautiful and free garden to visit for a nice walk/ stroll around central park. it’s a nice place to walk your dog, walk with friends or just enjoy a nice quiet sunny day. definitely recommend! the flowers are gorgeous and i loved looking at them while i walked:)

really convenient location just a few minutes walk from my hotel, or a short streetcar/bus ride from the french qtr area. came here early morning so everything was stocked up nice and clean. good prices and lots of options of la souvenirs and nola goodies too.

really cool area to check out. between the tomb and the museum. well worth the time. we originally came through and enjoyed the outside for free then came back another day to get a ticket to the indoor exhibits. really amazing. you could spend a day here if you like museums.

really cool area to check out. between the tomb and the museum. well worth the time. we originally came through and enjoyed the outside for free then came back another day to get a ticket to the indoor exhibits. really amazing. you could spend a day here if you like museums.

really cool experience!! where else in the usa can you literally drive by rhinos, zebras, giraffes, and lions while in your car??? with your ticket, you can drive through as many times as you want, have access to their park with water features, giraffe feeding and rides including miniature golf, and a petting zoo! some activities have additional costs but you can see a lot for free including the giraffes!

really cool experience. we arrived just after old faithful erupted so we had around an hour and a half to wait. luckily there was a great little cafeteria with good food, ice cream, and a gift shop. parking was pretty good considering how packed it was, we had a truck and trailer and still managed to find descent parking. it was pretty hot to sit and wait for the eruption but if you don’t get out there early you won’t get a seat. we went out 40 minutes beforehand and got up front. there is a ton of seating but way more people than benches. the eruption was pretty cool. super quick considering how long you wait but nothing compares to this incredible force of nature.

really cool experience. we went on a cloudy day but because it is high up on a mountain we passed the clouds and it was very sunny and hot. very beautiful forest with trees and lots of cows, it is as well good for children and also if you wanna sit and enjoy a book. walking a higher point will give you a beautiful view of the island or of the clouds which is what we saw. proper shoes is not a must, we went in flip-flops.

really cool fair to take part in. the fair only takes place twice a week on tuesdays and thursdays there is all different types of art. judaic art, israeli art and contemporary art as well. it is a must see if you are in tel aviv!
really cool geyser with a quick 2.5 mile in hike. check the book to see the times it erupts

really cool museum — you can easily spend half a day here exploring everything. i wouldn’t recommend getting a membership unless you plan on coming back multiple times. for a one-time visit, it’s more than enough. honestly, it’s perfect for families with kids. there’s a ton of new and interesting info to check out, but the real highlight is definitely the planetarium. the aquarium sections with all the fish are also a fun bonus!

really cool place but way too packed so many people its hard to fully enjoy but it is cool. the museum is really cool explains a lot of history. the trails were short and easy but just way too packed. i saw several near-misses in the parking lot. the bathrooms had a long line too. i enjoyed seeing all the vents, it seemed very active the day we went, and actually the same day we were here the biscuit basin blew up and damaged the boardwalk over on that side of the park. yellowstone is huge you can drive 3 hours west to east and still be in the park. its like 1/4 of the state of wyoming!

really cool place that is easily accessed from town. great location for pictures. great little restaurant at the top with out door tables where you can watch the parasailors flying down to the park. also at the bottom there is a small enclosure with ibex deer that you can see up close.

really cool place to go saturday night. nice entertainment, not overly crowded but busy. good restaurants and bars. the decor aligns with the historic railroad station. some of the basic necessities can use an upgrade (like the restrooms), but overall it was nice date night.

really cool place. we had lucky as our tour guide and he was a blast. funny, charismatic, knowledgeable, informative, inclusive, personal, and anything else you'd want in a guide. we got to see some of the artists working on current projects as well as the warehouse full of past and present props and floats. it was really interesting to learn how it's all made and how many things kern is involved in. a great place to find out the history and process of one of the things that makes nola unique.

really cool to check out, i was passing by the area and noticed this little park. it was cool to see the ruins. i always enjoy checking out these old monuments, it’s still in very good condition. it’s well preserved and maintained, if your in the area i would recommend checking it out.

really cool to see as you follow the trail! i would really just recommend taking a photo of the map though - we went too far and the signs along the way were not very good. if you reach #7 you've gone too far!!!

really cool! loved seeing the dogs and being able to pet them. the dogs are well cared for and the staff is knowledgeable. it was a great place to visit, and easy to get to and from with the free shuttles. definetly worth going. demo is short, 20-25min. mostly listening and a short visual demo which lasts maybe a minute.

really cute and fun art, many different mini museums on different floors. one by the entrance is always very interesting and inspirational and changes often enough to where coming back often is still entertaining and educational. easy to get lost in, but mainly very cool and awesome place to visit.

really dope venue. the djs they had were great, from the undercard to the headliners. reasonable drink prices considering it’s a club. just bear in mind it gets a little crowded for the busy events as it is a small venue.

really enjoy our visit to this castle. the gardens were absolute gorgeous, full of beautiful blooming flowers. children will definitely enjoy the little play park, a short walk from the gardens castle was full of interesting information and plenty to see and do. slight wait to get on but we arrived on a very busy day we enjoyed some delicious soup and bread from the cafe. lovely place and will definitely be back😁

really enjoyable guided private tour in the 1000cc can-am buggy which has plenty of power. marwan was a nice host, very freindly and the arrangements were all well organised. we'll use this company again when we return.

really enjoyed my experience snorkelling with them. 6 of us on this trip, included pick up (4 spots) and drive to fujairah from dubai. i booked via getyourguide and it was effortless. saw lots of sea turtles both in the boat and whilst snorkelling so i was very happy. great visibility and variety of fish, lots of parrot fish. had as good an experience as on maldives trips (experienced both atoll and handmade islands). better than bali / thailand snorkelling trips i experienced as barely saw any litter and it was a pretty private experience (just saw 2 other boats there on one location but timed it so we were leaving anyway) felt professional and safe even though i went as solo female.

really enjoyed our day here. and we didn’t even hit all the shops. it was such a nice day we could actually walk and be outside comfortably vs in the valley 😂. cool art all throughout as well. every shop was so unique and different. beautiful shopping center of you enjoy art and uniqueness.

really enjoyed our stay. great location next to etosha. beautifully appointed rooms. good breakfast and dinner. really enjoyed sitting in the lounge watching the animals at the watering hole. i also had a great massage.

really enjoyed our taco tour with alex! we visited three different places in the centro historico area- my personal favorite was tacos de canasta los especiales near the cathedral metropolitan. it was a great way to see and learn about the history of the area and alex stopped to explain different interesting parts along the way! we were full and informed by the end- would take it all again forsure

really enjoyed our visit today full of new experiences in a beautiful location. our hosts berghild and klaemint were warm and relaxed and clearly very committed to preserving traditional faroese sheep farming. our small group was able to ask plenty of questions during our delicious feed and eat experience today. we relished our hands on experience feeding the sheep as well. definitely one not to miss.
really enjoyed the boat trip very reasonable price and with kind and helpful staff

really enjoyed the guided tour, learning about maori culture & seeing the schools for carving & weaving. the geothermal pools& bubbling mud were amazing. loved that the tour was slow paced and relaxed and they split us into smaller groups. i didn't try the buffet but the food at the lunch counter was amazing. really enjoyed this place. well worth the admittance fee. oh, and the maori cultural performance, wow. amazing dancers with beautiful voices and smiles ( scary faces too for the haka). so powerful. loved it!

really enjoyed the storyville museum. it had a great balance of information, art, and interactions. i loved how the information sat in front of period correct backgrounds. i was fascinated by the pieces that the museum were able to find and bring together. highly recommend. self-guided so you can take as much/little time as you like.

really enjoyed the visit here. plenty to see while strolling around, both with garden areas, historical structures, and local birds flying around. i can see why some folks had set up shop with picnics here, it was very peaceful and beautiful.
really enjoyed this but do check maintenance as we had to get of the line then re join 6 blocks further down. but really enjoyed it

really enjoyed this facility! we rented surf boards, spent time in the sauna, and enjoyed dinner with life music. the facilities were clean and the staff was very friendly. we did not camp here but the camping looked nice with lots of rvs and tent campers. we visited in june and caught decent weather to surf but even on a stormy day the sauna is a great escape. enjoyed the lift music, lucia was a pleasure to listen to. i could see the facility was building out more rv sites. worth a stop when in lofoten!

really enjoyed this on saturday! despite having lived in london for decades and been on similar thames river cruises before, the commentary given by crew members is great, so interesting and entertaining. we'd highly recommend taking any trip with these guys!

really enjoyed this trail, clear and defined path and steps to follow. if you're wanting to see planes flying into the cairns airport you get a good view at the top, also the point where the red meets the yellow track. lovely flora and fauna to enjoy along the way. extends and connects to the other longer/more difficult trails in this region, if you want to be further challenged.

really enjoyed this unique experience from the time we entered the booking office we found the staff friendly and helpful. they managed to get us a tour same day. our guides worked hard to explain things to us in english before we entered cave only three on the tour. good amount of time to descend, explore, take photos and ascend.
really enjoyed with family. clean boat and well trained professional team
really entertaining, definitely worth a visit!

really exceeded expectations. coming from uk i was apprehensive paying before hand and relying on zanzibar tours to handle all my holidays needs. zanzibar tours kept me informed and was easily contactable via whatsapp from beginning enquires throughout the whole holiday. fully recommend.

really excellent experience - great diving and a really great bunch of people. the dive sites had a good range of fish and coral, particularly soft coral. only there for a couple of days as it was the end of a working trip to dubai - but really glad i went to nomad "dibba". massive thanks to pawline at nomad who reassured me over numerous e-mails about the oman crossing and the venue! would not have done the trip without her help.

really excited with the ally maze. enjoy and challenge the local guys , who always show you the way to go , and in the same time, another guy show in opposite! if they help and lead your way, relax and just pay for some money tips ~ 10-20 mad ! ask first :) and relax

really fabulous hotel, gorgeous modern rooms and lovely bathrooms. lovely pool and surrounding views of the sea etc . really enjoyed the breakfast albeit the service was slow at times for coffee and eggs . i am a coeliac so no gluten and the gluten free bread, muffins and banana bread was amazing! first hotel on a 4 week trip that had gluten free options . also in the restaurant, staff were knowledgeable about allergies and adjusted the dish to make it work . only downside here was the very slow service at one dinner , we were a party of 8. 5 got their food but 3 of us including me had to wait over 45 mins and so wasn’t acceptable for the price / rating of the hotel as meant didn’t have a relaxing dinner . other than that the staff were super helpful and friendly and the overall stay was fabulous
really fabulous. highlight of our trip. our fiaker gerry was really good and offered to take lots of photos. booking process was good too. thank you 😊

really fantastic khmer food, great atmosphere with a large ornamental pond. great service, and prices no different to any lesser establishment. $25 excluding tip for a meal for two (signature fish amok, and ban hoy) including a large beer each. can't fault it.

really friendly staff and very helpful, wheelchair and disabled access is easy with ramps etc in place to help. once on board someone comes around to take drink and food orders, very reasonably priced. guided tour over the speaker is really informative, learnt so much. highly recommended and the views from the top deck is worth the ticket price alone. will definitely use city cruises again.

really fun experience on the self drive buggy tour! super easy to get to their downtown queenstown location where they shuttle you to their spot on the hills 5 minutes out of town. the give you a bit of training, make sure you're good to go, and off you zip! the guides, bas and diego, were great and made sure everyone was comfortable and having a great time, and also telling us some history of the area at the same time. would definitely do this again! highly recommend.
really fun experience, the instructor was super helpful and nice, lots of focus on safety, and very professional. would definitely do again next time i’m in cartagena

really fun hike up and down to see the waterfall here. super grand and very memorable. we actually saw a black bear chase a couple out of the trail before he left the area and we opt for the hike ourselves. weather was good and despite being busy it never felt super crowded. trail is very well marked and child friendly enough if you have little ones. would recommend for the whole family.

really fun place to explore. do go to the baking market (every type of cooking and baking utensil you could ever need). the candle making market is really fun to explore and you’ll walk back with a new hobby for sure!

really fun time doing activities at belle mare and chilling at île aux cerfs. had some trouble finding the pickup point to take the boat to the island so i added a location on google maps for people searching it in the future (aquacity pickup point). wished the activities lasted a bit longer but apart from that i'd recommend them. their crew is very friendly for the most part and you'll definitely enjoy your time there.

really fun tour! everyone was extremely helpful. my boyfriend is in a wheelchair and they helped him to get in and out of the boat and around the islands!! i recommend this tour. martin was the life of the party he was dancing the whole way lol

really good beach, there are so many local homestay. the village is tidy and clean, the people are good and kind. bring your own food if possible because there is no warung or shop near by the beach. enjoy !!
really good ceramic, hand designs and so traditional. the staff it’s really friendly and you can negotiate the best price.

really good concert, combination of ballet, opera, and just instrumental. it combines the classical music with a more modern touch. it is a more toeristy spot. would recommend if you are looking for something different than the traditional concert, but would not recommend if you are really looking for the traditional concert/opera/ballet.

really good diving school amazing underwater dive sites, and you can feel the emotions what the dive project with young aged children which had no school time on mahé give a future to look forward! really great job! i love future projects like this! hopefully to see you again.

really good exhibition of quality photos depicting the grim reality of conflict. the current content is of the war in burma as well as the permanent display of the balkan wars in the 90s. a worthwhile but slightly depressing way to spend an hour or two. you get a discount if you have a dubrovnik pass.

really good experience for our first time on a license free boat. mario coached us well at the beginning. i recommend rather than the touristic guided boat tour that are more expensive and have more constraints.

really good experience if you haven’t been here before, we did the base all inclusive without adding. we got there at 9am, and there were plenty to do throughout the day, we barely had any downtime. we ate first at the mexican restaurant, supposedly all 3 restaurant breakfast is the same, so it doesn’t matter which one you go. we spent about 1.5 hrs snorkeling the whole inlet, saw some school of fish, nothing too special, but still fun to explore. we did the tower slide once, it’s not super fast, so some may find it boring. we then walked around the whole property and did the river tube, a little slow paced in my opinion, we got out of water early at the zip line to try that. i brought my phone with me without a waterproof pouch, so i couldn’t get on the zipline. later we had a late lunch at the international restaurant, note the queue to the restaurant did get long when it got closer to 430pm, everyone tries to grab last bit of bite to eat i guess. food and drinks are both pretty good considering it’s a buffet. beer/drinks stations usually have a line. but they work fast. overall good price for what we got, but i probably won’t come back again unless there is some specific add-on i want to do.
really good experience in this restaurant who has a tintin theme. the atmosphere is chill and nice. the dishes are very tasty and completely affordable. the chicken curry was simply awesome !
really good experience, well organised, great crew and lots of fun. highly recommended this company!

really good experience. i have never been near penguins like this before. how cute of them. highly recommend to watch penguins parade. some of penguins started to slide after walk through crowns. warning: please do not touch them just look at them, take photo or video and cheer up them because there no fence so some of tourist try to touch penguins. please be good tourists😉.

really good modern art exhibits by a wide range of artists and styles from statues to abstract art to traditional wall art. there are many different themes from religion to social commentary, and philosophy. there are free lockers and free toilets as part of the ticket. however be aware that on the first sunday when the tickets are free they still want you to book a slot through a qr code so make sure you have enough power on your phone.

really good river tour with our family including 2 children aged 8 and 10. we had booked tickets in advance and were late because of train cancellations from disneyland, they were brilliant and let us get onto the next cruise without an issue. it’s in a great location just under the eiffel tower. great information about the buildings, bridges and sights along the cruise which we wouldn’t have seen in the time we had in paris and it was in a few different languages. would highly recommend!
really good store, they have all groceries and a good produce department. their deli is good and they also have a hot food section. the staff are very nice and attentive and the prices are fine.

really gorgeous experience. we hiked instead of kayaking and the views were breathtaking. guides were very kind (and patient) as my 70 yr old mother lagged far behind the group. thank you so much! would definitely recommend

really great and quiet park. we did go on a monday morning at 8am so not sure if it becomes busy during the day; but at our time it was perfect, just local people walking their dogs :) it's fascinating to think that this was built to long ago with that amount of precision.

really great art museum! if you love art, i'd definitely see. one of my favorite museums. while i don't love art, i do enjoy a good museum and i was impressed with this one. nice gardens to walk around before or after. busses right at entrances and going through park.
really great chosun kingdoms palaces must see and visit point if you like history and culture thing you can feel the scent of korea history and that age

really great church. fabulous architecture! the inside was amazing and they should put a sign up to say you should get a ticket from across this square before you queue up for 10 minutes and then tell you at the door that you can't get in without a blooming ticket, but apart from that it's definitely worth going.

really great experience ! we went on june and had a great day. nice office. friendly staff. free parking right next to their office. saw some turtles and many fish. we had a lunch on board and unlimited water and juice during the day.

really great experience! the crew (armand, blue and thomas) was great, funny, obliging and really nice! we had a great moment thanks to them (and the landscape also :)) they prepared food for us. the "negative" point would be that, "îlot gabriel", is surrounded by rocks and dead corals, so bring swimming shoes not to hurt your feet. i recommend this cruise, we enjoyed the moment.
really great experience. the guides were very entertaining. to get to walk with and pet a lion is a once in a lifetime treat. great staff. thank you steve!

really great location with wonderful sea views, featuring modern, comfortable rooms, not forgetting the communal swimming pool, and games room. the hot-tub on the terrace is awesome, except for the fumes from the lower apartments coming through the windows above (the exits from the chimneys must be relocated much higher) fully equipped kitchen for cooking meals, or simply use the indoor braai (bbq) grill. the laundry service is really quick, too. absolutely friendly and efficient staff.
really great place for young kids! service at the restaurant is a work in progress at the moment

really great spot for kids bdays! and not super loud and crowded like some other places. very easy to book and amazing customer service. my son had his 10th birthday party and kids loved it! thank you so much and next time i’m aiming for adult party in there! looks so much fun.
really great stall with lots to offer, everyone is very welcoming and sweet. got to enjoy the most heart warming festival later that night. best day ever.

really great to go up and down the thames river. the guides are really great and have good knowledge that they share with you. our guide was very humorous which everyone enjoyed. you get to see all the main attractions from a different angle. really worthwhile!

really great tour if you’re wanting to see birds and sea cliffs. great piloting going in and out of tight spaces! we really enjoyed it even though apparently it was cut short due to the intense waves.

really great trip, we booked the private small boat for our group of 6. the captain was very accommodating and friendly, providing us with drinks, fresh fruit and snacks throughout the trip as well as showing us the beautiful islands of daymaniyat. we was shown the great spots for snorkelling to see the turtles and coral reef spots, as well as beautiful beaches. we was also provided with a kayak which we had great fun using. thank you again for a wonderful trip. we would 100% recommendation to book. 😊

really great waterfall. if you'll be there when the weather is nice, great pics are guaranteed. we hiked down from rabacal roadside parking. it is 3km each (back and forth) with approximately 300m of elevation difference. can be steep, but easy road resp. trail conditions.
really had a fun and enjoyable outing with the family. the food and entertainment was spectacular. really recommend 👌 👏
really helpful and friendly staff. brand new boat. the lake is stunning. very easy to ride. with this size of boat, you can sail, if confident, from 14yrs in switzerland.

really helpful staff. we were a little confused about what was available in advance. we were able to rent rubber boots for 500 yen each which were really handy in the snow. the first walk to furepe falls was 2km, it was a nice walk, the snow looked impressive and we saw some deer along the way. the waterfall was a trickle so not that much to see but the cliffs were impressive and worth a look. the wind was a bit scary when we visited! back at the centre we decided to do a second trail - we asked at the counter what's available and were given a map for another trail into woodland. it took us about an hour and a half on snow shoes (also rented for 500 yen each). hard work for the legs but good fun! some beautiful views of the trees in snow and the overlooking mountains, with an observation area at the halfway point. i wasn't that interested in the lectures/films at the centre itself but the staff were really friendly and helpful at setting us up for our walks. definitely worth a visit if you're in the shiretoko area

really impressed by this park - i was initially against going due to concerns over captive animals and views on zoos but the sustainability work is super impressive and research the park is doing for conservation. animals are in large open enclosures and staff are really informative and passionate about their work and animals. good they provide buggies for my mum who isn't as able walking long distances

really impressed with the newly renovated grand hyatt — the interior design is stunning and so thoughtfully done. we were pleasantly surprised with a complimentary upgrade to a suite, and the room design truly surpassed our expectations. room service was quick and efficient, and the whole atmosphere was comfortable and welcoming. a wonderful stay all around!
really interesting and enjoyable place to come! not only refreshing, i got deep knowledge about butterflies here. kudos for the team!
really interesting and well guided tour. if you would like to go on the long version you need to reserve at least 3 months in advance!

really interesting museum about the history and current use of coca, with good english descriptions and a lot of information on local customs. there is a special exhibitions of costumes that are used in puno's candelaria festival on the first floor. s/10 entry.

really interesting museum on the altar to pax, commissioned in 9bce. detailed models, information, timeline provide extra information and there's a short video that explains both the history and excavations. it's also a good spot to see the mausoleum of augustus, which is currently closed for renovations. well worth a visit and very accessible.

really interesting museum with lots of areas covering pre-history up to present day. lovely to learn about how people lived on the island. as a note though, not everything has an english translation. there was a guide in the halls who spoke to us and was really knowledgeable and interesting.

really interesting, i’ve learned a lot in a positive atmosphere.thank you manu

really kind and informed trips, nice vibe, good people. very happy!!

really love the prima. our first cruise was nothing but magical. the food was great and we loved the indulge food hall. smaller portions mean we could try more food. other restaurants were great but the small portions at indulge was really a highlight. we love to try all the food but don’t always want a whole meal. activities were great! will be cruising again with ncl soon!

recently, i had the privilege of offering the maghrib prayer at one of oman’s iconic mosques, and it was an experience that left a lasting impression on me. the architecture of omani mosques is simply awe-inspiring and stands as a brilliant blend of tradition and modern design. from the moment i stepped into the mosque, i was enveloped by a sense of serenity and awe that is hard to put into words. the mosque's architecture is a true masterpiece, combining the rich, centuries-old islamic architectural traditions with modern elements that enhance the functionality and beauty of the space. the exterior of the mosque is stunning, with its intricate arabesque patterns, soaring domes, and tall, elegant minarets. the design reflects the essence of islamic art and culture, with delicate geometric patterns and calligraphy adorning the walls, creating a sacred and contemplative atmosphere. one of the most remarkable features is the use of natural materials, which blend seamlessly with the modern design. the incorporation of local stone, wood, and glass gives the mosque an organic feel while maintaining its grandiosity. the careful attention to detail in both the interior and exterior design ensures that the mosque feels both contemporary and timeless. the lighting within the prayer hall is especially striking, with large windows allowing natural light to flood the space, complementing the softer artificial lighting that creates a peaceful, tranquil environment. upon entering the mosque, the sense of calm is immediately overwhelming. the prayer hall itself is vast, with high, vaulted ceilings that create an open and airy feeling. the floor is adorned with rich carpets that provide warmth and comfort for those performing their prayers. the mihrab, the focal point of the mosque, is beautifully designed, with intricate patterns that guide the worshippers’ focus toward the qibla. the blend of modern and traditional extends to the interior as well. while the basic layout and structure follow traditional islamic principles, the materials and finishes have been updated to provide both beauty and functionality. the space is designed with great attention to acoustics, ensuring that the imam’s voice resonates clearly throughout the hall without overwhelming the senses. the maghrib prayer, which i offered during my visit, felt incredibly moving in this setting. as the sun dipped below the horizon, the ambiance inside the mosque became even more magical. the peaceful, reflective mood of the prayer was heightened by the mosque’s architectural splendor, as the soft golden light filtered through the windows and illuminated the space. it was a perfect marriage of architecture and spirituality, enhancing the sacredness of the prayer. while the mosque’s design is steeped in tradition, it also offers all the modern facilities one could ask for. the ablution areas are well-maintained, spacious, and equipped with high-quality fittings. additionally, the mosque’s air conditioning ensures a comfortable environment, even in the heat of the day, while maintaining the serene and reverent atmosphere expected in a place of worship. omani mosques stand out not only for their striking beauty but also for how they manage to seamlessly blend modernity with tradition. the mosque where i offered the maghrib prayer was a perfect example of this. it was a place where one could connect with both history and contemporary design while finding peace and solace in the act of prayer. the experience left me in awe of how thoughtfully and skillfully these mosques are designed to provide both a spiritual and aesthetic experience. if you ever find yourself in oman, visiting one of these magnificent mosques should be a top priority.

reelig glen: a majestic woodland retreat reelig glen is a hidden gem just outside of inverness, offering a serene escape into nature. the towering trees, lush greenery, and tranquil river create a truly magical atmosphere. the well-maintained trails are perfect for a leisurely stroll or a more vigorous hike. the towering redwoods are particularly impressive, offering a glimpse into a different world. the gentle murmur of the river provides a soothing soundtrack to your walk, and the fresh, clean air invigorates the senses. whether you're seeking a peaceful retreat or a family-friendly outing, reelig glen is a must-visit destination. it's a place where you can reconnect with nature and appreciate the beauty of the scottish highlands.

refined culinary and aesthetic experience in the heart of miami’s design district. mia market is not just a food hall—it’s a curated intersection of art, flavor, and urban elegance. set within the sleek architecture of the design district, this venue manages to blend high-end sophistication with culinary accessibility. each vendor feels handpicked, offering distinct and ambitious menus, from handmade pasta to sushi with a modern twist and exquisite latin-fusion dishes. the ambiance is cosmopolitan without being sterile: polished concrete, warm lighting, and design-forward details that reflect miami’s creative pulse. what truly sets mia apart is the consistency—both in service and quality. staff are knowledgeable and welcoming, striking a balance between professionalism and miami cool. standouts include the truffle tagliatelle (rich yet delicate), the tuna tostadas (bright, fresh, textural), and an inventive cocktail program that would rival any standalone bar. seating can be competitive during peak hours, but if you find a corner, the vibe is unhurried and convivial. ideal for both solo foodies and stylish groups, mia market elevates the food hall experience into something truly memorable and editorial-worthy. a must-visit for anyone who believes dining is as much about space and spirit as it is about the plate.

review for ecocamp patagonia – a 10-star experience! if i could give ecocamp patagonia 10 stars, i absolutely would! everything about this place was incredible. we did the 5-day torres del paine short w trek and stayed in a superior dome—which was both cozy and breathtaking, offering stunning views of the landscape. the food was nutritious, plentiful, and incredibly tasty, with the added bonus of making our own lunches each day. the staff was hands-down the best part of the experience. every single person was kind, helpful, and genuinely cared about both the guests and each other. i also loved taking advantage of the yoga sessions whenever i had time—it was the perfect way to relax after trekking. and speaking of trekking… it was over-the-top crazy beautiful! our guides, daniel and nadia, were phenomenal—knowledgeable, supportive, competitive, fun, and deeply passionate about the region. they shared fascinating details about the wildlife and landscape, and we were lucky enough to see pumas and other incredible flora and fauna! another highlight was ecocamp’s commitment to sustainability. the focus on zero waste and eco-consciousness made the experience even more meaningful. i truly loved every aspect of this place and can’t thank the staff enough. if you’re considering ecocamp patagonia, don’t hesitate—it’s an unforgettable adventure!

review for singapore cable car to sentosa island the singapore cable car ride to sentosa island is a fantastic and scenic experience, offering stunning aerial views of the city skyline, lush greenery, and the harbor. it’s not just a mode of transport but an attraction in itself, making your journey to sentosa exciting from the very start. the cabins are spacious, clean, and comfortable, with large windows for 360-degree panoramic views. the ride is smooth and relaxing, perfect for capturing breathtaking photos of singapore from above. it’s a great way to reach sentosa island, avoiding traffic while enjoying a bird’s-eye view of attractions like universal studios singapore and siloso beach. the best time to ride is during sunset or at night, when the city lights create a magical experience. overall, the singapore cable car is a must-try experience, offering a fun, scenic, and memorable way to travel to sentosa island!

review of cerro campanario: cerro campanario is a must-visit spot in bariloche, offering one of the most stunning panoramic views in the region. the hike to the top is short but steep, taking about 30-40 minutes depending on your pace. for those who prefer not to hike, there’s a convenient chairlift that takes you up in just a few minutes. once at the summit, you’re rewarded with breathtaking 360-degree views of the surrounding lakes, forests, and mountains. it’s the perfect spot for photography or simply enjoying the natural beauty of patagonia. there’s also a small café at the top where you can relax with a coffee or snack while taking in the views. make sure to wear comfortable shoes if you plan to hike, as the trail can be slippery in some areas. it’s a relatively easy climb, suitable for families and people of all ages. highly recommended for anyone visiting bariloche!

review of lions gate bridge – vancouver’s iconic gateway crossing the lions gate bridge is one of the most visually stunning experiences in vancouver. whether heading north toward the lush slopes of grouse mountain and the hills of west vancouver or south into downtown, flanked by the towering trees of stanley park, the scenery is nothing short of breathtaking. on clear days, the green waters of burrard inlet shimmer on either side, making the journey feel like a postcard come to life. the bridge is more than just a crossing—it’s a moment of transition between the urban and the wild, the city and the sea. it can be enjoyed not only by vehicle but also on foot or by bike. walking across gives you a chance to fully take in the surrounding views—just be aware that the pedestrian path is quite narrow. if a cyclist is passing, it can get tight, so caution is needed. that said, the beauty comes with a price. traffic during rush hours can be intense, and any accident can bring things to a near standstill. in such moments, the iconic charm of the bridge can feel more like a bottleneck. still, despite its traffic woes, lions gate bridge remains one of the most scenic and symbolic landmarks in the region—a must-experience whether you are a local or a visitor.

review: an unforgettable tour with khalafa elasefar i recently had the most amazing experience exploring fez guided by khalafa elasefar and i can honestly say it completely changed the way i see this historic city. i knew nothing before arriving to fez, but the facts and stories i learned on this tour absolutely blew my mind! from the moment we stepped into the medina, our guide brought the city to life. he wasn’t just reciting facts—he was telling stories, sharing secrets hidden in the ancient walls, and making connections between fez’s past and present that i never would have noticed on my own. i had no idea that fez is home to the world’s oldest university, al quaraouiyine, founded by a woman in 859 ad! and learning about the intricate craftsmanship behind the zellige tiles and leatherwork made me appreciate every little detail in the city so much more. one of the highlights was visiting the tanneries. i’d seen pictures, but standing there, watching the traditional leather-making process in person while our guide explained every step was something else entirely. the way fez has preserved these ancient traditions for centuries is just incredible. beyond the history and architecture, our guide made sure we experienced the culture firsthand—taking us to hidden riads, introducing us to local artisans, and even helping us find the best spot for authentic turkish coffee. he had a way of making everything feel immersive, like we were part of the city rather than just visitors. if you’re planning to visit fez, i can’t stress enough how important it is to have a knowledgeable guide. fez is a maze of history, culture, and hidden gems, and without an expert leading the way, you’d miss so much. this tour wasn’t just informative—it was eye-opening, inspiring, and truly unforgettable. if you ever get the chance, take a guided tour in fez with khalafa elasefar you’ll walk away with a whole new appreciation for this magical city!

riisitunturi national park – a scenic surprise in the heart of lapland we came to riisitunturi with low expectations—and left thoroughly enchanted. nestled at the edge of lapland, this park offers a landscape unlike much of the rest of finland, making it a refreshing discovery for any nature lover. the hike up to riisi fell, is both gentle and rewarding. along the way, you’ll encounter unique flora and fauna, offering a delightful contrast to southern parts of the country. at the summit, it’s a paradise for birdwatchers and photographers—cameras and binoculars abound.

riisitunturi national park, also known as riisitunturin kansallispuisto in finnish, is a stunning national park located in lapland, finland. established in 1982, the park covers an area of approximately 77 square kilometers. the park is characterized by its unique landscape of rounded hills, known as "tunturi" in finnish. riisitunturi national park is home to a diverse range of arctic flora and fauna. the park is covered in snow and ice for most of the year, making it a winter wonderland. the park has several hiking trails, ranging from easy to challenging, that offer breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape. in the winter, the park is perfect for skiing and snowshoeing. in the summer, the park's hills are covered in delicious berries, such as cloudberries and blueberries. wildlife and naturethe park is home to a large population of reindeer.riisitunturi national park is a birdwatcher's paradise, with species such as the golden eagle and the gyrfalcon.the park's unique landscape supports a diverse range of arctic flora, including rare species such as the lapland rhododendron. the park is located in lapland, finland, approximately 150 km north of rovaniemi. the park can be reached by car or public transportation. there are several accommodation options available in the nearby town of poiso riisitunturi national park is a great place to see the northern lights. in the summer, the park experiences the midnight sun, where the sun remains visible at midnight. the park is home to the indigenous sami people, who have lived in the area for centuries. riisitunturi national park is a unique and breathtaking destination that offers a range of outdoor activities and stunning natural beauty.

rodrigues is a mascarene island under the protection and jurisdiction of mauritius. the mauritian mainland is a gem in its own right. but, the island of rodrigues is a gem within a gem. its focus on wildlife conservation would put many governments to shame. if you are privileged enough to reach rodrigues then the grande montagne information centre is a must visit. the staff at the centre are very dedicated to the centre and the conservation of rodrigues natural resources - this is an island where plastic bags are banned!! the grande montagne information centre is an absolute treasure for horticulturalists, and as a consequence the local fauna would also give it the thumbs up too! when my family and i visited the centre (october 2023) our tour guide was dani, who was very passionate about her job, but whom had a very light hearted approach. the centre is maintained by the mauritian wildlife foundation. it is one of the few places in the world where one can see café marron - aka wild coffee in its natural uncultivated form. this plant is native to rodrigues island. as well as an introduction to rodrigues flora and fauna (to a lesser extent), the centre is very high up on this mountainous island, from which one can get excellent views of the land and the indian ocean. i was told that if we had visited during the right season, we would be able to see whales breaching the surface of the sea. for example: sperm whales.

roni was great! we wanted to explore lake titicaca on our own by kayak, but it was nearly impossible to find a company willing to rent kayaks without bundling them into a typical tour package, which we weren’t interested in at all. ronald was kind and trusting, he rented us two of his double kayaks and even brought them down to the shore for us. the kayaks were spacious, a bit heavy of course, but very stable. we had plenty of room to pack our gear for three days. roni gave us some directions and off we went. i have to emphasize: if you’re planning to go out on your own on this lake, make sure you have solid navigation skills and paddling experience. the wind can change quickly, and distances are much longer than they appear in the clear air. (we were with our daughters but we used to paddle out on the sea back in sweden) paddling along the edge of the reeds is straightforward—you’ll pass many lovely floating islands with families. open water crossings require some planning, but the kayaks are sturdy and handled the waves well. it was easy to find accommodation along the shore, we went to the edge of capachica peninsula. we saw no other independent kayakers—just one double kayak with a motorboat escort. if you’re unsure about going solo, definitely ask roni—i’m sure he can arrange some kind of support. on our return, we dropped off the kayaks at roni’s place at uros, and he kindly gave us a lift back by motorboat. overall, a great experience—though having some physical maps would’ve been helpful, don’t know if such exists here. (we used google maps and maps.me but they weren’t accurate in the channels of the reeds). well worth to explore this part of this beautiful lake from kayak, a totally different experience than with the usual big boat tours.

royal national park coastal walk – a world-class hike just outside sydney if you’re looking for a hike that truly has it all — dramatic ocean cliffs, secluded beaches, waterfalls, native wildlife, and sweeping views — the royal national park coastal walk is an absolute must-do. located just an hour from sydney, this 26km trail offers one of the most scenic coastal walks in australia. whether you’re doing the full hike or just a section (like bundeena to wattamolla), every step delivers something memorable. expect turquoise waters, sandstone cliffs, wildflowers in spring, and maybe even a pod of dolphins if you’re lucky! what i love most is the variety: one minute you’re trekking through eucalyptus forest, and the next you’re standing on a clifftop watching waves crash below. highlights like wedding cake rock, eagle rock, curracurrong falls, and the many hidden beaches along the way make this a photographer’s dream. tips: • start early, bring plenty of water, and wear sturdy shoes. • there are toilets and picnic spots at key points like wattamolla and garie beach. • it’s well-marked and beginner-friendly, but the full trail is best spread over two days if you’re not a seasoned hiker. whether you’re a local or a visitor, this walk will remind you how incredibly diverse and beautiful the australian coastline really is. it’s peaceful, inspiring, and perfect for reconnecting with nature. rating: 5/5 – one of the best hikes near sydney. highly recommended for all nature lovers and adventure seekers.

rue st-jean runs through the saint-jean gate, a historical monument frequently photographed, in fact, this is the one gate that you see in photos. it is one of the entry points through the fortified walls surrounding old québec. many shops and restaurants can be found on the inside of the walls near the gate. québec city has seen many battles and sieges. to defend against such attacks, a wall was built around québec city in 1690. this original wall included 11 towers but was constructed hastily, having to be replaced three years later. the city’s current wall began to take shape in 1745, permanently surrounding the town. this iconic gate is part of the fortification system comprising bastions, gates, and defensive structures that account for québec city's renown as a fortified colonial city and the reason old québec was named a unesco world heritage centre. only three other gates (kent, saint-louis, and prescott) that were part of the original fortifications survive. from the top, you can enjoy views of rue saint-jean, a trendy street of cafes, restaurants, and shops, and place d’youville, a public square that is transformed into an outdoor skating rink during the winter. climb the stairs, which will also open onto the walkway running along the top of the fortifications. as you follow this walkway to two of the other three gates in the stone walls, you will marvel at the view of old québec afforded from this vantage point.

sagrado tepeyac garden, located on the eastern slopes of cerro de tepeyac in mexico city, is a serene and historically significant site within the basilica of our lady of guadalupe complex. the garden features lush, impeccably maintained greenery, providing a peaceful environment for reflection. ￼ a notable highlight is the impressive fountain area, sometimes referred to as the fuente de quetzalcóatl, which adds to the garden’s tranquil ambiance. ￼ visitors often appreciate the garden’s well-kept lawns and the sense of peace it offers, making it an ideal spot for contemplation amidst the bustling city. ￼ overall, sagrado tepeyac garden is a must-visit for those seeking a blend of natural beauty and spiritual significance in mexico city.

sai kung east country park is a 44.77 sq. kilometre country park that was designated in 1978 and includes some of the most beautiful and best hiking locations in hong kong. it is made up of rolling hills, large reservoir, wooded and rugged mountain terrain, coastal gems with isolated beaches and features geological treasures that form part of the hong kong unesco global geopark. early stages of the maclehose trail, one of national geographic's 20 world dream trails crosses through the sai kung east country park, providing hikers with long stretches of delightful trekking and view points. the beaches found along this hike are amongst the finest in hong kong. camping is available for those interested in overnight visits. other hiking highlights in the area include sharp peak, po pin chau and the short and easy geo trail below the high island reservoir east dam. at this location, you will find one the easiest places to enjoy the unesco global geopark where you see remarkable volcanic hexagonal columns and other geological features rarely seen anywhere. as for transportation, local bus routes connect various points within the country park from sai kung village. you can also hire boats to take you directly to some of the feature beaches around long ke and tai long wan. in the end, the sai kung east country park is one of the rural treasures in hong kong. it is rather isolated but connected well enough to enjoy some of its highlights as 1/2 day, full day and even overnight visits. this country park is a great place for outdoor enthusiasts who live in hong kong as well as visitors seeking a rural retreat from the busy city streets of the city.

salar de uyuni (or "salar de tunupa") is the world's largest salt flat, or playa, at over 10,000 square kilometres (3,900 sq mi) in area. it is in the daniel campos province in potosí in southwest bolivia, near the crest of the andes at an elevation of 3,656 m (11,995 ft) above sea level. the salar was formed as a result of transformations between several prehistoric lakes that existed around forty thousand years ago but had all evaporated over time. it is now covered by a few meters of salt crust, which has an extraordinary flatness with the average elevation variations within one meter over the entire area of the salar. the crust serves as a source of salt and covers a pool of brine, which is exceptionally rich in lithium. the large area, clear skies, and exceptional flatness of the surface make the salar ideal for calibrating the altimeters of earth observation satellites. following rain, a thin layer of dead calm water transforms the flat into the world's largest mirror, 129 km (80 mi) across.
