the anzac memorial in sydney is a profoundly moving and beautifully designed tribute to australian servicemen and servicewomen. its stunning art deco architecture and powerful sculptures create a solemn yet inspiring atmosphere. the recent centenary extension seamlessly blends with the original 1930s structure, offering a comprehensive and engaging historical narrative spanning over a century of service. visitors can explore thoughtfully curated exhibitions that tell individual stories of courage and sacrifice, fostering a deep sense of respect and remembrance. the daily service of remembrance, including the last post ceremony, is a particularly poignant experience. the memorial's location in hyde park provides a tranquil setting for reflection. while there are no public restrooms on-site, nearby cafes offer convenience. a visit to the anzac memorial is an essential and unforgettable experience for anyone wanting to understand australia's military history and honor those who have served.

the anzac memorial is truly something special. when you step inside, you immediately feel the weight of the history and the sacrifices made by those who fought in the war. the design and artwork inside really capture the emotions—there’s a quiet, respectful atmosphere that makes you stop and reflect. the exhibits tell powerful stories of courage, and it’s impossible not to get goosebumps walking through. if you want to understand and feel the history. this place is a must-visit. it’s more than just a memorial. it’s a deeply moving experience.

the apfelstrudel with vanilla sauce was good, but it was the esterhazy schnitten that really made my evening - creamy, sweet, and generously sized. the black coffee and melange were also enjoyable. the menu is beautifully designed, and the interior is lovely. prices are reasonable. i'll definitely be back.

the arch of constantine is a striking monument that stands proudly between the colosseum and the roman forum, serving as a testament to imperial power and victory. built in 312 ad to commemorate emperor constantine’s victory over maxentius, it is the largest triumphal arch in rome and an impressive blend of roman artistry and politics. what makes this arch unique is its reuse of earlier sculptures from previous emperors like trajan, hadrian, and marcus aurelius, symbolizing constantine’s connection to rome’s great rulers. the intricate carvings and reliefs, though weathered, still showcase the grandeur of roman craftsmanship. while you can’t walk through it, the arch is free to admire and perfectly placed for a great photo with the colosseum in the background. some details may be lost on casual visitors, but for history lovers, it’s a fascinating insight into rome’s past. 9/10 – a must-see, especially if you’re already exploring the colosseum!

the archibald memorial fountain is one of sydney’s most iconic and historically significant landmarks, and it’s a place that truly deserves a moment of your time. nestled in the beautiful domain, just a short walk from the royal botanic garden, the fountain combines art, history, and natural beauty in a way that feels timeless and evocative. built in 1932, the archibald memorial fountain was designed by sculptor margel hinder and architect bruce dellit, and it commemorates the life and legacy of j.f. archibald, the long-time editor of the bulletin. what makes this fountain so striking is its blend of classical and modern design elements, combining intricate sculptures with powerful symbolism. at the centre of the fountain, you’ll find a stunning bronze figure of apollo, surrounded by allegorical statues representing australia’s ties to the united kingdom, as well as figures from greek mythology. the water flows dramatically around these figures, adding an ethereal quality to the space. the fountain’s design was also inspired by the famous latona fountain at the palace of versailles, which gives it a sense of grandeur and elegance that feels both regal and peaceful. the surrounding area, with its lush greenery and tree-lined paths, creates a serene space for reflection, and it's easy to see why so many people come here to relax or take a break from the bustle of the city. the craftsmanship of the fountain is truly impressive. the intricate detailing in the sculptures, the movement of the water, and the way everything is arranged to catch the light makes it a photographer’s dream. whether it’s a sunny afternoon or a cloudy evening, the archibald memorial fountain offers a different perspective and beauty depending on the time of day. for anyone interested in sydney’s history, the fountain is also a quiet reminder of the city’s colonial past and its connection to european traditions, as well as its deep cultural ties to the arts. it’s a great spot to learn more about both the architectural and artistic heritage of australia. the archibald memorial fountain is not just a decorative feature; it’s a tribute to a man who helped shape australia’s literary and cultural identity, and it’s become a beloved part of the city’s public art scene. it’s a peaceful place to stop, take in the beauty of the fountain and the surrounding park, and reflect on the history it represents. if you’re visiting sydney, this is a spot you definitely shouldn’t miss. whether you're an art enthusiast, a history buff, or simply looking for a beautiful place to unwind, the archibald memorial fountain offers something for everyone.

the belvedere complex is made up of the upper palace, lower palace, and the stunning gardens in between — and the gardens are completely free to enter! of course, if you’re into art, the famous klimt’s “the kiss” is housed in the upper belvedere, but even if you skip the museum, the gardens alone are worth the trip. this time, i also explored the back side of the upper palace and found a beautiful pond and more peaceful garden paths. honestly, the entire space felt like a painting. i even saw locals jogging through the gardens — imagine having this as your morning run route! the berlin wall (german: berliner mauer, pronounced [bɛʁˌliːnɐ ˈmaʊɐ] ⓘ) was a guarded concrete barrier that encircled west berlin from 1961 to 1989, separating it from east berlin and the german democratic republic (gdr; east germany). construction of the berlin wall was commenced by the government of the gdr on 13 august 1961. it included guard towers placed along large concrete walls, accompanied by a wide area (later known as the "death strip") that contained anti-vehicle trenches, beds of nails and other defenses. the primary intention for the wall's construction was to prevent east german citizens from fleeing to the west.

the berlin wall is not just a historical structure it’s a symbol of separation, loss, and resilience. walking alongside it, seeing the murals the memorials and reading the stories of those who risked everything for freedom is a deeply emotional experience. it’s a place that speaks volumes without saying a word. while parts of it are surrounded by tourists and souvenir stands, and yes it can feel a bit commercialized at times the impact of standing before such a powerful piece of history is undeniable. there's a unique energy here like touching a scar that the world still remembers. a visit to the berlin wall is more than sightseeing it’s a moment of reflection. one of the most important stops in berlin and in our collective memory.

the best place of our trip, after petra. then desert is fantastic, the colors are insane and the views are amazing!! wadi rum, often referred to as the “valley of the moon,” is a stunning desert landscape in southern jordan renowned for its dramatic sandstone mountains, vast red dunes, and otherworldly rock formations. this unesco world heritage site offers visitors a unique blend of natural beauty and cultural heritage, with evidence of human habitation dating back thousands of years. highlights: • breathtaking scenery: the striking contrast of the reddish sands against the towering cliffs creates a mesmerizing visual experience, especially at sunrise and sunset when the colors are most vibrant. • outdoor activities: wadi rum is a haven for adventure enthusiasts. visitors can enjoy activities such as hiking, rock climbing, jeep tours, and camel trekking, allowing them to explore the vastness of the desert and its hidden wonders. • bedouin culture: the local bedouin tribes offer authentic cultural experiences, including traditional meals, music, and hospitality. staying in a bedouin camp under the stars adds a unique dimension to the visit. • film location: wadi rum has served as a backdrop for numerous films, including lawrence of arabia and the martian, making it famous in cinematic history. this adds an intriguing layer for film enthusiasts. • stargazing: the clear desert skies make wadi rum one of the best places in the world for stargazing, with minimal light pollution allowing for breathtaking views of the milky way. conclusion: wadi rum is a magical destination that captivates visitors with its rugged beauty and rich cultural experiences. whether you’re seeking adventure, relaxation, or a glimpse into bedouin life, this remarkable desert landscape is sure to leave a lasting impression. it’s a must-visit for anyone traveling to jordan.

the bismarck memorial is a monumental sculpture honouring one of the greatest germans who ever lived, the mastermind of the german unification and chancellor of the german empire for decades. this monument portrays bismarck standing in his ceremonial chancellor uniform surrounded by allegorical statues depicting german world power status at the end of the 19th century, german industrial and military might, german unity and german history. a monumental piece of work that should be on your berlin itinerary.

the bismarck national memorial is dedicated to otto von bismarck, minister president of the kingdom of prussia and the first chancellor of the german empire. it is one of 250 memorials to bismarck worldwide. completed in 1901 in the neo-baroque style, it portrays bismarck standing above statues of: atlas, showing germany's world power status at the end of the 19th century; siegfried, forging a sword to show germany's strong industrial and military might; germania pinning underfoot a panther, symbolizing the suppression of discord and rebellion; a sibyl reclining on a sphinx and reading the book of history.

the bismarck-nationaldenkmal (bismarck national monument) is a grand statue in berlin’s tiergarten, dedicated to otto von bismarck, the first chancellor of the german empire. unveiled in 1901, it was designed by reinhold begas and originally stood in front of the reichstag before being moved to its current location near the siegessäule (victory column). the monument features bismarck in a commanding pose, with allegorical figures representing war, diplomacy, legislation, and military strategy. it symbolizes his role in unifying germany in 1871 and shaping its political and military power. today, it remains a significant historical landmark in berlin.

the boat tour itself is pure magic. you glide across a lake that stretches 21 kilometers, framed by rugged peaks and dense forests. the water is that signature rocky mountain turquoise, shifting shades with the light, and on calm days it reflects the mountains so perfectly you’ll swear you’ve stepped into a postcard. what makes this tour stand out is the storytelling. the guides mix history, local legends, and geology with just the right dash of humor. you’ll hear about the original indigenous peoples who lived in the valley, the ghost town now submerged under the lake, and even how “minnewanka” translates to “lake of the spirits.” there’s something surreal about floating over a sunken village while learning about the myths tied to the waters beneath you. for photographers, every angle is a stunner. wide mountain backdrops, close-ups of rocky cliffs, and if you’re lucky, wildlife sightings — bighorn sheep on the slopes, bald eagles overhead, or even the occasional bear near the shoreline. the vibe is laid-back and welcoming. families, solo travelers, and couples all fit in — you can relax on the deck, snap a hundred photos, or just lean back and breathe in the crisp alpine air. tours are well-organized and punctual, so it’s easy to plan as part of a loop drive. pro tips for fellow road trippers: • book tickets ahead, especially in summer. • arrive early to wander the shoreline before boarding — the views are just as good from land. • bring a jacket, even on sunny days. the breeze on the lake can be cooler than expected. • pair it with stops at two jack lake or a picnic on the loop for a full day of adventure. bottom line: the lake minnewanka boat tour is one of those experiences that captures everything banff does best — big mountains, glacial water, rich history, and that feeling of being small in the most beautiful way possible. an absolute must-do for anyone who loves the open road and chasing unforgettable stops along the way.

the bondi to bronte coastal walk is one of sydney’s most iconic and breathtaking experiences — a must-do for locals and visitors alike. stretching along sandstone cliffs with uninterrupted ocean views, this walk offers a perfect blend of natural beauty, beach culture, and community energy. the trail is about 2.5 km and takes around 30–45 minutes one way at a leisurely pace. along the way, you'll pass stunning beaches like tamarama and mackenzies bay, dramatic lookout points such as marks park and mackenzies point, and even the historic waverley cemetery, perched right on the cliff’s edge. it’s an easy-to-moderate path, mostly paved with a few stairs, making it accessible for most fitness levels. expect ocean breezes, surfers riding the waves below, and plenty of photo-worthy moments around every corner. whether you're here for exercise, photography, or simply to take in the views, the bondi to bronte walk is a perfect slice of coastal sydney — scenic, vibrant, and unforgettable.

the bondi to bronte coastal walk squeezes a whole highlight reel into a couple of kilometres. you start with bondi’s curve of sand and that bright ocean pool clinging to the headland, then the path rises and the pacific fills your field of vision. spray hangs in the air, banksias rattle in the breeze and the rock shelves below boom as sets roll through. it is lively without feeling crowded first thing in the morning, a mix of runners, pram pushes, swimmers with goggles around their necks and visitors stopping every few metres because the outlook keeps changing. mackenzies bay appears like a stone amphitheatre, tamarama offers a pocket of clean sand and punchy surf, and bronte arrives with its grassy park and heritage baths cut into the southern rocks. the walking itself is straightforward but never dull. boardwalks glide above fragile dunes, then a string of stairs lifts you to the next headland for another angle on the cliffs. benches are placed where you would have stopped anyway. if you are tempted by the water, you are spoiled for choice. slip into icebergs for salty laps, time a dip at tamarama between sets, or finish with a float in bronte baths or a quick wallow in the bogey hole when the tide is kind. coffee and breakfast are never far away, which makes it easy to turn a short stroll into a relaxed morning out. a few things help. start early for cooler air and softer light, carry water and sunscreen because shade is patchy, and wear shoes you are happy climbing in. the route includes stairs, so some sections are awkward with a pram, but buses from bondi junction make it simple to begin at either end and ride back. after rain the rocks glisten and the sea goes slate blue, in winter you might spot whales from the lookouts. however you pace it, this small stretch delivers big views and that happy, salty reset you only get from walking beside open water.

the bondi to coogee coastal walk strings together some of sydney’s best ocean views like beads on a line. you start with bondi’s broad arc of sand, then the path rises to sandstone headlands where the pacific fills your peripheral vision and sea spray hangs in the air. the track dips and climbs in easy waves, revealing a new cove every few minutes. tamarama is a pocket beach with punchy surf, bronte brings a heritage ocean pool and grassy picnic lawns, and clovelly narrows into a snorkel friendly inlet where the water often looks aquarium clear. keep going and gordon’s bay appears with its tangle of fishing boats and rocky shelves, before coogee opens wide at the finish. what makes this walk special is how varied it feels over about six kilometers. one moment you are leaning on a cliff railing watching waves explode against the rock platform, the next you are wandering past banksias and coastal heath that buzz with honeyeaters. boardwalk sections keep the footing simple above fragile dunes, and staircases deliver you down to sand whenever a swim or coffee break calls your name. benches pop up in well chosen spots for lingering over the view, and there are plenty of side tracks if you like exploring. a few pointers make it smoother. start early for gentler light and fewer people, carry water and sunscreen, and wear shoes you are happy to climb stairs in. amenities are spaced sensibly along the route, with ocean pools and change rooms at several beaches, plus cafés within a minute or two of the path. buses connect both ends, so you can commit to the full distance without worrying about a loop back. however you pace it, the walk delivers that unbeatable mix of sea air, workout and postcard scenery that leaves you salty haired and grinning at the finish.

the botanical garden in prague is an absolute must-visit! nestled on a hillside, it offers beautiful views and a peaceful, well-maintained setting that feels both magical and unusual. the grounds are immaculate, with a charming mix of nature, art, and thoughtful design throughout. one of the highlights is the delightful little chapel tucked inside the garden, adding a quiet, almost secret charm to the place. there’s also a lovely bee garden that’s both educational and beautifully arranged. the glasshouse is a real standout—stepping inside feels like entering another world, with vibrant butterflies fluttering all around you. the garden is full of surprises, from fascinating sculptures scattered throughout to dedicated play areas that make it a fantastic spot for families with children. every corner offers something unique, whether you’re a plant lover, a photography enthusiast, or just looking for a peaceful escape. truly a gem of prague—don’t miss it!

the botanical garden is a beautiful escape into nature, offering a serene experience with meticulously maintained gardens and diverse plant collections. the layout makes it easy to wander through themed areas, each featuring unique flora from around the world, but mainly south america. highlights include vibrant seasonal blooms, calming water features, and shaded paths that make exploring relaxing even on warmer days. the garden is well-labeled, allowing visitors to learn more about each plant, and there are plenty of benches to sit and enjoy the peaceful surroundings. it’s a perfect spot for nature lovers, families, or anyone looking to unwind in a lush, tranquil setting.

the botanical garden of the city of prague is a nice and peaceful place, especially for nature lovers. it’s located about 15 minutes by car from the old town, and features a wide variety of plants and greenery, making it a pleasant spot for a relaxing walk or quiet time outdoors. that said, it’s more of a local gem than a must-see attraction. if you’re already nearby, it’s definitely worth stopping by. but if you’re staying in the old town or further and the weather is hot , it may not be worth the trip out of your way, especially with so many other iconic sights to see in the city center. in short, a nice spot if convenient, but not essential for first-time visitors on a tight schedule.

the boynton pass vortex hike is a must-do for those visiting sedona, offering a harmonious mix of natural splendor and spiritual ambiance. whether you’re seeking a physical adventure, a spiritual journey, or simply a peaceful retreat into nature, this trail provides an enriching experience that resonates with many who traverse it. • timing: early morning or late afternoon hikes offer cooler temperatures and softer lighting for photography. • preparation: wear sturdy hiking shoes, bring plenty of water, and consider sun protection, as shade is limited along the trail. • respect: the area holds spiritual significance for many; maintaining a respectful and quiet demeanor enhances the experience for all visitors.

the bradley's head to chowder bay walk is one of sydney's most picturesque and relaxing coastal trails, offering a perfect blend of natural beauty and historical significance. the walk is well-maintained and easy to follow, making it accessible for all fitness levels. as you meander along the path, you'll be treated to stunning views of sydney harbour, the opera house, and the harbour bridge, framed by lush bushland and towering eucalyptus trees. the track takes you through diverse landscapes, from the quiet, shaded forests to the open, breezy coastal edges, with plenty of spots to stop and take in the breathtaking scenery. along the way, you'll pass historical landmarks like bradley's head amphitheatre and the old military fortifications, adding an interesting layer of history to the experience. there are also parts of the forest burnt with what we assume to be bushfires. the walk ends at chowder bay, where you can relax by the water, grab a coffee, or even take a refreshing dip. many families of all cultural background can be found here doing picnic, barbecues and just playing on the grassy terrain. there are many dogs in the clifton gardens and they have a pretty wide area to play around. whether you're a local or a visitor, this walk is a must-do, offering a perfect escape into nature without leaving the city.

the cabildo is a must-see historical building located right on jackson square, next to the iconic st. louis cathedral. originally built between 1795 and 1799 as the spanish colonial city hall, it's now part of the louisiana state museum and offers a fascinating look into the history of louisiana. i was really impressed by the nice displays throughout the cabildo. it's amazing to walk through the same halls where the louisiana purchase transfer ceremony took place in 1803, a pivotal moment that doubled the size of the united states! one of the highlights for me was seeing the incredible and dazzling costumes worn for the famous mardi gras parades, a truly unique aspect of new orleans culture. it gives you a real sense of the excitement and artistry that goes into this annual event. the museum also features a moving room dedicated to the survivors of hurricane katrina, which provides an important reminder of the resilience and spirit of the people of new orleans. it's worth noting that the cabildo has served many important functions throughout its history, including as the new orleans city hall and the home of the louisiana supreme court. there is an admission fee to enter, but it's a worthwhile investment for anyone interested in history and the cultural heritage of louisiana. i would highly recommend spending a couple of hours here to fully appreciate all that the cabildo has to offer.

the cabildo: a treasure of louisiana’s history! standing proudly beside st. louis cathedral, the cabildo is one of the most beautiful and historically significant buildings in jackson square. its grand spanish colonial architecture immediately catches the eye, but what lies inside is even more remarkable—a journey through the history of louisiana, filled with stories of resilience, culture, and transformation. walking through its halls, i felt transported back in time. the museum’s exhibits cover everything from the louisiana purchase, which forever changed the course of american history, to the diverse cultures that have shaped new orleans into the vibrant city it is today. the artifacts on display—paintings, documents, and personal belongings of historical figures—bring the past to life in a way that’s both engaging and deeply moving. one of the highlights was seeing the death mask of napoleon bonaparte, an unexpected yet fascinating piece of history. but what struck me most was how the museum tells the story of louisiana’s people—from the indigenous tribes to the creole, african, and european influences that have blended together over centuries. for anyone visiting jackson square, the cabildo is a must-see. it’s not just a museum—it’s a gateway to understanding the heart and soul of new orleans. the stories within its walls remind us that this city has always been a place of change, culture, and enduring spirit. and the ticket was just $10 for adults, $8 for kids. make sure you visit it

the cairo citadel, also known as the citadel of saladin, is one of the most iconic historical sites in the city. perched on a hill, it offers a panoramic view of cairo that’s truly worth the visit—on a clear day, you can even see the pyramids in the distance. the complex is large and includes several notable buildings, the most famous being the mosque of muhammad ali. its impressive ottoman-style architecture and grand domes make it a highlight for many visitors. the interior is spacious and beautifully decorated, and it’s easy to spend a good amount of time just admiring the details. aside from the mosque, the citadel grounds also house other smaller mosques, museums (like the police museum and military museum), and historical buildings. walking around the area gives a real sense of cairo’s layered history—from islamic rule to modern military heritage. however, be prepared for some uneven paths and walking uphill. it’s best to wear comfortable shoes and bring water, especially if you’re visiting in the warmer months. also, some parts of the citadel are better preserved than others, but the overall atmosphere remains grand and meaningful. in short, the cairo citadel is a fascinating place to explore, both for its architecture and its views. it’s a perfect mix of history, culture, and scenery all in one location. definitely recommended for anyone spending a few days in cairo.

the capim acu is by far the most long, emotional and difficult trail in noronha. the complete u-shaped trail is around 12km, usually made around six hours of heavy walking, which offers views of the seas of dentro and fora, between the beaches of sancho and leão. starting from a dirt road in the village, the trail begins steeply on the steep slope that gives access to the lighthouse. after this step and followed in zigzagging between high vegetation, the trail descends to the sea level, towards the capim-açu cave, which has restricted access only in times of calmer seas. soon after, there are some beautiful natural pools that are inviting for a refreshing swim. after a tiring walk over rocks (this is the very hard part, lasting more than 3 hours - i suggest you to wear proper trail shoes), you reach praia do leão, where the trail ends. this beach is considered one of the most beautiful beaches in brazil, with a sea of green waters and some really unforgettable blue tones.

the carlo quarto (charles iv) monument in prague is a monumental bronze statue dedicated to emperor charles iv, located at křížovnické náměstí, near charles bridge. this statue honors one of prague’s most significant rulers, who was not only king of bohemia but also holy roman emperor, and who contributed greatly to the city’s cultural and architectural development. history & design: • the statue was unveiled in 1848, celebrating the 500th anniversary of charles iv’s reign and his founding of charles university in 1348. • the statue was designed by ernst julius hähnel and its base by josef kranner. • it depicts charles iv in regal attire, holding a charter (symbolizing the university), standing confidently at the center of the statue. • the base of the monument is decorated with four allegorical figures, representing the faculties of the university: theology, medicine, law, and philosophy. significance of charles iv: • charles iv was one of the most important monarchs of medieval europe, known for his visionary policies, cultural contributions, and architectural projects, such as the construction of st. vitus cathedral and the establishment of prague as the capital of the holy roman empire. • under his rule, prague flourished both culturally and economically, and his establishment of charles university marked a milestone in the development of higher education in europe. location & surroundings: • the carlo quarto statue stands near the charles bridge, facing toward old town square and the prague castle, offering stunning views of the historic center of the city. • the monument is a popular tourist attraction and an important symbol of prague’s rich medieval history. the carlo quarto monument serves as a tribute to a pivotal figure in prague’s history and as a reminder of the emperor’s enduring legacy in the city’s culture and architecture.

the catedral metropolitana de são sebastião was one of the most awe-inspiring stops during my day trip in rio de janeiro. from the outside, its unique, modernist design immediately grabs your attention—unlike any cathedral i’ve ever seen. the massive conical structure stands tall and proud in the heart of the city, blending bold architecture with spiritual serenity. stepping inside was truly breathtaking. the towering stained-glass windows reaching up to the dome fill the space with vibrant colors and an almost otherworldly glow. the vast interior, with its minimalist design and peaceful ambiance, invites you to pause and reflect. it's a powerful contrast to the energetic vibe of the city outside. apart from its architectural beauty, the cathedral also has a lovely little gift shop where we picked up a few meaningful souvenirs. from religious items to locally crafted mementos, the shop had a thoughtful selection that made it easy to take a piece of this spiritual and cultural experience home with us. the catedral metropolitana is not just a religious site—it's a symbol of rio’s blend of modernity, faith, and creativity. whether you're into architecture, history, spirituality, or simply looking for a quiet moment in the city, this place is a must-visit. highly recommended to anyone exploring rio de janeiro!

the cathedral of rio de janeiro leaves no room for ambivalence - its design is a bold unapologetic declaration. you either marvel at its raw beauty and echoes of ancient history, or you see nothing but a brutalist behemoth: cold, unyielding concrete cloaked in irreverence and incompletion. either way, no one can deny the bravado of the architect edgar de oliveira da fonseca. perhaps his wish to break away from the “european tradition” is most compelling - instead of copying european gothic or baroque styles (as many new world cathedrals did), fonseca wanted a modern, latin american identity. referencing the indigenous cultures of the americas created a more regionally authentic, contextually relevant and unique expression of faith. we were awestruck by the spatial drama, tactile richness, and muscular elegance of the interior - a space that demands recognition and reverence. the stained glass panels are a triumph: rigorously modern, boldly expressive, and soaring in scale. their crescendo, a grecian cross suspended at the apex, feels less like decoration and more like a modern masterpiece - worthy of a place in any major art museum. definitely a venue deserving an hour of your tour itinerary of rio.

the cathedral of the assumption is located in the historic center of dubrovnik, near the rector’s palace, and has an architecture perfectly in line with the rest of the town. originally built in the twelfth century, in place of pre-existing religious buildings, it took on its current baroque forms with reconstruction in the late seventeenth century and early eighteenth following a strong earthquake that had almost completely destroyed it.

the cathedral of the assumption of the blessed virgin mary, located in dubrovnik, is a noteworthy attraction that offers visitors a glimpse into the city's religious and architectural heritage. while it may not be the most awe-inspiring cathedral i've visited, it certainly holds its own charm and historical significance. the baroque architecture of the cathedral is elegant, with a beautifully crafted facade and an impressive interior adorned with intricate altars and lovely artwork. the treasury, which houses a collection of religious relics and artifacts, is particularly interesting for those who appreciate history and art. however, the experience can be somewhat underwhelming compared to other grand european cathedrals. the interior, though beautiful, is relatively small and may not captivate those seeking a more majestic or elaborate setting. additionally, during peak tourist seasons, the cathedral can become quite crowded, detracting from the overall experience. overall, the cathedral of the assumption of the blessed virgin mary is worth a visit if you're exploring dubrovnik's old town, especially if you have an interest in religious architecture and history. it's a pleasant stop, but perhaps not a standout in a city full of remarkable sights.

the chadar trek was truly a once-in-a-lifetime experience, and it surpassed all my expectations. from the moment we arrived in leh, where the temperature was a freezing -17°c, we knew this would be an adventure to remember. by the time we reached chadar, the temperature dropped even further to an icy -25°c, creating a surreal and challenging environment. walking on the frozen zanskar river was breathtaking. when the ice was stable, we trekked across it, and when sections began to melt, we had to climb steep hills, some reaching a height of 30 meters. these climbs added an extra layer of adventure to the trek. thankfully, our guide was incredibly experienced and always led us safely, skillfully navigating us away from any dangerous spots. at times, when the ice melted, we had to switch to rain boots to cross sections with water. it was tough but part of the charm of the trek. thankfully, our porters carried most of the heavy gear, allowing us to focus on the trek without being weighed down. the meals during the trek were another highlight. the cooks prepared delicious food every day, and to our surprise, they even baked a cake in such harsh conditions—what a treat! the 9-day program was very well-organized. the first two days were dedicated to thorough medical checkups and acclimatization, which ensured we were ready for the extreme conditions. the support from the team, the stunning landscapes, and the thrill of walking on a frozen river made this trek unforgettable. this journey tested my limits but left me with incredible memories of perseverance, camaraderie, and nature’s raw beauty. if you’re looking for an adventure that challenges both your body and spirit, the chadar trek is the ultimate choice!

the champlain monument on dufferin terrace pays tribute to the man who founded the city in 1608. it is one of the city's most spectacular landmarks, both because of its imposing size and its central location at a lively gathering place where locals and tourists come to watch street entertainers perform. samuel de champlain (1567–1635) was an explorer, geographer, and mapmaker who founded québec city in 1608. in 1613, he explored the ottawa river. he was called the ‘father of new france,’ champlain was an explorer who founded quebec city in july 1608, made the first accurate map of the area, and worked to find the first settlements. visitors to the monument can enjoy splendid views of the st. lawrence river, the lower town, île d'orléans, the south shore, and the laurentian mountain range! this statue commemorates the 300th anniversary of champlain’s second voyage on the ottawa river. it was erected at the same spot where champlain made his solar observation during his expedition in 1615.

the coastal walk from clovelly to tamarama is a spectacular stretch of sydney’s iconic bondi to coogee trail, offering some of the most scenic views, geological drama, and beachside charm you’ll find along the coast. this section is a perfect blend of natural beauty, cultural vibrancy, and well-maintained pathways that make the journey just as enjoyable as the destinations. starting at clovelly, you’re greeted with calm waters and a relaxed atmosphere — perfect for a morning swim or a quick snorkel before setting off. as you head north, the path winds along rugged cliffs and rocky outcrops, with dramatic ocean views that constantly shift with the light and weather. the trail is punctuated with informative signs and resting spots, giving you time to pause, reflect, and take in the scenery. one of the highlights along this route is bronte beach, a lively and family-friendly spot with grassy picnic areas, ocean pools, and cafés. it's an ideal midpoint to grab a coffee or just sit under a tree and soak up the atmosphere. from bronte, the walk becomes even more photogenic, with panoramic cliffside views, sandstone formations, and crashing waves below. the final stretch toward tamarama is breathtaking — a rugged, narrow beach tucked into a dramatic cove, often favored by surfers and creative souls. if you’re walking this path during the annual sculpture by the sea exhibition, the entire route transforms into an open-air gallery, with large-scale artworks integrated into the natural landscape. overall, the clovelly to tamarama walk is a compact but rich experience, blending wellness, nature, and local culture in one continuous line of beauty. whether you're walking, jogging, or just meandering with your camera, it's a must-do for anyone exploring sydney's coastline.

the coconut grove farmers market, held every saturday, is a fantastic place to discover unique, locally sourced products that stand out from what you’ll find at typical grocery stores. from innovative organic goods to fresh, healthy creations, it’s a haven for food lovers and health-conscious shoppers alike. a standout recommendation is glaser organic farms’ california rolls—absolutely delicious and packed with fresh, nutrient-rich ingredients. beyond these, they offer a vast array of daily-use products at impressive value. for instance, the green power blend at just $15 rivals anything you’d find in a store at two or three times the price. if you’re looking to explore an authentic local experience, find high-quality organic options, and snag a few great deals, coconut grove farmers market is well worth a saturday visit. for parking: try elizabeth street on the back side of the market! whoever created this - bravo!

the colborne lodge has reopened after renovations, and it is open from wednesday to sunday during guided tours offered at 11.30, 1.30 and 3.30. admission is free. it is a delightful place to visit. guided tours are lead by knowledgeable staff who shares history of the building and its inhabitants (mr and mrs howard who purchased the land in 1830s, and whose endowment originated what we now call the high park). the rooms are restored to look like they did nearly 200 years ago. while the original furniture and decorations were lost, the house is full of authentic beautiful artefacts from that period. the coach house (right next door) remains open (also wed-sun) from 11am to 4pm. it houses some temporary displays (currently: medicine of the victorian era) and a permanent exhibit dedicated to john g. howard, his professional achievements and also history of toronto. the museum also offers special seasonal events - like upcoming victorian christmas ghost stories at colborne lodge (december 7,8 and 14,15).

the conservatory of flowers in golden gate park is a peaceful and beautiful escape into nature. we visited with our family and enjoyed exploring the stunning collection of exotic plants and colorful blooms inside the victorian-era greenhouse. each room offers a different climate and plant theme, from tropical rainforests to highland orchids. tip: it’s warm and humid inside, so dress lightly. also, weekdays are less crowded, making for a quieter experience. don’t forget your camera—the building and plants are perfect for photos. a lovely stop for plant lovers, families, or anyone needing a relaxing break in the park!

the construction of al bastakiya dates to the 1890s. in its prime, the locality was capable of 60 housing units, most of which were separated by narrow, winding lanes. the town of al bastakiya was primarily built by the affluent persian merchants drawn to dubai by the rich trade opportunities and incentives offered by the emirati government; the district was named after the southern iranian town of bastak. in the 1980s half of al bastakiya was destroyed to make way for the development of a new office complex. the remaining houses were mostly used as warehouses or accommodation for foreign laborers. in 1989, the dubai municipality directed that the remaining parts of al bastakiya were to be demolished. rayner otter, a british architect, came to the area and made extensive renovation in the house where he was staying. rayner started a campaign to preserve the area and wrote a letter to prince charles, who was scheduled to visit dubai that year. on his arrival, prince charles asked to visit al bastakiya and explored the whole area with rayner otter. during his visit the prince suggested that al bastakiya should be preserved and the demolition was cancelled. in 2005, a project was initiated by the dubai municipality to restore the localities of old buildings and lanes. the name was later changed from al bastakiya to al fahidi historical neighbourhood.

the contemporary architecture tour of barcelona// lorenzo is an outstanding architect guide. as a repeat visitor to barcelona, this tour offered me a completely new perspective on the city’s urban planning and ongoing development. he provided fascinating insights into contemporary architecture and how it shapes daily life. we ended the tour at torre glòries, bringing everything full circle with stunning city views. the exhibitions there are also very engaging. highly recommended for architecture enthusiasts—and even families, as the experience can be adapted with fun activities in the area!

the convent of santa cruz de la popa is more than just a historical monument—it’s a peaceful retreat that connects you with the rich tapestry of cartagena’s past. i would highly recommend a visit to anyone who wants to experience a blend of history, spirituality, and stunning vistas.

the cooking class was phenomenal. i loved it. trust me when i say that the atmosphere is awesome. during the process of booking the class at the location we also booked the tour to the mud volcano so take advantage of this one stop shop to make your cartagena vacation memorable.
the coolest little coffee, prosecco, beer, wine and shop with funky gifts. kim (the owner) is super friendly!

the coolest part of the museum was the centrepiece viking long house foundations. it was difficult to view in total due to the low ceiling (presumably because there's stuff on top of it), but otherwise the exhibit was well done. the other exhibits were all about the history of reykjavik, which was presented in a fairly dry manner with minimal interaction and variety in the displays. the settlement exhibition cost as much as the national museum of iceland but had considerably less content.

the coptic museum is one of egypt’s most remarkable cultural institutions and offers a peaceful retreat from the hustle and bustle of cairo. located just a short metro ride from the city center, the museum houses an outstanding collection of coptic art, featuring exquisite late roman and early christian pieces, beautiful textiles, and fascinating manuscripts. the museum building itself—along with its serene gardens and annexes—is a true architectural treasure. a must-visit for anyone exploring cairo.

the corner is my go-to neighborhood bar right in downtown, it’s got that classic charm you don’t find much in here anymore. the drinks are solid, prices are fair, and the bartenders really know what they’re doing. in a city that’s always changing, the corner stands strong as one of the few spots that truly lasts.
the cottage was stunning! nicola was so helpful and great at communicating! such comfortable beds and a wonderful place to stay during our friend’s wedding! the wedding venue its self was incredible!

the cottages are called "gamplings" and have a decent bedroom with an attached toilet/bath. the cottages are comfy with adequate warm blankets. the camp fire at night is welcome part of the package. after 10:30 pm the lights are turned off and one can see beautiful night sky with milky way galaxy. we were lucky to observe around 30 odd starlink satellites traverse the sky. the staff are very courteous and the food they offer is very tasty. highly recommended for travellers.

the crew on the boat deserve 10 stars. i couldn’t be more grateful to everyone we had on the ship. from the tour director james, dive guides jamie, ryan, taku, hosts michelle, fiona, chef andrea, captain owen, everything was executed perfectly. the room was comfortable. the dive was well planned out. i loved the guides try to push you little but very safety conscious. food is amazing! we had amazing stay and dives with them and i strongly recommend it to everyone. i do think their office could improve a little on their knowledge of the boat because they have give some wrong info. the criterion theatre is a historic and architecturally stunning theatre located in the heart of london's west end, on piccadilly circus. it's known for its intimate atmosphere and its long history of hosting acclaimed productions. opened in 1874, it's one of the oldest continuously running theatres in the west end. the theatre is entirely underground and features a beautiful neo-byzantine interior with ornate tiling and marble. this creates a distinctive and intimate setting. over its long history, the criterion has hosted a wide range of plays, musicals, and other performances. situated on piccadilly circus, it's surrounded by other theatres, restaurants, and attractions, making it easily accessible. in summary, the criterion theatre is a jewel of the west end, offering a unique and intimate theatrical experience in a stunning historic setting. its prime location on piccadilly circus and its reputation for hosting quality productions make it a popular choice for theatregoers.

the dive center here is world-class — professional, well-equipped, and located in one of the most spectacular marine environments on the planet. this is the main reason to come, and it delivers. the setting is breathtaking, and the excursions offer unforgettable experiences. the resort itself is basic but functional. it’s more of a dive camp than a true resort, and that’s fine — as long as you know what to expect. there’s no luxury, no curated design, and no pretense of offering it. beds are comfortable, everything works, and the natural surroundings are the real draw. however, the deeper you look, the more unsettling the experience becomes. the staff are kind, hardworking, and the heart of the operation — yet their living conditions are extremely poor. after seeing the remote, trash-filled campsite they walk to and from multiple times a day, often via an unsafe trail over rocks and hills, it fundamentally changes your experience on the island. it’s hard to enjoy your stay knowing that those making it possible live in such undignified conditions. unfortunately, the management does not appear to have experience in hospitality or people care. the food is a consistent low point: small portions, outdated menus, and many items permanently “out of stock.” after a day of three dives, you need nourishing meals — not meals that leave you hungry. the overall service lacks warmth, energy, and proper oversight. after we left, we also heard reports of guests and staff getting sick from the food — which is alarming. this resort has incredible potential, and it’s clear it may have once lived up to that. today, the diving still shines — but the human and service elements are far behind. until the new owners invest in proper staff housing, trained kitchen staff, and real hospitality management, the imbalance between what this place could be and what it is will continue to grow — and that’s a real shame.

the dive center is located in and adjacent to a luxury hotel, the dubrovnik palace. i chose to stay at the hotel, because of the convenience. you don't have to, and many choose to stay elsewhere. but yeah it's *very* convenient to stay here if you want to dive with blue planet. my room was up one floor from the dive center. showering to warm up between dives (or getting into the hot tub, or going to the sauna) was a breeze. nitrox is available by special request, and if you are here for a series of dives i recommend that you take advantage. repetitive dives do cause a buildup of nitrogen, and this can sneak up on people, especially for those who like me don't dive as frequently as they want to. the house reef is endlessly fascinating. many octopus, and cuttlefish (see my youtube channel, rob corless). as you will see in those videos you can also arrange for night dives. i was here in april when the water was around 15 degrees c which some people think is cold. but it's much warmer here than at home so i had no complaints: merino base layer, rashie, and they gave me a 5.3mm wetsuit with integrated hood, and i was fine even without gloves. they have beautiful 15l steel tanks which mean that even for a large guts-for-air man like me every dive was about an hour long. i almost *never* get the chance to come up with 80bar of air after an hour's dive (avg depth 8m on that one). going to get me a tank like that. equipment is well-used: don't expect it to be pristine. they have lots, though, so if you get a piece that doesn't look right, they can exchange it quickly. staff (maro, andrea, vlaho, marko, michael, and bartok) are cheerful, professional, and hard-working. i dove with maro, andrea, and vlaho. andrea is wonderfully charming and professional and has extraordinary octopus-finding skills (she guided the night dive i took the videos on) and maro is also charming in a different way and *very* experienced. an excellent buddy! (divemaster, really, but it felt like he was my buddy). vlaho is much younger but similarly professional and competent. bartok was *always* hard at work supporting all of us, and instructing younger divers, and really never took a break: go go go every moment. excellent mixing of nitrox, too. i really hope that i get the chance to come back.

the dive shop was clean, organized and had gear in good condition. we made our booking online a month or two in advance to secure our spot but realized it was discounted when we heard a passerby walk in to inquire. regardless it was still a good deal for the price with all equipment included, lunch plus some gopro photos taken for you. don’t expect quality photos but it’s easier to dive and really enjoy the surroundings than having to see everything through a camera lens. what made this group stand apart from many was that the agents didn’t pressure you to buy and nor did the dive master close the tour with the same verbiage about tips etc. we happily gave tips regardless since the service and support was so good 😊 the gear was clean and we got fitted the day before to ensure we were ready for the dive the next day. they even had enough small size booties (size 5) which i often have issues in other locations where things are slightly too big. they had xs dives suits on hand and all their neoprenes were 5mm which i am also super grateful for - i often come out shivering by the end of an hours dive. this place was well equipped. the easiest dive was to isla floreana and that’s already 1.5+ hours boat ride out but luckily the boat itself is also equipped with a washroom and padding on the benches. the dives were easy and had lots to see under water including some white tip sharks, turtles, a giant marbled ray and a galapagos seahorse! byron m. is a patient dive teacher and really worked with my family to ensure a safe and enjoyable dive. would recommend this place for future visitors! also their website is super easy to navigate and they are very responsive

the dolomites are, without exaggeration, one of the most beautiful places i’ve ever seen in my life. it’s as if each mountain, valley and village had been drawn by hand. each curve of the road reveals a new scenario and they all seem to come out of a postcard. the combination of dramatic peaks, charming villages, crystal clear lakes and flowery fields creates a surreal landscape. one day you are climbing a trail to seceda, the next you are diving your feet in lake braies, and at night dining in a chalet overlooking the pink peaks by sunset. pure magic. although many areas require a car to explore more freely, public transport works well in larger cities and the structure is excellent, even for those who do not speak italian. i felt security, welcome and organisation all the time.

the dried seafood market offers a diverse range of products, including dried high quality fruits like pistachios, walnuts, dates, honey and dried seafood products. this is managed by experienced elderly individuals, the market exudes a traditional charm. communication might require a translator due to the vendors' limited understanding of english. while the quality remains high, it's notable that prices have seen a slight increase over the past two years. overall, the market provides a unique and nostalgic shopping experience for those seeking premium dried goods.

the drinks are good as i remember. the nachos have changed. i remember liking them when i first tried it last year. the vibe was still good though plus the dj was really good. but the nachos are not the same. 🥲

the drive to ardvreck castle offers spectacular views of beautiful mountains scenery... plenty of wild deer so drive safely at night. it's a shame the castle is a ruin but is still worth visiting due to its location on the loch and waterfall that adjacent. plenty of parking near by
the drive to the parking area is challenging, only one car can pass through. the oreum is quite tall, could view probably 40% of jeju island.

the dubai desert safari is a packed interesting experience. thrilling dune bashing:expert drivers navigating 4x4 vehicles through towering sand dunes. stunning desert vistas and sunsets. you get a cultural immersion with camel rides, belly dancing and fire dancing, and traditional arabic dinner. the downside is that some desert camps can feel crowded, detracting from the experience. the desert safari is a unique experience, offering a blend of adventure, culture, and natural beauty.

the dubai fountain show was absolutely spectacular! set against the backdrop of the burj khalifa and the dubai mall, the combination of water, music, and lights created a magical experience. the choreography is perfectly timed and each show feels unique. it's free to watch and runs multiple times in the evening, which makes it super convenient. i recommend arriving a bit early to get a good spot near the waterfront. truly one of the highlights of my dubai trip - a must-see for all visitors

the dubai fountain, located at the base of the burj khalifa, is the world's largest choreographed fountain system and a must-see attraction. it's a free and spectacular display that combines water, light, and music in a breathtaking show. the shows run every 30 minutes from 6 pm to 11 pm daily. during each five-minute performance, water jets shoot up to 140 meters high, dancing to a variety of musical tracks. while the main viewing area is free and offers a great perspective, for a closer look, you can pay for a ticket to the dubai fountain boardwalk or take a traditional "abra" boat ride on the lake. the best time to visit is in the evening when the thousands of lights illuminate the water, creating a truly magical atmosphere against the backdrop of the city lights. the dubai fountain is a remarkable display of art and technology that perfectly captures the city's innovative spirit.

the dubai mall is the largest shopping mall in dubai and also considered the largest mall in the world. everything about this mall is in the superlatives. starting with the beauty and elegance, the incredible size, the number of stores and restaurants, the number of visitors per year and more. a jewel of a mall! the mall is part of the downtown complex called downtown dubai that is next to and serves as the entrance to the burj khalifa. the mall includes over 1,200 shops. it also has 22 cinema screens and over 100 restaurants and cafes. the dubai aquarium and underwater zoo is part of the mall. another very nice future of the mall is the inside huge waterfall fountain with statures of divers jumping. the mall has over 14,000 parking spaces. visiting the dubai mall is an absolute must, as it serves also as the entrance to the burj khalifa. you can spend hours just strolling around and enjoying the more than thousand stores. to really appreciate and enjoy this wonder i would recommend you to invest at least a full day as part of your trip to dubai.

the dubai outlet village is a serene and lovely destination. the stone buildings and general ambiance give it an "out of the city" feel, it's a welcome respite from the typical dubai malls. there's ample parking, and the choice of brands is wonderful for those seeking a tranquil shopping experience.
the dubrovnik clock tower is a beautiful historic landmark at the end of stradun, adding charm to the old town’s skyline.

the dubrovnik fortress, part of the city’s historic walls, is a must-see for visitors. its towering stone structures offer a glimpse into medieval defense and a stunning view of dubrovnik’s iconic red rooftops and the adriatic sea. walking the walls, you’ll see preserved forts, gates, and bastions, each telling a story of the city’s resilience. the fortress area can get crowded, especially in peak season, but the panoramic views and historical ambiance make it an unforgettable experience for history and photography enthusiasts alike.

the dunes are massive and make a humming sound when the wind blows—locals call it the “singing sands.” climbing to the top is tough but worth it for the amazing view. the area also has a small green oasis nearby. getting there, the road is challenging, but the trip is totally worth it. a must-see if you’re visiting umnugovi!

the dylan scott concert was amazing on saturday. he is one of the most underrated performers in country music. let's keep it that way so we can afford good tickets! blew the jelly roll concert in ottawa out of the water easily for at least 1/4 of the price. great small venue for concerts as well.

the e sea diver sunset cruise was a great friday night experience with my daughter! it’s easy to find right on ala moana blvd with lots of parking. this was a pleasant way to enjoy the ocean, take in the scenery, and appreciate the fireworks. they provide lots of snacks and drinks. you can even bring your own food and beverages if you like. great, attentive staff - mahalo to isaiah, clint, riley, and jim! this is a must for small or large groups, and i encourage more kama’aina to check this out!

the east mebon temple is a stunning 10th-century hindu temple dedicated to shiva, built by king rajendravarman. located on an artificial island in the now-dry east baray reservoir, this temple offers a unique blend of history and architecture. what i loved: - stunning architecture – the temple features impressive brick and laterite towers, intricate carvings, and well-preserved elephant statues at each corner. - less crowded – unlike angkor wat or bayon, east mebon is quieter, allowing for a peaceful exploration. things to note: 🔸 the temple is part of the angkor pass (included in the 1-day, 3-day, or 7-day ticket). 🔸 some structures are weathered, but the grandeur of its design still shines through. 🔸 best visited as part of the "grand circuit" tour, along with pre rup and ta som. final thoughts: if you love history and want to explore beyond the main angkor temples, east mebon is a must-visit. its serene atmosphere and beautiful ruins make it a rewarding stop! highly recommended! 👍

the easterly wing is like a traditional viennese café, while the westerly resembles more a modern day bar and in-between one finds a cool little book store. we liked this atmosphere a lot, drinks and apple strudel were good, service a bit slow. outstanding selection of newspapers and weekly magazines.

the ecotourism boardwalk of the inner bay of puno on lake titicaca extends from avenida floral, height of the front of the university city of the national university of the altiplano, winds along the shore of the lake to the puno dock, then extends following that line passing the interdepartmental and zonal terminal of puno, to the óvalo salcedo (where it arrives with the name avenida bicentenario), running through that entire stretch, allowing you to see the city of puno to one side. and on the other the majestic lake titicaca, and the latter will not be possible over time because from the height of the isla de los enamorados (where the oxidation lagoon operates) towards the óvalo salcedo and the panamericana sur, invasions are emerging towards the side that faces the shore of the lake.

the edge is one of the most impressive observatories in new york—and for me, the best viewing spot in the city. the angled glass walls provide breathtaking, completely unobstructed views, making you feel like you're floating above manhattan. there's also a small glass floor that gives you a thrilling look straight down, adding to the excitement. if you're up for a real adrenaline rush, there's an optional experience where you’re harnessed and suspended outside the building. it’s intense, but unforgettable! there are also snack bars where you can relax and take in the views. a few helpful tips: the edge is included in the new york pass, so if you’re planning to visit more attractions, the pass is a smart investment. i highly recommend visiting at sunset and staying until nightfall—the transition from golden hour to city lights is truly magical. just keep in mind that sunset visits often come with an extra fee, even with a pass. also, it can get extremely windy up there, so bring a jacket! even with a reserved time slot, expect a bit of a wait—but it’s absolutely worth it. the edge offers an unforgettable experience and a unique perspective of the new york skyline.

the edinburgh castle was majestic, gorgeous, breath taking! every stone told a story and just glancing, gazing ,staring , soaking up the years of history and culture was worth every penny. make sure to do a small tour, because if you do a large tour you can’t go inside until your tour is done . also don’t overbook ( make sure to leave time after your tour if it’s like ours( we had 26 people in our tour , so we had to listen to our guide the entire time versus go inside and get a feel for ourselves. because we booked a tour of the whisky experience shortly after our tour, which didn’t leave us a lot of time to really soak every bit from the inside of the castle. the out side of the castle was so tremendously mesmerizing the tour with angus was still great. angus our tour guide was hilariously funny!! angus loved baseball and was thick in its history and knowledge, so honestly it was amazing to come all the way to edinburgh, and still feel like i was standing next to my best friends talking sports! coolest guide that i have talked with on a tour!

the el nido go tour! 🙏🏻 the best boat: comfortable, very spacious, double-decker with a canopy, comfortable bean bags, and nets. amazing crew: always attentive to your needs, very kind and friendly people. there was live music around lunchtime. they also have a big speaker, and we had a dj for the day playing chill music. catering: good traditional filipino food and drinks included (safe mineral water and ice). experience: we left a bit later than the normal tours and visited multiple amazing spots in el nido while there were no crowds! that was perfect, and we enjoyed the beach and snorkeling without the crowds. and the most important thing: the vibes! this is one of the only tours that lets you watch the sunset, which was stunning! thanks again, guys, for the experience!

the el yunque rainforest tour was an unforgettable adventure! julian, our tour guide, and luis, our driver, were both awesome from start to finish. they kept the energy high with their great sense of humor and made the whole experience feel fun and relaxed. julian shared so many interesting facts about the rainforest and made learning about the area super engaging. luis was just as great, and together they made an incredible team. they also went above and beyond taking tons of pictures for us, which i really appreciated. it let us stay in the moment without worrying about missing memories. highly recommend this tour if you’re visiting puerto rico!

the elephant house is apparently one of the largest in japan. what's great is that you can see the elephants from all sorts of angles even indoors. there's also a pool, so it would be impressive to see the elephants jump in. they've successfully bred asian elephants, and the baby elephant, tao, is adorable.

the elevation gain is challenging. there are views of the falls and half dome that i had assumed were the product of photo manipulation, but those pictures are real, and you can't truly experience yosemite without going up this trail.

the elim dune is easy to find, as you can see it from the sesriem gate, and it is just a short drive (about 5 km) away. the road to the dune is mostly gravel and overall it was in an average condition, however there were some bad parts here and there. if you take it slow through these parts it isn't too bad and it isn't necessary to have a 4x4 vehicle to visit the dune. en-route, as well as at the dune, you will have endless photo opportunities and we were lucky enough to even see some ostriches dashing across the road rounding out our experience. at the dune's parking area there are some trees spread around, giving some respite from the heat, and although i can't comment on it's condition, there was a long drop (pit) toilet available as well. overall, with it's close proximity to the main gate, i definitely think the dune is worth a visit, even just for a quick one to see it up close.

the ellis island museum tells a powerful and emotional story about america’s immigrant history. it has personal stories, photos, and artifacts that make the past come alive. standing in the great hall where millions passed through is very moving. it’s a must-see for anyone interested in history. i parked safely at liberty state park, which made getting there easy.

the embalmed body of the great ho chi minh is preserved and displayed here, and visiting the mausoleum is truly a moving experience. it reminded me of my visit to lenin’s mausoleum in moscow years ago — the setup and atmosphere are quite similar, filled with respect and solemnity. as it was a weekend, the place was very crowded, and the heat made the wait a bit challenging. still, it was worth every moment to witness such an important piece of vietnamese history. entry is free, but there are strict rules in place to maintain the sanctity of the site. photography and videography are strictly prohibited inside the mausoleum. visitors must dress modestly — clothing that reveals shoulders or knees is not allowed. silence and respectful behavior are expected throughout the visit. this is not just a tourist spot but a place of deep national pride for vietnam. if you’re in hanoi, don’t miss the opportunity to pay your respects to the man who played a pivotal role in the country’s independence.

the exhibition seeing sound, hearing time was amazing and totally used the space well. likely changes depending on the popularity of the exhibition but we had to wait about 1.5 hours to see it since we did not purchase a ticket. it's a large space, with a really beautifully designed exterior and interior. both the art and the architecture were totally worth seeing. highly recommend checking it out if you like the current exhibition

the experience of a lifetime. do yourself a favor and don’t miss out on this place! when planning our trip to thailand, we knew we wanted an elephant experience but wanted it to be the most ethical one. it is clear how much they love elephants at this place. we did the one hour feed experience. we started with a history lesson inside, washed our hands, picked out bananas, and were given a lesson on how to feed the elephants. our family was the first of the day so we basically had a private session. beware of fire ants! no one had issues but me, but just watch where you step :) the elephants really are gentle giants. we had a blast feeding them. everyone in our crew, all the way from 2-61 years old, loved this experience. and minty (like minty fresh) our guide was a caretaker, comedian, guide, and photographer all in one. the pictures she took for us were some of our best. she was even singing baby shark to get our niece to smile. this was a perfect experience, probably one of the best of our whole trip.

the experience on dhow cruise was amazing,i was there with my family for my daughter’s birthday. baljeet singh and imran service and hospitality were so nice. one suggestion for birthday parties…there should be a small separate portion for birthday parties with decorations so that people make their birthday parties memorable. in dinner…there should be addition of mutton. overall the food was amazing.

the experience through this trail was very nice. it's not too easy, but also not too hard. the views were very nice and breathtaking. it was a fairly long hike with a good amount of uphill hiking that will make your legs tired. there is a little rest area where you can sit down and rest/eat before continuing on the hike. i highly recommend packing water, sunscreen, a small towel, and extra clothing to change afterward. you can also add in a bit of food since you will need the energy. also, wear covered shoes as a good amount of the hike consists of dirt, rocks, and mud. since it is not as dangerous compared to other hikes, i can say that children are capable of pulling through the hike with adult supervision. nevertheless, i would just advise you to be cautious and be aware of your surroundings. please read and listen to the signs posted throughout the hike. do not venture too far off the intended trail. it isn't that hard to do that. in addition, there are many points on the hike where i had to stop and take pictures. i was enamored by my surroundings and the feeling of being in nature. overall, i really recommend this hike to people.

the experience to come and visit one of the seven wonders if the old world, equals no site i have ever visited before. to study the alignment, algebra, mathematics, astronomy, sound resonance, civil engineering is absolutely amazing for no one offers an explanation as to how they were built to reach such mathematic precision. to see this technology put to work and admire all these constructions to astronomical perfection is too much to grasp on a single visit. it sure does help to watch graham hancock''e netflix series and afterwards his videos on youtube to prepare before coming to this site. it is highly recommend to do a bit of research before coming down here to really admire such engineering works and value where you are located in this planet. top kudos for the guides who bust their chops to explain each and every single one of the sites and meanings. if coming down here, be prepare to bring sun blocker, a brim hat, a collapsible umbrella ☔🏖️ with you...and walk on the premises some 5 km2...it will be an excersice. for the wheelchair people, bring assistance for many parts will be needed to walk you in backwards . there is a lot of parts in gravel and not levelled terrain. enjoy your experience, open your mind to the possibilities.

the fee is about 25 pesos to enter. i really liked all the animals, it was fun exploring and studying them. but i hate to say that the facility is being cruel to them. instead of a sanctuary and a facility to protect these crocodiles, they are mostly captured and taken here basically as a prison. the crocodiles aren't taken here because they are endangered, they were taken to this facility as a "punishment". most of these crocodiles spend their years at the facility where they didn't release them back to the wild. with all due respect, most the crocodiles does have kill counts and records of them killing and eating people, specifically fishermen. the young crocodiles are bred and taken away, instead of releasing them to the wild they export it into different products. it's sad to see them tightly cramped into a small box which barely has any space. that includes the larger crocodiles that were kept in tiny concrete spaces which look quite uncomfortable. the staff are really quite friendly although the facility is old, runned-down and the crocodiles aren't taken care enough. these can lead them to distress and it is quite sad and cruel to see these animals kept in captivity for accidently attacking humans. the last part is, the last auction where you can hold a baby crocodile and take a picture with it. it seems cool at first but it gets dark and cruel instantly. the baby crocodile's mouths are shut tight and they are kept in tiny cramped corners. visitors are quite noisy and eager to touch them which is sad because crocodiles are sensitive to loud sound and can distress them. i noticed how the baby crocodiles always move around aggressively and tries to escape from the crowd. i support the staff, but the facility i really dislike. please don't support any of the business and the stuff they are doing to crocodiles. they are endangered species and should not be toyed and used for products and other commercial uses.

the ferocious animals hall (ferocious animal hall) is the park's dedicated area dedicated to exhibiting wild animals. it features action displays, allowing visitors to observe the animals' natural behaviors up close. lions, tigers, leopards, and other animals are housed here. the lion triplets born in 2022 are particularly eye-catching and now fully grown, displaying their lively demeanor. tigers often play or run in the pool, while leopards occasionally nap in high rock caves, showcasing their wild charm. the hall's design simulates a natural habitat, and glass windows and observation areas allow visitors to safely observe the animals' movements and subtle movements.

the fez tanneries (also known as the chouara tannery) are one of the most iconic and historic sites in fez, morocco, and are renowned for their traditional leather production methods, which have remained largely unchanged since medieval times. key facts: location: fez el-bali (the old medina of fez), morocco. established: at least since the 11th century. famous tannery: chouara tannery is the largest and most famous among several in fez. how it works: 1. soaking: animal hides (usually from cows, sheep, goats, and camels) are first soaked in a mixture of water, limestone, and pigeon droppings to loosen hair and soften the hides. 2. cleaning: workers then manually scrape off hair and fat. 3. dyeing: the cleaned hides are soaked in stone vats filled with natural dyes made from plants and minerals (e.g., poppy for red, saffron for yellow, indigo for blue). 4. drying: after dyeing, the hides are laid out on rooftops or open air to dry. unique aspects: smell: the process produces a strong, pungent odor. visitors are often given mint leaves to mask the smell. handcrafted: almost all processes are manual, showcasing centuries-old craftsmanship. tourism: popular tourist attraction—visitors usually observe the tannery from nearby terraces overlooking the dyeing pits.

the finca de los monos, an old colonial mansion in havana, has a fascinating history. built at the beginning of the 20th century, it was home to a wealthy family who transformed their gardens into a small exotic refuge, where they raised monkeys and other animals. over time, the farm became a recreational space, ideal for those seeking a unique experience in contact with nature. today, the finca de los monos in havana is a recreational park and natural space, focused on outdoor activities and family recreation. although it retains the name that alludes to its past as a refuge for monkeys and exotic animals, it does not currently house these animals. it is a popular place among locals to enjoy nature, go for walks and organize social or cultural activities in a quiet environment surrounded by vegetation.

the flower dome at gardens by the bay is a must-visit spot in singapore, especially for anyone who loves plants, flowers, or beautifully designed indoor spaces. it’s one of the largest glass greenhouses in the world, and stepping inside feels like entering a magical floral wonderland. the temperature inside is cool and comfortable, which is a refreshing break from singapore’s humid weather. the dome houses plants and flowers from various regions around the world, including mediterranean, south african, and australian landscapes. it’s fascinating to see so many rare and exotic plants all under one roof. one of the things i loved most was how each section is thoughtfully curated, with themed gardens, seasonal floral displays, and artistic landscaping. there were beautiful tulips during my visit, and the entire place smelled amazing. it’s also a great spot for photography—there are countless vibrant colors and creative arrangements to capture. everything is well-maintained, and the pathways make it easy to explore at a relaxed pace. whether you’re a plant lover or just looking for a peaceful, photogenic place to visit, flower dome delivers both beauty and serenity. i highly recommend visiting together with the cloud forest if you have time—they’re right next to each other and offer totally different but equally breathtaking experiences.
