the lodge is situated on top of a hill. the view from the rooms are fabulous. the lodge seems to have carved out a hill. the food is good with a wide choice. the staff is very polite. the rooms are a bit small but made entirely of wood. the bar is decorated beautifully.

the lodge is well situated in the picturesque okavango delta. there is plenty of game to see and the activities are great. we enjoyed the river safari as well as the canoeing, along with the regular safaris. it is a huge pity, though, that the camp is poorly run, the management does not seem to have a handle on things, the staff is sullen and distant, rather than friendly. communication was very poor, not only among the staff, but also between the staff and the guests. our guide was very knowledgeable, but a rude and arrogant man, which really affected our stay. the buffet style meals for such a small group of people don't make sense; reheated toasts for breakfast, hard and dry meat and fish for dinner, which has been too long on the buffet. the camp is not cheap and for them to serve meals like this - quite inedible- seems very cheap. in spite of the interesting activities, we would never visit a camp run by kwando safaris again.

the lodge was cozy and the staff were so welcoming. when we arrived the staff welcomed us with a delicious chacutterie board and the warmth of a roaring fire. the lodge offers several vintage games and puzzles and two guitars. the meals were classic comfort food and very delicious! we had a great time and were so grateful for the incredible the lodge staff.
the lombach is beautiful for walking. you can walk to lake thun. it is ideal for families with children, but also ideal for dogs. the lombach is also a wonderful way to cool off in summer.

the london eye delivers spectacular 360-degree views across london's skyline. the 30-minute rotation is perfectly paced, allowing ample time to spot landmarks like big ben, tower bridge, and st. paul's cathedral. while tickets are expensive and queues can be lengthy during peak times, the experience remains magical. book advance tickets to skip lines. the spacious glass pods accommodate groups comfortably. essential london attraction despite the cost.

the london eye is an excellent way to take in the city. you can see for miles from the top of the eye. moving at a speed of 0.6 mph, the pods rotate around the wheel as it slowly turns giving you a smooth ride. the transition from hanging beneath the giant wheel to being on top of as you gently ascend to a height of 394 feet is so peaceful that it doesn't feel like you are moving as the eye turns. you need a ticket to ride this landmark attraction and can choose a time to board the eye. the cost of admission is worth the price as you take in the spectacular sites of london. be sure to book your time early because the queues for tickets can be long.

the london eye is definitely worth the experience – the views over the city are fantastic and the whole process from ticketing to boarding was smooth and well organized. the staff were friendly and helpful, which made everything run easily. the only downside: the windows in our capsule weren’t really clean, which made taking good photos a bit tricky. otherwise, it was a great ride and something i’d recommend to anyone visiting london.
the lookout spectacular view before or end of marang trail faber side. no merlion here but you can go through the vivo city by marang trail.
the loop is nice with lots of geysers and pools. we were there late in the season so there were no estimated times on next eruption. pretty pool and colors.
the love for nature, the tranquility and the beautiful scenery made this first visit to interlaken an unforgettable memory. this is a place your heart will love and want to return to again and again.

the lunch tour was decent on a nice summer day. you get to have a unique view of all the sites without walking too much and having a 4 star meal to go with it. we got a bottle of champagne to start and the service was top notch. i would recommend this tour for first timers in paris. quality to value ratio is more than fair. will come back for the dinner cruise on our next visit!
the lungs of paris. massive park on the west edge of the city. something for everyone, sometimes too much. great to have a picnic and a bottle of wine.

the lutheran church of the redeemer is the second protestant church in jerusalem (the first being christ church near jaffa gate). it is a property of the evangelical jerusalem foundation, one of the three foundations of the evangelical church in germany in the holy land. inside the bell tower of the church of the redeemer, a circular staircase of 178 steps offers panoramic views of jerusalem from 40 metres up. it is the home to congregations that worship in arabic, german, danish and english.

the maasai mara had long been a dream destination for me, a place firmly etched on my bucket list. choosing where to stay was a significant decision, one that would shape the quality of my experience. after extensive research and conversations with friends based in nairobi, i ultimately settled on the mara siria camp. it turned out to be the perfect choice, surpassing all my expectations. my time at the mara siria camp was nothing short of extraordinary. the tents were impeccably clean and comfortable, offering a cozy retreat amidst the wilderness. the location boasted awe-inspiring vistas that left me speechless, while the attentive staff ensured that every aspect of my stay was catered to with utmost care. what truly set mara siria apart was the warmth and hospitality of its people. their genuine smiles and eagerness to assist made me feel right at home from the moment i arrived. their dedication to every detail and their unwavering focus on ensuring the satisfaction of every visitor was truly commendable. to the incredible mara siria crew, i extend my heartfelt gratitude for making my stay truly unforgettable. i look forward to returning soon for another remarkable experience. until then, thank you for everything. we'll reunite again very soon.
the magnetic hill mysteriously pulls/pushes heavy vehicles and any stationery object into movement. good place to visit. very windy! has atv rides nearby abd some local shops to eat!

the magnificent entrance to a very special place to me, the cne. it was opened the year my granddad was born, on my mum's birthday, and my family has gone to the cne every year since 1958. i always get a thrill of nostalgia and happiness when i'm down around here.

the main attraction of wat arun is the central prang, with other prangs/pagodas around it. it's a very unique and detailed structure. if you look close enough, you can see each piece of porcelain/other elements. they don't always match, but somehow they make a cohesive and colorful mosaic. climbing it can be quite an exercise, but it's worth it. the visitors have an option to dress up in traditional thai clothes and use a professional photographer to take one of the kind picture (for a price of course). i'm not gonna lie, the garments looked stunning and exactly like those in historical lakorns. i was tempted to try them on, but it would take too much time and it was a really hot day. speaking of which, there are stalls near the temple with foods and refreshments, and it was lovely to drink coconut water in such a heat. i arrived at and departed from wat arun by boat, which is a great way to do a bit of sightseeing by itself.

the main bot of this complex is located on a hill, from where a beautiful view of the city opens. in addition to white, gold predominates in the colors of the building. at the entrance to it there are large, majestic dragons (nagas), green and gold - guards of the altar. nearby there is a tower that you can climb and look at the territory from above. the complex is located near a busy road, but in a recessed part, which is why: the noise from cars here does not create any discomfort and it is quite comfortable to be here. this temple is almost invisible from the road, and those people who know about it come here. this is not a must-see place. being nearby, you can visit it to look at buddhist buildings, a beautiful panorama of the city and take interesting photos. full information with video and easy navigation - in the 👉 phuketon application

the main entrance gorge into the ancient city petra. it's a narrow winding path that is 1 kilometer in length leading up to the treasury building. make sure to bring a head covering and sunscreen especially during the summer months. be also wary of stray dogs wandering around.

the main gate to the historic fatimid cairo. very nice to see.
the main street in the old town. paved with limestone slabs so polished that they shine. shops, restaurants, hotels on both sides. indescribable crowd. the old town is wonderful, stradun as well!

the majestic meeting place between the zanskar and indus rivers. about 45kms from leh city on the kargil highway. the road is again beautiful like all highways around leh. sweeping bends and smooth surfaces. you can spot the sangam from the road as well and it's well worth it to take the detour down to the actual meeting point.

the mall has most of the leading brands ( watches, clothes, jewelry, perfumes, personal effects) that one would look for while going luxury shopping. truly a one stop shop for luxury shopping. simply a window shopping experience in this place is a delight. its a huge mall with almost 4 stories offering a luxury overdose. most of the shops have a fair price policy where a few shops were offering some good discounts. the mall is right next to the lake so its a pleasant walk in case one plans to tour the lake.

the mall is a premier shopping destination in seoul that perfectly blends international flair with local charm. featuring over 110 brands, it showcases a mix of global favorites like hollister, h&m, uniqlo, and zara, alongside popular korean labels. the modern shopfronts create an immersive and stylish shopping experience. beyond fashion, the mall offers a variety of options, including accessories, sportswear, beauty products, diverse restaurants, a cgv cinema, and the youngpoong bookstore. it’s a one stop destination for shopping, dining, and entertainment in seoul!

the mall is connected to swissotel al ghurair and swissotel living al ghurai. i recently visited al ghurair centre in deira and had a productive experience. the mall offers a variety of shopping options, from fashion to electronics, making it a convenient destination for all my needs. i started by checking out some gadgets at emax, then proceeded to daiso to purchase a few items. the convenience of having a money transfer service on-site made sending money a breeze. the mall's welcoming atmosphere and diverse offerings truly made my visit enjoyable. highly recommended for anyone looking to shop, dine, and take care of errands in one place! nearest metro station is union metro station. 3 minutes walk. exit 2

the mall is good. the library view another hyped up place from social media which looks better on your phone than in person. speaking of which it suffers from over tourism because of said social media.

the mall is located opposite burj al arab is less rush than other malls . the location is easily accessible. they have selected restaurants, hypermarket and other retail shops and cafe like costa coffee. paid parking is available. unfortunately there is no food court or any seating areas.

the mall is nice but nothing special other than the bookstore. it has all the stores you would expect for a mid range price shopping mall. there is a little track between the malls. some ok to good eating spots. but for great food try the intercontinental hotel which is in the same general location. the bookstore is really fun and a must do.

the mall jumeirah is a cozy and well-designed shopping destination, perfect for those looking for a relaxed shopping and dining experience. while it's not as large as other malls in dubai, it offers a variety of shops, cafes, and restaurants to explore. the ambiance is calm, making it ideal for a peaceful outing. parking is convenient, and the location is easily accessible. it's a great spot for casual visits, especially if you're looking to enjoy a meal at places like nawab restaurant. definitely worth checking out!

the man mo temple in sheung wan, hong kong, is dedicated to the god of literature, man cheong, and the god of war, kwan tai. from the outside, it looks like a historic chinese temple, and once you step inside, there’s a unique calm atmosphere. one of the most striking features is the spiral incense coils hanging from the ceiling, slowly releasing smoke and creating a mystical vibe. when visiting, i found that you can actually get three incense sticks for free to offer. the temple was smaller than i expected, and you can see everything in about 30 minutes. it’s easy to reach and makes for a nice stop in between sightseeing. just note that there isn’t any air conditioning, so on hot days it does get warm inside as well. it’s a popular spot for students to pray for success in exams or academic achievements, and a great place to experience a piece of traditional hong kong culture.

the management is of another era. quality of fresh produce is below average. ridiculous amount of time waiting in queues. as if they live forever...! there is almost always a queue of people at the tills, the checkout process is depressingly slow and the fact that there could be lots of people in queue does not seem to bother the staff.

the manhattan skyline from the boat returning from the statue of liberty is simply breathtaking. the glittering lights and towering skyscrapers create a magical panorama, offering a stunning view of new york city.

the map is inaccurate!! we are pretty avid hikers and i can say without a doubt the map is inaccurate. i recommend using a hiking app along with the map. the markers and map also do not coordinate well. we saw some cool ants and birds but nothing else. beautiful forest with nice paths. some areas very challenging. drive to the top to see the volcano!!

the mara triangle is a very interesting plateau of 510 sq. kilometers, about one third of masai mara national reserve. this is the area where the great migration takes place. you will also see in normal time herds of animals - wildbeests, zebras, buffalos. antilopes, giraffes... you are guaranteed to see animals in any period of the year and this, 5 minutes after you have passed the oloololo gate.

the marina bay sands observation deck offers a spectacular, unobstructed view of singapore’s skyline — absolutely worth seeing at least once. the crowd is well-controlled, so it doesn’t feel overwhelming, and the elevator ride up is impressively fast. that said, the deck itself is relatively small, especially considering the size of the boat-shaped top of the hotel. it would have been nice to explore more of that space. also, there aren’t many facilities or amenities available on the deck — a few seating areas, limited shade, and not much else besides the view. for the high ticket price, that’s a bit disappointing. overall, it’s a great experience for the breathtaking views, but loses a star for the lack of facilities and the price-to-value ratio.

the marina is ok if you wanna spend 1 or 2 nights there , the bathrooms are not so nice but for 2 nights absolutely enough, about the crew of the marina …i can say some people are really motivated to work and to help you and some not ..we had part of both …. honestly i will not choose this marina again .

the marine diversity absolutely takes your breath away, like no other in the world. i hope everyone will carry on improving the wildlife and corals. this "gem" will get more and more happy creatures. we really appreciated seeing u guys. 🩵

the maritime museum of barcelona was a true discovery for me. i'm writing this review more than a year after visiting, but the impression it left still resonates. maybe it's because i was born in a city by the sea, where ships, ports, and sailing were always part of the landscape. the exhibition was remarkable — rich with detailed ship models, ranging from historic wooden vessels to modern ones. it also featured interactive video displays and impressive large-scale exhibits, including a full-size replica of the royal galley, which left a lasting impact. i recommend setting aside at least 4–5 hours to fully enjoy the exhibition. there's also a cozy café inside and a souvenir shop, perfect for picking up something to remember barcelona by.

the market area is vast full folk tourists and local and donkeys, be alert at all times people and dont try the local free food and a guide is advised because you will get lost! on saying all that it is a fascinating look at life and worth doing at least once. been to fez lots of times overnighting on journey south and just once into the market.

the market has really bounced back since covid. plenty of options and quite the bustling market. it's a nice way to spend a weekend morning. parking can get really hectic later in the morning and early afternoon, so i go earlier and no issue finding parking. i love the variety of food vendors and it's a great way to support our local businesses.

the market, also known as soi wanit 1, is one of bangkok’s most historic and character rich markets. tucked away in the heart of chinatown, it’s a maze of narrow alleyways filled with wholesale shops offering everything from fabrics, jewelry, packaging, and toys to household goods and more. the market provides a great opportunity to explore local commerce in a truly authentic setting. its roots go back to the late 1700s, and much of that old world charm remains. with traditional shopfronts, busy storefronts, and a steady stream of local shoppers, sampheng gives a real sense of the city's trading heritage. while some areas have quieted down over the years and a number of shops have closed, the market still holds a unique atmosphere especially in the mornings when activity is at its peak. despite the decline in foot traffic, the market continues to offer excellent value. prices are very reasonable, making it especially appealing for those looking for great deals or shopping in bulk. the market may not have the modern appeal of newer shopping centers, but its blend of history, culture, and affordability makes it a worthwhile stop for anyone looking to experience a more traditional side of bangkok.

the mayan ruins of tulum, perched on a cliff overlooking the turquoise caribbean sea, are a striking blend of history and natural beauty. once a bustling port city between the 13th and 15th centuries, tulum was vital for trade in jade and turquoise. its well-preserved walls and temples, like el castillo, showcase mayan architecture and astronomy. the proximity to white sandy beaches enhances its allure, offering a stunning contrast of ancient culture and serene coastal landscapes.

the memorial itself is grand and imposing, reflecting the stature of bismarck in german history. designed by reinhold begas, the statue stands in front of the reichstag, providing a fitting backdrop that connects the memorial with germany's political history. the monument features a bronze statue of he bismarck nationaldenkmal is more than just an artistic landmark; it also serves as a reflection on germany's complex history. bismarck's policies and actions had far-reaching impacts, some of which are subjects of intense debate even today. thus, the monument can evoke varied reactions, encouraging visitors to engage with the nuanced legacy of bismarck and the era he shaped. overall, the bismarck nationaldenkmal is a significant monument that offers deep insights into german history and the legacy of one of its most influential figures. it stands as both a work of art and a historical artifact, inviting contemplation and appreciation from those who visit.

the mint is one of sydney’s most fascinating and beautifully preserved architectural landmarks, especially for those with an interest in history, adaptive reuse, and thoughtful design. located along macquarie street, it’s easy to walk past without realizing just how important—and elegant—this building really is. but for anyone who appreciates architecture, the mint is a must-see. originally built in the early 1800s as part of the city’s rum hospital, the building later became a branch of the royal mint—the first of its kind outside england. today, it stands as a brilliant example of colonial georgian architecture, thoughtfully preserved and reimagined for contemporary use. the sandstone façade, timber verandahs, and classical proportions give it a sense of dignity and restraint, characteristic of early institutional architecture in australia. what makes the mint particularly special is how it has been adapted for modern use without losing its historical character. the restoration and adaptive reuse project by fjmt architects is masterful. the way new structures have been inserted—lightweight, glassy, and deliberately contrasting—highlights rather than overwhelms the original heritage elements. the new interventions are respectful and refined, allowing the old and new to speak to each other in a quiet architectural dialogue. the courtyard is a particularly lovely space where you can appreciate this blend—surrounded by historic walls, softened by landscaping, and anchored by modern pavilions. inside, the use of materials like steel, glass, and timber creates a warm and contemporary feel, while still framing and honoring the building’s past. it’s a perfect example of how architecture can preserve history while remaining relevant and useful in the present. the mint now houses the headquarters of sydney living museums and a great little café, making it both a cultural destination and a peaceful retreat in the middle of the city. for architects, designers, and anyone interested in how old buildings can be given new life, the mint is a real inspiration. it’s not just a place to look at—it’s a place to experience. highly recommended for anyone exploring sydney’s rich architectural and urban heritage.

the monastery (aka aldayr in arabic) is one of the hidden gems and less visited places in petra. it is somewhere in the middle between the start of the little petra hiking trail and the qasr albint in the ancient petra city. if you come to the monastery from the little petra hiking trail, it is a 4 km walk that is moderate in terms of difficulty. this is the easier of the 2 paths. however, if you walk from the qasr albint, it is shorter (around 3 kms), yet is an uphill of stairs. either path is served with direction signs, and with kiosks if you need to buy anything. i would recommend that you start from the little petra hiking trail, walk to the monastery, and then continue to qasr albint. one other easier option is to take a donkey ride from qasr albint to the monastery, and then return back to qasr albint walking (or another donkey ride). the monastery looks very similar to the treasury. the area is served with cafeterias and plenty of photography spots. this visit is a 1-day visit that you can combine with a little petra tour plus exploring qasr albint and some of the surrounding stops, and maybe have a lunch at one of the 2 restaurants close to qasr albint. the monastery is free to visit, but you’ll still have to buy a ticket if you are heading back to qasr albint and the ancient petra city.

the monastery of the cross (georgian: ჯვრის მონასტერი) is an orthodox monastery in jerusalem, israel. it is located in the valley of the cross. the monastery was built in the 11th century, during the reign of king bagrat iv by the georgian giorgi-prokhore of shavsheti. it is believed that the site was originally consecrated in the 4th century under the instruction of the roman emperor constantine the great, who later gave the site to the georgian king mirian iii of iberia after the conversion of his country to christianity in 327 a.d. by the 14th century, the monastery had become the center of the georgian community in jerusalem. by 1685, however, the monastery had been taken over by the greek orthodox patriarchate.

the monastery of the flagellation is an important attraction along the via dolorosa in the muslim quarter of jerusalem. this is the location where is is believed that jesus was flogged by the roman soldiers.

the monastery of the flagellation is an important attraction along the via dolorosa in the muslim quarter of jerusalem. this is the location where is is believed that jesus was flogged by the roman soldiers. opening hours are from 9-1pm and 4-6pm daily. here you can find a pleasant but small courtyard flanked by two chapels. the chapel of the condemnation is a 20th century chapel built upon the grounds of medieval period chapel. the interior is that of a small seating area with nice stained glass windows. across the courtyard is a second chapel of the flagellation, which was originally built during the crusader period and then restored by italian architect antonio barluzzi in 1929. here you can see a nice altar with an image of christ being led beside the cross. between the two chapels is a small archaeological museum called terra sancta museum. we didn't have time to visit but this might be of interest to some. they have a website online if you want to know more about what can be experienced here. overall, we found the monastery of flagellation to be a nice addition to the various attractions along via dolorosa. its worth a visit if you plan to trace the steps of jesus and visit the 14 stations along this street.

the monument to máximo gómez, made by the italian aldo gamba in 1935, is a group of sculptures dedicated to general máximo gómez- independent cuban army chief considered a dominican republic war hero. he fought in a constant and disinterested way for the independence of cuba in the conflicts of 1868 and 1895 against the spanish.

the monument to the rights of man and of the citizen is located in paris, in the champ-de-mars gardens, avenue charles-risler. commissioned by the city of paris, of which jacques chirac was mayor, it was installed in 1989 on the occasion of the bicentenary of the revolution. it is the work of architect michel jantzen, and sculptor evan thimmer. inspired by egyptian mastabas, it includes many references to revolutionary iconography. the memorial consists of several elements: - it is built on a square plan, open to an internal space with an octagonal plan, illuminated from above, and its external facades are decorated with engraved texts, various inscriptions, and twelve stones with bronze seals of the countries of the european community for the year 1989. - two obelisks, one with a triangular base, and the other with a square base of bronze, covered with an abundance of symbols and texts containing delicate details and inscriptions, including the declaration of human rights of 1789. a statue of a man wearing a toga holding several documents in his hands. - a statue of a man inviting people to read the texts inscribed on obelisks; - statue of a woman with her child wearing a hat made of newspapers.

the monument à la république is an impressive symbol of french unity and freedom. standing tall in the square, marianne’s statue is surrounded by intricate bronze sculptures. the plaza buzzes with life, making it a powerful and vibrant paris landmark.

the monument à la république was inaugurated in 1883. it was designed by the morice brothers to celebrate the values of the french republic—liberty, equality, and fraternity. the central figure is marianne, the personification of the republic, surrounded by allegorical sculptures and historical reliefs. over the years, it has become a key site for public demonstrations and national expression.

the most epic underrated hike in yosemite! best time to go is spring, but be prepared, you wil get soaked! you need water for sure, it's a 5.5 mile round the trip hike. you will go up and down on mountain so be ready for adventure. some place you will find shades and places are completely open so you will feel hot ther. if you can start early in the morning then you can avoid heat. you can carry some food so you can have something to eat at the end of the hike and next to the fall. this is a good big waterfall with a beautiful rainbow.

the most grilling trek to the top! you need to be fit to climb this majestic mountain. we started at 2 am with our driver picking us up at the villa and dropping to the summit. we were served breakfast and tea and taken to another spot to meet our guide. we started the hike around 3:45 am. first part is paved and then groups are taken on different pathways to the top. lots of gravel on the way so make sure you have good shoes. my hamstrings and calf muscle was on fire 🤣. once you reach the top every ache and pain disappears. they have a tea shop with snacks and blankets for purchase if you feel cold. the sun played hide and seek for us. we have a very cloudy view from the top. the decent took another 2 hrs and equally tough. overall an excellent trek to the top and a must do for anyone visiting bali.

the most happening river about in prague. several small / big anchored boat restaurants, lively music , amazing street food and to top it of the most beautiful views of vltava with prague castle at backdrop . it is also a place for farmer market ( very famous) , serveral other permanent / temporary exhibitions and markets.

the most incredible day!!! we booked a sup tour with adonis following his amazing reviews that we found online and wow he did not disappoint! not only was adonis a fantastic teacher for us beginners but he was full of knowledge about the island and he was also super funny, making it even more enjoyable than we could have imagined. this is what we chose to do to celebrate my 30th birthday, and it couldn’t have been better. adonis certainly made this a day to remember. a true highlight of not only our holiday but of our life’s! an experience we’ll never forget. thank you adonis!

the most incredible experience i had in tulum. my partner and i just saw the catamaran on the beach and decided to inquire about a ride out to go snorkeling. we thought it would be a nicer experience than the crowded motor boats, and the adventure far exceeded anything we could have imagined. the captain was knowledgeable, but just about the area and the wildlife but about ecology and conservation. the whole team expressed a love for the ocean and natural environment. the trip out to the reef was was just as fast as the wind could take us. our guide brought us to a private area of the reef with zero other tourists. it was quiet and peaceful and he showed us around, pointing out features and bringing us to spots where he found schools of fish. he then let us adventure on our own for quite a while before calling us back to the boat. we then sailed toward the ruins which provided an amazing view and time to just enjoy being out at sea. i would recommend this experience to anyone and everyone. if we had more time in tulum we would have for sure done it again.

the museum of the imperial fora, in the trajan's markets, is topographically and conceptually linked to the impressive urban system of the imperial fora: of caesar (46 bc), of augustus (2 bc), of the temple of peace (75 ad), of nerva (97 ad) ) and of trajan (112 and 113 ad).the area was to house warehouses, shops, and offices of the imperial administration and serve other commercial and administrative purposes. this monumental complex has buildings rising on several levels, on the slopes of the quirinale hill and on a semi-circular, towards the trajan's forum.the monument, called trajan's market on the occasion of the rediscovery between 1926 and 1934, was a multifunctional center with administrative activities at the service of the trajan's forum, built in the same period. it on 6 levels and is divided into several buildings separated by streets along the slopes of the quirinal hill, which it supports with the great hemicycle. following the occupations and transformations over time, the area underwent state-of-the-art conservation and structural restoration work between 2005 and 2007.inaugurated in the autumn of 2007, the musum of the imperial fora constitutes the first museum of ancient architecture and exhibits recompositions of scores of the architectural and sculptural decoration of the fora, obtained with original fragments, casts, and modular additions in stone, according to the museographic choice of reversibility. this finds return the “perception” of the volumes and richness of the fora and of the figurative programs, both tools of imperial propaganda.the museum occupies the buildings of the great hall and the central body and includes the great hemicycle with the section of the trajan's forum. the exhibits are presented according to a mixed communication system with traditional panels, multimedia technologies, and interactive installations, for an original approach to visiting the museum. the exhibition itinerary starts in the great hall with the introduction into the forum area and their representation through the most important finds. the visits begin in the great hall, with an introduction to the area of ​​the forums, and with the representations of the various forums, illustrating the main finds recovered from each. on the upper level, are the sections of the forum of caesar and of the memory of the ancient one and, in the central body, of the forum of augustus, the model adopted in the roman provinces.

the museum's location by the whale watching docks makes sense, especially if you consider the full-size boat outside the museum! the museum itself is small, but it has everything related to the sea! if you visit, don't forget to try on one of the raincoats and take a photo on a "real" ship. overall, it was a nice place to visit. i would prefer if the cost of admission was lower, though, but with a city card, you can get more value for your money. bonus is the free parking at the docks, although due to ongoing construction the spaces are limited.

the museum, located in the old parliament house, offers a fair collection of artifacts showcasing greece's history from the fall of constantinople in 1453 to world war ii. the museum emphasizes the greek revolution and the establishment of the modern greek state, with exhibits including weapons, manuscripts, personal belongings of historical figures, and traditional costumes from various regions. the building itself, which served as the hellenic parliament from 1875 to 1932, adds to the historical atmosphere. the museum is fair in size and worth a visit if you're interested in greek history.

the museum’s slightly dim interior creates the perfect atmosphere for each animal and species to stand out beautifully under the spotlights. the architecture is stunning, the gardens are lovely to explore, and it’s very kid-friendly overall. a perfect weekend of knowledge and discovery!

the musicianship was brilliant. enjoyable evening and do recommend. classical music, dancing/ballet and opera, collectively. do take cash as card machines are not available for the cloakroom (2€ each) or bar. seating is generally good but bare in mind as it's not a formal event, you can get the odd coach load of americans that love to talk about themselves.... 😄. tickets can be booked online or in various locations. i'd recommend central seats and you can negotiate deals for multiple tickets. i would suggest arriving 30 minutes prior to performance. the dress code isn't strict. enjoy!

the musée de cluny, also known as the musée national du moyen âge, is a treasure trove for anyone fascinated by the medieval world. housed in a beautifully preserved 15th-century gothic mansion and built over ancient roman baths, the museum itself feels like stepping back in time. the collection is rich and varied—stained glass, illuminated manuscripts, medieval sculptures, tapestries, and everyday objects that tell the story of life during the middle ages. the star of the show is undoubtedly the lady and the unicorn tapestry series, which is absolutely breathtaking in both scale and detail. seeing it up close is worth the visit alone.

the múlafossur waterfall, located on the vágar island in the faroe islands, is not only a testament to the raw, untamed beauty of the faroese nature but also a popular attraction for those who seek a tranquil escape. your journey to the village of gásadalur, home to the stunning múlafossur waterfall, will take you through breathtaking scenery. upon arrival, a brief walk will lead you to the prime viewpoint. here, you will be greeted by the magnificent sight of water cascading into the atlantic ocean. the scene is enhanced by the vibrant green landscape and the unending harmony of the crashing waves. #faroeislands #vagar #waterfall #viewpoint #mulafossur

the name says for itself, a hill full of monkeys. to go up the there is a golf cart, 300 baht round trip ( we are a family of 4, with little kids, so we needed to take a cart). to go up cart was just there but on the top we had to wait for the cart for almost 30 minutes...among monkeys, that's something. dont take any bags, monkeys are smart. one of the monkeys ripped with his teeth my bag and took a bag of napkins (thank god it was just napkin,not wallet or a bag of my kid's cookies) the view is okay, but we came there for the monkeys, not for the view. at the entrance they give sticks, but that doesn't help, my husband tried to scare monkeys with a stick, but one of them just straight up kept aggressively going to my husband with teeth. anyways, dangerous hill, but for the experience. and is nice to see monkeys live in their natural habitat, even if they steal and drink coca colas

the name says it all. our day with reef magic was truly magical. it was a perfect blend of adventure, education, and pure beauty. their permanent pontoon at moore reef is the ideal launchpad for a day of fun. the staff, which includes marine biologists, dive instructors, and cultural guides, make the experience. their expertise and passion for the reef are evident in every interaction. i got to experience this passion for the guest experience firsthand when an unexpected opportunity led me to try my first introductory scuba dive. they could have said, "sorry, your booked experience is unavailable" instead they offered me an introductory scuba dive, completing the compulsory briefing on the pontoon just for me. my dive instructor was a master of her craft — patient, reassuring, and completely focused on my safety. she guided me through this unforgettable life-changing experience. my kids loved their time snorkeling, and i appreciated the constant vigilance of the lifeguards. my wife, who didn't care to get in the water, had the opportunity to see the reef in the glass-bottom boat and from the underwater observatory. i'm sorry if this sounds like an ad. it was just so ... magical. i can't express how great a day it was. if you're wondering, "should i spend the money?" yes! it's worth skipping restaurant meals for a couple months, walking instead of taking an uber. hell, it's worth taking a second job. do it!

the namgyal tsemo monastery is a must visit when you are in leh. we were at the leh palace when we noticed this monastery and decided to visit. the view point is simply beautiful and you can see the whole leh town. the monastery as such is beautiful too.

the national art center in tokyo is an architectural masterpiece in itself. with its strikingly futuristic design and spacious, light-filled interiors, the building feels like a work of art. the natural light streaming through the massive glass curtain walls creates a warm, tranquil atmosphere that enhances the entire experience. one of the center’s unique features is that it does not have a permanent collection, meaning every visit offers a new and different exhibition. when i visited, a contemporary art exhibition was on display. though the themes were complex, it offered fresh perspectives and left a lasting impression. the open layout, seating areas, and calming café inside the building also made it a perfect place to reflect and unwind after exploring the art. even on a rainy day, it’s a great place to visit, as you can stay completely sheltered while enjoying the space. the building’s design has a near-futuristic vibe—so much so that it felt like a location straight out of a sci-fi film, perhaps even something from star wars. it reminded me of the kind of pavilion i imagined as a child when dreaming about the osaka expo i never got to attend. and even if you’re not there for a specific exhibit, just visiting to admire the architecture and enjoy a coffee at the café is satisfying in itself. best of all, admission to the building is free. it’s a must-visit spot for anyone looking to enjoy art, architecture, and a peaceful escape from daily life.

the national art center in tokyo is an impressive place with its unique architecture and spacious design. i really enjoyed the variety of exhibitions, and the atmosphere felt calm and inspiring. the building itself is worth visiting, even if you’re not deeply into art. it’s also conveniently located near roppongi, making it easy to include in a day trip around the area. a must-visit for art lovers and anyone looking for a beautiful cultural experience in tokyo.

the national art center, tokyo the architecture is absolutely stunning. even if you don’t visit an exhibition, it’s a lovely place to relax at the café and soak in the unique atmosphere of tokyo. i imagine it would feel even more charming on a rainy day. highly recommended!

the national gallery of iceland is an art museum which is shared across two locations. this is the main gallery located in the early 20th-century ice house building along fríkirkjuvegur street facing tjörnin lake. the second location, makes use of the culture house (also referred to as the house of collections), early 20th-century library on hverfisgata street just a few minutes walk from here. opening hours are 10am to 5pm daily while entry ticket (2400kr for adults, 1200kr students) provides access to both locations as well. we visited both the national gallery of iceland and the house of collections during a recent visit to iceland. both focus on 19th and 20th century artworks by icelandic artists which are spaced out across several floors within the two museums. the house of culture location contains a much larger collection. we found the exhibitions at both museums interesting and worth visiting for art lovers who plan to spend time sightseeing around reykjavik.

the national gallery was made with beautiful modern architecture of glass and steel, which connects older looking structures. comparatively, it is a very small gallery which you can see in an hour or so. admission in 2024 was about $22cad and the ticket is also good for another venue: the collections gallery. the ticket is good for a 24 hr period. photography was permitted, and encouraged (there were signs), during our visit, and i *think* that's usually the case at this venue.

the national garden of athens is a true oasis in the heart of the city – and we absolutely loved it! 🌿 it’s the perfect place to take a break from the busy streets and enjoy some peace and shade under tall trees and along beautiful walking paths. what makes it even more special for families is that it’s not just a park – it’s also great fun for kids! there are a few playgrounds, plenty of open space to run around, and even a small animal area with goats, birds, and other animals that children find fascinating. 🐐🦆 everything is beautifully kept, and the garden feels safe, clean, and relaxing. whether you’re looking for a quiet place to sit, a fun stop for the kids, or just a scenic walk, this is a spot you shouldn’t miss while in athens. free to enter, easy to reach, and perfect for all ages – we highly recommend it!

the national maritime museum is a treasure trove of stories from the sea. one of the most striking exhibits is the original uniform of admiral nelson — seeing it up close, with its history and details, is unforgettable. there’s even the famous moment in naval slang to “uncork the admiral” that makes you smile once you learn the meaning behind it. every display here is worth lingering over: from ship models to navigational instruments, each one opens a window into a different chapter of maritime history. take your time — this museum rewards attention

the national museum in prague is truly impressive, filled with an incredible variety of exhibits that take you through the city’s rich history and beyond. from ancient statues and fossils—including real mammoth bones and a lifelike mammoth statue—to fascinating displays of sea creatures and a stunning mineral collection, the museum feels like stepping into a different time. it was such a magical experience that gave me goosebumps, realizing how deep and ancient prague’s history really is. definitely a must-visit for anyone curious about history, nature, and culture.

the national museum of egyptian civilization is a fascinating place that beautifully showcases egypt’s rich history and cultural heritage. the highlight is definitely the royal mummies hall — it’s both impressive and humbling to stand so close to ancient figures you’ve only read about in history books. the museum is modern, spacious, and well-organized, with clear explanations in multiple languages. that said, a few sections felt like they could use more interactive displays or multimedia elements to bring the stories to life. the café and gift shop options were also somewhat limited. overall, it’s absolutely worth a visit if you’re in cairo — a must-see for history lovers, and a wonderful complement to the egyptian museum in tahrir.

the national orchid garden is, without a doubt, one of the most amazing places in singapore. i’ve visited countless times, and i truly believe i will never get tired of its beauty. it’s a place of constant discovery, where every visit reveals a new bloom, a new colour, or a new piece of knowledge. you can feel the passion and hard work of the staff in every corner. they do an incredible job curating the displays, ensuring that no matter when you visit, you are seeing the plants and flowers at their absolute best. this consistent, breathtaking beauty has never once let me down. and keep an eye out for the garden's charming inhabitants! if you're lucky, you'll spot the resident water monitor lizards and other animals. they have lived there for a long time and wander around so comfortably, like it's their own home. it adds another layer of magic to this incredible sanctuary.

the national roman museum is one of my favorite places in rome, and i always love coming back. this museum has a unique atmosphere and offers a fascinating glimpse into the history of ancient rome. every visit is an unforgettable experience for me – from the beautifully preserved mosaics and frescoes to the majestic statues that seem to tell stories from centuries past. i am especially captivated by the collection of classical sculptures, particularly the iconic statue of emperor augustus and the incredibly detailed bronze busts. the museum is spread across multiple buildings, so there’s always something new to discover. palazzo massimo is my personal favorite – its frescoes and mosaics transport me to the lavish villas of ancient romans. plus, it’s never too crowded, allowing me to fully appreciate the exhibits in peace. if you love history and art, i highly recommend visiting. for me, it’s a place where i feel connected to the past and where i always find a moment to reflect and admire the beauty of roman civilization.

the national union of writers and artists of cuba is a professional, cultural, and social association that brings together writers and artists of different genres, of cuban nationality or at least with strong ties to cuba. it was founded on august 22, 1961, by the cuban poet nicolás guillén.

the natural history museum is absolutely phenomenal and a must-see in london, with incredible exhibits that can capture the imagination of any visitor. however, i highly recommend buying tickets in advance and arriving around 10 a.m. before the crowds build, especially if you are visiting with children. on busy summer days, it can get extremely crowded, which can be challenging if your kids are tired or, like our autistic son, need a bit more space. with some planning and knowing in advance which exhibits you most want to see, it can be an unforgettable and truly magical experience.

the natural history museum is rich with information about the animal kingdom in oman. it consists of many halls and the best one is the whale hall where you can see an actual whale skeleton. also you can see the fossil tree which is 260 million years old.

the natural surroundings are beautiful and full of life; however, the trail could need some maintenance. what truly bothers me is the amount of rubbish along the side facing malaysia. i understand that much of it is brought in by the sea, but it’s time to address the issue. perhaps regular weekly cleanups could be organized, or a more permanent cleaning system could be implemented?

the natural swimming pools in porto moniz, madeira, are a little piece of paradise. crystal-clear seawater, dramatic volcanic rocks, and breathtaking views make this place a unique and refreshing experience. that said, timing is everything. it’s definitely worth paying attention to when you go and making sure you’re well-prepared. one key tip: bring slippers or water shoes , the concrete around the pools gets very hot under the sun and can be painful to walk on barefoot. if i could offer one suggestion to the management, it would be to consider implementing a reservation system or time slots. this would help control the number of visitors and ensure that everyone can fully enjoy the space without it getting too crowded, especially during peak times. parking, sunbeds, and space to relax shouldn’t be in short supply and with some organization, they aren’t. overall, it’s an amazing experience and absolutely worth visiting. if you go prepared, you’re in for a real treat.
the nature center is very nice. staff was helpful (apart from a very rude and unhelpful guy at the bar). unfortunately no way to throw trash away.

the new museum, officially opened in 2021, has 20 mummies on the b1 level (i forgot to mention 22, but the paper guide i had only listed 20). among them are mummies of ramses ii, hatshepsut, and others. each mummy has an information plaque briefly describing their life stories. photography is strictly prohibited! on the 1st floor, the exhibits are arranged in a counterclockwise direction, taking visitors on a journey through the currents of history — from prehistoric cultures 10,000 years ago all the way to the modern islamic world. i think the civilization museum’s exhibition design is well-organized and definitely worth visiting! on april 3, 2021, the pharaoh’s golden parade was held, during which the mummies were transported from the egyptian museum to this new museum. -9/1/25

the new orleans jazz museum is a must-visit for any music lover or cultural enthusiast. housed in a beautifully preserved historic building in the heart of the city, the museum is as visually striking as it is rich in musical history. it does a phenomenal job of honoring the legends of jazz—both the iconic musicians who traveled to new orleans to perform and the many greats who proudly called the city home, such as louis armstrong, sidney bechet, and jelly roll morton. inside, you'll find fascinating exhibits filled with rare instruments, vintage recordings, and immersive stories that trace the roots and evolution of jazz in one of its most important birthplaces. the vibe is lively yet reflective, a true celebration of the genre and the culture that shaped it. parking can be a bit of a challenge, as there is only limited street parking available nearby. however, the experience is more than worth the effort. and for those who served, the museum offers a military discount—a thoughtful touch that adds to its welcoming atmosphere. whether you're a jazz aficionado or just curious about the soul of new orleans, this museum hits all the right notes.

the new york botanical garden in the bronx is truly one of the city’s most beautiful gems. it’s super easy to get to—whether you’re driving or taking public transit. if you’re coming from manhattan, the metro-north harlem line drops you off right at the garden’s doorstep, or you can take the b, d, or 4 train to bedford park blvd and it’s just a short walk from there. we hosted a corporate event here and it couldn’t have been more perfect. the gardens are breathtakingly beautiful—lush, peaceful, and immaculately maintained. the staff was incredibly kind and professional, and the food and drinks served were light, refreshing, and just right for the setting. whether you’re planning a romantic date, a family outing, or a special event, this is a must-visit spot. don’t forget your camera—you’ll definitely want to capture the magic here. highly, highly recommend!

the new york city skyline offers a breathtaking spectacle from spots like the brooklyn heights promenade or the top of the rock. with iconic landmarks and towering skyscrapers, it's an awe-inspiring sight that captures the city's energy and spirit in every glance.

the new york city skyline offers a surreal view. you absolutely must experience this amazing attraction at night. be sure to reserve your tickets early—the later in the evening during weekdays, the better, as there will be fewer people. it's a goldmine for photography and contemplation. as you gaze over the edge, you'll get a god's-eye view of locals enjoying their evening. the illuminated traffic, sparkling city lights, and stunning long exposures of the hudson river make the entire wait worthwhile. *visited in 2024

the nezu museum in tokyo’s aoyama district is a serene cultural gem. while photography is not allowed inside the museum itself, the experience is unforgettable. children enjoy free admission, making it a great family-friendly destination. the highlight is the breathtaking japanese garden, a winding labyrinth of charming pathways, lush seasonal plants, and impressive stone statues/ sculptures. it’s the perfect place to slow down, explore, and feel immersed in japan’s timeless beauty.

the night market in siem reap is quite lively, with delicious and unique insect dishes that are prepared hygienically. the people here are friendly, cheerful, and hospitable. there are many beautiful souvenir products and local textiles. i love this place and will return when i can.
the night market is still a go-to for great finds. we were able to buy some luggages at very good prices at excellent quality. food choices are abundant. come as early as 6pm and haggle your way!
the night view of the city from this gate was stunning. the stairways are open, and you can walk up to the top of the gate. a must-visit place for a nice photo.

the nile boat cruise was a typical tourist attraction that offered a buffet style dinner and live entertainment. the food was egyptian cusinse with a couple of western dishes (probably for children). buffets are usually not high quality food and this holds true for this cruise. the wait staff was friendly and efficient in taking drink orders and bringing them to your table. the entertainment consisted of a belly dancer, a whirling dervish dancer, and a combo of the belly dancer and a singer. it was amusing and we actually had a good time!

the nile cruise was an unforgettable experience! sailing through the heart of cairo, i got to see egypt from a whole new perspective. the calm of the nile, the birds flying above, and the stunning views made it feel like a dream. the tour guide was amazing, sharing stories about ancient egyptian history that gave so much depth to the journey. the food on board was delicious, and the staff were super friendly. it was the perfect mix of relaxation and culture!

the nine arch bridge in ella is a beautiful place to visit. the view is amazing, especially when the train goes over the bridge. it’s surrounded by green hills and tea plantations, which makes it perfect for photos. you can walk along the tracks safely and even go under the bridge. early morning or evening is the best time to go. it’s a peaceful and relaxing spot. a must-see if you are in ella!

the nine arch bridge is not just a bridge—it’s an experience of history, nature, and adventure. whether you’re a photographer, a traveler, or just someone looking to soak in sri lanka’s beauty, this is a must-visit spot! how to get there take a tuk-tuk from ella town (about 10–15 minutes) or enjoy a scenic 30-minute walk through tea plantations. the walk can be slippery after rain, so wear comfortable shoes. best time to visit early morning (6–8 am) for soft golden light and fewer crowds. afternoon (3–5 pm) to catch the train passing by and get the best photos. train schedule the train usually passes around 9 am and 11 am, but schedules can change. it’s best to ask locals or check at the ella railway station. safety tips the train moves slowly, but always stay off the tracks until it has passed. if climbing down for photos, be cautious as some paths are steep. nearby attractions little adam’s peak: a short hike with panoramic views of ella. ravana falls: a stunning waterfall just a short drive from ella.

the nordik spa is absolutely stunning and relaxing from the moment you step foot in it. the staff were very friendly and welcoming at the entrance, setting a great tone for the day. everything was clean, well-maintained, and thoughtfully designed to help you unwind. the hammocks, swinging egg chairs, lounges, saunas, warm and cold pools with waterfalls — all set in the middle of nature — made for an incredibly peaceful and rejuvenating experience. we loved every minute and will absolutely be returning. i’m giving 4 stars instead of 5 due to multiple disruptions regarding photography. according to the village code, guests are allowed to take photos and videos as long as they respect others’ privacy, which we fully adhered to. every photo we took was either of ourselves or of empty areas with no one else in view. still, we were approached multiple times and warned not to take pictures — once by the lady at the cash at the infinity pool bar who initially said no photos were allowed, then corrected herself and clarified that photos of ourselves were fine if no one else was in the shot. yet shortly after, she had another employee come and warn us again, even though we were not violating the stated guidelines. this repeated interruption — especially when we were following the rules — detracted from an otherwise seamless and relaxing visit. if the policy is that absolutely no photos or videos are allowed, this should be made explicitly clear in the spa’s rules to avoid confusion and ensure a more enjoyable experience for guests. that aside, the spa itself is beautiful, peaceful, and definitely worth visiting!

the norris black basin is one of the most famous sceneries in yellowstone, and it is definitely worth to visit here. you will see hundreds of geysers with various of color, and it is extremely exciting.

the norris geyser basin museum is a must-visit for anyone exploring yellowstone’s geothermal wonders. the museum offers fascinating insights into the park’s geology and the unique features of the norris geyser basin, which is home to some of the hottest and most dynamic thermal features in the park. combined with the nearby boardwalks, it’s an educational and awe-inspiring experience!

the nubra valley sand dunes are a unique and mesmerizing sight — a true desert experience right in the middle of the himalayas! surrounded by snow-capped mountains, the contrast of golden sand against the rugged landscape is simply breathtaking. one of the main highlights here is the double-humped bactrian camel rides, which add a fun and memorable touch to the visit. the evenings are especially beautiful, with cool breezes and a magical sunset over the dunes. facilities are basic, so it’s best to carry water and essentials with you. still, the natural beauty and the rare experience of walking on sand dunes at such high altitude make it totally worth it. overall, a must-visit spot in nubra valley — peaceful, scenic, and truly one of a kind.

the ny city skyline vista point on liberty island is one of the best spots to capture the stunning manhattan skyline in the background. whether you’re a photographer or just looking for the perfect vacation shot, this location is absolutely worth stopping by. scenic views: the view of the new york city skyline is panoramic and breathtaking. you get a clear, wide-angle shot of lower manhattan with the shimmering water in front, it’s perfect for photos or just taking in the moment. relaxing atmosphere: the area is surrounded by well-maintained gardens, trees, and shaded spots where you can sit and relax. it’s a peaceful break from the crowds, offering both beauty and calm. refreshments nearby: there are refreshment stands nearby offering lemonade, sodas, and snacks, making it a convenient place to recharge before continuing your exploration of liberty island. final thoughts: this vista point is a must-visit while on liberty island. the combination of skyline views, quiet seating areas, and nearby refreshments makes it a memorable and relaxing stop. highly recommended for photos, relaxation, or just soaking in the iconic new york views.

the nymphaeum at petra was a roman addition to the city after their annexation of nabataea in 106 ad. the monument is quiet ruined now. the central exedra was the fountain and the water was collected at a pool below. the water conduit that started at the siq passed behind this structure. behind the nymphaeum, the wadi al-mataha coming from the northeast joins wadi musa flowing from the east. it is reputed that the pistachio tree that has grown next to the nymphaeum is about half a century old.

the obelisk tomb is one of the many impressive rock-cut tombs that can be found at the ancient city of petra in jordan. it is located in the northern part of the city, along the street of facades, a row of tombs that served as the final resting place for the wealthy and powerful inhabitants of petra. the obelisk tomb gets its name from the four obelisks that are carved into the top of the facade, which were likely intended to symbolize the four corners of the world or to honor the four winds. the tomb is a prime example of the intricate and detailed craftsmanship that was typical of the nabataean people, who carved many of petra's most impressive structures out of the sandstone cliffs. the obelisk tomb consists of a central chamber with a vaulted ceiling, which would have housed the remains of the tomb's occupants. the facade of the tomb is adorned with a series of columns, pediments, and other decorative elements, which were carved out of the sandstone cliffs with incredible precision and attention to detail. like many of the tombs at petra, the obelisk tomb was likely plundered by looters over the centuries, and its contents have long since been removed. nevertheless, the tomb remains one of the most impressive and striking structures in petra, a testament to the incredible skill and artistry of the nabataean people who built it.

the old medina of fez, morocco, is a unesco world heritage site and one of the most well-preserved historic cities in the world. "medina" means old city, and fez’s dates back to the 8th and 9th centuries, with most of its structure built during the idrisid and marinid dynasties. it is famous for its narrow alleys, traditional markets (souks), ancient mosques, madrasas, and artisan workshops. walking through the old medina feels like stepping back in time—a place full of history, culture, and vibrant local life.

the old royal palace at prague castle is one of those places where i could really feel the weight of history. unlike some palaces that are packed with extravagant furniture and gold-covered walls, this one is more about the architecture and historical significance, and that made it even more fascinating. walking into vladislav hall was incredible. it’s huge, with these high vaulted ceilings that make it feel even grander. i could just imagine the banquets, jousting tournaments, and coronation ceremonies that took place here. the size and scale of it alone made it one of my favorite parts of the visit. one of the most interesting spots was the infamous window of the defenestration of prague. it’s wild to stand there and think about how in 1618, a couple of royal officials were literally thrown out of that window, which set off the thirty years’ war. that kind of history is what makes this place special—you’re not just looking at old rooms; you’re standing where major world events happened. another highlight for me was the new land rolls room, which had all these coats of arms and symbols of czech nobility. it gave a cool insight into the political and legal history of the country, which i hadn’t really thought about before visiting. the palace itself isn’t overly decorated, but that’s part of the appeal. it’s more about the history than luxury, and that made it feel authentic and powerful. if you’re visiting prague castle, the old royal palace is definitely worth seeing. i’d recommend taking your time and maybe even doing a guided tour because there’s a lot of history here that’s easy to miss if you just walk through quickly.

the parco degli acquedotti, a large park (280 hectares) that is situated to the south-east of rome, is named after the ancient aqueducts that run through it, such as the aqua marcia, the aqua claudia and the aqua felice. ancient rome was served by a total of 11 aqueducts, which were built over a period of 500 years, between 312 bce and 226 ce. their combined capacity was capable of supplying at least 1,127,000 cubic metres (300 million gallons) of water to the city each day. aqueducts moved water through gravity alone. channels were mostly underground; arches were only used to transport the water over low-lying areas.

the park contains a renovated complex of fortifications that the french originally began building in 1712. construction was paused when a treaty was signed with the british the following year. subsequently, the defenses were replaced by more formidable fortifications at the top of the cliffs and the buildings were converted to barracks 30 years later. the current site includes the foundry and arsenal that produced artillery shells and other ammunition for the french, the british, and through world war fought by the canadians. the current building provides a history of the site. the first floor has a recreation of the crowded french enlisted men’s quarters in which they cooked and ate their meals in the same room as they slept. the second floor, meanwhile, is reconstructed as the british officers’ quarters with a comfortable lounge with comfortable chairs and mahogany gaming tables, a large, formal dining room, and a hearth manned by a cook who officers hired to prepare their meals. the third floor houses the officer’s sleeping quarters and the apartment of the superintendent of the foundry. it is furnished with early 20th-century furniture and furnishings.

the peak tower offers one of the most iconic and breathtaking panoramic views in all of hong kong. perched atop victoria peak, it gives you a sweeping look over the city skyline, victoria harbour, and kowloon beyond. whether you visit during the day or at night, the view is simply unforgettable and a must-see for first-time visitors and returning travelers alike. the sky terrace 428 at the top of the peak tower is the highest viewing platform in hong kong and worth the small ticket fee. the 360-degree view is perfect for photos, especially during golden hour or after sunset when the city lights begin to sparkle. on a clear day, you can see all the way to the new territories. be sure to bring your camera or phone—this is one of the most photogenic spots in asia. the journey to the peak is part of the experience. taking the historic peak tram is recommended if you haven’t done it before—it’s a steep and scenic ride that adds to the charm. alternatively, buses and taxis are available, especially if you want to avoid queues or are visiting during busy times. once at the top, there’s a lively commercial area with restaurants, souvenir shops, and cafes inside the tower. while the main viewing platform requires a ticket, there are also free viewpoints nearby, such as the lugard road walking path, which offers equally stunning views in a more peaceful setting. but the peak tower’s sky terrace gives you a curated experience with information boards and an elevated angle that feels unmatched. it’s touristy, yes—but for good reason. in summary, the peak tower is a hong kong essential. the view is among the best urban landscapes anywhere in the world. whether you're into photography, sightseeing, or simply enjoying the city from above, this spot delivers. just check the weather before going—clear skies make all the difference!

the picasso museum in barcelona is a must-visit destination for art lovers and photographers alike, offering a deep dive into the formative years of one of the 20th century’s most influential artists. housed in a series of beautiful medieval palaces in the vibrant el born neighborhood, the museum’s setting is as captivating as its collection. inside, visitors can explore an extensive range of picasso’s early works, sketches, ceramics, and paintings, tracing the artist’s development from his youth through his blue and rose periods. the layout is thoughtfully designed to provide context and narrative, enriching the viewing experience. for photographers, the museum presents a wonderful blend of historic architecture and carefully curated exhibits. natural light filters through the stone courtyards, creating photogenic contrasts and serene spaces to capture. while photography inside the galleries is usually restricted, the surrounding architecture and public areas offer excellent opportunities for creative shots. the museum also features temporary exhibitions, a charming café, and a well-stocked bookstore. attending the picasso museum is not just about viewing art; it’s about stepping into the world that shaped a genius. whether you’re an art enthusiast or a cultural explorer, this museum is a highlight of barcelona’s rich artistic heritage.

the pok fu lam country park is situated in the area directly south and west of victoria peak. this is a 270-hectare park designated in 1979 that provides hiking trails and outdoors area for residents and tourists to enjoy on hong kong island. the most common way to enjoy pok fu lam country park is by way of the paved walking trails that wind through the park between the pok fu lam village and victoria peak. they are well maintained and a fairly easy grade of walk up and back down from the peak. the scenery throughout is lush, green and forested. in addition to the hikes within pok fu lam country park, you will find a small reservoir which was constructed in 1863, four masonry bridges (1863-1871), the former watchman's cottage (1860-1863) and other structures which are collectively designed as a declared monument or historical value in hong kong. note: for those who hike from the peak down through the country park. at the end of the trail, you can take bus transportation back towards mtr stations or central district, reconnecting you back to the main sightseeing areas of the city.

the princes’ gates stand as toronto’s grand eastern welcome to exhibition place—a monumental beaux‑arts triumphal arch constructed in 1927. designed by chapman & oxley with sculptures by charles d. mckechnie, it commemorated canada’s 60th confederation anniversary and was officially opened by princes edward and george ￼. 🏛 architectural highlights • the sweeping central arch is flanked by nine doric/ionic columns, symbolizing canada’s nine provinces in 1927 ￼. • on top, the winged victory statue—originally gilded—stands poised in a ship of state, clutching a maple leaf and laurel, signaling progress and national pride ￼. • surrounding sculptural detail includes beehives (industry), cornucopias (abundance), and figures representing farming and construction—a visual tribute to canada’s growth . 🕰 history & restoration • construction ran from april to august 1927, costing about ca$152,000 ￼. • originally named the “diamond jubilee of confederation gates,” it was renamed when the royal brothers were announced to inaugurate it ￼. • designated under the ontario heritage act in 1987, the structure underwent restoration: winged victory was replaced with a replica in 1987, other statues cast anew, and in 2006 the surrounding piazza was revitalized as part of a toronto–milan twinning project ￼. 🌆 significance today • the princes’ gates remain a beloved landmark and ceremonial gateway, honoured annually in cne parades and major events ￼. • the adjacent revitalized plaza reflects toronto’s multicultural partnerships and commitment to public art and urban design . ⸻ in summary: the princes’ gates are not just an entrance—they’re a timeless emblem of toronto’s heritage and canada’s identity. with rich symbolic details, storied history, and ongoing preservation, they continue to welcome visitors with dignity and pride. let me know if you’d like info on nearby landmarks like the dufferin gate or the garden of the greek gods!

the pyramid of caius cestius was a fascinating and unexpected discovery during our time in rome—an ancient egyptian-style pyramid tucked within the city walls that instantly captured our attention. built around 18–12 bce as a tomb for gaius cestius, a roman magistrate and member of the septemviri epulonum (a religious corporation), it stands over 120 feet tall and is made of brick-faced concrete covered with white carrara marble. what makes it especially unique is that it was constructed during a time when egyptomania swept through rome following the conquest of egypt, blending roman and egyptian architectural styles. the pyramid was later incorporated into the aurelian walls in the 3rd century, helping to preserve it for centuries. inside, a small burial chamber still holds faded frescoes, though it's only occasionally open to the public. visiting it felt like stepping into a little-known layer of rome’s rich and eclectic history, and it’s definitely worth seeing for anyone who appreciates the city’s unexpected architectural gems.

the pyramid of cestius is a truly unique and fascinating landmark in rome, a stunning blend of roman ambition and egyptian-inspired architecture. it's an unforgettable sight, especially when viewed against the backdrop of the ancient city walls. recently, the pyramid became a symbol of modern resilience and hope in an inspiring way. before the 2025 ukraine recovery conference in rome, the monument was beautifully illuminated, not just with light, but with the stories of ukrainians rebuilding their lives and homes. seeing this ancient symbol of a past civilization used to highlight the strength and determination of a people in the present was incredibly moving. it was a powerful reminder of how history and current events can intersect to create moments of profound meaning. a must-see for anyone interested in history, architecture, and the human spirit.

the qalawun complex, located in the heart of islamic cairo on al-muizz street, is one of the most impressive mamluk architectural achievements. built in 1284–1285 ad by sultan al-mansur qalawun, the complex includes a mosque, madrasa (islamic school), hospital, and mausoleum—all showcasing remarkable islamic artistry. the mausoleum, in particular, is considered one of the most beautiful in egypt, featuring intricate marble inlays, stained glass windows, and stunning domed ceilings. the complex reflects the grandeur of the mamluk era and remains a must-visit destination for history and architecture enthusiasts.

the reichstag building is one of berlin’s most iconic and historically significant landmarks, and seeing it in person is an experience that leaves a lasting impression. we visited both in daylight and after dark, and each offered a completely different kind of beauty. by day, the striking mix of classical architecture and the modern glass dome stands proudly against the skyline, a symbol of germany’s turbulent past and its modern democracy. you can really appreciate the fine details in the stonework and the grandeur of the structure as you walk around it. at night, the building transforms. soft, golden lighting washes over the façade, and the glass dome glows from within, giving it a majestic yet welcoming presence. standing there, it’s hard not to think of the pivotal moments in history that unfolded here. whether you come for the history, the architecture, or simply to take in one of berlin’s most remarkable sights, the reichstag is a must-see — both day and night if you can.

the reserve is located in the southwestern part of bolivia, close to the borders with chile and it is a very important protected area. it covers an area of 7.45 sq. klm and it includes the famous laguna colorada and laguna verde, among other lakes. in addition, there are two settlements inside the national reserve, quetena chico and quetena grande. the park includes around 50 mountain peaks in its protected area, most of which are active volcanoes. it was named after eduardo avaroa, the famous bolivian war hero of the 19th century. the reserve was created in the 70s and extended its protected area in the 80s.

the rosarium schönbrunn is a serene and enchanting garden that feels like stepping into a floral paradise. located within the sprawling schönbrunn palace grounds, this hidden gem is a must-visit for nature lovers, photographers, and anyone seeking a tranquil escape from the bustling city of vienna. its exquisite collection of roses, meticulously arranged in picturesque designs, is a testament to both horticultural excellence and timeless beauty. one of the most remarkable features of the rosarium is its diversity of roses. with hundreds of varieties in every imaginable color, the garden showcases blooms that range from delicate pastels to vibrant reds and yellows. each variety is carefully labeled, making it not just a visual feast but also an educational experience. walking through the archways of climbing roses or along paths lined with fragrant bushes feels like a journey through a dreamlike wonderland. the design of the garden is both elegant and harmonious, blending natural beauty with artistic landscaping. fountains, benches, and pergolas are strategically placed throughout, offering visitors plenty of spots to sit, relax, and admire the surroundings. the circular layout of the central rose beds, along with neatly trimmed hedges and manicured pathways, creates a sense of order and balance that enhances the garden’s charm. visiting the rosarium is especially delightful during late spring and early summer when the roses are in full bloom, filling the air with their intoxicating fragrance. however, even outside peak blooming season, the garden’s peaceful atmosphere and stunning architecture make it worth exploring. it’s an ideal spot for a leisurely stroll, a romantic outing, or simply a moment of quiet reflection.
