the royal botanic garden in sydney is a vast and breathtakingly beautiful haven nestled in the heart of the city, right by the harbour. it's not just a garden—it's an experience that invites you to pause, breathe, and reconnect with nature. whether you're looking to take a peaceful walk, lie down under the canopy of ancient trees, or simply enjoy some quiet reflection, this place offers the perfect setting. you could easily spend an entire day here and still not see it all. the variety of plant life is incredible, from exotic blooms to towering trees, each corner revealing something new and fascinating. for nature lovers and curious minds, exploring the garden in detail might even take days. as you walk through its winding paths, you're gently led to a scenic viewpoint that offers a spectacular panorama of sydney harbour, the opera house, and the harbour bridge—a truly iconic spot that makes the journey through the garden even more rewarding. the far end of the garden is equally serene, often less crowded, and ideal for a quiet sit-down or a final stroll before heading out. do note, though, that the garden closes relatively early, especially outside of summer months, so it's best to check the opening hours in advance. getting lost in its charm is easy—but it’s better to do so with enough time to make your way out.

the royal palace of fes (dar el-makhzen) in mechouar fes jdid is one of the city’s most iconic and cherished landmarks. while the palace itself is not open to the public, its stunning golden doors and intricate zellige tilework have made it a favorite backdrop for generations of fassi families. dating back to the 13th century and expanded under various dynasties, the palace is rich in moroccan royal history. but for many locals, including my own family, it holds a different kind of significance—this is where we come to mark milestones. over the years, we’ve taken countless photos here during weddings, eid, graduations, and family visits. the majestic architecture, the sense of pride it evokes, and the traditions it inspires make the royal palace a timeless piece of fes. a must-see for visitors and a cherished treasure for those of us lucky enough to call this city home. it is a must see when in fes, a true example of the beauty of moroccan architecture and beauty.

the royal tombs are four prominent grand tombs carved into the western side of khubtha mountain, overlooking the city center. their elaborate architecture and prominent locations indicate that they held families from petra's upper social strata, or royalty. from right to left, they are: the urn tomb, silk tomb, corinthian tomb, and palace tomb. each tomb has its own unique architectural style and historical significance. a must visit place in petra. the urn tomb derives its name from the funerary urn located on the pediment at the top of the façade. set back in a deep recess in the khubtha slope, the silk tomb is the smallest of the four and has drawn acclaim for the brilliant banded coloring of its sandstone façade. petra's corinthian tomb, named after greek corinthian-style capitals, is patterned after the khazna. the palace tomb, the largest and most elaborate, is believed to reflect a hellenistic or roman-period palace facade. the nabataeans were deeply concerned about their dead. they buried them in monumental tombs located in prominent positions around the city, where they dominate their surroundings and command views from afar.

the ruins of the almoravid koubba, or the ancient almoravid mosque, stand as a testament to marrakech’s rich historical tapestry. dating back to the 12th century, these ruins represent the architectural ingenuity of the almoravid dynasty, a berber muslim dynasty that significantly influenced the city’s development. historical significance built around 1125 ad, the almoravid koubba is one of the few remnants of almoravid architecture in marrakech. the site provides a fascinating glimpse into the early islamic art and architecture in morocco, showcasing the dynasty’s advanced craftsmanship and aesthetic sensibilities. the structure is particularly notable for its intricate stucco decoration and the use of water channels, which illustrate the sophisticated hydraulic techniques of the period. observation point while the site is primarily a place of historical interest, it doesn’t offer much in terms of activities beyond observation. visitors can appreciate the detailed architectural elements and imagine the grandeur of the mosque in its heyday. the surrounding area often enhances the experience, as the ruins are nestled in the heart of marrakech, providing a unique contrast between ancient and modern life. tips for visitors 1. brief visit: plan for a short visit, as the main activity is to observe and reflect on the historical significance of the site. 2. combine visits: pair your trip with other nearby historical sites such as the ben youssef madrasa or the marrakech museum to make the most of your time. 3. photography: the ruins offer excellent photo opportunities, especially for those interested in capturing historical architecture against the backdrop of the bustling city. in summary, the ruins of the almoravid koubba are a must-see for history enthusiasts and those interested in early islamic architecture. while the site may not provide extensive activities, its historical value and the visual appeal of the ruins make it a worthy stop in marrakech.

the sacred monkey forest sanctuary is a magical blend of lush jungle, ancient temples, and playful wildlife right in the heart of ubud. walking through the moss-covered paths, surrounded by towering trees and sacred sculptures, felt like stepping into a different world. the monkeys were curious, energetic, and often hilarious. as long as you follow the simple rules (don’t feed them, keep your belongings secure, and don’t make eye contact), it’s a peaceful and awe-inspiring experience. i especially loved watching the baby monkeys play and interact with their families, it’s nature at its best. the grounds are well-maintained, and there's a deep spiritual atmosphere here. it’s more than just a tourist spot, it’s a sacred place that’s been respectfully preserved. highly recommend this place if you're in bali. it’s one of those rare places where culture, nature, and a bit of fun all come together beautifully. tip: go early in the morning when it's less crowded and the light is perfect for photos. make sure to bring a secure bag and don’t carry any snacks, these clever little guys will find them!

the sacré-cœur basilica in montmartre is one of the most beautiful spots in paris, both for its architecture and its views. perched on the highest point in the city, it’s impossible not to be impressed when you see its bright white domes against the sky. getting there means a bit of a climb—either by stairs or the funicular—but it’s worth every step. inside, the basilica is peaceful and stunning, with incredible mosaics (the golden one of christ above the altar is jaw-dropping). it’s free to enter, but if you want to go up the dome for an even better panoramic view of paris, there’s a small fee. what i loved most was the atmosphere outside. the steps in front are always buzzing—street performers, people picnicking, and everyone just enjoying that breathtaking skyline view. at sunset, it’s pure magic. sacré-cœur isn’t just a church—it’s an experience, combining art, history, and some of the best views in the city. if you only have time for one viewpoint in paris, this should be it.

the salar de uyuni is, quite simply, a vast expanse of white. it's like a blank canvas, a world of endless possibilities, and a nightmare for cyclists with sensitive rear ends. i spent two days pedaling across this salty desert, and let me tell you, my backside has never been so grateful for a cushioned seat. the roads, or rather the tracks, are a mixed bag. some are well-defined and easy to follow, while others seem to vanish into the horizon. it's a bit like navigating a maze, but with fewer twists and turns. a drone would have been a lifesaver, providing a bird's-eye view of my surroundings. camping on the salt flats is a surreal experience. the silence is deafening, the stars are blinding, and the wind howls like a banshee. just remember to bring some extra pegs, as the salt can be surprisingly tough to penetrate. one word of caution for car travelers: watch out for those pesky salt holes. they're like landmines, lurking beneath the surface, ready to swallow your tires whole. but despite the challenges, the salar de uyuni is a truly awe-inspiring place. the sunrises and sunsets are beyond breathtaking, and the otherworldly landscapes are straight out of a science fiction movie. so, if you're looking for an adventure that's equal parts beauty and brutality, the salar de uyuni is the place to be.

the scuderie del quirinale, built in the early 18th century, originally served as stables for the papal state. designed by carlo fontana and later expanded by alessandro specchi and ferdinando fuga, the building reflects the architectural style of the time with its balanced proportions and decorative details. located near the quirinal palace, it was a functional space for housing horses and carriages, integral to the operations of the papal court and later the italian monarchy. between 1997 and 1999, the structure underwent a major restoration led by architect gae aulenti, converting it into a modern exhibition center. this renovation preserved its historical features while adding new elements, such as a panoramic window overlooking the city. in 1999, the space reopened as a venue for cultural events, hosting exhibitions of renowned artists like caravaggio and titian, as well as collections from institutions like the hermitage museum. the scuderie del quirinale stands on the site of the ancient temple of serapis, with some remnants of the roman structure still visible. positioned within a historically significant urban setting, it faces the quirinal palace and is adjacent to the palazzo della consulta. today, the building serves as a prominent cultural space, drawing visitors to its exhibitions and its role in rome’s architectural and historical landscape.

the secret garden is a historical haven, offers a captivating glimpse into royal life and serene landscapes. it is a separate admission section of the palace, with timed-entry tickets and re-entry is not allowed. we bought our tickets here for the english guided tour. the guide speaks good english. there were 2 guides helping with crowd control, which was necessary. highlights: * buyongji pond (芙蓉池 부용지): a small, historically lotus-filled pond symbolizing "square earth, round sky," once enjoyed by royalty for fishing and boating. * yeonghwadang pavilion (영화당 暎花堂) : beautiful hip-roofed pavilion by the pond, a former site for royal banquets and exams, once surrounded by vibrant flowers. * eosumun gate (어수문 魚水門): exquisite gate to the royal library, symbolizing the king's bond with his people ("like fish and water"), sadly inaccessible to the public. * juhamnu pavilion (주합루 宙合樓): the royal library on top of the hill. * aeryeonji pond (애련지 愛蓮池): true to its name ("love lotus"), this pond is filled with lotus, reflecting purity and integrity, with a small, secluded pavilion. * jondeokjeong pavilion (존덕정 or 尊德亭): the garden's grandest pavilion with unique double hexagonal roofs and dragon carvings, signifying "respect virtue" and royal authority. * pyeomusa pavilion (평우사 or 砭愚榭): once a study spot for the crown prince ("enlighten the foolish"), its pillars feature a poem beautifully describing the secret garden's charm. the secret garden isn't just a stroll, it's a carefully curated experience. embrace the history, appreciate the symbolism, worth spending the hour for an unforgettable journey through royal tranquility.

the setting of this resort is beautiful! you can walk out on the pier and see turtles every morning or small sharks in the evening. the house reef is well worth snorkeling, and of course there are dive excursions in the surrounding area. the staff is very friendly and the feeling of this place is homey. good food in the restaurant, and a lovely bar in the evening (although you can grab a beer of a bottle of wine from the fridge any time). this is just a wonderful place to be!

the sheer size of the structure is simply enormous. when i first saw it, i couldn’t believe my eyes. it’s a marvel to witness how they managed to construct an entire structure and place a modern dome on top. the entrance to the building is well-organized and heavily guarded, which is completely justified. as you ascend to the dome, you can explore the surrounding areas. it’s an incredible experience to walk up the slope of the dome to reach the top. at the base of the dome, you can learn about the building’s history and how the german government has evolved over time. the views are breathtaking, so i highly recommend hiring you to recommend this place to everyone. you will need to make sure to make arrangements ahead of time to visit this place. ticket is a must and needs to be planned in advance.

the shipyards night market is more than just a market – it’s an unmissable vibe! this place is bursting with life, and endless things to explore—an absolute must-visit. from the moment you arrive, the energy is contagious. the vibe here is just on a different level. it’s a beautiful place with so much diversity in offering that no matter what your taste is, you will find something you like. the vibrant mix of vendors offers everything from unique clothing, handmade jewellery, and vintage finds to delicious street food from all over the world. the atmosphere is always buzzing with energy. very vibrant night life market. the shipyards night market was the ultimate summer hangout—come hungry and leave with a camera full of memories! the atmosphere is buzzing with energy. the food scene? absolutely fire. the street food here is next level…you’ll for sure find something to satisfy your taste buds. this pineapple drink from island husk was served inside a whole pineapple for a next level refreshment! the pineapple juice they gave me in a cup was also so refreshing and perfect for summer. the greek food from the mad greek was on point, so much flavour in every bite. the tornado potato was such a fun and crispy snack! i ate a scrumptious burger from odd burger. the hot dog from j’s disco dogs was downright delicious and i loved the mouthwatering pretzel from mr. pretzel. the gelato from life is sweet confections had a super rich flavour and is incredibly creamy. and the food didn’t end there…i loved the sweet & juicy corn on the cob from roasted revolution. the kettle corn from garys kettle corn was super addicting and super delicious! i couldn’t resist the samosa from chai wagon. i had to wash everything down with the fruit smoothie from grub truck. this place is more than a market—it’s a full-on summer night adventure with food, fun, and live music. there’s something happening on every corner: music, art, fashion, and most importantly—food! add in the live music, and friendly atmosphere, and you’ve got a place that stays in your memory. shipyards night market is a vibrant and eclectic spot with endless street food options, unique little shops, and personalized items you won’t find anywhere else. shipyards night market is an absolute gem! the energy is unmatched, making it the perfect place to explore, eat, and soak in the vibrant market vibes.

the spirited garden is a magical place. i was in south korea for three weeks and fell in love with the people, the culture, the nature, the history -- all of it -- but the garden was the highlight of my trip. we planned to spend about an hour here and ended up spending more than 3. it's impossible to put into words how affected i was by the garden. it's enchanting, beautiful, haunting, peaceful, and it's a place that gives one a chance to ruminate on life should they choose. you get out what you put into it. if you rush right though, you will be missing so much. it may not be for everyone. if you are a time-is-money kind of a person, maybe you aren't open to this kind of experience, but you'll never know until you try. you don't have to love bonsai to love the garden, but if you take the time to read about the garden and the placards, you'll come to appreciate it on a deeper level. there are life lessons in the garden if you care to look. the garden was created in 1968 from nothing and is still cared for by sung bum-young, who is now about 90 i think. it has tiny bonsai (bunjae) and huge bonsai trees, koi ponds, sculptures, stone work, and cafes. for those who think the entrance fee is too high, consider this: it's less than a movie ticket and far more valuable. it's a couple of fancy cups of coffee but far more enriching. you are supporting an ongoing project that brings joy to so many.

the sponza palace is a stunning architectural gem that shouldn't be missed. its gothic and renaissance blend creates a visually captivating exterior, while the interior houses a poignant memorial to the city's defenders. documents from the state archives are marvelous, and many fascinating exhibits offer glimpses into dubrovnik's past. take a moment to appreciate the intricate details of this iconic building and pay respects to those who sacrificed for their city.

the stutfield glacier viewpoint is a stunning scenic stop along the icefields parkway (highway 93 north) in jasper national park. it offers breathtaking views of the stutfield glacier, a prominent tongue of the larger columbia icefield. located 1 km south of the columbia icefield discovery centre, between the athabasca glacier and sunwapta pass. parking is free, easy and enough spaces.

the sugarloaf cable car was one of the absolute highlights of my day trip in rio de janeiro! this iconic ride not only delivered a smooth and scenic journey, but also offered some of the most breathtaking panoramic views i’ve ever seen. from the moment the cable car began its ascent, i was in awe. the ride from the base at praia vermelha to morro da urca, and then up to the peak of sugarloaf mountain, was smooth, safe, and stunning. as we rose higher, the entire city of rio started to unfold before my eyes—the beaches, the bay, the bustling streets, the christ the redeemer statue in the distance, and the lush green hills. it felt like a moving postcard. at each stop, there were observation decks where i could pause and take in the views. i captured some incredible photos and simply took time to appreciate the natural beauty and unique cityscape that rio is so famous for. watching the boats glide across guanabara bay and the sun cast golden hues over the mountains was nothing short of magical. the facilities were well maintained, the staff were helpful, and everything felt organized and tourist-friendly. the entire experience—from boarding the cable car to spending time at the summit—was seamless, relaxing, and awe-inspiring. if you're in rio, this is a must-do experience. the views from the sugarloaf cable car are second to none, and the ride itself is a thrilling way to connect with the city’s landscape. i left feeling amazed and grateful for such an unforgettable experience!

the sultan qaboos grand mosque in muscat is breathtaking — a masterpiece of omani architecture with stunning domes, intricate mosaics, and a peaceful atmosphere. the massive prayer hall, sparkling chandelier, and warm hospitality make it an unforgettable and must-visit landmark.

the sultan qaboos grand mosque is one of the most stunning landmarks in muscat and absolutely worth a visit. its architecture is breathtaking, with intricate details, soaring minarets and a sense of calm that makes it feel both grand and serene. whether you're admiring the vast prayer hall or simply walking through the beautifully landscaped gardens, the mosque leaves a lasting impression. tourists are welcome to visit from 8am to 11am every day except friday. for muslim visitors, the mosque is open at all times, but if you're a woman and want to see the main prayer hall from inside, you'll need to come during the tourist hours. there is a separate women’s prayer area that’s open daily, including for jummah prayers. do keep in mind that bags and water bottles aren’t allowed inside, so it’s best to travel light. there are washing facilities available, and the entire space is kept immaculately clean and respectful. it’s not just a place of worship—it’s a place of beauty, reflection and cultural richness. if you’re in muscat, don’t miss it.

the sydney harbour bridge is one of the most marvelous landmarks that will blow your mind away. it pairs perfectly with the sydney opera house and is worth taking lots of photos from circular quay and also from the rocks district. the walk across the bridge is so enjoyable and you will have a big smile on your face at the top. i was hoping to do the bridge climb experience but i had lots of other locations planned so i will try it on my next visit. overall, it is a must-visit location and it is an unforgettable experience that will i enjoyed so much.

the sydney harbour national park on sydney’s north harbour is absolutely stunning! the cove boasts crystal-clear waters and golden sandy beaches, all nestled within the lush green canopy of the national park. it’s a slice of paradise that feels a world away from the city. you can explore this magical area by kayak, sup, or boat with manly kayak centre. they even offer guided kayak tours if you want to learn more about the history and hidden gems of the cove. there’s a stack of fun things to do; everything from supball, their unique and epic sup board game (seriously, if you haven’t tried it, you must), to sup lessons, kayak fitness sessions, sup yoga, and more. they even do picnics in paradise - need i say more? there’s a secluded beach you can only access by water, a small but sweet waterfall, and the historic quarantine station, which is well worth a visit. they run fascinating history tours, and the site includes a bar, cafe, and restaurant. keep an eye out for events like sunset sessions, where you can enjoy drinks and live music while watching the sun go down over sydney - it's truly a 'wow' moment. and of course, manly’s famous “office area” on east esplanade is one of the best spots in sydney to catch the sunset.

the sydney opera house is breathtaking — both inside and out. the architecture is iconic and even more impressive up close, especially with the harbour views. tours are well organized and give fascinating insights into its history and design. attending a performance here is unforgettable: the acoustics and atmosphere are world-class. even if you don’t go inside, walking around the building and enjoying the views is a must. a true symbol of sydney and australia.

the temple of the emerald buddha, located within the grand palace complex, is one of the most beautiful and spiritually rich places in bangkok. the entrance fee is 500 baht, which gives access to both the temple and the grand palace — a fair price for the experience you get. the architecture is absolutely stunning, with intricate gold work, colorful murals, and traditional thai design that reflects centuries of craftsmanship and devotion. the emerald buddha itself is quite small but deeply revered. though photography is not allowed inside the hall, the spiritual atmosphere is strong and calming. the surrounding temple buildings and statues are equally impressive and worth exploring in detail. the entire area is clean, organized, and well-preserved. there’s a strict dress code, so make sure to wear long pants and sleeves, or you’ll have to rent clothes before entering. despite the crowds, the management is efficient, and the visit feels peaceful. plan to spend at least 1.5 to 2 hours here to take everything in. a must-visit landmark that beautifully blends history, religion, and royal heritage. don’t leave bangkok without seeing it!

the theater has a long history, performing many classic plays. cheap ticket prices suitable for the whole family. history of the theater today's hanoi drama theater was founded in 1959. after 60 years of construction, growth and development. from a theater team in the capital people's opera troupe. in 1993, the hanoi drama troupe was transformed into the hanoi drama theater. with outstanding efforts in performance. in 2005, the hanoi people's committee decided to upgrade the theater to a grade i theater (decision no. 8574/qd-ub dated december 30, 2005 of the hanoi people's committee on ranking grade i for the hanoi drama theater). implement the decision of the national assembly on expanding hanoi's administrative boundaries. in april 2009, the ha tay drama troupe merged with the hanoi drama theater to become the hanoi drama theater under the hanoi department of culture, sports and tourism. hanoi drama theater has the function and task of performing dramatic art; collect, preserve and develop dramatic art; performing for political tasks, performing for domestic and foreign audiences contributes to improving the cultural, spiritual and aesthetic life of viewers. the theater's organizational structure and personnel were built according to the decision of the hanoi people's committee and the ministry of culture, sports and tourism for grade i theaters, including the board of directors, functional departments (general administration department, performance organization department, art department) and actor troupes (actors troupe 1, actors troupe 2, actors troupe 3) with a total of 109 officers, civil servants, public employees, and labor contracts. there are 66 actors, 10 people working in management and professional roles, and 33 people serving. professional qualifications: master's degree: 05 people, university-college level: 71 people, political level: advanced political theory 01 person, intermediate political theory 06 people. the theater party cell has 21 party members, the trade union has 98 members, the youth union branch has 33 members, the veterans association branch has 16 members and especially in the team of artists and actors, there are 03 artists who were awarded the title of people's artist by the state and 06 artists who were awarded the title of meritorious artist by the state while working and performing.

the theater still retains the essence of a culture that is gradually being forgotten. i would like to thank the tuong artists who are still very enthusiastic about preserving tuong so that it can continue to live and be passed on as a part of the beauty of vietnamese culture. the theater is well designed and has quality. the stage is full of smoke and lights, so the plays are beautiful.

the third trail of the day for us, this was well worth it! it was fairly well marked with rock baskets. a few scrambles and one slightly ridiculous–to–navigate, foothold/handhold-less crevice. i was a little worried about the crevice for the way back, but it was actually really easy. getting up into it was the hardest part. see pictures. i was there to hike, but i did see someone on a mountain bike on an adjacent trail. i am posting a map. there was a family there with five kids, i would guess between the ages of five and nine. everyone seemed pretty happy, so i’m guessing they didn’t lose anyone over the cliffs at the top. i can’t say that i would recommend taking a group of kids in that age range up, myself. especially not that many of them! it was a fairly fast hike, lasting about two hours round-trip with a good 10 to 15 minutes spent at the top.

the thousand islands hike, rated as easy to moderate, offered a good balance of challenge and reward. the early part of the hike, with its straight uphill walk, provided a bit of a workout, but it was well worth the effort. after about 30 to 40 minutes of ascending, you will reach the dirt path that eventually leads to the thousand islands viewpoint. and what a view it was! the sight of little island tops emerging from the water was simply breathtaking. it felt like stepping into a picture-perfect postcard. one of the things i appreciated most about this hike was that it wasn't very busy. the trail was relatively peaceful, with ample space to hang around at the viewpoint. the thousand islands viewpoint provides an excellent vantage point for photography enthusiasts. the picturesque islands, nestled in the water, created a captivating scene that begged to be captured. whether you're a professional photographer or simply enjoy snapping a few shots on your smartphone, this hike offers fantastic photo opportunities. if you're looking for a hike that offers beautiful views, a touch of tranquility, and ample space to relax and capture memories, i highly recommend exploring the thousand islands trail. you won't be disappointed.

the three holy brothers: phra serm, phra suk, phra sai regarding the discovery of a buddha statue on the lao side, some have speculated that it is the “phra suk” that was lost in the mekong river. however, this seems unlikely, as the artistic style and casting of the statue belong to a different era, and the locations along the mekong river where these events occurred are far apart. today, our news team takes you on a journey to trace the story of the three holy brothers: phra serm, phra suk, and phra sai. legend has it that the three daughters of the lan xang king commissioned the casting of three buddha statues, each named after one of the princesses. brought from lan xang across the mekong to siam originally, the three buddha statues were enshrined in vientiane. during the reign of king rama iii, in the campaign to suppress the vientiane rebellion, somdet phra bowornrajchao mahasakdiphonsep, who led the campaign, reportedly brought the three statues from buffalo mountain, where the locals had hidden them. the statues were transported on bamboo rafts. phra suk sinks in the mekong during the first attempt, the bamboo raft broke, causing the pedestal of phra suk to sink into the mekong, an area later called “wern thaen.” later, while navigating the mekong near the mouth of the ngum river, opposite ban nong kung, phon phisai district, nong khai province, a storm caused the raft carrying phra suk to break apart. phra suk sank into the river, and the area became known as “wern suk.” phra serm was enshrined at wat pho chai, while phra sai was taken to wat ho kong. brought to bangkok during the reign of king rama iv, king mongkut ordered khun worathani and chao men to bring phra serm and phra sai to bangkok. however, the brahmin responsible for transporting phra sai could not move the oxcart carrying it, and the cart eventually broke. after deliberation, it was decided to enshrine phra sai at wat pho chai instead. phra serm, however, was successfully brought to bangkok. originally, king rama iv intended to install phra serm as the principal buddha image at wat boworn suthawas. however, upon seeing its magnificent appearance, he decided to place it on a white umbrella pedestal in the royal palace. after his passing, king mongkut ordered phra serm to be enshrined as the principal image in the vihara of wat pathum wanaram in bangkok. references: somdet krom phraya damrong rajanubhab, article on “legends of important buddha statues” in silpa wattanatham magazine, phongsan linganchanabut.

the tokyo photographic art museum is currently hosting an exhibition of works by luigi ghirri. he doesn’t seem like the kind of person who became a photographer simply out of a love for taking pictures. rather, he feels more like a thinker—someone who encountered photography as a medium for reflection and, through that, became a photographer. for fans of contemporary art, his work is easy to connect with. some photos, for example, show people viewing paintings, captured from behind. the act of viewing itself—or perhaps the hesitation and awareness that comes with it—becomes the subject. if i could, i’d love to hang one of his works on my own wall and spend time reflecting on it myself.

the towers of the fort were decorated with illuminated candles at the beginning of each month, allowing visitors to trace the path of the sun as it moved from one tower to the next, earning this fort the nickname qasr el shamee, or the candles palace. within the fortress's perimeter are six coptic churches, a convent, and the coptic museum. according to historians, the name babylon originally referred to the capital of a neighboring nation by that name. however, another possibility links the name to the old pr-hapi-n-iwnw (nile house of heliopolis), which was the deity's residence in heliopolis city; habi was the nile's god.

the train night market, known locally as talad rot fai, is one of bangkok’s most iconic and vibrant night markets. located behind seacon square on srinakarin road, this sprawling market offers a perfect blend of street food, vintage shopping, and local culture. unlike tourist-heavy spots, talad rot fai has a laid-back, authentic vibe that appeals to both locals and curious travelers. what makes this market stand out is its diverse mix of offerings. you’ll find rows of stalls selling vintage clothing, retro home decor, antiques, and handmade accessories. for collectors and fashion hunters, it’s a goldmine of unique finds. the food scene is equally impressive—think grilled meats, seafood, spicy salads, thai desserts, and fun oversized dishes perfect for sharing. bars with live music, quirky container-style cafés, and open-air seating areas give the market a festival-like atmosphere. the energy picks up after 7 pm, and the place truly comes alive with music, lights, and the delicious aroma of street food. getting there requires a taxi or grab ride, as it’s not directly accessible by bts, but the experience is well worth the effort. it’s best to bring cash and arrive with an empty stomach and a sense of adventure. in short, train night market is more than just a market—it’s a cultural experience, offering a fun, flavorful, and visually rich night out in bangkok. a must-visit for anyone looking to dive into the city’s true street culture.

the trevi fountain is, without a doubt, a breathtaking sight to behold. it's a masterpiece of baroque sculpture and engineering, and seeing it in person is a truly iconic rome moment. the sound of the water, the intricate carvings, and the sheer scale of the fountain are absolutely magnificent. however, the reality of visiting it today is that it's just not like it used to be. the crowds are immense, and that’s a significant understatement. the piazza is absolutely packed with people, making it difficult to get anywhere near the fountain's edge, let alone find a spot to truly take it all in. it feels less like a tranquil roman square and more like a human traffic jam. while the beauty of the fountain is undeniable, the experience is definitely diminished by the sheer number of visitors. it's a testament to its fame, of course, but it makes it tough to appreciate the artistry. if you go, be prepared for a very crowded environment and maybe try to visit very early in the morning or late at night if you want even a glimmer of the experience you see in movies.

the walled city of cartagena is a historic gem that transports you back in time from the first step you take. surrounded by stone walls stretching some 11 kilometers, it was built over 400 years ago to protect the city from pirate attacks. entering through the iconic clock tower, also known as boca del puente, is a thrilling experience. this baroque gateway marks the boundary between modern and colonial. upon crossing, you'll find the plaza de los coches, with its lively atmosphere and stalls selling traditional sweets, and the plaza de bolívar, ideal for relaxing under trees and discovering the equestrian statue of the liberator. walking through the narrow cobblestone streets will allow you to admire flower-filled balconies, brightly colored facades, and small shops that reflect the blend of spanish, african, and indigenous cultures. within the city walls, highlights include las bóvedas, former warehouses converted into craft shops; the cathedral, with its beautiful dome; and the palace of the inquisition, now a spectacular museum. at nightfall, the place transforms. it's closed to traffic, live music plays in the plazas, and everything takes on a festive atmosphere that invites you to linger leisurely.

the walls of cartagena are a breathtaking reminder of the city's rich history, offering a perfect blend of colonial charm and modern beauty. walking along the massive stone fortifications, you can feel the echoes of the past while enjoying panoramic views of the city. what makes this place truly special is the contrast between the historic walls and the modern skyline in the background. on one side, you have the centuries-old fortresses, cannons, and charming colonial architecture; on the other, the sleek high-rises of bocagrande, creating a unique and picturesque fusion of old and new. at sunset, the views become even more magical, with golden hues reflecting off the walls and the caribbean breeze adding to the experience. whether you're a history lover or just looking for a beautiful spot to explore, the walls of cartagena are an absolute must-visit!

the wan chai pak tai temple, also known as yuk hui kung, was built by local residents of wanchai in 1863. the temple is dedicated to pak tai. there are several pak tai temples in hong kong and this is the biggest one. the temple is a declared monument of hong kong on 25 october 2019 and is protected under the antiquities and monuments ordinance. as of december 2024, there are 136 declared monuments in hong kong.

the white beach in boracay is simply breathtaking, especially during sunset. the view is absolutely stunning, with the sky turning into a canvas of warm colors as the sun dips below the horizon—an experience that's both peaceful and unforgettable. the beach itself is well-maintained and clean, with soft white sand and clear, inviting water. it’s a lively place, with lots of people gathering to enjoy the view, take pictures, and soak in the atmosphere. despite the crowds, it doesn’t feel overwhelming—instead, it adds to the vibrant and festive vibe of the area. in the evening, the energy shifts as music starts playing from a stage set up along the beach. the party atmosphere kicks in, with upbeat tunes and people dancing or just enjoying the moment. it's a great mix of natural beauty and fun social energy. overall, experiencing white beach in boracay, especially at sunset, is a must. whether you're looking for relaxation or a bit of nightlife, it offers the best of both worlds.

the whole trip was amazing! we had a great guide mohammad who brought us everywhere and showed us all the sites, felt very safe and looked after with him. when some people wanted to stay behind at some sites because we were tired, he sat with us and taught us games they play in the desert which was really cool! there was a lot of wind the day we were there and he helped us all make sure our scarves were tied correctly to protect our mouths from the sand, he was very helpful. the sites were amazing and the views were incredible, the car we were in was very comfortable. all the meals were really good with high quality ingredients, two of us were vegetarian (we did let them know before hand) and we were fully accommodated and didn't feel like we missed out at all. the meals were all traditional and we got a demonstration on how they cook their food outside under the ground for dinner. lunch was also during the hottest point of the day so we had a long break to rest up and eat away from the sun before setting out again. we didn't feel overworked or anything at all, a very good balance of activities and we also always had the option to stay back at any of the sites and have some tea if we weren't feeling up to it. the tents were unbelievable with amazing views, unfortunately it was cloudy during the morning but the window faces east, so if you get a clear day you can easily watch the sunrise from your bed. the beds were really comfortable with lots of blankets available in the room in case you get cold. we were also happy to see there were showers available, we didn't realise that! we had our own toiletries and i didn't notice any available so you should definitely bring your own shampoo and conditioner etc. i don't know what more we could've asked for with this trip, it was unbelievable and at such a good price, i cannot recommend this tour enough. met some really good people and had a great experience.

the woolworth building is an amazing and iconic skyscraper located in the tribeca neighborhood of lower manhattan, new york city. designed by renowned architect, cass gilbert and fully completed in april of 1913, the woolworth building is considered to be one of new york city’s earliest skyscrapers and reigned as the tallest building in the world from 1913-1929. it’s height is over 790 feet tall and has 60 floors, 30 of which is part of the base of the building and the other 30 is located at the building’s tower section. it is also one of the few new york destinations that has its own zip code. the construction of the woolworth building was financed by frank winfield woolworth, a successful pioneering retailer whom founded a popular brand of 5 & 10 cent stores in the early twentieth century. woolworth, whom the building is named after, built the skyscraper to house the headquarters of his retail empire, and serve as a living testament of his extraordinary wealth and power, and his immense success in the retail industry. other early tenants included the irving national bank, whom also helped to finance the building’s construction, prominent railroad companies; such as the new york central railroad, the union pacific railroad, and the telecommunications giant, the marconi wireless telegraph company of america. today, the building is jointly owned by the witkoff group & the kc properties. its resemblance to neo-gothic style cathedrals and its connections with huge and successful enterprises gave the woolworth building its most famous nickname, “the cathedral of commerce.” due to impressive architectural design, and its impact on urban planning and skyscraper construction, the woolworth building is listed on the national register of historic places and is recognized as a u.s national historic landmark. in february of 2019, i brought and treated my wife and myself for a guided tour of the woolworth building to celebrate our happy one year wedding anniversary!!! i also brought her to visit the building as a way of paying homage to the wonderful childhood memories she had when visiting and shopping at the woolworth stores with her late mother. both my wife and i were in absolute awe of the woolworth building’s beauty and glamour and were impressed with its limestone facade and glazed architectural terracotta panels. our tour guide did a fabulous job on explaining the building’s ground breaking architectural design, its inclusion of many modern day amenities, its notable tenants and its influence on future of skyscraper development. the highlight of our tour was getting the chance to see and learn about the building’s ornate and breathtaking lobby. it certainly is a sight to behold. my wife and i enjoyed seeing and taking pictures of lobby’s domed ceiling, the gorgeous glass mosaics that decorates the ceiling, and the plasters that hold grotesques which portray important figures that played a crucial role in the building’s development. sadly, the woolworth building is not open for public viewing or tours and this has been the case since the covid pandemic began in 2020. hopefully one day, and in the near future, the woolworth building will be open to public giving others the chance to visit and learn about this important new york landmark. my wife and i had an extraordinary time visiting and touring the woolworth building and highly recommended this location as must see destination, especially when it reopens its doors!!!

the yeongsil trail is a slightly challenging but rewarding trail. there is a good mix of rocky terrain, dirt paths and board walks, but the main challenge comes from the steepness of the hike and the distance that needs to be completed. it took about 5 hours to walk to the rest point and back, including a 1 hour lunch break and multiple rest/photo points. at more than 1km above sea level, while no prior training is necessary, it's definitely not a walk in the park. that being said, if you do make the journey, you will be rewarded with excellent views from the mountain overlooking the coastal areas that line jeju island, as well as the rock faces that can be seen from afar. in early june, the temperatures at the start of the climb is comfortable, but it does get very cold once you ascend above the treeline, and will remain cold for a good 70% of the trail. if you're driving, do come early, as you will need to look for parking spaces. if you're taking the bus, do note that you have to walk uphill for an additional 20-30 minutes to reach the starting point as the bus does not go all the way up. take note! this trail does not go up to the summit, though it's still a really beautiful trail!

there are lots of reviews here, so let's start with bullet points: - read other reviews! - the waterfall is beautiful! - rain - no go! - take two water-proof trashbags - take water/swimming shoes - take walking sticks - take swimming clothes - good hiking shoes is a must! - the trail is very steep, very dirty, and very slippery with very soft edges - plan for 1 hour "to", 1 hour "back" and 3 hours "there" - the path and the river sides are dirty, so wear appropriate clothes - ideally, have a spare set of clothes in the car. then: - park in the parking space as normal - go back (upwards) until the first sharp turn - look for the path, which goes sharply down - check the path with your walking sticks, as the sides are soft and may be dangerous to step on (roots and plants form a soft roof over tenths of meters of air) - watch for trail marks made with pieces of plastic and fabrics (to not get lost on the way back) - when you reach the river, put your walking shoes in the trashbag, and put on your water/swimming shoes - we found, that the easiest way up is via the boulders on the right - you have to climb them - to get closer to the waterfall, you will need to crawl on all fours (again, we found that the boulders on the right is the only way up) - the power of falling water and associated strong wind did not allow us to come closer than 3 meters. in any case, be very careful. do not underestimate the power of nature. - the rusty pools are the thermal pools - try them all. the water temperature is 35-40 degrees in some of them. - when you are ready to go home, put your swimming clothes in the second trashbag - at the forest entrance, change the shoes, put the wet ones in the first trashbag. - watch for the roadmarks! good luck!

there are some moments to be remembered when traveling and our tour with ozpaddle was definitely one of those for us. first ozpaddle travel path is unique as we started from the east and were lucky enough to witness all the green parks, city skyline and the naval boats before reaching the magnificent opera house. this side also seems to be much quieter with less boats and made things easier for us beginners to paddle! but, beyond the experience itself which was nothing short of amazing, we also met sophie, ozpaddle’’s owner who pioneered kayaking tours 16 year when it was not a buzz yet and who seems to do it with the same contagious passion, authenticity and aim. the high end, light and expensive gear she is using, her willingness to share her passion of kayaking and convert us to it, and all other little personal attention (that why she only accepts small groups) made us think that ozpaddle is not a business for sophie, more a calling or a mission she is on. inspiring ! if like us, you fancy a unique kayaking experience, that an experience is all about people first and think that small (local) business is beautiful and should be supported (she is alone running it!), then ozpaddle is a no-brainer. for us it was a fantastic start of our stay in sydney and a moment we will remember for a long time.

there is so much to do and see in dubrovnik and the area but if you have any interest in the history of the area or seafaring history you need to stop in this small museum. we were in dubrovnik for a day and so we didn't buy any pass or make specific plans. we came across the museum by accident and decided to go in and are glad we did. there are just a few rooms but the exhibits are of good or excellent quality. all the exhibits have an explanation in english (unlike some places we went in croatia). there are collections of artifacts grouped by type so you'll encounter several sextants and other navigational tools together. the building itself is of interest build on the city walls. outside the entrance you'll encounter some cannons pointing over the harbor and a very large anchor. inside you'll be able to see the harbor through windows and port holes. the first floor has small rooms with older artifacts and revealing the oldest knows aspects of the region. upstairs are displays of more recent seafaring events and objects. if you enjoy replicas of sailing ships you will enjoy the numerous models on the upper floor. there is a plaque that describes the ship, it's use and history. one of the display maps i didn't expect to appreciate so much showed in simple yet detailed display the trading routes and the role dubrovnik played in connecting the mediterranean world and beyond.

there’s not many reviews of zamerdius dive online but there should be! we dove tubbataha reef with them on april 5th for 5 days. a magical place! one of the best diving spots we’ve ever dove. contacting zamerdius was easy (google their website) . emma got back to me right away. in fact she always got back to me within hours after asking questions & for info. thanks emma! the process was smooth & you do need to wire money to their bank as they don’t take credit cards. the company is well organized. they are the only locally owned dive boat for t reef. the boat has room for 12 divers - for me, one of the big selling points of going with them. the other dive boats often have around 30 divers. i really liked our intimate group of 11. dive masters danny & bran were great. they are well seasoned & are good about safety. one highlight for me was that they really tried to avoid diving the same dive sites as the other boats at the same time. this would mean our 11 plus maybe 30-60 other divers!! i’ve dove around the world & so many dive boats all dive at the same time, same place but not zamerdius! not once did we dive at the same time as another dive boat! kudos to the crew! it’s a magical experience to dive with just our boat. the boat is well equipped. beds comfortable. it’s not 5 star but i didn’t care about that. there’s a hot shower. food was fantastic - every single meal! each crew knows what they are to do & it obviously a well oiled process that proves it’s self every single day. they do rent equipment from other dive shops & the equipment could have been better but danny was good at making sure everything worked properly. if you have your own equipment, it’s worth bringing but not always an easy thing to do. the price was lower than a lot of the bigger boats & that attracted me. sometimes people say you get what you pay for but i thought it was a good deal with 5 star service! if i ever dive tubbataha again i would definitely go with zamerdius! the owner also came onboard after the trip to make sure that we were happy & hear recommendations. a nice touch! thanks to the entire crew for making my trip fantastic.

they had some nice summer specials that were just right for hot weather- different salads. the fruit drinks were good and not too sweet. the service was good but slow- it took me time to get something i needed from time to time. but they are friendly and willing to serve. the apple strudel was good. it was worth getting. i have had better but definitely it was good. the whipped cream is not real whipped cream but it tasted good. i also like that the restaurant is at street level as that was convenient with my special needs son. the walls have posters of current and past things going on in the city. it is fun to look around and see them and see what this city puts together for entertainment.
they had some really good quality tea and the guy knew a lot about tea was very passionate about it! haven’t bought any tea in sri lanka up until now but splurged on wonderful tea in this shop :)!

they had to cancel the first reservation we made because of heavy winds and too high waves but were very transparent on this from the morning and informed us early enough around noon for our afternoon trip. they offered a new trip 2-3 days later. when we finally went, it was awesome. we saw four sperm whales, three beaked whales and five groups of dolphins (two different kinds). excellent trip. strong recommendation.
they have a little train you can pay like $1 and see everything. very nice! unfortunately the bay is pretty polluted though.

they have a promotion for a free drink if you leave 5 stars but i felt they did not meet my expectations for it. the food is good, but for the price, you’re really just paying for the name and their fresh ingredients. thought the red curry fish cakes with crab was sorta bland considering the price. their creamy egg omelette w/ pork and their salad was good and large enough to share. their drinks are actually perfect not too sweet or bland. service was alright and understood english but they’re not particularly friendly. overall, if you’re nearby it’s not awful but i probably wouldn’t go out of my way to come back when there’s other options . 7/10.

they have full package and complete water sports. if you're hungry after the activity, just head straight to their restaurant. its quite good for a quick bites.

they have indoor and outdoor activities. that can keep the children very busy. they have different activities. they have music, food, arts etc. outside, they have activities on the patio, an artificial turf green space. the children can water the plants, a huge sitting area with chairs and a fire pit etc

they have plenty halal things. i liked so much. they gave me a complementary nuts packet. their behaviour is so good. i bought so many snacks and halal ramen. got 5% discount also.

they have small but interesting exhibitions. i finished looking at the picasso exhibition from the summer of 2013 in 30 minutes. there were many works i had never seen before, such as posters from the exhibitions at the time. english is widely spoken, so it's not a problem.

they have the best and cleanest public washrooms here, they build a structure to look historic and made it into the nicest bathrooms, like wow, the parc itself if vast, huge, just green grass as far as the eye can see, there are a few spots of flowers like the plains of aberham, lots of benches on the water side facing lots of tall green bush, lots of old trees and endless room to wonder, its amazing having this oasis in the city.

they have the best goldfish selection anywhere. they stock the rare and hard to find wakin breed. the owner mentioned they source their goldfish from thailand. all beautiful and well priced. i highly recommend.

they have variety of water sports options, and offer very good packages. catamaran cruise and speed boat can be opted. they have an options for lunch/dinner date on isolated island, lovely dinner and great way to spend day in isolation doing water activities and exploring the blue lagoons and waterfalls. loved it.
they have vegan and gluten free options here so i was glad i was able to try! the vegetable ragu their vegan option and it was very delicious. service was excellent.
they have very nice clothes, both in design and fabric. the best store in santa cruz.
they have what you want
they helped us a lot with the design of the apartment, the result is great and the process was fun.

they literally are the best! i highly recommend them. genuine people. i won’t forget them. we did jet ski safari, flyboard (amazing), paddle. and if you could we would have come everyday of our stay 😄 thank you guys you rock!

they mostly say to visit early morning. i would recommend going at night. it is not crowded and you can experience the shrines lamps all turned on. it is calm and peaceful and a different experience from shrines during the day. it is also one of the few that have good lighting at night.

this a good way to get a quick overview of amsterdam. the view from the boat is different from land so it’s also a fun way to go through the canals. the audio guide was ok, there are different languages and the voice over was clear enough. however, there could have been more information given since there were many silent gaps and information was rather sparse considering we were going through many canals and passing many buildings. and the audio timing while passing by the landmarks were not in sync so sometimes we would miss it or it would be before we got to the place so a bit confusing at times. our captain did not add more information unlike the other reviewers experienced. other than this, it’s still a worthwhile thing to do, at least for fun.

this a vibrant and revitalized area in cartagena, possibly the historic center or a popular tourist spot. the efforts to enhance safety and restore the streets have clearly made a positive impact, making it a more welcoming environment for visitors. the local stalls offering trinkets, clothes, and colombian candies add a charming touch, giving tourists a chance to experience authentic local culture. if you're planning to visit or share this place with others, it seems like it's a great time to explore and enjoy everything it has to offer!

this adventure is totally overpriced and you get very low quality food for a lot of money, but the nature part of the w-trek was amazing and very beautiful. we hiked from central to grey and it was a wonderful experience. the hiking itself would be more fun and enjoyable if the trails would be better maintained. the park authority is not doing a good job to keep the trails in good condition. the accommodations and food packages are totally overpriced, it’s a rip off. the quality of the food at central and frances was really bad. for dinner (usd55 pp per day) we received watered down soup on both days. it was awful. the main course was cold by the time we had it on the table. cold rice and cold mashed potatoes isn’t very appealing. the lunch box that we received at central which costs about usd30-35 was a dry bun with one slice of ham and one slice of cheese. no mayo, no mustard, no lettuce, no tomatoes. a bag of nuts that had an expiration date of jan 2025 (we were there in april 2025), and an apple. the second day we ordered vegetarian, so they put some lettuce and a slice of tomato on the dry bun. breakfast was very simple, watered down juice that really tasted more like water than juice, white bread, a mini portion of scrambled eggs, ham and cheese. for usd30! one would expect for the $$ that they charge, you would get some energy loaded really good quality food that you need when doing the w-trek. except for the check-in desks and the bar, staff at central was not friendly, actually some were really rude. after dinner they kick you out of the dining area to make space for the next shift, which i understand if the place is fully booked but this was the end of the season, half of the dinning area was empty and we still couldn’t stay there. at frances dinner and breakfast were slightly better but the lunch box was the same 'rubber sandwich'. staff was at least very friendly. paine grande and grey had the best food (buffet style) and also the friendliest staff though the tents are very small and at grey the tents don’t have wooden platforms. our tent was on a slope so we constantly kept sliding into the same corner. again, overall it was a great experience that i don't want to miss but the bitter taste of being ripped of will remain. do your research before you book any packages with any operator. the park doesn't make it easy to book everything yourself but you can save a lot of money if you invest the research time and more importantly you don't pay a lot of money for crap food.

this ancient and aesthetically pleasing monastery, situated on the outskirts of leh, features a substantial, multi-story statue of lord buddha within its walls. the serene and captivating views from the monastery are complemented by its centuries-old architecture, which, while similar to other monasteries, distinguishes itself through its unique exterior color palette. the overall experience is remarkable, especially considering the high-altitude location. the monastery is expansive, requiring visitors to ascend several stairs to explore its multiple levels, typically ranging from four to seven floors.

this april we had the privilege to attend this masterfully and beautifully crafted event. when you say vienna, you think of classical music. here you can enjoy all of that and forget about everything else. we enjoyed our time here and will live in our memories forever. i want to congratulate your entire team for bringing us this joy. doing those concerts daily ain't easy, but i'm sure it's worth it. i highly recommend to book the first rows to enjoy the maximum experience. we also booked the dinner package and enjoyed a beautiful evening at the gerstner restaurant nearby. the concert itself it's a masterpiece, put together by great opera singers and musical players. you really feel like you're attending the new year's concert. the orangery building is nothing short of spectacular and the light show on the ceiling is breathtaking. would come again, for sure.

this aquarium shop carries advanced aquatic hobbyist supplies, fish, and plants. a must visit if you like aquascaping/aquarium and dont have much in your area. i will forgive them for not being open on time (so be aware of that if you're trying to hit them up right at opening. the employee was nice. there was only one person available at the time to help all the customers with questions and fish/plants. tanks were clean and clear. well taken care of aquatic store.
this arch on the passway inside the temple of literature is featured on the back of the 100000 ðong banknote, and apparently, holds a very important significance in the academic realm of hanoi.

this area consist of a network of jungle trails where you can trek. there many tracks that you can walk and the natural forest canopy provides a wonderful refreshing air with minimal pollution. many kind of flora that you can enjoy along the way. you can track anyway between 45 mins to over 4 hours.
this area is amazing, not just for swimming, but also for those who enjoy capturing beautiful landscapes through photography. don't miss out on this stunning location!
this area is very beautiful and peaceful .. i loved it.. but needs to study before you go as its very rich in facts and historical details

this area of mount zion is interesting to explore (see the bathroom area too!), king david's tomb has separate entrances for men and women, and is sometimes crowded, like when we visited in november 2022. this is probably not the real location of david's tomb, but this mount zion (and the nearby last supper room) is worth a trip for serious religious people.

this area showcases one of nature’s most fascinating wonders—natural geothermal springs so hot they can cook food! one of the highlights is trying the traditional “cozido” stew, which is slow-cooked underground for around six hours using the natural heat from the earth. the result is a rich, tender, and flavorful dish you won’t find anywhere else. you’ll definitely notice the distinct smell of sulfur in the air—it’s part of the experience and a reminder of the powerful geothermal activity below. a must-see attraction that blends nature, culture, and cuisine in a truly memorable way. highly recommended.

this astonishing, millennium-old gate offers a captivating glimpse into cairo's multifaceted history, acting as a profound separator between the medieval opulence of the saladin-era renaissance and the realities of modern urban life. it's truly fascinating to witness the stark interplay between the historical wealth and the contemporary surroundings, providing a unique perspective on the city's continuous evolution.

this attraction was less a garden and more of a historical insight to the former kings and the architecture of the ancient buildings on site. while beautiful on it's own, i would recommend a tour, which require a reservation. this is deep inside the palace structures so get their early and wear comfortable shoea.

this balloon safari was one of the highlights of our trip to tanzania! they did such a great job accommodating our large family of 12 which included multiple young kids (our youngest was 6)! many of our kids said that the balloon safari over the serengeti was one of the highlights of their lives in terms of experiences they have had. we had such a wonderful time viewing the serengeti from the air and it gives such a different perspective. on our hour long flight we got to see four lions, three cheetahs, multiple herds of cape buffalo, gazelles, a herd of elephants, secretary birds, giraffes, eland and so much beautiful scenery. our flight was piloted by captain muhammed who was the first tanzanian trained hot air balloon pilot and he did an amazing job catching the wind currants and pointing out wildlife. to top it off, we were greeted with champagne (and juice for the kids) when we landed and then picked up by jeeps and ushered to a wonderful english breakfast out in the bush! amazing! the service and quality is well worth the price!

this bar was a hidden gem! the atmosphere was cozy and stylish, with great music and even better drinks. the bartender was super friendly and made one of the best cocktails i’ve ever had. they had a great selection of japanese whisky too. a perfect spot for a chill night out—highly recommend!

this beach had some nice black sand. very fine and neat to look at. not as many folks on this beach as hamdeok beach, but it is both smaller and located much more residential. when i was there in 27 sep 2020, there seemed to be a lot of construction around the each which is why it lost a star. not a ton of benches or places to sit either. had a few restaurants near by as well.

this beach is a hidden gem ! the crystal-clear water is so calm and relaxing ️, and it feels like a true local spot. perfect if you want to escape the crowds ☀️. plus, it's super easy to get to, with parking nearby

this beach is absolutely stunning, probably one of the best in dubrovnik! it's about a 20-30 minute walk from the city, which was a little hot, but totally worth it. you can also drive or take a boat there. the beach has everything – you can rent chairs for about €7 each, or just use your own towel. there are restaurants for drinks and food, and it's a very family-friendly and calm atmosphere, a nice break from the city crowds. it was a bit crowded, but still one of the most beautiful beaches we've ever been to!

this beach is located after kvalvika beach, it can be reached via a path that splits into two: the upper part is very difficult to pass and dangerous (i do not recommend it), the lower part is slightly easier (you will find a broken rope that is used to climb, alternatively you can pass along the rocks but they are slippery and if the sea is rough i do not recommend it). from the beach you can reach a clearing with a beautiful lake.
this beach is one of my favorite all. an emerald color and quiet beach, taking a wedding picture popular place.

this beach is really really beautiful and when you visit udo island, you should visit this beach. the sand is like a popcorn and it doesn't stick on your feet for a long time. it's easy to remove it. anyway, the water is super clear and beautiful!

this beach located in front of the kempinski resort, right next to the baie lazare beach was a great find and was especially calm and sheltered (with a mild current) for snorkelling last wednesday and thursday when the waves were particularly strong in other parts of mahe island and majority of the beaches were covered in seaweed and had poor visibility in both the west and east coast. visibility was decent between 3-5m and we spotted a massive porcupine ray on both days, a large school of striped eel catfish (in hundreds, maybe thousands!) and a variety of other marine life such as trumpetfish, parrot fish, angel fish, spot-fin porcupine fish etc. bring some water shoes or fins and be careful with the sea urchins and giant porcupine puffer fish! they can be uncomfortably close at times in the shallow waters.

this beach stretches quite a bit and gives beach goers a lot of prime spaces for sunbathing. just keeping driving towards the north end of the beach to find parking. beach was clean and there was a bathroom where one can change. some shaded areas were available and the view was wonderful. the waves were a bit strong and not a good place for the young ones.

this beach used to be quite nice, but it has become incredibly busy, little space between the sun beds, expensive and unmaintained. the staff is not even bothering to clean the rubbish next to the sunbeds. but they're very proactive to charge you for their dirty and expensive sun beds. shame :(

this beautiful baroque monastery is located near prague castle. it is a place of pilgrimage to the virgin mary with the baroque church of the nativity, richly decorated in rococo style with many frescoes and cherubs, and a copy of the holy house, surrounded by cloisters and chapels. the tower houses a carillon of 27 bells that performs the loreto service (every hour from 10:00 to 17:00). the loreto treasure includes a rare collection of liturgical objects and other votive offerings from the 16th to 18th centuries, the most famous of which is the "prague sun" - a tabernacle encrusted with 6,222 diamonds.

this beautiful buddhist temple is a true gem—peaceful, serene, and rich in cultural charm. the surrounding area is filled with superb vegetarian restaurants, making it an ideal spot for mindful travelers and food lovers alike. the public toilets are impressively clean and well maintained, adding to the comfort of the visit. a perfect place to relax, reflect, and enjoy a nourishing meal nearby.

this beautiful building houses gibney’s downtown location. gibney is the home of move to move beyond storytellers. a collective which seeks to inform the public on gender-based violence and trauma through storytelling.

this beautiful lake is located about 6 km from city center. after visiting oldest buddhist temple tran quoc pagoda in hanoi, which is next to lake, we stopped here for some time. it's beautiful lake ideal for photo opportunity. three were few few vendors around selling souvenirs. we had cold fresh coconut water which was very nice. worth visiting for few minutes...

this beautiful location in lynn valley is my natural gym... the most beautiful place for trail running and day walk/hike. lots of options for any level and low or high intensity cardio workout. our evening training is to do the round trip 8 km trail running along the riverside. on weekends we enjoy running to norvan falls and longer plans is our seasonal hike and running all the way to hanes valley and grouse mountain. if you like to do a kind of easy hike in a beautiful loop then lynn loop is one of the best options for those looking for around 1 hour in and out easy hike. previously it was all free parking in the area but recently there is seasonal pay parking in effect. the parkings are limited to hour or full day so make sure to choose the right parking time accordingly to your plan and for sure underestimate unexpected nature events in case you couldn't make it on-time the parking is being watched frequently.

this beautiful multi-level garden might have been highlight of prague visit. i’ve stumbled on this garden quite accidentally observing a guide of one of tourist groups pointing out to unassuming entryway. had only less than half-hour to spend and fortunately it was more than enough. modest price of admission is well-worth excitement of suddenly getting into multi-layered garden with stunning views of the city with each level ascent. pretty cool place, don’t miss it.

this beautiful shrine was so peaceful. got there at 6am via taxi and only saw 3 other people. the latterns were still glowing on the trail. we got to walk through and take our time without feeling rushed through prayers and photos. on our walk down, we started passing several families and busses. glad we went early!

this beautiful spot is perfectly located in the city center. while the terrace offers a lovely view, the interior inside has an elegant vintage look that could transport you back in time. the staff were attentive and made us feel welcome. the food was delicious, with generous portions that left us too full to try the apfelstrudel. i did have the hot chocolate, though, and it was absolutely amazing, rich, velvety, and comforting. such a true gem and a great representative for vienna coffee houses.

this beautiful, unique building was the royal library of the deoksugung palace at the late xix century. jungmyeongjeong or "hall of everlasting brightness" was constructed by afanasy seredin-sabatin, a ukraine born architect, steersman-pilot and reporter, who was the first european (ukrainian and russian) architect to work in the korean empire from 1890 to 1904.

this bird park is a lovely place to visit! it’s not very big, but large enough to enjoy a nice walk and spend a couple of relaxing hours. the variety of birds is impressive, and everything is well-maintained. there are cozy rest areas and refreshing drinks available, which make the visit even more pleasant. highly recommended for nature and animal lovers!

this boat definitely exists...i've just had a great week on it...not sure why someone would say otherwise?? anyway, the crew were all lovely, competent, helpful and obviously knew their job well. the 2 person room below deck is a bit small so definitely take one above deck if you can, but otherwise it is good for a budget boat. the vessel is well maintained with a captain that has decades of experience on the reef and the food was excellent.

this boat is well maintained and definitely better-looking than most others we saw along the route. we stayed in one of the luxury cabins, which was spacious and comfortable. unfortunately, that’s where the positives end. the food was incredibly basic, repetitive, and often scarce. if you were one of the last to grab a plate, the trays might already be empty. for what we paid, it was shockingly underwhelming — you could easily buy better meals for the entire trip at a local warung for under $30. calling this a “luxury” boat is misleading, especially when you’re paying nearly double what other boats charge and getting the same generic itinerary. and speaking of the itinerary — it’s the same cookie-cutter route everyone follows. all the boats depart on wednesdays and saturdays, so every stop is crowded with hundreds of people. at times, it felt like a chaotic, off-season spring break. day one started with a long and disorganized 5-hour bus ride across lombok from bangsal to a random harbor where the boat was moored. we sailed for just two hours before stopping for sunset at a trash-strewn beach shared with seven other boats — imagine 250 people squeezed onto a dirty shore. on day two, we woke up early for what was advertised as a whale shark encounter. in reality, it was a disturbing display: a fisherman tube-feeding a whale shark while squirting water at its head to keep it visible, all while 50 snorkelers circled around. i refused to take part in such an unethical and pathetic spectacle. after that, we sailed non-stop for 24 hours, with just a quick swim break to break the monotony. day three — finally something worthwhile. we arrived in komodo, visited the park, saw the dragons, swam at a pink beach, and finished the day with a climb for sunset views. it was beautiful, but once again, we shared the moment with hundreds of people from 40 other boats. day four was a couple of beach stops before reaching labuan bajo. in total, the “four-day” trip is really just than 70 hours — most of it spent either sailing endlessly or stuck in crowds. would i recommend it? absolutely not. for a couple spending $1000, you’re much better off relaxing for a couple of days on a nice beach, then flying to labuan bajo and doing a focused two-day, one-night komodo tour. you’ll experience the best parts and you’ll definitely eat better.

this breathtaking view is absolutely free and not many know about it. it’s situated on the 55th floor of ion orchard and in order to take the lift right up to the top, you’ll have to walk into the art gallery which is also free. absolutely gorgeous view on a clear day or during sunset. if you like, there is also a restaurant where you can dine which has the view of marina bay sands etc.

this bridge connects downtown vancouver to vancouver and has fantastic views, as shown in the pictures and videos showing granville island, and marvelous views of false creek connecting to the ocean. pedestrians can walk on the side of the bridge and enjoy the views and sit on the benches as shown in the pictures and videos and enjoy your brisk walk.

this business definitely deserves a 5 star rating. everything they did was top-notch. the guides (ofir and tamar ) were knowledgable, friendly and engaging. truly passionate and eager to share their experiences in an honest and open way. the vip service arriving/departing the tlv airport is enough alone to recommend israel unlimited. i would not travel to israel again without it. worth every shekel.

this café served the best chocolate i’ve ever had in my life — rich, smooth, and unforgettable. the atmosphere was equally delightful, with a warm and inviting tone that made me want to linger. i would definitely come back again.

this camp has particularly took care to small things in providing basic requirements in the room. i recommend this camp for sure. niyaz bhai had been so generous all the time. even the room prices are pretty average. and food is so tasty.
