this camp is really nice. as soon as you get out of the door, they greet you with a warm towel to refresh yourself after your travel. the staff is absolutely great. wilford the manager was excellent and attending to my needs in any issues, i may have had. faith was so kind at the front desk as well as the remainder of the staff. you won’t even realize you’re staying in a tent. the room was so clean and the shower was nice and hot. i was super impressed that they put a hot water bottle by your feet inside the bed so when you get in, you’re able to warm your feet and the bed is so comfortable off you better hope you don’t have an early morning safari because you may oversleep. i’ve never seen any hotel do that it was such a nice surprise after a dip in the temperature outside. would definitely stay here again.

this camp made our wadi rum trip something we’ll never forget. from the moment we arrived, the staff treated us like old friends. the views are unreal red sand all around, huge rock formations, and sunsets that make you just stop and stare. our tent was clean, cozy, and had everything we needed. dinner was amazing proper jordanian food cooked fresh, and you could really taste the love in it. breakfast the next morning was just as good, simple, fresh, and exactly what you need to start a day in the desert.

this camp was truly magical, with beautiful sunsets overlooking the delta from the view of the deck. the lodging felt very clean and safe, and i loved the view of the delta from our room. the staff did an amazing job with providing an amazing environment to experience the magic of the okavengo delta. kaiser was an amazing guide and we loved getting to know him! we loved our bush walk, game drives, boat tours, and canoe rides. this camp has it all! the food was also amazing. definitely would love to come back here one day! i was sad to leave!

this castle is beautiful as you approach it. the grounds are well kept, and the views are amazing. there are multiple levels to see, and it's really well intact. my husband and i made a day of it doing castles, and we're glad we made it in time before closing for this one. there are lots of great historic sites and food nearby. this one is a must-see.

this castle is stunning, sitting on its own wee island with a beautiful bridge across to see it. i would definitely recommend stopping off here for some really nice pictures and to learn more about the castles history. you can pay a fee to go inside the castle walls which is fair. you also need to pay a fee to cross the bridge and walk around the outside of the castle which i thought was quite unfair. we came back on the way back from skye (after 5pm) and got across for free.

this cave is a significant site in the ramayana. the cave is located behind ravana falls. it is 2 km from ella town. the cave requires a climb up a steep path with steps, which can be challenging. the archaeological evidence suggests the cave was used for human habitation 25,000 years back. the legend says ravana used the cave network to hide princess sita and also for strategic purposes. the cave is a significant site in the ramayana.

this cave is next to the first attraction, about 10 minutes by boat. you can ask your guide. the ticket is 600 and you need to pay at the entrance of the cave. you need to walk through water about up to your chest to reach the entrance and get a safety helmet. there are stairs inside the cave, which is very narrow and you can only enter or exit at a time.
this cave winery was a great introduction into the unique traditional methods of santorini. the volcanic mineralogy was well showcased in these wines. definitely worth buying a couple of bottles.

this chapel nestled in the streets of old san juan is a mandatory stop since it is located next to the parque de las palomas. it is very old, small and cozy in plain sight, with its virgins and crucifixes.

this chapel was built between 1753 and 1780, tucked away in the corner of the old walled city of san juan is a tiny chapel. it was built on top of the ancient stone walls that protected puerto rico’s capital in 1753 to celebrate a miracle. since then, tens of thousands of faithful visitors have come to this humble chapel to pray for cures. it is near to famous la fortaleza street. as stated by guide - it is said, that in the year 1750 cristo street was host to a horse race where one of the participants could not stop his horse and fell off the cliff. the secretary of government at the time, don tomás mateo prats is said to have invoked the santo cristo de la salud and that the young man who fell off the cliff was saved. and so, the secretary of government ordered the construction of the chapel on sight to honor the miracle. it was later revealed that the young man died, but still, this chapel has a distinctly spiritual feel to it. how to better start your journey than in this miracle sight!

this charming beachfront park is an ideal destination for families and friends looking to gather and enjoy the outdoors. with its picturesque views of the ocean and soft sand, it's a perfect spot for picnics, leisurely strolls, or simply soaking in the sun. the park features ample parking, making it convenient for visitors, along with well-maintained public restrooms for added comfort. whether you're planning a fun day out with loved ones or a relaxing afternoon by the water, this park offers a welcoming atmosphere for everyone.

this charming little green space in nolita feels like a secret garden tucked between buildings. scattered with classical sculptures and flowering paths, it offers a refreshing pause from the surrounding city buzz. when we visited, one gate was open while the other remained locked, and puddles had formed due to rain—perhaps a drainage system would help. despite its modest size, the garden feels both historic and spontaneous, like a community space that grew organically. it’s not a destination on its own, but a perfect detour if you’re nearby.
this church is the start of via dolorosa , believed to be where jesus christ was condemned to die on the cross.

this church is truly a hidden gem that leaves visitors amazed. the chapel’s stunning stained glass windows are its main attraction, showcasing vibrant colors and intricate medieval designs that create a magical atmosphere inside. even though it’s a relatively small space, the history and artistry packed into it make it a must-visit for anyone interested in architecture or parisian history. i'm using paris museum pass, it allows me to skip the long ticket lines, however, even if you book in advance, you have to wait in the specific line assigned to your booked time, you can’t enter directly. also, early access is not possible, they follow your reservation time strictly. remember to make a reservation online in advance. this helps secure entry at a preferred time and avoids the stress of waiting in crowds, which can get quite busy, especially during peak tourist seasons. the chapel is located on île de la cité, near other famous landmarks like notre-dame, making it easy to include in a day of sightseeing. the visit doesn’t take long, usually under an hour, but it leaves a lasting impression thanks to the breathtaking stained glass that tells stories from centuries ago. overall, sainte-chapelle is a fantastic stop for travelers. i enjoyed a smooth and memorable experience exploring one of the city’s most beautiful and historic sites.

this cinema left me underwhelmed, feeling like a relic from two decades ago. parking scooters is a logistical nightmare for movie-goers and mall visitors alike: you have to switch off the engine and push the bike through a cramped, poorly ventilated area with far too few spaces. elevators crawl along, so a lot of people resort to the escalators. reaching the theater itself is confusing and time-consuming, you must navigate from the restaurant floor to the sixth-floor cinema, and the signage isn’t helpful. once inside, staff appeared indifferent. because i’d bought my ticket online, i was directed to a lone self-service machine: only one qr scanner worked, it had no backlight, and no one offered guidance. the guard stationed outside seemed equally disengaged, acting more like a gatekeeper to keep patrons from entering early than someone eager to assist. both the screening rooms and the restrooms feel date, as if they haven’t seen a renovation since 2007. all in all, this branch pales in comparison to other cgv locations and fails to deliver a satisfying movie experience

this city park appears to be more of an amusement park than a serious zoo with conservation and the welfare of the animals as the main priority. to be honest, i missed most of the animals and just concentrated on the island in the centre of the boating lake. some visitors were feeding the monkeys through the wire netting. it's clearly a big favourite with young families at the weekend, and although some people were teasing the animals, most were generally respectful, and the children were just curious. pricing for children is by height (!), great if your kids are late developers. i was charged 50,000vnd as a foreign tourist.

this club is more to edm music. we guide by staff from entrance (donut) hie a nice guy and friendly help us to look for table. (sweet person) the atmosphere here is great and you can enjoy it with fun.

this columbia road flower market is one of my favorite markets that i've visited so far. it runs on sundays from 8am to around 3pm and gets quite busy. there are many stalls selling a variety of potted plants, and it's great to see so many dog owners enjoying the atmosphere. the lively scene is enhanced by buskers performing throughout the market. in addition to flowers, there are also cafes & small shops nearby selling floral-related products and decorations. the staff in the shops are friendly and welcoming. overall, it’s a fantastic place to visit on a weekend, and i highly recommend it!!

this column is topped with the winged lion of saint mark, the symbol of venice’s patron saint. it stands proudly at the entrance to piazza san marco, alongside its twin, the colonna di san todaro. erected in the late 12th century, the column is believed to have been brought from constantinople (modern-day istanbul). it represents venice’s later spiritual identity, after saint mark became the city’s official protector.

this community garden behind jefferson market library is an oasis in the heart of greenwich village. they have benches to sit and relax or read. they have a small fountain by a bed of flowers. it's a beautiful space.

this company was awesome! our family of six had the best time last week rafting the 5 mile athabasca. we had for kids with us ranging from 6-17. all of them voted this was one their favorite things during our ten day canadian rockies vacation. ollie was our river guide and he was amazing! he kept us entertained the entire time, and also shared lots of really cool stories and history about jasper and the surrounding areas. the weather was very cool and a little rainy when we went, but the company had us more than prepared. our wet suits kept us very warm, and everything (the driving/changing/etc) was very efficient. we can’t recommend this company enough. please take the trip up the ice fields pkwy to jasper, stay a few days, and have an awesome time rafting with jasper rafting adventures!

this company was terrible. we were supposed to reach another tent camp of the same company placed in the middle of nowhere (serengeti kusini).with our driver we rescued another vehicle that was stuck in no man's land and it took us two hours of tries to eventually realise the car was going nowhere. we took the people we saved in our car, but it was too late to reach kusini before sunset, so we accompanied them to south serengeti ndutu lodge owned by the same company and asked if it was possible to either sleep there or for some of them who knew the way to the other lodge to escort us since it's not at all easy to find and it was getting dark. the manager deputy (because the one on charge was drunk) wrote to his company chat group, but after receiving no answer after two hours (and with the local ranger saying that it was now too dark and dangerous to try to reach the other place) he gave us a tent (with a broken window that made it freezing inside). the next morning they told us that we had to pay almost 400$ for that night, despite never saying anything the night before and never giving us the chance to decide if we wanted to try to reach our lodge before dark. they treated us as a bother and not as clients until it was time to pay, and they didn't even give our driver a blanket to cover himself during the cold night, or water to wash in the morning. overall extremely disappointed and would never recommend this company to anyone.

this company’s work vehicle backed into our car trying to park in an illegal/ no parking pick up zone. it dented and scraped the front of our car. the driver admitted fault and assured us the boss would be in touch to remedy the situation. we’ve tried to reach out and haven’t heard back at all. our car is still damaged due to driver negligence. very disappointing. update 7/23/2025 3:15 pm. called and was told “that’s why you have insurance” and to “deal with it with insurance” then we were hung up on. despite their initial response telling us to reach out directly which we’ve been trying to do. this company wrongfully backed into our vehicle and is refusing to cooperate amicably.

this cooking class done by memoire siem reap hotel. i was picked up from hotel and driving to chreav market to buy ingredients to cook then we are straight to the local village with nice green view and understand about people life over there. we can say that services are awesome staff and chief were lovely.
this cooking class was a lot of fun, the chef was very nice and the food was amazing ! i would highly recommend this activity during your trip to cartagena !

this cooking class was fantastic! the instructor was knowledgeable and engaging, making the experience both fun and educational. the hands-on approach allowed us to create delicious dishes with fresh ingredients, and i left feeling more confident in the kitchen. highly recommend for anyone looking to improve their cooking skills and enjoy a great time! thanks to dary and her partner ---
this cruise will get you around amsterdam city. the boat captain will give you a glimpse of amsterdam buildings and histories. it's a smooth sailing along the canal and open bay. great ride.
this cute area provide you a chance to seat and drink a cup of coffee/eat or just rest in the middle of usually a crowded place:) sometimes it can be crowded too or hot. but overall it's nice :)

this desert camp in wadi rum has everything you need, including really nice service from the staff and a generous buffet dinner demonstrating traditional bedouin cooking! but we especially enjoyed the sunset desert 4x4 tour with our driver aziz! his friendly conversation, really enjoyable driving and local knowledge of wadi rum was a highlight of our stay in the desert! if you’re staying at rum magic nights make sure to book a 4x4 tour through them!

this difficult-to-find museum is worth the search for a wonderful break from the crowds and heat and a very different view of the city walls than you get from above. that’s more than just the building where you enter; make sure to go out the back and follow the paths all the way to the southern/seaside wall. there are some bizarre “art” installations as well as stellar views with nobody else nearby.

this dinner far exceeded our expectations, it was pricey at $90 per person and $45 per child but we left feeling like we got our money's worth, the staff and entertainment were great i was really suprised by the level of talent from the performers. food was all you can eat and served "family style" everything was fresh and well seasoned. we had salmon bbq ribs, corn,biscuts, baked beans, mashed potatoes, salad and warm berry cobbler. the only thing i didnt care for was that soft drinks were not included in the ticket price however water and iced tea were on the table at no additional cost. would definitely do it again.

this distillery has a wide selection of products that can be sampled after the tour. the variety and quality is excellent. the gentleman who serves the tastings is very knowledgeable, friendly and fun. tell him the kind of alcoholic beverages that you like and he can make an appropriate suggestion to sample. kudos to you, andre! their gin - goshawk - is quite good but the white rum may be a little to harsh for some. their aged brandies - 10 & 20 yo - are great as are virtually all of their liqueurs. you are sure to find something that you like. highly recommend making a stop
this diving club was very nice, i learned to dive with a professional mentor, i like it

this dog sledding experience was unforgettable! best thing we did in alaska! happy trails has multiple locations in case of bad conditions. they accommodated our group last minute after another company canceled our run. our guide was so great, and the dogs were absolutely a force to be reckoned with! they were so sweet and so strong! you can tell they love what they are doing. thanks for the experience of a lifetime!
this educational institution is 7 centuries old and although it is not in use in that fashion anymore, it is still well maintained. there is a small section you can visit and enjoy the architecture.
this educational institution is 7 centuries old and although it is not in use in that fashion anymore, it is still well maintained. there is a small section you can visit and enjoy the architecture.

this elevated lookout of new york city’s manhattan skyline, which is located at squibb park bridge in brooklyn heights, is an absolutely lovely spot!! if you’re in bklyn and looking for a beautiful space to view the incredible + iconic architecture of nyc (without being overrun by tourists), this is your spot!!

this entertainment and educational park about equestrian and agricultural culture is a place for the whole family to enjoy. the "travesía" show tells the story of the horse, a musical and equestrian theatrical performance that deserves to be enjoyed in a wonderful amphitheater-style arena.

this event was absolutely incredible. i was scared at first but after the first 2 zip lines it was purely amazing. there were 7 lines total and took about 1.5 hrs to complete. it was absolutely worth it and i highly recommend if you visit pr !!

this excursion is pretty incredible! we did it with our four kids ranging from 15 to 8 and it was perfect for all of them. the buggy ride was super fun and you could stay as clean or get as dirty as you want. the zip lining was incredible. you get free lunch, which is always a win. their photo package was not very expensive. it was $90 for a group of six. you couldn’t take pictures on the zip line and they got some pretty great pictures of us driving through the mud with our buggies. well worth the money. i wouldn’t call the safari a safari. but you got to ride in a gigantic army truck and see more of the beautiful countryside. the horseback riding was fun and through some beautiful countryside. everything was very well run and organized. our tour guide went with us to every single activity. it was nice to have someone show you exactly what to do and when to do it. we did book through go majestic so that might not be included if you book online. the only downsides were that we came home with a few bug bites, but you’re out in the middle of the country and it is humid so it’s to be expected. the buggies kept breaking down. my husband‘s wheel actually came off. it was kind of funny though. but it was kind of to be expected in another country. my kids didn’t love the food, but that’s just because it was all local dishes. i thought it was okay. they didn’t nickel and dime you for everything. the lunch was included. they weren’t constantly asking for tips. there is a place to fill up your water bottles so you don’t have to buy water. you get a free locker. good pricing for picture packages. it was definitely more organized and cheaper than other excursions we’ve done in the dominican republic. with a lot more included for the money. i would highly recommend it! i’d go again for sure!

this excursion is so fun. we went with the jesus team and they were so fun and made sure everyone had a good time. it’s packed with activities and chill vibes. lots of time to go to the beach, shop for souvenirs and other goods. the water is beautiful. check them out you won’t regret it !

this excursion was amazing from start to finish. george who was our guide was the star of the day, extremely kind, funny and knows how to keep people engaged throughout. pick up was prompt and we set off to the first snorkelling stop. i absolutely loved the snorkelling as there was a vast array of fish and they came up really close. it was so beautiful. we couldn't go to the cocoloco beach due to the seaweed situation but jason, the guy who cuts the coconuts open for the coconut drinks came to on the catamaran to do it. the drinks were nice and light on rum which was good. then the floating kitchen arrived with our lunch. very tasty and good portions too of seafood (lobster, fish, prawns and grilled octopus with chips). the drinks flowed freely all through the excursion and all members of staff worked hard to ensure we had a great time. great music on board throughout too. had a final stop at a shallow natural pool where most people had a relaxing dip in the sea. even though it rained for a while during the excursion, it didn't impact on the overall fun in any way. this company certainly knows how good excursions should be run. highly recommended.👌🏾

this experience took almost 5 hours, but you only be underwater. for about 10 or 15 minutes period it was very unorganized, and i made my reservation on their site, but then they said they were full, so he tried to squeeze me in, but the ac on the van. kept going out and we were picking people up. for well over an hour before we headed to the marina, once we got there, all of the waiting and the unorganized set up made it very frustrating. the experiences fun, but with everything that you have to go through. and it take up half your day, it can be a letdown.

this experience was amazing! we were lucky enough to be part of a small group that included the parents of the american volunteers (translators). cesar was an incredibly knowledgeable guide. we saw some massive tortoises, did some bird watching and went into a lava tunnel. as an added plus we were met with a glass of fresh orange juice and were allowed to grab any mandarins off of their trees and munch on them (not inside the national park area) as we toured around.

this experience was amazing!! using the seongpanak trail (accessible by bus from the city), the trail was easy to follow and provided really scenic views the whole way up. 9.6km total, you have to reach a checkpoint about 3/4 of the way up by 1:30pm in order to keep going, and leave the summit by 2:30pm. i started at about 9:30 am and had plenty of time. the whole hike is not easy! the first half is relatively flat, but the terrain gets very tricky and to complete the whole hike took a lot of effort. our fast pace took us 3.5hrs up and 3 hrs back down again, but would expect it to take most people longer. nowhere to buy anything along the way, so take enough food and water. entirely worth it for some stunning views and a fabulous full-day experience.

this experience was incredible and breathtaking from start to finish. hashem is an amazing and smart guide who lets you feel at home very quickly and easily in the wadi rum desert. he explained lots of things very well and cooked amazing food for us. this was without a doubt the highlight of our trip to jordan. we got to see the sunset in the most amazing places and sleept under the start, which led to fantastic photos as well. i would definetely recommend this day tour in the jeep.

this experience was out of this world. bedouins love their desert and animals and that makes a big difference. i loved everything about my trip to the desert. amazing views, traditional food was so delicious, and people are so nice. it feels so relieving to be without internet connection. you get to really enjoy the desert and what it has to offer. big thanks to morgan, mohamed (manager) and mohamed (guide). can’t wait to do it again

this experience was turnt up ! nice ride through new orleans, great views, we went right at sunset. food fire, drinks great, def something great to do away from the city to see the real parts of new orleans. great customer service & staff ! 10/10 def recommend ! byob

this experience was well worth it! a super fun and easy way to get around the island and see different views! it was a beautiful sunny day! it’s nice and private so you can go at your own pace without the worry of what other people want to do or a time schedule! would definitely do this again!

this experience wasn’t our favourite for sure, it all felt very rushed and just get the money and go type way. there was very little chance to touch the dogs ,mas they were in cages with such tiny holes ti get your finger through to pet them. we could touch them after our sleigh ride but only very briefly. the sleigh ride itself was super fun and i recommend it for that however the rest of the experience wasn’t so great.

this fabulous geyser is a nice stroll from the old faithful inn and beyond, just stay on the paved road and it will take you there. you will see the boardwalk for daisy geyser, to the south, just keep walking west and you will see this marvelous geyser on the right. you can also access this geyser from the grand geyser boardwalk and from biscuit basin. i was lucky when i captured this awesome geyser in the evening in mid july during a thunderstorm..

this fall and surrounding area was beautiful. we encountered 2 little black snakes at the end of the steps. there are public toilets and a landing to stand an see the fall.. such a pretty place. large car park to swing your car around.

this farmer's market is very welcoming and has a great array of veggies, fruits, soap, clothing and handmade goods and trinkets. there are also a few stands serving hot food. the only downside is it is one of the smaller markets i've been too in the miami/broward area- we only spent about 25 minutes here. that being said, it's still worth a visit. we tried the smoothie station called blend bike (which had the longest line out of all the stands when we arrived). their "refreshing af" was a great dragon fruit and mint based smoothie. the appeal of the smoothie stand is getting to ride a bike to power blend your own smoothie. it's a little funny to do in front of the line of customers but the associate working the stand can take your place if you'd rather not ride the bike. this market is in the parking lot that belongs to vizcaya museum so it's a great stop before enjoying the museum and gardens right across the street on a sunday.

this fascinating location was part of our tour with infinity. accessed via watercraft, we arrived and then hiked the premarked pathway, which snaked its way through the protected area. the landscape is harsh and desert-like, but don't be fooled into thinking it lacks wildlife and vibrancy. look deeply into the brush and you will be rewarded with camouflaged "locals" doing their thing.
this feels like a hidden gem that is easily accessible and offers great views of the sunset. you just have to go to the fourth level to get here.

this food court is the latest addition in onebangkok. ordered pad thai, tom yum noodle, chicken rice and roti. pad thai are good. sweet and salty. add some chilli flakes to make it more flavourful. tom yum noodle taste different from malaysia style. they are tend to be more spicy with little to none sour note. chicken rice are surprisingly good. the fragrant of the rice quite close to the michelin chicken rice. chicken are tender and juicy. roti are ok. a bit different from the street where there are thick so it is crispy. good amount of chocolate and banana used. overall food are good. a lot variety for you to choose and not so much people compare to other malls. will i repeat? yes for sure. price are reasonable for a mall food.

this food street has its own color and culture. there are several restaurants, coffee shops, convenient shops and repair stores. the street is clean but there is some sewage smell in some areas of the street. we has lunch at a restaurant name asia. the restaurant was neat and clean. the food was also delicious. there is also coffee shop name paris baguette. they have a great variety of bakery stuff and coffee.

this food truck is my go to spot whenever i’m nearby. their chicken pita wrap is amazing the chicken is juicy and well seasoned, and the wrap is always fresh and perfectly made. everything is balanced just right, with great flavor in every bite. the service is fast and friendly too. definitely one of the best street food experiences in town!

this forest of healing is calling me back to jeju... i unfortunately could only spend an hour here, when i could have done at least 4 hours or more! wear covered shoes no food / picnics allowed parked along the main road (you'll see plenty others) and took a small pathway in to pay for an admission ticket & off we went! (reservations were not required when i went in may'24). a staff at the trail head told us where to go (take the boardwalk on right first) - this boardwalk is definitely doable for seniors & wheelchair bound visitors. loved the resting spots, where one lays and listens to the wind blowing n trees rustling. can't wait to return!

this forest was gorgeous in the orange sunset light. the guide, bravo, gave us an extended tour, explained the behaviors of animals present there, showed us the workings of nature, the topography and economics of the forest. highly recommended.

this former farm has a few original building, but mostly it is historic structures from around the country that have gather together and restored to different time periods. it was very interesting and we particularly enjoy the working 'general store' with a lovely variety of icelandic treats, toys, game, etc. for sale. my only regret is that we didn't have a little more time.

this fountain has been a focal point in this park promenade since 1930s. and as of today it is under maintenance for cleaning, repairing, and touching up. luckily it was able to see some historical photos displayed on the construction wall and noticed how beautiful this fountain it is and a symbol of this park. definitely recommended

this fountain is beautiful 😍 between the detail and the gorgeous background of historic old san juan, there's nothing not to like. it's a wonderful place yo relax on a weekday. when it's not so tourist filled. or a great place to take photos. it's also surrounded by so many sights and things to do. you can't go wrong!
this free museum documents the hero’s of the heydrich terror and project anthropoid. we make sure to visit and pay our respects on every visit to prague

this free, open-air memorial is definitely worth a visit. its thought provoking and very interesting. i particularly liked the viewing platform where you get a real feel of what the wall was like. also, this was not crowded at all.

this full day boat trip with dhow khasab tours was an unforgettable experience thanks to sohil. he made us feel very welcome and tried his best to show us the nicest spots. we saw lot’s of dolphins, small sharks, fish jumping out of the water, … snorkling was fun and our lunch was very tasty. we highly recommend this tour!

this gallery is exceptionally beautiful, with tons of amazing and talented local artists featured! i loved browsing all the different spaces that featured so many unique and one-of-a-kind pieces! highly recommend visiting!

this game reserve is very commercialized. the food is mediocre. the buffet includes desserts , cheese board and cake but no tea. not even an urn. so you actually gave to purchase tea or coffee. money making tactic. the rooms are very small and very tight. the bathroom is even worse. the tap in the sink is like a sprinkler and impossible to wash your hands without getting water all over you. breakfast is at 7am. game drive was 8am. it's a big rush and people had to rush through breakfast. hardly a holiday feel. also checkout is at 10am instead of the usual 11am. so after the game drive you need to rush to your room, get your belongings and leave. i wouldn't go back.

this garden is a real gem in rome. many tourists miss the entrance in the corner, so it is not crowded. a nice and relaxing place. beautiful fountain. beautiful architecture, just an amazing place to relax.

this garden is beautiful! it was the first place we visited on our first day in japan, as we stayed really close to it. adults have to pay ¥150 at the entrance and i'd recommend to visit it early when it opens. the place is perfectly maintained and also have an interesting stones collection. it's a great place to do some birdwatching too, as herons, egrets, ducks and small birds live here. we visited it 3 times because we really liked it!

this garden is full of history, it is large and you can take your pets for a walk. in its surroundings there is a wide variety of restaurants and shops. there are also crafts from different towns, museums and churches. enjoying a day in coyoacan is very pleasant with everything it offers.

this garden is magnificent just behind the chateau the vincennes. there is a wide variety of flowers and plants. there are small lakes, playground and activities like zip line for kids, a beutiful library and theater. it's a beautiful picnic spot for a summer days. entry fee is 2.7 euro.

this ger camp is perfectly nestled between several hills, perfect for exploring in nearly any direction. high-quality camp with above-average facilities, especially the restrooms and restaurants. staff is super-attentive, welcoming, and responsive. seems like a popular camp for many tours groups, and they manage the various needs quite well.
this geyser is a little fire cracker! it was so entertaining to watch.

this geyser was amazing! we waited here for over an hour and were fortunate enough to run into someone who loves this geyser and knows the tells of when an eruption is imminent! this geyser goes off once every 15-16 hours or so. if you can audibly hear water on the right side as you go on the walkway, you are 1-2 hours away from it going off. you will start to notice the equivalent of hot tub jets going on in the top pool and that you will start to hear water flowing down on the left. and then there will be more activity in the top pool until the activity really increases and gets big and then the show is on! the show lasted for 13 minutes! then paused for 4 minutes, and then went on for an additional 5 minutes. the show reminded me of a fireworks show. definitely worth it if you can time it up!

this great and fun (!) nonprofit saves historic sf photos, history, stories and artifacts that make me love san francisco even more—and make me feel more connected to my neighbors. awesome! thank you.

this grocery was close to our hotel. we visited a couple times. we bought sunscreen, food items and beer. they have great fruit and very reasonably priced. we had a great quarter of a watermelon and it was one of the best i have had. they also have a select number of beers in the cooler and there are wines and beers on the opposite wall. you can also get gelato. we appreciated this less expensive alternative for snacks and small meals. staff was also helpful!

this gurudwara is truly beautiful. the recent renovations have truly elevated this gurudwara to be a central part of hong kong. this sacred place serves as a living testament to the rich history and enduring legacy of sikhs in hong kong. this is also where sikhs who were involved in the komagata maru incident slept and prayed before departing for canada.

this hanok village is recommended. most of the old traditional houses has converted to become commercial purpose like restaurant or cafe but is still very nice for photography. i noticed most of the restaurant are serving western food.

this has become my go to masjid for jummah. well kept and maintained, clean carpets and a wonderful atmosphere. azan and reciter are beautiful, calming and peaceful. even though it's a bit of a drive from my residence, i will continue to go here for jummah. jummah prayer also finishes earlier than some of the other surrounding masjids. can visit the beach immediately after jummah too :) just does not have any women's prayer facilities from what i've seen. there is ablution facilities available, water is provided after jummah and there is ample qurans and islamic literature for you as you sit in peace and tranquillity.

this has been my favourite hostel ever! i had the time of my life here, made so many friends and memories for life. a special shout out to ivan, a member of the staff who i also consider a friend. made the experience there even better and took some time to hang out and make sure i had everything i needed! the staff are super friendly and want to make sure that you have a great time. another shout out to dario for being a great person. can’t wait to be back!! ❤️ 🇨🇭

this has been the only less pleasant stay during our safari. the room was freezing cold as the main curtain wasn’t let down before we arrived and, due to the umidity caused by the rain i think towels were dump. the water for the shower wasn’t even warm and especially in the morning when we woke up we had no water at all which was highly disappointing. highlight of the stay was the dinner, simply but comforting and tasty. they definitely have to improve on a few aspects.

this has one of the most beautiful roads into the park. the best spot to do an easy 5km walk/run from the entrance gate next to matala and back again. the best time to walk/run is very early (6am), at opening time to avoid cars and buses on the road. just magical!!

this has the best views of kyoto you'll ever see. the walk up is full of cute shops too. it's well worth the walk and the wind chimes are beautiful. a must see place in kyoto! even if you're only there for a day

this has to be my most memorable communal place in cairo. indeed an oasis in the middle of such a busy city. this park is for all generations where you will find families, older and young people/couples enjoying life. the park comes to life late afternoons and on some occasions you may come across couples taking their wedding photo shoots here. there are streams, fountains, restaurants/cafe on site. it is so nice to see families enjoying picnics. for photographers, this is a great place to capture images with your imagination running wild! it is a very local park which makes it so authentic. the views from here are really good; especially the sunset. one of few places where you can pay by cash nowadays. entry price for visitors is very reasonable. kudos to those who look after this space.

this has to be one of the most beautiful temples. you can feel the history as you enter. from outside, it does not look like much, but it is a very well preserved and old temple. one can highly appreciate if you wish to see the a part of history.

this heritage-listed late-19th-century building located at george street in the sydney central business district, is a popular building with romanesque design. it houses several restaurants, cafes and retail shops at 5 levels with access to trains and light rail, buses nearby. prices at shops appear to be more than surrounding streets as it considered a prime retail location. its lovely inside with unique architecture and is popular with tourists. there is escalator access to all floors and toilets are available.

this hidden gem is super wonderful. need to do walk about 40 minutes to get the top of waterfalls. but it was worth with the view also when you dip in to the water. try to walk very carefully because the path not quite good. nice and recommend place to spend your weekend away with family or friends. minus the road to get there a bit rough.

this hike can be a bit misleading if your goal is to get to the cave. devils kitchen is a very cool sinkhole. 7 pools isn't much. the entire trail is longer than it may seem depending on where you have to park. at a regular pace give yourself 3 hours round trip.

this hike is a must see in flores island, azores. take your time to appreciate nature here. the meandering path to the waterfalls is about 600 meters long. hiking boots or running shoes are recommended as the terrain is very rugged and inclined. this place is also known as poço da ribeira do ferreiro as indicated on the signs by the road .

this hike is about a mile long, and pretty flat the whole way. i'd really call it more of a walk than a hike. that being said, it's totally worth stopping and checking out. the walk out to the bridge is pretty the whole way, and the bridge itself is beautiful! i highly recommend following the trail up to the top of the bridge for great photo ops. dont forget your bear spray though, as this is also a popular spot for our furry friends.

this hike is challenging because of elevation that you need to overcome. at the same time, the trail is nicely marked and you just follow it. bring both a waterproof hard shell and some layer against cold, as it's pretty windy on the top, and the weather changes quite a lot. views are beautiful and you can see a football playground and a beach in the valley. the parking lot where you leave you car is paid so just count with that.

this hike is considered hard for a reason. it was challenging, to say the least. it took us an hour to get to the top. we sometimes went 20 steps and had to take a breather. the views were worth the time and effort. we started in the dark with flashlights, plenty of water, and some snacks. i highly recommend this hike because the views at the top are incredible.

this hike is definitely not for beginners! as someone not so used to mountain hiking, i found it quite difficult, very technical and physically demanding. it took us about 1.5 hours to reach the top and 1 hour to come back down. some sections are particularly exposed and impressive, requiring full concentration to stay on the path and not feel overwhelmed (at least for me). as like most mountain hikes in lofoten, you need proper hiking gear (shoes), without it this trail is nearly impossible. it’s all mud, rocks, and uneven terrain. the viewpoint where you can see the bridge is still a stretch away from the summit. i was already too overwhelmed to go all the way there but my husband did and is very nice :) finding the starting point can be a bit tricky. from the e10, turn south into skjelfjord. as you approach the village, look for an orange building on the right, with cod-drying racks on the opposite side. there’s a small parking area next to the building. this is where the trail begins.

this hike is hard as they didnt create switchbacks and you just go straight up. also there is no map that explains the options. in the loop itself there is zero view as its in the forest. in the upper part of the loop you can go further up a 100 meters and there would be a beautiful look out point which overlooks lake maligne. it was worth it. going to the peak of opal is very hard.

this hike is popular. and for good reason. it has some of the most fantastic views at the very top. because of this, it's always always always crowded from about 6:30am to around 3:00pm. i recommend waiting to do this hike until m-w and go later in the afternoon. especially if it's a cloudy/cooler day. normally there are almost 100 people at the top, all cramming for a picture. go later and you'll basically have the place to yourself. parking is wayyyyy easier that way, too. there are some sections that require something like climbing. i had to hoist my whole body up and over a rock. if you're in mediocre physical shape with no huge joint issues, you can do it. i have back, neck, and knee issues, but i was able to do the whole hike. i've seen babies and toddlers get to the top with significant help from parents. i did have to take like 50 breaks, though. it's pretty steep in some sections.

this hike is so worth it! it’s over 1000 steps so definitely a stair-master workout but the view at the top is stunning. take it slow and bring lots of water. it took us less than half an hour to get to the top and about 10-15 minutes getting down and we spent about an hour admiring the views at the top. we did it right before sunset which i highly recommend as the heat is much more bearable at this time compared to earlier
this hike is spectacular. the views provided are epically breathtaking. definitely worth the effort

this hike is very extensive and steep. there are a lot of places where you can slip and potentially fall off. i highly recommend not bringing children or eldery on the trail. come prepared with extra clothes and a towel as it can get wet and muddy. i also suggest having an extra set of socks and shoes as it will be a mess after returning back from the trail. also, keep in mind the weather as a rainy day will make the hike much more treacherous. the views were very nice, but there is a chance of fog that could block the scenery. please go with at least one more person. the trail is long and steep. having a buddy with you will make it more enjoyable. overall, a very challenging but fun hike. just accept the fact that you will get wet and muddy.

this hike was a highlight of our trip, an absolutely stunning way to experience the natural beauty of madeira. easy to moderate, with just enough challenge to feel like an adventure, but totally accessible. the path meanders alongside an aqueduct, past lush greenery, wildflowers, and waterfalls, with sweeping views of the mountains and valleys. the final lagoon and waterfall were the perfect reward. peaceful, scenic, and unforgettable. it was the perfect way to shake off the jet lag and get the day started.

this hike was beautiful, it took around 1.45 hours to walk to the viewpoint and 1.45 back, the sunset was amazing although make sure you have a flashlight of sorts to walk back when it’s dark, trail is not too strenuous and the drive up is okay as the roads are not too small. parking and driving up is great not too stressful.

this hike was the hardest hike i've ever done, however, i still made it to the top and i'm very proud of myself. will i ever want to do this hike again? never lol if you're out of shape like i am, this hike will test your willpower. walking sticks and waterproof hiking boots are a must. i used a camel back and brought an extra water bottle and finished it all. definitely bring snacks or food for energy. the first mile up, you're going up steep switchbacks. the next half mile gets a little easier, but still not easy. the best view is when you see the lower falls. after you pass the falls, the next half mile, or so, isn't as terrible but still hard. once you get to the second set of switchbacks, all covered in snow and slush, you really start wondering what possessed you to even try this. however, you just have to keep pushing forward. once you hike the mile of switchbacks, you'll hike up a small creek, and at that point, you're almost there. it was very rewarding getting to the top. again, this is the pov of someone who is out of shape. my friend who is in shape did not struggle as much as i did. the only reason i didn't give it 5 stars is i did feel disappointed in the view of the falls at the top. in the end, it took me almost 8 hours to hike up and down this mountain. my legs were wobbly in the end and i slept for almost 12 hours afterwards lol

this historic buddha temple is a serene and peaceful destination, ideal for those seeking tranquility. visitors are required to dress modestly, as shorts are not permitted. the temple's beautiful architecture is truly captivating and adds to its spiritual charm. as part of your old town tour, you can easily include a visit to this temple, the vibrant old town streets, and the bustling sunday night market. all three are located close to each other, making it convenient to explore these attractions in one trip.

this historic citadel offers a fascinating glimpse into the past. the architecture is impressive and well-preserved, making for a memorable visit. the grounds are expansive and perfect for a leisurely stroll. there are informative exhibits and displays throughout the citadel. it's a worthwhile destination for anyone interested in history and culture.

this historic mosque is a must-visit for its stunning architecture, blending fatimid, mamluk, and ottoman styles. visitors praise its peaceful atmosphere and intricate details, making it a great spot for those interested in islamic architecture13. maps should highlight its unique features like the monumental entrance and ornate minarets.

this historical palace is stunning. best to go late in the day after the crowds have gone. i went at 330pm and was able to enjoy most of the palace alone. it really feels like you have gone back in time.

this hot spring is truly the “secret lagoon” of the area! it’s small, theres only three little bathing areas, but it’s really not a problem with only a few other visitors. it’s quaint, peaceful, and well integrated into the landscape. highly recommend coming before it gets more popular

this hot spring site would be difficult to explore in warm weather as it gets extremely hot due to the active thermal springs. fortunately, the walkways are well-constructed and easy to navigate, making the experience more comfortable despite the heat. the restrooms are clean and well-maintained, which is always appreciated at tourist sites. there are souvenir shops available, though the selection is somewhat limited compared to other attractions. overall, it’s a worthwhile stop if you’re in the area, but i’d recommend visiting during cooler weather if possible. the natural phenomenon of seeing active hot springs is quite impressive, just be prepared for the heat and bring plenty of water. a good addition to your itinerary if you’re interested in geological sites.

this hotel cost 3x what i paid in swakopmund and 1.5x what i paid in windhoek so i was expecting a better experience overall, but felt underwhelmed. the food and food service was good, but the things that weren’t good were: the room was fine but not amazing for the bigger price tag. wifi was hit or miss and housekeeping came late in the afternoon after activities when i was already trying to relax in the room. they also left a note asking guests to conserve water with showers less than 4 minutes and not washing towels daily, but then watered the grass and plants daily? i’m happy to accommodate any requests for conservation, but i felt like they weren’t practicing what they preach. the guide to sossuvlei was trying the least. he barely spoke during the 4 hour round trip ride in the car, he drank a beer while driving (which normally i would say “yas, have fun” but when he didn’t try at all during the tour, it was annoying), and he didn’t explain the major undertaking of hiking big daddy. another guest and i were struggling with the hike so he suggested a “shortcut” and sent us on our way. the shortcut included extremely deep sand and he had to come down to get us, only to let us know that we “took the wrong route”. at one point i explicitly asked “is there a way to make this easier” and he said no, but then later gave the tips of following in others footsteps or removing shoes. i get that he does this every day, but he did very little to make the process more comfortable and informative, which is literally why i hired a guide. this hotel is in the middle of nowhere and when i tried to change my transport plans they kept telling me “sorry, it’s the weekend so we can’t help you” or “wait for the manager to come back.” at one point (after following up literally four times), i pushed for alternate solutions and the employee just started ignoring me as if i wasn’t talking. i’ve also lived and worked in hospitality in a remote place and you usually know people or services that aren’t obvious to guests, but they really made me fend for myself with the power of google on the spotty wifi. when i checked out one day early (as i noted when i checked in and when i asked for transportation 4x over two days), the staff seemed shocked and confused that i was leaving. they didn’t know what to do when i asked to apply the funds i paid for the extra unused night to activities, drinks, lunch, etc. and had to call the head office. the head office refused any type of concession, aside from a 10% refund of the unused night. overall i felt like an inconvenience and i was constantly begging for service on everything aside from the food.

this hotel has an amazing location. every room has a lake view either sunrise side or sunset side. probably built in the 70s so not super modern but rooms are clean and have everything with huge panoramic windows to see the sunrise or sunset which is spectacular. breakfast is very good. service is very friendly.

this hotel is a real gem, i highly recommend it to anyone that's looking for a real peaceful, serene getaway....at an amazing price. the hotel room is very large, bright, clean and equipped with everything you need to enjoy a real comfy, relaxing and hassle-free stay. a couple of specifics about the room is that: 1) they have excellent showers with amazing water pressure and the water can be adjusted to exactly the amount of heat that you wish = great shoulders and neck massage; 2) they have their own line of specialty pillows - also available for sale for a convenient price- which are specifically designed to meet your sleep position..i.e. stomach, back, right or left side; 3) the hotel is very quiet and safe and at the same time conveniently located in a short walking distance from various restaurants and even a convenient store. the staff girls are all so sweet, friendly and sincerely eager to help all the time. the spa is most definitely a must during your stay. i cannot say enough nice things about my experiences. i had a shellac manicure and pedicure done, along with a facial wax and facial. i had the pleasure of marie and stephanie helping me, both of whom i felt like i knew forever....it was so easy to chat and giggle with them...a real nice time. you definitely have to ask for stephanie's "special" if you want to have the best facial pampering experience of your lifetime....plus she's got some special tricks up her sleeves when it comes to making your pedicure even more relaxing. 😉 i can't wait to visite again, thanks!

this hotel is an exceptional choice for anyone looking to explore the national park. the modern and clean rooms provide a comfortable retreat after a day of adventure, ensuring guests feel refreshed and relaxed. the staff truly elevate the experience, consistently going above and beyond to accommodate every request with a warm and friendly demeanor. their attentiveness makes you feel valued and well taken care of throughout your stay. dining here is a delight, with the all-inclusive experience offering a remarkable variety of delicious food that caters to various dietary restrictions. the guides provided by the hotel are truly amazing. they are knowledgeable and supportive, allowing experienced hikers the freedom to set their own pace and enjoy the trails at their own rhythm. this flexibility ensures that everyone can fully appreciate the breathtaking scenery and challenges of the national park. after completing the w circuit, indulging in the spa services was the perfect way to unwind. overall, this hotel combines comfort, exceptional service, and fantastic amenities, making it an ideal base for exploring the national park while ensuring a rejuvenating getaway.

this hotel is in a fantastic location, and while the rooms are basic, they're quite spacious. we stayed for a day during a layover on our way to sydney, and it was a great choice. the nearby mall offers plenty of shops, but the water park was the real highlight. entry to the park was included with our booking, and you could easily spend four hours there, with all rides included. it's highly recommended if you have kids, but there are also good rides for adults to enjoy!

this hotel is luxury at a reduced price. the dining experience has the luxury flair and the food was great. there are wonderful views from up high in the dining area. there are robes in the room. the pool looks lovely. we needed to be picked up and taken to meals using walkie talkies to call, which was fine. the room had a great rustic feel and a free standing bath in addition to the shower.

this hotel offers excellent value in rovaniemi. clean, simple rooms. super friendly staff. good breakfast. great facilities including a pool with hot tubs, but also - at additional cost - a big kids play area, bowling, and all kinds of sports and/or equipment. they also have a restaurant with simple meals like burgers and chicken, etc. - decent food at very fair prices. great location if you have a car (parking available), but you could manage without a car too. you can walk to an observation tower just nearby if aurora forecast looks good - we saw amazing auroras here - no tour or car needed if the sky is clear. honestly, if you are a family traveling with kids, i can’t imagine a better place to stay in rovaniemi.

this hotel was centrally located. the service was outstanding! the food was great. the hot springs were the best. the icing on the cake was meeting the resident cat. he greeted us every day. we hated leaving him, but know he’s going to be well cared for by hotel staff.

this hotel was everything we were looking for. we wanted an authentic, real, cultural experience of bolivia and got exactly that. the hotel itself is surround by beautiful eucalyptus which gives it a nice nature scent. as part of the experience we were taken kayaking to lake titicaca. we went to some of the nearby islands and saw some really nice historic stuff, including the only complete mummy! we ate some native trout from the lake and it was overall just a perfect experience. could not recommend this hotel and experience enough!

this hto park has two sections-west and east-and is built on quays , previously used by ships in the inner harbour..this area has an urban beach design with sand and umbrellas…as i walked by this area was abuzz with activity…there is a humorous reference that hto is a word play for h2o in a wikipedia article….

this is a 1 stop shop with plenty of shopping, multiplex cinema, food court, snacks and drinks are spread out throughout the mall & if you have kids they will enjoy the magic planet which has something for every age! there is a huge arcade, plus bumper cars, a mini bowling alley, and an indoor play area where you can leave your kids while you shop or eat for some time. the food court has cuisine from around the world and also has an international food chain such as papa jones, mcdonald, burger king, and kfc, to name a few. this mall is at very close proximity to the old dubai, so if you are doing a guided or self tour around the old dubai, this is a good option to stop by for some shopping and food. also, it is connected to the dubai metro, and it is considered a major hub station as both green and red lines intersect here.

this is a beautiful and challenging hike (in a good way), probably medium+/hard- difficulty. there js around 1km elevation gain but overall there are no super steep steps etc - the main challenge is from the length and you need to be persistent. to hike the full thing i recommend to have at least 3 litres of water per person, definitely some food and plenty of sunscreen as some parts are very exposed to the sun (but overall there are many parts in the shadow too). i would also reserve at least 2.5-3 hours one way if you are not super experienced in hiking, so 5-6 hours in total. if you are experienced and physically fit you can easily do the whole thing in 3 hours but it will be quite a workout and no time to rest and enjoy. overall the best return on investment to me is up until you stop seeing the waterfall from the side. since then it’s just a hike to the top of the waterfall which is not that beautiful and the other views are marginally better than what you get on the way up. you obviously get a sense of achievement by doing the hike but views-wise i’d probably stop 20 minutes after the first time you see the waterfall, have some rest and go back to see more stuff after

this is a beautiful architectural building t and the coffee place inside was really good, but the personnel was horrible annoyed by our presence and don’t helpful at all, shame of such beautiful place, we asked a worker for bathroom and she was not happy to be bother by us.

this is a beautiful church with a lot of history. when you enter, you sense the centuries of prayer that have occurred there. the sanctuary evokes a spirituality that makes you want to linger. we also visited the crypt where bishops and archbishops from the founding of the church were buried. the guide mentioned that there are over 900 people are interned in the crypt.
this is a beautiful garden to explore lots of the indigenous flora. the orchid house has glorious stained glass and the design of the garden is quite contemporary in some places!

this is a beautiful hiking trail with stunning views throughout. it’s a restricted path, so you have to return the same way you came, which makes the overall hike shorter. however, the route is quite steep in places, so it still offers a moderate challenge. definitely worth it for the scenery!

this is a beautiful island and most of it is national park. beaches, hikes, it is all so pristine. the tax is worth it to have clean beaches and well maintained trails. sancho beach was a real highlight. physically gorgeous, plenty to see snorkeling, great spot for a swim. highly recommend coming to the island.

this is a beautiful island and most of it is national park. beaches, hikes, it is all so pristine. the tax is worth it to have clean beaches and well maintained trails. sancho beach was a real highlight. physically gorgeous, plenty to see snorkeling, great spot for a swim. highly recommend coming to the island.

this is a beautiful little park with outdoor trails. the stupa was the highlight of the visit and its picturesque surroundings. anyone who is buddhist or into meditations should visit this park if you are in the sedona area. there's parking too and it's free. the only thing is the parking area is small and first come-first served. i highly recommend a visit to the place. fyi - just keep your trash to yourself to maintain the pristine and clean surroundings and please do not touch the statue of the buddha there because most people do for photo op. there's a sign about not touching it, but most people ignore it. also, keep the noise to a minimum since a lot of people go there to meditate.

this is a beautiful museum, the building with neoclassical and renaissance architecture styles all over is wonderful, there is a permanent art paintings collection at the second floor of very well known mexican painters including many dr atl works, truly worth your time, also works from muralists like tamayo, siqueiros and other great artists. in addition there are non permanent exhibits which will surely surprise you. if you happen to have your student or teacher's id you will get a discount on the entrance ticket, however, i consider the normal price very affordable too.
this is a beautiful national parc, beautiful view from the cliff and nice waterfalls

this is a beautiful piece of murano that is great for pictures! i did not go inside. i would recommend checking out the food in the area nearby the faro di murano. one of the locals informed me that they prefer getting pizza from those spots rather than near the hyatt where i was staying.

this is a beautiful piece of well-preserved history! i'm not sure young ones would appreciate, but teens did. the back and garden is lovely, and the city view from the top is incredible! not a must do, but with the citypass, it was included. we didn't get get to do the royal museum or city cruise which would have been my preferred pick (i think) looking back. it was close by and a maybe on my list, so we enjoyed it. the climb to the 3rd floor top of through a small metal winding staircase which was worth it, but tough with hip/back issues. crowded -one way up and down. worth the wait.

this is a beautiful place filled with lots of different trees, shrubs and flowering bushes. there's ample space for walking and it is accessible for wheelchairs. there's a snack bar and restrooms. overall a beautiful experience!

this is a beautiful place to wonder around. although we’ve been here many times over the years, but we’ve always enjoyed our walks here, even in the rain as in this week of early may. there were some eateries here, and we tried some of them in the past, but weren’t too impressed. the shops, mostly art gallery type, were very interesting, especially the one that sells outdoor wind chimes (? not really chimes, but large art pieces that move with the wind).

this is a beautiful place! the path is actually a road so the footing is good. the hills, however, are punishing. the creek all along the way is lovely. we went when it was dry so would be better after more rain. you can swim at the top-well deserved when you get there. this track is 3kms in and 3kms out so be prepared with lots of water if you are doing it in summer. also beware the march flies! they hurt and they love the colour blue. this is a national park so no dogs and no camping (i read a review which suggested it as a good camping spot-it is illegal to camp). enjoy the bird song.

this is a beautiful property right next to sand river. the accommodations are stunning and welcoming. the food and service have been extraordinary. our guides very knowledgeable. the staff are very friendly. great for family travel! we had a multi-gen group with a variety of ages.

this is a beautiful scenic spot to enjoy seasonal flowers. the farm is large, and each area has its own vibrant color theme—purple lavender, bright red, sunny yellow, soft pink, and many other shades. it’s relaxing to walk around and take in the views from different angles, each corner offering a new photo opportunity. across the farm, there are several souvenir shops and dessert stalls, with lavender ice cream being a highlight. we visited in august when many tour buses were here, but the space is wide enough that it didn’t feel too crowded inside. it’s an easy place to spend an hour or two enjoying nature, tasting local treats, and picking up gifts to bring home. we really enjoy the fresh green and orange melons as well as lavender icecream.

this is a beautiful shop in sedona where you can find treasures and high end design souvenirs. we were spending new year’s eve and wanted to buy flute glasses to toast. the lady that runs the shop was super kind and showed us everything for all styles and budgets. she wrapped our flutes, we bought rainbow flutes

this is a beautiful spa retreat. nestled in one of the best areas in the eastern townships, you will find what nourishes you, whether on a day trip or an extended stay. the prices are reasonable, the service is excellent. go.

this is a beautiful spot for swimming and picnics, you can spend the whole day here. parking is tight so i recommend getting there early. there is staircase access to the beach at several places along the lower trail.

this is a beautiful temple next to the river. there is a pier by the somdet to memorial which can be reached from the tha chang pier. the interesting theme about this temple is that it has a big golden bell as well as a bell tower and other small rows of bells to ring. the somdet to memorial statue is also quite large and beautiful. i think this is a lesser known temple amongst tourists. you can also walk to the wang lang market nearby for food and browse various goods.
this is a beautiful viewpoint, perfect for watching the sunset and enjoying stunning ocean views.

this is a beautiful, hidden monastery with well-maintained grounds, and the buddha temple offers a serene and peaceful atmosphere. the gift shop is fairly average, but i’ve noticed a trend where vendors claim that items are locally made in ladakh, even when the packaging indicates otherwise.

this is a brilliant club hidden in the bustle of bangkok. the staff are absolutely brilliant and the owner is usually around too to help take care of you. the girls that work in there are also amazing and can make what would be a standard night out an amazing one. no watered down drinks here either they are very strong! all in all i can't recommend lucy club enough

this is a consecrated buddhist site that radiates spiritual energy and vitality, set amidst a beautifully vibrant landscape. i highly recommend a visit. having been to some of the oldest and most renowned monasteries in the himalayas, i can say this place evokes the same profound sense of peace and contentment.

this is a convenient food truck/convenience store along the highway coming to or from fairbanks. you order inside the store and pick up outside.. the service and the prices are great! they have a simple menu that has some good variety. yet, the food is lackluster and in need of seasoning.

this is a cute little park to stop and rest on your way to or from lombard street. it's quiet, not highly populated, and has a nice place to sit or smell the roses. i have been to many places before and i have never smelled better roses in my entire life. one smelled like candy, one smelled like perfume, all smelled so delicious and unique! 100% recommend stopping and smelling the roses!

this is a desert. it is filled with sand. it is dry, hot and does not care if you drank all your water, because you can't get no water from a desert. so if you visit, bring plenty of water. a single small bottle is not enough, and the desert will laugh as you die from thirst (if you get lost).

this is a eco friendly hotel. the owner, kelvin believes in sustainability and has a fleet of honest and passionate employees. some of their employees are gifted kids, they are gentle and committed, do be patient with them. i strongly recommended to those who loves the nature, sea and sun! surely will come back ❤️
this is a fairly challenging hike for novices like me. rocky uneven terrain and slick when you get an afternoon rain. the falls were worth the hike to me though!

this is a family and beginner friendly slope. i love the open wide slopes that annapuri offers. if you are a beginner like me, this would be the 2nd best option. the 1st being hanazono, however, annapuri offers a wider larger variety of green slopes for the beginners.

this is a family-friendly and kid-friendly place to see butterflies, moths, beetles, bugs, scorpions, and other insects. the area is not very huge, making it easy to monitor the kids, and a visit here doesn’t take too long. during our visit, we had a guide who provided information about the butterflies and other insects. she was very nice, friendly, and eager to answer our questions. we also had the chance to see the barong butterflies (which are actually moths) and even hold them and put them on our hands or shirts with the help of the staff. additionally, we saw cocoons hanging in the breeding room, which was fascinating. this place features a butterfly and insect museum, a semi-outdoor garden where butterflies freely fly around, and a cave showcasing other insects. however, many of the transparent cages inside the cave were empty. the place also includes a souvenir shop, parking lot, and some seats at the entrance. overall, it is a nice park, but some areas were still under construction, leaving certain sections empty. i believe it has the potential to be even better in the future.

this is a family-friendly ecological and cultural park located in the western part of amsterdam, developed as part of the city’s urban expansion. it features open lawns, waterfronts, and even a small petting zoo, offering a peaceful green retreat. the name was designated in 1958, and the design by f. g. breman and janneke willemsen was adopted in 1970. the park was completed in 1973 and is divided into several zones. while it is shaded by dense trees and offers a tranquil atmosphere, it remains quite dark at night due to the minimal street lighting.

this is a fantastic way to explore the caldera at santorini. steve and the team did a great job explaining everything we needed to know. the boat was sufficiently powered and very comfortable even in some of the early morning choppy conditions. the wind had abated by 1pm and the weather was perfect. would highly recommend this experience with sea4all.

this is a grand statue honoring the holy roman emperor and king of bohemia, charles iv. unveiled in 1848, it stands near the entrance to charles bridge in prague. the bronze monument, designed by sculptor ernst julius hähnel, depicts charles iv in regal robes, holding the foundation charter of charles university, which he established in 1348. surrounding him are allegorical figures representing the university’s faculties. as one of prague’s most significant rulers, charles iv played a key role in shaping the city’s medieval glory, and this monument serves as a tribute to his enduring legacy.

this is a great experience. something fun to do with a group. if you are going with a group is highly recommended to reserve a table in advance. we were 9 people, no reservation on a weekend and had to wait for anout an hour to get the table. once inside, the restaurant is bigger that what i expected, had to turn twice walking to get to our table. they have 3 all you can ear options with the cheapest one been $58 per person, and if you are in a group and want any of these options, everyone in the table has to get the same all you can eat, can’t have a mix of choices unless everyone does a la carte. the explanation on how it works was a little confusing at the beginning, cause you have 90 minutes once they bring the first dish, but they can only bring two items from the all you can eat at a time for you to cook. prices for the drinks were normal for a restaurant, $14-$16 for cocktails, the strawberry margarita was actually pretty good. the food itself was very tasty. the pork gyozas and spring rolls were delicious. the meats were very well marinated, tender, and a lot of variety on the items you can choose. overall a great way to spend a night with friends!

this is a great location for varied and interesting skiing for those coming from the northern hemisphere, but a few words of caution: the good bits - stunning setting with view of the high andes and the local lakes; it is breathtaking - a lot of wide, interesting skiing - a number of fast lifts - new snow cannons ensured a way home by skis - lots of potential for off-piste - some really nice restaurants in resort - people are friendly and seem very genuine - we mad friends with the local dogs who roam around the resort and the mountain. the not-so-good bits: - we had mixed weather (which is not the ski lift company's fault) and still enjoyed ourselves though; in patagonia, as the locals say, the weather changes very quickly. - some new lifts are slow, making queues for the fast ones - snow making needs extending (only one home run was open whilst we were here) - the road to resort (which we had to walk on with ski boots) is not a pleasant experience and feels unsafe: the mud and rock 'pavement' is often parked on by cars, so you have to dice with death and avoid the coaches whizzing by as you tread on the asphalt

this is a huge and beautiful park. i could.nit get enough of the beautiful mountains. there are 2 ways to see the entire park offered by the state park - a shuttle bus and a wilderness/historic tour busses. these are 4 to 6 hours tours with the shuttle bus option being an inexpensive option. very little can be done on your own. the shuttle busses run on a timely manner and everyone is very helpful. the shuttle bus driver can drop you off at any point if you would like to get off for any trails. the shuttle busses can pick you up any where in the road. the wilderness and historical tours are a pricier option which we cancelled last minute as the exact time is allowed 48 hours before the tour date. you only have a time window to pick while booking - morning or afternoon but the time assigned can be anywhere in a 4 hour window. you have cancellation fee if any changes are. made a week in advance. some trails are around the visitor center. the best thing we did was visit the dog kennels which included a presentation and dog petting. the rangers were amazing and educated us with all the historical facts and information. not many animals sighting though. we saw some moose. come prepared for cold/wet weather even in summer. definitely go to the denali visitor center.
