this is a less visited area on the northern side of bukit timah peak. the area was originally developed by the cold storage company for dairy farming, to provide a local supply of milk for singapore. the area was used for dairy farming up until 1980's. after farming operations were terminated, the national parks board began developing the area as a nature reserve. it was opened to the public in 2009. the descent from the bukit timah peak has several steep flights of stairs and it tends to be popular with people doing trail running activities. this area has thick surrounding rain forest and provides the opportunity for a bit of wildlife spotting. there are a couple of trails (called loops) which eventually lead to a sealed road called the wallace trail. safe travels, mega.

this is a lifetime bucket list trip. arza has each aspect of your trip down to a simple formula "do what is right ~ make it simple ~ do it each and every time." from orientation, packing, transportation, food prep, sanitation, general instructions, hikes, free time, camps, stories, individual / group interactions all were amazing. the simple thing i liked "best!" as we successfully shot the bigger rapids, we would do a 180 so we could see upriver and see where we just came from. each azra guide and employee brought a unique strength to our trip which all was appreciated. 5 stars. keep going for another 60.

this is a long history of good market while next to the public transit. the first time that i went to this market was 1986. they are still under the renovation now but remain open. the food court is small and not roomy while now. hopefully, they will finish it nicely later. if you are a visitor, this is a good spot for you since there are lots of things to do and see. it takes you only a few minutes walk to the shipyard plaza. don't miss this area. they offer free skate in winter. they had a big good view outdoor seating area around the old food court year ago. the ceiling high windows all around is good for the customers sitting inside but we still have nice view. the window can be closed or opened depends on the weather. this is a really lovely eating area for all. there are many restaurants, bakeries, sweet, ice-cream and shops in the market. we didn't find any seafood and fresh produce fruits like before. it's more likely a food place instead of market. if you look for quick food, this is the best place for you.

this is a longer hike but worth the climb we were there in the morning so we were alone but be aware this is a hike we did it with kids ages 5,6,8,9 and it was long. our kids are used to hiking though i would not recommend this for kids who are not used to hiking. google also gave us wrong directions for hiking, it was longer hike than expected because there was no right turn on the trail as google suggested.

this is a longer review, but i need to start it with everyone should book sydney kayak experience. :) i booked this for my partner’s 30th birthday - it was the perfect way to start the day and although we’re only 2 days into a 14 day trip we have a feeling this might end up being one of the best activities during our time in australia. a really beautiful activity, with the most perfect views of sydney. i knew as soon as we arrived it’d be a special morning - the staff were extremely attentive and made you feel comfortable from the start. through out the entire trip bo and sylvia shared stories about sydney, which we really appreciated. they also took plenty of photos and videos of us as well. the breakfast menu was also delicious, and the restaurant had incredible views. i can’t thank sylvia and bo enough for starting my partners birthday on such a high note! we’ll never forget it.

this is a lovely and secluded beach, perfect for a relaxing day with family. there are designated areas for picnics, making it easy to enjoy a meal outdoors. the views are stunning, and the sunsets are absolutely breathtaking. a wonderful spot to unwind and take in nature’s beauty!

this is a lovely andbeyond property where service is the number one priority. we never carried a bag or had to wait for any service. the staff always had a smile on their face and never appeared to assist because it was their job, but because they genuinely wanted the guests to feel welcome. klein's camp has a lovely pool and 2 masseuse. everything but the messages are included, which is nice since you don't have to wonder what you can use or drink.

this is a lovely dive and snorkel destination resort (though with a hefty price tag). it 100% delivers on any service related aspects of our stay. food selection and restaurant service was outstanding. turndown and general housekeeping impeccable with a lot of attention to detail. the rooms and bed don’t quite match with the maledives-like price tag of nearly usd800/night (which is including 3 meals per day). the bed was very uncomfortable. they let me try another one but it was the same. given the price you would expect aircon and wifi in the rooms. the overwater bungalows are very spacious and nice but given their “open” build they offer no sound protection whatsoever from rain, wind and ocean noise. we still very much enjoyed our stay here but just like with everything in raja ampat expect to pay a bit more for what you get. we stayed on other islands/resorts in the area and it was a very similar experience. needless to say the snorkel trips were amazing🤿

this is a lovely flohmarkt (flee market). there are lots of household items from door knobs to plates and glasses to decor items. you will also find quite a few spots with paintings, other artworks, mirrors and antique picture frames. what’s cool here is that it’s actually vintage / antique items! many can be priced quite highly compared to the more contemporary flee markets and sales, but that’s understandable. there are also just a couple of food spots to get a small bite if you need an energy boost :) i’ll definitely be back!

this is a lovely island. to get to it you need to go to the island if burano first (e.g. line 12 from venize f nove d) and then on burano go to platform a (as you come out of platform b or c turn right) to get line 6 to torcello. as you land there is a path along the island passing some houses, restaurants, a kids playground, the devil's bridge and finally a church. lots of plants and insects around but walking along the canal is very nice. there is a water tap near the church which is free there are also a wc (toilet/bathroom) there but costs 1.5 euros to use it. vibe is nature, quiet, peaceful
this is a lovely park, but it's usually close 😭😭 i wish it could be open so people could enjoy it

this is a lovely part of the park with it's carefully manicured trees, lake and pagoda. you could see almost every branch detailed in the shadows of some of the trees; the sun was just in the right position.

this is a lovely place to pause and catch your breath a quiet escape from the hustle and bustle of the city. the pond, greenery, and occasional wildlife make it feel almost meditative. it’s the kind of spot where you can sit for a while and just be. a rare slice of calm in the heart
this is a lovely place to visit on a nice day. busy but always lots of space.

this is a lovely zoo, not too big and not too small. the animals seemed well looked after and happy. we really enjoyed walking around. as it is beautifully designed, with lots of plants and greenery and shady places to sit in, it wasn't that tiring even though the day was super hot when we visited.i would really recommend the visit to the artis zoo, best is to visit on a weekday as it wasn't too busy (we were there on a monday). our highlights were the sloth, the penguins and the elephants.

this is a lovely zoo, not too big and not too small. the animals seemed well looked after and happy. we really enjoyed walking around. as it is beautifully designed, with lots of plants and greenery and shady places to sit in, it wasn't that tiring even though the day was super hot when we visited.i would really recommend the visit to the artis zoo, best is to visit on a weekday as it wasn't too busy (we were there on a monday). our highlights were the sloth, the penguins and the elephants.

this is a luxury lodge in the dryer part of the okavango delta. it's not cheap, but worth every penny. we stayed there the 2nd half of april for 3 nights. the lodge is beautiful designed, with luxurious modern cabins. the cabin is equipped with excellent comfy beds, shower and bath and a deck overlooking a pool frequented by wildlife, such as elephants, wildebeasts, warthogs, baboons, giraffes and zebras. even lions visited the camp one night. food is delicious, with several options for lunch and dinner and a great selection of drinks. the wildlife is abundant. we did have an excellent guide, mike. he was very friendly and entertaining, and also a great wildlife spotter. he did his utmost to share his knowledge about nature and wildlife. we learned a lot about the habits of the local wildlife and about how the delta was formed. we saw a pride of lions eating a buffalo, a group of 5 cheetah hunting wildebeests (unsuccessfully), leaopards eating an impala and much more! also many beautiful birds! highly recommended if you want to visit the okavango delta!
this is a market with many local food stores. surprisingly, they accept credit card payment. visitor can also buy some local made dried food such as seaweed, ginseng and other traditional herbs.

this is a marvelous experience i have ever had in my life so far particularly in this heaven like country switzerland. definitely i will revisit this lovely and unforgettable place and strongly recommend this beautiful place to all my friends.

this is a marvelous monument to visit in rio. truly iconic. the train ride was short yet enjoyable. the high altitude may cause you chills, so it is best to carry a light jacket (it was a windy and chilly day for us), particularly if you are visiting in the afternoon. the evening views from the top are equally mesmerizing! you wish to take the right side of the train on your way up and left on the way down to best sights on the way up and down. we prefer the after slot as we could enjoy both sunset and daytime (boarding around 3 pm and coming back after 6). booking/reservation your tickets ahead/online is the best idea. unfortunately the toilets are not clean up at the site (so best to use the ones at the station, which is very well maintained) and the cafe serves very overpriced and bad quality food (best to avoid that). so, plan accordingly. hope you enjoy your visit as well!
this is a massive produce and fish market with no ready-made made food. i wish we had more time to take some back to our place and make a meal.

this is a monument located in berlin that was built years ago and served as the dividing line between east and west germany. visitors used to climb to the top for a glimpse of the other side of the wall, and today it serves as a reminder of what happened as well as a symbol of unity.

this is a most magical experience for all of us. this aquarium opens till 10 pm at night, and there is a good reason to go there during the night. it's absolutely amazing to see so many aquatic animals in this building, and this month there is a special jellyfish exhibition in conjunction with tsukimi, the japanese moon viewing festival. there are even penguins on the 6th floor!
this is a mountain road, all dirt, with oyunuma below, and then you can take the highway.

this is a museum of the history of iceland mainly from a religious perspective. there are almost 2 floors of deity displays, everything from crosses, to things related to the church. there is a nice display of the ships from the crossing and a fisherman's life. overall, a good visit to learn about iceland.

this is a must do activity if you are visiting yosemite. plan to get to the raft rentals at 8 am when the reservations open to fill out the paperwork . in spite of reaching at 8:30 am we had to wait till 9:45 to get to the booth. the ride down the merced river patch is magical. you get great views of half dome and yosemite falls along the way. you can even stop by one of the small islands or beach patches. two adults needed if with young kids for paddling.

this is a must do when you are in the area. the experience and sunrise views are second to none. it is clear this team takes a ton of pride in their work. hearing from our driver that they play practical jokes on each other too makes you realize dennis as the owner has created a great culture for his team and contributes positively to the community as well. the champagne breakfast afterwards was delicious and more than we expected to have in the middle of a desert plain!

this is a must see adventure if you visit puerto rico. julian was amazing and so knowledgeable about the area. the rainforest was breathtaking and there were many opportunities to enjoy the waterfalls. i absolutely loved how he took pictures throughout the whole experience and easily airdropped them to us at the end of the day. this man even turned back around after discovering i left my phone on the van to deliver it to me personally. definitely best excursion i’ve ever been on.

this is a must see area when you visit the park. there are many kinds of thermal features next to the beautiful yellowstone lake. a small herd of elks live in the woods along the shore and come to visit this area often. ample parking with toilet. no drinking water.

this is a must see if you come to athens. the steps are very slippery, go slowly and wear good shoes. there will be crowds, but when you get up there, it’s breathtaking. pay for a guided tour do you can get the full experience. also, be sure to visit the museum not too far away.

this is a must see if you come to athens. the steps are very slippery, go slowly and wear good shoes. there will be crowds, but when you get up there, it’s breathtaking. pay for a guided tour do you can get the full experience. also, be sure to visit the museum not too far away.

this is a must see if you’re in the area. great views and lots of monkeys. just don’t get too close to the animals and don’t bring food with you. if you bring water, keep it out of site of the monkeys. you can purchase beverages and at the top and bottom of the hill. all the vendors were very nice and welcoming.

this is a must see in havana city,cuba. one of the oldest places with the most history in cuba. the surrounding areas are very beautiful as well and very clean. it has been a while since my last visit and can see that the state has done a lot of work keeping up the old havana alive.

this is a must see in havana city,cuba. one of the oldest places with the most history in cuba. the surrounding areas are very beautiful as well and very clean. it has been a while since my last visit and can see that the state has done a lot of work keeping up the old havana alive.
this is a must see in rio. if you have mobility issues, schedule an electric car guided tour and enjoy not only nature but a piece of brazil history.

this is a must see national park! stunningly dramatic landscapes that are picture perfect, beautiful glaciers, plentiful wildlife. for me, this national park was the highlight of my entire vacation. it is quintessential alaska! the best way to see the park will be to take a boat tour out of seward. i recommend major marine tours.

this is a must see site for anyone in iceland who is interested in history, especially medieval history. you can see an excavated tunnel and the foundation stones of snorri's house leading to the old pool. most of the area around the bathing pool has been reconstructed however the large base stones at the bottom are original. the whole area is very tranquil in a pleasant valley. seeing original medieval stone ruins in what used to be a fort back in the 13 century is definitely worth a visit, especially since iceland has very few medieval relics. i would also recommend visiting the museum which is wonderfully decorated and has a lot of information about snorri and the history of the area. the gift shop has a wonderful selection of books on icelandic history. hope they eventually get more funding to continue excavations in the area.

this is a must see!!!! the library is the most impressive thing i’ve seen in prague. the view from the tower equally impressive. all tours are guided so you need to buy tickets in advance. but what’s great is you can arrive 10 mins before your tour and you’re in. one thing to note: there are ~170 stairs but there are lots of breaks so it’s not too tiring. highly highly recommend.

this is a must stop place in the morning! beautiful walking trails and if you’re feeling adventurous - there are so many trails that wander off. cool experience. it’s about $6usd per person so explore, and use it as a workout!

this is a must visit for any disney fan, fan of history or anyone in the san francisco area looking for a great activity to do. allow yourself at least 2 hours to properly explore the museum, there is a lot to see, read and learn and you don’t want to miss anything! i recommend buying the tickets online before arrival, but there is the option to buy when you get there. there are several different price options for adults, kids etc. the museum itself is situated in a beautiful red building, close to the golden gate bridge. it has two levels to it. it is wheelchair friendly and also has lifts inside, so you don’t have to take the stairs. the museum takes you through walt disney and his family’s past, with historic items from his childhood to adulthood, and takes you through the journey he had to become the famous man everyone knows. you will see the various companies he worked for, his first drawings and designs, all the way up to the creation of disneyland itself. the museum boasts a massive replica model of disneyland park which is fascinating to view and admire and there is so much detail shown about the park around it. overall an incredible visit. i learnt so much i didn’t know about walt disney and the history behind the parks and it is a really enjoyable experience. all staff are friendly and professional and there to help you with any questions. the museum is easily accessible by car, with parking right outside, drop off via taxi or walking from nearby.

this is a must visit if you are in marrakech! i went here to treat myself on my birthday and it was an experience i will remember for years to come! everything was great and it felt like i was on a different world! they welcomed us with detox water, the staff was being lovely, the hammam spa and massage were just amazing. i wish i could come here often just to relax like this
this is a must visit if you're in havana. this large monument to jose marti, who was a political figure in the late 1800's. you can turn and see the wall memorials to castro and guevara.

this is a must visit place if you travel to puerto rico. take a full day to visit this natural tropical forest lots of waterfalls scenic locations that will definitely enjoy and will remember forever. very conveniently mark for all the sports that you need to stop by parking in northern issueoverall a fun place to visit.

this is a must visit place in paris. it’s full of great historical pieces. their website recommends that you spend two hours at the museum. however, i spent almost double that and had to skip some. so, i highly recommend that you get the 12pm entry ticket, especially if you enjoy the seeing the details.

this is a must visit. the best part is it is free. just lie down on the lawn area look up and watch the cartoon. excellent entertainment for 15 minutes. apparently you can also climb this government building for free and have a look at the view of the city. if i remember correctly there is a show every 30 minutes and the start time and end time changes as per the season.

this is a must-do activity if you’re in the honolulu area. it’s best to visit in the early morning, as the hike can be quite challenging during the day due to the sun and heat. once you reach the top of the crater, you’ll be rewarded with a stunning view of waikiki and its surroundings.

this is a must-do if you are visiting in santorini! we had no problem getting in to the museum and had no reservations prior. the self-paced 8m underground museum is narrated by an audio pack. after the museum, you’ll enjoy a wine tasting. angela (see center of the second photo) was so well-informed and personable! our teens were given snacks and sodas to enjoy. angela engaged us all in the conversation. if you are on a cruise, or if you’re in the area, this is a must-do while you are in santorini!

this is a must-do if you go to cancun. me (a 57 year old grandma) and my adult kids had an absolutely phenomenal time doing the flyboard (yes me too) and the jet skis. my son and daughter flew! i got up after alot of giggling, crashing, giggling some more 🤣. soooo much fun! hector and the crew were wonderful and truly did everything they could to make sure we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. thank you for a wonderful experience for me and my family!

this is a must-do in my opinion! i wish i could go again! i knew it would be great, but it truly exceeded my expectations. drew was absolutely wonderful and explained the process in detail, making everything super easy! each of the staff members were very friendly and knowledgeable. the experience felt very safe. i thought the take-off might be scary, but it wasn’t at all. you just “run” on a downwards hill (no jumping off a cliff edge or anything). the ride itself was very calm and the views were amazing. they ask you if you want to do tricks and how adventurous you want to be with them…. definitely recommend doing this to the full extent if you like things like rollercoasters and don’t get motion sick. otherwise just enjoy a calm, slow ride :) if you have anyone waiting at the bottom for you—- we landed in front of the field in front of victoria-jungfrau grand hotel. cannot recommend this experience enough! if you’re on the fence— do it!

this is a must-see in vienna if, like us, you love botanical gardens and parks. of course, if you visit schönbrunn palace, one of the top three places to see in vienna, you absolutely must visit the palmenhaus. one could say it's expensive, too humid and unpleasant inside, or that the selection of plants isn't up to our expectations... i nevertheless highly recommend you go and visit it. of course, as always, it's best to buy your tickets online to choose the time that suits you and avoid the endless lines: it's better to enjoy the magnificent plants than to wait in the endless queues. have fun and take many photos!

this is a must-see! we parked at the top parking lot, walked down the 387 steps, crossed the bridge to the funicular, took the funicular to the top, walked the lovely nature trail, crossed the suspension bridge back to where our car was. you can also park at the bottom and do the reverse. anyway the falls are awesome! a must-see! afterwards, we went all around île d’orleans. wonderful!

this is a must-visit check-in spot when you're in hong kong island, located very close to the popular photo-op streets in the central area. it's an old-style shopping building with a variety of stalls selling diverse products. there are many beautiful photo opportunities here, so don't miss the staircases and the iconic clock

this is a must-visit location for anyone interested in learning more about the past. every corner is rich with historical significance, and the exhibits are thoughtfully curated to offer both educational value and engaging stories. whether you’re a history buff or just curious, there’s so much to take in and appreciate. the staff is knowledgeable, and the atmosphere really brings the stories to life. highly recommended for families, students, or anyone looking to connect with history in a meaningful way.

this is a must-visit stop. it is very well organized, and you can download an app to learn more about some of the pieces. you will probably need half a day or more to visit this museum. one staff member asked me to hang up my phone call while waiting in line before getting into the museum. no sign prohibited cell phone use, and i was not even talking. training for staff and/or signs about policies can improve the experience.

this is a narrow strip of public garden sandwiched between via carlo felince and the old aurelian wall and linking piazza s. croce in gerusalemme (northeast) and piazza s. giovonni in laterano (southwest). the park was opened in 1999 and offers some basic green space and surprisingly good viewing conditions of the old wall along with some basic urban park facilities. there is an interesting monument of st. francis of assisi at the southwest end, facing basilica di san giovanni that is worth spending a few minutes to enjoy if you pass by or through this park.

this is a nice hike, with a few sections thst are risky. the path is washed out with a very long drop in two sections after the mosque you begin in the small village above turtuk and follow the well defined path up to the small mosque on the cliffs above town. from the mosque there is only one path to follow to the left. this path is along a water canal the whole way. very easy to follow! the waterfall at the end is peaceful and cold. toward september and october it is low flow. wear sunscreen, bring lots of water and be prepared for the heat! enjoy!

this is a nice little market with a wide selection of products for its size. we went to one stall that served a selection of sausages with a wide variety of different mustards, all of which were really tasty!

this is a nice little neighborhood market for you to try some thai food. a great deal if you're in the area and want a snack or just some lunch on the way to whatever you are doing. the day i went it rained and there may not have been as many stalls but i found it delicious anyways. i'm giving this a four star rating just because i would like to see a few more things out of it as it has so much potential. right now there's a number of stalls serving similar food and limited seating. even then i would go early and grab a seat especially on a nice day. there's some great stalls there that seem to be very popular, while you're there just see where other people are lining up. there's a lot of stalls where they cook the food fresh in front of you and i'd highly recommend trying those out.

this is a nice little path. not sure if it’s for bikers or what but it’s kind of hard to get started on. right after or before the bridge is a pullout and there is a very steep pathway up to the trail. it looks washed out but it’s legit and when you get up there is immediate trail markings.

this is a nice little ruin we had no idea would be next to our hotel! mexico has much more interesting ruins to offer. you can enter it by the beach or the park royal hotel. we stayed at the park royal hotel so we saw it about 10am when no one was there. no entry fee, just walk right in. later that afternoon while on the beach we noticed there must have been a tour bus that stopped by so if you want pics with no one in the way get there early. enjoy!

this is a nice museum for modern art, many pieces focusing on local artist. many pieces are also out in the garden so you will get a nice stroll. personally it's not my first choice for art museum in jeju but it's up there if you have time, it does worth a visit. a plus is that for last wednesday of the month the admission is free for this museum and many museum in the area, so it's good to check this area out.

this is a nice neighborhood bar with a fireplace. great old fashion cocktails. a wide variety of beer in cans, bottles, and on draft. bartenders are nice. don't forget to ask for peanuts and throw the shells on the floor. love this place

this is a nice park to bring you kids ... but you will be sharing it with lots of teens in the afternoons so come early. not an issue most times but can be a bit distracting. the washrooms are a very nice touch and much appreciated. the splash pad is awesome on hot days.

this is a nice park to walk and picnic in the middle of the city of skyscrapers. very peaceful park on the third floor/roof top of saleforce interchange for buses. there are variety of plants, flowers and trees from different parts of the world. there is a gondola to ride down. also playground in the middle, cafe, seats, benches and public restrooms.

this is a nice place to go and relax and destress for city life. a wonderful place to come and read a book in the gardens library upstairs in the structure here. there are so many different kids of plants here it was interesting to see all the different kinds they have here. come with friends or by yourself it’s a little getaway like you left the city.

this is a nice place to visit after the opera house. there are various types of flowers, plants trees and the botanical nomenclature to compliment its entirety. we couldn't find many birds though except for one friendly stork that didn't mind being photographed we revisited this place during our recent road trip from qld to melbourne. this place is also used as a retreat during hot days by the visitors to sit under shady areas and have picnics etc. lot of joggers also use this area. overall, it's a nice place to spend some time when in sydney.

this is a nice place to walk around after we had visited the nearby mosque. lots of people out and about and again plenty of horse drawn carriages if walking is not your thing. but a pleasant enough place just a bit away from the hustle and bustle of the main square in marrakesh.

this is a nice rose garden. the only good time to visit is end of may - beginning of june when the flowers are blooming. there are many rose plants of various colours. overall there is a better garden with roses in vienna but this one is also nice and conveniently located if you are visiting schönbrunn park or the zoo

this is a nice short hike that ends at a lovely beach. the start of the hike is a pretty big incline. but eventually evens out with some ups and downs as you walk. bring a blanket and some snacks and you can have a lovely little picnic at the end on the beach. the beach is quite rocky and challenging to walk around barefoot, so make sure to wear appropriate footwear. the water is clean and you can swim in it. saw a lot of sea stars! there is pay parking that starts at 10am.
this is a nice small park in downtown havana to relax after exploring the area. there is enough seating space.

this is a nice spot to visit, but a little pricey to get in and then pay again for the cable car or zip line. the falls themselves are beautiful and the walk across the suspension bridge is a really neat experience. i would recommend paying for a single trip on the cable car to go up and then walking the stairs back down.

this is a once in a lifetime experience. our tour guide, abu nader, took care of us every moment of our stay. he is knowledgeable and friendly. our family enjoyed every part : the stunning location, the delicious meals, tea and stargazing around the campfire, jeep tour, friendly guide, hiking and sunset camel ride. the accommodations exceeded our expectations. completely recommend.

this is a once in a lifetime experience. our tour guide, abu nader, took care of us every moment of our stay. he is knowledgeable and friendly. our family enjoyed every part : the stunning location, the delicious meals, tea and stargazing around the campfire, jeep tour, friendly guide, hiking and sunset camel ride. the accommodations exceeded our expectations. completely recommend.

this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity! the architecture is fantastic. i also visited the museum, which was an impressive experience. traveling by ferry added a unique touch to the trip. however, be cautious of scammers. if you have booked a city pass, just scan the qr code to enter—do not pay anyone standing by the roadside or at the entrance.

this is a paradise for food enthusiasts on the hunt for fresh ingredients. its vast selection of farm-fresh produce, aromatic herbs, and exotic spices will leave you amazed. friendly local vendors and the market's lively ambiance make sourcing ingredients an enjoyable adventure. get ready to elevate your culinary creations! male sure to come past 10pm or even better-midnight. activities will start winding down from about 3am.

this is a perfect self-guided excursion for a port of call. san cristobal is a short walk from the cruise port through historic san juan. the entry fee is reasonable and also provides access to castillo san felipe del morro. we had a wonderful time exploring the castle including its secret passages. the castle also provides wonderful views of the surrounding area. the rangers and staff are quite helpful. the only concern was that the water bottle filling station was out of order during our visit.

this is a place where you can get the pictures with marina bay sands, singapore flyer, the esplanade view. either on daytime or evening time, you can get the wonderful scenery of singapore river and the nearby buildings. to access this place, you can walk from singapore merlion statue or one fullerton, opposite the fullerton hotel.
this is a popular beach bar and shezlongs rental. the drinks and just long rentals here a little bit pricey. they do have a variety of drinks at the bar and quite an extensive beachfront.

this is a pretty cool museum for art exhibits from artists with african heritage! a lot of the artists use their art as a medium to communicate so many things! some are fun, some are thought-provoking, some are reflective, some are a window into the artists’ heritage. i really loved walking through the museum and reading about each art work. i enjoyed the paintings by rachel jones, the art pieces of scott johnson (bold and beautiful stone carvings) and morel doucet (delicate and gorgeous)!

this is a pretty good mall in terms of stores, architecture, and customer needs. it has all the basic amenities and more.pretty fun magic planet here, and there's also vox cinemas!!!.the place is very long, and although it might look like a small place at first, it's not. it's really long, and there's quite a lot to walk. i would say this is a nice place to hang with friends or family once in a while. the main highlight is that there is metro access available, so it makes this place pretty popular. pretty big food court and the washrooms are well maintained. overall, a solid 7/10... good job!!

this is a rating about the diving more than the dive shop itself. scuba diving is extremely expensive (two to three times the cost of mexico) and what you will see is just so-so. you can probably see just as much snorkeling especially in the port which has a lot of wildlife including sea turtles and sharks. and after paying really high prices, all the shops try to sell you overpriced photos of you diving. that part left a bad taste for me.

this is a really cool lodge on the skeleton coast where it feels like you’re at the end of the world. everyone who works here was so sweet and helpful, the rooms are totally unique with their shipwreck look and feel, and the food was very good. the outings were really great too. we saw the giant seal colony (likely 10k+ seals) at mowe bay, went up the ephemeral (mostly dry at this time of year) river to see the rock formations and animals, did the quad biking and dune boarding (basically sledding down the dunes) and spent time walking along the beach and having lunch on the beach. as for animals, we saw two brown hyena, jackals, springbok and a bunch of other animals. there’s no place like this - a total one of a kind type of experience. giant thanks to our guide shimi who was not only amazing as a guide but when the fog wouldn’t abate and we couldn’t fly out of mowe bay, he drove us all the way to the alternative airport 3hrs away for us to still make our flight that day. he was amazing. definitely give this place a try.

this is a really fun park, more laid back than some of the other adventure parks but still a very enjoyable experience. lots of things to do and take part in which keeps you busy until you get hungry and then you can enjoy the food at one of the restaurants. there was a good choice of food and the staff were all lovely. it’s easy to lose track of time here but thankfully there are clocks next to the maps dotted around the park. this was a great experience and i would definitely visit again. this park should definitely be included in your plans if you visit mexico!

this is a really nice market that has almost everything you need! most of all, the kinds of foods you can here. you can try traditional new orleans food and eat them with the sounds of the market. there are tons osmf stands that sell souvenirs, clothes, art, music, and so much more. the location is perfect! it is a few steps away from jackson square, from the waterfront, and from all the busy streets. also, you can have beignets at the famous cafe du monde.

this is a reasonably easy hike but it gives you some fantastic views of banff! starting at the lower parking area provides a bit more elevation but is pretty straightforward as a hike. i would recommend starting at the upper parking area (assuming the road is open!) as you are immediately on the trail and into the woods. grade is low to moderate from this point forward. there really aren’t any other trials branching off from the main trail so once you’re on it you just keep going. when you get near the summit, there are a number of lookout points behind guard rails that give you fantastic views east overlooking the bow river and the banff springs golf course. this is also the popular side for climbers and you might get a peak of them as well. continuing on to the top, you’ll be rewarded with expansive views of banff and the landmarks - banff springs hotel, rim rock, sulphur mountain and more. as with any hike in the mountains, it's always good to be on the lookout for animals. that said, this is such a popular hike, and it’s basically in banff, unless you go off peak hours, you likely won’t encounter anything. great hike to do if you’re in banff although i’m not sure i would make it a destination hike on its own. either way, highly recommend checking it out!

this is a reconstruction of king anawratha's palace, who reigned from bagan 1044-1077. he introduced theravada buddhism in the region, resulting in the many temples. there are 8 large wooden halls where the king conducted royal affairs, meetings, ceremonies etc. the restaurant under the shady trees is lovely. other attractions are costume rental, souvenir stalls, electric or horse buggy rental. a 5000kyat entry fee for foreigners.

this is a reliable, experienced and professional company that delivers. all of which is what you really want when planning ahead. our contact with maria in planning was great, while the guide themselves was attentive and experienced. they go to great lengths to cater for things like dietary requirements and/or allergies which was important for us. we only did a 2 day tour of the okavango and did the rest of botswana by ourselves as we are based in the region, but for those visiting from afar this would be a company i'd recommend without hesitation to do a longer tour with. for the okavango and moremi in particular they are fantastic,

this is a review of the mulstoa coastal walk, in winter, not of the mulstoa campground or beach. we spent a week in lofoten in early february and were looking for winter hikes. due to the weather conditions and too much snow on the mountains we looked for 'coastal walks' or easier, regular 'walking trails' we could do that would still offer great views and allow for a nice outdoors activity. it is incredibly difficult to find information online about such winter hiking opportunities on lofoten when the weather is too bad for 'real' mountain hikes. also most tour operators on lofoten are closed and only start offering guided tours again from mid february onwards. we found a nice coastal walk from haukland to uttakleiv beach which we can really recommend (but it's really just a 'walk', not really a 'hike') and this mulstoa coastal trail, which we really enjoyed. the trail starts right next to a beautiful beach, yttersand, (there is a small parking spot right at the trailhead which fits about 2-3 cars and which is a lot more convenient than the 2km distant parking place at fredvang for the kvalvika and ryten hikes) and opposite to it you see an impressive mountain range for the entire walk. we could only identify the official trail at the beginning, for about the first 200m (walk is 1.7km) it then disappeared under too much snow and there was just no way to spot it under the snow. we then basically made our own way across rocks and snow and ice, it took us about 1 hour to reach a rock formation on the other side, at the end of the mountain range, where we rested, took fotos and which is really beautiful and raw. it took so long because we had to really 'work' our way over those rocks and test every step with our sticks before moving forward. we did not go all the way to the mulstoa beach part since the trail on this last bit is a bit exposed on one side and was covered under too much snow, so it didn't feel safe to go. needless to say on the entire hike it was very cold, windy, no other hikers, we wore crampons and walking sticks and several layers of clothes. in a nutshell, if you are an experienced hiker it is possible to do this in winter in my personal view but if there is a lot of snow be aware that you might not be able to see the trail and you definitely need crampons (!) and walking sticks (!) to find a way over the rocks in snow and ice. overall, probably this hike cannot be recommended in winter conditions and can be dangerous to walk - but it definitely is beautiful and offers spectacular winter views of lofoten. we really enjoyed it but i wouldn't recommend it to everyone. if you do it in winter, really be careful...

this is a small, but well-designed aquarium spanning levels 4-6 of the shopping mall. don't expect to see big sea creatures here, but there are lots of small interesting and rare creatures which are classified according to their textures eg hairy, lumpy, spiky etc. when we were there, there's a spongebob squarepants theme and there were many cute decals, quizzes and stamps for visitors to collect around the aquarium. the highlight of the aquarium are the rock hopper penguins on level 6, which also houses a cafe/bar and a team labs-like interactive light display of sea creatures. overall, this aquarium may not appeal to those who get bored easily and expect the range found in bigger places. however, it's a nice and comfortable place to spend an hour or so for a date or with young children.

this is a special place, and we decided to go to misool for our 25th wedding anniversary. misool doesn't need more outstanding reviews. the word has already gotten out, and it already has a multi-year waiting list. i had been told that it was one of the nicest places in the world, and despite having to wait a long time to get to see it in person, it did not disappoint. we are still glowing from our trip a month ago. even if you are the type of person who likes to complain (and let's face it, there's a bit of that in all of us), they don't leave you much to complain about! they have thought about everything. 1. the place is wonderful and somewhat remote. you have to get to sorong (usually through jakarta or bali), and then it's a 5-hour private high-speed luxury boat ride from there. due to that remoteness, it's: (a) right in the middle of wonderful, pristine reefs and walls that are just a 5-minute boat ride from the resort and (b) there is no trash in the reef and no other tourists -- you are by yourselves in this marine paradise. 2. the marine life is outstanding: different types of sharks including leopard/zebra sharks, rays (including mantas), all types of fish, of course. crystal aquamarine water that is warm, clean, and refreshing. tons of turtles and countless black-tipped sharks. whether you're scuba diving, snorkeling or swimming, be prepared for a marine paradise. 3. the physical plant is gorgeous, eco-friendly, and luxurious. it's in an unbeatable location, surrounded by an aqua-green, pristine lagoon in the heart of marine-life-rich raja ampat. the buildings are a combination of eco-friendly and luxurious. there are fans and ac in every room with a big poster bed and mosquito net, nice appointments, outdoor showering area -- and spic and span clean. each cottage has a good amount of space and privacy. a lovely deck off every room for relaxing and reading. the hive (where there is good quality internet via a satellite and is the only place where there is wifi) is fantastic -- comfortable and very well-planned with comfy nooks for resting, private cubbies for you to store your stuff you don't want to carry back to your cottage and even places to take a nap, other areas on the big deck, living room type sitting areas for socialising, tables, etc. by the dive centre is a full-on separate cottage for storing and organising your photography equipment, as well as charging and maintaining your photo and video gear. the scuba/dive centre is amazingly organised, with each cottage having its own area. the equipment is high quality. we even tried the scooters (think james bond-type motorised jets for being able to speed underwater) -- super fun and highly recommended. 4. the food was terrific. the current chef prepares unique, healthy, fresh food that isn't too heavy. i was expecting a lot of heavy sauces and deep-fried food, and i was pleasantly surprised that there was very little (or none) of that. there were four full-on meals (including 1st and 2nd breakfast) and one snack per day--no one is going to starve! the food was masterfully prepared, offering a wide range of choices for every course, an infusion of local flavours, and refreshing culinary blends. the wait staff was exceptional, knowing your name and preferences. 5. finally, the staff is outstanding -- knowledgeable, committed to environmental concerns, extremely cordial and respectful, friendly, helpful, and going overboard to make sure your stay is as wonderful as possible. they seem to genuinely care about the place and have a personal attachment. saying goodbye (about 100 people work there, supporting around 48 guests) at the end of the trip was sad. i hope we can return as soon as possible!

this is a special small group kayak tour by matt who is also a local musician. was a decent workout to and around goat island. the short 1/2 hour walk on goat island was special given the aboriginal history and harsh colonization conditions. i would 100% recommend for those that are fit and wanting to get a unique view of sydney.

this is a spectacular waterfall, easily accessed via a 10 minute walk from the car park down to the bridge. there are 2 circular walks here, but the coloured signs get confusing and we just came back the way we went in. note - if you cross the bridge and keep going, you you’ll end up miles away in a different car park. small fee for parking, which is,li,tied, but runs over constantly. well worth the half hour stop on the way to or from ullapool.

this is a stunning and peaceful walk/hike. highly recommended to spend a day doing this and visiting oia to see the famous blue domes. are there toilets? yes, there is a toilet along the way - if you follow the coast the whole way and go via the church of prophet elias. it is a long drop toilet but is enclosed for privacy. time and length: it totals around 10km (6 miles). it took me 2.5 hours but i started from firofestani from my hotel. if you started in the centre of fira it would take you more like 3. this is based on walking at a moderate pace and only stopping for the odd photo or rest for water. a fast walker could do this in two hours with minimal stopping. difficulty: if you are an experienced hiker, it would probably seem a breeze. i'd say it's a medium difficulty if you are generally fit and healthy but don't have much hiking experience, like me. it was challenging, but totally doable. route and terrain: the trail has a nice mix of uphill and downhill, smooth and rocky, and you are rewarded often along the way with breathtaking views. you could follow the main road more if you wanted and it would probably be a bit easier but i wanted to stick to the coast for the views the whole way, which meant it was a bit more rocky and steep at some points. but extremely rewarding. it is not really signposted much, but there are a couple of signs along the way which reassure you, some of which are hand sprayed. if you go via the church of prophet elias as mentioned above you can stop at the toilet near there. that's about 30-50 minutes in. time to start: i would definitely start early as other reviews have suggested. there is no shade along the route! i started straight after breakfast at 8:30am but i went in late march in the low season when it wasn't baking hot so if i was doing it in summer i'd go earlier than that, take snacks and then get a nice breakfast in oia. going from fira to oia in the morning means the sun is on your back, probably better than walking into the sun. if you're walking back in the afternoon you may want to time it so that you arrive to see the sunset in fira while having dinner. what to bring: - good trainers or walking shoes - hat and sunglasses (shade is minimal) - water and supplies (there isn't an opportunity along the way to buy any, but in the high season there may be one or two small setups. i saw a little hut that looked like it would sell drinks about halfway, but it was closed) - a light shirt to cover arms from the sun if walking in the heat of the day other things to note: if you get tired closer to the end there is a spot where you can hire a donkey to ride the rest of the way to oia. when i passed it the sign said it cost €10 one way and took 30 minutes. this route is not wheelchair or stroller friendly. if you don't want to walk back, a taxi from oia to fira costs €30, or you can get the bus for €2-3

this is a stunning complex worthy of at least 90-120 minutes of just getting lost. make sure to go all the way to the very east side, better yet have your tuk tuk driver drop you off at the east side gate to the city and then pick you up at the west side gate. look up, look behind you, head down side corridors. there are treasures hidden around every corner. one of the best temples in all of the angkor archaeological park.

this is a stunning historic building originally built as a church but now serves as a mausoleum for famous french figures like voltaire, rousseau, and marie curie. it’s known for its impressive neoclassical architecture and its huge dome. inside, you can see the foucault pendulum demonstrating earth’s rotation. it’s a cool spot to learn about france’s history and see some beautiful design.

this is a stunning sculpture fountain found at the waterfront end of “paseo de la princesa”. this fountain celebrates the 500th anniversary of spain's 'discovery' of the new world. it was commerated on may 30, 1992 and was designed by architect miguel carlo. the fountain depicts bronze gods and goddesses of taíno, european and african descent. it showcases the diverity of puerto ricos heritage which includes african, spanish and taino / american descent.

this is a very important and poignant memorial to a horrific chapter in scotland's history. the monument itself depicts a family leaving our shores for parts unknown and is surrounded with plaques in gàidhlig and english. there are also interesting information boards explaining this awful episode. however, for such an important monument, it is curated very poorly. there is no signposting at all; we drove past it four times. the car park is not well maintained, and you think you're pulling up in front of a derelict, though modern, scout hut... i'm guessing the building was originally intended as some sort of small visitor centre, but it sits closed and apparently empty. once you realise you're in the right place, there is plenty parking. the statue is then accessed by some steep steps, rendering it completely inaccessible to wheelchair users and, indeed, anyone with restricted mobility. i'm not one to complain about unreasonable access problems but, as a relatively new monument (unveiled in 2007), this is pretty unacceptable. a sloping path would have been easy enough to build instead. if there is better access through the park, this is, again, not intimated anywhere. if you can get to the monument (my companions were able to, i was not), the views are spectacular, and it is a fascinating monument to the 19th century emigrants. but the implementation is sadly lacking.

this is a very popular spot to grab food and drinks after a long day at work or during your day off. whether you’re looking to unwind with a cocktail, enjoy a casual dinner, or simply hang out with friends, this place has you covered. the atmosphere is lively yet relaxed, making it perfect for both social evenings and laid-back afternoons. with a great menu and good vibes, it’s no surprise that it’s a favorite for locals and visitors alike.
this is a very scenic hike to get to the falls. it has some challenging portions with steep inclines and declines. many uneven parts where you need to maneuver, so proper footwear is a must.

this is a very small museum included in the dubrovnik pass. whilst there's very little "physical material" items, objects etc, there is a lot of information display on a chronological sequence of boards about the multifaceted life of this man. noted as the most famous playwright in croatian history, he also entered the priesthood, was an administrator and a skilled musician and writer.

this is a well maintained, beautiful cemetery. there is a kiosk near the entrance to help find graves of loved ones. the monuments and statues are incredible. we felt honored to pay our respects to the fallen veterans and their families. we are so glad we came to visit. it's very emotional to see this cemetery.

this is a wholesome and enjoyable experience. adrian was a fantastic guide for the day. the team are friendly and helpful from pickup through the market visit (an authentic local market with no tourists) and support for cooking. and the menu is soooo good. 50% of the fees go to the orphanage, a wonderful way to give back while enjoying your holiday.

this is a wonderful activity for all ages. there's so much to see. i particularly enjoy the japanese and rose gardens. bonsai trees date back to 1800's. restrooms are available and very clean. a great place to sit in the shade or enjoy a long walk.

this is a wonderful little cookery school. the owner puts all of the profits towards helping local disadvantaged and orphaned children. we not only learned about cambodian cooking, but also about cambodian history and culture. ben is an incredibly knowledgeable and friendly tour guide. he kept the class running even though the other guests dropped out and it was just my wife and i. the location in the countryside just took around 30 minutes to get to by tuk tuk and was so much nicer than simply staying in the city. it was a wonderful experience.

this is a wonderful museum to educate visitors on jeju island. there are exhibits on the people of jeju, and their traditions. there are detail exhibits that show the types of animals, vegetations, predators, and produce that are on and around the island. we really enjoyed our time in the museum. it gave us a lot of insight on how the island evolved and the eco system here. it's very affordable, i highly recommend coming here to learn about the island.

this is a wonderful museum—my husband and i absolutely loved it. if you're arriving by ferry or have time before your departure, it's well worth a visit. having spent the first years of my life in the former yugoslavia, walking through the exhibits felt like stepping back in time: the same kind of kitchen my grandmother had, the same old scale, and many other familiar details. it was both nostalgic and deeply moving.
this is a wonderful neighborhood local market, has almost everything you need and a staff that delivers excellent service. as a new orleans native this is a great asset to our community…

this is a wonderful place in the centre of athens. it’s perfect for some peace especially when it’s 40c in the summer. there is plenty of shade and places to sit down in the park. lots of walking. there’s also animals, such as turtles and ducks here. of course there are toilets and a kids playground too. would recommend for anyone visiting athens.

this is a wonderful place to visit with some very nice audio visual effects to show how settlers came and habitation developed. original archeology of long house is here and you can get close up to look. there is a lot of reading and information too so younger kids may lose interest. the museum is also linked to the oldest house museum. for best value visiting in reykjavik buy the city pass which allows access to most of the museums and also local swimming pools/geo heated pools.

this is a wonderful smaller camp in wadi rum in a gorgeous location. we stayed in one of the tent-style rooms, and it was clean and very comfortable, with sufficient outlets to charge phones. the view from the large windows was amazing, and we really appreciated having a nice deck to sit on and read and enjoy the beautiful view. the bathroom was large and clean with a very good shower and even a hair dryer. the common areas were also very comfortable and well decorated. the night we stayed was chilly, so we especially appreciated the fire places and hot tea. the food was very good and fresh as well. finally, the staff was incredibly kind, and we felt that we were being welcomed into their home. mohammed patiently answered all our questions and made sure we were well taken care of, and we received a great jeep tour from hassan. i highly recommend this camp and will absolutely stay here again.

this is a world-class natural history museum. it is great for both adults and children, and jam packed with fantastic exhibits. they do a particularly great job with a animal exhibits. i spent the most time in the rocks and minerals room. what an amazing collection. make sure you leave yourself enough time. the place is huge. if you are there with children, i suggest you go first to the dinosaur area. it is very kid-centered and not geared for adults at all, but it is a real draw for the kids. and it gets very crowded as the day progresses. the museum is free, but take the time to reserve a timed entry for your group. it will save you a lot of time waiting in a long line. this is really a fantastic museum. my only suggestion to the curators would be to label everything. we felt there was a lost educational opportunity to have so many items without labels.

this is a “must do” experience! we had the best time learning the history and meeting new people. so many activities to do. we got to stop by and see axolotls and buy souvenirs. our tour guide isa was the best keeping the energy up. the mariachi was fun and we also did a guacamole contest for those that are competitive. definitely recommend booking, especially with isa!

this is about a half km from the trail head. the view here is spectacular. another 1 and 1/2 km up the trail gets you to the two lakes lookout. absolutely amazing here. it's a steep climb to this point and my husband and i had to turn back as our combined age is 151.

this is absolutely amazing!! the trees, vines, palms, pandanus....and all on a boardwalk! this is the best way to experience the flora of the region if you can't make it all the way up to the daintree!

this is absolutely the one of the best museums i’ve been to. i’m not a big history person so i wasn’t very excited, but it’s set up beautifully. i appreciate that they focus on things they can improve on instead of just the positives. i 100% recommend this museum and think it’s a must.

this is actually a place to worship hindu gods. located at carnavanon road, it is easily approachable from both tst east n tst mtr. this place is actually an apartment converted to hindu temple very very nicely. it has nice sitting space. and yes there is a small gurudwara in this temple itself for our sikh brothers. a must place to visit. don't forget to take the prasad and say thanks to the nearby family who takes well care of this temple. #om sai ram

this is an aboslutely beautiful hike. it is short but it is pretty steep al the way to the top of the hill, that's why i wouldn't describe it as easy but as a moderate one. it took us a bit more than 1 hour to the top and then around 1 hour back. we were pretty fast so i guess hikers on average need up to 2 hours to come to the top. the trail is absolutely stunning. we were blessed with a great weather and the views were amazing.

this is an absolute must if you're visiting san juan. such a nice experience to be able to paddle board and see the manatees, turtles, and fishes in their habitat. the owner, julio, and his crew and their outstanding customer service and instructions will make sure everyone is safe while having a great time. totally recommended. im definitely coming back.

this is an absolute must see venue. the expansive, well documented display cases with adequate room to comfortably view and study. this place multistory so plan on several hours of enjoyment and learning. we need to go back a second time! the mosaics are beautiful.

this is an absolute must-visit if you’re in the san juan area. admission is only $10 and it’s well worth it for everything you get to explore. the fort is huge and rich with history with multiple floors, hidden rooms and various access points that make it feel like you’re walking through a living time capsule. the views are spectacular, captured some amazing cinematic photos and videos during my visit. overall though the fort and its rooms, dungeons, walls, etc. show their age but that’s exactly what makes it so special. every worn stone and weathered wall tells a story and it truly feels like stepping back in time. it can get busy and the sun is intense so i highly recommend bringing sunscreen and staying hydrated. other than that, i loved every square foot of this place, it left a lasting impression and i know i’ll be visiting again whenever i return to puerto rico. highly recommended!

this is an absolutely amazing museum. while you do need to get a ticket, tickets are by donation. they have some incredibly exhibits, entertaining and educational for people of all ages. the apollo command module, watson and crick’s dna model, and the exhibit on the evolution of medicine and vaccines are some of my highlights. the great thing is that it can be enjoyed whether you only have an hour to spare, or an entire day.

this is an absolutely beautiful lake that has many different aspects and habitats. the views from all sides were beautiful, especially the incredible wetland. there were massive amounts of dead and diseased trees around the edge, but it did not ruin the view. this lake is well worth it!

this is an absolutely gorgeous site and well worth your time to make the detour. walk around the wall and enter through the west gate. explorable yet very compact, the walled temple is highly recommended.

this is an amazing experience when you visit tokyo. the staff are cute and the angels are very professional. i must say this is a professional music festival :))) of course with some specialty that we not allow to take photos, media during the show.

this is an amazing experience. we booked a tube ride, parasailing and underwater sea walk. the underwater sea walk is a breathtaking experience, tube ride is exhilarating and parasailing is fun. then we went to ile aus cerfs on the beach, barbecue and waterfall. everything was perfect, the only - is that the parasailing was a little bit too short, we were up maybe like 3 minutes.😔 everything but that was perfect. people are friendly, on time and helpful. i would recommend it to everyone.

this is an amazing hidden gem. we cycled up from bellavista - which was a bit of a trek uphill (but we were in no rush). when we arrived it looked closed - but the sign said to ring the bell and sure enough the gate opened. for $5 each the site offers a lot. we walked up to the view point, walked down into the crater (also a bit of a trek, but well worth it), and went around the cycle loop. this is a great way to see tortoises, larva lizards, and all sorts of small birds. it was so quiet when we went - i think we were the only people there for most of the day. unfortunately i got a puncture - but the lady arranged a taxi to pick us up, which was really helpful. if you have some spare time and want to get away from the more crowded parts of santa cruz then this is perfect.

this is an amazing museum for contemporary art. the price is really cheap. and there are many different exhibitions going on. although some rooms was closed. they where setting new exhibitions. the current exhibitions where very good. specially the one about protests and the people who “disappeared “ during this period. there is an installation in the shape of a hut or a house. but with inclination, it is really awesome. the museum is very well designed and has various spaces that daylight comes in. the museum shop has a good selection of items and the restaurant is very nice. specially the patio side. this in of the museums in the city that one should really visit. metro 3 stop university. (last stop). and in university city the buses are for free. so you can hop on.

this is an amazing museum that shows many aspects of modern war. well worth a visit if you can make the time. war isn't a pretty subject but it is a harsh reality of our lives. the museum presents it all well. it isn't always uplifting but very informative.

this is an amazing place - very ‘zen’ and a really ‘must see’ when visiting japan. however, more tourist have this on their bucket list, so visiting or before 10h00 is advised. we did so and experienced beauty and serenity. everyone respected the beauty of the sacred place. the zen / rock garden is amazing - and the surrounding garden is also very inspiring. we visited in june (rain season) but we were lucky and had a nice sunny day.

this is an amazing place for sunset! just a few things to check in order to have the best experience: * better to come by car if you are planning to watch the sunset from here. the starting point is close to the city by car, but we had a very hard time trying to get an uber after the sunset and walking back to the city during the night was not fun at all! * the hike is short and easy, but there are plenty of steps so allow at least 30 minutes to make sure you can make it to the top at a comfortable pace * the golden hour here is stunning! i suggest coming about 1h20 -1h30 before the sunset starts if you like to just sit down, enjoy a snack and fascinating views * since the hike is very easy, i would recommend taking some snacks and even some drinks with you! we saw people drinking gin&tonic, champagne, a glass of wine… it feels really nice and relaxing! * don’t forget to put on sunscreen! even though it is sunset, the uv is very high in cape town!

this is an amazing place to go as a family with plenty of activities. whether you are going down the tube slide, going on the banana boat or ice skating, there is plenty to do for all ages. the kids used the zorbs, we all went down the slide, all went on the banana boat ride and got the chance to skate outdoors. the staff were fantastic to us. i would definitely recommend coming here if you are planning a visit with the kids to rovaniemi in the winter!
this is an amazing place to organize events,festivals and concerts.very clean,and accessible by train,has good large car parking area.

this is an amazing place! i would definitely recommend getting tickets ahead of time, since they were sold out for at least a week when we got into town. however, people with disabilities can get in free, and bring one other person, which you have to pay for, but it’s so worth it. and you can get right in. and as you can see from the pictures, frida’s house is just amazing, and amazingly wheelchair accessible . you can’t roll into the gift shop, or the upstairs portion of the blue house, but everywhere else is pretty smooth sailing. what i took in is an amazing story, and how she dealt with it all. there are amazing pictures that i’ve never seen in art history books, and i was even able to see a picture of marcel duchamp’s, “nude descending a staircase”, which in and of itself is amazing. i would highly recommend taking an afternoon to take in this beautiful house museum.
this is an amazing place, definitely visit. check the tour times, there are french speaking and english speaking tours at different times.
this is an amazing private beach. it’s quite the hike from the main ephelia resort. when we arrived, nobody was there and the tide was perfect. one of the nicest beaches on the island
this is an amazing spot to look at the sunset while visiting cartagena. the cafe was closed for remodeling, habit you can still go up and see the sunset.

this is an amazing spot to watch the sunrise! the hike is moderately difficult, even more so when wet. there are some steep and slippery areas that require good physical mobility. while it wasn't crowded, there will be plenty of other people there. everyone there was cool and respectful. the views were amazingly spectacular! remember, this is a residential area, so be quiet and respectful of those living nearby so as not to disturb them in the predawn hours.
this is an amazing viewpoint for the south rim! parking is great and fir those with some agility you can wander down the trail for unobstructed views. this is a popular spot so expect lots of people

this is an amazing walk from taronga zoo to middle head to chowder bay to balmoral track with beautiful views of sydney harbour bridge and opera house - best to go when sunset in the warmer months. there's also alot of history highlighting the japanese war and how they wanted to attack sydney's borders. go up and around to middle head then make your way back down and take right turn ending in balmoral beach for a dip. or have some fish and chips there.

this is an amazing winter zoo! the place is great… nice walk in the wild, great places for animals! highlights: polar bear, grizzly bear, lynx, and the reindeers… must visit, especially with kids! facilities include restaurant and bars, and a place for cooking your sausages in the wild!!! must see it!

this is an archeological museum with 4 floors of displays but one display floor was closed in the lower basement level. regardless, the antiquities are a fine way to bring to life all the brown/gray ruins around rome left partially intact or in a near rubble pile state. apply the color of every day roman living quarters to those sites you have seen and just imagine what they once actually looked like with frescoes on walls of dinning, living, and bedrooms rooms. the intricate mosaics decorating walls and floors with scenes of everything they cherished in their life time. the sculptures and busts of heroes and legends adorning their homes, gardens and bathhouses. now one begins to learn of the romans way of life. allow 3 hours to casually explore this ancient world treasure.

this is an authentic, traditional ceramic studio using 100-yr old machinery and hand-intensive methods to create household and souvenir items. we were guided by samuel of green corner tours who explained the various stages of the process. of course, the tour ends with the gift shop and there are dozens of designs and items available. the production portion is not open year-round, so check in advance. recommended.

this is an awesome hike! the exhibit and springs above are amazing, and also definitely worth a visit. this is a very easy trail with some wildlife like snakes and birds. the views down at the marsh are absolutely spectacular. definitely walk this easy and beautiful trail while at this park!

this is an awesome paved hike up to the top of the trail that has beautiful views of the pacific ocean and a lighthouse. it's a little over 2 miles out and back. we got to the trailhead around 7.15 am on sunday morning, and there were plenty of parking spaces. 45 minutes later, as we made our way back down, almost all the parking spaces were full, so get to this hike early. it's one of the best trails on the island.

this is an awesome trail project. i diverted off the great divide mountain bike route to ride through yellowstone. while the climb from big springs up to reas pass was a slog through sand, the descent on the shortline trail to west yellowstone made it worthwhile, plus i got to avoid riding highway! this will be an awesome trail once complete. i only hope that they make the ohv trail up from big springs more rideable (difficult to ride on anything less than 2.5”+ tires).

this is an easy hike on a paved road along a hillside. in the past it had been possible to drive the majority of the way to the viewpoint, but now the road is closed to local access. the hike takes about 20 minutes each way, and you can’t see trøllkonufingur until you reach the end of the viewpoint. the hike is super scenic and definitely worth the effort.
this is an easy hike, with a great reward. we unfortunately missed the geyser go off by the time we got there, so we waited the 2 hours and explored the surrounding area. worth the wait!
this is an easy, nice trail to walk to get a great view of yellowstone lake.

this is an eighteen metre tall monument dedicated to the men that fought in the jacobite rising. the scenery of the highlands all around is perfectly fitting for jacobite story tied to the monument. you can book to climb to the top of the monument if you book in advance if you can handle the height of it. it sits right at the shore of loch shiel and would offer amazing panoramic views from the top of the monument. we visited this while visiting the viaduct which is literally across the road from the monument.

this is an essence part of scotland (and of skye) so a traveler should do it. because it is not only about pubs and castles and cosy places ... it is also about nature, the mighty nature and about stretching ones legs onto path shared by man and sheep. such wonderful sights...!

this is an excellent beach, had little sargassum even though cancun beaches were full of it. it's about a 19 minute walk from the main port. has ropes to keep boats away and beyond that there is quite a bit of boat traffic. still, a wonderful beach with golden white sand and crystal clear turquoise azure waters. saw quite a bit of fish snorkeling here, from smelt size to 18". no corals, but there is sea grass beyond the ropes and i just stayed close to them. gentle waves that didn't create turbulence to stir sand. independent vendors run umbrella and chairs rentals, and will take and deliver drinks and food orders to you. restaurants close by if you'd rather walk and take a break from sun and heat. i read this is one of the best beaches in the world, and i've seen some of them, based on looks, water temperature and convenience, i agree.
this is an excellent excursion if you were in the area. beautiful scenery, great gift, shops, and restaurant/bar at the top. also access to fun hiking trails.

this is an excellent park, we were walking around here and about to go into a house when we realised we had to pay! there is a fee to explore this area but it’s a small fee which gives you a lot to look at. there is a lot of places to see and to learn if you are into this sort of history. we loved the views of the city from the different areas above. “jonique life” if you find value in our reviews please consider following our social media outlets on facebook and instagram as we highlight magical places you can add to your ever growing bucket list.

this is an excellent place for photos and videos. there’s a small parking lot at the corner and trail access to the hoodoo trail. descend down to the river and take a moment to listen to the power of the water rushing down the nearby bow falls or following trail and walk to the hoodoos viewpoint.
