this is an excellent place to visit. the food is gourmet. the icelandic ponies are a joy to ride. scenery is to die for. and the best part is everyone is friendly and helpful. try the sauna and plunge into the ocean.

this is an excellent shop and location to learn and do kite surfing!! jesus is an incredible instructor with patience and knows how to motivate and instruct perfectly. i have had only a few lessons in the past and i was almost able to get totally up in the board and ride in one hour after not doing it for almost a year!! camelo i believe the owner is also extremely nice and accommodating. in conclusion the price, kind waters, good wind and small crowds makes this my future go to spot for kite surfing!!! 🌊

this is an excellent venue for volleyball matches, and it ranks among my favorites in japan. the restroom facilities are well-maintained and can accommodate a large number of visitors. the seating arrangement, especially the super seats, is well-organized. however, on rainy days, despite its proximity to the station, reaching the venue can be quite challenging.

this is an experience of a lifetime for me, the highlight of my entire trip! the guide gunawan is experienced, friendly, knowledgeable and i felt so safe with him guiding and helping me reach the summit. not to mention an amazing photographer! the driver ady is communicative, friendly, punctual, skilled and armed with great local hotsprings tips. thank you gunawan and ady for the amazing experience!

this is an extraordinary beach / nature reserve. turtles lay their eggs, young sharks swim in the waves. the sand is golden and wildlife moves in the vegetation at the edge of the beach. remember to take plenty of water and photographs.

this is an extremely interesting museum which also has a separate hall dedicated to events in ukraine and the works that banksy did when he was in ukraine in november 2022. we highly recommend visiting, my daughter and i spent a wonderful 2 hours in this museum!
this is an important historical landmark. when in berlin, you do need to stop by. but don’t expect too much. during the day is usually very crowded. we walked by around 9pm and was much better.

this is an impressive column covered in the stories and victories of napoleon. it is set in a square which pedestrians need to be careful of, as it looks like it doesn’t permit cars but it does. around the square are all the high end designers and brands.

this is an interesting little shop with a combination of hand-made and mass-produced goods, some local, some asian. speak to the owners about your purchase to ensure you know what you are buying. one of the things i liked here is the extensive assortment of carving tools. i can't speak to the quality, but at about 30chf or more each, i would hope they are good for serious woodworkers.

this is an old factory with a great approach to customers. they show you the entire factory with a really proficient guide and offer you tee! everything for free! everything is well presented and the journey to see the machinery and plantations is amazing. clearly one piece to go if you are interested in tea. recommended!

this is an old food market that dates back to the 19th-century around front st and the esplanade. the market is held each day other than sunday with specific daily hours so visit the market website prior to scheduling your visit to know exact times. you'll find a fairly typical food market setup with over 100 venders dealing in fresh veg, fruits, meats, seafood, cheeses, breads, sweets, rice, spices, drinks and other fresh, perishable and canned food items. there are souvenir shops, prepared food eateries, coffee and flower vendors as well. the main hall is nice view architecturally and the food on display is presentable and photogenic. it is definitely a place worth checking out if you enjoy seeing local food and historic food markets during your travels.

this is an outstanding free community resource which shows off the rich military history of this area from ancient times all the way until current. this museum has everything you'd ever want to know about warfare on oahu going back hundreds of years. the exhibits were beautifully done and the staff was outstanding. please support this place by offering donations or shopping in the gift shop on your way out.

this is an outstanding hotel with great views of the lake. as we stumble in from days full of sight-seeing, we often resort to dining at this hotel's restaurant for convenience but soon discover that the staff and the food make it a worthwhile visit. eduardo, our server was attentive and helpful. he speaks fluent english too and this is helpful. this hotel offers spacious accommodation for a third person in the room; we didn't need it but i'm sure it might be a plus for someone else

this is not a food truck — this is a golden chariot sent from the heavens above to bring pure bliss and joy and meaning to my life. i have been hunting this food truck down for many months now, and im so glad i finally tracked it down. the hoisin chicken roll is immaculate — the green onion pancake wrap is flaky, a bit oily, and perfectly complemented by the crunchy lettuce. paired with the sweet salty hoisin and light, refreshing cucumbers, it tastes a lot like chinese beef rolls ! there’s also quite a lot of chicken inside, and every piece is coated in a generous amount of sauce. the chicken rice box was just as phenomenal, if not even more delicious than the roll. first of all, the portion was super generous and loaded with all the ingredients. in the rice box, you can really taste the quality and flavour of the chicken a lot better than in the wrap; it was super juicy and tender, and the best parts were the chunks of meat that had bits of indulgent, gelatinous chicken skin, some of which had this nice crunchy charred flavour. the heavy flavour chicken, hoisin, and garlic sauce all went so well with the aromatic jasmine rice. eat chicken wraps is the perfect fusion food and eating here was an experience that i never wanted to end — i will definitely be back.

this is not a rescue center — it’s a zoo disguised as one. the crocodiles here weren’t removed from their natural habitat because they were in danger, but because they attacked people. the baby crocodiles kept in cages are not part of any conservation program — they’re being bred for commercial sale, not to be released back into the wild, but handed over to farmers. at the end of the visit, tourists are encouraged to take photos with baby crocodiles whose mouths are tied shut, placed in a loud, chaotic room full of people shouting and excited to touch them. these animals are extremely sensitive to sound, and this is incredibly distressing for them. none of the animals here were rescued due to injury — they were taken from their natural habitat either because they were seen as dangerous or simply to turn them into a profit. please don’t support places like this. it’s not conservation — it’s animal cruelty.

this is one of my favorite farmer's markets in south florida. i have been going there for close to 20 years. they have amazing fresh fruits and vegetables from glaciers farms. amazing raw vegan options. a variety of vendors. this weekend we tried an indonesian vegan vendor the food was amazing.

this is one of my favorite museums in mexico city. free to visit. well air conditioned. bathrooms on site. check back bags at entry. no gum allowed. take the elevator up to the top and work your way down. this museum has one of the most extensive and varied collections i have seen in mexico city … from sculptures to modern art … including several works by marc chagall … definitely worth a visit!

this is one of my favorite museums i’ve been to! i really loved the louis armstrong exhibit and found it quite fascinating! it’s even cooler how the museum was once a mint! the employees were all very nice and friendly!

this is one of my favorite places to hike and enjoy both nature and the vibe of the ancient builders. the shiva linga's in the water baffle me, the amount of work needed to carve out the depictions in the stone of the mountain is huge and there is a great sense of little detail and symmetry. good place to walk the dog too

this is one of my favorite spots in iceland! we were the only ones there for hours (in early september). the natural pool is super hot and on a sunny day you can just rest in the grass when you take a break from the hot water. there‘s a changing room that‘s pretty clean. please don’t leave any garbage and if you enjoyed it donate something (there’s a small box).

this is one of the best beaches in mahé to spend some time in. this is one of those beaches not recommended for swimming due to strong waves, but you can admire the beauty of the place by just relaxing on the beach. it is normally not very crowded and you can have some good time for yourself here.

this is one of the best places i have ever stayed in, with amazing food, staff, cleanliness and rooms. we got a 2 bedroom family room and it was perfect from the size of the beds, the comfort and cleanliness. it was just walking distance to the city and had so many restaurants nearby and attractions. this is a perfect place to stay in ella. highly recommended

this is one of the best spots if you enjoy walking or running while taking in stunning views of lion’s head, camps bay, and table mountain. i went during sunset, and it was absolutely perfect. i highly recommend this place—whether you’re staying in cape town long-term or visiting for the first time, make sure to add it to your list. it’s a must-see!

this is one of the famous and most visited temple in bangkok thailand. when i was there no a lot of tourists but i do like it because i can enjoy the place without having too much people. i was so amazed by the design on how the architect did the concept and designing this incredible structure that can stay up today. i adore how people respect their religious beliefs. and also i admire how they took care of the place. every time i visited thailand i always visit this temple.

this is one of the famous markets in bangkok city, thailand. plenty of options to buy clothes, jewellery, bags and many more other items from here at a reasonable price. but one must definitely know how to bargain otherwise you will get conned. many restaurants were available too. night life was far better here. a very safe place. parking available. cleanliness and hygiene were properly maintained here in this area. the staff's behaviour was awesome and polite. must visit, highly recommended.

this is one of the four attraction places from the four attractions you can buy from their official website. you can see the darling harbour, hyde park and nearby city, from this place. very recommended to go during the sunset. waiting time is more so please go accordingly. you have a sky walk, for which you need to pay extra. the experience is enjoyable but there's nothing more to explore after some time. it's just a deck where you can see the whole city. it's good to see the city from here for us visitors. we'll enjoy the view.

this is one of the hottest attractions in sedona. first, you have to take a shuttle to get to the trailhead, either at dry creek or mescal trailhead. the waiting time to step on the bridge and take a photo can be easily more than an hour. for the most part of the trail, it is very easy. until you close to the bridge. the last scramble may be the hardest but still doable. we are lucky to have a sea of clouds as the background, making the shot more unique and mythical.

this is one of the iconic places of old city of dubrovnik. this is located one end of the city. tourists find this vicinity as a great place to rest while they roam around the old city ramparts of dubrovnik. this has a many vibrant photo locations and people prefer to spend time here leisurely. good to rest during the evenings and morning times.

this is one of the more unique viewpoints at grand canyon due to the proximity of the “duck of a rock” formation. there is still a small pull-out parking area, but usually you will find a parking space since people do not spend much time here. there are no restrooms available but the view from here is worth the stop. you will also have foot access to several outcrops on either side of the parking lot.

this is one of the most beautiful and accessible nature reserves in south africa. the park covers an area of ​​approximately 22,912 km² and can be explored on a guided safari or a self-driving tour. the park is home to over 100 species of mammals, including lions, leopards, cheetahs, hyenas, giraffes, zebras, and antelopes, including oryx, impalas, elands, dik-diks, and ostriches. it is also an ideal place to spot a black rhinoceros. other interesting spots in the park include ponds, where you can observe animals gathering at watering holes. depending on the time of day, you'll encounter animals heading for water, herds with cubs hiding in the tall grass, or the ubiquitous zebra at any time of day or night.

this is one of the most beautiful and stunning hot spring pools in yellowstone park. it is said it used to be entirely blue and now has colours of yellow and green at the edges due to vandalism and pollution from people throwing coins into the pool. will require an easy hike of 20-30 minutes from the old faithful geyser.
this is one of the most beautiful urban parks i have ever been to. i was immediately blown away by the beauty, silence and the nostalgic feeling it gave me!

this is one of the most famous spots here in old town quebec city. it can be very busy and picture taking is difficult unless you don’t mind lots of people in your photos 😂 the location is superb and picturesque with lots to do and see in the area. restaurants, shops are a dime a dozen. it’s never boring here. 👍😎

this is one of the most iconic landmarks in the world, to come to rio and not visit it would be unthinkable. i took the train up to see the statue. very busy, with big queues but they went down very quick. once at the top, you have options of stairs, escalators or a lift to get you up to the statue. brilliant views all around, with christ looking down on everything.

this is one of the most picturesque treks on the island with an almost 360 view near and at the top. this trek is somewhere between moderate and easy at the beginning (the lift is not small). however, there is a lot of climbing needed at the end of it if you wish to get to the le pouce mountain peak itself. the trek becomes very slippery and muddy after the rain, so one should be careful. mind that the upper you go, the windier it gets. and it can be quite cold at the top because of the wind - i recommend having something you can put on. there are places where the trek is very narrow and there are also parts where you'll be getting through the bushes. but the view makes it up for all the challenges. the last part of the trek is basically climbing. we've seen some people dealing with it easily, when others not even starting. it is challenging indeed and there will definitely be a rush of adrenaline because of the height. but no matter whether you decide to climb to the peak or not - you'll be enjoying the views anyways. this hike takes around 4 hours both ways (in a muddy condition) - from the car park to the peak and back. so probably it won't take that long when it's not slippery.

this is one of the most sacred temples in bali. it is located at the foot of mount batukaru and due to the higher altitude it is very humid up here and there's a lot of green moss covering the structures. built in the 11th century, this temple is dedicated to the ancestors of tabanan. you won't see too many tourists here thanks to its remoteness. this is a temple you could visit when you're on the way to jatiluwih rice fields.

this is one of the oldest mosques in mutrah built before 200 years and has been renovated and rebuilt twice. apart from prayers many shiite functions are held here during moharrum and holy month of ramadan. it can accommodate more than seven hundred persons. there is also a mosque on top of the building which is confined for women only. the mosque is built in a beautiful plot facing the mutrah beach and is also very near to mutrah souq (shopping place). although it’s built by shiite muslims but nonetheless all muslims are welcomed here. in oman all muslims live in harmony and there’s also internal marriage between the muslims. god bless them all💕

this is our experience in a 3 nights 4 days nile river cruise from aswan to luxor. the trip is very good and enjoyable, a different experience altogether. many ships are engaged in this trip and the comfort and luxury marginally varies depending on which vessel one has booked their trip in. our ship was named nile admiral and it appeared to be of a medium level luxury cruise. the room with a double bed is smallish with a good wash room (dry and wet area well separated). the bed is enough for two but small for three and occupies 70% of rooms area. other furniture occupied most of the remaining space leaving a very little space for opening luggage and normal movement. however, the space crunch is understood as the vessels can't be made too large keeping in mind the esna lock gate crossing which requires a uniform standard size vessel. the bed linens and toiletries provided were ok. the room has a big glass window for outside view which is fabulous. some of the passing vessels had balcony but ours didn't had one. the top deck or terrace was fantastic with a great wide and open view of both the sides of nile river and the beauty was enjoyed by us. evening tea was regularly served in this top deck everyday. the breakfast, lunch and dinner was served in the dining hall in the basement. the quality if the food was very good but not at all compatible with our indian taste buds. but i personally enjoyed the food on every occasion. wide variety and fresh and unique taste. the vessel also had a small swimming pool which was enjoyed by some members of our group. the ship also had a bar and an entertainment hall where one enjoy drinks and dance show organised by the cruise team. there was also a small souvenir shop inside the ship from where shopping can be done. expensive than market but not bad as in the ship shopping. the trip was as under: day 1 : boarded in stationary ship at afternoon at aswan. roaming locally at aswan, getting a glimpse of the city and a bit of shopping. day 2: abu simbel visit from the ship from aswan early in the morning and back to ship in afternoon. ship starts cruising. evening halt at kom ombo for temple visit. day 3: ship cruised overnight to edfu. visited edfu temple. ship again starts cruise, crosses esna lock gate and reaches luxor in late evening. ship ports. day 4 : checkout from ship to visit luxor temples and other sites. highly recommended trip.

this is our first time booking a shore excursion not with the ship. we were a bit anxious doing the shore excursions independently. i shouldn’t have been as our guide avi which we had both for a private tour and a non private tour was excellent. he was very professional and was very informative. also, we were on time both leaving and getting back to the ship. both these excursions were planned very well. i have also found that the same excursions offered by the ship are far more expensive. i cannot recommend bein harim tours enough. excellent tours and excellent guide!

this is part of the extended green space along with esplanade gaston monnerville and the luxembourg gardens in the 6th arrondissement. it is situated just south of the esplanade between rue michelet (north) and ave. de l'observatoire (south). the garden created in 1867 and is dedicated to world explorers marco polo (1254-1324) and rené-robert cavelier de la salle (1643-87). it is similar in shape and scale to the esplanade to the north and features a couple of the sister monuments that pair with those in the esplanade, flowerbeds, side walking paths, rows of trees on both sides and park benches. however, the most striking feature is the fountain of the four parts of the world at the southern end. this fountain monument was designed by gabriel davioud and completed between 1867-74 and is well worth spending a few minutes to enjoy during time spent at the garden of the grand explorers.

this is probably the first spot you hit once inside the yellowstone park. sure! mammoth hot springs is a truly mesmerizing natural wonder in yellowstone national park. the terraced limestone formations, created by centuries of geothermal activity, look like something from another planet. the colors and textures constantly change, making every visit unique. the boardwalks are well-maintained and offer easy access to stunning views, even for families and older visitors. early morning or late evening visits are especially magical, with steam rising and wildlife often nearby. the upper and lower terraces each offer distinct perspectives, and the historic mammoth hot springs hotel nearby adds charm to the experience. rangers are friendly and informative, enhancing the educational aspect of the visit. it’s a photographer’s dream and a must-see for nature lovers. be sure to bring water, wear comfortable shoes, and take your time exploring. mammoth hot springs is a highlight of yellowstone and a place you’ll never forget.

this is probably the most beautiful of all the tombs in the series of royal tombs. from outside, it looks like another tall facade of any other nabatean tomb in petra. but as soon as you step inside, it's a spectacular sight - bands of colors running across the walls of the carved mountain rock all around. it feels almost psychedelic inside here if there's no one around to disturb the feeling.

this is the grand throne hall within seoul's gyeongbokgung palace,. this magnificent structure is often cited by visitors as a highlight of their palace tour, and for good reason. the sheer scale and intricate details of the traditional korean architecture are breathtaking, offering a tangible connection to the joseon dynasty. aim to arrive at gyeongbokgung when it first opens to avoid the biggest crowds, allowing you to appreciate the grandeur of geunjeongjeon without too many people. remember that geunjeongjeon is part of the larger palace complex, so factor in at least a couple of hours to explore everything gyeongbokgung has to offer.

this is the gwaneumsa hiking trail leading to the hallasan summit. it is a hard trail. don’t be fooled by the relatively easy first 3 km. what comes after that is brutal - seemingly endless stairs and rocky paths. you need above-average fitness, good shoes and sufficient supplies (water and food). the trail is very well maintained, about 30-40pct is boardwalk/stairs. it is also fully marked and no forks or alternative routes so easy to follow. the scenery until the samgakbong shelter is uneventful but after that you get rewarded with sweeping views of the rocky slopes and valleys. there are toilets at two spots along the trail but no drinking water. early start highly recommended. it took me 7 hours to get up and down again, but estimate that for most people this will take around 8h. you cannot proceed past the samgakbong shelter after 12:30pm in summer (11:30am in winter) since from there, it is about 75-90 min to the summit and you will need between 3-4h to get back down before sunset. and yes, they do check up there at the samgakbong shelter and will stop you after that time. reaching the shelter from the trail head took me 2h30h. so counting on it taking 3h, there is no point getting on this trail after 09:30am (08:30am) if you want to reach the summer. until the samgakbong shelter, the path leads through a forest and is shady. above the shelter, the forest thins out and for the 45 min or so of summit ascent and descent you will be in full sun if the weather is clear. being protection (not just sunscreen, also hat and cover - you are at >1800m altitude, uv intensity is 25-30pct higher).

this is the largest and oldest square in the old town and was used as a parade ground. in colonial times all the important governmental and administrative buildings were here. the old royal customs house has been restored and is now the city hall. a statue of christopher columbus stands in the center of the square. worth visiting for the elegant, colorful architecture, plaza de la aduana is one of the most visited areas in the walled city, with many restaurants, banks and exchange shops. the square itself is very beautiful, surrounded by equally stunning buildings. it's a great place for memorable photographs and is often converted into an open-air concert venue and hosts many great events in the city including the cartagena de indias international film festival which uses the square as an open-air cinema, showcasing many of the festivals featured films.

this is the tallest waterfall in plitvice lakes national park, measuring approximately 78 meters in height. it is a single-drop waterfall, cascading straight down from a high cliff in a dramatic and powerful flow. the sight of the water plunging in a single stream is truly awe-inspiring. in spring and after rainfall, the volume of water increases, creating an even more impressive spectacle. during winter, the frozen form offers a completely different yet equally stunning view. visiting early in the morning rewards you with a magical atmosphere, as mist and sunlight create a dreamlike setting. it is the closest major attraction to ticket office 1, and certain trail routes allow you to reach a viewpoint right at the base of the waterfall.

this is very steep. and the rock can be pretty loose. so only the short footage should go down this. we went down about 1000 feet and that was far enough for me and my daughters. you’re constantly looking over the edge so if you’re afraid of heights, this isn’t the place. but if you wanna find a place to hike down the side of the grand canyon and back up, this is it.

this is what every restaurant should aspire to be. the ambiance was beautiful and well thought out, the service was attentive and top-notch, and the food was mind-blowing. every single dish had so much flavor and was interesting. some of my favorites were the fish, grilled cheese in mango sauce, endive salad, and the rum cake. every course was absolutely delicious. the chefs are creating magic back there. paya is one of the best restaurants i’ve been to, and i go to many. highly recommend to anyone when in miami.

this is where i started my kite surfing lessons and it was a great spot the water was super warm very reasonable price but be prepared to work hard this is not an easy sport but it’s worth every second of it!
this is where i turn left when going to old quarter. pleasant intersection with safe reds to drive through. be sure to signal and watch for motorbikes and cars as you're on the road here.
this is where the path to chico "crater" start, it is clearly marked with black and white poles so you can't get lost ;)

this is where you should start any trip into the park. it is fun and informative for any age group and they have great advice for making the best of your time in the park. i really enjoyed the model of the park which gave a bird's eye view of the whole landscape of the park. it helped to put everything in perspective. we ended up taking the bus deep into the park the next day which was fantastic and i would recommend it to anyone.
this is worth every dollar! doug is very nice and takes awesome pictures he knows what the sun will do for awesome pictures. the boat is kept up real nice and it’s a comfortable experience.

this is worth the hike! i think overall this is pretty good bang for your buck. you get a decent number of steps in and a great view but it is not super challenging. especially as someone who is not from vancouver, i thought this was a great warm up for some more challenging hikes! and the view at the end is a good reward too.

this is yet another site that's included within the dubrovnik pass (foundry museum also) despite it not being mentioned as included on the website. always best to ask at every place if included. for sure you get good views from this fort, but there's nothing else here. if i had to pay for this by itself i probably wouldn't go, but it gives you another perspective on the old town that you don't get from the walls.

this island is best place to chill out at beach. there are many activities, parasailing, snorkeling and cruises. there is a waterfall and the place is very beautiful.

this island is great ! i would recommend to visit it and do the tour to los tunnels. on the island you will find iguana everywhere, wild giant turtle, flamingo, seal (we spotted a 1week old seal next to the wharf). the airport is going to be extended to receive direct plane and a lot of new hostel are on construction which will help the island economy. 10$ entrance fee
this island is so incredibly beautiful to witness from afar and when you are on it. the trees towering over the walls is a remarkable sight.

this isn't your normal stuffy museum!! after hours of exploring ancient ruins in +35, we were delighted to laugh and be silly at this place! the staff happily helped us read the directions on each exhibit and took our pictures to become part of the illusions ourselves and capture our memories. the whole time we kept thinking, "our kids would have loved this place!" we just bought them the coolest souvenirs in greece from the gift shop as a consolation for leaving them at home. if you have an hour to spare, definitely go to the museum of illusions!

this jerricho beach park is a park which is made by a shore of the south vancouver area with lots of trees 🌲🌳, rabbits 🐇🐰 and a nice shore- ocean view scenery for you… it also provides exercise area for you such as tennis court 🎾🏓or running- tracking roads and trail for you… :);):) lots of cute 🥰 wild(?) bunnies too!!! for sure!!! 🐰🐰🐰🐰🐰

this journey was full of excitement and fun. even though i could only understand a few words from the tour guide, it didn’t stop me from enjoying the beauty around me. the magnificent scenery was mesmerizing, and every spot was worth capturing with my camera. i took photos to my heart’s content, feeling the perfect blend of nature and culture, and my heart was filled with joy and wonder.
this kayak is a club in granville isiand. it has a very calm bay, no wind and waves, a city view, and convenient transportation.

this kital ella waterfall could be seen from my resort (neon sky nest) entrance, and it makes the view extra pretty (see my attached photos and a video). not sure how this waterfall looks like up close, but it looks nice from a far! especially when it can be seen right outside my resort.

this landscaped strolling style garden was once frequently visited by emperor meiji and empress shōken. although some sections are currently undergoing replanting, the gardens are superbly photogenic. several interesting points are the tea house, south pond, bonsai trees and kiyomasa's well. tbh the well isn't that interesting.

this lesser-known east gate into old town dubrovnik is perfect for beating the crowds. taxis and ubers can drop you off here with ease. just be prepared for a scenic walk down several staircases into the heart of the city—it’s a peaceful entry point.

this levada hike is amazing! we did the round trip starting with levada nova and back through moinho. i’m sure both ways are great no matter the direction but i’d do it with nova first again. nova is a bit more dangerous because there is less fences but the path is better (less muddy!). i wouldn’t recommend going with children. wear waterproof shoes, since you will be walking through waterfalls. overall a great experience, it took us around 3 hours for the 8.7km. it was way less crowded than other routes so were all by ourselves for the first hour (started around 8:30 in march). for both ways you can park the car at the church, where the trail starts. levada nova entry was a bit hidden up the road (1. uphill on street for view minutes and then a small path to the left) but you can also access it through moinho (2. after view minutes stairs to your right and then you’re at 1.)

this levada was a little more challenging. we followed review advice and parked close to the lombada church (igreja da lombada). the walk to the levada itself was really hard, uphill, uphill, and more uphill. when we reached the levada it was a nice hike, views are stunning. but there was a lot of people there. easy trail but careful if you are prone to vertigo. i think it would make sense to drive closer but the streets are narrow and the drive is uphill, uphill and more uphill. still, worth a visit. we will go back next time we travel to madeira.

this little café hidden on a lovely block in strathcona is one of the quaintest cafés i’ve been to in the city. a friend and i went to another café nearby for lunch a week ago. i realized union market was only a few blocks from us and my husband had told me about the pasteis de nata at the market so we walked by after lunch to check it out. it looked lovely so i made a point to come back with my husband today. the street side patio is the nicest among the many cafés we’ve been to in the city. there are ample seating covered by strung lit awnings surrounded by lush landscaping and vegetation in the neighbourhood. we thoroughly enjoyed our quiet late morning having our brunch watching neighbours and commuters gently cycling by. we had a flat white, an americano, a blt, a prosciutto sandwich, a pastel de nata and a s’more cookie. my flat white was rich and strong. the bread of our sandwiches was soft, moist and thick. while my pastel de nata was good, the s’more cookie was sinfully good (and i do not like s’mores and never participated in roasting s’mores in any bbq). a bite of the gooey lightly charred marshmallow on top of a large piece of soft cookie with a graham cracker embedded inside almost tempted me to trade my pastel de nata with my husband’s cookie. the cookie is so much better than the traditional s’more.

this little gem of a temple is tucked away from the main road, maybe 300 meters or so. i wouldn't have even known about it had i not seen the sign for it while riding my bike around. it isn't on the typical tours and as a result few people that come to angkor wind up visiting. that's a shame because this relatively unrestored temple is perfect. it is small but there is a lot to see in such a small space. it is relatively unrestored, but easy to walk around in safely. and when you come here, there is a very good chance you will have the whole place to yourself. although this place isn't on the grand circuit, it is less than a half a kilometer detour after you are done with preah khan temple. i would definitely recommend you asking your driver if you can stop by this one for a few minutes if you have time. it is worth it in my opinion.

this little island had a nice viewpoint and a good place to collect a washed up shells. be careful to the climb to the top of the viewpoint - i ended up taking off my shoes and going barefoot because trail was so steep and treacherous that i needed the traction and flexibility of my bare feet. well worth it, but not everyone will be capable of making the hike.

this little museum and its grounds do not get the attention they deserve, which may be bad for the govt folks that track numbers of visitors, but is good for the weary tourist seeking a quiet place that lacks hordes of tourists. that is just one of its merits, the other for me was that it has so many exhibits showcasing reproduced paintings of how quebec developed over the centuries. a diorama of the fort is the centerpiece of this endeavor. it becomes obvious, if you were not already aware, of just how much use of the upper town's natural environment in terms of the cliff faces were used to provide a natural defense. and in turn the town and many of its defensive walls grew up around the original fortifications.

this little part of paris should not be missed. its a pleasant way to get a different view of paris, in a park high above the street. it’s calm and opens up views you otherwise wouldn’t experience. and it’s free :-)

this little science museum is an absolute gem! you pay a few euros over the reasonable admission fee to see the armour and music collections. nerds are well catered for with puzzles and games from ancient times. children love the 2000 year old door bell and alarm clock. guides in english and french.

this liveaboard gives good value for its price. i enjoyed my trip to tubbataha with them. the crew and dive pros are amazing. 20 dives for 5 days is really tiring but thanks to nitrox, we survived it! just one suggestion - it would be better if there were more available dry towels after the dive. other than that, i have no other concerns. thank you for taking us safely to tubbataha!

this local market is a great spot to catch a glimpse of everyday life, far from the usual touristy areas. it’s mostly locals here, which makes the experience feel more authentic. some vendors cook and sell food using fresh ingredients from the market itself, and there are plenty of snacks to try as you wander around. i didn’t get a chance to taste anything, but everything looked pretty tasty. it’s a nice place to stop by on your walk from the bus terminal to the city center. just be careful—the ground can be wet and a bit muddy in places, so your shoes might get dirty.

this local market is in my opinion much better then gwangjang market. not only is it much bigger but also it is untouched by tourism. which means this is as local as it gets. gyeongdong market also houses a uniquely made starbucks cafe, which makes it even more of a destination. more on the starbucks in a different post. it is cozy here with its own charm and vendors are friendly. if you are looking for a true local market, this is the place to go. forget about gwangjang market, visit gyeongdong market instead!

this local market people get up early in the morning since 3 pm to sale all vegetables, fish, meat, to all buyer from other hotel, restaurant, all people need non chemical and fresh with cheap price. please help to support with those people for khmer products mean you support their community. my house near this samiki market my family and i always bought over there.
this location has a good view, less people than the area near the pier. it has 4 hours free parking, a toilet near the parking lot and a small playground for children.

this location is a must visit when on madeira if you can work it into your itinerary. a few things to note. parking will be tricky as it's a super popular destination. however the best advice is to join a queue for one of the car parks. you'll get a space eventually. only criticism i would make of this location is that there are surprisingly no great restaurants, but there are a couple of ok ones. however the star of the show are the views and the experience. highly recommend a visit.

this location is definitely worth a visit—our earth provides natural springs that cause the water to boil. local restaurants make use of this unique phenomenon to prepare their food. a traditional stew is cooked in these hot springs, resulting in a delicious and perfectly tender dish after six hours of slow cooking. there is, however, a noticeable smell of sulfur in the air that’s hard to miss. this attraction is a must-see. highly recommended to visit.

this location is run by volunteers and requires a $1 reservation made in advance of the tour. we made our reservation on a sunday morning at 7:30 and took the first tour slot of 9:30am. when we arrived there was no one else in the parking lot and so we had a private tour which was fabulous. we entered at the museum house and looked around after checking in. we then made our way to the picnic tables to wait for the start of our tour. there we found a bin of walking sticks to choose from to use during the tour. our tour guide met us and walked with us up the 60 steps to the first tour site. i have bad feet and thought this would feel like a lot, but it was relatively easy. he explained vegetation, farming and other agriculture of the time along the way. he brought us to our first cliff dwelling view where he explained the difference between pictographs and petroglyphs. he had many props of tools that were used to achieve the scratches, drawings, what some of them meant and the way of life of the tribes that lived there. next, we went to another site with a different guide who showed us at least 4 different areas of cave dwellings, ceremony sites, the former spring, the opening to the underworld, where agave was roasted and more. this guide was even more informative about the history of the site, the upkeep of it, why the drawings are losing their visualization, and much more. the whole tour was about 2 hours and by the time we left there were groups all around of over 12 people a piece. we were able to have our lunch at the picnic tables before continuing to the honanki site for a self guided tour. we were happy to arrive there with so much knowledge from palatki. the 2 sites are 20 minutes apart. we almost drove a couple hours to walnut canyon to see cliff dwellings, but we are so glad we did this close tour instead and feel like we got more out of it then we would have elsewhere.

this location is very out of the way for most people visiting hanoi on a shorter stay. however it has its own vibes and artistic flair. with almost every house in the area having something to do with pottery. it is great if you want to get some quality pottery at what felt like fair prices. also pottery making is good fun also. the main reason this gets 3 stars is the location, it is very hard to get a grab back and also there is a lot of walking which can be hard for how hot it is in this area. overall worth it if you have the time and want to take back pottery.

this location was part of our 8 day luxury tour of the gobi desert. we stayed in a ger with a full bathroom. very convenient. the dining hall was first class, and so was the service. upon arrival, we were welcomed with a traditional drink from a silver bowl. when we departed, our vehicle was blessed with luck. from the moment we arrived until the moment we drove off, our stay was filled with beautiful mongolian traditions.

this lodge was the last place i stayed at with a birthday celebration group of a dear friend. skeleton coast is a remote, barren park with sand dunes on one side and the atlantic ocean on the other. it is almost has an apocalyptic landscape that has to be seen and experienced. it’s cooler and windier than the other areas of namibia we experienced during our tour. we found that shipwreck lodge was perfectly located and designed to fully immerse in this unusual area. bodo was super at organizing and catering to our specific requirements during our unique day experiences. matthew, margarete, rosicey and jackson provided great service. in the kitchen eugene created a great menu - highly recommend. overall: very good - for 2 - 3 day visit. the only fault was the temperature in the rooms. despite the rooms being amazingly clean despite all the sand outside and designed with a great design concept they are very warm due to no air conditioning and the sun burning in during the afternoons as it sets over the ocean. you will need to open the windows and use the tower fan provided. so please bear this in mind.

this long-standing market in bangkok is a shopping haven for bargain hunters. take a stroll through the alleys and marvel at all that's on offer—rolls of textiles, clothing and footwear, and even handmade crafts. there are even inexpensive laptops and cameras on offer for gadget lovers. remember to brush up on some basic thai phrases before you go—you might be surprised at the extra discounts or freebies you can score! buying in bulk is often a lot cheaper too. it's a popular stop on many city tours and food tours of bangkok, so go in the early

this looked to be quite a popular spot with tourists and beach bars. the shoreline is riddled with dead corals but a few meters inside the water is pretty good. bring water shoes. here too the currents are sometimes strong. enjoy wonderful sunsets sipping on juices and cocktails. 👍

this lookout area was a bit foggy when we went, but we could still make out plenty of great views. actually, the way the fog moved itself was pretty cool. as with most of the lookout points, there was enough parking, and there were walkways, and you could get off the walkways as well and explore.

this lynn canyon suspension bridge park in vancouver is absolutely incredible. the suspension bridge sways high above the canyon, giving a thrilling experience with stunning views. the scenic trails wind through lush forests, perfect for hiking and exploring nature’s beauty. there’s plenty to do....like walking the peaceful paths or relaxing by the river. best of all, entry is free, making it a budget-friendly adventure. the park offers lots of parking with spaces at both upper and lower levels, so it’s easy to visit. lynn canyon is a must-see for a fun, memorable day outdoors.

this magnificent theatre is a quick walk beyond the treasury and is a wonderful sight to visit. plus, there are other well preserved sights around the area if you walk around. i’d definitely recommend walking a bit beyond the treasury to see these sights.

this mall is built at an italian architecture design and has almost all brands from high end to middle class. a separate place for kids and an incredible slide for adults & kids. after every few hours there's a circus and the artists play very well. a number of brands offer a variety for shopping . you get an abundant parking at the main door but if it is full you can also park in the basement. parking is free. there's also a very mesmerizing cinema. in short it's a great place to go with kids and family.

this mall is lovely , not very busy as the other dubai malls , it has a variety of shops and food places to suit all budgets . what is most striking about it is the fact that it houses many government services and agencies who deal with immigration and legal matters , services such as visa applications and also other government offices . there is also a huge cooperative shopping centre and is located opposite the beautiful barsha pond park which makes it ideal for families with children

this mall is really nice! they have plenty of shops with a great variety for shopping, making it a one-stop destination for everything. you’ll also find grocery stores here, which is super convenient. the food court is great as well, with several options to satisfy any craving.a great place to visit for shopping and dining.

this mall is the perfect size — compact, easy to navigate, and well laid out for a stress-free shopping experience. it houses a great selection of well-known brands across various categories, including clothing, cosmetics, footwear, and even essentials like a pharmacy. there’s something for everyone, whether you're looking to shop, dine, or simply unwind. we had breakfast at toby’s estate and absolutely loved it — the ambiance, coffee, and food were all top-notch. the mall also offers a good variety of dining options to suit different tastes and occasions. overall, it's a convenient and enjoyable spot for a well-rounded outing without feeling overwhelming. ideal for both quick errands and leisurely visits.
this mall is unique italian-inspired design. variety of shops and restaurants. family-friendly atmosphere. best for photo shoot spot in dubai.

this maritime museum was a pleasant surprise. for €10, we gained access not only to this site but to nine other museums as well—great value, though it’s unclear if that was the regular deal or due to a printer issue on the day we visited. the collection spans two levels and includes a range of maritime artefacts, old paintings, navigational tools, and ship models—plenty to explore if you're interested in naval history. the upstairs area also features a children’s play section, which is a thoughtful touch for families. staff were polite, and although the printer was down, one of the attendants made the effort to find us later and hand us our printed tickets, which we appreciated. one concern: near the children’s play area upstairs, we noticed a large open window with no safety barrier or stopper. it felt unsafe, especially with young kids nearby. hopefully this gets addressed. overall, a place with interesting exhibits and good value, especially if you’re planning to check out other museums in dubrovnik.

this market has a strong smell due to the sale of meat and fermented foods, but it's still an interesting place to visit. you can buy all kinds of food items here, such as vegetables, fruits, meats, fish, live animals, and sweets. what i really liked is that there were no other tourists at all, it felt like a truly local market. the goods are very cheap, and we bought lots of fruits and vegetables here.

this market is listed as being open friday, saturday and sunday. do not go on a friday. there were only a few vendors here, and most of them were cleaning, not selling. it was a long uber ride from miami beach for nothing.

this market is located is down town where easy to find. there are plenty of goods here like many kind of meats, vegetables, freshness and surrounding by many local restaurant with tasty foods and hygiene as well. if you are living around here then you will be carefree about where to buy something to eat!

this market is not very big, take 10min to go from the start to end, if … you are not looking around. as for shopping, they do have some unique vendors that are not selling those typical souvenirs, including original arts and handmade items. there are many food and drinks options around, also close to other stores, super convenient location & close to other attractions.

this market is probably known to many people for featuring in the harry potter films and as a result, it is full of tourists. harry potter association aside, it's a really interesting-looking building, with a good mix of shops and places to eat. some places have outdoor seating too. worth visiting, even if it's just to admire the impressive architecture.
this market is wealth of fresh fruits. we enjoyed authentic mangoes, sugar cane, lychee, and jackfruit. 🙏

this market was a lot bigger than i thought it was because there’s a upstairs area that has a plethora of household goods, including stationary, school supplies, baby supplies, gardening accessories, pet supplies, and more
this mart has some interesting food items from all around the world

this modest park is a beautiful place to just relax. in addition to the benches and picnicking areas there is a trail which will take you around the entire lake. you can also rent boats to enjoy some time with family and friends on the water. ample parking is available as are public restrooms. we didn't have time to get to the boat rentals but they had ample boats available and lots of friendly staff there to assist. those that did rent seemed to have a good time.

this monastery is around 300 years old and it stands magnificently in the serene valley about 25kms from leh. you can see the indus river on its left and the beautiful village on the right. a panoramic view of the nearby villages and the mountains is something you cannot miss.

this monestry is situated just on the right point..from where you have a beautiful view of leh city along with leh airport. had an opportunity to witness landing and take off flights with breath taking views.. best surprise is that along with monestry you do have a kali mata temple situated on top of the hill...it so spiritual and peaceful once you reach on top. from there you too have a great view of indus river which is flowing back of the hill. worth a visit..😊

this monument honors barcelona’s emergence as a modern city on the world stage and the cultural and economic transformation brought by the olympic games. the 1992 olympics are considered a pivotal event that developed the city’s infrastructure, transformed it, and strengthened its status in tourism and international affairs. the olympic ring was built in memory of these games. the monument was designed by santiago calatrava. its vertical, spiral shape represents the olympic spirit, unity, and progress. it also functions as a sundial, symbolizing barcelona’s historical development and the games’ lasting impact on its future.

this monument in mengwi display rama and shinta are characters from the ancient indian epic, the ramayana. rama is the prince of ayodhya and is known for his righteousness and bravery, while shinta (also known as sita) is his devoted wife. in some cultures, statues or sculptures of rama and shinta are created to depict their love story and the values they represent, such as loyalty, honor, and devotion. these statues can be found in temples, shrines, and other places of worship, serving as symbols of love, virtue, and the triumph of good over evil. they are often depicted together, showcasing their eternal bond and the enduring nature of their love story. been renovated and maintain by government.

this monument is absolutely stunning and majestic! it’s one of the most impressive landmarks in rome. the white marble structure stands out beautifully, and the architecture is breathtaking — especially the huge staircases and bronze statues. i really enjoyed climbing up and seeing the tomb of the unknown soldier, which adds a deep historical and emotional meaning to the place. but the real highlight was taking the elevator to the top terrace — the view over rome is incredible. you can see the colosseum, roman forum, and even the vatican from up there. it’s totally worth a visit, both for the history and the views. a must-see if you’re in rome!

this morning, my family and i went on a boat excursion — my husband, our two children (aged 11 and 8), and myself. everything was perfect! the sea was calm, making it ideal even for kids. we were offered sandwiches, fresh water, and fruit on board, which was a nice touch. we also appreciated the complimentary water bottle given to each participant. swimming with the turtles was an exciting and unforgettable experience. highly recommended!
this mosque is beautiful but i did not go inside and enjoyed watching it only from outside.
this mosque is well connected with al khuwair souq road and resident road. nice mosque, but parking only during magrib prayer is difficult
this mosque was completely renovated and now this is one of the beautiful one in azaiba area.

this mountainous italian park is a perfect destination for those who love skiing or hiking, thanks to its breathtaking scenery and diverse flora and fauna. the park also has a rich history, with sites and artefacts dating back to prehistoric times, the roman empire and the middle ages that are best discovered on foot.
this municipal park has replaced the zoo. it has free parking, public restrooms, many picnic places, and is crossed by a creek. it is dog friendly. it has a playground for kids.

this museum expresses the authentic cultural identity of fez. i advise all visitors to the city to book an appointment to view this wonderful musical heritage. mr. hisham rais, the founder of the museum, is ready to tell you about the city's andalusian musical history.

this museum features a walk through tour with audio. there are 15-20 scenes setup inside with tales from iceland's history. my brother and i started our visit to reykjavik here, which was nice because we got a lot of background information about various figures we would see throughout our trip. of course, we also had to dress up like vikings and templar knights!

this museum has plenty to offer. it's spread across two buildings with an underground walkway that is full of funeral finery and even some tablets with roman laws on. one of the rooms is full of marble emperor heads and plenty of statues standing around. out in one of the courtyards is a very large statue of constantine i. they have a gallery with old coins that date right back to the early part of the roman empire. we came back to this museum as there is so much to see and marvel at. there are lifts available and the stairs have stairlifts on to assist wheelchair users.

this museum is a hidden gem that offers a fascinating glimpse into the natural world. the variety of exhibits is impressive, ranging from intricate displays of local wildlife to captivating prehistoric artifacts. each section of the museum is thoughtfully curated, and it's evident that a lot of care went into presenting the information in an engaging manner. families will appreciate the interactive features that allow both kids and adults to learn through hands-on experiences. while the space can get crowded on weekends, the atmosphere remains vibrant and lively, making it a welcoming place to explore. there are plenty of informative guides and friendly staff who are ready to help with any questions. the layout is user-friendly, ensuring that you can navigate the exhibits seamlessly. overall, it’s a great spot for anyone interested in understanding more about the planet’s diverse ecosystems and history.

this museum is a hidden gem. the building itself is stunning and meticulously maintained. the collection is truly fascinating and awe-inspiring featuring costumes and jewelry from all over the world. the staff are very welcoming and helpful. don’t forget to scan the qr codes as they offer insightful descriptions and photos. plus, there’s a lovely rooftop restaurant to enjoy afterward.

this museum is a little gem. history of san fran cable cars. just enough information without being overwhelmed. there’s no charge to enter but you can donate. there’s a gift shop that accepts only cash. some cool items there. definitely stop by, you can probably view everything under an hour.
this museum is a must visit in the heart of the city! do not miss this opportunity, such an amazing collection of oil paintings and ceiling freezes. very neat facilities as well.

this museum is a time machine and you will be traveling back to the greatest times of your life. the love story museum in dubrovnik is an absolutely enchanting and soul-stirring experience. from the moment you step inside, you're enveloped in warmth and tenderness, and each exhibit tells a unique, beautiful story of love that has endured through time, obstacles, and distance. this museum isn't just a collection of objects; it's a true sanctuary for romantics and all who believe in the power of genuine emotion. i was particularly touched by the stories from local history, which intimately and personally depicted how love blossomed even in past centuries. the interactive parts of the museum are brilliant, allowing you to truly connect with the narratives, making the experience even more personal and unforgettable.

this museum is absolutely exceptional for children. it’s so good it’s hard to believe it’s free to visit! my kids absolutely love it and so do i - it’s so great for them to get exposure to so many educational and interactive elements. there is a dedicated area for smaller babies to play away from bigger kids. a cafe for a coffee stop is greatly appreciated. the dinosaurs are also a big hit!

this museum is an absolute must see. its location is very close to the forum and easy to reach while walking near victor emmanuel monument. the actual reason for seeing this collection is the massive display. the statues, busts, paintings, coins, ceramics and other artifacts shall allow you to become immersed into the world in which there is no other corridors through time to explore them. look at socrates or apollo and imagine how their influence shaped our lives. one of the best views of the cityscape of rome is from the cafe and/or restaurant on the rooftop. the restaurant is also a very fine place to replenish with nutritionally delicious dishes. allow 3+ hours to enjoy yourself with seeing some of the beautiful treasures rome has to offer.

this museum is focused on the ancient writing of the old testament. no pictures can be taken of the documents stored there. when we visited, they were displaying a replica of the scroll of isaiah from the dead sea scrolls. they also told the story of the scrolls found in qumran and had some pieces on display. in the lower level they told the story of the aleppo codex, which is one of the most important findings for the old testament writings. it contains the entire old testament and is still very old. if you are interested in the bible, and the history of old testament writings, you will enjoy this museum!

this museum is free to visit on sundays and they charge 5 pesos to take pictures inside the museum. it is very popular and was good. a must visit. but the only drawback is most of them are in spanish.

this museum is located just a walk away from the yaesu exit of tokyo station. at first, the staff are all friendly. honestly, the museum itself lack explanation about the location of the exhibition. indie the building, the museum is apparently placed on the 4th,5th, and 6th floors. we were automatically taken to the 6th floor after the entrance on the 3rd floor by elevator. even there was no sign written for the "museum entrance" on the 3rd floor but "lecture room" was written there instead. we as foreigners misunderstood the japanese instructions and missed the 4th and 5th floor exhibition. although at the end when we asked the staff whether we could re-enter or not, they allowed us, but we feel the hospitality changed. i guess the system of bringing the guest directly to the 6th floor from the 3rd floor is pretty confusing in my opinion.

this museum is one of the most interactive i’ve ever been to, even though i’m not particularly interested in maritime subjects. it was really fun! make sure to go to the second floor, as that’s where most of the fun is.

this museum is probably the only museum in greece where you can still see the insides of a palace! it contains several objects relating to the everyday life of the king and the queen. the famous huge painting is somehow unreal!some of our favourite exhibits belonged to the first residents of the building, namely king otto and queen amalia who were here for some years before their move to the royal palace that is now the parliament building.rooms with preserved ornamentation and furnishings including a fully set banquet table reflect the splendour in which the wealthy lived during the 19th century.art pieces are numerous throughout and we very much enjoyed those.

this museum is rather hidden. i don't see alot of crowd but i was outside and didn't purchase tickets to go in. i feel the price is rather high and would rather stick to the main places rather than museums which aren't my main interest, or probably better museums elsewhere. from here, there are lots of stalls to pickup souvenirs.

this museum is so enjoyable. it's small, and the art is contemporary and somewhat political. we loved it. and there was a little concert going on in the foyer as we left that had drawn quite a crowd! no cafe, but there's a cute little coffee and snack spot in the park across the road from the parking lot.

this museum is so interesting. you can’t enter the house, but you can see through all the doors and windows. in addition, for a small tip, the women inside will take pictures for you. it’s very interesting and with information from local tour guides and a friend, i was also able to learn more about hemingway and his life when he lived here. i also took some of these photos myself. you are able to see his fishing boat, his hunting trophies, lots of photos, including him with fidel castro.

this museum is truly stunning a place where one can easily lose track of time, immersed in beauty, imagination, and contemplation. both the exterior and interior spaces are artistically designed, creating an inspiring atmosphere. the reception staff were highly professional and courteous, and i appreciated that there were no additional fees for taking photographs of the sculptures or the exhibits. visitors are also allowed to use professional cameras without restriction, which is rare and very thoughtful. this is undoubtedly one of those must-see places for anyone visiting the city. the paintings were breathtaking, and the sculptures crafted with such creativity from stone and wood were truly impressive. the marble staircases added yet another layer of elegance to the overall experience. the only suggestion i would make is regarding the organization of the exhibit halls. it would enhance the experience even further if paintings, sculptures, and photographs were displayed in clearly separated areas. while everything was incredibly beautiful, the arrangement at times felt a bit scattered. nevertheless, it was a wonderful and enriching experience, and i truly enjoyed my visit. with sincere appreciation and respect, mozhda

this museum is wonderful if you remember that what might not be modern elsewhere is modern in rome! i loved the quality of the paintings and sculpture, each one more special than the last. and at the end, you can collapse onto a comfy modern couch to relax!

this museum offers a fascinating glimpse into the past with its diverse collection. from preserved plants and their uses to antique machines, medical tools, and anatomical displays, there's something to pique everyone's interest. the historic building itself adds to the experience. best of all, admission is free, making it a worthwhile stop if you have some time to spare.

this museum was absolutely amazing. they have only replicas in the collection, but that is not a problem at all. de replicas are carefully reconstructed on the basis of ancient texts. the people of the museum know very much about the objects and give free tours in which they demonstrate the machines. it is absolutely a must visit!!

this museum was by far my favorite experience during my trip to nola. our tour guide was extremely informative. the exhibits are phenomenal. you can learn so much about new orleans just by dropping by here. i will return every time that i have the opportunity to travel to anew orleans. i love the culture, the community and the people!

this museum was easy to tackle in a few hours and brought us all over the world and through time. we especially enjoyed the free one hour tour through some highlighted spots. we learned things we couldn’t even read about from our tour guide. don’t miss the dinosaurs, gemstone collection, and bat cave! we enjoyed lunch from the cafeteria downstairs. it wasn’t cheap but nice to eat inside the museum. fun activity for a hot summer day. there was a really sweet kids area for littles to express some of their energy, too.

this museum was easy to tackle in a few hours and brought us all over the world and through time. we especially enjoyed the free one hour tour through some highlighted spots. we learned things we couldn’t even read about from our tour guide. don’t miss the dinosaurs, gemstone collection, and bat cave! we enjoyed lunch from the cafeteria downstairs. it wasn’t cheap but nice to eat inside the museum. fun activity for a hot summer day. there was a really sweet kids area for littles to express some of their energy, too.

this museum's collection of early ancient christianity is impressive!! i appreciate being able to take photos, too! the museum is a bit toasty, so bring a mini fan if you think you'll need one. it's in a great location near the gardens, tomb of the unknown soldier and presidential palace. if you're up for a walk, it's 20 minutes from the olympic stadium, too. good area. i felt very safe exploring alone.

this museum, i have to confess, is the one i enjoyed its rooftop view and the botanic garden next to it (with exotic green budgies) more than its art collections. i will definitely visit again for the collection, but my point is that the building (and the location of it) is so beautiful and quite different from all other major museums in other european cities, this museum has its own merit and is unique from the others. never miss it if you visit barcelona.

this must be a staple market... way, way too much inventory to be a casual street market... deep, and double-decked, this "supermercado" is stacked to the brim with retail merchandise, fresh and frozen foods, and literally every single beer and hard liquor you can fathom in one space... its a short walk from the port if you're coming in from the ship, but im sure even the locals, come from the island's interior to shop here... prices are dirt cheap, especially for it being a us municipality... shop with confidence... and budget some time, the place is huge... all the top tier retail name brands... all the zero calorie drinks and juice varieties you never knew existed, all the booze... tall one liter bottles of fiji water for under two dollars... even whole cabinets of cigars and tobaccos... .

this must be the most friendly place on earth. our host provided us with a room in her own house. provided meals and helped us out with everything. i can not recommend the place more. it was a great place to stay and within walking distance from everything in ulaan batar.
this national institution is the best theatre in london. i enjoy the awesome architecture everytime i visit the national theatre. the sound quality in the auditorium is spectacular.

this national museum displays things used in royal palaces especially by kings and queens. you can see clothes, paintings, ornament, decorations, tools for rituals and ceremonies, and many others. the admission is free. it is big and spacious and clean. i came to see the famous moon jar but unfortunately it wasn't here at the moment. last time i visited, i saw the moon jar, so it is okay.

this natural landmark is renowned for its picturesque trails that lead to stunning vistas of the surrounding lakes, forests, and the iconic llao llao hotel. the hike to the summit of cerro llao llao is relatively accessible and rewards visitors with panoramic views of the nahuel huapi lake and the andean mountain range, making it a popular destination for nature lovers and hikers.

this natural water spot is a hidden gem on the island. i loved simply walking around and sitting near the waterfall in a quiet, timeless summer moment. i took a photo — completely alone — and felt myself dissolve into nature during the golden hour. it was peaceful, healing, and beautifully unforgettable. 🌿💧✨

this nature park is a gem with the natural greenery and history of the abandoned hainanese village. the ruins of the old houses showcased some of the living condition in the early days of singapore. it is also part of the singapore grand prix street circuit before the famous marina bay.

this of dubrovnik’s most famous landmarks. the circular fountain was built in 1438 as part of a water-supply system that involved bringing water from a spring 12km away. originally the fountain was adorned with sculptures, but it was heavily damaged in the 1667 earthquake and only 16 carved masks remain, with their mouths dribbling drinkable water into a drainage pool. the fountain now serves as a relaxing/resting area or a meeting point for the throngs of tourists that come to visit the old city of dubrovnik. good experience to be here.
this one is for amir: this man is amazing and he really explained everything so well about vienna. i highly recommend visiting the city and especially with amir as a guide 🤝🏻

this one is kind of weird. it's very cool and feels like it should be a bigger attraction, but the parking and site are hidden behind a ymca with no signage. i don't know if that's intentional to keep tourist traffic down, but a huge site like this with some pretty interesting history should be a little more popular. beautiful view with a nice trail running through some marsh land.

this one is very strange. we walked all the way to the gate only to see it was closed. the guard at the gate pointed us to a sign in french and arabic, which i believe says it open only on fridays and sundays. we went there on a tuesday. the walk was not a waste though as the route was pretty. but it was nearly impossible to take a taxi back from the gate area. we had to walk to the medina.

this one of the most spectacular classical concerts i have ever experienced. the musicians have so much passion for the art and the venue itself only adds to the experience and ambiance of it all. there are many classical concerts to choose from when you are in vienna (and i've been to others), however, i have yet to attend one that is as magical as this. please do yourself a favor and attend. it was so breathtakingly beautiful and magnificent - words do not come close to expressing how amazing this was.

this one starts pretty much as soon as you step off the train, which is very convenient — no long trek just to get to the starting point. the build-up is great too, with shrines, stalls, and even some traditional performances going on when we arrived. sets the vibe right. the walk itself is no joke, especially in summer — lots of steps, and that sun and humidity really hit you. bring water, sunscreen, and a bit of grit. luckily, there are vending machines and toilets along the way, which helps heaps. there’s good signage the whole way, and if you’re aiming for a view, stop at the crossroads lookout (i think it’s stop #6 on the map). it’s got a beautiful view over kyoto and is a great spot to turn around. the trail does keep going to the mountain peak, but honestly, there’s not much up there — no better view or big payoff. just a nice brag if you make it all the way. all up, it’s a tough but rewarding walk, especially if you pace it out and don’t push in the heat. a great way to experience a bit of old japan in a stunning setting.

this one was fun, a nice bamboo forest, graffiti’d bunker, open field, and a good sized waterfall. everything you could ask for in a hawaii hike. somehow we got lost, and apparently that’s not uncommon. we ran into some other folks that were lost but it’s very easy to find where you need to go once you realize you’re off trail. download an offline map on all trails if you’re worried about running in circles. waters deep enough to swim in, fun rocks to climb on. lovely spot, not obnoxiously crowded either.

this one was really worth it. buggy ride for 2 hours was loads of fun, the scenery you pass by is just lovely, waterfall visit was perfect and we had a super nice guide, guillaume. also good value for money comparing to other activities on the island

this operator makes really good tours. my mom and i did the prison island/stone town tour and the zansibar spice delight & jozani forest tour with a german-speaking guide (mkubwa abdul) and he did a really great job. we can only recommend him. all in all, it was two really great and successful days with him. always my pleasure.

this palace is the palace used by the surviving queens of the joseon dynasty, there are many well known stories based in this palace. the palace was almost destroyed during the japanese colonial period when it was turned into a theme park and some buildings were removed/sold but since that time it has been restored/maintained to some of its former glory. we saw it around sunset and it was nice to walk around as the sun was setting. there is a lake with lovely surrounding gardens and greenery. towards the back of the palace is a european style greenhouse.

this palace is the ultimate destination for a photo session and some quality time with family. it has lots of exhibitions. there were guides everywhere to explain the meanings behind most of the objects scattered around the place. i obviously took a lot of photos, cause almost every corner is worthy of a frame. the arabs tickets were for 20 egp and students were for 5 egp. also, they don't accept cash only visa. it closed at 5 pm.
