this paragliding experience was the best one ive ever had. although not a first timer, it felt better than my first time. my instructor daniel is a cool pro and was very communicative throughout the experience, including rescheduling when the weather was bad. if you’re in rio de janeiro and have never done this before i highly recommend you do so!!

this park clearly does not worth the price of the entrance. trail by itself has very limited interest. the view on the volcano is beautiful but not significantly different from any point of view from la fortuna. the lava field is very tiny. many other better trails and activities can be done from la fortuna

this park does not have a lot to offer but this is one good place to spend some time off, peaceful "me time" and have picnics with your loved ones. this is just a 5 minute walk from the meiji shrine. by the time i visited, roses are in bloom making the park more interesting to visit.

this park has a great network of trails that connect to rice lake, lynn canyon, and even seymour. right now, the river has a low water level, making it perfect for playing by the water’s edge. but be cautious during other times of the year when the river can be quite fast-flowing. it’s a beautiful place to explore, with something to offer in every season.
this park has been left in its natural state with the ruins of the hainan village. there are many monkeys inside so don’t go feed them. you don’t disturb them and they won’t disturb you

this park has everything. from the old stately manor to the botanical gardens to kids playgrounds and forest walks. i have been here for beerfests, picnics and just plain ol hiking. on my first visit i saw a classy wedding, a classic english car show and a manga convention, all within meters of each other. there is also a pool complete with life guards to cool down after your adventure. highly recommended.

this park has to be one of my favorite hiking areas, the scenery is incredible, there is the salmon hatchery were they give you a lot of info about all the diffrent kinds of salmon plus you can see all the young salmon up close. 15 minute hike or less to the cleveland dam and the lake wicked view from up at the top of the dam both sides. there are washrooms, you can hike the other direction down the river as well. trails are well maintained, go early so u can get a parking spot. wildlife, i seen a snake, a snail & a salmon.

this park is a beautiful green space right in the city, perfect for a relaxing stroll or a peaceful break. the views from the top are really nice, and i loved how quiet it felt even though it’s in the middle of sf. there are plenty of trails to explore, and it’s surrounded by charming old homes that add to the charm of the area. i’d definitely recommend stopping by.

this park is a gem. it offers a respite from the busy city. the park gets drenched in the sunlight making it a perfect spot in winter mornings and spring. well maintained with pretty flowers and seasonal art installations. it has its own cozy looking shake shack with exclusively outdoor seating. children's and dog's park present. the energy of the park is lively, casual in perfect congruency with the city. the park has multiple chairs and benches, don't worry, you will get to sit.

this park is a landing place for paragliding at interlaken...large open place with trees, benches on the main street side. great place to see paraglider landing - mostly commercial tandem paragliding- and feel the excitement from the gliders and pilots.

this park is a life saver if you live nearby. very beautiful, peaceful and well maintained. i wish the patrolling police went after the drug dealers and shady types (who are always there, especially after dark) instead of chasing cute dogs playing unleashed, just to write tickets, so we would actually feel safer.

this park is a stunning blend of natural beauty and urban charm, offering a unique experience that’s hard to find elsewhere. the picturesque trees, beautifully designed walkways, and serene bay views create the perfect setting for relaxation or an active day out. one of the most captivating features is the view of the skyscrapers juxtaposed against nature, along with the mesmerizing sight of vessels passing by and water airplanes landing and taking off—it’s truly a photographer's dream! the park is free to visit, which makes it even more appealing. for those seeking adventure, you can rent a boat or a bike to explore further. the dedicated cycling track is great for riders of all skill levels. after your activities, the nearby seafood options provide a delicious way to wrap up your visit. this park is a gem that offers something for everyone, whether you're looking for tranquility, a place to exercise, or a fun outing with family and friends. highly recommended!

this park is across from the pretty, cafe-lined rue st. anne in upper quebec. two arts venues ran off of it. rue de tresor, on which the old law courts building (formerly a monastery) is located, has streets lined with art produced and being sold by local artists. surrounded by tourist attractions and historic architecture, this tree-filled park and public square is said to be the hub of old québec. given its strategic location next to the tourist information centre, château frontenac, and dufferin terrace. in the middle of the park is a gothic fountain on which stands the faith monument (monument de la foi) commemorating the three hundredth anniversary of the arrival of the recollet fathers in québec. it is the departure point for many guided tours of the city, as well as the boarding point for various motorcoach excursions.

this park is beautiful. i highly recommend renting a bike and going around all the different parts of the park. it was big, but not so big that you would get lost. i love all the different parts of the park! if you get a bike, i think a 2 hour rental is perfect.

this park is considered huge and it serves ang mo kio and bishan residents. a very vibrant park with lots of variety of activities. walkers, bicyclists as well as roller bladders love coming here due to its massive space catering to almost any activities or event. at times the park will host movie by the park too for the public. it also has a dog playing area which is superbly ideal for animal lovers to walk their dogs in the park too. food wise there’s mcdonald and 1 more bistro restaurants as well as a spa too. parking is free!

this park is extremely well-maintained, with a beautiful sea of flowers and meadows. the tulips and cherry blossoms are especially stunning, and it's a wonderful place to go for a relaxing walk. you can also lie down on the soft grass and enjoy the sunshine. i highly recommend this park to anyone staying in the sapporo city center.
this park is gorgeous! run or bike along the canal, many small ponds around, a cafe/bar on the inside.
this park is great for skipping the crossings it goes for about 20 blocks and is a nice park, great views and good for getting though the city.

this park is located next to the east gardens of the imperial palace. it has nice paths snaking along the park and even a small lake. it is a shame that parts of this park are so abandoned, as the tall grass seems to be growing everywhere.

this park is located next to the imperial palace and it’s a beautiful park with lots of trees and flowers. it’s a very popular spot for seeing sakura blossom espacilly in chidorigafuchi moat. the garden is also home to the famous nippon budokan which is a great place to visit. however, be prepared it will be very crowded during peak season.
this park is old and in need of some maintenance. once you have paid to get in, you have to pay for a tube to ride the main attraction. food and drinks well priced. the kids loved it.

this park is one of my favorite. the park is completely amazing. i love to go there for a run or to walk my dog. the environment will make you feel so relaxed. there are a lot of people, it is really popular place. great place for taking pictures or just to hang out with your friends.

this park is pretty underrated as compared to most of the parks on toronto waterfront, but it really is a hidden gem. the walk along the pier gives a spectacular view of the toronto skyline along with the fabulous view of the billy bishop airport. you can enjoy planes landing and taking off with some amazing sunset views. would highly recommend visiting.

this park is quite big, lots of playgrounds space for kids, including slides and swings and monkey bars. i like how this park is well maintained and organized. there is a free to use water dispenser as well which is good for hot days.

this park is really underrated. there’s some cool trails without the crowds of other national parks. we hiked the curry ridge trail which offered some amazing views and a nice alpine lake. there wasn’t a lot of mosquitoes either which was a relief! the trail was well maintained. there’s different trails of various difficulty and length so there’s something for everyone- if you’re in the area it’s a great place to find a nice hike.

this park is so big! we had a private driver take us from our lodge and it took an hour to get into the park. we needed our passports to pass security and sign a form that our guide helped us fill out. you can only drive on the road to protect the national park but the things you see are amazing. this is the wild and it’s kept like that. you see tons of herds just grazing. it’s all about luck on what you get to see! you will see many zebras, giraffes, elephants, antelopes etc but if you’re lucky you will see the rarer animals like lions, cheetahs, leopard. the guides and others talk amongst each other to help each other out and if they see something interesting they will let jen know. even if you don’t see something like a hunt, this park is amazing. you get to see the wild up close and open. it’s so big and just amazing to look at.

this park is truly one of the best spots to relax, go hiking, have a picnic, and enjoy a peaceful photoshoot. the natural scenery is breathtaking—lush greenery, well-maintained trails, and plenty of shaded areas to sit and unwind. there are scenic walking paths perfect for all ages, a serene atmosphere for meditation or reading, and open spaces that are ideal for family gatherings or simply spending quiet time in nature. it’s also a great place for birdwatching, or just getting some fresh air away from the noise of the city. highly recommended for nature lovers.

this park is truly peaceful and calm. the ambiance is wonderful. there are amazing bird sounds. peaceful and pleasant people are sitting on benches and on the grass, enjoying life. it’s a place where you can easily spend hours.

this park is wonderful, truly large and spacious, full of interesting species of plants, trees and animals, quiet, and tremendously beautiful. we've been here a couple of times as we live far south of bali. our 1.5-year-old puppy loves the park over the moon! it isn't a must-visit for everyone, as many tourists want to see this full-throttle essence of bali, which this park is not. it is more about nature, peace, calmness, and sweet moments, such as sitting on the grass surrounded by gigantic trees and seeing mountains and a volcanic lake. but if you love parks, forests, views, picturesque spaces, cooler temperatures, fresh air, and long walks, this place is perfect for 2 hours or half a day. amazing!

this picnic area has an amazing view of the yellowstone river. to get there, follow the small dirt path in the back of the parking circle near the bathrooms. it is only 600 feet one way. be aware that you must walk uphill, but otherwise it is a very short walk. don’t go on the path to the left of the parking area (assuming you’re facing away from the road) if you are only interested in the viewpoint seen below. that path is the 3.7 mile (round-trip) out-and-back yellowstone river overlook trail. that trail runs parallel along the river, while the viewpoint is on the 600-foot trail that leads straight back. be very careful when you get to the top. there are many small, loose rocks that you can easily slip on and fall if you are not careful. don’t get too close to the edge, obviously. be careful bringing small children up there. you should have bear spray with you. if you want to be extra cautious, you can clap or make loud noises while walking up the hill to try and scare away any potential bears.

this place has a lot of history. it is jarringly small for a place called a palace. one “ballroom” the size of a largish mainland living room, four bedrooms/rooms from small to medium size, a central connecting chamber the size of a modest lavatory , and an entrance hall/sitting room the size of a medium foyer. kitchens were separate structures in those days due to fire hazards apparently. there are many carefully preserved relics of the hawaiian royalty. or careful attempts at preservation i’d have to say. so much of that native culture valued artifacts incorporating feathers (because the meticulous methods of acquiring the materials and constructing these articles demonstrated immense skill and immense commitment of man-hours) while i believe all appropriate acts of preservation were taken, the results at times are still…sad. but feathers, even with the best preservation techniques, fade and disintegrate.

this place has been here since 1932. i grew up coming here as a kid and bringing my kids here as well. it is a unique and enjoyable experience with a friendly staff with feeding and educational shows that they provide through out the day. as you check in you have the opportunity to purchase food to feed the monkeys and the fish. the gift shop is reasonably priced with many gift choices. unfortunately today they had a large portion of the park closed for repairs, and because of that they offered the entrance fee at a discount; it was 20 for adults, so you may want to call before coming to confirm if the entire park has reopened. there was no water fountains throughout the park but vending machines. no food was available the day we were here. as you walk through this place you can clearly see that it has been around for many years and could use some updates and repairs, but it is clean and managed well but no updates. they keep the area looking like a natural habitat so it is not manicured for that reason. they charge 150 if you want to have a private guided tour and a more personal experience with the monkeys but we did not choose to do this. parking was easy and there was no charge to park. overall we had a great day enjoying a place that we remembered very well as a kid.

this place has the best view over the valley. is a bit of a hike but nothing too difficult nor complicated and the view from the top is definitely worth the time and effort!! the high place of sacrifice in petra is one of the ancient city’s most fascinating and spiritually significant sites. perched high above the city, it requires a climb up a series of rock-cut steps that offer scenic views of petra’s rugged landscape along the way. dating back to the 1st century bce, the site was used for ceremonial rituals and offerings to nabatean deities, with altars, obelisks, and channels carved directly into the rock. once at the top, visitors find a large sacrificial altar with stunning panoramic views over petra and the surrounding valleys. the experience of reaching the summit, combined with the site’s historical depth, makes the high place of sacrifice both a rewarding and contemplative destination for those interested in petra’s religious and cultural heritage.

this place is free but exists on donations so we put in £15 as three of us visited and thought that was a fair donation. there are 6 hangers but in reality, hangers 3, 4 & 5 are all the same hanger. there is so much to see and took us approximately 4 hours to look around including eating in the cafe. the cafe was well priced and good choices of food and very clean.you can use blue-light discount in the cafe too. also in the first hanger there is a good sized gift shop which you have to go passes when exiting as the first hanger is the entrance and exit for the museum. although we went on the train, i see that there is a good sized carpark if arriving by car. i fully recommend visiting this place and me and my family had a really good day.

this place is great for relaxation. perhaps residents of this area come here for walks and picnics. but this is part of canadian history, and such an interesting one. and the picturesque landscapes and views of the river and city are remembered forever. there are many paid parking lots for cars, and the price is not high.

this place is great, open late and super fun. highly recommended. drinks are not expensive but average. djs play unlimited hits, fun to dance to, and dancers come to show you. the bathrooms are clean. lots of people but not crowded. overall, it's fun.

this place is just amazing. we were watching the sunset, drinking beer, enjoying the hot water and that made our day. thanks for this tresure.

this place is kind of unique.. at first i thought it would be like other places in tokyo that i had visited. a range of big shops or a short passage with small shops. but this has completely different vibe for me. it's a bit more "oldies", less crowded and we even surprised to hear a very loud "old chinese music" from a shop. for a second we thought it's not japan but hong kong. love it though.. we took a leisure walk and snacking.

this place is literally one of the highlights of our trip to all of japan! the energy in this place is unreal and it’s so much fun! all of the staff are friendly, engaging, and very talented. the dance routines are creative, their outfits are fun, the music is energizing, and the stage lighting is beautiful. there’s literally not a bad seat in the house either, as every seat has a great view. easily one of my favorite things to do in tokyo!

this place is locally known as 'malah' it is very close to bahia palace and is a good landmark if you want to get picked up for your day tours or to tell your taxi. loads of little food places. we went to eat at a place(restaurant) in this square called "malah". extremely great food and very reasonably priced. so make sure you go for food where you see plenty of people already enjoying their meals. it has many souvenir shops and alongside spice souk. the evening here is even better with much lesser chaos than jama el fena. kids play around here but unfortunately they come to you to ask for money so ignore them. overall great location in marakkech

this place is located in the outskirts of the main berlin city area. not too difficult to get too if you have access to the u-bahn. the palace is wonderful and you can get the audio guide to visit the old wing. i would highly recommend taking the free audio guide. i would say it was the best audio guide i have had till date. it is very to the point and succinct. there was no long drawn music in the audio and it allowed us to enjoy the rooms without getting into long drawn details about the rooms. the newer wing was okay but the lawn/garden area was nice and a manageable size. the whole sight can be seen 1.5 to 2 hours. i would recommend going here if you are in berlin. to save time i would recommend buying tickets online. good to visit in the morning if you want less crowd.

this place is magical. we just spent 3 night there during the migration and basically saw everything in one shot. our guide alex - was incredible. the food was amazing you will gain about 5 pounds. i can not express how much i loved this place.

this place isn't as crowded as waikiki beach, and the waves are gentle, making it easy for children to play. today, the wind was a bit strong, but with occasional clouds, it wasn't too hot even without a parasol, making it comfortable.😊 04/28/2024 today was clear and windless, making it perfect for tanning, so we relaxed at the beach. as a result, we got a nice tan.🌞 05/12/2024 today, we enjoyed snorkeling at the southern end of kahanamoku beach, next to the hilton lagoon. the waves were high, and there were several surfers beyond the breakwater. inside the breakwater, there were fewer people, and when we swam to the edge, we saw colorful fish and the water was relatively clear. the sandy beach is clean, but it quickly becomes rocky. near the breakwater, there is no sandy beach at all, just rocks, so if you plan to go into deeper water, marine shoes are necessary. on our way back, we entered the lagoon and saw many schools of white, translucent fish. the center of the lagoon was nearly 6 feet deep. it seems you can also rent a sup (stand-up paddleboard) and practice here.😊👍

this place on jeju island feels like a scene from a movie. towering cliffs disappearing into the clouds, emerald waters, and black volcanic rocks create a breathtaking landscape. the colors are so vivid it feels almost unreal — like stepping into a cinematic world. at the foot of the mountain, horses graze peacefully, adding a touch of serenity and charm. a walk along the shore, with waves gently crashing against the rocks, leaves unforgettable memories. it’s one of those places where you just want to pause, take it all in, and feel deeply connected to nature.

this place open its shutters at 4am for food prep and start serving only after 5 ish. there are 6 individual stalls, one selling drinks. for tourists its best to come for breakfast or brunch as the office workers start pouring in around 11am- 1.30pm it can get super crowded. by 2pm the stall selling different main & side courses to go with rice have not much left. we had the kway chap which is the pork meat & offals with rice noodles, really tasty. but if business is good that day, there isn’t much left so no point going after 2pm. food is as local as you can get, tasty and cheap.

this place truly has an incredible vibe that caters to everyone. you’ll find all types of people hanging out, whether they're listening to music, meeting up with friends, or simply relaxing. it's family-friendly, with something for everyone to enjoy. you can have a smoke, grab a drink, or just take in the atmosphere. the area exudes a bit of luxury, with ferraris and porsches cruising by, and high-end stores like versace just around the corner. it's also got tokyo smoke, gelato shops, barbers, sushi spots, and pizza takeout. it really feels like an old town square, but with a modern twist.

this place truly stands out for its impressive and extensive selection of food and drinks—there’s something for everyone, whether you’re in the mood for a quick snack, a full meal, or a refreshing beverage. every item we tried was fresh, flavorful, and thoughtfully prepared. what really made the experience even better was the exceptional service. the staff were incredibly friendly, attentive, and genuinely seemed to care about making sure every guest felt welcome and well taken care of. from the moment we arrived to the time we left, the customer service and overall support were top-notch. it’s clear that the team takes pride in what they do, creating an inviting atmosphere where you can relax and enjoy your time. i would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for great food, a wide variety of choices, and outstanding hospitality

this place was a game changer, the owner is very knowledgeable and happy to offer advice. he had us completely drain and clean our tank and start over. after 5 yrs of struggling our water conditions are now perfect and our fish are thriving. we've recently switched to live plants with their help and after 2 months it's still looking and testing great and with fewer water changes. thank you!!!

this place was absolutely amazing. we went here for my birthday and it definitely did not disappoint. all the workers were very helpful and friendly, but one girl who stood out and went above and beyond was an adorable girl named serena. she made our visit and even took a ton of pictures of me and my girlfriend feeding the giraffes so we could enjoy our experience. serena deserves a raise!!! we also went through the drive-through safari twice and the indoor sanctuary twice. this place is absolutely worth the money, and we saved a lot buying tickets online. we will certainly be back.

this place was absolutely fantastic !on top of the mountains, with a magic view, very well located next to the serengeti , amongst real masai villages, masai boma is a dream come true . on top of that , the staff , 95% masai , managed by nicholas, are very caring about all your needs . the food is cooked lovely . the dinner was around a lovely fireplace in a wooden style dining room facing the mountains around . the room , like all the hotel , is masai style , very wide, peaceful and with a lovely view . we will come back for sure !

this place was absolutely stunning—it reminded me of my time in japan. i visited on a weekend, so it was extremely busy and crowded, which was a bit of a downside for me. that said, i’m hoping i can gradually get more comfortable with navigating large crowds in tight spaces. thankfully, the weather was perfect that day, which made the entire setting look even more beautiful. the temples, lush greenery, and serene water features created such a beautiful scene. there was also a small tea house on-site that looked lovely, though it was packed with visitors. i imagine visiting during a quieter time would allow for a much more peaceful and immersive experience. when i went, there were kids running around and a lot going on, but even amid the chaos, the place remained incredibly beautiful. (if big touristy crowds don’t bother you, don’t let it bother you just because of my experience with it. it was memorial day weekend too.) if you’re planning a visit, i’d also recommend looking into the three-park pass—it’s a great way to explore more of the area’s natural beauty.

this place was amazing. we stayed for 5 nights and enjoyed every second there. the excursions were great, we went to the hot springs which i would totally recommend, the geisers which were really cool, rainbow valley which had really cool colored rocks and my favorite, the sand dunes. the restaurant was great. they have a menu that changed every day. if you don't want what's on the main menu they have an alternative menu that has more classic food like pasta or burgers. the staff were even better than the food and the excursions combined. some of the best staff are chris (the assistant manager) who greets you as soon as you walk in and is super funny, carole who gives you a tour of your futureistic room which has a heated towel rack, heated floors and my favorite- the outside shower. benjamin who was the best and kindest server, adrian who was so nice and helped answer all of our queries and questions and was our star gazing guide. we went to the pool a lot and trust me its the perfect temperature. its about 90°f or 35°c indoors in the spa. the spa is great, we got massages which are very reasonably priced. they have a sauna and a steam room and a relaxing room to chill in. you can order tea as well. we went star gazing but it was very cloudy but our guide adrian said we should try again tomorrow or the next day. we did and it was amazing!

this place was amazing. we went as soon as they opened on a saturday morning and the kids were able to do everything they wanted to do. they had sunblock dispensers at the entrance and hand sanitizer placed throughout. indoor areas are amazing, awesome toddler area, the outdoor spots were clean and fun, the art station and water stations were easily the best. the staff was all fantastic as well. i could go on and on, this was a definite hit. it felt amazing to be somewhere designed for kids, not just accommodating or tolerate of them.

this point and the area is probably the best for sunset in sydney. 🌅 if you are coming from opera house direction, you need to get through royal botanical gardens. unfortunately the gardens close before sunset. it is hard to reach here by navigation. i will share my walkthrough to get to here around sunset. 1. navigate to "state library of new south wales" by walking. when you see or get close to the building, 2. navigate to "art gallery of new south wales" you will be getting through "the domain - phillip precinct" park inner ways. 3. when you are exitting the park now navigate to "mrs macquarie's chair" you will be walking on art gallery road towards mrs macquaries road and you're on your way for the best sunset. you are welcome.

this puppet show is amazing!! it showcases a different point of view of vietnamese life like in agriculture, fishing and beliefs. even though i do not understand what they say, there is an lcd screen on the top right of the water stage that will tell you what that event is for that was written in english. the real people performing at the back handling the puppets are so talented. great effort!! kudos also to the singers and musicians. you're all an artist at a different level!! congratulations on your successful saturday night show!! gladly i booked the vip seat in front in the agoda app for only 25 ringgit. i highly recommend this for all ages.
this quiet square is an island of peace in l'île de la cité. worth your time and ideal for a pause between the long walks in paris to refill your batteries.

this really is a under rated place in venice. there are quite remarkable views of venice and the surrounding area. it was worth the wait in the queue for this. there is a fast track option but we didn't use it. s lift takes you up to the top of the tower. then enjoy the incredible view. highly recommended

this really is more a museum dedicated to the "spanish inquisition". there are other historical facts present, but the chambers where witches were denounced and questioned and executed are the main attraction and really take away from anything one sees. its interesting to see the atrocities for what they really were, which was sadly religious persecution and quite disturbing. i don't think this is a good place to bring children but the twice i have been i have been happy that this accurate piece of history has been maintained so we can hopefully avoid such future acts.

this resort is so beautiful. the activities were so fun: horseback riding in the ocean, some of the best snorkeling we have ever done, the peri peri beach club, and amazing picnics and dinners on the beach! we loved our stay and hope to return someday. the staff was so kind and went above and beyond to make our trip so special, especially olivia. loved this place!

this resort is spectacular: the staff, service & rooms are all to an extremely high standard. the helicopter transfer to the island is just the beginning of the magic - couldn't recommend this place more!

this restaurant easily became my favorite in miami!!! service was amazing, our incredible waitress, tesla, was perfectly attentive. there was so much food for the price and i feel that this is one of the best places to get a good amount of food for the price!!

this restaurant is a fantastic find—great food at a reasonable price. the dishes were outstanding and arrived quickly. the oysters were incredibly fresh, while the kale salad and tostones were packed with flavor. the atmosphere was a bit lively, making conversation challenging at times, but overall, the experience was excellent. i would definitely return!

this restaurant is a hidden gem for anyone who loves bold indian flavors. the chaat menu is packed with crowd-pleasers—pani puri is crisp and refreshing, each menu ..melts in your mouth, and the chat menu has the perfect mix of spice and crunch. every bite feels like a burst of street food magic. on the south indian side, the dishes are just as impressive. the masala dosa is perfectly crisp, filled with flavorful potato masala, and paired with fresh chutneys and sambar that hit all the right notes. the idlis are soft and fluffy, and the medu vadas have that ideal golden crunch. the place is clean, the service is quick, and the prices are fair for the quality. whether you're in the mood for a quick chaat snack or a full meal, this spot delivers on taste and authenticity.

this restaurant is a hidden gem! it is such a value in a place where so much is overpriced. the 10 course tasting menu has a little bit of everything. spicy, sweet, savory. standouts to our group were the papaya salad, the lamb chops, the skirt steak, the curried fish, and the rum cake. also, we got the jell-o shots, which were an elevated, foodie take and nothing like the ones we grew up with. they were so fun! we will definitely be back to this beautiful and delicious restaurant.

this restaurant is amazing! we tried the miami spice menu and were very impressed. the dishes were excellent. the drinks were delicious and the atmosphere is great. we had beef tartare, ceviche, lamb shank, catch of the day, rum cake, and key lime tart. everything was 10/10.

this review comes a bit late since i visited this beautiful shrine in early november 2024, but it’s been an unforgettable trip and truly a rather hidden gem for kyoto shrines. shimogamo is one of the two oldest and most important shrines in kyoto, dating back further than the settlement of kyoto as ancient japan’s capital. its importance throughout history is felt as you walk through the grounds that are much more spacious than other temples and shrines, the walk through the garden was especially serene - and the rain made it all feel even more connected with nature, as is the spirit of shintoism. even more poignant since the shrine was settled here for the kamo river. there are also several marked archeological sites and protected ancient trees to remind you of the age of this sacred place. yet despite its historical significance, it (luckily) does not receive the level of tourist attention which other more widely known temples/shrines do, so it was a very peaceful experience. there was an ongoing ceremony for an event hence the group of people in my photos, but otherwise quite empty. the gift shop was quite popular since this shrine sells a famous season edition omamori - a special momento capturing the season you visited. entry to the grounds and surrounding garden is also free but there is a fee to enter the prayer halls, which i didn’t do. they also have the water omikuji in japanese only (i got great fortune yay 🙏) i will definitely visit again and also its connected kamigamo shrine further upriver.

this review is based solely on my experience walking on the beach and surrounding area during the off-season in winter. deck walkway, palm tree path. the scenery is okay. it's hard to give 5 stars to this place, but i gave it 5 because it's a shame that not many people know it or stop by. there is a restroom. from a beach bather's point of view, there's a strange mudflat smell (there are a lot of birds right next to the bridge? there's water), and the white sand beach is just a beach... there's a lot of seaweed that hasn't been cleaned up. can be annoying. however, the beach is wide and has a sandy ledge, so it would be good for families with children to swim. in fact, there is less fishing gear waste than other beaches. the only commercial area nearby is kayak rental, so i recommend bringing a car...

this review is for one of the vegetable stands. i came here on an evening right before closing when it was dark outside. the owners of the stand was packing everything up. i asked for two heads of dark swiss chard and in the dark, i could not see them very clearly. i paid 5€ for them. when i got home to wash them, i discovered to my horror that every leaf on the chard had small insect-made or parasitic holes. i would strongly advise to closely inspect the produce here before purchasing.

this review is for upper geyser basin & old faithful observation point loop which was a ~4.9 miles round trip that took ~2.5 hours to complete. this was one of those unique hikes with various geysers and pools. the trails are located within walkable distances from the old faithful hotels and visitor center. ideally, it would be best to start the hike early in the morning to avoid the crowd. most of the trail consisted of flat boardwalks and paved asphalt. the boardwalks were icy in some spots during the morning. observation point part of the trail was somewhat pointless because there was no "wow factor" in terms of any view. it was still a nice stroll in the wooded areas, eventually reaching solitary geyser. furthermore, this part of the trail had some inclines and declines. the steam from the geysers have an unpleasant sulfur smell. carry bear spray; the chances of encountering a bear is lower at popular trails but you never know. short video of the hike for those interested! https://youtu.be/wjgwi2obiwa

this review is from a couple of 'oldies', who decided at 60 and 62 wanted to do something new. jenny was our instructor and she was amazing and very patient with us. she explained and instructed so well that we felt at ease and comfortable immediately. one thing you should know about me is i have always had a fear of putting my head into water (done it once that i remember) but with jenny's instructions and her own exuberance of what she does i wasn't afraid and we had an absolute blast. i didn't stop smiling the whole time and now feel confident to go snorkelling again. we loved looking at the coral and especially seeing the types of fish. the videos that she took were a bonus and were sent straight to our grown up children as proof. i would certainly recommend this company to learn from.

this review is hard to write, but i was touched inappropriately by the diving instructor during a session, and i don’t want anyone else to go through what i did. i wasn’t completely alone on this trip — i had a male friend with me, but he didn’t join the dive session. so when i joined this beginner diving course, i was essentially a solo female diver, not from the philippines, not a swimmer, and with no prior diving or snorkeling experience. the instructor assigned to me was reyjie arboleda (instructor #101109). because i was the only total beginner, he said he would “focus on me.” at first, i was thankful — until i realized how vulnerable i was. while underwater, the session went smoothly. but everything changed the moment we surfaced. i was extremely dizzy, seasick, disoriented, and i couldn’t find my regulator. i panicked and tried to signal for help. that’s when the instructor repeatedly touched and caressed my chest, even though i was fully wearing my diving suit. i tried to move away, thinking maybe it was accidental — but then he grabbed my lower body, and when i pushed his hands away, he smiled and said, “this is nice.” i was floating helplessly in the open water. there were strong waves, and we were waiting for the boat. it was just the two of us — i had no way to escape, and i was terrified. once the boat arrived and other people were around, he immediately switched back to “professional mode” — offered me water, asked if i felt okay, and even told me to unzip my diving suit “so i could breathe better.” i want to be clear — the other staff at the dive center were warm, helpful, and very kind. but i was too afraid to raise what had happened in front of them. i was just one girl, alone in a foreign country, surrounded by people from their team. i didn’t know who i could trust, or whether speaking up would make things worse for me. so i stayed quiet — until now. i don’t have video proof, but i know what i experienced. i’m not here to cancel anyone. i’m here to warn other women — especially solo travelers, beginners, or non-swimmers. be extremely careful when choosing dive centers, even if the reviews look good. sometimes, the danger happens when you’re the only one left vulnerable. if you’re reading this and have experienced something similar — you’re not alone.

this review is long overdue, but has been on my mind. we stayed at your beautiful camp in september 2024. we also stayed at your other accommodation, giraffe manor at the beginning of our trip. both were outstanding. sala’s camp had beautiful and very comfortable, clean tents…..even with our own private pool! the food was delicious, the wine was wonderful and the people couldn’t have been nicer. i even had a wonderful unexpected birthday celebration one night!🎉 we were lucky to meet and have an interesting conversation one evening with the owner of the camp. of course the animals on the drives were fabulous and we had a wonderful guide and spotter on our bucket list trip who found every animal we wanted to see. definitely a trip of a lifetime and would recommend this camp to everyone. thank you for everything.💕

this review is mostly about the sculpture gardens. although the museum is nice, it's the sculpture gardens that really wow you. the landscapes, combined with the outdoor art is just incredible. paths wander around ponds, and sculptures are located along the paths, each one has a plaque telling you who the artist is and when it was sculpted. we went during the week, so it was probably less crowded. so many great photo opportunities along the way. highly recommend going. what a gem.

this review is only based on the scuba offering from watercolors and quality service in providing facilities and food. first of all the scuba offering was just impeccable. it was literally half the price of what the hotel offered and i received one on one beginner class which went most of the day. my instructor gunther or "jimmy" as he's known locally, was an absolute genuine legend. patient with me and communicated well. although it was my first time i did not feel uncomfortable at any point. while awaiting the boat i enjoyed the french toast and french press coffee from my hosts at watercolors. effective way to prepare for scuba and delicious. really pleased with this adventure and would highly recommend.

this review is specifically for the shiretoko-goko lakes or the shiretoko five lakes at the shiretoko national park. as a first time foreign tourist in hokkaido, i visited this attraction this afternoon and i was impressed by the "as far as the eye can see" wooden boardwalks to see the main lake here, making it a relatively comfortable walk among nature - whereas the other four lakes are in a less accessible situation for the ordinary tourist. while this place boasts the lake(s) and its wooden boardwalks, the scenery of its surroundings is very beautiful and if you are lucky, you would be able see wildlife nearby - especially deer. so if you are in shiretoko, i highly recommend this place for you to visit.

this review is to bring up how dedicated and fun our tour guides alicia and geo were, they explained everything in detail and made the whole experience enjoyable, it is a long day, so make sure to bring water and a hat for the sun at the pyramids …. it tends to get hot .

this review is way overdue (5/2023) but it is rated as one of the best experiences that i've ever had. alex jr. was my divemaster and he was kind, patient and put safety first. he knew that it was my first time diving in cenotes and i was nervous! he eased my nerves and even held my hand during my descent into cenote angelita because i couldn't see a thing as we were descending through the halocline (i didn't pick this dive)! if you're not familiar with this cenote, google it. it's pretty cool! my favorite was cenote was aktun ha/car wash because it was so diverse (mangrove, caverns and marine life). i also got to meet alex sr. who helped to map out most of the cave systems in the yucatan. what's really cool is that he and a few of his dive buddies made a massive discovery - they discovered the remains of a near complete skeleton of a teenage girl known as naia that was 12,000-13,000 years old...one of the oldest in n. america! if you're trying to find a dive shop in the tulum area, definitely check out acuatic tulum!

this roman catholic church is located in the muslim quarter of the old city, near st. stephen's gate (lions' gate) and you will find that it is part a complex which also includes the church of the condemnation and imposition of the cross. this is the traditional second station of the cross on the via dolorosa and just an amazing place. according to tradition, the church enshrines the spot where jesus christ was flogged by roman soldiers before his journey down the via dolorosa to golgotha.

this roman nymphaeum (public fountain) is in utter ruins - just a bunch of ancient stones with a dried up water channel behind it. this is where the colonnaded street of petra starts. there is a pistachio tree growing wild in ruins and a bunch of shops selling souvenirs. it is said that the water that flowed through the treasury siq used to come till here and flow in the fountain.
this route along the river is so beautiful! very nice during the winter but also so nice during summer. feels like you are waking in the middle of the nature instead of the city.
this russian orthodox cathedral, located at the heart of the so-called russian compound, was built in 1872, when the holy city was part of the ottoman empire. you should check it out

this safari is incredibly affordable and never feels overcrowded, which makes for a really enjoyable visit. make sure to bring yen with you since most of the feeding stations only take coins. you can feed almost every animal for just 100 yen, and the bigger attractions are 500 yen with set times. there are a lot of chances to get up close and personal with the animals, which is rare at most places. the bird exhibit, though, is wild — the birds get aggressive, especially once they see you’ve bought seeds. i did read some news saying the place might be illegal. honestly, it wouldn’t be too surprising, but it would be really sad if it shuts down as rumored in september. despite the controversy, it’s a unique and memorable experience.

this scenic snow-capped mountain ski resort offers breathtaking views. for first-time visitors, it's recommended to make a phone reservation for snow gear rentals 2-3 days in advance. however, those arriving early can still secure equipment through on-site rentals without significant concern about stock depletion. the slopes tend to be relatively steeper - beginners may want to test their skills on the short practice chairlift before attempting the main gondola ride to higher elevations. the price for ropeway ticket is 5000 yen. the price of equipment renting is around 6000 yen.

this seems like the biggest square in downtown jerusalem, and a main intersection point where beautiful streets such as king george v, keren ha'yesod and ramban st. meet together. the buildings all around give it a neoclassical feel and look of a western european metropolin. take a walk down any direction and despite the busy streets you'll enjoy nice views and a real feeling of the city. near the kings hotel and the convent of tera sancta, a nice small square on the corner of balfur street, the site of the official residence of the prime minister of israel. the square a symbol of feriendship with france became a site of very frequent demonstrations. very interesting.

this seems really nice from other reviews (the pictures) but on closer inspection the grass is scruffy and knobbly. it's certainly not as lush as you would like from a park. i managed to find a fairly private spot where i was able to sleep under the glourious sun, listen to music, read and then meditate for a while. it's what you make it but on a purely visual front this is not a park for high standard beauty seekers!

this shop has the most beautiful masks i’ve ever seen. the artistry, creativity, and craftsmanship are remarkable. i bought 2 masks when i visited in person, then contacted the shop to buy 2 larger masks i saw during my visit and couldn’t stop thinking about. leo went above and beyond to provide the best customer service. he was super responsive, sent me pictures of masks in the shop to make sure i got the ones i wanted, provided details about the masks, and answered all of my questions. the masks were very well packaged and delivered to the us in a week. when i received the masks, they were in perfect condition and even more beautiful than i remembered. the masks remind me of the opulence, beauty, magic, and mystery of venice. gorgeous venetian masks, incredible shopping experience! grazie mille, leo! i love the masks so much! they are magnificent!

this shopping mall is a massive and vibrant destination, offering an extensive range of shopping and dining options. with numerous brands to choose from, it caters to all tastes and preferences. the mall is creatively divided into themed zones, including chinese and other themes, adding a unique cultural touch to the shopping experience. there are plenty of picturesque spots perfect for capturing memorable moments. conveniently located right next to the metro station, it’s easily accessible. the atmosphere is especially lively in the evenings, making it a great place to visit and explore.

this short hike through the ancient forest is absolutely beautiful! pretty easy-moderate hike for most people and the atmosphere is majestic. must see for every nature loving person. it feels like walking through a movie scene from lord of the rings or star wars. i love seeing cool trees so it was a shock and awe experience for me. check it out.

this show museum is pretty cool!!! 😎 can see lots of kind of shoes and about its history, and about its overall uses in criminology, or by fashion. i recommend you going to this bata shoe 👠 museum in weekend with your near family and friends!! this museum has 3 floors including the museum basement, and also provides overall old historical relics about shoes too….👞

this show was absolutely beautiful. between the singing, music, and the craftsmanship of the puppets, it was mesmerizing. i also appreciated the audio device support. i was able to watch the show and understand what i was watching in my language so that i could capture the true essence of this show. i loved it. definitely go see this show if you are in hanoi. you won't be disappointed.
this shrine is spacious, well kept and peaceful. minimal tourists so you can spend some quality time resting your mind and regroup.

this si giardino di sant’andrea al quirinale, a hidden gem in the heart of rome. tucked away from the city’s chaos, this serene park offers a refreshing escape with its lush greenery, winding pathways, and a peaceful atmosphere. it’s not just a beautiful garden but also a place steeped in history and symbolism. the highlight of the park is the monumento celebrativo del bicentenario dei carabinieri, a striking bronze statue titled “la pattuglia nella tempesta” (the patrol in the storm). this powerful artwork, crafted by antonio berti, depicts two carabinieri walking resolutely through a storm, symbolizing the unwavering dedication of italy’s national military police. the monument, inaugurated in 2014, commemorates 200 years of service by the carabinieri and adds a profound sense of purpose to this tranquil space. whether you’re a history enthusiast, an art lover, or simply looking for a quiet place to reflect, this park has something for everyone. its central location near the quirinale makes it an easy stop for visitors exploring the area.

this small, almost inconspicuous, quiet square in the heart of historic berlin – located halfway between the gendarmenmarkt and the palace – has a rather eventful past. it achieved its most lasting significance a good 150 years ago as the center of berlin's then world-leading fashion and clothing industry. it was here that the "ready-to-wear" size, as we know it today, was invented. at that time, hundreds of small and large businesses producing "ready-to-wear" fashion were located around the square. at its peak, approximately 20,000 seamstresses were employed around the square. a monument commemorates this era and, above all, its inglorious end (see photos). today, two embassies are located here, the federal foreign office is located not far from the square, and most of the commercial buildings here are listed buildings. two small restaurants invite you to linger.

this spot is a neat archaeological find right in the middle of athens. it’s super close to the acropolis, so you can easily check it out. even if you don’t have a ticket, you can see a lot of the roman agora from the nearby streets. just a little note: there’s not a ton of shade, so don’t forget your water, sunscreen, and a hat! it tends to be way less busy than the acropolis, which makes it a chill place to wander around the ruins. this site really shows how athens evolved during roman times. it’s a quieter place, but you still get a glimpse of the city’s rich history. the overall architecture is awesome, though most of the structures are gone, a few are still standing tall.

this spot is beautiful. we were staying at krystal grand and decided to walk through the back of hyatt to the lighthouse lol. we made it without any trouble, however, according to other reviews, use caution and be respectful to any security personnel.

this spot is definitely worth a visit! while the murals aren’t all that big and there’s not a ton to see, the walk up is really pleasant and offers a great view of the city and namsan tower. it’s a perfect little area if you’re looking for a scenic stroll. our visit was made even better by the bonus of being greeted by a super cute and cuddly cat. overall, it’s a nice, relaxing spot to enjoy the view and get a little fresh air, highly recommend it!
this spot is fantastic and pretty low key - not too many tourists going into this area, since it's already pretty high up and out of the way. awesome views, whether during the day or for the sunset.
this spot is so cool. the roses are beautiful and it’s a perfect setting in the park.

this spot is the best place you will see in jeju. do not go to the north path (nothing much too see, just for 10km of walking). if you want to walk, just walk here for 5hours. i walked to the north 2 times and it was boring. anyway this is very close to the bus stop, just walk upside for 100m. there are quite huge path to the right and the left side. i reccomend the right road(all connected so dont worry. you will just walk circle). and also in the morning, this place is filled with moistured tree scent wich is beautiful experience you will have. so go ealry in the morning!! as time goes by, many people visit here and talking aloud with their stinky cosmetic all around the air. it was terrible. so you cant enjoy the fresh air after these disaster. and dont forget to bring water and simple snack.

this spot is truly amazing! the caves are comfortable, spotless, and offer a breathtaking view of the desert. it's the perfect place to unwind and find the peace you’ve been craving. both dinner and breakfast were delicious, and the hosts are incredible storytellers. spending time around the fire with them creates unforgettable memories. an outstanding experience. i totally recommend it!
this spot offers a panoramic view of prague's old town. there are very few people so you can enjoy it at your own pace. i parked in the nearby street car park which was a very reasonable price.

this spot used to be a bustling night street food corner with many stalls, but after a ban on street seating, only a few remain, most closing by 10 pm. however, one stall stays open until midnight, offering an extensive menu. it's one of the few places to find good, affordable street food late in the evening. please visit and support them.

this store is offering amazing quality products for any outdoor fan. you will definitely find what you need. what we really liked is the good advices for equipment and the nice attitude of the people working there. 🏕 we would like to thank the staff for helping us far beyond equipment related support. thank you, and hope to see you again. 😊

this street hawker stall was an absolute gem. from the moment i walked up, the smell of sizzling spices and grilled meat pulled me in. i ordered a plate of their signature noodles with grilled chicken, and it blew me away — perfectly seasoned, cooked to order, and packed with flavor. you could taste the freshness in every bite. what really stood out, though, was the energy and passion of the vendor. you could tell they genuinely care about what they’re serving. even though it was busy, the service was fast and friendly. the portions were generous, and the prices? unbeatable. this is the kind of food that makes you appreciate street cuisine — honest, flavorful, and rooted in tradition. i’d choose this over a fancy restaurant any day. highly recommend stopping by if you’re nearby. you won’t regret it!

this sunset boat tour was hands-down one of the highlights of our trip to dubrovnik! from the moment we stepped on board, the vibes were perfect. our captain, ivan was absolutely amazing - friendly, knowledgeable, and so much fun. he shared fascinating bits of dubrovnik’s history while effortlessly answering every random tourist question we threw at him. what made the experience extra special were the thoughtful touches: he snapped polaroid photos of us to take home as souvenirs (such a cool keepsake!), let us dj with our own music, and created such a chill, personalized atmosphere. the timing of the cruise was perfect for catching the golden hour and watching the sun dip behind the adriatic, it was stunning. highly, highly recommend this tour if you’re looking for a memorable and relaxed way to experience the magic of dubrovnik from the water. thank you for such a wonderful evening!

this sunset cruise was a fantastic way to spend our trip in santorini. my husband and i booked it after our wedding to enjoy quality time together and witness the stunning sunset, which truly lived up to the hype. we loved snorkeling in the clear waters and exploring the vibrant sea life. the food was also incredible. additionally, the crew shared interesting historical insights about santorini at various sites, which was a nice bonus. they made sure we stayed hydrated by constantly offering us drinks and even played music so we could dance and enjoy ourselves. with great company, an attentive crew, and excellent staff, i would definitely recommend this experience before leaving santorini!

this supermarket in whistler really caught my attention, so i decided to visit their downtown location a few times after returning to vancouver. i enjoy shopping for groceries, pastries, and food from their hot bar. the produce and seafood always look fresh and appealing. one standout item was the brussels sprouts from the hot bar—they were delicious! slightly charred, with a hint of sweetness and the perfect texture. however, the whole bbq chicken wasn’t to my taste—the seasoning and meat flavor fell short. today, i also tried their café and was pleasantly surprised. the décor is bright, welcoming, and accented with warm wooden touches. the prices are great, and they serve coffee from bean around the world, which i’m familiar with and really enjoy. i ordered the tuna melt sandwich, and it exceeded my expectations. they used marble rye bread instead of regular bread, which was a nice touch. the portion size was generous, and the chipotle mayo added a bold, flavorful kick to the tuna. lastly, i tried the chocolate croissant, which was absolutely delicious. the chocolate filling was rich and indulgent—i highly recommend it if you’re in the downtown area! overall, this place is worth visiting for its fresh groceries, tasty hot bar options, and cozy café offerings.

this temple feels very commercial—almost like a business built around belief. you get what you pay for, quite literally. it’s less about spiritual connection and more about hoping for quick rewards, especially wealth. many people come here with the strong belief that praying and making offerings will help them get rich. you’ll see lots of people buying amulets and charms, hoping they’ll bring money, luck, and success. it’s fascinating how belief can be such a powerful motivator—when people believe something strongly enough, they’re willing to spend a lot for even the smallest chance of fortune. but at the same time, it makes you wonder: is belief enough? or are we just buying hope? personally, i believe that success still comes from effort, discipline, and hard work. praying might bring peace of mind or motivation, but if you’re relying only on luck or blessings without action, it’s not likely to take you far. so while this place might be interesting to visit for its atmosphere and rituals, i’d recommend putting more faith in your own abilities—and using belief as inspiration, not a shortcut.

this temple has some great paintings - well preserved. what was interesting to see was that there seemed to be two layers of paintings from different times - and some script as well. detailed paintings of stories with boats and people - we didn’t have a tour guide so not sure of the story behind it - would recommend going with one for the full experience.

this temple houses the ashes of thailand’s first king rama. the boat ride along the river to the temple is enjoyable. you can feed the big catfish with bread sold on the boat for just 20 baht. there isn’t a whole lot to see, and it’s not the most visually stunning temple, but it becomes the perfect photo spot if you rent traditional thai clothing, make up and take pictures around the grounds. it’ll make for a unique and memorable souvenir. if you visit, make sure to rent the thai traditional outfit and take photos on-site. otherwise, it’s just an average photo spot. there’s also a small market nearby selling souvenirs, drinks, snacks, and ice cream, and they accept foreign currencies in addition to thai baht.

this temple is a great spot for tourists—not just for its religious value, but also for its beautiful architecture. i really love how it’s located near the hills or mountains. when i parked my scooter at the temple and looked back, i saw the mountain just behind it—it was such a stunning view. the air there is very fresh, and the area is spacious. you can feed the fish in the pond, which is full of life, and there are also many birds around. i enjoyed playing with the birds—they’re very friendly and make for beautiful videos. i was actually surprised to see so many tourists here, but i believe it’s because they also appreciate the stunning architecture and peaceful atmosphere like i do. i think there are around 5 or 6 different temples in this area, each with its own unique style and different buddha images. my favorite was the tallest one—you can walk inside, and it has several floors. if i remember correctly, the first floor is filled with many buddha images. on the second floor, there’s a large white buddha statue. the third floor offers an amazing 360-degree view of the surrounding area. and on the top floor, there’s something very special—i’m not sure what it’s called, but it seems to be a relic, possibly a tooth of the buddha. it’s interesting to watch people, especially thai visitors, insert coins or bills as they make wishes or prayers for good luck.

this temple is beautiful, you can see more of it within 15 minutes but has a largish lake outside and has a toilet out back. tickets were 30.000 each and you can get there using the grab app, but asking the driver to stay is a wise idea because getting back can be difficult. overall it's very peaceful and worth adding to your list when traveling too hanoi.

this temple is considered one of the largest in thailand. i had the opportunity to visit it with my local friend (micky), and the tranquility inside was truly remarkable. i also had the chance to listen to the monks’ meditation at 7 pm, an experience that lasted for an hour and was deeply soothing.

this temple is in siem reap and worth a walk or a tuk tuk to. you walk thru the main gate and go around the pagoda building to the back. when we were there several local people were placing alters and praying. of course we respected their privacy and waited for them to finish before approaching the temple. the area is flat you walk around everywhere and do not go in so there are no stairs. while there we were approached by an english teacher at who teaches at the orphanage (100 children live there) and we gave a donation. please donate if you can, every little bit helps.

this tour was absolutely magical from start to finish! watching the sunset while cruising was a stunning experience, with beautiful views that made for amazing photos. the atmosphere was relaxed and enjoyable, and the guides were friendly and knowledgeable. just when we thought the evening couldn’t get any better, the fireworks show began—an unforgettable finale that added a perfect touch of excitement and wonder. the reflections on the water made it even more mesmerizing. if you’re looking for a unique and memorable experience, i highly recommend this tour. book with zach. it’s the perfect mix of relaxation and excitement, and the fireworks at the end make it truly special!

this tour was amazing! our tour guide, tyler, was awesome and very knowledgeable. even though it was snowing a little and over cast, tyler made the trip great! he pointed out all the wildlife as we drove by. he also stopped for picture opportunities. i highly recommend this trip with tyler.

this tour was amazing!! we were picked up right on time at 2:15am, driven to the mt. batur area, and led on a guided hike up the volcano. both our driver and our hiking guide were so great, and while the hike up was a bit challenging, it was absolutely beautiful. the views from the top were stunning, and we were provided with breakfast and hot drinks as we watched the sunrise. after hiking down, the tour went beyond my expectations, as we were taken to a hot springs and a coffee plantation before being dropped back at our hotel. this tour was 100% worth the money we paid and ended up being one of our favorite things that we did in bali. would definitely recommend!

this tour was an absolute dream come true! the views were breathtaking and truly unforgettable. our guide, tyler, was incredible, so knowledgeable and passionate about the area. i learned so much history thanks to him, and we were all impressed by the depth of his knowledge. we also really appreciated the cozy blankets provided when the evening got cooler, as well as the many great photo opportunities. this experience is a must-do if you're in the area!

this tour was exceptionally well-organized, with outstanding logistics and seamless communication. the team excelled at keeping us informed about meeting points and scheduling details, ensuring a smooth experience right from the start. the exposure to the uros and taquile communities and their rich culture was truly unforgettable—a perfect match for what we had hoped to discover in puno. the tour provided a meaningful and authentic connection to the local traditions, making our visit all the more special. sammy, our guide, was phenomenal. his depth of knowledge and attentiveness to the group’s needs elevated the experience. we were especially impressed by his bilingual fluency, effortlessly switching between spanish and english to engage everyone. his concise and clear explanations meant we never felt left waiting for the english translation. overall, this tour exceeded our expectations and was exactly the kind of experience we traveled to puno for. we couldn’t recommend it highly enough!

this tour was fantastic! the tour guides were funny, knowledgeable, and a blast to hang out with! we saw two separate pods of spinner dolphins, snorkeled with sea turtles and beautiful fish, slid down the inflatable slide, and enjoyed some hula dancing. bonus: lauren, their photographer, took amazing photos of us, the dolphins, the sea turtles, etc. so i wasn't scrambling to get photos of everything. this was an excursion the whole family enjoyed (including our autistic daughter)!

this tour was one of the best things we did across our entire trip to greece! our guide, maria, was absolutely amazing: extremely knowledgeable, engaging, and fun. we loved getting to visit multiple wineries, learning about their production processes, and, of course, seeing an amazing sunset at santo winery to end the evening. highly recommend!

this tour was one of the highlights of our 2 weeks in alaska. we initially scheduled our flight for our first of three days in denali. the weather didn't cooperate the first two days, but denali air was very flexible and allowed us to reschedule twice. finally on our last day in denali, we were able to get up in the air. it was 1000% worth the wait. our pilot, dan (who was amazing), flew us low over the park landscape to see the beautiful fall colors, glaciers, and even some wildlife from the air. after 10-20 minutes we broke through the low-lying clouds to see denali towering over us. it was one of the most surreal moments in my life. dan flew us right up next to the mountain - so much closer than i was expecting! he even did multiple passes so that people on both sides of the plane had a front row view. so thankful we did this trip as it was the only time we saw the mountain due to low-lying clouds all week. if you are in denali, this is a must-do! **tip** book this trip at the beginning of your stay in denali. if bad weather rolls in, it will give you the best chance to reschedule.

this tour was so magical! i could not recommend it enough! i did the 3d2n tour with captain paul and crew. the crew were so smiley, happy to help and friendly and we got to know each one of them. there was a small group of us so it never felt overcrowded. the food was tasty, the rooms were lovely and the views were just incredible. there isn’t one thing i would change! we were brought to the best snorkel spots with snorkel guide sandro who was able to spot everything. we saw manta rays, sharks and so many fish and beautiful coral. a trip of a lifetime 🤩

this tour was the highlight of our vacation in the faroe islands. this farm is set in the beautiful village of selatrað, which is about 30 minutes outside of torshavn. our hosts were gracious and highly knowledgeable. we started the tour inside the barn where the rams live, and i also had the opportunity to "hug" a four day old lamb. we then took a scenic tractor ride to where the ewes and lambs are fed, and also got to feed some of the sheep. our tour concluded in the home of our hosts, who prepared a delicious faroese meal for us. we learned a lot from them about sheep farming and the faroese way of life. this tour enhanced everything else we experienced while we were in the faroes: it helped us to not only appreciate a very beautiful country, but to also appreciate the unique culture and hardworking people who make the faroes a very special place. we will always remember this visit very fondly, and hope to return to the faroes someday!

this tour was the least informative distillery i’ve ever been to. it started off with an amateur film that had very little historical detail. the tour was vague. the guide spent more time doing pop translations than anything else. the longest time we spent was on the model train set—why? no idea. there were no tastings mid tour to show the flavour change through the process. i’ve been to 60 countries and seen many tours—this was the worst one i’ve ever been on.
this tower is on the more slower area of the city and is a wonderful experience at night. there are many cafes and high end restaurants close by. worth your time.

this track starts at the carpark near the fernhill roundabout and ends at sunshine bay beach, about a 1.5 hour return if you don’t stop and enjoy the beach (pretty hard not to). the walk is almost like a mini abel tasman experience, as it stretches along the lake. rumour has it that the more adventurous hikers have seen an 8-foot waterfall along this track, which has eluded even doc staff. we asked a local, and she brought us to an innocuous point that will lead us to the waterfall (i uploaded a photo of this point. it’s about 10-15 min in from one mile carpark, on the left before you go up to the highest point of the track) - you can barely see the path as it literally goes through the tall grass and bushes. i tried to explore it with an acquaintance i met there - we got to a point where we had to sit and scramble down a steep slope. i gave up and turned back at this point, but she continued. i never found out if she found the waterfall. this path is very overgrown and there are sharp branches so please cover up your limbs before you go in. honestly though i don’t think it’s worth the effort, there are much bigger waterfalls in mount aspiring national park you can see just by driving in.

this trail (we did the medium level trail) is one of the best trails in the national park. we did especially like that it is a path through rainforests with many plants to see. it does go rather steep down on some points, so appropriate shoes are definitely recommended. this also the way back can be exhausting, especially during the hot and humid weather. this, also make sure to bring enough water and mosquito spray. the view at the end is amazing and one of the most wonderful places in mauritius. to enter the trail, start by turning left (coming from the parking space) before entering the bridge to the viewpoint (see photos). there's also plenty of parking available, as it's the viewpoint parking space.

this trail goes uphill—it's definitely not an easy walk. once you find the starting point though, it's well marked throughout. great views from the top, and you'll save money by skipping the cable car.

this trail is a fantastic adventure for hikers of all ages. it lifts you out of the valley and delivers jaw-dropping views that make every step worth it. as you near the top, brace yourself—the last 400 meters are a bit of a scramble, but the payoff is incredible. heads-up: it can get pretty windy at the summit, so don’t forget a windbreaker or a cozy layer. you’ll want to hang out and soak in the scenery for a while. time? depends who you ask. the posted hiking time is 4–5 hours, but let’s be real: i made it to the top (with photo stops, two water breaks, and a lightning-fast lunch) in under 2 hours—though i’ll admit, i was dragged up. so yes, the timing could use a bit of an update depending on your pace.

this trail is a must if you’re up for a hiking challenge when visiting the island of oahu! it took our group 42 minutes to reach the summit, which is not that fast as locals can do it under 30 minutes. i’d recommend doing the hike in the morning or late afternoon as it gets warm. i don’t recommend this hike without proper footwear and clothing, as it’s not recommended to hike in flip flops and nice clothing.

this trail is awesome and not for beginners. kids don’t belong on this trail and dogs don’t belong on it either. we started at 5:30am and made it back down at 10am. it’s 5 miles, treacherous, extremely steep, and you’re climbing most of the time as well as walking along the edge of the cliffs. if you think you’re done climbing, you aren’t. if you think you might be at the top, you’re not. if you think the flat area lasts, it doesn’t. this was a really awesome hike.. beautiful. but be safe and make sure you’re wearing hiking boots and have enough water.

this trail is more moderate for any experienced hiker... but if you are not that active and or have any pre-existing conditions that make it difficult for you to walk on a steep incline with slippery rocks and mud do not take this hike to avoid injury on your vacation. it will take about 2 hours round trip and be very muddy at the top and will ruin your shoes. this is more of a trail for working out as opposed to a tourist trail. while out there were many people were in flip flops/tennis shoes not prepared for the mud and rocks. and also has no water 😬 there's not many views during the hike but at the end is a nice look out point that's breezy and cool! note this will not take you to the top of the falls!

this trail is one of the easiest in this area, but don't let this fool you. it is therefore not an easy trail. there are actually a lot of steps before you get to the elevated part that offers the best views. it took the whole morning to be here and do it at our own pace before getting back to the car. we arrived very early before sunrise to make sure we had a parking spot, and there were many already taken. bring enough water for sure! the views are gorgeous, so definitely worth it.

this trail is strenuous, but extremely well kept. the sights along the way are second to none. it is not recommended for someone other than an experienced hiker to attempt doing the trail to the river and back, as per the warning sign. be prepared, but do not fear. it's doable and so so worth it.

this trail is the best for me because i am kind of beginner. so lovely and short enough to little kid too. there are many of dogs and neighbors. in winter time we can make snowman and anywhere! enjoy this could be extended to ubc

this trail is very easy to walk as it is pretty much flat with beautiful waterfalls and nice scenery , only inside the tunnels is a bit narrow and can be crowded with the people coming from the other direction , we did it with the phones but having a flash light or head light to is recommended. also wear waterproof jackets as it gets very wet in the tunnels and under the waterfalls.

this trail offers an exceptionally accessible hiking experience, with convenient parking readily available. the path to the trailhead and the trail itself are suitable for strollers and wheelchairs. the waterfall at the end of the trail, near the initial bridge, presents a stunning visual spectacle. while it is possible to climb closer to the waterfall for a more intimate view, it is recommended to do so at your own risk. we observed some individuals attempting to scale the mountain near the waterfall, which is not advisable. the area beneath the bridge provides a safe and enjoyable opportunity for children to engage in water play. the trail loops back towards the restrooms near the trailhead after crossing the bridge. this trail is easily manageable with two children and a stroller, and is considered one of the most accessible trails in yosemite.

this trail was absolutely beautiful, offering stunning scenery throughout and ending with a peaceful, relaxing beach. a truly enjoyable experience!

this trail was described as moderate by a local here. i would say this trail was difficult. the roots of the trees are exposed, there's boulders, loose rocks, steep uneven stairs, among other hard spots of this trail. it's nice thst it's shady in some parts though. this was a very challenging but very rewarding hike. the view at the top is unmatched. make sure you bring lots of water and good hiking boots.

this trail was fantastic. variety of greenery, roosters along the route and the reward of this beautiful gift of nature (the waterfall) in mid way of the trail. i put moderate but some people might find it hard. lots of inclines, loose rocks, roots on path. i took it slow ( it added about an hour to my hike) it was worth it. sanquinho the name of the hike, after the falls on the way back we visited the town that has been abandoned but slowly being revived. we were greeted by lovely cats, had a drink and enjoyed the scenery before heading back on a beautiful steep winding cobblestone path to end the trail
