this was my most favorite place in our entire cr trip. just $10 each to get into some amazing hikes. we did the full route all around the park. there were times i felt like we were deep in the amazon rainforest. at the top you come out into some open fields. we saw some wildlife like moneys. also ran into some friendly cows. it was a cloudy day so we didn’t get a good view of the volcano, but it was still 100% worth the trip. it was quite a hike and did take some effort.
this was my preference for temples. still busy but not as commercial as che kung temple. it is small and gets a little smoky. but still a very nice temple to visit.

this was my second cruise to tubbataha with the zamerdius team, and once again, the experience was exceptional. i loved my first trip, and this new adventure only confirmed my deep attachment to this crew. the guides are passionate, highly skilled, and their knowledge of the site is truly impressive. what truly makes the stay unique is the family spirit on board — you feel at ease, welcomed, and surrounded. it’s a human and marine experience i wholeheartedly recommend. tubbataha reef is a place of breathtaking beauty, with its towering, vertigo-inducing drop-offs and endless gardens of hard and soft corals. the marine biodiversity is incredibly rich. each dive is a discovery, a moment of awe — a true hymn to contemplation. an unforgettable experience that i recommend without hesitation. thank you to the whole team. i’ll be back next season!

this was my second time here after my first visit 6 years ago. it was annoying to get in as cars were filed in a long line, even people who had reservations. but the laguna was just as nice as i remembered. as someone who isn’t a strong swimmer, it was fun to float around

this was my second time staying at the enchantment resort and both times have been such a beautiful stay. this time we celebrated our wedding anniversary and all the staff at the resort were so, so kind and attentive. all of our encounters with the staff were great. i love coming back to this place because of its location. every day you wake up and look around at the beauty of the red rocks. the hotel rooms are nicely decorated, clean, and has all the things we would need. all the meals were delicious at the resort restaurants. the pool is slightly heated so it is a welcome relief after a full day of hiking. the spa is wonderful and everyone really goes out of their way to make sure you are enjoying your stay. i can’t wait to come back here.

this was my second time visiting centre pompidou - the first was three years ago, when everything was still open, and now for the wolfgang tillmans exhibit. i had a great time! the place is definitely worth visiting if you have any interest in art. i can’t wait for it to fully reopen so i can enjoy the views from the upper levels again.

this was my second trip to musandam, sulthanate of oman with family.. this time i was totally disappointed as the boat was fully packed.. there were more than 100 people in the boat.. by gods grace the boat didn’t sink.. a very very long queue everywhere.. for better experience i will suggest not to go there in peak time and if you are travelling in november - february better go for lesser crowded boats.. i was unaware as i had a great experience last year.. also better avoid smart travel because they are not professionals.. poor behaviour from the staffs.. food was not sufficient as i had to hunt for a chicken piece in the curry.. a horrible experience with smart travels ( boat of suhail ) .

this was my wife’s first introduction to surfing, and i couldn’t have asked for a better experience. nicki had us up and shredding in no time! i’m so grateful for this class. it really put us on the fast track to progress quickly and comfortably on what i’m sure will be a fruitful lifelong surfing journey.

this was not a good experience. it felt very odd and displaced. front desk experience is off and aura photo was overpriced and not how others typically look. just go down the street or somewhere else unfortunately i lost $55. the aura photo person is also a psyhic tarot reader.... and everything else so this should be factored in. but did not seem to pick up anything off my energy the reading was text book. nty.

this was not what i expected at all. it was about 100m from our camp in the middle of light pollution. to be fair they were enthusiastic and did show interesting things in the telescope. however the photography time at the end was basically just a group photo we were forced to be in. immediately after that spot lights went on and we were rushed home. if you want to go somewhere to take photos in a dark sky this is not for you!

this was one of favorite things about costa rica. i thought it would be more crowded but we almost always had an area/pool all to ourselves. the resort is very clean and beautifully maintained. the restaurant was wonderful and everyone was very nice. we can’t wait to come back again.
this was one of my favorite parts of schönbrunn!! we used the vienna city pass to get in. beautiful plants inside!!

this was one of my favorite things to do in amsterdam. they do an amazing job telling the story and showing you what they went through. i also appreciated they provided free audio tours. we were there for about an hour and felt that was a great amount of time.

this was one of my stops while being on oahu for the first time ever, my boyfriend and i did the splatter room and it was so. fun. the entire place is covered in really cool art and it is such a vibe! the staff were so cool and so nice, we will definitely be going back because of how fun this experience was!!!

this was one of our favorite spots during our trip. we ventured out there twice taking different trails each way and exploring all around! my husband and i even danced in the bamboo forest to our favorite song it was magical. the falls were gorgeous but slippery so be very careful. we wore hiking shoes and clothes over our swimsuits the first time the next time we went we wore water shoes and just our swimsuits and brought water. the less you bring the better! we had no trouble finding a parking spots when we went but there is limited parking.

this was one of the best experiences i have had to see the grand canyon. the views are very stunning and our pilot sarah added much appreciated points of commentary to go along with the audio recording on the headphones. she was very professional, friendly, and knowledgeable. i would highly recommend this tour for anyone wishing to see the grand canyon.

this was one of the best experiences in my life! we contacted them in the morning and arranged 1 hour camel ride with sunset for 20 rial per person. they met us at this location at 4 pm and took us 20 minutes by car into the desert. from there, we rode the camels for more than half an hour to the top of the dunes to watch the sunset. and then we rode them back. it was amazing! totally recommend.

this was one of the best experiences i’ve had. we saw so many animals and we got to get so close! the animals would walk right by and totally ignore the vehicle. our guide was knowledgeable and had answers to all of our questions. the place is so big. they have trackers on some of the animals so you will see all of them. they don’t interfere with animals and they are great with the conservation. definitely worth paying for. the rooms are so big and nice. there is a pool and spa. drives are about 3 hours long. the workers are all so nice and care about your stay. all of the food is included and believe me you will never go hungry, the food is amazing. there are different lodges including a family lodge so you won’t have kids on your drives. defiantly would tell everyone to go there, it’s amazing!
this was one of the best experiences me and my family have ever been a part of, my son chose to do this for his 21st birthday and honestly it was awesome. thank you to matt and his team.

this was one of the best experiences we had in bali! driving over the lava rocks with stunning views and ending the day with a beautiful sunset on mount batur was unforgettable. our driver, arman, was fantastic – friendly, knowledgeable, and made us feel completely safe and relaxed. highly recommend this tour, especially with arman as your guide!

this was one of the best hotel and travel experiences we’ve had!! from the beautiful lake, the amazing amenities (hot tub, gorgeous room view, massage, woodfire stove etc) to the delightful team that was caring kind and thoughtful, as well as the delicious meals, we loved everything about our stay. the daytime offerings were great - we went birdwatching, learned about the lake and boated across visiting tequile island, and also spent time taking in archeological sites including the portal at amaru mara. thank you, thank you for a wonderful stay!!!

this was one of the best hotel and travel experiences we’ve had!! from the beautiful lake, the amazing amenities (hot tub, gorgeous room view, massage, woodfire stove etc) to the delightful team that was caring kind and thoughtful, as well as the delicious meals, we loved everything about our stay. the daytime offerings were great - we went birdwatching, learned about the lake and boated across visiting tequile island, and also spent time taking in archeological sites including the portal at amaru mara. thank you, thank you for a wonderful stay!!!

this was one of the best museums that my kids loved would not compare it with madame tussaud but it was great for the kids would love to take them back and the games were ok as well but quality of the figures are not super good

this was one of the best parts of our family trip! out of all the places we wanted to use for our jet ski rental, this was the only one that allowed my 7-year-old to participate. safety was clearly their top priority. while we were there, we saw maybe two or three people fall off or flip their jet skis, and the response time from the staff was immediate, they were on it within seconds! we purchased two 30-minute freestyle rentals along with the photo and video package, since we wouldn’t be able to film ourselves during the ride. it was the best decision we made! although they initially forgot to capture our photos and video, once we informed them when we returned, they immediately sent us back out to complete the service. incredible customer service and an awesome correction! thank you, archie jet ski! we’ll definitely be back again!

this was one of the best tours that i have ever been on. the tour showed history of puerto rico as well as current culture. it showed not only the cities, but also took us to the mountains. it took us to a local owned restaurant and a local owned coffee shop where we were treated like royalty and the food and beverage were not only authentic puerto rican, but contained a large variety. there was no time constraint on any portion of the tour. if a passenger wanted to stop and see something or take pictures, the tour guide was very willing to stop. this tour was well beyond our expectations. the tour guide, jerry, was excellent and beyond with an awesome personality.

this was one of the first places we visited on our tour of jeju island. on this tour i was the only american tourist in the group. this performance was absolutely amazing. energetic, intense, acrobatic, musical and funny with audience participation. the entire show is in the korean language, so be prepared. i enjoyed it immensely. cost $20. one thing, the seating is is very steep, arena style seats. not for the faint of heart.

this was one of the highlights of our trip to paris. the private river cruise was fantastic. we did a sunset river cruise and it is magical to see the paris landmarks lit up at night along the river. i highly recommend green river cruises. it’s worth the money to do your own private cruise instead of getting on a boat with 200 other people.

this was one of the highlights of our trip! the entire experience was so organic, from the friendly dogs greeting us at the ranch, the ride and trail itself, and the owners teaching and conversation! our group of 4 (myself, my husband, and another couple) had one beginner, one expert who owns a horse, and two people with some experience riding. all four of us had a blast and improved our skills. the horses are all clearly well-trained and easy to ride. you will ride through a large valley including up and down slopes and forest, through a creek, past cattle, and up to a great lookout of the valley. charlotte, our guide, was so knowledgeable and friendly and helped us improve our riding skills while making sure we felt comfortable and safe. it was the most supportive, encouraging environment. we especially loved all of the beautiful photo opportunities! it was a wonderful half-day ride with a small private group through the beautiful patagonian countryside. one of the most freeing and genuine experiences of our whole trip! cannot recommend enough

this was one of the highlights of our trip! we were early in the season, and oda was great communicating about potential weather issues. thankfully, we didn't have to adjust or cancel our plan, but it was nice to know she was paying attention ahead of time and was ready to reschedule if necessary. oda met us at the ferry dock on mykines, and we hiked up to see the puffins and gannets. oda is very knowledgeable about the island and it's history, and excited to share. we stayed overnight, and got to enjoy a delicious dinner and breakfast. we would highly recommend using golocal for your mykines adventures, and we would absolutely book with her again in the future!

this was one of the highlights of our trip. we did the jazz dinner cruise on a saturday evening. the cruise set out at about sunset for greenwich and came back into london to see the beautiful night skyline. the entertainment was top-notch and the food was better than we had at other places around london. overall, a great experience, if a bit pricey, but well worth.

this was one of the most exhilarating adventures i (we've) ever experienced. viewing the canyon from the edges by foot is amazing enough, but doesn't even compare to the experience you get from above. we highly recommend this experience to anyone going to the grand canyon. the only recommendation would be to make the ride just a bit longer. seemed it took a long time to get to the canyon and a long time coming back. the 25-30 timeframe should start when you actually reach the edge of the canyon. but, still well worth it. oh, and the staff were very friendly, accommodating, and professional. travelers from delaware

this was one of the most exhilarating trips i’ve been on. we chose the mild trails but also got to do some of the bumpy roads but nothing “crazy” we bounced around a bit ,it was awesome. we got to see all the cool rock formations even got out to look at the gorgeous views and our tour guide eric even took plenty of photos. eric was a fun and interactive guide that knew what he was taking about and really helped us make our experience even more memorable. thank you for the amazing trip.

this was one of the most memorable and meaningful memorials we have ever visited. our pearl harbor national memorial experience was humbling to say the least. the entire staff did a great job helping the visitors and providing so much information & history, very professional and knowledgeable. the entire memorial park is very well maintained, clean and well organized. we visited during a flight layover and only had a few hours to explore, but i could have spent the whole day. i definitely suggest giving yourself plenty of time to check it out. hard to believe that oil still leaks from the hull of the ships 84 years later! we learned more than we ever knew about the attack, there are prenty of postings, videos and artifacts throughout the memorial. much respect and prayers to all of the brave souls we lost during the pearl harbor attacks, and to all of the brave men & women who have paid the ultimate sacrifice throughout history to defend the united states of america! highly recommend the pearl harbor memorial!

this was one of the most, if not the most, special experiences that my wife and i had during our mini-honeymoon trip to banff. i have loved and worked with horses for much of my life and have a special love for draft horses. to dress up in our warm winter clothes, snuggle up and enjoy the spectacular views on a horse-drawn sled was pure magic. the experience is not cheap but we were able to go after being gifted some honeymoon "adventure money" from family and friends. we were pretty choosy about what we did on our holiday and i am so happy that this was one of the things we chose. it was romantic, exciting, beautiful and luxurious. the sun was shining, it wasn't too cold and our guide was a ton of fun. giving local history and facts about the area. all of the staff, from the folks who helped us with the booking, to the driver / guide to the hotel staff were patient, kind and accommodating. well done brewsters! lake louise is not to be missed anyway, but to experience it this way was an incredible gift. if you can, definitely treat yourself to this adventure.

this was one of, if not, the best thing we’ve done on our 3 and a half month travels around south east asia. this 4 day cruise from lombok to komodo island is an amazing experience. filled with activities, great people and great food it is so so worth doing for all ages! also a huge mention to the staff on board who looked after us throughout. alfi was our main guide. genuinely one of the most amazing people i have ever met in my life. this guy is amazing! so kind and so helpful. just book this cruise you will not regret it! thank you so much alfi my brother ❤️

this was our 3rd safari collection property we visited and just like the others we were warmly greeted by staff on arrival. salas gives a more “camp” feel with tents that are beautifully done. the managers eric and caroline are extremely pleasant and are always around for any concerns you may have or just to see how your day is going . our game drives with masic and david were spectacular, who really go out of there way to take care of you while you’re with them. redempta is the sweetest young lady who is always ready to serve you any drink of your choice. james was awesome as well. again, this property gave more of a “camp/community ” feel. in the evening guests and managers sitting outdoor by the campfire also during dinner on the last night . i was a little concerned about dealing with heat since none of the safari collection properties have air conditioning but definitely was not a problem. i reserved a relaxing outdoor massage our last day there with paris and it was simply the best! definitely recommend if you have the time .

this was our favorite activity in siem reap. the visit to the market is authentic and informative. we learn we so much and were inspired by sophos story. everyone we interacted with was friendly and welcoming. the food we prepared was delicious. they will send a tuktuk to pick you up. we would love to do it again!

this was our favorite camps during our trip to botswana. kane and modd were the best driver and tracker duo, we had such a wonderful time with them. the staff was so friendly and took time to get to know us and make us feel welcome. the food was delicious as well and the rooms and views were fantastic! highly recommend!

this was our favorite expedition in patagonia! if you love nature or animals this is the best experience you can book! lynn will guide you and teach you into such a beautiful day where you will genuinely connect with your horse and learn about yourself. the views are indescribable, lynn’s knowledge of the area is so vast, and the “box lunch” is delicious. we loved learning about the local flora and fauna and geological formations while we rode. lynn deepened our understanding and appreciation of patagonia at large! lynn is the best guide, she will help you connect with your horse, teach you how to trot and canter all while ensuring you feel safe. we learned so much about horses as well as ourselves. this experience refreshed our souls!
this was our favourite water feature in the garden. the beautiful reflections and the really lovely wooden bridges really provide the most outstanding setting.

this was our first cooking class as a family, and it was such a special experience! we’ve traveled to many places but never tried a cooking class until now. my husband booked this class a few months ago, and we feel truly blessed to have been taught by chef maria. she’s an incredibly confident and knowledgeable chef who knows exactly how to include everyone and make the experience enjoyable. her teaching style helped our kids feel confident and excited about cooking. the space was spotless, warm, and very welcoming. chef maria’s co-chef, sophia, was also amazing—kind, generous, and extremely helpful. our daughter hasn’t stopped talking about how supportive sophia was during the class. as vegetarians, we were especially grateful for the thoughtful accommodations made for us. we felt completely comfortable and included in every part of the meal preparation. on top of learning delicious recipes, we also got to learn about the rich history of cartagena and chef maria’s own story. this was one of our favorite activities, and we highly recommend it for couples or families looking for a meaningful and fun experiences.

this was our first time here, and we absolutely loved it. the music was pleasant, the seating was comfortable, and the staff were friendly. the hookah was top-quality, one of the best we’ve had in miami. our waiter melcy was incredibly attentive and made sure we had everything we needed. and the oreo milkshakes were so good! definitely coming back!

this was our first time in zanzibar and our first time snorkeling and the first time on the sunset cruise and teacher was extremely helpful and supportive throughout the whole experience. even if you are not a strong swimmer, he made sure to keep everyone safe.we really appreciate it and hopefully we will return sometime to come to him again. we absolutely loved it

this was our first time visiting the museum and our 5-year-old absolutely loved all the activities—his favorites were the pretend play kitchen and water play. they have a beautiful outdoor space where parents can relax while the kids play. he didn’t want to leave and is already asking to come back! this place was a highlight of our nola trip. you can easily spend a whole day here—explore the museum, take a stroll through the nearby sculpture garden, stop by cafe du monde and soak in the beauty of the oak trees.

this was our most expensive hotel on our stay to chile and we felt disappointed with the experience. the highlight is by far the location and views, it really is incredible. however, this is not a luxury hotel. £60 to use the jacuzzi for 90 minutes, a big sign by the coffee machine saying you can only use it at breakfast, no bottled water or kettle or coffee in the room. we felt like we were under supervision and we were not made to feel welcome. this hotel has the potential to be great but they need to put their feet in the paying customers shoes.

this was our most wow moment in mauritius, and that's saying something! guides are available, but we decided not to use one based on the amount of information available online. follow google maps to the hiking trailhead point, and you can park there near the temple - ignore the guys a kilometer before that at the bus station who will tell you you're at the falls. as you walk down the side of the sugar cane field, you can pop into the left to see the first waterfall, but the second one is where the real wow factor begins. follow the dirt road from the main road, and where it begins to turn to the right you go straight onto the trail there, and then follow it down to the left to reach the top of the waterfall, and be blown away by it! to continue, you cross the river and into the forest again, the trail will bring you down behind that waterfall, and from there it's easy enough to follow the trail down past waterfalls 3, 4, 5 and 6. from there you can climb back uphill and you'll emerge onto the dirt road again, and follow that back to the car. we did this with a 7, 9 and 11 year old, and while challenging, is not terribly difficult. it is absolutely worth doing and will be a highlight of any trip to mauritius

this was our second time booking with riviera charters, and they continue to blow us away! from start to finish, the crew goes above and beyond to make sure we’re having the best time possible. they anticipate everything we could need — the food is plentiful and absolutely delicious, and they never let our glasses go empty. the atmosphere is relaxed, fun, and so well taken care of that all we have to do is sit back and enjoy. if you’re looking for a charter experience where you feel pampered, fed, and constantly smiling, riviera charters is it! can’t wait for next year!

this was our second time visiting, and it was just as captivating as the first. the experience is beautifully done—visually stunning and emotionally engaging. it really helps you understand who van gogh was, what inspired him, and how his unique style evolved. a great mix of art, storytelling, and atmosphere. definitely worth visiting, even more than once!

this was our second trip to namibia and really exceeded the expectations. a perfect planning and booking by wilmari, together with the brefing done before starting the engine of a great toyota, made the self-drived discovery of namibia a true but always safe adventure. smiles and kindness of the local people were also a great support in the rare difficult moments. the changing landscapes in the different point visited was a continuous discovery, we really passed through a national geographic documentary

this was our second trip to namibia and really exceeded the expectations. a perfect planning and booking by wilmari, together with the brefing done before starting the engine of a great toyota, made the self-drived discovery of namibia a true but always safe adventure. smiles and kindness of the local people were also a great support in the rare difficult moments. the changing landscapes in the different point visited was a continuous discovery, we really passed through a national geographic documentary

this was our second visit to see this show and it was just as good as the first time. the girl who plays the young girl tina was amazing, i look forward to following her career. the theatre itself is easy to find, well run and very clean. i liked the way that you can order your drinks online and they are ready for you at the intermission. look forward to coming back.

this was our second visit to the 9/11 memorial site. what a beautiful space to remember the heroic way in which americans responded to the attacks on our country and our people. many wonderful people died on that day and days to follow. may we never forget. the freedom tower is a wonderful reminder of our nation's ability to come back stronger and more determined. the two foundation pools signify the depth of our sorrows for those who died in the attack or gave their lives trying to save others. god bless our first responders.

this was our very first visit to kenya, and choosing drunken elephant mara turned out to be the best decision we made! right from the start, their coordination and hospitality were exceptional. as i was traveling with my family, including our 5-year-old daughter, i had many questions around logistics, bookings, and safety. every query was answered promptly and patiently, which gave me great confidence and peace of mind. a big thank you to the amazing staff – especially henry, our courteous and reliable chauffeur, and william, our knowledgeable safari guide and driver, who made our wildlife experience unforgettable. the food was absolutely delicious – every meal was a treat! the location is perfect – just 5 minutes away from the sekenani gate – and the entire property felt completely secure and family-friendly. highly recommended for anyone looking for a smooth, warm, and memorable safari experience in the heart of the masai mara. we can’t wait to return!

this was part of a 4 day tour starting in tupiza and finishing in uyuni with the salt flat as the grand finale. amazing landscapes of the altiplano with it’s lagoons with flamingos and multicoloured snow capped volcanoes. a trip of a lifetime. only bad point is that the tours all seem to arrive at the stop off points at the same time so the experience is somewhat diluted.

this was part of a 4 day tour starting in tupiza and finishing in uyuni with the salt flat as the grand finale. amazing landscapes of the altiplano with it’s lagoons with flamingos and multicoloured snow capped volcanoes. a trip of a lifetime. only bad point is that the tours all seem to arrive at the stop off points at the same time so the experience is somewhat diluted.

this was part of our trip to the underground river - it is 300pesos to do the cave walk, which you can then walk back down, or zip line for 250-350 more. we chose to walk back down. overall it was fine - interesting enough but our guide didn't really explain much and it felt quite rushed to just get to the top.

this was part of our vacation package. we had a cabin on the river. it was small with very limited outlets to access. but we anticipated that with being so remote. it was clean and shower was hot, but it is a studio pretty much. food prices were extremely high. mediocre breakfast buffet that was lukewarm food was $30 per adult. we understand its remote and food costs are going to be more, but that seemed excessive and kept us from really eating there again. service in restaurant was good. overall, not a bad place for remote denali. very quiet and peaceful for as many guests that were there.

this was part of the dubrovnik pass and we were passing by so thought we'd take a look in, but i'm sad to say it's a total waste of time. i'm sure it's very worthy and that he's an important figure in dubrovnik's cultural history but if you want visitors to engage with his story then you really need to freshen up the exhibition and make it more interactive/interesting. there's plenty of reading on each floor, but it's pretty overwhelming.

this was probably the highlight of our trip to hawaii!! it was so much fun! the crew was awesome and had so much fun!! ryan did an amazing hula dance. we got to see so many turtles, fish and eels, and dolphins and got some amazing views and awesome ride on the boat!!

this was so fun! my husband and i did the 4 hour tour and got to see manatees, a crab, so many birds, and an iguana. the 40 min float in the mayan canal was so beautiful and so relaxing - highly recommend!!

this was so fun! way more activities than i expected! it just kept going and going and my kids loved all of it we spent three hours left for lunch and came back for three more hours and could’ve stayed longer. definitely fun way to escape the heat. all ages from 6-adult

this was such a memorable trip, all thanks to the wonderful wisesa crew! my husband and i did the 11 night raja ampat cruise, which gave ample time to relax, explore, and snorkel as much as we wanted. the ship was comfortable and quite beautiful, i enjoyed spending time reading and napping on the shaded "sun deck" up top, or having a cup of coffee in the common area. the food was excellent and abundant, and i loved getting to try indonesian dishes and seafood local to the area. dylan was our cruise director, who was easy-going but also on top of all of the details, and went above and beyond to make sure we had what we needed and were enjoying ourselves (including the truly endless amount of coffee our group could drink!). there was a mix of opportunities to socialize (including a very fun new years' eve with fireworks and dancing) and have down time, and dylan followed the group's lead on striking a good balance of activities. yorenzo was an excellent snorkeling guide from raja ampat, who was patient, knowledgeable, and had a super-keen eye for wildlife. dylan described his eyes as "bionic", and we agree! we saw a ton of incredible wildlife--birds of paradise, manta rays on christmas, turtles, wobegong, cuttlefish and squid, sharks, endless fish and corals. my husband was a novice snorkeler and had a great time, and the group had a range of newer to seasoned snorkelers and dylan did well to accommodate everyone. some snorkels had stronger currents, though these were navigated expertly by the guides--that said, being a decently strong swimmer definitely helped. the whole rest of the crew was helpful and friendly; udo, ketut, and mawan especially stood out, i loved chatting with them and they even helped me practice my indonesian :) we had a great time and would recommend this trip to anyone who wants to spend a week or two in beautiful scenery with world-class snorkeling!

this was the site of the prison of ancient athens. the prison was built in the 5th century bc and is located southwest of the ancient agora, near both the court of helia and the areopagus hill. it is a building 40 meters long and 17 meters wide, which had 12 rooms. it also had an entrance on the north side that was guarded and led to the piraeus gate. the prison was used to accommodate prisoners but also to carry out the death penalty, as in the case of socrates, in 399 bc. some rooms were certainly cells, but there is evidence that there was also a room in the area that served as a bath. during excavations, water storage vessels, such as a jar and a basin, have been found. thirteen bottles used to store the cone were also found and are exhibited in the museum of the ancient agora, as well as a statuette from the 4th century bc depicting socrates himself. the philosopher, who was convicted of disrespect for the gods, spent a period of approximately 30 days in the desotorium until his execution. during this time, he refused proposals from his friends, who suggested that he escape. part of the building's foundations survives today.

those walls talked poetry to me and this is what they said... in the cradle of cambodia’s timeless plains, banteay samre rises, where stillness reigns. a sentinel of sandstone, weathered but proud, its whispers of history pierce through the crowd. here, the sun's golden kiss graces every wall, carving shadows of kings who once heard its call. intricate carvings, a tapestry of lore, tell stories of valor, of gods, and of war. the lotus blooms on lintels finely wrought, echoing a time when divinity was sought. every archway and corridor, a sacred hymn, a dance of light and shadow, ancient and grim. amidst its ruins, tranquility sings, a temple of men but a home for kings. less trodden by crowds, its secrets remain, a haven of silence, untouched by disdain. banteay samre, a jewel in angkor’s crown, a place where eternity quietly bows down. to walk through your halls is to touch the divine, a sacred communion of mortal and time.

tickets are $10, only credit cards are accepted, no cash! opening hours: sunday-thursday 10:00-16:00 not open for visits on friday and saturday! the museum was originally divided into two parts: the old hall and the new hall. the old hall is currently closed, and all exhibits are on display in the new hall. but it is still necessary to introduce the history of the old hall: the old hall is located in sultan park in the city center, and was originally part of the maldives palace in the 17th century. it was first opened on november 11, 1952 (national day) and was founded by prime minister mohamed amin didi to preserve history and inspire the patriotism of the people. the new hall was donated by china in 2010 and officially opened on independence day. currently, only two floors are open for visits: the lower floor (ground floor): focuses on the early history of buddhism to islam, exhibiting buddha statues, stone carved wood boards, weapons, daily utensils, etc. upper floor: modern treasures on display: court supplies (throne, top hat), the country's first phonograph, telephone, mainframe, president nasheed's "underwater cabinet" meeting minutes, 6-meter-long whale bone exhibition, etc. 🎬2025.7.17

tierra atacama is an unforgettable experience in the desert. we’ve been lucky enough to travel to 53 countries, and tierra atacama ranks among the very best places we’ve ever stayed. from the moment we arrived, the staff went above and beyond. christian was incredible—he made sure every detail was perfect and was always there to help with a smile. paula, our tour guide, was a true gem—knowledgeable, thoughtful, and clearly passionate about the atacama. we felt completely cared for during each daily excursion. and a big thank you to esteban, our driver, for getting us everywhere safely and comfortably. the food? honestly, it exceeded even our high expectations. every meal was beautifully prepared, and the service was warm and professional. bbq night was a standout—amazing meats, fresh salads, and even pizza. special thanks to ignacio, aledia, carol, royer, benjamin, and carolina at the bar—you all made each meal feel like a celebration. our room was fantastic. spacious, beautifully renovated, and incredibly comfortable. the outdoor shower and private pool were just the cherry on top. housekeeping came by twice a day and made sure we always had everything we needed. the spa was another highlight. with a long list of treatments and such a welcoming team, we ended up booking treatments three days in a row—and would’ve done more if we had the time. if you’re headed to the atacama, tierra atacama should be your first choice. it’s not just a hotel—it’s an experience. hats off to the entire team for making our time here truly unforgettable.

tijuca national park is a breathtaking escape in the heart of rio de janeiro and stands as one of the world’s largest urban rainforests. visiting here is pure magic—expect to be wowed by dense canopies, hidden waterfalls, birdsong, and panoramic vistas of the city below. my visit was an unforgettable blend of adventure, tranquility, and discovery. highlights and experience from the very start at the park gates, you’re welcomed by the sounds and sights of the atlantic forest: the rustle of leaves, the chattering of capuchin monkeys, and the misty spray of waterfalls like taunay. don’t miss iconic landmarks such as the chinese pavilion, mayrink chapel, and, higher up, views from pico da tijuca—the park’s highest peak. for thrill-seekers, activities range from hiking and mountain biking to rapelling and guided eco-tours. picnic spots and scenic lookouts make this an excellent day for families, nature-lovers, or photographers seeking unique wildlife shots. the park is steeped in conservation history, from 1800s coffee plantations to modern rewilding efforts, which lend a fascinating backdrop to every trail. best time to visit season months conditions & tips dry season may–sept best for hiking, clear views, cooler temperatures, least rainfall spring sept–nov lush blooms, mild weather, quieter trails summer dec–mar dense foliage, long days, some humidity, park is busier rainy season dec–mar (peaks jan–mar) trails may be slippery, waterfalls fuller, flash floods possible early morning arrivals are recommended for cooler temperatures, active wildlife, and fewer crowds. weekdays are less busy; avoid thursdays, fridays, and sundays if possible for a more peaceful experience. do’s and don’ts do’s wear proper footwear: sturdy hiking shoes are essential—trails can be rugged, and flip-flops are unsafe. pack sun and insect protection: hats, sunscreen, and repellent are musts. bring water and snacks: few shops exist inside the park, so come prepared. respect wildlife: watch, photograph from a distance, never feed or approach animals. use official trails: stay on marked paths to prevent erosion and preserve the forest. start early: enjoy wildlife at their most active and avoid midday heat. check weather before visiting: trails can be dangerous in rain or fog. hire a certified guide: especially useful for new visitors or those seeking in-depth knowledge of flora and fauna. visit the visitor center: for information, trail maps, and park history. don’ts don’t litter: pack out what you bring—it’s a conservation area. don’t make loud noises or play music: it disturbs both wildlife and fellow visitors. do not exit trails or take shortcuts: this can cause damage to sensitive habitats. do not feed or get too close to animals: some may bite, and it disrupts their natural behavior. avoid the park after sunset: there’s no lighting, and getting lost is dangerous. don’t swim in unmarked waters: only use designated areas for waterfall baths for your safety. do not wear camouflage clothing: it can cause misunderstandings with authorities and is discouraged. final thoughts tijuca national park is a rare urban treasure—a living, breathing rainforest with rich biodiversity just minutes from city hustle. whether you’re hiking to summit views, exploring waterfalls, or simply immersing yourself in birdsong and leafy tranquility, this park offers something for everyone. respect the park’s rules and rhythms, and you’ll enjoy a safe, memorable adventure in one of rio’s proudest jewels. highly recommended—don’t miss it!

timeless charm has transformed this walkway into a market for delicious food and dance during the weekends and a romantic and elegant pathway to enjoy day and night, all week-long. paseo de la princesa is a 19th-century promenade that has stretched to become a reflection of the city: a center of commerce and cultural exchange.

tiny but verdant oasis in the village. a little path circumscribes the park, with a dozen little benches. beautiful for sitting on a spring day. no food allowed, though, so you can’t bring snacks or anything. also, the lawn seems to be off limits. but it’s a lovely space to pass an afternoon with a sketchbook or a friend.

tiny rossi garden is one of those special spots in paris where you just can't help but smile. in the afternoons, this cozy little garden turns into a lively dance floor, where people gather to dance and have a great time. it's like stepping into a scene from a movie! the vibe here is incredible—everyone is so friendly, and you can feel the love for dancing in the air. whether you're a seasoned dancer or just enjoy watching, it's impossible not to get caught up in the energy. the music, the laughter, and the rhythm of the dancing feet make it a perfect place to hang out and soak in some real parisian joy. the garden itself is lovely and peaceful, a great spot to relax. but when the dancing starts, it’s pure magic. if you're looking for a unique experience in paris, you’ve got to check out tiny rossi garden. you might even find yourself joining in!

tip for finding it: it’s not the easiest spot to reach, so here’s how we got there. if you’re walking along the top of iva vojnovića, turn onto liechtensteinov put heading towards the rixos hotel. once you reach the hotel, take the small road running along its left side — it looks like a staff access route, but just keep going down. at the bottom, you’ll find two options: take the steps down to the cliffs attached to the hotel, or follow the path to the left. you’ll come across a fixed gate with a warning sign about falling rocks. it looks off-limits, but as long as you’re careful, you can get around it. behind the bushes there’s a hidden staircase leading to the beach. review: we visited several beaches in dubrovnik and this was by far our favourite. the water is crystal clear, and the old, unused dock area turned out to be a great place to sunbathe and jump into the water — it’s deep and rock-free, so ideal for swimming. there’s also a proper pebble beach on the other side if you prefer to set up there. the pebbles near the shoreline were surprisingly easy on the feet compared to others we’d been to. you’ll also see locals cliff diving from 20+ metres — not something we tried, but definitely fun to watch.

tip-if you don’t do hikes and want to see the geese and beginning bits, we didn’t pay for parking cuz it only took half hour! bonus! we came to see the lovely steps with wood woven banisters, geese and the sleepy cats. saw hikers covered in mud and decided that wasn’t for me. quick pit stop well worth it!

tips for the marvelous experience! we spent 7 hours walking in this incredible park and it wasn’t enough to see all of this beauty! ancient site with lots of history. quick tips: 1. if you want to have a picture from the top with the treasury in the background, pay 10-15$ per person max!! no more!! the local guys will help you with that, you won’t be able to do it on your own! 2. there are no shortcuts! do not believe the locals who are trying to take money from you for that. you will spend more time ans energy with these shortcuts. 3. from the beginning of the walk they offer the ride on the horse that is included in your tickets. however, they want you to tip them afterwards. we never used them tbh, cause the animals look really sad and they have the marks all over their bodies 4. if you would like to help some kids, they would love to get some sweets/ fruits from you :)

tips from a mediocre hiker: go early! it’s an oven below the rim and once the sun passes over the cliffs (mid morning/early afternoon) you won’t be able to escape the blazing heat. it can easily feel above 100 below the rim. stay hydrated (preferably a few days or maybe even a week prior to the hike) but include electrolytes - this part is very important. i give five stars for the view, but i would keep in mind this is not an easy trail. although it is marked, it is not paved, and it can be uneven and steep. not ideal for people with knee, ankle, or back issues. i would also warn against hiking this trail if you have high blood pressure or heart problems, particularly in the afternoon.

tirta empul temple is truly beautiful and definitely a must-visit while in bali. although it can get quite crowded, the experience is still very special. one thing that really stood out is how respectful and fair everything felt, they don’t overcharge or exploit tourists, which is rare and deeply appreciated. i’ve visited many countries, and it was refreshing to see such honesty here.

titanique is a hysterical musical with fantastic performances and a unique perspective on the iconic story. we expected to see a musical but instead were taken by surprise by this absolutely hilarious spectacle, clever writing and lots and lots of laughter. we were in genuine stitches throughout the show, especially when it came to jack’s drawings, his hilarious mannerisms, jack painting rose scene, every time the iceberg b#tch appeared on stage, celine’s narration, among many many others but it would give away the story so i won’t spoil it! the musical part of the show was phenomenon, every performer’s singing was incredible – fantastic casting. this is a must-see musical. well done to everyone on stage! seating – the theatre layout is tricky. unless you’re in the first ten rows or upstairs, you are likely to have an obstructed view of the stage given the amount of pillars and the low ceiling. i took a picture from the very back of the theatre – you will miss some of the show and its definitely worth sitting close to the stage.

titilaka is an exceptional retreat that redefines luxury at lake titicaca. nestled on a private peninsula, the hotel offers breathtaking 360-degree views of the lake, creating an atmosphere of serene isolation and connection with nature. the suites are spacious, elegantly designed, and perfectly equipped for comfort, with floor-to-ceiling windows that frame the ever-changing colors of the lake. every detail, from the bedding to the locally crafted decor, reflects thoughtful curation and authenticity. service is outstanding—personalized, intuitive, and genuinely warm. the all-inclusive experience is flawless, with gourmet cuisine highlighting andean flavors, expertly prepared and paired with fine wines. activities are tailor-made, from sunrise boat rides to immersive cultural excursions with local communities. titilaka isn’t just a place to stay; it’s an immersive, once-in-a-lifetime experience that blends luxury, nature, and cultural richness in perfect harmony.

title: a hidden gem in queenstown jardine park in queenstown, new zealand, is simply an oasis of tranquility. with its verdant greenery, well-maintained amenities, and fantastic views, it offers a unique blend of natural beauty and thoughtful design that makes every visit truly memorable. the park impresses with its diverse range of attractions. from picnic spots highlighted by the enthralling mountain backdrop, engaging birdlife that adds a dynamic touch to the serene environment, to the trails that crisscross the park - every detail contributes to a wholesome outdoor experience. the children's playground is a safe and inviting space for the children while the expansive open fields are perfect for a great family picnic or a casual game of football or frisbee. more active visitors can appreciate the beautifully maintained walking and biking trails. what strikes me the most about jardine park is its immaculate cleanliness and efforts towards preserving the environment. the park administration ensures their space is habitable for local wildlife while providing exceptional facilities for visitors. jardine park represents a proud attribute of queenstown's beauty and hospitality, a must-visit for locals and tourists alike. my family and i have made countless memories here, and i highly recommend this park to anyone seeking a peaceful retreat amidst the naturally charming queenstown. a five-star experience every time!

title: brooklyn's best-kept secret: vista point's panoramic splendor review: in brooklyn's dumbo neighborhood, vista point offers a compelling view of new york city's iconic structures. having visited vista point multiple times, each experience remains as memorable as the last. its strategic position along washington street provides an unparalleled view of the manhattan bridge and the brooklyn bridge, set against the east river. witnessing the two bridges, the manhattan bridge from 1901 and the brooklyn bridge spanning 6,016 feet across the river, is truly impressive. the nyc skyline, with the prominent empire state building, further enhances the panorama. early mornings offer a serene atmosphere ideal for photography, while nighttime unveils the city's vibrant lights. dumbo's surrounding area enriches the experience. the east river greenway is perfect for walks, and nearby restaurants cater to diverse palates. open 24/7, vista point attracts global tourists and locals throughout the year. for visitors to nyc and its residents, a trip to vista point showcases the city's magnificence. a combination of sights and experiences, it's a representation of new york city's essence. it is highly recommended for those wanting to immerse themselves in the city's spirit. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

tjóðsavnið – national museum of the faroe islands is a small but interesting museum showcasing the history and culture of the archipelago. exhibits cover viking heritage, traditional faroese life, and natural history. well-organized and informative, it's a great stop for those interested in the islands' rich past.

tlaquepaque is such a beautiful and unique spot in sedona — full of charm, art, and character. the architecture and atmosphere make you feel like you’ve stepped into a quaint mexican village, and every shop has something special to offer, from handmade crafts to upscale galleries. it’s a perfect place to wander, take photos, and find one-of-a-kind gifts. the only downside is that everything closes by 5 pm, which feels a little early, especially if you’re trying to explore after a day of hiking. still, it’s definitely worth the visit!

tlaquepaque – a magical sedona gem this was our third visit to tlaquepaque, and it only grows more enchanting each time. nestled beneath a canopy of mature oak trees, the architecture is absolutely stunning — a gorgeous blend of old-world charm and vibrant artistry that instantly transports you to a quaint mexican village. wandering the winding cobblestone paths and vine-draped archways feels like stepping into a hidden oasis. every corner reveals something new, from trickling fountains to beautifully tiled courtyards that invite you to linger and soak up the atmosphere. the shops are an absolute delight, filled with incredible finds that celebrate both local artists and international craftsmanship. whether you’re looking for unique jewelry, fine art, handblown glass, or artisanal home décor, tlaquepaque offers treasures for every taste. it’s the perfect place to discover one-of-a-kind pieces that carry the spirit of sedona home with you. tlaquepaque is more than just a shopping destination — it’s a true feast for the senses and a highlight of any sedona trip. we can’t wait for our next visit!

tldr: don't skip this dive shop - this was all-in-all the best experience i've had as an open water diver. my friend and i happened to walk in to blue marlin dive while walking down one of the main streets in labuan bajo and we are so happy we did! the front desk staff was very warm and recommended we did the quick refresher course a day before our dive. doing this was absolutely worth it. our instructor, philip, was very thorough and made sure we felt comfortable with emergency procedures and the standard stuff, like ascending, descending, and equalizing. he also made a point to tell us a bit about what to expect during our dives. my friend and i had only planned on doing 2 dives (the rest of the folks on the boat were doing 3), but because of how fun the dives were and how comfortable we felt, we also ended up doing the third! philip - thank you so much! not only are you an amazing teacher, you were such great company. we both had such a fun time chatting and hanging with you on the boat.
to all my fellow runners out there, there is a good cycling track behind the monument, that goes all the way down to the beaches on south. worth giving a try on weekend mornings.
to be fair we went on a very foggy and slightly drizzling day. just a 5 minute walk from carpark but unfortunately no water-falling at all. due to fog no view of surroundings, so quite underwhelming

to be honest i wasn’t expecting much but this park is a really fun way to spend the day. now that’s it’s scorching hot out you should go early in the day or late. the animals seem to be more active then too. i did the drive-thru twice there are dozens of species of prarie dwelling antelopes, bison, camels, zebras, water buffaloes etc. spread throughout. great photo opportunities and there’s also elk and various species of deer in the cypress swamp area too. ostrich and emu are lurking around, and giraffes are near the exit, they can be hand fed. the exhibit park is also a lot of fun, and well organized. lots of reptiles, a walk thru aviary, and many exotic animals including lemurs, kangaroos, sloths, some unusual foxes & squirrels, snakes and wide variety that should interest any curious kid as well as adults. plus there’s a petting area featuring the all time great rodent capybara! i didn’t try the restaurant but looks solid, the gift shop has loads of items and the staff everywhere were extremely friendly and helpful. i had never even heard of this place until a friend invited me to tagalong, so glad i did. you will be too if you’ve got a lazy summer day that you’re not sure of what you want to do, then check this place out you won’t regret it.

to be in puerto rico, to visit old san juan and not go through la perla, is to have never come to puerto rico, to stop setting foot in old san juan and not to be part of the history of la perla.

to be true it was my unexpected trek and what i found was truly amazing, i never thought the langtang trek will be so beautiful like the 360 mountain range view. a super smooth trek followed my true beauty, and the most beautiful and kind hearted people during this trek. it is a short trek that can be completed in 4 days. you will love the hospitality here. was journey to this place was an unforgettable journey the trek to kyanjin ri view point and the tserego ri view point is so mesmerising, i never had added this place to the bucket list but when i visited this place i was just shocked with the beauty.

to begin, if you have the chance to make the escape to the surrounding forests past quebec city, please do yourselves a favor and make a stopover for a day of complete relaxation. me and my partner booked a couples package on january 22nd as part of our anniversary trip. the immediate first impression of the area is of calm as it is nestled in the trees and nature all around. note that we started at 10:30am until mid afternoon on one of the coldest but beautifully sunny days so there was a small amount of other guests. the reception takes the time to accompany all guests outside to describe where each hot and cold station of the thermal experience can be located, a personal touch that is worth noting for its attentiveness to service from the start. the hot tubs, barrel saunas, fire pits, yurts with full views of the river, and eucalyptus steam spa are not even the full spectrum of the outdoor experience you’ll find. mid way through our visit we had a fantastic couples massage and were so well taken care in the hands (literally) of chantal and akiko. a recommendation to book either of them if you get the chance. on the grounds of the spa, the siberia cafe offers traditional or more gourmet treats and drinks depending on your liking. our package includes a very deluxe treatment of food, drink, and a platter of meats and cheeses that were deliciously comforting. thank you for contributing to the memories of a great week getaway up north!

to cap off our mexican adventure, we booked a dhow cruise through aqua tours, and it was absolutely magical. the evening was filled with romance — from the soft, enchanting music played on a flute, to dancing under the stars. the hosts truly knew how to create an atmosphere of love and celebration. the food was incredible, the drinks were flowing (unlimited, might i add!), and every detail made us feel closer than ever. it was the perfect grand finale to an amazing trip.

to check off a must-do adventure in honolulu, my wife and i planned a morning hike on the manoa falls trail, and it was such a treat! we researched this one well in advance, wanting an easy, fun hike that would let us soak in hawaii’s stunning nature. just a quick 20-minute uber ride from our waikiki hotel, the trail was super easy to find, with clear signs pointing us toward the waterfall. the round trip is under 2 miles, but heads-up—it can get a bit slippery and wet, especially since it rains often. luckily, we had dry weather, which made the trek even more enjoyable. the hike itself was a total delight, winding through a lush forest with towering trees, vibrant native flowers, and plants that made us feel completely immersed in hawaii’s natural beauty. every step felt like a little escape into paradise, with greenery all around and the fresh scent of the forest. the payoff at the end was the manoa falls, hawaii’s tallest waterfall, and it was absolutely worth it—just breathtaking! we spent some time taking it all in before heading back, snapping photos and savoring the peaceful vibe. this was the perfect morning adventure, leaving us plenty of time to relax at waikiki beach for the rest of the day. our tip: skip renting a car and just take an uber to the trailhead—it’s hassle-free and super convenient. the manoa falls trail was everything we hoped for—simple, scenic, and a beautiful way to connect with hawaii’s natural charm. big thanks to this trail for making our trip extra special!

took the 6km self drive huskies tour, we drove for around 30min with a small break to swap the driver. one of the best experiences i had. it was around -30 degrees, and the eyelashes and beard got frozen 😅. we borrowed the gear from the tour and it helped. 10 out of 10 experience, staff are really friendly and know what they are doing.

took the cruise through all the stops for around 3 hours and it was really nice. one of the crew narrated the tour and it was a beautiful day. we didn’t do the hop on hop off because we just wanted a ride, but it would have been perfect for that. we were staying around greenwich for a concert so this was a perfect place to come.

took the doggo to the baby bell, llama, and bail trail loop. went around 830 and parking was packed. parked around the loop where it said "no parking" and was fine for the 1.5 hours. the morning at 830 wasn't too hot or sunny but by the time the hike was over it was a bit much for the dog. thankfully there were many shady spots to stop and cool off. bring water to make life easier. many blind corners for bikers so a short leash is definitely recommended. multiple scenic view points to take it all in. lizards running over , some sharp rocks in areas. highly recommend for a 1.5 -2 hour hike. was apox 6km in 1:45 mins (with stops)
took the family for a very pleasant walk and picnic in the forest near the river.

took the full day cape tour. our guide dillon was excellent. loved being at cape point and cape of good hope. saw eland, ostriches in wild. loved the penguins. this costs extra so be prepared for that.

took the guided safari jeep tour. booked online in advance. very knowledgeable guide who made the visit very enjoyable. the views from sublime point are amazing. this is a good option if you are in any doubt about your ability to do the hikes.

took the kids here. we did the smash it package. had fun taking photos with all the cool 3d art and enjoyed throwing plates at the smash it target. had the whole place to ourselves.

took the lake minnewanka cruise and it was such a lovely experience — once we actually managed to park! honestly, parking was a bit of a mission. we had to circle around a few times before finally getting a spot. kind of glad we didn’t book tickets online in advance, because if we had missed the boat due to parking, it would’ve been a very different kind of review! that said, once we were on the cruise, it was smooth sailing (literally). the staff were super welcoming, and the captains were amazing — full of fun facts and stories about the lake’s history, and kept the whole vibe relaxed and enjoyable. it was especially cool to see that most of the boat captains were women — love to see it! the lake itself is stunning, and the cruise gives you a great view of the mountains and a peaceful moment away from the crowds. definitely worth doing — just give yourself plenty of time to find parking!

took the last trip from greenwich to westminster in the evening. the cabin was warm for an evening chilly weather. you do get to enjoy as well as take photos of the scenery so the speed is right! the london skyline with a setting sun looks very nice, they should clean the glass screen of the cabin more frequently, tourists will enjoy it more. value for money if you take a day pass rather than one way trip.

took the mescal trail that links to the devil's bridge trail. amazing views and lots of clean air on the way to the devil's bridge! i would rate this trail as easy with the last section being moderate to difficult as there are some steep parts to ascend. the trail to and from mescal and devil's bridge is ~ 4.9 miles round trip. take plenty of water and snacks. note, because there were so many people, we had to wait about an hour to take our pics on the bridge.

took the mossman gorge, daintree river cruise and cape tribulation tour. our knowledgeable and friendly guide filled the trip with many relevant facts and pieces of trivia. the "welcome to country" ceremony gave a personal insight into indigenous culture and knowledge, and the sights at mossman gorge were fantastic. the daintree river cruise guide certainly knew his stuff, but it was a shame we didn't see any crocs -- wrong time of year (hotting up, so the crocs spend more time underwater to regulate their temperature, rather than sunning themselves on the riverbank). first two photos are at mossman gorge, third is on the daintree river cruise, and last one at thornton beach (looking out at truck island). my only criticism of the trip was that everything felt quite rushed, which was a shame because everything was so beautiful, and longer to soak it up would have been great.

took the shared 5 island tour. good value for money. the staff is helpful although i was slightly late; captain is welcoming and fun. he provided explaination in both french & english...and ensure everyone have fun.
took the shortest trail and already had calf pain the next day. the guide only speaks korean and we returned without following the group which was good as we can walk more casually.

took the tour with the catamaran. we were lucky and we’ve seen 2 species of dolphins and 1 species of whales (sea whale). dolphins were swimming in front of our boat and jumping around! the marine biologist, gina, was super nice and prepared and spent quite some time with me telling me anecdotes and about her experiences with cetacean watching. if you’re not going to see any cetacean they refund you or you can rebook the tour for another day.

took the tram up to get here (its really steep) great views. the weather was really hot and humid so we went up early in the morning like 9am but very little was open. there were crowds wandering around 9am with nothing to do, if some of the cafes were open they would have customers. but the views on the on the observation deck were great.

took the “hike and kayak costa brava” with serge. serge was very polite and made sure everyone is included but he wasn’t organized which caused a-lot of delays. enjoyed the hike and the view was amazing. kayak was very long, got bored and tired mid way. the caves are not interesting at all not what i expected. as for snorkelling, there’s nothing to see! just green water. and i thought i would get to jump off cliffs as advertised. also, we didn’t go as planned and got some delays due to the van’s parking and kayak’s availability. wasn’t able to order lunch since we were late.

took us about 50 mins to get down and 1.5h to get back up. the stairs are steep and not horizontal which makes it more challenging. luckily there are plenty of restaurants in paul do mar to sit and relax before you go back up. its not busy at all and the views are amazing. definitely better than some of the very touristy hikes
took us on a boat trip to prison island. excellent quick service with friendly and knowledgeable staff. recommend if looking for a good trip

took us one hour to get here from shinjuku station. we watched tokyo verdy vs osaka cerezo match that evening. the stadium was amazing! just watch the video we recorded! clean rows of seats! even the toilet was also clean and it’s quite rare to see that in other countries we’ve been to! the atmosphere was great! both team played well! it was a delightful experiences! japan never disappoints!!

took us roughly an hour to walk each way, with some challenging hills. i would have to say that the waterfall at the end with its swimming holes are amazing, and very well worth the walk in the end. i went not long ago (summertime), and although we were met with rain, it was welcome because it cooled us down, and easily dried off once the rain stopped anyways. 100% would recommend it. it has got to be the best waterfall around cairns!!! i would suggest if you are going to bring some snacks or a little packed lunch to bite when you reach the falls.

top notch homestay in raja ampat! andy and esni are very kind, helpful and caring. this applies as well for the staff. the rooms are nice, the bathroom facilities are great (fresh water for shower and flush for toilet). they thought of every small details. food is delicious. dive center is great. there is power and internet 24/7, thanks to the solar power (backed up by a generator in case of bad weather). after our stay in nyande, we went to another homestay as nyande was fully booked. i got very sick and esni picked us up to bring us to the clinic. we truly appreciated her help!! we will be back!

top notch service from whizzy, highly recommend. nick picked us up from our accommodation, set us up with the bikes with easy instructions. extremely knowledgeable of trails across queenstown which made us feel at ease setting off on our adventure. we did almost 50km from thompson hill to jack's point, plenty of views to enjoy. easy, quick collection of bikes once we completed the trails. thanks nick!

top of the rock is still the best deal when it comes to observation decks. this time, i also tried both new attractions – the beam and the 360° deck. as for the beam, i definitely want to point out that if you’re a couple or a group, don’t go all together on this attraction if you want nice photos. you can’t take your phone with you, and the photos they take of you are only two – and you have to pay extra for them. considering you’ve already paid for the attraction and the observation deck, this can get quite pricey, and the photos often look staged. on the other hand, your partner or family can easily take beautiful photos and videos of you from the upper level – and those will be more authentic, even better, and free. otherwise, the view from there is fantastic. as for the 360° tower, it’s better to wait until there are fewer people at the top. make sure to really enjoy it, because you won’t be up there for long, but if you’re already visiting the observation deck, this attraction is definitely worth it.

top of the rock offers one of the best panoramic views of new york city — especially of central park and the empire state building. we really enjoyed it because, unlike some other observatories, it wasn’t overly crowded, so taking photos and enjoying the view felt much more relaxed. the observation decks are located at the top of the rockefeller center, an iconic art deco skyscraper with lots of history. the building itself is beautiful and well maintained, and the whole experience is organized and smooth. if you're looking for a stunning view without the overwhelming crowds, top of the rock is a great choice!

topside beef cooking class what a great experience! we really enjoyed the cooking class. we learned about the origins of the key ingredients and what flavors they bring to the dishes. the class was completely interactive! from chopping of veggies to deciding the amount of panela or salt to final plating. we enjoyed talking to daniel and learning about his culinary background. francisco, the sous chef was lightning fast making sure we had everything we needed. the food was fabulous and we received access to the recipes right away. daniel even talked about where we could possibly get some of the ingredients when we get back home. we highly recommend this class.

torcello is a hidden gem — quiet, mysterious, and steeped in history. far from the crowds, it feels like stepping into another time. the island has a peaceful, almost spiritual atmosphere, with wide open spaces, greenery, and a slow, meditative pace. the highlight is the ancient basilica of santa maria assunta with its stunning byzantine mosaics — absolutely breathtaking and unexpectedly powerful. a short walk from the pier brings you past canals, stone bridges, and the legendary attila’s throne. it’s a perfect escape from the tourist buzz of venice and a must for anyone who appreciates history, nature, and tranquility.

torcello was absolutely beautiful and a must see when you visit venice. it is truly a hidden gem of history and cute building surrounded by water. we got the boat tour of the day which included also going to morano which was amazing as well. highly recommend the boat tour and also seeing the islands when you’re in venice.

torres del paine national park, located in the magallanes and chilean antarctica region of southern chile, is widely celebrated as one of the world’s most spectacular natural reserves. the park is renowned for its dramatic landscapes, marked by the iconic granite spires known as las torres, which rise sharply above the surrounding plains and are a magnet for trekkers and climbers. these distinctive peaks, along with the striking cuernos del paine-mountains with unique black and white banding-form the visual heart of the park. the geography of torres del paine is a study in contrasts. snow-capped mountains tower over golden pampas, while turquoise lakes such as pehoé and grey reflect the jagged skyline. the park’s glacial features, especially the immense grey glacier, offer awe-inspiring views and opportunities for boat excursions or hikes along icy shores. valleys like the french valley and ascencio valley provide access to some of the most breathtaking vistas in patagonia, each with its own unique geological formations and panoramic lookouts. beyond its famous peaks and glaciers, the park is a haven for biodiversity. visitors often encounter native wildlife including guanacos, foxes, pumas, and a variety of bird species such as the andean condor. the lenga and ñirre forests add a lush green contrast to the otherwise rugged terrain, especially in the spring and summer months. torres del paine is accessible for all types of travelers. while seasoned hikers can embark on challenging multi-day treks like the w trek or the full circuit, there are also shorter, well-marked trails and scenic viewpoints accessible by car, making the park enjoyable for families and those with limited mobility. the infrastructure within the park is well-developed, with options for guided tours, horseback riding, and all-inclusive lodges that offer comfort and convenience amid the wild surroundings. the weather in torres del paine is famously unpredictable, with strong winds and sudden changes in temperature, so visitors should come prepared for all conditions. despite the sometimes harsh climate, the park’s beauty is undiminished, and each season brings its own charm-whether it’s the wildflowers of summer or the snow-dusted peaks of winter. overall, torres del paine national park stands out as a masterpiece of nature, offering visitors an unforgettable experience of patagonia’s raw and untamed beauty. from its world-famous trekking routes to its serene lakes and abundant wildlife, the park promises adventure, tranquility, and some of the most stunning scenery on the planet.

totally agree with other reviews referring to this as a "hidden gem". having done the city walls the previous day, this nicely complemented the experience taking you below the walls into the oldest and only preserved structure from the medieval history of dubrovnik. in complete contrast to the walls above, i had this place to myself. the foundary museum below one of the towers offers a good insight into the casting & moulding processes undertaken here. i hadn't realised that entry to this museum includes a whole section following the west side of the wall down to the south in an area between the main wall and an outer wall with more ruins at the southern end. from the dubrovnik pass website this wasn't on the list of inclusions; this needs to be corrected with all the places that are included with the pass.

totally recommended experience, ride on a sailboat on the nahuel huapi for approximately 2 hours at the petuña campsite. they served us coffee, tea and some delicious cakes at one of the stops. ideal to go with children because it is not as extensive as other navigations they offer. it's a pleasure to have met people like pablo who knows a lot about sailing and the history of the place, in addition to his good vibes. i recommend!!!

totally recommended. we paid $99 p/p. they picked us up at the hotel (1 hr away), it included lunch, buggy ride, horse ride, 8 zip lines and they also take you to see how they do tabaco and cocoa and also to a beach. you pay $3 for a locker and if you don’t have glasses or bandana, you can buy them there. go dressed and prepare to get dirty. we had so much fun and everybody there was so nice. specially carlos (owner) and jason (one of the tour guys). i started to feel nauseous and dizzy and everyone was very courteous and trying to help me feel better. unfortunately i wasn’t feeling good enough to continue the tour and carlos offered to take us back to the hotel personally in his vehicle. i’ll never forget that. you can get the pictures package for $55 (we got 78 pictures).

totally underrated hike compared to others like reinebringen ... you should go this one. less people - more interesting. you can start from "ballstadt fisk as" or at the south end of the parking of "kræmmervika havn" - the trailhead there is opposite to the sign on the street! shortly before you reach the sherpa's steps i recommend to go the "alternative route" - as this one is easier to go up than to go down - while the steps are easier to go down than being interesting to go up. once you reach the end of the stairs or the alternative path there is an easy-to-walk plateau at the top - and the views are just lovely!

traditional japanese tea ceremony- in a 300 year old samurai house. wow!!! i cannot say enough about how amazing this was! the family was wonderful! we took stunning photos in our kimonos. highly recommended!!!!

traditional korean village that can be visited for free. a lot of old houses are perfectly preserved and is one of the rare places where we can see pieces of furniture and other indoor decorative elements. the garden is calm and offers many opportunities to wander. excellent place to visit in seoul.
