trail for the canyon is easy peasy, went at 5pm during the week so not busy. the path is roughly paved to the top waterfall. the ink pots trail is another 2.7 past that. most of the tourist crowd will have thinned out by this point, you know, the ones wearing those sparkly white runners! ink pots trail goes up, then down, then up then down again. felt longer than it was. coming back way faster! haha

trail is beautiful. it’s very rocky. easier going up than down for me. it is a hiking trail and can be steep at times. there is a gondola at top if you don’t want to walk down. round trip for me was 2 plus hours. i spent time taking pictures. bring water.

trail is very easy to follow and well maintained. the crowds thin out a lot after the upper falls. the trail has some ups and downs so the total elevation gain is minimal after the falls. we did this in the winter, so spikes were helpful. generally not that scenic after the canyon, but the ink pots are cool.

trail is very easy to follow! after parking the road is only for residents. free to visit! even on a foggy day i was still able to see a bit of the cliff, so by the end of the day i went back and had this amazing view! i am glad there wasn’t an entrance fee 😄

trail with amazing views. we did not manage to get to the very top as we arrived quite late in the evening and was with two young teenagers. parking large enough for a few cars at entrance . gate is to keep sheep in , it’s not a private gate , so open it and get rolling . after first incline behind the buildings there is a muddy section so good hiking shoes are required .

trailhead was easy to find, and the trail itself was easy and well maintained. it takes about an hour round trip, taking time at the view point. absolutely stunning and highly recommend a visit. free to visit. road actually goes further than the parking but is intended for locals only. be respectful.

trails are moderate in scale, definitely wear hiking boots and have fun! use the cairns as trail markers and watch for them. take plenty of water, enjoy the views, talk softly and enjoy the immense beauty.
trails so pretty with cool breeze from the seas. take 20-45 mins. love it!
trails with good maintenance and unique landscape. good sturdy shoes needed!

trajan’s column is a stunning monument with intricate carvings depicting his military victories. a masterpiece of roman engineering and propaganda, it stands proudly in the heart of rome, surrounded by ruins. even from a distance, the detailed reliefs remain impressive and tell a fascinating story of ancient warfare.

transpirenaica september 24: there were 12 days of emblematic routes between cadaqués and hondarribia organized by nic, who took care of us during the great adventure so that everything went perfectly. fond memories and eager to repeat.

transportation was on time and smooth start to finish. company was very helpful a few days prior to our trip in switching our tour type. saw plenty of gators as well as turtles and bird wildlife. tour guide was great and you can tell he knew a lot about the bayou. i wish there was a little more history about new orleans included on the tour.

tried the relaxing and tonic massage and it was amazing. the staff is very kind and the space is very comfy. came back twice in my staying in marrakech. and they serve an amazing tea.

tried the venice water taxi while i was in venice. definitely a remarkable experience. the vibe really feels romantic if you’re traveling with your loved one, but even with a group of friends, we still had so much fun. enjoyed the whole journey and caught the perfect sunset. a memory to remember!

tried wild art paint fight with my friends, and we absolutely loved it! it was a rainy day, so we were looking for indoor activities and we found this amazing place. definitely a must-try. highly recommend!

trilhas tours is who you want to hire when you come to terceira island! juca is an amazing tour guide. marisa is a huge help in providing information about the island before you arrive and during your stay. meeting these two is like coming to see family. they love the island and they enjoy sharing it with visitors. we had a few days of bad weather during our visit. juca gave us the option to reschedule our tour. he then combined the best views and photo tours in one day, accommodating all four in our party. he was terrific at teaching us tricks with the camera and how to make really great vacation photos. he knows the best places that you will never find on your own or that others would spend the time showing you. we also took the archeology tour another day and it was impressive. if you are into history at all, this tour is for you. he takes you to great eating places for lunch. and we had a surprise visit by marisa, which was a delight. this is a private tour for you in his great van that is terrific for seeing the island. there were four of us and we were never crowded and everyone was pleased with the experience. i travel extensively and take many tours. this far exceeds any i have experienced.

trip of a lifetime is how i would describe our 2 weeks in south africa. timeless africa safaris didn’t miss a beat from the initial planning, with multiple options for our family of 6, to finalizing our trip with our preferences. when the time came to start our adventure, we had a call a few weeks out to go over it as well as get restaurant booked for dinner in cape town. finally, when our trip started, we had our travel packs at our hotel in j-berg to being checked in for all our flights along the way as well as little subtle touches and each and every place we stayed (roses around our bed, birthday cakes, baths drawn, i could go on and on). our trip truly was seamless and the most amazing trip we have ever taken. we did 2 safaris, sabi sands, lion sands river lodge and in zimbabwe at matetsi. we also went to victoria falls (a must see) than down to leeu estate in franschhoek for a few days in wine country before concluding our trip in cape town at the one and only to see all the sites before heading back to the usa. i highly recommend using timeless africa safaris if you are traveling to africa. we worked with zita and she was amazing and very well traveled and knowledgeable. she made us feel like family as well as was able to pivot when we had a change of plans.

trip of a lifetime! natural world safaris knocked this trip for us out of the park!! our driver, george, was prompt, professional, knowledgeable, and fun - just the best!! we enjoyed driving with him for 9 days. our accommodations varied from tents to lodges and at each place we were met with friendly staff, great food, and comfortable sleeping arrangements. i am vegan and was cheerfully accommodated. the itinerary was varied and interesting. would 100% book with natural world kenya safaris again.

truc bach lake in hanoi is a peaceful spot, perfect for a morning walk. the calm waters and fresh breeze make it a refreshing start to the day. surrounded by charming coffee shops, it’s ideal for a quiet break. you can sit by the lake with a cup of vietnamese coffee and just unwind. the views are soothing, especially during sunrise and sunset. a lovely place to relax and soak in the city’s slower, scenic side.

truck went out the moment we ordered but they still pushed through. the food was unbelievable. definitely going to have it again when i visit vancouver. the philly cheesesteak was done to perfection and the shawarma toum (garlic sauce ) was really creamy and tasty. fries were also fantastic. 7.9/10 - take a 30 minute detour for this

true to its name, this park features six different types of flowers. you can search for the flowers in the picture while taking a leisurely stroll. there are several exhibition spaces here showcasing a variety of hand-drawn and related artworks. there are also vast meadows and art sculptures. the sound of the flowing stream and the chirping of birds in the trees create the most natural white noise. if possible, please spend some time here, as it will bring you great peace of mind.

truly a hidden gem of a tour! we took this tour at 2:30 today, and it was an unforgettable experience. captain keaka was incredibly patient, skillfully following the humpback whales to give us the best opportunities for photos. he also took the time to answer every question we had about these amazing creatures. nick and dustin were super helpful to make sure we had a great time, providing refreshments and sharing fun facts about whales. highly recommend this tour for anyone looking for an incredible whale-watching experience!”

truly a hidden gem of the city, and one you can find in the very centre of it; stroll by basilica di san giovanni and take a right near the entrance to the museum, and you'll find yourself transported in a different world altogether. the classy, well maintained garden with parrots flying about, the fountain in the middle and the history buzzing in the walls of the palazzo were all downright entrancing, filling you with an impeccable wanderlust you can only ever feel in italy. definitely one of ym favourite places in all of rome, and you can go in for free.

truly a magical escape for all ages! ✨🏰 the rides, parades, and character shows are top-notch. loved the mix of classic disney and asian touches. the park is clean, well-managed, and super friendly. must try the themed snacks — they’re adorable and tasty!🍦 a dream day come true — can’t wait to visit again! 🌟

truly a must-stay when visiting québec city! the experience was wonderful. the staff is very nice and professional. the hotel itself is so beautiful and centrally located. we had an upgraded room which was a good size. very clean, comfortable bed, nice amenities. the bathroom was on the smaller side but still very good with lots of complementary toiletries. the breakfast was delicious. would definitely stay here again.

truly a once-in-a-lifetime experience. housing more than 13,000 ancient antiquities dating back thousands of years, it offers an incredible journey through ancient egypt’s history and culture. one of the highlights is the complete tutankhamun collection, displayed together for the first time, allowing visitors to witness the golden treasures of the young pharaoh in all their glory. the exhibits are thoughtfully arranged, with breathtaking treasures from the time of the pharaohs, including beautifully preserved statues, jewelry, and everyday items that bring the past to life. the museum’s modern architecture and spacious layout make exploring comfortable and enjoyable, and the views of the giza pyramids from the grounds add a magical touch. a must-visit for anyone passionate about history and heritage.

tucked away on the verdant slopes of rome’s janiculum hill, between the cobbled charm of trastevere and the elegant streets of monteverde vecchio, lies one of the city’s best-kept secrets: villa sciarra. far from the crowds of the colosseum or the vatican, this peaceful garden offers a different kind of roman experience—lush, whimsical, and steeped in centuries of fascinating history. as you step through the wrought-iron gates—whether from the elegant piazzale wurts or the quieter largo filippo minutilli—you’re immediately immersed in a green haven. towering mediterranean pines, cascading ivy, and the gentle trickle of fountains create a timeless atmosphere. yet, this serenity hides a layered past. long before this was a landscaped villa, the land was sacred. in ancient rome, it was home to a grove dedicated to the nymph furrina and later absorbed into the gardens of caesar—where, legend says, julius caesar hosted cleopatra during her dramatic visit to the capital. fast forward to the renaissance, and the property was transformed into a noble estate, passing through the hands of illustrious families like the malvasia, the barberini, and the colonna di sciarra, each leaving their mark. in the early 1900s, the villa entered a new era thanks to american diplomat george washington wurts and his wife henrietta tower, who lovingly restored the grounds. they collected statues and fountains from across italy—especially from the visconti palace in lombardy—and arranged them throughout the garden, turning it into a fantastical open-air museum. when george died, henrietta made a bold gesture: she donated the villa to mussolini, with one request—that it become a public park for all to enjoy. today, wandering through villa sciarra feels like strolling through a storybook. you’ll pass by the fontana dei fauni, where mischievous fauns hold up a seashell, crowned by a playful putto. nearby, diana and endymion are frozen in myth, eternal in their chase beneath a laurel canopy. the esedra arborea encircles you with statues representing the twelve months, each tucked into a green alcove. don’t miss the sphinx fountain, a quiet corner where four enigmatic figures seem to guard the secrets of the villa. and at the heart of it all stands the casino barberini, once the noble residence, now home to the prestigious italian institute of germanic studies. look out for the curious castelletto, a neo-gothic mini-castle now used as a museum of mathematics, and the remnants of a roman sanctuary dedicated to mysterious eastern deities—proof that this ground has always been more than a park.

tucked quietly in the bustle of chinatown, elizabeth street garden is a curated little escape—a whimsical patch of greenery dotted with statues that make you feel like you’ve wandered into a forgotten european courtyard or a dream set from an indie film. think: serenity meets sculpture garden with just a touch of brooklyn mysticism. the layout is simple but charming: winding paths, blooming flowers, ivy-laced corners, and plenty of seating if you want to pause for a sandwich, a book, or just a deep existential thought. the statues give the place an ethereal edge—my personal favorite was a lion mid-snarl next to a rather pensive cherub. is it art? is it a secret garden of marble personalities? who knows—but it works. admittedly, the mosquitoes also found the vibe appealing, and i had to cut my visit short lest i become a buffet. but that’s nature for you: beautiful, buzzing, and occasionally hungry. still, i’d absolutely return. bring bug spray and something poetic to do—it’s that kind of place.

turtuk village, nestled in the majestic landscape of ladakh, is a hidden gem that whispers tales of a bygone era. located on the banks of the shyok river, this quaint village is the last outpost of india before the pakistan border. as you wander through its narrow alleys, you'll discover a unique blend of tibetan and balti cultures, reflected in the warm smiles of its inhabitants and the rustic charm of its wooden houses. the village is surrounded by towering mountains, their rugged beauty softened by the lush greenery of apricot orchards and the gentle rustle of willow trees. turtuk's strategic location has made it an important stopover for traders and travelers since ancient times. the village is dotted with ancient monasteries, mosques, and temples, each telling a story of its rich history. the villagers, known for their hospitality, welcome visitors with open arms, offering a glimpse into their simple yet rich way of life. as you explore the village, you'll come across ancient artifacts, traditional handicrafts, and local cuisine that will leave you enchanted. with its surreal vistas, turtuk village is a trekker's paradise, offering breathtaking views of the karakoram range and the majestic nubra valley. as the sun sets, casting a golden glow over the village, you'll feel the serenity and timelessness of this enchanting corner of ladakh. turtuk village is a must-visit destination for those seeking an immersive experience in the unspoiled beauty and rich culture of ladakh. its untouched charm and warm hospitality will leave you with memories to last a lifetime.

twin falls bridge in lynn canyon park, north vancouver, offers a serene and accessible hiking experience amidst the lush temperate rainforest of the north shore. this short loop trail, approximately 1.5 km round-trip with an elevation gain of about 65 meters, is ideal for families, casual hikers, and visitors seeking a quick nature escape. the journey begins at the lynn canyon park entrance, where you'll find the lynn canyon suspension bridge—a free and exhilarating crossing over lynn creek, suspended 50 meters above the canyon floor. after crossing, follow the well-marked baden powell trail, which meanders through a verdant forest adorned with moss-covered trees and ferns. the trail descends via a series of stairs and switchbacks to the twin falls bridge, offering picturesque views of the cascading waterfalls below. while the hike is considered easy, the trail includes uneven terrain and stairs, so sturdy footwear is recommended. be cautious during wet conditions, as the paths can become slippery. swimming in the canyon is strongly discouraged due to dangerous undercurrents and past fatalities. parking is available near the lynn canyon ecology centre. from march 1 to october 31, pay parking is in effect from 8 am to 6 pm, costing $3 per hour for a maximum of four hours. payment can be made via various methods, including credit cards and mobile apps. free parking is also available in the east lot off lillooet road near the lower seymour conservation area. for those relying on public transit, the #228 and #227 buses provide access to the park, with stops within a short walking distance. the #228 runs from lonsdale quay, while the #227 connects lynn valley centre and phibbs exchange. twin falls bridge offers a tranquil and rewarding experience, combining natural beauty with accessible trails, making it a must-visit spot in north vancouver.

two things make mahali mzuri special. it’s location overlooking the kenyan landscape, and the people. it feels like you are on safari even when at home base. the service is also second to none. the staff is so kind and willing to help in any way. special shoot out to johnstone, levi and dennis. there’s many nice touches throughout the stay: varied locations for dinner, small attentions to detail - it feels as if they think of everything. i thought the food overall would be better. breakfast was a fairly average buffet. we had three lunches and three dinners. two of the dinners i thought missed the mark but the third was outstanding. lunches generally speaking were very good. the soups and bread were particularly good. the hotel is very expensive and i thought there was entirely too much noticeable wear and tear throughout the camp for the cost. they told us they plan to renovate february 2025 which makes sense, but given the current conditions of some areas you’d think the price would reflect that. debated dropping a star for this fact but the setting and service was just too good not to give anything less than five stars.

two views, one unforgettable waterfall! we saw barron falls twice — first from the kuranda scenic railway, then later from the skyrail cableway — and both were absolutely stunning in their own way. from the train, you get a dramatic, close-up view of the falls thundering through the gorge. on the way down with the skyrail, the panorama opens up, and you see the full scale of the landscape from above. two totally different experiences — both breathtaking! don’t miss the boardwalk lookout stops. this waterfall is a true highlight.

two years ago we booked a private boat tour with oliver and had a great trip. this time it was fantastic again. we were very close to lots of dolphins, turtles and monkeys. steban being the captain did a very good job. you can book at the shandrani beachcomber with oliver on the beach.

ueno ameyoko shopping street offers a vibrant night-time atmosphere with plenty of dining options to suit all tastes. many stores remain open late, and the area stays lively well into the night. its close proximity to the shopping mall adds further convenience, and easy access to the nearby train station makes it an ideal spot for both locals and tourists. a great destination for evening strolls, street food, and shopping.

unacceptable service – completely unprofessional and unaccommodating i’ve done escape rooms all over the world — in europe, the us, and asia — and i’ve never experienced anything like this. we arrived slightly late for our booking (we were a group of six), and while we fully understand that punctuality is important, what followed was completely uncalled for. we rang the bell multiple times and waited outside for 40 minutes — yet no one came to the door. no staff, no message, no contact. just silence. there wasn’t even the decency of someone opening the door to speak with us. it felt incredibly petty and childish — like we were being deliberately ignored rather than treated like paying customers. every other escape room i’ve visited has been welcoming, flexible, and professional, even when we’ve been a few minutes late. this was the only place where we were met with such cold, passive-aggressive behavior. if you’re thinking of booking here — don’t. there are plenty of amazing escape rooms in london run by people who actually value their customers. this is not one of them.

undeniably legendary. this place has real presence and even for a few moments i hope you are struck by what “history” really means. you don’t have to study it. you don’t need a special tour. this is what humans do given time and pride and enough cooperation. religion, government, society… it’s all just people cooperating to create monuments both real and imagined. take it all in. breathe out. stand where so many have stood. this is an important place and i hope we continue to respect and protect it. stamped on these lifeless things are the hands and the hearts of people just like us from so long ago. and there is so much more history to write, if only we understood what it’s like to make it. enjoy. 🏛️

underrated gem with peaceful vibes and rich history changgyeonggung palace (창경궁) is a beautiful and often underrated historical site in seoul. it’s less crowded than other major palaces, which makes for a peaceful and relaxed visit where you can really soak in the surroundings at your own pace. the architecture is elegant and well-preserved, and the palace grounds are spacious with plenty of open areas, ponds, and trees — especially lovely in spring and autumn. it’s a great place to stroll, take photos, and learn about joseon dynasty history without the big crowds. if you're looking for a quieter alternative to gyeongbokgung or changdeokgung, this is a perfect spot to explore. highly recommended for history lovers, photographers, or anyone wanting a calm break in the middle of the city. more pics at my ig: @ogolphotos

unexpectedly, i found myself wandering through the botanical garden, away from the main entrance. this expansive, well-maintained garden is a delightful surprise. while the majority of visitors stick to the more popular paths, the quieter, forested areas offer a truly authentic nature experience. the garden is thoughtfully designed to be accessible to visitors of all abilities, with well-paved paths and gentle slopes. it's a perfect place to immerse yourself in the lush greenery, admire the diverse plant life, and simply relax. i particularly enjoyed the back section of the garden, where the dense forest creates a serene and secluded atmosphere. despite being the rainy season, the weather was ideal for a leisurely stroll. it's a fantastic opportunity for all ages to connect with nature without the need for strenuous hiking or long journeys.

unforgettable 3d2n el nido to coron trip (july 2–4, 2025) a huge thank you to team dugong—especially our amazing guide elmar—for an unforgettable 3-day, 2-night adventure from el nido to coron. we had such a great time and will be talking about this trip for a long time to come. right from the start, the whole crew made us feel welcome and completely at ease. elmar was kind, funny, and always made sure everyone was comfortable. the vibe onboard was just perfect—professional, yet warm, relaxed, and fun. we got to explore so many incredible places: snorkeling and freediving in crystal-clear waters (saw many species incl. turtle, barracuda, clownfish, trumpetfish, eel etc.), lounging on remote beaches, cliff jumping, kayaking through mangroves, and swimming beneath a waterfall. one of the biggest highlights was the camp bonfire night, followed by a fantastic fire show performed by two crew members - so impressive and such a fun surprise! the food throughout the trip was absolutely delicious, with plenty of variety and thoughtful options. drinks—both alcoholic and non-alcoholic—were available, and we really appreciated that there was zero pressure to drink. the evenings were laid-back and cozy. since karaoke isn’t really our thing, we were grateful that the crew let us just hang out, play cards, and enjoy each other’s company. special thanks to elmar for teaching us the card game cambio/dutch—we’re hooked and still playing it regularly! and of course, we can’t forget dugong, the boat dog! her hilarious personality had us smiling the entire trip—such a quirky and lovable presence. thank you again to the entire team dugong for an amazing trip. we can’t recommend this experience enough. with love and thanks, bettina, marie, aleks & sondre

unforgettable adventure from start to finish.. the cruise was a total blast packed with fun, stunning views, and gill vibes all around. the only downside was that the ac in room wasn't working, it got pretty warm night, especially while the boat was moving at full speed, which made sleeping a bit uncomfortable it you're booking, i recommend choosing a room toward the front of the shared cabin where there's better airflow or a fan just in case the ac doesn't hold up. that said i'm only dropping one star for that because evryting else totally made up for it l, the sunset and sunrise were magical. the food exceeded my expectations (yes, you can go back for second/, and the atmosphere on the boat want cheerful and full of great energy, the highlight, meeting wild komodo dragons and connecting with awesome fellow traveler. is joined solo, but left with new friends and amazing memories. one the best trips i've ever done 100% recommended and i'd absolutely do it again

unforgettable adventure on the tuolumne river with sierra mac! sierra mac is a family-owned operation, led by marty and tom and it shows. everything felt personal, intentional and deeply rooted in a love for the river that they share with guests. the tuolumne is fortunate to have great stewards in the mcdonnell family, preserving the beauty and experience for future generations. this was my second trip with sierra mac and i look forward to bringing family and friends for years to come. our guides - jordan, andrew and jackson - were absolute legends. not only were they technically excellent and deeply knowledgeable, but they seamlessly became part of our group's vibe. they struck the perfect balance of safety and stoke - reading the river like poetry, sharing stories and laughs, and keeping the energy high and adventure close! these gentlemen demonstrated an admirable commitment to their craft and always kept the guest experience at the forefront. the biggest surprise on your first trip with sierra mac will likely be the food; it will blow you away. restaurant-quality food served in the middle of the wilderness added a layer of comfort (and really comfy chairs!). big shout-out to armando who preps all the meals for the guides to cook up on the trip. you may find yourself looking forward to the food as much as the rapids! if you're looking for a real adventure - one that is expertly guided, deeply human and absolutely unforgettable - go with sierra mac. you'll come for the rapids, but you'll leave with something much more.

unforgettable buggying adventure in the agafay desert! we had the most incredible experience going buggying in the agafay desert – it completely exceeded our expectations. from start to finish, everything was perfectly organised. the people were so warm, welcoming, and genuinely accommodating, making sure we felt safe, comfortable, and excited for the ride. the trail itself was absolutely amazing – a perfect balance of thrill and beauty. we drove through wide, open landscapes with just the right mix of challenge and fun. but the true highlight? the views. they were absolutely breathtaking – endless desert stretches, rolling dunes, and golden tones under the moroccan sun. it felt like we were in another world. this experience was a perfect blend of adventure and natural beauty, and we can’t recommend it highly enough. if you’re looking for something unforgettable, this is it!

unforgettable desert safari experience! i had an amazing time with next trip travel llc on their desert safari tour. from the moment we were picked up in a comfortable 4x4 to the thrilling dune bashing ride, everything was well organized and professional. the guide was friendly and knowledgeable, making the experience even more enjoyable. the views during sunset over the dunes were absolutely breathtaking 🌅, and the camp activities—like camel rides, henna, and live performances—were top-notch. the bbq dinner had a great variety of delicious food, and the vibe was authentic and lively. if you're visiting dubai and want a true taste of desert adventure, i highly recommend booking with next trip travel llc. worth every dirham!

unforgettable desert safari in dubai! we had an amazing experience on the desert safari definitely a highlight of our trip! our guide aman was super friendly, attentive, and made sure we felt comfortable the whole time. everything was well organized and absolutely suitable for kids. a must do adventure highly recommended. thank you, aman!

unforgettable dive adventure – spirit of freedom is truly next level if you’re dreaming of diving the great barrier reef in a way that’s immersive, luxurious, and soul-stirring, spirit of freedom is the liveaboard experience that turns that dream into reality. we joined the charter from lizard island to osprey and bougainville reefs, and every moment exceeded expectation. the reefs were bursting with life—vibrant, colorful coral gardens stretched endlessly, alive with fish of every shape and shade. and then came the magic: a pod of minke whales, gracefully gliding past us in one of those once-in-a-lifetime encounters that leaves you speechless underwater. the vessel itself was beautifully maintained and comfortable, but what truly elevated the experience was the international crew—warm, funny, and wildly competent. from dive briefings to post-dive banter, they made us feel like part of a global family. the food? phenomenal. every meal felt like it came out of a boutique restaurant kitchen. they catered thoughtfully and consistently over-delivered. a personal highlight for me: i completed both my advanced open water and nitrox certifications on board, and the instruction was thorough, supportive, and highly personalized. the staff accommodated every need with genuine care. ryan >> thanks for your immense patience! spirit of freedom isn’t just a dive trip—it’s a floating community of ocean lovers, unforgettable memories, and pure joy. if you’re serious about diving and ready for something truly special, this is it.

unforgettable el yunque experience with maddy! our tour of el yunque with maddy was absolutely incredible. from the moment we stepped into the van, everything was seamless the ride was clean, spacious, and comfortable, setting a great tone for the day. maddy brought such vibrant energy and was incredibly informative throughout the tour. he has a natural gift for teaching and made sure everyone felt included and safe every step of the way. he clearly explained what to expect next, ensured nothing was left behind, and answered every question with patience and care. what truly stood out was maddy’s deep respect and love for the rainforest. he took the time to educate us on the ecosystem, including why wearing mosquito repellent during the day is unnecessary and how some repellents can harm the rainforest. his thoughtful approach really made me appreciate the importance of preserving this beautiful natural space. this tour was more than just a hike—it was an inspiring, educational, and fun experience. if you’re considering a visit to el yunque, don’t miss the chance to go with maddy. it’s truly a must!

unforgettable experience – a true highlight of our us trip the grand canyon was hands down the highlight of our entire trip to the us. it’s one of the most awe-inspiring natural wonders i’ve ever visited. we started at mather point, which is an incredible viewing spot—you can honestly spend hours just admiring the view from there. from mather point, we began our hike along the rim trail, which took us about two hours to complete. the trail is easy to follow and offers constant views of the canyon, with plenty of photo opportunities along the way. the changing light and perspectives make every section unique. highly recommended for anyone visiting the grand canyon—even if you’re not into intense hiking, this trail is a must-do.

unforgettable experience – incredible food & amazing people! our 4-day tao expedition from el nido to coron was hands down one of the best experiences we had in the philippines. it’s a back-to-basics trip, but in the best way—simple yet unforgettable. the food was incredible, easily the best we had in the philippines. every meal was fresh, flavorful and cooked with so much care. whether it was seafood, veggies, or local specialties, there was something for everyone. what made the trip even better was the people. our guides, christian and alvin, were absolutely fantastic—knowledgeable, fun, and always making sure everyone had a great time. whether you’re traveling solo or with friends, the mix of like-minded travelers and the welcoming crew made it feel like one big adventure together. there was a great balance of activity and downtime—snorkeling, island-hopping, fishing, and even making shell bracelets with the locals. and of course, plenty of time to just relax on a beach with a coconut in hand. if you’re looking for a unique, off-the-grid experience with amazing food and great company, this is it. worth every penny!

( a bit scary at first, but fun once you step on it.) the tower is well organized with smooth ticketing and helpful staff. the high speed elevator ride up is quick and exciting. i visited in the evening, when the city lights up.

unforgettable family experience! we went on the arielle glass bottom boat tour with my wife and son — and it was an amazing experience from start to finish. the places we visited were stunning, and we got to feed the fish, spot rays, turtles, and so many colorful species through the glass bottom. the staff was absolutely adorable — warm, friendly, and even offered us food, which wasn’t part of the package. a beautiful, family-friendly activity we’ll never forget. highly recommended!

unforgettable fun at trans studio bali – flying over indonesia steals the show! trans studio bali in denpasar is a must-visit for families and thrill-seekers! the park is impeccably clean, bursting with energy, and the staff are incredibly welcoming. the rides are exhilarating, and the food options are tasty, offering a great mix of local and international dishes. nestled in trans studio mall, it’s perfect for a full day of fun, dining, and shopping. the absolute highlight is flying over indonesia—a jaw-dropping 7-minute virtual paragliding experience soaring over indonesia’s stunning landscapes and cultural treasures in vivid 8k resolution. highly recommend this amazing destination for an action-packed, memorable day!

unforgettable greek adventure! i can't recommend this experience enough! the helicopter ride from mykonos to santorini was breathtaking, and pairing it with the speedboat tour around greece and the luxury driving tour made for an absolutely perfect day. from the moment we booked until our final drop-off, everything was seamless and incredibly enjoyable. thanos was fantastic with his recommendations, ensuring we made the most of our trip. the pilot, george formerly flew fighter jets and made you feel so comfortable during the helicopter ride. our driver, juliano with kostas, was not only kind and informative but also went the extra mile to capture some truly beautiful photos for us. and a huge shout-out to nikos, the skipper from black swan yachts, and his delightful dog, dior – they were a real treat! this was truly an unforgettable day trip and a highlight of our time in greece! aegean vip should be everyone’s first stop to booking experiences in greece.

unforgettable kilimanjaro climb – 6-day machame route climbing mount kilimanjaro was one of the most unforgettable adventures of my life. we did the 6-day trek via the machame route, starting from machame gate and making our final summit push from kosovo camp. i was part of a group of 14 trekkers from all over the worldl, and i’m proud to say everyone made it to the summit – uhuru peak, the highest point in africa! the route was incredibly scenic — from lush rainforests to alpine deserts and snow-covered slopes near the top. every day brought something new. highlights included the challenging barranco wall, the peaceful karanga camp, and of course, standing on the roof of africa at 5,895 meters. the local guides and porters were outstanding — supportive, experienced, and truly the heart of the journey. reaching the summit together with my group was an emotional and proud moment. if you’re dreaming of climbing kilimanjaro, i highly recommend the machame route. it’s physically demanding but incredibly rewarding. a once-in-a-lifetime experience!

unforgettable musandam khasab dhow cruise! our dhow cruise to the musandam khasab peninsula with "durar kumzar tours" was absolutely unforgettable! we were thrilled to see playful dolphins swimming around our boat. the snorkeling was incredible, with clear waters revealing vibrant coral reefs and colorful fish. swimming in the serene sea was a refreshing escape. the crew was exceptional, providing great service and insights about the local marine life. this cruise was the highlight of our trip – a must-do for anyone visiting the region!

unforgettable panoramas: a must-visit for city views 5 stars ascend to new heights and immerse yourself in breathtaking vistas at lookout point in victoria peak garden. this iconic vantage point offers unparalleled panoramic views of hong kong's cityscape, harbor, and surrounding islands. here's what makes it an essential stop: 1) unrivaled views: perched atop victoria peak, lookout point provides a bird's-eye perspective of the city's sprawling skyline, with its towering skyscrapers, bustling harbor, and verdant hills. the vibrant energy of hong kong comes alive before your eyes, creating a mesmerizing spectacle. 2) serene tranquility: despite its prime location, lookout point offers a surprisingly peaceful escape from the urban bustle. the lush gardens surrounding the lookout create a tranquil atmosphere, inviting you to relax and soak in the sights and sounds of the city. 3) iconic landmark: as part of the renowned victoria peak garden, lookout point holds historical significance as a popular recreational spot for locals and visitors alike. its enduring charm and captivating views have made it a beloved landmark for generations. 4) easy accessibility: the lookout point is easily accessible by foot or public transportation, making it a convenient destination for all visitors. a short walk from the peak tram terminus leads you to this scenic gem, where you can savor the panoramic beauty of hong kong. don't miss it! if you're seeking panoramic views that will take your breath away, lookout point in victoria peak garden is an absolute must-visit. its breathtaking vistas, serene atmosphere, and historical significance make it an unforgettable experience

unforgettable private mount batur sunrise tour with parno we reached out to parno to book a private sunrise trek to mount batur, and the experience was absolutely amazing. communication was smooth and easy from the beginning. we asked if he could expand the tour beyond just the volcano, and he suggested some fantastic additions like waterfall swimming and coffee tasting — all of which made the day even more special. he picked us up from canggu early in the morning, and everything was well-organized and stress-free. for our group of six, we had two guides, which felt much safer and more personal than the large group tours we saw. both guides spoke excellent english and shared interesting facts about the volcano and the local area. at the summit, they provided breakfast, tea, and warm blankets — a very thoughtful touch. all entrance fees for the hike and the additional activities were included, which made everything super convenient. we couldn’t have asked for a better experience. if you’re thinking about trekking mount batur, definitely book with parno!

unforgettable sailing experience with the amazing viktoria! we were a group of 10 girls from cyprus on a bachelorette trip, and this sailing day was by far the highlight of it all! the boat was spacious, super clean, and perfect for a day full of sun, music, laughs, and unforgettable moments. viktoria, our skipper, was absolutely incredible. so professional, friendly, and full of positive energy ! she made us feel safe and relaxed from the very beginning. she took us to stunning spots , chilling, and taking the most beautiful photos. she had the perfect balance of guiding the trip while giving us the freedom to enjoy it our own way. it was a magical day for the bride-to-be and for all of us .we laughed, danced, and created memories that we’ll cherish forever. thank you viktoria for everything !you made our experience truly special. we’re already dreaming about doing it again! 💙

unforgettable santorini cruise – as sky blue as the boat! from the moment we stepped aboard the stunning sky-blue boat, we knew we were in for something special. the entire experience was nothing short of magical. the staff welcomed us with warm smiles and genuine hospitality, making everyone feel relaxed and cared for right away. the views were absolutely breathtaking—crystal-clear waters, dramatic cliffs, and those iconic whitewashed villages perched high above the caldera. every moment felt like a postcard coming to life. we cruised along the coast, discovering hidden gems and scenic coves that we never would have found on our own. one of the highlights was definitely the swimming spots. the water was the perfect temperature, and we had plenty of time to jump in, float, and enjoy the peaceful beauty around us. the crew provided everything we needed and made sure everyone felt comfortable and safe. if you’re visiting santorini, this cruise is a must. whether you’re looking to relax, explore, or just take in some of the most stunning views in the world, this tour delivers. truly one of the best experiences of our trip!

used to be a 5 stars for me. i have visited this park many times. i love exploring the nature, the secluded temple, the nursery, grass fields, trees, moss path, etc. the weather is pleasant as it is located on higher ground. there are less or no crowds inside. the previous procedure was that cars were allowed to go in and we paid tickets for the humans and the car. july 2025 visit drops 4 stars for me:: 1. we came here during weekdays. during weekdays cars are not allowed inside the park, while it's allowed on the weekend. i would say the other way around should be implemented, if you want to implement this at all. there should be a significant less crowd on weekday. 2. so, on top of paying for ticket (which is also more expensive), you have to rent transport. yes, you can go in by foot, but if you have visited this park before, walking wouldn't get you far because this place is huge. if you are fit and want to exercise, it's perfect, i think it would be good, no sarcasm. however, if you want to have a relaxing day, physically less able to, bring young kids, elderly, this is not an option, unless you just hang around nearby. you have to have transport, this brings me to point number 3. 3. you can rent bicycle/electric bike (30-75k/hour depending on types), or bus (25k pp one route) or golf car (250k max 4 people per hour). see pictures. so, if you have physical limitation, you can only go with golf car or bus. the bus only serves one route which you can choose. this means one destination and back, that's all. if you know this place, this is utterly ridiculous and overpriced. there are many spots to visit but there is no option to drop by or do multi-route. you want to visit another spot? go back to the start and buy another bus ticket. since we brought elderly and guest and wanted to visit multiple place, we had no choice but to rent a golf car which is ridiculously expensive as well because one hour barely covers anything here. the safety standard was also horrible, we got the one without handle at the rear which we only realized after we saw the others. the terrain is up and down, one can easily fall down on slope. we ended up only visit two spots that were next to each other and we had to rush it. we had to grab the side bars like monkeys. no joke, i don't think this is safe when the terrain is up. i was very worried for my mom's safety since we were sitting on the back. 4. i'm all for conservation and dedication to the park, but with all the cost that make this place very expensive now in proportion to the standard, there is barely any facilities or improvement. there are many holes on the road, lack of restroom facilities inside. the is no emergency procedure which should be much more important now since we barely see anyone inside because of the inaccessibility. there is no map and we couldn't find some spots even though we are regular. we used to take our time to visit them, now by getting lost once or twice, the time was up. if they want to make this place more natural, less cars (wasn't a problem previously because the place is huge), there should be shuttle that go around the spots and they shouldn't charge by route, but it should be unlimited because that would be the only way for guests to visit all the spots they want. i think this would make it less natural compared to few cars in between here and there. so everything doesn't make sense to me for now. will i come again? van phuc silk village, also known as the silk village of hanoi, offers a captivating glimpse into vietnam’s rich textile heritage. situated approximately 10 kilometres southwest of hanoi’s city centre, this historic village has been a hub for silk weaving for over a millennium . ￼ upon entering through the traditional red-brick gate, visitors are greeted by a vibrant scene: colourful umbrellas suspended above the streets, bustling silk shops, and the rhythmic clatter of looms in operation. the village’s artisans produce a variety of silk products, including scarves, garments, and accessories, each reflecting meticulous craftsmanship . ￼ a highlight of the visit is observing the silk-making process firsthand. from raising silkworms to weaving and dyeing, the traditional methods employed here have been preserved through generations . the village also hosts the van phuc silk festival annually in november, featuring cultural performances, exhibitions, and a lively atmosphere that celebrates its enduring legacy .

vera did an amazing job arranging a last minute hour long boat tour of the canals and for us to be dropped off at a roof-top restaurant for our 40th anniversary. it was all inclusive. this was due to our other supper experience being cancelled by the vendor. i would have given a 5 except for two things: one, the boat driver dropped us off at the pick-up spot after the canal tour instead of the restaurant private dock. we tried to explain that we did not know where the restaurant was or even the name and that he was to take us there. he said he did not know english. i asked him to call vera. he did not so i did. he just left. vera called him for us and had him come back and take us to where we were supposed to be ushered to the upper terrace as what was supposed to be arranged. it was described as being private which it was not. it was still nice. the second reason is that it was very expensive and was not near worth the cost. we appreciate that we paid for someone else to make last minute arrangements for us but i accidentally saw what the company was charged for the food and wine. also, the water taxi we took later was nicer than the boat that did the tour and the water taxi was cheap. i multiplied the water taxi by six for an estimated cost for one hour. in the end, it was a great night and we appreciated the help setting it up and the restaurant was very accommodating to my husband’s gluten free requirements. i just wish i had arranged it myself and saved quite a few euros. i just ran out of time to do so. when you pay extra (and that is not usual for us) you expect quite a bit. if we had paid less maybe it would not bother me as much. that’s an honest opinion. you pay for the convenience sometimes but it did not dampen our spirits. vera was a dear and i appreciated the help.

very beautiful and unique work done by gaudi. just amazing to see he did this back in the early 1900s, the design and the creative mind is truly astonishing. it’s definitely a piece of art even to this day! i was very happy to visit this place and see it in person. the audio self guided tour is very simple and easy to use. each room tells you more than what the eye sees and a small story behind it. i do wish there were earphones rather than just holding it against your ear. we visited around 5:30 on a weekday and it was not overly crowded but still decently busy. when we left, it was definitely busier but not sure if that was general public or for an event as they were starting to do a setup inside when we were there. the only thing i don’t truly understand is there ticketing system. the different options should be better explained. and the packages that are sold on external websites are also just as confusing so we bought the basic standard tickets but it would be nice to understand the other tickets so we could have enjoyed it even more. they also do not allow stroller inside so you can hold your baby or they have baby carriers for you to use. but we could not figure out the carrier; it just wasn’t comfortable for our baby so either come prepared with extra time to figure it out so your baby is comfortable, especially if your baby is 1+ year or bring your own to enjoy the experience properly as holding your baby for 45-60 mins is not ideal.

very comprehensive museum covering the expanse of history and prehistory in relation to greece and war. beginning with neolithic artifacts, moving through the bronze age through the 20th century, this museum has artifacts, diorama, uniforms, and an enormous collection of weaponry from all over the world. there is also a section dedicated to alexander the great. as of july 2025, there is a special exhibition on the greek war of independence. this museum covers history as well as biographies of particular greeks. the 20th century includes the balkan wars, both world wars, the korean war, and the turkish invasion of cyprus in 1974. there are many disturbing important photos depicting civilians' struggles during wartime. this museum is an excellent counterpart of the greek national museum. we spent four hours here and did not see everything.

very disappointed by the "speed and relaxation tour" and would not recommend it at all. we did other tours in smaller places during our stay in levi and it was so much nicer. here everything seems to be made to make money without any magic for the tourists. the "speed" part of the tour was almost ok with a nice person taking care of the dogs but only one sleigh for an entire group so we had to wait during 7 tours. while we waited it was not possible to do anything else, like having a look at the other huskies, because other husky tours were arriving all the time so we had to stay in a very small area not to be in their way. the husky tour was short (maybe 3 to 4 minutes) but it was ok because it was the speed part of the tour. the real problem was the "relaxation" part with the reindeers. the team taking care of the reindeers was really unpleasant with us and we didn't feel welcome at all. we had a long talk about all the things we shouldn't do during the tour, as if we were completely dumb tourists, and then an extremely short tour, shorter than the lesson about how we should behave and shorter than the "speed" tour with the dogs. and again very rude staff at the end of this tour. so no relaxation at all. it was the most expensive thing we did in levi and the most disappointing one.

very disappointed by their handling of customer credit card information. i rented a waterproof jacket here and was asked to provide my full credit card details — including the cvv security code — handwritten on a piece of paper as a deposit. i was shocked that such an outdated and risky practice is still being used. this is absolutely not in line with basic credit card security standards. when i returned the jacket and asked to have my sensitive card information returned or destroyed properly, the staff member tore the paper in front of me and tossed it in the bin, all while smiling and saying “have a good one.” it felt dismissive and disrespectful, especially considering the seriousness of the issue. if you’re a traveler concerned about your financial safety, i would strongly advise against providing full card details in this way. the shop should really update their procedures to follow modern, secure practices like digital pre-authorizations or refundable deposits — not insecure handwritten records. i rarely write negative reviews, but this was unacceptable.

very good experience at this hammam! it was our first time in morocco and we wanted to try a hammam. was a little nervous and unsure on what to expect so here's a rundown: i reserved the soin nour el hammam (the most basic of all options) the night before. the location is very central, a few mins walk from jemma el-fnaa. we arrived and checked in, waited for 5 mins~ before being taken to the changing room (private area). we took our clothes off (but kept underwear on) and put them in the spacious lockers provided. each locker also has 2 bathrobes to put on. afterwards, we were taken to a very steamy, hot room where 2 women washed us and scrubbed us with black soap, then left us for 10mins. when they came back they scrubbed us with a glove, which was very good and thorough with a lot of pressure, they put some more soaps + masks on us then left us in the hot room for another 10-15 mins then finally washed us off. we got very steamy and sweaty (which is the point ofc) afterwards we sat in our robes and drank some lovely mint tea while we cooled down. all in all, a great experience for only 280 dh each. wish we bought massages too! what we didn't expect: we did take our bras off when we got to the hot room, but it was just us in there so it was private. also our underwear got wet, which was a little annoying on the way home. i wouldn't say this place is exactly hijab friendly, yes it's only ladies that do the massages etc but the cool-down area is a mixed space

very important: read this before booking. i was going to book this company for their "the best of raja ampat" one day tour. i did not stay at their accommodation. thankfully before paying i thought to ask some important questions about toilet breaks and toilet facilities. they do not voluntarily disclose this information unless pushed, so in the spirit of full public transparency and so prospective customers can arm themselves with important information before they book (rather than discover it after they've paid) i've decided to post this review. first off all they do not own or operate a "speed boat" as per the definition that is commonly understood in western countries. it is more akin to an oversized long boat. it has a canopy that provides some protection from the sun but it's mostly open so is unprotected from the elements (wind, rain and noise). in its defense, it is twin engine, which does give it some speed but again it certainly isn't a speed boat. most importantly of all however, it does not have a toilet. the longest stretch of water on this tour is between waisai and piaynemo. on this boat (which can take a maximum of 10 people, 8 passengers and 2 crew) this journey takes about 2 hours. when i asked customer service on whatsapp (from memory her name was caressa and she was based in the netherlands) what a passenger is supposed to do if they needed the toilet (either no.1 or no.2) during the 2 hours journey, this was her answer: "there is no possibility to go to the toilet you are on the open sea, you have to wait until you are at the next stop. we have had a person before for whom this was important and advised to book a speed boat with toilet, they then rented a private speed boat but that is high costs." i think this is extremely important information that is deliberately withheld from potential customers. if it was only a 30 minute journey that would be a different story but the reality is families with children, the elderly or perhaps someone with traveller's diarrhoea should definitely be made aware that a toilet break "is not a possibility" for 2 hours. i left a 3 star review because up until the point that i asked about toilet breaks, customer service on whatsapp was very attentive and helpful. and i am sure based on previous reviews that luzo tours offer a satisfactory economical tour of raja ampat. however based on victoria peak offers an absolutely stunning view over hong kong — definitely one of the best cityscapes you can find. from the top, the skyline, the harbor, and the mountains all blend into a breathtaking panorama, especially around sunset. it's a must-visit spot if you're in the city. however, be prepared for large crowds. the area gets extremely busy, especially during peak hours. long lines are common, both for the peak tram and the observation deck. it can feel quite hectic and a bit overwhelming. another downside is the commercialized photo spot, where staff try to sell you photos they take of you. they're constantly announcing things on a loudspeaker, which really disturbs the otherwise peaceful moment you might want to have while enjoying the view. in short: amazing views, but the overall experience could be better without the noise, crowds, and commercialization.

victoria peak pavillion: a breathtaking oasis amidst urban beauty 5 stars nestled atop victoria peak, the iconic pavillion offers a unique blend of history, nature, and panoramic views that will leave you mesmerized. here's what makes it an unforgettable experience: 1) historic charm: built in 1910, the pavilion boasts a classic colonial architecture that blends seamlessly with its natural surroundings. its intricate details, arched windows, and elegant stonework evoke a sense of timeless beauty. 2) panoramic views: perched at an elevation of 552 meters (1,811 feet), the pavilion provides breathtaking vistas of hong kong's cityscape, harbor, and surrounding islands. the vibrant energy of the city comes alive before your eyes, creating a mesmerizing spectacle. 3) serene gardens: the pavilion is surrounded by beautifully landscaped gardens, offering a tranquil escape from the urban bustle. stroll along the winding paths, admire the colorful blooms, and relax under the shade of towering trees, creating a peaceful haven amidst the city's excitement. 4) cultural significance: the pavilion has served as a popular recreational spot for over a century, hosting various events and exhibitions. it remains an important cultural landmark, reflecting the city's rich history and heritage. don't miss it! if you're seeking a blend of history, nature, and breathtaking views, victoria peak pavillion is an absolute must-visit. its unique charm, panoramic vistas, and serene atmosphere make it an unforgettable experience.

view @ tokyo metropolitan art museum. . established in 1926 as japan’s first public art museum and founded with financial support from industrialist keitaro sato, the tokyo metropolitan art museum building was designed by modernist architect kunio maekawa. . the museum does not maintain a vast permanent collection, being best known for hosting nearly 300 temporary exhibitions annually, but the small permanent collection of art includes 12 sculptures and 36 calligraphic pieces, featuring japanese artists such as haruo igarashi, bukichi inoue, and kakuzo tatehata. . the unique citizen’s gallery aims to democratize art and foster a vibrant inclusive art community, and is thus designed as an inviting, participatory space where art made by local citizens finds a formal platform within a major cultural institution. . the curated works on display typically cover a broad range of mediums, including painting, sculpture, calligraphy, installation, and even multimedia approaches; reflecting the diverse, everyday experiences of tokyo’s residents.

view @ yamatane museum of art. . founded in 1966 by taneji yamazaki, this is the country's first museum dedicated to the traditional nihonga (japanese watercolour painting) style. . the museum exhibits a small, rotating collection of nihonga works, highlighting the subtle beauty and sophisticated techniques that define this unique art form. . the collection (comprising over 1,800 works, though only a few are displayed at any point) is a carefully curated assemblage that includes traditional watercolours, ukiyo-e prints, oil paintings, and ancient calligraphy.

visited funky chocolate club switzerland and it was a great experience! i tried the profiterole, chocolate waffle, and a café latte – everything tasted super fresh and delicious. i’m not the biggest chocolate fan myself, but my wife loves it, so we gave it a try and we’re happy we did. definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area!
visited here during the dia de muertos and this place had beautifully deceratode altars and papel picado. it was a quick visit but absolutely stunning decorations.

visited here early july, the flowers still in a young stage 🪻🌷🌻💐🌺. you can buy a ticket for riding the chairlift to the top. better check the operating time first as we visited there since 8:30 and still not operated yet. nothing much up there but you can walk around and enjoy the nice scenery and furano view from the top!
visited here on 11 november 2022. dropped off by our uber driver, it is an impressive city gate and the beginning point for an islamic architecture walk towards the bazaar.

visited here while in vacation as we saw it was recommended online. i love the cause and purpose of the exhibit and everyone working there was very helpful. it did seem lacking in some ways though. as beautiful as the are displays were, the tablet we had just seemed very laggy or glitchy. some of the panels in the interactive display were not working, and my vr set kept quitting on me halfway through. it's fun, but maybe not at that price point.

visited here while on vacation in toronto. the experience was fun and there are some great photo opportunities. i'm not sure if i felt the price was worth what there is to do however. the staff seemed friendly but not overly involved at all. they do have a good little gift shop! worth doing if you're in toronto, but don't expect to spend a tonne of time here.
visited hortpark on a sunday evening—peaceful and relaxing with a lovely sunset. great spot for a walk and to unwind after a long week.

visited in april & the entrance was under renovation, therefore not many people noticed this monastery museum. it was a hidden gem as the interiors were absolutely stunning. no photos allowed in the museum except the hallways & garden. included in dubrovnik pass!

visited in april 2025, and it was amazing ! la pedrera was absolutely beautiful. the moment i saw it, i was struck by how unique and dreamlike the whole building felt. the flowing shapes of the stone façade, the iron balconies that almost look like vines—everything felt so alive, like the building was part of nature. inside, it was just as stunning. the way gaudí played with light and space made each room feel open and full of life. it’s one of those places where you keep noticing new details the longer you look. honestly, it didn’t feel like just a building—it felt like walking through a piece of art. gaudí really had a way of turning everyday structures into something magical.

visited in early june. just a couple of rows of flowers in sight. it’s a park but well maintained. free parking onsite.
visited in early june. seems most of the plants have not bloomed. free parking onsite

visited in june 2025 and really enjoyed our visit. a very knowledgeable guide, a lovely factory and superb tea tasting. we took the factory tour (lkr 2.000 per person). this was not our first tea factory visit but definitely one we'd recommend. walkable distance from downtown ella along the main road or of course a tuktuk is a good option. both the visitors' center and the factory are directly on the main road, the google map location is not very precise.

visited in june 2025. it is a buddhist temple and known as the marble temple. ticket price is thb 100 per person. visited in the morning and there was very few tourists. easily reachable by motorbikes and cars.
visited in late spring — the view from the top was beautiful! it's the perfect spot for photos and a great way to take in the charm of old québec.

visited in may 2025, and the museum was quite busy. the view from the top was decent, though not particularly impressive. overall, i enjoyed the visit, but i’d say it’s primarily geared toward families with children rather than adults looking for a traditional museum experience. it’s fun and interactive, but not a place for in-depth exhibitions.

visited in may 2025. this was probably the most touristy thing we did on our trip. the boat was packed like sardines. we were sitting knee to knee with the people across from us. you will get to know some strangers really well. some of the people were getting seasick which made me nervous as i was wondering where they were going to blow with all the people around. the cliffs were very beautiful to see. i feel like the best seats were on the right side of the boat. going out, the right side were closer to the cliffs versus when we came back, we were further away from the cliffs on the left side. the elephant rock was my favorite. we didn't see too many birds on our trip. this was my third favorite boat tour that i took while visiting.
visited in the middle of aug and there were still enough lovely flower. the view from the garden was amazing. after vising the garden went to the cafe and tried sake less ice cream that was tasty!!

visited january 2025 for a hammam, leg and foot massage and head massage. all treatments were excellent with tea and water included. friendly staff. clean. lockers on arrival. easy to email and book directly paid on card plus 2% bank fee. very easy. would definitely return.

visited los túneles 2 years ago which turned out to be the best snorkel tour i had done… then this time managed to top it! swam with eagle rays, turtles, black tip sharks, lots of big white tips too, a seahorse and even saw mantas and a potential galapagos or tiger shark (both from boat not snorkelling). 100% would recommend and the price has only increased by $10 in 2 years so you really can’t argue the value for money!

visited maligne lookout in may 2025. honestly, it was sad to see so many trees burned out from last year’s wildfire. the damage is really noticeable. would only recommend visiting if you’re interested in seeing the impact of the wildfire—there’s not much of the usual scenic beauty left right now.

visited marina mall recently, and i have to say — it’s one of those places that feels low-key luxe without trying too hard. it’s not massive like dubai mall, but that’s exactly why i like it. you can actually breathe, walk around without bumping into a crowd every two seconds, and still find all your favourites. there’s a good mix of shopping — high street, a few luxury names, and just enough variety to keep you browsing. but what i always enjoy here is the overall vibe. it’s calm, clean, and everything feels easy. you can come here alone, with friends, or even with family — and it works every time. the location is a win too. right by the water, with that little tower section where you get the best views if you feel like going up. and if you’re in the mood for a coffee or a bite, there are some solid options — whether you want something quick or a proper sit-down with a view.

visited marrakesh from canada, and it was a great experience. i recommended it. they came to pick us up and we're on time and actually dropped us back at our hotel. the owner was very nice he shared his life story with us and made sure we were happy with the experience. his staff muhammad was a very reliable guide and took great picture of us as you can see below. we stopped halfway for great snacks and morrocan tea and we enjoyed the sunset.

visited maruyama park in early spring while there was still snow on the ground, and it was absolutely magical. the park was peaceful and quiet, with snow-covered trees and paths that made it feel like a winter wonderland. it’s a great spot for a calm walk and taking in the beauty of nature even in the colder months. the nearby hokkaido shrine surrounded by snow was especially beautiful. definitely worth visiting even before the cherry blossoms bloom!

visited may 14, 2025. a very walk-friendly park. still could catch the last glimsp of the cherry blossom. thereès a shrine, souvenir shop (with local sweets/cakes). public toilets are free and very clean.
visited may 2025. beautiful waterfall in the city. this is a great place to visit. so peaceful and not far from the capital. totally worth the trip.
visited may 2025. beautiful waterfall in the city. this is a great place to visit. so peaceful and not far from the capital. totally worth the trip.

visited may 2025. this was our last hike in the faroe islands before we left. two magical weeks ending on a high note. there is a nice big parking lot available. you can pay your hiking fee in the office. they also have a gift shop with food and drinks. there were some cattle at the beginning of the hike like 10 ft away from the path which was really cool to see. the hike is longer than others, but it is relatively flat getting out to the viewpoints. it is a dirt and rock path with rolling little hills. there are a couple water runoff paths to traverse but you won't get wet. you hike along the lake, so there are plenty of old houses and graves to see on your way. at the viewpoints at the end, you will need to hike a steep incline to get up to the top. the views are amazing. there was little rain in the two weeks we were there, so the waterfall wasn't flowing. we still went down to see it. there are a bunch of large rocks to hike around to get there. i would walk west to try and get the best viewpoint of the falls. if you walk right to the falls the view is clipped.

visited mec today to pick up a pair of hiking boots that were on sale. the store was quite busy, so i didn’t expect much assistance . the boots were just sitting on a table on the first floor, so i grabbed my size and headed to the cashier. when i asked if i could get a bag or box to carry them (since i had a 30-minute walk home), i was told “no” without any other option offered. it felt a bit ridiculous that nothing , not even a reusable shopping bag was available to help customers carry their purchase, especially for something bulky like boots. i couldn’t help but feel like i was being treated differently because it was a sale item. then i walked over to another counter, and a kind staff member found a plastic bag from the trash to help me out. i really appreciated his effort, but overall the experience was disappointing. i get it the store is clean and offers a wide range of products. but honestly, train your staff better. a little empathy and problem solving would go a long way lmao

visited monkey jungle on a sunday morning- no line, no wait; very peaceful. staff is very friendly and knowledgeable. the shows are informative and fun. can’t wait to come back and do the guided tour where you interact with the monkeys… the group ahead of us looked like they were having a wonderful time. our favorite part was learning about their way of living and feeding them, so adorable. they also have a reptile and amazonian rainforest presentation. the gift shop has a wide selection of souvenirs and memorable gifts.

visited on 21st march 2025, introduced by local people. i don't find this place from any post nor any information from youtube. thank you the local driver brought us to this beautiful natural scene, they have temple, rice terrace, small waterfall and of course many stair cases. i went there on friday, no crowds, free and easy to walk around. please go down stairs until the end, you will see the beautiful temple with nice weather.
visited on 6 may 2025 alongwith family. nice place . everywhere the " door to heaven". must see while in bali.

visited on 7/11/25 from arizona. there are more geysers in yellowstone than anywhere else on earth! however, old faithful is the most famous. we arrived at old faithful at 6:22pm and unfortunately it had just erupted at 6:03pm. barely missed it. while we killed time waiting for the next eruption, we went shopping in the visitor center. there’s also a free museum that did a great job of explaining geysers. there’s a nice board walk that goes around all the geysers. gorgeous scenery and a peaceful walk. there’s plenty of benches near old faithful so you can get a good view. the estimated time for eruption was 7:43pm but that’s give or take 13 min. old faithful ended up erupting at 8:03pm. exactly 2 hours from the previous eruption. it lasted 4 minutes! it was incredible! it shot up so high too! the longer the interval between eruptions, the bigger/better the eruption! since there was 2 hours of time between each, old faithful didn’t disappoint with its 4 minute show. this is a must see when you’re at yellowstone!

visited on a leisurely sunday afternoon and was pleasantly surprised by the absence of crowds. purchasing tickets online was smooth and effortless. the staff were exceptionally friendly and efficient. why not a perfect five stars, you might wonder? the admission price was a bit steep, which gave me pause, as the experience its self is around 20 minutes.

visited on a monday afternoon and it was packed. i enjoyed the architecture however i cannot imagine how disturbing it must be for the locals as even though there some locals telling you to be quiet it is just too busy. it’s closed between 5pm and 10am as well as sunday.

visited on a rainy day when even the squirrels were taking shelter, so there wasn’t a great deal of wildlife to see, but the garden is peaceful and well looked after. it’ll depend on the time of year as to what you see, but it’s a nice way to spend an hour or two walking around and experiencing japanese nature. the garden has a long history and a big shop and a small cafe are attached.

visited on a weekday afternoon around 1-2pm and this area is a large outdoor shopping street with many types of shop. they include shops which sell fresh or dried fruits, seafood, drugs/ convenience store, shops which sell local snacks, crackers, candies, bags, and also cafes, restaurants with good prices. it’s recommended to have a look at shop listing on google maps before heading there as it’s easy to get lost. this area is a short walk (cross one pedestrain traffic to ueno train station). hope to be back again in future and try at least the pizza shop there! prices within shops selling for example vitamin, medicine and beauty products can vary, they also have tax refund available for some shops and usually shopkeepers can speak either chinese or another language as well to cater to travellers. please like this review or share your own experience after visiting!

visited on a weekday afternoon in june after lunch. the weather was chilly but pleasant, perfect for a light walk. the pond wasn’t frozen and the water was truly blue. it was a spectacular sight in person. we overheard a few tour guides explaining that the color comes from aluminum sediments in the water, which were washed down from a nearby waterfall. a neat little fact, and yes, there were quite a number of tour groups during our visit. that said, there is not much else to see beyond the pond itself. it is beautiful, but not a place where you would spend a long time. realistically, you would spend 30 to 60 minutes here at most. parking is not free and is charged in 30-minute blocks, if i remembered correctly. so once you are done with your photos and sightseeing, it is better to head off rather than hang around.

visited on a weekday afternoon so it wasn't crowded. there were shops selling sesame seeds and oil. the smell of sesame oil was very nice. i think they press it in the shops to get the oil. a variety of dried seafood like fish, cuttlefish, octopus, shrimp and freeze dried fruits like strawberries, persimmons, vegetables are sold here. fresh fruits are also sold but not as much as dried ones. of course, seaweed is everywhere too. a nice place to visit and get some good dried produce.

visited on april 6, 2025 beautiful in all seasons. less crowded during sakura season. perfect for picnics. there are fewer number of sakura trees than other famous spots but the trees are well maintained and can enjoy flowers up close. the japanese garden area is absolutely stunning. * entry fee: 500 yen (per person) * no trash cans, bring back all your trash.

visited on july 20, 2025 – this was day 17 of our trip through india. our driver hadi brought us to the hunder sand dunes for the double-humped camel ride experience. we were traveling with our two young daughters, ages 5 and 7. the setting is unique – desert-like sand dunes surrounded by mountains, and the bactrian camels are impressive to see up close. but unfortunately, the experience wasn’t a good one for us. the camel handlers were very insistent that our daughters ride either alone or together, which we didn’t feel was safe given how young and small they are. we asked for one of us to accompany each child, and they were very unhappy about that. one handler kept berating me for the decision, even though there was another camel nearby that looked larger and better suited for doubling up. the whole situation made my 7-year-old very scared. i ended up singing the “sally the camel” song over and over just to keep her calm. she eventually sang along, and that helped. but the ride itself was physically uncomfortable. i couldn’t feel my hands by the end because i was holding onto her so tightly, worried she’d fall. my legs hurt for the rest of the day. we’ve done camel rides in other countries, but this was by far the most uncomfortable. the scenery is beautiful and it’s a unique experience, but i would not recommend it for families with young kids unless the handling practices become more accommodating.
