walking into santa claus village felt like stepping straight into a christmas storybook! from the moment i arrived, i was swept up in the magic-it really does feel like you’ve traveled a million miles away from home into a winter wonderland! whether you're a kid or just a kid at heart, it’s impossible not to get caught up in the excitement of it all! one of my favorite moments was standing right on the arctic circle line-such a surreal and bucket-list experience! i also loved exploring all the little shops and restaurants around the village. there’s a huge variety of things to see, buy, and experience, and everything is super festive! the santa claus post office was another highlight. being able to send postcards stamped from the arctic circle—and even pre-post christmas cards to friends and family around the world - is so cool! you can find reindeer rides, sledding, snowmobiling, and other activities for additional charges that you can sign up for in separate buildings around the property. the only thing that surprised me (in a not-so-magical way) was the state of the restrooms in some of the main areas. for a place that puts so much effort into making everything feel happy and spotless, i think the elves definitely need to step up their cleaning game to keep things as beautiful as the rest of the village! overall, though, santa claus village was everything i hoped it would be! it’s a place i’d recommend to absolutely anyone looking for an unforgettable experience, especially around the holidays. it was truly a magical trip i’ll never forget!

walking into the empire state building, you can feel the history and pride of new york right away. the art deco design is breathtaking, the lobby alone is a work of art, with its intricate details and timeless elegance. once you get to the top, the views are unreal. seeing the city stretch out in every direction makes you realize just how massive and alive new york really is. on top of that, the whole experience is well organized and easy to follow, from the entrance to the elevators to the observation decks. everything runs smoothly, which lets you just enjoy the moment without stress. it’s more than just a famous building, it’s an experience that captures the spirit and energy of the city. a true must-see.

walking through gyeongbokgung palace, i stumbled upon hyangwonjeong pavilion, and it felt like discovering a serene secret tucked away in the busy city. the small hexagonal pavilion, built on a little island in the middle of a tranquil pond, seemed to float peacefully on the water. crossing the wooden chwihyanggyo bridge—aptly named “the bridge intoxicated with fragrance”—i found myself naturally slowing down, taking in the calm surroundings and admiring the elegance of the pavilion. originally built during the reign of king gojong in the late 19th century, it’s a beautiful example of harmony between architecture and nature. i visited in early spring, when the pond was still and the trees just beginning to bloom. the reflections on the water were soft and dreamy, and the entire scene felt like it was straight out of a painting. i later learned that the pavilion even had ondol (traditional korean floor heating), which speaks to the thoughtful design of the joseon era. what i loved most was how peaceful it felt. while the main palace areas were crowded, hyangwonjeong was quiet and almost meditative. i sat on a bench nearby and just watched the koi swim lazily in the pond while soaking in the stillness. if you’re visiting gyeongbokgung, don’t miss this little corner of calm. it’s a beautiful place to take a break, reflect, and enjoy a different side of the palace grounds.

walking through the 1.2 km narrow siq(arabic of canyon) is like stepping back in time, surrounded by history and the impressive natural beauty of the rock formations. the walk through this magical corridor, as it snakes its way towards the hidden city, is one full of anticipation for the wonders ahead. i will recommend to take the walk instead of buggy as it’s truly a unique and unforgettable experience of visiting petra. every turn will make you excited if it’s the turn when treasury can be seen. it’s around 35/40 minutes while you go but may take longer time during return as the it’s bit steeper in some places. take water bottles with you. and please please take a good guide because every spot, stone or curve has some significance and good guide can give you better information.

wander waves is hands down one of the best tour companies i’ve ever booked with! from start to finish, the whole experience was amazing. the team was super friendly, fun, and really made sure everyone was comfortable and having a good time. they were also very accommodating with everyone's needs, which made the trip even more enjoyable. i’ve been to a few snorkeling spots around the philippines before, but nothing comes close to what they showed us. the coral reefs and islands were absolutely breathtaking—like something out of a travel magazine. you can really tell they know the best hidden gems. it honestly felt like a once-in-a-lifetime experience. totally worth every penny. if you’re thinking of booking a snorkeling tour, i highly recommend going with wander waves—you won’t regret it!

wang lang market in bangkok is a true haven for food lovers and shoppers alike! this bustling market offers an authentic slice of local thai life, packed with vibrant energy, mouthwatering food, and endless treasures waiting to be discovered. it’s a paradise for those looking to immerse themselves in the rich culture and flavors of thailand. the food scene here is absolutely incredible. from freshly grilled skewers to aromatic curries, and sweet desserts like mango sticky rice and coconut pancakes, every stall is a feast for the senses. the quality and variety of the food are unbeatable, and the prices are budget-friendly, making it a must-visit for both locals and travelers. the crispy pork belly and pad thai i tried were nothing short of perfection. beyond the food, wang lang market offers a unique shopping experience. you’ll find everything from trendy clothing and accessories to quirky souvenirs and handmade crafts. it’s the perfect place to pick up unique gifts or simply enjoy browsing through the colorful stalls. what i love most about wang lang market is the lively and authentic atmosphere. the friendly vendors, the tantalizing aromas, and the cheerful buzz of locals and visitors create a truly unforgettable experience. if you’re in bangkok and looking to explore beyond the typical tourist spots, wang lang market is an absolute must. you’ll leave with a full stomach, great finds, and memories to cherish!

warning: really hard. anyone who says otherwise is misleading. no shade available in the hot sun. your legs will be absolutely gassed from the 1000+ steps up and 1000 steps down. 3 different people (one in rotc so great shape) had to be helicoptered out while we did the hike. this isn’t like doing a stair master, each step is technical. and then the trek down can be a bit dangerous since your legs are noodles. was with some competitive fitness instructors, marathoners, etc and while it wasn’t “hard” for them it was not easy. this is a difficult and challenging hike. with out of the way, it is also a very cool and unique hike. climbing the stairs/rail line is different and offers a cool and challenging environment. the payoff at the top is incredible views of the crater and the sense of accomplishment having just bested the rail line. definitely would do again, but this is for people who are in shape.

warning: two different trails start from this location. if hiking up stormappstinden, you want to head to the right after the sheep gate. if you end up walking over wooden planks, you are on the wrong trail. don't be like me and hike the wrong trail for thirty minutes before realizing.... the hike is long and steep. took me 2 hours up, 1 hour down. but the view is incredible - one of the best in lofoten. and it's not a particularly popular trail for whatever reason so it's not crowded. i recommend bringing hiking poles, hiking shoes, and a map. the way up is clear but i did briefly lose the trail on the way down (near the summit), and alltrails helped me get back on course. enjoy the hike.

was lucky enough to go with a tour guide and get a full run down of the space - it’s obviously supremely important to many sects and denominations in christianity and the reverence for that was evident - many people were over come with emotions. as well as pointing out various things to us, the guide pointed out some of the possible over zealous aspects too, saying people had fought over the privilege of clearing the area outside the church (including a fight to the death over whether the bottom step was to be cleaned by one group or another) and a bench occupied by a large man in religious robes who sits there all day, because that is his denominations bench and no others are allowed to sit there. it’s amazing to see the various places where jesus’ body was placed and buried, but also to see the reaction of people to those things. it’s also one of the areas where you feel tourism hasn’t taken over - quiet reverence in full effect. make the trip if you ever can

washington place is a greek revival palace in the hawaii capital historic district in honolulu, hawaiʻi. it was where queen liliʻuokalani was arrested during the overthrow of the hawaiian kingdom. later it became the official residence of the governor of hawaiʻi. in 2007, it was designated as a national historic landmark. the current governor's residence was built in 2008 behind the historic residence, and is located on the same grounds as washington place. william little lee made washington place his home from 1849–1854. lee was instrumental in integrating a western legal system in the hawaiian islands, based upon the massachusetts model. lee also authored the great mahele, which introduced private land ownership into hawaiian culture. lydia kamakaeha pākī, the future queen liliʻuokalani and the heir apparent to the throne of the kingdom of hawaiʻi, married john owen dominis in 1862, making washington place the private residence of the princess and future queen. another massachusetts lawyer, alfred s. hartwell, rented a guest room from 1868 until 1872. he describes mary as still expecting her husband to return any day. mary dominis died on april 25, 1889, and john owen dominis died on august 27, 1891, leaving the property to liliʻuokalani, who had just become queen after the death of her brother, king kalākaua.

washington place washington place was built in 1846 named in honor of george washington, the first president of the united states. from the 1840s through the 20th century, washington place was the center of critical events that eventually led to the overthrow of the hawaiian kingdom in 1893 and hawaiʻi becoming the 50th and final u.s. state. it also served as an executive mansion for territorial governors (1919-1959) and the governor’s mansion for the state of hawaiʻi from 1959-2002. this house was also the home of queen liliʻuokalani, hawaiʻi’s last reigning monarch. it was where queen liliʻuokalani was arrested during the overthrow of the hawaiian kingdom. this storied mansion is a registered national historic landmark and on the national register of historic places. washington place is open to the public monday through friday by reservation only in advance to schedule a 30-45 minute tour. admission is free, but donations are welcome and appreciated. the address of washington place is located at 320 s beretania st., honolulu.

wat arun temple located alongside the chao praya river is one of the most thailandesque locations that you can visit. if there is one thing thailand is known for popularly aside from elephants and muay thai it is temples. wat arun is one of the best aesthetic temples you can visit while in bangkok. •wat arun towers with its heritage seen in the intricate temples designed by previous monarchs, with every inch of design and pagodas every detail are meticulously placed and treated with the utmost repsect which contributes to the overall beauty and honor of the place. •visitors can rent traditional thai attires for females and males although i suggest you rent early because some are reused all throughout the day. the cheaper the rent cost the dirtier it gets. i highly recommend this place paired with the wat pho temple across the chao praya as a day tour. i also suggest to be respectful of the people and the places. •visitors can also be filled with thai merchandise sold at a market within the wat arun complex. it is a treasure trove of trinkets and souvenirs that some can only be found at this location. •the place is quite convenient if you plan on visiting the other temple known for the reclining buddha temple at the other side of the river which can be accessed via boat ride.

wat athvea is a beautiful and lesser-known temple located just a short drive from siem reap. this quiet, atmospheric site combines an active buddhist monastery with the ruins of an ancient angkorian-era temple, offering a unique blend of history and spirituality. what makes it special? ancient & modern harmony: the temple features a well-preserved laterite structure similar to angkor wat but on a smaller scale, surrounded by a still-functioning pagoda with vibrant monks’ quarters. peaceful atmosphere: unlike the crowded major temples, wat athvea remains serene, making it perfect for quiet exploration and photography. local experience: you’ll see monks going about their daily routines and locals praying, giving an authentic glimpse into cambodian buddhist culture.

wat benchamabophit dusitwanaram, also known as the marble temple, is one of the most beautiful temples in bangkok, thailand. it is located in the dusit area and was built in 1899 by king chulalongkorn (rama v). the temple is famous for its white marble, which was brought all the way from italy. the marble gives the temple a shiny and royal look. the main hall, called the ubosot, has a large golden buddha statue in the sukhothai style. this statue is very peaceful and beautiful. underneath the statue are the ashes of king rama v, which makes the temple an important historical place too. one of the most interesting things here is the walkway around the main hall, which displays 52 different buddha statues. these statues show different poses and styles of buddha from all over thailand. it’s a great place to learn about thai culture and buddhism. the temple is very clean and quiet, perfect if you want to take a break from the busy city. you can also see monks doing their daily routines, especially in the morning. the entrance fee is 50 baht for adults and free for small children. if you’re in bangkok, don’t miss this peaceful and beautiful temple.

wat bo is a peaceful and beautiful temple in siem reap, offering a quiet escape from the busy town. the architecture is stunning, with intricate carvings and vibrant colors. the temple is well-maintained and provides a serene atmosphere for reflection and exploration. a great place to visit for those interested in cambodia’s spiritual and cultural heritage.

wat bowonniwet ,is a first class royal temple of the rajavihara class.situated along phra sumern road,phra nakhon district.the temple was constructed between 1824-1832,the architecture was a mix of thai/chinese influence.this was a final resting place for 2 former kings of the chakri dynasty, king vajiravudh (rama vi) & king bhumibol (rama ix).it was also a monastery where many royalties studied and served their monkhood.somdet phra sangharaja chao krommaluang vajirananasamvara the 19th supreme patriarch of thailand,was a former abbot of the temple in 1921 to 1958. the temple houses 2 important buddha images, phra phuttha suwannakhet (wat sa taphan) from phetchaburi province & phra phuttha chinasi(wat phra si rattana mahathat)from phitsanulok province.phra chedi thong, a large chedi, is located next to the ubosot, the buddha's sacred relic is enshrined inside.no entrance fees, definitely worth a visit if you're nearby

wat bowonniwet vihara in bangkok, thailand. the temple was founded by king rama iii in 1826 and is the center of the dhammayuttika nikaya sect of thai buddhism. it is famous as the place where several thai kings, including king rama iv (mongkut) and king rama ix (bhumibol adulyadej), once lived as monks. wat bowonniwet also houses several important artifacts and beautiful architecture, including the buddha statues phra phuttha chinnasi and phra phuttha saiyat. the temple played an important role in the history and development of buddhism in thailand. entering or visiting this place must be dressed modestly and behave politely. for those of you who are buddhists, you understand better. i entered and visited this temple to see for myself the architecture of the building which is very beautiful and interesting.

wat chalong is absolutely stunning—full of intricate detail and rich history. the buildings are beautifully maintained, and the peaceful atmosphere makes it a lovely place to walk around and take it all in. you can climb to the top of the main pagoda for views and to see relics. we heard the sound of firecrackers in the prayer house, which is part of the local ritual and added to the unique experience. it’s free to enter, but make sure to dress respectfully—shoulders and knees covered. the only downside was seeing some tourists treating it more like a photo op than a place of worship—doing silly poses with statues and shrines while locals were trying to pray. it’s important to be mindful and respectful in a sacred space. definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area, especially for a moment of calm and culture.

wat intharawihan may not be as famous as some of bangkok’s larger temples, but it holds its own with quiet power and grace—especially thanks to the towering 32-meter-tall standing buddha, known as luang pho to. clad in gold and rising high above the temple grounds, the statue is both humbling and awe-inspiring. it’s one of the tallest standing buddha images in thailand, and seeing it up close, you can’t help but feel a deep sense of peace and respect. unlike the busier temples, wat intharawihan has a more relaxed, less commercial vibe. it feels genuinely local, where people still come to pray, light incense, and quietly reflect. the surrounding grounds include smaller shrines, statues, and murals that add layers of detail to the experience—each corner holding a piece of thailand’s spiritual and artistic heritage. the temple’s history stretches back to the ayutthaya period, and you can feel that legacy in the architecture and the reverence with which it’s maintained. wat intharawihan is a beautiful reminder that you don’t have to be in the most famous place to feel something meaningful. it’s perfect for those looking to connect more deeply with thai buddhist culture in a quieter, more personal setting—away from the crowds, but full of heart.

wat kanlayanamit woramahawihan: a historic riverside gem nestled along the chao phraya river, wat kanlayanamit woramahawihan is a significant testament to thailand’s cultural and historical richness. built in the early 19th century by chao phraya nikorn bodin during king rama iii’s reign, this temple boasts a fascinating blend of thai and chinese architecture. the main wihan houses luangpor toh (sam pho kong), a highly revered and towering buddha image. the temple also uniquely features murals from king rama iii’s era and the only palilai buddha statue in thailand, providing an added layer of cultural depth. accessible by car or boat, visitors can enjoy serene riverside views, explore intricately decorated halls, and immerse themselves in the peaceful ambiance. the temple’s giant bell, the largest in thailand, adds to its distinct character. while not as crowded as other temples, its historic significance, architectural splendor, and riverfront setting make it a must-visit for anyone seeking a true cultural experience in bangkok.

wat mangkon kamalawat, also known as wat leng noei yi, is one of the most captivating temples i've visited in bangkok. tucked away in the bustling streets of chinatown, this chinese-buddhist temple is a true cultural treasure. the moment you step inside, you're greeted by the rich scent of incense, intricate carvings, and a calming atmosphere that feels worlds away from the city chaos.

wat mongkhon wararam, located in phuket, is a buddhist temple that is definitely worth a visit. this temple is a serene and peaceful escape from the hustle and bustle of phuket city. the temple is beautifully designed and well-maintained, with intricate carvings and colorful decorations that reflect the culture of thailand. one of the most striking features of wat mongkhon wararam is the large golden buddha statue, which is the centerpiece of the temple. the statue is majestic and awe-inspiring, and it is surrounded by offerings of flowers and candles left by the devotees. the temple also has a large courtyard where visitors can sit and relax, enjoying the peaceful ambiance and the scenic views. in addition to the main temple, there are several smaller shrines and statues that are equally impressive. each of these shrines is dedicated to a different buddhist deity, and they are adorned with intricate carvings and colorful paintings. visitors can learn more about the buddhist religion by observing the rituals and traditions that are practiced at the temple. another highlight of wat mongkhon wararam is the food market, which is held on sunday mornings. this market is a popular attraction for locals and tourists alike, and it offers a wide variety of delicious thai dishes and snacks. the market is also a great place to interact with the friendly locals and learn more about their culture. overall, wat mongkhon wararam is a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to phuket. whether you are interested in buddhism, thai culture, or just seeking a peaceful retreat from the busy city, this temple is sure to impress. the stunning architecture, intricate carvings, and peaceful ambiance make it a truly memorable experience.

wat ratchanatdaram worawihan, often referred to as loha prasat, is a significant buddhist temple in bangkok, thailand. here are some key facts: * historical significance: * it was constructed during the reign of king rama iii in the 19th century. * it was built to honor princess somanass waddhanawathy. * it was completed in 1846. * architectural uniqueness: * the temple is famous for its "loha prasat," or metal castle, a multi-tiered structure with distinctive spires. * it's known for its 37 metal spires. * it has architectural influences from both thai and sri lankan styles. * cultural importance: * it is a royal temple and an important place of buddhist worship. * it represents thailand's rich historical and cultural heritage. * loha prasat: * loha prasat is considered to be one of only a few metal castles that have ever been built. * it is a very unique structure within bangkok. * royal temple: * it is a third-class royal temple of the worawihan class. ps. there are lots of cat there. the old lady there is a cat lover

wat saket – the golden mount is an absolute must-see in bangkok. the climb up the 344 gentle steps is surprisingly easy and even feels fun, with plenty of spots to pause and catch your breath along the way. it’s also very doable with kids, who will enjoy all the little things to explore. at the top, you’re rewarded with a stunning panoramic view of bangkok in every direction. along the path and around the temple grounds, there are lots of charming details to discover – statues, small waterfalls, and ringing bells – which make the visit engaging for all ages. there’s also a drink stand at the top with very affordable prices, perfect for cooling down after the walk up. overall, it’s a beautifully maintained and atmospheric site, offering both cultural interest and a fun experience for families. truly a must-visit in bangkok. entrance fee is 100 thb per person, children are free. temple clothing regulation are less strict.

wat sri sunthon (wat lipon) is a buddhist temple in thalang, around 14.5 km north of phuket town. one of the first things you'll see when entering the temple grounds is the 29-metre-high sleeping buddha sculpture, which occupies the top of the wat’s central building. there are also 9 smaller buddha images in different positions – all facing the entrance as if welcoming you to this holy place of worship. if you look around the temple, you will notice that there are quite a few non-buddha images, including a giant and lions from thai myths. they are believed to act as the temple’s guardians. you can find wat sri sunthon around 5 km north of the phuket heroine's monument. the temple is on the left-hand side of thepkasathri road.

watarium has a special spot in my heart and is in my top 3 tokyo art galleries of all time. watari-um is well known for its dynamic exhibitions that showcase both international and japanese artists. the museum, established in 1990, has hosted so far works by famous artists such as andy warhol, nam june paik, keith haring, yayoi kusama, and yoshitomo nara . worth mentioning is the fact, that keith haring’s connection with the watarium dates back to 1983, when he held his first solo exhibition in japan at galerie watari, the precursor to watari-um. this exhibition was haring’s introduction to the japanese art scene. i can asure you that 90% of their exhibitions are fantastic (with 10% being just good 😉). the museum is housed in a outstanding building designed by swiss architect mario botta (and sometimes itself becomes a canvas for paintings and performances). last but not least - discount for pairs is a nice touch that allows you to enjoy art without breaking the bank. make sure to check out their shop in b1f where you can purchase some amazing books and an artwork by japanese and foreign artist.

we are going with insight tour, one of the best holyland tour from jakarta, indonesia. the pater noster church is a significant religious site located on the mount of olives in jerusalem. it is believed to be the site where jesus christ taught his disciples the lord's prayer, also known as the pater noster in latin, hence the name of the church. the current structure of the church was built in the 19th century by french architect, antonio barluzzi, and is adorned with beautiful mosaics depicting the lord's prayer in various languages. the church also contains a small cave believed to be the spot where jesus taught his disciples. throughout history, the pater noster church has undergone several renovations and changes in ownership. in the 4th century, a small church was built on the site, which was later destroyed by the persians in the 7th century. the church was rebuilt by the crusaders in the 12th century and was later destroyed again by the muslim conqueror saladin in the 13th century. the church remained in ruins until it was rebuilt in the 19th century. today, the pater noster church is a popular destination for tourists and pilgrims visiting jerusalem. its stunning architecture and rich history make it a must-see attraction for anyone interested in religious sites and architecture.

we arrived around 10 a.m. there were two of us, and we paid 300 pesos per person for entry. it’s cheaper for mexican nationals — the 300 peso price is for foreigners. i had read that the entrance is hard to find, but we had no issues. we came from tulum by scooter, and the ride took about 20 minutes. the staff weren’t super friendly, but i wasn’t expecting top-notch service either. we took a shower before entering — not all showers worked properly, but two of them were fine. we used reef-safe sunscreen. there are plenty of restrooms, though they’re a bit far from the lake. the area itself isn’t very large. there are only two accessible piers and one viewing tower. there’s also a bar, but we didn’t use it. i had read mixed reviews about the water color, but we took a chance — and it turned out to be incredibly clear and bright blue. it’s a shallow lagoon with a cenote in the center where diving is allowed. we just swam and jumped off the pier. i personally really enjoyed it — i love shallow water. there are lots of small fish that nibble a bit. so based on the reviews i’ve seen, i can’t say whether i’d recommend it for everyone, but overall, i liked it.

we arrived there at ~8.40 (tuesday) and were the first one on the hike. there is a free parking: when the asphalt road ends, turn to the left and you will find it. no toilets available nearby. the hike is easy, but the long tunnel might cause difficulties, especially if you go there with small kids. there are three tunnels on the way: two small (3-5 min to pass) and the long one (10-15 min to pass depending on the situation). it might be hard to pass by if other people are going towards you there, the path is really narrow, that’s why i recommend to be there earlier, we met many people on the way back. flashlight on the your phone should be enough, the raincoat is needed mostly for the long tunnel + there are some waterfalls to pass on the way. trail boots are preferable or bring an extra pair to change — the road is really wet at some parts. the hike ends quite abruptly with no sign or a place to have a snack, took us 2.5-3h round trip.

we asked information from the visitor center (at dana guesthouse) where we were kindly encouraged to go on a hike on our own (we also didn’t pay any entrance fee). we chose a gorgeous wadi dana trail (the red trail) which is a one way 14km, but we chose to hike for some time and then return. the beginning of the trail is a bit tricky to find - because you don’t expect it to be what it is. it starts from behind the dana tower hotel, really in the end of the village, a paved road down the hill. there are no signs, but if you find the starting point (locals are helpful) then the rest is really easy, because you really see the road in front of you the whole time and there are not really chance to get lost. first 1,6km and app 45min is really steep way down, but as it is basically by a road wide as a driveway, it’s easily doable. we ended up doing a 7,5km and app 3hrs hike back and forth in the gorge. we absolutely loved the scenery and the views. we really recommend the hike and it’s really not that complicated.

we attempted this trail on a hot day with a 7 and 10 year old. fresh out the gate the buffalo started following us. the book said take the trail straight uphill and that is how it felt at elevation.. and hot. we made it past the petrified forest, nearly to the summit. however, we decided to turn back rather than finish because we could not tell which was the longer option. the views were phenomenal. it was near 90 that day, and if we had left earlier we may have made it. lots of flies. still, well worth the attempt. enjoy!

we attended a sunset cruise and had a blast. it rained but didn't stop any of us from having a fantastic time. the guys were funny, personable, and pretty darn cute. 100% recommended attending one of the many tours they have!

we attended alexandra dhow cruise dinner on 16.01.2025 during our visit to dubai, and overall, it was a memorable evening with some highs and lows. the views are absolutely stunning during the whole cruise journey in marina area. the cruise takes you along the dubai marina, offering breathtaking vistas of the skyline, towering skyscrapers, and the luxury yachts that line the water. it's an incredibly picturesque setting while the whole dubai twinkle with lights. the atmosphere was relaxed, we have to wear jackets as temperature was around 12 degree centigrade. the view of dubai ain led lights was mind blowing. the staff was friendly and attentive, started with the juices and cold drinks. sadly dates coffee was missing as was mentioned in the menu. the boat was well-maintained, and the traditional dhow design added a charming, cultural touch to the experience. the food was fresh, and there were not many options for the vegetarians. the best part was the birthday of my son on that day, the cruise staff arranged a lovely cake for this occasion and they all came together for cake cutting. after dinner there was a musical show/performance by which they also involves the guests on the deck. overall this was a must add place during the dubai visit. one suggestion that you book slot for upper deck to get best views around.

we attended bavaro adventure park on april 23rd under bradley webb. i wanted to share our experience. we arrived looking forward to a great adventure and that is exactly what we experienced. we started off on the polaris ride with carlos as our guide it was so fun and carlos was great we really enjoyed the stop at the cenote and learning how it was created then onto the dominican village and got to see the houses and culture i absolutely enjoyed trying the coffee and hot chocolate so good, and purchased some of the coconut products. then we enjoyed a dominican lunch loved the chicken so did my husband and our daughter it’s nice to try authentic foods in the country your visiting. we then enjoyed a nice horseback ride i love horses and being from alberta canada horses are our life. next was zip lining not gonna lie i was a bit scared i’m terrified of heights but up i went first so there was no way i could back out and i absolutely loved it so did my husband and daughter, we did stop at crossing the bridge but that was by our own choice i would of kept going but that bridge was my stopping point, i was just to scared but that’s a me issue not the park issue. then we enjoyed the lazy river and the swimming pool. my family is so glad we did this excursion it was an absolutely great day and great memories trying new things.

we attended the cooking class with the menu “cabrito de pescado.” since a large group canceled at the last minute, it ended up being just the two of us—essentially a private lesson with the founder, maria. the entire experience was absolutely amazing. everything was fresh, and we got to prepare each dish together with her. the location was beautiful, and everything was very clean and hygienic. the food tasted incredible. maria was a fantastic host, and we had such a great time spending the evening with her. francisco also supported us throughout the evening and ensured everything stayed clean and was very sweet. it was one of our highlights during our travels. we would 100% recommend this cooking class!

we attended the live adaptation of my neighbour totoro at the gillian lynne theatre, and we had a fantastic time. the show was an absolute joy. the performance and puppetry were amazing, and the set was brilliant, and it's a production i won't forget! the venue is beautiful, and the seats were very comfortable. the staff were friendly and helpful. it's conveniently located just a short walk from holborn tube station.
we attended the summer mushers experience last month and had a fantastic time with paige! highly recommend attending any of the programs that squid acres does.

we attended this lovely place to enjoy a relaxing spa. if you attend with a member your entry fee is $15 for no set time in the spa. we stayed for just over 30 mins. the two pools had different temperatures which was lovely 😍 it does echo in the room if you speak loudly. the receptionist was very polite and welcoming. im quite sure if you are a member you can access the gym and many other facilities. nice shower, gel is provided, hair dryer please be careful of the floors it can be a little slippery. (just be mindful)🫠

we avoided going there on weekends and long holidays. the road was smooth and there was no need to queue anywhere. there were very few tourists. it was so beautiful and it is a place worth visiting in life!

we avoided going there on weekends and long holidays. the road was smooth and there was no need to queue anywhere. there were very few tourists. it was so beautiful and it is a place worth visiting in life!

we basically stumbled across it while on the way to the colosseum. we could not see it at first because of construction works and then there it was: all mighty and wonderful! it looks very impressive and reading a bit of the history really makes you understand the significance of it! i tried to find decebal on it, but was not successful. the sheer size of the column and surrounding remaining ruins, make you truly appreciate the old roman architecture - that building was simply massive and so very intricate! would love it if one day we can generate some immersive experiences with ai, which display how all these incredible ruins used to look like in their golden age!
we basically stumbled upon this spot while cruising around town for street food. found some great cháo (rice porridge).

we baught 4 different products here. the owner is very kind and proud of his work. we see his sincerity on his products and they look gorgeous. there are a lot of leather shops around but we see the uniqueness here.

we began the tree top walk trail, parking at the winsor car park and embarking on a scenic 3.5km journey. the moderate walk took approximately 35 minutes each way, with a mix of easy strolls and challenging uphill and downhill steps. the well-maintained trail wound through a tropical rainforest, offering breathtaking views and the chance to spot monkeys and snakes. while the distance and slopes might pose difficulties for elderly visitors, regular resting points provided relief. the atmosphere was peaceful and serene, with the sights and sounds of nature creating an immersive experience. however, some groups' constant chatter detracted from the tranquility. overall, the tree top walk trail is a must-visit for nature lovers and those seeking a moderate hiking challenge. good outdoor adventure for family and friends.

we book the island tour online for our second day in noronha and it was very good! noronha agency had a chat service which allowed us to ask questions ahead of booking and the service was prompt and attentive. on the tour we had a good guide, however there were two other foreigners in the tour who didn’t speak portuguese and the guide couldn’t speak english so we ended up translating for them. the tour allowed us to visit the main points of interest on the island — it is a packed schedule but doesn’t feel rushed. i would recommend it!

we booked 2 tours with rioxtreme and would recommend to future travelers. we were picked up at our condo on time. guides were great to work with on each tour. the booking team was quick to respond with answers to our questions prior to the tours.

we booked 3 nights stay with safarinut (along with the rest of our month long trip to africa) and we would suggest everyone else to as well! we cannot recommend porini mara camp more highly, what an incredible place, with incredible people! we feel very privileged to have experienced the wildlife so close up in the ol kinyei conservancy. stanley and joshua were amazing guides and we had a great time on the game drives with them, learning soo much about the mammals, birds and the nature! we also had the experience of a nature walk, night drive and were able to visit a local village and learning more about the masai culture, incredibly interesting. the camp itself is idyllic, set completely in the bush, with friendly wildlife wandering through, fully protected by the masai staff. the food was delicious, we enjoyed many lovely meals and relaxed in our very comfy tenet between activities! thank you all for such a brilliant 3 days which we will never forget, we had some of the best days of our lives at this amazing camp!!

we booked 4 people canoe for 2 hours. derek met us at kendrick park, gave us some advice on which route to take and basic of current flow. we like the small details of the service - case for our phone, waterproof bag, life jackets and sunscreen. he also told us to pick up rubbish along away - which we really like to keep our water clean, they donate $1 to the local water cleaning project. kendrick park is hard to get too with these small roads but there are ample parking spots. will definitely go back.

we booked a "swimming with dolphins" tour. the communication before the tour worked perfectly. when we arrived, we received a warm welcome and a short briefing. afterward, we were outfitted and escorted to the boat. after a somewhat wild but thoroughly entertaining ride, we found what we were looking for: a huge group of atlantic dolphins. there were probably over 100 of them, an incredible sight! then, as instructed beforehand, we were lowered into the water with help. there were so many young dolphins that the group didn't seem particularly interested in us and changed direction almost every time someone was lowered into the water. but that's just the way nature is, and we should understand and respect that! for me, at least, the tour wasn't any worse for it; it was incredibly beautiful to be able to observe the animals in the wild and even hear their sounds underwater! all in all, it was a wonderful experience that i would recommend to anyone. many thanks to the entire crew for the great tour!!!

we booked a 3 hour snorkeling tour of the barra da tijuca islands in second week of aug. this tour was expensive, and there were several surprises once payment was done. (24 hrs before the tour was to happen) they asked us to come to urca, which is more than 1 hr drive in the morning rush hour. (from barra da tijuca) citing weather reasons. the guide spoke no english, he was using google translator. why would you sell the boat ride as a tour? they took us to a different island, where we did not see a single fish or anything under water. i can imagine animals can decide to not show up, but them as the organizer of the tour, should have some clue of what to expect. the water also had very little visibility. as a professional tour operator, they claim to be, i would expect them cancel the tour and refund money. they advertised to take on small hike, show other land animals etc, they did not do any of that. the captain instead showed us cagarras island, which was the only good thing about the tour, but definitely not worth the price. on the way back, he stopped at a beach which we could visit from land as well, nothing interesting. overall 1 * for the tour itself, and also i would not trust such company. attached photos of the caggaras island it has large number of birds.

we booked a day of boating, swimming, and snorkeling on a 42-foot catamaran for us and our wedding party of 13 people a couple of days before our wedding in cancun, and we cannot recommend going through riviera charters enough! the entire booking process and then the day of fun out on the ocean exceeded our expectations at every turn. we had done a lot of research on various boat rental companies in the area as we wanted to have the best day possible for our wedding party, and riviera charters looked to be the best from the reviews we found.. they were right! the crew on the boat were extremely attentive, always making sure people had drinks and food, going out of their way to take photos of us and our party, and getting us towels after jumping in the ocean. and the food!!!!! oh my god. the food was incredible! amazing ceviche and guac as snacks, and the fish tacos were still being talking about by our wedding party days later. chef sandy is amazing! shout out to our captain who made sure the party was lively with our music pumping all over the boat. everyone in our group had an amazing time because of our wonderful crew! thank you!

we booked a dolphin trip from heritage awali (mauritius). everyone from kiteglobing were incredibly professional and helpful, especially aleyna. they picked us up on time and we had the most amazing dolphin encounter; we even got to swim with them. truly incredible. the boat was modern and clean, the captain and assistant were kind and professional and tried their best to give the ultimate experience. the snorkelling afterwards was equally breathtaking. would highly recommend.

we booked a frozen waterfall hiking tour. our group comprised 7 tourists and our chilean guide tomas. we had a good time. while we had our own hiking and snow gear, it was available from wild about lapland. the van left rovaniemi at 07:30, making the 90-minute drive to korouoma with a midpoint rest stop. tomas was a very smooth driver. we were the first vehicle in the large parking lot. and the first to make footprints in the one inch of new snow on the trails. tomas led us on the snow-packed hiking trails at a fairly rapid pace, stopping to explain some of the plants and wildlife along the way. we saw no other hikers until about halfway into our tour. about an hour in, we stopped to build a fire, roast sausages, and drink tea and cocoa. restrooms (pit toilets) were available at the campfire stop. by the time we finished the hike, the parking lot was full, including tour busses. large groups were entering the park. we napped on the smooth ride back, having gotten our vigorous exercise.

we booked a full day tour and night under the stars and had an absolutely unforgettable experience. we even decided to book an extra night because we couldn’t get enough! this family run business makes you feel instantly at home in the desert, giving you an insight into the traditional bedouin way of life. our guides abdul and salim were not only hospitable and knowledgeable but kind, entertaining and a joy to be around. as two female travellers, they made us feel so safe and we had such a laugh! the full day tour of various sights in the desert was fascinating, including canyons, springs, nabatean inscriptions and breathtaking views. we would definitely recommend to choose to sleep in the cave: away from light pollution the starry views are a marvel. they cooked delicious meals for us on the camp fire so we were never hungry. i would recommend this experience to anyone wanting to have the best time of their life! we will definitely be back. if you are debating between camps, take this as a sign to book this one. thank you so much wadi rum stars valley!

we booked a gondola ride to celebrate a special anniversary in december. everything was easy to book and was promptly confirmed. robert made the experience amazing and even better than our already high expectations! we chose the sunset gondola ride and were able to experience the local wildlife, peace of cruising serene waters in the beautiful gondola, a majestic sunset and the spectacle of christmas lights in city park. we would highly recommend this experience any time of year!

we booked a group hiking tour on the athabasca glacier with rockaboo, and max was our guide. i wasn’t sure what to expect by booking privately versus just heading out onto the glacier ourselves - but i was quickly blown away by the experience. max was incredible - passionate, knowledgeable, and clearly excellent at what he does. he instantly put the group at ease, made safety a priority, and took the time to share fascinating details about the glacier’s history and the environmental impacts it’s facing - his love for the landscape was infectious. one of the highlights was being lowered (safely!) into a crevasse - a proper team effort where we all learned rope skills and supported one another throughout. max gave us plenty of time to take photos and videos without ever rushing us, and the whole experience felt thoughtful, immersive, and safe from start to finish. the hike itself was around 4 hours, plus setup and gear time so it’s a full-day activity - we left with not only an adventure under our belts, but a much deeper appreciation for the incredible landscape. i’m so glad we chose to book with a private, local tour. you learn so much more, and it becomes clear very quickly just how dangerous glaciers can be if you’re not with someone who knows exactly what they’re doing!! ***** couldn’t recommend it more. max is amazing - if you get the chance to book with him, do it!

we booked a guided tour through langtang ri trekking & expedition to do the langtang valley trek in december 2024. we chose the company partly because of lonely planets recommendation and due to price and the quick answering time pafma delivered. pafma, the owner, was very quick in her response time which helped us feel secure that they were going to provide us with a good trek. she was very accommodating and nice to us when we arrived in kathmandu and even stayed later in her office past closing hours just to meet with us. even when we had to sligthly further reschedule due to our arrival time in kathmandu. during this meeting, we also met shishir, our guide, which made us more secure knowing who we were going to trek with during the next couple of days. it all made us feel that we had made the right choice by choosing them as our trekking company. shishir travelled with us to say bu bresi on a local bus along with pafma’s daughter (so nice and sweet) who we were trekking with. after the first day of trekking, we unfortunately got food poisoning. shishir was very calm and reassuring. we ended up taking a rest day. it was very nice that shishir remained calm and reassured us that it was still possible to do rhetorical climb but without ever pressuring us to do anything. the third day (our second day of trekking), shishir carried one of our bags which was not a part of the service that you could expect but very kind and actually also essential to us being able to further trek up the mountains. we got up the mountain to kyanjin gompa and we also took the side trek to kyanjin ri with shishir. he was great all the way through. he was aware of our limited trekking experience, didn’t pressure us, walked according to our pace and was overall everything and more you could expect of a guide to lead you safely up the treks, whichever one you chose. after our trek, we had to get to pokhara from say bu bresi (a non-direct route), which means that we had to change local bus somewhere along the way. this can be very confussing and tricky for foreigners not used to the nepali bus-system but shishir offered to stop with us to find our bus, even though he was going to kathmandu and would be able to directly drive back to kathmandu. this was such a big help to us and just an unexpected level of kindness, helpfulness and service. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ out of five stars. cannot recommend shishir and langtang ri trekking & expedition enough. would choose every time again. thanks!

we booked a jetski and arrived on time at the pick up location. we tried to contact the responsible person by calling and texting him, but we didn't get any response. we wouldn't have minded to wait if the guy at least had answered our calls or messages, but since he didn't, we just left. we never heard from the guy again. it was a waste of time for us.

we booked a last minute cartagena cooking class and had a great time. the instructor was helpful and guided us through the recipes. we made a delicious 4 course meal (too much food to eat!) looking forward to cooking the recipes at home!
we booked a lunch trip, it was really nice, everything was organized and the cleanliness was very clear. i salute them.🫶🏻👍🏻

we booked a one hour horseback riding + pickup/drop off session at the last minute and we were thoroughly impressed by the experience. pickup was on time with a good driver who was friendly. the tour was appropriate for kids and adults of different experience levels. it was not a private tour but there were plenty of guides with the group. the horses seemed well cared for as far as we could tell and the guides were friendly. this was exactly what we were looking for and we are happy we picked the right place to go with!

we booked a private boat tour to the three northern islands. from the booking to the tour itself, it was a nice experience. the captain was so nice to let us in the water back again because there was a tortoise even though we just hopped back on to drive back to the main island. highly recommanded!

we booked a private car for our family and mohammed was a superb guide for us. he picked us up in time at our hotel, came with a perfectly clean and prepared car, and took us out into the desert including different stops along the route. the best thing - he was very attentive to the kids age, what everyone needed and we enjoyed literally hours of great conversations about life and our experiences. i cannot recommend this tour and mohammed as a guide enough!

we booked a private evening tour on mykines with oda who runs golocal.fo, and we couldn't have found a better guide. we returned glowing on the inside from the stunning views, fresh air, and dizzying activity of puffins circling and landing in the distance, while other puffins were so close to the path that i could take great photos with just my cell phone. we were there for the puffins, which are so much cuter than we expected, but as we walked through the tiny village and hiked up to the sea cliffs with oda we discovered what a wealth of information and history she has to share, her love for the islands and, how involved she is in working towards sustainability in the tourism industry and land use in the faroes. thank you oda for my happiest memories of the faroe islands!

we booked a private pirate boat trip with family and friends and it was great! the kids absolutely love it, especially the waterslide before lunch. even the adults really got into it! we visited the waterfalls, saw loads of monkeys, had a rain shower and a beautiful day. stopped off at an island, had a swim and a couple of drinks before heading back with some traditional dancing. thanks to all the crew for a great day once again.

we booked a private snorkeling trip for our family and had high hopes based on previous boat excursions we’ve done. the boat itself was very nice and clean, and we appreciated that the captain and his mate shared some interesting information about the area. we even spotted a few sea turtles, both from the boat and briefly in the water. that said, this experience fell short in several ways. the captain had a very different personality than what we’re used to—while not outright rude, he was extremely short and hard to connect with. my daughters actually mentioned feeling uncomfortable around him, which is unfortunate when you’re hoping for a light, fun outing. in past charters, we’ve had captains who made the experience feel warm, welcoming, and even a little magical—this was not that. conditions were incredibly rough that day, and i expected we might be taken to a more sheltered cove to snorkel. instead, we dropped anchor in very choppy water about 600 yards off waikīkī beach, where visibility was poor and the current made it difficult to enjoy the experience. i even became seasick—something that never happens to me, despite growing up on boats as a military brat. on the bright side, the captain’s mate was wonderful—kind, attentive, and genuinely tried to help us spot marine life and manage the rough conditions. she even offered ginger candy to help with my nausea. unfortunately, for over $850, this ended up being the most disappointing boat outing we’ve had. while the boat and crew weren’t bad overall, the vibe and location choices just didn’t meet expectations, and we left feeling like it wasn’t worth the cost.

we booked a private tour for our group of 27, and we all had so much fun! amanda even helped arrange transportation for us from our hotel and back. the crew had plenty of food and drinks prepared for everyone. our group ages ranged from 5-61 and everyone had such a great time! even my sister who was 6 months pregnant felt safe and had fun. the crew was amazing at hosting. i will definitely recommend to anyone visiting cabo. hope to visit again in the future!

we booked a private tour of two people as we want flexibility and privacy. the price is really affordable compared to other tours we did. the guide is very thoughtful and eager. we love his assistance

we booked a room with beautiful advertised features, but upon arrival, these were our actual views: garbage and construction works 24/7. we paid over 15 million rupiah, and the truth is we are very saddened. that said, the staff are wonderful, and we truly regret having to write this, but the price is not at all justified. this room should not be available under these conditions.

we booked a scenic flight via email. everything was very professional and straight forward. the staff was welcoming and helpful and our pilot very experience. as there were no other guests booked on the flight it was basically a private charter. we dreamed about seeing the delta from above since a long time and enjoyed every moment. thanks a lot.

we booked a snorkeling tour with octopus oman and it was amazing from start to finish. the boat was comfortable, the water crystal clear, and the coral reef was full of colorful fish. our guide was friendly, professional, and made sure everyone felt safe. highly recommended if you're looking for a top-quality snorkeling experience in oman.

we booked a snowmobile tour to a reindeer yard. it was really fun and the track was long enough so both of us could drive. we enjoyed the beautiful nature and we had enough time to pet and feed the reindeers 🦌

we booked a team excursion for a sunday ride and shay took us up the hilliest of hills, and even they were no match for his epic e-bikes! we had an absolute blast as a team. his knowledge and humour are unmatched. thanks for an awesome day out! we’d highly recommend this experience to anyone keen on team bonding or just getting out to see the best of queenstown.

we booked a tour through vibe adventures via the get your guide app to visit a monarch butterfly sanctuary. they coordinated with us to pick us up at our hotel in mexico city and utilized a private driver to take us to the sanctuary. once there, we were able to experience one of the last groups of monarchs before they migrate north. our guide diego was fantastic and very knowledgeable! we had a great lunch in nearby angangueo and learned about the town's history as well. overall, we were very pleased with our tour and would recommend the experience to everyone!
we booked a trip from sedona to antelope canyon. we found this place to be an absolute class act. we got the absolutely amazing, professional and talented kate as our pilot. 5 stars highly recommend!

we booked a trip to komodo island with this agency and were picked up directly by mr. william, the agency's owner. our 2-day, 1-night sailing experience was excellent. we highly recommend this agency. thank you very much, mr. william.

we booked a two day tour with moses and he was the best! thank you moses from maryann, jay, helen and charlie. we saw bison, black bears, and stunning views of yellowstone national park. the views were spectacular and moses was very accommodating. we did the lower loop the first day and the upper loop the 2nd day. i hope you enjoyed my pictures. our trip was so fun thanks to moses of yellowstone tours from jackson hole!!

we booked an 8-day luxury safari with safari soles and i cannot begin to put into words how amazing it was! kudos to douglas who helped us so enthusiastically from the start to stitch together a fabulous trip, amazing accommodations and covered all the places we had time to see. safari soles comprise of professionals who are truly committed to making your holiday special. we would like to express our heartfelt gratitude to our guide, ally kimea, for his hard work, guidance, enthusiasm, expertise and commitment to making our trip so memorable. we were so lucky because he knows the serengeti so well! he took us to some amazing spots and ensured we saw not only the big five but so much live action in the wild. he was so pleasant and friendly, yet very professional. the car was spotless and fresh each morning and he paid special attention to our comfort throughout. there isn’t a doubt we will return to tanzania and when we do we will be thrilled to be on safari with safari soles & ally again. have no hesitation that this is the company you should book with - they are truly amazing and very experienced in what they do! thank you so much for a wonderful experience that we will always cherish.

we booked an unlimited laser tag party for 15 but nearly two weeks out from party i confirmed it would be ok for up to 20 people to which i was told this was ok. we ended up with 17. barely enough working laser packs and staff had another group in our unlimited time slot resulting in use having to wait for packs. the other booking would have been ok provided enough packs and staff should have discussed this on arrival but we had no mention of it. email sent explaining my disappointment at the booking. yet no reply. at over $600 for the booking i expected working packs and enough packs for all the group to enjoy "unlimited" laser tag as per booking.

we booked arik for three days worth of tours. they were the best part of our whole vacation, and arik was a great tour guide. he was easy to get in touch with, and always responded quickly. he provided us with so much information and answered all our questions. he was also flexible on what we wanted to do and see, and really tailored the tour to our interests. could not recommend highly enough.

we booked both cenotes snorkling tour and scuba dive trip with adventure tour center, and was very pleased with everything. all are well organized, on time, clear explanation, friendly supportive staff. the scuba experience was exceptional, we were very happy to have giulio as our dive guide, he's a solid diver, very professional, knowledgeable and good conversationalist. me and my partner are both advanced divers and been diving many times in numerous places around the world, and definitely can tell if we can trust our dive guide for a safe diving session. highly recommended!

we booked both cenotes snorkling tour and scuba dive trip with adventure tour center, and was very pleased with everything. all are well organized, on time, clear explanation, friendly supportive staff. the scuba experience was exceptional, we were very happy to have giulio as our dive guide, he's a solid diver, very professional, knowledgeable and good conversationalist. me and my partner are both advanced divers and been diving many times in numerous places around the world, and definitely can tell if we can trust our dive guide for a safe diving session. highly recommended!

we booked five star helicopter tours for a flight around las vegas out over lake mead/hoover dam and around the grand canyon. the flight was spectacular and the surroundings are indeed awe inspiring. our pilot was creative and a good flyer. although it was somewhat difficult to see some of the sites well from the cramped backseat. unless you have the window, i do not recommend the backseat, especially the one in the middle just behind the pilot. although we booked it for five people, and expected to be alone in the chopper, at the last minute we were informed that they had an additional full grown adult customer to accompany us. in itself, that did not bother us except that when we got in and realized that none of us could really sit back without scrunching the others, we proceeded to have a pretty uncomfortable 90 minute flight. although our group clearly covered the bulk of the cost that came to nearly $3000 with tip, our new guest was assigned a window seat. that left me not only scrunched in the back but basically unable to see much over the heads of the passengers in front and my fellow sardines in the back. so, i could not snap a single decent photo of the entire trip. all of these are from the window seat passengers our pilot from texas was a good flyer with good skills and confidence. his willingness to scare those on the ground i'm sure would appeal to many yahoos but we found it offensive and are glad that the folks in a camp were not armed because they could've easily shot us right out of the sky. i certainly might've at least fired a warning shot if a helicopter did that to me. so, all in all, well worth the beautiful scenery if you are seated where you can enjoy it but not the best managed seat assignment or flight.

we booked for a company event the 90min underground tour and were really content. the guide was really competent and we learned a lot of interesting and surprising facts and stories. a very good option if you don't want to do the "typical" tourist tour!

we booked husky ride with 5km on website visit rovaniemi. it says that it’s self driving but it was 6 of us on cart and guide drowe us. in the video they send us it was shown that we drive a sled and there were information how to drive it. trip also wasn’t 5km long, it was about 2km. we had 5 minutes with huskys and then they locked them up. we didn’t have a chance to pet not one husky. it says it was 3 hours long trip but it was less than 2 hours (driving was not included in that beacase it was optional and we drowe our self there). pretty much of a scame and false advertising.

we booked island hooping from hotel counter. agents help us arranged shuttle and when we got there the tour guide already waited for us. our guide was dahan, he’s awesome and really careful. my kids like him a lot, also dan takes a good care of them. we have a great experience of island hopping at boracay.🤩

we booked island hooping from hotel counter. agents help us arranged shuttle and when we got there the tour guide already waited for us. our guide was dahan, he’s awesome and really careful. my kids like him a lot, also dan takes a good care of them. we have a great experience of island hopping at boracay.🤩
