we stayed at the hilltop house and it was such a memorable experience. i can be a pretty needy guest when it comes to planning. i like to ask lots of questions and make sure everything is in order ahead of time, but the team was incredibly responsive and thoughtful. i really appreciated how their contactless system was set up (i’ve had bad contactless experiences in the past)… the arrival process was seamless, and the care they put into setting everything up was obvious. chocolate and wine… literally my favorite food groups ❤️ during our stay, we had a few additional questions and small needs come up, and every single one was handled right away. that kind of responsiveness makes such a difference. the grounds themselves are stunning. literally 360 views. i highly recommend setting aside a full day just to wander and explore. there’s so much to discover. the kitchen was well equipped with everything we needed to grill/cook, and they provided a great selection of coffee and teas. there’s also a restaurant down at the public springs, which is a nice option to have. some of my favorite touches: the robes. so cozy, and perfect for lounging around in. i had requested yoga mats ahead of time for our group and they provided them, which made it easy to do yoga on the balcony, truly the best possible setting for it. the trampoline, probably one of the coolest things ever - just jumping around looking at the views or laying on it to look at stars/the aurora… a literal dream. the space inside isn’t huge, but it’s intimate and cozy, and we honestly spent most of our time outdoors anyway. the experience felt like a grown-up scavenger hunt, with multiple hot springs tucked around the property, plus the barn house, game rooms, and gym (they have everything you need for a good workout). we even saw little seals swimming by the ocean springs, cutest thing ever. the wildlife in the area is incredible (still sad we missed the whales, though!). a couple of things worth noting: there was some trash and glass around parts of the property—most likely washed up from the ocean. not necessarily within their control, but it might be nice to have a designated area with supplies for guests who want to help clean up. we actually found it fun to poke around and look at sea glass, rocks, and the creatures along the shore. the colder, lower pool at the hilltop house had small worm-like insects in it. one person from our group went in and felt like they were getting bit (though there were no marks or effects after). they seemed harmless and likely natural, but we couldn’t find any info about them, maybe adding a note about that would ease guests’ minds? all in all, i’m genuinely sad we didn’t have time to try out the public pools, but we did stop by briefly and the staff was beyond welcoming. great way to end our trip, i feel recharged and relaxed. truly one of the most hospitable places i’ve ever stayed. we will 100000% be back.

we stayed at the house of jose luis and his wife, the stay was perfect, jose luis speaks english so it helped a lot during the stay. the apartments were charming and well maintained, the food was perfect. highly recommended, very recommended haim

we stayed at the igloo for a couple of days! had the best possible experience. joni was an excellent host and took good care of us. we loved the sauna. the igloo is completely isolated and we were in a world of our own! it's small but functional and the location is just fabulous.
we stayed at the nickelodeon resort and my baby absolutely loved it. the characters would take pictures with the kids and on site food and drinks, made this an all day plan.

we stayed at this riad for three nights, and below are our honest and genuine thoughts based on our experiences staying at various riads across morocco: pros: the bedroom: our room was on the ground floor, spacious with high ceilings. the beautifully painted wooden furniture and mosaic wall and floor tiles showcased the house’s rich history and the unique art of fez. the bed was large and very comfortable, with clean and cozy bedding. the room was equipped with central air conditioning, and the tv worked perfectly. the riad: this riad is historic, with original decorations dating back to 1176. apart from modern additions like a swimming pool, lift, and wooden staircase, all other elements remain authentic. it has been passed down through generations, and the local family managing it clearly takes pride in preserving its legacy. the location is great—just a short walk to the blue gate and other city gates where taxis are easily available. the area feels safe to walk around. the rooftop is charming, with tables and lots of local plants, offering a fantastic view of the mountains and medina. the service: the family running the riad was welcoming and attentive, available 24/7 for any questions or concerns. they strike a nice balance between providing support and giving guests enough independence and privacy to feel at ease. suggestions for improvement: the bedroom: the large windows on the ground floor could benefit from proper curtains to allow guests to enjoy natural light while maintaining privacy. the bathroom would be improved with a toilet roll holder and could be a bit cleaner. additionally, the towels seemed old and could be upgraded in quality. the riad: breakfast was lovely, but it might be easier for staff if each table had its own coffee, milk, or tea pots so guests can serve themselves. adding soft background music in the main hall (traditional moroccan or otherwise) between 10 am and 10 pm would create a relaxing atmosphere and mask any noise from staff activity. the pool to be cleaner.

we stayed during the national day weekend. we visited as a group of 12 adults. we got double double rooms. the hotel is beautifully designed. i must say i saw the staff try very hard. it was positioned as a 5 star resort, but it didn’t feel 5 star. few suggestions: 1. lack of entertainment options other than the zoo. i wish there were more breakaway niches with seating that allow groups to gather for board games or communal activities. there were such spaces we saw, but there wasn’t enough seats or tables for communal activities. we knew it would be a crowded time to visit, and but everywhere we went, we saw running kids and were reminded of crowds in public spaces. this made it feel like a tourist-class hotel and didn’t feel exclusive or restful. if the hotel wants to operate as a 5 star, it needs to carry the beautiful rainforest surroundings from the visual into a more all-encompassing multi- sensorial experience : scent, tranquility, sound, less people, more nature. it should have been a more restful experience. 2. check-in lobby was crowded and unfortunately, it marred the experience of the resort. we are frequent visitors of 5 star hotels. check-in should already be a well-oiled machine having guests fill out advanced check in requests. 3. the rooms were decent and clean. some of us got rooms without view and didn’t mind it; but calling a run-of-house room double double can be misleading as it builds expectations. 4. we ate at forage and the service was impeccable. if we wanted crowds, we could have spent the money on hotels in a more central urban location with better entertainment and food options. it would be much cheaper too.

we stayed for 2 weeks and had a great time! staff are very welcoming and polite. food was also excellent. our bungalow with panorama sea view window was beautiful and clean, with mosquito net installed for the bed. we went for a total of 17 dives with the dive center. they are professionally run and very safety concious. both the manager and the guides went out of their way to meet all of our wishes. marine wildlife in komodo is world class and never disappointed. we warmly recommend staying and diving here!

we stayed for 3 nights and it was wonderful. the staff, the cooks, the guides were all top notch. the remote location and amazing architecture and design was stunning. special thanks to our fun, knowledgeable, and engaging guide ballack! we so loved the atvs, sand boarding, and time on the beach. many thanks also to eugene, abel, messie (sp?), bodo, and serafina. you all were amazing hosts of the lodge and your country.

we stayed for 3d2n over the weekend in july. hotel is absolutely stunning! the area is large for us to stroll around and explore. the pool has an awesome view of sunset. first and foremost, i would like to commend your staff member sabrina at the rangers’ club. her genuine warmth and love for the children truly stood out during our visit. she actively engaged with my 6-year-old daughter and other children through games and conversation. her passion and positive attitude were incredibly admirable and left a lasting impression on our family. the housekeeping team at l1 was great for keeping our room clean and tidy. i’ve wrapped our bathing suit in the towels and was taken away for cleaning. when i told the front desk, they were very swift to assist. i managed to find the housekeeper and he quickly assisted me. the restaurant for breakfast was too small to accommodate the guests during peak. the staffs also lacked of hospitality. i have written an email feedback of an unpleasant situation during breakfast. i hope the management look into it.

we stayed here for one night and thoroughly enjoyed the overall experience. the hotel is conveniently located and easily accessible by car, with just a short 500-meter off-road drive from the main road. the property had everything we needed for a comfortable and memorable stay. we booked the 2-hour desert safari, which was an incredible experience and absolutely worth it. we also opted for dinner at the hotel, which was quite good. one of the highlights of our stay was the live music arranged at night—it really added a special touch to the trip. overall, we loved this place for the unique experience it offers and would definitely recommend it.

we stayed here for the first part of our honeymoon. the location was great, the staff were lovely and welcoming, even surprising us with a bottle of champagne on our first night. walks on the beach with the owners dogs in toe is definitely a must. the cultural town tour should also be on your list of things to do - guys ask to get a suit jacket made from the local sarong material, it's a great souvenir to take home. girls invest in the sarong bags, they are great as well. ask the owners to book the tour for you when you arrive. in all honesty the best b&b in the town and we had a look around at a few of them.

we stayed here four nights and had a fabulous time. the location is fantastic - the background consists of mountains, sand dunes and the yellow grasslands that cover the namib desert. it’s about a 45 min drive to the sossuvlei and deadvlei park where you can climb the sand dunes and see the dead trees in deadvlei. there are lots of other activities to do from the lodge as well including sundowners to closer sand dunes, walks to see san bushmen rock art, helicopter rides over the dunes and to the coast (from the lodge’s helipad), atvs, ebiking, hot air ballooning (which we did and loved), etc. or you can just relax and take in the spectacular views outside your giant windows or from your pool. and there’s so much more wildlife here than we expected. we saw tons of oryx, zebra and jackals (including two jackals on our patio this morning) and even saw a brown hyena at the watering hole on the property. the rooms are giant and very well decorated and everything has been thought out including fridges, freezers (with ice and ice cream and iced fruit pops), your own bar full of alcohol, indoor/outdoor showers, etc. the food was excellent / the best we’ve had on our southern africa trip so far. lots of game meats like oryx and springbok but nothing was gamey at all. just cooked so tender and very well seasoned. and our guide and the entire staff were all so sweet and helpful and knowledgeable. five stars across the board. couldn’t recommend this place more. and even if you don’t stay here do yourself a favor and come to sossusvlei. it’s like nowhere else on earth (at least not to our knowledge).

we stayed here on our honeymoon and were floored by the experience. the game is unbelievable. we had 7 lions on camp and saw hundreds of elephants in the pond by the camp. the mokoro and boat ride were a great change of pace and beautiful. above all, the hospitality at this camp was 11 out of 10. they made every aspect of our stay so special and were beyond accommodating. they even organized a special romantic dinner on our last night that was legitimately a scene out of the bachelor (except with the sounds of lions and elephants fighting in the background). we stayed at "fancier" places during our trip, but no one put in the exceptional attention to detail that splash did, paired with unbelievable game, and top tier food. cannot recommend enough.

we stayed here two nights and couldn’t recommend more. a stunning location in the hills with beautiful views of ella rock and around. the staff were fantastic, with great service and delicious meals cooked up. a beautiful room and the facilities made it the perfect place to relax, even when the storms rolled in. all the produce is delicious, especially the jams and the tea. definitely tick off all of the guided walks, especially to get down to the pool - we only managed a few and be sure to do the tea tour. thanks again to all the staff and owners!

we stayed here with some other family members, including the bbq area rental. we rented 3 rooms in total. all the rooms are nice and clean. location is nice for access to wild wild wet water park. also easy access to the mall next door. in the morning, my wife and i found the gate entry to pasir ris park. overall, we enjoyed our stay here.

we stayed in 6 different serena hotels in tanzania. rooms are generally very good. staff are excellent with some providing truly exceptional service. food and drinks good. would be nice to have some local food offerings on the menu. only real downside after 11 nights in different serena hotels is the coffee. they all serve the same horrible coffee; weak, tasteless american drip style dirt water. otherwise our stay was great. this lodge had wonderful views from the room. we even had an elephant munching on the long grass only a few meters off our balcony.

we stayed in a bubble and had an amazing experience and view. we were welcomed in and made delicious, traditional bedouin food. during our tour of wadi rum, we saw many other camps, even some with bubbles, but the view provided here was by far the best.

we stayed in daroyan village for an 8 day dive trip. we brought our own equipment and only required tanks and weights. at out request herman provided us with 15 liter tanks which was greatly appreciated. our small group was treated like kings. we were picked up at sorong airport and he escorted us to kri. same service when we left. accommodation is very basic but clean and comfortable. the meals are local food but tasteful. rice vegies and fish for the hot meals. different kinds of buns for breakfast. we often had fruit with the meals. we had erick as a divemaster. we selected the dive sites together with him and he checked conditions before the dive and if they were unsuitable we went to dive elsewhere. we did 22 dives and all of them were great. almost all dive sites were less than 30 minutes from the homestay. we had a great time and felt very welcome. herman and erick have made our trip unforgettable.

we stayed in early june and our experience was amazing. the service as soon as we arrived was top notch. when lucas, our guide, got us at the airport we were greeted with snacks and drinks. it was a nice welcome after a long travel day. at the hotel, we were greeted by the hotel manager and the head of the food and they were visible the entire trip checking to see if everything was ok. the servers were always attentive and went over and beyond. our safari guide lucas was fantastic. our only issue was the hyrax droppings. i think more attention could be paid in the future to cleaning the balcony because the hyrax would leave droppings. i’m not taking a star off for this because as soon as we brought it up the concierge, the balcony was cleaned everyday. this was the trip of a lifetime and i can’t wait to go back.

we stayed in the beautiful quiet s.erasmo for a week and it was a great choice. you only hear the birds chirping. very kind residents always willing to help. very good energy of the island that relaxes you after the much tourism of venice. in half an hour you are in venice on a quiet journey with few passengers. it also has night itineraries. we had a lovely week in s.erasmo and we recommend it to people who want to combine tranquility in nature and enjoy the day in the wonderful city of venice.

we stayed in the cheaper side and it was still lovely, but no real view. the other rooms have great views over the park where you could easily watch elephant strolling past. the staff are extremely pleasant and helpful. horse riding and quad bikes in the wild. i would recommend you check it out. big 5, 2.5 hrs from cape town is not a good advert of what you get

we stayed in two horrendous accomodation in ella before getting to hikers lodge, and finding it was such a blessing. great location, clean rooms, and lovely staff :) great value for money for those who want to keep on the budget but stay in a clean, basic room that is 5 min away from the main street.

we stayed inside the walled city and passed this square a few times to go to bars and restaurants. it’s a lively area with street vendors and surrounded by shops and restaurants. pretty to see in the night and in the day.

we stayed last november (sorry for taking so long to review !) we had a absolutely fabulous stay and we felt like we were so welcome, karen was our host and she really does go over and above to make sure everything is simply perfect. i even got ill and needed some medicine which karen quickly sorted. the food from their own restaurant was very high quality & we enjoyed a bottle or two of wine as well 😉 there was also a good selection of local tours which we took several and each expertly organised by karen for us . the scuba dive shop is also next door. a easy walk upto the main town centre offered an interesting glimpse into bustling daily life. we enjoyed beach walks & definitely the sunday vibe on the beach is not to be missed ! one of the best things about the location of casa babi is the perfect view over the ‘local’ ferry / boat service out to the islands and the comings and goings of the villagers who work out on the islands. we also really enjoyed watching all the fishermen sailing into shore with their catch of the day. we were so grateful to be able to watch the flow of life, the people & especially the awesome tides of vilaculos from the beautiful garden of casa babi. we highly recommend this lovely little piece of paradise

we stayed one night at ella flower garden resort, and it was truly a memorable experience. the location is absolutely stunning, the food was delicious and exceeded expectations. what made the stay even more special was the warm and attentive service. a special thanks to chandrawathi from housekeeping who helped us a lot during our stay. highly recommended for anyone visiting ella—great food, amazing views, and top-notch service.

we stayed one night at ikoma wild camp and had a great experience. the tents were spacious, super comfy, and perfect for relaxing after a long day. what really stood out was the staff—they were so friendly and attentive. special thanks to the young girl in the restaurant (i forgot her name) who was always smiling and so kind. she made our stay even better. highly recommend this place for a unique and welcoming stay!

we stayed one night in richar and lucretia’s house and it was fantastic. great food and basic accommodation- warm blankets, superb views and super clean. such friendly hosts - they met us in the harbour and took us to a fiesta. just great. highly recommend - wish we could stay one more night!

we stayed one night with at jamal rum camp. we found it in a facebook group and reading the good comments about it, we decided to contact salem. he replied instantly and we agreed on a date for us to stay. he also arranged our taxi from petra to wadi rum for a more than fair price. he also arranged for us a day trip to the dead sea from and back to amman, that would have been way more expensive if had done it ourselves. the jamal rum camp did not disappoint. we stayed in of the bubble tents with a great view of the dessert. the tent itself has all you need to feel at home, ac, private bathroom, great bed, terrace and a panoramic window facing the desert that will make you feel like in another planet. a 4 hour tour exclusively for us in the desert was also included and provided by salem's son. the food included, especially dinner was delicious cooked in the traditional bedouin way. salem itself is a very talkative and funny guy and will go above and beyond to make you feel like family and welcomed. unexpectedly, we got a second short "desert tour", as salem himself took us back to the visitor center, through the desert, instead of the road 😃 overall salem and his family proved to be an excellent host, not only within his camp, but also helping us arrange part of our trip inside jordan. thank you for everything salem, we will be back some day.

we stayed overnight in new york city after returning from vacations in france. my kids wanted to see the 9/11 memorial so we took the e train early (7am) and arrived when the place was empty. the memorial was cordoned off until 8am when public access was allowed. it was beautiful, and very emotional. highly recommended. we did not visit the museum nearby due to lack of time but it looks very interesting.

we stayed there for one night during our visit to pangong, and the hospitality was even more impressive than the stunning location. the entire team was extremely helpful and went out of their way to make our stay memorable. the breakfast and lunch offered a delightful selection of delicious dishes. at night, we enjoyed stargazing right from our bed through the glass ceiling. they also offered two telescopes for stargazing near bonfire area. please note that there is no wifi and no cellular connection (airtel) in that location.

we stayed two nights with richar and his family and it was truly wonderful. you get the most scenic view of the lake right from their home, no cars on the island so only the sound of the birds and the sheep. all this while someone cooks you all three meals a day with fresh ingredients from the island! richar and his family were so sweet, making us feel at home and telling us about life and culture on the island. i am so glad we found this place!

we stopped at koko crater arch trail on the way, and it was an incredible experience! you can easily pull over on the side of the road and take in the stunning ocean view. the feeling of getting close to the water and heading towards the edge of the mountain was absolutely breathtaking. the sunset view, along with the mountains and water, made for an unforgettable moment. we only stayed for 10 minutes, but the beauty of the place left us in awe. highly recommend stopping here for a quick and relaxing break to soak in the amazing views!

we stopped by café diglas after dinner and had a lovely experience. the waiters were super friendly and welcoming, and the desserts were really good! a cozy spot that’s definitely worth visiting in vienna.
we stopped due suuden rain and discovered a jem in the mountain. very clean, hot shower, amazing view and tasty food. family took very nice care of us.

we stopped here during a 2-week cruise of the galapagos. it is a small island so we only walked around here for an hour. our guide told us how this island was a sort of 'kindergarten' for young sea lions, and bachelors. wildlife spotted: sea lions, lava lizard, brown pelican, frigatebirds.
we stopped here for over night stay during our komodo sailing trip. the water lookef great. yet we didn't get to swim in the water as our guide decided to move to different spots for snorkeling.
we stopped here on the party bus excursion. there is a bathroom for a fee and vendors. we could have skipped

we stopped in for food. we had traveled 1300 miles in the last 6 hours. tired and hungry, we entered. the food was over the top favorable. i had steak and eggs and my love had a jumbolaya omelette. her food smelled great and she loved it. drinks were ice cold. great view of jackson center. i got here 30 minutes before lunch and had breakfast. i wanted to eat breakfast and then lunch. lol. stop in. eat. enjoy.

we strongly recommend starting here and going south for this one way hike. beautiful along the way. took our group 4.5 hours to do so make sure to bring enough water and a snack and it’s intense at spots. loved the different terrain throughout! felt like ireland, costa rica, hawaii, and yosemite all in one… but it’s norway!

we stubbled across bernie and his team, inquiring about paragliding but eric said hang gliding was way cooler and more fun than anything else we could do. my kids ages 7 and 9 were the ones that wanted to fly. the whole team was super nice, experienced and made the kids (and parents) feel very safe and comfortable. the kids had an incredible experience. they came back with the biggest smiles on their faces. they are completely hooked. thank you bernie and team for the amazing memories and experience and for bringing them back in one piece!

we stumbled across arborek on accident. we had planned to stay in the pam islands but decided we must leave to find something new and followed some friends to arborek. now i realize this was meant to happen. when arriving to arborek we met githa the owner of arborek dive shop and she quickly fit is into her schedule and we went diving the next day. you can really tell that githa truly has a passion for diving and customer service. the prices were unbelievably fair at 600k idr (~37$ usd) per dive and she doesn’t try to charge you extra for boat transfers like other dive shops in raja. githa really makes this island special and i believe i will have to come back just for this dive shop. make the journey to come to arborek and see girha. make sure you’re certified because you need to be to dive with her.

we stumbled upon this place and ate here twice. over the 2 time visit we had sushi, frappe, noodles and breakfast. all of them were very tasty. in the morning, you can get freshly pressed orange juice. the place looks very well decorated and in style. good prices as well for what you get. coming back here again!

we stumbled upon this place while looking for somewhere to rent snorkel equipment in the middle of day and many other places were closed! we ended up renting equipment a few times as well as doing the discovery dive. the staff were great and i believe they have their own boat, which made the logistics more seamless. equipment was in good condition

we swam with penguins! what better way to describe what this site in galapagos has to offer. this place also has great scenery, and the opportunity to swim with crystal clear waters. definitely a unique place to visit.

we tackled this hike all the way to the ink pots, and i have to say for someone who doesn't regularly hike, it was quite a challenge with so many inclines. as other reviewers mentioned, it was no problem up to the upper falls of johnston canyon but the 3 kms to the pots were much tougher. the scenery was spectacular, though, and ended up being quite the accomplishment that i made it all the way. thank goodness it was mostly downhill to get back.
we take the walk with them. excellent experience, attention, the tour is a dream. thank you team for this beautiful excursion. 100% recommendable

we talked with a young man at the desk....he had a wealth of knowledge. talk to him!!! beautiful view! thee most sentimental part of this experience was seeing the names of the people who paid the ultimate sacrifice and the many monuments reflecting gratitude.

we thoroughly enjoyed our tour ! the tour guides were friendly and informative. they were highly skilled and knew how to guide us to all of the wildlife we wanted to see . we saw hammerheads , turtles , a sea lion and so much more . the tour felt very personal and they took their time with our family of 4. they seemed to really care about our experience. our dive master jonas put our mind at ease with his patience and assurance. we will be back !

we thought it was quite a cool place to visit. it's a controversial building that many do not like because of its deconstructivist style which goes against pretty much everything architecturally in the classical city of prague. great views though of that part of prague right on the eastern bank of the vlatava river. the observation platform at the very top is not disabled friendly. the ticket price is a relatively modest czk150/person. purchase of a drink from the glass bar does not gain you free admission to the observation deck! (well, it didn't for us when we visited in early july 2025). but overall, we thought it was worth a visit. unique building design. great views from the observation deck. friendly staff. a modest entrance fee. top tip: the toilets at the top of the building are free. 🥳🥂🎊🎉. it's expensive to pee in prague ☹️.

we thought it will be a nice park but it was so rundown. this park/, garden must be very nice in it's hay days but it has been neglected now. there were a couple of dog walkers there and nothing else. sat on the bench for a few minutes but atmosphere wasn't very appealing.

we thought reading the reviews that without a guide was good. we are above normal hikers and thought we do it. fortunately we ran in a local guide (maxwell) who took us for 1000 rps down the (trail). slippery and sliding and a trail??? he did a great job and we had to say. with a guide it made t way easier and felt more save. so find maxwell👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼

we throughly loved our best of yellowstone tour with gary! it was well worth the money! we weren’t in montana for too long but wanted to see as much as possible and gary made sure to make it happen! he was awesome! he taught us a lot of things and even told us interesting stores! can’t say enough wonderful things about this tour. may 2025!!

we took 2 motocross bikes for an hour ride and it was fabulous. driving off road for whole time and the guide adapts to your driving style. the best part is that we didn't have restrictions while driving, we could go as fast as we wanted and do whatever we want. at the begining you sign in the concract to provide security for you and for them. good thing is that they acept card payment. the service was amazing as well from our driver, to mechanics and to our guide abdul. stopped for a tea break what was good as well. we stayed in morroco for 10 days and this was the highlight of our visit. definitley would recomend to try motocross if you ride bikes. we were scared to book because we didn't find many reviews but this is new company( everything is new bikes, buggies and quads). we didn't regret choosing this company. it was absolutley amazing!!!
we took a boat tour out of here, it was a lot of fun!!

we took a combo tour (living desert in the morning and sandwiche harbour in the afternoon), and i don't regret a dollar spent. we had a wonderful day! during a living desert trip, you get to know creatures living in the desert that normal people can't see. the guide could find even very small animals. he gave a lot of information but in a very easy way. i loved it. there were snacks and drinks available during that tour. sandwich harbour ride was my main pointbof interest in namibia. our driver was great. the views were amazing. 5 cars were driving together, and all of got lovely lunch at the desert. with a sparkling wine for those who wanted.

we took a cooking class here and it was the best experience to have in siem reap. everything was well planned out and taken care of, and the staff was wonderful. we learned 3 delicious dishes and got to enjoy them in the restaurant afterwards. i cannot recommend enough!!

we took a day tour of titicaca lake from puno one day that included a stop on taquile island. we spent a few hours here, walking on the very well developed trails across the island, having a nice lunch at a restaurant run by local people, watching a local dance demonstration, and doing some shopping for woven goods and trinkets. we enjoyed the amazing panoramic views from the island, and exploring the large fresh water white sand beaches. be aware that there is some uphill walking, and even though the paths are paved for the most part, wear good and comfortable shoes. also, the weather can turn nasty at times, so be prepared for rain and take a jacket for windy days. be sure to wear a hat, too, as the sun can be brutal.

we took a great hike here. we have chosen a bigger round and just walked along paths to see the great sights and beautiful trees covered in snow and ice. it has been great. i can really recommend the trails.

we took a helicopter tour around zion national park and it was beautiful! it's definitely a must-see! great experience all the way around - from the friendly staff to the knowledgeable pilot to the great views. it's hard to capture how big everything looks from above, so these pictures are just a glimpse of what you will see!

we took a kayak tour in dubrovnik with this company. the guides and experience were worth the trip. they were very helpful giving us instruction and breaks through out the tour. the cave was amazing. it’s perfect for days when you want to cool off ! if you do book through them make sure to get matthew and roman! thank you for the great experience!

we took a kayak tour with yellowstone hiking guides. the team was all very friendly and accommodating and helped us get eveything set up. while we had experience with kayaking previously, they had great info and provided tips to help us improve our form. our guides were very knowledgeable and taught us new things we didn't know about the park wildlife and history. we had some great scenic and wildlife viewing opportunities and were able to experience yellowstone in a new, unique way.

we took a lovely horse-drawn carriage tour through the area surrounding the hofburg palace. the driver and her colleague were very friendly and gave us some interesting information about the sights along the route. however, they were unable to answer my very specific questions (i think i know vienna quite well). the horses seemed to be handled well. there is a short route (20 minutes, €60) and a long route (40 minutes, €105).
we took a nice walk around our airbnb and stumbled across this park. enjoyed some of the ruins

we took a party boat trip to the isla. the island is awesome. beautiful beaches. the market area is very much a hustle zone (i don’t particularly like being hustled to buy things). we drove golf carts round the island. it was fun and worthwhile.

we took a private boat tour of the elaphiti islands with toni as our captain. it was spectacular. toni was very competent and knew where to take us to snorkel and swim. he made dinner reservations for us on one of the islands. it was the best fish meal we consumed on the trip. he was able to tell us some of the history about the islands as well. we had a wonderful afternoon and would definitely book again.

we took a ride with karim and he was absolutely fantastic! so much knowledge and even a bit different take and path than when i went on a different cruise with floris! we loved the smaller boat with only a few other people! we were able to ask many questions of him and he had all the answers! he definitely knows the ins and outs of amsterdam! highly recommend him to be your tour guide!

we took a spectacular half-day safari with steve in early august, and had a delightful time looking for reindeer, grouse, a variety of ducks, and many other birds and mammals of the highlands. steve is a knowledgeable and engaging guide who pays enormous attention to his guests' comfort, and brings decades of experience to his role. on top of the focus on birds and mammals, steve knew the answers to my questions about the local wildflowers and trees, and provided an unforgettable touring drive through the moors. i would absolutely recommend making a tour with steve part of any visit to the cairngorms to get the most out of your time there!

we took a three-day tour. it was an unforgettable experience and our fondest memory of two months in bolivia. this wouldn't have been possible without our fantastic, attentive english-speaking guide, edwin. he took everything and everyone into account and made sure everything went smoothly. we also had a fantastic driver, bernardo, who created a great atmosphere in the car and guided us well along the way. we recommend it to everyone!

we took a tour for 2 people and traveled around this whole place. it was an absolutely exclusive experience 😍 here we saw a lot of deer, they live here freely ❤️ i recommend visiting this place, it is amazingly full of trees and plants. you will see rare white birds. we stopped for photos and to relax. of course, the experience will be exceptional if you go through this whole place on quad bikes. we were as if alone in this huge green space

we took a tour on a golf cart. we do not usually take a tour but i highly recommend this tour because it is crowded on the road with cars, buses, bikes and pedestrians. it was nice to have someone to maneuver you efficiently around to see all the different sights along this road. this area is incredible.

we took an amazing trip to the off the beaten path island of dominica, where the owner, chris, led a week long sperm whale encounter tour. the indigo team was incredibly respectful of the whales, and great at finding them. we swam with whales 4 of 6 days and dolphins the other 2 days. this part of the caribbean is full of life, and you’ll watch the fisherman pull bigger fish than you’ve ever caught into their small boats on hand lines. we stayed in the basic guesthouse in a small, rustic fishing village nestled in a rainforest basin. the jungle bay resort is a 20 minute walk or a short cab ride if you want a resort break. bring cash. if you have the energy after long days on the boat, there’s interesting snorkeling and hiking right in town, and a few tasty restaurants. we’d go with indigo again tomorrow if we could!
we took an hour cruise on thames river. it was ok , nothing extraordinary. you can combine with tower castle visit and make it a day. there are beverages for sale on board.

we took half day riding trip through the desert (4 hours) with sleep in the camp and camel ride in the sunrise, i recommend taking such a combination. alternatively if you have a time you can take whole day trip with cooking lunch on the desert. owner is organising whole experience, but is mostly responsible for the ride, other activites are handled by external places, but everything was nice and very well organised, you don't have to worry about anything and just enjoy your time.

we took our 6 year old on this hike in mid-may and the pine forest part of the trail was still completely snow -packed. he loved it. zero complaints the entire hike. the scenery is lovely, views phenomenal, decent trail conditions (had to climb over/under 3 fallen trees) and well worth the time

we took out gca tour on march 24,2025 out of flagstaff. our tour guide erick gonzalez was an excellent tour guide, who shared his experiences , knowledge and motivation. erick's knowledge of the geographical history of the area was very informative. erick also shared his musical talent playing the flute and singing a tribal song as we enjoyed the view. the lunch was exceptionally delicious. there was 4 people from sedona and 5 from flagstaff. a great group. thank you erick and gca.

we took out the e-mountain bikes today for the amazing 3 hour $49 winter special. we had time to do a range of the fantastic tracks and the bikes were excellent. communication and flexibility from nick was great, highly recommend!

we took part in level 3/4 rapids and it was amazing!! the experience was the best i had in comparison with colorado and tennessee. oso was our guide and he was funny (our raft name was the titanic!), knowledgeable and provided the best adventure out of everyone. the snacks and lunch were a nice touch. chose arenal rafting for all your white water rafting needs, you won’t regret it!

we took phi phi island tour with phuket sail tour. it was wonderful experience . it was a small group of 10 people. guide was very friendly. we started early , so found no crowd. we get ample time for snorkelling, did it at two places. no crowds. to our surprise, vegetarian food was very delicious. it is bit expensive compared to others, but worth every penny .

we took safari puffin tour with sea travel on our recent visit to farore island. captain rain was very informative and friendly. the tour was great and we were able to see the landmarks as well as the puffins. highly recommended sea view travel.

we took some family from out of town to better days bar in brickell this past saturday, and it was hands down one of the best nights we’ve had since moving to south florida. the vibe was incredible—great music, welcoming bartenders & crowd, and just an all-around fun energy. definitely a new favorite spot!

we took the 2-hour english underground pharmacy tour with helena. highlight of our trip! helena was so knowledgeable and passionate about the history of the city and the cellars we visited were so cool - the perfect balance of creepy and interesting! there are not many ways to see the real underground tunnels of the city aside from this. i highly recommend! not all of the tours are available in english so i am so glad this one was! such a unique experience we will never forget.

we took the 45 min okavango explore scenic flight. the plane was a 5 passengers single engine cessna, all passengers gets a window seat. the flight time from take off to landing was truly 45 min. the plane cruised at 500 ft the whole way, but it is still too far from the ground to take a good look or take photos of the animals. we did see elephants, zebras, hippos, giraffes and some types of antelopes. my iwatch was pinging throughout the flight that the background noise exceeded 90db which could cause temporary hearing loss. it would be good if the passengers are provided with a headset for noise reduction and also to communicate with the pilot in emergency.

we took the 7 lakes tour from bariloche to san martin de los andes. the van picks you up at your hotel and brings you back. it’s a 9 hour tour from point to point. the van is for 10-12 people. after 1 1/2 hrs we stopped in a small swiss style town for a 1/2 hr break. all buses stop here too. then you proceed on the road and stop at an overview of each lake. it was a clear sunny morning and the views were beautiful. the lakes are huge and at a distance. you eventually arrive at san martin de los angeles for about 2 hrs for lunch, shopping, or walking. san martin is a swiss style town with many restaurants and shops and flat surface walking. it is on the coast of the 7th lake. we enjoyed being able to stretch our legs and walk. our drive back was long and we didn’t stop again until we reached the town from the morning where all buses stop. we had a 25 min break then returned to the van for the trip back to bariloche. although it was a tour viewing beautiful lakes, the ride is very long. one more stop for bathroom breaks would have been appreciated. the ride back was a long time to be seated in a van. if you are older than 40, as we are, it can be very uncomfortable. my joints became too stiff at the end from lack of movement. we don’t regret being on the tour. but perhaps renting a car where we had control of when and where to stop would have been better for us.

we took the catamaran excursion to deer island with catamaran cruises and, although it wasn't a very sunny day, the experience was excellent. the attention of the team was remarkable, always helpful and attentive. the food was very good, they played good music and the general atmosphere was very relaxed and fun. we were lucky to share the ride with a group of locals who added a lot of good vibes. we had done other boat tours before, but this one really stood out above the rest. as for the island itself, we did not find it the most attractive part of the walk, perhaps also because of the weather that day. there isn't much to do, although they do offer optional activities like parasailing. personally, the beach we liked the most was le morne. beyond that, the best thing was the attention of the team, the catamaran (we went on the rapid) was very clean and well maintained, and a plus to highlight: the open bar of alcoholic beverages throughout the day, not only at lunch as on other tours. in short, a highly recommended experience. —- we did the île aux cerfs catamaran tour with catamaran cruises, and even though the day wasn't super sunny, the overall experience was excellent. the crew was very attentive and friendly, the food was good, the music set a great vibe, and the atmosphere was relaxed and fun. we were lucky to share the cruise with some locals, which made the day even more enjoyable — the group was really fun. we had done other boat tours before, but this one truly stood out from the rest. as for the island itself, we didn't find it especially exciting, maybe partly because of the weather. there aren't many things to do, although they offer optional activities like parasailing. personally, our favorite beach in mauritius was le morne. that said, the service from the team was excellent, the catamaran (speedboat) was super clean and well-kept, and one big plus: they offered unlimited alcoholic drinks all day long, not just at lunch like other tours. all in all, a very recommendable experience.

we took the cruise to spirit island and we were not disappointed! our guide, emily, and captain alec, made it the experience i hoped for and even more! i have wanted to do this for years and i am very happy it is now a reality!

we took the daughter of the peaks 2, on thursday july 31st and our tour guides were hayden and captain jenna, who were pretty awesome! although we felt like the price was steep, the trip was overall really nice. my in-laws absolutely loved it and especially enjoyed the 10seconds of complete silence to appreciate the nature, which was a great initiative led by hayden. the narration by hayden was also amazing and much appreciated, he managed to captivate my 4years old's attention, who listened very deligently and even had lots of questions for hayden later! thanks to hayden for being a great educator! overall a very relaxing and a peaceful way to experience and appreciate the lake minnewanka!

we took the denali helihiking tour on the tundra with denali backcountry guides . this was truly a “ bucket list” adventure! jeff and kathryn guided us safely and expertly on the helicopter and through the tundra , teaching us about the beautiful and special land above the tree line ! we saw a caribou herd , golden eagles , marmots , explored bear habitats and saw bear “diggings” , animal bones and antlers , fossil rocks and crossed crystal clear streams as they identified amazing flowers , grasses, vines and edible berries . thank you for a perfect day !

we took the dune buggy drive with dare devil adventures, and it was a blast—way more fun than we anticipated! the dunes were absolutely stunning, offering breathtaking views. one highlight was stopping for a beer atop a dune, soaking in the scenery. highly recommend for anyone seeking a fun, scenic ride close to swakopmund.

we took the first tundra wilderness tour (twt) of the day at 6 am on may 25. gorgeous day, excellent driver/guide in becky as 25-year veteran of the park, and blessed to get great views of denali and wildlife.
we took the funicular down to lower qc to look at all the historic sites. walking around we found the place royal with the old church and statue of louis xiv. very peaceful area.

we took the half day tour as a couple, it was over expectations, hadi from the reservation office was amazing, welcoming and made us feel comfortable, clean boat, friendly staff, the gentleman with the drinks and fruits onboard made us feel home and like a 5 stars hotel, overall it’s worth it and a must, thx again

we took the hidden wine cellar tour and it was absolutely wonderful! we had the best time with our guide and on a tour with only seven people, it was nice to be able to get to know other travelers. i would highly recommend this tour. we visited three locations with three full pours of unique, amazing austrian wines. there were also little snacks to accompany each of the tastings and we learned a great deal about the history of the city and its wine production. definitely take this tour!!!

we took the history-focused tour on the creole queen and loved it. charles chestnut was a great narrator, and his narration of hurricane katrina while coming up on the new orleans skyline -- and passing some of the levees that breached during the storm -- was a highlight of our trip. it's a great way to spend your time in new orleans.

we took the kids, this splash waterpark as part of our stay at the riu bambi hotel. this was one of the nicer venue for the kids. well worth the visit if your kids meat the age and high requirements. if not they have a smaller younger kid friendly attached water park. my only complaint is you were not allowed to bring food from the hotels to the venue. the only local drinks available or from machines that were partially not working and the location closes at 5 pm.

we took the phuket city tour and this was one of the places to visit. it is a beautiful and peaceful temple. the main chalong temple is built on three floors and there are stunning buddha statues on each floor. the terrace can also be accessed to enjoy a beautiful view of the temple park. don’t be surprised when the quiet and austere atmosphere of the temple is interrupted by the loud crackling sound of fire crackers. at wat chalong, phuket's largest buddhist temple, visitors light these crackers in large clay ovens near the temple's sermon hall as a traditional act of gratitude. the practice stems from a belief in the spiritual power of the temple's former abbots - when prayers are answered, devotees celebrate by igniting strings of firecrackers, their sharp reports echoing across the temple grounds. there are also some shops and eateries across the temple grounds. i would recommend this place.

we took the puffin tour on july 27. they use their charter fishing boat for the puffin tour, which has a great engine, plenty of outside seating and an enclosed cabin. no trouble going place to place to see puffins, caves and all the birds. loved our faroese captain and always felt safe. what a great way to see the faroe islands if you only have a day.

we took the sat2 tour and it was definitely worth the money. not only will you get a hotel pickup, blankets and a heaters to keep you warm, a lot(!) of good food, hot and cold beverages after the 1,5h introduction, but you will get jorge as well 😄 he is super knowable, enthusiastic and friendly. explains everything, answers your question and gives tips about buying, using and maintaining a telescope. the 5,5h until sunrise went by in no time. it was simply amazing and definitely worth the money. if there is one thing i would optimize, then it's the amount of food. at the end there were quite a lot of leftovers. either offer them as take away or bring a bit less in the first place. it hurts my heart, when food gets disposed. other than that, there is really nothing i can complain about. thank you, jorge, for this incredible night!

we took the sloth tour in the afternoon with our guide monica and it was awesome! with the help from monica we spotted 4 sloths and 1 of these 4 had a (not so small) baby and they were moving around as well. we also saw 2 red dart frogs (called blue jeans because of their blue legs) and 2 armadillos. monica was very friendly and knowledgeable and told us a lot of interessant facts about both the animals and the trees and plants! i can really recommend the sloth tour of go adventures!

we took the sold san juan boat tour february 10, 2020. the most amazing $10.00 we spent on the trip. i would suggest taking the tour at the beginning of your trip because the tour guide gives lots of useful information as well as places to visit and place to eat! beautiful views and great guide!! would do it again for sure!!

we took the sold san juan boat tour february 10, 2020. the most amazing $10.00 we spent on the trip. i would suggest taking the tour at the beginning of your trip because the tour guide gives lots of useful information as well as places to visit and place to eat! beautiful views and great guide!! would do it again for sure!!

we took the splash package and had a good time as a family. the aquarium is really small but the real thing we went for is the interaction with the dolphins. we took the splash package that comes with basic activities with the dolphins for about 20 minutes. the staff is friendly and they provide towels and shower access. i booked it online which gives you a 30% discount of the max price. the photo package is certainly expensive but they are good and if you want all the memories you will need to pay around $260 us dollars.

we took the sultan to the island of burano for lunch at the trattoria da romano! our only regret is that we didn’t book the sultan for the entire day! our captain was fun, knowledgeable and explained different areas of the lagoon on our way from venice to burano. we sipped prosecco under the canopy and enjoyed the tour and ride. i cannot recommend this enough!

we took this excursion just yesterday and happens to be my birthday, i must say it’s well worth it. not just because of the activities that includes in this trip but most of all the service we had. special mention to our group leader/guide “pineapple” at least that’s how he wanted to be called in our group iguana. he just served us very well and very energetic, fun guy, went above and beyond his duties. did not even expect or ask anything in return like tips but he very well deserved it and me and my espousa did just that. generally the whole experience and service were commendable, facilities are clean, great tasting food by their chef. five stars rating for the whole thing and if i can only give more than 5 stars to our leader guide then i would without a doubt. anyone visiting dr should try this excursion and i can guarantee you won’t be disappointed. cheers !!!

we took this hike at 12:00 p.m. luckily it was a breezy day, so we did not get too hot. i suggest you go early in the morning and take plenty of water. the hike is mainly an uphill climb. don't believe all of the people that promise you there is beer and margaritas at the top. lol just when you thought you were done you encounter the 99 steep stairs! though it is worth it. the site at the top is amazing. you get a beautiful view of the ocean and a lighthouse. make reservations ahead of time they fill up quickly.

we took this tour earlier this year in january and it was an absolutely fantastic day and one of the highlights of our trip in australia. our guide peter was one of the best tour guides i have ever had. so knowledgeable and passionate about the area and could answer any question. my advice to anyone considering a day trip to daintree - do it! and book with daintree tours! thank you again for such a wonderful experience :)

we took two hour morning trip through this beautifull area. the skipper took us to the sea eagles, which we were able to see from very close and we enjoyed some moments of speed on the water. it was great for me as well for the kids

we took two of our grandchildren for their 15th birthday for 10 days to cancun and this place was their favorite. raul was our tour guide and he went above and beyond to make our experience memorable. omar was our photographer and captured so many great moments. i would highly recommend this place

we totally enjoyed our sunrise trip and it exceeded our high expectations! very good communication & quick responses, from the very start. we did the phi-phi (not pee-pee!) sunrise tour, which i totally recommend, in order to avoid the large crowds on the islands, but also to experience the sunrise from out on the water, which is absolutely beautiful. pick up in vip van was on time and nice. the royal marina is a beautiful waiting spot. nice mini breakfast there, before we went out. i needed that first coffee, so early in the morning… wonderful, friendly and professional staff, including the captain (name), our guide noi noi , and the mate, weed. i hope i’ve got those names correct? safety first: very good attention to safety on & in the water. this is important to me, especially with children on board. the boat (simba 8) itself is ok. we sat at the back, which is the best place for getting an almost 360° view & taking photographs, plus also enjoying the great sound of the twin 250 engines, if you’re into that kind of thing, like me. .. the views on the trips themselves were fantastic. the boat is comfortable, even at high speed. maya bay was already filling up when we got there and looked great, but i wouldn’t wanna be there when it’s full… there was some mosquitoes on the short walk between the landing spot and the beach itself. tip: advise travelers to bring mosquito repellent. we got quite a few bites. lovely breakfast on the beach, well prepared by weed. the toilets on the island were unfortunately diabolical! the snorkeling gear provided was excellent. better than my own gear, which i took with me. there was plenty of sea life, like nemo, to be seen. that was quite a highlight, and it was fun in the water. and good to cool down. tip: pay attention to the strong sun and be sure to reapply some protection! some of us got quite a bit of sunburn on the tour. the buffet lunch back at the marina was excellent, with a good variety. every option was delicious. big thank you to the staff there! all in all, this was the highlight of our first visit to thailand. we will be back again and we’ll certainly be going on another sunrise tour with simba! our sincere so thanks again to all the great crew for making this possible!

we traveled with pablo for about 2 hours by sailboat, beautiful! he took us to all the places he could, halfway through the trip he made us a delicious coffee with bunin and pastafrola. it's very cold so if you don't have enough coat pablo will lend you one, a genius.

we travelled as a couple and stayed 6 nights at daroyen in december 2024. we chose to come there to dive around kri island. we used booking for the reservation. diving herman (the owner) arranged the diving with erik, a dive master that he hires for customers. equipments were in good condition, erik was very careful about safety of the dives and we had amazing dives with him. if you want to have a personalised dive trip and you don’t like to dive with a big group, then you will love it! room the chalets are very basic, just a mattress on the floor. a fan would be great as it becomes hot at night and despite asking prior to our trip there was none. if you are looking for comfort that’s not the place but we knew what we booked and it was fine for us. food the food was very basic and repetitive. one morning we had donuts coated with sugar with ants all over…and the last day i got a mild food poisoning. overall, food can be improved. staff & communication like many homestays in raja ampat, the locals speak little english. as my wife can speak bahasa it was easier otherwise it can be difficult to communicate. herman welcomed us and then had to leave for personal reasons and we didn’t see him again… erik could speak enough english for the diving. herman’s son was helpful to arrange the boats. the good point is the credit card accepted which is not so common for homestays. overall we had a great diving experience. the stay was average but good if you look at the price.

we travelled extra to try some food, but it was very overpriced. delicious, but not worth the extra journey. they have good baked goods and veggies. the overall feeling in the markthalle was very "modern", i would suggest farmers markets instead

we travelled with the company from puno to copacabana. the lady selling the ticket was very nice, but the 'guide' on the bus incredibly rude. didn't even let us open the curtain to see the supposedly scenic view we would have had all the way driving along the titicaca lake. very disappointed for a much higher price than other companies.

we tried more than one lodge in the uros community, and this one is definitely by far the best one! it is amazing the way the family makes you feel part of their community. the apartments are new and well kept, food is delicious, you are all the time involved in many activities. the family really puts an effort to make you feel home, welcomed, and to let you understand their roots and tradition (in other lodge is not the same for sure). moreover, good point, everything is included in the initial price (taxi boat; excursions; other activities; meals) - whereas in the other lodges they give you the initial price but once you get there they sum up any kind of fee for anything. iquiña lodge is 6/5! thank you so much❤️

we tried the wiener schnitzel which met our expectations. our table was a bit small to fit our dinner plates & drinks but as we didn't make a reservation, we were happy with it. waiters were friendly. my only disappointment was the state of the toilets, they should definitely be cleaned more frequently.

we truly enjoy looking for flea market wherever we travel. this outdoor market sells new and used items. our favorite that we came back two days in a row for were the large cups of natural fruit drinks, you definitely get your monies worth.

we truly enjoyed our visit to the lotus water puppet theater. this traditional vietnamese art form, performed on water with live music and narration, was both enchanting and educational. the puppeteers are clearly masters of their craft, and the show was full of humor, symbolism, and vibrant storytelling. the theater itself is cozy and well-organized, making it easy to enjoy the performance up close. we appreciated the english translations and program guide, which helped us follow each scene. it’s a wonderful way to connect with vietnam’s rich cultural heritage—suitable for all ages. highly recommended as part of your hanoi itinerary!

we turned up to their little place to book a custom private tour for 4 people the next day. absolutely fantastic, they took us to a private beach for lunch, unbelievable spots for snorkelling and other quiet beaches and lagoons. the lunch was great and a huge portion for us, they also provided great snorkelling gear. would definitely recommend for day trips out.

we underestimate the track, we thought it's gonna be easy since we've been to agung. but the view was so beautiful ❤️ too bad it was so cloudy when we reach the peak because we hike around 12 pm. the parking location was hard to find there's not much information about this hike on google, we almost hike in wrong path.

we used sundog tours for a full day tour and transportation from banff to jasper in may 2025 and for a couple of tours in jasper. on multiple tours/trips we had mike as our driver/tour guide. there are not enough words to describe what a great guide he was for us on our trip. can you say above and beyond? he's knowledgeable and funny and made sure everyone was comfortable and had everything they needed, took extra time to ensure we had amazing opportunities to see wildlife and helped one member of our party who has physical limitations to ensure she didn't miss out on anything. by the end of our two days with mike i felt we'd made a new friend. if you get mike as your guide you are 100% in good hands. highly recommend!

we used sundog tours twice during our stay and would highly recommend them. first we travelled from banff to jasper including photo opportunities at lake louise, peyto lake, and an extended stop at the columbia icefields where we could explore the athabasca glacier and step out onto the skywalk! lutz was our guide who was very informative and full of interesting stories! we also used sundog for an airport transfer from jasper to edmonton. dave was our driver who was friendly and attentive to the needs of the group, including a partially sighted passenger.

we used the get out pass and had a great experience. super easy and would do again. they even allow free re entry as long as you you’re there and had not left. instructions were pretty clear. 5mph, keep windows rolled up, doors shut. i believe tickets are $20 per person at the gate. there’s also a petting zoo that was included with the ticket. there’s a fish pond, food was 50 cents, it was definitely worth it seeing all the fish jumping for the food. only downside is that they didn’t have physical maps and only had a qr code at the entrance. i don’t find qr codes to always be the most convenient, but didn’t find this to be a huge issue.

we used this company for a private tour. nelson was our guide. we explored the ruins in tulum, swam in two incredible cenotes, snorkeled in a lagoon and the finally was swimming with sea turtles. this was by far the best excursion any of us had been on! nelson was very knowledgeable about the ruins and was an amazing guide in the cenote. we also had lunch which was mayan cooked chicken and pork. it was fantastic!! if you are ever in tulúm mexico i highly recommend do an excursion with this company. ed and bonnie were so great to work with on the planning side of things and fun people to hang out with as well. these pictures don’t do it all justice!

we used this for a one-day private tour to visit chichen itza, ek balam ruins, and cenotes. the price is higher than other tours because a japanese guide will be there all day in addition to the driver, but i think it is well worth it. they will introduce you to secluded cenotes that other tours do not cover, and you can incorporate them into your plan. thanks to this tour, we were able to go to a cenote that you can hardly find any photos of even if you search it on google. it was the new year's holiday and cancun itself was very crowded, but there were no other people in this cenote, so we were able to swim in it privately. our tour guide was the manager, mr. yoshida, and he is very knowledgeable about mayan ruins. he seems to have personally studied mayan ruins, and he will answer any questions you have. thank you very much for your help. thanks to you, we had a great trip.

we used to go here with my family about 20 years ago. it has changed: many of the small beautiful exclusive boutiques that carry italian leather shoes and bags are no longer there. saks fifth avenue has permanently closed. it looked sad ;( i’m glad the nice hotel st francis is still there as well as the sf cable cars

we used tourist israel for our airport transfers, hotel, and 4 tours while in the holy land. the customer service was amazing. they were responsive when we had questions and we loved all of our guides and drivers. we even spent a long day in petra, jordan and i would have never been able to do the border crossings without their guidance. go to israel! enjoy the beauty and no lines to see things. use tourist israel especially our guides: george, yana and omer

we very much enjoyed our gondola tour. we began with a short ~20 minute walk with a guide speaking via earphones about the history of venice and its gondolas. we then boarded the gondolas (we were lucky enough to get a full gondola for our party, not having to share it) and went on a ~30 minute trip along the canals. for a short while the route also took us into the grand canal itself. no guiding during the gondola trip, but we enjoyed taking pictures and looking at the scenery. catching a gondola via a "drop in" booking was 90 euros per boat so depending on how many you are, and you're mostly interested in the gondola ride itself, that might be more cost effective.

we visited 2 days in a row. the cost was reasonable. you pay by car load. we bought a senior pass for all national parks for a year and it was $20. no charge for the second day obviously. if i remember right it was $17 for a car for 3 days without a pass but i can't guarantee it. the first day we got there around noon. it was an hour wait to get in the gate. the second day we drove right in at about 8:30 am. both days the visitor center area was packed. you could barely get to the rim. once there you had to wait to get a clear shot. don't get me wrong, do it if it's what you can do. i was shocked that all across the top of the rim was asphalt trails and it made for much easier walking. it was relatively easy to get to the rim at the visitor center area and handicap accessible. i had flown over the canyon a few times, i'd seen lots of pictures. when you look over the rim of it the first time.... it will take your breath away. i've traveled to a lot of beautiful places, this was truly awe inspiring. so glad i could check it off my bucket list while i was still pretty mobile. the second day, we drove on past the visitor center. we found an empty parking lot and a sign that said 'to rim'. we had a bottle of water apiece and set off up the trail. i hadn't realized we were at 7,400 ft or so until we started a steady climb. my husband and i are in our mid 60's and after about 20 minutes of a steady up grade he was ready to turn back. i talked him into a few more yards and we saw the opening in the trees. we walked out of the trees and we were totally alone with the canyon. we almost cried because it was so incredibly beautiful. we spent about 2 hours walking the edge of the rim. we maybe saw 6 people.

we visited 20.november.2016. king nayapati sithu ,he has wronged his father and grandparents in the past . so he apologized them for his sin at the place at which pagodas was built for remembrance. he passed away while the temple has not been completed yet, and his son king zay ya thein ka continued to finish construction of temple.( by the history of stone letter)
