we visited 3 times within the same week. did various activities but on our third and final visit the staff’s attitude changed. when we arrived for 2x scuba dive we were correctly advised by a team member not to dive if you were not in good health or if you had any ear issues. after the first dive one of us did have ear pain so following the advice one of us didn’t have a second dive. subsequently we were told that they could not issue any refund. i then requested to change the activity instead of a refund to be told only if you want to snorkel, to which i declined not wanting to go back in the water with a bad ear also i’m not very good at it either! i then had to just sit and wait in the bar area whilst the others did their second dive. the bar man then proceeded to follow me around until the drinks bill was paid when my partner returned from the second dive. only after we were ready to leave and my partner also complained was i offered 10 minutes on a jet ski, despite having been sat waiting for an hour with nothing to do by myself and at this point it was already too late. i have to finish on a positive thought, the dive master is an amazing guy. from start to finish he made the dive an experience we won’t forget, the one star is all his!

we visited aeroxspace in july 2025 and our families had so much fun! we spent over 3 hours playing and having fun plus the food was really good. the vr experience was worth the extra cost and the kids loved the space coaster ride. highly recommended for a great family day out and parents can join in too 🤩

we visited american social, in brickell, for the first time this past weekend, looking for a cool water-front brunch place. american social did not disappoint! what a fun place to watch yachts go by all day long across the river. the music was a little loud for our taste, but it was a great atmosphere nonetheless. the booze list was extensive & their frosé was amazing! our brunch dishes were very good also. lavin, our female server, was super sweet, attentive & profesional. definitely recommend it for a super fun "boozy brunch" or any other occasion.

we visited arcos da lapa during the daytime and were thoroughly impressed by its stunning architecture and historic significance. the area is lively, with plenty of street vendors and local culture to experience. even though we didn't get to see it at night, the daytime visit alone made it a highlight of our trip. a must-see landmark for anyone visiting rio de janeiro!

we visited as part of our walking tour in kyoto and enjoyed our time wandering through all the beautiful areas near the shrine. the entrance is quite impressive leading you into a large area filled with many smaller shrines and walking paths that lead you through the park. the entire area is a peaceful place to spend time away from the crowded street of kyoto. overall, quite beautiful and worth a visit.

we visited as the 2.30pm tour was starting so we joined the group ($45 for a family of four - you can pay by card, no cash). aillie was our tour guide and she made it an interesting hour long visit to bare island uncovering the history of this unique location.
we visited awasi patagonia in march 2025 mainly for wildlife. we had a fantastic time. it is an amazing location with a great team. the food is amazing as well. thanks to everybody at awasi.

we visited beautiful oman in december 2024. after going through websites of various tour organisers in muscat, we apprehensively connected with charan jaimini of oman safari tour. his prompt responses and knowledge of the country put our doubts to rest. our 8 day itinerary was planned by charan and everything such as accommodation, vehicle etc were booked in a short time . the accommodation in all the cities was comfortable and we enjoyed our stay thoroughly. our driver cum guide, mehmood made our tour extra special. courteous, knowledgeable,and a charming person, mehmood made us feel very comfortable and educated us about oman's rich culture and modern endeavours. needless to say, we thoroughly enjoyed our trip and would love to return to oman soon to explore the other cities. we would highly recommend charan and his team at oman safari tour if you are planning to visit oman .

we visited bukha fort while driving along the scenic coastal road to khasab, it is situated just across the road from the beach and the location is very beautiful. while there is no entrance fee, the fort doesn't offer much in way of information on its history, the fort is completely empty and there was no one present at the time of our visit to give us a guided tour. it would have really enhanced the experience to know more about the history of the fort.

we visited cape town in june 2025 and were blown away by the beautiful nature, wildlife and cityscape. we were extremely fortunate to have experienced this beautiful city with our amazing guide, mr neil ferguson. upon greeting us at the airport, neil instantly made us feel at home with his warm hospitality and lively energy, and we couldn't help but feel his enthusiasm and love for the city rub off on us. he is "google, cape town edition" - ask him any question and be prepared to learn many bonus gems of information about the city on top of the wealth of knowledge he has on all the major sites. his heart, humour and dedication to showcase cape town to the world is a big reason why this trip will hold a special place in our hearts. you will not regret choosing neil as your guide.

we visited during the summer festival. there was a concert projected on the rathaus exterior while the park was filled with vendors selling a variety of food and drinks. it was very crowded, but a lot of fun.

we visited gibson house today as part of open house toronto and were thoroughly impressed. tucked away in the modern bustle of north york, this beautifully preserved georgian home offers a fascinating window into toronto’s early settler history. the staff and volunteers were incredibly knowledgeable and welcoming, providing great context on the gibson family and life in the 1850s. from the working kitchen hearth to the intricate period furniture and textiles, every room was filled with detail and care. we especially appreciated the stories about david gibson and his involvement in the 1837 rebellion—history really came alive! this site is a peaceful, well-curated experience that’s perfect for history lovers, families, or anyone looking to discover a quiet and educational escape in the city. highly recommend stopping by if you’re in the area—or planning next year’s open house itinerary!

we visited golden lane to know about the history. it is small and crowded during peak times. can not visit alone to golden lane and it is required to buy full package of czk 450 which includes cathedral and prague castle. tickets can be bought at the entrance.

we visited golden lane to know about the history. it is small and crowded during peak times. can not visit alone to golden lane and it is required to buy full package of czk 450 which includes cathedral and prague castle. tickets can be bought at the entrance.

we visited here at night in mid-june. the main gate is perfect, it's impressive on its own, but the view through it toward the lit street was just as stunning. at night the shrine is lit and having quite cozy atmosphere. i was lucky to watch a festival performance. the kagura stage decorated with lots of lanterns looked pretty nice. there’s a park behind the shrine, but it was quite dark, so we didn’t explore it further.
we visited here just for the bridge. we like to pay tribute to the bridge builders 75 years ago. without them, we won't have today's sedona. besides, the bridge looks beautiful.

we visited immersive gamebox in southbank for a birthday celebration, and it was the perfect activity for the occasion. it’s such a fun and unique experience, especially for couples or groups looking for something different. the motion-tracking, touch-sensitive walls, and projection-mapped environment make the gameplay incredibly immersive without the need for bulky headsets. with a great selection of games like squid game, angry birds, alien aptitude test, and temple of coins, there’s something for everyone. we played squid game, and it was a fantastic mix of teamwork, strategy, and excitement. the gameplay was smooth, interactive, and just the right level of challenging. whether you’re celebrating a special occasion, planning a date, or just looking for something fun to do, this is an amazing experience for couples, friends, and families. the staff were friendly and helpful, and the prime southbank location makes it easy to turn into a full day out.
we visited in june 2023, food is good, ambience is breathtaking, just a small suggestion- go for cottages than tents. the washrooms and tents are very tiny and average.

we visited in late june and although the lavender weren't in full bloom, the sights were lovely. the staff was kind and purchasing tickets for the tractor were very easy. overall, i strongly recommend visiting in july when everything is in full bloom. unfortunately there are many tourists even in june so be prepared for long lines. overall a great experience.

we visited in late june and although the lavender weren't in full bloom, the sights were lovely. the staff was kind and purchasing tickets for the tractor were very easy. overall, i strongly recommend visiting in july when everything is in full bloom. unfortunately there are many tourists even in june so be prepared for long lines. overall a great experience.

we visited in march and were extremely disappointed. the pictures online make this place look like a lush paradise, but the reality was far from it. the trail was in poor condition—muddy, slippery, and clearly neglected. when we finally reached the waterfall, the water was brown and foamy, likely polluted, and it smelled awful. it honestly looked like cow waste was running through it. this place is totally not worth the visit. save your time and go somewhere else that’s better maintained and cleaner.

we visited in may 2025. we took the hestur cave boat tour. this was our favorite boat trip by far in the faroe islands. the tour starts at the gamlarætt ferry port which is a short ride from torshavn. we parked along the water. there isn't a parking lot so just park near where you can without blocking any access. leave everything in your car as you only need your keys and camera. we were outfitted with waterproof full body suits, helmets, and gloves. your shoes will be splashed so make sure they are protected. the rib boat sits two by two. the seats looked like as if you are riding a horse with some bars to hold on to. the closer to the front, the more you will buck. we were the last ones on the boat, so we got the bench seating in the back behind the captain. i feel like these were the best seats on the boat. the captain talked to us the whole trip pointing out different features and telling us stories. the water will definitely spray you in the back of the boat. i rather get wet versus banged around in the front. we were able to stand and sit in the back as we wanted. on our trip the weather didn't allow for access to the largest cave due to the roughness of the seas, but the trip was spectacular anyways. we went into plenty of caves and saw puffins and seals. the boat is powerful, and the captain is a real captain. not just a tour guide. he mastered the waves with skill. i loved the rock music played while driving through the sea. it made it really fun like we were on a mission.

we visited in november, planning to do some birdwatching and see if we can find squirrels. the park was perfectly described with the word 'koyo', as the autumn foliage was outstanding! in the pond we found a group of mandaring ducks, mallards and other songbirds. we also found squirrels! some people offered nuts and acorns. don't feed the crows! if you visit this park, i'd recommend to also see the hokkaido jingu shrine and the jingu tea room!

we visited in sept. '23 and it did not disappoint. absolutely stunning - and truly one of the most beautiful thermal features in the entire park. the vivid blues, greens, and yellows swirl together like a painting in motion. standing at the edge of it feels almost sacred. but it’s also bittersweet. morning glory has faded from its once-brilliant sapphire hues because of trash and debris thrown in over the years, blocking its vents and cooling the water. people literally treated this natural wonder like a garbage can. it’s heartbreaking - and a powerful reminder of how fragile these places are. still, even in its changed state, morning glory pool is breathtaking. i’m so glad i got to see it… and i hope future visitors treat it with the awe and care it deserves.

we visited in the last week of april. it was extremely sunny and windy, but that didn’t take away from the experience. we took a ferry that brought us up close to the statue of liberty—it was truly amazing! the views of the statue and the new york city skyline were breathtaking. a must-visit spot for anyone coming to nyc.

we visited in the morning around 10-11 and it was already full of people. do note there is a limited timeframe that we can visit the place to be respectful of the locals living there. we also have to whisper when talking to each other to keep the voices down. it's nice to walk around and explore the traditional village. do walk into some shops or cafes as they would also have nice interiors reflecting the traditional designs. it really does feel like you're back in the olden times.

we visited isokuru gorge. fantastic & very interesting sights, and a good staircase workout at one point😅. easy enough access and a wooden walkway in the gorge itself.

we visited israel february 2022 and ami was our private guide for 4 days. we did 2 days of walking tours in old jerusalem, a day in bethlehem plus herodium, and a day visiting qumran, masada, ein gedi, dead sea and jericho. we were amazed with his vast knowledge and entertaining style; his understanding of history and religion was the reason why our trip was outstanding. multiple guides we met on our way confirmed he is the best israel guide. we felt very safe everywhere we went with him. we also experienced a variety of local food enhanced by his past experience as a chef. a+++

we visited jazz museum during our visit to new orleans. it was my first time visiting the city and the french quarters. i loved it. we liked the museum too. i was not very familiar with jazz culture but i learned a lot during my visit to museum. the third floor had a stage with live performing artists. and we enjoyed that too. we visited new orleans during the french quarters festival and defiantly would love to come again.

we visited kailua beach park on a wednesday afternoon. even though it wasn’t a weekend or holiday, both parking lots were completely full. after driving around for a bit, we luckily found a spot near buzz’s original steak house across the street. parking here is definitely more challenging than some reviews suggest. the beach itself is gorgeous — super soft white sand and clear blue water. we even spotted a sea turtle! honestly, while it’s beautiful, it didn’t completely blow me away compared to some other beaches in oahu. the shallow bay and protection of popoia island provide calm waters, great if you have small children not used to the surfing waves of most beaches. watching people kayaking and sailing turned out to be part of the fun. with the picnic grounds, public restrooms and showers the park is great for a full day outing. one of my favorite parts was the small stretch of rocky shoreline at the southeastern end of the beach, near the lanikai monument. it’s peaceful, picturesque, and perfect for photos. from there, you can enjoy sweeping views of kailua beach, the nearby lanikai beach, and the beautiful offshore islands, moku nui and moku iki.

we visited kamari beach watersports last summer for jet ski rental. was one of the most beautiful moment that we had and we created very nice memories ! the team was very helpfull and profesional with service on very high level ! the equipment was brand new and the jet ski that we rent was the latest model of yamaha from luxurious series! we was also very impressed of the safety briefing and how important is the safety of the customers to them ! was the most nice moment that we had when we visited the island ! highly recommended !!!

we visited kenya in summer 2024 and we stayed at mara kimana camp when we visited masai mara national park. we had visited several other parks during the trip but this was our favorite place to stay! the place is beautiful and very family friendly with several board games, fire and popcorn available every evening. we enjoyed safaris during the day and looked forward to coming back to the camp for a relaxed evening with family amidst beautiful surroundings and always a twist of humor (see pic). food was delicious and the staff was very friendly and our 11-year old kid made a special bond with a few of them and was a tad bit sad to leave them. if we find ourselves in mara again, we would definitely stay at mara kimana.

we visited leh palace during our family trip, and it was a great experience. the palace is old and beautiful, with amazing views of the mountains and the city below. it felt like stepping back in time. the walk up to the palace is all by stairs, but it was worth it. be aware for someone in wheelchair. inside, we saw old paintings, wooden windows, and traditional rooms. there's also an exhibition room, and theatre room for film projection about the history of the venue. it was a peaceful and special place to visit. took many nice photos. a must-see in leh!

we visited mandai rainforest resort by banyan tree over the weekend with my family. since the resort is quite new, the facilities were very clean and well-maintained. although i’ve been to mandai many times to visit the singapore zoo and bird paradise, this was my first time coming to the resort area. we arrived by taxi, and check-in was not the smoothest experience. the kiosk wasn’t functioning properly, and since the lobby is an open-air space, my 3-year-old son had a hard time waiting. thankfully, the staff were very kind and assisted us through the process, which helped a lot. in the afternoon, we tried the swimming pool. it wasn’t particularly special — the pool was smaller than expected, and there weren’t many sunbeds, so it could get uncomfortable when more guests arrived. still, swimming while overlooking the rainforest was a unique and refreshing experience. the room itself wasn’t extraordinary, though i appreciated the sustainability efforts, such as limiting the temperature control to not go below 24°c. we completely understood the intent, but the touchscreen control panel kept malfunctioning, which made things a bit inconvenient. for dinner and breakfast, we had the buffet at the same venue. the food was not bad at all, though the variety was limited, and the wine selection felt a bit lacking. on the positive side, the portions were generous, which we appreciated. overall, it was an interesting experience, but i’m not sure if we’ll return. with so many excellent hotels in the city and better options in nearby countries at a similar price point, it may not be our first choice next time.

we visited may 2025. the food here was excellent. it was so good we came back a second time on our trip. this was one of the top restaurants. the fried chicken and fish were all delicious. good desserts as well. we beat the rush of a bus load of tourists who emptied into the restaurant for the buffet. if you have the time, order a meal from the counter.

we visited may 2025. there is a parking lot on the left side of the road before you get into town. there is a red house near the start of the trail that collects the hiking fee. the trail out to the lighthouse is uphill. the trail needs some maintenance as it gets very muddy and is difficult to traverse in some areas. walking sticks were necessary to keep balance through the muddy ridges. the view of the ocean and cliffs near the lighthouse are spectacular and worth the hike.

we visited may 2025. there is a parking lot on the left side of the road before you get into town. there is a red house near the start of the trail that collects the hiking fee. the trail out to the lighthouse is uphill. the trail needs some maintenance as it gets very muddy and is difficult to traverse in some areas. walking sticks were necessary to keep balance through the muddy ridges. the view of the ocean and cliffs near the lighthouse are spectacular and worth the hike.

we visited midday and had an amazing experience—no lines, no waiting. we walked right in and were able to explore freely. the area is beautiful and perfect for taking photos. we enjoyed the sights, soaked in the atmosphere, and appreciated the opportunity to see so much culture and history in one place. it’s definitely a cool spot to bring someone special, hang out, and even take time to read up on the local landmarks and museum exhibits. highly recommend if you're in the area!

we visited mikra thira winery in july — just a short 10-minute ferry ride from ammoudi bay. upon arrival, we were warmly welcomed by efi, our guide, whose deep knowledge made the tour both informative and engaging. take the time to visit, do some wine tasting, and simply enjoy the peaceful surroundings. and don’t leave without picking up a few bottles — you’ll definitely want to bring the taste of this place home!

we visited misool september 2024 and had an incredible week on this secluded island. from the pickup in sorong until the drop off, everything was so well organized, which we did appreciate. from the first step on the island until we left, every second was top notch. the whole team of misool is friendly, welcoming, smiling all the time and letting you feel like part of the family. the food was so various, healthy and we missed nothing. really enjoyed the vegan and vegetarian choices a lot and liked every single meal. the diving and snorkeling trips were all great and but the house reef as well was one of a kind, with a varity of fish, turtles, sharks, squids etc. you could not ask for more. of course the costs are not low but they are worth it and we will definitely come back! thanks to the whole misool team! felix and sandra

we visited mookiland bali yesterday with our daughter and her cousins and had such a great time! the outdoor play area has a fantastic variety of bouncy castles and obstacle courses that cater to different ages and difficulty levels. when we arrived around 1:00pm, it was still quite empty which was perfect for the kids to explore freely. it did get busier as time went on, but never felt too crowded or overwhelming. the area is relatively shaded, with a comfortable seating area for adults to relax, grab a bite, and stay cool. the bathrooms were clean, and all the staff we interacted with were super friendly. we stayed for about 2 hours and were lucky with the weather—it was breezy with little sun, which made the experience even better. despite being near rice fields, there were surprisingly no mosquitoes, which was a pleasant surprise! one thing to note: pricing seems to vary depending on whether you speak bahasa or english, and you can get a discount if you follow them on instagram first, so that’s worth doing. overall, the place was clean, well-run, and the kids had an absolute blast. we’d definitely recommend it and plan to come back again in the future!

we visited museum gherdëina on the last day of a week long stay in ortisei, and it truly enhanced the cultural, linguistic, historical, architectural, geological observations we had been making and discussing during our travels. i was happy to support this museum and their work to preserve thousands of years of history and culture in the region. i urge anyone with a critical and curious mind to visit.

we visited on a day when the temperature was a freezing -15°c, making it an incredibly cold experience! despite the chilly weather, exploring the local market, food stalls, and wet market was absolutely worth it. the market had a vibrant atmosphere with a great variety of fresh produce, local delicacies, and street food. even in the cold, the vendors were friendly and welcoming, offering warm and hearty dishes that were perfect for the weather. if you’re planning to visit during winter, be sure to dress warmly! the cold can be intense, but the amazing food and unique market experience make it a must-visit spot. definitely a place to explore for those who love authentic local vibes and delicious street eats!

we visited on a tuesday evening, arrived around 6pm. 2 kids (7 and 8). it's not really a theme park, rather a fairground. there are 2 tickets: a basic ticket (85k; entry only) and a full ticket (250k; entry plus every ride one time). 3 of the main rides (including the ferris wheel) were closed but you don't get a compensation for it, can't do an extra ride on something else. if you want to do extra rides, you pay extra - and those, too, have inflated prices for foreigners. the park was deserted and in dire need of repairs. most attractions were really old, damaged or out of order. there was only 1 5d film on show and since there isn't really a lot else to do and i specifically asked if it was appropriate for children, we went in to see it. it was some kind of dated horror/monster film, my 7 year old was completely freaked out. there are only 10-12 working attractions, all of which are old and very basic (i would not recommend going with children over 8 or 9 years old if you are used to european/american/australian theme parks). there are no queues so it took us just an hour to do all of them. staff are friendly but there are more of them than there are visitors. the kids had a good time but they don't pay the bills of course and frankly i don't think it's worth the money. indonesians pay 105k which is a fair price seeing how basic and decrepit the attractions are. for 14€ per person (250k) there are way better playgrounds in europe (belgium/netherlands) with more modern equipment and better safety instructions where the kids can play all day. now i paid 42€ for 1 hour which is just not worth it. there is a restaurant with some very simple fast food options on the menu, but that too was mostly deserted.

we visited on a weekday morning and there were already many visitors. there are three waterfalls - it's easy to get the first and second but beware that the path to the third is very muddy and slippery. we enjoyed the first waterfall because there were less people and felt more relaxing. spent around 30-40 minutes here.
we visited on august 3rd. it was a great visit. everyone had a section of the museum that was awesome for them.

we visited on sunday, this is a fabulous day out for all the family. lots of lovely stalls with such a variety of items, new, vintage, handmade etc including some personalised while you wait. loads of places to eat and drink, some inside, and some great street food outside. excellent food hygiene ratings for most. all stall holders were helpful and friendly at times giving tourist information support.
we visited only the red building. inside it has a big statue of budhha. we skipped white building coz it has many stairs

we visited phantom peak on a very hot day, but the heat definitely didn’t take away from how brilliant the experience was! the activities, immersive world, and puzzles kept us fully engaged and entertained throughout. we went as a group of five for a chilled hen do, and it was such a fun and unique way to celebrate together—there’s something for everyone to enjoy. honestly, we could’ve stayed all day exploring everything! the attention to detail is incredible, and the staff really help bring the whole adventure to life. highly recommend for anyone looking for something quirky, fun, and memorable!

we visited phuket elephant sanctuary and it was truly a memorable and meaningful experience. i had been wanting to get up close to elephants, but only in a respectful and ethical way—and this sanctuary is exactly that. it’s a peaceful haven where rescued elephants can roam freely, heal, and live out their lives as they should—without riding, forced bathing, or unnatural interactions with humans. the sanctuary is fully focused on the well-being of these majestic animals, and your visit directly supports their ongoing care—providing food, medical treatment, and funding for future rescues. i highly recommend visiting to witness these incredible creatures in a kind, ethical environment. not only will you have a fantastic day, but you’ll also be contributing to something truly worthwhile.

we visited pura puseh desa batuan in mid-april 2025 and were truly captivated by its rich balinese heritage and stunning architecture. the temple is beautifully preserved and offers a peaceful atmosphere, perfect for learning about local culture and history. a must-visit for anyone interested in bali's spiritual and artistic traditions!

we visited scape park during a family vacation to the dominican republic after coming across it online—it looked like a fun, adventurous way to explore some of the country’s natural beauty. although our hotel concierge seemed uninterested and recommended a different park, we chose this one for its variety of activities, and overall, it delivered a memorable day. the park offered stunningly clear water to swim in, a zip-line straight into a pool, an underground cave tour, and walked a self-guided historical and cultural trail where you can learn a lot. the cenote was beautiful and cold, though the walk there was unexpectedly long and through muddy, uneven terrain, so be prepared. other unique touches included an iguana enclosure you could walk through and a lively “monkey island” full of mischievous, entertaining monkeys. we didn’t do everything, but what we did was enjoyable. that said, the park layout requires a lot of walking, and things are spread out more than you’d expect. the map doesn’t quite reflect the actual distances, and it’s definitely not suited for young kids, people with mobility issues, or anyone pregnant (many activities prohibit participation for safety reasons). food options were limited and overpriced for the basic item you get. lockers are also inconveniently located far from most activities, so if you’re visiting, it’s really helpful to go with someone willing to sit some things out and keep an eye on your belongings. in the end, i’m glad we went—it was a full, adventurous day and gave us a great mix of nature and excitement. but it’s also the kind of place where one visit feels like enough. if you’re in punta cana and up for a high-energy day outdoors, it’s worth checking out—but go prepared, wear good shoes, and pack light.

we visited seixal before but missed this beautiful spot. only when we booked a local guide and traveled to seixal again he showed this beautiful natural lava pool which is must see! also the water is quite warm at the end of april so consider taking a nice swim!

we visited seven dials right after opening hours. we were attracted by the smell of freshly prepared food and inadvertently stumbled upon this jewel. the pulled pork bagel here is easily one of the best i've ever had.

we visited several exhibitions that were held there, some of them were useless, some of them were nice, but i have to say what i enjoyed the most was the view from the highest floor, from which you can see all the major monuments of paris. the gift shop had some nice things, although it’s a bit expensive. the building is ugly from the outside, but very spacious from the inside.

we visited several hot pools on our trek north and waikite valley was the hottest and the most "natural" in it's relationship to the environment. a very pleasant stay and a bargain at $79 for a powered site and all the hot soaks you could wish for

we visited sydney zoo with my old parents and the kids. we had a good day and enjoyed it. we couldn’t find some animals, which was funny — maybe we missed them! the zoo isn’t very big, and there weren’t tons of animals, but what we saw was nice. the entrance fee was a bit pricey, i think. overall, we had fun and everyone enjoyed it. the kids loved seeing the animals, and my parents liked the easy access and shade. would go again, just maybe not for the animals alone, it’s more for a family day out.

we visited the aquarium for something to do that was kid friendly while in town. we did appreciate the aesthetics for many of the exhibits, and it was fun seeing the insect portion. walking through the butterflies was very enjoyable, and you can interact with the stingrays, too. pricing was quite steep in comparison to other, larger aquariums that we have visited. you are paying for the big, city location more than you are paying for the experience, in my opinion. we walked the whole thing in about 1.5 hours. overall a fun little place if you need a break from the heat!

we visited the bali swing with some friends during our holiday, and it was such a fun experience! the hill leading up was a little steep, but once you’re there the swings are absolutely fantastic and well worth it. some of the girls hired dresses for photos, which added an extra touch and made the experience even more memorable. the staff were friendly and helpful, and the whole setup felt safe and well organised. we had a great time and would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for something unique and exciting to do while in bali.

we visited the baths as part of a group tour from 9:30-10:30 am and the place was virtually deserted which gives a nice break from the crowd of the colosseum and other popular roman landmarks. the structures are impressive and show how powerful rome was at its apogee.

we visited the berliner trödelmarkt on a hot day and still really enjoyed it. there’s an impressive variety of jewelry, porcelain, and glassware for sale, plus plenty of other vintage finds. prices range from cheap to definitely overpriced, so be ready to haggle—most vendors expect it. it’s split between more antique/art-style pieces and classic flea market goods. there are food and drink stands nearby, and you can always escape into tiergarten for some shade after browsing. it’s a fun stop if you like hunting for treasures, but bring cash, water, and your bargaining skills.

we visited the convent garden market today before heading to lunch. there's some construction going on in front of the market, but the market remains open for local tourists. the market was enticing to the eyes with a variety of products, we visited the plant store and bought a bamboo shoot which is right opposite the entrance of the market. we also found a lot of scrumptious desserts in the market. there was also a person hand crochetting characters like stuffed toys to the end of the market adjoining an uncle selling handmade clay ornaments made by his daughter. we bought toys and earrings from both the stores to support local businesses. i would definitely recommend the two stores if you're looking for something unique and a gifting experience. the bakery to the end next to new delhi had a lot of interesting desserts. you should actually visit the place, it's amazingggg 🤩🤩🤩

we visited the dubai frame back in may 2025, and overall it was a unique and enjoyable experience. the iconic structure offers breathtaking panoramic views—with old dubai on one side and the modern skyline on the other, perfectly capturing the city’s transformation. smooth lift experience: the high-speed glass elevator ride to the top was seamless and comfortable. it offers a quick, scenic ascent with minimal wait time. observation deck & glass floor: the views from the top are stunning, and the glass floor walkway adds a fun, slightly daring twist that’s great for photos. museum experience: the ground-level museum gives an engaging overview of dubai’s past, present, and future in a compact and visually rich format. note: it can get crowded during peak hours, especially near the glass floor section. the entire visit can be done in about 45–60 minutes, making it a perfect quick stop for tourists with a tight itinerary.

we visited the garden because it was included in our city card and we were completely grateful. it’s a small garden but very nice and cozy, it was very well keep and all the plants looked great. nice spot to chill for a wile, as there is plenty of place to sit and enjoy nature. i recommend visiting the cafe! it’s a very cool restaurant and the beverages were good. the butterflys and the bamboo were our favourite.

we visited the lodge while camping at the campsite. the staff were friendly and we were impressed with the lodge facilities. a downside for us was that after our stay, we received an email that we did not pay for one item from the curio shop. however, this item was paid for in cash by us at the lodge. this discrepancy does leave a bit of a sour taste and causes us to distrust the staffmember who handled the transaction.

we visited the museum of the southern jewish experience and found it to be a very well done museum with interesting content. after entering we watched a short film that we found to be well done. after watching the film we walked through several galleries, each depicting a different topic. the staff is always close by and eager to answer any question. for us this was a truly enjoyable experience.

we visited the museum while sightseeing in london. we went with my wife and two sons, ages 4 and 2. there were many exhibits that were just for viewing, and the children seemed disappointed that there were few rides they could actually ride. there were also not many play areas and exhibits for the large number of visitors. while it was nice that the annual pass allowed unlimited entry, it seemed a bit pricey. you might be more satisfied if you went somewhere else for sightseeing.

we visited the national maritime museum in greenwich, and it was a fantastic experience—especially since admission is free and there was no lineup when we arrived! as soon as we walked in, the ocean-themed ocean court greeted us with its soaring glass ceiling and striking ship models, creating a bright, welcoming atmosphere that's both grand and engaging . it felt like stepping into another world—full of maritime adventure and history. the museum’s galleries are thoughtfully laid out, guiding us from the icy arctic to the sun-soaked pacific. highlights included the nelson, navy, nation gallery, where you can see nelson’s actual uniform, complete with the bullet hole—a vivid piece of history . other favorites were the sea things gallery, showcasing a fascinating collection from treasure trove pieces to roman anchors, and the pacific encounters gallery, illustrating cultural connections across the ocean . a major bonus for families: the ahoy! children’s gallery and the cove playground offer interactive fun, making it easy to spend a few hours exploring with kids without breaking the bank . the museum is free to enter—though some temporary exhibitions may have a fee—and despite its popularity, we walked right in without waiting at all . spending an hour or two is possible at a relaxed pace, though with all the exhibits, you could easily linger for three hours or more . what made our visit so great: no lines: instant entry and no queues. free admission: access to vast, beautifully curated galleries. rich story-telling: from epic sea voyages to nelson’s wartime legacy. family-friendly: interactive areas kept everyone engaged. stunning design: striking architecture and a welcoming central court. in short, the national maritime museum is a hidden gem in greenwich—free, fascinating, and surprisingly relaxed. whether you're a history enthusiast, a family with little explorers, or just browsing between other greenwich landmarks, it's a must-visit. highly recommended!

we visited the old town square during the christmas market, and it was an absolutely magical experience. the entire square was beautifully decorated with festive lights, a stunning christmas tree, and charming wooden stalls that created a warm and joyful atmosphere, even in the cold december air. there was a wide variety of food to try from traditional roasted chestnuts to mulled wine and hearty sausages. each stall offered something unique, and the aromas alone were enough to make you stop and explore. christmas music played in the background, and occasional live performances added to the festive vibe. despite the crowds, everything felt organized and welcoming. one of the highlights of our visit was taking a horse chariot ride around the old town. it was a fun and peaceful 20 minute ride that gave us a unique view of the square and surrounding streets, all lit up for the season. it felt like stepping into a fairy tale. it was a memorable time and a highlight of our trip. if you’re in prague during the holiday season, don’t miss the old town square christmas market, it captures the spirit of christmas in the most enchanting way.

we visited the park today and had an amazing time. we came early so we could join the free tour at 9:30, the lady that did the tour was absolutely fantastic, she was very informative and communicative and she has a great sense of humor. after the tour we decided to go to the viewpoint which did not dissapoint. this is a must see when at praslin, do not miss it.

we visited the park today and had an amazing time. we came early so we could join the free tour at 9:30, the lady that did the tour was absolutely fantastic, she was very informative and communicative and she has a great sense of humor. after the tour we decided to go to the viewpoint which did not dissapoint. this is a must see when at praslin, do not miss it.

we visited the salt lagoons and it was an incredible experience! the views were breathtaking – it felt like everything was covered in salt, creating a surreal and magical landscape. you can swim in the lagoon, although we expected the water to be warm… it was actually very cold (we went in the winter season). important notes: – don’t jump into the water – the cold shock can be dangerous. – the water is extremely salty, so it’s best to float on your back, not your stomach. even though the water was cold, the air temperature was very pleasant, and the swim was absolutely worth it. one important warning: check the condition of your rental car’s tires before heading out. we got a flat – not because of the road, but because the rental car had severely worn-out (bald) tires. we weren’t the only ones – several travelers had the same issue. so double-check the tires before your trip to avoid a nasty surprise in the middle of nowhere. other than that – the road to the lagoons and the views at the destination are simply stunning. highly recommended!

we visited the san miguelito archaeological site, which is part of the maya museum, and had a wonderful experience. we managed to see everything in about 1.5 hours, but we recommend dedicating 2–3 hours if you want to take your time reading the detailed captions about maya history in the museum before heading to the archaeological site. one important tip: while the museum is open until 6 pm, the archaeological site seems to close at 5 pm. if you’re on a tight schedule, it’s a good idea to visit the archaeological site first and then explore the museum. the entrance fee is just 70 pesos, which is more than justified for the experience. the maya museum offers fascinating insights into the history and culture of this ancient civilization, and the captions provide valuable context. the archaeological site itself is a peaceful park, offering a welcome escape from the heat of the sun. you’ll find a few well-preserved structures that have survived the industrialization and the construction of massive tourist hotels on the nearby coast. if you’re interested in history and looking for a break from cancun’s modern hustle, this spot is a must-visit. it’s informative, affordable, and a refreshing connection to the past.

we visited the sydney tower eye as a family, and it went really well. it was a great experience to see the city from such a high point. the escalators were smooth and worked well. some of my family members felt a bit scared, but a staff member stepped in and was very kind and helpful, which we appreciated. overall, the staff were extremely helpful. we took photos at the photo booth, but the quality wasn’t as good as before when they used professional cameras like canon. the current setup seems to use a special camera, and while the photos were okay, they lacked the sharpness and clarity we expected. the experience itself was enjoyable, but after about 30 minutes, the view doesn’t change much, so it can start to feel repetitive. it’s definitely something nice to do, but it’s not a must-do activity on its own. it would be better to combine it with other attractions in sydney. i recommend buying a combo ticket that includes the sydney tower eye along with other places like the aquarium or the wildlife park. buying two or three attractions together gives you more value, and the third one is usually added at a much lower price.

we visited the traditional hammam at riad karawan as a couple and had an amazing experience. hanan was incredibly kind and treated both of us at the same time with great care and professionalism. the treatment was absolutely perfect, and we felt completely relaxed and taken care of. everyone at the riad was warm and welcoming. after the hammam, we were invited to enjoy the beautiful rooftop terrace — a perfect way to end the experience. highly recommended!

we visited the vatican museums on a monday morning in early may, and it was already extremely crowded — shoulder-to-shoulder with other tourists and tour groups. if you can, definitely avoid weekends, as i can only imagine it’s even more intense. weekdays may be slightly better, but this is one of those places that’s always busy. we had pre-booked a french-language guided tour exactly 60 days in advance via the official website— a must if you want a guided experience in your language of choice. i was traveling with someone with a disability, and although she had contacted the vatican in advance via email to secure the reduced-rate disabled ticket, staff had trouble locating it at the entrance. on top of that, the security team was a bit brusque, making the experience unnecessarily stressful despite our early arrival (30 minutes ahead of our 11 a.m. tour). thankfully, the issue was resolved fairly quickly. once inside, things improved drastically. our guide was phenomenal — deeply knowledgeable, articulate, and genuinely passionate about renaissance art. her energy was contagious, and she brought the masterpieces to life, especially in the raphael rooms and the classical sculpture galleries. because of the ongoing conclave, we couldn’t visit the sistine chapel, which was disappointing — but at the same time, it was surreal to be there during such a significant moment in vatican history. in short: go for the art, prepare for the crowds, and don’t expect a serene experience. but with a good guide and a bit of patience, the vatican museums still deliver one of the most incredible art collections on earth.

we visited the week of easter and to our surprise, it was not very busy. though we got there as soon as the park opened. the staff were nice and helpful. we purchased the tram ride which was $50 for 2 seniors. the park staff on the tram were friendly and knowledgeable. the tram stopped often to view the wildlife. lots of gators! it was a 2 hour ride with a stop at an observation area as shown in the picture. i was disappointed though that it was very dry when we visited. not much water when i thought it would be swampy. i would return.

we visited the werner mozart hall in vienna with great excitement, and although we encountered a small issue with our tickets upon arrival, the team resolved it quickly, professionally, and with the utmost kindness. they welcomed us with a smile and found the best solution so we could enjoy the concert without any inconvenience. thanks to their excellent organization and attention to detail, they not only solved the problem but also made us feel truly valued and cared for. the hall itself is beautiful, with impeccable acoustics and a unique atmosphere that makes the music come alive. place and a team that prove excellence lies not only in the music but also in how they treat their audience. we will definitely be back! 🎶❤️

we visited this attraction in july expecting cool temperatures and shady environment. when you enter, it’s not clear where to buy the entry tickets. just follow the crowd to the entry… and join the rather long line to buy the tickets. i don’t know why the line is long because they only accept cash. as a foreigner, you need 73 brl per ticket. they give you a detailed map of things to see. cash only place… remember that! there are no matching numbers or markings to ensure that you are on the desired path. we chose the longest path and got lost a fee times. i wish there were some markers on the trails. i also wish the focal points were numbered as they are in the map making the tour easy to follow. but i guess that’s too much to ask!! the entire path inside the garden takes you to various well-arranged and incredible areas of interest. you also see part of the ancient aqueduct passing at the north end of the park. we visited on a thursday and it was fairly quiet and peaceful. it took us nearly two hours to cover the trail with over 8000 steps. except for a single trail to the aqueduct, all other trails are flat and easy to navigate. wear comfortable shoes. shorts and light clothing recommended- as we walked, we got pretty hot in our jeans even though the temperature was supposed to be 22-23c. do bring water and any snacks you need to stay energized. it’s a very pleasant walk around the park and we definitely enjoyed our morning there. after the visit, we walked 30 minutes to the lagoa area (10 min uber ride for 10-15brl as an alternative) and had a fabulous churrascaria late lunch at rio bras near the lake. check out that review too- we highly recommend that restaurant. visit to this botanical garden is a nice thing to do if you have some time and don’t mind walking for a couple of hours. like this review if you found it useful!

we visited this flower field in early october, and most of the flowers were well past their peak. but on the upside, the sunflower fields were fantastic, it was pretty quiet (and it was a saturday), there was free parking and free entry, we didn't have to wait for a cart (it was 2000 yen for 15 minutes), and there was no one else driving around, so we could stop on the track and take photos. it was a great experience. i recommend you hire a cart to really see the sunflowers properly because you can't walk through this field. you can only go with a cart. they're very easy to drive.

we visited this food truck for a quick dinner tonight and had a mixed experience. service is friendly and quick, and the area is near robson square, which provides decent entertainment. the hoisin chicken wrap is fantastic! the wraps are freshly made and are delicious. the chicken is very flavourful and the sauces are great! they used fries similar to costco, which are crispy and delicious. they provide a great white sauce with them too. not to the drawback, the taco wasn’t great. honestly, they should just remove it from the menu as it doesn’t really make sense with what their menu and it’s just not good. i would have given them 5 stars if it wasn’t for the tacos.

we visited this park after masai mara to admire the beautiful elephants and this park did not disappoint. we saw elephants on multiple occasions as well as other animals. an amazing experience, i only wish i had spent more time here. one downside is that i found there too be way too many jeeps blocking the road and creating queues, so on our evening drive we couldn't even get close to some of the animals we saw earlier in the day. nevertheless the park is an exceptional place worth visiting.

we visited this place in july 2025 and found unique experiences like scenic rides that offered breathtaking views. even in the middle of summer, we found snow on the top of the mountain! afterward, we had an eagle coaster ride, and my daughter asked to repeat it. we visited this place on a weekday and found it quite and nice. there weren’t many people, and the parking lot was huge. the service was fast and nice everywhere. the staff was always ready to assist you and truly cared about safety.

we visited this place on a cold october day as we were needing to get out and enjoy the sites. there were no english speakers that day for the tour, but that didn't stop us from getting our own tour guide and having a blast. we learned what the dinosaur names were in spanish compared to english. it was pretty fun.

we visited this place out of season but were able to pick some strawberries. the owners of the farm are very friendly people and they take good care of the plantations. you can also buy homemade yogurt and ice cream (sugar free) there. it's incredibly delicious! i recommend visiting this small strawberry farm when you are around 😇

we visited this place today and had an amazing time with the elephants. 🐘💚 this is a real sanctuary. every elephant here has been rescued and is now living a peaceful life. when we arrived, they were simply eating and relaxing. we got to feed them, gently touch them, and take photos, all without disturbing them. everything was done on the elephants’ terms, and we really appreciated that. there was no mud bath today, so we didn’t get any of those “muddy elephant” photos. but that’s okay. what matters most is that the elephants were happy and comfortable. the local caretakers feed them bananas, pumpkins, and watermelons every day. by visiting, we are also supporting them and their important work. these elephants need care, food, and freedom—and places like this make it possible. please support humane sanctuaries like this. don’t go to places that offer elephant rides. let’s protect and respect these amazing animals. our team lead max was amazing and fun too btw!

we visited this place while passing by with a tour. it was very cool and the storytelling about the place was very interesting also. i would have enjoyed a freshly baked bread but i guess you would need to wait for quite some time before it would be done. but still the whole idea seemed very cool. also be careful with the water it is boiling hot in some places so just look before touching the water if there are bubbles.

we visited this restaurant on a friday night at 8 p.m. with a reservation, and i’m glad we had one, because shortly after we say down there was a lineup outside. the place was buzzing and definitely on the louder side, which made conversation a bit tricky. there was a big group celebrating a birthday, which might’ve added to the volume, but overall, expect a lively atmosphere. as for the food, it was pretty good across the board. we tried the arancini, which were crunchy on the outside and perfectly soft inside. the panzanella was another highlight: fresh, flavourful tomatoes and a really well-balanced dressing. the pappardelle alla guancia was rich and satisfying, and the pollo alla diavola was also great, cooked thoroughly and nicely spiced. the only note i’d make is that the sauce was quite spicy. i personally loved it, but it might not be for everyone. also, the chicken skin was a bit too salty, so i ended up removing it, but the meat itself was still delicious. for drinks, the house wine was average, but the pinot grigio was enjoyable. we also tried the berry smash from the non-alcoholic menu, and that was a standout, super refreshing and flavourful. to finish, we had the tiramisu and it did not disappoint, rich, creamy, and the perfect ending to the meal. overall, i’d give this place a solid 4 out of 5. the food was great, the energy was fun (if a bit loud), and the service kept up with the busy pace. would definitely return, just maybe not for a quiet date night.

we visited this shrine and found it absolutely beautiful. we also paid to access the garden, which was incredibly peaceful and calm. it was such a lovely experience walking around the shrine grounds everything felt serene and well cared for. a perfect spot to slow down and enjoy the quiet beauty of kyoto.
we visited this small museum on the dubrovnik pass and enjoyed the insights into dubrovnik life hundreds of years ago.

we visited this temple on a week day, it was much spiritual and well organized. puja and architecture was pleasant, we were surprised to see so many thai people in a hindu temple doing rituals. planned d to visit here again.

we visited this theatre for the first time on wednesday evening and the musical "just for one day" was an absolutely fantastic show with a great cast and atmosphere. the theatre itself (founded in 1911) has a great and comfortable layout, air conditioning and legroom with comfortable seats to make you feel comfortable. very friendly staff, everything is at a high level👍🤗

we visited this trail recently and noticed that there were no signs indicating where the hike begins. we parked at haukland beach, which had plenty of parking and amenities. to reach the top viewpoint, take the right-hand gate just to the right of the tunnel (marked in red in my photo). if you prefer a flatter route around the area, take the left-hand gate instead — though we didn’t try that one ourselves. the difficulty really depends on your hiking experience. i’m not a frequent hiker and i’m used to switzerland’s well-marked trails, which are usually equipped with ropes or rails for support. this hike was had no markings, no safety features. from a technical perspective, i’d rate it as moderate to hard, though physically it wasn’t demanding. it took us about 45 minutes to go up (not sure if we reached the very top, but we were high enough to see both beaches and the lake) and 45 minutes to come down, with two more technical, rocky sections. this may be considered an easy or standard trail in lofoten, but just be aware it’s quite rugged, expect rocky paths, some mud, and no trail infrastructure. if you’re used to mountain hiking and wear proper hiking shoes, it should be manageable. my husband, who is more experienced with mountain trails, found it easy. that said, the views from the top are really nice!!

we visited this venue in may 2025. the nature reserve has exceptional wild life which the trip is a great experience. clearly, your visit will have some negative impact on the park but it has to be a once in a lifetime event. highly recommended but also remember we need to preserve this location of outstanding beauty.

we visited to go to a baseball game - it was a sold out game. it's a nice stadium and well organised. we arrived about 45 mins early and there was barely any wait time to get in. it was a little difficult to find our seats and the seats are a little small but have arm rests and a drinks holder in front. there are lots of places to grab food from inside or drinks, but we brought our own food. lots of people eat drinking the game, just make sure it's not soup or strong smelling. there are people walking around you can wave down for beer or soft drinks who will come to your seat to serve you - as a tourist this is quite a fun thing to do and not something in our own country. the toilet queue at the end of the event was quick as was exiting the stadium, everyone was very calm and we felt safe, despite the large crowd. we walked about 15 mins to our metro line and it was quiet, so not sure about other closer lines.

we visited today and it was so much fun. vanessa was our guide. she was amazing. she has so much knowledge about the animals and their background. you can tell how much she loves all of the animals and how attached to them she is. tuna her sidekick helped with the tour. tuna is the resident cat there. there was an elderly man on our tour and vanessa made sure to check on him throughout and found seating for him during different times. she was absolutely wonderful with us and her caring heart came through the whole tour, not only with all of the animals but also with us. now the animals. from feeding the goats and donkeys and cows to seeing the zebras and lemurs and porcupines to the otters! oh those otters. just when you thought it couldn't get any better you got to pet the sloth and feed and play with the kangaroos. amazing time. the place is very clean and the animals are very well cared for. they run the place for sure. we did the vip tour. if you are in the area its a must see. such a great experience. i cant say enough good things about our time there.
we visited today. the weather was also very nice. the breads are very good, i recommend them. you can find various fresh fruits, cheeses, flowers. it was a very enjoyable activity with children.

we visited vallée de mai on a rainy day, and it was magical. despite the rain, we stayed completely dry — the enormous jungle leaves created a natural umbrella over the entire trail. it felt like walking through a prehistoric world, surrounded by lush greenery and the unique beauty of the coco de mer palms. we chose the longest trail, about an hour and a half, and it was a peaceful, easy walk through this stunning unesco-listed forest. a beautiful, calming experience — perfect even in the rain. 🌿🌧️✨ after the walk, we had coffee at the on-site bar, but it wasn’t particularly impressive — there are much better spots for coffee elsewhere on the island. still, the nature experience itself was unforgettable and well worth the visit. 🌴☕🌧️

we visited vanilla today, as my son was avidly wanting pancakes! we are so pleased that we did! what a cool little find with a chilled vibe and friendly staff. coffee was lovely and the food was tasty! loved that chickens were roaming and there things for children to do (the staff were actively encouraging our son to watch a movie and colour in!!). the decor was great and all in all it was time well spent! thank you vanilla

we visited when only the greenhouse was open -- the place is small. two greenhouses. but, the area outside looks like it would be beautiful during spring/summer/fall! i wish we could see it then (why i'm giving it 4 stars). the greenhouse itself is a little underwhelming, but for 120y per person, i'm not one to complain. just want to set the expectations properly for the winter season. entrance is a bit difficult to find, but follow the signs. seems the main entrance / ticket area is not open during the winter, and you need to go to the greenhouse. i couldn't find parking specifically for the garden, so i parked in a nearby lot for 440y per hour.

we visited with a tour (i think that is the only option) first with the bus to the jetty, then with the boat to cerro dragon, very nice walk, saw lots of land iguanas. snorkeling afterwards was not special but ok

we visited yesterday friday 1st august as a family of four with two children aged 12 & 9 from the u.k. when we started planning our holiday to the area we knew we must do the family vip tour as it looked amazing, but kept it a surprise from the kids. we are so glad we did this, five stars is not enough for how much fun we had. all the staff are extremely friendly and knowledgeable of the animals, they make sure everyone gets a chance to interact with the animals. they also ensure all children get to go first when it comes to holding the animals. gabe was our tour guide for the afternoon and made the tour even more memorable for us. giving great background on each animal, checking on us and the kids to make sure we was all ok and having a good time and not once making it feel like we was rushed. i don’t think i could say which part was my favourite, of course the otter interaction was amazing. but then the kangaroo’s was such a delight, i never thought i’d get a chance to feed a kangaroo let alone have one hug me. we have already said once the kids are big enough to do the otter swim and monkey meeting we will be back. thank you gabe and animal edventures for such a wonderful experience.

we waited 3 hours for this geyser to erupt but it was worth it. they have a couple of benches but you may as well bring some chairs, a cooler and a good book to read while you wait. nice experience to see and hear the buildup to the eruption.

we walked 30 min with 6 year old son from grand anse. so the way is suitable for children, but you need to be careful with high stones in some places. when we came, waves were very strong and tide is high, so it was not possible to swim. and because of the high tide we decided not to go to natural swimming pool in the end. overall, beach is beautiful and we liked fruit juices from beach bar.

we walked along a really dusty and busy dual carriageway for what seemed like forever along the boundary of the jardins d’agdal. all we could see were acres of olive trees in a parched landscape (and it’s the end of december…). we couldn’t find an obvious entrance so we stopped in the shade to read the reviews. should have done that first. basically that was all there is. not wanting to waste the long walk we crossed the road to the botanical gardens. i’m no botanist so probably didn’t know the subtleties. but it was green and there was a cafe at the end with the footie on, so it wasn’t a total waste🙄😂

we walked away from this place when they want to charge 100,000rp per person to enter restaurant for coffee & food. we have done the tour several times taking guests that have stayed with us in our villa in baturiti, i feel this place is turning away paying customers as we do not wish to repeat tour or access shop on each visit. i may not visit again unless their charging policy changes to access restaurant only. such a pity as we like to support our local businesses in this area.

we walked from wattamolla beach along the coast. stunning views of the ocean and surroundings and there was a nice pathway that was mostly flat. there was a $12 fee for a day pass that was required to get in. adequate parking, even on a public holiday at 11am.

we walked here from lofts les-billie, and the kids enjoyed it so much. there was a re-enactment of the war between the french and the british, i believe, the brits were being “hammered” in the narratives. the crowd loved it, but hey, this is quebec, they can say what they like, but the french took a whopping from the brits. the process was light hearted and lots of laughs. there are very good restaurants around the place, with lots of ice cream parlours to me meet every sugar craving taste. i found the prices in the restaurants quiet reasonable, and services fantastic all in all. we ate in a different restaurant and tasted varying ice creams almost every other day on our five day stay.

we walked the walls. fantastic views from all angles. a well maintained landmark. a few cafes and places to stop for a drink and a rest. not suitable for anyone with mobility problems, it's quite strenuous in places and lots and lots of steps!

we walked up this very steep 3 km road not realizing how steep or far it was to the top. once there we were happy to see a snack bar with water for 1 e. it was 10e to enter. it was very interesting ancient site with so much to see. it took us about 2 hours to walk through all of it.

we wanted to buy cacao beans, hence we came here. it is a very unique mercado. i was very surprised especially with the whole young piglets and big rabbits for sale!! vendors are very helpful and friendly. we ate at one of the eateries and the food and drinks were super! they have exotic tacos- crocodile. garantula, crickets, etc etc. prices are very cheap! service was also excellent! i love this mercado!

we wanted to explore sian ka'an, but all we found were gentrified over the top "deluxe" tours. finally, we found this tour. it is reasonably priced. and it feels more authentic. you go on a small boat driven by a mayan guide. he will take you to a cenote in the middle of the lagoon, where manatíes will come out for air. you will then go through the mangroves, where a whole bunch of herons will greet you. eventually, you will get to a small natural (or mayan-made) channel where you will let yourself float through it. after that, you will get to another cenote in the middle of the river that looks like a water mirror. eventually, you will get to one of the most gorgeous beaches you'll ever see. white sand and all the possible tones of blue water. finally you'll get to the birdwatching part of the tour, at the isla de pájaros, where we saw nesting roseated spatula birds and a lot more species. overall it was an incredible diverse experience for a fraction of the price of other tours.

we wanted to go there from the ruines, but it was closed and it looked dirty also. they took us by mini “bus” for free (the entrance fee to the reservatum contained it) to other beaches so it was good finally to visit nice beaches also after the ruins. if it would be open and cleaned it would be 5 stars!

we wanted to take the gondola of san paolo at sunset but we missed it. eventually we found this one and it did not dissapoint! it was a calm gondola ride with a really nice gondola driver(cristiano) and you could see a lot of the inside rivers and also a big part of the grand canal. really nice ride and thank you cristiano!

we wanted to try a new spot and chose nonnas. great spot for a quick delicious bite. we ordered a couple of sandwiches and pastas to sample the menu. everything was fantastic. the man working the counter made some suggestions and we went for it. their customer service was on point and made sure we had everything we needed! for “street food” i felt like it was a top tier restaurant from the food i received. would highly recommend.

we watched a basketball game here and we loved the experience. we bought our tickets online from fc barcelona offcial website. there is a food stall from where you can buy popcorn and drinks. (popcorn was waaay to salty). overall a great experience if you love sports as much as we do. 🇹🇩

we watched the catalan derby as barca fans. getting in and out of the stadium was smooth, and the staff were helpful in guiding us to our seats. we were even allowed to bring in our own food and water, which was a nice surprise.

we watched the show alma, fantastic play with some of the best dancers and singers in cuba. tickets cost 40 pesos for the second row middle, it is the best deal we have ever had watching a show. highly recommended. getting a ride afterwards maybe tough, one has to walk a little bit to find a taxi.

we went about an hour before sunset. it’s a beautiful park, and the sunset at the top is absolutely gorgeous. the swallows flying around, the golden hour on the acropolis and a great vibe of people hanging out and taking it all in.
