we went at 9pm. the planarium show was great. i loved the 4d show, the chairs move and it was so much fun. and the observatory to see mars, the moon and yellow star that looked blue because of pressure.

we went cage shark diving thanks to cregg and the crew. it was an exhilarating adventure. it is very appreciated that the personnel maintains an exceptionally professional approach. getting thrilled about the prospect of booking yet another thrilling journey.
we went during the ice skating season. two levels of ice skating were amazing and well organized. good music, lighting, and staff are helpful, and all the locals are so friendly. i'm glad we did it.

we went firefly watching here and aj was a great guide. they were helpful organising private tour despite bad weather and their communication and understanding was lovely. we got to see plenty of fireflys on the mangroves but the clear sky and seeing the stars was truly beautiful and well worth a visit just for this in my opinion. tour lasted about 1hr and we thought it was good value. it is a bit off the beaten track away from pp but fortunately we knew the route as had visited in the day and were renting a car.

we went for a 4x4 safari tour. we were just amazed by the beauty of this place. my daughter even had a nice swim under the waterfall. akash, our guide, was just wonderful. so wonderful that we decided to come back very soon for the trek this time! highly recommended

we went for a bachelorette trip and had a wonderful time at the new orleans pedal barge!! we booked the private pontoon boat (for up to six people & 1 hr 45 min trip for reference) and it was perfect for our group. the tiki boats looked fun as well, but if your group is looking for a more private experience, this is the way to go!!! we had captain ben and he went above and beyond. he celebrated the bride, took photos so we could all be in one, introduced us to the gator friends, and taught us about the wildlife/nature. the speakers are great if you have a friend who you want to be the dj. since it was the private boat, they were also able to accommodate some craziness that happened on the way there! our driver got confused (they give a heads up on the website but sharing here if you haven’t seen it yet- there are two “2101 paris road” addresses in the area. one is in new orleans, the correct one, and wrong one is chalmette.) despite clarifying with our transportation, we were taken to the wrong one and barely made it a few minutes before our check in time. thank goodness we left early!! highly recommend leaving at least an hour early in case that happens to you & do a quality assurance/double check with your uber/taxi, even if they said they put the right address in! 😂 note: if you’re on a group boat, i don’t think they’re able to do the same thing as they have a responsibility to be fair to the other customers by leaving the dock on time, whereas arriving late for a private tour, it would shorten your time on the boat. still not what you want to do out of respect for the captain ofc, but just sharing here so you are aware!) ps - do your waiver in advance to make things easy! there is also a hangout area for when you arrive with music that you can wait at when you arrive. overall, we had a five star experience!!! thanks captain ben for helping us celebrate our bride!

we went for a tour and then stayed for a tasting. fantastic experience! we had the impression every staff member was very knowledgeable about the wines. every question we had got answered. the tour was nice but not that long. for the tasting we took the bigger menu which was great. a must visit for wine lovers.

we went for dolphin watch and enjoyed a lot. we witnessed lot of dolphins. many dolhpins in a single place (dolphin family). our boat captain rode the boat very nice like adventures ride. worth to visit with muscat sea tours. our trip co-ordinator sathish guided us very well.

we went for mt. agung climbing and all the way all 5 stars. booked in the morning for the same night and it worked. both the driver (forgot the name :( ) and the guide (rudy) were amazing. rudy was so much fun and friendly and caring. he took some incredible photos of us at the summit. definitely would recommended this agency and we might use their services in the future.

we went for rafting here. they are charging 1800 for 16 km and it takes almost 2 hours of time. believe me it's worth it as it has almost 5-6 rapid and they allow you to swim in river wherever water is stable. they also charge 200 for transport if you don't have vehicle to go to starting point. they charge 1500 for photos/videos from go pro camera. please don't take 900 package if you want some adventure as it's only boating without any splash.

we went for sunrise on mount batur jeep tour. great service. tasty breakfast. very good photography by our amazing guide and driver "wayan gunawan". flawless pickup from hotel by "melta". fantastic staff. unforgettable experience !!! keep up good service .

we went for the 1-hr bow river ride since it was the first trail run for one of our companions. the weather was great and check in was smooth. after fitting the helmet and weighing in we were assigned our horses which are all very beautiful! there were 8 of us in the group and led by rachel in the front and flanked by a cowboy at the back. rachel was enthusiastic and pointed out instructions clearly. horse-riding is inherently an all weather outdoor sports and horses like people have moods and personalities. so we were prepared! the trail runs alongside the bow river and this ride does not cross the river. it is a natural trail that meanders through some forests, bridges and meadows with muddy areas. some forested areas have a few lower lying branches so need to push them aside or duck your head. it gives nice views of the cascade, rundle and the tunnel mountains. we even saw a coyote on our way back. some tips for prospective riders: - this trail may be too straightforward for those who have done trail riding a few times and expect more eg river crossing. - you should be able to understand instructions in english. this is because you should be able to perform simple maneuvers when instructed by the staff when the horse is distracted and not follow the group, like steer the rein left / right/ halt, gently kick the horses belly with your heels if the horse stops or does not follow the horse in front as a single file. getting on or off the horse is quite ok as they provide platforms. - this trail is suitable for beginners. but for younger kids, i saw some very young looking child riders being led by an adult on horseback, not sure if that’s part of the service or not. a older child in our group had a horse which was feeling playful and distractible, enjoyed munching grass and sometimes not following the group. also the horse might not know that over hanging tree branches might brush up against the rider - for instance a girl (maybe 7 or 8) in front of us had her head and neck pushed back against a tree branch…..luckily the horse was in slow motion and she did not panic or cry and was able to soldier on and steered the horse away from the trees. the cowboy did make an effort several times to guide the horse. the little girl deserves a big applause for keeping her cool and getting herself out of the woods literally !! - yes the trail is natural and so when the hooves trudges over muddy areas your shoes and pants will get a little bit dirty, that’s horse riding ! wear something easy to wash. - the staff helped ensuring the saddle and stirrups are fastened and your feet are comfortable. - when taking photos with your phone, tie your phone around your neck with a lanyard ! - do some simple stretching before you ride helps to reduce strains and aches afterwards - plenty of parking at the stables. washrooms available. no cafe - on a rainy day, i think a poncho might be a good idea overall we had a great time and highly recommend this !

we went for the dinner degustation with wine pairing which was incredible. the team were really knowledgeable and very good at explaining the differences between the wines and various processes which was really interesting to see how it compares to other areas of the world, and it helped that the wine was great! the food was also really well paired and we had the best orange cake i’ve ever had, beautifully paired with the vinsanto sweet wine. highly recommend!

we went here a few days ago. the communication with princess was efficient. the pick up in the van and speedboat was good. the van just didn't take us home? only one way transport 😂 it was alot of fun on the rides and the staff is very nice. the place itself is quite a dump of rusty steal, old everything and really not representable like on the photos. it could be quite amazing though if some work was done. i thought that while the kids where out doing there things, i could get a swim and lie in the sun. but actually, thats not possible. but the glider and other watersports are perfect.

we went here a few times and each time was a completely different experience. we saw an art installation, a small peaceful protest for gaza, a flash mob dancing the macarena, and a various amount of people each time. there are many statues and iconic monuments to look at and snap photos of. it sits right next to the national gallery so a nice convenient location. you can also see big ben off in the distance.

we went here for a relaxing time and were disappointed. you make reservations via whatsapp, however, the owner doesn't have a clear system to allocate the requests and customers into one clear plan, as such, we were allocated the wrong procedure which left us diaspointed. the spa is also a converted hair salon and still has the feeling of a 90s hair studio. there are simply better places within the city that give a more atmospheric experience. the owner was likewise discourteous to us, explaining how many messages he gets and that things always go wrong. a sentiment that as a customer i feel is inappropriate and disrespectful to voice to me. i want a functioning system and service when i am trying to relax. this place didn't provide either.

we went here for my sisters birthday holiday and my mums first time on a jet ski. really nice staff, especially thomas who got us ready to go have fun rapid and very helpful. he also took some photos of us riding the skis and sent them all asap to us on a very busy day! would highly recommend

we went here for water sports and were surprised with the white sand beach and blue water. tirta benoa is a good place to do water sport, they have many water sport at affordable price. we did couple of water sports here and loved the experience. worth it !!

we went here to see a photography exhibition and we were also treated to a lifetime retrospective of george hadjimichalis. it's a beautiful space and the exhibitions were very well installed. the museum is huge and handicapped accessible. we spent the entire day and enjoyed lunch at the cafe. extensive gift shop, helpful staff, spotless restrooms. highly recommend.

we went here to see the catacomb tour. i’m about 5.5 months pregnant right now and struggling in the heat at 32 degrees c. the staff was so kind to me. they put me in front of a fan, gave me water, made sure i was safe getting up and down the stairs to the catacombs. absolutely the kindest people and an amazing tour! the history was so well explained and everything preserved so well! will 100% return. thank you for your kindness
we went here to see the desierto florido.... was beautiful. we also did the 11km hike - advertised as taking 5.5 hours but we did it in 3.5/4 hours so don't let this out you off! was a lovely hike

we went in a large group and unfortunately didn't have time to visit inside the church, instead we went straight downstairs to the prison area. we had to wait awhile because of other large groups in front of us. definitely the tour guides control the flow, it must be hard for individuals to get through! every group goes down the stairs when it is their turn, to the cave dungeon and spends time praying before returning up, to let in the next group.

we went in early summer in june. it was pretty hot day so we were sitting on the edges. it would be nice if they could have a colder pool to cool off on hot days. the swimsuit drying machine didn’t work which was a bummer. however, its a very cool experience. it is first come first serve so be there early. gondola is a street down so if you can plan accordingly can go right after. they have a family price for 2 adults and 2 children which was nice and lockers come with the cost. you will need to bring your towels and swimsuit or pay extra. the view is amazing
we went in for the last hour, definitely need a couple hours to see it all properly. some weird and wonderful things to see and do. enjoyed by teen and adults. staff nice.

we went in july and it was the worst hike i ever did. starting at riviere noire entrance there is no trail, only a path full of stones in different sizes so you always have your eyes on ground not to fall. after a while it gets very muddy, then you have to cross the river several times over some slippery stones. you can of course wade through the water but the stones under water are also unpredictable and slippery and you shouldn't wear long trousers as it is advised because of the mosquitos. after crossing the river three times which took us already 2 hours we decided to return. on our way back we were attacked by dozens of biting flies. not an experience i want to make again.

we went in sea angel cruise 2. keep in mind you will be in the boat for 90% of the time sightseeing for just a little bit and will only get off at phi phi island. 1 stars for the air conditioning in the big boat, which was good and our baby was mostly comfortable; and 1 star for the food they have at phi phi island. the tour is a scam from start to finish since you have to pay for literally everything. do not buy anything from the shops. they're overpriced and the information their staff gives is to manipulate you into buying glasses, hat, drinks etc. they have different tiers for "comfort", which they extort you into paying more. it starts from 600 baht for silver seats, which offers "unlimited snacks and basic drinks", but it will magically finish within the first hour. stick to the basic package and don't be tricked into upgrading for comfort, it's not worth it. on top of it, if you pay by card they will charge you extra. what they don't tell you is that there is a 20 baht per person entry fee to phi phi island. i will only recommend this tour if you have a baby with you and you want an air conditioned experience with them, or if you are aged and get sea sick easily. otherwise avoid this one. it's not worth it.

we went in the winter and the view was outstanding. shiretoko with the drift ice is beautiful. what isn't is the train ride there made for tourists, horribly noisy, the staff says everything on a loudspeaker ("see the drift ice" , "look at the mountain" etc.). insufferably loud and very unnecessary service - you can see all without help obviously. but the most disappointing part is how we don't speak about fishing activities in a national park area... we went to the port and saw a fish drying facility which is protected by nets from the birds that would go and "steal" the fish. marine birds are hung up and dying as they get caught in these nets. commercial fishing already has a huge amount of bycatch on the sea, we have to add a lot more to it on land too. and all this in a national park - a should be protected area.

we went on a 9 day trip to botswana organised by wilderness safaris. what an unbelievable experience. their camps are 5 star, the staff well trained, friendly and professional. the guides and vehicles are next level. they offer sadc rates for us who use monopoly money.

we went on a boat cruise from cape town to walvisbaai recently and booked for the historical quad tour with fanie. we had an amazing experience in the desert of namibia. fanie has a lot of knowledge of the desert and its history and he is an excellent quad driving instructor. we felt safe all the way. we definitely recommend this quad tour and will visit again. thanks oom fanie. this was the highlight of our holiday!!!

we went on a boat cruise that included a stop at cholon, and it was sooo much fun—honestly, one of the highlights of our trip! the whole experience turned into a huge party on the water, with music, dancing, and great vibes all around. what really stood out was how well the crew balanced the fun with safety. they made sure we were always taken care of, and anything we needed, they had it covered without hesitation. special shoutout to isa, our guide—she was absolutely amazing! super friendly, energetic, and made sure we were having the best time from start to finish. can’t recommend this experience enough!

we went on a diving tour with tusa and had an amazing experience! the staff were super friendly and helpful, the food was excellent and it was great having a smaller group of people on the boat. i was particularly grateful to my dive instructor julia, who took me on my very first intro dive. her calm, patient and knowledgeable instruction meant it was an excellent experience! would 100% go again with tusa!

we went on a foggy day to the “mirador” (sightseeing spot) at the top of the village of pria da vitoria, terceira. it was beautiful.

we went on our tour on our first full day in port douglas on the 15th. from the moment we were picked up from our hotel we felt at ease by knowledge and care shown by our tour guide steve. he ensured we were all at ease and that we knew the plan for the day. he kept the day easy and light hearted with his humour and insane amount of knowledge of the daintree and the animals which inhabit it. he was very clear from the beginning of setting expectations and making sure we all knew not to get our hopes up of seeing massive animals. instead he spoke so highly and lovingly of the small creatures which inhabit the forest, from the ants, to the flowers and the fish. we could not have dreamed of a better guide and he made it feel so special. he was just incredible, thank you steve!!! liv and rhys

we went on the aquila collection safari in december 2024 and were very satisfied with the experience. we paid around €195 (approximately 3,700 zar) per person. the day started with a morning pick-up in cape town. the van was brand new, and the driver was very friendly. the journey took about two hours, with a short 10-minute stop at a gas station halfway through. upon arrival at aquila, we were greeted with a small glass of sparkling wine and completed the check-in process (passport or id can be shown digitally). breakfast was provided before the safari, and while the quality was not great, it didn’t bother us much as we came for the safari, not the food. after an hour of breakfast, we embarked on a 2.5-hour safari. it was fantastic—we saw all the animals we had hoped to see. our guide was incredibly kind, took the time to explain everything, and made the experience memorable. midway through, we had a break with water and access to restrooms. while it’s not a private safari and you’re not alone, i didn’t feel like it was a mass experience. for something more exclusive, you’d need to pay extra. after the safari, lunch was served as a buffet, which i found to be much better than breakfast. the only downside was the long wait (about 3 hours) until the return journey. i recommend bringing a towel and swimwear to enjoy the pool. if, like me, you’re not a fan of pools, bring a book or something to keep you occupied. lastly, don’t forget sunscreen, and i highly recommend choosing a morning safari to avoid the intense afternoon sun.

we went on the eagle and seal safari with our children. the staff were really accommodating. we saw both animals, the skipper told us interesting local information and we kept an appropriate distance from the seals to not disturb them. great trip.

we went on the freaking hottest day of the summer (40⁰c), it's hell. therefore, we arrived at the cafe outside the destination around 2p.m and stayed there until 5p.m or 6p.m, i 'm not sure (still hot tho), the ticket counter was closed so we can enter there for free. remember, do not rent bicycles (50k/pax) or electic cars (400k/car), it's a waste of money when you can litetally walk, on the map the place can be big but you can explore by foot. the village was living in the past. you can experience the old vietnam here.

we went on the island tour last week and we loved it! cousin john jr. was the best tour guide! loved his ukulele playing and singing! our 8 old year daughter enjoyed it too. she especially liked the snorkeling with the turtles! highly recommend!

we went on the margarita for the sunset luxury semi-private cruise and it was fantastic. the crew were nice and helpful and the food was so fresh and delicious. there was also a lot of space on the boat. perfect way to spend an afternoon/evening in santorini!

we went on the swamp boat ride and oak alley plantation tour and it was amazing! our guide robert told us everything and more about louisiana history, he gave us insights during the whole trip and we’re so thankful for that. 100% recommended, would definitely do it again! ps. during the swamp tour you also get to hold a small gator!!

we went on the tour sian kaan deluxe by boat last week and it was wonderful; our tour guide abraham spoke english and german among other languages. if you love being out on a boat and the open this is a beautiful unesco world heritage site, 780,000 acres that is very special and not to be missed! abraham was very knowledgeable and engaging and we had lots of fun! the day was just spectacular. a beautiful boat ride through the lush lagoons stopping to see an crocodile (just under the water) and then out to the open and saw very graceful dolphins and a beautiful big white turtle (24"diameter). it is so great to see these guys in their natural habitat and to not support any animals in captivity! then off to snorkel near the reef. lunch in the small village of punta alen was nothing fancy but lovely people and a simple meal of rice and chicken or fish and salad. very clean place. walked through the village after lunch and then back in the boat; went swimming in a lovely pure sand beach area and toasted mexico. we saw 2 beautiful birds high up in a very large nest made up of twigs and plastic, a sad commentary of all the plastic that reaches even this beautiful eco area. my husband is taking our 2 kids back out this week; it was that good. the company was excellent ensuring everyone had life jackets on and very safety conscious with everyone snorkeling. i highly recommend this trip!

we went on the wilderness tundra bud tour in late june. wild life is hit or miss but we did get to see a bunch of dall sheep from afar and a bull moose up close. try to sit towards the front of the buss if possible. it is nice that they pick you up at your lodge/hotel.

checked in with us before and after the tour, and he seemed to care about ensuring we had a good experience. we didn’t see him at any point but communicated through whatsapp and calling. unlike the 7am tour, we didn’t need to arrive so early before the “departure time.” it most likely would’ve been ok to arrive just before 9am.* we arrived at 8:30am to scuba cancun, and it wasn’t clear who was with 360 sup tours until we got going. expect to rely on david for communication while at scuba cancun.* we were scheduled with todd, but evidently something happened, and we waited a bit before starting the tour. fabian was there while we waited though, and he introduced himself and assumed todd’s position as our guide. it was a little hard communicating with him sometimes bc of our language barrier, but that’s part and parcel of cancun. despite this, he was such a great guide and a cool guy that we couldn’t have asked for someone better. he graciously gave us his bug repellent to use (which isn’t included in the tour according to the details we got). we put our stuff in a locked bin. and we set out at about 9:30am and followed his lead. it was just us and fabian. he pointed out wildlife (sting rays, birds, starfish, barracudas, needlefish, spider crabs, etc) and vegetation (the different mangroves and corals), and he taught us some spanish to identify some of them. he cautioned us, explained what’s ahead, and let us enjoy the sights in silence whenever was appropriate. he led us through mangroves, which was a unique experience—there were sooo many mosquitoes, though, so bug spray is very very useful.* you will get swarmed by mosquitoes.* during the tour, we also stopped, and he gave us free water, a snack bar, and took photos of us.* we ended our tour at around 12pm, so it was a little extended! and we were particularly satisfied to learn that fabian was born and raised in cancun, planted mangroves to develop more channels in the lagoon, and cleans the channels out of his love for his home. although because of the language barrier we didn’t learn as much about the ecosystem as i think todd would’ve communicated, i was very glad to have been led by someone like fabian through the tour!

we were able to climb the towers on either end of the charles bridge. i apologize if i’ve mixed the photos up between the two. the views were fabulous from both ends! i would recommend that you climb both towers. the people that work at the towers are super nice and very informative about the history of the towers and prague. it was nice to climb up above all of the crowds crossing the bridge. i would definitely recommend that you visit both of these towers! if you don’t have tickets ahead, just walk into the towers to their ticket booth and purchase tickets on site. your ticket also gives you a discount for the tram on that day.
we were able to get to the boats quickly by paying for the various fees and boat ticket in advance through boracayipass.ph highly recommend instead of standing in line to pay at the dock.

we were able to pick up bus #800 near our apartment and ride it for the twenty minutes or so to the falls. by the time we got to the final bus stop, all riders were heading to the falls. we moved as an awkward group back down the road to the falls’ entrance, where we were processed and paid our dues (25 cent senior discount!). there’s an old lodge/chalet that serves meals and has a small gift shop and a landscaped garden leading down to the gondola. free stairs lead down to the waterfall for the fit, but we paid our fee and chose the gondola. the falls themselves were quite lovely and full following a heavy rain and we had the extra treat of a rainbow. several tour buses arriving during our visit, though the metropolitan bus was a cheap and easy option for us.

we were able to see the cemetery via a local taxi tour, this was one of our first stops. only having to pay around 5 cuc per person it was a steal considering the massive walking grounds of the cemetery. we saw tombs and graves of all sizes and shapes, the history contained within the walls were extraordinary and i would love to have heard some of the stories. be advised that the church is still used today, we happened to pass during a funeral, so keep that in mind and be respectful.

we were absolutely thrilled with our experience! we booked a private tour with nico and captain buibui, and they gave us one of the most memorable days of our four-month journey. we were able to choose the stops ourselves, but we trusted nicos recommendations – and we’re so glad we did. at every location, he shared fascinating facts, showed us the coolest hidden spots, and pointed out marine life we never would have seen on our own. we spotted lots of starfish, turtles, and colorful corals, and nico had so many interesting things to share about them. lunch on a secluded beach was delicious – freshly prepared and grilled right on the boat. the whole day was just perfect. because it was a private tour and we started about half an hour earlier than all the other boats, we had most places all to ourselves. it felt very intimate, peaceful, and truly special. we’ve added some pictures and videos to share a few impressions of this unforgettable day. highly recommended!
we were at the gourmet side, yet one of us had a pizza. food was great, service very caring but a little slow at the end.

we were blown away with how awesome our 6 day oar & paddle rafting trip was!! the main credit goes to the guides. **richard, curtis, devin, sierra, taylor, and jon.** they are amazing. not only in the way they expertly navigated the rafts through the canyon and in rapids, but also their interesting stories (both personal and historical) they are also fantastic chefs! we had no idea the food was going to be so good!! they whipped up meals on the riverside that were better than i make at home haha. steaks, pasta, tamales, burritos, salads, pancakes, bacon & eggs, fresh fruit, smoked salmon, and so much more! and if that wasn’t enough to blow our socks off, they also magically baked me a birthday cake! and i have to mention just how helpful and friendly they all were. you can tell they love their job and are happy to share that stoke with all of us. it was actually really hard to say goodbye at the end. if you’re considering any other company for your rafting adventure, stop. these are the people you want to experience the canyon with. thank you x1000000 for everything

we were blown away with the attention to detail in the recreation of his works. it is as if the artist himself created all of his works in a single location. very authentic. also, the exhibit is easy to access and flows well. the staff is very helpful and are clearly committed to the success of the museum. highly recommend seeing this!

we were completely mislead, the tunnel tours no longer involve exploring the 17th century tunnels underneath cape town city, it's now exploring the bunkers at fort wynyard next to the green point stadium. the whole time we were told that ok now we going to explore the tunnels but what we actually explored were ammunition rooms next to the cannons, not tunnels at all. this company shouldn't operate under the name tunnel tours anymore and they're just miss leading tourists into expecting that they're going to explore the old 17th century tunnels. (the website even still shows pictures of the old tunnels and nothing of ford wynyard).

we were delighted with this experience! we didn’t want to go to a hotel for a cooking class. we wanted a local person who lives locally. the trip to the local market and the cooking class were great. the food was delicious. savuth is a very creative person who has created an oasis where his class is held. he is helping other local people by training them which is inspiring. i would highly recommend.
we were disappointed that all the small reptiles were not in their cages and were moved elsewhere. we didn’t get to see them

we were doing a liveaboard trip on the jaya and would instantly go back! the boat is really nice with good common areas. our cabin was cozy with ac. the trip took 7 days / 6 nights and to our surprise linen and towels (you receive two) we're changed mid trip unexpected but very welcome. the dives were incredible and well guided. we always felt safe and well taken care of. except for dugongs which another group on our boat has seen, we saw everything we've wished for (a manta, different rays, sharks, moray eels and simply tons of fish and beautiful coral). the good was simply amazing, every single dish was super delicious. the crew is amazing and very friendly and take care of everything. simply put, we would book this trip again and fully recommend it as the value price ratio combined with getting around in raja ampat is worth it.

we were dropped off and had a short walk in the canyon to our lunch spot before driving the rest of the way thru. it was largely empty and most people don’t walk it. some parts of the canyon is really quite pretty with some amazing rock formations (or erosions).
we were during summer! the colour of grass is amazing here
we were during week and there were a lot of people. nice but i think that there are many more amazing places in faroe islands than this.

we were faced with the difficult challenge of finding the right kite school for us among all the different ones. as there was little wind at the time, we wanted to try wing foiling. we decided in favour of the freestyle academy with ken because of the good reviews. and we have not regretted our choice!!! ken is a really nice, relaxed and good trainer. with his motivating manner, we were able to overcome the difficulties of the first few attempts. but what is particularly noteworthy is that we stayed in contact with him via whatsapp app when the best wind window was and he didn't send us out on the water when there was too little wind just to be able to charge for the hour. we've had very different experiences with other companies. and it's also important to him that the setup is clear to prepare you for independent surfing. thank you ken, we can recommend you without reservation.

we were for 4 days in dubrovnik and we decided one day to go to jet ski safari. we booked 2 hours safari and it was amazing. we had a tour guide named vlaho who take us into the blue cave which is an absolutely must-see attraction in dubrovnik. he was very fun, interesting and polite. tour was great. we saw city walls of dubrovnik and fort lovrijenac and the lokrum island. it was beautiful experience and we enjoyed it every moment. if you come to dubrovnik you must go to this safari it is worth it.

we were four people and were treated to a memorable and wonderful personal experience at the sophos family cooking class. we were treated to a tour of the local farms and a trip to the local market where we purchased ingredients for the evening meal preparation. the meal was the best we’ve had in cambodia. the amok fish was so good and the green mango chicken salad superb. i highly recommend.

we were here at an all inclusive resort. one of the group suggested we take some of the boys over to the surf adventure and get some time in the water. it was a fantastic idea! after we got dropped off on the beach beside the dreams resort it was a short walk to the surf adventure. they had everything you needed to get surfing or body boarding. they even had shirts for the group. we went surfing for a couple of hours. the waves were very large. they have a great beach. depending on the wind direction, we were able to get up into the cove - with smaller waves. this worked out perfect. if you are looking to surf, this is the place for your adventure!

we were here in mid march. the road is open year round to cook city. visitor center and gift shop only open in monmouth, kinda quiet, not many people. winter time is a nice time to go, very quiet some trails closed, they are open to snowshoeing. we would definitely come back at this time again.

we were here on a staycation and it was nothing short of luxurious. we took the deluxe king pool view and were upgraded to the top level 6 and we had great views of the pool, golf course, distant sea view and planes taking off. it was such a relaxing trip and the rooms were also beautifully designed. really satisfied with the stay and the early bird deal i got for booking around a month in advance for july stay.

we were here on the 25th november 24. i personally had been to many other masjids but this one is exceptionally stunning. the interiors inside and out were so beautiful. it was a huge masjid. the staff were lovely and friendly. i would recommend friends to come here for a good experience.

we were here today, the place is beautiful- but this review is especially for the guide lukas. my youngest fainted due to dehydration and lukas and his colleagues instantly jumped into action. lukas took a special interest, bringing my daughter a drink, and coming back a few times just to check on her. thank you so very much to him and also the team for being such wonderful humans, besides doing an excellent job of giving an informative tour. lukas and his kindness will be remembered by my family. thank you!

we were hiking ka'au crater hiking trail. got lucky and got one of the 5 parking spots near the trailhead. otherwise you park in the neighborhood and walk. i advise following the pipe if you're doing the waterfall trail. we didn't and failed.

we were impressed by this church. the pipe organ playing music was amazing to hear while we were checking out the church’s interior and a smaller version of a pipe organ player. although the gift shop is small, you can purchase tickets to check out the bell tower at the top of the building, which is nice to offer. highly recommend checking out this church!

we were in need of some ribbon to fix a dress. amy got us ribbon and was so insanely helpful and kind. she literally saved the day and could not have been more modest about it. while waiting we bought three masks! the quality of them is wonderful. pictures of the mask i was wearing and of me wearing it with my lovely wives dress that was saved by ribbon from amy.

we were in nola on vacation and while walking through the french quarter, the display commemorating 50 years of south vietnamese settling in new orleans caught our attention. it was a very beautiful and well done display and it was free.

we were in quebec for a few days. this magnificent statue of champlain in on the promenade in front of the frontenac hotel. lots is historic and touristy things to se around here. only a short walk from our hotel.
we were just mindlessly walking around the french quarters when this facade design caught our eyes. the structure incorporated classical themes and design into a modern approach

we were just two people, but we are happy we did this! we only paid for 1 hour. 1 hour is 600 pesos, do not pay more. if possible, join with others to make it cheaper per person! we were not scammed or pressured to pay more or tip. we paid 600 and that was that. we got drinks to take with us before getting on the boat. we stopped and bought tacos for lunch which we ate on our boat. nice environment, lots of boats have music and parties so it’s a fun vibe.

we were looking for a place to book a tour to the gbr. found it on google maps and drove there. it was the best decision! peter was very nice and knowledgeable and helped us find the perfect trip. it was a great experience and we got to snorkel with turtles among other things. thanks again peter! we can highly recommend booking through this company!

we were looking for an activity for my 3 year old and we found this amazing horse and pony ride stable in the heart of banff. the service was amazing! the staff were absolutely amazing with my 3 year old daughter. we even went back for a second horsey ride.

we were looking for head to the spot with summer in winter. after looking at the temperatures in december ended up landing at sydney airport. took rest after a long flight from the netherlands to sydney via china. first we plan was to visit sydney opera house and its amazing. due to heatwave it wasnt much crowded. overall, a great location to visit.

we were looking forward so much to go to this place for 6 years after our first stay in bangkok. the food is great and quickly served and delivered. there is an ample selection of dishes and the protein you want to enjoy it with, there are endless possibilities to create your dish. great value for money too! highly recommend going there.

we were looking to visit a saturday local flea market and was recommended this one! there were food, wine, booths, art and flowers! i would definitely recommend you to visit the local market on saturday or sunday! the time it opens differ for every market, so please check the opening hours prior to going!

we were lucky enough to have the desierto florido in season, it was spectacular. if you're in the area and have a chance to visit during one of these events you should rent a car and head over because the colours and the smell are a rare beauty. photos honestly do not do it justice.

we were lucky to find this company last minute! we did the via ferrata baumes corcades in centelles with alex - he's a nice, good english speaking guide and we had a fun day. i would love to come back one day for the canyoning. highly recommended!

we were lucky to have perfect weather for our canal cruise, which of course made everything better. we chose to leave from the rijksmuseum, so we could visit the art then go directly to a canal cruise. bit of initial hassle, as we booked for noon but they asked us to switch to 11:30 or 1; we switched to 11:30 which actually left at 11:40 and was combined with the heineken experience so we didn't get the boat we'd hoped for - but did get a beer, all good. our captain marcus was great, and our guide (andrew garfield look-alike, drama student) was excellent and shared really interesting info about amsterdam and our route. we specifically chose a tour with a smaller boat so we didn't have to take photos through glass, and would go on the smaller canals and the amstel river rather than the ij. great decision, as we really enjoyed the route. excellent canal tour!
we were lucky to see the current artist performing a workshop and doing a live demonstration. beautiful architecture, artwork, and sculpture garden. would recommend!

we were lucky – we managed to attend a real sumo tournament, and not a demonstration match for tourists. this is perhaps the most powerful impression of the trip. on the one hand, the tournament is a bright part of japanese cultural traditions, on the other – proof that strength, tenacity, athleticism and even grace can coexist in an “unathletic” body. i have much more respect for japanese strongmen than for slender office workers puffing in gyms after work. by the way, one of the best sumo wrestlers in japan is mongolian, so there is enough room for everyone in this exciting fight.

we were lured here by a local who rode up to us while we were riding to another temple to view the sunrise claiming that he knows of secluded off-the-track temples where we can climb.. but turns out to be not so secluded at all. to his credit, the view is pretty nice. -1 star for crowd. to add on these "well meaning" locals who want to share with you a "exclusive" spot. they just want to sell you things. and if you decided not to buy, it can go a few directions from there: 1) they'll hit you with a sob story to garner pity from you, 2) they'll claim that it's not fair since they shared this location with you. not the most fun thing to deal with in the morning.

we were made very welcome at the farm. we chatted about the farm history, family history and of the sheep, lambs and the land including sheep hill farming methods. a lovely meal was prepared and we enjoyed the food in the family home along with some local produce and beer. then, after loading the tractor with feed we travelled in the tractor along the farm road where the sheep and lambs met us to be feed. we were delighted to hold a day old lamb and watched after feeding how mother and lamb found each other. a great experience and our hosts were a pleasure to be with and very informative to the old and new ways of sheep farming on the islands. a great experience and a pleasure to be involved in the feeding, enjoying great food and a lovely welcome to the family and farm.

we were on a self-drive tour of namibia, arranged by audley travel, when we traveled to desert rhino camp in damaraland. the camp is somewhat difficult to reach - 5 hour drive from swakopmund and then a 2 hour transfer by jeep from the welcome station to the camp - but it is worth every minute. i have been many places in the world, but i have rarely met such a wonderful staff. the facilities are rustic but elegant. the food was excellent. and the wildlife, in the middle of the desert, was amazing. we saw wild black rhinos (while we were on foot!), elephants, jackals, giraffes, and a stunning collection of birds, all desert-adapted. this is one of the few places in the world where you can see black rhinos that are being studied and protected; the camp coordinates with the save the rhino trust, wildlife safaris, and the minnesota zoo to provide that balance between tourism and conservation.this spot is well-worth the effort to reach it. make sure not to miss the "scorpion hunt"!

we were on a tasting tour with ronen at levinsky market and it was excellent!! ronan knows everyone in the market, it's fun to walk around and taste, hear stories about shops behind the scenes and the food arrives fresh with a smile on your face! an experiential tour and return with a stomach full of food. highly recommended!

we were on a tight schedule with broken bikes. mateo was exceptional with his expertise, communication and professionalism. got our bikes repaired and ready for our next ride. impressive as we were just passing thru …..they did a great job fitting in 2 bikes with our limited time and short notice. highly recommend these guys.

we were on the bonita for our sunset cruise and it was amazing! the perfect ending to our time in santorini. george and the rest of the crew were fantastic. the food was very good. i was on the cruise with my 20yr old daughter and we both had a lot of fun. the crew were knowledgeable, engaging, and fun. we enjoyed meeting other people on the boat and we all became friends by the end of the night. from honeymooners to families to empty-nesters a great night was had by all and the sunset was beyond words.

we were on the stand by line and were able to take the boat. we had to wait around 45 mins but i know it depends on the day and time you are going. there's plenty to do and museums to see while you wait. rangers are very helpful, there's a lot of information and i loved the volunteer inside the memorial telling us about history. so grateful for their work.

we were only 5 people and a very knowledgeable guide. the departure is from pointe jerome, the boat trip to the island is very quick. the tour is amazing and lasts over all approximately two hours. we saw skink, bat, pink pigeon and other birds and tortoises. we were taught about different plants as well. if you like tours which respect nature, i sincerely recommend.

we were originally booked on a tunda wilderness tour bus that ended up skipping our stop and started the tour without us. however, after raising our disappointment (this was the whole reason we came to denali), the manager, randy mantler, went above & beyond to not only refund us the full amount but also arranged a private bus tour to take us to east fork with the best driver! we saw bears, moose, caribou, dall sheep, a porcupine, fox & wolverine among other things. the tour was nothing short of incredible and i’m partially convinced that randy was personally driving up ahead of us, dropping these critters off for us to see because it was unreal to get to see that much wildlife in one shot! shout out to justin & tracy who gave up their evening plans to drive us and give us an unforgettable experience!!!!

we were passing by austria and decided to try some desserts and drinks. their desserts were pretty good, and the soup was a traditional austrian soup, which is refreshing and savoury. i like their interior and the atmosphere in the cafe. the staff members welcomed us graciously. however, a waitress with black hair asked for a tip at the end of the payment, which was a little surprising because, in my opinion, giving tips should be more voluntary and less of a request.

we were picked up from our cairns hotel for a day tour to mossman gorge, lunch at daintree village, croc-spotting river cruise, thornton beach with a stop at the daintree ice creamery and port douglas. our tour guide was fantastic: informative with a great sense of humour. felt very safe with his driving. great day out and value for money.

we were picked up in a hotel by a bus with open windows, like a safari type of bus. this is fun during hot weather: gives one a fresh breeze, however: those who go with smaller kids or with vulnerable people: if you leave at 7:15am, it gets very breezy, on the edge of feeling cold and wishing you had a hat on, to cover the ears :) especially when the drive goes amidst a busy city traffic, with a speed of 50-60km/h. so i would kindly recommend having a sweater and even a hat, if you leave at 7:15am :) we had a great excursion. the boat experience was something, the snorkeling was fun. the sea zoo was a bit depressing… i wanted to just let them al out, those fishes… i did not know it would be a sea zoo.. i thought we would be in some special area of habitat of the herbivore sharks… anyways: whats done is done. but for sensitive empaths: a warning: a sea zoo would break your heart a little. the experience in helmets 10 out of 10, that was great :) i liked the safety measures. i coykd really see that me and my kids are under protection of specially trained staff under water. we were guided practically by hand! i appreciate it. thank you!! and the pictures were fun and nice and lots of them. thanks for that too!!

we were pleasantly surprised to see so much under one roof. it took about four hours to visit all the exhibits. i am sure we missed a few a long the way, as this place is enormous and very busy. it was a great learning experience. the rom is definitely worth checking out and we look forward to exploring the museums again in the future.

we were really looking forward to our stay given the hotel’s scenic location, which truly is stunning—with lakes, mountains, multiple pools, hot tubs, saunas, mini golf, and outdoor activities like canoeing. unfortunately, the service and experience did not live up to the setting. we were locked out of our room for over an hour due to key card issues, which happened multiple times during our stay. the wi-fi was unreliable, the ac extremely loud, and there was a bug on our bed. staff were polite but consistently unresponsive. requests (like bathrobes for the spa) were met with promises of “5–10 minutes,” yet we were left waiting for over 1.5 hr, multiple times, with no follow-up. housekeeping is by request only, which is fine in theory, but in practice our room was not cleaned the first day at all, and only very late in the afternoon on the second—despite repeated reminders and the housekeeping sign being up all day. when cleaning finally happened, we were told they don’t make beds unless you’re checking out, which was baffling. it was also concerning that there was no manager on site during our 3-day stay, and the staff seemed overwhelmed and under-supported. sadly, while the amenities are great, the poor service, lack of reliability, and general disorganization made this a frustrating and disappointing experience. multiple people had problems with their rooms, 2 rooms had their toilets clogged after multiple requests, 3 other parties were locked out of their room with one that had a baby needing to sleep, and another room that had a leaking fridge. we wouldn’t return or recommend it unless major changes are made.

we were recommended la riviera by another tourist couple and we're so glad we went! the hammam and massage were amazing and the staff were extremely kind. we left feeling so relaxed and we'll definitely visit again next time we come to marrakech!
we were recommended this by a local guide. definitely had fun! the inner 5 year old loved dressing up! great to learn the history of mardi gras.
we were recommended this place by family member. ahmed who runs the place is very nice and welcoming. a great camp with good food and people. the tour afterwards was greatly appreciated.

we were sightseeing in the neighborhood and stopped for a picnic behind the flatiron building. the dog fountain is quite comical. there are lots of benches and plenty of grass, both in the sun and in the shade. it was a bit unkept, but not nasty at all. plenty of space for kids to run around.

we were so glad that we didn’t meet the owners and the dive instructors of the crystal divers in our first week! we think that if we would have met them in the first week of our three-weeks-holiday, we wouldn’t have seen anything else of this beautiful island … we would have stayed there at the top of the north of mauritius and would have done nothing else than do one dive after the next. they made diving so much fun for us! it was great! it’s now over a year ago (august 2024) that we have been at their school and they are still part of our best mauritius memories! my girlfriend started there with an open water i course. she loved it! i dive for thirty years. i dived in ten different countries, in three different oceans … but in these thirty years i collected only about 80 dives. sometimes with breaks of seven years in between. so, i became more and more insecure with diving. and with this insecurity i lost a part of the fun and a part of the relaxation diving can bring. so, i decided to do an open water i course like my girlfriend … and i loved it! the crystal divers took it seriously … with a lot of fun! and everything they did they did it in a very professional way! it was a very good decision to repeat my open water i … and it was the best decision to do it at the crystal divers!!! i admit that i didn’t see a lot in thirty years but the crystal divers are the best diving school i’ve ever seen: very friendly, very competent and very helpful owners (emmy and tony), a very friendly, very funny and very competent team of young but very experienced dive instructors (a big thank you to george, chris and ruby!!!), a very nice and very well equipped diving center, very professional equipment in a very, very good condition (everything!). they impressed us with their standards, with their professional attitude and with this family feeling which came up by itself. now it’s hard for the rest of the diving schools worldwide to stand comparisons with the crystal divers … : ) they were so helpful in everything: they had a lot of patience with us, they helped us to arrange our two courses so that always one of us could take care for our 5 years-old daughter, they helped us so much in choosing the right equipment! it was so nice and so great with them! thank you very, very much!!! they showed my girlfriend the magic of diving and they brought back to me the fun of diving! when i started diving with 21 i thought for a while i would like to become a dive instructor … then i chose a different way …. but in the time with the crystal divers this thought came back to me … and made me smile for a long moment! thank you very, very much!

welcome to lake titicaca – the highest navigable lake in the world at 3812m above sea level, stretching across 8562 km² between peru and bolivia. the air’s thin, but the legends are thick. this sacred lake was considered the birthplace of the inca civilization, where the sun god allegedly sent down manco cápac and mama ocllo to kickstart a whole empire. no pressure. the real magic? the uros people, who live on floating reed islands crafted from totora reeds – yes, actual floating islands made of squishy lake plants. they even cruise around in straw boats 🛶 that look like viking ships made by a children’s art class with engineering degrees. functional, photogenic, and slightly surreal. expect breathtaking views, mild altitude-induced confusion, and a newfound appreciation for ancient lakefront architecture made entirely of straw.

welcome to the upper geyser basin, home of the famous old faithful! not only that, but the majority of the world's active geysers are located here, too. if you plan on watching old faithful erupt, make sure you get here early. the limited benches will fill up fast. there is an observation point to view old faithful. it's a bit of a hike, but there are fewer people. the observation point is roughly 0.8 miles from the visitor center. if you want to walk the entire loop, then it is roughly 2.1 miles. i recommend circling the entire upper geyser basin. the entire loop, including the observation point, is roughly 4.0 miles (6.4 km). feel free to go your own path, but i suggest walking up the mountain to the observation point, coming down via the solotary geyser trail. then, circle the geyser hill before continuing down to the morning glory pool. you then walk the road back to old faithful, passing by daisy geyser and castle geyser. speaking of which, there are 4 other geyser eruptions you can view other than old faithful: castle, grand, daisy, and riverside! eruption time and day(s) are posted in the visitor center and online. so, be sure to do your research before heading out for the day!

well if you're in rome and you walk by it, it's interesting. but there are lots of columns and obelisks in rome and although you can see it for free, it doesn't seem particularly remarkable with the naked eye and i think most people just give it a glance and walk right by. i would suggest to appreciate the detail in the column to bring a pair of binoculars or camera with a telephoto lens and take some pictures of it close up and you can appreciate the amazing detail on the column. for all the interesting marble and stone reliefs that you'll find in say the capitoline or the palazzo massimo museums, there's very little that is superior to what you'll find on trajan's column. the problem is seeing it and in enough detail to appreciate what's there. as a retired classics professor, i can tell you there is interesting discussion on how the ancients would have been able to appreciate this detail, but that's neither here nor there for the average person. we have a way a fairly easy way to view the detail on it; simply a close-up with your phone camera is not going to suffice. again, bring those binoculars or your favorite canon camera with a telephoto lens. it is very beautiful and for the storytelling on it, there's almost no comparison anywhere from the classical world. and if you go into the forum, you'll see there are fixing up and improving the visitor experience in there every year. so it's well worth your visit, although if you're photographing it with a telephoto lens, you might as well do it from street level for free.
