went on a free tour on a saturday morning of susannah place. need to book the tickets online in advance. our tour started promptly at 11am and our tour guide ted was entertaining, factual, and a great storyteller. i thought there was the right mix with reference to indigenous history while acknowledging that this house and most of its history is european centric. two of the four buildings were open on this visit. we started in the backyard with laundry and bath and made our way into the basement kitchen before heading upstairs to the bedroom. each room was woven with stories from past tenants and we were shown pictures of them on the ipad including pics showing the exact location we were in. we then went into the building next door with a more recent interior. the ethos at this living museum is to preserve the heritage - so yes the paint is peeling from the walls and the floor has been covered over in parts, but renovating it would lose its authenticity. would be interested to see the other 2 buildings when they open later in the year. worth checking this and other museum of history properties out while entry is still free to them (via a multi year government funding). time your tour and head across to the heritage pub for lunch before or after. no photography is allowed inside.

went on a gcw trip with a group of 18 -including my family and closest family friends. we all raved about every second of the trip. we did the 4 day and hike out motor trip and would recommend it to anyone. seeing the grand canyon from this perspective was so special, you learn so much and the guides were so fun and knowledgeable. everyone became close by the end of the trip and being able to sleep under the stars and go down a level 10 rapids are memories we will cherish forever!

went on a graffiti tour with my coworkers! the instructors were friendly, very considerate of our wants and needs, and very knowledgeable about the graffiti around tel aviv and around the world. a great and interesting experience for groups wanting to get to know tel aviv! highly recommended!

went on a hike last oct with ketut as our guide. it was the first time my girl-friend and i climb a mountain. we didn’t expect the trek to be this challenging and tiring as we did the hike on the 2nd day of the trip. the trek was made easier as we had a good conversation with ketut and he introduced us to the life of a balinese. as we made our descend, ketut was very sweet. with his friend who he met on the way, he took good care of us throughout the trip by ensuring that we are comfortable and ready to walk further. (be prepared for steep slopes and pebbly walkway. we slipped and almost fell a couple of times 🥴). ketut has great photography skills as well! thankfully the weather was great when we did the hike and we had beautiful pictures/video. if you want to challenge your physical limits, feel free to try mount batur as a start. ketut mentioned that the best weather is in the period of august which means bali might also be crowded. highly recommend to request for ketut services if you’re going for this challenge.

went on a hot, steamy sunday morning at 10am. very peaceful and quiet with cooling stations. a variety of garden types - from traditional to evergreen stands. lots of room for kids and seniors. i can imagine it's a delightful place during cooler weather.

went on a hot, steamy sunday morning at 10am. very peaceful and quiet with cooling stations. a variety of garden types - from traditional to evergreen stands. lots of room for kids and seniors. i can imagine it's a delightful place during cooler weather.

went on a sat morning 9.30am. my last visit was so many years ago. visitor centre so much better and hiking paths are paved. this visit, we saw birds, squirrels, monitor lizards, a crocodile and a rare close encounter with a long king cobra.

went on a sunday so i think it was less crowded. the dinner buffet was quite good. they did refill all the food that was low so running out. they give you until 8pm to eat. there is also a la carte ordering on the mid level which might be a better deal depending on your hunger level. after dinner we just found a cozy spot with our drinks and enjoyed the ride.

went on a sunny day in july- absolutely incredible views all the way up but especially at the top. there are various views about the difficulty…we went up with our 4 year old who did great but there were many spots where we were very cautious with her due to steepness and slippery spots due to sandy loose dirt and pebbles. it’s absolutely a moderate to difficult hike- maybe on the easier side in terms of lofoten hikes, but still quite steep and parts where you’ll use your hands to assist. find the trail on alltrails to help determine which way is best for you…we started from across the street from the wc (in red circle on the photo) which took us past the lake before heading up up up. the section past the lake gave us a minute to catch our breath before continuing to the summit which was nice. it took us ~ 4 hours round trip but with plenty of time to relax at the top and plenty of stopping with our daughter. we parked at 930am and there were plenty of spots- by time we returned it was packed.

went on a trip hoping to be lucky to see the dolphins as it is sometimes a question of fortunate to see them, luckily we were able to see it. but the experience is much more than that, catarina and hugo make it a learning trip and explained about some of the species we found in the way, not only for the cetaceous but also for the birds. the boat is fantastic, very comfortable and secure, plus we were explained about all the security procedures before the trip. they are very professional since the booking until we finish our trip, so i can only recommend them to anyone who want to have a fantastic experience in the sea. thanks

went on a tuesday. this place feel almost abandon, everything is like closed, messy, only 2 - 3 staff max. its ok :/ just not what it used to be. the room 7 screen is not in the middle ._. its heavily left sided, so when we pick middle sits, tends to be the best spots, it still way off :v

went on an amazing tour with pako tours. enrique was a fantastic tour guide and kisseyfur captained the boat like an absolute champion! we had some of the greatest tacos i’ve had in mexico from their recommendations. 100% would do again. what a great day out.
went on submarine trip.... great views under water and went down to 45m. missed somethings as commentary only in korean

went on the canyoning interlaken adventure today! seriously #bestdayever buzz tour guide approved 😎 felt so safe the whole experience and every step of the way. has some epic jumps and rock slides. canyoning so such a cool sport to learn about here in interlaken! can’t wait to upgrade to the next canyon next time!

went on the cheese and wine evening cruise. we got on board and asked to get seated at a certain spot, first come first served, but they said it was for a larger group, but the very next people that came got the seat we requested. there were no seconds on cheese, and don't come hungry and think you will get a lot, you won't. basically just bites from 3 different cheeses, but they had plenty of crackers, and wine albeit a narrow selection. there wasn't much of a tour, it was just a cruise, no pointing out or saying anything about anything. maybe i read it wrong when they have in their logo and ad, canal tours.

went on the co-ed morocco trip with kite sister with my wife who had previously gone on a trip with ks and we absolutely loved it. everything is really well thought out, the itinerary was great, the locations outstanding and staff/instructors were world class. highly recommend this trip and ks in general. would definitely do it again, it's worth it every step of the way.

went on the jungle adventure tour with my daughter and mom. our tour guide was shy, she was great! the scenery was absolutely breathtaking! we learned alot about the culture on the island, as well as seeing a few props from movies made here. i loved the open air caravan we were riding in. we got front seats so wasn't as bumpy as the back most likely would have been. if you are taking a vacation on oahu i would highly suggest coming on a tour here. the whole grounds are just beautiful, being right in the mountains. so glad we experienced this.

went on the months (july to august) when there were no flowers in bloom, but the scenery was still good despite the fact. plenty of shaded areas if it ever gets too hot with adequate spaces for resting and vending machines for refreshments. for the second tjme, went during spring and was pleased to see the flowers. would definitely go here again to see the other seasons.

went on the unlimited cocktail cruise and all i can say it was amazing, our skipper and driver rene, told us lots of history of what we were seeing and just was funny in general. however the hostess, tilda was the best as she was very attentive and just in general kind and welcoming and talkative, got our drinks very fast each time and had a lovely time. the caramel vodka is also yummy. would come again thank you for the best experience tilda and rene.

went on whale spotting week, but didnt manage to see one (or did we??). the trail was easy, minimal strain on knees. weather was perfect for it. the views were so pretty. some ppl went fishin there as well. will def do this walk again.
went one saturday morning and it was really worth visit. good electic mix of things, easy to walk around, relaxed atmosphere, local coffee places to sit and take time to enjoy.

went scuba diving today! 🌊 our instructor rida was incredibly patient and professional. step by step, he helped me—someone who can’t really swim—get used to the feeling of water filling my ears. he taught us how to clear water from the mask and regulator underwater, and always used professional hand signals to ensure our safety. the best part: we’ll also get lots of free underwater videos 📹! rida even caught a sea cucumber for us to touch—it was unbelievably soft. such an amazing experience! ✨

went scuba diving. it was my first time in korean waters and it is quite okay underwater despite the corals were damaged. the surface waves were strong so it was dangerous. what was more dangerous was the fishing boats that were inconsiderate of floating smbs. the safety is not quite ensured yet compared to other countries' famous diving spots.
went snorkeling with them a while back. the staff was professional and the locations were great. facilities and food were average at best, hence the 4 stars.

went sunrise paddleboarding with coco and teo this morning and it was amazing! the company gave us clear communication and confirmation of booking. once we got there the whole experience was great. we walked along the beach with our paddle boards and went out on the water to watch the sunrise, couldn’t have asked for a better start to my birthday. couldn’t recommend enough :)

went there as a first date to paddle surf and it couldn't have been a better. we are both very outdoorsy and the move definitely worked, we are married now. i want to point out marti, he was amazing and he made it very fun for us. it's a no brainer, you should go!
went there at 6 pm and many seller already there. didnt buy things there but several seller sell their omelete rice & rice box for 25-30 baht.

went there at 7 pm on a weekday and a lot of places were already closed. i was hoping for more stands selling goods and "arts&crafts", but there were only restaurants open. i'm sure it's a good place to eat if that's what you're there for.

went there during a weekday afternoon there were a lot of people including young children. adult tickets cost 50k and audio guide cost 100k. definitely need the audio guide to truly take in the experience. it is haunting reminder that freedom is not free for the coming generations of vietnamese seeing peace in their time.

went there during summer. the weather was moderate and it was sunny. there is a car park nearby so no problem if u drive here. the blue pond nearby has a blue colour, which makes the water from the waterfall cyan too. there is a bridge, great place for pictures with the waterfall. hope ya have a g'day.

went there early in the morning to get some drone shots of the entire old town. the experience was great but had my black drone down moment when portions took it out. the peace and quiet in the morning is nice. when ships come in bay with passengers exploring, this place gets shoulder to shoulder busy. so time your visit.

went there for a concert, the place is not that big so it is quite easy to get to your seat, but the gate to get in is so small so we unnecessarily have to queue so long to get inside. lots of toilets and reasonably clean. also got shops that sells snacks and drinks.

went there for a late night walk after dinner. pleasant weather and the mesmerizing sound of sea waves against the coast. what a lovely sight. you can see the beautiful tel aviv coastline. the flea market is open till late. lots of pubs and bars. lively atmosphere there. i am sure it will be a different scene in the morning as well. there's a steep walk up. good views of the sea from up there. probably it was a bit quiet as it was a weekday

went there for lunch. had a delicious meal at salpike. very basic but the food was delicious and the soft drinks were free. will go back for more. maybe try out the starters. i had the pork belly, rice and peas with coleslaw and mango chutney

went there on a public holiday, the museums were closed however one could easily access and visit the public spaces. the place is walking distance away from other places of tourist importance so should be clubbed along with them. one can also find souvenir shops around with tiny remnants of berlin wall. a great place that reinforces a strong sense of german resilience and a must visit.

went there on vietnam national day. the road was closed on that day. traffic jam everywhere, need to walk there. the place was very crowded with lots of street food & children activities. need to pay for entrance fees. there are many eateries ( french pastry, italian food, cafes with nice cakes), nearby the lake. there is a high end shopping mall which is within walking distances while you slowly stroll along the lake.

went there on weekday (monday) and still crowded especially for the tree tunnel where people are lined up for taking photos or videos. but you can also check other places within the fort canning park that are quite interesting

went there with my friend to the christmas market and it's such a cute little place. reached there through sea bus, perfect place to spend your weekend if you don't want to spend too much. love the ice skating rink 💖

went there yesterday to watch a movie from kumamoto titled "boneless lantern." it is one of the most beautiful films i have ever watched. the film will help you understand what happens when we grieve for our loved ones - the pain and the beauty of its all. it also portray th beauty of community, something that is increasingly rare in the city life nowadays. the ticket costs 2,000 yen for adult. the film provide english, chinese, and french subtitles depending on the showtime, which is available in the museum's website. it will be screened until 22 june. the museum shop on the second floor is wonderful with creative items. i bought many gifts and postcards with joy. would love to come again the next time i visit japan.

went to a paintball event with a few buddies and honestly, it was a blast. wasn’t sure what to expect since it was my first time, but the staff (shout out to aaron) was very cool and explained everything without overdoing it. gear was solid, and the field had a good mix of cover and open spots—made for some intense moments. it’s one of those things where you start off a little nervous, then by game two you’re fully into it, diving behind barriers and trying to outsmart your friends. we laughed a lot, got hit a few times, and left with some good stories (and a couple bruises). 100% doing it again.

went to an event and moms did the food. it was amazing to try for the first time. really inventive flavours. we ordered fancy sandwiches the day before from a local place and could not believe how much better moms is. they obviously care about their food. yum!

went to anse la raie alone while on holiday with family in mauritius last summer. i hired some equipment from evans and his team, and as a lower intermediate with no kiting in the previous couple of years, i also asked for some lessons/supervision. it was great to deal with evans, since apart from being a great instructor, he's passionate with a easy-going helpful attitude and honest with his prices! hopefully see you again!
went to asia bar. the place was amazing and the food was one of the best asian food i ever had in cairo. service was amazing and extremely professional. highly recommended

went to china town and quickly moved to sampheng...we got there at 22:30 and most shops were still closed..in 23:30 the market was alive with lots of people, however very little food stores (unlike other markets). shopping at midnight is much more fun, you don't suffer from the hot sun and the vibe is different in a good way. prices are so cheap.. that u regret buying things before. lots of stores sell starting for 10bat per item, like beauty items / clips/ earings, shoes & bags i recommend it

went to diymaniyat islands for new year (2 nights camping) and definitely recommend. great food, snorkeling with turtles, barbecue and camp fire at night, and in the end we left no trace of our stay. perfect organisation by said and ghalib, who go the extra mile to make you feel welcome and relaxed. will certainly go again with them

went to polynesian spa for the first time with my partner, mother in - law and brother in - law and this visit did not disappoint!! once we arrived we were greeted by a lovely lady at the main counter who made us feel like we were at home and welcomed. we did the private lake view room and deluxe spa combo and it was so amazing, we felt like we were the only ones there as there were multiple pools. any thing we needed the staff were attentive and helpful!! the gelato at the end was also amazing so delicious and so many flavors to choose from 😍 will be recommending this place in the future and will definitely visit again!

went to see a saturday matinee of the two man play " this bitter earth " . storming performances from both actors , most excellent production. the theatre is cosy and intimate , the staff front of house and bar are amazin , friendly and helpful. would definately return. well worth the trip from manchester

went to see my neighbour totoro at the gillian lynne theatre, and was really impressed by the modern feel and comfort of the venue. one of the standout features? legroom! so much better than most other west end theatres — i didn’t feel cramped at all. a heads-up: there’s no middle aisle, so if you’re seated around 18–25, you’ll be in the middle and need to shuffle past quite a few people (cue lots of “sorry” and “excuse me” 😂). the restrooms were spacious with a good number of toilets, meaning intermission queues moved quickly — such a bonus! the stage is well designed, and i genuinely believe you’d get a good view from nearly any seat, not just those in the stalls. one of my favourite theatres so far in terms of comfort and modern facilities — would happily return!

went to see the excellent my village show here. would highly recommend it. the theatre itself is a very smart little place, staff were helpful and friendly. they provided some lemongrass tea and another drink that i can't recall. we all had the lemongrass tea, and it was lovely. nice place.

went to see the pharoah body! . defo recommend this museum as its defo worth it. the museum also has different artifcacts of islam including old kabah kiswa. beautiful lake and opportunity to get your name in hebrew on book mark.

went to the bridge at night. all the buildings around are beautifully lit up. just a nice evening on the bridge across the nile. lively yet perfectly safe. this should be on your list when visiting cairo
went to the farmers market on saturday. excellent range of things to buy and a good range of food.
went to the olympic ring to see a barca game. it was amazing!! we were able to get a tour as well!

went to the tournament in jan. got a boxed seat stadium side, you sit on the mat for a long time so be prepared. starts at 1030am to 630pm. the elite wrestlers start later in the day so check the schedule. i thoroughly enjoyed learning about the rituals and the traditions and seeing all the different styles and athleticism.
went to try gondola and ended up doing the luge too. so much fun! wish we had more time to do luge but we had a tour booked after. but, overall was amazing!!

went to visit the legendary windmill of jerusalem where they used to make flour from. a very stunning monument in one of the now richest districts of jerusalem. many beautiful houses are surrounding the windmill and it's an amazing place to check out!

went to watch tina turner the muscial at aldwych theatre . the theatre is very spectualar seats as with all old theatres do not have massive leg room however my husband and i were both comfortable with our seats which was central of the stage . good view and sound . the show was brillant ❤️ my second time of seeing the show .

went with an organised tour to bathe in the thermal waters. the park was beautiful, i would have loved to stay longer. the lockers for the bathing were complicated but manageable. the changing rooms were very busy but were a stunning design. despite heavy azourian rain this was still a very enjoyable experience. the jacuzzi (hotter pools) were a great temperature and the large pool was very comfortable.

west coast of the island, with its fishing boats and their fresh morning fish for dinner at the renowned el comejen restaurant. beautiful vegetation, unique place for mangroves. nice walk on the sidewalk. we see cancun there. near the city center. for swimmers in this area, it is required (see the photo of the sign) not to use sunscreen.

west fork trailhead – sedona, az west fork trailhead is the gateway to one of sedona’s most scenic and accessible hiking experiences. located in oak creek canyon, this trail offers a well-maintained, shaded path alongside the west fork of oak creek, featuring towering red rock cliffs, lush vegetation, and seasonal water crossings. suitable for hikers of all levels, the trail provides a combination of natural beauty, wildlife viewing, and photography opportunities. visitors are advised to wear sturdy footwear and bring water, as the trail can be rocky and uneven in places. parking is limited, so arriving early is recommended, especially on weekends and holidays.

wester martinez is impeccable, amazing, thorough and helpful!! i had an amazing time with his tour in dr, he gave a well thought out experience. from the food, to the views and just being a great help it was nothing short of fantastic! i’d absolutely recommend using him for a local tour in dr! 10/10

wester martinez was super super amazing! he was so kind to us, explaining fascinating details about his wonderful country. at first me and my family were worried we wouldn’t be able to be picked up since our resort is sort of far away, but the company made sure to accommodate to us and make our experience so fun and informative. in total, the experience was so worth it; if i could i’d give it one thousand stars!!! we are so happy!

wester martínez was absolutely fantastic. highly, highly recommended as a tour guide, specially for groups with children. he is so patient and kind, and goes out of his way to accommodate all needs. if we ever come back for a tour, we will be doing it with webster again!

western river did not disappoint and delivered an unforgettable experience. pictures simply do not do it justice. this 3 day trip was amazing, spiritual and humbling. the professionalism of the guides (marade, skinny, sara and josh) made this experience even better with the history and knowledge of the canyon, the costume party, home cooked meals, sara’s guitar picking and josh’s enthusiasm for doing what he loves. thank you for making this great.

western river expeditions – grand canyon, az ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (wish i could give them six!) let me just say it: this was not just a trip—it was a full-blown grand adventure down the colorado river, complete with laughter, rapids, jaw-dropping scenery, and… a cobbler miracle. from the moment we hit the river, our crew—lucky, steph, caden, and jace—made sure we felt safe, informed, and seriously entertained. they learned all our names faster than i learn my wi-fi password, which made everything feel personal and welcoming right from the start. now let’s talk food—because wow. this wasn’t your standard “camping chili and mystery granola” situation. we’re talking real, delicious, belly-happy meals. there was a minor tragedy involving a doomed pecan pie (rip), but fear not—jace casually whipped up a cobbler from scratch like some kind of wilderness wizard. and yes, it was delicious. steph captained our raft like she was born in the whitewater (“like a boss” doesn’t even do her justice). lucky kept everything running smoothly while charming the kids and cracking jokes, and caden serenaded us with his ukulele one night after dinner. if that’s not luxury river life, i don’t know what is. we had two rafts, 14 guests each, and by the end of the trip it felt like a big, sun-kissed family reunion (minus the awkward cousins). everyone was friendly, helpful, and happy to be unplugged and present in such a breathtaking place. hydration? covered. sun safety? covered. good vibes? overflowing. if you’re even thinking about a grand canyon rafting trip, stop thinking and book with western river expeditions. trust me—you’ll come back with stories, friendships, and probably a craving for cobbler. if you want to know what a grover is, you have to participate in one of these rafting tours. groovers = if you know, you know

we’re from the sunshine coast and really enjoyed our visit to the australian museum. it’s super easy to get there from chinatown, we caught the tram, then walked just a few minutes to the entrance. the location is really convenient if you’re already around the city. inside, there’s a lot to explore! they have everything from cool indigenous history displays to natural science exhibits. my favorite was definitely the dinosaur section — it’s really impressive and fun to see those huge skeletons up close. it’s a great spot for families, students, or anyone who loves learning new things without it feeling boring. overall, it’s a relaxed place where you can spend a good few hours discovering stuff and enjoying the exhibits. if you’re in sydney and want something interesting and educational, this museum is definitely worth checking out !

we’re very happy with our rug and the assistance we received from abdul and his team. he made the rug buying process fun and was very knowledgeable. we can’t wait to put the rug in our home and will cherish our purchase!

we’ve been on a 4 days/3 nights camping trip in the okavango delta and it has been the best experience ever! on top of the guys driving us there and back we had one guide/mokoro driver, 2 cooks and one helper: all of them went really out of their way to make us feel comfortable and safe. the camp is neat and well organised with a bush bathroom and shower, the food was the best we’ve eaten in the whole trip. during the bush walks you obviously don’t get as close to the animals as you would in a game drive (so binoculars are recommended) but the experience of walking around in their natural habitat is a once in a lifetime opportunity.

we’ve been to a few elephant “sanctuary” places over the years in phuket and this has been the only place that is truly ethical and lets the old elephants just be in their natural habitat without having to trained/forced to perform for things like tricks or allowing humans to bathe them. we could feed them but then only observe during the canopy walking tour. each elephant had a story and are clearly so cared for.

we’ve had the pleasure of staying at the fitzroy island resort before, and each visit further deepens our appreciation for the island’s natural beauty. the coral reef and vibrant marine life that surround this unique destination is always a highlight, and this trip was no different; it felt as special as ever. emma’s guided snorkeling tour was one of the most memorable parts of our stay. her expertise made it easy to explore the crystal-clear waters, where we encountered an impressive variety of colourful fish and coral types. emma’s knowledge added a thoughtful layer to the experience, helping us better understand and appreciate the delicate balance of the reef’s ecosystem. the glass-bottom boat tour with jacob was another standout moment. his thorough understanding of the coral and marine life, combined with a genuine commitment to reef conservation, made the tour both informative and enjoyable. jacob’s ability to share insights from his aboriginal heritage added depth and meaning, giving us a greater connection to the surrounding environment. he is a natural presenter and his playful humour balanced with ecological insights make for a captivating tour! we’d also like to extend a sincere thank-you to the resort staff, who made our stay smooth and comfortable from start to finish. from the warm welcome upon arrival to the attentive service throughout, every interaction was thoughtful. after a day of exploring, unwinding with a cocktail at foxy’s and enjoying the beautiful views was the perfect way to end the day. we would happily recommend this tour and resort to anyone looking for a relaxing and enriching getaway. fitzroy island offers a blend of natural beauty and warm hospitality that leaves a lasting impression, and we look forward to returning for another peaceful, tropical escape.

what a disappointment for such an important historical landmark! la casa blanca, built in 1521 as the main residence for puerto rico's first governor juan ponce de león, should be a crown jewel of old san juan's historical sites. instead, it feels like a forgotten relic, abandoned to the whims of fate. the museum's administration appears completely disorganized. there's no official website with reliable information about opening hours, ticket sales, or exhibits. i arrived during what was supposedly "closed hours" according to information i'd found, yet the museum was inexplicably open and staff allowed me to enter. while the $5 entrance fee is reasonable, what follows hardly justifies even this modest price. once inside, you're essentially on your own. there are no explanatory brochures, no suggested route through the rooms, no informational plaques on the walls—nothing to guide visitors or provide context about what they're seeing. the 16th and 17th-century artifacts are displayed with minimal care or explanation, leaving visitors to guess at their significance. the building itself is undeniably impressive—old san juan's oldest residence has an inherent historical gravitas that even neglect can't completely erase. the architecture and glimpses into colonial life are interesting, but without proper interpretation, much of its educational value is lost. most concerning is the general sense that there's a desire to forget rather than celebrate this important piece of puerto rico's viceroyalty past. whether due to budget constraints, administrative issues, or perhaps more complex cultural attitudes toward the spanish period, the result is a significant missed opportunity to showcase an important historical site. this could be a world-class museum with proper investment and curatorial attention. instead, it feels like walking through an abandoned home filled with artifacts no one cared to explain. a true shame for a structure with such historical significance as the residence of juan ponce de león and his descendants.

what a fantastic experience! tucked away on the beautiful carrer de montcada in the el born district, the moco museum is a real gem. the first thing that strikes you is the building itself – a gorgeous, historic palace that has been beautifully maintained. the contrast between this old-world architecture and the vibrant, modern art inside is just brilliant. the overall organisation of the art is captivating and helps to grasp the attention of visitors from the moment you step in. the curators have done an incredible job. the layout is minimalist and yet it feels so vibrant and interactive, allowing each piece enough space to breathe while contributing to a collective, energetic vibe. the choice of art, from kaws to yayoi kusama and andy warhol, is ideal for the atmosphere they've cultivated. it’s fresh, relevant, and engaging. i have to give a special shout-out to the staff, who were incredibly helpful and friendly. we had a bit of a self-inflicted issue – i'd accidentally bought tickets online back in july, not realising they were for immediate use and not for a future date. i was fully expecting to have to buy new ones, but they kindly accepted our original tickets without any fuss. that kind of understanding and excellent service really sets the tone for a wonderful visit. my only minor observation, and it's a very small one, was that in the description for banksy's work, there was no mention of him being an artist from bristol, england. as a fellow brit, i know he is incredibly proud of his heritage, and he is one of the core reasons bristol has found its place on the international map. i feel he would appreciate that being mentioned! but honestly, this is a tiny detail in what was an otherwise flawless exhibition. if you're looking for a break from the classic museums and want to see a brilliantly curated collection of modern and contemporary art in a stunning setting, you absolutely have to visit the moco. it’s an inspiring and thought-provoking couple of hours. highly recommended!

what a great day! it was fascinating to learn about the dogs who ran and sometimes won, the iditarod. the highlight was learning how to drive a sled. i guess you do have to be a little adventurous for this - and in fairly good shape. there is a lot of balancing and braking that you do. but i'm an "old lady", and it was fantastic, and the dogs love to run so much! as i was solo, i had the advantage of having a guide as my passenger, and she directed me as we went along. afterwards, you thank your dogs for a great job, pats and rubs for all. chloe was/is so great, explaining about dallas seavy (who owns the kennel), the iditarod and the dogs. it's amazing that these dogs have the heart to run in that race, and win! and chloe is an up and coming musher - she will be in the the winner's circle one day (you heard it here first)! then the kennel tour - and the puppies! they even picked us up at our hotel, but the usual meeting place is easy to get to from main street talkeetna. this is a a+++ tour to go on, and no, it is fine if you don't want to drive, it is just as thrilling as a passenger too! thanks to ak sled dog tours for a great day!

what a truly beautiful mosque! visiting it is a memorable experience that i highly recommend to anyone in the area. the interior is open to tourists from 8 am to 11 am, offering a peaceful and quiet atmosphere to admire its stunning architecture. but let me share a little tip: while the morning visit is wonderful, i highly encourage you to also come in the evening, especially at sunset. the mosque takes on an entirely different charm as it glows beautifully under the night lights. the way it is illuminated makes it even more majestic, providing a perfect opportunity to capture breathtaking photos and create unforgettable memories. this mosque is somewhat of a hidden gem, not very well-known among tourists, which means you can enjoy it without the usual crowds. it feels more intimate and serene this way. you can visit on your own or with your family—it’s perfectly easy to navigate, and there’s no need for a guide to appreciate its beauty and cultural significance. when visiting, remember that you’ll need to remove your shoes as a sign of respect. don’t worry, though—there’s a designated shoe rack to the right, just after entering through the main door. the process is straightforward and adds to the authentic experience. what makes this mosque even more appealing is that it’s completely free to enter, unlike the larger, more famous mosque nearby, which now charges over 20 usd per person. this free access makes it all the more worthwhile, especially considering how much there is to admire here. so, if you’re looking for a peaceful and enriching experience, don’t hesitate to visit this mosque. it’s truly a hidden treasure, and its quiet, tourist-free atmosphere makes it even more enjoyable. whether you visit in the morning or evening (or both!), it’s a place that will leave a lasting impression.

what a truly magical and beautiful wonderland! i seriously could've walked this area for 3 to 4 hours but the heat was scorching. i loved how serene and visually stimulating this place is. it is accessible- friendly. there were benches appropriately placed throughout the property for those who have limited mobility or who need a break from walking for a bit. also, this is a great place to consider having a picnic, a date, an engagement, or a wedding party. there were a few places i wanted to visit but time and heat were not on my side so i must return on a future date.

what a view of morning sunrise. be sure to check out the timing of sunrise. it takes about 15mins to hike up to the summit if you are fit. plan to arrive at least 15mins before sunrise. go to the further end (where you will descend later) to avoid the crowd and a better view.
what a view! breathtaking place. there is a parking in the village (also a small cafe worth visiting). the viewing point is really close to the parking so it's worth to walk around some more.

what a way to see the great barrier reef! the crew was fantastic! we could choose 4 dives in a day! star dive guide alexis made our stay aboard the boat exceptional. he thought of absolutely everything we might need …even before we thought of it. waited on us with tremendous patience. each dive was unique and @alexis gave so much confidence to try new things. he even delivered beer to our post-dive jacuzzi! purser talia took care of the interior of the ship, made us feel very welcome from the minute we entered the ship.

what a week at the lofoten ski lodge. incredible hospitality by the staff of the lodge and exceptional ski guiding by seth hobby and his staff at northern alpine guides. great food, wonderful cabins and perhaps one of the most stunning settings in the world. if you put just one location in your ski bucket list, this is the one. treat yourself to the trip lifetime.

what a wonderful and peaceful place to go for a walk and clear your mind. the trail is practically surrounded by a wide assortment of forest trees and plants, providing a cool shade, and beauty for the eye to behold. it's the ideal location to go for a walk with both kids and dogs alike.

what a wonderful and relaxing way to spend the day. since we stayed in centro de tulum, our guide birgit was able to pick us up and drive us to casa cenote. we had a leisurely paddle through the mangroves with scuba divers below us, herons beside us, plenty of fish, and even the local crocodile (harmless as he slept soundly in the sun!). we took a refreshing dip in the water and just slowly enjoyed spotting more and more wildlife around us. one note is to make sure you don't wear sunscreen as it disrupts the ecosystem. wear a rashguard if you need to respect the nature.

what an amazing fishing trip!! i spent three days with german, lukas and sebastian fishing some of the most pristine waters in the world. the scenery was incredible, the rivers were crystal clear and we managed to catch a great array of rainbow, brown and brook trout!! the guides are incredibly friendly and professional and i learned several new skills working with them. in addition to great fishing, the meals prepared by the guides along the way were by far the best i have ever had on a fishing trip - one lunch included phenomenal argentinian steak grilled on a picturesque river bank with a great bottle of wine! beyond the great days fishing, martin is one of the easiest people to plan a fishing trip with. he was extraordinarily responsive, sometimes responding to my emails within minutes of me hitting send. he understood exactly what i wanted to achieve and put together an itinerary that included a great combination of different fly fishing experiences in a relatively short period of time.

what an amazing gem this place is! this is an amazing location to stay, especially if you plan to see a mara river crossing during the great migration. the architecture is so cool, built on top of a large rock while seamlessly integrating the bare rock into the design of the common areas. it’s really giving 1960s safari fantasy. there are adorable rock hyrax running around all over. they are soooo cute to watch, and they won’t ever bother you. the pool deck is an incredible place yo enjoy a cocktail and gaze out over the vast savannah. this was a daily activity each day coming back from safari. there are also some lovely viewing spots for sunset and star gazing in the evenings. the food was very good compared to the previous lodge we were in (around karatu). whether buffet or made to order the food was always enjoyable and satisfying. the staff were incredibly friendly and accommodating. they made our stay really feel amazing. the rooms are just okay. pretty bland and the beds are super firm. there are also a lot of small things that could use some fixing and tlc to really take this place to the next level (loose shower head holder, many lights on the pool deck are out, etc.) the hotel runs on a diesel generator for electricity so the power and hot water aren’t turned on until 6pm, which was sometimes a little frustrating, but not a huge issue.

what an amazing hike! we did the red loop and it had beautiful views, well kept trails, and lots of wildlife. the staff was amazing— the woman working at the entrance gate was very friendly and knowledgeable, she gave us a thorough rundown of all the trails with what landscapes and wildlife we could expect to see. to top it all off the trail ends at the cafeteria where we enjoyed a cerveza with beautiful views of the volcano. the entrance fee is a bit pricey ($26) but with our experience i think it is well worth it. it was a great way to start our stay in la fortuna!

what an amazing hike. a bit challenging for individuals that never hiked or haven't hiked in a while. reaching the top felt like an achievement and the view is so beautiful. took the bus, walked to the main entrance where the visitor center is located. recommend hydrating the day before and the day before starting. use the restroom before going since there are no restrooms along the trail. hydrating and sun block are your best friends. cooling towels or cooling shirt (uv shirt or rash guard shirt) and a hat help. wetting the shirt and cooling towel helped reduce the heat fatigue. taking breaks along the way in certain areas allows for recharging. wear very comfortable shoes with good grip will allow a comfortable hike and minimize back pain. there are certain resting areas that allow a beautiful view of the city and the ocean.

what an amazing place and lovely surprise. we were supposed to go to a different zipline on our underground river tour but at the last minute it was canceled due to maintenance so we were redirected here instead. i’m so glad we were! had i known how amazing it was, i would’ve absolutely booked this. the staff and guides were informative, friendly, funny and so very helpful. at 67 years, i wasn’t confident about climbing up inside the cave, but the women that were the guides inside the cave helped me at every moment, showing me where to place my hands, my feet and how to get me and my belly through the crevices, making me laugh and facilitating me to achieve a wonderful climb that i never thought i would be able to do. don’t be intimidated by age or ability as you are in assisted the entire time by the guides, with harnesses and ropes and pulleys to help you climb the more difficult parts. all of the gear and safety equipment is provided. if i can do this, you can! i want to thank them all and would give them a ten out of five stars. the zip line was just the thrilling cream on top and fun reward. thank you! thank you! thank you! i’ll definitely be back. big hugs from santa!
what an amazing place to watch a show. the theatre is one of the finest, my only complaint was the leg room in our seats. however the view of the stage & the building are top notch.

what an amazing place you can explore a whole day in! during the day it slowly starts getting busier and then the evenings feel like it's times square in new york. so heads up haha. might be lucky to catch some performances! so many food places and cafes to explore and there's pop up events. i recommend checking out colline, such a lovely cafe surrounded by flowers. lovely aesthetic.

what an amazing place. the falls in yellowstone are endless. i had an opportunity this past july 4th weekend and what great time to be there. i would highly recommend stopping to see the falls. you can also take a trail to the upper falls. i went a step further and walked the south rim trail to explore from the other side.

what an amazing safari trip we had . thanks a lot to mr evarist for his professional skills in organising the best 7 days in safari . before trip i have messaged around 20 companies in tanzania , and only him replied immediately and was always available on the phone to offer and tailor everything for me . we have visited: tarangire national park , serengeti, arusha national park, ngorongoro national park , massai village and manyara lake . he found for us best tented camps and lodges with amazing service. special thanks to our private tour guide elly for this unforgettable experience. when reality is better than expectations. well done , team . can’t wait to come back and see animals migration next year.

what an amazing scenery, we went twice, one time during the day and then returned in the evening. we visited on mid may, so not too crowded. it's not far from shirogane blue pond, we also checked out the tokachidake observatory.

what an amazing theme park!! there are lots of fun interactive spots and fun rides! when you’re hungry, there’s lots of great places to eat, especially burger way! the food is delicious and affordable, and staff and manager there will treat you very well!!

what an amazing time! flying to the grand canyon on the king of canyons package at sunset was hands down the best thing i've ever done in las vegas. we departed from the strip's vip terminal around 5:30 pm. after landing on a private plateau in the canyon, we enjoyed champagne and a picnic basket, with about 50 minutes to explore. it was the perfect time of day, no direct sun, so we weren't baking! the flight back to vegas treated us to a beautiful sunset, incredible views, and the dazzling city lights. they even played '80s and '90s music in our headsets, making the experience even better than i'd imagined. our pilot was super friendly, and we had a great chat with him in the canyon. i'd recommend this package to anyone without hesitation. thank you, papillon helicopter!

what an amazing time!! our hosts david and miguel were fantastic. they provided fresh fruit, chips, guacamole, drinks and great energy. the boat was shaded so it was nice and cool the entire time and i really enjoyed learning about the history of xochimilco. would definitely recommend to anyone visiting mexico city!

what an amazing tour !! i did the boat-tour to bazaruto twice, because i fell in love with this place. everyone on the boat was so friendly and helpful. i felt really comfortable during the whole trip. the food is amazing and i never saw something more beautiful under water as i saw while snorkeling. i also met raimundo und jeff, who are two wonderful souls :) i definitely would recommend everyone to do this trip, it’s worth every cent. thank you ! ❤️

what an amazing walk. praise the lord for his creation is so beautiful! 5km walk with bit of altitude but doable. definitely recommended for sunrise or sunset walk. has rockpool next to the beach! would be visiting again.

what an amazing way to finish our trip in amsterdam. would highly recommend to those wanting to avoid the usual ‘booze cruise’ canal trips! our wonderfully friendly skipper showed us her city from the water and our host, andrea, was delightfully hospitable (& also a very talented double bass player)! the jazz band were exceptional & truly made the relaxing 1.5hr canal cruise unforgettable.

what an amazing way to see the city at night! i have gone on a sunrise kayak of middle harbour previously and that was an incredible experience but to see the city lit up at night for vivid from the water was just beautiful and whilst other boats are out on the water, it actually was a peaceful paddle. this is worth checking out whilst vivid is on, the guides are really professional and take their time and give you insights to the surrounding area and history. thank you for a great night out!

what an awesome discovery! we thought that we had died and gone to heaven. absolutely one of the best indian meals we have ever had and we have lived in a large asian community portion sizes are large - we ended up taking a doggy bag home! prices are a bit more than other places but well worth it. great service, friendly staff. will definitely return!!!

what an awesome environment! i had an absolute blast at this place and it has the most pleasant and friendliest staff imaginable. i'm a solo traveller and paid a visit on my own the first day which was immensely exhilarating! sadly, the video footage on my jump was lost, yet they offered me back for a free jump the following day, which i so happily obliged to! the second day i bonded with a few folk on the free transfer over which added to my second experience and the excitement of it all. we were on such a high after the first jump that we all decided to go again and give a different jump a try, of which the price decreases every time and seemed like great value in my opinion. overall, i can't recommend this place enough and it's both a place to feel safe and to indulge in a wild thrill for solos, friends, or families, of which you easily bond with over the mutual hype! thanks so much for an epic time!

what an awesome experience yet it didn't cost a dime! the water ride was very slow but it was fun to see all the decor lapping around the course.

what an awesome experience! i was a last minute addition and i was accommodated no problem. i was able to join up with a tour that had just started and fell in with them seamlessly. the locations they took us to were beautiful and away from crowds. lunch and the teas throughout were great. we had a gorgeous view for sunset, then returned to our camp out in the desert where a delicious zarb dinner was prepared for us. afterwards music was played around the fire and of course, more tea. after the group broke for the night i spent time on my balcony stargazing and enjoying the beautiful night sky out in the remote desert. this is a great crew and you'd make a great decision to spend your wadi rum adventure with them!

what an experience! i enjoyed the full day out on the tully. from the moment we boarded the bus to tully, the fun didn’t stop until we were safely returned to our accommodation, pretty much in one piece. we were lucky enough to have not one, but two kick ass river guides, mat and tom, leading us down the tully. mat and tom were able to perfectly balance the jokes/banter (ensuring we enjoyed every minute), the info sessions (allowing us to fully understand what makes the land and water so special), and safety. while the rafting itself was an exhilarating experience to say the least, and while you truly are at the mercy of the rapids, mat and tom kept us feeling safe for the entire journey. we were even lucky enough to experience the chaos of a raft flip in a controlled setting! 10/10 experience, the highlight of our trip to cairns, and i can’t wait to do it again! thanks to the guys at raging thunder!!

what an experience! this is a must for anyone visiting israel. my family and i visited israel this month and joined shuka tours on a fabulous culinary tour in tel-aviv! for sure a highlight of our trip. ronnen was such an easy going host full of energy, and brought israeli culture to the tips of our tongues. the experience was great for the kids too! we highly recommend, this is something you don’t want to miss!
what an experience! we had a lot of fun! david is a great guide. he explained to us what to do perfectly, and always kept an eye on us. very safe! i will do it again 100%!!

what an experience. 10 day motor. with matt, dean, blake, and anna. day 1 started with rain and a short raft. great beach party until wind came up. managed and had an awesome salmon dinner. the crew were great leaders, chefs 👨‍🍳, and seekers of suitable lunch and camp sites. with multiple levels of physical abilities this was key for amenity set ups. day 2 brought cold water and rain. again we endured the raging white water from the river and the drops from the sky. matt and dean were great story tellers and historians. i think blake and anna had the same stories. we ad opportunities to challenge ourselves throughout the trip with 22 passengers plus the kitchen, food, and other essentials, a fireside brought creativity and new words: 'cot' ya, 'tent'alizing..tantalizing... etc. i was able to kayak a short distance as were others. stake dinner to order with simulated campfire was a nice closure for the last night. our group found new friends amongst ourselves and with our hosts. wish i were there again already. looking forward to the next time. thank you for helping me discover more of my abilities. toni

what an experience. extremely bumpy ride, but very enjoyable. generally, planes are 10-20 people capacity. pilots are great, very well trained and handled the flights so well. you get the best view of the grand canyon from the top. colorado river was so clear. one must not miss the experience.

what an extraordinary place and landscape. we stayed 1 night there with our small kids (in the farmhouse) and we had excellent, home made curry dinner in our house. the details of the house are very inspiring, from the beautiful books and carefully selected furniture to the warm cashmere blankets. staff is super helpful. highly recommended for hikers and families. will return.

what an extraordinary place and we were fortunate to have a very informative guide who after telling us about the geological formations took us to the sunset viewpoint. this was magical. the valle de la luna is located about and 17 km west of san pedro de atacama and is part of the cordillera de la sal (salt mountain range) and the los flamencos national reserve. it has beautiful lunar-like landscape with unique geological formations shaped by wind and water, including salt flats, dunes, caverns, and sculptural saline outcrops. the area is one of the driest on earth, with no flora or fauna due to its extreme aridity.

what an impressive museum! very well organized and in an impressive building. the exhibits were really well done. note that almost all signage for exhibits were exclusively in french, but big fonts made it easy to leverage a translation app. on a rainy day, no lines, had a/c, and kids are free!

what an incredible and magical experience, we were so close to not going as it appeared on google as if this was closed. we arrived via the hotel grounds by the pier near the boat and after waiting on the pier for less than ten mins the engineer on the yavari sailed out in a small boat to collect us. the story behind this boat is crazy … built in the 1800s and shipped all the way from london to lake titicaca, with more than 2000 individual pieces being hauled 190 miles over the andes (and more than 15,000 ft elevation) to reach the shores of lake titicaca where it was assembled, finished on christmas day 1870. originally a steam boat fuelled by llama dung! now has a petrol engine. i won’t say anymore other than what an incredible privilege to have set foot on this boat and had the honour of all the knowledge and passion from the engineer on board. truly a hidden gem and will go down as one of the most special experiences i have had in all my travels.

what an incredible experience! i can't recommend this place enough. my sisters and i spent a night at wadi rum dream camp and it was one of the best experiences ever! from the moment we arrived, everyone was lovely, hospitable and so helpful. they upgraded our room - which was super nice and what a view from there! they arranged a sunset tour and stargazing - which is def not to be missed. it wasn't just an experience, but an education and was truly an unforgettable trip. thank you so much to all of dream camp for making our time so amazing. we'll be back for sure!

what an incredible experience! initially booked a 1 hour hammam for my husband and i. it was an easy booking process via whatsapp with follow-up morning of to confirm, including a link with directions. upon arrival, we were kindly greeted and provided tea and a warm cloth. we decided to upgrade our service to a 45 minute hammam + thai massage. best decision! for a 10:30 booking, we officially started close to 11. it was worth the wait. started at the changing room where we slipped into disposable underwear, a robe and slippers. proceeded downstairs to the hammam for the most unique experience. not sure what to expect, we both loved our treatment. next up massages. relaxing, perfect pressure and we felt well taken care of. this place is clean, beautiful and everyone was wonderful. at a higher price point, we felt it was well worth it. highly recommend. we will definitely return on our next visit to marrakech.

what an incredible experience! this diving center truly impressed me with their professionalism and attentiveness. a major plus was having several english-speaking divers on staff, which made communication seamless. the team made sure i felt completely comfortable with the equipment before we even got into the water, which was especially reassuring since i was quite nervous about diving. the small group size was perfect, making everything feel more manageable and personalized. my instructor, roberto, was exceptional. his calm and patient demeanor instantly put me at ease. he understood my apprehension and went above and beyond to help me feel confident, even holding my hand throughout the dive, which made a huge difference in my comfort and safety. we saw so much amazing sea life! roberto took us to a spot teeming with turtles and fish, making the experience even more unforgettable. i wholeheartedly recommend them—it was a super great experience!

what an incredible experience! we were lucky to see a wide variety of wildlife including elephants, zebras, giraffes, warthogs, dik-diks, impalas, baboons, hornbills, brown mongoose, lions, ostriches, and so many beautiful birds. the sightings were unforgettable and the overall experience exceeded expectations. highly recommend to anyone looking for an authentic and thrilling safari adventure!

what an incredible experience. totally ethical. really focused on making sure the elephants feel psychologically safe and comfortable. really lovely area; well set up and great staff. the 90min session was excellent and more than enough time, just perfect. loved my morning there. highly recommend.

what an incredible little island paradise. it was exactly what i had hoped for. spending the days reading on the veranda while only listening to the waves of lake titicaca. wonderful sunrises every morning and mystical island ruins to explore. after reading that everyone regretted only spending one or two nights here, i booked three. and well... i also regret not staying longer, haha. i feel like you can easily spend a week here and not get tired of this amazing place. it is that kind of location to just relax and disconnect from everything.

what an incredible piece of history. admission is cheap and covers both castles in the city. be prepared for stairs. the triangle stairway has some really large stairs. the whole fort is full of amazing views and cool displays. the breeze through the fort is so nice on those hot days. it's amazing to see all the work our national parks are doing.

what an incredible tour! i usually love hiking solo, but experience jordan made this trip so much fun that i never once felt like i was missing out by being in a group. they kept the group together while still giving us space to go at our own pace, which was the perfect balance. from start to finish, everything was smooth. the hotel in amman was fantastic and pick-up times were spot on. our guide mahmood was an absolute legend. he had us laughing the whole time and made sure everyone felt comfortable and taken care of. the hike started off easy on day one, then gradually got harder each day, which was the perfect way to warm up. the support team was amazing. they set up our tents, transported our bags, and cooked incredible meals. they felt more like family, and walking into camp each evening to find everything set up with tea and food waiting was such a treat. the meals were delicious, and there was always plenty to go around. one of the best moments was making traditional bedouin bread in the fire with eid. i even got to join his wife in the kitchen and learn local cooking techniques, which was such a special experience. walking into petra was unreal. instead of starting at the treasury with the crowds, we arrived slowly from the 'back door' entrance, taking it all in along the way. mahmoud’s stories and history lessons made every site come alive, and i loved how easy he made it to understand. i also really appreciated how thoughtful the team was. they checked in to see if we were happy with the schedule, if we needed more breaks, or if our tents and beds were comfortable. experience jordan has thought of everything to make sure this trip is unforgettable. if you are looking for a truly epic adventure, this is it. finishing off in wadi rum with a bit of luxury and then floating in the dead sea was the perfect ending. huge thanks to the team for putting together such an amazing trip. i cannot wait to come back one day! kiera

what more can i say about the greatness of cape fusion tours? we first booked a cape town eats tour for our first trip to south africa in february 2020. you can also find that review on tripadvisor. five years later and we’re on our third round of tours with pam. this time, we brought family with us to experience it all. we booked two private tours – a food tour and a tour of the peninsula. both were amazing. day 1: updated cape town eats tour – when pam arrived to pick us up for this tour, she said the sky is blue and conditions on table mountain are perfect. she suggested we rearrange the day slightly and sneak in a cable ride up the mountain while we could. yes! we ate our way around our first stop (oranjezicht market), then booked express passes for the table mountain cable car. we love the flexibility we have while on a private tour. we had previously mentioned our hope to get in a table mountain visit during our stay – we just weren’t sure if/when we could fit it in. unsurprisingly, pam found a way. after about an hour on the mountain, we made our way down and continued the food tour. in all we visited at least 5 different places all around cape town. she tailored the tour to the varied appetites in our group – from no game meat to low gluten – she handled it all without missing a beat. almost all of the places we visited were different from our first tour five years ago. the only “complaint” i have is too much food!! ha ha. every place we visited had amazing foods to try. as usual, pam was warmly welcomed wherever we went. yes, she seems to know everyone in south africa and they love her as much as we do!! day 2: peninsula tour – on our second day with pam, we decided to tour the peninsula her way – relaxed and chill. we told pam we loved to walk, and she made sure we had opportunities wherever we went. for example, we hiked from the lighthouse to the cape of good hope. pam drove to the bottom with one member of our party that wasn’t up for a hike. we never felt rushed. all in all it was a wonderful day filled with sightseeing, shopping and eating. we highly recommend cape fusion tours. we’ve met some of her other tour guides along the way (ryan, shelly) and they are just as genuine and energetic as pam.

when i enter the square de berlin in paris, i immediately feel the calm atmosphere of this small, hidden park. located in the 8th arrondissement, near place de la madeleine, it is often visited by locals looking for a break from busy city life. i can see the trees surrounding the square and the manicured lawns that give the place a welcoming and relaxing atmosphere. as i walk around i start to think about the history of this place. the square de berlin was created in 1822 and was originally known as the square d'action sociale. the name refers to the growing social responsibility of the city administration during this time. the square was designed as a place to promote the common good and create a green oasis in the emerging city. as i observe the people around me, i feel the connection to the past that this place embodies. in 1871, after the end of the franco-german war, the square was renamed in honor of the capital of germany, berlin. it was a symbolic gesture that reflected the new geopolitical realities and berlin's influence on europe. i wonder how people felt about these changes at the time and what feelings the renaming made them feel. as i sit on a bench and enjoy the beauty of the square, i notice the little details that make this place so special. there are pretty flowerbeds decorated with colorful blossoms and i can hear the chirping of the birds nesting in the trees. the small sculptures and benches scattered throughout the park also give the square an artistic touch. i can well imagine that this place was once a meeting place for artists and thinkers who sought inspiration in nature. as i continue to stroll through the square de berlin, i notice the diversity of people who come here. families enjoy a picnic, friends chat, and couples stroll hand in hand. it is a place of encounter and exchange that brings people together. i am drawn to this community and can't help but feel a sense of belonging, even if i'm only here temporarily. for me, the square de berlin is more than just a beautiful park; it is a place with a rich history that reflects the social changes and political upheavals in france. as i finally stand up to move on, i carry with me the feeling of calm and respect for the past. this little green retreat in the middle of the vibrant city reminds me of the importance of pausing in the hustle and bustle of life and appreciating the beauty around us. as of: december 22, 2023

while marina bay sands dazzles visitors with its luxury shopping, world-class restaurants, and breathtaking architecture, my lasting memory comes from a group often overlooked: the housekeeping team. during what was otherwise a very difficult trip, these professionals became the highlight of my stay. the scale of their work is extraordinary—cleaning massive, high-tech rooms with meticulous precision, restocking coolers and amenities, and ensuring no detail is overlooked, all within tight time frames. as someone with severe ocd, i notice everything, and i was genuinely in awe. one housekeeper, in particular, came to refill my ice bucket—something i didn’t even need—yet she bowed repeatedly and apologized as though she were inconveniencing me. her humility and dedication were deeply touching. later, another staff member surprised me with a vegan birthday cake, complete with a candle. i had forgotten it was even my birthday, but that thoughtful gesture nearly brought me to tears. it wasn’t just a dessert; it was a reminder that i was seen and valued. in a hotel renowned for grandeur, it’s the quiet diligence of the housekeeping team that, in my view, forms the true backbone of marina bay sands. they made me feel special, cared for, and genuinely welcome. i would return not just for the stunning rooms, but to personally thank and see these remarkable individuals again. thank you so much for this experience, it made my birthday trip.

while visiting new orleans, my daughter and i stopped by the ogden museum of southern art, and it was an absolute highlight of our trip. staying at the hilton riverside, we found it an easy, flat, 20-minute walk to the museum. the admission price was very reasonable at $15 for adults and just $7 for kids/teens up to 17. the staff was incredibly friendly and helpful, suggesting we start on the 5th floor and work our way down. this was great advice—giving us a wonderful perspective and made the experience feel cohesive and well-paced. the exhibits were thoughtfully curated, showcasing a fantastic mix of southern art, culture, and history and diverse exhibit showcasing everything from traditional paintings to modern art installations. the architecture of the museum is stunning—bright, airy, and thoughtfully designed. the open layout, with views across all levels, added to the experience, making it both visually striking and easy to navigate. whether you’re an art enthusiast or just looking for something memorable to do in new orleans, this museum is a must-visit. highly recommend!

while wandering through bangkok’s lively chinatown, i found myself drawn toward wat mangkon kamalawat, also known as wat leng noei yi. the moment i stepped through its grand chinese-style gates, i was hit by the aroma of incense and the gentle hum of prayers being chanted—it immediately felt like i had entered a completely different world. this temple is a beautiful fusion of chinese and thai buddhist traditions. the red pillars, golden altars, and dragon motifs created a visually rich atmosphere, and even though i’m not buddhist, there was something very grounding and peaceful about being there. i watched locals perform their rituals—lighting incense, bowing with folded hands, and making quiet offerings. it was calming to just observe and absorb the spiritual energy of the place. what i really appreciated was how authentic and alive everything felt. this wasn’t a touristy stop—it was a functioning temple where people genuinely came to pray, reflect, and seek blessings. it gave me a glimpse into the local culture that goes far deeper than street food and shopping. if you’re in bangkok and want a short escape from the chaos of the city, this is a perfect little sanctuary. i walked out feeling lighter and more centered.

whilst i imagine many tours take you to a similar place, we had an experience that was unforgettable. hamed and mohammed took us on a trip which felt like no other. we see the typical areas of wadi rum, but when it came to having lunch, a sunset view, or a talking about bedouin life, that is where the experience became something more personable and memorable than we could have ever imagined. we arrived in the evening, had the most amazing dinner cooked underground and spent the evening talking into the hours about life in wadi rum, how it has changed and how it compares to life as western europeans under a starlit sky like no other. the next day, we had breakfast followed by a full day in wadi rum until sunset exploring landscapes hard to believe exist on earth. wadi rum is amazing, but what made the trip more beautiful than we could imagine was the bedouin stories and hospitality we received from our friends at bedouin nights camp the pictures i have posted are nothing compared to the actual experience. the most beautiful tour parts are on my friends camera and we will add them soon, but i promise you could not be disappointed with the experience we have from ahmed and mohammed.

wild life sydney zoo is an indoor zoo located in darling harbour, adjacent to sea life sydney aquarium. the zoo features nine pavilions showcasing australia’s iconic wildlife—including the beloved koalas and kangaroos, as well as the mischievous yet intriguing tasmanian devils, giant saltwater crocodiles, and lizards with quirky personalities. in addition to viewing the animals from a distance, visitors also have opportunities for close encounters and interactive experiences. 🐾 wild life sydney zoo offers a series of immersive exhibits that showcase australia’s most iconic and intriguing animals in habitats designed to reflect their natural environments. kangaroo walkabout a spacious, open-range enclosure where kangaroos and wallabies roam freely. visitors can walk among them and observe their natural behaviors up close. 🐨 koala rooftop a tranquil rooftop habitat featuring eucalyptus trees and lounging koalas. includes opportunities for photos and even a “breakfast with the koalas” experience. 🦎 devil’s den home to the tasmanian devils, showcasing their feisty personalities and conservation story. learn about efforts to protect this endangered species. 🐊 kakadu gorge a dramatic exhibit inspired by the northern territory’s rugged landscapes. features a massive saltwater crocodile named rocky, one of the zoo’s star residents.

winter season holiday review. (why you should visit was water park in winter instead of summer) so me and a couple friends came to water world during our winter break cause tickets were really cheap. i got it for like 50$ hkd for some winter student promotion. to sum it up, it was really fun and facilities are really clean and state of the art and best of all, barely anyone was there so we pretty much had the whole place to ourselves. however the only downside was the temperature and some parts were really cold, especially by the end. it just gradually becomes colder. majority of the park is indoors and there is heating and everything but even still, we felt a bit chilly in the water and in addition, we had to walk on outdoor stairs to reach the slides. they do have heaters on the stairs but don't really do much. but honestly for 50$, i can't complain much. the entering process was smooth alongside locker booking. (fyi, the lockers are smaller we expected so take that into consideration when renting). i had heard in the summer seasons, you may have to wait up to an hour just to get to go down one slide but to our amazement, the park barely had any people and 90% of the time, there was no one in line waiting for the slides. the 10% were like 2-3 people infront of us. and of course no trouble finding tables and chairs. in the giant wave pool, there was maybe like 30 people inside at the peak. it could probably fit like 500 people easily. very nice. food was decent but the price was quite good, compared to other amusement parks. and the staff, they were honestly so friendly and even gave us discount coupons. very nice people. to end it off, i would recommend going during winter seasons. ticket prices are way cheaper, no crowds, no wait time, can relax without stressing about lines and seat finding, etc. so unless you're bad with cold weather or you're going there to soak up the sun, go during winter at least once. but be warned of the rainbow slide. turns out that thing finishes in an outside pool and we pretty much swam in an ice pool for 10 seconds. needless to say, we were all screaming. enjoy!

with its open landscape surrounded by mountains, vestvågøy is like an oasis in the centre of lofoten. this is a big farming area, and i found here lots of products from local producers. in times gone by, vestvågøy was called lofotr, and after a while it gave its name to the entire archipelago. for hundreds of years, the island was hiding treasures in the form of the biggest chieftain’s house to date that has been found. every year, visitors from around the world come to the viking museum, which bears witness to riches and power going back to the middle ages. white sandy beaches and nice walks await, and elite surfers come here to unstad to surf on one of the best surfing beaches in europe. vestvågøy is sparsely populated, leading to the creation of small villages and communities along the coast and further inland. there are lots of shops and nice little cafés here. i traveled from vestvågøy to stamsund with the hurtigruten boats, fly to leknes and drive on the e10. i experienced here the head sculpture at eggum, then visited to ballstad, one of lofoten’s biggest fishing villages, taken a fishing trip, after that i had been wear a wetsuit and go to scuba diving. there is so much to do in vestvågøy!

with my 65th a week away and age-related stamina decline apparent, the way this life-long dream hike spontaneously came together on father's day was a miracle. the month before, the covid north entrance closure surprise disrupted my 3 am morning start from bozeman. i wasn't ready. our june stay in helena brought me the two books that did. "fools crow" and "the great divide"...the later being the extraordinary 1874 account of earl of dunhaven's travels thru upper yellowstone. on trail june 22nd by 7:30 am after light fog rose off lamar river and the two wolves seceded their buffalo carcass. had the entire ridge to myself for entire hike. after 2.5 miles in in complete wonder, i had idea to share some of this magic with my grandson. making short humorous video clips of my adventures of getting around the buffalo. peak excitement was when i came over ridge about 4.5 miles in and was looking a grizzly's backend 100 yards away. i quietly took my grandson's highlight vid and then, unnoticed, safely turned around. i can't begin to describe the full morning i spent walking on that ridge. the views of lamar valley on one side and yellowstone river on the other. i was just left with the blessed feeling that as much as nature is part of us, we are also as much a part of her.

wochenmarkt boxhagener platz is a charming local market with a great selection of fresh produce, artisan products, and street food. the vibrant atmosphere makes it a fun weekend spot, whether you’re looking for organic fruits and vegetables, unique handmade crafts, or simply enjoying a snack from one of the many food stands. the quality of the products is generally good, with many stalls offering local, seasonal, and sometimes even hard-to-find items. it’s a great place for those who appreciate supporting local businesses and discovering something new. that said, the market can get very crowded, especially on weekends, which makes moving around a bit hectic at times. prices can also be on the higher side for some products, but considering the quality and the experience, it’s usually worth it. if you’re in the area or just love exploring markets, it’s definitely worth a visit, though arriving earlier might give you a more relaxed shopping experience.
