🛒✨ angkor market ii – a grocery wonderland in siem reap! 🌿🥩 if you’re looking for a one-stop shop in siem reap, angkor market ii is the place to be. it's not just one of the biggest supermarkets in town – it’s also one of the most well-organized and well-stocked. i still remember the first time i walked through those doors – i was genuinely amazed by the modern exterior and the wide, carefully curated selection of goods inside. from international products to local essentials, this place has everything. 🥕 their fresh produce and meat section is top-notch. most of the veggies are super fresh, and they even carry a good amount of organic options, which can be tricky to find elsewhere. whether you're cooking up a healthy meal or hunting for snacks, you're covered. 🔧 but wait – there's more! head up to the second floor, and you’ll find a whole section for home essentials like appliances, kitchenware, cleaning supplies, and more. it’s like a mini department store hidden inside a supermarket! 🚻 bonus points for the clean public toilet – a small detail, but it really makes a difference, especially if you're doing a big shopping run. honestly, i get the same giddy feeling walking into angkor market ii as a kid entering a candy store.

🛕 goa gajah - a peaceful temple experience beyond the cave 🌿 we really enjoyed our visit to goa gajah, also known as the elephant cave and found it to be a peaceful and culturally rich stop in bali. the entrance fee is 50,000 idr, and it includes a free sarong rental, which is required to enter the temple area. no need to buy one from the many shops outside, even though some sellers may try to convince you otherwise. while the main cave/temple isn’t overly large or spectacular on its own, the surrounding area is where the real charm lies. you can explore beautifully carved shrines, small hidden temples, and even a buddha temple nestled in the jungle. there’s also a lovely water ceremony area that adds to the spiritual feel of the place. we loved wandering through the tranquil paths and soaking in the calm atmosphere. just a heads-up, the shopkeepers outside can be quite pushy, so it’s best to head straight into the temple grounds and enjoy the peace inside. overall, goa gajah is definitely worth a visit if you’re interested in bali’s cultural and spiritual heritage, and it offers much more than just the famous cave.

🥿 oia loop from finikia – discover santorini authentically this 10.6km circular tour is perfect for anyone who wants to experience oia not just through a lens, but truly experience it. starting in finikia, the route first leads through quiet alleys and vineyards, past traditional houses and small churches. from there, the route takes a wide arc towards the coast – with sweeping views of the caldera and the neighboring islands. oia itself seems almost silent at off-peak times (morning or evening). away from the well-known photo spots, you'll discover narrow staircases, blue domes, and quiet courtyards glowing in the daylight. the return route leads through green valleys and offers a completely different, more rural santorini. conclusion: a wonderfully balanced route with true contrasts – between silence and photo opportunities, nature and architecture, coast and alleyways. those who allow a little more time will be rewarded – with impressions they won't soon forget. 📘 you can find a suitable travel companion for the tour online – just search for “dr moments santorini”.

🧧✨ welcome to sampeng market – a wild ride through the beating heart of bangkok’s chinatown! ✨🧧 if you’re looking for an afternoon adventure with a dash of mystery and a whole lot of “what even is that?” — then more markets to discover, deep in sampeng, is where your senses come alive. 🎎🌶️ this isn’t just a market. oh no no. this is one of the longest roads of organized chaos you’ll ever follow. imagine a never-ending alleyway maze packed with wholesale treasures, hidden food stalls, oddities, and tiny shops tucked into even tinier nooks. you want duck noodle soup? done. 🍜 you want fabric, hair accessories, hardware, paper lanterns, and plastic bananas that sing? they got it. 🎋🔧🎤 you want something so weird you don’t even know what it is? oh yes. many. i’ve taken photos. please explain. 😂 every corner is an adventure. you’ll weave between delivery carts, bargain-hunting aunties, and shopkeepers shouting prices in stereo. don’t worry — just smile and keep walking. 🧺🏃‍♀️ it’s chaotic. it’s colorful. it’s chinatown gold. and on a lazy sunday afternoon, there’s really no better way to explore the hidden pulse of the city. just bring comfy shoes, an open mind, and maybe a small fan (it gets steamy in those alleys!). 😅🧃 whether you’re hunting for souvenirs, odd finds, or just soaking in the wild charm — sam peng market is a must on your bangkok list. 📸 follow fauzia for more street adventures, strange discoveries, and secret foodie gems — on facebook, instagram, youtube, and tiktok. because in bangkok, the best stories are the ones you never planned for. 🐉❤️
